skills.search_text: 0fold-4fold-coding-site-classification Use when you need per-gene, per-population unfolded 0-fold/4-fold SFS counts and divergence counts (mi, Di, m0, D0) from DGN FASTA alignments or 1000GP Phase III VCFs to run McDonald-Kreitman tests with iMKT. You already possess SFS and divergence tables (daf: daf/Pi/P0 and divergence: mi/Di/m0/D0 data frames) — feed them directly to the iMKT R package or web service instead of re-running the pipelines Your data is not D. melanogaster (DGN) or human (1000GP Phase III) protein-coding data; the pre-calculated pipelines cover only these two species http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Pre-processing pipelines (iMKTData Jupyter notebooks, Python/bash) that classify protein-coding sites into MKT functional classes — 0-fold (selected) and 4-fold (neutral) — to build unfolded site frequency spectrum (DAF) and divergence tables per gene and population, enabling on-the-fly MKT analyses in iMKT. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkz372
skills.summary: Pre-processing pipelines (iMKTData Jupyter notebooks, Python/bash) that classify protein-coding sites into MKT functional classes — 0-fold (selected) and 4-fold (neutral) — to build unfolded site frequency spectrum (DAF) and divergence tables per gene and population, enabling on-the-fly MKT analyses in iMKT.

skills.search_text: 16s-abundance-kmer-filtering Use when building or validating a k-mer detection library for baseLess 16S sequence detection on MinION raw signal, where selected k-mers must maximize Smith–Waterman sequence and dynamic-time-warping squiggle dissimilarity. You only need species-level abundance classification with a pre-built model — use baseLess compile_model --model-type abundance or the pre-generated update_16s_db k-mer models instead. You are detecting a non-16S target for which no large read set of a known species and good reference genome is available — the README notes the pre-generated set is attuned to 16S. Input is already a trained baseLess .h5 model or a k-mer list; this skill generates and filters candidate k-mers, it does not run inference. http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Selects a library of 1500 16S k-mers that are mutually dissimilar in sequence and produce easily distinguishable squiggles, using an evolutionary algorithm within baseLess's run_production_pipeline so that the k-mer detection neural networks give unambiguous signals. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017
skills.summary: Selects a library of 1500 16S k-mers that are mutually dissimilar in sequence and produce easily distinguishable squiggles, using an evolutionary algorithm within baseLess's run_production_pipeline so that the k-mer detection neural networks give unambiguous signals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need species-level abundance classification with a pre-built model — use baseLess compile_model --model-type abundance or the pre-generated update_16s_db k-mer models instead. skills.description: Use when you need to decide which 16S OTU-retrieval pipeline preserves raw paired-end read information, or when benchmarking merging-free (CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq/CDSnake) against merging-based pipelines (DADA2, deblur) on mock community datasets.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-pipeline-evaluation
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-pipeline-evaluation Use when you need to decide which 16S OTU-retrieval pipeline preserves raw paired-end read information, or when benchmarking merging-free (CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq/CDSnake) against merging-based pipelines (DADA2, deblur) on mock community datasets. Your input is already a processed OTU/feature table — this skill evaluates raw paired-end FASTQ-to-OTU pipelines, not downstream table analysis. Your reads are single-end or non-overlapping paired-end data, where the merging-free CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq rationale (separate clustering of R1/R2) and the 2 × 250 bp overlapping-read benchmarking design do not apply. You need to benchmark ASV inference on real (non-mock) communities with no known strain ground truth for the OTU-count-vs-reality comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmarking method for comparing 16S rRNA amplicon OTU-retrieval pipelines (CDSnake/CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq vs QIIME2-DADA2 vs deblur) on mock community paired-end 2 × 250 bp datasets, using total outputted read counts, OTU counts, and annotation accuracy as evaluation metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03591-6
skills.summary: Benchmarking method for comparing 16S rRNA amplicon OTU-retrieval pipelines (CDSnake/CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq vs QIIME2-DADA2 vs deblur) on mock community paired-end 2 × 250 bp datasets, using total outputted read counts, OTU counts, and annotation accuracy as evaluation metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is already a processed OTU/feature table — this skill evaluates raw paired-end FASTQ-to-OTU pipelines, not downstream table analysis. Your reads are single-end or non-overlapping paired-end data, where the merging-free CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq rationale (separate clustering of R1/R2) and the 2 × 250 bp overlapping-read benchmarking design do not apply. You need to benchmark ASV inference on real (non-mock) communities with no known strain ground truth for the OTU-count-vs-reality comparison.

skills.description: Use when a 16S rRNA amplicon OTU table (biom, QIIME, GAAS, Unifrac or generic format) with read counts and unaltered Greengenes taxonomic assignments needs GCN bias correction, or when 16S qPCR total abundances must be corrected by community-average GCN.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-profile-correction
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-profile-correction Use when a 16S rRNA amplicon OTU table (biom, QIIME, GAAS, Unifrac or generic format) with read counts and unaltered Greengenes taxonomic assignments needs GCN bias correction, or when 16S qPCR total abundances must be corrected by community-average GCN. The input table contains percentages rather than raw read counts, or taxa have altered/non-Greengenes assignments — CopyRighter requires unaltered taxonomic strings and its GCN data currently cover Greengenes only (Silva extension is anticipated, not available) The goal is to correct GC percent bias, genome length bias, or fungal ITS variation — CopyRighter is currently limited to 16S rRNA gene GCN pending appropriate pre-computed estimates Only relative abundance without any GCN-bearing taxonomy is available (e.g. unclassified OTUs dominate), making community-average-GCN fallback the only correction possible and accuracy gains uncertain http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Corrects 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) bias in amplicon profiles and qPCR total abundance using CopyRighter, which weights each OTU's read counts by the inverse of its lineage-specific GCN inferred within a phylogenetic framework on the Greengenes database. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Corrects 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) bias in amplicon profiles and qPCR total abundance using CopyRighter, which weights each OTU's read counts by the inverse of its lineage-specific GCN inferred within a phylogenetic framework on the Greengenes database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input table contains percentages rather than raw read counts, or taxa have altered/non-Greengenes assignments — CopyRighter requires unaltered taxonomic strings and its GCN data currently cover Greengenes only (Silva extension is anticipated, not available) The goal is to correct GC percent bias, genome length bias, or fungal ITS variation — CopyRighter is currently limited to 16S rRNA gene GCN pending appropriate pre-computed estimates Only relative abundance without any GCN-bearing taxonomy is available (e.g. unclassified OTUs dominate), making community-average-GCN fallback the only correction possible and accuracy gains uncertain

skills.description: Use when paired-end 16S FASTQ reads show good base quality over an initial stretch (e.g. ~200 bp R1 / 180 bp R2) followed by a sudden quality drop, and reads must be trimmed and length-filtered before OTU clustering.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-quality-filtering Use when paired-end 16S FASTQ reads show good base quality over an initial stretch (e.g. ~200 bp R1 / 180 bp R2) followed by a sudden quality drop, and reads must be trimmed and length-filtered before OTU clustering. Input is not paired-end 16S amplicon FASTQ data (e.g. shotgun metagenomic or already-merged reads), since the downstream CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq scheme relies on separate R1/R2 clustering without merging Reads lack a clear high-quality prefix with a sudden quality drop that can be captured by fixed p/q lengths, making fixed-length cropping inappropriate A feature/OTU table already exists and no raw-read trimming is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Cropping paired-end 16S amplicon reads to their high-quality prefixes and quality-filtering them with Trimmomatic, as configured in the CDSnake pipeline, so that only reliable bases enter the downstream CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq clustering. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03591-6
skills.summary: Cropping paired-end 16S amplicon reads to their high-quality prefixes and quality-filtering them with Trimmomatic, as configured in the CDSnake pipeline, so that only reliable bases enter the downstream CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not paired-end 16S amplicon FASTQ data (e.g. shotgun metagenomic or already-merged reads), since the downstream CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq scheme relies on separate R1/R2 clustering without merging Reads lack a clear high-quality prefix with a sudden quality drop that can be captured by fixed p/q lengths, making fixed-length cropping inappropriate A feature/OTU table already exists and no raw-read trimming is required

skills.description: Use when Illumina MiSeq 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (primer-removed, paired, trimmed to 250 bases) must be de novo clustered into true sequence variants with one-mismatch children assessed against sequencing error.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-sequence-clustering
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-sequence-clustering Use when Illumina MiSeq 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (primer-removed, paired, trimmed to 250 bases) must be de novo clustered into true sequence variants with one-mismatch children assessed against sequencing error. Goal is detection of true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq is not sensitive there; the article recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 Variants involve insertions/deletions or indel variation relative to a parent — HashSeq considers only one-mismatch variants and treats indel events as separate parent sequences; the article suggests Deblur or other multiple-sequence-alignment methods instead Data come from long-read technologies such as PacBio, where the assumption of rarity of multiple-mismatch sequences may not hold http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Cluster pre-processed 16S rRNA gene FASTQ reads into parent sequences and one-mismatch children using HashSeq's HashMap-based de novo variant caller, then infer true biological sequences against a normally distributed background error model estimated by LOESS regression. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Cluster pre-processed 16S rRNA gene FASTQ reads into parent sequences and one-mismatch children using HashSeq's HashMap-based de novo variant caller, then infer true biological sequences against a normally distributed background error model estimated by LOESS regression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is detection of true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq is not sensitive there; the article recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 Variants involve insertions/deletions or indel variation relative to a parent — HashSeq considers only one-mismatch variants and treats indel events as separate parent sequences; the article suggests Deblur or other multiple-sequence-alignment methods instead Data come from long-read technologies such as PacBio, where the assumption of rarity of multiple-mismatch sequences may not hold

skills.description: Use when calling de novo sequence variants from primer-trimmed, paired Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (e.g., mock communities like PRJEB24409), especially when a conservative, fast, scalable caller with explicit P values is preferred over DADA2 defaults.
skills.name: 16s-amplicon-variant-calling
skills.search_text: 16s-amplicon-variant-calling Use when calling de novo sequence variants from primer-trimmed, paired Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (e.g., mock communities like PRJEB24409), especially when a conservative, fast, scalable caller with explicit P values is preferred over DADA2 defaults. Detection of true low-abundance sequences — the article recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 for that purpose Long-read data such as PacBio, where the assumption of rarity of multiple-mismatch sequences does not hold Analyses requiring indel variation relative to a parent, or two-or-more-mismatch variants — use Deblur or methods with multiple-sequence alignments instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infer true 16S rRNA gene sequence variants from Illumina amplicon reads using HashSeq, a de novo caller that clusters one-mismatch children to parents via a HashMap approach and models background error rates with a normal distribution fitted by LOESS regression, yielding explicit P values per variant. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Infer true 16S rRNA gene sequence variants from Illumina amplicon reads using HashSeq, a de novo caller that clusters one-mismatch children to parents via a HashMap approach and models background error rates with a normal distribution fitted by LOESS regression, yielding explicit P values per variant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Detection of true low-abundance sequences — the article recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 for that purpose Long-read data such as PacBio, where the assumption of rarity of multiple-mismatch sequences does not hold Analyses requiring indel variation relative to a parent, or two-or-more-mismatch variants — use Deblur or methods with multiple-sequence alignments instead

skills.search_text: 16s-copy-number-estimation Use when inferring gene family content or 16S copy number for unsequenced organisms on a Greengenes/IMG 16S reference tree, or normalizing 16S OTU tables by predicted copy number. The organisms of interest already have complete reference genomes — use their direct IMG/KEGG genome annotations instead of inferring traits You need viral or eukaryotic metagenome components — PICRUSt only covers bacterial and archaeal 16S sequences Marker gene sequences are identical among strains — the method cannot distinguish strain-level variation http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 An extended ancestral state reconstruction method (PICRUSt) that predicts gene family content and 16S rRNA copy number for all tips on a 16S marker gene reference tree, enabling metagenome prediction for organisms without sequenced genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: An extended ancestral state reconstruction method (PICRUSt) that predicts gene family content and 16S rRNA copy number for all tips on a 16S marker gene reference tree, enabling metagenome prediction for organisms without sequenced genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organisms of interest already have complete reference genomes — use their direct IMG/KEGG genome annotations instead of inferring traits You need viral or eukaryotic metagenome components — PICRUSt only covers bacterial and archaeal 16S sequences Marker gene sequences are identical among strains — the method cannot distinguish strain-level variation

skills.description: Use when demultiplexed, trimmed paired-end 16S reads must be processed through multiple denoising/clustering alternatives (DADA2, Deblur, vsearch open/closed/de novo) and the resulting representative sequence sets compared via pairwise UniFrac distances.
skills.name: 16s-denoising-execution-dada2-deblur
skills.search_text: 16s-denoising-execution-dada2-deblur Use when demultiplexed, trimmed paired-end 16S reads must be processed through multiple denoising/clustering alternatives (DADA2, Deblur, vsearch open/closed/de novo) and the resulting representative sequence sets compared via pairwise UniFrac distances. Input is already a feature/OTU table from a single denoising or clustering run — the DC comparison step presupposes raw demultiplexed reads processed under all five alternatives Only one DC method is of interest and no cross-method agreement assessment (UniFrac comparison) is needed Data are not 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., shotgun metagenomics) — the pipeline is built around 16S rRNA amplicon profiling http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Executes the MiCoNE denoising/clustering (DC) step on demultiplexed 16S paired-end reads using five alternatives — vsearch open-reference, closed-reference, and de novo clustering, DADA2, and Deblur — then compares the representative sequence sets by mean weighted and unweighted UniFrac distances between method pairs. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: Executes the MiCoNE denoising/clustering (DC) step on demultiplexed 16S paired-end reads using five alternatives — vsearch open-reference, closed-reference, and de novo clustering, DADA2, and Deblur — then compares the representative sequence sets by mean weighted and unweighted UniFrac distances between method pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/OTU table from a single denoising or clustering run — the DC comparison step presupposes raw demultiplexed reads processed under all five alternatives Only one DC method is of interest and no cross-method agreement assessment (UniFrac comparison) is needed Data are not 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., shotgun metagenomics) — the pipeline is built around 16S rRNA amplicon profiling

skills.description: Use when benchmarking 16S-based metagenome prediction (e.g. PICRUSt KOs) against observed shotgun KO profiles as a function of sequencing depth, to identify the read depth at which prediction equals or exceeds a rarefied metagenome.
skills.name: 16s-otu-rarefaction-depth-normalization
skills.search_text: 16s-otu-rarefaction-depth-normalization Use when benchmarking 16S-based metagenome prediction (e.g. PICRUSt KOs) against observed shotgun KO profiles as a function of sequencing depth, to identify the read depth at which prediction equals or exceeds a rarefied metagenome. You already have deep shotgun metagenomes for every sample — rarefying to shallow depths only tests prediction against artificially degraded data, not real sequencing alternatives The community includes substantial viral or eukaryotic components, since PICRUSt's reference contains only bacterial and archaeal 16S marker gene sequences and does not infer those components Samples have very high NSTI values (reference database phylogenetic gaps), so predicted metagenomes carry wide confidence intervals and depth-based correlation comparisons are dominated by prediction uncertainty http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Rarefaction-based benchmarking that compares PICRUSt-predicted KO metagenomes (from 16S OTU tables) against rarefied shallow shotgun metagenomes across matched read depths, using Spearman rank correlation to find the crossover depth (~72,000 total sequences) below which prediction outperforms sequencing. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Rarefaction-based benchmarking that compares PICRUSt-predicted KO metagenomes (from 16S OTU tables) against rarefied shallow shotgun metagenomes across matched read depths, using Spearman rank correlation to find the crossover depth (~72,000 total sequences) below which prediction outperforms sequencing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have deep shotgun metagenomes for every sample — rarefying to shallow depths only tests prediction against artificially degraded data, not real sequencing alternatives The community includes substantial viral or eukaryotic components, since PICRUSt's reference contains only bacterial and archaeal 16S marker gene sequences and does not infer those components Samples have very high NSTI values (reference database phylogenetic gaps), so predicted metagenomes carry wide confidence intervals and depth-based correlation comparisons are dominated by prediction uncertainty

skills.search_text: 16s-otu-table-processing Use when marker-gene (16S) abundance data must be converted into a PICRUSt-compatible closed-reference OTU table as the first step of metagenome prediction, NSTI calculation, or accuracy-vs-NSTI analysis. The data are shotgun metagenome reads rather than 16S marker gene sequences — direct functional profiling (e.g., HUMAnN annotation to KOs) is appropriate instead of 16S-based prediction Open-reference or de novo OTU picking is desired — unclassified OTUs without reference tree tips cannot be normalized or predicted by PICRUSt's ancestral state reconstruction The community contains viral or eukaryotic components whose function should be inferred — only bacterial and archaeal 16S sequences are included in this version http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Constructs closed-reference 16S OTU tables (e.g., with QIIME 1.5.0-dev pick_reference_otus_through_otu_table.py using uclust against Greengenes+IMG) in the format required by PICRUSt so that OTU abundances can be normalized by 16S copy number and used for metagenome prediction and NSTI-based accuracy assessment. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Constructs closed-reference 16S OTU tables (e.g., with QIIME 1.5.0-dev pick_reference_otus_through_otu_table.py using uclust against Greengenes+IMG) in the format required by PICRUSt so that OTU abundances can be normalized by 16S copy number and used for metagenome prediction and NSTI-based accuracy assessment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are shotgun metagenome reads rather than 16S marker gene sequences — direct functional profiling (e.g., HUMAnN annotation to KOs) is appropriate instead of 16S-based prediction Open-reference or de novo OTU picking is desired — unclassified OTUs without reference tree tips cannot be normalized or predicted by PICRUSt's ancestral state reconstruction The community contains viral or eukaryotic components whose function should be inferred — only bacterial and archaeal 16S sequences are included in this version

The community contains viral or eukaryotic components, since only bacterial and archaeal 16S marker gene sequences are included in the reference Strain-level functional variation matters and strains share identical marker gene sequences, which PICRUSt cannot distinguish Reference genomes phylogenetically close to the sampled organisms are lacking (high NSTI), indicating unreliable predictions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Predicts gene family (KO) abundance metagenomes from 16S rRNA OTU tables using PICRUSt's metagenome inference step: 16S copy-number normalization followed by multiplying normalized OTU abundances by pre-calculated per-taxon gene contents and summing per sample. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Predicts gene family (KO) abundance metagenomes from 16S rRNA OTU tables using PICRUSt's metagenome inference step: 16S copy-number normalization followed by multiplying normalized OTU abundances by pre-calculated per-taxon gene contents and summing per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The community contains viral or eukaryotic components, since only bacterial and archaeal 16S marker gene sequences are included in the reference Strain-level functional variation matters and strains share identical marker gene sequences, which PICRUSt cannot distinguish Reference genomes phylogenetically close to the sampled organisms are lacking (high NSTI), indicating unreliable predictions

skills.description: Use when running HashSeq's inferTrueSequences on Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data and a filtering threshold must be set to remove low-abundance parent variants before LOESS-based error modeling and variant calling.
skills.name: 16s-rrna-abundance-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-abundance-threshold-filtering Use when running HashSeq's inferTrueSequences on Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data and a filtering threshold must be set to remove low-abundance parent variants before LOESS-based error modeling and variant calling. The goal is detecting true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq is deliberately conservative and the paper recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 for low-abundance variants. Input is already a filtered count table (e.g., SvTable.txt from a prior inferTrueSequences run) rather than raw/trimmed FASTQ files. The analysis requires modeling indels or multi-mismatch variants; HashSeq only considers one-mismatch children and treats indel events as separate parent sequences. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Removes 16S rRNA gene sequence variants whose total reads across all samples fall below a parent-abundance threshold (default 1,000 reads; 10,000 for the largest data sets) during HashSeq variant inference, so that downstream inference and the LOESS background error model operate only on well-supported parents. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Removes 16S rRNA gene sequence variants whose total reads across all samples fall below a parent-abundance threshold (default 1,000 reads; 10,000 for the largest data sets) during HashSeq variant inference, so that downstream inference and the LOESS background error model operate only on well-supported parents.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detecting true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq is deliberately conservative and the paper recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 for low-abundance variants. skills.description: Use when assembling overlapping paired-end Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g. 108-base M. capsulatus pairs) and deciding whether lowering the PANDAseq quality threshold from 0.9 to a looser cutoff (e.g. 0.6) recovers more sequences.
skills.name: 16s-rrna-amplicon-count-comparison
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-amplicon-count-comparison Use when assembling overlapping paired-end Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g. 108-base M. capsulatus pairs) and deciding whether lowering the PANDAseq quality threshold from 0.9 to a looser cutoff (e.g. 0.6) recovers more sequences. Input reads have already been assembled into a single contig per pair — re-merging and re-thresholding would change the underlying sequence set, not test the threshold effect. The library is not expected to contain overlapping paired-end reads (PANDAseq discards pairs with no suitable overlap), so count comparisons between thresholds would not be meaningful. Goal is de novo assembly of long reads (e.g. whole-genome data) rather than assembling overlapping short paired-end Illumina amplicon reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantifies how the PANDAseq assembly quality-score threshold changes sequence recovery for a paired-end Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon library, using the M. capsulatus single-template benchmark (598,775 reads at threshold 0.9 vs 652,249 at 0.6). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Quantifies how the PANDAseq assembly quality-score threshold changes sequence recovery for a paired-end Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon library, using the M. capsulatus single-template benchmark (598,775 reads at threshold 0.9 vs 652,249 at 0.6).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have already been assembled into a single contig per pair — re-merging and re-thresholding would change the underlying sequence set, not test the threshold effect. The library is not expected to contain overlapping paired-end reads (PANDAseq discards pairs with no suitable overlap), so count comparisons between thresholds would not be meaningful. Goal is de novo assembly of long reads (e.g. whole-genome data) rather than assembling overlapping short paired-end Illumina amplicon reads.

skills.description: Use when a 16S rRNA amplicon or qPCR analysis needs GCN estimates for bacterial or archaeal taxa lacking a sequenced genome, and a phylogenetic tree with taxonomy (e.g. Greengenes 99%-identity OTUs) is available.
skills.name: 16s-rrna-gene-copy-number-inference
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-gene-copy-number-inference Use when a 16S rRNA amplicon or qPCR analysis needs GCN estimates for bacterial or archaeal taxa lacking a sequenced genome, and a phylogenetic tree with taxonomy (e.g. Greengenes 99%-identity OTUs) is available. The target taxonomy is not Greengenes (e.g. Silva); coverage extension is only anticipated in the article All taxa of interest already have sequenced genomes with directly measured GCN, making phylogenetic inference unnecessary Bias in the profile is not due to 16S rRNA gene copy number (e.g. GC percent, genome length, or fungal ITS variation, which lack appropriate pre-computed estimates) http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 Infers 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) of unsequenced Greengenes taxa by mapping curated genome GCN values onto an OTU tree and propagating them with phylogenetically independent contrasts (PIC), since GCN is strongly linked to microbial phylogeny. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Infers 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) of unsequenced Greengenes taxa by mapping curated genome GCN values onto an OTU tree and propagating them with phylogenetically independent contrasts (PIC), since GCN is strongly linked to microbial phylogeny.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target taxonomy is not Greengenes (e.g. Silva); coverage extension is only anticipated in the article All taxa of interest already have sequenced genomes with directly measured GCN, making phylogenetic inference unnecessary Bias in the profile is not due to 16S rRNA gene copy number (e.g. GC percent, genome length, or fungal ITS variation, which lack appropriate pre-computed estimates)

skills.description: Use when you have curated full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences (e.g. ≥800 bp aligned bases) and need to flag which carry ≥10 bp insertions and report max/mean/sd insertion lengths, or when replicating the Brown et al. 2015 (10.1038/nature14486) CPR insertion statistics.
skills.name: 16s-rrna-insertion-boundary-detection
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-insertion-boundary-detection Use when you have curated full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences (e.g. ≥800 bp aligned bases) and need to flag which carry ≥10 bp insertions and report max/mean/sd insertion lengths, or when replicating the Brown et al. 2015 (10.1038/nature14486) CPR insertion statistics. Sequences are shorter than the ≥800 bp aligned-sequence threshold the paper used for phylogenetic/insertion analysis — boundaries will be unreliable The goal is insertion detection in transcribed rRNAs — the paper's metatranscriptomic mapping showed insertions are not retained in transcribed RNAs and are probably rapidly degraded You need insertion detection in eukaryotic or archaeal rRNAs, or in non-CPR bacterial sets, where the paper found such insertions are rare (SILVA v115 analysis) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Detects and characterizes large (≥10 bp) insertion sequences within bacterial 16S rRNA genes by identifying large gaps in HMM/covariance-model alignments (e.g. cmscan against Rfam or a sequence-only model built from the Comparative RNA Web seed alignment), then computes fraction-inserted and insertion-length statistics as a structured JSON record. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: Detects and characterizes large (≥10 bp) insertion sequences within bacterial 16S rRNA genes by identifying large gaps in HMM/covariance-model alignments (e.g. cmscan against Rfam or a sequence-only model built from the Comparative RNA Web seed alignment), then computes fraction-inserted and insertion-length statistics as a structured JSON record.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are shorter than the ≥800 bp aligned-sequence threshold the paper used for phylogenetic/insertion analysis — boundaries will be unreliable The goal is insertion detection in transcribed rRNAs — the paper's metatranscriptomic mapping showed insertions are not retained in transcribed RNAs and are probably rapidly degraded You need insertion detection in eukaryotic or archaeal rRNAs, or in non-CPR bacterial sets, where the paper found such insertions are rare (SILVA v115 analysis)

skills.description: Use when validating that a salient 16S k-mer subset (baseLess read_detection k-mers) can support species detection against an arbitrary genomic background, by quantifying unique-k-mer identifiability across simulated mixture sizes from 1 up to 10,000 constituents.
skills.name: 16s-rrna-kmer-uniqueness-analysis
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-kmer-uniqueness-analysis Use when validating that a salient 16S k-mer subset (baseLess read_detection k-mers) can support species detection against an arbitrary genomic background, by quantifying unique-k-mer identifiability across simulated mixture sizes from 1 up to 10,000 constituents. The goal is to run baseLess signal-level inference on real fast5 reads rather than evaluate k-mer uniqueness in silico (use baseLess run_inference instead). Targets are whole genomes or non-16S sequences; read_detection k-mers have been tested for and attuned to 16S sequence. Sample composition is already known (e.g. the 20-bacterial-species classification benchmark), so uniqueness against an arbitrary background need not be simulated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 In silico benchmark of the salient 16S k-mer subset used by baseLess: for mixtures of 1 to 10,000 species drawn from the NCBI 16S pool (BioProject PRJNA33175), it computes the fraction of species possessing at least one k-mer that occurs uniquely within the mixture, demonstrating the subset identifies the majority of species even at 10,000 constituents (Supplementary Fig. S2). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017
skills.summary: In silico benchmark of the salient 16S k-mer subset used by baseLess: for mixtures of 1 to 10,000 species drawn from the NCBI 16S pool (BioProject PRJNA33175), it computes the fraction of species possessing at least one k-mer that occurs uniquely within the mixture, demonstrating the subset identifies the majority of species even at 10,000 constituents (Supplementary Fig. S2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to run baseLess signal-level inference on real fast5 reads rather than evaluate k-mer uniqueness in silico (use baseLess run_inference instead). Targets are whole genomes or non-16S sequences; read_detection k-mers have been tested for and attuned to 16S sequence. Sample composition is already known (e.g. the 20-bacterial-species classification benchmark), so uniqueness against an arbitrary background need not be simulated.

skills.name: 16s-rrna-multirank-classification-head-design
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-multirank-classification-head-design Use when building or reconstructing a 16S rRNA classifier that must predict all seven Linnean ranks (Domain through Species) in a single forward pass, or when verifying that a checkpoint exposes exactly seven per-rank output distributions. The task requires only a single taxonomic rank prediction (e.g., species-only assignment) rather than the full seven-rank hierarchy the parallel heads produce Input is a feature/abundance table or sequence variants rather than raw 16S rRNA sequences, or the marker gene is 18S rRNA or shotgun metagenomic data, which the article notes remain untested for this framework Base-level quality scores must be incorporated — DeepTaxa operates on FASTA-formatted sequences only http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 Design pattern from DeepTaxa for emitting taxonomic predictions at all seven Linnean ranks simultaneously: seven parallel linear classifier heads attached to the fused 896-dim CNN-BERT representation, each with softmax at uniform temperature T=1.0, so one forward pass over a 512-token BPE input yields domain-through-species distributions. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166

skills.description: Use when you have curated 16S rRNA gene sequences (e.g. assembled from metagenomes, ≥800 bp) and need to estimate which taxa a specific primer pair would miss in an amplicon survey.
skills.name: 16s-rrna-primer-binding-assessment
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-primer-binding-assessment Use when you have curated 16S rRNA gene sequences (e.g. assembled from metagenomes, ≥800 bp) and need to estimate which taxa a specific primer pair would miss in an amplicon survey. Input is a raw amplicon read set or OTU/feature table rather than curated full-length (≥800 bp) 16S rRNA gene sequences — binding cannot be assessed without sequence spanning the primer sites 16S sequences still contain large (≥10 bp) intron/insertion sequences that were not removed, since insertions within the primer region would spuriously inflate evasion rates Sequences that do not span the 515–806 E. coli-coordinated region — they cannot be scored for 515F/806R binding and should be excluded rather than counted as evading http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A method for quantifying what fraction of assembled 16S rRNA gene sequences would evade detection by a given amplicon-survey primer pair (here 515F/806R), by first de-redundantizing sequences at 97% identity with USEARCH and then scoring primer binding with Primer Prospector. It quantifies amplification bias of common 16S primers against divergent lineages such as the CPR. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: A method for quantifying what fraction of assembled 16S rRNA gene sequences would evade detection by a given amplicon-survey primer pair (here 515F/806R), by first de-redundantizing sequences at 97% identity with USEARCH and then scoring primer binding with Primer Prospector. It quantifies amplification bias of common 16S primers against divergent lineages such as the CPR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw amplicon read set or OTU/feature table rather than curated full-length (≥800 bp) 16S rRNA gene sequences — binding cannot be assessed without sequence spanning the primer sites 16S sequences still contain large (≥10 bp) intron/insertion sequences that were not removed, since insertions within the primer region would spuriously inflate evasion rates Sequences that do not span the 515–806 E. coli-coordinated region — they cannot be scored for 515F/806R binding and should be excluded rather than counted as evading

skills.description: Use when you have per-sequence species predictions from a 16S rRNA classifier (e.g., DeepTaxa on the Greengenes2 2024.09 69,335-sequence test set) and need to show whether accuracy degrades for test sequences distant from the 277,336-sequence training pool.
skills.name: 16s-rrna-similarity-bucket-stratification
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-similarity-bucket-stratification Use when you have per-sequence species predictions from a 16S rRNA classifier (e.g., DeepTaxa on the Greengenes2 2024.09 69,335-sequence test set) and need to show whether accuracy degrades for test sequences distant from the 277,336-sequence training pool. You only need overall species accuracy/F1 on the Greengenes2 test set (e.g., 92.95% accuracy / 0.9212 F1) — aggregate metrics require no similarity stratification. The classifier's training pool is unknown or disjoint from the reference used for the identity search, so 'nearest training neighbor' identity is undefined. Evaluating a different marker gene or modality (e.g., 18S rRNA or shotgun metagenomic data) for which no Greengenes2 training-pool identity relationship exists. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Stratifies 16S rRNA taxonomic-classifier performance by evolutionary novelty: each test sequence is BLAST/VSEARCH-aligned against the training FASTA to get nearest-neighbor percent identity, binned into >97%, 90–97%, and <90% buckets, and species-level weighted F1 is computed per bucket to expose degradation that a single aggregate F1 (e.g., DeepTaxa's 0.9212) hides. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Stratifies 16S rRNA taxonomic-classifier performance by evolutionary novelty: each test sequence is BLAST/VSEARCH-aligned against the training FASTA to get nearest-neighbor percent identity, binned into >97%, 90–97%, and <90% buckets, and species-level weighted F1 is computed per bucket to expose degradation that a single aggregate F1 (e.g., DeepTaxa's 0.9212) hides.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need overall species accuracy/F1 on the Greengenes2 test set (e.g., 92.95% accuracy / 0.9212 F1) — aggregate metrics require no similarity stratification. The classifier's training pool is unknown or disjoint from the reference used for the identity search, so 'nearest training neighbor' identity is undefined. Evaluating a different marker gene or modality (e.g., 18S rRNA or shotgun metagenomic data) for which no Greengenes2 training-pool identity relationship exists.

skills.description: Use when assembled 16S rRNA genes from metagenomes contain large insertion sequences (≥10 bp, e.g. CPR self-splicing introns up to 2,004 bp) that would corrupt a naive sequence alignment, and a reliable domain-level or phyla-level phylogeny is the goal.
skills.name: 16s-rrna-structural-alignment
skills.search_text: 16s-rrna-structural-alignment Use when assembled 16S rRNA genes from metagenomes contain large insertion sequences (≥10 bp, e.g. CPR self-splicing introns up to 2,004 bp) that would corrupt a naive sequence alignment, and a reliable domain-level or phyla-level phylogeny is the goal. If the 16S rRNA genes contain no large insertion sequences (insertions are rare in bacteria outside the CPR per the SILVA database search) — a standard sequence alignment suffices. If the goal is amplicon-survey detectability assessment rather than phylogeny — use the primer-binding analysis (515F/806R) workflow instead. If sequences are shorter than 800 bp of aligned sequence, they will be excluded and cannot support this phylogeny. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Removes large (≥10 bp) intron insertions from 16S rRNA gene sequences, then performs structural (covariance-model-based) alignment with SSUAlign to produce an insertion-free bacterial alignment suitable for maximum-likelihood phylogeny in which the candidate phyla radiation (CPR) is recovered monophyletic. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: Removes large (≥10 bp) intron insertions from 16S rRNA gene sequences, then performs structural (covariance-model-based) alignment with SSUAlign to produce an insertion-free bacterial alignment suitable for maximum-likelihood phylogeny in which the candidate phyla radiation (CPR) is recovered monophyletic.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the 16S rRNA genes contain no large insertion sequences (insertions are rare in bacteria outside the CPR per the SILVA database search) — a standard sequence alignment suffices. If the goal is amplicon-survey detectability assessment rather than phylogeny — use the primer-binding analysis (515F/806R) workflow instead. If sequences are shorter than 800 bp of aligned sequence, they will be excluded and cannot support this phylogeny.

Input is a feature/abundance table or ASV matrix rather than raw 16S FASTA sequences — DeepTaxa operates on FASTA-formatted sequences only Sequences are not 16S rRNA (e.g., 18S rRNA or shotgun metagenomic data) — the paper states performance on other marker genes and modalities remains untested Base-level quality scores are essential to the analysis — the model does not incorporate quality scores and takes FASTA-only input http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Classifies 16S rRNA gene sequences into all seven Linnean ranks (domain through species) in a single forward pass using DeepTaxa's HybridCNNBERTClassifier, which fuses a multiscale CNN with a from-scratch transformer on the DNABERT-2 BPE vocabulary, reaching 92.96% species-level accuracy on the Greengenes2 2024.09 test set. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166

skills.description: Reference for assigning taxonomy to 16S rRNA representative sequences when comparing multiple reference databases (e.g., Greengenes vs NCBI RefSeq) or when predicted taxonomic abundances are needed for mock-community accuracy assessment.
skills.name: 16s-taxonomy-assignment
skills.search_text: 16s-taxonomy-assignment Reference for assigning taxonomy to 16S rRNA representative sequences when comparing multiple reference databases (e.g., Greengenes vs NCBI RefSeq) or when predicted taxonomic abundances are needed for mock-community accuracy assessment. Input is already a taxonomy-annotated feature table or abundance profile — assignment has already been performed and re-running classifiers would not change results. The goal is de novo taxonomic discovery of novel lineages — closed-reference Naive Bayes/BLAST assignment against Greengenes/RefSeq only classifies sequences the references can explain. You need a single canonical taxonomy for downstream analysis and cannot afford to run multiple databases — this skill is explicitly for comparing database-dependent outputs, since no database performed better than the others in absolute terms. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assigns taxonomy to 16S amplicon representative sequences using parallel taxonomic classifiers (QIIME2 Naive Bayes with the Greengenes 'gg_13_8_99_515_806' classifier and BLAST against 'ncbi_refseq') as implemented in the MiCoNE pipeline, enabling comparison of how taxonomy database choice affects downstream taxonomic abundance profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: Assigns taxonomy to 16S amplicon representative sequences using parallel taxonomic classifiers (QIIME2 Naive Bayes with the Greengenes 'gg_13_8_99_515_806' classifier and BLAST against 'ncbi_refseq') as implemented in the MiCoNE pipeline, enabling comparison of how taxonomy database choice affects downstream taxonomic abundance profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a taxonomy-annotated feature table or abundance profile — assignment has already been performed and re-running classifiers would not change results. The goal is de novo taxonomic discovery of novel lineages — closed-reference Naive Bayes/BLAST assignment against Greengenes/RefSeq only classifies sequences the references can explain. You need a single canonical taxonomy for downstream analysis and cannot afford to run multiple databases — this skill is explicitly for comparing database-dependent outputs, since no database performed better than the others in absolute terms.

skills.search_text: 454-homopolymer-error-modeling Use when gene-finding on 454 metagenomic reads where homopolymer-run artifacts cause frame-disrupting indels, or when simulating/validating 454 read error models against true gene coordinates.
