skills.name: abundance-error-distance-metrics
skills.search_text: abundance-error-distance-metrics Use when comparing abundance accuracy of a counting AMQ (e.g. counting Bloom filter) against fimpera and you need overestimation proportions and error-distance statistics on true-positive calls. Input query results are false-positive calls rather than true-positive calls — this skill only characterizes abundance correctness on true positives The indexes being compared are not identically sized counting Bloom filters — size-reduction experiments (two-orders-of-magnitude smaller filters) measure a different property (precision at reduced size), not this same-size correctness comparison The AMQ does not support abundance queries, so reported abundances and overestimation distances cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reproduce the fimpera paper's abundance-correctness metrics by classifying true-positive k-mer abundance calls as exact or overestimated and computing the proportion of overestimations and the average distance of incorrect calls from ground truth, comparing an original cBF against fimpera (z=3) on identically sized indexes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad305
skills.summary: Reproduce the fimpera paper's abundance-correctness metrics by classifying true-positive k-mer abundance calls as exact or overestimated and computing the proportion of overestimations and the average distance of incorrect calls from ground truth, comparing an original cBF against fimpera (z=3) on identically sized indexes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input query results are false-positive calls rather than true-positive calls — this skill only characterizes abundance correctness on true positives The indexes being compared are not identically sized counting Bloom filters — size-reduction experiments (two-orders-of-magnitude smaller filters) measure a different property (precision at reduced size), not this same-size correctness comparison The AMQ does not support abundance queries, so reported abundances and overestimation distances cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when comparing a metagenomic read classifier's genus-level sensitivity and abundance profiles against multiple baselines on mock communities with known ground-truth abundances.
skills.name: abundance-estimation-comparison
skills.search_text: abundance-estimation-comparison Use when comparing a metagenomic read classifier's genus-level sensitivity and abundance profiles against multiple baselines on mock communities with known ground-truth abundances. Input reads come from a real clinical/environmental metagenome with no ground-truth community composition, so precision/recall against a true profile cannot be computed Reads have strongly different lengths and error profiles (e.g. long-read sequencing), where the authors state retraining might be required The target organisms are novel uncultured species absent from the training repertoire, since adding new species requires retraining the entire deep neural network http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmark DeepMicrobes' genus-level read classification and abundance estimation against eight state-of-the-art taxonomic classifiers (Kraken, Kraken 2, Centrifuge, CLARK, CLARK-S, Kaiju, DIAMOND-MEGAN, BLAST-MEGAN) on ten HBC mock communities with known ground-truth genus profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Benchmark DeepMicrobes' genus-level read classification and abundance estimation against eight state-of-the-art taxonomic classifiers (Kraken, Kraken 2, Centrifuge, CLARK, CLARK-S, Kaiju, DIAMOND-MEGAN, BLAST-MEGAN) on ten HBC mock communities with known ground-truth genus profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads come from a real clinical/environmental metagenome with no ground-truth community composition, so precision/recall against a true profile cannot be computed Reads have strongly different lengths and error profiles (e.g. long-read sequencing), where the authors state retraining might be required The target organisms are novel uncultured species absent from the training repertoire, since adding new species requires retraining the entire deep neural network

skills.description: Use when you have genome FASTAs for a target species plus closely related background species and need a model to classify raw MinION fast5 reads (pure samples) by k-mer abundance without basecalling.
skills.name: abundance-kmer-model-compilation
skills.search_text: abundance-kmer-model-compilation Use when you have genome FASTAs for a target species plus closely related background species and need a model to classify raw MinION fast5 reads (pure samples) by k-mer abundance without basecalling. Sample is amplified/metagenomic (e.g. 16S amplicon or microbial mixture) — use read_detection mode instead, which retains reads with >66% of target k-mers No reference genome FASTA is available for the target or background species Input is already basecalled sequence data where standard alignment/classification pipelines are appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Compile a baseLess abundance-mode .h5 model that discriminates one target genome from specified background genomes by comparing k-mer abundances found in MinION electrical signal to genome k-mer abundances, enabling species-level detection without basecalling. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017
skills.summary: Compile a baseLess abundance-mode .h5 model that discriminates one target genome from specified background genomes by comparing k-mer abundances found in MinION electrical signal to genome k-mer abundances, enabling species-level detection without basecalling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample is amplified/metagenomic (e.g. 16S amplicon or microbial mixture) — use read_detection mode instead, which retains reads with >66% of target k-mers No reference genome FASTA is available for the target or background species Input is already basecalled sequence data where standard alignment/classification pipelines are appropriate

skills.description: Use when comparing taxonomic profiling tools on simulated metagenome samples and you need a per-sample abundance estimation error metric (L1-norm) alongside F1-score, from AMBER rank/cumulative results.
skills.name: abundance-l1-norm-error-quantification
skills.search_text: abundance-l1-norm-error-quantification Use when comparing taxonomic profiling tools on simulated metagenome samples and you need a per-sample abundance estimation error metric (L1-norm) alongside F1-score, from AMBER rank/cumulative results. The task is taxonomic binning evaluation, not profiling — AMBER's binning metrics (purity, completeness, Rand index) apply instead You have no ground-truth read-to-taxon mapping, so abundance error cannot be computed against known composition Input is real (non-simulated) data where the true per-species abundances are unknown and the L1-norm error is undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies the L1-norm error in abundance estimation from taxonomic profiling results by extracting cumulative abundance errors per sample from AMBER 2.0.21-beta .rank.tsv outputs, as used in the ganon2 benchmark on 16 simulated CAMI 1+2 samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaf094
skills.summary: Quantifies the L1-norm error in abundance estimation from taxonomic profiling results by extracting cumulative abundance errors per sample from AMBER 2.0.21-beta .rank.tsv outputs, as used in the ganon2 benchmark on 16 simulated CAMI 1+2 samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is taxonomic binning evaluation, not profiling — AMBER's binning metrics (purity, completeness, Rand index) apply instead You have no ground-truth read-to-taxon mapping, so abundance error cannot be computed against known composition Input is real (non-simulated) data where the true per-species abundances are unknown and the L1-norm error is undefined

skills.description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic classifiers (e.g. AFS-MetaCache, MetaCacheSpark, CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken) on samples with known ingredient compositions to quantify false-positive rates and abundance-estimation error.
skills.name: abundance-quantification-accuracy-assessment
skills.search_text: abundance-quantification-accuracy-assessment Use when benchmarking taxonomic classifiers (e.g. AFS-MetaCache, MetaCacheSpark, CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken) on samples with known ingredient compositions to quantify false-positive rates and abundance-estimation error. Samples have unknown composition — no ground truth exists to compute Σ FP or Σ Dev, so accuracy assessment is meaningless The goal is database construction or read-level classification speed benchmarking rather than quantification accuracy Input is raw unassembled reads without a corresponding reference database (e.g. AFS20) — classification cannot proceed http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Evaluates metagenomic classifier quantification accuracy by classifying calibrator food samples of known composition (Kal A-E and KLyo A-D calibrator sausage read datasets) and computing per-sample sums of false positives (Σ FP) and sums of absolute deviations (Σ Dev) between predicted and true ingredient abundances. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Evaluates metagenomic classifier quantification accuracy by classifying calibrator food samples of known composition (Kal A-E and KLyo A-D calibrator sausage read datasets) and computing per-sample sums of false positives (Σ FP) and sums of absolute deviations (Σ Dev) between predicted and true ingredient abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples have unknown composition — no ground truth exists to compute Σ FP or Σ Dev, so accuracy assessment is meaningless The goal is database construction or read-level classification speed benchmarking rather than quantification accuracy Input is raw unassembled reads without a corresponding reference database (e.g. AFS20) — classification cannot proceed

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how much taxonomic assignments of the same OTU representative sequences disagree between 16S reference databases (Greengenes vs SILVA vs NCBI RefSeq), pairwise at each taxonomic level from Phylum to Species.
skills.name: abundance-ranked-taxon-matching
skills.search_text: abundance-ranked-taxon-matching Use when you need to quantify how much taxonomic assignments of the same OTU representative sequences disagree between 16S reference databases (Greengenes vs SILVA vs NCBI RefSeq), pairwise at each taxonomic level from Phylum to Species. Input is raw 16S reads with no OTU representative sequences or OTU table yet — the DC (denoising/clustering) step must run first The goal is a single consensus taxonomy assignment for one database rather than a pairwise cross-database similarity comparison You need to compare the full taxon universe including rare taxa — this skill is scoped to the top-100 most abundant taxa per database http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 A comparison procedure from the MiCoNE paper that quantifies how much taxonomic assignments of the same OTU representative sequences diverge between 16S reference databases (Greengenes, SILVA, NCBI RefSeq), by ranking taxa by abundance, retaining the top 100, and computing pairwise similarity at each taxonomic level. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: A comparison procedure from the MiCoNE paper that quantifies how much taxonomic assignments of the same OTU representative sequences diverge between 16S reference databases (Greengenes, SILVA, NCBI RefSeq), by ranking taxa by abundance, retaining the top 100, and computing pairwise similarity at each taxonomic level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw 16S reads with no OTU representative sequences or OTU table yet — the DC (denoising/clustering) step must run first The goal is a single consensus taxonomy assignment for one database rather than a pairwise cross-database similarity comparison You need to compare the full taxon universe including rare taxa — this skill is scoped to the top-100 most abundant taxa per database

skills.description: Use when a PICRUSt2-derived KO or pathway abundance table is about to be transformed or analyzed, and you must confirm rows are features (KO orthologs or KEGG pathways), columns are samples, and post-conversion output preserves sample columns.
skills.name: abundance-table-format-validation
skills.search_text: abundance-table-format-validation Use when a PICRUSt2-derived KO or pathway abundance table is about to be transformed or analyzed, and you must confirm rows are features (KO orthologs or KEGG pathways), columns are samples, and post-conversion output preserves sample columns. The table is already pathway-level and no conversion (e.g. ko2kegg_abundance) is planned, so only trivial checks apply The input is a differential abundance results table or per-sequence contribution file (e.g. pred_metagenome_contrib.tsv), which has a different schema than a feature-by-sample abundance matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Validate that an abundance table (e.g., a PICRUSt2-format KO table or a converted KEGG pathway table) has the expected feature-by-sample matrix structure before and after conversion steps such as ggpicrust2's ko2kegg_abundance(). This guards downstream differential abundance analysis against malformed or mis-shaped inputs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad470
skills.summary: Validate that an abundance table (e.g., a PICRUSt2-format KO table or a converted KEGG pathway table) has the expected feature-by-sample matrix structure before and after conversion steps such as ggpicrust2's ko2kegg_abundance(). This guards downstream differential abundance analysis against malformed or mis-shaped inputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The table is already pathway-level and no conversion (e.g. ko2kegg_abundance) is planned, so only trivial checks apply The input is a differential abundance results table or per-sequence contribution file (e.g. pred_metagenome_contrib.tsv), which has a different schema than a feature-by-sample abundance matrix

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how fimpera's threshold parameter z controls false positive calls on a counting Bloom filter, e.g. verifying the reported ~0.4%/0.56% FPR at z=3 and near-100% FPR at z=20.
skills.name: abundance-threshold-parameter-sweep
skills.search_text: abundance-threshold-parameter-sweep Use when you need to quantify how fimpera's threshold parameter z controls false positive calls on a counting Bloom filter, e.g. verifying the reported ~0.4%/0.56% FPR at z=3 and near-100% FPR at z=20. When only a single fixed threshold query is needed (e.g. the recommended z=3) rather than characterizing the whole z trade-off curve When the index is not an AMQ supporting abundance queries — fimpera requires abundance-supporting structures such as counting Bloom filters http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Sweeps fimpera's abundance threshold z (0–20) on a counting Bloom filter index to map the trade-off between false positive rate and retained k-mer calls, reproducing the paper's Table 2. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad305
skills.summary: Sweeps fimpera's abundance threshold z (0–20) on a counting Bloom filter index to map the trade-off between false positive rate and retained k-mer calls, reproducing the paper's Table 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single fixed threshold query is needed (e.g. the recommended z=3) rather than characterizing the whole z trade-off curve When the index is not an AMQ supporting abundance queries — fimpera requires abundance-supporting structures such as counting Bloom filters

skills.description: Use when reproducing or reporting phenotype-classification accuracy from metagenomic feature tables (16S or WGS MetaPhlAn/QIIME profiles) where both held-out test accuracy and cross-validated accuracy with a 95% CI must be quoted, e.g. against MegaR Table 2 values.
skills.name: accuracy-confidence-interval-reporting
skills.search_text: accuracy-confidence-interval-reporting Use when reproducing or reporting phenotype-classification accuracy from metagenomic feature tables (16S or WGS MetaPhlAn/QIIME profiles) where both held-out test accuracy and cross-validated accuracy with a 95% CI must be quoted, e.g. against MegaR Table 2 values. The model has not been cross-validated — reporting only a single train/test split accuracy without the N-run 10-fold estimate (MegaR treats CV as essential to check that the model is 'not overfitted and not having bias') The dataset is very small or single-cohort, where k-fold CV itself can have high variance and the 80–90% DIABIMMUNE benchmark ranges do not apply The goal is benchmarking against MetAML or comparing SVM/GLM classifiers rather than quoting accuracy with uncertainty for a single RF model http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Report Random Forest classification performance on metagenomic profiles by combining the test-set confusion-matrix accuracy with accuracy from N independent runs of 10-fold cross validation, each quantified with a 95% confidence interval. This is how the MegaR paper validates model robustness and avoids quoting a single split-dependent number. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03933-4
skills.summary: Report Random Forest classification performance on metagenomic profiles by combining the test-set confusion-matrix accuracy with accuracy from N independent runs of 10-fold cross validation, each quantified with a 95% confidence interval. This is how the MegaR paper validates model robustness and avoids quoting a single split-dependent number.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model has not been cross-validated — reporting only a single train/test split accuracy without the N-run 10-fold estimate (MegaR treats CV as essential to check that the model is 'not overfitted and not having bias') The dataset is very small or single-cohort, where k-fold CV itself can have high variance and the 80–90% DIABIMMUNE benchmark ranges do not apply The goal is benchmarking against MetAML or comparing SVM/GLM classifiers rather than quoting accuracy with uncertainty for a single RF model

skills.description: Use when evaluating phenotype classifiers from cross-validation folds (e.g., Traitar phypat/phypat+PGL over the 67 GIDEON phenotypes) and reporting macroaccuracy alongside overall accuracy.
skills.name: accuracy-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: accuracy-metrics-computation Use when evaluating phenotype classifiers from cross-validation folds (e.g., Traitar phypat/phypat+PGL over the 67 GIDEON phenotypes) and reporting macroaccuracy alongside overall accuracy. The input is an independent test set rather than cross-validation folds — the article phenotyped an independent GIDEON test set separately, and these fold-aggregated metrics would not apply Predictions come from incomplete genomes or SAGs — the article notes phypat assigns more phenotypes to incomplete genomes at the price of more false positives, so fold-level accuracy metrics would be misleading without adjusting expectations Only overall accuracy is needed and phenotype imbalance matters — macroaccuracy over the 67 phenotypes is the headline metric and requires per-phenotype confusion counts, not just pooled accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Compute overall accuracy and macroaccuracy for bacterial phenotype classifiers (Traitar phypat and phypat+PGL) across 67 GIDEON phenotypes during 10-fold nested cross-validation on 234 GIDEON I genomes, so that reproduced performance can be compared directly to the published values. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00101-16
skills.summary: Compute overall accuracy and macroaccuracy for bacterial phenotype classifiers (Traitar phypat and phypat+PGL) across 67 GIDEON phenotypes during 10-fold nested cross-validation on 234 GIDEON I genomes, so that reproduced performance can be compared directly to the published values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an independent test set rather than cross-validation folds — the article phenotyped an independent GIDEON test set separately, and these fold-aggregated metrics would not apply Predictions come from incomplete genomes or SAGs — the article notes phypat assigns more phenotypes to incomplete genomes at the price of more false positives, so fold-level accuracy metrics would be misleading without adjusting expectations Only overall accuracy is needed and phenotype imbalance matters — macroaccuracy over the 67 phenotypes is the headline metric and requires per-phenotype confusion counts, not just pooled accuracy

skills.description: Use when quantifying how genome incompleteness (e.g. metagenomic bins at 60-70% completeness) degrades binary phenotypic trait prediction accuracy, and when visualizing accuracy-vs-completeness curves per trait.
skills.name: accuracy-vs-completeness-curve-visualization
skills.search_text: accuracy-vs-completeness-curve-visualization Use when quantifying how genome incompleteness (e.g. metagenomic bins at 60-70% completeness) degrades binary phenotypic trait prediction accuracy, and when visualizing accuracy-vs-completeness curves per trait. Inputs are metagenomic reads or raw assemblies with no COG presence/absence annotation — the trait models operate on eggNOG COG features, not sequence data The goal is novel trait model training rather than evaluating robustness of already-trained trait models to genome incompleteness Traits lacking sufficient positive training genomes (the paper notes further ecological traits await sufficient training data) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces the paper's Figure 5 analysis: sigmoidal balanced-accuracy response curves per phenotypic trait as a function of simulated genome completeness, showing how much incompleteness SVM-based PICA trait prediction can tolerate. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-16-s14-s1
skills.summary: Reproduces the paper's Figure 5 analysis: sigmoidal balanced-accuracy response curves per phenotypic trait as a function of simulated genome completeness, showing how much incompleteness SVM-based PICA trait prediction can tolerate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inputs are metagenomic reads or raw assemblies with no COG presence/absence annotation — the trait models operate on eggNOG COG features, not sequence data The goal is novel trait model training rather than evaluating robustness of already-trained trait models to genome incompleteness Traits lacking sufficient positive training genomes (the paper notes further ecological traits await sufficient training data)

skills.description: Use when training a logistic matrix factorization (e.g. ILMF/NRLMF-style) whose latent factors need element-wise adaptive learning rates — e.g. after building virus-host heterogeneous networks with c=5 and K1=K2=5 regularization.
skills.name: adagrad-optimization
skills.search_text: adagrad-optimization Use when training a logistic matrix factorization (e.g. ILMF/NRLMF-style) whose latent factors need element-wise adaptive learning rates — e.g. after building virus-host heterogeneous networks with c=5 and K1=K2=5 regularization. The goal is only to construct input networks (SNF fusion of host similarities or d2* virus dissimilarity); this skill covers the optimizer stage, not network construction. The input matrices are raw d2* dissimilarities — the README states 'you should transform to similarity' before they can regularize the objective. http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Element-wise adaptive learning-rate (AdaGrad) optimization of the ILMF-VH kernelized logistic matrix factorization objective (Eq. 11, importance weight c=5) over the virus-host heterogeneous network, iterated until convergence to reconstruct virus-host association scores. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Element-wise adaptive learning-rate (AdaGrad) optimization of the ILMF-VH kernelized logistic matrix factorization objective (Eq. 11, importance weight c=5) over the virus-host heterogeneous network, iterated until convergence to reconstruct virus-host association scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only to construct input networks (SNF fusion of host similarities or d2* virus dissimilarity); this skill covers the optimizer stage, not network construction. The input matrices are raw d2* dissimilarities — the README states 'you should transform to similarity' before they can regularize the objective.

skills.description: Use when raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ metagenomic reads must be cleaned before assembly — adapters, low-quality bases, PhiX spike-in, or host contamination would degrade downstream MAG assembly and binning.
skills.name: adapter-and-contaminant-read-filtering
skills.search_text: adapter-and-contaminant-read-filtering Use when raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ metagenomic reads must be cleaned before assembly — adapters, low-quality bases, PhiX spike-in, or host contamination would degrade downstream MAG assembly and binning. Input is long-read (PacBio/Nanopore) data — the pipeline uses Porechop adapter trimming and minimap2 alignment for long reads instead of fastp and Bowtie2 Reads are already adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered and only require assembly or binning PacBio reads are the input — Porechop adapter trimming is skipped for PacBio reads, so adapter-trimming logic does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Pre-processes short Illumina metagenomic reads in the nf-core/mag pipeline by trimming adapters and low-quality bases with fastp, then mapping reads with Bowtie2 against PhiX and host references to discard contaminant reads, with FastQC documenting pre- and post-cleaning quality. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Pre-processes short Illumina metagenomic reads in the nf-core/mag pipeline by trimming adapters and low-quality bases with fastp, then mapping reads with Bowtie2 against PhiX and host references to discard contaminant reads, with FastQC documenting pre- and post-cleaning quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read (PacBio/Nanopore) data — the pipeline uses Porechop adapter trimming and minimap2 alignment for long reads instead of fastp and Bowtie2 Reads are already adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered and only require assembly or binning PacBio reads are the input — Porechop adapter trimming is skipped for PacBio reads, so adapter-trimming logic does not apply

skills.description: Use when building a taxonomic k-mer database (e.g., Kraken-GB from GenBank draft microbial genomes) where draft contigs may contain adapter contamination or unreliable terminal sequence, and classification accuracy would suffer if those k-mers were included.
skills.name: adapter-and-contig-edge-kmer-filtering
skills.search_text: adapter-and-contig-edge-kmer-filtering Use when building a taxonomic k-mer database (e.g., Kraken-GB from GenBank draft microbial genomes) where draft contigs may contain adapter contamination or unreliable terminal sequence, and classification accuracy would suffer if those k-mers were included. The database is built from complete RefSeq genomes (standard Kraken), which do not require adapter or contig-edge trimming The goal is reduced memory usage (MiniKraken-style shrinking) rather than removing contaminant/edge k-mers Draft contigs are already adapter-trimmed and quality-trimmed at the read/assembly level, making the filtering redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A database-cleaning step from Kraken-GB construction: k-mers derived from known adapter sequences, plus the first and last 20 k-mers of each draft contig, are removed from the k-mer database before taxonomic labeling, so that contaminants and contig-edge artifacts do not bias classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: A database-cleaning step from Kraken-GB construction: k-mers derived from known adapter sequences, plus the first and last 20 k-mers of each draft contig, are removed from the k-mer database before taxonomic labeling, so that contaminants and contig-edge artifacts do not bias classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The database is built from complete RefSeq genomes (standard Kraken), which do not require adapter or contig-edge trimming The goal is reduced memory usage (MiniKraken-style shrinking) rather than removing contaminant/edge k-mers Draft contigs are already adapter-trimmed and quality-trimmed at the read/assembly level, making the filtering redundant

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end RNA-seq/metatranscriptome FASTQ files have been merged (e.g. with PEAR) and still contain adaptor contamination and low-quality bases that would hurt downstream DIAMOND annotation.
skills.name: adapter-and-quality-trimming
skills.search_text: adapter-and-quality-trimming Use when raw paired-end RNA-seq/metatranscriptome FASTQ files have been merged (e.g. with PEAR) and still contain adaptor contamination and low-quality bases that would hurt downstream DIAMOND annotation. Input reads have not yet been merged from paired-end form (run PEAR first, as SAMSA2 recommends PEAR for paired-end data) Sequences are not raw FASTQ reads but already-annotated results or abundance summary tables The goal is rRNA depletion rather than quality/adapter cleaning (that is SortMeRNA's role in SAMSA2) http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Cleaning of merged metatranscriptome FASTQ reads with Trimmomatic to remove adaptor contamination and low-quality sequences, as performed in the SAMSA2 pipeline between PEAR merging and SortMeRNA rRNA filtering. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-018-2189-z
skills.summary: Cleaning of merged metatranscriptome FASTQ reads with Trimmomatic to remove adaptor contamination and low-quality sequences, as performed in the SAMSA2 pipeline between PEAR merging and SortMeRNA rRNA filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not yet been merged from paired-end form (run PEAR first, as SAMSA2 recommends PEAR for paired-end data) Sequences are not raw FASTQ reads but already-annotated results or abundance summary tables The goal is rRNA depletion rather than quality/adapter cleaning (that is SortMeRNA's role in SAMSA2)

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads enter the ViroProfiler pipeline and need adapter removal, quality trimming, and contaminant stripping before assembly or viral identification; skip only when input reads are already cleaned.
skills.name: adapter-sequence-removal-paired-end
skills.search_text: adapter-sequence-removal-paired-end Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads enter the ViroProfiler pipeline and need adapter removal, quality trimming, and contaminant stripping before assembly or viral identification; skip only when input reads are already cleaned. Input reads are already cleaned — ViroProfiler's cleaning step is skipped when input reads are already cleaned. Data are not shotgun viral metagenomic reads (e.g., amplicon or assembled contigs) — ViroProfiler is designed for analyzing shotgun viral metagenomic data. Samples contain excessive environmental contaminations that were not fractionated before sequencing, which could increase running time and result in lower precision; isolate the viral fractions before sequencing instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quality-control of raw paired-end shotgun viral metagenomic FASTQ reads in ViroProfiler, using FASTP trimming (adapter auto-detection, low-quality base removal, short-read dropping) followed by optional DECONTAM (BBMap) host/contaminant filtering, producing cleaned R1/R2 FASTQ pairs. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Quality-control of raw paired-end shotgun viral metagenomic FASTQ reads in ViroProfiler, using FASTP trimming (adapter auto-detection, low-quality base removal, short-read dropping) followed by optional DECONTAM (BBMap) host/contaminant filtering, producing cleaned R1/R2 FASTQ pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already cleaned — ViroProfiler's cleaning step is skipped when input reads are already cleaned. Data are not shotgun viral metagenomic reads (e.g., amplicon or assembled contigs) — ViroProfiler is designed for analyzing shotgun viral metagenomic data. Samples contain excessive environmental contaminations that were not fractionated before sequencing, which could increase running time and result in lower precision; isolate the viral fractions before sequencing instead.

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina metagenomics reads (e.g. FASTQ/FASTQ.gz such as SRA SRR5381736) must be adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered prior to 16S/18S read extraction with SortMeRNA or BBMap.
skills.name: adapter-trimming-quality-control
skills.search_text: adapter-trimming-quality-control Use when raw paired-end Illumina metagenomics reads (e.g. FASTQ/FASTQ.gz such as SRA SRR5381736) must be adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered prior to 16S/18S read extraction with SortMeRNA or BBMap. Input is already trimmed FASTQ or a filtered 16S/18S read set from SortMeRNA — re-trimming would risk over-trimming before SSU extraction Data are long-read (e.g. PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) rather than Illumina FASTQ, since the BBTools parameters here (ktrim, kmer=21, qtrim=rl) target short Illumina reads The analysis goal is classification of already-reconstructed full-length SSU sequences (handled by QIIME 2 sklearn classifier/VSEARCH), not read preprocessing http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Preprocess Illumina (meta)genomic FASTQ reads with FastQC/MultiQC quality control and BBTools adapter/quality trimming (ktrim=r, kmer=21, minlength=60, trimq=20, qtrim=rl, maxns=1) before SSU read extraction and rRNA gene reconstruction, as done in the RiboTaxa pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Preprocess Illumina (meta)genomic FASTQ reads with FastQC/MultiQC quality control and BBTools adapter/quality trimming (ktrim=r, kmer=21, minlength=60, trimq=20, qtrim=rl, maxns=1) before SSU read extraction and rRNA gene reconstruction, as done in the RiboTaxa pipeline.

skills.description: Use when you have a DAF spectrum plus divergence counts (Ds, Dn, Ps, Pn or mi, Di, m0, D0) for selected (0-fold) and neutral (4-fold) classes and need to estimate α and classify the selection regime for coding genes.
skills.name: adaptive-substitution-estimation
skills.search_text: adaptive-substitution-estimation Use when you have a DAF spectrum plus divergence counts (Ds, Dn, Ps, Pn or mi, Di, m0, D0) for selected (0-fold) and neutral (4-fold) classes and need to estimate α and classify the selection regime for coding genes. Data is a raw VCF or FASTA alignment without unfolded DAF/divergence counts — preprocess with the iMKTData pipelines first Derived allele frequency is unavailable (no ancestral-state information), since DAF-based exclusion of weakly deleterious variants and unfolded SFS computation cannot be performed The goal is per-gene selection classification rather than a single regime for a concatenated gene set — in concatenate mode iMKT analyzes the whole gene set, not each gene individually http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3050 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Estimates the fraction of adaptive substitutions (α) and other selection regimes (neutral, strongly deleterious, weakly deleterious) from polymorphism and divergence count tables using the four MKT variants implemented in iMKT (standard MKT, FWWMKT, eMKT, aMKT), optionally with the CMH heterogeneity test and bootstrap 95% CI for multi-gene sets. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkz372
skills.summary: Estimates the fraction of adaptive substitutions (α) and other selection regimes (neutral, strongly deleterious, weakly deleterious) from polymorphism and divergence count tables using the four MKT variants implemented in iMKT (standard MKT, FWWMKT, eMKT, aMKT), optionally with the CMH heterogeneity test and bootstrap 95% CI for multi-gene sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is a raw VCF or FASTA alignment without unfolded DAF/divergence counts — preprocess with the iMKTData pipelines first Derived allele frequency is unavailable (no ancestral-state information), since DAF-based exclusion of weakly deleterious variants and unfolded SFS computation cannot be performed The goal is per-gene selection classification rather than a single regime for a concatenated gene set — in concatenate mode iMKT analyzes the whole gene set, not each gene individually

skills.description: Use when testing H0: β = 0 for multivariate association between a selected subset of microbial taxa and an outcome in high-dimensional compositional OTU data, where the number of taxa (e.g. 856 OTUs) exceeds the sample size.
skills.name: adaptive-sum-of-powered-score-testing
skills.search_text: adaptive-sum-of-powered-score-testing Use when testing H0: β = 0 for multivariate association between a selected subset of microbial taxa and an outcome in high-dimensional compositional OTU data, where the number of taxa (e.g. 856 OTUs) exceeds the sample size. When the goal is single-taxon univariate association rather than a multivariate clade/community test When no feature screening is desired and all p taxa should enter the multivariate statistic with non-zero weights (AMAT's premise is shrinking noise features to exactly zero) When the taxa-set being tested contains fewer than five taxa, since the paper restricted association analysis to taxa-sets with at least five taxa http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 AMAT's two-stage testing procedure: after distance-correlation feature selection shrinks noise taxa to zero weight, an adaptive sum of powered score (aSPU) statistic with a power set Γ = {2,3,4,8} is computed on the selected subset under a generalized linear model, with permutation-based calibration shared between the PSPU(γ) combination step and the final P-value. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab120
skills.summary: AMAT's two-stage testing procedure: after distance-correlation feature selection shrinks noise taxa to zero weight, an adaptive sum of powered score (aSPU) statistic with a power set Γ = {2,3,4,8} is computed on the selected subset under a generalized linear model, with permutation-based calibration shared between the PSPU(γ) combination step and the final P-value.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is single-taxon univariate association rather than a multivariate clade/community test When no feature screening is desired and all p taxa should enter the multivariate statistic with non-zero weights (AMAT's premise is shrinking noise features to exactly zero) When the taxa-set being tested contains fewer than five taxa, since the paper restricted association analysis to taxa-sets with at least five taxa

skills.description: Use when you have interaction/adjacency matrices from many MiCoNE tool-parameter combinations across pipeline steps and need to quantify which step (denoising-clustering, chimera-checking, taxonomy-assignment, OTU-processing, network-inference) drives the total variation among the inferred networks.
skills.name: adjacency-matrix-stacking-and-pca
skills.search_text: adjacency-matrix-stacking-and-pca Use when you have interaction/adjacency matrices from many MiCoNE tool-parameter combinations across pipeline steps and need to quantify which step (denoising-clustering, chimera-checking, taxonomy-assignment, OTU-processing, network-inference) drives the total variation among the inferred networks. The inputs are raw 16S reads or a single abundance table — this skill operates on inferred interaction matrices, not upstream sequence processing or OTU assignment itself Only one network is available — variance across tool/parameter combinations cannot be decomposed from a single adjacency matrix The goal is consensus network generation or selecting tools with optimal agreement with mock and synthetic benchmark data sets, rather than quantifying per-step variance contributions http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A method for attributing variation among co-occurrence networks to 16S pipeline steps: flatten each MiCoNE-inferred network's adjacency matrix into a vector, stack all tool/parameter combination vectors, run scikit-learn PCA, and regress principal components on the categorical step indicators (DC, CC, TA, OP, NI) by ANOVA. It reveals that taxonomy assignment — the choice of 16S reference database — contributes 65.4% of network variation and OTU processing 26.8%. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: A method for attributing variation among co-occurrence networks to 16S pipeline steps: flatten each MiCoNE-inferred network's adjacency matrix into a vector, stack all tool/parameter combination vectors, run scikit-learn PCA, and regress principal components on the categorical step indicators (DC, CC, TA, OP, NI) by ANOVA. It reveals that taxonomy assignment — the choice of 16S reference database — contributes 65.4% of network variation and OTU processing 26.8%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The inputs are raw 16S reads or a single abundance table — this skill operates on inferred interaction matrices, not upstream sequence processing or OTU assignment itself Only one network is available — variance across tool/parameter combinations cannot be decomposed from a single adjacency matrix The goal is consensus network generation or selecting tools with optimal agreement with mock and synthetic benchmark data sets, rather than quantifying per-step variance contributions

Input is raw unassembled metagenomic reads with no reference annotation — Glimmer-MG parameterizes models from phylogenetic classification (Phymm) and clustering (Scimm), not from an annotated complete genome The goal is eukaryotic gene structure prediction with introns/exons — the adjacent-gene orientation and intergenic distance model is specific to prokaryotic operon-style gene layouts http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Extracts adjacent-gene orientation category frequencies and intergenic distance distributions from a genome annotation, as used by Glimmer-MG to model downstream and intervening adjacent gene pairs when scoring predicted ORFs on metagenomic fragments. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067

skills.description: Use when genome-wide biallelic SNP data (VCF or PLINK binary) need individual-level ancestry proportions and an objective choice of cluster number K via ADMIXTURE CV-error minimization.
skills.name: admixture-ancestry-estimation
skills.search_text: admixture-ancestry-estimation Use when genome-wide biallelic SNP data (VCF or PLINK binary) need individual-level ancestry proportions and an objective choice of cluster number K via ADMIXTURE CV-error minimization. Input VCFs are not yet sample/site filtered or LD-pruned — run the scalepopgen filtering/basic-statistics sub-workflow first (site filtering after sample filtering, MAF/missingness/LD pruning) before ADMIXTURE Data are not biallelic SNPs (e.g. multiallelic, indel, or structural variant calls) — scalepopgen is designed for biallelic SNP data in VCF or PLINK binary format The goal is tree-based population relationships with migration edges rather than individual ancestry proportions — use the TreeMix sub-workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Runs ADMIXTURE ancestry-proportion inference on a LD-pruned PLINK binary (BED) genotype file across a user-defined range of ancestral components (K), selects the optimal K by lowest cross-validation (CV) error, and renders the resulting Q-matrices as interactive plots (Bokeh/Plotly) plus PONG-ready inputs — as implemented in the scalepopgen Nextflow 'explore genetic structure' sub-workflow. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Runs ADMIXTURE ancestry-proportion inference on a LD-pruned PLINK binary (BED) genotype file across a user-defined range of ancestral components (K), selects the optimal K by lowest cross-validation (CV) error, and renders the resulting Q-matrices as interactive plots (Bokeh/Plotly) plus PONG-ready inputs — as implemented in the scalepopgen Nextflow 'explore genetic structure' sub-workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input VCFs are not yet sample/site filtered or LD-pruned — run the scalepopgen filtering/basic-statistics sub-workflow first (site filtering after sample filtering, MAF/missingness/LD pruning) before ADMIXTURE Data are not biallelic SNPs (e.g. multiallelic, indel, or structural variant calls) — scalepopgen is designed for biallelic SNP data in VCF or PLINK binary format The goal is tree-based population relationships with migration edges rather than individual ancestry proportions — use the TreeMix sub-workflow instead

skills.description: Use when ADMIXTURE has been run over multiple user-defined K values on PLINK binary (bed/bim/fam) SNP data and the optimal K must be identified via CV error and the Q-matrices visualized interactively.
skills.name: admixture-q-matrix-plotting-and-k-selection
skills.search_text: admixture-q-matrix-plotting-and-k-selection Use when ADMIXTURE has been run over multiple user-defined K values on PLINK binary (bed/bim/fam) SNP data and the optimal K must be identified via CV error and the Q-matrices visualized interactively. Input is raw VCF rather than the Q-matrices/log files produced after running ADMIXTURE on the plink-generated binary files — run the genetic-structure sub-workflow first (including LD pruning and VCF-to-BED conversion). Only a single K was run and no CV errors are available — K selection via CV error requires ADMIXTURE runs over multiple user-defined K values. The goal is phylogenetic tree rendering or PCA scatter plots — those use TreeMix/Toytree/ete3 and Plotly outputs, not the ADMIXTURE Q-matrix path. http://edamontology.org/topic_2815 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Parses ADMIXTURE log files to extract cross-validation (CV) errors per K, selects the K with the lowest CV error, and renders the corresponding Q-matrix as an interactive Bokeh bar plot plus PONG visualization inputs with a consistent population-color mapping. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Parses ADMIXTURE log files to extract cross-validation (CV) errors per K, selects the K with the lowest CV error, and renders the corresponding Q-matrix as an interactive Bokeh bar plot plus PONG visualization inputs with a consistent population-color mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw VCF rather than the Q-matrices/log files produced after running ADMIXTURE on the plink-generated binary files — run the genetic-structure sub-workflow first (including LD pruning and VCF-to-BED conversion). Only a single K was run and no CV errors are available — K selection via CV error requires ADMIXTURE runs over multiple user-defined K values. The goal is phylogenetic tree rendering or PCA scatter plots — those use TreeMix/Toytree/ete3 and Plotly outputs, not the ADMIXTURE Q-matrix path.

skills.description: Use when an in-place, allocation-free algorithm implementation (e.g. sliding-window minima over fixed windows of size W) must be proven correct against a brute-force oracle and benchmarked before adoption.
skills.name: algorithm-correctness-testing
skills.search_text: algorithm-correctness-testing Use when an in-place, allocation-free algorithm implementation (e.g. sliding-window minima over fixed windows of size W) must be proven correct against a brute-force oracle and benchmarked before adoption. When the analysis goal is k-mer abundance indexing or querying itself — that is fimpera's fimpera_index/fimpera_query pipeline, not the sliding-minimum test harness. When windows are variable-size or streaming and dynamic allocation of the output vector is acceptable — the deque or 'rotation deque' variants, not the fixed in-place window approach, are the right comparison points. When inputs are not numeric vectors whose per-window minimum is well-defined (the oracle check 'brute-force minimum over the corresponding window' has no meaning otherwise). A validation-and-benchmark skill for the fixed-window sliding-minimum algorithm: it verifies that an in-place implementation's minL/minR outputs equal brute-force per-window minima and compares its runtime against the naive O(W*|v|) recompute-per-window baseline. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad305
skills.summary: A validation-and-benchmark skill for the fixed-window sliding-minimum algorithm: it verifies that an in-place implementation's minL/minR outputs equal brute-force per-window minima and compares its runtime against the naive O(W*|v|) recompute-per-window baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is k-mer abundance indexing or querying itself — that is fimpera's fimpera_index/fimpera_query pipeline, not the sliding-minimum test harness. When windows are variable-size or streaming and dynamic allocation of the output vector is acceptable — the deque or 'rotation deque' variants, not the fixed in-place window approach, are the right comparison points. When inputs are not numeric vectors whose per-window minimum is well-defined (the oracle check 'brute-force minimum over the corresponding window' has no meaning otherwise).

skills.search_text: aligner-benchmarking-f1-throughput Use when comparing accuracy and speed of read classification tools against large, repetitive references (e.g. human pan-genomes) in nanopore depletion or targeted-sequencing scenarios. skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for comparing read classifiers/aligners (SPUMONI vs minimap2) on host-depletion tasks, scoring per-read decisions with F1 and reporting throughput (kbp/s) and index size across one-genome vs multi-genome indexes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is real-time signal-level read-until control — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences and cannot directly interact with the Read Until API When the target and non-target sequences share substantial similarity (e.g. conserved genes between species), since the null-index hypothesis testing may be insufficient When the reference is small and non-repetitive, where the compressed-index advantages (index size, memory) being benchmarked do not apply

skills.description: Use when you have raw whole-genome sequences (e.g. NCBI viral and bacterial genomes) and need virus-virus or host-host similarity without alignment, to seed network-based virus-host prediction methods.
skills.name: alignment-free-d2-star-dissimilarity-measurement
skills.search_text: alignment-free-d2-star-dissimilarity-measurement Use when you have raw whole-genome sequences (e.g. NCBI viral and bacterial genomes) and need virus-virus or host-host similarity without alignment, to seed network-based virus-host prediction methods. Known virus-host associations or alignment-based homology scores already provide the required similarity signal (the article notes homology methods depend on whether hosts exist in the host genome database) The downstream method requires raw interaction profiles rather than ONF similarities — e.g. computing Gaussian interaction profile kernel similarity, which ILMF-VH derives from known associations via similarity_os.py/main.py instead Genomes are highly fragmented or lack sufficient sequence length for stable 6-mer frequency estimates http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Computes alignment-free d2* oligonucleotide frequency dissimilarities (k=6) between whole-genome sequences of viruses and hosts using Jie Ren's tools, then transforms the dissimilarity matrices into similarity matrices for network construction in the ILMF-VH pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Computes alignment-free d2* oligonucleotide frequency dissimilarities (k=6) between whole-genome sequences of viruses and hosts using Jie Ren's tools, then transforms the dissimilarity matrices into similarity matrices for network construction in the ILMF-VH pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Known virus-host associations or alignment-based homology scores already provide the required similarity signal (the article notes homology methods depend on whether hosts exist in the host genome database) The downstream method requires raw interaction profiles rather than ONF similarities — e.g. computing Gaussian interaction profile kernel similarity, which ILMF-VH derives from known associations via similarity_os.py/main.py instead Genomes are highly fragmented or lack sufficient sequence length for stable 6-mer frequency estimates

skills.search_text: alignment-free-dissimilarity-computation Use when input is assembled genomic FASTA files or unassembled NGS shotgun reads (.fasta/.fa/.fna) and the goal is a pairwise alignment-free dissimilarity matrix for clustering, PCoA, heatmap or network analysis. skills.summary: Compute pairwise dissimilarity matrices among genomes or metagenomes without alignment, using CAFE's 28 k-mer-based measures (conventional count measures like Manhattan, background-adjusted measures like D2star/D2shepp/CVtree, and presence/absence measures like Jaccard), accelerated by JELLYFISH k-mer counting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question requires detailed alignment information (e.g. mutation positions, homologous region annotation) — the article notes alignment-based methods are inappropriate for some tasks, but alignment-free distances discard per-site alignment detail.
