skills.summary: Compute an r x g similarity matrix between metagenomic reads and reference genomes by scanning the eBWT, LCP and document array of the combined collection S, using the alpha-clusters built by ClusterLCP (Step 2 of LiME's fixed three-step pipeline).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is alignment-based mapping or base-level alignment of reads to reference genomes (LiME is explicitly alignment-free and mapping-free) Only reads are available and no reference genome collection G (or its data structures) exists — the scoring is a read-versus-genome comparison The similarity measure must ignore IUPAC ambiguity codes while still scoring them — the EBWT=1 variant is required; the preliminary LightMetaEbwt_Alcob version treated ambiguity symbols as placeholders

skills.description: Use when comparing assembled genomic sequences or unassembled NGS shotgun reads without alignments, and the Markov order required by background-adjusted k-mer measures (CVTree, D2star, D2shepp) is unclear to the user.
skills.name: alignment-free-sequence-analysis
skills.search_text: alignment-free-sequence-analysis Use when comparing assembled genomic sequences or unassembled NGS shotgun reads without alignments, and the Markov order required by background-adjusted k-mer measures (CVTree, D2star, D2shepp) is unclear to the user. When an alignment-based approach is appropriate — CAFE targets cases where alignment-based methods are not appropriate, such as gene regulatory regions, NGS short reads, and virus-host associations. When the user already knows the Markov order — a single explicit order (or a per-sequence comma-separated list matching the number of FASTA files) can be given with -M, avoiding the time cost of BIC inference. For JS (Jensen-Shannon divergence) — the -M -1 automatic BIC order inference is explicitly documented as 'not suitable for JS'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Method for computing alignment-free dissimilarity measures between genomes or metagenomic reads with CAFE, including automatic selection of the Markov model order required by background-adjusted measures (CVTree, d2*, D2shepp) via the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx351
skills.summary: Method for computing alignment-free dissimilarity measures between genomes or metagenomic reads with CAFE, including automatic selection of the Markov model order required by background-adjusted measures (CVTree, d2*, D2shepp) via the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When an alignment-based approach is appropriate — CAFE targets cases where alignment-based methods are not appropriate, such as gene regulatory regions, NGS short reads, and virus-host associations. When the user already knows the Markov order — a single explicit order (or a per-sequence comma-separated list matching the number of FASTA files) can be given with -M, avoiding the time cost of BIC inference. For JS (Jensen-Shannon divergence) — the -M -1 automatic BIC order inference is explicitly documented as 'not suitable for JS'.

skills.description: Use when quality-filtered FASTQ shotgun metagenomic reads (MetaLAFFA naming: <sample_id>.<type_id>.fastq.gz) must be aligned to UniRef90 gene sequences and the DIAMOND tabular hits need processing for -hit selection and gene abundance computation.
skills.name: alignment-hits-tabular-output-processing
skills.search_text: alignment-hits-tabular-output-processing Use when quality-filtered FASTQ shotgun metagenomic reads (MetaLAFFA naming: <sample_id>.<type_id>.fastq.gz) must be aligned to UniRef90 gene sequences and the DIAMOND tabular hits need processing for -hit selection and gene abundance computation. Input is not raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQ but an already-computed gene abundance table or orthology-group profile (the annotation/counting steps downstream are already done). The goal is host-read removal (e.g. filtering human reads against hs37d5) — MetaLAFFA uses Bowtie 2 nucleotide mapping for that step, not DIAMOND translated alignment to UniRef90. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Maps quality-controlled shotgun metagenomic reads to the UniRef90 protein database with DIAMOND in translated-alignment mode and processes the resulting m8-style tabular hit tables into per-FASTQ read-to-gene match files for downstream best-hit filtering and gene counting. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: Maps quality-controlled shotgun metagenomic reads to the UniRef90 protein database with DIAMOND in translated-alignment mode and processes the resulting m8-style tabular hit tables into per-FASTQ read-to-gene match files for downstream best-hit filtering and gene counting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQ but an already-computed gene abundance table or orthology-group profile (the annotation/counting steps downstream are already done). The goal is host-read removal (e.g. filtering human reads against hs37d5) — MetaLAFFA uses Bowtie 2 nucleotide mapping for that step, not DIAMOND translated alignment to UniRef90.

skills.description: Use when building or validating an alignment/annotation pipeline and you need to empirically choose identity-percentage, read-coverage, and e-value cutoffs that maximize true positive mapping without inflating false positives.
skills.name: alignment-parameter-tuning
skills.search_text: alignment-parameter-tuning Use when building or validating an alignment/annotation pipeline and you need to empirically choose identity-percentage, read-coverage, and e-value cutoffs that maximize true positive mapping without inflating false positives. Input is real metagenomic data without ground truth — the sweep requires simulated reads with known species origin to compute true pass rates The task is taxonomic profiling against marker genes (FunOMIC-T with bowtie2 and >80% alignment length, q-score >30 filters), not translated functional annotation against a protein database Short-read aligners for nucleotide-level mapping are sufficient — Diamond blastx translated search is specific to protein-level functional annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A threshold-sweep procedure for tuning sequence-alignment parameters: simulate reads with ART, align them against a reference database with Diamond blastx v2.0.8, and sweep identity/coverage cutoffs to find the combination that maximizes the retained hit rate. In the FunOMIC paper this identified read coverage >95%, identity percentage >99%, and e-value <10e-10 as optimal for fungal functional annotation against FunOMIC-P (~70% of fungal read hits retained). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: A threshold-sweep procedure for tuning sequence-alignment parameters: simulate reads with ART, align them against a reference database with Diamond blastx v2.0.8, and sweep identity/coverage cutoffs to find the combination that maximizes the retained hit rate. In the FunOMIC paper this identified read coverage >95%, identity percentage >99%, and e-value <10e-10 as optimal for fungal functional annotation against FunOMIC-P (~70% of fungal read hits retained).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real metagenomic data without ground truth — the sweep requires simulated reads with known species origin to compute true pass rates The task is taxonomic profiling against marker genes (FunOMIC-T with bowtie2 and >80% alignment length, q-score >30 filters), not translated functional annotation against a protein database Short-read aligners for nucleotide-level mapping are sufficient — Diamond blastx translated search is specific to protein-level functional annotation

skills.description: Use when quantifying cross-mapping or contamination between sequence databases (e.g., fungal markers vs. a bacterial reference) and strict alignment-quality criteria are needed to call a read 'mapped'.
skills.name: alignment-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: alignment-quality-filtering Use when quantifying cross-mapping or contamination between sequence databases (e.g., fungal markers vs. a bacterial reference) and strict alignment-quality criteria are needed to call a read 'mapped'. Input is already a feature/abundance table or summary counts — no alignment step exists to filter The analysis goal is functional protein annotation, where Diamond blastx thresholds (coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10) apply instead of bowtie2/samtools read filtering Sensitive detection of divergent homologs is the goal — the >80% length and q>30 cutoffs are deliberately exceedingly strict and will discard weak-but-real cross-matches http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A read-mapping readout filter that retains only high-confidence alignments — reads where more than 80% of the read length aligns to the reference with a q-score over 30 — used in FunOMIC to quantify cross-mapping of fungal marker genes against the UHGG bacterial catalog. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: A read-mapping readout filter that retains only high-confidence alignments — reads where more than 80% of the read length aligns to the reference with a q-score over 30 — used in FunOMIC to quantify cross-mapping of fungal marker genes against the UHGG bacterial catalog.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/abundance table or summary counts — no alignment step exists to filter The analysis goal is functional protein annotation, where Diamond blastx thresholds (coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10) apply instead of bowtie2/samtools read filtering Sensitive detection of divergent homologs is the goal — the >80% length and q>30 cutoffs are deliberately exceedingly strict and will discard weak-but-real cross-matches

skills.description: Use when comparing resource footprints (peak memory, throughput) of read-decontamination or alignment pipelines across tools, e.g. Hostile vs HRRT on Illumina and ONT FASTQ inputs.
skills.name: alignment-throughput-measurement
skills.search_text: alignment-throughput-measurement Use when comparing resource footprints (peak memory, throughput) of read-decontamination or alignment pipelines across tools, e.g. Hostile vs HRRT on Illumina and ONT FASTQ inputs. The goal is accuracy evaluation (human read removal rate or bacterial read retention), not resource benchmarking — use the paper's accuracy evaluation workflow instead The aligner or decontamination tool does not support streaming FASTQ input or thread-count control, making wall-clock and peak-RAM comparison non-comparable The dataset is not microbial host-contaminated reads (e.g. pure human samples), where throughput-to-decontamination mapping is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmarking skill for measuring wall-clock throughput (Mbp/s, reads/sec) and peak RAM of host-read decontamination aligners (Hostile with Bowtie2/Minimap2 vs NCBI HRRT) on short and long microbial reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad728
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for measuring wall-clock throughput (Mbp/s, reads/sec) and peak RAM of host-read decontamination aligners (Hostile with Bowtie2/Minimap2 vs NCBI HRRT) on short and long microbial reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy evaluation (human read removal rate or bacterial read retention), not resource benchmarking — use the paper's accuracy evaluation workflow instead The aligner or decontamination tool does not support streaming FASTQ input or thread-count control, making wall-clock and peak-RAM comparison non-comparable The dataset is not microbial host-contaminated reads (e.g. pure human samples), where throughput-to-decontamination mapping is meaningless

skills.description: Use when per-locus MAFFT alignments of Patchwork-recovered USCO (near-universal single-copy ortholog) sequences contain gap-rich columns that must be removed before concatenating a supermatrix and inferring a maximum-likelihood phylogeny.
skills.name: alignment-trimming-gap-based-filtering
skills.search_text: alignment-trimming-gap-based-filtering Use when per-locus MAFFT alignments of Patchwork-recovered USCO (near-universal single-copy ortholog) sequences contain gap-rich columns that must be removed before concatenating a supermatrix and inferring a maximum-likelihood phylogeny. Sequences are not yet aligned — trimming requires a multiple sequence alignment, so run MAFFT (or equivalent) first Reference sequences are not near-USCOs: the article recommends limiting references to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences, which trimming thresholds alone will not fix The goal is marker retrieval itself from WGS data rather than post-alignment cleaning — use Patchwork's retrieval/stitching workflow instead of (or before) trimming http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Gap-based alignment trimming cleans per-locus MAFFT alignments of Patchwork-recovered USCO markers with trimAl (-gt 0.9, -cons 60), removing columns with more than 90% gaps while retaining at least 60% of each alignment, before concatenation and ML tree inference. In the louse phylogenomic benchmark this retained 3,454,320 positions (~64% of the untrimmed supermatrix) and still yielded a well-supported, congruent tree. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Gap-based alignment trimming cleans per-locus MAFFT alignments of Patchwork-recovered USCO markers with trimAl (-gt 0.9, -cons 60), removing columns with more than 90% gaps while retaining at least 60% of each alignment, before concatenation and ML tree inference. In the louse phylogenomic benchmark this retained 3,454,320 positions (~64% of the untrimmed supermatrix) and still yielded a well-supported, congruent tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are not yet aligned — trimming requires a multiple sequence alignment, so run MAFFT (or equivalent) first Reference sequences are not near-USCOs: the article recommends limiting references to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences, which trimming thresholds alone will not fix The goal is marker retrieval itself from WGS data rather than post-alignment cleaning — use Patchwork's retrieval/stitching workflow instead of (or before) trimming

skills.description: Use when replacing or validating an alignment-per-genome pipeline (BWA/Bowtie2/CUSHAW) with an alignment-free classifier and you must quantify speed-up (build time, MR/m query speed) and accuracy trade-offs (Σ FP, Σ Dev) on identical inputs.
skills.name: alignment-vs-alignment-free-pipeline-performance-comparison
skills.search_text: alignment-vs-alignment-free-pipeline-performance-comparison Use when replacing or validating an alignment-per-genome pipeline (BWA/Bowtie2/CUSHAW) with an alignment-free classifier and you must quantify speed-up (build time, MR/m query speed) and accuracy trade-offs (Σ FP, Σ Dev) on identical inputs. The goal is classification accuracy benchmarking against other metagenomic classifiers (CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken) rather than alignment-based vs alignment-free pipeline comparison. Input data are already classified abundance tables, not raw reads and reference genomes. Only a single pipeline can be run — the skill requires running both pipelines on the same samples and database for a fair side-by-side comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmarks an alignment-based pipeline (BWA per reference genome) against the alignment-free, k-mer/minhash-based AFS-MetaCache on the same reference database and read samples, tabulating database build time, query speed (MR/m), and quantification accuracy (Σ FP, Σ Dev) as reported in Tables 9-10 of the all-food-sequencing study. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Benchmarks an alignment-based pipeline (BWA per reference genome) against the alignment-free, k-mer/minhash-based AFS-MetaCache on the same reference database and read samples, tabulating database build time, query speed (MR/m), and quantification accuracy (Σ FP, Σ Dev) as reported in Tables 9-10 of the all-food-sequencing study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is classification accuracy benchmarking against other metagenomic classifiers (CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken) rather than alignment-based vs alignment-free pipeline comparison. Input data are already classified abundance tables, not raw reads and reference genomes. Only a single pipeline can be run — the skill requires running both pipelines on the same samples and database for a fair side-by-side comparison.

skills.description: Use when you need to characterize how an all-vs-all metagenome comparison tool's runtime scales with input volume, or when validating that Libra's Hadoop MapReduce scoring remains near-linear as sample counts grow despite quadratic pair growth.
skills.name: all-vs-all-comparison-pair-count-analysis
skills.search_text: all-vs-all-comparison-pair-count-analysis Use when you need to characterize how an all-vs-all metagenome comparison tool's runtime scales with input volume, or when validating that Libra's Hadoop MapReduce scoring remains near-linear as sample counts grow despite quadratic pair growth. You want to evaluate clustering accuracy or distance-metric sensitivity — use dedicated validation datasets (HMP, CAMI toy dataset) rather than synthetic scaling data, which only measures runtime. The input dataset is far smaller than the benchmark range (e.g. a handful of small samples), where runtime scaling effects will be dominated by Hadoop startup overhead rather than pair-count growth. You need presence/absence or sketch-based comparisons (e.g. Mash/Sourmash-style MinHash sketches) — this skill specifically benchmarks Libra's full-read k-mer abundance scoring, not data-reduced methods. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark and analyze the all-vs-all metagenome comparison workload of Libra by running its k-mer scoring on datasets of increasing size (10–40 synthetic samples) and tabulating runtime against the quadratically growing number of sample pairs, to verify near-linear scaling. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Benchmark and analyze the all-vs-all metagenome comparison workload of Libra by running its k-mer scoring on datasets of increasing size (10–40 synthetic samples) and tabulating runtime against the quadratically growing number of sample pairs, to verify near-linear scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to evaluate clustering accuracy or distance-metric sensitivity — use dedicated validation datasets (HMP, CAMI toy dataset) rather than synthetic scaling data, which only measures runtime. The input dataset is far smaller than the benchmark range (e.g. a handful of small samples), where runtime scaling effects will be dominated by Hadoop startup overhead rather than pair-count growth. You need presence/absence or sketch-based comparisons (e.g. Mash/Sourmash-style MinHash sketches) — this skill specifically benchmarks Libra's full-read k-mer abundance scoring, not data-reduced methods.

skills.description: Use when you must quantify how accurately an MLST deconvolution pipeline recovers fractional allele composition and complete strain types from simulated mixed reads, and need a baseline comparison against abundance-estimation tools like Kallisto or strainEST.
skills.name: allele-abundance-estimation
skills.search_text: allele-abundance-estimation Use when you must quantify how accurately an MLST deconvolution pipeline recovers fractional allele composition and complete strain types from simulated mixed reads, and need a baseline comparison against abundance-estimation tools like Kallisto or strainEST. Input is real WGS tick-sample data rather than controlled simulations — the Kallisto/strainEST baseline comparison was validated only on ART-simulated reads with known ground-truth allele and strain composition The goal is strain deconvolution itself (solving the Allele/Strain Diversity Problem via ILP with CPLEX), not benchmarking an already-produced allele/abundance call set Working with a different organism whose MLST scheme lacks the B. burgdorferi allele database and edit-distance structure used to set the d ∈ {5,10,15,20,25} parameter grid http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark the allele diversity pipeline (B-MLST) against Kallisto and strainEST on ART-simulated B. burgdorferi MLST read sets, quantifying precision, recall, Total Variation Distance per housekeeping gene, and Earth-Mover's distance for strain-level recovery. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Benchmark the allele diversity pipeline (B-MLST) against Kallisto and strainEST on ART-simulated B. burgdorferi MLST read sets, quantifying precision, recall, Total Variation Distance per housekeeping gene, and Earth-Mover's distance for strain-level recovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real WGS tick-sample data rather than controlled simulations — the Kallisto/strainEST baseline comparison was validated only on ART-simulated reads with known ground-truth allele and strain composition The goal is strain deconvolution itself (solving the Allele/Strain Diversity Problem via ILP with CPLEX), not benchmarking an already-produced allele/abundance call set Working with a different organism whose MLST scheme lacks the B. burgdorferi allele database and edit-distance structure used to set the d ∈ {5,10,15,20,25} parameter grid

skills.description: Use when validating an allele-diversity or strain-deconvolution stage against known simulated allele mixtures, and you need per-locus precision/recall and TVD statistics to compare with published baselines.
skills.name: allele-call-accuracy-evaluation-tvd
skills.search_text: allele-call-accuracy-evaluation-tvd Use when validating an allele-diversity or strain-deconvolution stage against known simulated allele mixtures, and you need per-locus precision/recall and TVD statistics to compare with published baselines. Input is real tick-sample WGS data with unknown allele composition — no ground truth exists to compute Precision/Recall/TVD against Evaluating the second Strain Diversity Problem (SDP) stage, which is validated with random strain-type distributions and perfect allele calls rather than read-level ADP simulation The goal is comparing against alternative abundance estimators like Kallisto or strainEST using their native outputs rather than the ADP simulation framework http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarking protocol that quantifies how accurately the Allele Diversity Problem (ADP) stage of the B. burgdorferi MLST pipeline recovers simulated fractional allele compositions, using Precision, Recall and Total Variation Distance (TVD) aggregated per locus. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol that quantifies how accurately the Allele Diversity Problem (ADP) stage of the B. burgdorferi MLST pipeline recovers simulated fractional allele compositions, using Precision, Recall and Total Variation Distance (TVD) aggregated per locus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real tick-sample WGS data with unknown allele composition — no ground truth exists to compute Precision/Recall/TVD against Evaluating the second Strain Diversity Problem (SDP) stage, which is validated with random strain-type distributions and perfect allele calls rather than read-level ADP simulation The goal is comparing against alternative abundance estimators like Kallisto or strainEST using their native outputs rather than the ADP simulation framework

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomic BAMs aligned to a reference gene database must be converted into allele-depth pile-ups (cellSNP VCF), clustered via MetaQuad, and normalized into per-gene nucleotide diversity for group comparisons.
skills.name: allele-depth-pileup-processing
skills.search_text: allele-depth-pileup-processing Use when shotgun metagenomic BAMs aligned to a reference gene database must be converted into allele-depth pile-ups (cellSNP VCF), clustered via MetaQuad, and normalized into per-gene nucleotide diversity for group comparisons. Input is already a computed Nucleotide_diversity.csv table — proceed directly to the diversity > 0.005 filter and Wilcoxon rank-sum comparison rather than re-running the pile-up pipeline. The goal is single-cell mitochondrial clonal substructure inference (MQuad/vireoSNP path), not shared informative variant discovery in shotgun metagenomic populations. Variants of interest are non-bi-allelic or occur at frequencies below the cellsnp-lite minMAF = 0.02 / minCOUNT = 100 pile-up thresholds, so AD/DP counts will be too sparse to cluster. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Processes cellSNP-lite allele-depth (AD/DP) pile-ups of shotgun metagenomic reads aligned to ARG references into MetaQuad cluster parameters and per-gene, per-sample nucleotide diversity, enabling detection of shared informative variants (e.g., ARG diversity shifts after LEVO treatment). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Processes cellSNP-lite allele-depth (AD/DP) pile-ups of shotgun metagenomic reads aligned to ARG references into MetaQuad cluster parameters and per-gene, per-sample nucleotide diversity, enabling detection of shared informative variants (e.g., ARG diversity shifts after LEVO treatment).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a computed Nucleotide_diversity.csv table — proceed directly to the diversity > 0.005 filter and Wilcoxon rank-sum comparison rather than re-running the pile-up pipeline. The goal is single-cell mitochondrial clonal substructure inference (MQuad/vireoSNP path), not shared informative variant discovery in shotgun metagenomic populations. Variants of interest are non-bi-allelic or occur at frequencies below the cellsnp-lite minMAF = 0.02 / minCOUNT = 100 pile-up thresholds, so AD/DP counts will be too sparse to cluster.

skills.description: Use when WGS reads have been mapped to a curated MLST allele database and you must infer, per locus, which alleles are present and their fractional proportions in mixed (within-host heterogeneous) samples.
skills.name: allele-diversity-integer-linear-programming
skills.search_text: allele-diversity-integer-linear-programming Use when WGS reads have been mapped to a curated MLST allele database and you must infer, per locus, which alleles are present and their fractional proportions in mixed (within-host heterogeneous) samples. No curated reference allele database exists for your species — the ADP is reference-based (unlike de novo methods such as DESMAN) and requires known MLST alleles The goal is direct strain-type calling from perfect allele inputs — that is the second-stage Strain Diversity Problem MILP, not this allele-assignment ILP Reads are unmapped or mapping information has not been extracted from SAM files — the ILP consumes the sampleX_geneY_paired_reads.txt files, not raw FASTQ http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Solves the Allele Diversity Problem (ADP) from the MLST strain-deconvolution pipeline: given per-locus read-to-allele mapping information, a 0-1 ILP selects the smallest set of known database alleles (with normalized Phred mismatch weights in the objective) that explains each sample's reads, then computes fractional allele proportions per locus. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Solves the Allele Diversity Problem (ADP) from the MLST strain-deconvolution pipeline: given per-locus read-to-allele mapping information, a 0-1 ILP selects the smallest set of known database alleles (with normalized Phred mismatch weights in the objective) that explains each sample's reads, then computes fractional allele proportions per locus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No curated reference allele database exists for your species — the ADP is reference-based (unlike de novo methods such as DESMAN) and requires known MLST alleles The goal is direct strain-type calling from perfect allele inputs — that is the second-stage Strain Diversity Problem MILP, not this allele-assignment ILP Reads are unmapped or mapping information has not been extracted from SAM files — the ILP consumes the sampleX_geneY_paired_reads.txt files, not raw FASTQ

skills.description: Use when you have one FASTA file per locus with all identified alleles from a chewBBACA cg/wgMLST schema and need to assess allelic variability per locus via per-locus MSAs and phylogenetic trees.
skills.name: allele-fasta-sequence-processing
skills.search_text: allele-fasta-sequence-processing Use when you have one FASTA file per locus with all identified alleles from a chewBBACA cg/wgMLST schema and need to assess allelic variability per locus via per-locus MSAs and phylogenetic trees. Input is genome assemblies or reads rather than per-locus allele FASTA files — use chewBBACA allele calling (AlleleCall) instead. You need a single whole-cgMLST alignment rather than per-locus assessments — use the ComputeMSA module, which produces the cgMLST MSA (protein_msa.fasta) via the AlleleCallEvaluator. The schema loci have not yet been filtered for paralogs (e.g. the 20 RepeatedLoci.txt loci in the tutorial), since paralogous loci confound per-locus variability interpretation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Processes the per-locus allele FASTA files output by chewBBACA (each containing the full allelic diversity of a locus) by building a MAFFT nucleotide multiple sequence alignment per locus and reconstructing a ClustalW2 neighbour-joining tree per locus, enabling exploration of the consequences of allelic variability at each schema locus. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000166
skills.summary: Processes the per-locus allele FASTA files output by chewBBACA (each containing the full allelic diversity of a locus) by building a MAFFT nucleotide multiple sequence alignment per locus and reconstructing a ClustalW2 neighbour-joining tree per locus, enabling exploration of the consequences of allelic variability at each schema locus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is genome assemblies or reads rather than per-locus allele FASTA files — use chewBBACA allele calling (AlleleCall) instead. You need a single whole-cgMLST alignment rather than per-locus assessments — use the ComputeMSA module, which produces the cgMLST MSA (protein_msa.fasta) via the AlleleCallEvaluator. The schema loci have not yet been filtered for paralogs (e.g. the 20 RepeatedLoci.txt loci in the tutorial), since paralogous loci confound per-locus variability interpretation.

skills.description: Use when you have cellsnp-lite AD/DP allele count matrices from shotgun metagenomic samples and need to identify shared informative variants versus background noise based on clustering of sample allele frequencies.
skills.name: allele-frequency-density-clustering
skills.search_text: allele-frequency-density-clustering Use when you have cellsnp-lite AD/DP allele count matrices from shotgun metagenomic samples and need to identify shared informative variants versus background noise based on clustering of sample allele frequencies. Input is single-cell mitochondrial data rather than shotgun metagenomic samples — the predecessor MQuad uses a binomial mixture model with BIC-based filtering for that setting You need a statistical significance/informativeness score (e.g., deltaBIC) rather than a density-cluster count per variant Variants have not been piled up with cellsnp-lite and only raw BAMs or VCFs without AD/DP counts are available http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Distinguish shared informative variants from sequencing errors and non-polymorphic sites in metagenomic allele count data by running one-dimensional OPTICS density-based clustering (scikit-learn) over per-sample alternate-allele frequencies for each cellsnp-lite variant, flagging variants with >=2 clusters. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Distinguish shared informative variants from sequencing errors and non-polymorphic sites in metagenomic allele count data by running one-dimensional OPTICS density-based clustering (scikit-learn) over per-sample alternate-allele frequencies for each cellsnp-lite variant, flagging variants with >=2 clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell mitochondrial data rather than shotgun metagenomic samples — the predecessor MQuad uses a binomial mixture model with BIC-based filtering for that setting You need a statistical significance/informativeness score (e.g., deltaBIC) rather than a density-cluster count per variant Variants have not been piled up with cellsnp-lite and only raw BAMs or VCFs without AD/DP counts are available

skills.description: Use when comparing treatment groups (e.g. CLA, LEVO vs OTHERS) at a time point such as T+6W using allele-frequency profiles of shared informative variants from a cellSNP-lite/MetaQuad pipeline on ARG VCF data.
skills.name: allele-frequency-dissimilarity-computation
skills.search_text: allele-frequency-dissimilarity-computation Use when comparing treatment groups (e.g. CLA, LEVO vs OTHERS) at a time point such as T+6W using allele-frequency profiles of shared informative variants from a cellSNP-lite/MetaQuad pipeline on ARG VCF data. The question is gene-level nucleotide diversity of ARGs rather than between-sample allele-frequency dissimilarity — use the nucleotide_diversity_code.R workflow instead. The variant set lacks shared informative variants (e.g. fewer than the minSample = 5% threshold or num_of_clusters < 2), so no informative dissimilarity signal exists between groups. skills.name: amber-rank-based-profile-evaluation
skills.search_text: amber-rank-based-profile-evaluation Use when per-sample taxonomic profiling results (e.g. ganon2, kraken2+bracken, kmcp outputs on simulated CAMI/RefSeq samples) must be scored against ground-truth taxon assignments to compare F1-score by rank and abundance accuracy. The task is taxonomic binning evaluation rather than profiling — AMBER also reports binning metrics (purity, completeness, UniFrac), but this skill targets rank-based profiling F1 and L1-norm error Input reads are real (non-simulated) samples with no ground-truth taxon assignments to compare against Raw read FASTQ files that have not yet been classified/profiled by a tool such as ganon2 or kraken2+bracken http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Evaluates taxonomic profiling outputs against ground truth using AMBER 2.0.21-beta, extracting per-rank (tp, tp_direct, tp_indirect, fp_lower, fp_higher, sens, prec, f1s) and cumulative metrics, plus L1-norm abundance error and runtime, to compare profilers such as ganon2 vs kraken2+bracken on simulated samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaf094
skills.summary: Evaluates taxonomic profiling outputs against ground truth using AMBER 2.0.21-beta, extracting per-rank (tp, tp_direct, tp_indirect, fp_lower, fp_higher, sens, prec, f1s) and cumulative metrics, plus L1-norm abundance error and runtime, to compare profilers such as ganon2 vs kraken2+bracken on simulated samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is taxonomic binning evaluation rather than profiling — AMBER also reports binning metrics (purity, completeness, UniFrac), but this skill targets rank-based profiling F1 and L1-norm error Input reads are real (non-simulated) samples with no ground-truth taxon assignments to compare against Raw read FASTQ files that have not yet been classified/profiled by a tool such as ganon2 or kraken2+bracken

skills.description: Use when enumerating k-mers from metagenomic reads that contain ambiguous bases ('N'), adapter remnants, or concatenated paired mates, to decide which k-mers contribute LCA taxa to the classification tree.
skills.name: ambiguous-nucleotide-kmer-filtering
skills.search_text: ambiguous-nucleotide-kmer-filtering Use when enumerating k-mers from metagenomic reads that contain ambiguous bases ('N'), adapter remnants, or concatenated paired mates, to decide which k-mers contribute LCA taxa to the classification tree. The input is a raw k-mer count table or feature matrix rather than nucleotide sequences — there are no per-base characters to screen for ambiguity A downstream alignment-based classifier (e.g. BLAST/Megablast) is being used, where ambiguous bases can be handled by alignment scoring rather than k-mer exclusion Abundance estimation workflows (e.g. MetaPhlAn) that only classify a small percentage of sequences and do not enumerate all query k-mers http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Kraken's rule of skipping any k-mer containing ambiguous nucleotides (e.g. 'N') during k-mer enumeration and database lookup, so that low-quality or masked positions do not contribute spurious evidence to the classification tree. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Kraken's rule of skipping any k-mer containing ambiguous nucleotides (e.g. 'N') during k-mer enumeration and database lookup, so that low-quality or masked positions do not contribute spurious evidence to the classification tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw k-mer count table or feature matrix rather than nucleotide sequences — there are no per-base characters to screen for ambiguity A downstream alignment-based classifier (e.g. BLAST/Megablast) is being used, where ambiguous bases can be handled by alignment scoring rather than k-mer exclusion Abundance estimation workflows (e.g. MetaPhlAn) that only classify a small percentage of sequences and do not enumerate all query k-mers

skills.description: Use when LiME's Classify step labels paired-end reads as Ambiguous (status 'A') in the OutputFile and you need to convert those entries into single-taxon assignments (C/U) before computing species-level SEN/PREC/F1/specificity on datasets such as setA2/setB2.
skills.name: ambiguous-read-re-examination
skills.search_text: ambiguous-read-re-examination Use when LiME's Classify step labels paired-end reads as Ambiguous (status 'A') in the OutputFile and you need to convert those entries into single-taxon assignments (C/U) before computing species-level SEN/PREC/F1/specificity on datasets such as setA2/setB2. The read collection is single-end — the re-examination relies on mate-summed similarity (M' and M'') from paired-end reads, so no mate evidence exists to disambiguate the entry No reads were flagged Ambiguous ('A') by Classify — the second phase only considers ambiguous entries, so there is nothing to re-examine You want a fast first-pass taxonomic screen rather than final per-read assignments — the standard single-pass classification output (with 'A' entries retained) is sufficient http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Second-pass classification step of LiME that resolves reads flagged Ambiguous ('A') by re-examining them with paired-end mate information, using maximum mate-summed similarity (M' and M'') to assign each read pair to a single taxon (e.g. species) instead of leaving it ambiguous. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03628-w
skills.summary: Second-pass classification step of LiME that resolves reads flagged Ambiguous ('A') by re-examining them with paired-end mate information, using maximum mate-summed similarity (M' and M'') to assign each read pair to a single taxon (e.g. species) instead of leaving it ambiguous.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The read collection is single-end — the re-examination relies on mate-summed similarity (M' and M'') from paired-end reads, so no mate evidence exists to disambiguate the entry No reads were flagged Ambiguous ('A') by Classify — the second phase only considers ambiguous entries, so there is nothing to re-examine You want a fast first-pass taxonomic screen rather than final per-read assignments — the standard single-pass classification output (with 'A' entries retained) is sufficient

skills.description: Use when two non-redundant protein/gene catalogues (e.g. VMGC-90 vs VIRGO-90) must be compared to compute mutual gene coverage and protein-space expansion fractions.
skills.name: amino-acid-identity-alignment-filtering
skills.search_text: amino-acid-identity-alignment-filtering Use when two non-redundant protein/gene catalogues (e.g. VMGC-90 vs VIRGO-90) must be compared to compute mutual gene coverage and protein-space expansion fractions. The catalogues were clustered at a different amino-acid identity threshold (e.g. VMGC-50 or VMGC-95), since 90%/80% cutoffs and expected fractions only apply to 90%-identity catalogues The inputs are nucleotide contigs or genomes rather than protein-coding gene catalogue FASTA files The goal is functional annotation overlap (e.g. KEGG/CAZy categories) rather than sequence-level gene coverage http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies overlap between large protein-coding gene catalogues by running an MMseqs2 all-vs-all alignment under strict amino-acid identity and coverage cutoffs (e.g. 90% identity, 80% coverage), as done to compare the VMGC-90 vaginal gene catalogue with VIRGO-90. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Quantifies overlap between large protein-coding gene catalogues by running an MMseqs2 all-vs-all alignment under strict amino-acid identity and coverage cutoffs (e.g. 90% identity, 80% coverage), as done to compare the VMGC-90 vaginal gene catalogue with VIRGO-90.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The catalogues were clustered at a different amino-acid identity threshold (e.g. VMGC-50 or VMGC-95), since 90%/80% cutoffs and expected fractions only apply to 90%-identity catalogues The inputs are nucleotide contigs or genomes rather than protein-coding gene catalogue FASTA files The goal is functional annotation overlap (e.g. KEGG/CAZy categories) rather than sequence-level gene coverage

skills.description: Use when training Snekmer supervised models or clustering protein families (e.g., nitrogen cycling families or UniProt genomes) and you must choose among the 7 AAR alphabets (sizes 2–20) and k=4–16 via config.yaml sweeps.
skills.name: amino-acid-recoding-alphabet-selection
skills.search_text: amino-acid-recoding-alphabet-selection Use when training Snekmer supervised models or clustering protein families (e.g., nitrogen cycling families or UniProt genomes) and you must choose among the 7 AAR alphabets (sizes 2–20) and k=4–16 via config.yaml sweeps. Input is nucleotide sequence or an already-encoded feature/kmer table — the skill assumes raw amino acid FASTA input to the AAR-kmer recoding pipeline The goal is exact sequence similarity search or the highest-sensitivity de novo clustering regardless of method — MMseqs2 easy-cluster achieved higher V-scores than any Snekmer AAR/kmer parameterization on the 10-genome benchmark Only a single alphabet/k combination is of interest with no comparison — the value of this skill is the full 7x13 sweep and its validation against reported best combinations http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Systematic selection of the amino acid recoding (AAR) alphabet (hydro, standard, solvacc, hydrocharge, hydrostruct, miqs, or no recoding) and kmer length (k=4–16) for Snekmer's supervised 'model' and unsupervised 'cluster' modes, judged by cross-validation ROC AUC/PR AUC and clustering V-scores. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad005
skills.summary: Systematic selection of the amino acid recoding (AAR) alphabet (hydro, standard, solvacc, hydrocharge, hydrostruct, miqs, or no recoding) and kmer length (k=4–16) for Snekmer's supervised 'model' and unsupervised 'cluster' modes, judged by cross-validation ROC AUC/PR AUC and clustering V-scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is nucleotide sequence or an already-encoded feature/kmer table — the skill assumes raw amino acid FASTA input to the AAR-kmer recoding pipeline The goal is exact sequence similarity search or the highest-sensitivity de novo clustering regardless of method — MMseqs2 easy-cluster achieved higher V-scores than any Snekmer AAR/kmer parameterization on the 10-genome benchmark Only a single alphabet/k combination is of interest with no comparison — the value of this skill is the full 7x13 sweep and its validation against reported best combinations

skills.description: Use when protein FASTA sequences must be vectorized as reduced-alphabet AAR kmers, or when supervised family-scoring semantics (F_kmer, F'_kmer, S_kmer with values in (-1, 1)) must be reproduced or unit-tested in Python.
skills.name: amino-acid-recoding-kmer-vectorization
skills.search_text: amino-acid-recoding-kmer-vectorization Use when protein FASTA sequences must be vectorized as reduced-alphabet AAR kmers, or when supervised family-scoring semantics (F_kmer, F'_kmer, S_kmer with values in (-1, 1)) must be reproduced or unit-tested in Python. The goal is unsupervised clustering of sequences (use Snekmer's cluster mode with agglomerative-jaccard or density-jaccard) rather than supervised family scoring The input is already a feature/embedding table and no AAR kmer vectorization is needed The sequences are not proteins (e.g. nucleotide FASTA) and no amino-acid recoding is intended http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Implements Snekmer's AAR-kmer feature construction and supervised kmer scoring: proteins are recoded into reduced-alphabet amino-acid-recoded (AAR) kmer vectors, and family scores F_kmer = n_kmer/N, modified scores F'_kmer (penalizing kmers shared with other families), and overall scores S_kmer in (-1, 1) are computed. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad005
skills.summary: Implements Snekmer's AAR-kmer feature construction and supervised kmer scoring: proteins are recoded into reduced-alphabet amino-acid-recoded (AAR) kmer vectors, and family scores F_kmer = n_kmer/N, modified scores F'_kmer (penalizing kmers shared with other families), and overall scores S_kmer in (-1, 1) are computed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is unsupervised clustering of sequences (use Snekmer's cluster mode with agglomerative-jaccard or density-jaccard) rather than supervised family scoring The input is already a feature/embedding table and no AAR kmer vectorization is needed The sequences are not proteins (e.g. nucleotide FASTA) and no amino-acid recoding is intended

skills.description: Use when protein FASTA sequences (e.g., nitrogen cycling families) must be recoded into AAR k-mer vectors, or when comparing feature-generation runtime/model performance of MIQS-recoded k-mers versus unencoded k-mers at a fixed k.
skills.name: amino-acid-reduction-encoding
skills.search_text: amino-acid-reduction-encoding Use when protein FASTA sequences (e.g., nitrogen cycling families) must be recoded into AAR k-mer vectors, or when comparing feature-generation runtime/model performance of MIQS-recoded k-mers versus unencoded k-mers at a fixed k. Input is already a vectorized k-mer feature table or model output (e.g., results/apply/snekmer_results.csv) rather than raw FASTA sequences The goal is downstream prediction/annotation scoring (apply mode with Score/delta/Confidence columns), not feature generation or its runtime benchmarking Input sequences are nucleotide (e.g., FASTQ) rather than protein sequences — Snekmer recodes proteins http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Recodes protein sequences into amino-acid-reduced (AAR) k-mer vectors with Snekmer (e.g., MIQS reduced alphabet, k=4) and benchmarks the feature-generation cost against unencoded native-sequence k-mers. The MIQS-recoded vectorization is nearly 4x faster while yielding comparable models (Supplementary Table S2). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad005
skills.summary: Recodes protein sequences into amino-acid-reduced (AAR) k-mer vectors with Snekmer (e.g., MIQS reduced alphabet, k=4) and benchmarks the feature-generation cost against unencoded native-sequence k-mers. The MIQS-recoded vectorization is nearly 4x faster while yielding comparable models (Supplementary Table S2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a vectorized k-mer feature table or model output (e.g., results/apply/snekmer_results.csv) rather than raw FASTA sequences The goal is downstream prediction/annotation scoring (apply mode with Score/delta/Confidence columns), not feature generation or its runtime benchmarking Input sequences are nucleotide (e.g., FASTQ) rather than protein sequences — Snekmer recodes proteins

skills.description: Use when a curated set of amoA-AOB (or similar functional gene) reference protein+nucleotide sequences must be clustered into representative clusters and prioritized by abundance/prevalence across environmental metagenomes before primer design.
skills.name: amoa-aob-gene-cluster-analysis
skills.search_text: amoa-aob-gene-cluster-analysis Use when a curated set of amoA-AOB (or similar functional gene) reference protein+nucleotide sequences must be clustered into representative clusters and prioritized by abundance/prevalence across environmental metagenomes before primer design. Input is uncurated raw metagenomic reads rather than a curated functional gene reference set (Fungene-style HMM filtering has not been applied) The goal is primer design or in silico PCR coverage evaluation itself — those belong to the downstream MetaFunPrimer/EcoFunPrimer skills that consume this skill's ranked gene output Reference metagenomes are not environment-relevant, since gene target prioritization depends on ranking gene presence in user-defined environment-specific metagenomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Clusters curated FunGene amoA-AOB reference protein sequences into representative gene clusters with CD-HIT and ranks those clusters by an R-score (mean of normalized abundance and prevalence) computed from DIAMOND alignments against 1,550 publicly available soil metagenomes, to identify environment-abundant amoA-AOB targets. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00201-21
skills.summary: Clusters curated FunGene amoA-AOB reference protein sequences into representative gene clusters with CD-HIT and ranks those clusters by an R-score (mean of normalized abundance and prevalence) computed from DIAMOND alignments against 1,550 publicly available soil metagenomes, to identify environment-abundant amoA-AOB targets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is uncurated raw metagenomic reads rather than a curated functional gene reference set (Fungene-style HMM filtering has not been applied) The goal is primer design or in silico PCR coverage evaluation itself — those belong to the downstream MetaFunPrimer/EcoFunPrimer skills that consume this skill's ranked gene output Reference metagenomes are not environment-relevant, since gene target prioritization depends on ranking gene presence in user-defined environment-specific metagenomes

skills.description: Use when you have overlapping paired-end Illumina FASTQ/SAM reads (e.g. 16S rRNA amplicons) and must merge them while probabilistically correcting uncalled or miscalled bases, then filter assemblies by quality score.
skills.name: amplicon-assembly-validation
skills.search_text: amplicon-assembly-validation Use when you have overlapping paired-end Illumina FASTQ/SAM reads (e.g. 16S rRNA amplicons) and must merge them while probabilistically correcting uncalled or miscalled bases, then filter assemblies by quality score. Reads are not expected to overlap (e.g. non-overlapping paired-end libraries) — SeqPrep's README warns to save overlapping for libraries with known overlap; naive assembly or no merge is more appropriate Input is already an assembled contig or a post-assembly feature/OTU table — no overlap-assembly step remains to apply The platform is not Illumina or reads have high gap probability — PANDAseq exploits Illumina-specific properties including low probability of gap-inclusion http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Probabilistically assemble paired-end Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon reads with PANDAseq, which determines the optimal overlap from quality-score-derived match probabilities, corrects mismatches and uncalled bases in the overlap, and rejects assemblies failing quality/length/uncalled-base criteria. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Probabilistically assemble paired-end Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon reads with PANDAseq, which determines the optimal overlap from quality-score-derived match probabilities, corrects mismatches and uncalled bases in the overlap, and rejects assemblies failing quality/length/uncalled-base criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are not expected to overlap (e.g. non-overlapping paired-end libraries) — SeqPrep's README warns to save overlapping for libraries with known overlap; naive assembly or no merge is more appropriate Input is already an assembled contig or a post-assembly feature/OTU table — no overlap-assembly step remains to apply The platform is not Illumina or reads have high gap probability — PANDAseq exploits Illumina-specific properties including low probability of gap-inclusion

skills.description: Use when building or validating a background error model for amplicon variant calling: one-mismatch child abundances (mean/SD per cluster) must be related to parent sequencing depth to justify an abundance threshold.
skills.name: amplicon-error-background-modeling
skills.search_text: amplicon-error-background-modeling Use when building or validating a background error model for amplicon variant calling: one-mismatch child abundances (mean/SD per cluster) must be related to parent sequencing depth to justify an abundance threshold. The input is not a HashSeq run output — e.g. you only have a finalized feature/count table with no one-mismatch cluster statistics You need to capture indel variation relative to a parent, since HashSeq does not explicitly model insertions or deletions (methods like Deblur that use multiple-sequence alignments are suggested) The target variants are true low-abundance sequences below the 1,000-read threshold — the article recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 for those http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Estimate a depth-dependent background sequencing-error model for 16S rRNA amplicon data by regressing the mean and standard deviation of one-mismatch child variant abundances against parent sequence abundance with LOESS, as implemented in the HashSeq package. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Estimate a depth-dependent background sequencing-error model for 16S rRNA amplicon data by regressing the mean and standard deviation of one-mismatch child variant abundances against parent sequence abundance with LOESS, as implemented in the HashSeq package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a HashSeq run output — e.g. you only have a finalized feature/count table with no one-mismatch cluster statistics You need to capture indel variation relative to a parent, since HashSeq does not explicitly model insertions or deletions (methods like Deblur that use multiple-sequence alignments are suggested) The target variants are true low-abundance sequences below the 1,000-read threshold — the article recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 for those

skills.description: Use when paired amplicon (16S) and metagenomic profiles exist for the same mock or known communities and you need to test whether GCN correction (or another bias correction) brings the amplicon profile closer to the metagenomic or expected composition.
skills.name: amplicon-metagenome-profile-agreement-analysis
skills.search_text: amplicon-metagenome-profile-agreement-analysis Use when paired amplicon (16S) and metagenomic profiles exist for the same mock or known communities and you need to test whether GCN correction (or another bias correction) brings the amplicon profile closer to the metagenomic or expected composition. Your study relies on taxonomies other than Greengenes (e.g. Silva) — CopyRighter's pre-computed GCN estimates cover the Greengenes taxonomy; Silva support was only anticipated in the discussion You need correction of GC percent bias, genome length bias, or fungal ITS variation — these are only hypothetical pending appropriate pre-computed estimates The input community file contains percentages rather than read counts, or taxa have altered taxonomic assignments http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantify how closely 16S rRNA gene amplicon microbial profiles agree with matched metagenomic (shotgun) profiles of the same mock communities, before and after GCN correction with CopyRighter. Agreement serves as validation evidence that gene copy number correction makes amplicon-based relative abundances more accurate. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Quantify how closely 16S rRNA gene amplicon microbial profiles agree with matched metagenomic (shotgun) profiles of the same mock communities, before and after GCN correction with CopyRighter. Agreement serves as validation evidence that gene copy number correction makes amplicon-based relative abundances more accurate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your study relies on taxonomies other than Greengenes (e.g. Silva) — CopyRighter's pre-computed GCN estimates cover the Greengenes taxonomy; Silva support was only anticipated in the discussion You need correction of GC percent bias, genome length bias, or fungal ITS variation — these are only hypothetical pending appropriate pre-computed estimates The input community file contains percentages rather than read counts, or taxa have altered taxonomic assignments

skills.description: Use when raw amplicon FASTQ reads (454 or Illumina 16S/ITS) need primer trimming plus adaptive quality filtering before OTU clustering, and reads exceeding a maximum expected error (EE) budget must be discarded.
skills.name: amplicon-metagenomic-preprocessing
skills.search_text: amplicon-metagenomic-preprocessing Use when raw amplicon FASTQ reads (454 or Illumina 16S/ITS) need primer trimming plus adaptive quality filtering before OTU clustering, and reads exceeding a maximum expected error (EE) budget must be discarded. Input reads are already primer-trimmed and quality-filtered (e.g., downstream of MICCA's trim/filter, feeding OTU clustering or chimera detection directly) The goal is UPARSE-style stringent quality filtering, which truncates reads at the first base below a quality threshold and discards a large fraction of sequence data — MICCA's EE-based filtering is deliberately more flexible Data are shotgun metagenomic reads rather than targeted conserved amplicons (16S rRNA, ITS, 18S, 28S), which is MICCA's declared scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 MICCA's raw-read preprocessing skill for targeted metagenomic (amplicon) data: primer removal followed by sliding-window adaptive quality filtering that discards reads whose expected error (EE) exceeds the allowed maximum. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/srep09743
skills.summary: MICCA's raw-read preprocessing skill for targeted metagenomic (amplicon) data: primer removal followed by sliding-window adaptive quality filtering that discards reads whose expected error (EE) exceeds the allowed maximum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already primer-trimmed and quality-filtered (e.g., downstream of MICCA's trim/filter, feeding OTU clustering or chimera detection directly) The goal is UPARSE-style stringent quality filtering, which truncates reads at the first base below a quality threshold and discards a large fraction of sequence data — MICCA's EE-based filtering is deliberately more flexible Data are shotgun metagenomic reads rather than targeted conserved amplicons (16S rRNA, ITS, 18S, 28S), which is MICCA's declared scope

skills.description: Use when a validation study needs communities of known composition to benchmark amplicon profiling or GCN correction — e.g. to test whether CopyRighter-corrected 16S profiles match expected and metagenomic profiles.
skills.name: amplicon-metagenomic-read-simulation
skills.search_text: amplicon-metagenomic-read-simulation Use when a validation study needs communities of known composition to benchmark amplicon profiling or GCN correction — e.g. to test whether CopyRighter-corrected 16S profiles match expected and metagenomic profiles. Real environmental sequencing data — simulation is only useful when the true community composition is known (mock communities); for real samples, compare amplicon vs. metagenomic profiles directly instead GCN correction itself — this skill is the upstream read-simulation step that produces benchmark inputs; correction is done downstream with CopyRighter Studies targeting non-16S markers (e.g. fungal ITS) — the Greengenes-based simulation and correction framework described here covers Bacteria (GCN 1–15) and Archaea (up to 5) only http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Generate in silico mock communities (low/medium/high richness, 10–1,000 species) and simulate both 16S rRNA gene amplicon reads and shotgun metagenomic reads with Grinder, producing paired ground-truth datasets to benchmark GCN-corrected amplicon profiles against known compositions and metagenomic references. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Generate in silico mock communities (low/medium/high richness, 10–1,000 species) and simulate both 16S rRNA gene amplicon reads and shotgun metagenomic reads with Grinder, producing paired ground-truth datasets to benchmark GCN-corrected amplicon profiles against known compositions and metagenomic references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real environmental sequencing data — simulation is only useful when the true community composition is known (mock communities); for real samples, compare amplicon vs. metagenomic profiles directly instead GCN correction itself — this skill is the upstream read-simulation step that produces benchmark inputs; correction is done downstream with CopyRighter Studies targeting non-16S markers (e.g. fungal ITS) — the Greengenes-based simulation and correction framework described here covers Bacteria (GCN 1–15) and Archaea (up to 5) only

skills.description: Use when you have an OTU representative-sequence FASTA file from MICCA de novo clustering and need an aligned set and phylogenetic tree (Newick) for downstream phylogenetic diversity metrics.
skills.name: amplicon-metagenomic-workflow-command-execution
skills.search_text: amplicon-metagenomic-workflow-command-execution Use when you have an OTU representative-sequence FASTA file from MICCA de novo clustering and need an aligned set and phylogenetic tree (Newick) for downstream phylogenetic diversity metrics. Input is raw reads or a sample-by-OTU abundance table rather than an OTU representative-sequence FASTA — the msa/tree commands operate on sequences from the pipeline's clustering step You need taxonomy assignment rather than a phylogeny — use MICCA's 'classify' command (RDP classifier) instead Sequences are unrelated or non-homologous such that a NAST alignment against a common backbone is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Reconstructs the MICCA multiple-sequence alignment (MSA) and FastTree phylogenetic inference step for OTU representative sequences, closing the amplicon pipeline from clustered OTUs to a Newick tree usable for diversity analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/srep09743
skills.summary: Reconstructs the MICCA multiple-sequence alignment (MSA) and FastTree phylogenetic inference step for OTU representative sequences, closing the amplicon pipeline from clustered OTUs to a Newick tree usable for diversity analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or a sample-by-OTU abundance table rather than an OTU representative-sequence FASTA — the msa/tree commands operate on sequences from the pipeline's clustering step You need taxonomy assignment rather than a phylogeny — use MICCA's 'classify' command (RDP classifier) instead Sequences are unrelated or non-homologous such that a NAST alignment against a common backbone is meaningless

skills.description: Use when OTU representative sequences need taxonomic labels under alternative 16S reference databases (Greengenes, SILVA, NCBI RefSeq) to quantify how database choice affects downstream community-composition inferences.
skills.name: amplicon-naive-bayes-taxonomy-assignment
skills.search_text: amplicon-naive-bayes-taxonomy-assignment Use when OTU representative sequences need taxonomic labels under alternative 16S reference databases (Greengenes, SILVA, NCBI RefSeq) to quantify how database choice affects downstream community-composition inferences. Input is raw 16S reads that have not yet been demultiplexed, denoised/clustered into OTU representative sequences (the TA step expects qiime2-supported sequence inputs) The goal is comparing taxonomic diversity or alpha/beta metrics rather than comparing assignments across reference databases A de novo OTU or ASV workflow outside MiCoNE's configuration system is required (e.g., custom classifier training beyond gg_13_8_99_515_806 / SILVA defaults) Assigns taxonomy to 16S OTU representative sequences using the MiCoNE taxonomy-assignment (TA) step: QIIME2 Naive Bayes classifiers trained on Greengenes (gg_13_8_99_515_806) or SILVA at confidence 0.7, and BLAST against ncbi_refseq, enabling database-comparison analyses. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: Assigns taxonomy to 16S OTU representative sequences using the MiCoNE taxonomy-assignment (TA) step: QIIME2 Naive Bayes classifiers trained on Greengenes (gg_13_8_99_515_806) or SILVA at confidence 0.7, and BLAST against ncbi_refseq, enabling database-comparison analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw 16S reads that have not yet been demultiplexed, denoised/clustered into OTU representative sequences (the TA step expects qiime2-supported sequence inputs) The goal is comparing taxonomic diversity or alpha/beta metrics rather than comparing assignments across reference databases A de novo OTU or ASV workflow outside MiCoNE's configuration system is required (e.g., custom classifier training beyond gg_13_8_99_515_806 / SILVA defaults)

skills.description: Use when demultiplexed 16S amplicon reads must be processed by multiple OTU-assignment/denoising methods and the similarity of the resulting representative sequence sets needs to be quantified with UniFrac distances.
skills.name: amplicon-otu-clustering-method-comparison
skills.search_text: amplicon-otu-clustering-method-comparison Use when demultiplexed 16S amplicon reads must be processed by multiple OTU-assignment/denoising methods and the similarity of the resulting representative sequence sets needs to be quantified with UniFrac distances.
