skills.description: Use when assessing how alternative tools/parameters at each 16S pipeline step (DC, CC, TA, OP, NI) affect the inferred co-occurrence network, or when quantifying which step contributes most to total network variation.
skills.name: amplicon-pipeline-combination-enumeration
skills.search_text: amplicon-pipeline-combination-enumeration Use when assessing how alternative tools/parameters at each 16S pipeline step (DC, CC, TA, OP, NI) affect the inferred co-occurrence network, or when quantifying which step contributes most to total network variation. Input is already a feature table or interaction matrix/edge list — use MiCoNE's Network import from tsv/csv or edge list instead of re-running sequence-processing combinations. Goal is a single fixed pipeline run rather than systematic evaluation of alternative tools and parameters at each step. Data are not 16S amplicon sequences — MiCoNE workflows are designed to convert raw 16S sequencing data into co-occurrence networks. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Runs every tool/parameter combination across the DC, CC, TA, OP, and NI steps of a 16S co-occurrence pipeline with MiCoNE/Nextflow, then decomposes total network variation by step using PCA plus regression and ANOVA — revealing which step (e.g. taxonomy assignment at 65.4%) dominates. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: Runs every tool/parameter combination across the DC, CC, TA, OP, and NI steps of a 16S co-occurrence pipeline with MiCoNE/Nextflow, then decomposes total network variation by step using PCA plus regression and ANOVA — revealing which step (e.g. taxonomy assignment at 65.4%) dominates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or interaction matrix/edge list — use MiCoNE's Network import from tsv/csv or edge list instead of re-running sequence-processing combinations. Goal is a single fixed pipeline run rather than systematic evaluation of alternative tools and parameters at each step. Data are not 16S amplicon sequences — MiCoNE workflows are designed to convert raw 16S sequencing data into co-occurrence networks.

skills.description: Use when validating OTU-count accuracy of a 16S amplicon pipeline against a ground-truth synthetic dataset with known OTU composition, or when comparing de novo OTU-picking pipelines across sequencing depths.
skills.name: amplicon-rarefaction-depth-analysis
skills.search_text: amplicon-rarefaction-depth-analysis Use when validating OTU-count accuracy of a 16S amplicon pipeline against a ground-truth synthetic dataset with known OTU composition, or when comparing de novo OTU-picking pipelines across sequencing depths. Input data is real (non-synthetic) amplicon data with no known true OTU number, so accuracy of OTU-count estimation cannot be scored The goal is taxonomic composition or alpha-diversity estimation rather than OTU-count accuracy benchmarking The input is already an OTU table or feature table, i.e. OTU picking has already been performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A benchmarking protocol that compares how accurately amplicon pipelines (MICCA, MICCA-FAST, QIIME, mothur, UPARSE) estimate the number of OTUs as a function of sequencing depth on a synthetic 16S-R dataset with 500 true OTUs, by rarefying reads in steps of 1000 and plotting estimated/true OTU-count curves. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/srep09743
skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol that compares how accurately amplicon pipelines (MICCA, MICCA-FAST, QIIME, mothur, UPARSE) estimate the number of OTUs as a function of sequencing depth on a synthetic 16S-R dataset with 500 true OTUs, by rarefying reads in steps of 1000 and plotting estimated/true OTU-count curves.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is real (non-synthetic) amplicon data with no known true OTU number, so accuracy of OTU-count estimation cannot be scored The goal is taxonomic composition or alpha-diversity estimation rather than OTU-count accuracy benchmarking The input is already an OTU table or feature table, i.e. OTU picking has already been performed

skills.description: Use when quality-filtered FASTQ/FASTA amplicon reads must be collapsed to unique sequences with abundance vectors before de novo OTU inference, chimera filtering, or benchmarking dereplication speed.
skills.name: amplicon-read-dereplication
skills.search_text: amplicon-read-dereplication Use when quality-filtered FASTQ/FASTA amplicon reads must be collapsed to unique sequences with abundance vectors before de novo OTU inference, chimera filtering, or benchmarking dereplication speed. Input is already a dereplicated unique-sequence set with abundance counts The goal is reference-based OTU picking against a curated database rather than de novo inference Reads have not yet passed expected-error (EE) based quality filtering, since dereplication is a step that precedes chimera removal and clustering in the MICCA pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Collapses quality-filtered amplicon reads (e.g. 16S rRNA, ITS) into unique sequences with abundance counts prior to OTU clustering, using either exact string matching (MICCA-FAST) or VSEARCH-backed dereplication as implemented in the MICCA pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/srep09743
skills.summary: Collapses quality-filtered amplicon reads (e.g. 16S rRNA, ITS) into unique sequences with abundance counts prior to OTU clustering, using either exact string matching (MICCA-FAST) or VSEARCH-backed dereplication as implemented in the MICCA pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a dereplicated unique-sequence set with abundance counts The goal is reference-based OTU picking against a curated database rather than de novo inference Reads have not yet passed expected-error (EE) based quality filtering, since dereplication is a step that precedes chimera removal and clustering in the MICCA pipeline

skills.description: Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing reads (e.g., FASTQ deposited in QIITA) must be quality-filtered in QIIME 2.0 before downstream feature table, taxonomy, and phylogeny generation for MiSurv-style survival analysis.
skills.name: amplicon-read-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: amplicon-read-quality-filtering Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing reads (e.g., FASTQ deposited in QIITA) must be quality-filtered in QIIME 2.0 before downstream feature table, taxonomy, and phylogeny generation for MiSurv-style survival analysis. Input is already processed data — the phyloseq object biom.Rdata or the four files (otu.tab.txt, sam.dat.txt, tax.tab.txt, tree.tre) already in the MiSurv Data folder; go straight to the Data Processing module instead Data are shotgun metagenomic rather than 16S rRNA amplicon reads (the paper maps those to MEGAN/MetaPhlAn, not to this 16S QC step) Only post-read-level quality control is needed, e.g., the library-size/taxonomic-name QC or rarefy_even_depth rarefaction inside the MiSurv Data Processing module http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reconstructs the read-level quality control that the MiSurv authors applied to raw 16S rRNA reads from QIITA study 10508: QIIME 2.0 filtering that retains reads with >75% of the original length and removes reads with more than three consecutive low-quality bases (Phred score <20), as the first stage before OTU picking, RDP taxonomy, and FastTree tree building. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/spectrum.05059-22
skills.summary: Reconstructs the read-level quality control that the MiSurv authors applied to raw 16S rRNA reads from QIITA study 10508: QIIME 2.0 filtering that retains reads with >75% of the original length and removes reads with more than three consecutive low-quality bases (Phred score <20), as the first stage before OTU picking, RDP taxonomy, and FastTree tree building.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already processed data — the phyloseq object biom.Rdata or the four files (otu.tab.txt, sam.dat.txt, tax.tab.txt, tree.tre) already in the MiSurv Data folder; go straight to the Data Processing module instead Data are shotgun metagenomic rather than 16S rRNA amplicon reads (the paper maps those to MEGAN/MetaPhlAn, not to this 16S QC step) Only post-read-level quality control is needed, e.g., the library-size/taxonomic-name QC or rarefy_even_depth rarefaction inside the MiSurv Data Processing module

skills.description: Use when evaluating or reproducing an inference test on one-mismatch children in HashSeq cluster output (OneMismatchCluster.txt, childrenProperties.txt), e.g. to benchmark Poisson-based variant-calling error models.
skills.name: amplicon-sequence-variant-cluster-analysis
skills.search_text: amplicon-sequence-variant-cluster-analysis Use when evaluating or reproducing an inference test on one-mismatch children in HashSeq cluster output (OneMismatchCluster.txt, childrenProperties.txt), e.g. to benchmark Poisson-based variant-calling error models. You want a conservative variant caller for production use — the Poisson test is anticonservative because its equal mean-variance assumption is violated by overdispersion, so it calls nearly all one-mismatch variants as true Your goal is de novo variant calling itself — use HashSeq's inferTrueSequences (normal distribution + LOESS regression) instead of the Poisson-based inference test The data contain true low-abundance variants or two-or-more-mismatch variants — HashSeq/Poisson cluster analysis does not address these cases http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Analyzes HashSeq's parent/one-mismatch children cluster structure by running a one-sided Poisson test per one-mismatch child against the LOESS-estimated background error rate, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, to assess whether the Poisson model can discriminate true one-mismatch variants from sequencing-error artifacts. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Analyzes HashSeq's parent/one-mismatch children cluster structure by running a one-sided Poisson test per one-mismatch child against the LOESS-estimated background error rate, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, to assess whether the Poisson model can discriminate true one-mismatch variants from sequencing-error artifacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want a conservative variant caller for production use — the Poisson test is anticonservative because its equal mean-variance assumption is violated by overdispersion, so it calls nearly all one-mismatch variants as true Your goal is de novo variant calling itself — use HashSeq's inferTrueSequences (normal distribution + LOESS regression) instead of the Poisson-based inference test The data contain true low-abundance variants or two-or-more-mismatch variants — HashSeq/Poisson cluster analysis does not address these cases

skills.description: Use when you have curated 16S rRNA gene sequences (e.g. assembled and intron-stripped) and need to estimate which taxa a specific primer pair would fail to amplify in a cultivation-independent amplicon survey.
skills.name: amplicon-survey-detection-bias-analysis
skills.search_text: amplicon-survey-detection-bias-analysis Use when you have curated 16S rRNA gene sequences (e.g. assembled and intron-stripped) and need to estimate which taxa a specific primer pair would fail to amplify in a cultivation-independent amplicon survey. Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than curated, intron-stripped 16S rRNA gene sequences — insertion sequences (up to 2,004 bp) must be removed first or binding calls will be confounded The question is abundance estimation in amplicon data itself, not detection-bias assessment of primer coverage Sequences do not span the 515-806 E. coli coordinate region — partial sequences cannot support a valid binding call http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Quantifies what fraction of bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequences would fail to bind common amplicon-survey primers (515F/806R), per lineage and overall. This skill reproduces the primer-evasion analysis from Brown et al. 2015, which showed 515F/806R would miss ~50% of Microgenomates and Saccharibacteria, 60% of WWE3, 100% of WS6, and ~20% of all bacteria sampled. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: Quantifies what fraction of bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequences would fail to bind common amplicon-survey primers (515F/806R), per lineage and overall. This skill reproduces the primer-evasion analysis from Brown et al. 2015, which showed 515F/806R would miss ~50% of Microgenomates and Saccharibacteria, 60% of WWE3, 100% of WS6, and ~20% of all bacteria sampled.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than curated, intron-stripped 16S rRNA gene sequences — insertion sequences (up to 2,004 bp) must be removed first or binding calls will be confounded The question is abundance estimation in amplicon data itself, not detection-bias assessment of primer coverage Sequences do not span the 515-806 E. coli coordinate region — partial sequences cannot support a valid binding call

skills.description: Use when you need a simulated paired-end Illumina benchmark with known ground-truth sequences but realistic, experimentally derived per-base error probabilities for validating an assembler.
skills.name: amplicon-template-synthesis
skills.search_text: amplicon-template-synthesis Use when you need a simulated paired-end Illumina benchmark with known ground-truth sequences but realistic, experimentally derived per-base error probabilities for validating an assembler. You need real sequencing data with biological variation — this skill produces a single-template synthetic benchmark, not experimental reads You lack access to real Illumina quality-score profiles, since substituting synthetic quality values would invalidate the error-mask fidelity this method depends on The assembler under test does not consume standard FASTQ paired-end input (forward/reverse files) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Constructs a simulated benchmark of error-free paired-end FASTQ reads by splicing a known amplicon template (e.g., the 135-base Sinorhizobium meliloti 16S V3 region amplified by 341f/518r) onto real Illumina quality-score profiles from a published run (NCBI SRA024100), enabling error-free ground-truth testing of paired-end assemblers like PANDAseq. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Constructs a simulated benchmark of error-free paired-end FASTQ reads by splicing a known amplicon template (e.g., the 135-base Sinorhizobium meliloti 16S V3 region amplified by 341f/518r) onto real Illumina quality-score profiles from a published run (NCBI SRA024100), enabling error-free ground-truth testing of paired-end assemblers like PANDAseq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need real sequencing data with biological variation — this skill produces a single-template synthetic benchmark, not experimental reads You lack access to real Illumina quality-score profiles, since substituting synthetic quality values would invalidate the error-mask fidelity this method depends on The assembler under test does not consume standard FASTQ paired-end input (forward/reverse files)

skills.description: Use when raw pre-processed 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (e.g., PRJEB24409 mock communities with primers removed, reads paired, trimmed to 250 bases) must be converted into a filtered variant count table for downstream analyses.
skills.name: amplicon-variant-count-table-processing
skills.search_text: amplicon-variant-count-table-processing Use when raw pre-processed 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (e.g., PRJEB24409 mock communities with primers removed, reads paired, trimmed to 250 bases) must be converted into a filtered variant count table for downstream analyses. The goal is to detect true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq is conservative and not sensitive for low-abundance sequences; the article recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 Variants with two or more mismatches, indel variation relative to a parent, or long-read data such as PacBio are of interest — HashSeq considers only one-mismatch children and does not explicitly model indels Input is already a filtered count/feature table (e.g., an existing SvTable.txt); re-running variant calling would be redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Process 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing data into filtered sequence-variant count tables by calling variants with HashSeq's inferTrueSequences (HashMap-based clustering plus normal-distribution/LOESS error modeling) and removing variants below an abundance threshold (1,000 reads total; 10,000 for the largest data set), yielding SvTable.txt/sequences.fasta suitable for downstream BLAST identity checks and supervised classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Process 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing data into filtered sequence-variant count tables by calling variants with HashSeq's inferTrueSequences (HashMap-based clustering plus normal-distribution/LOESS error modeling) and removing variants below an abundance threshold (1,000 reads total; 10,000 for the largest data set), yielding SvTable.txt/sequences.fasta suitable for downstream BLAST identity checks and supervised classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to detect true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq is conservative and not sensitive for low-abundance sequences; the article recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 Variants with two or more mismatches, indel variation relative to a parent, or long-read data such as PacBio are of interest — HashSeq considers only one-mismatch children and does not explicitly model indels Input is already a filtered count/feature table (e.g., an existing SvTable.txt); re-running variant calling would be redundant

skills.description: Use when predicting bacterial phenotypes from Pfam presence/absence profiles and you want to incorporate horizontal gene transfer by augmenting phyletic patterns with ancestral gains/losses inferred on the species tree.
skills.name: ancestral-character-state-inference
skills.search_text: ancestral-character-state-inference Use when predicting bacterial phenotypes from Pfam presence/absence profiles and you want to incorporate horizontal gene transfer by augmenting phyletic patterns with ancestral gains/losses inferred on the species tree. Input is already a trained model or a phenotype prediction table — ancestral-state inference is a training-time feature-construction step, not needed for applying phypat+PGL to new genomes. No species phylogeny is available or the genome set is too small for meaningful ancestral reconstruction — fall back to the phypat phyletic-pattern-only classifier. The goal is exploratory phenotyping of incomplete genomes, where the article notes phypat assigns more phenotypes (at the price of more false positives) and may be preferable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Maximum-likelihood inference of ancestral protein family gains and losses on a species phylogeny, used by Traitar's phypat+PGL classifier to account for horizontal gene transfer when predicting bacterial phenotypes. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00101-16
skills.summary: Maximum-likelihood inference of ancestral protein family gains and losses on a species phylogeny, used by Traitar's phypat+PGL classifier to account for horizontal gene transfer when predicting bacterial phenotypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a trained model or a phenotype prediction table — ancestral-state inference is a training-time feature-construction step, not needed for applying phypat+PGL to new genomes. No species phylogeny is available or the genome set is too small for meaningful ancestral reconstruction — fall back to the phypat phyletic-pattern-only classifier. The goal is exploratory phenotyping of incomplete genomes, where the article notes phypat assigns more phenotypes (at the price of more false positives) and may be preferable.

skills.description: Use when you must infer gene content (e.g. KO/COG abundances, 16S copy number) for organisms without sequenced reference genomes from a 16S phylogenetic tree plus a gene-by-genome annotation table, as required to build PICRUSt reference files.
skills.name: ancestral-state-reconstruction-gene-content
skills.search_text: ancestral-state-reconstruction-gene-content Use when you must infer gene content (e.g. KO/COG abundances, 16S copy number) for organisms without sequenced reference genomes from a 16S phylogenetic tree plus a gene-by-genome annotation table, as required to build PICRUSt reference files. The input is already shotgun metagenome data annotated to KOs (e.g. via HUMAnN) — no gene content prediction is needed; this step is only for marker-gene-only samples. The marker gene tree lacks tips with known reference genome gene content, so ancestral states cannot be anchored by extant genomes. The trait of interest is dominated by lateral gene transfer (e.g. some environmental information processing genes), where prediction will be poor with broad confidence intervals. http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Predicts gene family content (KO/COG) and 16S copy number for every tip of a marker-gene (Greengenes 16S) reference tree by applying ancestral state reconstruction (APE ACE ML/REML/PIC or COUNT Wagner Parsimony) to IMG-derived gene-by-genome annotations and averaging extant plus ancestral genomes weighted exponentially by the reciprocal of phylogenetic distance. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Predicts gene family content (KO/COG) and 16S copy number for every tip of a marker-gene (Greengenes 16S) reference tree by applying ancestral state reconstruction (APE ACE ML/REML/PIC or COUNT Wagner Parsimony) to IMG-derived gene-by-genome annotations and averaging extant plus ancestral genomes weighted exponentially by the reciprocal of phylogenetic distance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already shotgun metagenome data annotated to KOs (e.g. via HUMAnN) — no gene content prediction is needed; this step is only for marker-gene-only samples. The marker gene tree lacks tips with known reference genome gene content, so ancestral states cannot be anchored by extant genomes. The trait of interest is dominated by lateral gene transfer (e.g. some environmental information processing genes), where prediction will be poor with broad confidence intervals.

skills.description: Use when constructing a de novo source-associated genome database (sourceapp_build.py) where redundant reference genomes and MAGs must be collapsed to 95% ANI species representatives per fecal source category before metagenomic source tracking.
skills.name: ani-based-genome-dereplication
skills.search_text: ani-based-genome-dereplication Use when constructing a de novo source-associated genome database (sourceapp_build.py) where redundant reference genomes and MAGs must be collapsed to 95% ANI species representatives per fecal source category before metagenomic source tracking. Input is raw shotgun FASTQ reads or assemblies rather than curated genome FASTA files — this dereplication operates on genomes, not reads Strain-level source discrimination is required — 95% ANI collapses strains into species representatives, and ≥95% ANI species shared between source categories are explicitly not resolvable (cross-reactive) Genomes have not passed the aggregate quality cutoff of 50 (completeness − 5 × redundancy) — low-quality MAGs are discarded upstream and would distort clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Dereplicates source-associated genome databases at 95% ANI so each fecal source category (e.g., cow, pig, dog, cat, chicken, goat, sewage, septage) is represented by species-cluster representative genomes, with cross-category pairs at ANI ≥ 95% flagged as cross-reactive for SourceApp metagenomic source tracking. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: Dereplicates source-associated genome databases at 95% ANI so each fecal source category (e.g., cow, pig, dog, cat, chicken, goat, sewage, septage) is represented by species-cluster representative genomes, with cross-category pairs at ANI ≥ 95% flagged as cross-reactive for SourceApp metagenomic source tracking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw shotgun FASTQ reads or assemblies rather than curated genome FASTA files — this dereplication operates on genomes, not reads Strain-level source discrimination is required — 95% ANI collapses strains into species representatives, and ≥95% ANI species shared between source categories are explicitly not resolvable (cross-reactive) Genomes have not passed the aggregate quality cutoff of 50 (completeness − 5 × redundancy) — low-quality MAGs are discarded upstream and would distort clustering

skills.description: Use when a MAG-level taxonomy classifier (e.g. kMetaShot) assigns MAGs only to a species/genus because the corresponding mock-community or reference genomes lack strain annotation, and strain-level resolution is required for benchmarking.
skills.name: ani-based-strain-refinement
skills.search_text: ani-based-strain-refinement Use when a MAG-level taxonomy classifier (e.g. kMetaShot) assigns MAGs only to a species/genus because the corresponding mock-community or reference genomes lack strain annotation, and strain-level resolution is required for benchmarking. When the classifier already resolved strain-level labels for the MAG (no unlabelled genomes to refine) When candidate genomes share ANI <97%, below the strain-delineation threshold used in the article — assignment would be unreliable When the goal is genus- or species-level benchmarking only, where strain refinement is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Refines strain-level taxonomic assignments of MAGs by comparing them against all RefSeq genomes of observed strains with Mash ANI, assigning each unlabelled MAG to the strain with the highest ANI (≥97%). This resolves cases where the classifier cannot distinguish closely related strains lacking reference strain annotation. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: Refines strain-level taxonomic assignments of MAGs by comparing them against all RefSeq genomes of observed strains with Mash ANI, assigning each unlabelled MAG to the strain with the highest ANI (≥97%). This resolves cases where the classifier cannot distinguish closely related strains lacking reference strain annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the classifier already resolved strain-level labels for the MAG (no unlabelled genomes to refine) When candidate genomes share ANI <97%, below the strain-delineation threshold used in the article — assignment would be unreliable When the goal is genus- or species-level benchmarking only, where strain refinement is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when the goal is to decide, from metagenomic read mappings to a set of sub-species genomes, which strains are shared between samples, and to compare strain-sharing calls across ANI thresholds (e.g., 99.999% strain clustering vs. 98% dereplication).
skills.name: ani-threshold-strain-sharing-analysis
skills.search_text: ani-threshold-strain-sharing-analysis Use when the goal is to decide, from metagenomic read mappings to a set of sub-species genomes, which strains are shared between samples, and to compare strain-sharing calls across ANI thresholds (e.g., 99.999% strain clustering vs. 98% dereplication). Input is only assemblies/reference genomes with no sample read mappings — ANI dereplication alone (dRep, FastANI) suffices and popANI read-based microdiversity comparisons are not possible The question is within-sample microdiversity, SNV calling, or linkage rather than between-sample strain sharing Species-level presence/absence profiling is the goal, and strain-level (99.999% ANI) resolution is not required http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Determines which microbial strains are shared between samples by mapping reads to sub-species genome sets, computing microdiversity-aware popANI comparisons with inStrain, clustering subspecies into strains at a 99.999% ANI threshold, and benchmarking the shared-genome counts against ANI-based tools (dRep, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Determines which microbial strains are shared between samples by mapping reads to sub-species genome sets, computing microdiversity-aware popANI comparisons with inStrain, clustering subspecies into strains at a 99.999% ANI threshold, and benchmarking the shared-genome counts against ANI-based tools (dRep, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only assemblies/reference genomes with no sample read mappings — ANI dereplication alone (dRep, FastANI) suffices and popANI read-based microdiversity comparisons are not possible The question is within-sample microdiversity, SNV calling, or linkage rather than between-sample strain sharing Species-level presence/absence profiling is the goal, and strain-level (99.999% ANI) resolution is not required

skills.description: Use when you have raw per-read annotation output files from MG-RAST (or DIAMOND) and need to condense them into abundance summary tables of organism or functional hits before statistical comparison.
skills.name: annotation-abundance-counting
skills.search_text: annotation-abundance-counting Use when you have raw per-read annotation output files from MG-RAST (or DIAMOND) and need to condense them into abundance summary tables of organism or functional hits before statistical comparison. Annotation has not yet been performed - files must first be submitted to and returned by the MG-RAST server (or annotated locally with DIAMOND in SAMSA2); counting cannot precede annotation Input is already a condensed summary table (e.g. output of RefSeq_output_reducer.py or func_data_trimmer.py); re-counting would only duplicate existing tallies You need p-values or log2FoldChange scores for differential expression - that is the separate R/DESeq2 analysis step (R_organism_script.Rmd, R_functional_script_w-md5s.Rmd), not the aggregation counting step http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Aggregation-phase skill from the SAMSA pipeline: parse per-read MG-RAST annotation results line by line, tally occurrences of each unique annotation in a dictionary, and export a sorted, tab-delimited abundance summary for downstream DESeq2 analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1270-8
skills.summary: Aggregation-phase skill from the SAMSA pipeline: parse per-read MG-RAST annotation results line by line, tally occurrences of each unique annotation in a dictionary, and export a sorted, tab-delimited abundance summary for downstream DESeq2 analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Annotation has not yet been performed - files must first be submitted to and returned by the MG-RAST server (or annotated locally with DIAMOND in SAMSA2); counting cannot precede annotation Input is already a condensed summary table (e.g. output of RefSeq_output_reducer.py or func_data_trimmer.py); re-counting would only duplicate existing tallies You need p-values or log2FoldChange scores for differential expression - that is the separate R/DESeq2 analysis step (R_organism_script.Rmd, R_functional_script_w-md5s.Rmd), not the aggregation counting step

skills.description: Use when you have protein-coding genes predicted on viral contigs and need per-gene functional hits from multiple databases (EggNOG5, VOGDB) plus auxiliary metabolic gene (AMG) calls merged into one tabular annotation table.
skills.name: annotation-table-integration
skills.search_text: annotation-table-integration Use when you have protein-coding genes predicted on viral contigs and need per-gene functional hits from multiple databases (EggNOG5, VOGDB) plus auxiliary metabolic gene (AMG) calls merged into one tabular annotation table. When the goal is viral taxonomic classification or host prediction rather than gene-level functional annotation — ViroProfiler's annotation step targets gene products, not taxonomy. When the input sequences are not viral (e.g., whole microbial metagenome bins) — DRAM-v is applied here specifically to distill AMG calls for viral contigs. When samples contain excessive environmental contamination, since the article notes this could increase the pipeline running time and result in lower precision. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 ViroProfiler's functional-annotation integration skill: merge eggNOG-mapper, VOGDB, and DRAM-v outputs into a single gene-by-annotation table with an AMG flag, after building a non-redundant gene catalog from viral contigs. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: ViroProfiler's functional-annotation integration skill: merge eggNOG-mapper, VOGDB, and DRAM-v outputs into a single gene-by-annotation table with an AMG flag, after building a non-redundant gene catalog from viral contigs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is viral taxonomic classification or host prediction rather than gene-level functional annotation — ViroProfiler's annotation step targets gene products, not taxonomy. When the input sequences are not viral (e.g., whole microbial metagenome bins) — DRAM-v is applied here specifically to distill AMG calls for viral contigs. When samples contain excessive environmental contamination, since the article notes this could increase the pipeline running time and result in lower precision.

skills.description: Use when many co-occurrence networks have been generated from all tool/parameter combinations of a multi-step 16S pipeline and you must quantify which pipeline step contributes most to network-to-network variation.
skills.name: anova-variance-partitioning
skills.search_text: anova-variance-partitioning Use when many co-occurrence networks have been generated from all tool/parameter combinations of a multi-step 16S pipeline and you must quantify which pipeline step contributes most to network-to-network variation. Input is raw 16S sequencing reads or a single abundance table — the networks must already be inferred; use the MiCoNE processing pipeline (micone init / run.sh) first The goal is to compare individual tools' agreement with mock/synthetic ground truth rather than to attribute network variance to pipeline steps Networks were produced with heterogeneous thresholds (not the paper's interaction_threshold = 0.3 and pvalue_threshold = 0.05), so step effects would be confounded with threshold effects http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Attributes the total variation among inferred microbial co-occurrence networks to the MiCoNE pipeline steps (DC, CC, TA, OP, NI) by combining PCA of flattened adjacency matrices with linear regression and ANOVA, revealing which pipeline step (e.g. taxonomy assignment, 65.4%) dominates network variance. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: Attributes the total variation among inferred microbial co-occurrence networks to the MiCoNE pipeline steps (DC, CC, TA, OP, NI) by combining PCA of flattened adjacency matrices with linear regression and ANOVA, revealing which pipeline step (e.g. taxonomy assignment, 65.4%) dominates network variance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw 16S sequencing reads or a single abundance table — the networks must already be inferred; use the MiCoNE processing pipeline (micone init / run.sh) first The goal is to compare individual tools' agreement with mock/synthetic ground truth rather than to attribute network variance to pipeline steps Networks were produced with heterogeneous thresholds (not the paper's interaction_threshold = 0.3 and pvalue_threshold = 0.05), so step effects would be confounded with threshold effects

skills.description: Use when you need to detect shared informative variants across a population of shotgun metagenomic samples aligned to a reference gene database (e.g., antibiotic resistance genes), and want to separate shared polymorphic sites from background noise.
skills.name: antibiotic-resistance-gene-variant-detection
skills.search_text: antibiotic-resistance-gene-variant-detection Use when you need to detect shared informative variants across a population of shotgun metagenomic samples aligned to a reference gene database (e.g., antibiotic resistance genes), and want to separate shared polymorphic sites from background noise. Input is single-cell mitochondrial data rather than shotgun metagenomic samples — MQuad (the parent tool) is tailored for that setting, not this one. The goal is calling variants within a single sample rather than shared informative variants across a population of samples (minSample filtering requires multiple samples). Reads cannot be aligned to a reference gene database (e.g., no suitable ARG reference), since the pipeline starts from bwa/bowtie2 alignment to a reference. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A pipeline for detecting shared informative variants across antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in shotgun metagenomic samples, using cellsnp-lite pileup followed by MetaQuad's density-based BIC clustering. Applied to 121 H. pylori eradication therapy samples, it recovered 7591 informative variants across 529 ARGs in about 60 minutes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: A pipeline for detecting shared informative variants across antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in shotgun metagenomic samples, using cellsnp-lite pileup followed by MetaQuad's density-based BIC clustering. Applied to 121 H. pylori eradication therapy samples, it recovered 7591 informative variants across 529 ARGs in about 60 minutes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell mitochondrial data rather than shotgun metagenomic samples — MQuad (the parent tool) is tailored for that setting, not this one. The goal is calling variants within a single sample rather than shared informative variants across a population of samples (minSample filtering requires multiple samples). Reads cannot be aligned to a reference gene database (e.g., no suitable ARG reference), since the pipeline starts from bwa/bowtie2 alignment to a reference.

skills.description: Use when merging several existing antimicrobial resistance (or biocide/metal resistance) gene catalogs into one non-redundant curated database, and you need reproducible filtering, deduplication, and centroid counts.
skills.name: antimicrobial-resistance-gene-database-curation
skills.search_text: antimicrobial-resistance-gene-database-curation Use when merging several existing antimicrobial resistance (or biocide/metal resistance) gene catalogs into one non-redundant curated database, and you need reproducible filtering, deduplication, and centroid counts. You already have a curated, non-redundant ARG database and only need to profile reads against it — use ARGprofiler's KMA-based abundance profiling instead of re-curating. You need to process long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data. You need a single-source database specific to one scope — PanRes combines sources with different scopes, and which subsets are appropriate depends on the individual research question. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Build a combined ARG reference database (like PanRes) by downloading multiple source gene collections (ResFinder, ResFinderFG v2.0, CARD v3.2.5, MegaRes v3.0.0, AMRFinderPlus, ARGANNOT, MetalResistance), applying source-specific inclusion filters, deduplicating with Usearch fastx_uniques, and homology-reducing with Usearch cluster_fast at 90% identity and 90% coverage. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Build a combined ARG reference database (like PanRes) by downloading multiple source gene collections (ResFinder, ResFinderFG v2.0, CARD v3.2.5, MegaRes v3.0.0, AMRFinderPlus, ARGANNOT, MetalResistance), applying source-specific inclusion filters, deduplicating with Usearch fastx_uniques, and homology-reducing with Usearch cluster_fast at 90% identity and 90% coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a curated, non-redundant ARG database and only need to profile reads against it — use ARGprofiler's KMA-based abundance profiling instead of re-curating. You need to process long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data. You need a single-source database specific to one scope — PanRes combines sources with different scopes, and which subsets are appropriate depends on the individual research question.

skills.description: Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ data must yield assembled genomic context (100–5000 bp flanks) around ARGs, but full metagenomic de novo assembly is computationally prohibitive or unnecessary.
skills.name: antimicrobial-resistance-gene-flank-reconstruction
skills.search_text: antimicrobial-resistance-gene-flank-reconstruction Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ data must yield assembled genomic context (100–5000 bp flanks) around ARGs, but full metagenomic de novo assembly is computationally prohibitive or unnecessary. Input is long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler is designed to only work with short-read data No target ARGs are detected by the KMA pre-screen (filters not met: >90% query identity, >90% global consensus identity, mean depth >6) — assembly is skipped to avoid expense A full, unbiased metagenomic assembly is required rather than targeted assembly around known ARG references http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs genomic flanking regions around antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) from metagenomic short reads via iterative targeted de novo assembly (ARGextender: KMA read recruitment + SPAdes assembly), avoiding the cost of full metagenomic assembly. Implemented within the Snakemake-based ARGprofiler pipeline with the PanRes database of 14,078 unique ARGs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Reconstructs genomic flanking regions around antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) from metagenomic short reads via iterative targeted de novo assembly (ARGextender: KMA read recruitment + SPAdes assembly), avoiding the cost of full metagenomic assembly. Implemented within the Snakemake-based ARGprofiler pipeline with the PanRes database of 14,078 unique ARGs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler is designed to only work with short-read data No target ARGs are detected by the KMA pre-screen (filters not met: >90% query identity, >90% global consensus identity, mean depth >6) — assembly is skipped to avoid expense A full, unbiased metagenomic assembly is required rather than targeted assembly around known ARG references

skills.description: Use when raw reads (Illumina MiSeq/HiSeq or ONT MinION FASTQ) from S. aureus or M. tuberculosis isolates need antibiotic-resistance calls across a drug panel, without assembly or phenotype testing.
skills.name: antimicrobial-resistance-prediction
skills.search_text: antimicrobial-resistance-prediction Use when raw reads (Illumina MiSeq/HiSeq or ONT MinION FASTQ) from S. aureus or M. tuberculosis isolates need antibiotic-resistance calls across a drug panel, without assembly or phenotype testing. Species or resistance mechanisms are poorly characterized outside S. aureus, M. tuberculosis, Shigella, or Salmonella — large training sets with WGS and phenotype data are required to build panels You need pyrazinamide resistance prediction in M. tuberculosis — known mutations are poorly predictive and the drug is excluded You require direct-from-sputum M. tuberculosis mixture analysis — the current model only handles major/minor clones, not a general mixture model http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Predict antibiotic resistance directly from raw bacterial sequence data using Mykrobe predictor's de Bruijn graph genotype caller, which maps known resistance-causing mutations and presence/absence genes against panels for S. aureus and M. tuberculosis and emits clinician-friendly resistance calls within ~3 minutes. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Predict antibiotic resistance directly from raw bacterial sequence data using Mykrobe predictor's de Bruijn graph genotype caller, which maps known resistance-causing mutations and presence/absence genes against panels for S. aureus and M. tuberculosis and emits clinician-friendly resistance calls within ~3 minutes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Species or resistance mechanisms are poorly characterized outside S. aureus, M. tuberculosis, Shigella, or Salmonella — large training sets with WGS and phenotype data are required to build panels You need pyrazinamide resistance prediction in M. tuberculosis — known mutations are poorly predictive and the drug is excluded You require direct-from-sputum M. tuberculosis mixture analysis — the current model only handles major/minor clones, not a general mixture model

skills.description: Use when comparing an Approximate Membership Query data structure (e.g., a counting Bloom filter) against its fimpera-wrapped version on abundance queries, to quantify false-positive rate, overestimation score, space, and query time.
skills.name: approximate-membership-query-benchmarking
skills.search_text: approximate-membership-query-benchmarking Use when comparing an Approximate Membership Query data structure (e.g., a counting Bloom filter) against its fimpera-wrapped version on abundance queries, to quantify false-positive rate, overestimation score, space, and query time. The data structure is a plain AMQ without counts (no abundance support), since fimpera requires abundance queries. The goal is only presence/absence indexing without abundance information — fimpera's benchmarking here targets counting structures for k-mer abundances. Index scale exceeds available memory even after fimpera's 100x reduction and petabyte-scaled k-mer indexing with abundance is required, as no existing method scales to that. Benchmark fimpera-wrapped counting Bloom filters against raw cBFs by measuring false-positive/overestimation scores (sum-of-squared overestimation errors) and space trade-offs, and query time as z increases. Demonstrates that fimpera achieves equal precision at two orders of magnitude less filter size with no query-time penalty. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad305
skills.summary: Benchmark fimpera-wrapped counting Bloom filters against raw cBFs by measuring false-positive/overestimation scores (sum-of-squared overestimation errors) and space trade-offs, and query time as z increases. Demonstrates that fimpera achieves equal precision at two orders of magnitude less filter size with no query-time penalty.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data structure is a plain AMQ without counts (no abundance support), since fimpera requires abundance queries. The goal is only presence/absence indexing without abundance information — fimpera's benchmarking here targets counting structures for k-mer abundances. Index scale exceeds available memory even after fimpera's 100x reduction and petabyte-scaled k-mer indexing with abundance is required, as no existing method scales to that.

skills.description: Use when building an approximate membership query index over k-mer abundances where false positive k-mer calls or overestimated abundances must be reduced without memory overhead.
skills.name: approximate-membership-query-false-positive-handling
skills.search_text: approximate-membership-query-false-positive-handling Use when building an approximate membership query index over k-mer abundances where false positive k-mer calls or overestimated abundances must be reduced without memory overhead. The application only needs presence/absence of k-mers, not abundances — fimpera targets cAMQs that support abundance queries The dataset is too small to be affected by AMQ false positives, where the added z-window averaging machinery is unnecessary A non-counting AMQ (plain Bloom filter without abundance support) is the only available structure, since fimpera requires abundance queries http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 fimpera-style s-mer indexing reduces false positives (and abundance overestimations) of counting AMQs such as counting Bloom filters by splitting each indexed k-mer into its k−s+1 constituent s-mers and requiring all s-mer queries to succeed before a k-mer is called present. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad305
skills.summary: fimpera-style s-mer indexing reduces false positives (and abundance overestimations) of counting AMQs such as counting Bloom filters by splitting each indexed k-mer into its k−s+1 constituent s-mers and requiring all s-mer queries to succeed before a k-mer is called present.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The application only needs presence/absence of k-mers, not abundances — fimpera targets cAMQs that support abundance queries The dataset is too small to be affected by AMQ false positives, where the added z-window averaging machinery is unnecessary A non-counting AMQ (plain Bloom filter without abundance support) is the only available structure, since fimpera requires abundance queries

skills.description: Use when you have SynTracker's raw synteny_scores_per_region.csv output and need APSS values per pair of samples or genomes, with subsampled or all-region aggregation for comparisons or cutoff-based strain designation (e.g., APSS 0.95).
skills.name: apss-aggregation-and-subsampling
skills.search_text: apss-aggregation-and-subsampling Use when you have SynTracker's raw synteny_scores_per_region.csv output and need APSS values per pair of samples or genomes, with subsampled or all-region aggregation for comparisons or cutoff-based strain designation (e.g., APSS 0.95). When the goal is SNP-sensitive strain discrimination — the article shows SynTracker/APSS has low sensitivity to SNPs (minimal APSS ~0.981–0.995 for SNP-only simulations vs ~0.103–0.206 for indel-only), so combine it with an SNP-based tool like MIDAS or StrainPhlAn instead of relying on APSS alone. When sample pairs have fewer than n available homologous regions — such pairs are excluded from downstream analysis, so APSS with large N is inappropriate for sparse or highly divergent comparisons. When you need a universal same/different strain threshold — the APSS 0.95 cutoff is subjective, species-dependent, and may not be optimal for all settings. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aggregates SynTracker's per-region pairwise synteny scores into Average Pairwise Synteny Scores (APSS) via random subsampling of n regions per sample pair (default N = 40, 60, 80, 100, 200, or all regions), producing the avg_synteny_scores CSV outputs used for strain relatedness and benchmarking. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Aggregates SynTracker's per-region pairwise synteny scores into Average Pairwise Synteny Scores (APSS) via random subsampling of n regions per sample pair (default N = 40, 60, 80, 100, 200, or all regions), producing the avg_synteny_scores CSV outputs used for strain relatedness and benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is SNP-sensitive strain discrimination — the article shows SynTracker/APSS has low sensitivity to SNPs (minimal APSS ~0.981–0.995 for SNP-only simulations vs ~0.103–0.206 for indel-only), so combine it with an SNP-based tool like MIDAS or StrainPhlAn instead of relying on APSS alone. When sample pairs have fewer than n available homologous regions — such pairs are excluded from downstream analysis, so APSS with large N is inappropriate for sparse or highly divergent comparisons. When you need a universal same/different strain threshold — the APSS 0.95 cutoff is subjective, species-dependent, and may not be optimal for all settings.

skills.description: Use when you need to isolate the contribution of individual model pathways (CNN vs transformer vs input tokenization) by training variant architectures on the same data/schedule and comparing species-level top-1 accuracy and F1.
skills.name: architectural-ablation-model-training
skills.search_text: architectural-ablation-model-training Use when you need to isolate the contribution of individual model pathways (CNN vs transformer vs input tokenization) by training variant architectures on the same data/schedule and comparing species-level top-1 accuracy and F1. Your goal is the best possible species classification accuracy rather than attribution — use the full HybridCNNBERT model or the 5-seed soft-vote ensemble instead of ablation variants You changed more than one variable (data, split, epochs, seed) relative to the full-model run — F1 deltas would no longer isolate the architectural effect You need classification of non-16S marker genes (e.g., 18S rRNA or shotgun metagenomic data) — DeepTaxa was trained and evaluated primarily on Greengenes2 16S rRNA http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Trains architectural ablation variants of DeepTaxa (CNN-only, BERT-only, one-hot CNN) alongside the full HybridCNNBERT model under the identical compact hyperparameter configuration on Greengenes2 2024.09, to quantify each pathway's contribution to species-level F1. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Trains architectural ablation variants of DeepTaxa (CNN-only, BERT-only, one-hot CNN) alongside the full HybridCNNBERT model under the identical compact hyperparameter configuration on Greengenes2 2024.09, to quantify each pathway's contribution to species-level F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is the best possible species classification accuracy rather than attribution — use the full HybridCNNBERT model or the 5-seed soft-vote ensemble instead of ablation variants You changed more than one variable (data, split, epochs, seed) relative to the full-model run — F1 deltas would no longer isolate the architectural effect You need classification of non-16S marker genes (e.g., 18S rRNA or shotgun metagenomic data) — DeepTaxa was trained and evaluated primarily on Greengenes2 16S rRNA

skills.description: Use when choosing among candidate DNN architectures for classifying short metagenomic sequencing reads and you need head-to-head read-level precision/recall on held-out genomes to justify the selection.
skills.name: architecture-variant-benchmarking
skills.search_text: architecture-variant-benchmarking Use when choosing among candidate DNN architectures for classifying short metagenomic sequencing reads and you need head-to-head read-level precision/recall on held-out genomes to justify the selection. The task is abundance estimation or genus-level profiling of mock communities rather than architecture selection by read-level precision/recall Reads have lengths and error profiles strongly different from the training data (e.g. long-read sequencing), where retraining is required and benchmarked short-read architectures may not transfer Reference database curation output (e.g. incorporating new MAGs into Kraken/Kaiju databases) is the goal rather than training and comparing neural architectures http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark multiple deep neural network architectures (one-hot CNN, hybrid, seq2species, embedding baseline, LSTM, and self-attention variants) on identical training and held-out test reads to select the best architecture for a sequence-classification task, as done for DeepMicrobes species-level metagenomic read classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple deep neural network architectures (one-hot CNN, hybrid, seq2species, embedding baseline, LSTM, and self-attention variants) on identical training and held-out test reads to select the best architecture for a sequence-classification task, as done for DeepMicrobes species-level metagenomic read classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is abundance estimation or genus-level profiling of mock communities rather than architecture selection by read-level precision/recall Reads have lengths and error profiles strongly different from the training data (e.g. long-read sequencing), where retraining is required and benchmarked short-read architectures may not transfer Reference database curation output (e.g. incorporating new MAGs into Kraken/Kaiju databases) is the goal rather than training and comparing neural architectures

skills.description: Use when you have assembled scaffolds (targeted ARGextender or full SPAdes) from metagenomic reads and need to identify which ARG database sequences are present and count ARG-scaffolds per sample.
skills.name: arg-scaffold-matching-with-kma
skills.search_text: arg-scaffold-matching-with-kma Use when you have assembled scaffolds (targeted ARGextender or full SPAdes) from metagenomic reads and need to identify which ARG database sequences are present and count ARG-scaffolds per sample. Input is raw reads rather than assemblies — ARGextender's KMA-based read recruitment stage, not scaffold matching, is the right entry point Data are long reads — ARGprofiler/ARGextender is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data The target gene family is not ARGs and the database has different scope — note PanRes combines sources of different scope, so subset appropriateness must be judged per research question http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 Match ARG reference sequences (ResFinder/PanRes) against targeted ARGextender scaffolds or full SPAdes assemblies using KMA 1.4.12a, enabling per-sample counting of ARG-containing scaffolds and distinct ARGs detected. This is the comparison step that lets ARGextender's targeted de novo assembly be benchmarked against full metagenomic assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Match ARG reference sequences (ResFinder/PanRes) against targeted ARGextender scaffolds or full SPAdes assemblies using KMA 1.4.12a, enabling per-sample counting of ARG-containing scaffolds and distinct ARGs detected. This is the comparison step that lets ARGextender's targeted de novo assembly be benchmarked against full metagenomic assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than assemblies — ARGextender's KMA-based read recruitment stage, not scaffold matching, is the right entry point Data are long reads — ARGprofiler/ARGextender is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data The target gene family is not ARGs and the database has different scope — note PanRes combines sources of different scope, so subset appropriateness must be judged per research question

skills.description: Use when classifying MAGs with kMetaShot and you need to discard unreliable strain- or species-level assignments: apply the -a/ass2ref filter to the classifier output so only classifications whose minimizer support meets the ratio threshold are retained.
skills.name: ass2ref-confidence-filtering
skills.search_text: ass2ref-confidence-filtering Use when classifying MAGs with kMetaShot and you need to discard unreliable strain- or species-level assignments: apply the -a/ass2ref filter to the classifier output so only classifications whose minimizer support meets the ratio threshold are retained. You are using a marker-gene/alignment classifier such as GTDBtk or CAMITAX, which rely on marker gene identification and sequence alignments rather than minimizer ratios You need classifications of MAGs against a custom reference not represented in the kMetaShot prokaryotic RefSeq reference, since ass2ref is defined against the assigned strain's reference minimizers http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Apply kMetaShot's ass2ref ratio — the ratio between the observed MAG minimizers and the reference minimizers of the assigned strain — as a reliability measure to drop out unreliable strain/species classifications, typically with a threshold of 0.2. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: Apply kMetaShot's ass2ref ratio — the ratio between the observed MAG minimizers and the reference minimizers of the assigned strain — as a reliability measure to drop out unreliable strain/species classifications, typically with a threshold of 0.2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are using a marker-gene/alignment classifier such as GTDBtk or CAMITAX, which rely on marker gene identification and sequence alignments rather than minimizer ratios You need classifications of MAGs against a custom reference not represented in the kMetaShot prokaryotic RefSeq reference, since ass2ref is defined against the assigned strain's reference minimizers

skills.description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking a short-read de novo assembler against published baselines on the Assemblathon1 dataset, or when reproducing reported N50 and error-rate reductions (e.g. 90.12% structural error reduction).
skills.name: assemblathon-benchmark-assembly
skills.search_text: assemblathon-benchmark-assembly Use when evaluating or benchmarking a short-read de novo assembler against published baselines on the Assemblathon1 dataset, or when reproducing reported N50 and error-rate reductions (e.g. 90.12% structural error reduction). Input is single-cell or metagenomic data — the README directs such data to MEGAHIT, which 'generates longer contigs and consumes less memory', with SOAPdenovo-fusion for scaffolding The goal is scaffolding contigs from another assembler rather than whole-pipeline assembly comparison — use SOAPdenovo-fusion (map/scaff) instead of the full benchmark workflow The genome/experiment requires k-mers above 63 (or below 13) — SOAPdenovo2's -K option accepts kmers only between 13 and 63/127 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A benchmarking workflow that reproduces the SOAPdenovo2 vs SOAPdenovo1/1.05 (and ALLPATHS-LG) comparison on the Assemblathon1 simulated-read dataset, quantifying scaffold N50 continuity and structural, substitution, and copy-number error rates. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: A benchmarking workflow that reproduces the SOAPdenovo2 vs SOAPdenovo1/1.05 (and ALLPATHS-LG) comparison on the Assemblathon1 simulated-read dataset, quantifying scaffold N50 continuity and structural, substitution, and copy-number error rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell or metagenomic data — the README directs such data to MEGAHIT, which 'generates longer contigs and consumes less memory', with SOAPdenovo-fusion for scaffolding The goal is scaffolding contigs from another assembler rather than whole-pipeline assembly comparison — use SOAPdenovo-fusion (map/scaff) instead of the full benchmark workflow The genome/experiment requires k-mers above 63 (or below 13) — SOAPdenovo2's -K option accepts kmers only between 13 and 63/127

skills.description: Use when input is long reads or already-assembled contigs to supply via -A, or when short reads must be assembled by SPAdes, metaSPAdes, or MEGAHIT with the assembly chosen by N50.
skills.name: assembled-contig-fasta-handling
skills.search_text: assembled-contig-fasta-handling Use when input is long reads or already-assembled contigs to supply via -A, or when short reads must be assembled by SPAdes, metaSPAdes, or MEGAHIT with the assembly chosen by N50. Input is raw short reads and you want virMine's own read QC followed by assembly — supply them with -p/-s instead of importing a contig FASTA via -A. The FASTA is a protein reference database (viral_aa.fasta or nonviral_aa.fasta) — these are scoring inputs via -v/-nv, not contig assemblies to handle with -A. The task is long-read assembly/polishing itself — virMine accepts supplied long-read/contig files but delegates assembly of short reads to SPAdes/metaSPAdes/MEGAHIT; it does not assemble long reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Handling assembled contig FASTA within virMine 2.0: either supplying pre-assembled contigs/long reads via the -A option, or generating contigs from short reads using one of the three bundled assemblers (SPAdes 3.15.3, metaSPAdes, MEGAHIT) and carrying the greatest-N50 assembly into downstream gene prediction and viral scoring. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/mra.00107-22
skills.summary: Handling assembled contig FASTA within virMine 2.0: either supplying pre-assembled contigs/long reads via the -A option, or generating contigs from short reads using one of the three bundled assemblers (SPAdes 3.15.3, metaSPAdes, MEGAHIT) and carrying the greatest-N50 assembly into downstream gene prediction and viral scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw short reads and you want virMine's own read QC followed by assembly — supply them with -p/-s instead of importing a contig FASTA via -A. The FASTA is a protein reference database (viral_aa.fasta or nonviral_aa.fasta) — these are scoring inputs via -v/-nv, not contig assemblies to handle with -A. The task is long-read assembly/polishing itself — virMine accepts supplied long-read/contig files but delegates assembly of short reads to SPAdes/metaSPAdes/MEGAHIT; it does not assemble long reads.

skills.description: Use when you have newly generated contig FASTA files from one or more short-read assemblers and must verify they fall within expected total-length and contig-count ranges for a known-size genome before deeper evaluation.
skills.name: assembled-contig-length-and-count-qc
skills.search_text: assembled-contig-length-and-count-qc Use when you have newly generated contig FASTA files from one or more short-read assemblers and must verify they fall within expected total-length and contig-count ranges for a known-size genome before deeper evaluation. Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) rather than assembled contig FASTA files — run the assemblers first Assemblies are metagenomic datasets where no single expected genome size exists — use MetaQUAST-style reference detection instead of fixed-length range checks Assemblies target large genomes (e.g. mammalian) where the small-genome metric set is uninformative — QUAST-LG is the appropriate extension http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Sanity-check de novo genome assemblies at the contig level — total length, contig count, and contiguity metrics (N50, N90, auN, largest contig) — before downstream evaluation, using the expected ranges established in the WebQUAST E. coli K-12 MG1655 four-assembler benchmark (ABySS, MEGAHIT, SPAdes, Velvet). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad406
skills.summary: Sanity-check de novo genome assemblies at the contig level — total length, contig count, and contiguity metrics (N50, N90, auN, largest contig) — before downstream evaluation, using the expected ranges established in the WebQUAST E. coli K-12 MG1655 four-assembler benchmark (ABySS, MEGAHIT, SPAdes, Velvet).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) rather than assembled contig FASTA files — run the assemblers first Assemblies are metagenomic datasets where no single expected genome size exists — use MetaQUAST-style reference detection instead of fixed-length range checks Assemblies target large genomes (e.g. mammalian) where the small-genome metric set is uninformative — QUAST-LG is the appropriate extension

skills.description: Use when comparing metaMDBG, metaflye and hifiasm-meta on the same HiFi read set of a taxonomically rich metagenome to quantify uncaptured diversity (unaligned bases) and bases aligned to medium-or-better bins.
skills.name: assembler-comparison-benchmarking
skills.search_text: assembler-comparison-benchmarking Use when comparing metaMDBG, metaflye and hifiasm-meta on the same HiFi read set of a taxonomically rich metagenome to quantify uncaptured diversity (unaligned bases) and bases aligned to medium-or-better bins. The input is a single user-provided assembly with no alternate assembler to compare — Mapler's evaluation-only mode (config_test_evaluation_only.yaml) is the right choice instead The reads are short reads or non-HiFi nanopore data; Mapler focuses on evaluating HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies You only want assembly statistics (contiguity, N50) rather than uncaptured-diversity metrics based on read-to-contig alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark multiple HiFi metagenome assemblers (metaMDBG, metaflye, hifiasm-meta) on the same read set using the Mapler Snakemake pipeline, comparing the diversity left uncaptured by assembly through aligned read/base ratios and per-bin-quality mapping breakdowns. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple HiFi metagenome assemblers (metaMDBG, metaflye, hifiasm-meta) on the same read set using the Mapler Snakemake pipeline, comparing the diversity left uncaptured by assembly through aligned read/base ratios and per-bin-quality mapping breakdowns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single user-provided assembly with no alternate assembler to compare — Mapler's evaluation-only mode (config_test_evaluation_only.yaml) is the right choice instead The reads are short reads or non-HiFi nanopore data; Mapler focuses on evaluating HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies You only want assembly statistics (contiguity, N50) rather than uncaptured-diversity metrics based on read-to-contig alignment

skills.description: Use when benchmarking de novo short-read assemblers on datasets with known reference genomes (GAGE Staphylococcus aureus, Rhodobacter sphaeroides, human chr14; Assemblathon1) and you need a quantitative improvement table versus a predecessor or competing assembler.
skills.name: assembler-comparison-table-compilation
skills.search_text: assembler-comparison-table-compilation Use when benchmarking de novo short-read assemblers on datasets with known reference genomes (GAGE Staphylococcus aureus, Rhodobacter sphaeroides, human chr14; Assemblathon1) and you need a quantitative improvement table versus a predecessor or competing assembler. Input is single-cell or metagenomic sequencing data — the README directs such projects to MEGAHIT (scaffolded via SOAPdenovo-fusion) instead of SOAPdenovo2 The reference genome or GAGE-style ground truth needed to compute correct assembly length and error counts is unavailable, so N50/error columns cannot be filled You only need to run a single assembly, not compare assemblers — use the plain SOAPdenovo2 pipeline skill instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Compiles a head-to-head benchmark table (e.g. SOAPdenovo2 vs SOAPdenovo1.05 vs ALLPATHS-LG) on GAGE and Assemblathon1 datasets, recording correct assembly length increase, contig/scaffold N50, and structural/substitution/copy-number error counts, mirroring the paper's Table 1 and Figure 1. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: Compiles a head-to-head benchmark table (e.g. SOAPdenovo2 vs SOAPdenovo1.05 vs ALLPATHS-LG) on GAGE and Assemblathon1 datasets, recording correct assembly length increase, contig/scaffold N50, and structural/substitution/copy-number error counts, mirroring the paper's Table 1 and Figure 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell or metagenomic sequencing data — the README directs such projects to MEGAHIT (scaffolded via SOAPdenovo-fusion) instead of SOAPdenovo2 The reference genome or GAGE-style ground truth needed to compute correct assembly length and error counts is unavailable, so N50/error columns cannot be filled You only need to run a single assembly, not compare assemblers — use the plain SOAPdenovo2 pipeline skill instead

skills.description: Use when several de novo assembly contig sets in FASTA format (e.g. ABySS, Velvet, SPAdes, MEGAHIT output) must be compared without a reference genome to select the most contiguous, complete assembly.
skills.name: assembler-output-comparison-across-assemblies
skills.search_text: assembler-output-comparison-across-assemblies Use when several de novo assembly contig sets in FASTA format (e.g. ABySS, Velvet, SPAdes, MEGAHIT output) must be compared without a reference genome to select the most contiguous, complete assembly. A close or true reference genome is available and reference-aware metrics such as NGA50, genome fraction, duplication ratio, and misassemblies are required (>60 metrics instead of 30) The dataset is a metagenomic assemblage of genomes, where MetaQUAST's per-genome reference detection is the appropriate mode Only one assembly needs validation without cross-assembler comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reference-free quality assessment and comparison of multiple genome assemblies using QUAST/WebQUAST, extracting contiguity and completeness metrics (contig count, total length, largest contig, N50, N90, auN, G+C content, # N's per 100 kbp) from report.tsv to identify the best assembler. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad406
skills.summary: Reference-free quality assessment and comparison of multiple genome assemblies using QUAST/WebQUAST, extracting contiguity and completeness metrics (contig count, total length, largest contig, N50, N90, auN, G+C content, # N's per 100 kbp) from report.tsv to identify the best assembler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A close or true reference genome is available and reference-aware metrics such as NGA50, genome fraction, duplication ratio, and misassemblies are required (>60 metrics instead of 30) The dataset is a metagenomic assemblage of genomes, where MetaQUAST's per-genome reference detection is the appropriate mode Only one assembly needs validation without cross-assembler comparison
