skills.search_text: assembler-output-comparison-against-reference-variants Use when shotgun metagenomic reads from a mock/defined community have been processed through several SSU extraction and reference-targeted assembly combinations and you must decide which combination recovers the most known 16S rRNA variants. No ground-truth panel of reference 16S variants exists for the input community, so recovery cannot be scored Input is already amplified 16S amplicon data rather than shotgun metagenomic reads, where extractor/assembler benchmarking against full-length reconstruction is not the analysis goal You only need taxonomic classification of reads, not evaluation of which SSU reconstruction combination best recovers variants http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark multiple SSU rRNA read-extraction/assembler combinations by aligning each set of reconstructed full-length 16S sequences against a known panel of reference 16S variants, tabulating recovered variants, microorganisms and sequence length distributions. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple SSU rRNA read-extraction/assembler combinations by aligning each set of reconstructed full-length 16S sequences against a known panel of reference 16S variants, tabulating recovered variants, microorganisms and sequence length distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth panel of reference 16S variants exists for the input community, so recovery cannot be scored Input is already amplified 16S amplicon data rather than shotgun metagenomic reads, where extractor/assembler benchmarking against full-length reconstruction is not the analysis goal You only need taxonomic classification of reads, not evaluation of which SSU reconstruction combination best recovers variants

skills.description: Use when reproducing the four E. coli K-12 MG1655 sample assemblies from trimmed paired-end FASTQ reads (SRA ERR008613) as input for WebQUAST/QUAST assembly evaluation, or when comparing short-read assemblers under their citation-standard parameter settings.
skills.name: assembler-parameter-recipe-execution
skills.search_text: assembler-parameter-recipe-execution Use when reproducing the four E. coli K-12 MG1655 sample assemblies from trimmed paired-end FASTQ reads (SRA ERR008613) as input for WebQUAST/QUAST assembly evaluation, or when comparing short-read assemblers under their citation-standard parameter settings. The input is already assembled contigs — this skill generates assemblies from trimmed reads; feed existing FASTA files directly to WebQUAST/QUAST instead The target organism or read data is not short-read (e.g. long-read or hybrid data) — the recipes here are for the four shortlisted short-read assemblers on Illumina-style paired-end reads A single assembler with custom k-mer optimization is required — this skill executes documented default/recommended settings or the GAGE-B recipe, not bespoke parameter tuning Reconstructs the four-assembler E. coli K-12 MG1655 demonstration assemblies (ABySS, MEGAHIT, SPAdes, Velvet) by installing each assembler via Bioconda and running them on trimmed paired-end reads with default or recipe-specific parameters, producing contig FASTA files whose properties match the assemblies evaluated with WebQUAST. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad406
skills.summary: Reconstructs the four-assembler E. coli K-12 MG1655 demonstration assemblies (ABySS, MEGAHIT, SPAdes, Velvet) by installing each assembler via Bioconda and running them on trimmed paired-end reads with default or recipe-specific parameters, producing contig FASTA files whose properties match the assemblies evaluated with WebQUAST.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already assembled contigs — this skill generates assemblies from trimmed reads; feed existing FASTA files directly to WebQUAST/QUAST instead The target organism or read data is not short-read (e.g. long-read or hybrid data) — the recipes here are for the four shortlisted short-read assemblers on Illumina-style paired-end reads A single assembler with custom k-mer optimization is required — this skill executes documented default/recommended settings or the GAGE-B recipe, not bespoke parameter tuning

skills.description: Use when you have deposited LMAS benchmark output (e.g. Zenodo/GigaDB deposit for giac122) for repeated runs and need per-assembler runtime, CPU/hour, memory, and data read/written statistics, or must justify excluding assemblers on resource grounds.
skills.name: assembler-resource-usage-extraction
skills.search_text: assembler-resource-usage-extraction Use when you have deposited LMAS benchmark output (e.g. Zenodo/GigaDB deposit for giac122) for repeated runs and need per-assembler runtime, CPU/hour, memory, and data read/written statistics, or must justify excluding assemblers on resource grounds. When you only need assembly-quality metrics (N50, misassembly categories, contigs >1 kbp) rather than computational cost — use the LMAS report's assembly-evaluation outputs instead. When runs used non-default assembler parameters — the article notes assembler usability was assessed only with the default parameters used, so resource figures are not transferable to tuned settings. When the deposit lacks per-run resource records (e.g. a single collapsed report), aggregation across repeated runs is impossible and consistency cannot be assessed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Extract and tabulate the five computational resource metrics (Avg Time, CPU/Hour, Max Memory (GB), Average Read (GB), Average Write (GB)) that the LMAS Nextflow pipeline registers per assembler, to expose which assemblers have inconsistent or prohibitive resource requirements across repeated runs on a ZymoBIOMICS sample. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Extract and tabulate the five computational resource metrics (Avg Time, CPU/Hour, Max Memory (GB), Average Read (GB), Average Write (GB)) that the LMAS Nextflow pipeline registers per assembler, to expose which assemblers have inconsistent or prohibitive resource requirements across repeated runs on a ZymoBIOMICS sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only need assembly-quality metrics (N50, misassembly categories, contigs >1 kbp) rather than computational cost — use the LMAS report's assembly-evaluation outputs instead. When runs used non-default assembler parameters — the article notes assembler usability was assessed only with the default parameters used, so resource figures are not transferable to tuned settings. When the deposit lacks per-run resource records (e.g. a single collapsed report), aggregation across repeated runs is impossible and consistency cannot be assessed.

skills.description: Use when comparing the computational cost and assembly output (wall-clock time, total contigs, contigs >50 Kb) of a targeted assembly pipeline against complete metagenomic assembly or alternative assemblers on identical raw sequencing reads.
skills.name: assembler-runtime-and-contig-count-profiling
skills.search_text: assembler-runtime-and-contig-count-profiling Use when comparing the computational cost and assembly output (wall-clock time, total contigs, contigs >50 Kb) of a targeted assembly pipeline against complete metagenomic assembly or alternative assemblers on identical raw sequencing reads. Input is already assembled contigs — the benchmark requires raw unassembled FASTQ reads so all assemblers start from the same point The goal is gene abundance quantification across samples rather than assembler speed/output profiling Datasets are small isolate genomes where targeted assembly shows little runtime advantage (e.g., E. coli KLY was faster by complete assembly: 17.4 vs 23.3 min) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Profiles the wall-clock runtime and contig yield of a targeted assembler (CasCollect) against complete metagenomic assembly plus annotation and a rolling-circle-style assembler (PRICE) on the same paired-end FASTQ datasets, quantifying the speed advantage of targeted over whole-sample assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Profiles the wall-clock runtime and contig yield of a targeted assembler (CasCollect) against complete metagenomic assembly plus annotation and a rolling-circle-style assembler (PRICE) on the same paired-end FASTQ datasets, quantifying the speed advantage of targeted over whole-sample assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled contigs — the benchmark requires raw unassembled FASTQ reads so all assemblers start from the same point The goal is gene abundance quantification across samples rather than assembler speed/output profiling Datasets are small isolate genomes where targeted assembly shows little runtime advantage (e.g., E. coli KLY was faster by complete assembly: 17.4 vs 23.3 min)

skills.description: Use when you have de novo diploid assemblies (e.g. Supernova2 output from 10x Linked-Read data) and need to quantify how accurately their variant calls agree with reference-based call sets and GIAB benchmarks.
skills.name: assembly-based-variant-concordance-assessment
skills.search_text: assembly-based-variant-concordance-assessment Use when you have de novo diploid assemblies (e.g. Supernova2 output from 10x Linked-Read data) and need to quantify how accurately their variant calls agree with reference-based call sets and GIAB benchmarks. Input is simulated Linked-Read data being generated or parameter-tuned (use the LRTK-SIM simulation/assembly-quality workflow instead of variant concordance benchmarking) No GIAB benchmark call sets or trusted truth sets exist for your sample, since vcfeval/truvari concordance scoring requires a benchmark to compare against The goal is assembly contiguity assessment (N50/NA50, phase blocks) rather than variant-call accuracy evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks variant calls derived from de novo diploid assemblies against calls from standard reference-based pipelines (Illumina and 10x Linked-Read), quantifying precision, recall, and F1 against GIAB benchmark call sets. It answers whether assembly-derived SNV/SV calls can match reference-mapping-based calling accuracy. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Benchmarks variant calls derived from de novo diploid assemblies against calls from standard reference-based pipelines (Illumina and 10x Linked-Read), quantifying precision, recall, and F1 against GIAB benchmark call sets. It answers whether assembly-derived SNV/SV calls can match reference-mapping-based calling accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is simulated Linked-Read data being generated or parameter-tuned (use the LRTK-SIM simulation/assembly-quality workflow instead of variant concordance benchmarking) No GIAB benchmark call sets or trusted truth sets exist for your sample, since vcfeval/truvari concordance scoring requires a benchmark to compare against The goal is assembly contiguity assessment (N50/NA50, phase blocks) rather than variant-call accuracy evaluation

skills.description: Use when validating that a targeted assembly tool recovers comparable gene-containing scaffolds and gene diversity to full de novo assembly on the same samples, at lower computational cost.

skills.search_text: assembly-benchmark-comparison-against-reference Use when validating that a targeted assembly tool recovers comparable gene-containing scaffolds and gene diversity to full de novo assembly on the same samples, at lower computational cost. Input is long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler/ARGextender is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data The goal is whole-community profiling (taxonomy/abundance) rather than evaluating assembly recovery of targeted genes No reference gene database exists for the targets of interest, since both arms of the benchmark are matched against the same database http://edamontology.org/topic_3837 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Benchmark a targeted de novo assembly method (ARGextender, combining KMA and SPAdes) against a full metagenomic de novo assembly (SPAdes) by matching a reference gene database (ResFinder/PanRes) to both outputs and comparing per-sample scaffold counts and distinct gene detections across a large cohort (951 urban sewage samples). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Benchmark a targeted de novo assembly method (ARGextender, combining KMA and SPAdes) against a full metagenomic de novo assembly (SPAdes) by matching a reference gene database (ResFinder/PanRes) to both outputs and comparing per-sample scaffold counts and distinct gene detections across a large cohort (951 urban sewage samples).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler/ARGextender is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data The goal is whole-community profiling (taxonomy/abundance) rather than evaluating assembly recovery of targeted genes No reference gene database exists for the targets of interest, since both arms of the benchmark are matched against the same database

skills.description: Use when preparing assembler contigs (e.g. from results/assembly/<assembler>/) for reference-based benchmarking in LMAS: contigs must be length-filtered and mapped to a multi-FASTA of reference replicons before computing global and replicon-specific metrics.
skills.name: assembly-benchmarking-metrics-preparation
skills.search_text: assembly-benchmarking-metrics-preparation Use when preparing assembler contigs (e.g. from results/assembly/<assembler>/) for reference-based benchmarking in LMAS: contigs must be length-filtered and mapped to a multi-FASTA of reference replicons before computing global and replicon-specific metrics. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than assembler-generated contigs — this skill operates downstream of the de novo assembly step in LMAS No reference replicon multi-FASTA is available and only reference-free assembly metrics are required The goal is assembling new samples rather than evaluating existing assemblies; use the upstream LMAS assembly stage instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reconstructs the LMAS pre-metric preparation stage: filtering assembler-generated contig FASTA files down to the filtered set (FS) by minimum sequence length with BBTools v38.44, then aligning FS contigs to reference replicons with minimap2 v2.22 so reference-dependent quality metrics can be computed. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Reconstructs the LMAS pre-metric preparation stage: filtering assembler-generated contig FASTA files down to the filtered set (FS) by minimum sequence length with BBTools v38.44, then aligning FS contigs to reference replicons with minimap2 v2.22 so reference-dependent quality metrics can be computed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than assembler-generated contigs — this skill operates downstream of the de novo assembly step in LMAS No reference replicon multi-FASTA is available and only reference-free assembly metrics are required The goal is assembling new samples rather than evaluating existing assemblies; use the upstream LMAS assembly stage instead

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic assemblers against a known mock community with reference replicons, and you need a per-replicon contiguity fraction (LSA) from contig-vs-reference alignments.
skills.name: assembly-contig-alignment-metrics
skills.search_text: assembly-contig-alignment-metrics Use when benchmarking metagenomic assemblers against a known mock community with reference replicons, and you need a per-replicon contiguity fraction (LSA) from contig-vs-reference alignments. No reference replicons are available (LSA is a reference-based metric requiring defined mock community ground truth). Evaluating non-prokaryotic or eukaryotic assembly targets — LMAS was designed for short-read prokaryotic replicon assembly. Input is raw reads or unassembled contigs without an assembler comparison goal — LSA only meaningfully ranks assemblies, not raw data quality. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Computes reference-based contiguity metrics (notably LSA, the longest single alignment fraction) for metagenomic de novo assemblies by aligning filtered-size contigs against reference replicons with minimap2 and normalizing alignment lengths by replicon length. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Computes reference-based contiguity metrics (notably LSA, the longest single alignment fraction) for metagenomic de novo assemblies by aligning filtered-size contigs against reference replicons with minimap2 and normalizing alignment lengths by replicon length.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference replicons are available (LSA is a reference-based metric requiring defined mock community ground truth). Evaluating non-prokaryotic or eukaryotic assembly targets — LMAS was designed for short-read prokaryotic replicon assembly. Input is raw reads or unassembled contigs without an assembler comparison goal — LSA only meaningfully ranks assemblies, not raw data quality.

skills.description: Use when comparing how completely two de novo genome assembly versions represent annotated repeat/segmental duplication sequences, or when auditing whether an assembler upgrade improved recovery of known genomic sequence.
skills.name: assembly-contig-sd-representation-quantification
skills.search_text: assembly-contig-sd-representation-quantification Use when comparing how completely two de novo genome assembly versions represent annotated repeat/segmental duplication sequences, or when auditing whether an assembler upgrade improved recovery of known genomic sequence. The goal is assembly base-level or structural error assessment (e.g. substitution, copy number, or structural error rates vs a reference) rather than sequence-recovery completeness of annotated regions Input is unassembled read data rather than contigs from a completed assembly — the metric is defined on aligned assembly contigs No reference annotation of the target repeat class (e.g. hg19 segmental duplication track) exists for the genome in question http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quantifies how completely a de novo assembly represents known human segmental duplication (SD) sequences by aligning assembly contigs to a reference SD set (134 Mb of hg19 SD sequences) and computing the fraction of SDs sufficiently covered (≥90% of each sequence). Used in the SOAPdenovo2 paper to show the updated YH v2 assembly represents up to 99% of published SDs versus only 21.5% for the first (2008) YH version. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: Quantifies how completely a de novo assembly represents known human segmental duplication (SD) sequences by aligning assembly contigs to a reference SD set (134 Mb of hg19 SD sequences) and computing the fraction of SDs sufficiently covered (≥90% of each sequence). Used in the SOAPdenovo2 paper to show the updated YH v2 assembly represents up to 99% of published SDs versus only 21.5% for the first (2008) YH version.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is assembly base-level or structural error assessment (e.g. substitution, copy number, or structural error rates vs a reference) rather than sequence-recovery completeness of annotated regions Input is unassembled read data rather than contigs from a completed assembly — the metric is defined on aligned assembly contigs No reference annotation of the target repeat class (e.g. hg19 segmental duplication track) exists for the genome in question

skills.description: Use when planning or evaluating de novo diploid genome assembly from 10x Chromium Linked-Read data, especially to choose fragment length (Mu_F) or physical coverage (CF) parameters and predict contig N50 outcomes at a fixed total coverage such as C = 56x.
skills.name: assembly-contiguity-assessment
skills.search_text: assembly-contiguity-assessment Use when planning or evaluating de novo diploid genome assembly from 10x Chromium Linked-Read data, especially to choose fragment length (Mu_F) or physical coverage (CF) parameters and predict contig N50 outcomes at a fixed total coverage such as C = 56x. Input data are long-read (PacBio/ONT) or non-barcode-based short reads rather than 10x Chromium Linked-Reads — the LRTK-SIM model and CF/CR parameter space are specific to partitioned linked-read data The goal is variant calling or phase-block extension rather than contig contiguity — long fragments extend phase blocks but decrease contig N50, so the two objectives pull in opposite directions No high-quality reference exists and only N50 is available as a metric — N50 alone is misleading for accuracy; accuracy assessment (NA50) requires a reference-backed gold standard http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Simulate 10x Linked-Read libraries with LRTK-SIM across controlled parameter combinations (C, CF, CR, Mu_F), assemble them de novo with Supernova2, and tabulate contig/scaffold contiguity metrics (e.g. N50, NA50) to determine how fragment length and physical coverage affect diploid assembly quality. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Simulate 10x Linked-Read libraries with LRTK-SIM across controlled parameter combinations (C, CF, CR, Mu_F), assemble them de novo with Supernova2, and tabulate contig/scaffold contiguity metrics (e.g. N50, NA50) to determine how fragment length and physical coverage affect diploid assembly quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are long-read (PacBio/ONT) or non-barcode-based short reads rather than 10x Chromium Linked-Reads — the LRTK-SIM model and CF/CR parameter space are specific to partitioned linked-read data The goal is variant calling or phase-block extension rather than contig contiguity — long fragments extend phase blocks but decrease contig N50, so the two objectives pull in opposite directions No high-quality reference exists and only N50 is available as a metric — N50 alone is misleading for accuracy; accuracy assessment (NA50) requires a reference-backed gold standard

skills.description: Use when FASTA assemblies (contigs/scaffolds) from metagenome assemblers must be scored against a known reference to compare contiguity (NGA50), misassemblies, and base-level accuracy across tools or ablation modes.
skills.name: assembly-contiguity-metric-computation
skills.search_text: assembly-contiguity-metric-computation Use when FASTA assemblies (contigs/scaffolds) from metagenome assemblers must be scored against a known reference to compare contiguity (NGA50), misassemblies, and base-level accuracy across tools or ablation modes. Reference genomes are unavailable or the study is fully de novo with unknown community composition — NGA50 and misassembly counts are reference-based and cannot be computed. Input is raw reads rather than an assembled FASTA; use a metagenome assembler (e.g., MetaPlatanus) first. Only base-level error profiling of a single assembly is needed without contiguity or misjoin assessment across tools. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Compute reference-based assembly-quality metrics — misassembly counts, NGA50, and mean sequence identity — to quantify contiguity and accuracy of metagenome assemblies (e.g., MetaPlatanus out_final.fa) and to validate ablation and assembler-comparison benchmarks. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Compute reference-based assembly-quality metrics — misassembly counts, NGA50, and mean sequence identity — to quantify contiguity and accuracy of metagenome assemblies (e.g., MetaPlatanus out_final.fa) and to validate ablation and assembler-comparison benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference genomes are unavailable or the study is fully de novo with unknown community composition — NGA50 and misassembly counts are reference-based and cannot be computed. Input is raw reads rather than an assembled FASTA; use a metagenome assembler (e.g., MetaPlatanus) first. Only base-level error profiling of a single assembly is needed without contiguity or misjoin assessment across tools.

skills.description: Use when comparing multiple assemblies of the same genome (e.g. outputs from different assemblers such as SPAdes, Velvet, ABySS, MEGAHIT) and you need contiguity statistics like N50, N90, auN, or largest contig length to rank them.
skills.name: assembly-contiguity-metric-computation
skills.search_text: assembly-contiguity-metric-computation Use when comparing multiple assemblies of the same genome (e.g. outputs from different assemblers such as SPAdes, Velvet, ABySS, MEGAHIT) and you need contiguity statistics like N50, N90, auN, or largest contig length to rank them. skills.name: assembly-misassembly-quantification
skills.search_text: assembly-misassembly-quantification Use when a metagenomic assembly attributes many misassembled blocks to a genome sequenced at ultra-high coverage (>1000x) and you need to test whether excess coverage, not biology, caused the errors. The assembly error is suspected to arise from strain diversity or graph variation rather than excess read depth — MetaCortex's variation-capturing mode is the intended path there, not coverage subsampling No reference genome is available for the genome in question, so misassembled blocks cannot be counted against a reference Input reads are already low-coverage, so a 10% subsample would not test a coverage-driven hypothesis http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Diagnoses coverage-driven assembly errors by subsampling a metagenomic read set to 10% of its original coverage, reassembling with MetaCortex under identical parameters, and comparing misassembled-block counts against a reference between the full-coverage and subsampled assemblies. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad020
skills.summary: Diagnoses coverage-driven assembly errors by subsampling a metagenomic read set to 10% of its original coverage, reassembling with MetaCortex under identical parameters, and comparing misassembled-block counts against a reference between the full-coverage and subsampled assemblies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly error is suspected to arise from strain diversity or graph variation rather than excess read depth — MetaCortex's variation-capturing mode is the intended path there, not coverage subsampling No reference genome is available for the genome in question, so misassembled blocks cannot be counted against a reference Input reads are already low-coverage, so a 10% subsample would not test a coverage-driven hypothesis

skills.description: Use when comparing memory consumption of genome assembler graph-construction modes on a fixed read set, or when quantifying the assembly (N50) tradeoff introduced by a memory-saving algorithm such as the sparse de Bruijn graph.
skills.name: assembly-peak-memory-profiling
skills.search_text: assembly-peak-memory-profiling Use when comparing memory consumption of genome assembler graph-construction modes on a fixed read set, or when quantifying the assembly (N50) tradeoff introduced by a memory-saving algorithm such as the sparse de Bruijn graph. The goal is overall assembly quality rather than isolating graph-construction memory cost — full 'all' runs conflate pregraph, contig, map, and scaff memory footprints. Input is long reads or metagenomic data better served by MEGAHIT, which the README notes generates longer contigs with less memory than SOAPdenovo. The genome size is unknown and no reasonable -z estimate can be supplied, since sparse_pregraph requires -z (mandatory) to allocate memory. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark peak resident memory of de Bruijn graph construction by running SOAPdenovo2's sparse_pregraph mode against the dense pregraph build of SOAPdenovo on identical short-read input (e.g., GAGE S. aureus), capturing resource usage with /usr/bin/time -v and pairing memory figures with contig N50 to expose the assembly-continuity tradeoff. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: Benchmark peak resident memory of de Bruijn graph construction by running SOAPdenovo2's sparse_pregraph mode against the dense pregraph build of SOAPdenovo on identical short-read input (e.g., GAGE S. aureus), capturing resource usage with /usr/bin/time -v and pairing memory figures with contig N50 to expose the assembly-continuity tradeoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is overall assembly quality rather than isolating graph-construction memory cost — full 'all' runs conflate pregraph, contig, map, and scaff memory footprints. Input is long reads or metagenomic data better served by MEGAHIT, which the README notes generates longer contigs with less memory than SOAPdenovo. The genome size is unknown and no reasonable -z estimate can be supplied, since sparse_pregraph requires -z (mandatory) to allocate memory.

skills.description: Use when preprocessed paired-end metagenomic reads must be de novo assembled and the resulting contigs must be quality-checked via contig count, total length (bp), and N50, e.g. to reproduce VIRGO's assembly cohort statistics.
skills.name: assembly-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: assembly-quality-assessment Use when preprocessed paired-end metagenomic reads must be de novo assembled and the resulting contigs must be quality-checked via contig count, total length (bp), and N50, e.g. to reproduce VIRGO's assembly cohort statistics. Input is already a set of assembled contigs or a finished gene catalog (e.g. VIRGO's 0_db sequences) — mapping or annotation skills apply instead The goal is taxonomic/functional profiling of a sample against VIRGO — use the reference-based mapping workflow rather than re-assembling Working with metatranscriptomic-only data where the article notes de novo assembly 'complicates integration of metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data' http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 De novo assembly of vaginal metagenome reads with IDBA-UD (k-mer 20-100) followed by computation of assembly statistics — number of contigs, total assembled bp, and N50 — used to build and validate the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: De novo assembly of vaginal metagenome reads with IDBA-UD (k-mer 20-100) followed by computation of assembly statistics — number of contigs, total assembled bp, and N50 — used to build and validate the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a set of assembled contigs or a finished gene catalog (e.g. VIRGO's 0_db sequences) — mapping or annotation skills apply instead The goal is taxonomic/functional profiling of a sample against VIRGO — use the reference-based mapping workflow rather than re-assembling Working with metatranscriptomic-only data where the article notes de novo assembly 'complicates integration of metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data'

skills.description: Use when assemblies from multiple de novo assemblers must be scored per contig against known reference replicons, requiring a Phred-like quality metric derived from alignment identity rather than raw sequence features.
skills.name: assembly-quality-assessment-metrics
skills.search_text: assembly-quality-assessment-metrics Use when assemblies from multiple de novo assemblers must be scored per contig against known reference replicons, requiring a Phred-like quality metric derived from alignment identity rather than raw sequence features. When no reference replicons are available for the sample — the metric is reference-based and requires aligning contigs to known community replicons. When the goal is reference-free assembly validation based only on contig features themselves (e.g. QUAST-style metrics without reference alignment). When contigs below the --minLength threshold (e.g. <1 kbp) are the object of study — they are excluded before scoring. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Computes per-contig Phred-like assembly quality scores (Pls) in LMAS by converting contig-to-reference alignment identity into an error-based score, so assembly quality of individual contigs can be compared across assemblers against known reference replicons. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Computes per-contig Phred-like assembly quality scores (Pls) in LMAS by converting contig-to-reference alignment identity into an error-based score, so assembly quality of individual contigs can be compared across assemblers against known reference replicons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no reference replicons are available for the sample — the metric is reference-based and requires aligning contigs to known community replicons. When the goal is reference-free assembly validation based only on contig features themselves (e.g. QUAST-style metrics without reference alignment). When contigs below the --minLength threshold (e.g. <1 kbp) are the object of study — they are excluded before scoring.

skills.description: Use when scoring assembled Illumina paired-end (FASTQ, PHRED/CASAVA qualities) sequences by overlap base agreement and filtering them against a quality threshold such as p = 0.9 or p = 0.6.
skills.name: assembly-quality-score-geometric-mean-aggregation
skills.search_text: assembly-quality-score-geometric-mean-aggregation Use when scoring assembled Illumina paired-end (FASTQ, PHRED/CASAVA qualities) sequences by overlap base agreement and filtering them against a quality threshold such as p = 0.9 or p = 0.6. Input reads have no overlapping region, so there is no overlap evidence from which to compute match probabilities (PANDAseq discards such pairs) Input is already an assembled sequence or feature table without per-base quality strings — no per-base error probabilities can be derived The goal is generic read QC (e.g. adapter trimming or FastQC-style reports) rather than scoring the correctness of a paired-end overlap assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reconstructs PANDAseq-style assembly quality scoring: per-base match probabilities in the paired-end overlap (with CASAVA quality-mask handling) are aggregated over the full assembled sequence via a geometric mean, and the score is compared to acceptance thresholds (0.9 and 0.6) to accept or discard assemblies. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Reconstructs PANDAseq-style assembly quality scoring: per-base match probabilities in the paired-end overlap (with CASAVA quality-mask handling) are aggregated over the full assembled sequence via a geometric mean, and the score is compared to acceptance thresholds (0.9 and 0.6) to accept or discard assemblies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have no overlapping region, so there is no overlap evidence from which to compute match probabilities (PANDAseq discards such pairs) Input is already an assembled sequence or feature table without per-base quality strings — no per-base error probabilities can be derived The goal is generic read QC (e.g. adapter trimming or FastQC-style reports) rather than scoring the correctness of a paired-end overlap assembly

skills.description: Use when PANDAseq has assembled Illumina overlapping paired-end (e.g. 16S rRNA amplicon) reads and you must choose how many low-confidence assemblies to retain or discard via the assembly quality score cutoff.
skills.name: assembly-quality-score-thresholding
skills.search_text: assembly-quality-score-thresholding Use when PANDAseq has assembled Illumina overlapping paired-end (e.g. 16S rRNA amplicon) reads and you must choose how many low-confidence assemblies to retain or discard via the assembly quality score cutoff. The reads do not overlap or are not paired-end Illumina reads matched by flow-cell template position — there is no overlap-region quality score to threshold. You need to filter raw unmerged reads by per-base Phred quality instead of an assembly-level quality score. The input is already an assembled or clustered sequence set (e.g. an OTU table); thresholding has already been applied upstream. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Filter PANDAseq-assembled Illumina paired-end reads by their assembly quality score, using thresholds such as 0.9 for high-confidence output or relaxed 0.6 to increase sequence recovery. The threshold trades recall of assembled sequences against confidence that the overlap region was correctly reconstructed. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Filter PANDAseq-assembled Illumina paired-end reads by their assembly quality score, using thresholds such as 0.9 for high-confidence output or relaxed 0.6 to increase sequence recovery. The threshold trades recall of assembled sequences against confidence that the overlap region was correctly reconstructed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads do not overlap or are not paired-end Illumina reads matched by flow-cell template position — there is no overlap-region quality score to threshold. You need to filter raw unmerged reads by per-base Phred quality instead of an assembly-level quality score. The input is already an assembled or clustered sequence set (e.g. an OTU table); thresholding has already been applied upstream.

skills.description: Use when paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads have been assembled (or must be filtered) and you need to set an accept/discard cutoff on the PANDAseq assembly quality score to control sequence recovery, as for the 673 845-read M. capsulatus 16S rRNA library.
skills.name: assembly-quality-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: assembly-quality-threshold-filtering Use when paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads have been assembled (or must be filtered) and you need to set an accept/discard cutoff on the PANDAseq assembly quality score to control sequence recovery, as for the 673 845-read M. capsulatus 16S rRNA library. Input is already an assembled FASTA or feature table without per-base PHRED quality strings — there is nothing to rescore against a threshold. Read pairs have no suitable overlap and are discarded by the assembler before scoring — lowering the quality threshold cannot recover them. Sequencing is not Illumina paired-end with CASAVA-style quality masks (e.g. SAM/BAM, long reads) — use pandaseq-sam or a different QC approach instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Filter PANDAseq-assembled Illumina paired-end reads by the probabilistic assembly quality score, tuning the acceptance threshold (e.g. 0.9 vs 0.6) to trade sequence recovery against error rate. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Filter PANDAseq-assembled Illumina paired-end reads by the probabilistic assembly quality score, tuning the acceptance threshold (e.g. 0.9 vs 0.6) to trade sequence recovery against error rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an assembled FASTA or feature table without per-base PHRED quality strings — there is nothing to rescore against a threshold. Read pairs have no suitable overlap and are discarded by the assembler before scoring — lowering the quality threshold cannot recover them. Sequencing is not Illumina paired-end with CASAVA-style quality masks (e.g. SAM/BAM, long reads) — use pandaseq-sam or a different QC approach instead.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a de novo (strain-resolved or strain-oblivious) metagenome assembly against known reference genomes, needing per-contig reference coverage percentages and nucleotide identity to judge strain separation quality.
skills.name: assembly-reference-coverage-ani-assessment
skills.search_text: assembly-reference-coverage-ani-assessment Use when evaluating a de novo (strain-resolved or strain-oblivious) metagenome assembly against known reference genomes, needing per-contig reference coverage percentages and nucleotide identity to judge strain separation quality. No reference genomes are available for the community — coverage and ANI cannot be computed; use completeness/contiguity metrics instead. You only need to check that Strainberry ran and produced scaffolds, not quantify separation quality against references. The community is high-complexity and uncharacterized; Strainberry and this evaluation target low-complexity metagenomes with known strains. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies strain-resolved assembly quality by computing per-scaffold reference coverage and average nucleotide identity (ANI) against known strain references, the metrics Strainberry's Fig. 4 sensitivity curves are built on. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Quantifies strain-resolved assembly quality by computing per-scaffold reference coverage and average nucleotide identity (ANI) against known strain references, the metrics Strainberry's Fig. 4 sensitivity curves are built on.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genomes are available for the community — coverage and ANI cannot be computed; use completeness/contiguity metrics instead. You only need to check that Strainberry ran and produced scaffolds, not quantify separation quality against references. The community is high-complexity and uncharacterized; Strainberry and this evaluation target low-complexity metagenomes with known strains.

skills.description: Use when a newly proposed assembly or gene-targeting pipeline needs quantitative comparison of runtimes and contig outputs against a standard complete-assembly baseline on identical sequencing datasets.
skills.name: assembly-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: assembly-runtime-benchmarking Use when a newly proposed assembly or gene-targeting pipeline needs quantitative comparison of runtimes and contig outputs against a standard complete-assembly baseline on identical sequencing datasets. The goal is the biological discovery itself rather than performance comparison of assembly strategies Input is already assembled contigs or a finished genome — runtime benchmarking of read-to-assembly pipelines is not applicable The target genes lack profile HMMs or reference sequences, so no targeted-assembly arm can be configured for the benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarking skill for comparing targeted assembly pipelines (e.g. CasCollect) against conventional complete assembly baselines by wall-clock runtime and assembled contig counts on the same input read sets, optionally including third-party assemblers like PRICE. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for comparing targeted assembly pipelines (e.g. CasCollect) against conventional complete assembly baselines by wall-clock runtime and assembled contig counts on the same input read sets, optionally including third-party assemblers like PRICE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is the biological discovery itself rather than performance comparison of assembly strategies Input is already assembled contigs or a finished genome — runtime benchmarking of read-to-assembly pipelines is not applicable The target genes lack profile HMMs or reference sequences, so no targeted-assembly arm can be configured for the benchmark

skills.description: Use when building or extending a non-redundant gene catalog from mixed inputs (e.g., vaginal metagenome assemblies plus urogenital isolate genomes) and you need predicted CDS counts and per-gene lengths attributed to each assembly source.
skills.name: assembly-source-attribution
skills.search_text: assembly-source-attribution Use when building or extending a non-redundant gene catalog from mixed inputs (e.g., vaginal metagenome assemblies plus urogenital isolate genomes) and you need predicted CDS counts and per-gene lengths attributed to each assembly source. Input is raw reads rather than assembled contigs/genome sequences — gene prediction here is run on assemblies, not FASTQ files You need taxonomic/functional annotation (eggNOG, KEGG, protein families) for existing catalog genes — use the VIRGO annotation lookup modules instead Your target microbes are viral or fungal — the catalog this feeds is primarily focused on bacteria with limited inclusion of viral and fungal gene sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Predicts coding sequences (CDSs) from assembled metagenomic contigs and isolate genome assemblies using MetaGeneMark, then attributes each predicted gene to its assembly source to quantify each contribution to a gene catalog. This produced the per-gene length annotation file underlying the VIRGO human vaginal non-redundant gene catalog. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Predicts coding sequences (CDSs) from assembled metagenomic contigs and isolate genome assemblies using MetaGeneMark, then attributes each predicted gene to its assembly source to quantify each contribution to a gene catalog. This produced the per-gene length annotation file underlying the VIRGO human vaginal non-redundant gene catalog.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than assembled contigs/genome sequences — gene prediction here is run on assemblies, not FASTQ files You need taxonomic/functional annotation (eggNOG, KEGG, protein families) for existing catalog genes — use the VIRGO annotation lookup modules instead Your target microbes are viral or fungal — the catalog this feeds is primarily focused on bacteria with limited inclusion of viral and fungal gene sequences

skills.description: Use when binned contig FASTA files (MAGs) have been produced by a binning step and you must judge per-bin assembly quality before downstream taxonomic or functional annotation.
skills.name: assembly-statistics-interpretation
skills.search_text: assembly-statistics-interpretation Use when binned contig FASTA files (MAGs) have been produced by a binning step and you must judge per-bin assembly quality before downstream taxonomic or functional annotation. Input is raw metagenomic reads (Illumina/Nanopore/PacBio) that have not yet been assembled and binned — assembly must precede QC of MAGs The goal is taxonomic classification of MAGs rather than quality assessment — use the pipeline's taxonomic classification step instead Only assembly continuity metrics (N50, total length) are needed with no completeness/contamination requirement — plain QUAST without BUSCO suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Interprets per-bin assembly statistics (contig count, total length, N50) computed by QUAST alongside BUSCO completeness/contamination to quality-control metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) in the nf-core/mag pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Interprets per-bin assembly statistics (contig count, total length, N50) computed by QUAST alongside BUSCO completeness/contamination to quality-control metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) in the nf-core/mag pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metagenomic reads (Illumina/Nanopore/PacBio) that have not yet been assembled and binned — assembly must precede QC of MAGs The goal is taxonomic classification of MAGs rather than quality assessment — use the pipeline's taxonomic classification step instead Only assembly continuity metrics (N50, total length) are needed with no completeness/contamination requirement — plain QUAST without BUSCO suffices

skills.description: Use when you need to measure how fast a paired-end assembler processes a large Illumina FASTQ dataset and what fraction of input read pairs it recovers, e.g. to compare PANDAseq against alternative assemblers.
skills.name: assembly-throughput-benchmarking
skills.search_text: assembly-throughput-benchmarking Use when you need to measure how fast a paired-end assembler processes a large Illumina FASTQ dataset and what fraction of input read pairs it recovers, e.g. to compare PANDAseq against alternative assemblers. Input reads are not overlapping Illumina paired-end reads (e.g. non-overlapping or single-end libraries), where overlap-based assembly and its coverage metric do not apply The goal is assembly accuracy/error profiling rather than throughput and recovery benchmarking (accuracy requires the 0.02–0.08% introduced-error analysis, not timing) Working with SAM/BAM formatted input, which requires the pandaseq-sam variant rather than the FASTQ short form http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark the wall-clock speed and read-recovery (coverage) fraction of an Illumina paired-end assembler, using PANDAseq on the Methylococcus capsulatus 16S rRNA single-template library (673,845 paired-end 108-base reads) as the reference workload. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock speed and read-recovery (coverage) fraction of an Illumina paired-end assembler, using PANDAseq on the Methylococcus capsulatus 16S rRNA single-template library (673,845 paired-end 108-base reads) as the reference workload.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not overlapping Illumina paired-end reads (e.g. non-overlapping or single-end libraries), where overlap-based assembly and its coverage metric do not apply The goal is assembly accuracy/error profiling rather than throughput and recovery benchmarking (accuracy requires the 0.02–0.08% introduced-error analysis, not timing) Working with SAM/BAM formatted input, which requires the pandaseq-sam variant rather than the FASTQ short form

skills.description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking the CPAR2SVM pipeline of PICA — association-rule-based feature selection of COG profiles followed by libSVM — for phenotypic trait prediction on ten example traits such as aerobe, motile, or therm.
skills.name: association-rule-feature-selection-cpar
skills.search_text: association-rule-feature-selection-cpar Use when reproducing or benchmarking the CPAR2SVM pipeline of PICA — association-rule-based feature selection of COG profiles followed by libSVM — for phenotypic trait prediction on ten example traits such as aerobe, motile, or therm. When speed matters more than feature interpretability: SVM-only classification achieved comparable phenotype prediction quality with roughly 3x lower runtime on the ten example traits When working with the successor workflow: phenotrex replaces PICA and offers new classifiers (e.g. XGboost) beyond the CPAR/libSVM plug-in pair When genomes are less than roughly 60-70% complete: most traits can only be reliably predicted above that completeness threshold Feature-selection/classification workflow from the PICA framework in which association rule mining (CPAR) selects informative eggNOG 2.0 COG presence/absence features from microbial genomes before a libSVM classifier predicts microbial phenotypic traits. Serves as the methodological baseline against which PICA's purely SVM-based classification was compared. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-16-s14-s1
skills.summary: Feature-selection/classification workflow from the PICA framework in which association rule mining (CPAR) selects informative eggNOG 2.0 COG presence/absence features from microbial genomes before a libSVM classifier predicts microbial phenotypic traits. Serves as the methodological baseline against which PICA's purely SVM-based classification was compared.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When speed matters more than feature interpretability: SVM-only classification achieved comparable phenotype prediction quality with roughly 3x lower runtime on the ten example traits When working with the successor workflow: phenotrex replaces PICA and offers new classifiers (e.g. XGboost) beyond the CPAR/libSVM plug-in pair When genomes are less than roughly 60-70% complete: most traits can only be reliably predicted above that completeness threshold

skills.description: Use when the input is a marker-gene (16S rDNA) ASV abundance table with its corresponding sequence FASTA and the goal is to predict metagenome functional profiles from that marker-gene input.
skills.name: asv-abundance-table-processing
skills.search_text: asv-abundance-table-processing Use when the input is a marker-gene (16S rDNA) ASV abundance table with its corresponding sequence FASTA and the goal is to predict metagenome functional profiles from that marker-gene input. The input is already shotgun metagenomic data with measured functional profiles, so functional prediction from marker-gene sequences is unnecessary. You only need taxonomic classification of amplicon reads rather than functional prediction from an abundance table. The ASV abundance table lacks a corresponding sequence FASTA, since picrust2_pipeline.py requires both abundance (-i) and study-sequence (-s) inputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Run the PICRUSt2 end-to-end prediction pipeline on an ASV abundance table plus a study-sequence FASTA to produce predicted gene-family (EC) and MetaCyc pathway abundance tables for each sample, as documented in the PICRUSt2 wiki tutorials. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-0548-6
skills.summary: Run the PICRUSt2 end-to-end prediction pipeline on an ASV abundance table plus a study-sequence FASTA to produce predicted gene-family (EC) and MetaCyc pathway abundance tables for each sample, as documented in the PICRUSt2 wiki tutorials.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already shotgun metagenomic data with measured functional profiles, so functional prediction from marker-gene sequences is unnecessary. You only need taxonomic classification of amplicon reads rather than functional prediction from an abundance table. The ASV abundance table lacks a corresponding sequence FASTA, since picrust2_pipeline.py requires both abundance (-i) and study-sequence (-s) inputs.

skills.description: Use when you have a set of predicted viral contigs (post VirSorter2/VIBRANT) and need to annotate their genes and flag which encode auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs).
skills.name: auxiliary-metabolic-gene-identification
skills.search_text: auxiliary-metabolic-gene-identification Use when you have a set of predicted viral contigs (post VirSorter2/VIBRANT) and need to annotate their genes and flag which encode auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs). Input is raw shotgun metagenomic reads rather than assembled, virus-identified contigs — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses, so isolate viral fractions and run viral identification/binning (VirSorter2/VIBRANT, vRhyme/phamb) first You need to annotate microbial (non-viral) MAGs rather than viral contigs — DRAM-v AMG distillation is tailored to viral sequences Excessive environmental contamination is present in the metagenome sequences, which the paper notes increases running time and lowers precision http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Functional annotation of protein-coding genes on viral contigs within ViroProfiler, combining eggNOG-mapper (EggNOG5), VOGDB, and DRAM-v to distill auxiliary metabolic gene (AMG) calls into a gene-by-annotation table. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Functional annotation of protein-coding genes on viral contigs within ViroProfiler, combining eggNOG-mapper (EggNOG5), VOGDB, and DRAM-v to distill auxiliary metabolic gene (AMG) calls into a gene-by-annotation table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw shotgun metagenomic reads rather than assembled, virus-identified contigs — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses, so isolate viral fractions and run viral identification/binning (VirSorter2/VIBRANT, vRhyme/phamb) first You need to annotate microbial (non-viral) MAGs rather than viral contigs — DRAM-v AMG distillation is tailored to viral sequences Excessive environmental contamination is present in the metagenome sequences, which the paper notes increases running time and lowers precision

skills.description: Use when a quality-controlled collection of prokaryotic genome FASTAs (MAGs plus isolates) must be dereplicated into species-level bins at 95% ANI, or when reproducing a published species count such as the VMGC's 786 SGBs.
skills.name: average-nucleotide-identity-clustering
skills.search_text: average-nucleotide-identity-clustering Use when a quality-controlled collection of prokaryotic genome FASTAs (MAGs plus isolates) must be dereplicated into species-level bins at 95% ANI, or when reproducing a published species count such as the VMGC's 786 SGBs. Viral or fungal genomes — the VMGC dereplicates viruses into 4,263 vOTUs and processes fungi through separate pipelines (e.g. virusClstr.sh), not the prokaryotic 95% ANI species clustering. Strain- or subspecies-level resolution is required — the 95% ANI / 30% coverage cutoff deliberately collapses strains into single species bins. Genomes have not passed the >=50% completeness and <5% contamination quality screen, so low-quality or contaminated MAGs would distort ANI-based clustering. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Species-level dereplication of a quality-controlled prokaryotic genome collection by average nucleotide identity (ANI): the 19,542 VMGC prokaryotic genomes (18,570 MAGs plus 972 isolate/reference genomes) are clustered with dRep/fastANI at a 95% ANI threshold to recover 786 species-level genome bins (SGBs) and a nonredundant representative genome set. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Species-level dereplication of a quality-controlled prokaryotic genome collection by average nucleotide identity (ANI): the 19,542 VMGC prokaryotic genomes (18,570 MAGs plus 972 isolate/reference genomes) are clustered with dRep/fastANI at a 95% ANI threshold to recover 786 species-level genome bins (SGBs) and a nonredundant representative genome set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Viral or fungal genomes — the VMGC dereplicates viruses into 4,263 vOTUs and processes fungi through separate pipelines (e.g. virusClstr.sh), not the prokaryotic 95% ANI species clustering. Strain- or subspecies-level resolution is required — the 95% ANI / 30% coverage cutoff deliberately collapses strains into single species bins. Genomes have not passed the >=50% completeness and <5% contamination quality screen, so low-quality or contaminated MAGs would distort ANI-based clustering.

skills.description: Use when MAG or genome FASTA assemblies must be assigned species labels relative to a reference genome database via closest-relative search plus AQ/ANI alignment thresholds.
skills.name: average-nucleotide-identity-computation
skills.search_text: average-nucleotide-identity-computation Use when MAG or genome FASTA assemblies must be assigned species labels relative to a reference genome database via closest-relative search plus AQ/ANI alignment thresholds. The input is metagenomic sequencing reads to be classified, not genome assemblies — read-level classification is the job of DeepMicrobes, not Mash/MUMmer genome comparison. Query genomes are so distant from all references that AQ <= 60% or ANI < 95% — the criterion only supports same-species labeling, not de novo species delineation or higher-rank assignment. skills.search_text: bacterial-phenotype-prediction Use when you have tens or hundreds of bacterial genome sequences (nucleotide or protein FASTAs) and need trait calls for any of Traitar's 67 phenotypes, or when benchmarking genotype-to-phenotype classifiers against curated phenotype labels such as GIDEON or Bergey's Manual entries. The trait of interest is outside Traitar's 67 supported phenotypes (e.g. plant biomass degradation — that predictor is not included in the Traitar release). You need genotype-phenotype inference that integrates other omics data or expression levels — Traitar uses only presence/absence of protein families.
