skills.name: bayesian-core-trait-likelihood-partitioning
skills.search_text: bayesian-core-trait-likelihood-partitioning Use when estimating core genomes from genome sets (MAGs, SAGs, or complete genomes) of highly variable or low completeness, where presence/absence patterns of gene-encoded traits must be evaluated against a completeness prior instead of simple occurrence thresholds. All input genomes are high-quality/complete — Roary and PPanGGOLiN give comparable estimates to mOTUpan on high-quality genomes, so the Bayesian incompleteness correction adds little The goal is OTU/species binning of genomes by ANI similarity network rather than core-genome partitioning — use mOTUlize.py (fastANI, 95% ANI default --similarity-cutoff) instead Input is raw reads with no proteomes or precomputed gene clusters — the method needs protein sequences or gene-cluster/trait files as input http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 mOTUpan computes the likelihood of each gene cluster belonging to the core vs accessory genome from its presence/absence pattern, using a completeness prior that is iteratively updated until convergence. This makes core-genome estimation robust for MAGs/SAGs of highly diverse completeness where tools like Roary collapse. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac060
skills.summary: mOTUpan computes the likelihood of each gene cluster belonging to the core vs accessory genome from its presence/absence pattern, using a completeness prior that is iteratively updated until convergence. This makes core-genome estimation robust for MAGs/SAGs of highly diverse completeness where tools like Roary collapse.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All input genomes are high-quality/complete — Roary and PPanGGOLiN give comparable estimates to mOTUpan on high-quality genomes, so the Bayesian incompleteness correction adds little The goal is OTU/species binning of genomes by ANI similarity network rather than core-genome partitioning — use mOTUlize.py (fastANI, 95% ANI default --similarity-cutoff) instead Input is raw reads with no proteomes or precomputed gene clusters — the method needs protein sequences or gene-cluster/trait files as input

skills.description: Use when running CAFE's background-adjusted k-mer measures (CVtree, D2star, D2shepp) on FASTA sequences and the appropriate Markov order encoding the sequence model is unclear to the user.
skills.name: bayesian-information-criterion-model-selection
skills.search_text: bayesian-information-criterion-model-selection Use when running CAFE's background-adjusted k-mer measures (CVtree, D2star, D2shepp) on FASTA sequences and the appropriate Markov order encoding the sequence model is unclear to the user. When using the JS (Jensen-Shannon divergence) measure, for which the '-1' automatic order inference is explicitly not suitable When the Markov order is already known — pass a non-negative integer less than K (e.g. -M 0) instead of paying the time cost of BIC inference When the analysis is alignment-based (e.g. BLAST against RefSeq) rather than an alignment-free k-mer comparison requiring a background sequence model http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Automatic inference of the optimal Markov model order for background-adjusted alignment-free measures (CVTree, D2star/D2shepp) by setting the CAFE Markov order option to '-1', which evaluates candidate orders (each below the k-mer length K) with the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx351
skills.summary: Automatic inference of the optimal Markov model order for background-adjusted alignment-free measures (CVTree, D2star/D2shepp) by setting the CAFE Markov order option to '-1', which evaluates candidate orders (each below the k-mer length K) with the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When using the JS (Jensen-Shannon divergence) measure, for which the '-1' automatic order inference is explicitly not suitable When the Markov order is already known — pass a non-negative integer less than K (e.g. -M 0) instead of paying the time cost of BIC inference When the analysis is alignment-based (e.g. BLAST against RefSeq) rather than an alignment-free k-mer comparison requiring a background sequence model

skills.description: Use when you have Mykrobe predictor JSON output for an M. tuberculosis sample and need to reproduce or audit the susceptible/minor/major genotype logic behind each resistance call.
skills.name: bayesian-map-model-selection
skills.search_text: bayesian-map-model-selection Use when you have Mykrobe predictor JSON output for an M. tuberculosis sample and need to reproduce or audit the susceptible/minor/major genotype logic behind each resistance call. Analysing M. tuberculosis direct from sputum, where a general mixture model rather than simple major/minor clonal models is needed The goal is per-drug frequency thresholds for M. tuberculosis — the paper states there was not enough MTBC data to estimate them, so only the single 10% threshold is defensible Input is not Mykrobe JSON output with k-mer depth fields (e.g. already-parsed resistance calls), leaving no depths to fit the Poisson models http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Re-derives Mykrobe predictor's per-mutation-site genotype calls by comparing Poisson likelihoods of observed reference/alternate k-mer depths under three clonal models — susceptible, minor resistant (10% frequency), and major resistant (75% frequency) — and selecting the maximum a posteriori model. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Re-derives Mykrobe predictor's per-mutation-site genotype calls by comparing Poisson likelihoods of observed reference/alternate k-mer depths under three clonal models — susceptible, minor resistant (10% frequency), and major resistant (75% frequency) — and selecting the maximum a posteriori model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analysing M. tuberculosis direct from sputum, where a general mixture model rather than simple major/minor clonal models is needed The goal is per-drug frequency thresholds for M. tuberculosis — the paper states there was not enough MTBC data to estimate them, so only the single 10% threshold is defensible Input is not Mykrobe JSON output with k-mer depth fields (e.g. already-parsed resistance calls), leaving no depths to fit the Poisson models

skills.description: Use when computing core-genome partitioning for a set of closely related genomes of mixed quality (complete genomes plus incomplete/contaminated MAGs, SAGs, SUBs) from presence/absence patterns of gene clusters.
skills.name: bayesian-presence-absence-likelihood-estimation
skills.search_text: bayesian-presence-absence-likelihood-estimation Use when computing core-genome partitioning for a set of closely related genomes of mixed quality (complete genomes plus incomplete/contaminated MAGs, SAGs, SUBs) from presence/absence patterns of gene clusters. You need OTU clustering of genomes into mOTUs or ANI network construction from nucleotide sequences — use mOTUlize.py with fastANI similarities instead Your goal is read-based OTU-table construction (the unrelated 'mOTUs' tool at motu-tool.org), not core-genome estimation from genome sets The genomes are not closely related (mOTUlizer targets 'a group of closely related MAGs/Genomes/bins/SUBs'); the 95% ANI species cutoff defines the expected relatedness scale http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Iterative Bayesian estimation of whether each gene cluster belongs to the core or accessory genome by computing the probability of its presence/absence pattern across genome sets that include incomplete MAGs/SAGs, implemented in mOTUpan (mOTUlizer package). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac060
skills.summary: Iterative Bayesian estimation of whether each gene cluster belongs to the core or accessory genome by computing the probability of its presence/absence pattern across genome sets that include incomplete MAGs/SAGs, implemented in mOTUpan (mOTUlizer package).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need OTU clustering of genomes into mOTUs or ANI network construction from nucleotide sequences — use mOTUlize.py with fastANI similarities instead Your goal is read-based OTU-table construction (the unrelated 'mOTUs' tool at motu-tool.org), not core-genome estimation from genome sets The genomes are not closely related (mOTUlizer targets 'a group of closely related MAGs/Genomes/bins/SUBs'); the 95% ANI species cutoff defines the expected relatedness scale

skills.description: Use when relating a covariate matrix (e.g., dietary or clinical variables) to compositional taxa count data that have a known phylogenetic tree, and the goal is sparse branch-by-covariate association selection with uncertainty quantification.
skills.name: bayesian-variable-selection-mcmc-inference
skills.search_text: bayesian-variable-selection-mcmc-inference Use when relating a covariate matrix (e.g., dietary or clinical variables) to compositional taxa count data that have a known phylogenetic tree, and the goal is sparse branch-by-covariate association selection with uncertainty quantification. The compositional data have no known tree-like structure and a non-phylogenetic parameterization is preferred — although MicroBVS can handle data without a tree, this skill centers on the DTM tree-structured model The goal is penalized (frequentist) selection rather than Bayesian posterior inference — the article's case study shows the penalized approach identified 271 associations overall vs. 232 with the Bayesian DTM method The outcome is a phenotypic prediction or mediation effect rather than covariate-branch association selection — the repository's separate joint/mediation models are the appropriate entry points http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Fits Dirichlet-tree multinomial (DTM) regression with Bayesian variable selection via MCMC to identify covariate associations with phylogenetically structured compositional (microbiome) count data, then selects associations by marginal posterior probability of inclusion (MPPI) thresholding. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03640-0
skills.summary: Fits Dirichlet-tree multinomial (DTM) regression with Bayesian variable selection via MCMC to identify covariate associations with phylogenetically structured compositional (microbiome) count data, then selects associations by marginal posterior probability of inclusion (MPPI) thresholding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compositional data have no known tree-like structure and a non-phylogenetic parameterization is preferred — although MicroBVS can handle data without a tree, this skill centers on the DTM tree-structured model The goal is penalized (frequentist) selection rather than Bayesian posterior inference — the article's case study shows the penalized approach identified 271 associations overall vs. 232 with the Bayesian DTM method The outcome is a phenotypic prediction or mediation effect rather than covariate-branch association selection — the repository's separate joint/mediation models are the appropriate entry points

skills.description: Use when you have reconstructed full-length SSU sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta) from a metagenomic pipeline and need per-sequence relative abundance from the original high-quality reads before 97% clustering and taxonomic classification.
skills.name: bbmap-read-assignment-counting
skills.search_text: bbmap-read-assignment-counting Use when you have reconstructed full-length SSU sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta) from a metagenomic pipeline and need per-sequence relative abundance from the original high-quality reads before 97% clustering and taxonomic classification. Input is already a taxonomy or abundance table — this skill computes abundance from raw read-to-reconstruction mapping, not from existing profiles You need 16S rRNA gene copy-number corrected abundances — RiboTaxa explicitly chose not to use gene copy number correction, so this skill provides raw mapping-based relative abundance only You only have the SortMeRNA-filtered 16S/18S read subset — this skill requires mapping the unfiltered high-quality reads to estimate abundance http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 In the RiboTaxa pipeline, this skill estimates relative abundance of reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences by mapping unfiltered high-quality metagenomic reads onto them with BBMap (BBTools) and normalizing per-sequence assigned read counts to percent, prior to 97% clustering (VSEARCH) and taxonomic affiliation. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: In the RiboTaxa pipeline, this skill estimates relative abundance of reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences by mapping unfiltered high-quality metagenomic reads onto them with BBMap (BBTools) and normalizing per-sequence assigned read counts to percent, prior to 97% clustering (VSEARCH) and taxonomic affiliation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a taxonomy or abundance table — this skill computes abundance from raw read-to-reconstruction mapping, not from existing profiles You need 16S rRNA gene copy-number corrected abundances — RiboTaxa explicitly chose not to use gene copy number correction, so this skill provides raw mapping-based relative abundance only You only have the SortMeRNA-filtered 16S/18S read subset — this skill requires mapping the unfiltered high-quality reads to estimate abundance

skills.description: Use when you have multiple reconstructed SSU sequences (from EMIRGE and MetaRib) with per-sequence read counts and need de-redundant cluster representatives with combined abundances for downstream taxonomic profiling.
skills.name: bbmap-read-count-summarization
skills.search_text: bbmap-read-count-summarization Use when you have multiple reconstructed SSU sequences (from EMIRGE and MetaRib) with per-sequence read counts and need de-redundant cluster representatives with combined abundances for downstream taxonomic profiling. Input is already a de-redundant set of SSU cluster representatives with cluster-level abundances (no further consolidation is needed before classification). You are classifying raw short Illumina reads directly rather than reconstructed full-length SSU sequences — the article notes direct classification of short reads yields a high rate of false positives. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Consolidates RiboTaxa's reconstructed SSU rRNA sequences by clustering the MetaRib/EMIRGE full-length sequences at 97% identity with VSEARCH v2.17.0, then summing the per-sequence 'Assigned reads' counts (obtained by BBMap short-read mapping) for all members of each cluster to obtain per-cluster abundances prior to taxonomic affiliation. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Consolidates RiboTaxa's reconstructed SSU rRNA sequences by clustering the MetaRib/EMIRGE full-length sequences at 97% identity with VSEARCH v2.17.0, then summing the per-sequence 'Assigned reads' counts (obtained by BBMap short-read mapping) for all members of each cluster to obtain per-cluster abundances prior to taxonomic affiliation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a de-redundant set of SSU cluster representatives with cluster-level abundances (no further consolidation is needed before classification). You are classifying raw short Illumina reads directly rather than reconstructed full-length SSU sequences — the article notes direct classification of short reads yields a high rate of false positives.

skills.description: Use when MAGs from CAMI II mock community datasets have been classified by multiple taxonomic tools and you need a ranked accuracy comparison (sensitivity, precision, BA, F1, FPR) at strain/species/genus levels against the CAMI gold standard.
skills.name: benchmark-accuracy-table-compilation
skills.search_text: benchmark-accuracy-table-compilation Use when MAGs from CAMI II mock community datasets have been classified by multiple taxonomic tools and you need a ranked accuracy comparison (sensitivity, precision, BA, F1, FPR) at strain/species/genus levels against the CAMI gold standard. No expected taxonomy (CE/gold standard) is available for the sample set — sensitivity, precision, FPR, BA, and F1 all require ground truth and cannot be computed Classifications are of individual reads rather than binned MAGs — this benchmark operates on MetaBAT2-binned MAG FASTAs, not raw read classifiers Only one tool's classification output exists — the purpose of this skill is a cross-tool accuracy ranking (kMetaShot vs GTDBtk vs CAMITAX), which needs comparable outputs from ≥2 tools on identical MAGs http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Compile a per-tool taxonomic classification accuracy benchmark table by comparing observed classifications (CO) of MAG taxonomers (kMetaShot, GTDBtk, CAMITAX) against expected CAMI taxonomies (CE), computing sensitivity, precision, FPR, balanced accuracy, and F1-score per rank and aggregating them into a single CSV. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: Compile a per-tool taxonomic classification accuracy benchmark table by comparing observed classifications (CO) of MAG taxonomers (kMetaShot, GTDBtk, CAMITAX) against expected CAMI taxonomies (CE), computing sensitivity, precision, FPR, balanced accuracy, and F1-score per rank and aggregating them into a single CSV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No expected taxonomy (CE/gold standard) is available for the sample set — sensitivity, precision, FPR, BA, and F1 all require ground truth and cannot be computed Classifications are of individual reads rather than binned MAGs — this benchmark operates on MetaBAT2-binned MAG FASTAs, not raw read classifiers Only one tool's classification output exists — the purpose of this skill is a cross-tool accuracy ranking (kMetaShot vs GTDBtk vs CAMITAX), which needs comparable outputs from ≥2 tools on identical MAGs

skills.description: Use when a set of real DNA FASTA datasets with ground-truth cluster labels needs a head-to-head accuracy comparison between a deep-learning clustering method and classical or DNA-specialized baselines, with aggregate gap reporting.
skills.name: benchmark-aggregate-gap-analysis
skills.search_text: benchmark-aggregate-gap-analysis Use when a set of real DNA FASTA datasets with ground-truth cluster labels needs a head-to-head accuracy comparison between a deep-learning clustering method and classical or DNA-specialized baselines, with aggregate gap reporting. Datasets lack ground-truth labels, so post-hoc unsupervised clustering accuracy cannot be computed and gaps versus baselines cannot be scored Input is not raw DNA sequences (e.g. already a feature table or alignment), since iDeLUCS is alignment-free and operates on k-mer genomic signatures from FASTA files Only a single clustering algorithm is of interest without baseline comparison, since the skill's purpose is aggregate gap analysis across five methods http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmarking skill for reproducing the aggregate unsupervised clustering accuracy comparison of iDeLUCS against classical (k-means++, GMM) and DNA-specialized (MeShClust v3.0, DeLUCS) baselines on 11 real DNA sequence datasets, quantifying the average accuracy gaps reported in the iDeLUCS paper. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad508
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for reproducing the aggregate unsupervised clustering accuracy comparison of iDeLUCS against classical (k-means++, GMM) and DNA-specialized (MeShClust v3.0, DeLUCS) baselines on 11 real DNA sequence datasets, quantifying the average accuracy gaps reported in the iDeLUCS paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets lack ground-truth labels, so post-hoc unsupervised clustering accuracy cannot be computed and gaps versus baselines cannot be scored Input is not raw DNA sequences (e.g. already a feature table or alignment), since iDeLUCS is alignment-free and operates on k-mer genomic signatures from FASTA files Only a single clustering algorithm is of interest without baseline comparison, since the skill's purpose is aggregate gap analysis across five methods

skills.description: Use when a new genome assembly (contigs/scaffolds from a de Bruijn graph assembler such as SOAPdenovo2) must be benchmarked against a predecessor or competitor on a reference-backed dataset.
skills.name: benchmark-assembly-evaluation
skills.search_text: benchmark-assembly-evaluation Use when a new genome assembly (contigs/scaffolds from a de Bruijn graph assembler such as SOAPdenovo2) must be benchmarked against a predecessor or competitor on a reference-backed dataset. The assembly has no reference genome available, so error classification (structural/substitution/copy-number) and coverage against hg19-style references cannot be computed The goal is metagenomic or single-cell assembly, where MEGAHIT-style evaluation rather than SOAPdenovo2's large-genome benchmarking applies Input is raw reads only and no assembly has been produced yet — pregraph/contig/map/scaff must run before evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Evaluate de novo short-read genome assemblies by comparing an assembler's output (e.g., SOAPdenovo2 vs. SOAPdenovo1 or ALLPATHS-LG) on benchmark datasets such as Assemblathon1 and GAGE, using contig/scaffold N50, error classes, and genome coverage to judge assembly quality. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: Evaluate de novo short-read genome assemblies by comparing an assembler's output (e.g., SOAPdenovo2 vs. SOAPdenovo1 or ALLPATHS-LG) on benchmark datasets such as Assemblathon1 and GAGE, using contig/scaffold N50, error classes, and genome coverage to judge assembly quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly has no reference genome available, so error classification (structural/substitution/copy-number) and coverage against hg19-style references cannot be computed The goal is metagenomic or single-cell assembly, where MEGAHIT-style evaluation rather than SOAPdenovo2's large-genome benchmarking applies Input is raw reads only and no assembly has been produced yet — pregraph/contig/map/scaff must run before evaluation

skills.description: Use when the goal is to validate a gene predictor's real-read performance by reproducing published BLAST-hit count tables from 454 metagenomic reads, e.g. the TS28/TS50 human gut twin-study samples.
skills.name: benchmark-count-table-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-count-table-reproduction Use when the goal is to validate a gene predictor's real-read performance by reproducing published BLAST-hit count tables from 454 metagenomic reads, e.g. the TS28/TS50 human gut twin-study samples. Input data are simulated metagenomes rather than real error-prone 454 reads — the paper reports simulated-read results separately from the real-read Table 3 validation The aim is novel benchmarking rather than reproducing the published counts; Glimmer-MG is 'more computationally expensive than existing software', so avoid it when cost dominates Reads come from a platform without homopolymer-associated indels (e.g. Illumina), where the 454-specific error modeling is not the relevant validation axis http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduce the published Table 3 benchmark counts by running three metagenomic gene predictors (Glimmer-MG, FragGeneScan, MetaGeneMark) on the real 454 human gut microbiome reads (TS28, TS50), BLASTing translated predictions against NCBI nr at E < 0.001, and matching counts/proportions to the paper's table. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: Reproduce the published Table 3 benchmark counts by running three metagenomic gene predictors (Glimmer-MG, FragGeneScan, MetaGeneMark) on the real 454 human gut microbiome reads (TS28, TS50), BLASTing translated predictions against NCBI nr at E < 0.001, and matching counts/proportions to the paper's table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are simulated metagenomes rather than real error-prone 454 reads — the paper reports simulated-read results separately from the real-read Table 3 validation The aim is novel benchmarking rather than reproducing the published counts; Glimmer-MG is 'more computationally expensive than existing software', so avoid it when cost dominates Reads come from a platform without homopolymer-associated indels (e.g. Illumina), where the 454-specific error modeling is not the relevant validation axis

skills.description: Use when you need to produce de novo assemblies from benchmark Illumina short-read datasets to compare assembler versions or tools on N50, error counts, and correct assembly length.
skills.name: benchmark-dataset-assembly-execution
skills.search_text: benchmark-dataset-assembly-execution Use when you need to produce de novo assemblies from benchmark Illumina short-read datasets to compare assembler versions or tools on N50, error counts, and correct assembly length. Input is single-cell or metagenomic data — the README directs such projects to MEGAHIT, which generates longer contigs with less memory, with SOAPdenovo-fusion for scaffolding its contigs The goal is comparing raw kmer/scaffolding modules rather than producing whole assemblies for benchmark scoring — use the stepwise module runs directly instead Read data are long reads (e.g. PacBio/ONT); SOAPdenovo2 is designed for Illumina GA short reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Run a de novo assembler end-to-end on standard benchmark read sets (GAGE datasets such as S. aureus, R. sphaeroides, human chr14; Assemblathon1) using SOAPdenovo2's six-module pipeline so that assemblies can be scored against reference-based metrics and compared with predecessor or competitor assemblers. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: Run a de novo assembler end-to-end on standard benchmark read sets (GAGE datasets such as S. aureus, R. sphaeroides, human chr14; Assemblathon1) using SOAPdenovo2's six-module pipeline so that assemblies can be scored against reference-based metrics and compared with predecessor or competitor assemblers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell or metagenomic data — the README directs such projects to MEGAHIT, which generates longer contigs with less memory, with SOAPdenovo-fusion for scaffolding its contigs The goal is comparing raw kmer/scaffolding modules rather than producing whole assemblies for benchmark scoring — use the stepwise module runs directly instead Read data are long reads (e.g. PacBio/ONT); SOAPdenovo2 is designed for Illumina GA short reads

skills.description: Use when two sequence-classification tools must be compared on fragments with known chromosomal/plasmid origin, and you need per-tool error rates (FPR, FNR) plus a concordance fraction between their predictions.
skills.name: benchmark-error-profile-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-error-profile-reproduction Use when two sequence-classification tools must be compared on fragments with known chromosomal/plasmid origin, and you need per-tool error rates (FPR, FNR) plus a concordance fraction between their predictions. Fragments are shorter than 1000 bp — kmer-based methods like PlasFlow do not perform well on short sequences and results are unreliable No ground-truth origin labels exist for the sequences, so true/false positive and negative classes cannot be assigned The goal is recovering circular plasmids from an assembly graph with paired reads (use Recycler or PlasmidSpades instead of signature-based classification) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Head-to-head benchmarking of two plasmid classifiers (cBar and PlasFlow) on the same RefSeq-derived validation fragments, computing false-positive/false-negative rates per tool and pairwise prediction concordance to reproduce the comparison reported in the PlasFlow paper. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Head-to-head benchmarking of two plasmid classifiers (cBar and PlasFlow) on the same RefSeq-derived validation fragments, computing false-positive/false-negative rates per tool and pairwise prediction concordance to reproduce the comparison reported in the PlasFlow paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Fragments are shorter than 1000 bp — kmer-based methods like PlasFlow do not perform well on short sequences and results are unreliable No ground-truth origin labels exist for the sequences, so true/false positive and negative classes cannot be assigned The goal is recovering circular plasmids from an assembly graph with paired reads (use Recycler or PlasmidSpades instead of signature-based classification)

skills.description: Use when reproducing or re-evaluating a published classifier benchmark figure — specifically false-positive behavior on reads simulated from species absent from reference databases — using the DeepMicrobes Figure 4 design.
skills.name: benchmark-figure-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-figure-reproduction Use when reproducing or re-evaluating a published classifier benchmark figure — specifically false-positive behavior on reads simulated from species absent from reference databases — using the DeepMicrobes Figure 4 design. The source species ARE present in every classifier's database — the benchmark's premise (novelty cutoffs AQ<60%, ANI<95%) is violated, so the false-positive comparison is meaningless The goal is to reproduce the mock-community abundance profiles or the IBD species profiles rather than the absent-species false-positive Figure 4 benchmark Evaluating genus-level or abundance-estimation performance, which this figure-level skill does not cover (it tallies species-level misclassification only) http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Reproduces the DeepMicrobes Figure 4 absent-species false-positive benchmark: reads simulated from 121 genomes whose species are absent from all reference databases are classified by DeepMicrobes, Kraken, Kraken 2, CLARK and CLARK-S, and misclassified reads/misidentified species are tabulated and plotted into figure4_misclassification_results.csv. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Reproduces the DeepMicrobes Figure 4 absent-species false-positive benchmark: reads simulated from 121 genomes whose species are absent from all reference databases are classified by DeepMicrobes, Kraken, Kraken 2, CLARK and CLARK-S, and misclassified reads/misidentified species are tabulated and plotted into figure4_misclassification_results.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The source species ARE present in every classifier's database — the benchmark's premise (novelty cutoffs AQ<60%, ANI<95%) is violated, so the false-positive comparison is meaningless The goal is to reproduce the mock-community abundance profiles or the IBD species profiles rather than the absent-species false-positive Figure 4 benchmark Evaluating genus-level or abundance-estimation performance, which this figure-level skill does not cover (it tallies species-level misclassification only)

skills.description: Use when reproducing a taxonomic-classifier benchmark with genome exclusion, or regenerating sensitivity/precision comparison figures for reads stratified by number of reference genomes per genus.
skills.name: benchmark-figure-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-figure-reproduction Use when reproducing a taxonomic-classifier benchmark with genome exclusion, or regenerating sensitivity/precision comparison figures for reads stratified by number of reference genomes per genus. When the sequenced strain is present in the reference database: Kaiju is less sensitive than nucleotide-level classifiers, which can assess the entire genome (as seen in the HiSeq and MiSeq data sets) When the analysis goal is classifying real metagenomic samples rather than measuring classifier sensitivity/precision in a controlled exclusion benchmark When target genera have fewer than 2 or more than 10 reference genomes, or no reference genomes at all — genus-level classification is impossible for genera with no available reference genomes and the 882-genome stratification only covers 242 genera with 2-10 genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduces the Kaiju genome exclusion benchmark on 882 genomes: ART-simulated reads (Illumina SE100/SE250, PE250, Roche/454) are classified against source-genome-excluded protein references with Kaiju (Greedy and MEM), Kraken v0.10.4b, and Clark v1.1.3, then genus/phylum sensitivity and precision are aggregated and plotted as ggplot2 figures matching Fig. 1, Fig. 2, and Supplementary Figures 1-3. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Reproduces the Kaiju genome exclusion benchmark on 882 genomes: ART-simulated reads (Illumina SE100/SE250, PE250, Roche/454) are classified against source-genome-excluded protein references with Kaiju (Greedy and MEM), Kraken v0.10.4b, and Clark v1.1.3, then genus/phylum sensitivity and precision are aggregated and plotted as ggplot2 figures matching Fig. 1, Fig. 2, and Supplementary Figures 1-3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the sequenced strain is present in the reference database: Kaiju is less sensitive than nucleotide-level classifiers, which can assess the entire genome (as seen in the HiSeq and MiSeq data sets) When the analysis goal is classifying real metagenomic samples rather than measuring classifier sensitivity/precision in a controlled exclusion benchmark When target genera have fewer than 2 or more than 10 reference genomes, or no reference genomes at all — genus-level classification is impossible for genera with no available reference genomes and the 882-genome stratification only covers 242 genera with 2-10 genomes

skills.description: Use when you need to reproduce or audit per-assembler computational cost from deposited LMAS benchmark outputs — e.g. comparing runtime, memory, CPU/hour, and data read/written across assemblers or checking consistency across repeated runs of the same mock community sample.
skills.name: benchmark-performance-tabulation
skills.search_text: benchmark-performance-tabulation Use when you need to reproduce or audit per-assembler computational cost from deposited LMAS benchmark outputs — e.g. comparing runtime, memory, CPU/hour, and data read/written across assemblers or checking consistency across repeated runs of the same mock community sample. The goal is assembly quality assessment (N50, misassemblies, reference-based metrics) rather than computational resource accounting Only a single LMAS run is available per sample, so run-to-run consistency of resource requirements cannot be evaluated The pipeline outputs were not produced by LMAS (the Performance tab metrics are LMAS-specific and not registered by other assembly benchmarks) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Tabulates the five computational resource metrics (Avg Time, CPU/Hour, Max Memory (GB), Average Read (GB), Average Write (GB)) that the LMAS report's Performance tab registers per assembler, aggregated across repeated runs on the same sample (e.g. ZymoBIOMICS), to expose run-to-run variability in resource requirements. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Tabulates the five computational resource metrics (Avg Time, CPU/Hour, Max Memory (GB), Average Read (GB), Average Write (GB)) that the LMAS report's Performance tab registers per assembler, aggregated across repeated runs on the same sample (e.g. ZymoBIOMICS), to expose run-to-run variability in resource requirements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is assembly quality assessment (N50, misassemblies, reference-based metrics) rather than computational resource accounting Only a single LMAS run is available per sample, so run-to-run consistency of resource requirements cannot be evaluated The pipeline outputs were not produced by LMAS (the Performance tab metrics are LMAS-specific and not registered by other assembly benchmarks)

skills.description: Decision support for choosing a 16S paired-end read processing pipeline when you have raw paired-end FASTQ data and want to compare how many total reads (and OTUs) each candidate pipeline (merging-free CD-HIT-based vs merging-based) retains across benchmark datasets.
skills.name: benchmark-read-count-comparison
skills.search_text: benchmark-read-count-comparison Decision support for choosing a 16S paired-end read processing pipeline when you have raw paired-end FASTQ data and want to compare how many total reads (and OTUs) each candidate pipeline (merging-free CD-HIT-based vs merging-based) retains across benchmark datasets. You already have a finalized feature/OTU table and only need taxonomy or diversity analysis — no raw-read count comparison is possible The comparison targets OTU counts rather than read counts; note CDSnake outputs fewer OTUs than DADA2 and deblur, so read-count benchmarks should not be conflated with OTU-count accuracy benchmarks Your reads are single-end or non-overlapping pairs; the merging-free rationale applies to highly overlapping paired-end reads (e.g. 2 x 250 bp) http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A benchmarking skill for comparing total outputted read counts across 16S rRNA OTU-retrieval pipelines (CDSnake/CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq vs. merging-based DADA2 and deblur) over paired-end mock datasets, to quantify how much raw data each pipeline preserves. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03591-6
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for comparing total outputted read counts across 16S rRNA OTU-retrieval pipelines (CDSnake/CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq vs. merging-based DADA2 and deblur) over paired-end mock datasets, to quantify how much raw data each pipeline preserves.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a finalized feature/OTU table and only need taxonomy or diversity analysis — no raw-read count comparison is possible The comparison targets OTU counts rather than read counts; note CDSnake outputs fewer OTUs than DADA2 and deblur, so read-count benchmarks should not be conflated with OTU-count accuracy benchmarks Your reads are single-end or non-overlapping pairs; the merging-free rationale applies to highly overlapping paired-end reads (e.g. 2 x 250 bp)

skills.description: Use when validating or reproducing published computational-efficiency claims for a metagenomic gene-prediction pipeline — specifically wall-clock timing on a fixed-length test sequence, time-in-scan profiling, and database size reduction factors.
skills.name: benchmark-result-reproducibility-analysis
skills.search_text: benchmark-result-reproducibility-analysis Use when validating or reproducing published computational-efficiency claims for a metagenomic gene-prediction pipeline — specifically wall-clock timing on a fixed-length test sequence, time-in-scan profiling, and database size reduction factors. The goal is accuracy evaluation of gene prediction (start/stop errors, TGA coding) rather than computational-efficiency reproduction — use an annotation-accuracy protocol instead Input is not a human-microbiome metagenome assembly; pan-genome assignment rates and databases are specific to human gut/oral/skin metagenomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduce published performance benchmarks for the GeneMark-HM gene prediction pipeline by measuring single-CPU wall-clock run-times, profiling the BLASTn similarity-scanning fraction, and computing the pan-genome database volume/memory reduction factor against stated published targets. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047
skills.summary: Reproduce published performance benchmarks for the GeneMark-HM gene prediction pipeline by measuring single-CPU wall-clock run-times, profiling the BLASTn similarity-scanning fraction, and computing the pan-genome database volume/memory reduction factor against stated published targets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy evaluation of gene prediction (start/stop errors, TGA coding) rather than computational-efficiency reproduction — use an annotation-accuracy protocol instead Input is not a human-microbiome metagenome assembly; pan-genome assignment rates and databases are specific to human gut/oral/skin metagenomes

skills.description: Use when several metagenome assemblers have been run on the same sample (e.g. MetaPlatanus vs metaFlye, OPERA-MS, MEGAHIT) and the goal is to tabulate scaffold counts, CheckM completeness/contamination, and reference-alignment edge error rates per assembler.
skills.name: benchmark-result-table-compilation
skills.search_text: benchmark-result-table-compilation Use when several metagenome assemblers have been run on the same sample (e.g. MetaPlatanus vs metaFlye, OPERA-MS, MEGAHIT) and the goal is to tabulate scaffold counts, CheckM completeness/contamination, and reference-alignment edge error rates per assembler. You have only a single assembler's output and no competitor assemblies to compare — there is no comparison table to compile. You lack a reference genome for the target species, so alignment-based edge-error (minor 1k-mer) metrics cannot be computed. Your question concerns raw read QC or short-read preprocessing rather than assembly benchmarking. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compiles assembler benchmark results into a per-assembler comparison table (TSV) that quantifies contiguity, completeness, contamination, and edge-level misassembly for a target genome. In the MetaPlatanus paper this is instantiated as the B. longum 51A scaffold comparison (e.g. scaffold2094 of sample V06-T-0501-S07) to show only MetaPlatanus yields a single near-complete scaffold while competitors fragment into >7 sequences. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Compiles assembler benchmark results into a per-assembler comparison table (TSV) that quantifies contiguity, completeness, contamination, and edge-level misassembly for a target genome. In the MetaPlatanus paper this is instantiated as the B. longum 51A scaffold comparison (e.g. scaffold2094 of sample V06-T-0501-S07) to show only MetaPlatanus yields a single near-complete scaffold while competitors fragment into >7 sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single assembler's output and no competitor assemblies to compare — there is no comparison table to compile. You lack a reference genome for the target species, so alignment-based edge-error (minor 1k-mer) metrics cannot be computed. Your question concerns raw read QC or short-read preprocessing rather than assembly benchmarking.

skills.description: Use when comparing runtime, CPU usage, and peak memory of MAG taxonomy classifiers across the same benchmark datasets, especially when one tool's cost is dominated by reference loading (e.g. kMetaShot's ~22Gb HDF5 matrix requiring ≥32Gb RAM).
skills.name: benchmark-results-tabulation
skills.search_text: benchmark-results-tabulation Use when comparing runtime, CPU usage, and peak memory of MAG taxonomy classifiers across the same benchmark datasets, especially when one tool's cost is dominated by reference loading (e.g. kMetaShot's ~22Gb HDF5 matrix requiring ≥32Gb RAM). When the goal is classification accuracy (sensitivity, false positive rate, balanced accuracy) rather than computational cost — use accuracy benchmark workflows instead When measuring a tool whose resource use cannot be attributed to a single container or process (e.g. orchestration wrappers whose main process underestimates true consumption) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Tabulates computational resource measurements (RAM, CPU%, execution time) for kMetaShot, GTDBtk, and CAMITAX across benchmark MAG datasets into a single comparison table (computational_requirements_table.csv), enabling reproducible tool-efficiency comparison. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: Tabulates computational resource measurements (RAM, CPU%, execution time) for kMetaShot, GTDBtk, and CAMITAX across benchmark MAG datasets into a single comparison table (computational_requirements_table.csv), enabling reproducible tool-efficiency comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is classification accuracy (sensitivity, false positive rate, balanced accuracy) rather than computational cost — use accuracy benchmark workflows instead When measuring a tool whose resource use cannot be attributed to a single container or process (e.g. orchestration wrappers whose main process underestimates true consumption)

skills.description: Use when two or more assembly versions (or assemblers) must be compared under identical settings and the results tabulated, e.g. contig/scaffold N50, coverage percentages, or per-sequence representation rates of a reference set.
skills.name: benchmark-table-compilation
skills.search_text: benchmark-table-compilation Use when two or more assembly versions (or assemblers) must be compared under identical settings and the results tabulated, e.g. contig/scaffold N50, coverage percentages, or per-sequence representation rates of a reference set. The comparison involves metagenomic or single-cell data where MEGAHIT rather than SOAPdenovo is the appropriate assembler Input is a single assembly with no predecessor version to serve as a baseline for side-by-side tabulation The reference set (e.g. SD sequences) is not fixed between versions, so per-sequence coverage rates would not be comparable http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Compiles side-by-side benchmark tables that quantify assembly improvement of a new assembler release against its predecessor, as done when SOAPdenovo2-updated YH assembly was tabulated against the 2008 YH v1 for SD sequence representation (21.5% vs ~99%), N50, genome coverage, and error rates. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: Compiles side-by-side benchmark tables that quantify assembly improvement of a new assembler release against its predecessor, as done when SOAPdenovo2-updated YH assembly was tabulated against the 2008 YH v1 for SD sequence representation (21.5% vs ~99%), N50, genome coverage, and error rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison involves metagenomic or single-cell data where MEGAHIT rather than SOAPdenovo is the appropriate assembler Input is a single assembly with no predecessor version to serve as a baseline for side-by-side tabulation The reference set (e.g. SD sequences) is not fixed between versions, so per-sequence coverage rates would not be comparable

skills.description: Reference for extracting per-pipeline OTU counts, total read counts, and annotation/correct-annotation values from benchmark tables that compare CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq-based CDSnake against QIIME2 DADA2 and deblur on mock communities.
skills.name: benchmark-table-value-extraction
skills.search_text: benchmark-table-value-extraction Reference for extracting per-pipeline OTU counts, total read counts, and annotation/correct-annotation values from benchmark tables that compare CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq-based CDSnake against QIIME2 DADA2 and deblur on mock communities. The input is raw paired-end FASTQ reads rather than published benchmark values — use the CDSnake/DADA2/deblur pipelines themselves instead The comparison needs time benchmarking or annotation-quality columns (annotated/correctly annotated counts) that the table transcription does not cover without extra care to the table's compact numeric encoding http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Transcribe benchmark result tables from an article's results section (e.g. Table 1 of the CDSnake paper: OTU counts, annotation statistics, and total counts for CDSnake vs DADA2 vs deblur on the Balanced, HMP, and Extreme mock datasets) into a validated CSV for downstream comparison. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03591-6
skills.summary: Transcribe benchmark result tables from an article's results section (e.g. Table 1 of the CDSnake paper: OTU counts, annotation statistics, and total counts for CDSnake vs DADA2 vs deblur on the Balanced, HMP, and Extreme mock datasets) into a validated CSV for downstream comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw paired-end FASTQ reads rather than published benchmark values — use the CDSnake/DADA2/deblur pipelines themselves instead The comparison needs time benchmarking or annotation-quality columns (annotated/correctly annotated counts) that the table transcription does not cover without extra care to the table's compact numeric encoding

skills.description: Use when comparing read-classification tools' benchmark tables (bases/second throughput, index size, peak RSS) and you need quantitative advantage ratios across references of increasing repetitiveness, e.g. single-genome vs many-strain pan-genome indexes.
skills.name: benchmark-throughput-ratio-computation
skills.search_text: benchmark-throughput-ratio-computation Use when comparing read-classification tools' benchmark tables (bases/second throughput, index size, peak RSS) and you need quantitative advantage ratios across references of increasing repetitiveness, e.g. single-genome vs many-strain pan-genome indexes. The goal is to rerun the raw alignment/classification benchmarks rather than recompute or verify ratios from already-published per-tool measurements The comparison is between tools other than SPUMONI and minimap2 and no equivalent paired throughput/index-size/peak-RSS measurements exist for both The input is raw nanopore signal or basecalled FASTQ reads — this skill consumes tabular benchmark figures, not sequencing data http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Computes and cross-checks throughput, index-size, and peak-RSS ratios between SPUMONI and minimap2 from published benchmark tables (simulated ZymoMC, real ZymoMC mock community, and 3-genome human microbiome experiments), assembling the ratios into a single summary CSV ordered by reference repetitiveness. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Computes and cross-checks throughput, index-size, and peak-RSS ratios between SPUMONI and minimap2 from published benchmark tables (simulated ZymoMC, real ZymoMC mock community, and 3-genome human microbiome experiments), assembling the ratios into a single summary CSV ordered by reference repetitiveness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to rerun the raw alignment/classification benchmarks rather than recompute or verify ratios from already-published per-tool measurements The comparison is between tools other than SPUMONI and minimap2 and no equivalent paired throughput/index-size/peak-RSS measurements exist for both The input is raw nanopore signal or basecalled FASTQ reads — this skill consumes tabular benchmark figures, not sequencing data

skills.description: Use when deposited assembler benchmark logs (e.g. Zenodo record 7996690) contain per-run timing/memory records across thread counts and you must reproduce or re-aggregate speed claims such as the 3- to 10-fold Plassembler vs Unicycler improvement.
skills.name: benchmarking-log-parsing
skills.search_text: benchmarking-log-parsing Use when deposited assembler benchmark logs (e.g. Zenodo record 7996690) contain per-run timing/memory records across thread counts and you must reproduce or re-aggregate speed claims such as the 3- to 10-fold Plassembler vs Unicycler improvement. The goal is assembly accuracy comparison (plasmid recovery, misassemblies) rather than runtime/memory benchmarking — this skill only handles timing and memory records The source data are raw FASTQ read sets rather than completed assembler run logs, so no timing records exist to parse Comparing against tools or versions not present in the deposited benchmarking outputs (e.g. the older v1.2.0 benchmarks used different simulated R9 vs R10 read sets and are not a fair comparison) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Parse recorded wall-clock run times and maximum memory usage from deposited benchmarking outputs (Plassembler/Flye, Plassembler/Raven, and Unicycler runs) and aggregate them into per-thread-count summary statistics and Plassembler-to-Unicycler speedup ratios. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Parse recorded wall-clock run times and maximum memory usage from deposited benchmarking outputs (Plassembler/Flye, Plassembler/Raven, and Unicycler runs) and aggregate them into per-thread-count summary statistics and Plassembler-to-Unicycler speedup ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is assembly accuracy comparison (plasmid recovery, misassemblies) rather than runtime/memory benchmarking — this skill only handles timing and memory records The source data are raw FASTQ read sets rather than completed assembler run logs, so no timing records exist to parse Comparing against tools or versions not present in the deposited benchmarking outputs (e.g. the older v1.2.0 benchmarks used different simulated R9 vs R10 read sets and are not a fair comparison)

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ pairs (e.g. Acinetobacter_baumannii_1.fastq.gz/_2.fastq.gz from Zenodo 7996690) must be adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered before hybrid plasmid assembly with Plassembler.
skills.name: benchmarking-read-preprocessing
skills.search_text: benchmarking-read-preprocessing Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ pairs (e.g. Acinetobacter_baumannii_1.fastq.gz/_2.fastq.gz from Zenodo 7996690) must be adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered before hybrid plasmid assembly with Plassembler. Input reads are long reads (Nanopore/PacBio) — fastp is designed for short reads; the Plassembler QC stage targets the paired-end short-read input set only The Plassembler run was launched with --skip_qc, so the short-read FASTQs should be passed through without fastp trimming Reads have already been trimmed/filtered — re-running fastp would only shorten reads without benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quality-controls paired-end Illumina short-read FASTQ inputs with fastp (>=0.24.2) as the short-read QC stage of the Plassembler pipeline/benchmarking workflow, producing cleaned, gzip-compressed R1/R2 reads for downstream hybrid assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Quality-controls paired-end Illumina short-read FASTQ inputs with fastp (>=0.24.2) as the short-read QC stage of the Plassembler pipeline/benchmarking workflow, producing cleaned, gzip-compressed R1/R2 reads for downstream hybrid assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are long reads (Nanopore/PacBio) — fastp is designed for short reads; the Plassembler QC stage targets the paired-end short-read input set only The Plassembler run was launched with --skip_qc, so the short-read FASTQs should be passed through without fastp trimming Reads have already been trimmed/filtered — re-running fastp would only shorten reads without benefit

skills.description: Use when comparing case-control metagenomic feature tables (e.g. healthy vs adenoma vs carcinoma CSS-normalized abundance at five annotation levels) and you need per-feature P-values corrected for multiple testing.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction Use when comparing case-control metagenomic feature tables (e.g. healthy vs adenoma vs carcinoma CSS-normalized abundance at five annotation levels) and you need per-feature P-values corrected for multiple testing. Input data are raw un-normalized gene counts — compositional bias must first be removed with CSS normalization before testing The goal is a single pre-specified comparison with no multiple-testing burden across thousands of features, where BH correction is unnecessary Normality of the feature distribution is acceptable and the analysis plan calls for one-way ANOVA instead of the non-parametric test http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3055 Statistical significance testing stage of the CAMAMED metagenomic pipeline: per-feature non-parametric testing across phenotype groups (Kruskal-Wallis H test, with one-way ANOVA where normality is acceptable) followed by Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction of raw P-values across taxon, gene, KO, EC number and reaction levels. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Statistical significance testing stage of the CAMAMED metagenomic pipeline: per-feature non-parametric testing across phenotype groups (Kruskal-Wallis H test, with one-way ANOVA where normality is acceptable) followed by Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction of raw P-values across taxon, gene, KO, EC number and reaction levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are raw un-normalized gene counts — compositional bias must first be removed with CSS normalization before testing The goal is a single pre-specified comparison with no multiple-testing burden across thousands of features, where BH correction is unnecessary Normality of the feature distribution is acceptable and the analysis plan calls for one-way ANOVA instead of the non-parametric test

skills.description: Use when evaluating one-mismatch children from HashSeq's OneMismatchCluster.txt against a background error rate with poisson.test, and per-child P values must be multiple-hypothesis corrected with BH at 5% FDR before writing InferenceTestSignificantChildren.txt.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction Use when evaluating one-mismatch children from HashSeq's OneMismatchCluster.txt against a background error rate with poisson.test, and per-child P values must be multiple-hypothesis corrected with BH at 5% FDR before writing InferenceTestSignificantChildren.txt. You need a well-controlled variant caller for production: the Poisson test is anticonservative (>83% rejection) because of overdispersion; use HashSeq's normal-distribution + LOESS inference instead True low-abundance variant detection: HashSeq-based inference is not sensitive there, and more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 are recommended The data involve multiple mismatches or indels, which the one-mismatch Poisson framework does not model http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies one-sided Poisson tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (5% threshold) to classify one-mismatch child sequences in HashSeq clusters as true variants versus sequencing-error artifacts, demonstrating the anticonservatism of the Poisson error model. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Applies one-sided Poisson tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (5% threshold) to classify one-mismatch child sequences in HashSeq clusters as true variants versus sequencing-error artifacts, demonstrating the anticonservatism of the Poisson error model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a well-controlled variant caller for production: the Poisson test is anticonservative (>83% rejection) because of overdispersion; use HashSeq's normal-distribution + LOESS inference instead True low-abundance variant detection: HashSeq-based inference is not sensitive there, and more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 are recommended The data involve multiple mismatches or indels, which the one-mismatch Poisson framework does not model

skills.description: Use when hundreds/thousands of taxa (phylum through genus) each yield a raw P-value from group-comparison regression and a family-wise-error-controlled, FDR-adjusted significance list is needed.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when hundreds/thousands of taxa (phylum through genus) each yield a raw P-value from group-comparison regression and a family-wise-error-controlled, FDR-adjusted significance list is needed. The comparison involves a single hypothesis or a small prespecified set of taxa, where a family-wise-error method or no correction may be more appropriate than FDR over the full taxon family The abundance data have not yet been CLR (centered log-ratio) transformed or the regression has not been fit per taxon — this skill corrects P-values only, it does not perform the differential abundance testing itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at a 5% threshold to raw P-values from per-taxon covariate-adjusted CLR-based differential abundance testing, as used in the MiSurv Module 2 analysis of the control-vs-tylosin example trial, yielding 66 significant taxa from phylum to genus. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/spectrum.05059-22
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at a 5% threshold to raw P-values from per-taxon covariate-adjusted CLR-based differential abundance testing, as used in the MiSurv Module 2 analysis of the control-vs-tylosin example trial, yielding 66 significant taxa from phylum to genus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison involves a single hypothesis or a small prespecified set of taxa, where a family-wise-error method or no correction may be more appropriate than FDR over the full taxon family The abundance data have not yet been CLR (centered log-ratio) transformed or the regression has not been fit per taxon — this skill corrects P-values only, it does not perform the differential abundance testing itself

skills.description: Use when amplicon OTU tables (e.g. Greengenes-based twin gut cohort profiles) are being corrected with CopyRighter and you must verify that per-sample dominance changes fall in a reported range (0-23.3%) or summarize community dominance shifts.
skills.name: berger-parker-dominance-estimation
skills.search_text: berger-parker-dominance-estimation Use when amplicon OTU tables (e.g. Greengenes-based twin gut cohort profiles) are being corrected with CopyRighter and you must verify that per-sample dominance changes fall in a reported range (0-23.3%) or summarize community dominance shifts. Input profiles are already relative abundances (percentages) — CopyRighter requires raw read counts, so dominance correction on pre-normalized data is invalid The community profile was generated by shotgun metagenomics without genome-length trait estimates rather than 16S rRNA amplicons, or uses a taxonomy other than Greengenes (e.g. Silva), which CopyRighter does not yet cover You only need generic alpha diversity and have no need to assess GCN-bias effects on dominance http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Compute the Berger-Parker dominance index (relative abundance of the single most abundant taxon) per sample in 16S rRNA amplicon profiles, before and after CopyRighter 16S gene copy number (GCN) correction, to quantify how lineage-specific GCN bias skews dominance estimates. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Compute the Berger-Parker dominance index (relative abundance of the single most abundant taxon) per sample in 16S rRNA amplicon profiles, before and after CopyRighter 16S gene copy number (GCN) correction, to quantify how lineage-specific GCN bias skews dominance estimates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input profiles are already relative abundances (percentages) — CopyRighter requires raw read counts, so dominance correction on pre-normalized data is invalid The community profile was generated by shotgun metagenomics without genome-length trait estimates rather than 16S rRNA amplicons, or uses a taxonomy other than Greengenes (e.g. Silva), which CopyRighter does not yet cover You only need generic alpha diversity and have no need to assess GCN-bias effects on dominance

skills.description: Use when you need simulated longitudinal metagenomic reads carrying within-strain mutations with user-specified allele-frequency trajectories across timepoints, to benchmark mutation-detection tools.
skills.name: bernoulli-read-carrier-mutation-injection
skills.search_text: bernoulli-read-carrier-mutation-injection Use when you need simulated longitudinal metagenomic reads carrying within-strain mutations with user-specified allele-frequency trajectories across timepoints, to benchmark mutation-detection tools. Your input is real metagenomic data from species with low sequencing depth or poorly characterized genomes — the README states STEMSim 'only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes' You need between-strain or long-term evolutionary divergence rather than within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations in longitudinal samples Your raw reads are not simulated reads from a single reference genome or CAMISIM community output (the two supported input modes) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A STEMSIM-based method for injecting within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations into longitudinal metagenomic reads by Bernoulli-sampling the read carriers at each configured per-timepoint allele frequency, so observed trajectories match specified ones (e.g., increasing 0.2/0.5/0.8/1 under positive selection, decreasing 0.8/0.5/0.3/0 under purifying selection). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad302
skills.summary: A STEMSIM-based method for injecting within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations into longitudinal metagenomic reads by Bernoulli-sampling the read carriers at each configured per-timepoint allele frequency, so observed trajectories match specified ones (e.g., increasing 0.2/0.5/0.8/1 under positive selection, decreasing 0.8/0.5/0.3/0 under purifying selection).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is real metagenomic data from species with low sequencing depth or poorly characterized genomes — the README states STEMSim 'only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes' You need between-strain or long-term evolutionary divergence rather than within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations in longitudinal samples Your raw reads are not simulated reads from a single reference genome or CAMISIM community output (the two supported input modes)

skills.description: Use when processing per-sample DIAMAND tabular alignment output during metagenomic read mapping and you must reduce many-to-many read-gene hits to matches before gene counting.

Input is a single biodiversity metric or a single predictor set — the skill requires paired ALS and radar predictor tables over 48 response variables to compare median R-squared losses Goal is Sentinel-1 SAR data pre-processing (GRDH to gamma_0 via the SNAP/GPT batch file Sentinel1_GRDH_to_gamma0.xml) — use the pre-processing workflow instead of this modelling skill Plots are not spatially replicated across the five forest regions, so a region random-intercept factor cannot be defined Models ground-truth taxonomic and phylogenetic biodiversity metrics (alpha- and beta-diversity across 12 functional groups, 48 response variables) with ALS versus Sentinel-1 radar per-plot predictors in R, and quantifies how much explained variance (R-squared) is lost when forest region is added as a random intercept factor. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Models ground-truth taxonomic and phylogenetic biodiversity metrics (alpha- and beta-diversity across 12 functional groups, 48 response variables) with ALS versus Sentinel-1 radar per-plot predictors in R, and quantifies how much explained variance (R-squared) is lost when forest region is added as a random intercept factor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single biodiversity metric or a single predictor set — the skill requires paired ALS and radar predictor tables over 48 response variables to compare median R-squared losses Goal is Sentinel-1 SAR data pre-processing (GRDH to gamma_0 via the SNAP/GPT batch file Sentinel1_GRDH_to_gamma0.xml) — use the pre-processing workflow instead of this modelling skill Plots are not spatially replicated across the five forest regions, so a region random-intercept factor cannot be defined

The paper reports only accuracy metrics (F1 scores, precision/recall) without per-tool runtime, index-size, or memory measurements to tabulate The benchmark compares tools on a single reference condition with no variation in repetitiveness or scale, making ratio-scaling analysis uninformative Raw timing logs or profiling output must be produced from scratch rather than extracted from published tables (use actual re-benchmarking instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Tabulates comparative benchmark metrics (throughput, index size, peak RSS) for two or more bioinformatics tools from published result tables, computing ratio summaries that quantify performance scaling across experimental conditions (e.g., reference repetitiveness). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Tabulates comparative benchmark metrics (throughput, index size, peak RSS) for two or more bioinformatics tools from published result tables, computing ratio summaries that quantify performance scaling across experimental conditions (e.g., reference repetitiveness).

skills.description: Use when longitudinal sequencing count data (OTU table, taxa by samples over time) contain many observed zeros and you need posterior probabilities distinguishing biological zeros from technical/sampling zeros.
skills.name: biological-versus-technical-zero-classification
skills.search_text: biological-versus-technical-zero-classification Use when longitudinal sequencing count data (OTU table, taxa by samples over time) contain many observed zeros and you need posterior probabilities distinguishing biological zeros from technical/sampling zeros. Taxa are ultra-sparse (>90% missing/nonzero entries): the README recommends filtering such taxa out as a pre-processing step because there is little information in their trajectories over time. Data are not raw longitudinal sequencing counts (e.g. already composited, imputed, or pseudo-count-transformed relative abundances), since zero classification relies on observing sampling zeros in count data. Single cross-sectional samples without longitudinal structure, since the state-space model pools information across longitudinal samples to classify zeros. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classify observed zeros in longitudinal 16S count data as biological zeros (taxon absent from the community) versus technical/sampling zeros (taxon below the detection threshold) using LUMINATE's variational state-space inference, which also yields denoised relative-abundance trajectories. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2020.05.006
skills.summary: Classify observed zeros in longitudinal 16S count data as biological zeros (taxon absent from the community) versus technical/sampling zeros (taxon below the detection threshold) using LUMINATE's variational state-space inference, which also yields denoised relative-abundance trajectories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Taxa are ultra-sparse (>90% missing/nonzero entries): the README recommends filtering such taxa out as a pre-processing step because there is little information in their trajectories over time. Data are not raw longitudinal sequencing counts (e.g. already composited, imputed, or pseudo-count-transformed relative abundances), since zero classification relies on observing sampling zeros in count data. Single cross-sectional samples without longitudinal structure, since the state-space model pools information across longitudinal samples to classify zeros.

skills.description: Use when longitudinal count data contain many zeros and the analysis must decide whether a taxon is truly extinct from the community or merely under the sequencing detection threshold.
skills.name: biological-zero-posterior-inference
skills.search_text: biological-zero-posterior-inference Use when longitudinal count data contain many zeros and the analysis must decide whether a taxon is truly extinct from the community or merely under the sequencing detection threshold. The dataset contains ultra-sparse taxa (>90% missing/zero entries) — these should be filtered out as a pre-processing step because there is little information to reconstruct their trajectory over time. The data are cross-sectional (single time point) rather than longitudinal; LUMINATE pools information across longitudinal samples of a time series. The goal is to model external perturbations such as antibiotics affecting zero status — the paper explicitly lists this as future work, not supported by the current framework. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computes, for every observed zero in a longitudinal OTU table, the posterior probability that it is a biological zero (taxon absent from the community) versus a technical zero (taxon present but below detection threshold) using LUMINATE's variational inference with forward-backward HMM updates of the hidden state q(w_t^d). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2020.05.006
skills.summary: Computes, for every observed zero in a longitudinal OTU table, the posterior probability that it is a biological zero (taxon absent from the community) versus a technical zero (taxon present but below detection threshold) using LUMINATE's variational inference with forward-backward HMM updates of the hidden state q(w_t^d).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains ultra-sparse taxa (>90% missing/zero entries) — these should be filtered out as a pre-processing step because there is little information to reconstruct their trajectory over time. The data are cross-sectional (single time point) rather than longitudinal; LUMINATE pools information across longitudinal samples of a time series. The goal is to model external perturbations such as antibiotics affecting zero status — the paper explicitly lists this as future work, not supported by the current framework.

skills.description: Use when you have qPCR-derived total microbial abundance estimates for paired samples (e.g., day 27 vs day 362 anaerobic digester biomass) and need to test temporal trends before and after GCN correction.
skills.name: biomass-trend-significance-testing
skills.search_text: biomass-trend-significance-testing Use when you have qPCR-derived total microbial abundance estimates for paired samples (e.g., day 27 vs day 362 anaerobic digester biomass) and need to test temporal trends before and after GCN correction. The abundance data are already trait-corrected (e.g. previously run through CopyRighter) — re-correcting would double-weight by inverse GCN Samples are not paired (independent groups), in which case a paired t-test is inappropriate and a different test is required The amplicon profile was assigned with a taxonomy other than Greengenes, since CopyRighter's pre-computed GCN data files cover the Oct 2012 Greengenes taxonomy http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Statistical skill for testing whether total microbial abundance (qPCR-derived biomass) changes significantly over time, comparing results with and without 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) correction via CopyRighter. It reveals how GCN bias can create or remove apparent biomass trends. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Statistical skill for testing whether total microbial abundance (qPCR-derived biomass) changes significantly over time, comparing results with and without 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) correction via CopyRighter. It reveals how GCN bias can create or remove apparent biomass trends.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The abundance data are already trait-corrected (e.g. previously run through CopyRighter) — re-correcting would double-weight by inverse GCN Samples are not paired (independent groups), in which case a paired t-test is inappropriate and a different test is required The amplicon profile was assigned with a taxonomy other than Greengenes, since CopyRighter's pre-computed GCN data files cover the Oct 2012 Greengenes taxonomy

skills.search_text: biosample-taxonomy-classification Use when you have positive genome hits (e.g. from COBS queries against a compact index of ENA bacterial genomes) mapped to BioSample accessions and need to classify them by isolate taxonomy and count distinct known genera and species. Your input is raw reads or contigs rather than already-mapped BioSample-level genome hits — taxonomy classification here presupposes a parsed COBS hit list You need novel IS discovery or ITR identification from metagenomic reads — that is Palidis's role, not this metadata-classification step The BioSamples lack any associated taxonomic metadata, leaving nothing to classify or count http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Attach taxonomic identity metadata to ENA BioSample accessions recovered from COBS query hits and tally how many samples come from isolates with known taxonomy, spanning how many distinct genera and species — as done when tracing ISC insertion sequence hits back to 661,405 microbial genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Attach taxonomic identity metadata to ENA BioSample accessions recovered from COBS query hits and tally how many samples come from isolates with known taxonomy, spanning how many distinct genera and species — as done when tracing ISC insertion sequence hits back to 661,405 microbial genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is raw reads or contigs rather than already-mapped BioSample-level genome hits — taxonomy classification here presupposes a parsed COBS hit list You need novel IS discovery or ITR identification from metagenomic reads — that is Palidis's role, not this metadata-classification step The BioSamples lack any associated taxonomic metadata, leaving nothing to classify or count

skills.search_text: biosynthetic-gene-cluster-genome-mining Use when you have complete strain genomes (e.g. RefSeq FASTA) and need per-genome counts of BGCs, RiPP-encoding clusters, and short ORF candidates under motif-ORF vs all-ORF mining modes to benchmark mining sensitivity.
