skills.description: Use when assembled nucleotide contigs must be partitioned into putative RiPP-encoding BGC regions, by anchoring fixed-size (10 kbp) windows on HMMer-detected modification enzyme hits before candidate ORF extraction.
skills.name: biosynthetic-gene-cluster-window-construction
skills.search_text: biosynthetic-gene-cluster-window-construction Use when assembled nucleotide contigs must be partitioned into putative RiPP-encoding BGC regions, by anchoring fixed-size (10 kbp) windows on HMMer-detected modification enzyme hits before candidate ORF extraction. Precursor peptides have sequence similarity to known RiPPs and a more sensitive motif-ORF strategy would suffice — the all-ORF window approach yields a very large candidate set (e.g., 14,694 short ORFs across six BGCs in one genome) at the cost of search space The BGC boundaries are already known from prior annotation (e.g., antiSMASH-identified clusters), so fixed 10 kbp enzyme-centered windows add no information Input is raw short reads without assembly — contigs must be produced first, since windows are defined on assembled sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs putative biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) regions in MetaMiner by building a 10 kbp window centered on each RiPP modification enzyme detected with HMMer on six-frame-translated nucleotide contigs. These windows define the search space from which candidate precursor ORFs are extracted. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.09.004
skills.summary: Constructs putative biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) regions in MetaMiner by building a 10 kbp window centered on each RiPP modification enzyme detected with HMMer on six-frame-translated nucleotide contigs. These windows define the search space from which candidate precursor ORFs are extracted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Precursor peptides have sequence similarity to known RiPPs and a more sensitive motif-ORF strategy would suffice — the all-ORF window approach yields a very large candidate set (e.g., 14,694 short ORFs across six BGCs in one genome) at the cost of search space The BGC boundaries are already known from prior annotation (e.g., antiSMASH-identified clusters), so fixed 10 kbp enzyme-centered windows add no information Input is raw short reads without assembly — contigs must be produced first, since windows are defined on assembled sequences

skills.description: Use when you have a set of inferred amplicon sequence variants (e.g., HashSeq sequences.fasta) and need to confirm they match previously observed references by BLASTing against SILVA132 and keeping the top bit-score hit per variant.
skills.name: bit-score-best-hit-selection
skills.search_text: bit-score-best-hit-selection Use when you have a set of inferred amplicon sequence variants (e.g., HashSeq sequences.fasta) and need to confirm they match previously observed references by BLASTing against SILVA132 and keeping the top bit-score hit per variant. Input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been variant-called (pre-process and run inferTrueSequences first) Input is already a taxonomic assignment or feature table rather than variant sequences needing reference validation Variants contain insertions/deletions you care about — HashSeq does not explicitly model indels, so percent identity over a single aligned variant may not capture indel variation; the paper recommends Deblur or alignment-based methods in that case http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Selects, for each HashSeq- or DADA2-inferred 16S rRNA sequence variant, the single best SILVA132 BLASTN hit by top bit score and computes percent identity (identical positions over aligned length) to validate that inferred variants are real biological sequences rather than sequencing errors. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Selects, for each HashSeq- or DADA2-inferred 16S rRNA sequence variant, the single best SILVA132 BLASTN hit by top bit score and computes percent identity (identical positions over aligned length) to validate that inferred variants are real biological sequences rather than sequencing errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been variant-called (pre-process and run inferTrueSequences first) Input is already a taxonomic assignment or feature table rather than variant sequences needing reference validation Variants contain insertions/deletions you care about — HashSeq does not explicitly model indels, so percent identity over a single aligned variant may not capture indel variation; the paper recommends Deblur or alignment-based methods in that case

skills.description: Use when assigning taxonomy to reconstructed viral contigs from metagenomic assemblies using combined nucleotide (BBMap) and translated/protein (DIAMOND) alignments, especially for low-coverage or divergent viruses that defeat read- or kmer-based classifiers.
skills.name: bits-per-base-alignment-scoring
skills.search_text: bits-per-base-alignment-scoring Use when assigning taxonomy to reconstructed viral contigs from metagenomic assemblies using combined nucleotide (BBMap) and translated/protein (DIAMOND) alignments, especially for low-coverage or divergent viruses that defeat read- or kmer-based classifiers. Input is raw reads rather than assembled contigs — the bits-per-base scoring operates on improved contigs, not individual reads The analysis goal is host or non-viral organism classification — this engine explicitly filters to the superkingdom Virus and discards contigs mapping outside it A kmer/read-level classifier (e.g. Kraken-style) suffices — the article targets cases where reads, contigs, or kmers map equally well to different genomes and coverage is too low for confident assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 VirMAP's two-pass taxonomic scoring engine: accumulate maximum bits-per-base scores per taxon in pass one, then compute pass-two relative weights (exponential for nucleotide, tetrational for protein alignments) followed by virus-superkingdom filtering and rank-wise LCA. This enables classification of low-coverage, divergent viral contigs independent of genome coverage or read overlap. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: VirMAP's two-pass taxonomic scoring engine: accumulate maximum bits-per-base scores per taxon in pass one, then compute pass-two relative weights (exponential for nucleotide, tetrational for protein alignments) followed by virus-superkingdom filtering and rank-wise LCA. This enables classification of low-coverage, divergent viral contigs independent of genome coverage or read overlap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than assembled contigs — the bits-per-base scoring operates on improved contigs, not individual reads The analysis goal is host or non-viral organism classification — this engine explicitly filters to the superkingdom Virus and discards contigs mapping outside it A kmer/read-level classifier (e.g. Kraken-style) suffices — the article targets cases where reads, contigs, or kmers map equally well to different genomes and coverage is too low for confident assembly

skills.description: Use when the input is an eBWT file (e.g. reads.fasta.bwt built with BCR_LCP_GSA) of raw sequencing reads and reference-free SNP/INDEL detection requires positional clustering without storing LCP or gSA arrays.
skills.name: bitvector-computation-kmin-kright-localmin
skills.search_text: bitvector-computation-kmin-kright-localmin Use when the input is an eBWT file (e.g. reads.fasta.bwt built with BCR_LCP_GSA) of raw sequencing reads and reference-free SNP/INDEL detection requires positional clustering without storing LCP or gSA arrays. The variant caller is a mapping-based pipeline expecting a reference genome and VCF input rather than an eBWT of raw reads The dataset has not been preprocessed (reads still contain N characters or the reverse-complement was not added, hurting sensitivity) Only the old ebwt2snp workflow is acceptable and the LCP/gSA arrays are available, in which case the LCP-materializing version is applicable directly http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Computes the Kmin, Kright, and localMin bitvectors in a single streaming pass over the extended Burrows-Wheeler Transform (eBWT) of a read collection, by simulating suffix-tree navigation and extracting local LCP minima on-the-fly. This avoids materializing the full LCP array and generalized suffix array, reducing working space by an order of magnitude. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Computes the Kmin, Kright, and localMin bitvectors in a single streaming pass over the extended Burrows-Wheeler Transform (eBWT) of a read collection, by simulating suffix-tree navigation and extracting local LCP minima on-the-fly. This avoids materializing the full LCP array and generalized suffix array, reducing working space by an order of magnitude.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant caller is a mapping-based pipeline expecting a reference genome and VCF input rather than an eBWT of raw reads The dataset has not been preprocessed (reads still contain N characters or the reverse-complement was not added, hurting sensitivity) Only the old ebwt2snp workflow is acceptable and the LCP/gSA arrays are available, in which case the LCP-materializing version is applicable directly

skills.description: Use when building a RawHash-style index or mapping pipeline in which quantized raw-signal event means must be converted into 32-bit hash values for storage in or querying against a hash table.
skills.name: bitwise-hash-packing-of-quantized-events
skills.search_text: bitwise-hash-packing-of-quantized-events Use when building a RawHash-style index or mapping pipeline in which quantized raw-signal event means must be converted into 32-bit hash values for storage in or querying against a hash table. The task is basecalling or base-level alignment — this skill operates purely on quantized event levels and does not recover nucleotide sequences You need full quantization design itself (e.g., RawHash2's dynamically arranged bucket sizes) rather than the downstream bit-packing hash stage Signal-to-reference alignment requires base-level resolution (e.g., DTW signal alignment as in RawAlign), which this hashing stage cannot provide http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Implements the terminal stage of RawHash's signal-to-hash pipeline: compressing the bits of n consecutive quantized nanopore event values (Q-bit trimmed, p-bit pruned) into a single low-collision 32-bit hash value so signals from the same DNA content collide identically. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad272

skills.description: Use when auditing a sequence clustering's sensitivity at a fixed identity threshold (e.g., 50%): you need a BLAST-derived reference of clusterable sequence pairs (≥90% coverage of the shorter sequence) to compute per-tool false-negative fractions.
skills.name: blast-all-against-all-identity-computation
skills.search_text: blast-all-against-all-identity-computation Use when auditing a sequence clustering's sensitivity at a fixed identity threshold (e.g., 50%): you need a BLAST-derived reference of clusterable sequence pairs (≥90% coverage of the shorter sequence) to compute per-tool false-negative fractions. The goal is to produce a production clustering of a large sequence set rather than to validate/benchmark an existing clustering's false-negative rate The sequence set is small enough for exhaustive exact all-against-all comparison, making BLAST-based sampling estimation unnecessary The required coverage convention differs from cov-mode 1 (coverage relative to the shorter sequence), e.g., when coverage must be computed over the full representative length http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark the sensitivity of sequence clustering tools by computing BLAST all-against-all identities among 1000 randomly sampled cluster representatives, filtering to pairs that satisfy the clustering threshold with ≥90% coverage (cov-mode 1), and measuring the fraction of these clusterable pairs each tool missed (false negatives). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-04964-5
skills.summary: Benchmark the sensitivity of sequence clustering tools by computing BLAST all-against-all identities among 1000 randomly sampled cluster representatives, filtering to pairs that satisfy the clustering threshold with ≥90% coverage (cov-mode 1), and measuring the fraction of these clusterable pairs each tool missed (false negatives).

skills.description: Use when a kmer-signature classifier (e.g. PlasFlow) has binned assembly contigs as plasmids and you need sequence-level confirmation against known, manually curated plasmid references.
skills.name: blast-based-sequence-similarity-verification
skills.search_text: blast-based-sequence-similarity-verification Use when a kmer-signature classifier (e.g. PlasFlow) has binned assembly contigs as plasmids and you need sequence-level confirmation against known, manually curated plasmid references. Input contigs have not been classified yet — run PlasFlow.py (--threshold 0.7) on length-filtered (>1000 bp) assembly first; BLAST verification is a downstream confirmation step, not a classifier. No curated plasmid reference sequences exist for the organism/sample, since database-similarity verification depends on matching known references (a limitation of BLAST-based approaches such as PLACNET). Contigs are shorter than 1000 bp — PlasFlow explicitly recommends filtering these out because kmer-based results for short sequences are unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Verify computationally predicted plasmid sequences (e.g. the plasmid bin FASTA produced by PlasFlow at threshold 0.7) by BLAST-searching them against a set of manually curated known plasmids to confirm which predictions are sequence-similar to validated references. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Verify computationally predicted plasmid sequences (e.g. the plasmid bin FASTA produced by PlasFlow at threshold 0.7) by BLAST-searching them against a set of manually curated known plasmids to confirm which predictions are sequence-similar to validated references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contigs have not been classified yet — run PlasFlow.py (--threshold 0.7) on length-filtered (>1000 bp) assembly first; BLAST verification is a downstream confirmation step, not a classifier. No curated plasmid reference sequences exist for the organism/sample, since database-similarity verification depends on matching known references (a limitation of BLAST-based approaches such as PLACNET). Contigs are shorter than 1000 bp — PlasFlow explicitly recommends filtering these out because kmer-based results for short sequences are unreliable.

skills.description: Use when a set of nucleotide sequences (e.g. a FASTA catalogue of ISs) must be classified against a reference database and the goal is a reproducible strict/loose/novel homology split based on BLAST e-value thresholds.
skills.name: blast-evalue-threshold-interpretation
skills.search_text: blast-evalue-threshold-interpretation Use when a set of nucleotide sequences (e.g. a FASTA catalogue of ISs) must be classified against a reference database and the goal is a reproducible strict/loose/novel homology split based on BLAST e-value thresholds. The query sequences are not the nucleotide IS catalogue entries (e.g. protein sequences or non-IS contigs), since the strict/loose e-value bands were calibrated for IS-vs-ISfinder nucleotide queries. The analysis goal requires richer homology evidence than e-value alone (e.g. coverage, percent identity, or transposase-domain annotation), which this binning scheme does not capture. Only a strict-homology judgement is needed at the 0.01 cutoff, i.e. a single-tier hit/miss call, since the two-tier scheme adds overhead without benefit. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Classifies catalogue sequences (here, the 879 insertion sequences of ISC v1.0.0) against a reference database such as ISfinder by binning BLAST e-values into strict hits (e-value <1e-50), loose hits (0.01 > e-value >= 1e-50), and novel (no hit at the 0.01 cutoff), yielding a quantitative homology breakdown. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Classifies catalogue sequences (here, the 879 insertion sequences of ISC v1.0.0) against a reference database such as ISfinder by binning BLAST e-values into strict hits (e-value <1e-50), loose hits (0.01 > e-value >= 1e-50), and novel (no hit at the 0.01 cutoff), yielding a quantitative homology breakdown.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query sequences are not the nucleotide IS catalogue entries (e.g. protein sequences or non-IS contigs), since the strict/loose e-value bands were calibrated for IS-vs-ISfinder nucleotide queries. The analysis goal requires richer homology evidence than e-value alone (e.g. coverage, percent identity, or transposase-domain annotation), which this binning scheme does not capture. Only a strict-homology judgement is needed at the 0.01 cutoff, i.e. a single-tier hit/miss call, since the two-tier scheme adds overhead without benefit.

skills.description: Use when homologous genomic regions must be recovered from per-sample assemblies via BLASTn against a fragmented reference, and each hit needs flanking context for synteny block detection.
skills.name: blast-hit-flanking-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: blast-hit-flanking-sequence-extraction Use when homologous genomic regions must be recovered from per-sample assemblies via BLASTn against a fragmented reference, and each hit needs flanking context for synteny block detection. The goal is SNP-based strain comparison rather than synteny — tools like MIDAS, StrainPhlAn, or inStrain are more appropriate, and SNP-based methods are insensitive to the structural changes SynTracker targets Target sequences do not meet the 97% identity / 70% coverage thresholds or lack ≥2 kbp flanking sequence on both sides — such hits are excluded and cannot support region binning Working with phages/plasmids or low-data contexts requiring no database — while SynTracker suits these, this flanking-extraction step specifically presumes a reference-fragmented BLAST workflow with per-sample assemblies http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extracts BLASTn hits plus fixed 2-kbp flanking sequences on both sides from metagenomic assemblies, binning hit-plus-flank sequences by reference region for downstream synteny scoring in SynTracker. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Extracts BLASTn hits plus fixed 2-kbp flanking sequences on both sides from metagenomic assemblies, binning hit-plus-flank sequences by reference region for downstream synteny scoring in SynTracker.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is SNP-based strain comparison rather than synteny — tools like MIDAS, StrainPhlAn, or inStrain are more appropriate, and SNP-based methods are insensitive to the structural changes SynTracker targets Target sequences do not meet the 97% identity / 70% coverage thresholds or lack ≥2 kbp flanking sequence on both sides — such hits are excluded and cannot support region binning Working with phages/plasmids or low-data contexts requiring no database — while SynTracker suits these, this flanking-extraction step specifically presumes a reference-fragmented BLAST workflow with per-sample assemblies

skills.description: Use when raw 454 metagenomic reads (e.g. human gut microbiome samples TS28/TS50) have gene predictions from multiple callers and an independent, database-grounded estimate of prediction correctness is needed for tool comparison.
skills.name: blast-homology-validation-against-nr
skills.search_text: blast-homology-validation-against-nr Use when raw 454 metagenomic reads (e.g. human gut microbiome samples TS28/TS50) have gene predictions from multiple callers and an independent, database-grounded estimate of prediction correctness is needed for tool comparison. Evaluating predictors on simulated metagenomes where true gene coordinates are known — use nucleotide-level sensitivity/precision against the known truth instead of BLAST validation Input is assembled genomes or complete prokaryotic genomes — the validation problem for short, error-prone metagenomic reads (truncated genes, homopolymer-run indels) does not apply in the same way The analysis goal is functional annotation rather than gene-predictor benchmarking; BLAST hits would then be an end product, not a validation signal http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validates metagenomic gene predictions by translating predicted coding regions and BLAST-searching the translated proteins against the NCBI non-redundant protein database, counting predictions with hits (E < 0.001) as an independent accuracy proxy for Glimmer-MG, FragGeneScan, and MetaGeneMark on real 454 human gut microbiome reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: Validates metagenomic gene predictions by translating predicted coding regions and BLAST-searching the translated proteins against the NCBI non-redundant protein database, counting predictions with hits (E < 0.001) as an independent accuracy proxy for Glimmer-MG, FragGeneScan, and MetaGeneMark on real 454 human gut microbiome reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating predictors on simulated metagenomes where true gene coordinates are known — use nucleotide-level sensitivity/precision against the known truth instead of BLAST validation Input is assembled genomes or complete prokaryotic genomes — the validation problem for short, error-prone metagenomic reads (truncated genes, homopolymer-run indels) does not apply in the same way The analysis goal is functional annotation rather than gene-predictor benchmarking; BLAST hits would then be an end product, not a validation signal

skills.description: Use when running SynTracker strain-tracking analyses and you need to filter BLASTn hits of reference central regions against target assemblies/genomes by identity and coverage thresholds, or when reproducing sensitivity tests over these parameters.
skills.name: blast-identity-coverage-filtering
skills.search_text: blast-identity-coverage-filtering Use when running SynTracker strain-tracking analyses and you need to filter BLASTn hits of reference central regions against target assemblies/genomes by identity and coverage thresholds, or when reproducing sensitivity tests over these parameters. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than metagenomic assemblies or assembled genomes — SynTracker compares assemblies/genomes, not reads, so BLAST-based filtering cannot be applied directly Strains/species are so divergent that homologous central regions fall below the 97% minimal BLAST identity threshold — hits will be filtered out and pairs with fewer than n regions are excluded from downstream analysis You need SNP-level strain discrimination (e.g., popANI-style comparison with inStrain or MIDAS) — SynTracker's synteny approach is explicitly insensitive to SNPs, so identity/coverage filtering here does not capture point-mutation differences http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Apply SynTracker's default BLAST-based filters — minimal 97% identity and 70% query coverage — to retain only high-confidence homologous region hits between a reference genome and target genomes/metagenomes before synteny scoring, plus exclusion of hits lacking ≥2 kbp of flanking sequence on both sides. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Apply SynTracker's default BLAST-based filters — minimal 97% identity and 70% query coverage — to retain only high-confidence homologous region hits between a reference genome and target genomes/metagenomes before synteny scoring, plus exclusion of hits lacking ≥2 kbp of flanking sequence on both sides.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than metagenomic assemblies or assembled genomes — SynTracker compares assemblies/genomes, not reads, so BLAST-based filtering cannot be applied directly Strains/species are so divergent that homologous central regions fall below the 97% minimal BLAST identity threshold — hits will be filtered out and pairs with fewer than n regions are excluded from downstream analysis You need SNP-level strain discrimination (e.g., popANI-style comparison with inStrain or MIDAS) — SynTracker's synteny approach is explicitly insensitive to SNPs, so identity/coverage filtering here does not capture point-mutation differences

skills.search_text: blast-score-ratio-loci-merging Use when constructing a novel wg/cgMLST schema seed from a set of draft or complete genome assemblies and you need to define distinct loci from predicted CDSs via BSR-based similarity clustering. Allele calling against an already-existing schema — use chewBBACA's AlleleCall instead of rebuilding loci from scratch Adapting an external schema from another cg/wgMLST platform (EnteroBase, PubMLST, Ridom) — use PrepExternalSchema Allele definitions must come directly from sequencing reads or an existing nomenclature rather than de novo assembly-derived CDSs (e.g. MentaLiST-style read-based calling is a different approach) http://edamontology.org/topic_3292 Clustering step within chewBBACA's CreateSchema that merges translated CDSs into wg/cgMLST loci using an all-against-all BLASTP search: sequences with BLAST Score Ratio (BSR) >= 0.6 become alleles of the same locus, with the larger allele retained as representative. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000166

skills.description: Use when benchmarking GeneMark-HM run-time on a real metagenome FASTA (~45 Mb) with one CPU, quantifying the BLASTn fraction of wall-clock time against the pan database, or measuring the volume/memory reduction of species-level pan-genomes vs. the non-redundant SGB/tCluster gene set.
skills.name: blastn-database-scanning-profiling
skills.search_text: blastn-database-scanning-profiling Use when benchmarking GeneMark-HM run-time on a real metagenome FASTA (~45 Mb) with one CPU, quantifying the BLASTn fraction of wall-clock time against the pan database, or measuring the volume/memory reduction of species-level pan-genomes vs. the non-redundant SGB/tCluster gene set. Input metagenomes are not from the human microbiome — the pan-genome database was built specifically for human gut, oral, and skin microbiome species, and assignment coverage drops to 89.0% (oral) and 79.4% (skin). You need gene predictions rather than computational-efficiency measurements — this skill benchmarks run-time and database size, it does not evaluate annotation accuracy (use the simulated-metagenome accuracy workflow instead). The pipeline is run multi-threaded — published run-time targets (~12 min vs MetaGeneMark ~10 s and MetaProdigal ~3.5 min) hold only under single-CPU conditions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Profile a GeneMark-HM run to quantify how much of its wall-clock time is spent in the BLASTn similarity scan against the ~20 Gb human microbiome pan-genome database, and benchmark single-CPU run-times against MetaGeneMark and MetaProdigal on a 45 Mb test metagenome. This grounds the paper's computational-efficiency claim that pan-genome construction reduces the GeneMark-HM model database volume/memory by a factor of ~15 (Table 5). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047

This grounds the paper's computational-efficiency claim that pan-genome construction reduces the GeneMark-HM model database volume/memory by a factor of ~15 (Table 5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input metagenomes are not from the human microbiome — the pan-genome database was built specifically for human gut, oral, and skin microbiome species, and assignment coverage drops to 89.0% (oral) and 79.4% (skin). The pipeline is run multi-threaded — published run-time targets (~12 min vs MetaGeneMark ~10 s and MetaProdigal ~3.5 min) hold only under single-CPU conditions.

skills.description: Use when reconstructing latent relative-abundance trajectories from longitudinal OTU/count tables (taxa by samples) where sequencing noise causes technical zeros, and you need efficient posterior inference plus biological-vs-technical zero discrimination.
skills.name: block-tridiagonal-matrix-inference
skills.search_text: block-tridiagonal-matrix-inference Use when reconstructing latent relative-abundance trajectories from longitudinal OTU/count tables (taxa by samples) where sequencing noise causes technical zeros, and you need efficient posterior inference plus biological-vs-technical zero discrimination. Your data are cross-sectional or otherwise non-longitudinal — the model pools information across longitudinal samples via the state-space structure and cannot be applied to single-time-point counts. The OTU table contains ultra-sparse taxa (>90% missing entries); the README recommends filtering these out first, and reconstructing their trajectories yields little information. You need inference under external perturbation dynamics or full gLV parameter prediction — cLV training and prediction are flagged as experimental in the README. LUMINATE's core inference engine: coordinate ascent variational inference for a state-space model of longitudinal microbiome counts, where q(x_1:T) is updated in closed form via a block-tridiagonal precision inverse exploiting O(TD^3) banded structure, q(w_d,1:T) for zero-type indicators is updated with HMM forward-backward recursions, and q(z_1:T) means are optimized by conjugate gradient. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2020.05.006
skills.summary: LUMINATE's core inference engine: coordinate ascent variational inference for a state-space model of longitudinal microbiome counts, where q(x_1:T) is updated in closed form via a block-tridiagonal precision inverse exploiting O(TD^3) banded structure, q(w_d,1:T) for zero-type indicators is updated with HMM forward-backward recursions, and q(z_1:T) means are optimized by conjugate gradient.

skills.search_text: boosted-gam-model-fitting Use when tabular plot-level predictor sets (e.g., Sentinel-1 gamma_0 time-series statistics vs ALS structural metrics) must be compared for modelling biodiversity responses such as NMDS axes, species richness, or phylogenetic diversity with cross-validated regression. The inputs are still raw Sentinel-1 GRDH scenes — this skill consumes plot-level predictor tables produced after the SNAP/GPT gamma_0 processing chain (Apply precise orbit → Remove border noise → Remove thermal noise → Radiometric calibration → Radiometric terrain flattening → Range-doppler terrain correction) and the R pixel/neighbourhood summary statistics. The goal is external validation on independent data collected outside the five training regions (e.g., bird and saproxylic beetle species composition) rather than cross-validated comparison on the training plots. The target is area-wide biodiversity mapping or monitoring of biodiversity change rather than quantifying per-plot predictive power of a predictor set for the 12 functional groups. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Cross-validated boosted generalized additive models (R, mboost/gamboost) that model NMDS1/2 assemblage-composition scores, log-transformed species richness, and phylogenetic diversity for 12 functional groups from either Sentinel-1 gamma_0 time-series predictors or ALS structural predictors. Its five-fold region-grouped CV and out-of-fold R² medians (NMDS1: 0.57 radar vs 0.51 ALS) are the quantitative basis for the paper's claim that radar performs as well as ALS. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x

skills.name: bootstrap-pvalue-network-filtering
skills.search_text: bootstrap-pvalue-network-filtering Use when converting a bootstrapped interaction/correlation matrix from a network inference method (sparcc, propr, spieceasi, flashweave, cozine, harmonies, spring, mldm) into a significant co-occurrence network via Resample bootstraps, per-edge p-values, and threshold filtering. skills.name: bowtie2-alignment-based-read-classification
skills.search_text: bowtie2-alignment-based-read-classification Use when paired or single-end Illumina FASTQ reads from a microbial sample must be screened for human origin: aligning to a host reference index is needed to remove human contamination while retaining bacterial reads. Input is long-read (ONT/PacBio) data — Hostile routes long reads to Minimap2 (13GB RAM) instead of Bowtie2 Maximum viral or phage sequence retention is the priority — use a masked index such as human-t2t-hla.argos-bacteria-985_rs-viral-202401_ml-phage-202401 rather than the unmasked default The goal is masking rather than removing suspected host reads (e.g. NCBI HRRT-style 'N' masking) — alignment-based removal discards aligned reads entirely http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classify sequencing reads as host or non-host by aligning them with Bowtie2 against a human reference index (e.g. human-t2t-hla, T2T-CHM13v2.0 + IPD-IMGT/HLA v3.51) and discarding aligned reads, as implemented in Hostile for short-read decontamination. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad728
skills.summary: Classify sequencing reads as host or non-host by aligning them with Bowtie2 against a human reference index (e.g. human-t2t-hla, T2T-CHM13v2.0 + IPD-IMGT/HLA v3.51) and discarding aligned reads, as implemented in Hostile for short-read decontamination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read (ONT/PacBio) data — Hostile routes long reads to Minimap2 (13GB RAM) instead of Bowtie2 Maximum viral or phage sequence retention is the priority — use a masked index such as human-t2t-hla.argos-bacteria-985_rs-viral-202401_ml-phage-202401 rather than the unmasked default The goal is masking rather than removing suspected host reads (e.g. NCBI HRRT-style 'N' masking) — alignment-based removal discards aligned reads entirely

skills.description: Use when aligning metagenomic reads against a partial or remotely related viral reference (e.g. bat coronavirus NC_014470.1) and you need to choose the read-mapping scoring that yields the richest seed set for overlap-based recruitment.
skills.name: bowtie2-score-min-parameter-sweep
skills.search_text: bowtie2-score-min-parameter-sweep Use when aligning metagenomic reads against a partial or remotely related viral reference (e.g. bat coronavirus NC_014470.1) and you need to choose the read-mapping scoring that yields the richest seed set for overlap-based recruitment. The reference genome is complete and high-quality, so straightforward read mapping suffices without a parameter sweep A completely new virus shares no conservation with any reference genome — TAR-VIR's mapping-based recruiting (and hence this sweep) cannot detect it Reads have not been error-corrected (e.g. with Karect), since TAR-VIR's overlap recruitment relies on exact overlaps http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Sweeps Bowtie2 score-min settings (e.g. 'L,0,-0.6' through 'L,0,-1.2') against BWA mismatch-penalty (-B) settings to find the seed-read alignment that maximizes downstream TAR-VIR overlap recruitment of viral reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2
skills.summary: Sweeps Bowtie2 score-min settings (e.g. 'L,0,-0.6' through 'L,0,-1.2') against BWA mismatch-penalty (-B) settings to find the seed-read alignment that maximizes downstream TAR-VIR overlap recruitment of viral reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference genome is complete and high-quality, so straightforward read mapping suffices without a parameter sweep A completely new virus shares no conservation with any reference genome — TAR-VIR's mapping-based recruiting (and hence this sweep) cannot detect it Reads have not been error-corrected (e.g. with Karect), since TAR-VIR's overlap recruitment relies on exact overlaps

skills.description: Use when decontaminating paired or single short reads (e.g. Illumina 2x150bp) from microbial samples by removing human host reads with Hostile's Bowtie2 mode, or when benchmarking retention of bacterial reads versus human read removal.
skills.name: bowtie2-short-read-alignment
skills.search_text: bowtie2-short-read-alignment Use when decontaminating paired or single short reads (e.g. Illumina 2x150bp) from microbial samples by removing human host reads with Hostile's Bowtie2 mode, or when benchmarking retention of bacterial reads versus human read removal. Input is long-read (ONT) data — use Hostile's Minimap2 mode (-x map-ont preset, --secondary no) instead, which requires ~13GB RAM The goal is masking human reads in place rather than removal — HRRT masks identified spots with 'N' via its k-mer database, a different output paradigm Retention of specific microbial sequences is the priority and the unmasked default index would falsely deplete them — instead use a masked index (e.g. human-t2t-hla-argos985 or the viral/phage-masked index) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Bowtie2-based short-read host decontamination mode of Hostile, aligning paired or single Illumina FASTQ reads against the human-t2t-hla index (T2T-CHM13v2.0 + IPD-IMGT/HLA v3.51) and removing aligned reads to clean microbial metagenomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad728
skills.summary: Bowtie2-based short-read host decontamination mode of Hostile, aligning paired or single Illumina FASTQ reads against the human-t2t-hla index (T2T-CHM13v2.0 + IPD-IMGT/HLA v3.51) and removing aligned reads to clean microbial metagenomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read (ONT) data — use Hostile's Minimap2 mode (-x map-ont preset, --secondary no) instead, which requires ~13GB RAM The goal is masking human reads in place rather than removal — HRRT masks identified spots with 'N' via its k-mer database, a different output paradigm Retention of specific microbial sequences is the priority and the unmasked default index would falsely deplete them — instead use a masked index (e.g. human-t2t-hla-argos985 or the viral/phage-masked index)

skills.description: Use when deep-learning classification of 16S rRNA (or other nucleotide) sequences requires fixed-size tokenized inputs for a transformer trained on the DNABERT-2 BPE vocabulary, e.g. before HybridCNNBERTClassifier inference or training on Greengenes2 FASTA data.
skills.name: bpe-sequence-tokenization
skills.search_text: bpe-sequence-tokenization Use when deep-learning classification of 16S rRNA (or other nucleotide) sequences requires fixed-size tokenized inputs for a transformer trained on the DNABERT-2 BPE vocabulary, e.g. before HybridCNNBERTClassifier inference or training on Greengenes2 FASTA data. Input sequences are meant for the one-hot CNN ablation variant, which replaces DNABERT-2 BPE tokenization with raw one-hot nucleotide encodings Input is a nucleotide count/feature table or non-16S data (e.g. 18S rRNA, shotgun metagenomes) outside DeepTaxa's FASTA-only scope Base-level quality scores must be used, since DeepTaxa operates on FASTA-formatted sequences and does not incorporate quality scores http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Tokenizes 16S rRNA gene sequences into fixed-length inputs for DeepTaxa's transformer pathway using the DNABERT-2 byte-pair-encoding (BPE) vocabulary, truncating or padding each sequence to 512 tokens so the from-scratch BERT encoder and hybrid CNN-BERT heads receive uniform tensor shapes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Tokenizes 16S rRNA gene sequences into fixed-length inputs for DeepTaxa's transformer pathway using the DNABERT-2 byte-pair-encoding (BPE) vocabulary, truncating or padding each sequence to 512 tokens so the from-scratch BERT encoder and hybrid CNN-BERT heads receive uniform tensor shapes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are meant for the one-hot CNN ablation variant, which replaces DNABERT-2 BPE tokenization with raw one-hot nucleotide encodings Input is a nucleotide count/feature table or non-16S data (e.g. 18S rRNA, shotgun metagenomes) outside DeepTaxa's FASTA-only scope Base-level quality scores must be used, since DeepTaxa operates on FASTA-formatted sequences and does not incorporate quality scores

skills.description: Use when you need an abundance-based all-vs-all distance matrix over sequencing samples (reads or assembled contigs) to benchmark abundance-ignoring methods like Mash or normalization-limited methods like Simka.
skills.name: bray-curtis-abundance-distance-calculation
skills.search_text: bray-curtis-abundance-distance-calculation Use when you need an abundance-based all-vs-all distance matrix over sequencing samples (reads or assembled contigs) to benchmark abundance-ignoring methods like Mash or normalization-limited methods like Simka. Input is not raw reads or contigs but an already-computed feature/abundance table where Bray-Curtis can be computed directly without Libra's k-mer indexing The analysis goal is purely composition-based comparison where abundance should be ignored (Mash sketching is the article's comparator) The metric requires normalization to minimum sample depth in a way that collapses low-count contig datasets — the article shows Simka's normalization reduced all assembled-contig samples to the smallest contig count, yielding near-maximum distances http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Computes abundance-aware Bray-Curtis distance matrices between metagenomic samples from k-mer abundance profiles, using Libra's BRAYCURTIS scoring algorithm as a comparison point to its default Cosine Similarity metric. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Computes abundance-aware Bray-Curtis distance matrices between metagenomic samples from k-mer abundance profiles, using Libra's BRAYCURTIS scoring algorithm as a comparison point to its default Cosine Similarity metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw reads or contigs but an already-computed feature/abundance table where Bray-Curtis can be computed directly without Libra's k-mer indexing The analysis goal is purely composition-based comparison where abundance should be ignored (Mash sketching is the article's comparator) The metric requires normalization to minimum sample depth in a way that collapses low-count contig datasets — the article shows Simka's normalization reduced all assembled-contig samples to the smallest contig count, yielding near-maximum distances

skills.description: Use when mock-community 16S data have been taxonomically assigned with alternative reference databases/classifiers and you need a single [0,1] dissimilarity metric per taxonomic level to compare assignment accuracy against a known expected composition.
skills.name: bray-curtis-dissimilarity-computation
skills.search_text: bray-curtis-dissimilarity-computation Use when mock-community 16S data have been taxonomically assigned with alternative reference databases/classifiers and you need a single [0,1] dissimilarity metric per taxonomic level to compare assignment accuracy against a known expected composition. Input is already a co-occurrence network or interaction matrix — MiCoNE handles those separately via Network objects, not via taxonomy-accuracy dissimilarity There is no known expected composition (real environmental samples), so no reference distribution exists to compare against The goal is network-inference step comparison (correlation/direct methods) rather than taxonomy assignment accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A validation-oriented skill for quantifying how accurately 16S taxonomy assignment recaptures expected mock-community composition, by computing Bray-Curtis dissimilarity between predicted and expected taxonomic distributions at Family, Genus, and Species levels (as used in the MiCoNE benchmarking of Greengenes, SILVA, and NCBI RefSeq). metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: A validation-oriented skill for quantifying how accurately 16S taxonomy assignment recaptures expected mock-community composition, by computing Bray-Curtis dissimilarity between predicted and expected taxonomic distributions at Family, Genus, and Species levels (as used in the MiCoNE benchmarking of Greengenes, SILVA, and NCBI RefSeq).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a co-occurrence network or interaction matrix — MiCoNE handles those separately via Network objects, not via taxonomy-accuracy dissimilarity There is no known expected composition (real environmental samples), so no reference distribution exists to compare against The goal is network-inference step comparison (correlation/direct methods) rather than taxonomy assignment accuracy

skills.description: Use when you have a ground-truth presence-absence species composition matrix (plots × species) grouped into taxonomic/functional groups and need assemblage-composition response variables (β-diversity axes) for downstream modelling.
skills.name: bray-curtis-dissimilarity-computation
skills.search_text: bray-curtis-dissimilarity-computation Use when you have a ground-truth presence-absence species composition matrix (plots × species) grouped into taxonomic/functional groups and need assemblage-composition response variables (β-diversity axes) for downstream modelling. The response variable is α-diversity (species richness) or phylogenetic diversity rather than assemblage composition — those were modelled separately in the paper and do not require NMDS ordination Input data are abundance counts or continuous environmental rasters rather than presence-absence species composition per plot — the Bray-Curtis computation as applied here expects presence-absence data Input is already a feature table of remote-sensing predictors (ALS or radar metrics) — this skill only builds the response variables, not the predictor set Quantifies β-diversity of species assemblages by computing Bray-Curtis dissimilarity from a presence-absence composition matrix (463 monitoring plots × twelve functional groups) in R, then running non-metric multidimensional scaling (metaMDS in vegan) so that the resulting NMDS1/NMDS2 site scores can serve as response variables in biodiversity models. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Quantifies β-diversity of species assemblages by computing Bray-Curtis dissimilarity from a presence-absence composition matrix (463 monitoring plots × twelve functional groups) in R, then running non-metric multidimensional scaling (metaMDS in vegan) so that the resulting NMDS1/NMDS2 site scores can serve as response variables in biodiversity models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response variable is α-diversity (species richness) or phylogenetic diversity rather than assemblage composition — those were modelled separately in the paper and do not require NMDS ordination Input data are abundance counts or continuous environmental rasters rather than presence-absence species composition per plot — the Bray-Curtis computation as applied here expects presence-absence data Input is already a feature table of remote-sensing predictors (ALS or radar metrics) — this skill only builds the response variables, not the predictor set

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a k-mer MinHash tool's clustering resolution on 16S amplicon metagenomes is adequate by comparing its sample-cluster visualization against a full k-mer abundance cosine-similarity method.
skills.name: broad-category-cluster-visualization-comparison
skills.search_text: broad-category-cluster-visualization-comparison Use when evaluating whether a k-mer MinHash tool's clustering resolution on 16S amplicon metagenomes is adequate by comparing its sample-cluster visualization against a full k-mer abundance cosine-similarity method. Inputs are whole-genome shotgun (WGS) HMP samples or the CAMI toy PacBio dataset — reproduce the corresponding Fig. 2/4 workflows instead of the 16S amplicon comparison The goal is to test a novel scoring algorithm (e.g. BRAYCURTIS or JENSENSHANNON in Libra) rather than the default COSINESIMILARITY comparison against Mash Samples number in the thousands/millions and a small 48-sample visual check is not the intended deliverable http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces the Libra paper's Fig. 3 comparison of all-vs-all distance matrices (Mash MinHash, Libra cosine similarity, Simka Jaccard-abundance, Simka Bray-Curtis) on 48 matched HMP 16S rRNA amplicon samples, showing that Mash clusters at lower resolution than Libra. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Reproduces the Libra paper's Fig. 3 comparison of all-vs-all distance matrices (Mash MinHash, Libra cosine similarity, Simka Jaccard-abundance, Simka Bray-Curtis) on 48 matched HMP 16S rRNA amplicon samples, showing that Mash clusters at lower resolution than Libra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inputs are whole-genome shotgun (WGS) HMP samples or the CAMI toy PacBio dataset — reproduce the corresponding Fig. 2/4 workflows instead of the 16S amplicon comparison The goal is to test a novel scoring algorithm (e.g. BRAYCURTIS or JENSENSHANNON in Libra) rather than the default COSINESIMILARITY comparison against Mash Samples number in the thousands/millions and a small 48-sample visual check is not the intended deliverable

skills.description: Use when binned contig FASTA files (MAGs) from metagenome binning need per-bin completeness and contamination estimates and assembly QC metrics (contig count, total length, N50).
skills.name: busco-automated-lineage-selection
skills.search_text: busco-automated-lineage-selection Use when binned contig FASTA files (MAGs) from metagenome binning need per-bin completeness and contamination estimates and assembly QC metrics (contig count, total length, N50). Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) rather than binned contig FASTA files — the reads must first go through assembly and binning. The goal is de novo metagenome assembly itself, not assessment of the quality of already-reconstructed MAGs. The bins are viral/plasmid or otherwise lack the near-universal single-copy orthologs BUSCO relies on; an ortholog-based completeness estimate is not meaningful in that regime. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quality-control step of the nf-core/mag pipeline in which binned metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) are assessed with BUSCO's automated lineage selection to estimate completeness and contamination, complemented by QUAST assembly statistics. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Quality-control step of the nf-core/mag pipeline in which binned metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) are assessed with BUSCO's automated lineage selection to estimate completeness and contamination, complemented by QUAST assembly statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) rather than binned contig FASTA files — the reads must first go through assembly and binning. The goal is de novo metagenome assembly itself, not assessment of the quality of already-reconstructed MAGs. The bins are viral/plasmid or otherwise lack the near-universal single-copy orthologs BUSCO relies on; an ortholog-based completeness estimate is not meaningful in that regime.

skills.description: Decision support for routing metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) FASTA bins between GTDB-Tk and CAT/BAT during the taxonomic annotation stage of nf-core/mag, using BUSCO quality summaries as the gate.
skills.name: busco-quality-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: busco-quality-threshold-filtering Decision support for routing metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) FASTA bins between GTDB-Tk and CAT/BAT during the taxonomic annotation stage of nf-core/mag, using BUSCO quality summaries as the gate. Input bins have no BUSCO quality summary available — the routing gate cannot be evaluated without upstream completeness/contamination estimates. The goal is taxonomic classification of contigs or reads rather than assembled MAG bins (CAT/BAT and GTDB-Tk here operate on binned genome FASTAs). The pipeline run is assembly/binning-only; nf-core/mag's functional annotation and bin refinement steps are noted as not yet included, so this skill only concerns the taxonomic annotation stage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A routing step in the nf-core/mag pipeline that gates MAGs by BUSCO-derived completeness and contamination thresholds so that only marker-gene-containing, quality-passing bins go to GTDB-Tk, while all remaining bins are classified with CAT/BAT and both results are merged into mag_taxonomy.tsv. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: A routing step in the nf-core/mag pipeline that gates MAGs by BUSCO-derived completeness and contamination thresholds so that only marker-gene-containing, quality-passing bins go to GTDB-Tk, while all remaining bins are classified with CAT/BAT and both results are merged into mag_taxonomy.tsv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input bins have no BUSCO quality summary available — the routing gate cannot be evaluated without upstream completeness/contamination estimates. The goal is taxonomic classification of contigs or reads rather than assembled MAG bins (CAT/BAT and GTDB-Tk here operate on binned genome FASTAs). The pipeline run is assembly/binning-only; nf-core/mag's functional annotation and bin refinement steps are noted as not yet included, so this skill only concerns the taxonomic annotation stage.

skills.description: Use when you need to profile completeness of MAGs via universal single-copy orthologs, or detect systematic absence of USCO genes (e.g. purine biosynthesis) across a clade of genomes.
skills.name: busco-single-copy-ortholog-profiling
skills.search_text: busco-single-copy-ortholog-profiling Use when you need to profile completeness of MAGs via universal single-copy orthologs, or detect systematic absence of USCO genes (e.g. purine biosynthesis) across a clade of genomes. Input is protein or transcript data rather than genome assemblies — BUSCO must be rerun with the appropriate mode instead of -m genome The goal is general genome quality scoring with CheckM2/CheckM-style completeness only, not per-gene USCO presence/absence inference Studying lineages whose USCO set differs from the bacteria_odb10 124-ortholog prokaryote set (e.g. eukaryotic or viral genomes) http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Run BUSCO in genome mode against the bacteria_odb10 lineage (124 universal single-copy orthologs, USCOs, for prokaryotes) to build a genome-by-USCO presence/absence matrix, used in the VMGC paper to show that Saccharofermentanales genomes lack nine USCO genes, five of which encode de novo purine biosynthesis enzymes. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Run BUSCO in genome mode against the bacteria_odb10 lineage (124 universal single-copy orthologs, USCOs, for prokaryotes) to build a genome-by-USCO presence/absence matrix, used in the VMGC paper to show that Saccharofermentanales genomes lack nine USCO genes, five of which encode de novo purine biosynthesis enzymes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is protein or transcript data rather than genome assemblies — BUSCO must be rerun with the appropriate mode instead of -m genome The goal is general genome quality scoring with CheckM2/CheckM-style completeness only, not per-gene USCO presence/absence inference Studying lineages whose USCO set differs from the bacteria_odb10 124-ortholog prokaryote set (e.g. eukaryotic or viral genomes)

skills.description: Use when reads must be recruited to a target virus via a distant reference genome and you need to sweep BWA mismatch penalties (e.g., -B 1/2/4/8) to build seed-read sets for overlap-based recruitment.
skills.name: bwa-mismatch-penalty-tuning
skills.search_text: bwa-mismatch-penalty-tuning Use when reads must be recruited to a target virus via a distant reference genome and you need to sweep BWA mismatch penalties (e.g., -B 1/2/4/8) to build seed-read sets for overlap-based recruitment. A complete, high-quality reference genome of the target virus is available — plain read mapping suffices and overlap extension is unnecessary The target virus shares no conservation with any reference genome — TAR-VIR cannot detect it Reads are raw and uncorrected — exact overlap detection requires prior error correction (Karect), so penalty tuning would propagate mapping errors http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Tune BWA's mismatch penalty (-B 1, 2, 4, 8) when aligning metagenomic reads against a remotely related viral reference, then feed each SAM into TAR-VIR's overlap recruitment stage to find the seed set that maximizes recruited-read genome coverage rather than raw alignment counts. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2
skills.summary: Tune BWA's mismatch penalty (-B 1, 2, 4, 8) when aligning metagenomic reads against a remotely related viral reference, then feed each SAM into TAR-VIR's overlap recruitment stage to find the seed set that maximizes recruited-read genome coverage rather than raw alignment counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A complete, high-quality reference genome of the target virus is available — plain read mapping suffices and overlap extension is unnecessary The target virus shares no conservation with any reference genome — TAR-VIR cannot detect it Reads are raw and uncorrected — exact overlap detection requires prior error correction (Karect), so penalty tuning would propagate mapping errors

skills.description: Use when the input is an eBWT file (e.g. reads.fasta.bwt) of a raw-read collection and candidate variant intervals have been found, and read contexts flanking each variant must be extracted for variant-fragment assembly without aligning to a reference genome.
skills.name: bwt-backward-search-context-extraction
skills.search_text: bwt-backward-search-context-extraction Use when the input is an eBWT file (e.g. reads.fasta.bwt) of a raw-read collection and candidate variant intervals have been found, and read contexts flanking each variant must be extracted for variant-fragment assembly without aligning to a reference genome. The reads contain 'N' or other non-ACGT symbols and have not been filtered or replaced — the eBWT backward-search workflow assumes DNA fragments with only A, C, G, T A reference genome is available and a standard aligner-and-caller pipeline is acceptable — this skill is specifically for reference-free, alignment-free variant discovery Only the parallel pipeline is desired for INDELs — the parallelization described in the paper works for SNPs only Extracts left and right read contexts around candidate variant positions by performing backward search directly on the extended Burrows-Wheeler Transform (eBWT) using the FL mapping, without materializing the suffix array or LCP array. This enables reference-free assembly of variant fragments for SNP/INDEL detection with roughly one order of magnitude less working space than LCP/GSA-based approaches. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Extracts left and right read contexts around candidate variant positions by performing backward search directly on the extended Burrows-Wheeler Transform (eBWT) using the FL mapping, without materializing the suffix array or LCP array. This enables reference-free assembly of variant fragments for SNP/INDEL detection with roughly one order of magnitude less working space than LCP/GSA-based approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads contain 'N' or other non-ACGT symbols and have not been filtered or replaced — the eBWT backward-search workflow assumes DNA fragments with only A, C, G, T A reference genome is available and a standard aligner-and-caller pipeline is acceptable — this skill is specifically for reference-free, alignment-free variant discovery Only the parallel pipeline is desired for INDELs — the parallelization described in the paper works for SNPs only

skills.description: Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (Illumina or Roche/454) against a protein reference database at taxon level, especially when nucleotide-level k-mer classifiers miss divergent organisms.
skills.name: bwt-backwards-search-mem
skills.search_text: bwt-backwards-search-mem Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (Illumina or Roche/454) against a protein reference database at taxon level, especially when nucleotide-level k-mer classifiers miss divergent organisms. Reads originate predominantly from non-protein-coding genomic regions, where protein-level classification cannot assign them The sequenced strains are already in the reference database with nucleotide sequences, where nucleotide-level classifiers assessing the entire genome are more sensitive Input is already protein sequence and no six-frame translation is wanted (still usable via -p, but the translation-centric workflow does not apply) http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Kaiju's protein-level taxonomic classification via maximum exact matches (MEMs) found with a backwards search on a Burrows-Wheeler transform/FM-index of a reference protein database, assigning reads to NCBI taxa or their least common ancestor. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Kaiju's protein-level taxonomic classification via maximum exact matches (MEMs) found with a backwards search on a Burrows-Wheeler transform/FM-index of a reference protein database, assigning reads to NCBI taxa or their least common ancestor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads originate predominantly from non-protein-coding genomic regions, where protein-level classification cannot assign them The sequenced strains are already in the reference database with nucleotide sequences, where nucleotide-level classifiers assessing the entire genome are more sensitive Input is already protein sequence and no six-frame translation is wanted (still usable via -p, but the translation-centric workflow does not apply)

skills.description: Use when you have a SAM file of reads aligned to a partial or remotely related viral reference (e.g. bat coronavirus NC_014470.1) and need to recruit reads of the true target virus (e.g. SARS-CoV haplotypes) for strain assembly.
skills.name: bwt-based-overlap-read-recruitment
skills.search_text: bwt-based-overlap-read-recruitment Use when you have a SAM file of reads aligned to a partial or remotely related viral reference (e.g. bat coronavirus NC_014470.1) and need to recruit reads of the true target virus (e.g. SARS-CoV haplotypes) for strain assembly. The target virus shares no conservation with any available reference genome — 'A completely new virus that does not share any conservation with any reference genome won't be detected by our method.' Reads are uncorrected and exact overlap detection cannot be trusted (Karect correction is a required preprocessing step). You already have a complete, high-quality reference of the target virus, making direct read mapping more appropriate than overlap-based recruitment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Recruit viral reads from a metagenomic dataset using the TAR-VIR overlap-extension module, which takes a seed-read SAM alignment and a BWT/FM-index of the reads to recruit additional reads sharing exact overlaps with seed reads. It targets viral strain reconstruction from remotely related or partial references. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2
skills.summary: Recruit viral reads from a metagenomic dataset using the TAR-VIR overlap-extension module, which takes a seed-read SAM alignment and a BWT/FM-index of the reads to recruit additional reads sharing exact overlaps with seed reads. It targets viral strain reconstruction from remotely related or partial references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target virus shares no conservation with any available reference genome — 'A completely new virus that does not share any conservation with any reference genome won't be detected by our method.' Reads are uncorrected and exact overlap detection cannot be trusted (Karect correction is a required preprocessing step). You already have a complete, high-quality reference of the target virus, making direct read mapping more appropriate than overlap-based recruitment.

skills.description: Use when raw NGS reads (FASTA/FASTQ) need to be indexed for reference-free, alignment-free variant discovery, and the downstream tool (ebwt2InDel) consumes a .bwt file as input.
skills.name: bwt-construction-of-read-collections
skills.search_text: bwt-construction-of-read-collections Use when raw NGS reads (FASTA/FASTQ) need to be indexed for reference-free, alignment-free variant discovery, and the downstream tool (ebwt2InDel) consumes a .bwt file as input. The downstream analysis needs the full generalized suffix array/LCP anyway (e.g. running the legacy ebwt2snp pipeline) — use egsa or eGap --lcp instead, but expect ~10x more disk (73 GB vs 9.5 GB on a 20x real dataset) Reads still contain 'N' symbols and have not been filtered or randomized — the BWT-based variant pipeline requires fragments containing only 'A', 'C', 'G', 'T' The goal is reference-based variant calling on aligned reads (BAM) — this skill indexes raw reads only, not reference-aligned data http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Build the (extended) Burrows-Wheeler Transform of one or two raw read collections (FASTA/FASTQ) as the sole input structure for reference-free SNP/INDEL discovery with ebwt2InDel, using a multi-string BWT builder such as BCR (BCR_LCP_GSA), eGSA, or eGap instead of constructing the heavier GSA/LCP arrays. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Build the (extended) Burrows-Wheeler Transform of one or two raw read collections (FASTA/FASTQ) as the sole input structure for reference-free SNP/INDEL discovery with ebwt2InDel, using a multi-string BWT builder such as BCR (BCR_LCP_GSA), eGSA, or eGap instead of constructing the heavier GSA/LCP arrays.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream analysis needs the full generalized suffix array/LCP anyway (e.g. running the legacy ebwt2snp pipeline) — use egsa or eGap --lcp instead, but expect ~10x more disk (73 GB vs 9.5 GB on a 20x real dataset) Reads still contain 'N' symbols and have not been filtered or randomized — the BWT-based variant pipeline requires fragments containing only 'A', 'C', 'G', 'T' The goal is reference-based variant calling on aligned reads (BAM) — this skill indexes raw reads only, not reference-aligned data

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is INDEL detection with the parallel pipeline — the parallel version works for SNPs only because HARC pre-processing does not account for INDELs in the read set Input is already an indexed or aligned dataset (BAM/CRAM or a precomputed BWT), since the skill profiles construction time from raw reads only Timing the sequential variant-detection step without excluding eBWT computation, which the paper explicitly excludes from the reported computational cost of EBWT2INDEL

skills.description: Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (FASTQ/FASTA, Illumina or Roche/454) to NCBI taxa at the protein level, especially when k-mer classifiers like Kraken or Clark would need 65–78 GB of RAM but only a standard PC is available.
skills.name: bwt-fm-index-alignment
skills.search_text: bwt-fm-index-alignment Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (FASTQ/FASTA, Illumina or Roche/454) to NCBI taxa at the protein level, especially when k-mer classifiers like Kraken or Clark would need 65–78 GB of RAM but only a standard PC is available. Reads originate from non-protein-coding genomic regions — protein-level classification cannot assign them, so nucleotide-level classifiers are preferable The sequenced strains are already present in the reference database — nucleotide-level classifiers assessing the entire genome (e.g., as seen on the HiSeq and MiSeq data sets) are more sensitive Taxon identifiers in the custom database FASTA headers are not contained in nodes.dmp/names.dmp, or sequences contain characters other than the 20 uppercase standard amino acids http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Protein-level metagenomic read classification by finding maximum (in-)exact matches via a backwards search in the Burrows-Wheeler transform and FM-index, as implemented in Kaiju, enabling millions of reads per minute on a standard PC with under 6 GB of memory. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Protein-level metagenomic read classification by finding maximum (in-)exact matches via a backwards search in the Burrows-Wheeler transform and FM-index, as implemented in Kaiju, enabling millions of reads per minute on a standard PC with under 6 GB of memory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads originate from non-protein-coding genomic regions — protein-level classification cannot assign them, so nucleotide-level classifiers are preferable The sequenced strains are already present in the reference database — nucleotide-level classifiers assessing the entire genome (e.g., as seen on the HiSeq and MiSeq data sets) are more sensitive Taxon identifiers in the custom database FASTA headers are not contained in nodes.dmp/names.dmp, or sequences contain characters other than the 20 uppercase standard amino acids

skills.description: Use when a SAM seed alignment and a FASTA read set must be searched for read–read overlaps via an FM-index, e.g. to expand a small seed set before de novo haplotype assembly with TAR-VIR/PEHaplo.
skills.name: bwt-fm-index-construction-for-reads
skills.search_text: bwt-fm-index-construction-for-reads Use when a SAM seed alignment and a FASTA read set must be searched for read–read overlaps via an FM-index, e.g. to expand a small seed set before de novo haplotype assembly with TAR-VIR/PEHaplo. The target virus shares no conservation with any available reference genome — TAR-VIR's read classification stage cannot detect such a virus, so no seed SAM can be produced The task is de novo haplotype assembly rather than read recruitment — use PEHaplo directly instead of building the overlap-extension index The read set has not been error-corrected (e.g. with karect) — uncorrected errors undermine overlap-based recruitment http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Builds a BWT/FM-index (a generalized suffix array over the concatenated reads) with TAR-VIR's Overlap_extension 'build' binary so that overlap detection between seed queries and the full read set is efficient during overlap-extension read recruitment. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2
skills.summary: Builds a BWT/FM-index (a generalized suffix array over the concatenated reads) with TAR-VIR's Overlap_extension 'build' binary so that overlap detection between seed queries and the full read set is efficient during overlap-extension read recruitment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target virus shares no conservation with any available reference genome — TAR-VIR's read classification stage cannot detect such a virus, so no seed SAM can be produced The task is de novo haplotype assembly rather than read recruitment — use PEHaplo directly instead of building the overlap-extension index The read set has not been error-corrected (e.g. with karect) — uncorrected errors undermine overlap-based recruitment

skills.description: Use when reimplementing or tuning Kraken-style exact k-mer/LCA lookup over a minimizer-partitioned database and you classify consecutive k-mers of a read, so the prior query's range can be searched before recomputing the M=15 minimizer.
skills.name: cached-query-range-optimization
skills.search_text: cached-query-range-optimization Use when reimplementing or tuning Kraken-style exact k-mer/LCA lookup over a minimizer-partitioned database and you classify consecutive k-mers of a read, so the prior query's range can be searched before recomputing the M=15 minimizer. Random-access queries of isolated k-mers (e.g., database validation sampling) where consecutive k-mers rarely share a minimizer — the cached range gives no benefit and a fresh index lookup is simpler A k-mer store that is not partitioned by minimizer with an offset/length index (e.g., a plain sorted k-mer table), since the cached range would not bound valid records for the query http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Kraken's optimization for its minimizer-indexed k-mer/LCA database: after answering a k-mer query, the previous database range is cached, and subsequent queries first search that range and skip minimizer recomputation when the 15-bp minimizer is unchanged. This exploits the locality of consecutive k-mers within one read to avoid repeated index lookups. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Kraken's optimization for its minimizer-indexed k-mer/LCA database: after answering a k-mer query, the previous database range is cached, and subsequent queries first search that range and skip minimizer recomputation when the 15-bp minimizer is unchanged. This exploits the locality of consecutive k-mers within one read to avoid repeated index lookups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Random-access queries of isolated k-mers (e.g., database validation sampling) where consecutive k-mers rarely share a minimizer — the cached range gives no benefit and a fresh index lookup is simpler A k-mer store that is not partitioned by minimizer with an offset/length index (e.g., a plain sorted k-mer table), since the cached range would not bound valid records for the query

skills.search_text: canonical-kmer-representation-xor-scrambling Reference for implementing or reproducing Kraken-style minimizer indexing: when building a k-mer/LCA database that groups k-mers by 15-bp minimizers and needs a fast index-lookup-plus-binary-search query path. When the input k-mers contain ambiguous nucleotides — Kraken ignores k-mers with ambiguous nucleotides, so they do not participate in classification When alignment-based sensitivity is required for sequences with no exact k-mer matches — exact-match database queries, not inexact alignment, underpin this skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Kraken's technique for computing evenly distributed minimizers: the canonical representation of each M-mer (M=15) is XOR-toggled on half its bits before lexicographical comparison, so that k-mer records grouped by minimizer form balanced blocks that support index lookup plus binary search for per-k-mer LCA queries. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads (isolates or metagenomes) must be screened for CRISPR arrays and cas operons without performing a complete de novo genome assembly, e.g. for phage-susceptibility assessment.
skills.name: cas-operon-targeted-assembly
skills.search_text: cas-operon-targeted-assembly Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads (isolates or metagenomes) must be screened for CRISPR arrays and cas operons without performing a complete de novo genome assembly, e.g. for phage-susceptibility assessment. The question requires whole-genome de novo assembly or genome-wide annotation beyond CRISPR/Cas loci—CasCollect only assembles genomic regions seeded by cas HMM matches or CRISPR repeats. The input is already assembled contigs rather than raw short reads; run CRISPRCasFinder (or similar) directly on the assemblies instead. skills.name: cgmlst-allele-calling
skills.search_text: cgmlst-allele-calling Use when you have draft/complete genome FASTA assemblies and a defined MLST schema (schema_seed) and need to determine allelic profiles, identify known/novel alleles, or scale calling to hundreds/thousands of assemblies.
