skills.search_text: cross-assembly-diploid-overlap-analysis Use when multiple Supernova2 assemblies exist for the same sample and you need per-assembly diploid/hemizygous/uncovered fractions plus cross-assembly diploid overlap percentages. Input is simulated Linked-Read data rather than real assemblies evaluated against hg38 (use the LRTK-SIM gold-standard path instead) Only a single assembly is available, so cross-assembly diploid overlap cannot be computed Assemblies are not from Supernova2 phase blocks (e.g. PacBio/ONT haplotig-style assemblies), since megabubble haplotype scaffold extraction is Supernova2-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quantifies how much of the human genome is recovered in a diploid state by 10x Linked-Read Supernova2 assemblies and measures diploid-region overlap across independently generated assemblies of the same cell line (NA12878, NA24385). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Quantifies how much of the human genome is recovered in a diploid state by 10x Linked-Read Supernova2 assemblies and measures diploid-region overlap across independently generated assemblies of the same cell line (NA12878, NA24385).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is simulated Linked-Read data rather than real assemblies evaluated against hg38 (use the LRTK-SIM gold-standard path instead) Only a single assembly is available, so cross-assembly diploid overlap cannot be computed Assemblies are not from Supernova2 phase blocks (e.g. PacBio/ONT haplotig-style assemblies), since megabubble haplotype scaffold extraction is Supernova2-specific

skills.description: Use when comparing two or more 16S rRNA gene variant callers on the same data set and you need to show their variant tables give near-equivalent supervised classification/association performance against metadata variables.
skills.name: cross-caller-variant-performance-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-caller-variant-performance-comparison Use when comparing two or more 16S rRNA gene variant callers on the same data set and you need to show their variant tables give near-equivalent supervised classification/association performance against metadata variables. Detecting true low-abundance sequence variants is the goal — the article notes HashSeq is not sensitive for low-abundance sequences and recommends DADA2 instead The study involves indel variation relative to a parent sequence or long-read technologies such as PacBio, where HashSeq's one-mismatch, no-indel assumptions fail Input is raw FASTQ rather than per-caller variant count tables — variant calling (e.g., inferTrueSequences) must be run first http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks whether sequence variant callers (HashSeq vs. DADA2, with Deblur and Unoise2 as comparators) yield comparable downstream association performance by training random forest classifiers on each caller's variant count table and comparing cross-validated performance for gut microbiota metadata variables. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Benchmarks whether sequence variant callers (HashSeq vs. DADA2, with Deblur and Unoise2 as comparators) yield comparable downstream association performance by training random forest classifiers on each caller's variant count table and comparing cross-validated performance for gut microbiota metadata variables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Detecting true low-abundance sequence variants is the goal — the article notes HashSeq is not sensitive for low-abundance sequences and recommends DADA2 instead The study involves indel variation relative to a parent sequence or long-read technologies such as PacBio, where HashSeq's one-mismatch, no-indel assumptions fail Input is raw FASTQ rather than per-caller variant count tables — variant calling (e.g., inferTrueSequences) must be run first

skills.description: Use when a newly built gene catalogue must be benchmarked against a published catalogue by reciprocal gene-level similarity search, to report directional coverage percentages and catalogue expansion.
skills.name: cross-catalogue-gene-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-catalogue-gene-overlap-analysis Use when a newly built gene catalogue must be benchmarked against a published catalogue by reciprocal gene-level similarity search, to report directional coverage percentages and catalogue expansion. The comparison target is genome-level or taxonomic overlap (e.g. Kraken2/Bracken profiling against SGBs), not protein-coding gene-set overlap. The two catalogues use incompatible gene prediction or clustering units (e.g. nucleotide contigs vs 95%-identity clusters) so identity/coverage thresholds are not comparable. You need novel gene discovery rather than a benchmark against an existing catalogue (use de novo clustering at 50/90/95% identity instead). http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Quantifies mutual gene coverage between two protein-coding gene catalogues (here VMGC-90 versus the published VIRGO-90 vaginal catalogue) by all-vs-all sequence search at fixed identity/coverage thresholds, yielding directional overlap fractions and a protein-space expansion statistic (Fig. 6b: 70.6%, 30.8%, 162%). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Quantifies mutual gene coverage between two protein-coding gene catalogues (here VMGC-90 versus the published VIRGO-90 vaginal catalogue) by all-vs-all sequence search at fixed identity/coverage thresholds, yielding directional overlap fractions and a protein-space expansion statistic (Fig. 6b: 70.6%, 30.8%, 162%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison target is genome-level or taxonomic overlap (e.g. Kraken2/Bracken profiling against SGBs), not protein-coding gene-set overlap. The two catalogues use incompatible gene prediction or clustering units (e.g. nucleotide contigs vs 95%-identity clusters) so identity/coverage thresholds are not comparable. You need novel gene discovery rather than a benchmark against an existing catalogue (use de novo clustering at 50/90/95% identity instead).

skills.description: Use when multiple metagenomic classifiers have been run on admixture/quantification samples containing cross-reacting species pairs, and you need to extract per-tool false-positive percentages and compute relative FP-reduction factors.
skills.name: cross-classifier-benchmark-table-construction
skills.search_text: cross-classifier-benchmark-table-construction Use when multiple metagenomic classifiers have been run on admixture/quantification samples containing cross-reacting species pairs, and you need to extract per-tool false-positive percentages and compute relative FP-reduction factors. The benchmark has only one classifier (no competitor output to compute FP-reduction factors against). The samples contain no closely related cross-reacting species pairs, so cross-reactivity FP rates are not the quantity of interest. You need quantification accuracy (true-abundance error) rather than false-positive cross-reactivity, which requires a different comparison table. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Builds a structured false-positive comparison table quantifying cross-reactivity of closely related species pairs (water buffalo vs. cattle, goat vs. sheep) across AFS-MetaCache, CLARK, Kraken2, and Kraken2+Bracken in all-food-sequencing admixture benchmarks, and computes the FP-reduction factor of AFS-MetaCache relative to each competitor (~4–10x on the Klyo samples). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Builds a structured false-positive comparison table quantifying cross-reactivity of closely related species pairs (water buffalo vs. cattle, goat vs. sheep) across AFS-MetaCache, CLARK, Kraken2, and Kraken2+Bracken in all-food-sequencing admixture benchmarks, and computes the FP-reduction factor of AFS-MetaCache relative to each competitor (~4–10x on the Klyo samples).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The benchmark has only one classifier (no competitor output to compute FP-reduction factors against). The samples contain no closely related cross-reacting species pairs, so cross-reactivity FP rates are not the quantity of interest. You need quantification accuracy (true-abundance error) rather than false-positive cross-reactivity, which requires a different comparison table.

skills.description: Use when the same OTU representative sequences have been taxonomically assigned with multiple reference databases and you need to quantify assignment concordance per taxonomic level (Phylum through Species).
skills.name: cross-database-taxonomic-similarity-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-database-taxonomic-similarity-analysis Use when the same OTU representative sequences have been taxonomically assigned with multiple reference databases and you need to quantify assignment concordance per taxonomic level (Phylum through Species). You only have a single taxonomic assignment (one reference database) — there is no second table to compare, so pairwise similarity is undefined Your goal is OTU picking or denoising rather than evaluating assignment concordance — use the MiCoNE OTU assignment (dada2/deblur/closed-reference gg_97) step instead Your sequences are shotgun metagenomic reads rather than 16S amplicon representatives — the MiCoNE TA step and this comparison are built for 16S data http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Quantifies how much taxonomic assignments of the same OTU representative sequences disagree when three 16S reference databases (Greengenes, SILVA, NCBI RefSeq) are used, by computing pairwise similarity of the top-100 most abundant taxa at each taxonomic level. It exposes reference-database choice as a major variance source in 16S pipelines such as MiCoNE. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: Quantifies how much taxonomic assignments of the same OTU representative sequences disagree when three 16S reference databases (Greengenes, SILVA, NCBI RefSeq) are used, by computing pairwise similarity of the top-100 most abundant taxa at each taxonomic level. It exposes reference-database choice as a major variance source in 16S pipelines such as MiCoNE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single taxonomic assignment (one reference database) — there is no second table to compare, so pairwise similarity is undefined Your goal is OTU picking or denoising rather than evaluating assignment concordance — use the MiCoNE OTU assignment (dada2/deblur/closed-reference gg_97) step instead Your sequences are shotgun metagenomic reads rather than 16S amplicon representatives — the MiCoNE TA step and this comparison are built for 16S data

skills.description: Use when a newly assembled viral genome catalogue (e.g. 14,224 quality-filtered genomes >=50% CheckV completeness) must be dereplicated into vOTUs and its novelty estimated against existing virome reference databases.
skills.name: cross-database-virome-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-database-virome-overlap-analysis Use when a newly assembled viral genome catalogue (e.g. 14,224 quality-filtered genomes >=50% CheckV completeness) must be dereplicated into vOTUs and its novelty estimated against existing virome reference databases. Input viral genomes are already dereplicated vOTUs or a published catalogue's representative set — reclustering would change the unit of comparison The comparator databases are gut/oral-focused catalogues but your study question is strain-level overlap rather than database-absence novelty — BLASTn presence/absence is too coarse Viral contigs have not passed completeness quality filtering (>=50% by CheckV), which would inflate the novel-vOTU count with fragments http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Quantifies the novelty of a newly assembled viral genome catalogue by clustering its genomes into vOTUs (95% nucleotide identity over 85% of the genome) and cross-referencing vOTU representatives via BLASTn against established virome databases, reporting the fraction absent from all of them. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Quantifies the novelty of a newly assembled viral genome catalogue by clustering its genomes into vOTUs (95% nucleotide identity over 85% of the genome) and cross-referencing vOTU representatives via BLASTn against established virome databases, reporting the fraction absent from all of them.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input viral genomes are already dereplicated vOTUs or a published catalogue's representative set — reclustering would change the unit of comparison The comparator databases are gut/oral-focused catalogues but your study question is strain-level overlap rather than database-absence novelty — BLASTn presence/absence is too coarse Viral contigs have not passed completeness quality filtering (>=50% by CheckV), which would inflate the novel-vOTU count with fragments

skills.description: Use when a biomarker-discovery pipeline (e.g. CAMAMED with cumulative sum-scaling and metagenomeSeq) has produced case-control marker taxa/genes from one metagenome dataset and an independent dataset from the same study context is available to test whether the markers reproduce.
skills.name: cross-dataset-biomarker-reproducibility-assessment
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-biomarker-reproducibility-assessment Use when a biomarker-discovery pipeline (e.g. CAMAMED with cumulative sum-scaling and metagenomeSeq) has produced case-control marker taxa/genes from one metagenome dataset and an independent dataset from the same study context is available to test whether the markers reproduce. The analysis goal is taxonomic/functional profiling itself rather than validating whether discovered biomarkers reproduce across datasets Only a single dataset is available — no independent second cohort exists to test cross-dataset marker consistency The count tables are already normalized or derived from RNA-seq-style workflows; metagenomeSeq's zero-inflated log-normal model with CSS is designed for sparse metagenomic count data and CAMAMED's compositional correction would not be appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Validates metagenomic case-control biomarker discoveries by rerunning the CSS-corrected metagenomeSeq differential abundance analysis on a second, independent dataset (taxon and gene levels) and comparing marker-set overlap against uncorrected analyses, which confirms that compositional correction — not dataset-specific noise — drives the findings. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Validates metagenomic case-control biomarker discoveries by rerunning the CSS-corrected metagenomeSeq differential abundance analysis on a second, independent dataset (taxon and gene levels) and comparing marker-set overlap against uncorrected analyses, which confirms that compositional correction — not dataset-specific noise — drives the findings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is taxonomic/functional profiling itself rather than validating whether discovered biomarkers reproduce across datasets Only a single dataset is available — no independent second cohort exists to test cross-dataset marker consistency The count tables are already normalized or derived from RNA-seq-style workflows; metagenomeSeq's zero-inflated log-normal model with CSS is designed for sparse metagenomic count data and CAMAMED's compositional correction would not be appropriate

skills.description: Use when a pipeline's paper or documentation points to a deposited output archive (e.g., figshare doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.20424705) and you need to verify that your rerun reproduces the reference report structure and figures.
skills.name: cross-deposit-output-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-deposit-output-comparison Use when a pipeline's paper or documentation points to a deposited output archive (e.g., figshare doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.20424705) and you need to verify that your rerun reproduces the reference report structure and figures. No deposited reference output exists for the pipeline version you ran — there is nothing to diff against and validation must rely on internal checks instead You only need a single analysis result (e.g., one vOTU count) and not a report-structure comparison — inspecting the specific output file directly is simpler The deposited archive version differs substantially from your pipeline version (e.g., dev branch with updated miners), making panel-level comparison misleading http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Validates a locally regenerated analysis (e.g., a MetaPhage HTML report for the VLP dataset) by structurally and visually comparing it against the authors' deposited full output on figshare, confirming that every expected report panel and key figure reproduces. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Validates a locally regenerated analysis (e.g., a MetaPhage HTML report for the VLP dataset) by structurally and visually comparing it against the authors' deposited full output on figshare, confirming that every expected report panel and key figure reproduces.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No deposited reference output exists for the pipeline version you ran — there is nothing to diff against and validation must rely on internal checks instead You only need a single analysis result (e.g., one vOTU count) and not a report-structure comparison — inspecting the specific output file directly is simpler The deposited archive version differs substantially from your pipeline version (e.g., dev branch with updated miners), making panel-level comparison misleading

skills.description: Decision support for choosing a taxonomic profiling tool and reference database when in silico ground-truth data (e.g. CAMI) are available and per-tool performance must be compared across multiple environments or sampling groups.
skills.name: cross-environment-profiler-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-environment-profiler-comparison-analysis Decision support for choosing a taxonomic profiling tool and reference database when in silico ground-truth data (e.g. CAMI) are available and per-tool performance must be compared across multiple environments or sampling groups. Input consists of real (non-simulated) metagenomic data without ground truth — no true positives can be defined, so binary classification metrics cannot be computed (the article notes real data may contain many more unknowns) Input is raw sequencing reads rather than already-produced profiler output profiles that can be converted to CAMI format The goal is ARG abundance quantification rather than taxonomic profiler benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark multiple metagenomic taxonomic profilers (e.g. KMA with different reference databases, MetaPhlAn 4, mOTUs 3, Bracken 2.8/Kraken2) on CAMI in silico datasets by computing OPAL-style binary classification metrics (Purity, Completeness, F1) per taxonomic level and per sampling group, to select the best profiler–database combination. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple metagenomic taxonomic profilers (e.g. KMA with different reference databases, MetaPhlAn 4, mOTUs 3, Bracken 2.8/Kraken2) on CAMI in silico datasets by computing OPAL-style binary classification metrics (Purity, Completeness, F1) per taxonomic level and per sampling group, to select the best profiler–database combination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of real (non-simulated) metagenomic data without ground truth — no true positives can be defined, so binary classification metrics cannot be computed (the article notes real data may contain many more unknowns) Input is raw sequencing reads rather than already-produced profiler output profiles that can be converted to CAMI format The goal is ARG abundance quantification rather than taxonomic profiler benchmarking

skills.description: Use when you have closed-reference 16S OTU tables from multiple habitat types (e.g. mammal gut, soil, hypersaline mat) plus matched shotgun metagenomes, and need to test whether prediction accuracy decays with phylogenetic distance to reference genomes.
skills.name: cross-habitat-microbiome-validation-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-habitat-microbiome-validation-comparison Use when you have closed-reference 16S OTU tables from multiple habitat types (e.g. mammal gut, soil, hypersaline mat) plus matched shotgun metagenomes, and need to test whether prediction accuracy decays with phylogenetic distance to reference genomes. Your community's NSTI is very high (distant from any sequenced reference genome) — the paper shows accuracy decays with NSTI and recommends NSTI be used to qualify expected accuracy rather than trust predictions unconditionally The community contains viral or eukaryotic components you hope to recover — PICRUSt only covers bacterial and archaeal 16S marker gene sequences You need strain-level resolution — PICRUSt cannot distinguish variation at the strain level when the marker gene sequence is identical among strains http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmark PICRUSt metagenome-prediction accuracy across host-associated and environmental microbiomes by regressing per-sample prediction accuracy against NSTI, the abundance-weighted phylogenetic distance to the nearest sequenced reference genome on the 16S marker tree. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Benchmark PICRUSt metagenome-prediction accuracy across host-associated and environmental microbiomes by regressing per-sample prediction accuracy against NSTI, the abundance-weighted phylogenetic distance to the nearest sequenced reference genome on the 16S marker tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your community's NSTI is very high (distant from any sequenced reference genome) — the paper shows accuracy decays with NSTI and recommends NSTI be used to qualify expected accuracy rather than trust predictions unconditionally The community contains viral or eukaryotic components you hope to recover — PICRUSt only covers bacterial and archaeal 16S marker gene sequences You need strain-level resolution — PICRUSt cannot distinguish variation at the strain level when the marker gene sequence is identical among strains

skills.description: Use when a sink community's origins must be quantified and validated by benchmarking a new source tracking method (STENSL) against a baseline (SourceTracker2) on the exact same candidate source set, e.g., 88 HMP individuals across 15 body sites.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-comparison Use when a sink community's origins must be quantified and validated by benchmarking a new source tracking method (STENSL) against a baseline (SourceTracker2) on the exact same candidate source set, e.g., 88 HMP individuals across 15 body sites. The goal is method development or simulation benchmarking rather than reproducing a published real-data analysis on a fixed sink-source configuration Candidate source environments are few and known a priori (no 'source exploration' problem) — plain FEAST estimation without cross-method comparison is sufficient The input already contains per-source mixing proportions from one method only, with no second method run on the identical configuration http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Runs two or more microbial source tracking methods (here STENSL and SourceTracker2) on an identical sink-source configuration and compares estimated mixing proportions against published reference values, to quantify how much of a sink (e.g., HMP saliva) is attributed to focal-source environments. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00995-21
skills.summary: Runs two or more microbial source tracking methods (here STENSL and SourceTracker2) on an identical sink-source configuration and compares estimated mixing proportions against published reference values, to quantify how much of a sink (e.g., HMP saliva) is attributed to focal-source environments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is method development or simulation benchmarking rather than reproducing a published real-data analysis on a fixed sink-source configuration Candidate source environments are few and known a priori (no 'source exploration' problem) — plain FEAST estimation without cross-method comparison is sufficient The input already contains per-source mixing proportions from one method only, with no second method run on the identical configuration

skills.description: Use when a binning/clustering tool must be benchmarked against published baselines on mock data with known per-contig genome labels, requiring recomputation of metrics (F-score, ARI, NMI, homogeneity) and vMAG quality counts.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-recomputation
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-recomputation Use when a binning/clustering tool must be benchmarked against published baselines on mock data with known per-contig genome labels, requiring recomputation of metrics (F-score, ARI, NMI, homogeneity) and vMAG quality counts. When no ground-truth genome labels exist for the contigs — the article notes true labels of viral contigs in real datasets are unknown, so metrics like the fraction of spurious host-proximity contacts cannot be computed When evaluating HiCBin for viral contigs — TAXAassign can hardly annotate viral contigs, so HiCBin cannot bin them and is not a valid comparator here When the goal is virus-host pair detection or CRISPR-based validation rather than binning performance benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Recompute and compare clustering/binning performance metrics across multiple methods on a shared mock benchmark with ground-truth genome labels, as done for ViralCC vs. VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, and MetaTOR on the 1010 mock viral contigs of the mock human gut Hi-C dataset. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Recompute and compare clustering/binning performance metrics across multiple methods on a shared mock benchmark with ground-truth genome labels, as done for ViralCC vs. VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, and MetaTOR on the 1010 mock viral contigs of the mock human gut Hi-C dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no ground-truth genome labels exist for the contigs — the article notes true labels of viral contigs in real datasets are unknown, so metrics like the fraction of spurious host-proximity contacts cannot be computed When evaluating HiCBin for viral contigs — TAXAassign can hardly annotate viral contigs, so HiCBin cannot bin them and is not a valid comparator here When the goal is virus-host pair detection or CRISPR-based validation rather than binning performance benchmarking

skills.description: Use when evaluating a new unsupervised DNA sequence clustering tool and you need a fair, like-for-like accuracy comparison against specialized (DeLUCS, MeShClust v3.0) and classical (k-means++) baselines on unbalanced multi-genome datasets.
skills.name: cross-method-clustering-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-clustering-comparison Use when evaluating a new unsupervised DNA sequence clustering tool and you need a fair, like-for-like accuracy comparison against specialized (DeLUCS, MeShClust v3.0) and classical (k-means++) baselines on unbalanced multi-genome datasets. Sequences require alignment or taxonomic identifiers for the analysis goal — iDeLUCS is explicitly an alignment-free method that clusters genomic signatures without either The dataset is a single-cluster or trivially separable dataset where a hyperparameter-matched three-way benchmark adds no information You need a clustering method that automatically discovers the number of clusters (k-means++ with k=8 and iDeLUCS n_clusters>=8 both require the true cluster count to be known or upper-bounded) http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark a deep-learning DNA sequence clustering method (iDeLUCS) head-to-head against a specialized DNA clustering baseline (DeLUCS) and a classical baseline (k-means++) on identical k-mer-encoded inputs, scoring all methods with unsupervised clustering accuracy against held-out ground truth. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad508
skills.summary: Benchmark a deep-learning DNA sequence clustering method (iDeLUCS) head-to-head against a specialized DNA clustering baseline (DeLUCS) and a classical baseline (k-means++) on identical k-mer-encoded inputs, scoring all methods with unsupervised clustering accuracy against held-out ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences require alignment or taxonomic identifiers for the analysis goal — iDeLUCS is explicitly an alignment-free method that clusters genomic signatures without either The dataset is a single-cluster or trivially separable dataset where a hyperparameter-matched three-way benchmark adds no information You need a clustering method that automatically discovers the number of clusters (k-means++ with k=8 and iDeLUCS n_clusters>=8 both require the true cluster count to be known or upper-bounded)

skills.description: Use when two genotype-based antibiotic-resistance prediction tools must be compared on the same isolates and phenotypic DST labels, e.g. per-drug sensitivity of Mykrobe vs. KvarQ on first-line TB drugs.
skills.name: cross-method-diagnostic-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-diagnostic-comparison Use when two genotype-based antibiotic-resistance prediction tools must be compared on the same isolates and phenotypic DST labels, e.g. per-drug sensitivity of Mykrobe vs. KvarQ on first-line TB drugs. Estimating false-negative rates for a drug with ≤10 resistant samples in the validation set — the article only estimated FNRs where '>10 resistant samples' were available Comparing methods for pyrazinamide — known mutations are poorly predictive and the drug was completely excluded from the M. tuberculosis panel Reproducing a comparator like SeqSphere whose gene-panel template was not publicly released, making the comparison non-reproducible http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Head-to-head benchmarking of genotypic resistance-prediction methods (Mykrobe predictor vs. KvarQ) on the same independent validation set, computing per-drug sensitivities so the two tools' performances can be compared side by side. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Head-to-head benchmarking of genotypic resistance-prediction methods (Mykrobe predictor vs. KvarQ) on the same independent validation set, computing per-drug sensitivities so the two tools' performances can be compared side by side.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Estimating false-negative rates for a drug with ≤10 resistant samples in the validation set — the article only estimated FNRs where '>10 resistant samples' were available Comparing methods for pyrazinamide — known mutations are poorly predictive and the drug was completely excluded from the M. tuberculosis panel Reproducing a comparator like SeqSphere whose gene-panel template was not publicly released, making the comparison non-reproducible

skills.description: Use when several co-occurrence networks (e.g., SparCC, propr, SpiecEasi, FlashWeave, COZINE, HARMONIES, SPRING, mLDM) have been inferred from the same abundance table and you need to quantify shared vs. unique nodes/edges to reveal method-driven rewiring.
skills.name: cross-method-network-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-network-comparison Use when several co-occurrence networks (e.g., SparCC, propr, SpiecEasi, FlashWeave, COZINE, HARMONIES, SPRING, mLDM) have been inferred from the same abundance table and you need to quantify shared vs. unique nodes/edges to reveal method-driven rewiring. You have only one inferred network per dataset — intersection analysis needs at least two NI methods' edge lists to compare. The inputs are raw 16S reads rather than filtered, genus-level networks; this skill assumes the bootstrap/Make-network/Group steps have already been run. You need to benchmark network accuracy against a ground-truth (mock/synthetic) community rather than assess cross-method consistency alone. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies how consistent co-occurrence networks inferred by multiple network inference (NI) methods are, by computing UpSet-style node and edge intersections across the eight methods run in the MiCoNE pipeline on the same genus-level counts table. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: Quantifies how consistent co-occurrence networks inferred by multiple network inference (NI) methods are, by computing UpSet-style node and edge intersections across the eight methods run in the MiCoNE pipeline on the same genus-level counts table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only one inferred network per dataset — intersection analysis needs at least two NI methods' edge lists to compare. The inputs are raw 16S reads rather than filtered, genus-level networks; this skill assumes the bootstrap/Make-network/Group steps have already been run. You need to benchmark network accuracy against a ground-truth (mock/synthetic) community rather than assess cross-method consistency alone.

skills.description: Use when you have reconstructed GSMMs from MAGs and matched complete genomes and need to quantify whether annotation expansion (e.g. KEMET-recovered KOs) closes the metabolic-capability gap between draft and reference models.
skills.name: cross-model-capability-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-model-capability-comparison Use when you have reconstructed GSMMs from MAGs and matched complete genomes and need to quantify whether annotation expansion (e.g. KEMET-recovered KOs) closes the metabolic-capability gap between draft and reference models. Only one model set exists (no matched complete-genome reference), so no gap-closure comparison is possible The goal is KEGG Module completeness reporting rather than phenotype/capability comparison — use kemet.py with --skip_hmm to get recap tables only Existing draft models will be rebuilt rather than extended — when a CarveMe/gapseq draft already exists, use KEMET --gsmm_mode existing instead of de-novo reconstruction http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark genome-scale metabolic models by running flux variability analysis (FVA) on matched model sets (MAG-only, KEMET-annotation-expanded, and complete-genome reference) at fixed maximal growth rate and comparing exchange-reaction flux ranges to quantify how recovered KOs improve phenotype prediction. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Benchmark genome-scale metabolic models by running flux variability analysis (FVA) on matched model sets (MAG-only, KEMET-annotation-expanded, and complete-genome reference) at fixed maximal growth rate and comparing exchange-reaction flux ranges to quantify how recovered KOs improve phenotype prediction.

skills.description: Use when the same clinical isolate has raw reads from both a high-error single-molecule platform (e.g. MinION) and a short-read platform (e.g. MiSeq) and you need to verify that genotypic resistance predictions agree across platforms.
skills.name: cross-platform-resistance-call-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-platform-resistance-call-concordance-analysis Use when the same clinical isolate has raw reads from both a high-error single-molecule platform (e.g. MinION) and a short-read platform (e.g. MiSeq) and you need to verify that genotypic resistance predictions agree across platforms. You only have reads from a single platform — there is no second platform call set to compare against, so a concordance analysis is undefined. The target organism is one where Mykrobe panels are unavailable or poorly characterized (the paper notes resistance mechanisms for such species require large training sets not yet available). You need per-drug diagnostic sensitivity/specificity estimates — the paper's N=1 MinION test is explicitly 'only proof-of-principle' and cannot support performance statistics. http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_2815 Runs Mykrobe predictor independently on ONT MinION and Illumina MiSeq reads of the same isolate and compares the resulting antibiotic-resistance calls drug-by-drug to quantify cross-platform concordance, as demonstrated in the paper's N=1 S. aureus proof-of-principle that yielded 12/12 identical calls. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Runs Mykrobe predictor independently on ONT MinION and Illumina MiSeq reads of the same isolate and compares the resulting antibiotic-resistance calls drug-by-drug to quantify cross-platform concordance, as demonstrated in the paper's N=1 S. aureus proof-of-principle that yielded 12/12 identical calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have reads from a single platform — there is no second platform call set to compare against, so a concordance analysis is undefined. The target organism is one where Mykrobe panels are unavailable or poorly characterized (the paper notes resistance mechanisms for such species require large training sets not yet available). You need per-drug diagnostic sensitivity/specificity estimates — the paper's N=1 MinION test is explicitly 'only proof-of-principle' and cannot support performance statistics.

skills.description: Use when terrain-corrected Sentinel-1 gamma_0 stacks for VV and VH plus an acquisition-dates table (e.g., ALB_acquisition_dates.csv) are available and per-pixel cross-polarization difference/ratio rasters are needed as radar habitat-structure predictors.
skills.name: cross-polarization-metric-calculation
skills.search_text: cross-polarization-metric-calculation Use when terrain-corrected Sentinel-1 gamma_0 stacks for VV and VH plus an acquisition-dates table (e.g., ALB_acquisition_dates.csv) are available and per-pixel cross-polarization difference/ratio rasters are needed as radar habitat-structure predictors. Inputs are uncalibrated GRDH digital numbers or beta_0 - metrics require gamma_0 after radiometric calibration, radiometric terrain flattening (SRTM 1 sec DEM), and range-doppler terrain correction, otherwise values are incomparable across acquisitions. Only a single acquisition is available - speckle handling here relies on medians across a multi-date Sentinel-1 time series, not spatial speckle filters. The target is understorey structure or understorey-driven biodiversity - C-band SAR's weak permeability through overstorey layers limits these backscatter metrics. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Computes per-pixel cross-polarization summary statistics - the VV-VH difference, the VV/VH ratio, and winter-minus-summer differences - from temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 gamma_0 backscatter, yielding 10 m habitat-structure predictor rasters for forest biodiversity models. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Computes per-pixel cross-polarization summary statistics - the VV-VH difference, the VV/VH ratio, and winter-minus-summer differences - from temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 gamma_0 backscatter, yielding 10 m habitat-structure predictor rasters for forest biodiversity models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inputs are uncalibrated GRDH digital numbers or beta_0 - metrics require gamma_0 after radiometric calibration, radiometric terrain flattening (SRTM 1 sec DEM), and range-doppler terrain correction, otherwise values are incomparable across acquisitions. Only a single acquisition is available - speckle handling here relies on medians across a multi-date Sentinel-1 time series, not spatial speckle filters. The target is understorey structure or understorey-driven biodiversity - C-band SAR's weak permeability through overstorey layers limits these backscatter metrics.

skills.description: Use when constructing a reference protein database from coding genes of collected genomes plus curated entries (e.g. UniProt fungal subset), and redundancy and annotation quality must be controlled.

skills.search_text: cross-source-protein-sequence-integration Use when constructing a reference protein database from coding genes of collected genomes plus curated entries (e.g. UniProt fungal subset), and redundancy and annotation quality must be controlled. When building a taxonomic marker-gene database — FunOMIC-T uses 99% identity CD-HIT clustering of single-copy marker genes instead of 95% protein clustering When input proteins are already non-redundant or pre-clustered; re-clustering with CD-HIT would discard legitimate near-identical sequences When functional annotation of metagenomic reads is not the goal, since ~1.5 million unannotated proteins are deliberately discarded here http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Build a non-redundant functional protein reference (e.g. FunOMIC-P) by integrating amino-acid sequences from multiple repositories (NCBI, JGI, UniProt), filtering to explicitly annotated proteins, and clustering at 95% identity with CD-HIT. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Build a non-redundant functional protein reference (e.g. FunOMIC-P) by integrating amino-acid sequences from multiple repositories (NCBI, JGI, UniProt), filtering to explicitly annotated proteins, and clustering at 95% identity with CD-HIT.

skills.description: Use when choosing or defending an overlap/identity cutoff for viral read recruitment or strain separation: you need to know how much sequence two viral genomes or a virus and another microbe can share by chance before setting the threshold.
skills.name: cross-species-viral-genome-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-species-viral-genome-comparison Use when choosing or defending an overlap/identity cutoff for viral read recruitment or strain separation: you need to know how much sequence two viral genomes or a virus and another microbe can share by chance before setting the threshold. The virus of interest shares no conservation with any reference genome — TAR-VIR's recruitment stage cannot detect a completely new virus, so LCS-based cutoff calibration is moot You already have a validated overlap cutoff for your read length and platform and only need to run recruitment (see TAR-VIR's -c parameter), not re-derive it Your genomes are so divergent that pairwise alignment statistics (not exact-substring measures) are needed to capture homology http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies sequence conservation between viral (and virus-vs-other-microbe) genome pairs by computing longest common substring (LCS) sizes, then uses an ROC analysis over candidate LCS cutoffs to justify overlap thresholds for read recruitment in TAR-VIR. This grounds a cutoff such as 100 bp in the empirical separation between within-quasispecies and cross-species shared strings. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2
skills.summary: Quantifies sequence conservation between viral (and virus-vs-other-microbe) genome pairs by computing longest common substring (LCS) sizes, then uses an ROC analysis over candidate LCS cutoffs to justify overlap thresholds for read recruitment in TAR-VIR. This grounds a cutoff such as 100 bp in the empirical separation between within-quasispecies and cross-species shared strings.

skills.description: Use when a mock-community or benchmark sample has both a newly computed per-lineage classification profile and published reference proportions from another study, and you need a single agreement statistic (e.g., R²) to validate the new method's quantitative accuracy.
skills.name: cross-study-classification-agreement-correlation
skills.search_text: cross-study-classification-agreement-correlation Use when a mock-community or benchmark sample has both a newly computed per-lineage classification profile and published reference proportions from another study, and you need a single agreement statistic (e.g., R²) to validate the new method's quantitative accuracy. The sample is not a characterized mock community with published independent per-lineage proportions — there is no reference vector to correlate against, so R² cannot be computed meaningfully You need absolute abundance accuracy rather than cross-study agreement: R² captures rank/proportion agreement between studies and can be high even when total classified fraction differs substantially between pipelines The new method's per-lineage profile has a different lineage granularity than the published proportions (e.g., species-level vs. the paper's 10 distinct viral lineages) without a documented mapping between the two taxonomic levels http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Quantify agreement between a tool's per-lineage taxonomic classification fractions on a shared mock-community sample and previously published proportions from an independent study, using the coefficient of determination (R²) computed with Statistics::Basic. skills.description: Use when you have comparable per-study differential abundance result tables (estimates + standard errors from GAMLSS-BEZI taxa.compare on the same taxa levels) and need pooled effects, heterogeneity, and FDR-adjusted p-values across studies.
skills.name: cross-study-microbiome-pooled-effect-estimation
skills.search_text: cross-study-microbiome-pooled-effect-estimation Use when you have comparable per-study differential abundance result tables (estimates + standard errors from GAMLSS-BEZI taxa.compare on the same taxa levels) and need pooled effects, heterogeneity, and FDR-adjusted p-values across studies. skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate or compare ANI/strain-comparison accuracy of inStrain versus other tools (dRep, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn) using simulated genomes with known ground-truth ANI values.
skills.name: cross-tool-ani-accuracy-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-tool-ani-accuracy-comparison Use when you need to quantitatively validate or compare ANI/strain-comparison accuracy of inStrain versus other tools (dRep, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn) using simulated genomes with known ground-truth ANI values. Input is real (non-simulated) metagenomic data where true ANI between strains is unknown — this skill depends on ground-truth ANI from SNP Mutator-mutated genomes Goal is ordinary genome dereplication or clustering of a genome set (use dRep dereplicate directly, e.g. dereplicating at 98% ANI to reduce multi-mapped reads) rather than tool-accuracy benchmarking Genomes are so distantly related that inStrain popANI is expected to deviate from true ANI — the reported Figure 2b trend holds for closely related genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmark the accuracy of strain-level ANI estimation across tools by simulating genomes of known true ANI (SNP Mutator mutations of an E. coli SQ88 reference), generating synthetic Illumina reads at 20x coverage with pIRS, and comparing inStrain's microdiversity-aware popANI against dRep, MIDAS, and StrainPhlAn estimates. This reproduces the paper's Figure 2b / Supplemental Table S1 validation showing inStrain's popANI closely tracks true ANI for closely related genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Benchmark the accuracy of strain-level ANI estimation across tools by simulating genomes of known true ANI (SNP Mutator mutations of an E. coli SQ88 reference), generating synthetic Illumina reads at 20x coverage with pIRS, and comparing inStrain's microdiversity-aware popANI against dRep, MIDAS, and StrainPhlAn estimates. This reproduces the paper's Figure 2b / Supplemental Table S1 validation showing inStrain's popANI closely tracks true ANI for closely related genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) metagenomic data where true ANI between strains is unknown — this skill depends on ground-truth ANI from SNP Mutator-mutated genomes Goal is ordinary genome dereplication or clustering of a genome set (use dRep dereplicate directly, e.g. dereplicating at 98% ANI to reduce multi-mapped reads) rather than tool-accuracy benchmarking Genomes are so distantly related that inStrain popANI is expected to deviate from true ANI — the reported Figure 2b trend holds for closely related genomes

skills.description: Use when a study requires reproducing a published tool-benchmark (same input dataset, multiple strain-comparison tools) with ROC/AUC and detection-count metrics, e.g. validating SynTracker's reported AUC 0.93 and 112 strain pairs.
skills.name: cross-tool-benchmark-reproduction
skills.search_text: cross-tool-benchmark-reproduction Use when a study requires reproducing a published tool-benchmark (same input dataset, multiple strain-comparison tools) with ROC/AUC and detection-count metrics, e.g. validating SynTracker's reported AUC 0.93 and 112 strain pairs. The goal is continuous genomic-difference measurement rather than same/different-strain classification — the article warns that strain delineation thresholds (e.g. popANI 99.999%, APSS 0.95) are subjective and species-dependent Only one tool is being run and no comparative baseline (inStrain/MIDAS/StrainPhlAn) is needed, so an AUC/detection-count benchmark adds no information Input is raw reads rather than assemblies — SynTracker requires per-sample assembled contigs/genomes as target input http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Reproduce the premature-infant-twin strain-tracking benchmark in which SynTracker (APSS-based synteny scoring) is compared head-to-head against MIDAS, StrainPhlAn and inStrain using AUC and number of detected strain pairs, including phage/plasmid tracking. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Reproduce the premature-infant-twin strain-tracking benchmark in which SynTracker (APSS-based synteny scoring) is compared head-to-head against MIDAS, StrainPhlAn and inStrain using AUC and number of detected strain pairs, including phage/plasmid tracking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is continuous genomic-difference measurement rather than same/different-strain classification — the article warns that strain delineation thresholds (e.g. popANI 99.999%, APSS 0.95) are subjective and species-dependent Only one tool is being run and no comparative baseline (inStrain/MIDAS/StrainPhlAn) is needed, so an AUC/detection-count benchmark adds no information Input is raw reads rather than assemblies — SynTracker requires per-sample assembled contigs/genomes as target input

skills.description: Use when multiple viral binning tools must be compared on identical scaffold inputs with sorted BAM coverage, and a reproducible metrics table (F1, precision, redundant-protein counts) is the deliverable.
skills.name: cross-tool-binning-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-tool-binning-benchmark-comparison Use when multiple viral binning tools must be compared on identical scaffold inputs with sorted BAM coverage, and a reproducible metrics table (F1, precision, redundant-protein counts) is the deliverable. The input is a whole (non-viral) metagenome or predominantly non-viral sequences — vRhyme is not meant to bin microbes, and on a synthetic non-viral dataset MetaBat2 performed better than vRhyme Scaffolds are already binned, or the input is a bin/feature table rather than scaffold FASTA plus per-sample coverage BAMs Only a single coverage sample is available and dataset construction does not support coverage variance comparisons — vRhyme performs optimally with multiple input samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark viral metagenome binning tools (vRhyme, MetaBat2, VAMB, CONCOCT, BinSanity, CoCoNet) on the same scaffold sets under equivalent conditions, scoring bins against ground-truth genomes (simulated viromes) or against protein-redundancy/CheckV metrics (natural datasets like GOV2) to rank binners by precision and completeness. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Benchmark viral metagenome binning tools (vRhyme, MetaBat2, VAMB, CONCOCT, BinSanity, CoCoNet) on the same scaffold sets under equivalent conditions, scoring bins against ground-truth genomes (simulated viromes) or against protein-redundancy/CheckV metrics (natural datasets like GOV2) to rank binners by precision and completeness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a whole (non-viral) metagenome or predominantly non-viral sequences — vRhyme is not meant to bin microbes, and on a synthetic non-viral dataset MetaBat2 performed better than vRhyme Scaffolds are already binned, or the input is a bin/feature table rather than scaffold FASTA plus per-sample coverage BAMs Only a single coverage sample is available and dataset construction does not support coverage variance comparisons — vRhyme performs optimally with multiple input samples

skills.summary: Benchmark a metagenomic fecal source tracking tool (SourceApp) head-to-head against alternative methods (FEAST, metaSourceTracker, decOM) on identical spike-in mesocosm samples, scoring source attribution and apportionment against ground-truth cell fractions.
