skills.search_text: fungal-detection-rate-summary-statistics Use when profiling fungal taxonomic presence across a large cohort of human shotgun metagenomes and you need cohort-level detection rates and per-species prevalence tables (e.g. prevalence of S. cerevisiae across thousands of samples). skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is amplicon (ITS) data rather than shotgun metagenomes — FunOMIC-T marker-gene mapping is designed for shotgun reads and the article notes its taxonomy coverage may be lower than fungal amplicon databases The goal is fungal functional profiling (proteins) rather than taxonomic detection — that requires the FunOMIC-P database and Diamond blastx thresholds instead Only a single sample or small cohort is available, where cohort-level detection-rate and prevalence statistics are not meaningful

skills.description: Use when performing fungal functional profiling of shotgun metagenomic reads against the FunOMIC-P protein database, especially when distinguishing fungal signal from dominant bacterial backgrounds.
skills.name: fungal-functional-profiling
skills.search_text: fungal-functional-profiling Use when performing fungal functional profiling of shotgun metagenomic reads against the FunOMIC-P protein database, especially when distinguishing fungal signal from dominant bacterial backgrounds. Reads should be taxonomically profiled first with FunOMIC-T if the question is species/strain identification — FunOMIC-T gave 0.9999 specificity on mock bacterial reads, whereas FunOMIC-P retains some bacterial contamination due to conserved proteins Input is amplicon data (ITS) rather than shotgun metagenomic reads; FunOMIC is designed for next-generation sequencing read mapping to protein/marker databases Bacterial functional profiling is the goal — FunOMIC-P is a fungal-only protein database and the pipeline treats bacterial reads as background to be excluded http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Functional annotation of mycobiome sequencing reads by mapping them against the FunOMIC-P database (3.4 million non-redundant fungal proteins) using Diamond blastx, with strict identity/coverage/e-value thresholds tuned to suppress bacterial cross-mapping. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Functional annotation of mycobiome sequencing reads by mapping them against the FunOMIC-P database (3.4 million non-redundant fungal proteins) using Diamond blastx, with strict identity/coverage/e-value thresholds tuned to suppress bacterial cross-mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads should be taxonomically profiled first with FunOMIC-T if the question is species/strain identification — FunOMIC-T gave 0.9999 specificity on mock bacterial reads, whereas FunOMIC-P retains some bacterial contamination due to conserved proteins Input is amplicon data (ITS) rather than shotgun metagenomic reads; FunOMIC is designed for next-generation sequencing read mapping to protein/marker databases Bacterial functional profiling is the goal — FunOMIC-P is a fungal-only protein database and the pipeline treats bacterial reads as background to be excluded

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples need fungal taxonomic profiling (species detection rates, prevalence, abundance tables) via read mapping to a curated fungal marker-gene database rather than ITS amplicon-style analysis.
skills.name: fungal-marker-gene-read-mapping
skills.search_text: fungal-marker-gene-read-mapping Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples need fungal taxonomic profiling (species detection rates, prevalence, abundance tables) via read mapping to a curated fungal marker-gene database rather than ITS amplicon-style analysis. The goal is functional (protein-level) annotation of reads — that requires DIAMOND blastx against FunOMIC-P (coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10), not marker-gene read mapping The input is already a taxonomy/abundance table rather than raw sequencing reads Fungal genome assembly and marker gene extraction from Candida/isolate data is the goal (BBNorm/SPAdes/BUSCO database-construction steps), not profiling of metagenomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Maps metagenomic shotgun reads against the FunOMIC-T database of 1.69 million fungal single-copy marker genes using bowtie2, then filters alignments with samtools (>80% read length aligned, q-score >30) to build per-sample fungal species abundance/prevalence profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Maps metagenomic shotgun reads against the FunOMIC-T database of 1.69 million fungal single-copy marker genes using bowtie2, then filters alignments with samtools (>80% read length aligned, q-score >30) to build per-sample fungal species abundance/prevalence profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is functional (protein-level) annotation of reads — that requires DIAMOND blastx against FunOMIC-P (coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10), not marker-gene read mapping The input is already a taxonomy/abundance table rather than raw sequencing reads Fungal genome assembly and marker gene extraction from Candida/isolate data is the goal (BBNorm/SPAdes/BUSCO database-construction steps), not profiling of metagenomes

skills.description: Use when metagenomic sequencing reads must be assigned fungal functions via a fungal protein database, and the Diamond blastx threshold combination (identity, read coverage, e-value) needs to be selected or applied for fungal functional profiling.
skills.name: fungal-protein-database-alignment
skills.search_text: fungal-protein-database-alignment Use when metagenomic sequencing reads must be assigned fungal functions via a fungal protein database, and the Diamond blastx threshold combination (identity, read coverage, e-value) needs to be selected or applied for fungal functional profiling. Input is a nucleotide/amplicon dataset intended for taxonomic profiling — use the FunOMIC-T marker-gene mapping route instead of Diamond blastx against FunOMIC-P A bacterial contamination filtration step is required before functional annotation — the current pipeline has none, so reads must be pre-filtered elsewhere The database needed is not fungal (e.g., bacterial-only functional profiling against a non-fungal protein set) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Align (meta)genomic sequencing reads against the FunOMIC-P fungal protein database using Diamond blastx with tuned identity/coverage/e-value thresholds to achieve fungal functional annotation, as established in FunOMIC's mock-community threshold optimization. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Align (meta)genomic sequencing reads against the FunOMIC-P fungal protein database using Diamond blastx with tuned identity/coverage/e-value thresholds to achieve fungal functional annotation, as established in FunOMIC's mock-community threshold optimization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a nucleotide/amplicon dataset intended for taxonomic profiling — use the FunOMIC-T marker-gene mapping route instead of Diamond blastx against FunOMIC-P A bacterial contamination filtration step is required before functional annotation — the current pipeline has none, so reads must be pre-filtered elsewhere The database needed is not fungal (e.g., bacterial-only functional profiling against a non-fungal protein set)

skills.description: Use when constructing a fungal taxonomic marker-gene database from a pool of assembled, quality-filtered fungal genomes (e.g., ~4,839 NCBI/JGI MycoCosm genomes) and you need per-genome single-copy ortholog extraction and redundancy removal.
skills.name: fungal-single-copy-marker-gene-identification
skills.search_text: fungal-single-copy-marker-gene-identification Use when constructing a fungal taxonomic marker-gene database from a pool of assembled, quality-filtered fungal genomes (e.g., ~4,839 NCBI/JGI MycoCosm genomes) and you need per-genome single-copy ortholog extraction and redundancy removal. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than assembled, quality-filtered genomes — BUSCO genome mode with AUGUSTUS requires assemblies Goal is building the functional protein database (FunOMIC-P) — that uses annotated coding proteins clustered at 95% identity, not single-copy marker genes at 99% A genome yields fewer than 30 single-copy marker genes — it should be discarded from the marker catalog rather than included http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Identifies single-copy marker genes in curated fungal genomes using BUSCO 5.0.0 with the Fungi OrthoDB v10.1 set of 758 universal single-copy ortholog HMMs and the AUGUSTUS gene predictor, then deduplicates them into a taxonomic marker catalog (FunOMIC-T, ~1.69 million genes). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Identifies single-copy marker genes in curated fungal genomes using BUSCO 5.0.0 with the Fungi OrthoDB v10.1 set of 758 universal single-copy ortholog HMMs and the AUGUSTUS gene predictor, then deduplicates them into a taxonomic marker catalog (FunOMIC-T, ~1.69 million genes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than assembled, quality-filtered genomes — BUSCO genome mode with AUGUSTUS requires assemblies Goal is building the functional protein database (FunOMIC-P) — that uses annotated coding proteins clustered at 95% identity, not single-copy marker genes at 99% A genome yields fewer than 30 single-copy marker genes — it should be discarded from the marker catalog rather than included

skills.description: Use when building a strain/species-level fungal taxonomic reference database for read-mapping mycobiome profiling from NCBI/JGI fungal genome assemblies.
skills.name: fungal-taxonomic-database-construction
skills.search_text: fungal-taxonomic-database-construction Use when building a strain/species-level fungal taxonomic reference database for read-mapping mycobiome profiling from NCBI/JGI fungal genome assemblies. You need a functional (protein/pathway) reference rather than a taxonomic marker catalog — use the 95% CD-HIT clustering of annotated fungal proteins (FunOMIC-P) instead Your target taxa are bacteria/archaea — marker genes from fungal OrthoDB 10.1 will not capture prokaryotic diversity Input data are already metagenomic reads rather than reference genome assemblies — this skill constructs the reference, not the read-mapping profiling step http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Reconstructs a fungal single-copy marker-gene taxonomic reference (like FunOMIC-T, ~1.69 million genes) by BUSCO-based marker extraction from thousands of curated fungal genomes followed by 99% identity CD-HIT de-redundancy. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Reconstructs a fungal single-copy marker-gene taxonomic reference (like FunOMIC-T, ~1.69 million genes) by BUSCO-based marker extraction from thousands of curated fungal genomes followed by 99% identity CD-HIT de-redundancy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a functional (protein/pathway) reference rather than a taxonomic marker catalog — use the 95% CD-HIT clustering of annotated fungal proteins (FunOMIC-P) instead Your target taxa are bacteria/archaea — marker genes from fungal OrthoDB 10.1 will not capture prokaryotic diversity Input data are already metagenomic reads rather than reference genome assemblies — this skill constructs the reference, not the read-mapping profiling step

skills.description: Use when testing between-group differences in microbiome taxon relative abundances (phylum–genus levels) from compositional data with many zeros, especially with covariate adjustment and repeated-measures/longitudinal designs.
skills.name: gamlss-bezi-differential-abundance-testing
skills.search_text: gamlss-bezi-differential-abundance-testing Use when testing between-group differences in microbiome taxon relative abundances (phylum–genus levels) from compositional data with many zeros, especially with covariate adjustment and repeated-measures/longitudinal designs. Input is raw counts or OTU/ASV feature counts rather than relative abundances — GAMLSS-BEZI models compositional relative abundance data and expects transformed/normalized proportions The analysis goal is pooling effect estimates across studies — use meta.taxa random-effects meta-analysis instead of a single-cohort taxa.compare test The question concerns alpha diversity indexes or microbiome age prediction — use alpha.compare or the Random Forest microbiomeage workflow, not taxa.compare http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Differential relative abundance testing of microbial taxa using zero-inflated beta GAMLSS (BEZI family) via metamicrobiomeR's taxa.compare, which directly models the zero-inflated beta distribution of microbiome relative abundance data instead of transforming it (as in MaAsLin's arcsin square-root linear models). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2744-2
skills.summary: Differential relative abundance testing of microbial taxa using zero-inflated beta GAMLSS (BEZI family) via metamicrobiomeR's taxa.compare, which directly models the zero-inflated beta distribution of microbiome relative abundance data instead of transforming it (as in MaAsLin's arcsin square-root linear models).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts or OTU/ASV feature counts rather than relative abundances — GAMLSS-BEZI models compositional relative abundance data and expects transformed/normalized proportions The analysis goal is pooling effect estimates across studies — use meta.taxa random-effects meta-analysis instead of a single-cohort taxa.compare test The question concerns alpha diversity indexes or microbiome age prediction — use alpha.compare or the Random Forest microbiomeage workflow, not taxa.compare

skills.description: Use when testing differential relative abundances of taxa between groups (e.g. diarrhea vs. no diarrhea, breastfeeding status, gender) in microbiome relative abundance tables with covariate adjustment and repeated samples per subject.
skills.name: gamlss-bezi-longitudinal-modeling
skills.search_text: gamlss-bezi-longitudinal-modeling Use when testing differential relative abundances of taxa between groups (e.g. diarrhea vs. no diarrhea, breastfeeding status, gender) in microbiome relative abundance tables with covariate adjustment and repeated samples per subject. Input is not relative abundance data (e.g. counts, compositional transforms already applied, or alpha diversity indexes — use alpha.compare or other methods instead) The goal is pooling effect estimates across multiple studies — use meta.taxa/metatab.show on taxa.compare outputs instead of running taxa.compare per stratum The comparison variable distribution does not resemble a zero-inflated beta (e.g. the article notes arcsin square root transformation approaches like MaAsLin address continuous-transformed data, not zero inflation) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Differential abundance testing of microbiome relative abundances using GAMLSS with a zero-inflated beta (BEZI) family in metamicrobiomeR, optionally modeling repeated samples per infant via longitudinal='yes', with FDR correction. This directly models the zero-inflated beta distribution of relative abundance data instead of applying transformations. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2744-2
skills.summary: Differential abundance testing of microbiome relative abundances using GAMLSS with a zero-inflated beta (BEZI) family in metamicrobiomeR, optionally modeling repeated samples per infant via longitudinal='yes', with FDR correction. This directly models the zero-inflated beta distribution of relative abundance data instead of applying transformations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not relative abundance data (e.g. counts, compositional transforms already applied, or alpha diversity indexes — use alpha.compare or other methods instead) The goal is pooling effect estimates across multiple studies — use meta.taxa/metatab.show on taxa.compare outputs instead of running taxa.compare per stratum The comparison variable distribution does not resemble a zero-inflated beta (e.g. the article notes arcsin square root transformation approaches like MaAsLin address continuous-transformed data, not zero inflation)

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing the Glimmer-MG gene-length model: you have annotated ORF lengths (e.g. from a GenBank/FASTA genome annotation) and need a blended coding/non-coding length distribution to score ORF lengths, especially for truncated genes on short metagenomic reads.
skills.name: gamma-distribution-maximum-likelihood-fitting
skills.search_text: gamma-distribution-maximum-likelihood-fitting Use when building or reproducing the Glimmer-MG gene-length model: you have annotated ORF lengths (e.g. from a GenBank/FASTA genome annotation) and need a blended coding/non-coding length distribution to score ORF lengths, especially for truncated genes on short metagenomic reads. Predicting genes in complete, well-annotated prokaryotic genomes where standard Glimmer's IMM training on the whole genome is adequate — the length model exists to handle fragmented genes on short metagenomic reads The input is already a set of predicted genes/lengths and no length-distribution scoring model is needed The ORF-length data are not from coding regions, since the blended model is specifically a coding/non-coding length distribution http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Fit a Gamma distribution by maximum likelihood to annotated coding ORF lengths and blend it with a kernel-smoothed histogram to reproduce Glimmer-MG's gene-length probability model. This models the length distribution used to score partial genes on short metagenomic fragments, as visualized in Figure 1 for Deinococcus radiodurans R1. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: Fit a Gamma distribution by maximum likelihood to annotated coding ORF lengths and blend it with a kernel-smoothed histogram to reproduce Glimmer-MG's gene-length probability model. This models the length distribution used to score partial genes on short metagenomic fragments, as visualized in Figure 1 for Deinococcus radiodurans R1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predicting genes in complete, well-annotated prokaryotic genomes where standard Glimmer's IMM training on the whole genome is adequate — the length model exists to handle fragmented genes on short metagenomic reads The input is already a set of predicted genes/lengths and no length-distribution scoring model is needed The ORF-length data are not from coding regions, since the blended model is specifically a coding/non-coding length distribution

skills.description: Use when clustering protein sequence sets at thresholds like --min-seq-id 0.9 --cov-mode 1 -c 0.9 and survivors of the k-mer, Hamming, and ungapped filters must be verified with exact gapped local alignments before greedy incremental clustering.
skills.name: gapped-local-sequence-alignment
skills.search_text: gapped-local-sequence-alignment Use when clustering protein sequence sets at thresholds like --min-seq-id 0.9 --cov-mode 1 -c 0.9 and survivors of the k-mer, Hamming, and ungapped filters must be verified with exact gapped local alignments before greedy incremental clustering. When sequences are expected to share similarity only outside any of the m selected lowest-hash k-mers, since Linclust aligns only center–member pairs sharing a k-mer and may miss such links When input is already a non-redundant sequence set or a precomputed clustering result — rerunning gapped alignments adds cost without benefit When exact all-against-all pairwise similarities beyond shared-k-mer pairs are required; Linclust's linear O(mN) time applies only to center-restricted comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 Align candidate sequence pairs to their center sequences with an AVX2/SSE4.1-vectorized gapped local alignment module (Blosum62 with compositional bias correction), linking pairs that meet identity/coverage/E-value criteria. This is step 4 of the Linclust linear-time clustering pipeline, after Hamming-distance and ungapped-alignment filters have reduced the candidate set. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-04964-5
skills.summary: Align candidate sequence pairs to their center sequences with an AVX2/SSE4.1-vectorized gapped local alignment module (Blosum62 with compositional bias correction), linking pairs that meet identity/coverage/E-value criteria. This is step 4 of the Linclust linear-time clustering pipeline, after Hamming-distance and ungapped-alignment filters have reduced the candidate set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When sequences are expected to share similarity only outside any of the m selected lowest-hash k-mers, since Linclust aligns only center–member pairs sharing a k-mer and may miss such links When input is already a non-redundant sequence set or a precomputed clustering result — rerunning gapped alignments adds cost without benefit When exact all-against-all pairwise similarities beyond shared-k-mer pairs are required; Linclust's linear O(mN) time applies only to center-restricted comparisons

skills.description: Use when comparing de novo assemblies (e.g. ABySS, Velvet, SPAdes, MEGAHIT contigs in FASTA) and QUAST's report.tsv G+C content or # N's per 100 kbp columns are needed to detect contamination, divergence from the expected organismal G+C range, or uncalled-base problems.
skills.name: gc-content-and-uncalled-base-interpretation
skills.search_text: gc-content-and-uncalled-base-interpretation Use when comparing de novo assemblies (e.g. ABySS, Velvet, SPAdes, MEGAHIT contigs in FASTA) and QUAST's report.tsv G+C content or # N's per 100 kbp columns are needed to detect contamination, divergence from the expected organismal G+C range, or uncalled-base problems. A reference genome is available and reference-based metrics (mismatches, indels, genome fraction, duplication ratio, NGA50) are the relevant quality signals Input is not assembled contigs but raw reads or a single already-validated assembly with no comparison baseline Metagenomic datasets, where a single expected G+C range does not apply and MetaQUAST-style per-reference evaluation is needed instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Interprets the G+C content (%) and # N's per 100 kbp columns from QUAST/WebQUAST reference-free evaluation reports to judge assembly purity and base-calling quality, using organism-expected G+C ranges and per-assembler N-content comparisons as calibration (e.g. E. coli K-12 MG1655 expected 50.4–50.8% G+C, observed ~50.7% across all four assemblers). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad406
skills.summary: Interprets the G+C content (%) and # N's per 100 kbp columns from QUAST/WebQUAST reference-free evaluation reports to judge assembly purity and base-calling quality, using organism-expected G+C ranges and per-assembler N-content comparisons as calibration (e.g. E. coli K-12 MG1655 expected 50.4–50.8% G+C, observed ~50.7% across all four assemblers).
skills.when_to_use_negative: A reference genome is available and reference-based metrics (mismatches, indels, genome fraction, duplication ratio, NGA50) are the relevant quality signals Input is not assembled contigs but raw reads or a single already-validated assembly with no comparison baseline Metagenomic datasets, where a single expected G+C range does not apply and MetaQUAST-style per-reference evaluation is needed instead

skills.description: Use when a presence/absence analysis calls a gene absent in lineages represented mainly by draft bins — especially when completeness estimates (e.g. ≥75% single-copy genes, ≤1.125 copies) are available and you must decide if the absence call is trustworthy.
skills.name: gene-absence-confidence-statistics
skills.search_text: gene-absence-confidence-statistics Use when a presence/absence analysis calls a gene absent in lineages represented mainly by draft bins — especially when completeness estimates (e.g. ≥75% single-copy genes, ≤1.125 copies) are available and you must decide if the absence call is trustworthy. The genome set consists only of complete genomes, so incomplete-sampling artifacts cannot explain absences Gene detection relies on keyword-based annotation alone rather than HMM profiles — divergent homologs would inflate apparent absences before any probability calculation is meaningful The genes of interest are not single-copy or cannot be enumerated (n undefined), making the (1 − c)^n computation inapplicable This skill quantifies whether a gene's absence from a lineage matrix (e.g. ribosomal protein L30 across CPR/TM6 bacteria) is a true biological absence rather than an artifact of incomplete draft genomes, by computing the probability that a complete genome would have missed n genes given its completeness estimate. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: This skill quantifies whether a gene's absence from a lineage matrix (e.g. ribosomal protein L30 across CPR/TM6 bacteria) is a true biological absence rather than an artifact of incomplete draft genomes, by computing the probability that a complete genome would have missed n genes given its completeness estimate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The genome set consists only of complete genomes, so incomplete-sampling artifacts cannot explain absences Gene detection relies on keyword-based annotation alone rather than HMM profiles — divergent homologs would inflate apparent absences before any probability calculation is meaningful The genes of interest are not single-copy or cannot be enumerated (n undefined), making the (1 − c)^n computation inapplicable

skills.description: Use when a set of clustered gene representatives must be prioritized by how abundant and how widespread they are across a defined collection of metagenomes, e.g. to select representative amoA-AOB clusters from soil metagenomes for primer design.
skills.name: gene-abundance-and-prevalence-quantification
skills.search_text: gene-abundance-and-prevalence-quantification Use when a set of clustered gene representatives must be prioritized by how abundant and how widespread they are across a defined collection of metagenomes, e.g. to select representative amoA-AOB clusters from soil metagenomes for primer design. The goal is primer thermodynamics or degeneracy design rather than gene prioritization (use EcoFunPrimer/Primer3 instead) Input sequences have not yet been clustered into representatives — raw gene sets must first be clustered (e.g., CD-HIT at 96%) to avoid redundant ranking Reference metagenomes are from a different environment than the target system, since R-scores are environment-specific and would not reflect the target habitat's gene abundance http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Ranks representative gene clusters by an R-score — the mean of normalized abundance and normalized prevalence — computed by aligning each representative to a panel of reference metagenomes, here 60 amoA-AOB cluster representatives from 96% CD-HIT clustering searched against 1,550 publicly available soil metagenomes. This prioritizes gene clusters for environment-specific primer design. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00201-21
skills.summary: Ranks representative gene clusters by an R-score — the mean of normalized abundance and normalized prevalence — computed by aligning each representative to a panel of reference metagenomes, here 60 amoA-AOB cluster representatives from 96% CD-HIT clustering searched against 1,550 publicly available soil metagenomes. This prioritizes gene clusters for environment-specific primer design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is primer thermodynamics or degeneracy design rather than gene prioritization (use EcoFunPrimer/Primer3 instead) Input sequences have not yet been clustered into representatives — raw gene sets must first be clustered (e.g., CD-HIT at 96%) to avoid redundant ranking Reference metagenomes are from a different environment than the target system, since R-scores are environment-specific and would not reflect the target habitat's gene abundance

skills.description: Use when constructing a non-redundant species pan-genome reference from predicted genes, or when assigning human-microbiome metagenomic contigs to reference taxa by -match gene similarity to pick a gene prediction model.
skills.name: gene-based-similarity-screening
skills.search_text: gene-based-similarity-screening Use when constructing a non-redundant species pan-genome reference from predicted genes, or when assigning human-microbiome metagenomic contigs to reference taxa by -match gene similarity to pick a gene prediction model. The contig cannot be reliably assigned to one of the ~5000 reference taxa (e.g. oral or skin metagenome contigs from environmentally mixed microbes) — GeneMark-HM falls back to MetaGeneMark or GeneMarkS-2 by contig length instead The target data are not human microbiome metagenomic contigs; the pan-genome database and models were built for species known to be present in human gut metagenomes The input is already a curated, non-redundant gene database — re-applying the ANI >95% / >90% coverage admission filter would not change it and would waste blastn compute on a ~20 Gb database http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A BLAST-driven screening strategy in the GeneMark-HM pipeline that uses initially predicted protein-coding genes as nucleotide queries against the species-level pan-genome gene database (pan) — both to build a non-redundant pan-genome reference and to assign metagenomic contigs to a taxon whose species-specific model is then used for gene prediction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047
skills.summary: A BLAST-driven screening strategy in the GeneMark-HM pipeline that uses initially predicted protein-coding genes as nucleotide queries against the species-level pan-genome gene database (pan) — both to build a non-redundant pan-genome reference and to assign metagenomic contigs to a taxon whose species-specific model is then used for gene prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The contig cannot be reliably assigned to one of the ~5000 reference taxa (e.g. oral or skin metagenome contigs from environmentally mixed microbes) — GeneMark-HM falls back to MetaGeneMark or GeneMarkS-2 by contig length instead The target data are not human microbiome metagenomic contigs; the pan-genome database and models were built for species known to be present in human gut metagenomes The input is already a curated, non-redundant gene database — re-applying the ANI >95% / >90% coverage admission filter would not change it and would waste blastn compute on a ~20 Gb database

skills.description: Use when you have a chewBBACA AlleleCall results_alleles.tsv profile matrix over a strain collection and need to define the core-genome (cgMLST) locus set at a presence threshold such as 95%.
skills.name: gene-by-gene-allele-profile-filtering
skills.search_text: gene-by-gene-allele-profile-filtering Use when you have a chewBBACA AlleleCall results_alleles.tsv profile matrix over a strain collection and need to define the core-genome (cgMLST) locus set at a presence threshold such as 95%. Input is raw assemblies or reads and no allele calling has been performed yet — run chewBBACA CreateSchema and AlleleCall first to obtain the profile matrix. Goal is the full wgMLST schema rather than the core genome — the wgMLST locus set should not be thresholded at 95% presence. Loci are used for strain-level wgMLST surveillance where accessory-genome loci matter; thresholding to 95% would discard them. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Derives a cgMLST schema from a wgMLST allelic profile matrix by removing paralogous loci and retaining only loci with valid allele calls in a chosen fraction (typically 95-99%) of analysed strains, using chewBBACA's RemoveGenes, TestGenomeQuality, and ExtractCgMLST modules. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000166
skills.summary: Derives a cgMLST schema from a wgMLST allelic profile matrix by removing paralogous loci and retaining only loci with valid allele calls in a chosen fraction (typically 95-99%) of analysed strains, using chewBBACA's RemoveGenes, TestGenomeQuality, and ExtractCgMLST modules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw assemblies or reads and no allele calling has been performed yet — run chewBBACA CreateSchema and AlleleCall first to obtain the profile matrix. Goal is the full wgMLST schema rather than the core genome — the wgMLST locus set should not be thresholded at 95% presence. Loci are used for strain-level wgMLST surveillance where accessory-genome loci matter; thresholding to 95% would discard them.

skills.description: Use when comparing a newly built non-redundant gene catalogue against a published one (e.g. VMGC-90 vs VIRGO-90) to report bidirectional coverage fractions and protein-space expansion.
skills.name: gene-catalogue-expansion-quantification
skills.search_text: gene-catalogue-expansion-quantification Use when comparing a newly built non-redundant gene catalogue against a published one (e.g. VMGC-90 vs VIRGO-90) to report bidirectional coverage fractions and protein-space expansion. The catalogues being compared use different amino acid identity clustering thresholds than 90%, so the shared/covered fractions are not comparable at the reported 70.6%/30.8% benchmarks. The goal is functional annotation of genes (KEGG, CAZy) rather than measuring catalogue-to-catalogue sequence overlap. Input sequences are nucleotide contigs or genomes rather than predicted protein-coding gene catalogues. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantifies mutual gene coverage between two protein-coding gene catalogues (here VMGC-90, ~26M clustered genes, and the 0.95M-gene VIRGO catalogue) via all-vs-all protein search at 90% amino acid identity and 80% sequence coverage, to measure how much one catalogue expands the protein space of the other. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Quantifies mutual gene coverage between two protein-coding gene catalogues (here VMGC-90, ~26M clustered genes, and the 0.95M-gene VIRGO catalogue) via all-vs-all protein search at 90% amino acid identity and 80% sequence coverage, to measure how much one catalogue expands the protein space of the other.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The catalogues being compared use different amino acid identity clustering thresholds than 90%, so the shared/covered fractions are not comparable at the reported 70.6%/30.8% benchmarks. The goal is functional annotation of genes (KEGG, CAZy) rather than measuring catalogue-to-catalogue sequence overlap. Input sequences are nucleotide contigs or genomes rather than predicted protein-coding gene catalogues.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking the read-capture efficiency of a gene catalogue (e.g., VMGC-90 vs VIRGO) by aligning clean metagenomic reads and computing per-sample mapping rates.
skills.name: gene-catalogue-mapping-rate-quantification
skills.search_text: gene-catalogue-mapping-rate-quantification Use when benchmarking the read-capture efficiency of a gene catalogue (e.g., VMGC-90 vs VIRGO) by aligning clean metagenomic reads and computing per-sample mapping rates. Estimating per-gene abundances or functional profiles — this skill only computes catalogue-level mapping rates, not gene counts or KEGG/CAZy annotations. Reporting whole-genome capture — the VMGC README reports a median mapping rate of 91.7% against the genome collection, which is a different metric from the 74.5% VMGC-90 gene-catalogue average. Taxonomic composition profiling — use the customized Kraken2/Bracken VMGC SGB database pipeline instead of gene-catalogue read mapping. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Benchmarks the read-capture efficiency of a vaginal gene catalogue by aligning clean vaginal metagenomic reads against competing catalogues (VMGC-90 vs VIRGO) and computing per-sample mapping rates. In this paper it shows VMGC-90 captures 74.5% of reads on average versus 71.7% for VIRGO. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Benchmarks the read-capture efficiency of a vaginal gene catalogue by aligning clean vaginal metagenomic reads against competing catalogues (VMGC-90 vs VIRGO) and computing per-sample mapping rates. In this paper it shows VMGC-90 captures 74.5% of reads on average versus 71.7% for VIRGO.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Estimating per-gene abundances or functional profiles — this skill only computes catalogue-level mapping rates, not gene counts or KEGG/CAZy annotations. Reporting whole-genome capture — the VMGC README reports a median mapping rate of 91.7% against the genome collection, which is a different metric from the 74.5% VMGC-90 gene-catalogue average. Taxonomic composition profiling — use the customized Kraken2/Bracken VMGC SGB database pipeline instead of gene-catalogue read mapping.

skills.description: Use when you have VAMB-derived gene cluster assignments plus ORF sequences retaining per-contig gene ordering, and you want to group gene clusters into synteny clusters based on genomic adjacency to infer shared pathways.
skills.name: gene-cluster-adjacency-graph-construction
skills.search_text: gene-cluster-adjacency-graph-construction Use when you have VAMB-derived gene cluster assignments plus ORF sequences retaining per-contig gene ordering, and you want to group gene clusters into synteny clusters based on genomic adjacency to infer shared pathways. When operon-level precision is required — accuracy is limited by MAGinator's lack of operon awareness When gene calls lack per-contig ordering information, since adjacency cannot be computed When the goal is pathway reconstruction from annotation alone (e.g. KEGG via EggNOG mapper) rather than genomic co-localization http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 MAGinator's method for building synteny clusters: a weighted adjacency graph over gene clusters, with edge weights counting how often genes from each cluster pair are genomically adjacent on contigs, partitioned with Markov clustering (MCL) so that co-localized genes are grouped together. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8
skills.summary: MAGinator's method for building synteny clusters: a weighted adjacency graph over gene clusters, with edge weights counting how often genes from each cluster pair are genomically adjacent on contigs, partitioned with Markov clustering (MCL) so that co-localized genes are grouped together.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When operon-level precision is required — accuracy is limited by MAGinator's lack of operon awareness When gene calls lack per-contig ordering information, since adjacency cannot be computed When the goal is pathway reconstruction from annotation alone (e.g. KEGG via EggNOG mapper) rather than genomic co-localization

skills.description: Use when you need to benchmark primer-set sensitivity against a curated reference gene set, e.g., recomputing the 94% (MetaFunPrimer) vs 49% (published) amoA-AOB coverage or per-cluster coverage like cluster 3 at 96% vs 19%.
skills.name: gene-cluster-coverage-quantification
skills.search_text: gene-cluster-coverage-quantification Use when you need to benchmark primer-set sensitivity against a curated reference gene set, e.g., recomputing the 94% (MetaFunPrimer) vs 49% (published) amoA-AOB coverage or per-cluster coverage like cluster 3 at 96% vs 19%. Input is not a fixed reference gene set with known size (the denominator, e.g., 720 targets, is required to compute coverage fractions) The comparator primers should not be benchmarked by thermodynamic PCR simulation rather than the strict 100% both-primer match criterion used by MetaFunPrimer Sequences have not been filtered/curated (unfiltered Fungene-style inputs lack the HMM score >400 and coverage over 70.2% quality gate, distorting coverage estimates) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantifies how many reference gene products (e.g., 720 curated amoA-AOB genes from Fungene v9.6) are amplified by a set of designed vs. published primers via in silico PCR, reporting coverage per set and per sequence cluster (e.g., 96% amino acid similarity clusters). metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00201-21
skills.summary: Quantifies how many reference gene products (e.g., 720 curated amoA-AOB genes from Fungene v9.6) are amplified by a set of designed vs. published primers via in silico PCR, reporting coverage per set and per sequence cluster (e.g., 96% amino acid similarity clusters).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a fixed reference gene set with known size (the denominator, e.g., 720 targets, is required to compute coverage fractions) The comparator primers should not be benchmarked by thermodynamic PCR simulation rather than the strict 100% both-primer match criterion used by MetaFunPrimer Sequences have not been filtered/curated (unfiltered Fungene-style inputs lack the HMM score >400 and coverage over 70.2% quality gate, distorting coverage estimates)

skills.description: Use when validating phylogeny-based gene-family prediction accuracy on genomes with known annotations, e.g. measuring per-genome and per-functional-category accuracy of PICRUSt predictions from a KO/COG reference table and a 16S marker-gene tree.
skills.name: gene-content-prediction-accuracy-assessment
skills.search_text: gene-content-prediction-accuracy-assessment Use when validating phylogeny-based gene-family prediction accuracy on genomes with known annotations, e.g. measuring per-genome and per-functional-category accuracy of PICRUSt predictions from a KO/COG reference table and a 16S marker-gene tree. The input community lacks genomes with known KO/COG annotations, so no held-out truth exists against which prediction accuracy can be scored The goal is metagenome prediction from an OTU table rather than benchmarking gene-content prediction accuracy Assessment targets viral or eukaryotic metagenome components, which PICRUSt does not infer (only bacterial and archaeal 16S marker gene sequences are included) http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A leave-one-genome-out holdout validation protocol that quantifies how accurately PICRUSt's ancestral-state-reconstruction-based gene-content predictions recover true KO/COG annotations, reported per taxon (archaea vs bacteria) and per KEGG/BRITE functional category. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: A leave-one-genome-out holdout validation protocol that quantifies how accurately PICRUSt's ancestral-state-reconstruction-based gene-content predictions recover true KO/COG annotations, reported per taxon (archaea vs bacteria) and per KEGG/BRITE functional category.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input community lacks genomes with known KO/COG annotations, so no held-out truth exists against which prediction accuracy can be scored The goal is metagenome prediction from an OTU table rather than benchmarking gene-content prediction accuracy Assessment targets viral or eukaryotic metagenome components, which PICRUSt does not infer (only bacterial and archaeal 16S marker gene sequences are included)

skills.description: Use when amplicon (16S/18S rRNA) or microarray profiles in biom, QIIME, GAAS, Unifrac, or generic tabular format with read counts and unaltered Greengenes taxonomic assignments must be corrected for GCN bias, or when qPCR total abundances need correction.
skills.name: gene-copy-number-correction
skills.search_text: gene-copy-number-correction Use when amplicon (16S/18S rRNA) or microarray profiles in biom, QIIME, GAAS, Unifrac, or generic tabular format with read counts and unaltered Greengenes taxonomic assignments must be corrected for GCN bias, or when qPCR total abundances need correction. The input profile is shotgun metagenomic data where genome-length bias (not 16S GCN bias) dominates — CopyRighter handles it only with the genome-length trait file, and this skill targets 16S GCN correction Taxonomic assignments are not Greengenes (e.g. Silva), since pre-computed GCN files currently cover only Greengenes and extension to other taxonomies is only anticipated The input file contains percentages rather than read counts or has altered taxonomic strings, which the README explicitly requires for valid correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Corrects 16S rRNA amplicon (and optionally qPCR total) abundance bias caused by lineage-specific gene copy number (GCN) variation using CopyRighter, weighting read counts by the inverse of pre-computed Greengenes GCN estimates to yield more accurate relative and absolute microbial profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Corrects 16S rRNA amplicon (and optionally qPCR total) abundance bias caused by lineage-specific gene copy number (GCN) variation using CopyRighter, weighting read counts by the inverse of pre-computed Greengenes GCN estimates to yield more accurate relative and absolute microbial profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input profile is shotgun metagenomic data where genome-length bias (not 16S GCN bias) dominates — CopyRighter handles it only with the genome-length trait file, and this skill targets 16S GCN correction Taxonomic assignments are not Greengenes (e.g. Silva), since pre-computed GCN files currently cover only Greengenes and extension to other taxonomies is only anticipated The input file contains percentages rather than read counts or has altered taxonomic strings, which the README explicitly requires for valid correction

skills.description: Use when you have GCN trait estimates for Greengenes OTUs/taxa plus the Greengenes phylogeny or taxonomy, and need to quantify how strongly GCN tracks phylogeny (e.g. Pagel's lambda) before inferring GCN for unsequenced lineages.
skills.name: gene-copy-number-tree-annotation
skills.search_text: gene-copy-number-tree-annotation Use when you have GCN trait estimates for Greengenes OTUs/taxa plus the Greengenes phylogeny or taxonomy, and need to quantify how strongly GCN tracks phylogeny (e.g. Pagel's lambda) before inferring GCN for unsequenced lineages. You want to correct an amplicon or metagenomic abundance profile — that is CopyRighter's correction mode, not the trait-onto-tree annotation/phylogenetic-signal estimation described here Your trait estimates come from a taxonomy other than Greengenes (e.g. Silva); the article notes CopyRighter does not yet cover other taxonomies and extension is only anticipated Your trait values lack a phylogenetic or taxonomic tree structure to map them onto — lambda estimation requires a tree http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Maps CopyRighter's phylogenetically-based 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) estimates onto the Greengenes phylogenetic tree and taxonomic tree, then quantifies the strength of phylogenetic signal with Pagel's lambda to justify tree-based GCN inference. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Maps CopyRighter's phylogenetically-based 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) estimates onto the Greengenes phylogenetic tree and taxonomic tree, then quantifies the strength of phylogenetic signal with Pagel's lambda to justify tree-based GCN inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to correct an amplicon or metagenomic abundance profile — that is CopyRighter's correction mode, not the trait-onto-tree annotation/phylogenetic-signal estimation described here Your trait estimates come from a taxonomy other than Greengenes (e.g. Silva); the article notes CopyRighter does not yet cover other taxonomies and extension is only anticipated Your trait values lack a phylogenetic or taxonomic tree structure to map them onto — lambda estimation requires a tree

skills.description: Use when you hold one two-column gene abundance file per sample (gene identifier + raw count, or gene identifier + FPKM) and need a single merged matrix to feed differential expression tools like DESeq2Shiny.
skills.name: gene-count-matrix-merging
skills.search_text: gene-count-matrix-merging Use when you hold one two-column gene abundance file per sample (gene identifier + raw count, or gene identifier + FPKM) and need a single merged matrix to feed differential expression tools like DESeq2Shiny. Input is already a single merged gene-by-sample matrix — no merging is needed Gene identifier columns do not match in all files — the README warns the tool will not work in this case Input is raw reads, single-cell count data, or already-normalized expression values rather than per-sample gene count/FPKM tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Merges per-sample gene count files (e.g. HTSeq output count files) or per-sample FPKM files into a single gene-by-sample matrix, as implemented by NASQAR's GeneCountMerger preprocessing app, so downstream bulk RNA-seq apps like DESeq2Shiny can consume the data. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03577-4
skills.summary: Merges per-sample gene count files (e.g. HTSeq output count files) or per-sample FPKM files into a single gene-by-sample matrix, as implemented by NASQAR's GeneCountMerger preprocessing app, so downstream bulk RNA-seq apps like DESeq2Shiny can consume the data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single merged gene-by-sample matrix — no merging is needed Gene identifier columns do not match in all files — the README warns the tool will not work in this case Input is raw reads, single-cell count data, or already-normalized expression values rather than per-sample gene count/FPKM tables

skills.description: Use when reproducing or validating gene catalog construction counts — e.g. after running MetaGeneMark CDS prediction or after BLASTP/Jaccard de-redundification — to check totals and per-source partitions against published VIRGO values.
skills.name: gene-count-qc-verification
skills.search_text: gene-count-qc-verification Use when reproducing or validating gene catalog construction counts — e.g. after running MetaGeneMark CDS prediction or after BLASTP/Jaccard de-redundification — to check totals and per-source partitions against published VIRGO values. Input is already a final annotated gene catalog or abundance table (e.g. summary.Count.txt from a VIRGO mapping run) rather than raw prediction or clustering outputs requiring count validation The gene catalog being built is not the vaginal microbiome VIRGO-style catalog, so published count thresholds (~5.5M predicted, 948,158 non-redundant) are not meaningful invariants http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Verification skill for quantitative checkpoints in vaginal gene-catalog construction: confirming total predicted CDS counts (~5,509,298 from MetaGeneMark) and the de-redundified non-redundant gene count (948,158 genes >99 bp, 17.2% of original predictions) with correct source-partition breakdowns. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Verification skill for quantitative checkpoints in vaginal gene-catalog construction: confirming total predicted CDS counts (~5,509,298 from MetaGeneMark) and the de-redundified non-redundant gene count (948,158 genes >99 bp, 17.2% of original predictions) with correct source-partition breakdowns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a final annotated gene catalog or abundance table (e.g. summary.Count.txt from a VIRGO mapping run) rather than raw prediction or clustering outputs requiring count validation The gene catalog being built is not the vaginal microbiome VIRGO-style catalog, so published count thresholds (~5.5M predicted, 948,158 non-redundant) are not meaningful invariants

skills.description: Use when combining multiple reference gene collections (e.g. ResFinder, CARD, MegaRes, AMRFinderPlus, ARGANNOT, ResFinderFG) into one non-redundant database and you need reproducible source-specific inclusion filters plus identity/coverage-based clustering.
skills.name: gene-database-inclusion-filtering
skills.search_text: gene-database-inclusion-filtering Use when combining multiple reference gene collections (e.g. ResFinder, CARD, MegaRes, AMRFinderPlus, ARGANNOT, ResFinderFG) into one non-redundant database and you need reproducible source-specific inclusion filters plus identity/coverage-based clustering. Input is a single homogeneous database or an already non-redundant gene set — the merge/deduplicate/centroid pipeline adds no value You need a curated subset chosen by biological judgment rather than type/subtype filters; the paper notes that because PanRes combines different sources and scopes, 'it will be up to the individual research questions, which subsets are appropriate for consideration' The workflow targets long reads or non-ARG gene families without their own metadata fields for the CARD/MegaRes/AMRFinderPlus filters http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Merge heterogeneous antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) databases into a single curated collection by applying source-specific inclusion filters, collapsing redundant sequences with Usearch fastx_uniques, and homology-reducing the result into centroids clustered at 90% identity and 90% coverage — the procedure used to build the PanRes database (30,400 genes → 14,078 unique sequences → 5,280 centroids). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Merge heterogeneous antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) databases into a single curated collection by applying source-specific inclusion filters, collapsing redundant sequences with Usearch fastx_uniques, and homology-reducing the result into centroids clustered at 90% identity and 90% coverage — the procedure used to build the PanRes database (30,400 genes → 14,078 unique sequences → 5,280 centroids).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single homogeneous database or an already non-redundant gene set — the merge/deduplicate/centroid pipeline adds no value You need a curated subset chosen by biological judgment rather than type/subtype filters; the paper notes that because PanRes combines different sources and scopes, 'it will be up to the individual research questions, which subsets are appropriate for consideration' The workflow targets long reads or non-ARG gene families without their own metadata fields for the CARD/MegaRes/AMRFinderPlus filters

skills.description: Use when you have an ASV/OTU abundance table plus a FASTA of marker-gene study sequences and need inferred functional profiles (EC gene families, MetaCyc pathways) without shotgun metagenomics data.
skills.name: gene-family-abundance-inference
skills.search_text: gene-family-abundance-inference Use when you have an ASV/OTU abundance table plus a FASTA of marker-gene study sequences and need inferred functional profiles (EC gene families, MetaCyc pathways) without shotgun metagenomics data. Input is already a shotgun metagenome functional profile rather than marker-gene sequence data — prediction is unnecessary. Only a species/composition table is available without the underlying study sequences, since the pipeline requires a FASTA of study sequences for placement. The goal is taxonomy-based functional profiling with habitat-specific references (e.g. Tax4Fun2/Piphillin-style approaches) rather than PICRUSt2's tree-placement workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Predicts metagenome gene-family (e.g. EC) and pathway (MetaCyc) abundance profiles from 16S/ITS amplicon sequence data using PICRUSt2, which places study sequences into a reference tree and infers functional potential from ASV abundances. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-0548-6
skills.summary: Predicts metagenome gene-family (e.g. EC) and pathway (MetaCyc) abundance profiles from 16S/ITS amplicon sequence data using PICRUSt2, which places study sequences into a reference tree and infers functional potential from ASV abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a shotgun metagenome functional profile rather than marker-gene sequence data — prediction is unnecessary. Only a species/composition table is available without the underlying study sequences, since the pipeline requires a FASTA of study sequences for placement. The goal is taxonomy-based functional profiling with habitat-specific references (e.g. Tax4Fun2/Piphillin-style approaches) rather than PICRUSt2's tree-placement workflow.

skills.description: Use when a workflow needs predicted gene family content for unsequenced taxa on a 16S marker gene reference tree, e.g. preparing the pre-calculated PICRUSt gene content file before metagenome inference.
skills.name: gene-family-content-prediction
skills.search_text: gene-family-content-prediction Use when a workflow needs predicted gene family content for unsequenced taxa on a 16S marker gene reference tree, e.g. preparing the pre-calculated PICRUSt gene content file before metagenome inference. The taxa of interest already have complete reference genomes — use their actual annotated gene content instead of inference. The community includes viral or eukaryotic components: PICRUSt only includes bacterial and archaeal 16S marker gene sequences, so viral/eukaryotic metagenome components are not inferred. Strain-level functional variation matters and the marker gene sequence is identical among strains — the method cannot distinguish variation at the strain level. http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Predict the gene family (KO/COG) content and 16S copy number of organisms lacking sequenced genomes by applying ancestral state reconstruction to the Greengenes marker gene reference tree and combining extant and ancestral genomes with exponential reciprocal phylogenetic-distance weighting, as implemented in PICRUSt. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Predict the gene family (KO/COG) content and 16S copy number of organisms lacking sequenced genomes by applying ancestral state reconstruction to the Greengenes marker gene reference tree and combining extant and ancestral genomes with exponential reciprocal phylogenetic-distance weighting, as implemented in PICRUSt.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The taxa of interest already have complete reference genomes — use their actual annotated gene content instead of inference. The community includes viral or eukaryotic components: PICRUSt only includes bacterial and archaeal 16S marker gene sequences, so viral/eukaryotic metagenome components are not inferred. Strain-level functional variation matters and the marker gene sequence is identical among strains — the method cannot distinguish variation at the strain level.

skills.summary: Aligns per-sample gene abundance files (e.g., Cufflinks-style FPKM outputs) on their shared gene identifier column and merges them into a single genes-by-samples matrix, as implemented in NASQAR's mergeFPKMs/GeneCountMerger preprocessing apps so downstream RNA-seq apps like DESeq2Shiny can consume one unified table.

skills.description: Use when a mapped gene frequency count table (reads per gene across samples) is the input and gene-level abundances must be compared across samples; long genes systematically accumulate more reads, biasing downstream normalization.

skills.search_text: gene-length-normalization Use when a mapped gene frequency count table (reads per gene across samples) is the input and gene-level abundances must be compared across samples; long genes systematically accumulate more reads, biasing downstream normalization. Input is already normalized (e.g. relative frequencies or previously CSS-scaled data) — dividing by length again would introduce bias Input is taxon-level abundance rather than gene-level counts; species-level data undergo CSS normalization directly without gene-length correction Working with assembly-based gene content prediction rather than mapping-based counts against a gene catalog http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Length-corrects mapped gene frequencies by dividing each gene's read count by its gene length before CSS normalization, as done in the CAMAMED pipeline so that longer genes do not accrue inflated abundance purely from being longer mapping targets. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Length-corrects mapped gene frequencies by dividing each gene's read count by its gene length before CSS normalization, as done in the CAMAMED pipeline so that longer genes do not accrue inflated abundance purely from being longer mapping targets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized (e.g. relative frequencies or previously CSS-scaled data) — dividing by length again would introduce bias Input is taxon-level abundance rather than gene-level counts; species-level data undergo CSS normalization directly without gene-length correction Working with assembly-based gene content prediction rather than mapping-based counts against a gene catalog

skills.description: Reference for computing per-gene abundances from read-to-gene alignment hits when reads may match multiple genes equally well, and when gene-length bias in shotgun metagenomic count data must be corrected.
skills.name: gene-length-normalization
skills.search_text: gene-length-normalization Reference for computing per-gene abundances from read-to-gene alignment hits when reads may match multiple genes equally well, and when gene-length bias in shotgun metagenomic count data must be corrected. Input is already a gene abundance table — this skill operates on raw read-to-gene alignment hits, not on existing feature tables Aggregating gene abundances into orthology groups or pathways (this is MetaLAFFA's separate ortholog-counting and aggregation steps) When alignments retain only a single unambiguous best hit per read, fractional tie distribution reduces to plain integer counting http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 MetaLAFFA's gene abundance calculation: per-gene read counts are computed with fractional counting for reads tied across multiple equally-good hits, then normalized by gene length so longer genes are not over-counted. This is implemented in a custom Python script that consumes hit-filtered DIAMOND alignments and a gene-length normalization (.norm) table. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: MetaLAFFA's gene abundance calculation: per-gene read counts are computed with fractional counting for reads tied across multiple equally-good hits, then normalized by gene length so longer genes are not over-counted. skills.summary: MAGinator's synteny clustering groups gene clusters (ORFs) by how often they occur adjacent on contigs, producing synteny_clusters.tab associations that link shared pathways to subspecies-level MAG clusters. When combined with eggNOG-mapper KEGG ortholog annotations, it enables quantitative functional-coherence evaluation of each synteny cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Accuracy is limited by MAGinator's lack of operon awareness, so avoid over-interpreting synteny clusters as true operons when precise operon boundaries matter If you only need taxonomic profiles or abundances without gene-content/pathway association, use MAGinator's signature-gene abundance output instead of the synteny-clustering step When input is raw reads without prior assembly, binning (VAMB clusters.tsv) and ORF calling, the pipeline prerequisites are missing

skills.description: Use when a case-control gene association test has flagged disease-associated genes (e.g. from KEGG/UniRef90-based gene analysis of SCZ metagenomes) and you need a gene-to-taxon attribution by tracing sequencing reads back to source organisms.
skills.name: gene-taxa-link-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-taxa-link-analysis Use when a case-control gene association test has flagged disease-associated genes (e.g. from KEGG/UniRef90-based gene analysis of SCZ metagenomes) and you need a gene-to-taxon attribution by tracing sequencing reads back to source organisms. The input reads have not passed OMARU read QC and profiling steps (OMARU_read_QC.sm, OMARU_QCed1.sm, OMARU_QCed2.sm) and no QCed sample list has been generated The goal is a case-control differential abundance MWAS (phylogenetic, gene, or pathway association testing) rather than assigning organisms of origin to already-identified genes No target genes have been shortlisted from the gene association test — TARGETS would be empty and there is nothing to trace back http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Attribute disease-associated metagenomic genes to their organisms of origin via read-level phylogenetic traceback in OMARU. skills.summary: Attribute disease-associated metagenomic genes to their organisms of origin via read-level phylogenetic traceback in OMARU. This links gene-level MWAS findings (e.g. the SCZ-associated gene Vpar_1847) to taxa, resolving which organisms carry the associated genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input reads have not passed OMARU read QC and profiling steps (OMARU_read_QC.sm, OMARU_QCed1.sm, OMARU_QCed2.sm) and no QCed sample list has been generated The goal is a case-control differential abundance MWAS (phylogenetic, gene, or pathway association testing) rather than assigning organisms of origin to already-identified genes No target genes have been shortlisted from the gene association test — TARGETS would be empty and there is nothing to trace back

skills.description: Use when quantifying how a hierarchical taxonomic classifier generalizes to species labels absent from its training vocabulary — e.g., after training on Greengenes2 2024.09 and evaluating on the 69,335-sequence held-out test set.
skills.name: generalization-evaluation-on-unseen-labels
skills.search_text: generalization-evaluation-on-unseen-labels Use when quantifying how a hierarchical taxonomic classifier generalizes to species labels absent from its training vocabulary — e.g., after training on Greengenes2 2024.09 and evaluating on the 69,335-sequence held-out test set. When the goal is overall accuracy/F1 on the full held-out test set rather than label-novelty stratification — the Seen/Unseen split would discard the majority (Seen) signal. When evaluating on reference databases outside Greengenes2 (e.g., SILVA or RDP), since the Seen/Unseen rule is defined against the Greengenes2 2024.09 training vocabulary. When inputs are quality-scored reads rather than FASTA sequences, since DeepTaxa currently operates on FASTA and does not incorporate base-level quality scores. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A stratified evaluation protocol that partitions held-out test sequences into Seen (species label present in training vocabulary) and Unseen (label absent) subsets, then measures how per-rank accuracy degrades on the Unseen subset, evaluated only up to the rank preceding each lineage's first missing rank. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: A stratified evaluation protocol that partitions held-out test sequences into Seen (species label present in training vocabulary) and Unseen (label absent) subsets, then measures how per-rank accuracy degrades on the Unseen subset, evaluated only up to the rank preceding each lineage's first missing rank.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is overall accuracy/F1 on the full held-out test set rather than label-novelty stratification — the Seen/Unseen split would discard the majority (Seen) signal. When evaluating on reference databases outside Greengenes2 (e.g., SILVA or RDP), since the Seen/Unseen rule is defined against the Greengenes2 2024.09 training vocabulary. When inputs are quality-scored reads rather than FASTA sequences, since DeepTaxa currently operates on FASTA and does not incorporate base-level quality scores.

skills.description: Use when testing association between a microbial taxa-set (e.g. ≥5 taxa at genus/family/order/class/phylum level) and a continuous or binary outcome, where most taxa in the clade are noise and a data-adaptive multivariate GLM test with permutation calibration is needed.
skills.name: generalized-linear-model-association-testing
skills.search_text: generalized-linear-model-association-testing Use when testing association between a microbial taxa-set (e.g. ≥5 taxa at genus/family/order/class/phylum level) and a continuous or binary outcome, where most taxa in the clade are noise and a data-adaptive multivariate GLM test with permutation calibration is needed. The input is a single taxon or a taxa-set with fewer than five taxa — the article restricts association analysis to taxa-sets containing at least five taxa The association signal is extremely sparse — AMAT was not the most powerful method in that simulation regime The outcome requires a link function outside the standard GLM framework (linear/logistic) implemented by the AMAT package http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Performs multivariate microbiome association testing of H0: β = 0 between a selected set of taxa and a continuous or binary outcome using AMAT's data-adaptive sum of powered score (aSPU/SPU) statistic within a generalized linear model framework, with permutation-based P-value calibration. Feature selection via distance correlation learning shrinks noise taxa to exactly zero before testing. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab120
skills.summary: Performs multivariate microbiome association testing of H0: β = 0 between a selected set of taxa and a continuous or binary outcome using AMAT's data-adaptive sum of powered score (aSPU/SPU) statistic within a generalized linear model framework, with permutation-based P-value calibration. Feature selection via distance correlation learning shrinks noise taxa to exactly zero before testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single taxon or a taxa-set with fewer than five taxa — the article restricts association analysis to taxa-sets containing at least five taxa The association signal is extremely sparse — AMAT was not the most powerful method in that simulation regime The outcome requires a link function outside the standard GLM framework (linear/logistic) implemented by the AMAT package

skills.description: Use when a reference-free variant-discovery workflow (e.g. ebwt2snp-style positional clustering) requires the LCP array and generalized Suffix Array of a FASTA/FASTQ read collection, or when benchmarking disk/RAM footprint of GSA+LCP pipelines against BWT-only ones.
skills.name: generalized-suffix-array-lcp-construction
skills.search_text: generalized-suffix-array-lcp-construction Use when a reference-free variant-discovery workflow (e.g. ebwt2snp-style positional clustering) requires the LCP array and generalized Suffix Array of a FASTA/FASTQ read collection, or when benchmarking disk/RAM footprint of GSA+LCP pipelines against BWT-only ones. The downstream tool is ebwt2InDel, which works directly on the BWT alone and computes the LCP on-the-fly — building the GSA and LCP array is unnecessary and costs roughly one order of magnitude more disk space (73 GB vs 9.5 GB on a 20x real dataset) Reads contain unknown characters 'N' — the input fragments must contain only 'A','C','G','T', so filtering or randomizing N-carrying reads must happen first http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Build the generalized Suffix Array (GSA) and LCP array of a collection of sequencing reads using external-memory tools (egsa, egap, or BCR_LCP_GSA), as required by the old ebwt2snp variant-discovery pipeline and to quantify its space cost relative to BWT-only approaches. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Build the generalized Suffix Array (GSA) and LCP array of a collection of sequencing reads using external-memory tools (egsa, egap, or BCR_LCP_GSA), as required by the old ebwt2snp variant-discovery pipeline and to quantify its space cost relative to BWT-only approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream tool is ebwt2InDel, which works directly on the BWT alone and computes the LCP on-the-fly — building the GSA and LCP array is unnecessary and costs roughly one order of magnitude more disk space (73 GB vs 9.5 GB on a 20x real dataset) Reads contain unknown characters 'N' — the input fragments must contain only 'A','C','G','T', so filtering or randomizing N-carrying reads must happen first

skills.description: Use when the input is a complete genome annotation (GenBank .gbff/.gbk plus FASTA, e.g. Deinococcus radiodurans R1) and the goal is to extract all annotated CDS/ORF lengths or adjacent-gene features for fitting a gene-length distribution model.
skills.name: genome-annotation-parsing-with-biopython
skills.search_text: genome-annotation-parsing-with-biopython Use when the input is a complete genome annotation (GenBank .gbff/.gbk plus FASTA, e.g. Deinococcus radiodurans R1) and the goal is to extract all annotated CDS/ORF lengths or adjacent-gene features for fitting a gene-length distribution model. Input is metagenomic read data rather than a finished genome annotation — this skill derives training statistics from curated annotation, it does not predict genes (use Glimmer-MG itself) You only need gene predictions and have no reference genome annotation to parse — the parsing step adds nothing for a pure prediction run The annotation is in formats Biopython SeqIO cannot parse (e.g. raw GFF3 without conversion) — convert first rather than hand-rolling a parser http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Parses GenBank/FASTA genome annotation records with Biopython to extract annotated coding ORFs and derived per-gene features (lengths, adjacent-gene orientations, intergenic distances). It is the data-preparation layer used to fit ORF length distributions such as those Glimmer-MG models for metagenomic gene prediction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067

It is the data-preparation layer used to fit ORF length distributions such as those Glimmer-MG models for metagenomic gene prediction.

skills.description: Use when a draft assembly contains N-wildcard gaps between contigs in scaffold sequences and the goal is to close them with short-read data (e.g. GAGE PE datasets) and quantify remaining gap content.
skills.name: genome-assembly-gap-statistics
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-gap-statistics Use when a draft assembly contains N-wildcard gaps between contigs in scaffold sequences and the goal is to close them with short-read data (e.g. GAGE PE datasets) and quantify remaining gap content. The input consists of unassembled contigs with no scaffold gap regions to close The goal is initial scaffold construction or PE-read mapping rather than gap closure (use the pregraph/contig/map/scaff steps without -F instead) Only long reads or non-Illumina data are available — GapCloser is designed for Illumina GA short-read assemblies http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reconstructs and evaluates the SOAPdenovo2 GapCloser-style gap closing step, replacing N-wildcard gap regions in scaffold FASTA files via local reassembly with paired-end reads, then tabulating closed-gap counts and residual N-run statistics. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: Reconstructs and evaluates the SOAPdenovo2 GapCloser-style gap closing step, replacing N-wildcard gap regions in scaffold FASTA files via local reassembly with paired-end reads, then tabulating closed-gap counts and residual N-run statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input consists of unassembled contigs with no scaffold gap regions to close The goal is initial scaffold construction or PE-read mapping rather than gap closure (use the pregraph/contig/map/scaff steps without -F instead) Only long reads or non-Illumina data are available — GapCloser is designed for Illumina GA short-read assemblies

skills.description: Use when a released genome assembly (contig/scaffold FASTA files) needs its reported statistics — contig N50, scaffold N50, and coverage against a reference genome — independently reproduced and validated.
skills.name: genome-assembly-n50-calculation
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-n50-calculation Use when a released genome assembly (contig/scaffold FASTA files) needs its reported statistics — contig N50, scaffold N50, and coverage against a reference genome — independently reproduced and validated. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than an assembled FASTA — assembly must first be produced (e.g. with SOAPdenovo2's pregraph/contig/map/scaff steps) No reference genome is available, since the coverage metric (93.91% for YH v2) requires aligning scaffolds to a reference such as hg19 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Recompute contig N50, scaffold N50, and reference-coverage metrics from a de novo genome assembly (FASTA) to independently verify published assembly statistics, as done for the YH genome v2 assembly produced by SOAPdenovo2. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: Recompute contig N50, scaffold N50, and reference-coverage metrics from a de novo genome assembly (FASTA) to independently verify published assembly statistics, as done for the YH genome v2 assembly produced by SOAPdenovo2.

skills.search_text: genome-assembly-quality-assessment Use when FASTA contig files from one or more genome assemblers need multifaceted quality assessment and comparison, with or without a reference genome, as in the four E. coli K-12 MG1655 assembly evaluation. When no reference is available and you need reference-aware metrics (NGA50, genome fraction, misassembly coordinates) — reference-free mode only yields contiguity/completeness metrics When the goal is downstream structural/functional annotation or genome mining rather than assembly quality comparison When evaluating a metagenomic dataset with plain QUAST instead of the MetaQUAST extension http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Evaluate and compare genome assemblies using QUAST/WebQUAST, which computes contiguity metrics (N50, N90, auN, largest contig), completeness via BUSCO, and reference-based misassembly and NGA50 statistics, producing a report.tsv summary table with assessment plots and Icarus viewers. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad406
skills.summary: Evaluate and compare genome assemblies using QUAST/WebQUAST, which computes contiguity metrics (N50, N90, auN, largest contig), completeness via BUSCO, and reference-based misassembly and NGA50 statistics, producing a report.tsv summary table with assessment plots and Icarus viewers.

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic binning study reports genome yields (e.g. complete vs draft counts) and you need to reproduce or extract the per-category, per-phylum breakdown from abstract text, tables, or supplementary tables.
