skills.description: Use when comparing metagenomic sequence classifiers on the same read sets and you need genus-level sensitivity/precision tables, or when quantifying accuracy loss from a reduced Kraken database such as MiniKraken 4-GB or Kraken-GB.
skills.name: genus-level-sensitivity-precision-evaluation
skills.search_text: genus-level-sensitivity-precision-evaluation Use when comparing metagenomic sequence classifiers on the same read sets and you need genus-level sensitivity/precision tables, or when quantifying accuracy loss from a reduced Kraken database such as MiniKraken 4-GB or Kraken-GB. The goal is abundance estimation rather than per-read classification — abundance programs (e.g. MetaPhlAn) classify only a small percentage of sequences and are not comparable on per-read sensitivity/precision Reads lack a genus-level taxonomic entry for their origin, or fewer than two other taxa at the excluded rank share the origin's clade — such reads must be excluded, so evaluation on such data is invalid The database variant under test was not built by the documented procedure (e.g. MiniKraken shrinking factor 19, Kraken-GB adapter and contig-end k-mer removal), since the expected accuracy deltas will not be reproducible http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark taxonomic classifiers by computing genus-level sensitivity and precision on metagenomic read sets (real HiSeq/MiSeq and simulated simBA-5/simMC reads), comparing Kraken against Megablast, PhymmBL, PhymmBL65 and NBC, and measuring database-reduction effects (MiniKraken, Kraken-GB, -Q mode). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Benchmark taxonomic classifiers by computing genus-level sensitivity and precision on metagenomic read sets (real HiSeq/MiSeq and simulated simBA-5/simMC reads), comparing Kraken against Megablast, PhymmBL, PhymmBL65 and NBC, and measuring database-reduction effects (MiniKraken, Kraken-GB, -Q mode).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is abundance estimation rather than per-read classification — abundance programs (e.g. MetaPhlAn) classify only a small percentage of sequences and are not comparable on per-read sensitivity/precision Reads lack a genus-level taxonomic entry for their origin, or fewer than two other taxa at the excluded rank share the origin's clade — such reads must be excluded, so evaluation on such data is invalid The database variant under test was not built by the documented procedure (e.g. MiniKraken shrinking factor 19, Kraken-GB adapter and contig-end k-mer removal), since the expected accuracy deltas will not be reproducible

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a metagenomic read classifier on genome-exclusion simulations where the true source genome is known, and per-read calls must be summarized into genus-/phylum-level sensitivity and precision stratified by reference-genome availability.
skills.name: genus-level-taxonomic-aggregation
skills.search_text: genus-level-taxonomic-aggregation Use when benchmarking a metagenomic read classifier on genome-exclusion simulations where the true source genome is known, and per-read calls must be summarized into genus-/phylum-level sensitivity and precision stratified by reference-genome availability. Classifying real metagenomes without ground-truth source genomes — there is no known correct genus per read, so sensitivity cannot be computed and only fraction-classified metrics (e.g. Kaiju classifying up to 10x more reads) apply Genera with no available reference genomes — the paper states genus-level classification of shotgun reads is impossible there, so stratified sensitivity is undefined Evaluating on data where the sequenced strain is already in the reference database — nucleotide-level classifiers assess the entire genome and Kaiju is less sensitive in that regime, inverting the benchmark's conclusion http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Aggregates per-read taxonomic classifications from metagenomic classifiers (Kaiju, Kraken, Clark) into genus- and phylum-level sensitivity and precision, stratified by how many reference genomes each genus has, to quantify classifier behavior in underrepresented genera. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Aggregates per-read taxonomic classifications from metagenomic classifiers (Kaiju, Kraken, Clark) into genus- and phylum-level sensitivity and precision, stratified by how many reference genomes each genus has, to quantify classifier behavior in underrepresented genera.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Classifying real metagenomes without ground-truth source genomes — there is no known correct genus per read, so sensitivity cannot be computed and only fraction-classified metrics (e.g. Kaiju classifying up to 10x more reads) apply Genera with no available reference genomes — the paper states genus-level classification of shotgun reads is impossible there, so stratified sensitivity is undefined Evaluating on data where the sequenced strain is already in the reference database — nucleotide-level classifiers assess the entire genome and Kaiju is less sensitive in that regime, inverting the benchmark's conclusion

skills.description: Use when you have variant calls (VCF) from multiple strategies — e.g. FreeBayes/SvABA on Illumina BAMs, Long Ranger on 10x Linked-Reads, or calling directly from Supernova2 assemblies — and need to score them against GIAB truth sets.
skills.name: giab-variant-benchmarking
skills.search_text: giab-variant-benchmarking Use when you have variant calls (VCF) from multiple strategies — e.g. FreeBayes/SvABA on Illumina BAMs, Long Ranger on 10x Linked-Reads, or calling directly from Supernova2 assemblies — and need to score them against GIAB truth sets. This provides the ground-truth comparison that in the source study showed reference-based SNV calls outperform assembly-derived SNV calls. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Benchmark variant call sets (SNVs and SVs) from reference-based Illumina/10x pipelines and de novo assemblies against GIAB benchmark call sets, quantifying precision, recall, and F1 per caller and sample. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is simulated data with a known truth set (e.g. LRTK-SIM-generated Linked-Reads from gen_fasta.py haplotypes) — compare directly to the simulated truth instead of GIAB. skills.name: gibbs-sampler-clustering-of-sequencing-reads
skills.search_text: gibbs-sampler-clustering-of-sequencing-reads Use when error-prone shotgun or amplicon NGS reads (e.g. 454 Titanium pyrosequencing of HIV-1 pol) aligned to a reference must be partitioned into local-haplotype clusters to correct sequencing errors before quantifying genetic diversity. You need global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction from adjacent overlapping reads — ShoRAH2 has global mode disabled; use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or V-pipe's global haplotype options instead The goal is single-nucleotide variant calling with strand-bias accounting — that is shorah snv's role, not read clustering for error correction Input reads are not yet aligned to a reference — alignment is a prerequisite step before windowing and clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Clusters error-prone deep-sequencing reads by genome window using a Dirichlet process mixture with Gibbs sampling (ShoRAH's diri_sampler), so that read clusters define local haplotypes whose majority-vote consensus corrects sequencing errors and whose cluster sizes estimate haplotype prevalence. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: Clusters error-prone deep-sequencing reads by genome window using a Dirichlet process mixture with Gibbs sampling (ShoRAH's diri_sampler), so that read clusters define local haplotypes whose majority-vote consensus corrects sequencing errors and whose cluster sizes estimate haplotype prevalence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction from adjacent overlapping reads — ShoRAH2 has global mode disabled; use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or V-pipe's global haplotype options instead The goal is single-nucleotide variant calling with strand-bias accounting — that is shorah snv's role, not read clustering for error correction Input reads are not yet aligned to a reference — alignment is a prerequisite step before windowing and clustering

skills.name: gibbs-sampler-convergence-tuning
skills.search_text: gibbs-sampler-convergence-tuning Use when running diri_sampler-based error correction on overlapping windows of a read alignment (BAM/CRAM or MSA) and you must set sampler iterations and the Dirichlet hyperparameter alpha to achieve proper mixing for haplotype reconstruction. Input is raw unaligned FASTQ reads — reads must first be aligned to the reference sequence of the amplified region before windowing You need global haplotype reconstruction from ShoRAH2 — global mode is disabled there; use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or the global haplotype options in V-pipe instead The task is strand-bias-aware SNV calling only and you will not tune or inspect sampler convergence — invoke shorah snv directly rather than re-tuning diri_sampler http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Tuning skill for the Dirichlet-process mixture Gibbs sampler (diri_sampler) in ShoRAH, which clusters reads overlapping the same genomic window to correct sequencing errors and infer local haplotypes. skills.summary: Tuning skill for the Dirichlet-process mixture Gibbs sampler (diri_sampler) in ShoRAH, which clusters reads overlapping the same genomic window to correct sequencing errors and infer local haplotypes. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unaligned FASTQ reads — reads must first be aligned to the reference sequence of the amplified region before windowing You need global haplotype reconstruction from ShoRAH2 — global mode is disabled there; use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or the global haplotype options in V-pipe instead The task is strand-bias-aware SNV calling only and you will not tune or inspect sampler convergence — invoke shorah snv directly rather than re-tuning diri_sampler

skills.name: glcm-texture-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: glcm-texture-feature-extraction Use when Sentinel-1 gamma_0 backscatter stacks (e.g. ALB_gamma0_VH.tif / ALB_gamma0_VV.tif) must be converted into spatial-heterogeneity texture predictor variables for habitat-structure or biodiversity modelling on a 10 m grid. skills.search_text: greedy-incremental-sequence-clustering Use when you need to partition a large protein sequence set (e.g. UniProt-scale, hundreds of millions of sequences) into redundancy-reduced clusters after a k-mer prefilter and alignment steps have produced verified edges. The set of items lacks a definable set of m keys (e.g. k-mers) per item such that cluster members are likely to share at least one key — the article notes this shared-key condition restricts Linclust's generalizability Falsely clustered pairs are costly and every pairwise link must be verified with the exact similarity measure against all sequences — that regime still requires quadratic time, which this skill does not cover A clustering algorithm other than greedy-incremental is required, e.g. when representatives need not be the longest member or when non-overlapping assignment is enforced downstream before edge construction http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 Final clustering stage of the Linclust algorithm: after filtering and gapped alignment, sequences are added as reverse edges, sorted by decreasing length, and greedily peeled into clusters so that the longest sequence always becomes the cluster representative. This yields clustering in linear time O(mN) with representatives that maximize cluster stability. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-04964-5

The input is raw metagenomic reads or an unassembled FASTA with no bins — binning (e.g. MetaBAT2) and CheckM2 assessment must happen first You need MAG quality estimates themselves rather than categorization — run CheckM2 to produce completeness/contamination before applying these thresholds The input already consists of a completed quality-category table; re-running the categorization would only duplicate existing labels http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Applies GSC-style MAG quality thresholds to CheckM2 completeness/contamination estimates to categorize metagenomic assembly bins into near complete, high quality, medium quality, and low quality classes, as implemented in the Mapler pipeline's checkm report step. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Applies GSC-style MAG quality thresholds to CheckM2 completeness/contamination estimates to categorize metagenomic assembly bins into near complete, high quality, medium quality, and low quality classes, as implemented in the Mapler pipeline's checkm report step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw metagenomic reads or an unassembled FASTA with no bins — binning (e.g. MetaBAT2) and CheckM2 assessment must happen first You need MAG quality estimates themselves rather than categorization — run CheckM2 to produce completeness/contamination before applying these thresholds The input already consists of a completed quality-category table; re-running the categorization would only duplicate existing labels

skills.description: Use when GTDBtk (v1.0.2) classifications of MAGs or genomes must be compared against NCBI-taxonomy-based ground truth (e.g., HMP genome labels or CAMI taxonomies), because GTDBtk outputs use GTDB taxonomy.
skills.name: gtdb-to-ncbi-taxonomy-conversion
skills.search_text: gtdb-to-ncbi-taxonomy-conversion Use when GTDBtk (v1.0.2) classifications of MAGs or genomes must be compared against NCBI-taxonomy-based ground truth (e.g., HMP genome labels or CAMI taxonomies), because GTDBtk outputs use GTDB taxonomy. kMetaShot classification results — the reference uses NCBI taxonomy, so no conversion is needed for kMetaShot outputs HMP genomes labelled with NCBI-based flat-file taxonomy where GTDBtk was not run — labels are already NCBI-native Analyses comparing tools purely within the GTDB framework where NCBI nomenclature is not the reference standard http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Converts taxonomic labels produced by GTDBtk from the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB) taxonomy to NCBI taxonomy using the ncbi_vs_gtdb_r89 conversion tables, so that classifier outputs (GTDBtk vs. kMetaShot) can be compared against NCBI-based expected taxonomies such as those of the HMP genomes and CAMI II reference taxonomies. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: Converts taxonomic labels produced by GTDBtk from the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB) taxonomy to NCBI taxonomy using the ncbi_vs_gtdb_r89 conversion tables, so that classifier outputs (GTDBtk vs. kMetaShot) can be compared against NCBI-based expected taxonomies such as those of the HMP genomes and CAMI II reference taxonomies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: kMetaShot classification results — the reference uses NCBI taxonomy, so no conversion is needed for kMetaShot outputs HMP genomes labelled with NCBI-based flat-file taxonomy where GTDBtk was not run — labels are already NCBI-native Analyses comparing tools purely within the GTDB framework where NCBI nomenclature is not the reference standard

skills.description: Use when you have assembled and binned MAG FASTA files with BUSCO quality summaries and need GTDB lineage assignments per bin, with a fallback classifier for bins that fail quality gates.
skills.name: gtdbtk-genome-taxonomy-assignment
skills.search_text: gtdbtk-genome-taxonomy-assignment Use when you have assembled and binned MAG FASTA files with BUSCO quality summaries and need GTDB lineage assignments per bin, with a fallback classifier for bins that fail quality gates. Bins have no accompanying BUSCO quality summaries, so the completeness/contamination gating required to route bins to GTDB-Tk cannot be applied Input is raw reads rather than assembled, binned MAG FASTA files — this skill operates only on the taxonomic-classification stage after assembly and binning Functional (non-taxonomic) annotation of MAGs is the goal; the article lists functional annotation as a step not yet included in nf-core/mag http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Taxonomic classification of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) in the final stage of nf-core/mag, using GTDB-Tk for quality-gated bins and CAT/BAT as the fallback so that every bin receives a lineage assignment. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Taxonomic classification of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) in the final stage of nf-core/mag, using GTDB-Tk for quality-gated bins and CAT/BAT as the fallback so that every bin receives a lineage assignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Bins have no accompanying BUSCO quality summaries, so the completeness/contamination gating required to route bins to GTDB-Tk cannot be applied Input is raw reads rather than assembled, binned MAG FASTA files — this skill operates only on the taxonomic-classification stage after assembly and binning Functional (non-taxonomic) annotation of MAGs is the goal; the article lists functional annotation as a step not yet included in nf-core/mag

skills.description: Use when a GTF/GFF annotation built on a linear reference genome must be lifted onto a pangenome graph (constructed with VARI-merge, k=22) so gene regions can be located via cSupB bubble coordinates.
skills.name: gtf-annotation-coordinate-projection
skills.search_text: gtf-annotation-coordinate-projection Use when a GTF/GFF annotation built on a linear reference genome must be lifted onto a pangenome graph (constructed with VARI-merge, k=22) so gene regions can be located via cSupB bubble coordinates. Gene elements shorter than k (k=22): they may map to multiple nodes on the graph, making the analysis complicated and ambiguous The graph is degenerate or contains unresolved cycles — the method requires a directed, acyclic, nondegenerate graph with unique start and end nodes The annotation references an organism/genome absent from the sample color set, so no parent source node containing the reference genome exists for RPD http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Projects linear-reference GTF gene annotations (e.g., mitochondrial gene coordinates) onto a colored de Bruijn graph pangenome by mapping reference positions through the tri-tuple coordinate system (position, bubid, basecolor) derived from the cSupB decomposition. It demonstrates that existing linear annotation data remain usable on graph-based pangenome coordinates. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04149-w
skills.summary: Projects linear-reference GTF gene annotations (e.g., mitochondrial gene coordinates) onto a colored de Bruijn graph pangenome by mapping reference positions through the tri-tuple coordinate system (position, bubid, basecolor) derived from the cSupB decomposition. It demonstrates that existing linear annotation data remain usable on graph-based pangenome coordinates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene elements shorter than k (k=22): they may map to multiple nodes on the graph, making the analysis complicated and ambiguous The graph is degenerate or contains unresolved cycles — the method requires a directed, acyclic, nondegenerate graph with unique start and end nodes The annotation references an organism/genome absent from the sample color set, so no parent source node containing the reference genome exists for RPD

skills.description: Use when GWAS summary statistics are available and the goal is pathway-level enrichment (PASCAL) followed by overlap testing against disease metagenome (MWAS) pathway enrichment at P<0.05.
skills.name: gwas-summary-statistics-pathway-enrichment
skills.search_text: gwas-summary-statistics-pathway-enrichment Use when GWAS summary statistics are available and the goal is pathway-level enrichment (PASCAL) followed by overlap testing against disease metagenome (MWAS) pathway enrichment at P<0.05. When raw genotype data (not GWAS summary statistics) are the input — PASCAL in this workflow consumes precomputed summary statistics only When the aim is metagenome-side pathway enrichment alone; use the OMARU functional association test (OMARU_Func_AS.sm / OMARU_Func_permutation.sm) without the GWAS overlap step When confounders should be integrated into the case-control model — the article notes covariate integration is not currently implemented in OMARU http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Compute host germline pathway enrichment from GWAS summary statistics with PASCAL and test overlap with MWAS-enriched pathways via Fisher's exact test. In OMARU this links the metagenome and host genome at pathway level, yielding PFisher = 0.011 (SCZ) and 0.008 (T2D). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: Compute host germline pathway enrichment from GWAS summary statistics with PASCAL and test overlap with MWAS-enriched pathways via Fisher's exact test. In OMARU this links the metagenome and host genome at pathway level, yielding PFisher = 0.011 (SCZ) and 0.008 (T2D).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When raw genotype data (not GWAS summary statistics) are the input — PASCAL in this workflow consumes precomputed summary statistics only When the aim is metagenome-side pathway enrichment alone; use the OMARU functional association test (OMARU_Func_AS.sm / OMARU_Func_permutation.sm) without the GWAS overlap step When confounders should be integrated into the case-control model — the article notes covariate integration is not currently implemented in OMARU

skills.description: Use when raw FASTQ reads (Illumina MiSeq or ONT MinION 2D) from the same bacterial isolate must yield comparable drug-resistance calls, and a single known SNP (gyrA S84L) is expected as the resistance determinant.
skills.name: gyra-resistance-snp-interpretation
skills.search_text: gyra-resistance-snp-interpretation Use when raw FASTQ reads (Illumina MiSeq or ONT MinION 2D) from the same bacterial isolate must yield comparable drug-resistance calls, and a single known SNP (gyrA S84L) is expected as the resistance determinant. The isolate has multiple unknown resistance mechanisms — Mykrobe's panel is trained on known mutations, so uncharacterized mechanisms (e.g. pyrazinamide in M. tuberculosis) will not be detected The input is assembled/variant-called VCF data rather than raw sequence data — Mykrobe predictor takes raw sequence data as input The analysis goal is per-drug sensitivity estimation for rare resistant phenotypes — the article notes false-negative rates were only estimated where >10 resistant samples existed in the validation set http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Interprets a single gyrA S84L SNP as the ciprofloxacin resistance determinant in a multi-drug-resistant S. aureus isolate, using Mykrobe predictor's de Bruijn graph genotype caller on both Illumina MiSeq and ONT MinION raw reads, and validating platform concordance (12/12 identical calls). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Interprets a single gyrA S84L SNP as the ciprofloxacin resistance determinant in a multi-drug-resistant S. aureus isolate, using Mykrobe predictor's de Bruijn graph genotype caller on both Illumina MiSeq and ONT MinION raw reads, and validating platform concordance (12/12 identical calls).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The isolate has multiple unknown resistance mechanisms — Mykrobe's panel is trained on known mutations, so uncharacterized mechanisms (e.g. pyrazinamide in M. tuberculosis) will not be detected The input is assembled/variant-called VCF data rather than raw sequence data — Mykrobe predictor takes raw sequence data as input The analysis goal is per-drug sensitivity estimation for rare resistant phenotypes — the article notes false-negative rates were only estimated where >10 resistant samples existed in the validation set

skills.description: Use when raw or pooled long-read (ONT/PacBio) FASTQ.gz files must be filtered for minimum read length and average Phred quality before assembly or benchmarking, e.g. pre-processing ONT reads for Plassembler.
skills.name: gzip-fastq-stream-processing
skills.search_text: gzip-fastq-stream-processing Use when raw or pooled long-read (ONT/PacBio) FASTQ.gz files must be filtered for minimum read length and average Phred quality before assembly or benchmarking, e.g. pre-processing ONT reads for Plassembler. Input is short-read (Illumina/MGI) FASTQ that needs adapter/polyG trimming — that is the domain of fastp, not chopper The FASTQ has already been quality- and length-filtered and only needs downstream processing (e.g. subsampling with rasusa or minimap2 mapping) The objective is trimming/adaptor removal rather than whole-record quality/length filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Quality- and length-filter pooled, gzipped ONT long-read FASTQs by streaming from stdin to stdout with chopper, retaining only reads meeting a minimum length (500 bp) and minimum average Q-score (9), as done in the Plassembler QC/benchmarking workflow. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Quality- and length-filter pooled, gzipped ONT long-read FASTQs by streaming from stdin to stdout with chopper, retaining only reads meeting a minimum length (500 bp) and minimum average Q-score (9), as done in the Plassembler QC/benchmarking workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read (Illumina/MGI) FASTQ that needs adapter/polyG trimming — that is the domain of fastp, not chopper The FASTQ has already been quality- and length-filtered and only needs downstream processing (e.g. subsampling with rasusa or minimap2 mapping) The objective is trimming/adaptor removal rather than whole-record quality/length filtering

skills.description: Use when you must verify that a MapReduce-based analysis tool's runtime scales acceptably (linearly) with input volume, or when you need a per-metric/per-mode runtime breakdown to identify the most expensive computation.
skills.name: hadoop-mapreduce-job-benchmarking
skills.search_text: hadoop-mapreduce-job-benchmarking Use when you must verify that a MapReduce-based analysis tool's runtime scales acceptably (linearly) with input volume, or when you need a per-metric/per-mode runtime breakdown to identify the most expensive computation. Input data are small (single-run, GB-scale or less) where wall-clock timing without a scaling sweep suffices and Hadoop overhead dominates. The goal is to compare clustering accuracy or distance-metric quality rather than runtime/scaling behavior. The tool under test is not a Hadoop MapReduce job, since the -s/-m/-w option matrix and MapReduce scaling semantics will not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmark the runtime scaling of a Hadoop MapReduce tool (Libra) across synthetically generated metagenome datasets of increasing input volume (10, 20, 30, and 40 samples of 9.3 GB each, 93–372 GB total), tabulating elapsed times by dataset size, scoring algorithm (-s), and run mode (-m) to verify approximately linear scaling despite quadratic growth in all-vs-all sample pairs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Benchmark the runtime scaling of a Hadoop MapReduce tool (Libra) across synthetically generated metagenome datasets of increasing input volume (10, 20, 30, and 40 samples of 9.3 GB each, 93–372 GB total), tabulating elapsed times by dataset size, scoring algorithm (-s), and run mode (-m) to verify approximately linear scaling despite quadratic growth in all-vs-all sample pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are small (single-run, GB-scale or less) where wall-clock timing without a scaling sweep suffices and Hadoop overhead dominates. The goal is to compare clustering accuracy or distance-metric quality rather than runtime/scaling behavior. The tool under test is not a Hadoop MapReduce job, since the -s/-m/-w option matrix and MapReduce scaling semantics will not apply.

skills.description: Use when you need an all-vs-all distance/similarity matrix across many metagenomic FASTA/FASTQ read sets where data reduction or presence/absence metrics (e.g., Mash sketches, Simka Jaccard-ab) lose clustering resolution by community composition and abundance.
skills.name: hadoop-mapreduce-metagenomic-scoring
skills.search_text: hadoop-mapreduce-metagenomic-scoring Use when you need an all-vs-all distance/similarity matrix across many metagenomic FASTA/FASTQ read sets where data reduction or presence/absence metrics (e.g., Mash sketches, Simka Jaccard-ab) lose clustering resolution by community composition and abundance. You only need sketch-based proximity and compute is the bottleneck and resolution loss is acceptable — Mash is faster since it indexes samples by unique k-mers Input is a feature/abundance table rather than raw FASTA/FASTQ reads — Libra's preprocess and k-mer counting operate directly on read files A presence/absence or Jaccard-ab-based metric is explicitly desired (Simka-style comparison) rather than abundance-aware Cosine Similarity http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Run Libra, a Hadoop MapReduce-based k-mer tool, to compute all-vs-all similarity/distance matrices between metagenomic samples using Cosine Similarity on k-mer abundance, enabling scalable clustering (e.g., of 48 HMP WGS read samples by body site). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Run Libra, a Hadoop MapReduce-based k-mer tool, to compute all-vs-all similarity/distance matrices between metagenomic samples using Cosine Similarity on k-mer abundance, enabling scalable clustering (e.g., of 48 HMP WGS read samples by body site).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need sketch-based proximity and compute is the bottleneck and resolution loss is acceptable — Mash is faster since it indexes samples by unique k-mers Input is a feature/abundance table rather than raw FASTA/FASTQ reads — Libra's preprocess and k-mer counting operate directly on read files A presence/absence or Jaccard-ab-based metric is explicitly desired (Simka-style comparison) rather than abundance-aware Cosine Similarity

skills.description: Use when you must run Libra's Hadoop indexing (preprocess) and scoring (core) stages on large FASTA/FASTQ metagenome collections to produce an all-vs-all cosine-similarity matrix, e.g., global-ocean virome comparisons.
skills.name: hadoop-mapreduce-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: hadoop-mapreduce-pipeline-execution Use when you must run Libra's Hadoop indexing (preprocess) and scoring (core) stages on large FASTA/FASTQ metagenome collections to produce an all-vs-all cosine-similarity matrix, e.g., global-ocean virome comparisons. No Hadoop cluster is available and the sample set is small — a single-node Hadoop deployment for a handful of small samples adds setup overhead without benefit A sketch-based or presence/absence comparison is explicitly desired — note the article warns that data reduction and presence/absence metrics diminish resolution of large-scale comparative analyses Input is already a k-mer index or a distance matrix rather than raw/QC'd FASTA-FASTQ reads — the preprocess stage expects sequencing reads in /source_dir http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Executes Libra's two-stage Hadoop MapReduce pipeline — k-mer indexing of QC'd FASTA/FASTQ reads followed by all-vs-all scoring — to compare massive metagenome collections (e.g., 43 Tara Ocean Viromes, ~4.2 billion reads) without data reduction, using every read for k-mer abundance. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Executes Libra's two-stage Hadoop MapReduce pipeline — k-mer indexing of QC'd FASTA/FASTQ reads followed by all-vs-all scoring — to compare massive metagenome collections (e.g., 43 Tara Ocean Viromes, ~4.2 billion reads) without data reduction, using every read for k-mer abundance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No Hadoop cluster is available and the sample set is small — a single-node Hadoop deployment for a handful of small samples adds setup overhead without benefit A sketch-based or presence/absence comparison is explicitly desired — note the article warns that data reduction and presence/absence metrics diminish resolution of large-scale comparative analyses Input is already a k-mer index or a distance matrix rather than raw/QC'd FASTA-FASTQ reads — the preprocess stage expects sequencing reads in /source_dir

skills.description: Use when clustering large protein sequence sets (e.g., UniProt-scale FASTA) with Linclust/MMseqs2 and needing a fast, SIMD-vectorized exact-distance filter to prune center–member pairs after exact k-mer matching but before gapped alignment.
skills.name: hamming-distance-sequence-preclustering
skills.search_text: hamming-distance-sequence-preclustering Use when clustering large protein sequence sets (e.g., UniProt-scale FASTA) with Linclust/MMseqs2 and needing a fast, SIMD-vectorized exact-distance filter to prune center–member pairs after exact k-mer matching but before gapped alignment. When pairwise links must be verified with a measure Hamming distance along diagonals cannot capture, e.g., gapped similarities not detected by any exact k-mer match — no diagonal is stored and the pair is never compared When clustering items without definable keys — Linclust requires a set of m keys per item such that clustered items likely share at least one key When only a handful of sequences need clustering; simpler exact all-against-all tools avoid the pipeline's false-negative approximation http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 Step 3A of the Linclust five-step pipeline: compute Hamming distances in the full amino acid alphabet between each sequence and its k-mer group's center along stored diagonals, to cheaply remove matches that already satisfy sequence identity and coverage thresholds before slower alignment steps. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-04964-5
skills.summary: Step 3A of the Linclust five-step pipeline: compute Hamming distances in the full amino acid alphabet between each sequence and its k-mer group's center along stored diagonals, to cheaply remove matches that already satisfy sequence identity and coverage thresholds before slower alignment steps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When pairwise links must be verified with a measure Hamming distance along diagonals cannot capture, e.g., gapped similarities not detected by any exact k-mer match — no diagonal is stored and the pair is never compared When clustering items without definable keys — Linclust requires a set of m keys per item such that clustered items likely share at least one key When only a handful of sequences need clustering; simpler exact all-against-all tools avoid the pipeline's false-negative approximation

skills.description: Use when downstream EHH-based scans (iHS, XP-EHH, SweepFinder2 inputs) require phased haplotypes but the input is unphased chromosome-split VCF files from biallelic SNP data.

skills.search_text: haplotype-phasing-snp-vcf Use when downstream EHH-based scans (iHS, XP-EHH, SweepFinder2 inputs) require phased haplotypes but the input is unphased chromosome-split VCF files from biallelic SNP data. Input data are already phased (e.g. the cattle Animal_SNPAtlas data set of phased and imputed autosomal SNP genotypes) and the scan tool accepts phased haplotypes directly Analysis goal is genetic structure or phylogeny (PCA, ADMIXTURE, TreeMix), which do not require haplotype phasing Data are multiallelic variants or structural variants rather than biallelic SNPs, which the scalepopgen workflows are not designed for http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3056 Phase biallelic SNP VCFs (chromosome-split, tabix-indexed) with Beagle v5.2 or SHAPEIT5 v5.1.1 so that EHH-based selection scans such as selscan (iHS, XP-EHH) can be run in scalepopgen's signatures-of-selection sub-workflow. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Phase biallelic SNP VCFs (chromosome-split, tabix-indexed) with Beagle v5.2 or SHAPEIT5 v5.1.1 so that EHH-based selection scans such as selscan (iHS, XP-EHH) can be run in scalepopgen's signatures-of-selection sub-workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already phased (e.g. the cattle Animal_SNPAtlas data set of phased and imputed autosomal SNP genotypes) and the scan tool accepts phased haplotypes directly Analysis goal is genetic structure or phylogeny (PCA, ADMIXTURE, TreeMix), which do not require haplotype phasing Data are multiallelic variants or structural variants rather than biallelic SNPs, which the scalepopgen workflows are not designed for

skills.description: Use when performing multiple testing correction in metagenome-wide case-control association tests where an empirical null distribution of minimum P-values is built by permuting binary phenotype labels and the uncertainty of the resulting Psig threshold must be quantified.
skills.name: harrell-davis-bootstrap-confidence-intervals
skills.search_text: harrell-davis-bootstrap-confidence-intervals Use when performing multiple testing correction in metagenome-wide case-control association tests where an empirical null distribution of minimum P-values is built by permuting binary phenotype labels and the uncertainty of the resulting Psig threshold must be quantified. When a standard analytical multiple testing correction (e.g. standard Bonferroni on the number of tests) is sufficient and no permutation framework is being used — OMARU's empirical threshold is specifically built for clade-level MWAS P-values When input is raw sequencing data or pre-association profiling (Steps 1–3 of OMARU); the permutation threshold is applied only after association test summary statistics exist When analyzing continuous (non-case-control) phenotypes, since the permutation scheme permutes binary labels 1/0 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 In OMARU, the Harrell-Davis estimator is used to construct a 95% bootstrap confidence interval around the empirical Bonferroni significance threshold (Psig), which itself is derived as the 95th percentile of the minimum P-value (Pmin) distribution from 10,000 phenotype permutations in the phylogenetic case-control association tests. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: In OMARU, the Harrell-Davis estimator is used to construct a 95% bootstrap confidence interval around the empirical Bonferroni significance threshold (Psig), which itself is derived as the 95th percentile of the minimum P-value (Pmin) distribution from 10,000 phenotype permutations in the phylogenetic case-control association tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a standard analytical multiple testing correction (e.g. standard Bonferroni on the number of tests) is sufficient and no permutation framework is being used — OMARU's empirical threshold is specifically built for clade-level MWAS P-values When input is raw sequencing data or pre-association profiling (Steps 1–3 of OMARU); the permutation threshold is applied only after association test summary statistics exist When analyzing continuous (non-case-control) phenotypes, since the permutation scheme permutes binary labels 1/0

skills.description: Use when converting matching seed hash values between a raw nanopore signal (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5/BLOW5) and a reference genome into a mapped region via hash-table lookup followed by colinear chaining of seed matches.
skills.name: hash-table-index-lookup
skills.search_text: hash-table-index-lookup Use when converting matching seed hash values between a raw nanopore signal (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5/BLOW5) and a reference genome into a mapped region via hash-table lookup followed by colinear chaining of seed matches. No reference genome is available and all-vs-all overlaps between raw signals are needed — use Rawsamble's overlapping mechanism instead. Base-level or high-accuracy end-to-end alignment of sequence reads is required — use a sequence mapper such as minimap2 rather than raw-signal hash lookup. Input is already assembled/sequence reads rather than raw electrical signals — the signal-quantization hash lookup does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs RawHash's mapping step: seed hashes generated from raw nanopore signals are looked up in a hash-table index built from the reference genome's expected signal representation, and matching seed hash positions are chained (Sigmap-style, distance coefficient disabled) into the colinear chain that defines the mapped region. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad272
skills.summary: Reconstructs RawHash's mapping step: seed hashes generated from raw nanopore signals are looked up in a hash-table index built from the reference genome's expected signal representation, and matching seed hash positions are chained (Sigmap-style, distance coefficient disabled) into the colinear chain that defines the mapped region.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome is available and all-vs-all overlaps between raw signals are needed — use Rawsamble's overlapping mechanism instead. Base-level or high-accuracy end-to-end alignment of sequence reads is required — use a sequence mapper such as minimap2 rather than raw-signal hash lookup. Input is already assembled/sequence reads rather than raw electrical signals — the signal-quantization hash lookup does not apply.

skills.search_text: hashmap-based-sequence-clustering Use when Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ reads (primer-trimmed, paired, trimmed to 250 bases) need de novo variant calling, and one-mismatch child sequences must be grouped with abundant parents before error-rate modeling. Detecting true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq is not sensitive here; use more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 Data with two or more mismatches, indel variation, or long reads such as PacBio where multiple-mismatch sequences are not rare Input is already a feature/count table — this skill operates on raw (preprocessed) fastq reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Cluster one-mismatch 16S rRNA amplicon sequence variants onto their most abundant parent using HashSeq's fast HashMap-based approach, as a precursor to LOESS-based background error estimation and true-sequence inference. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Cluster one-mismatch 16S rRNA amplicon sequence variants onto their most abundant parent using HashSeq's fast HashMap-based approach, as a precursor to LOESS-based background error estimation and true-sequence inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Detecting true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq is not sensitive here; use more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 Data with two or more mismatches, indel variation, or long reads such as PacBio where multiple-mismatch sequences are not rare Input is already a feature/count table — this skill operates on raw (preprocessed) fastq reads

skills.description: Use when a time-to-event (survival) outcome must be associated with taxon-level microbial abundances (e.g., phylum CLR values), optionally covariate-adjusted and subgroup-stratified, yielding per-taxon hazard ratios.
skills.name: hazard-ratio-interpretation-microbiome-survival
skills.search_text: hazard-ratio-interpretation-microbiome-survival Use when a time-to-event (survival) outcome must be associated with taxon-level microbial abundances (e.g., phylum CLR values), optionally covariate-adjusted and subgroup-stratified, yielding per-taxon hazard ratios. The number of studies (rows of est/std.err) is fewer than 10 — mMeta.aMeta requires at least 10 studies Only raw sequence data or OTU tables are available with no study-specific effect estimates and standard errors, since mMeta and aMeta require only effect estimates and their standard errors, which must already be computed (e.g. via least squares regression adjusting for x1 and x2) Fixed-effects meta-analysis is appropriate (no between-study heterogeneity expected), as this skill exists specifically to estimate the random effects heterogeneity variance http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Method for estimating the between-study (heterogeneity) variance tau^2 in random effects meta-analysis by choosing between the Sidik-Jonkman (SJ/robust sandwich) estimator and the DerSimonian-Laird (DL) method-of-moments estimator.
