skills.name: hi-c-alignment-filtering
skills.search_text: hi-c-alignment-filtering Use when raw Hi-C paired-end reads have been aligned to assembled contigs (BAM available) and downstream binning or graph construction requires a curated set of high-confidence inter-contig contact pairs. Input is raw uncleaned FASTQ — first run adaptor removal, quality trimming (bbduk trimq=10 qtrim=r ftm=5 minlen=50), Hi-C first-10-nt trimming (ftl=10), and PCR duplicate removal (clumpify.sh) before alignment The BAM is coordinate-sorted rather than name-sorted — ViralCC requires name sorting to pair Hi-C mates Goal is taxonomic annotation of contigs rather than Hi-C contact curation — use TAXAassign/Demovir instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Filters metagenomic Hi-C alignments before graph construction by removing unmapped/supplementary/secondary records with samtools view -F 0x904, enforcing a name-sorted BAM, and applying ViralCC's per-alignment thresholds (MAPQ ≥ 30, ≥ 30 matches, contigs ≥ 1000 bp) so only reliable inter-contig contacts feed the Hi-C interaction graph. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Filters metagenomic Hi-C alignments before graph construction by removing unmapped/supplementary/secondary records with samtools view -F 0x904, enforcing a name-sorted BAM, and applying ViralCC's per-alignment thresholds (MAPQ ≥ 30, ≥ 30 matches, contigs ≥ 1000 bp) so only reliable inter-contig contacts feed the Hi-C interaction graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw uncleaned FASTQ — first run adaptor removal, quality trimming (bbduk trimq=10 qtrim=r ftm=5 minlen=50), Hi-C first-10-nt trimming (ftl=10), and PCR duplicate removal (clumpify.sh) before alignment The BAM is coordinate-sorted rather than name-sorted — ViralCC requires name sorting to pair Hi-C mates Goal is taxonomic annotation of contigs rather than Hi-C contact curation — use TAXAassign/Demovir instead

skills.description: Use when you have Hi-C paired-end read alignments (BAM sorted by name) to assembled contigs plus a list of identified viral contigs, and you need to bin viral contigs using virus-host proximity structure.
skills.name: hi-c-contact-graph-construction
skills.search_text: hi-c-contact-graph-construction Use when you have Hi-C paired-end read alignments (BAM sorted by name) to assembled contigs plus a list of identified viral contigs, and you need to bin viral contigs using virus-host proximity structure. Input is shotgun-only data with no proximity-ligation (Hi-C) read pairs — the host proximity structure cannot be derived. The Hi-C BAM is sorted by coordinate rather than by name, so read-pair mates cannot be reliably paired. Contigs have not passed the minimum length threshold (1000 bp), which the pipeline filters out via --min-len. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Constructs the Hi-C interaction graph and the complementary host proximity graph from a name-sorted Hi-C BAM: viral contigs are linked when they share at least k common host contigs contacted in Hi-C, with k auto-selected so |E_host| <= |E_hic|. In ViralCC this dual graph feeds Leiden clustering to reconstruct draft viral genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Constructs the Hi-C interaction graph and the complementary host proximity graph from a name-sorted Hi-C BAM: viral contigs are linked when they share at least k common host contigs contacted in Hi-C, with k auto-selected so |E_host| <= |E_hic|. In ViralCC this dual graph feeds Leiden clustering to reconstruct draft viral genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is shotgun-only data with no proximity-ligation (Hi-C) read pairs — the host proximity structure cannot be derived. The Hi-C BAM is sorted by coordinate rather than by name, so read-pair mates cannot be reliably paired. Contigs have not passed the minimum length threshold (1000 bp), which the pipeline filters out via --min-len.

skills.description: Use when raw Hi-C paired-end and shotgun FASTQ reads must be converted into a name-sorted, filtered BAM aligned to assembled contigs before running a Hi-C-based binning pipeline such as ViralCC.
skills.name: hic-alignment-contact-processing
skills.search_text: hic-alignment-contact-processing Use when raw Hi-C paired-end and shotgun FASTQ reads must be converted into a name-sorted, filtered BAM aligned to assembled contigs before running a Hi-C-based binning pipeline such as ViralCC. The Hi-C BAM already exists, is read-pair (name) sorted, and filtered of unmapped/secondary/supplementary alignments Input is single-cell or non-proximity-ligation data without paired-end Hi-C contacts, where a read-pair contact map is meaningless The goal is taxonomic annotation of host contigs (e.g. TAXAassign) rather than producing ViralCC's alignment input http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Preprocess raw shotgun and Hi-C reads, assemble contigs, align Hi-C paired-end reads to the assembly, and filter/sort the BAM so it is suitable for ViralCC's Hi-C interaction and host proximity graph construction. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Preprocess raw shotgun and Hi-C reads, assemble contigs, align Hi-C paired-end reads to the assembly, and filter/sort the BAM so it is suitable for ViralCC's Hi-C interaction and host proximity graph construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The Hi-C BAM already exists, is read-pair (name) sorted, and filtered of unmapped/secondary/supplementary alignments Input is single-cell or non-proximity-ligation data without paired-end Hi-C contacts, where a read-pair contact map is meaningless The goal is taxonomic annotation of host contigs (e.g. TAXAassign) rather than producing ViralCC's alignment input

skills.description: Use when assembling draft viral genomes (vMAGs) from metagenomic Hi-C data: you have assembled contigs (FASTA), a name-sorted Hi-C alignment BAM, and a viral contig list, and need contact/proximity graphs for binning.
skills.name: hic-contact-graph-construction
skills.search_text: hic-contact-graph-construction Use when assembling draft viral genomes (vMAGs) from metagenomic Hi-C data: you have assembled contigs (FASTA), a name-sorted Hi-C alignment BAM, and a viral contig list, and need contact/proximity graphs for binning. When no Hi-C (proximity-ligation) data are available — shotgun co-abundance-based binning tools like CoCoNet or vRhyme are the relevant alternatives, though they need enough samples for reliable co-abundance profiles When the input BAM is not name-sorted or still contains unmapped/supplementary/secondary alignments (unfiltered with -F 0x904), as ViralCC requires a name-sorted, filtered BAM http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Constructs the ViralCC Hi-C interaction graph (G_hic) from a name-sorted Hi-C alignment BAM and the host proximity graph (G_host) from k-mer-based virus-host links, which are then integrated into G_int for Leiden clustering of viral contigs into draft viral genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Constructs the ViralCC Hi-C interaction graph (G_hic) from a name-sorted Hi-C alignment BAM and the host proximity graph (G_host) from k-mer-based virus-host links, which are then integrated into G_int for Leiden clustering of viral contigs into draft viral genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no Hi-C (proximity-ligation) data are available — shotgun co-abundance-based binning tools like CoCoNet or vRhyme are the relevant alternatives, though they need enough samples for reliable co-abundance profiles When the input BAM is not name-sorted or still contains unmapped/supplementary/secondary alignments (unfiltered with -F 0x904), as ViralCC requires a name-sorted, filtered BAM

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end metagenomic Hi-C FASTQ files must be preprocessed and aligned to assembled contigs to produce a name-sorted BAM for Hi-C-based binning.
skills.name: hic-read-alignment-and-filtering
skills.search_text: hic-read-alignment-and-filtering Use when raw paired-end metagenomic Hi-C FASTQ files must be preprocessed and aligned to assembled contigs to produce a name-sorted BAM for Hi-C-based binning. Input is already a name-sorted, filtered BAM file from a prior ViralCC run — re-running cleaning and alignment would duplicate effort Data are shotgun-only reads with no Hi-C library, since the trimming steps (e.g., ftl=10) and proximity-ligation alignment settings are Hi-C-specific The assembly contains contigs shorter than 1000 bp, which fall below the ViralCC --min-len default and should be filtered before binning http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Cleans metagenomic Hi-C paired-end reads (adaptor/quality/first-10-nt trimming, duplicate removal), aligns them to shotgun-assembled contigs with BWA MEM, filters the BAM with samtools, and name-sorts it to produce the BAM input required by ViralCC and other Hi-C binners. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Cleans metagenomic Hi-C paired-end reads (adaptor/quality/first-10-nt trimming, duplicate removal), aligns them to shotgun-assembled contigs with BWA MEM, filters the BAM with samtools, and name-sorts it to produce the BAM input required by ViralCC and other Hi-C binners.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a name-sorted, filtered BAM file from a prior ViralCC run — re-running cleaning and alignment would duplicate effort Data are shotgun-only reads with no Hi-C library, since the trimming steps (e.g., ftl=10) and proximity-ligation alignment settings are Hi-C-specific The assembly contains contigs shorter than 1000 bp, which fall below the ViralCC --min-len default and should be filtered before binning

skills.description: Use when raw metagenomic Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads must be cleaned before assembly/alignment or before Hi-C library quality assessment such as qc3C 3D-ratio estimation.
skills.name: hic-read-cleaning-with-bbduk-and-clumpify
skills.search_text: hic-read-cleaning-with-bbduk-and-clumpify Use when raw metagenomic Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads must be cleaned before assembly/alignment or before Hi-C library quality assessment such as qc3C 3D-ratio estimation. Input reads have already been quality-trimmed and deduplicated — re-running clumpify.sh or ftl=10 trimming would remove additional legitimate data The data are not proximity-ligation (Hi-C) reads and the first-10-nucleotide ftl=10 trim is not warranted The goal is single-end read processing — the pipeline and its tpe/tbo paired-end bbduk parameters assume paired-end input http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Standardized cleaning of metagenomic Hi-C paired-end reads using BBTools: adapter/quality trimming with bbduk (trimq=10 qtrim=r ftm=5 minlen=50, ftl=10 for Hi-C) followed by removal of identical PCR optical and tile-edge duplicates with clumpify.sh, as used in the ViralCC Hi-C processing pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Standardized cleaning of metagenomic Hi-C paired-end reads using BBTools: adapter/quality trimming with bbduk (trimq=10 qtrim=r ftm=5 minlen=50, ftl=10 for Hi-C) followed by removal of identical PCR optical and tile-edge duplicates with clumpify.sh, as used in the ViralCC Hi-C processing pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have already been quality-trimmed and deduplicated — re-running clumpify.sh or ftl=10 trimming would remove additional legitimate data The data are not proximity-ligation (Hi-C) reads and the first-10-nucleotide ftl=10 trim is not warranted The goal is single-end read processing — the pipeline and its tpe/tbo paired-end bbduk parameters assume paired-end input

skills.description: Use when longitudinal sequencing count data contain observed zeros and you need posterior probabilities distinguishing biological zeros (extinct taxa) from technical zeros (below detection threshold), e.g. in a state-space/variational inference model of community composition.
skills.name: hidden-markov-model-forward-backward-inference
skills.search_text: hidden-markov-model-forward-backward-inference Use when longitudinal sequencing count data contain observed zeros and you need posterior probabilities distinguishing biological zeros (extinct taxa) from technical zeros (below detection threshold), e.g. in a state-space/variational inference model of community composition. The data have no observed zeros — the HMM zero-indicator layer is unnecessary and standard trajectory estimation suffices A taxon is ultra-sparse (>90% missing entries), which the paper recommends filtering out as a pre-processing step since there is little information about its trajectory over time The task is cross-sectional (no longitudinal structure), since the forward-backward updates exploit temporal dependencies between adjacent time points http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies forward-backward dynamic programming for hidden Markov models, as used in LUMINATE's variational inference, to compute posteriors over per-taxon, per-timepoint zero indicators w_t^d that discriminate biological zeros (taxon absent from the community) from technical zeros (taxon below detection threshold). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2020.05.006
skills.summary: Applies forward-backward dynamic programming for hidden Markov models, as used in LUMINATE's variational inference, to compute posteriors over per-taxon, per-timepoint zero indicators w_t^d that discriminate biological zeros (taxon absent from the community) from technical zeros (taxon below detection threshold).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have no observed zeros — the HMM zero-indicator layer is unnecessary and standard trajectory estimation suffices A taxon is ultra-sparse (>90% missing entries), which the paper recommends filtering out as a pre-processing step since there is little information about its trajectory over time The task is cross-sectional (no longitudinal structure), since the forward-backward updates exploit temporal dependencies between adjacent time points

skills.description: Use when a colored de Bruijn graph (directed, acyclic, nondegenerate, unique start/end nodes, node color sets per sample) must be decomposed into colored superbubbles and arranged into a parent-child tree that supports tri-tuple coordinates.
skills.name: hierarchical-bubble-tree-organization
skills.search_text: hierarchical-bubble-tree-organization Use when a colored de Bruijn graph (directed, acyclic, nondegenerate, unique start/end nodes, node color sets per sample) must be decomposed into colored superbubbles and arranged into a parent-child tree that supports tri-tuple coordinates. Sequence similarity is insufficient (source number far less than variant number), so the variant detection model built on the cSupB tree is not applicable The graph is degenerate or has multiple start/end nodes — the method assumes a directed, acyclic, nondegenerate colored de Bruijn graph with unique start and end nodes The goal is detecting large indels, inversions, or reverse tandem duplications — the article states no effective solution exists for these complicated conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs the cSupB decomposition algorithm from the colored de Bruijn graph: a single postorder-like traversal identifies colored superbubbles (cSupBs) via color-intersection matching, then organizes them into a hierarchical tree (the basis of the paper's tri-tuple coordinate system). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04149-w
skills.summary: Reconstructs the cSupB decomposition algorithm from the colored de Bruijn graph: a single postorder-like traversal identifies colored superbubbles (cSupBs) via color-intersection matching, then organizes them into a hierarchical tree (the basis of the paper's tri-tuple coordinate system).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequence similarity is insufficient (source number far less than variant number), so the variant detection model built on the cSupB tree is not applicable The graph is degenerate or has multiple start/end nodes — the method assumes a directed, acyclic, nondegenerate colored de Bruijn graph with unique start and end nodes The goal is detecting large indels, inversions, or reverse tandem duplications — the article states no effective solution exists for these complicated conditions

skills.description: Use when you have raw 16S rRNA or WGS metagenome reads for a sample set and need to cluster samples by community composition and abundance, or to compare how different distance metrics (Libra cosine, Mash MinHash, Simka) resolve sample groupings.
skills.name: hierarchical-clustering-of-metagenome-samples
skills.search_text: hierarchical-clustering-of-metagenome-samples Use when you have raw 16S rRNA or WGS metagenome reads for a sample set and need to cluster samples by community composition and abundance, or to compare how different distance metrics (Libra cosine, Mash MinHash, Simka) resolve sample groupings. Input is already a feature table or OTU/ASV abundance matrix rather than raw reads — Libra's k-mer counting pipeline expects FASTA/FASTQ sequence data Sample-to-sample comparison requires alignment-based taxonomic or functional profiling rather than composition-level k-mer clustering The dataset is too large for local processing and no Hadoop/CyVerse infrastructure is available (though the iMicrobe web implementation on CyVerse is an alternative) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Cluster metagenomic samples hierarchically from all-vs-all distance matrices computed on k-mer content — e.g. Libra Cosine Similarity, Mash MinHash, and Simka Jaccard-abundance/Bray-Curtis matrices — to compare clustering resolution across distance metrics (Fig. 3 of the Libra paper, HMP 16S rRNA dataset). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Cluster metagenomic samples hierarchically from all-vs-all distance matrices computed on k-mer content — e.g. Libra Cosine Similarity, Mash MinHash, and Simka Jaccard-abundance/Bray-Curtis matrices — to compare clustering resolution across distance metrics (Fig. 3 of the Libra paper, HMP 16S rRNA dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or OTU/ASV abundance matrix rather than raw reads — Libra's k-mer counting pipeline expects FASTA/FASTQ sequence data Sample-to-sample comparison requires alignment-based taxonomic or functional profiling rather than composition-level k-mer clustering The dataset is too large for local processing and no Hadoop/CyVerse infrastructure is available (though the iMicrobe web implementation on CyVerse is an alternative)

skills.description: Use when a YAML report config must be turned into instantiated section/subsection/component objects — e.g., implementing or extending VueGen's report generators (Streamlit, notebook, document) for bioinformatics outputs like plots, tables, networks, Markdown, and HTML.
skills.name: hierarchical-section-component-instantiation
skills.search_text: hierarchical-section-component-instantiation Use when a YAML report config must be turned into instantiated section/subsection/component objects — e.g., implementing or extending VueGen's report generators (Streamlit, notebook, document) for bioinformatics outputs like plots, tables, networks, Markdown, and HTML. The report structure is not described in a YAML config — e.g., hand-authored documents or notebooks where no report/section/subsection/component hierarchy exists to instantiate. The desired output is a raw visualization of multi-omics data rather than a structured report assembled from existing output files — VueCore-style plotting is the wrong layer. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3071 Parses a YAML configuration describing a report → sections → subsections → components hierarchy, instantiates the corresponding report/section/subsection classes and type-specific component objects, and maps that hierarchy onto output renderers (e.g., Streamlit multipage apps). This is the core internal logic of VueGen's report-creation pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf149
skills.summary: Parses a YAML configuration describing a report → sections → subsections → components hierarchy, instantiates the corresponding report/section/subsection classes and type-specific component objects, and maps that hierarchy onto output renderers (e.g., Streamlit multipage apps). This is the core internal logic of VueGen's report-creation pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The report structure is not described in a YAML config — e.g., hand-authored documents or notebooks where no report/section/subsection/component hierarchy exists to instantiate. The desired output is a raw visualization of multi-omics data rather than a structured report assembled from existing output files — VueCore-style plotting is the wrong layer.

skills.description: Use when HiFi long reads (FASTQ) from a metagenomic sample must be de novo assembled with multiple assemblers to compare assembly strategies or feed downstream binning/quality evaluation.
skills.name: hifi-long-read-metagenome-assembly
skills.search_text: hifi-long-read-metagenome-assembly Use when HiFi long reads (FASTQ) from a metagenomic sample must be de novo assembled with multiple assemblers to compare assembly strategies or feed downstream binning/quality evaluation. The input is short-read or hybrid data for which an assembler like OPERA-MS (hybrid metagenomic assembler) is intended rather than the HiFi-only assemblers configured here Only a precomputed assembly needs quality evaluation with no assembly step — use the evaluation-only config (config_test_evaluation_only.yaml) or submit the assembly as a custom assembler instead of re-assembling The sample is a simple isolate/low-complexity genome where metagenome-specific assemblers and bin-quality diversity metrics add no value over a standard isolate assembly workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assemble PacBio HiFi metagenomic reads with state-of-the-art long-read assemblers (metaMDBG, metaflye, hifiasm-meta) orchestrated by the Mapler Snakemake pipeline, producing per-assembler contig sets (assembly.fasta) that can then be quality-evaluated and compared on taxonomically rich samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Assemble PacBio HiFi metagenomic reads with state-of-the-art long-read assemblers (metaMDBG, metaflye, hifiasm-meta) orchestrated by the Mapler Snakemake pipeline, producing per-assembler contig sets (assembly.fasta) that can then be quality-evaluated and compared on taxonomically rich samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read or hybrid data for which an assembler like OPERA-MS (hybrid metagenomic assembler) is intended rather than the HiFi-only assemblers configured here Only a precomputed assembly needs quality evaluation with no assembly step — use the evaluation-only config (config_test_evaluation_only.yaml) or submit the assembly as a custom assembler instead of re-assembling The sample is a simple isolate/low-complexity genome where metagenome-specific assemblers and bin-quality diversity metrics add no value over a standard isolate assembly workflow

skills.description: Use when binning assembled metagenomic contigs whose feature vectors are too high-dimensional for reliable Euclidean/Manhattan metrics — e.g. composition vectors built from multiple k-mer sizes — and hull-based assignment is preferred.
skills.name: high-dimensional-data-clustering
skills.search_text: high-dimensional-data-clustering Use when binning assembled metagenomic contigs whose feature vectors are too high-dimensional for reliable Euclidean/Manhattan metrics — e.g. composition vectors built from multiple k-mer sizes — and hull-based assignment is preferred. When the number of bins cannot be anchored by single-copy marker gene seeds — CH-Bin relies on marker-gene analysis for both bin count (ScmSelectPercentile percentile of seed counts) and initial binning. When contigs are well separated in low-dimensional space and Euclidean/Manhattan-distance clustering suffices — the hull-distance QP machinery targets the high-dimensionality regime where those metrics become unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Cluster high-dimensional metagenomic contig feature vectors (composition + coverage) by assigning each contig to the bin whose convex hull minimizes the convex hull distance, as implemented in CH-Bin. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.compbiolchem.2022.107734
skills.summary: Cluster high-dimensional metagenomic contig feature vectors (composition + coverage) by assigning each contig to the bin whose convex hull minimizes the convex hull distance, as implemented in CH-Bin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the number of bins cannot be anchored by single-copy marker gene seeds — CH-Bin relies on marker-gene analysis for both bin count (ScmSelectPercentile percentile of seed counts) and initial binning. When contigs are well separated in low-dimensional space and Euclidean/Manhattan-distance clustering suffices — the hull-distance QP machinery targets the high-dimensionality regime where those metrics become unreliable.

skills.description: Use when the feature matrix is high-dimensional relative to the sample size (e.g. hundreds of standardized OTUs vs tens of samples) and most taxa are expected to be noise, so the multivariate association test must operate on a selected subset S of taxa.
skills.name: high-dimensional-feature-screening
skills.search_text: high-dimensional-feature-screening Use when the feature matrix is high-dimensional relative to the sample size (e.g. hundreds of standardized OTUs vs tens of samples) and most taxa are expected to be noise, so the multivariate association test must operate on a selected subset S of taxa. When the number of taxa in the tested clade is small and there is no noise-accumulation concern — the article notes accumulation of small noises deteriorates performance 'especially when the number of taxa being tested is moderate or relatively large' When the input is raw unnormalized count data — counts must first be converted to compositional form and OTU-wise standardized before screening When the goal is per-taxon univariate association testing rather than multivariate clade-level association with FWER control via Bonferroni correction http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Pre-filters high-dimensional compositional microbiome feature matrices (e.g. hundreds of OTUs) down to an associated-feature subset S using distance correlation learning, so that the subsequent adaptive multivariate association test (AMAT's T_AMAT / aSPU with Γ = {2, 3, 4, 8}) is computed on selected taxa rather than all p features, alleviating noise accumulation. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab120
skills.summary: Pre-filters high-dimensional compositional microbiome feature matrices (e.g. hundreds of OTUs) down to an associated-feature subset S using distance correlation learning, so that the subsequent adaptive multivariate association test (AMAT's T_AMAT / aSPU with Γ = {2, 3, 4, 8}) is computed on selected taxa rather than all p features, alleviating noise accumulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the number of taxa in the tested clade is small and there is no noise-accumulation concern — the article notes accumulation of small noises deteriorates performance 'especially when the number of taxa being tested is moderate or relatively large' When the input is raw unnormalized count data — counts must first be converted to compositional form and OTU-wise standardized before screening When the goal is per-taxon univariate association testing rather than multivariate clade-level association with FWER control via Bonferroni correction

skills.description: Use when you need to verify that a core-genome estimation pipeline (mOTUpan/mOTUlizer with mmseqs2 gene clustering) scales to thousands of MAGs/genomes before committing to a full production run, or to reproduce the published resource benchmarks.
skills.name: high-throughput-genome-scalability-testing
skills.search_text: high-throughput-genome-scalability-testing Use when you need to verify that a core-genome estimation pipeline (mOTUpan/mOTUlizer with mmseqs2 gene clustering) scales to thousands of MAGs/genomes before committing to a full production run, or to reproduce the published resource benchmarks. The genome set is small (tens of genomes) — scalability benchmarking adds no information over simply running the pipeline You lack the *.faa inputs and your own gene clusters are not in the --cog_file JSON-compatible format expected by mOTUpan.py The goal is read-based OTU table generation from the unrelated mOTUs tool rather than core-genome partitioning http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark the runtime and memory footprint of mOTUpan-based core-genome partitioning at the scale of thousands of genomes, using the reported 9443 Staphylococcus aureus GTDB run (mmseqs2 clustering in ~4 min on 24 threads; mOTUpan in ~2 h 15 min single-threaded at ~3 GB RAM on a Ryzen 9 3900X) as the reference envelope. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac060
skills.summary: Benchmark the runtime and memory footprint of mOTUpan-based core-genome partitioning at the scale of thousands of genomes, using the reported 9443 Staphylococcus aureus GTDB run (mmseqs2 clustering in ~4 min on 24 threads; mOTUpan in ~2 h 15 min single-threaded at ~3 GB RAM on a Ryzen 9 3900X) as the reference envelope.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The genome set is small (tens of genomes) — scalability benchmarking adds no information over simply running the pipeline You lack the *.faa inputs and your own gene clusters are not in the --cog_file JSON-compatible format expected by mOTUpan.py The goal is read-based OTU table generation from the unrelated mOTUs tool rather than core-genome partitioning

skills.description: Use when multiple overlapping or adjacent DIAMOND (tabular BLASTX) hits map to the same reference protein and must be merged into a single continuous sequence while resolving overlaps by HSP score.
skills.name: highest-scoring-segment-pair-selection
skills.search_text: highest-scoring-segment-pair-selection Use when multiple overlapping or adjacent DIAMOND (tabular BLASTX) hits map to the same reference protein and must be merged into a single continuous sequence while resolving overlaps by HSP score. Only a single nonoverlapping hit exists per reference — no stitching or HSP comparison is needed Hits come from different references and should not be merged into one sequence The query is unaligned raw reads rather than translated contig hits from DIAMOND — retrieval then relies on the read-based mode of Patchwork, not hit stitching of BLASTX tabular output http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 During Patchwork's hit-stitching phase, overlapping or adjacent DIAMOND BLASTX hit regions against a reference protein are merged so that only the highest-scoring segment pair (HSP) is retained for each overlapping interval, producing one continuous stitched sequence per reference. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: During Patchwork's hit-stitching phase, overlapping or adjacent DIAMOND BLASTX hit regions against a reference protein are merged so that only the highest-scoring segment pair (HSP) is retained for each overlapping interval, producing one continuous stitched sequence per reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single nonoverlapping hit exists per reference — no stitching or HSP comparison is needed Hits come from different references and should not be merged into one sequence The query is unaligned raw reads rather than translated contig hits from DIAMOND — retrieval then relies on the read-based mode of Patchwork, not hit stitching of BLASTX tabular output

skills.description: Use when choosing or configuring a hit-filtering strategy for DIAMOND alignment output in read-based functional annotation, or when reasoning about sensitivity/specificity trade-offs from multi-match reads.
skills.name: hit-filtering-sensitivity-specificity-tradeoff-analysis
skills.search_text: hit-filtering-sensitivity-specificity-tradeoff-analysis Use when choosing or configuring a hit-filtering strategy for DIAMOND alignment output in read-based functional annotation, or when reasoning about sensitivity/specificity trade-offs from multi-match reads. Input is not a per-read alignment hit table but an already-aggregated gene or ortholog abundance table The alignment was produced by a tool whose output schema differs from DIAMOND tabular format without adaptation http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Analyzes how alternative read-mapping hit refinement strategies (best e-value match with tie retention vs. keeping all hits) affect sensitivity and specificity of metagenomic functional profiling, as implemented in MetaLAFFA between DIAMOND alignment and gene counting. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: Analyzes how alternative read-mapping hit refinement strategies (best e-value match with tie retention vs. keeping all hits) affect sensitivity and specificity of metagenomic functional profiling, as implemented in MetaLAFFA between DIAMOND alignment and gene counting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a per-read alignment hit table but an already-aggregated gene or ortholog abundance table The alignment was produced by a tool whose output schema differs from DIAMOND tabular format without adaptation

skills.description: Use when reconstructing Patchwork's hit-stitching phase: DIAMOND tabular BLASTX hits against protein references must be merged into a single continuous sequence per reference for marker retrieval.
skills.name: hit-stitching-overlap-merging
skills.search_text: hit-stitching-overlap-merging Use when reconstructing Patchwork's hit-stitching phase: DIAMOND tabular BLASTX hits against protein references must be merged into a single continuous sequence per reference for marker retrieval. The input is raw DIAMOND hits that are already nonoverlapping and ordered per reference — stitching has nothing to merge The goal is trimming noncoding regions from an already-stitched sequence — that is Patchwork's separate sliding-window alignment trimming step References are not single-copy or near-USCO sequences — the article warns against chimeric sequences when references are not limited to near-USCOs http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Patchwork's hit-stitching step merges adjacent or overlapping DIAMOND BLASTX hits into one continuous translated amino acid sequence per reference protein, retaining only the best-scoring HSP for each overlapping region. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Patchwork's hit-stitching step merges adjacent or overlapping DIAMOND BLASTX hits into one continuous translated amino acid sequence per reference protein, retaining only the best-scoring HSP for each overlapping region.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw DIAMOND hits that are already nonoverlapping and ordered per reference — stitching has nothing to merge The goal is trimming noncoding regions from an already-stitched sequence — that is Patchwork's separate sliding-window alignment trimming step References are not single-copy or near-USCO sequences — the article warns against chimeric sequences when references are not limited to near-USCOs

skills.description: Use when retrieving phylogenetic markers (e.g. USCOs/near-USCOs) from fragmented WGS assemblies or reads with Patchwork, and DIAMOND search sensitivity, frameshift, or tantan masking parameters must be set to maximize retrieval and coverage.
skills.name: hit-stitching-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: hit-stitching-parameter-configuration Use when retrieving phylogenetic markers (e.g. USCOs/near-USCOs) from fragmented WGS assemblies or reads with Patchwork, and DIAMOND search sensitivity, frameshift, or tantan masking parameters must be set to maximize retrieval and coverage. Reference sequences are not near-USCOs — the article recommends limiting references to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences The query is already high-quality annotated sequence rather than fragmented WGS assembly or reads, where marker retrieval from WGS is unnecessary Tantan masking removal is undesirable because target sequences contain low-complexity regions that would produce spurious hits http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Configure Patchwork's hit-stitching phase, in which adjacent or overlapping DIAMOND alignments to a protein reference are merged into one continuous sequence, and tune the benchmark search options (--ultra-sensitive --frameshift 15 --masking 0) so that homologous markers can be recovered even between highly divergent species. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Configure Patchwork's hit-stitching phase, in which adjacent or overlapping DIAMOND alignments to a protein reference are merged into one continuous sequence, and tune the benchmark search options (--ultra-sensitive --frameshift 15 --masking 0) so that homologous markers can be recovered even between highly divergent species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference sequences are not near-USCOs — the article recommends limiting references to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences The query is already high-quality annotated sequence rather than fragmented WGS assembly or reads, where marker retrieval from WGS is unnecessary Tantan masking removal is undesirable because target sequences contain low-complexity regions that would produce spurious hits

skills.description: Use when benchmarking ShoRAH's error-correction (diri_sampler) and frequency-estimation (freqEst) stages on large HIV-1 amplicon/pyrosequencing read sets, or when validating reported runtimes against the paper's hardware configuration.
skills.name: hiv-amplicon-read-processing
skills.search_text: hiv-amplicon-read-processing Use when benchmarking ShoRAH's error-correction (diri_sampler) and frequency-estimation (freqEst) stages on large HIV-1 amplicon/pyrosequencing read sets, or when validating reported runtimes against the paper's hardware configuration. Input reads are already error-corrected or a haplotype frequency table already exists — re-running the timed steps adds no information Global haplotype reconstruction is required on ShoRAH2, where global mode is disabled (use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or V-pipe global options instead) A packaged binary/container or Windows-native execution is required without WSL/Cygwin, and compiling from the command line is not feasible http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A runtime-benchmark skill for ShoRAH-based amplicon read processing: it reproduces the paper's computational-efficiency measurements for the error-correction (local haplotype reconstruction) and frequency-estimation steps on a large pyrosequencing sample, recording hardware configuration and wall-clock timings. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: A runtime-benchmark skill for ShoRAH-based amplicon read processing: it reproduces the paper's computational-efficiency measurements for the error-correction (local haplotype reconstruction) and frequency-estimation steps on a large pyrosequencing sample, recording hardware configuration and wall-clock timings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already error-corrected or a haplotype frequency table already exists — re-running the timed steps adds no information Global haplotype reconstruction is required on ShoRAH2, where global mode is disabled (use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or V-pipe global options instead) A packaged binary/container or Windows-native execution is required without WSL/Cygwin, and compiling from the command line is not feasible

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end genomic FASTQ reads (isolate or metagenome) should be scanned for cas genes/CRISPR arrays without a complete assembly, e.g. phage-therapy susceptibility screening or novel CRISPR/Cas discovery.
skills.name: hmm-based-cas-protein-search
skills.search_text: hmm-based-cas-protein-search Use when raw paired-end genomic FASTQ reads (isolate or metagenome) should be scanned for cas genes/CRISPR arrays without a complete assembly, e.g. phage-therapy susceptibility screening or novel CRISPR/Cas discovery. The dataset already has a high-quality complete genome assembly and annotation; running the targeted HMM-seeded pipeline adds overhead without benefit The target genes lack representative profile HMMs and no reference nucleotide sequences are available to reconfigure the pipeline Input is not short DNA sequencing reads (e.g. long-read-only data), since the pipeline depends on short-read ORF prediction and VSEARCH seed expansion http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Identify CRISPR-associated (cas) protein coding reads in raw Illumina data by searching translated reads against a curated set of 120 Cas protein family profile HMMs with HMMER, producing 'seed' reads that prime targeted assembly. This avoids complete genome assembly when the goal is CRISPR/Cas discovery. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Identify CRISPR-associated (cas) protein coding reads in raw Illumina data by searching translated reads against a curated set of 120 Cas protein family profile HMMs with HMMER, producing 'seed' reads that prime targeted assembly. This avoids complete genome assembly when the goal is CRISPR/Cas discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already has a high-quality complete genome assembly and annotation; running the targeted HMM-seeded pipeline adds overhead without benefit The target genes lack representative profile HMMs and no reference nucleotide sequences are available to reconfigure the pipeline Input is not short DNA sequencing reads (e.g. long-read-only data), since the pipeline depends on short-read ORF prediction and VSEARCH seed expansion

skills.description: Use when starting from nucleotide (or already gene-predicted) bacterial genome FASTAs and you need Pfam protein family presence/absence profiles as features for trait prediction or comparative genomics, following Traitar's Prodigal + HMMER/Pfam 27.0 workflow.
skills.name: hmm-based-genome-annotation
skills.search_text: hmm-based-genome-annotation Use when starting from nucleotide (or already gene-predicted) bacterial genome FASTAs and you need Pfam protein family presence/absence profiles as features for trait prediction or comparative genomics, following Traitar's Prodigal + HMMER/Pfam 27.0 workflow. Protein sequences rather than nucleotide genomes are the input only if you switch to Traitar's from_genes/protein path — do not run Prodigal on protein FASTA Genes have already been predicted externally with a different caller and GFFs from img/RefSeq are used — from_genes feature tracks are experimental and gene IDs are inconsistent across sources You need trait predictions from other omics data (transcriptomics, metabolomics) — Traitar only uses presence/absence of protein families http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Annotate bacterial genomes with protein family profiles by predicting ORFs with Prodigal and scanning the coding sequences against Pfam 27.0 HMM models using HMMER's hmmsearch, as implemented in the Traitar pipeline. These Pfam profiles are the feature basis for downstream genotype-phenotype inference (67 traits) with the phypat and phypat+PGL classifiers. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00101-16
skills.summary: Annotate bacterial genomes with protein family profiles by predicting ORFs with Prodigal and scanning the coding sequences against Pfam 27.0 HMM models using HMMER's hmmsearch, as implemented in the Traitar pipeline. These Pfam profiles are the feature basis for downstream genotype-phenotype inference (67 traits) with the phypat and phypat+PGL classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Protein sequences rather than nucleotide genomes are the input only if you switch to Traitar's from_genes/protein path — do not run Prodigal on protein FASTA Genes have already been predicted externally with a different caller and GFFs from img/RefSeq are used — from_genes feature tracks are experimental and gene IDs are inconsistent across sources You need trait predictions from other omics data (transcriptomics, metabolomics) — Traitar only uses presence/absence of protein families

skills.description: Use when mining nucleotide genomes (FASTA contigs or assemblies) for RiPP-encoding BGCs and you need to locate modification enzyme homologs to define candidate precursor peptide regions before spectra matching.
skills.name: hmm-based-modification-enzyme-annotation
skills.search_text: hmm-based-modification-enzyme-annotation Use when mining nucleotide genomes (FASTA contigs or assemblies) for RiPP-encoding BGCs and you need to locate modification enzyme homologs to define candidate precursor peptide regions before spectra matching. When the goal is exhaustive precursor enumeration regardless of enzyme homology — all-ORF mode (6-frame translation + <200 aa ORF threshold) is the alternative, at the cost of ~4 orders of magnitude more candidates When peptides of interest lack sequence similarity to known RiPP modification enzymes — the motif-ORF strategy misses them, so HMM anchoring is inappropriate When the RiPP class has no curated HMM profile available; the enzyme-based windowing cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Uses HMMer profile hidden Markov models to detect RiPP modification enzymes (e.g. lanthionine synthetases, lasso cyclases, cyanobactin proteases) in translated genome sequences, anchoring the construction of putative biosynthetic gene cluster windows for RiPP precursor mining in MetaMiner. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.09.004
skills.summary: Uses HMMer profile hidden Markov models to detect RiPP modification enzymes (e.g. lanthionine synthetases, lasso cyclases, cyanobactin proteases) in translated genome sequences, anchoring the construction of putative biosynthetic gene cluster windows for RiPP precursor mining in MetaMiner.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is exhaustive precursor enumeration regardless of enzyme homology — all-ORF mode (6-frame translation + <200 aa ORF threshold) is the alternative, at the cost of ~4 orders of magnitude more candidates When peptides of interest lack sequence similarity to known RiPP modification enzymes — the motif-ORF strategy misses them, so HMM anchoring is inappropriate When the RiPP class has no curated HMM profile available; the enzyme-based windowing cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when input is a protein sequence set in FASTA format and the goal is automatic detection and enzyme-type prediction of proteins belonging to known paralogous families, where blast-based or phylogenetic assignment is too slow or error-prone.
skills.name: hmm-based-protein-classification
skills.search_text: hmm-based-protein-classification Use when input is a protein sequence set in FASTA format and the goal is automatic detection and enzyme-type prediction of proteins belonging to known paralogous families, where blast-based or phylogenetic assignment is too slow or error-prone. Input is nucleotide sequence (e.g. raw reads or contigs) rather than a protein FASTA set — DiSCo requires user-supplied protein sequences The goal is de novo phylogenetic reconstruction of DsrAB rather than automatic family/type assignment from sequence data Proteins of interest fall outside the Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism families covered by the DiSCo HMM library http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Identify and type-classify proteins from FASTA-formatted protein data by searching them against a curated profile HMM library with HMMER3 hmmsearch, then filtering and assigning hits via a best-hit strategy. This is the core mechanism of DiSCo, a Perl 5 tool for Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism protein classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000603
skills.summary: Identify and type-classify proteins from FASTA-formatted protein data by searching them against a curated profile HMM library with HMMER3 hmmsearch, then filtering and assigning hits via a best-hit strategy. This is the core mechanism of DiSCo, a Perl 5 tool for Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism protein classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is nucleotide sequence (e.g. raw reads or contigs) rather than a protein FASTA set — DiSCo requires user-supplied protein sequences The goal is de novo phylogenetic reconstruction of DsrAB rather than automatic family/type assignment from sequence data Proteins of interest fall outside the Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism families covered by the DiSCo HMM library

skills.description: Use when you need to detect SSU rRNA genes within large sequence collections (e.g. non-redundant SILVA releases or metagenome assemblies) so that structural features such as ≥10 bp insertion boundaries can be located from alignment gaps.
skills.name: hmm-based-rrna-gene-identification
skills.search_text: hmm-based-rrna-gene-identification Use when you need to detect SSU rRNA genes within large sequence collections (e.g. non-redundant SILVA releases or metagenome assemblies) so that structural features such as ≥10 bp insertion boundaries can be located from alignment gaps. Input sequences are already structurally aligned and curated — apply the gap-based insertion boundary detection directly instead of re-running database search The goal is ribosomal protein gene (rp16) phylogeny, which requires ≥1,000 aligned residues rather than SSU rRNA model search Sequences contain introns that have not been removed; all insertions ≥10 bp must be removed before multiple sequence alignment and phylogenetic analysis of 16S rRNA gene sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Identifies 16S/SSU rRNA gene sequences in a nucleotide database by searching all records against a manually curated structural alignment model using Infernal cmsearch in hmmonly mode, enabling reproducible rRNA detection and downstream gap-based insertion analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: Identifies 16S/SSU rRNA gene sequences in a nucleotide database by searching all records against a manually curated structural alignment model using Infernal cmsearch in hmmonly mode, enabling reproducible rRNA detection and downstream gap-based insertion analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are already structurally aligned and curated — apply the gap-based insertion boundary detection directly instead of re-running database search The goal is ribosomal protein gene (rp16) phylogeny, which requires ≥1,000 aligned residues rather than SSU rRNA model search Sequences contain introns that have not been removed; all insertions ≥10 bp must be removed before multiple sequence alignment and phylogenetic analysis of 16S rRNA gene sequences

skills.description: Use when KEMET --hmm_mode onebm HMM hits on MAGs must be validated against the same HMM search on corresponding NCBI/PATRIC complete isolate genomes, and precision/sensitivity of recovered missing KOs is needed.
skills.name: hmm-hit-precision-sensitivity-calculation
skills.search_text: hmm-hit-precision-sensitivity-calculation Use when KEMET --hmm_mode onebm HMM hits on MAGs must be validated against the same HMM search on corresponding NCBI/PATRIC complete isolate genomes, and precision/sensitivity of recovered missing KOs is needed. Only KEGG Module completeness evaluation is needed without HMM-based annotation expansion (use --skip_hmm instead) No matched complete reference isolate genome exists for the MAG, so no pair-wise concordance can be computed Input KO annotations are not in a supported KEGG annotation format (eggnog / kaas / kofamkoala), which KEMET requires for the MODULES recap and HMM workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies concordance between KEGG ortholog (KO) hits recovered by KEMET profile HMM searches on MAGs versus the identical searches on matched complete reference isolate genomes, yielding per-pair common/MAG-only/complete-genome-only splits and derived precision and sensitivity (e.g. 84.76% shared, 7.62% each discordant class, 91.75% precision/sensitivity). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Quantifies concordance between KEGG ortholog (KO) hits recovered by KEMET profile HMM searches on MAGs versus the identical searches on matched complete reference isolate genomes, yielding per-pair common/MAG-only/complete-genome-only splits and derived precision and sensitivity (e.g. 84.76% shared, 7.62% each discordant class, 91.75% precision/sensitivity).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only KEGG Module completeness evaluation is needed without HMM-based annotation expansion (use --skip_hmm instead) No matched complete reference isolate genome exists for the MAG, so no pair-wise concordance can be computed Input KO annotations are not in a supported KEGG annotation format (eggnog / kaas / kofamkoala), which KEMET requires for the MODULES recap and HMM workflow

skills.description: Use when KEMET HMM-search (--hmm_mode onebm/module/kos) output must be filtered so only KOs whose HMM profile score passes the quality cutoff (default 0.43) count as recovered annotations, e.g. in truncation or KO-removal recovery tests.
skills.name: hmm-hit-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: hmm-hit-threshold-filtering Use when KEMET HMM-search (--hmm_mode onebm/module/kos) output must be filtered so only KOs whose HMM profile score passes the quality cutoff (default 0.43) count as recovered annotations, e.g. in truncation or KO-removal recovery tests. When the goal is only KEGG Module completeness evaluation without HMM searches (use --skip_hmm instead) When hits are already filtered by another downstream quality control, so applying the 0.43 cutoff again would double-filter and underestimate recovery When evaluating KEMET's Module partitioning against KEGG Mapper or METABOLIC, which does not involve HMM hit scoring A filtering step from the KEMET workflow that differentiates legitimate HMM hits from spurious profile-HMM matches by applying a quality threshold (default 0.43) to HMMER search scores when recovering missing KEGG ortholog annotations. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: A filtering step from the KEMET workflow that differentiates legitimate HMM hits from spurious profile-HMM matches by applying a quality threshold (default 0.43) to HMMER search scores when recovering missing KEGG ortholog annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only KEGG Module completeness evaluation without HMM searches (use --skip_hmm instead) When hits are already filtered by another downstream quality control, so applying the 0.43 cutoff again would double-filter and underestimate recovery When evaluating KEMET's Module partitioning against KEGG Mapper or METABOLIC, which does not involve HMM hit scoring

skills.description: Use when starting from nucleotide FASTA genomes (or already-predicted ORFs) and you need Pfam-A protein family profiles as features for Traitar phenotype prediction across tens or hundreds of bacterial samples.
skills.name: hmm-profile-annotation-against-pfam
skills.search_text: hmm-profile-annotation-against-pfam Use when starting from nucleotide FASTA genomes (or already-predicted ORFs) and you need Pfam-A protein family profiles as features for Traitar phenotype prediction across tens or hundreds of bacterial samples. Input consists of raw reads or transcriptomic/proteomic data — Traitar only takes nucleotide or protein sequences of genomes and uses only protein family presence/absence, not other omics data Input is already an annotated Pfam domain table — in that case proceed directly to Traitar's phenotype-prediction stage rather than re-running Prodigal/HMMer Only a handful of traits tied to specific curated gene sets are needed and a genotype-phenotype association tool like PICA is more appropriate for the question http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3301 Annotate predicted protein-coding sequences from microbial genomes with Pfam protein family profiles using HMMER hmmsearch, as implemented in the Traitar microbial trait analyzer, to build the binary presence/absence protein-family profiles that feed its 67-phenotype SVM classifiers. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00101-16
skills.summary: Annotate predicted protein-coding sequences from microbial genomes with Pfam protein family profiles using HMMER hmmsearch, as implemented in the Traitar microbial trait analyzer, to build the binary presence/absence protein-family profiles that feed its 67-phenotype SVM classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of raw reads or transcriptomic/proteomic data — Traitar only takes nucleotide or protein sequences of genomes and uses only protein family presence/absence, not other omics data Input is already an annotated Pfam domain table — in that case proceed directly to Traitar's phenotype-prediction stage rather than re-running Prodigal/HMMer Only a handful of traits tied to specific curated gene sets are needed and a genotype-phenotype association tool like PICA is more appropriate for the question

skills.description: Use when a curated HMM-based classifier (e.g. the DsrABCMK model set behind DiSCo) needs its stability tested against training-set composition, i.e. checking whether model assignments or type predictions change when single training sequences are dropped.
skills.name: hmm-profile-leave-one-out-validation
skills.search_text: hmm-profile-leave-one-out-validation Use when a curated HMM-based classifier (e.g. the DsrABCMK model set behind DiSCo) needs its stability tested against training-set composition, i.e. checking whether model assignments or type predictions change when single training sequences are dropped. When the goal is to re-tune or re-optimize model thresholds — this skill deliberately keeps the original user-defined cut-offs fixed to isolate training-set effects When input is not protein sequence data in FASTA format; DiSCo runs protein sets against its curated HMM library, not nucleotide data When testing robustness to algorithm parameters or cutoff choices rather than to training-set composition — a different sensitivity design is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Robustness assessment for curated HMM model sets: each training sequence is excluded one at a time, the HMM profile is rebuilt with hmmbuild, and the original user-defined score/E-value cut-offs are kept fixed so downstream assignments can be compared against the full-model reference hitlist. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000603
skills.summary: Robustness assessment for curated HMM model sets: each training sequence is excluded one at a time, the HMM profile is rebuilt with hmmbuild, and the original user-defined score/E-value cut-offs are kept fixed so downstream assignments can be compared against the full-model reference hitlist.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to re-tune or re-optimize model thresholds — this skill deliberately keeps the original user-defined cut-offs fixed to isolate training-set effects When input is not protein sequence data in FASTA format; DiSCo runs protein sets against its curated HMM library, not nucleotide data When testing robustness to algorithm parameters or cutoff choices rather than to training-set composition — a different sensitivity design is needed

skills.description: Use when eggNOG-mapper/.emapper.annotations or similar KO annotations are suspected incomplete (e.g. fragmented MAG assemblies or truncated genes) and missing KOs from KEGG Modules need evidence-backed recovery via HMM profile search.
skills.name: hmm-profile-ortholog-recovery
skills.search_text: hmm-profile-ortholog-recovery Use when eggNOG-mapper/.emapper.annotations or similar KO annotations are suspected incomplete (e.g. fragmented MAG assemblies or truncated genes) and missing KOs from KEGG Modules need evidence-backed recovery via HMM profile search. The goal is only KEGG Module completeness summarization with no need to expand annotations — use KEMET with --skip_hmm instead of HMM searches The genome annotation comes from a format other than eggnog/kaas/kofamkoala, since KEMET's -a parameter only supports these KO annotation formats Genes are severely fragmented (e.g. ~70% sequence truncation), where recovery rates decline markedly and HMM hits may not be trustworthy, especially in MAGs http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Recover missing or unannotated KEGG orthologs (KOs) by searching KEGG Module-specific profile HMMs with KEMET's --hmm_mode onebm against genome/MAG protein sequences, using a default score threshold of 0.43 to call legit hits and expand KEGG Module completeness beyond sequence-similarity annotations like eggNOG-Mapper. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Recover missing or unannotated KEGG orthologs (KOs) by searching KEGG Module-specific profile HMMs with KEMET's --hmm_mode onebm against genome/MAG protein sequences, using a default score threshold of 0.43 to call legit hits and expand KEGG Module completeness beyond sequence-similarity annotations like eggNOG-Mapper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only KEGG Module completeness summarization with no need to expand annotations — use KEMET with --skip_hmm instead of HMM searches The genome annotation comes from a format other than eggnog/kaas/kofamkoala, since KEMET's -a parameter only supports these KO annotation formats Genes are severely fragmented (e.g. ~70% sequence truncation), where recovery rates decline markedly and HMM hits may not be trustworthy, especially in MAGs

skills.description: Use when building protein-family inventories or presence/absence matrices from predicted ORFs whose sequence divergence defeats keyword-based annotation — e.g. surveying ribosomal protein L30, L9, L1 absence across divergent lineages such as CPR and TM6.
skills.name: hmm-profile-protein-family-detection
skills.search_text: hmm-profile-protein-family-detection Use when building protein-family inventories or presence/absence matrices from predicted ORFs whose sequence divergence defeats keyword-based annotation — e.g. surveying ribosomal protein L30, L9, L1 absence across divergent lineages such as CPR and TM6. When the goal is annotating well-conserved, already-keyword-labeled proteins in non-divergent reference genomes — keyword gene lists are sufficient and faster When genomes are highly fragmentary: absence calls from missing HMM hits are unreliable unless the bin meets the near-complete quality gate (≥75% single-copy genes, ≤1.125 copies, assembled 16S rRNA gene) When the family of interest has no curated Pfam HMM profile — hmmscan cannot detect it and a custom profile or keyword search is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Inventory protein families (e.g. ribosomal proteins rpL30, rpL9, rpL1, Der) across genome bins by scanning all translated ORFs against Pfam HMM profiles with HMMER hmmscan, capturing divergent homologs that keyword-based annotation misses. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: Inventory protein families (e.g. ribosomal proteins rpL30, rpL9, rpL1, Der) across genome bins by scanning all translated ORFs against Pfam HMM profiles with HMMER hmmscan, capturing divergent homologs that keyword-based annotation misses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is annotating well-conserved, already-keyword-labeled proteins in non-divergent reference genomes — keyword gene lists are sufficient and faster When genomes are highly fragmentary: absence calls from missing HMM hits are unreliable unless the bin meets the near-complete quality gate (≥75% single-copy genes, ≤1.125 copies, assembled 16S rRNA gene) When the family of interest has no curated Pfam HMM profile — hmmscan cannot detect it and a custom profile or keyword search is required

skills.description: Use when MAG or draft-genome eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKoala KO annotations leave KEGG Modules incomplete and unannotated genes (including partially truncated sequences) need evidence-based KO recovery via profile HMMs.
skills.name: hmm-profile-search-annotation-recovery
skills.search_text: hmm-profile-search-annotation-recovery Use when MAG or draft-genome eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKoala KO annotations leave KEGG Modules incomplete and unannotated genes (including partially truncated sequences) need evidence-based KO recovery via profile HMMs. The goal is only KEGG Module completeness evaluation without annotation expansion — use --skip_hmm instead; --no_genome mode stops after completeness evaluation A genome-scale metabolic model must be gapfilled rather than annotated — this is the HMM search stage only; run KEMET's --gsmm_mode (denovo/existing) with CarveMe v1.4.1 (--fbc2 -u) models separately Input KOs are already exhaustively annotated or the genome is complete with high-confidence KOs, so HMM recovery adds no missing-ortholog signal Recover missing KEGG ortholog (KO) annotations in MAGs or draft genomes by running KEMET's profile HMM searches (HMMER/MAFFT under the hood) against curated KO profiles, and benchmark recovery quality by comparing MAG hits against the corresponding complete reference isolate genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Recover missing KEGG ortholog (KO) annotations in MAGs or draft genomes by running KEMET's profile HMM searches (HMMER/MAFFT under the hood) against curated KO profiles, and benchmark recovery quality by comparing MAG hits against the corresponding complete reference isolate genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only KEGG Module completeness evaluation without annotation expansion — use --skip_hmm instead; --no_genome mode stops after completeness evaluation A genome-scale metabolic model must be gapfilled rather than annotated — this is the HMM search stage only; run KEMET's --gsmm_mode (denovo/existing) with CarveMe v1.4.1 (--fbc2 -u) models separately Input KOs are already exhaustively annotated or the genome is complete with high-confidence KOs, so HMM recovery adds no missing-ortholog signal

skills.summary: Translates raw short-read sequencing data into candidate proteins and searches them with HMMER against Cas protein profile HMMs to identify seed reads, as used in CasCollect's default protein mode for targeted CRISPR/Cas assembly.

skills.description: Use when you need to identify and type-classify Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism proteins from FASTA protein data using profile HMMs with model-specific score and E-value cut-offs rather than phylogenetic assignment.
skills.name: hmm-search-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: hmm-search-threshold-filtering Use when you need to identify and type-classify Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism proteins from FASTA protein data using profile HMMs with model-specific score and E-value cut-offs rather than phylogenetic assignment. Input is raw nucleotide data — DiSCo.pl requires FASTA protein sequences and does not translate. You need de novo phylogenetic placement of DsrAB sequences rather than fast HMM-based family/type assignment — the article contrasts DiSCo with time-consuming phylogenetic classification. Proteins fall outside the Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism families covered by the DiSCo HMM library (e.g. unrelated paralogous markers or non-Dsr pathways). http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 DiSCo's two-stage identification filter: hmmsearch of FASTA protein input against the curated DiSCo HMM library (HMMER 3.1b2), followed by a Perl filter script that applies model-specific user-defined score/E-value cut-offs (thresholds.txt) and a best-hit strategy to assign each input sequence to one protein family and predicted enzyme type. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000603
skills.summary: DiSCo's two-stage identification filter: hmmsearch of FASTA protein input against the curated DiSCo HMM library (HMMER 3.1b2), followed by a Perl filter script that applies model-specific user-defined score/E-value cut-offs (thresholds.txt) and a best-hit strategy to assign each input sequence to one protein family and predicted enzyme type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nucleotide data — DiSCo.pl requires FASTA protein sequences and does not translate. You need de novo phylogenetic placement of DsrAB sequences rather than fast HMM-based family/type assignment — the article contrasts DiSCo with time-consuming phylogenetic classification. Proteins fall outside the Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism families covered by the DiSCo HMM library (e.g. unrelated paralogous markers or non-Dsr pathways).

skills.summary: Construct profile hidden Markov models from curated ortholog sequence alignments (hmmbuild, HMMER) and search them against protein sequences from MAGs/genomes (nhmmer) to recover missing KEGG ortholog (KO) annotations, as implemented in KEMET.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has no genome/MAG FASTA available and only precomputed KEGG annotations — use --no_genome / --skip_hmm, as the pipeline stops after KEGG MODULES Completeness Evaluation The goal is only KEGG Module completeness summarization of existing annotations without searching for missing KOs — the --skip_hmm flag makes this skill unnecessary Input sequences are not protein-coding genes or the KOs of interest lack a taxonomically relevant subset of KEGG GENES sequences to build a reliable profile HMM

skills.description: Use when evaluating how k-mer distance metrics (Cosine Similarity, Bray-Curtis, MinHash, Simka) cluster metagenomic samples by body site, especially to test whether analysis of assembled contigs instead of reads degrades separation.
skills.name: hmp-body-site-clustering-evaluation
skills.search_text: hmp-body-site-clustering-evaluation Use when evaluating how k-mer distance metrics (Cosine Similarity, Bray-Curtis, MinHash, Simka) cluster metagenomic samples by body site, especially to test whether analysis of assembled contigs instead of reads degrades separation. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than assembled contigs — the known failure mode being reproduced (Simka near-maximum distances, Libra low resolution) applies to the contig-based setting Goal is abundance-sensitive comparison where reads and their k-mer counts must be fully used (Libra's intended mode, which requires reads rather than assemblies) Dataset is not a body-site-annotated collection such as HMP, so body-site clustering cannot serve as an acceptance check http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reproduces the Libra paper's assembled-contigs comparison on the 48-sample Human Microbiome Project (HMP) WGS dataset, benchmarking Mash, Libra (Cosine Similarity and Bray-Curtis), and Simka distance matrices for clustering samples by body site. It demonstrates that data reduction (contigs instead of reads) and count normalization strip clustering resolution. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Reproduces the Libra paper's assembled-contigs comparison on the 48-sample Human Microbiome Project (HMP) WGS dataset, benchmarking Mash, Libra (Cosine Similarity and Bray-Curtis), and Simka distance matrices for clustering samples by body site. It demonstrates that data reduction (contigs instead of reads) and count normalization strip clustering resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than assembled contigs — the known failure mode being reproduced (Simka near-maximum distances, Libra low resolution) applies to the contig-based setting Goal is abundance-sensitive comparison where reads and their k-mer counts must be fully used (Libra's intended mode, which requires reads rather than assemblies) Dataset is not a body-site-annotated collection such as HMP, so body-site clustering cannot serve as an acceptance check

skills.description: Use when a benchmark requires the HMP prokaryotic genome set with trusted NCBI-taxonomy labels — e.g. evaluating a MAG taxonomy classifier where strain-level assignments are needed and GTDB-based tools cannot provide them.
skills.name: hmp-genome-dataset-retrieval
skills.search_text: hmp-genome-dataset-retrieval Use when a benchmark requires the HMP prokaryotic genome set with trusted NCBI-taxonomy labels — e.g. evaluating a MAG taxonomy classifier where strain-level assignments are needed and GTDB-based tools cannot provide them. The benchmark targets GTDB-based evaluation or requires GTDB taxonomy natively — HMP labels are NCBI-based and would need conversion tables in the opposite direction. The question requires CAMI II mock community or real metagenomic sample data (e.g. GI-Illumina, SRR606249) rather than isolated reference genomes. Only MAGs from binning pipelines are available (e.g. MetaBAT2 bins) — this skill retrieves reference-grade complete genomes, not binned assemblies. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Retrieves the 939 bacterial and archaeal Human Microbiome Project (HMP) genomes and their expected NCBI taxonomic labels from the NCBI Human Microbiome FTP site, forming the reference ground-truth set used to benchmark kMetaShot against GTDBtk and CAMITAX at strain, species, and genus levels. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: Retrieves the 939 bacterial and archaeal Human Microbiome Project (HMP) genomes and their expected NCBI taxonomic labels from the NCBI Human Microbiome FTP site, forming the reference ground-truth set used to benchmark kMetaShot against GTDBtk and CAMITAX at strain, species, and genus levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The benchmark targets GTDB-based evaluation or requires GTDB taxonomy natively — HMP labels are NCBI-based and would need conversion tables in the opposite direction. The question requires CAMI II mock community or real metagenomic sample data (e.g. GI-Illumina, SRR606249) rather than isolated reference genomes. Only MAGs from binning pipelines are available (e.g. MetaBAT2 bins) — this skill retrieves reference-grade complete genomes, not binned assemblies.

skills.description: Use when a candidate bait-region table (CandidateBaitRegions.tab) from the identification stage must be purged of probes with homologous hits to host or contaminant reference sequences before final probe selection.
skills.name: homology-based-offtarget-probe-filtration
skills.search_text: homology-based-offtarget-probe-filtration Use when a candidate bait-region table (CandidateBaitRegions.tab) from the identification stage must be purged of probes with homologous hits to host or contaminant reference sequences before final probe selection. The input is not yet a candidate bait-region table — e.g. raw FASTQ reads needing human-read filtration or deduplication, which are downstream analysis filters, not probe-set filtration. The target genomes are unknown or unannotatable, so no candidate probes could be identified and there is nothing to filter. You only need the final balanced probe set and have no off-target/contaminant sequences to screen against — in that case the Selection stage alone may suffice, though skipping filtration risks cross-reactivity. http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 A HUBDesign pipeline stage that removes candidate hybridization probes predicted to capture off-target sequences by BLASTn screening against blacklist databases, and masks low-complexity regions, before balanced probe selection. It is the step that converts SA_BOND-identified candidate bait regions into a specificity-checked candidate pool. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: A HUBDesign pipeline stage that removes candidate hybridization probes predicted to capture off-target sequences by BLASTn screening against blacklist databases, and masks low-complexity regions, before balanced probe selection. It is the step that converts SA_BOND-identified candidate bait regions into a specificity-checked candidate pool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not yet a candidate bait-region table — e.g. raw FASTQ reads needing human-read filtration or deduplication, which are downstream analysis filters, not probe-set filtration. The target genomes are unknown or unannotatable, so no candidate probes could be identified and there is nothing to filter. You only need the final balanced probe set and have no off-target/contaminant sequences to screen against — in that case the Selection stage alone may suffice, though skipping filtration risks cross-reactivity.

skills.search_text: homology-search-against-viral-refseq Use when viral contigs (>10 kbp, already identified as viral) need reference-backed taxonomy, and you want homology-based calls against NCBI viral RefSeq to complement clustering-based assignment.
