skills.summary: Assign taxonomy to filtered viral contigs by running the MMseqs2 taxonomy module against the NCBI viral RefSeq database, producing homology-based taxonomic calls that are later reconciled with vConTACT2 cluster-based assignments via lowest-common-ancestor voting within ViroProfiler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contigs are shorter than 10 kbp — ViroProfiler retains only sequences longer than 10 kbp for taxonomy assignment The goal is classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses, which is outside ViroProfiler's stated design scope Sequences are not yet confirmed viral — this skill assumes viral identification (e.g., VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder) has already been performed

skills.description: Use when generating custom k-mer detection networks with baseLess run_production_pipeline and you need to purge homopolymeric candidate k-mers from the evolutionary pool so only signal-distinguishable 16S k-mers survive.
skills.name: homopolymer-kmer-rejection
skills.search_text: homopolymer-kmer-rejection Use when generating custom k-mer detection networks with baseLess run_production_pipeline and you need to purge homopolymeric candidate k-mers from the evolutionary pool so only signal-distinguishable 16S k-mers survive. You only need off-the-shelf 16S detection — baseLess ships a pre-generated set of k-mer networks for k-mers salient in 16S detection ('baseLess update_16s_db'), so no custom selection or homopolymer filtering is needed Your input is already-basecalled FASTQ without raw signal — the pipeline requires resquiggled fast5 signal reads for squiggle-based selection You are compiling an abundance-mode model with --train-on-the-fly against large non-16S genomes where the 16S-specific abundance filtering and homopolymer rejection tuning does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A filtering rule inside baseLess's evolutionary k-mer selection that discards candidate k-mers containing homopolymer runs (repeated identical bases) before the surviving 1500 16S k-mers are written to the k-mer list, because homopolymeric k-mers produce ambiguous squiggles that small k-mer-detecting neural networks cannot reliably discriminate. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017
skills.summary: A filtering rule inside baseLess's evolutionary k-mer selection that discards candidate k-mers containing homopolymer runs (repeated identical bases) before the surviving 1500 16S k-mers are written to the k-mer list, because homopolymeric k-mers produce ambiguous squiggles that small k-mer-detecting neural networks cannot reliably discriminate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need off-the-shelf 16S detection — baseLess ships a pre-generated set of k-mer networks for k-mers salient in 16S detection ('baseLess update_16s_db'), so no custom selection or homopolymer filtering is needed Your input is already-basecalled FASTQ without raw signal — the pipeline requires resquiggled fast5 signal reads for squiggle-based selection You are compiling an abundance-mode model with --train-on-the-fly against large non-16S genomes where the 16S-specific abundance filtering and homopolymer rejection tuning does not apply

skills.search_text: horizontal-gene-transfer-evidence-analysis Use when you have a catalogue of putative ISs (e.g. the 879-sequence ISC FASTA) and need to identify their isolate origins, taxonomic sharing breadth, and whether cross-genera or cross-class sharing implies horizontal transfer. skills.description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ files from ribodepleted or poly(A)-enriched stool metatranscriptomes must be screened for human-derived reads, e.g. to test whether host transcriptomes are recoverable or to quantify host contamination.

skills.search_text: host-read-alignment-against-human-genome Use when raw paired-end FASTQ files from ribodepleted or poly(A)-enriched stool metatranscriptomes must be screened for human-derived reads, e.g. to test whether host transcriptomes are recoverable or to quantify host contamination. skills.summary: Quantifies host transcript recovery from human stool metatranscriptomes by cleaning FASTQ reads with Trimmomatic, joining paired-end reads with FLASH, aligning them against the human genome reference, and tabulating human-matching reads per replicate as counts and percentages of total reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a SAMSA/MG-RAST annotation summary file (organism or functional tables) — those pipeline outputs contain no raw FASTQ to align against the human genome. The goal is microbial metatranscriptome annotation, where MG-RAST (or DIAMOND in SAMSA2) is used and remaining rRNA reads are discarded instead — host-read quantification is a separate alignment step. Sequences are short single-end reads under 100 bp — SAMSA requires long reads (>100 bp) or joined paired-end reads, so raw unjoined short reads cannot be processed this way without a merging step.

skills.search_text: host-read-decontamination-benchmarking Use when microbial FASTQ (short-read Illumina or ONT long-read) data must be decontaminated of human host sequences, or when comparing Hostile vs HRRT on human removal, microbial retention, throughput, and memory. The input is already a cleaned FASTQ or you need to keep host reads for human genetics analysis without an explicit --invert workflow You need taxonomic classification of reads rather than binary host/non-host depletion — Hostile only discards reads aligning to the index You require viral read retention but use the unmasked default index instead of human-t2t-hla.argos-bacteria-985_rs-viral-202401_ml-phage-202401 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A benchmarking skill for Hostile, an alignment-based host read decontamination tool, against the NCBI Human Read Removal Tool (HRRT), quantifying human read removal and simulated bacterial/mycobacterial read retention on Illumina and ONT FASTQ data. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad728
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for Hostile, an alignment-based host read decontamination tool, against the NCBI Human Read Removal Tool (HRRT), quantifying human read removal and simulated bacterial/mycobacterial read retention on Illumina and ONT FASTQ data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a cleaned FASTQ or you need to keep host reads for human genetics analysis without an explicit --invert workflow You need taxonomic classification of reads rather than binary host/non-host depletion — Hostile only discards reads aligning to the index You require viral read retention but use the unmasked default index instead of human-t2t-hla.argos-bacteria-985_rs-viral-202401_ml-phage-202401

skills.description: Use when raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQs contain host contamination (e.g. human gut samples) and host-derived reads must be removed before gene mapping and functional annotation.
skills.name: host-read-filtering
skills.search_text: host-read-filtering Use when raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQs contain host contamination (e.g. human gut samples) and host-derived reads must be removed before gene mapping and functional annotation. Input data are not shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. amplicon data or already host-filtered FASTQs) The host organism is not human and no alternative host reference database has been prepared — an appropriate host index must be substituted The goal is a later pipeline step such as duplicate read filtering or quality trimming, which are separate MetaLAFFA steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quality-control step in MetaLAFFA that removes host reads from shotgun metagenomic FASTQs by aligning them to the hs37d5 human genome reference (with 1000 Genomes Project decoy sequences) using Bowtie 2 and discarding reads matching the host above a quality threshold. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: Quality-control step in MetaLAFFA that removes host reads from shotgun metagenomic FASTQs by aligning them to the hs37d5 human genome reference (with 1000 Genomes Project decoy sequences) using Bowtie 2 and discarding reads matching the host above a quality threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. amplicon data or already host-filtered FASTQs) The host organism is not human and no alternative host reference database has been prepared — an appropriate host index must be substituted The goal is a later pipeline step such as duplicate read filtering or quality trimming, which are separate MetaLAFFA steps

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ reads from a host organism must be separated from microbial (bacterial, archaeal, viral) content before taxonomic classification or metagenomic reporting.
skills.name: host-read-filtering-against-reference-genome-index
skills.search_text: host-read-filtering-against-reference-genome-index Use when RNA-seq FASTQ reads from a host organism must be separated from microbial (bacterial, archaeal, viral) content before taxonomic classification or metagenomic reporting. Input is not host-derived RNA-seq data (e.g. shotgun metagenomic reads with no host background) — host filtering adds no value No reference genome FASTA/GTF or indexes are available for the host organism and they cannot be generated The goal is de novo host transcriptome analysis, where removing host reads would discard the signal of interest http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Filters host-organism reads out of RNA-seq FASTQ input by aligning against a reference genome index, then classifies the remaining exogenous reads with kraken2, as implemented in the nf-rnaSeqMetagen Nextflow/Singularity pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.medmic.2020.100011
skills.summary: Filters host-organism reads out of RNA-seq FASTQ input by aligning against a reference genome index, then classifies the remaining exogenous reads with kraken2, as implemented in the nf-rnaSeqMetagen Nextflow/Singularity pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not host-derived RNA-seq data (e.g. shotgun metagenomic reads with no host background) — host filtering adds no value No reference genome FASTA/GTF or indexes are available for the host organism and they cannot be generated The goal is de novo host transcriptome analysis, where removing host reads would discard the signal of interest

skills.search_text: host-read-filtering-rnaseq Use when RNA-seq FASTQ data must be stripped of host-organism reads before microbial taxonomic characterization, e.g. paired-end SSc skin RNA-seq against Mus_musculus.GRCm38. Input is already filtered exogenous FASTQ or a taxonomy table rather than raw RNA-seq reads Reads are metagenomic shotgun data with no host component to remove — the host alignment stage adds no value No host reference genome/annotation is available, since STAR/bowtie2 indexes cannot be generated http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filters host-organism reads out of RNA-seq FASTQ input using the nf-rnaSeqMetagen pipeline, which aligns reads against STAR and bowtie2 indexes of the host reference genome so that only exogenous reads pass onward to kraken2 taxonomic classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.medmic.2020.100011
skills.summary: Filters host-organism reads out of RNA-seq FASTQ input using the nf-rnaSeqMetagen pipeline, which aligns reads against STAR and bowtie2 indexes of the host reference genome so that only exogenous reads pass onward to kraken2 taxonomic classification.

skills.description: Use when you have two complementary host similarity sources (e.g., genome k-mer ONF similarity and GIP kernel similarity from known virus-host associations) and need a single square host-host similarity matrix to feed a heterogeneous virus-host network model.
skills.name: host-similarity-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: host-similarity-matrix-construction Use when you have two complementary host similarity sources (e.g., genome k-mer ONF similarity and GIP kernel similarity from known virus-host associations) and need a single square host-host similarity matrix to feed a heterogeneous virus-host network model. You only have one host similarity source (e.g., only ONF or only GIP) — SNF fusion requires at least two input similarity networks to diffuse between Your goal is direct sequence homology-based host assignment for a query virus whose candidate hosts are absent from the host genome database — the article notes such homology methods are limited because they 'depend on whether hosts of the query virus exist in the host genome database' http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs a fused host-host similarity network for ILMF-VH by combining oligonucleotide frequency (d2*, k=6) similarity with Gaussian interaction profile kernel similarity using similarity network fusion (SNF), replacing a single-sequence-similarity host network with a multi-source integrated one. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Constructs a fused host-host similarity network for ILMF-VH by combining oligonucleotide frequency (d2*, k=6) similarity with Gaussian interaction profile kernel similarity using similarity network fusion (SNF), replacing a single-sequence-similarity host network with a multi-source integrated one.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have one host similarity source (e.g., only ONF or only GIP) — SNF fusion requires at least two input similarity networks to diffuse between Your goal is direct sequence homology-based host assignment for a query virus whose candidate hosts are absent from the host genome database — the article notes such homology methods are limited because they 'depend on whether hosts of the query virus exist in the host genome database'

skills.description: Use when preparing inputs for Nano2NGS-Muta: a hotspot panel must be encoded as a BED-style configure file plus a complete check-hotspot.list before running nano2ngs-muta.pl on nanopore FASTQ reads.
skills.name: hotspot-bed-configuration-parsing
skills.search_text: hotspot-bed-configuration-parsing Use when preparing inputs for Nano2NGS-Muta: a hotspot panel must be encoded as a BED-style configure file plus a complete check-hotspot.list before running nano2ngs-muta.pl on nanopore FASTQ reads. If the input is an NGS short-read dataset rather than nanopore long reads — the configure/check files exist only to seed extraction from long reads. If the goal is metagenomic classification (Nano2NGS-Meta), which uses -fq/-read_len/-time and has no hotspot configure file. If mutations of interest are genome-wide rather than a hotspot panel; the method is described as particularly suitable for hotspot panel mutation detection for clinical diagnosis. Parse the hotspot BED configure file (chr, start, end, gene symbol, mutation, optional transcription ID) and the companion check-hotspot.list that Nano2NGS-Muta requires to seed short-read extraction and final hotspot mutation calling from nanopore FASTQ data. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac033
skills.summary: Parse the hotspot BED configure file (chr, start, end, gene symbol, mutation, optional transcription ID) and the companion check-hotspot.list that Nano2NGS-Muta requires to seed short-read extraction and final hotspot mutation calling from nanopore FASTQ data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the input is an NGS short-read dataset rather than nanopore long reads — the configure/check files exist only to seed extraction from long reads. If the goal is metagenomic classification (Nano2NGS-Meta), which uses -fq/-read_len/-time and has no hotspot configure file. If mutations of interest are genome-wide rather than a hotspot panel; the method is described as particularly suitable for hotspot panel mutation detection for clinical diagnosis.

skills.description: Use when you have Papillomavirus (Papillomaviridae) genomes — e.g. from the VMGC's 627 genomes in 61 vOTUs — and need L1-based type/species/genus classification plus a phylogeny of human vaginal papillomaviruses.
skills.name: hpv-type-assignment-by-l1-sequence-similarity
skills.search_text: hpv-type-assignment-by-l1-sequence-similarity Use when you have Papillomavirus (Papillomaviridae) genomes — e.g. from the VMGC's 627 genomes in 61 vOTUs — and need L1-based type/species/genus classification plus a phylogeny of human vaginal papillomaviruses. Viral genomes are not Papillomaviridae — the 90/70/60% L1 thresholds are papillomavirus-specific and invalid for phage or other DNA virus families Genomes are too fragmented to carry an intact L1 ORF, since type calling depends entirely on the L1 major capsid protein gene The goal is species-level prokaryotic typing (e.g. Kraken2/Bracken SGB profiling against VMGC prokaryotic SGBs), which uses a completely different database and read-mapping approach http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Assigns Papillomaviridae vOTUs to HPV types by predicting the L1 major capsid protein from each vaginal viral genome and applying ICTV-style pairwise nucleotide identity thresholds (>90% type, >70% species, >60% genus), then placing the VMGC L1 sequences into a RefSeq-anchored maximum-likelihood phylogeny. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Assigns Papillomaviridae vOTUs to HPV types by predicting the L1 major capsid protein from each vaginal viral genome and applying ICTV-style pairwise nucleotide identity thresholds (>90% type, >70% species, >60% genus), then placing the VMGC L1 sequences into a RefSeq-anchored maximum-likelihood phylogeny.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Viral genomes are not Papillomaviridae — the 90/70/60% L1 thresholds are papillomavirus-specific and invalid for phage or other DNA virus families Genomes are too fragmented to carry an intact L1 ORF, since type calling depends entirely on the L1 major capsid protein gene The goal is species-level prokaryotic typing (e.g. Kraken2/Bracken SGB profiling against VMGC prokaryotic SGBs), which uses a completely different database and read-mapping approach

skills.description: Use when the input consists of multiple per-sample HTSeq output count files that must be combined into one matrix of samples and corresponding gene counts before differential expression or enrichment analysis.
skills.name: htseq-count-file-parsing
skills.search_text: htseq-count-file-parsing Use when the input consists of multiple per-sample HTSeq output count files that must be combined into one matrix of samples and corresponding gene counts before differential expression or enrichment analysis. The input is already a single gene-by-sample count matrix and only needs normalization, filtering, or differential expression analysis (use NASQAR's DESeq2Shiny or downstream apps instead) The individual count files have non-matching gene columns — the GeneCountMerger README states 'If the gene columns do not match in all files, this tool will not work' The task is conversion of gene IDs to gene names rather than merging count files http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Parses per-sample HTSeq-style gene count files (two-column tables of gene identifier and raw count) and merges them into a single gene-by-sample count matrix, as implemented in NASQAR's GeneCountMerger preprocessing tool, to prepare input for downstream RNA-seq differential expression analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03577-4
skills.summary: Parses per-sample HTSeq-style gene count files (two-column tables of gene identifier and raw count) and merges them into a single gene-by-sample count matrix, as implemented in NASQAR's GeneCountMerger preprocessing tool, to prepare input for downstream RNA-seq differential expression analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a single gene-by-sample count matrix and only needs normalization, filtering, or differential expression analysis (use NASQAR's DESeq2Shiny or downstream apps instead) The individual count files have non-matching gene columns — the GeneCountMerger README states 'If the gene columns do not match in all files, this tool will not work' The task is conversion of gene IDs to gene names rather than merging count files

skills.name: human-population-genomic-variant-analysis
skills.search_text: human-population-genomic-variant-analysis Use when you have human population VCF-derived unfolded SFS / MKT count tables (e.g. 1000GP populations like CEU or YRI) and need to estimate α or compare selection regimes between a candidate gene set and the genome-wide distribution. Input data are Drosophila (DGN/PopFly FASTA) alignments rather than human 1000GP VCF-derived tables — use the D. melanogaster pipeline with Comeron et al. 2012 recombination data instead You only have raw VCFs without ancestral-state information or functional-class annotation (0-fold/4-fold), since MKT tests require unfolded SFS and divergence counts The question concerns weakly/strongly deleterious fractions without the polymorphism-divergence structure (daf + divergence tables) required by iMKT functions http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Analyzes human population genomic variation (1000GP Phase III VCF from PopHuman) together with human–chimpanzee divergence to compute McDonald–Kreitman-derived estimates of adaptation (α) and other selection regimes for user-defined gene sets, e.g. high-recombination vs whole-genome comparisons using Bhèrer et al. 2017 recombination maps. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkz372

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are Drosophila (DGN/PopFly FASTA) alignments rather than human 1000GP VCF-derived tables — use the D. melanogaster pipeline with Comeron et al. 2012 recombination data instead You only have raw VCFs without ancestral-state information or functional-class annotation (0-fold/4-fold), since MKT tests require unfolded SFS and divergence counts The question concerns weakly/strongly deleterious fractions without the polymorphism-divergence structure (daf + divergence tables) required by iMKT functions

skills.description: Use when you have paired short-read FASTQ plus matching long-read FASTQ/FASTA from the same metagenomic samples (e.g. CAMISIM-simulated mouse-gut time-series data) and want to improve assembly N50, size, and MAG recovery.
skills.name: hybrid-assembly-configuration-short-and-long-reads
skills.search_text: hybrid-assembly-configuration-short-and-long-reads Use when you have paired short-read FASTQ plus matching long-read FASTQ/FASTA from the same metagenomic samples (e.g. CAMISIM-simulated mouse-gut time-series data) and want to improve assembly N50, size, and MAG recovery. Only short reads are available and no long-read data exist for the samples — the hybrid configuration cannot be applied and short-read-only assembly should be used Reads are metatranscriptomic rather than metagenomic — the article notes this workflow does not yet cover metatranscriptomic data analysis The goal is bin refinement or functional annotation of existing assemblies — these steps are not yet included in nf-core/mag v2.1.0 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Configure nf-core/mag v2.1.0 for hybrid metagenome assembly that combines Illumina short reads with long reads (Nanopore/PacBio) to increase assembly continuity, including the read-type-specific alignment and preprocessing gating (Bowtie2 for short reads, minimap2 for long reads). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Configure nf-core/mag v2.1.0 for hybrid metagenome assembly that combines Illumina short reads with long reads (Nanopore/PacBio) to increase assembly continuity, including the read-type-specific alignment and preprocessing gating (Bowtie2 for short reads, minimap2 for long reads).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only short reads are available and no long-read data exist for the samples — the hybrid configuration cannot be applied and short-read-only assembly should be used Reads are metatranscriptomic rather than metagenomic — the article notes this workflow does not yet cover metatranscriptomic data analysis The goal is bin refinement or functional annotation of existing assemblies — these steps are not yet included in nf-core/mag v2.1.0

skills.description: Use when a task requires capturing both local sequence motifs and long-range dependencies of 16S rRNA sequences for hierarchical taxonomic prediction across domain-through-species ranks, or when reimplementing/verifying the DeepTaxa architecture.
skills.name: hybrid-cnn-bert-parallel-fusion-architecture
skills.search_text: hybrid-cnn-bert-parallel-fusion-architecture Use when a task requires capturing both local sequence motifs and long-range dependencies of 16S rRNA sequences for hierarchical taxonomic prediction across domain-through-species ranks, or when reimplementing/verifying the DeepTaxa architecture. Input is not 16S rRNA sequence data — the article notes evaluation on other marker genes (18S rRNA, shotgun metagenomics) remains untested Input requires base-level quality-score awareness — the model operates on FASTA only and does not incorporate quality scores A lightweight fast classifier is needed and long-range context is unnecessary — the README notes CNNClassifier is faster to train with only slightly lower species accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Reconstruct the DeepTaxa HybridCNNBERTClassifier: a multiscale CNN (kernels 3/5/7, 256 filters) fused via learnable scalar weights with a from-scratch 4-layer BERT encoder on the DNABERT-2 BPE vocabulary, feeding seven parallel per-rank linear heads for 16S rRNA taxonomic classification at all seven Linnean ranks. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Reconstruct the DeepTaxa HybridCNNBERTClassifier: a multiscale CNN (kernels 3/5/7, 256 filters) fused via learnable scalar weights with a from-scratch 4-layer BERT encoder on the DNABERT-2 BPE vocabulary, feeding seven parallel per-rank linear heads for 16S rRNA taxonomic classification at all seven Linnean ranks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not 16S rRNA sequence data — the article notes evaluation on other marker genes (18S rRNA, shotgun metagenomics) remains untested Input requires base-level quality-score awareness — the model operates on FASTA only and does not incorporate quality scores A lightweight fast classifier is needed and long-range context is unnecessary — the README notes CNNClassifier is faster to train with only slightly lower species accuracy

skills.description: Use when you need to attribute DeepTaxa's species-level performance to its components by training ablation variants (CNN pathway only, BERT pathway only, or DNABERT-2 BPE tokenization replaced by one-hot encodings) and comparing species F1 to the full hybrid baseline.
skills.name: hybrid-cnn-bert-variant-training
skills.search_text: hybrid-cnn-bert-variant-training Use when you need to attribute DeepTaxa's species-level performance to its components by training ablation variants (CNN pathway only, BERT pathway only, or DNABERT-2 BPE tokenization replaced by one-hot encodings) and comparing species F1 to the full hybrid baseline. The goal is benchmarking DeepTaxa against external tools (DADA2, QIIME 2, Kraken2, SINTAX) rather than attributing performance to internal architecture components The working data are in-silico V3–V4 or V4 amplicons rather than the full-length 16S split — the published ablation was run on the Greengenes2 full-length training set only Only predictions from already-published checkpoints are needed; no retraining or component-removal experiment is required http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Trains DeepTaxa architecture ablation variants (CNN-only, BERT-only, one-hot CNN) under the compact hyperparameter configuration on the Greengenes2 2024.09 full-length 16S training set, then compares their species-level F1 on the shared 69,335-sequence held-out test set against the full HybridCNNBERT model to quantify each component's contribution. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Trains DeepTaxa architecture ablation variants (CNN-only, BERT-only, one-hot CNN) under the compact hyperparameter configuration on the Greengenes2 2024.09 full-length 16S training set, then compares their species-level F1 on the shared 69,335-sequence held-out test set against the full HybridCNNBERT model to quantify each component's contribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is benchmarking DeepTaxa against external tools (DADA2, QIIME 2, Kraken2, SINTAX) rather than attributing performance to internal architecture components The working data are in-silico V3–V4 or V4 amplicons rather than the full-length 16S split — the published ablation was run on the Greengenes2 full-length training set only Only predictions from already-published checkpoints are needed; no retraining or component-removal experiment is required

skills.description: Use when you have Illumina paired-end metagenomic reads plus at least one long-range library (ONT or PacBio long reads, mate pairs, or 10x linked reads) and need de novo scaffolds with high contiguity and few interspecies misassemblies.
skills.name: hybrid-metagenome-assembly-execution
skills.search_text: hybrid-metagenome-assembly-execution Use when you have Illumina paired-end metagenomic reads plus at least one long-range library (ONT or PacBio long reads, mate pairs, or 10x linked reads) and need de novo scaffolds with high contiguity and few interspecies misassemblies. Only short-read data is available — MetaPlatanus requires at least one short-read paired-end library and is designed to exploit long-range links; a short-read-only assembler such as MEGAHIT is more appropriate Reference-guided assembly is desired — the study focuses on de novo methods and reference information has not been well examined Only HiFi long reads are available and short-read sequencing is not planned — this hybrid pipeline is built around accurate short-read contigs plus error-prone long-range links http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Run MetaPlatanus, a hybrid metagenome assembler that combines accurate short-read contig assembly (MEGAHIT) with long-range links (ONT/PacBio long reads or mate pairs), species-specific coverage/k-mer features and binning (MetaBAT2), followed by TGS-GapCloser gap closing and NextPolish polishing, to produce low-misassembly, high-contiguity metagenomic scaffolds. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Run MetaPlatanus, a hybrid metagenome assembler that combines accurate short-read contig assembly (MEGAHIT) with long-range links (ONT/PacBio long reads or mate pairs), species-specific coverage/k-mer features and binning (MetaBAT2), followed by TGS-GapCloser gap closing and NextPolish polishing, to produce low-misassembly, high-contiguity metagenomic scaffolds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only short-read data is available — MetaPlatanus requires at least one short-read paired-end library and is designed to exploit long-range links; a short-read-only assembler such as MEGAHIT is more appropriate Reference-guided assembly is desired — the study focuses on de novo methods and reference information has not been well examined Only HiFi long reads are available and short-read sequencing is not planned — this hybrid pipeline is built around accurate short-read contigs plus error-prone long-range links

skills.name: hybrid-neural-network-extra-trees-probability-classification
skills.search_text: hybrid-neural-network-extra-trees-probability-classification Use when classifying pairs of viral scaffolds/fragments as same or different genome origin from sequence-feature distances (k-mer/tetranucleotide frequencies, GC content), or when retraining/loading vRhyme's .sav ML models. Input is an entire metagenome rather than predicted viral scaffolds — vRhyme is built to run on viral sequences/scaffolds and performance on whole metagenomes has not been fully evaluated The goal is binning non-viral (microbial) genomes — an anticipated limitation of vRhyme, and MetaBat2 outperformed vRhyme on non-viral synthetic data Only one input sample is available and coverage variance cannot be leveraged, or you need unsupervised clustering (e.g. VAMB variational autoencoders or CONCOCT Gaussian mixture models) instead of supervised pair classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reproduces and applies vRhyme's hybrid supervised classification scheme, in which scikit-learn MLPClassifier (neural network) and ExtraTreesClassifier models are trained on 69,632 same/different scaffold pairs built from 39,105 fragmented viral genomes, and their probability outputs are combined to classify scaffold pairs as 'same' or 'different' genome origin. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Reproduces and applies vRhyme's hybrid supervised classification scheme, in which scikit-learn MLPClassifier (neural network) and ExtraTreesClassifier models are trained on 69,632 same/different scaffold pairs built from 39,105 fragmented viral genomes, and their probability outputs are combined to classify scaffold pairs as 'same' or 'different' genome origin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an entire metagenome rather than predicted viral scaffolds — vRhyme is built to run on viral sequences/scaffolds and performance on whole metagenomes has not been fully evaluated The goal is binning non-viral (microbial) genomes — an anticipated limitation of vRhyme, and MetaBat2 outperformed vRhyme on non-viral synthetic data Only one input sample is available and coverage variance cannot be leveraged, or you need unsupervised clustering (e.g. VAMB variational autoencoders or CONCOCT Gaussian mixture models) instead of supervised pair classification

skills.description: Use when you have annotated genomes (e.g., PROKKA GFFs) and NCBI taxon-ids for a diverse pathogen group and need a bounded, tiled bait set that captures known plus up-to-20%-divergent related sequences.
skills.name: hybridization-probe-design
skills.search_text: hybridization-probe-design Use when you have annotated genomes (e.g., PROKKA GFFs) and NCBI taxon-ids for a diverse pathogen group and need a bounded, tiled bait set that captures known plus up-to-20%-divergent related sequences. Targets have unknown or unannotatable genomes — HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes and can only target close relatives The goal is detection of a single known locus via PCR/amplicon methods rather than hybridization-capture of diverse whole genomes The input is raw sequencing reads or an unannotated metagenome assembly rather than annotated genomes with taxon-ids http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Design compact hybridization-capture probe sets (e.g., 75-mers) that simultaneously and specifically enrich diverse, divergent microbial targets over host/environmental background, using HUBDesign's hierarchical clustering, pseudo-genome construction, and balanced bait selection. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: Design compact hybridization-capture probe sets (e.g., 75-mers) that simultaneously and specifically enrich diverse, divergent microbial targets over host/environmental background, using HUBDesign's hierarchical clustering, pseudo-genome construction, and balanced bait selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Targets have unknown or unannotatable genomes — HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes and can only target close relatives The goal is detection of a single known locus via PCR/amplicon methods rather than hybridization-capture of diverse whole genomes The input is raw sequencing reads or an unannotated metagenome assembly rather than annotated genomes with taxon-ids

skills.description: Use when two independent strain-similarity metrics (e.g. APSS from SynTracker and popANI from inStrain) have been computed on the same sample pairs and you must identify species whose within-species diversity arises preferentially from point mutations versus structural differences.
skills.name: hypergeometric-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: hypergeometric-enrichment-testing Use when two independent strain-similarity metrics (e.g. APSS from SynTracker and popANI from inStrain) have been computed on the same sample pairs and you must identify species whose within-species diversity arises preferentially from point mutations versus structural differences. When the two tools' comparison sets do not overlap substantially (fewer than the ~12,000 shared comparisons), since enrichment is defined only against the shared background When strain similarity is measured by a single metric only — the hypermutator vs hyper-recombinant contrast requires both a synteny-based (APSS) and an SNP-based (popANI) top-5% set When comparing isolates rather than metagenomic sample pairs, where the comparison background and 5% selection logic do not apply as designed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A statistical classification step in which, for each microbial species, a hypergeometric test (e.g. scipy.stats.hypergeom) asks whether pairwise strain comparisons that are most similar by SynTracker (synteny-based APSS) or by inStrain (popANI) are over-represented in the shared comparison background, distinguishing hypermutator from hyper-recombinant species. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: A statistical classification step in which, for each microbial species, a hypergeometric test (e.g. scipy.stats.hypergeom) asks whether pairwise strain comparisons that are most similar by SynTracker (synteny-based APSS) or by inStrain (popANI) are over-represented in the shared comparison background, distinguishing hypermutator from hyper-recombinant species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the two tools' comparison sets do not overlap substantially (fewer than the ~12,000 shared comparisons), since enrichment is defined only against the shared background When strain similarity is measured by a single metric only — the hypermutator vs hyper-recombinant contrast requires both a synteny-based (APSS) and an SNP-based (popANI) top-5% set When comparing isolates rather than metagenomic sample pairs, where the comparison background and 5% selection logic do not apply as designed

skills.description: Use when a model such as ILMF-VH has multiple tunable parameters (k, alpha, beta, lambda, gamma, K) and you must sweep each while fixing the others, scoring every setting by mean AUPR under five-fold cross-validation.
skills.name: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis Use when a model such as ILMF-VH has multiple tunable parameters (k, alpha, beta, lambda, gamma, K) and you must sweep each while fixing the others, scoring every setting by mean AUPR under five-fold cross-validation. The goal is comparing ILMF-VH against the five baseline network-based methods (KBMF, NetLapRLS, BLM-NII, CMF) with fixed settings rather than tuning parameters No ground-truth virus-host association matrix is available, so five-fold cross-validated AUPR cannot be computed The input is a parameter-tuning request for a model without neighborhood regularization or SNF components, where alpha, beta, and K are undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Sweeps the tunable parameters of a predictive model (here, ILMF-VH's matrix factorization factor k, neighborhood regularization alpha/beta, Gaussian kernel lambda, learning rate gamma, and SNF neighbor K) and records mean AUPR under five-fold cross-validation to identify optima and produce sensitivity trend panels. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Sweeps the tunable parameters of a predictive model (here, ILMF-VH's matrix factorization factor k, neighborhood regularization alpha/beta, Gaussian kernel lambda, learning rate gamma, and SNF neighbor K) and records mean AUPR under five-fold cross-validation to identify optima and produce sensitivity trend panels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is comparing ILMF-VH against the five baseline network-based methods (KBMF, NetLapRLS, BLM-NII, CMF) with fixed settings rather than tuning parameters No ground-truth virus-host association matrix is available, so five-fold cross-validated AUPR cannot be computed The input is a parameter-tuning request for a model without neighborhood regularization or SNF components, where alpha, beta, and K are undefined

skills.description: Use when reanalyzing gut metagenomes (e.g. 106 iHMP / PRJNA398089 samples) from IBD cohorts (CD, UC, healthy) to find differentially abundant uncultured metagenomic species as disease biomarkers.
skills.name: ibd-microbiome-biomarker-interpretation
skills.search_text: ibd-microbiome-biomarker-interpretation Use when reanalyzing gut metagenomes (e.g. 106 iHMP / PRJNA398089 samples) from IBD cohorts (CD, UC, healthy) to find differentially abundant uncultured metagenomic species as disease biomarkers. When the target species are already in curated reference databases, where alignment/k-mer tools (e.g. Kraken) suffice and building a custom database is practical When reads have strongly different lengths or error profiles from short reads (e.g. long-read sequencing), since the pretrained model would require retraining When the goal is genus-level signatures only with established cultured taxa, rather than novel uncultured MGS associations http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Discover IBD-associated uncultured metagenomic species (UMGS/MGS) by classifying gut metagenome reads with DeepMicrobes' pretrained LSTM species model and identifying differentially abundant biomarkers with Kruskal-Wallis + LDA (LEfSe-style) analysis in R. Enables investigation of novel uncultured organisms from genome reconstruction that classical reference-database classifiers miss. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Discover IBD-associated uncultured metagenomic species (UMGS/MGS) by classifying gut metagenome reads with DeepMicrobes' pretrained LSTM species model and identifying differentially abundant biomarkers with Kruskal-Wallis + LDA (LEfSe-style) analysis in R. Enables investigation of novel uncultured organisms from genome reconstruction that classical reference-database classifiers miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target species are already in curated reference databases, where alignment/k-mer tools (e.g. Kraken) suffice and building a custom database is practical When reads have strongly different lengths or error profiles from short reads (e.g. long-read sequencing), since the pretrained model would require retraining When the goal is genus-level signatures only with established cultured taxa, rather than novel uncultured MGS associations

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end or single-end Illumina FASTQ reads (fastq/fastq.gz) enter a metagenomic pipeline and must be stripped of Illumina adapters and low-quality bases before SSU rRNA filtering or assembly.
skills.name: illumina-adapter-trimming-bbduk
skills.search_text: illumina-adapter-trimming-bbduk Use when raw paired-end or single-end Illumina FASTQ reads (fastq/fastq.gz) enter a metagenomic pipeline and must be stripped of Illumina adapters and low-quality bases before SSU rRNA filtering or assembly. Input reads are long-read (PacBio/ONT) data — the workflow and parameters target short Illumina shotgun reads Reads are already adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered (e.g. input is the trimmed 16S/18S output of a prior bbduk step) The goal is SSU read extraction or taxonomic classification rather than quality control — use SortMeRNA or the QIIME2 sklearn classifier instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Adapter removal and quality trimming of raw Illumina (meta)genomic reads with bbduk.sh from BBTools, as implemented in the RiboTaxa quality-control stage prior to SSU rRNA read extraction and reconstruction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Adapter removal and quality trimming of raw Illumina (meta)genomic reads with bbduk.sh from BBTools, as implemented in the RiboTaxa quality-control stage prior to SSU rRNA read extraction and reconstruction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are long-read (PacBio/ONT) data — the workflow and parameters target short Illumina shotgun reads Reads are already adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered (e.g. input is the trimmed 16S/18S output of a prior bbduk step) The goal is SSU read extraction or taxonomic classification rather than quality control — use SortMeRNA or the QIIME2 sklearn classifier instead

skills.description: Use when you need to characterize which reads PANDAseq's error corrections come from — e.g. testing whether uncertain corrections concentrate in reads with many low-quality (CASAVA-masked) bases rather than high-quality positions.
skills.name: illumina-phred-quality-decoding
skills.search_text: illumina-phred-quality-decoding Use when you need to characterize which reads PANDAseq's error corrections come from — e.g. testing whether uncertain corrections concentrate in reads with many low-quality (CASAVA-masked) bases rather than high-quality positions. Input is already an assembled feature table or count matrix with no per-base quality strings — quality decoding cannot be performed Reads were not produced by Illumina/CASAVA processing with the end-of-read lowest-quality mask convention, so the masking annotation rule does not apply The goal is assembly itself (overlap detection and sequence reconstruction), not post-hoc characterization of where corrections occur http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Decodes Illumina CASAVA PHRED quality characters of conflicting forward/reverse bases at corrected overlap positions into error probabilities (10^(-A/10)), then classifies each mismatched base pair by whether it was quality-masked in neither, one, or both reads. Used to test PANDAseq's claim that uncertain error corrections come from reads with many low-quality bases identified by upstream processing. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Decodes Illumina CASAVA PHRED quality characters of conflicting forward/reverse bases at corrected overlap positions into error probabilities (10^(-A/10)), then classifies each mismatched base pair by whether it was quality-masked in neither, one, or both reads. Used to test PANDAseq's claim that uncertain error corrections come from reads with many low-quality bases identified by upstream processing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an assembled feature table or count matrix with no per-base quality strings — quality decoding cannot be performed Reads were not produced by Illumina/CASAVA processing with the end-of-read lowest-quality mask convention, so the masking annotation rule does not apply The goal is assembly itself (overlap detection and sequence reconstruction), not post-hoc characterization of where corrections occur

skills.description: Decision support for setting PANDAseq assembly quality-score thresholds when recovering more overlapping Illumina paired-end reads matters more than maximum stringency, e.g. 16S rRNA amplicon libraries with many low-quality tail bases.
skills.name: illumina-quality-probability-scoring
skills.search_text: illumina-quality-probability-scoring Decision support for setting PANDAseq assembly quality-score thresholds when recovering more overlapping Illumina paired-end reads matters more than maximum stringency, e.g. 16S rRNA amplicon libraries with many low-quality tail bases. Read pairs have no sufficient overlap — PANDAseq discards these pairs regardless of threshold, so the skill cannot recover them Sequences contain uncalled bases that must be excluded outright when the downstream pipeline forbids N calls Assembly of non-overlapping paired-end reads (e.g. fragment libraries without overlap) where quality-probability scoring in the overlap region is not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Uses Illumina per-base quality scores within the paired-end overlap to compute the probability that true nucleotides match, so mismatches and uncalled bases are corrected probabilistically instead of discarding read pairs. Lowering the assembly quality-score threshold (e.g. 0.9 to 0.6) trades stringency for higher sequence recovery. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Uses Illumina per-base quality scores within the paired-end overlap to compute the probability that true nucleotides match, so mismatches and uncalled bases are corrected probabilistically instead of discarding read pairs. Lowering the assembly quality-score threshold (e.g. 0.9 to 0.6) trades stringency for higher sequence recovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Read pairs have no sufficient overlap — PANDAseq discards these pairs regardless of threshold, so the skill cannot recover them Sequences contain uncalled bases that must be excluded outright when the downstream pipeline forbids N calls Assembly of non-overlapping paired-end reads (e.g. fragment libraries without overlap) where quality-probability scoring in the overlap region is not applicable

skills.description: Use when benchmarking ANI/strain-comparison methods on metagenomic data and you need synthetic read sets with known ground-truth ANI values derived from genomes mutated at controlled rates.
skills.name: illumina-read-simulation-from-mutated-genomes
skills.search_text: illumina-read-simulation-from-mutated-genomes Use when benchmarking ANI/strain-comparison methods on metagenomic data and you need synthetic read sets with known ground-truth ANI values derived from genomes mutated at controlled rates. You need to compare real biological samples rather than validate method accuracy on simulated ground truth — use inStrain profile/compare directly on real metagenomic .bam files instead Your input is already a set of unmapped real reads with no known reference ANI; there is no ground truth to benchmark against You need long-read or non-Illumina read simulation — pIRS simulates Illumina reads only http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark strain-comparison accuracy by introducing a known number of mutations into a reference genome (E. coli strain SQ88, RefSeq GCF_000988385.1) with SNP Mutator, simulating 20x Illumina reads with pIRS, and mapping them back with Bowtie2 so that calculated popANI can be compared against true ANI. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Benchmark strain-comparison accuracy by introducing a known number of mutations into a reference genome (E. coli strain SQ88, RefSeq GCF_000988385.1) with SNP Mutator, simulating 20x Illumina reads with pIRS, and mapping them back with Bowtie2 so that calculated popANI can be compared against true ANI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to compare real biological samples rather than validate method accuracy on simulated ground truth — use inStrain profile/compare directly on real metagenomic .bam files instead Your input is already a set of unmapped real reads with no known reference ANI; there is no ground truth to benchmark against You need long-read or non-Illumina read simulation — pIRS simulates Illumina reads only

skills.description: Use when deep-sequencing reads (BAM/CRAM aligned to a reference such as HIV-1 subtype B pol) from a genetically heterogeneous mixed sample must be error-corrected and rare variants down to 0.1% frequency quantified.
skills.name: illumina-short-read-error-correction
skills.search_text: illumina-short-read-error-correction Use when deep-sequencing reads (BAM/CRAM aligned to a reference such as HIV-1 subtype B pol) from a genetically heterogeneous mixed sample must be error-corrected and rare variants down to 0.1% frequency quantified. When global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction is required: current ShoRAH2 has global mode disabled; use the v1.1.3 tarball with global mode or V-pipe's global haplotype options instead. When the sample is homogeneous or low-frequency variants are not of interest — the error-correction/clustering machinery targets heterogeneous mixed samples, not consensus-only analyses. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Correct Illumina short-read sequencing errors and reconstruct local haplotypes by clustering reads that overlap the same genomic window via Gibbs sampling with a Dirichlet process mixture (ShoRAH's diri_sampler), then estimate haplotype frequencies from cluster read counts. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: Correct Illumina short-read sequencing errors and reconstruct local haplotypes by clustering reads that overlap the same genomic window via Gibbs sampling with a Dirichlet process mixture (ShoRAH's diri_sampler), then estimate haplotype frequencies from cluster read counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction is required: current ShoRAH2 has global mode disabled; use the v1.1.3 tarball with global mode or V-pipe's global haplotype options instead. When the sample is homogeneous or low-frequency variants are not of interest — the error-correction/clustering machinery targets heterogeneous mixed samples, not consensus-only analyses.

skills.description: Use when you need a known-composition paired-end Illumina FASTQ set from reference bacterial assemblies to quantify what fraction of true bacterial reads a decontamination tool retains or incorrectly removes.
skills.name: illumina-short-read-simulation
skills.search_text: illumina-short-read-simulation Use when you need a known-composition paired-end Illumina FASTQ set from reference bacterial assemblies to quantify what fraction of true bacterial reads a decontamination tool retains or incorrectly removes. Input is real metagenomic or clinical data with unknown composition — simulation is for ground-truth benchmarking, not production decontamination You need long-read (ONT) benchmarks — this skill covers paired short reads; use PBSIM2-based ONT simulation instead The goal is to measure human read removal efficiency — use real human reads (e.g. 1000 Genomes Project samples) rather than simulated bacterial reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Simulate paired Illumina short reads from complete bacterial genome assemblies (e.g. 985 FDA-ARGOS or 140 mycobacterial genomes) using DWGSIM to create a ground-truth read set for benchmarking host-decontamination tools such as Hostile and HRRT. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad728
skills.summary: Simulate paired Illumina short reads from complete bacterial genome assemblies (e.g. 985 FDA-ARGOS or 140 mycobacterial genomes) using DWGSIM to create a ground-truth read set for benchmarking host-decontamination tools such as Hostile and HRRT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real metagenomic or clinical data with unknown composition — simulation is for ground-truth benchmarking, not production decontamination You need long-read (ONT) benchmarks — this skill covers paired short reads; use PBSIM2-based ONT simulation instead The goal is to measure human read removal efficiency — use real human reads (e.g. 1000 Genomes Project samples) rather than simulated bacterial reads

skills.description: Use when reproducing the simulated metagenomic reads benchmark comparing iDeLUCS, DeLUCS, and k-means++ clustering accuracy on unbalanced multi-genome DNA read datasets.
skills.name: imbalanced-metagenomic-cluster-benchmarking
skills.search_text: imbalanced-metagenomic-cluster-benchmarking Use when reproducing the simulated metagenomic reads benchmark comparing iDeLUCS, DeLUCS, and k-means++ clustering accuracy on unbalanced multi-genome DNA read datasets. Datasets with perfectly balanced clusters, where the iDeLUCS advantage from contrastive loss on unbalanced clusters is not exercised Tasks requiring supervised classification — ground-truth labels in the GT file must never be used during training, only for posthoc accuracy alignment Datasets needing more than 199 clusters, since n_clusters is limited to the range 0, 2-199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark iDeLUCS against DeLUCS and k-means++ on simulated long metagenomic reads (432,333 PacBio reads from 8 microbial genomes) to quantify its advantage on unbalanced clusters, attributed to its clustering ensemble and contrastive loss. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad508
skills.summary: Benchmark iDeLUCS against DeLUCS and k-means++ on simulated long metagenomic reads (432,333 PacBio reads from 8 microbial genomes) to quantify its advantage on unbalanced clusters, attributed to its clustering ensemble and contrastive loss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with perfectly balanced clusters, where the iDeLUCS advantage from contrastive loss on unbalanced clusters is not exercised Tasks requiring supervised classification — ground-truth labels in the GT file must never be used during training, only for posthoc accuracy alignment Datasets needing more than 199 clusters, since n_clusters is limited to the range 0, 2-199

skills.description: Use when you need to benchmark a strain-tracking or genome-comparison tool's sensitivity to specific mutation types (SNPs vs indels) by simulating controlled in silico evolution and comparing pairwise score distributions across mutation regimes.
skills.name: in-silico-genome-evolution-simulation
skills.search_text: in-silico-genome-evolution-simulation Use when you need to benchmark a strain-tracking or genome-comparison tool's sensitivity to specific mutation types (SNPs vs indels) by simulating controlled in silico evolution and comparing pairwise score distributions across mutation regimes. When the goal is to compare real clinical/environmental strains rather than to benchmark tool sensitivity against known ground-truth mutation regimes — simulation-based APSS values do not transfer directly to biological interpretation. When the tool under evaluation is specifically designed to quantify SNP differences and structural changes are out of scope, since SynTracker's differentiating feature is its low SNP sensitivity and high indel sensitivity. When sequencing data are raw reads rather than assemblies or genomes, as SynTracker requires per-sample assemblies or assembled genomes as targets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Simulate bacterial genome evolution under controlled mutation regimes (SNP-only vs indel-only) using Bacmeta to benchmark the sensitivity of strain-comparison tools such as SynTracker, and quantify regime differences with Welch's t-tests on Average Pairwise Synteny Scores (APSS). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Simulate bacterial genome evolution under controlled mutation regimes (SNP-only vs indel-only) using Bacmeta to benchmark the sensitivity of strain-comparison tools such as SynTracker, and quantify regime differences with Welch's t-tests on Average Pairwise Synteny Scores (APSS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to compare real clinical/environmental strains rather than to benchmark tool sensitivity against known ground-truth mutation regimes — simulation-based APSS values do not transfer directly to biological interpretation. When the tool under evaluation is specifically designed to quantify SNP differences and structural changes are out of scope, since SynTracker's differentiating feature is its low SNP sensitivity and high indel sensitivity. When sequencing data are raw reads rather than assemblies or genomes, as SynTracker requires per-sample assemblies or assembled genomes as targets.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking strain-variant discovery (e.g. MetaQuad) and you need simulated shotgun metagenomic samples with known strain composition, planted substitutions, and controlled mean depths instead of real clinical reads.
skills.name: in-silico-mutagenesis-strain-generation
skills.search_text: in-silico-mutagenesis-strain-generation Use when benchmarking strain-variant discovery (e.g. MetaQuad) and you need simulated shotgun metagenomic samples with known strain composition, planted substitutions, and controlled mean depths instead of real clinical reads. Input is real clinical shotgun metagenomic data (e.g. the H. pylori post-eradication-therapy samples in this study) — skip simulation and go straight to bwa/bowtie2 alignment, cellsnp-lite pileup, and metaquad The goal is single-cell mitochondrial variant discovery (MQuad's original scope), not strain mixtures in shotgun metagenomic data No ground-truth strain composition is needed, so simulated data would add no evaluation value over real reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Builds simulated shotgun metagenomic benchmark data by mutating reference Fusobacterium genomes into strain variants with BBMap mutate.sh, then simulating 151 bp NovaSeq paired-end reads with InSilicoSeq across 100 samples at prescribed mean depths (3x-35.5x) to evaluate MetaQuad's shared-variant discovery. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Builds simulated shotgun metagenomic benchmark data by mutating reference Fusobacterium genomes into strain variants with BBMap mutate.sh, then simulating 151 bp NovaSeq paired-end reads with InSilicoSeq across 100 samples at prescribed mean depths (3x-35.5x) to evaluate MetaQuad's shared-variant discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real clinical shotgun metagenomic data (e.g. the H. pylori post-eradication-therapy samples in this study) — skip simulation and go straight to bwa/bowtie2 alignment, cellsnp-lite pileup, and metaquad The goal is single-cell mitochondrial variant discovery (MQuad's original scope), not strain mixtures in shotgun metagenomic data No ground-truth strain composition is needed, so simulated data would add no evaluation value over real reads

skills.description: Use when a set of primer pairs (designed or published) must be scored for detection of a curated reference gene set — e.g., computing what fraction of 720 amoA-AOB target genes are amplified in silico, or comparing coverage between two primer sets.
skills.name: in-silico-pcr-primer-matching
skills.search_text: in-silico-pcr-primer-matching Use when a set of primer pairs (designed or published) must be scored for detection of a curated reference gene set — e.g., computing what fraction of 720 amoA-AOB target genes are amplified in silico, or comparing coverage between two primer sets. When experimental wet-lab qPCR validation is required — the article notes computational in silico results still require further experimental validation When the input is not a matched primer/reference-gene pair problem (e.g., you already have an amplification/feature table rather than sequences) When reference gene diversity is so high that MetaFunPrimer would design numerous primer pairs exceeding qPCR platform run capacity http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates designed or published primer sets computationally by expanding degenerate primers to all nondegenerate forms and scoring amplification against reference gene sequences, using MetaFunPrimer's criterion that both forward and reverse primers must 100% match a sequence. This is how the paper quantified 94% (676/720) coverage for 78 designed amoA-AOB primer pairs versus 49% (356/720) for previously published primers. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00201-21
skills.summary: Evaluates designed or published primer sets computationally by expanding degenerate primers to all nondegenerate forms and scoring amplification against reference gene sequences, using MetaFunPrimer's criterion that both forward and reverse primers must 100% match a sequence. This is how the paper quantified 94% (676/720) coverage for 78 designed amoA-AOB primer pairs versus 49% (356/720) for previously published primers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When experimental wet-lab qPCR validation is required — the article notes computational in silico results still require further experimental validation When the input is not a matched primer/reference-gene pair problem (e.g., you already have an amplification/feature table rather than sequences) When reference gene diversity is so high that MetaFunPrimer would design numerous primer pairs exceeding qPCR platform run capacity

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how reliably an AMP-based predictor (Mykrobe) detects a low-frequency contaminant or resistant subpopulation in NGS reads, e.g. down to 0.5–2% minor-population frequency.
skills.name: in-silico-read-mixture-simulation
skills.search_text: in-silico-read-mixture-simulation Use when you need to quantify how reliably an AMP-based predictor (Mykrobe) detects a low-frequency contaminant or resistant subpopulation in NGS reads, e.g. down to 0.5–2% minor-population frequency. When you need to model within-sample mixtures of M. tuberculosis directly from sputum — the article notes the current implementation models only major/minor clones and a more general mixture model would be needed. When the goal is phenotypic resistance assessment rather than read-level detection of genetic determinants — simulated mixtures only calibrate genotypic detection power. When your samples lack sufficient depth: simulations were built from samples with at least 100 × mean sequencing depth, and power estimates will not transfer to low-coverage data. Pools FASTQ reads from real sequencing runs to construct simulated mixed infections, then runs Mykrobe predictor on each mixture to measure the detection power of the tool for minor-population species and resistance determinants at defined frequencies. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Pools FASTQ reads from real sequencing runs to construct simulated mixed infections, then runs Mykrobe predictor on each mixture to measure the detection power of the tool for minor-population species and resistance determinants at defined frequencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need to model within-sample mixtures of M. tuberculosis directly from sputum — the article notes the current implementation models only major/minor clones and a more general mixture model would be needed. When the goal is phenotypic resistance assessment rather than read-level detection of genetic determinants — simulated mixtures only calibrate genotypic detection power. When your samples lack sufficient depth: simulations were built from samples with at least 100 × mean sequencing depth, and power estimates will not transfer to low-coverage data.

skills.name: in-silico-read-simulation
skills.search_text: in-silico-read-simulation Use when benchmarking a metagenomic assembler or contig extender and a ground-truth-controlled read set is needed spanning known read lengths, error rates, coverage depths, and uneven coverage profiles. The goal is to benchmark on real metagenomic samples — this skill yields synthetic data with known ground truth, not biological complexity of clinical/animal metagenomes. The analysis target is host genome assembly or eukaryotic reference genomes — the article's simulation scope is viral reference genomes only. Reads have already been sequenced; simulation is only needed when controlled ground-truth read sets must be generated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Generate synthetic FASTQ read sets from viral reference genomes (BASV, BKV, HIV-1) with pIRS and custom simulations across read lengths (100 bp/250 bp), error rates (1%/5%), coverage depths (10x/20x/50x), and 1 kb spike-in coverage peaks to benchmark contig extension under controlled conditions. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04038-2
skills.summary: Generate synthetic FASTQ read sets from viral reference genomes (BASV, BKV, HIV-1) with pIRS and custom simulations across read lengths (100 bp/250 bp), error rates (1%/5%), coverage depths (10x/20x/50x), and 1 kb spike-in coverage peaks to benchmark contig extension under controlled conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to benchmark on real metagenomic samples — this skill yields synthetic data with known ground truth, not biological complexity of clinical/animal metagenomes. skills.description: Use when predicting protein-coding genes in error-prone sequencing reads (especially 454 reads with homopolymer-run indel artifacts and per-base quality values) where indel errors shift the reading frame and truncate ORFs.
skills.name: indel-error-modeling-in-gene-prediction
skills.search_text: indel-error-modeling-in-gene-prediction Use when predicting protein-coding genes in error-prone sequencing reads (especially 454 reads with homopolymer-run indel artifacts and per-base quality values) where indel errors shift the reading frame and truncate ORFs. Input reads are high-accuracy Illumina reads where the dominant error mode is substitution, not indel — use Glimmer-MG's stop-codon substitution mode instead of indel branching Assembled contigs or complete genomes where few indel errors remain; the plain Glimmer framework already identifies >99% of genes in complete prokaryotic genomes The goal is only classifier training or clustering (Phymm/Scimm) with no gene prediction step http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A Glimmer-MG technique that predicts insertion and deletion sequencing errors in raw metagenomic reads by branching each ORF into alternate reading frames at low-quality base calls (e.g. 454 homopolymer runs), so gene predictions track the true coding frame despite indel errors. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: A Glimmer-MG technique that predicts insertion and deletion sequencing errors in raw metagenomic reads by branching each ORF into alternate reading frames at low-quality base calls (e.g. 454 homopolymer runs), so gene predictions track the true coding frame despite indel errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are high-accuracy Illumina reads where the dominant error mode is substitution, not indel — use Glimmer-MG's stop-codon substitution mode instead of indel branching Assembled contigs or complete genomes where few indel errors remain; the plain Glimmer framework already identifies >99% of genes in complete prokaryotic genomes The goal is only classifier training or clustering (Phymm/Scimm) with no gene prediction step

skills.description: Use when a vOTU count table from a longitudinal infant virome (e.g., Liang et al. VLP metagenomes sampled at 0-4 days, 1 month, and 4 months) must be compared across sampling-time groups to test whether virome diversity increases with age.
skills.name: infant-virome-temporal-comparison
skills.search_text: infant-virome-temporal-comparison Use when a vOTU count table from a longitudinal infant virome (e.g., Liang et al. VLP metagenomes sampled at 0-4 days, 1 month, and 4 months) must be compared across sampling-time groups to test whether virome diversity increases with age. The input is raw sequencing reads rather than a vOTU count table — first run the MetaPhage reads-to-report pipeline (QC, assembly, phage detection, classification, quantification) before diversity computation. The dataset is not longitudinal/age-stratified (no sampling-month metadata), so the month-0-vs-month-1-vs-month-4 comparison cannot be defined. skills.summary: Reproduces the age-stratified alpha-diversity pattern (richness and diversity of vOTUs) in the Liang et al. infant gut VLP virome dataset by computing observed richness, Shannon, Simpson, and Fisher's alpha per sample with vegan-style diversity functions and comparing month 0, month 1, and month 4 groups, mirroring the MetaPhage alpha-diversity report (Fig. 4B).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw sequencing reads rather than a vOTU count table — first run the MetaPhage reads-to-report pipeline (QC, assembly, phage detection, classification, quantification) before diversity computation. The goal is phage detection or classification itself rather than downstream diversity comparison of already-quantified vOTUs.

skills.description: Use when paired-end metagenomic FASTQ from influenza-positive respiratory samples must be assembled into contiguous genome segments and per-sample segment counts compared against the VirMAP reference results.
skills.name: influenza-segment-reconstruction-from-metagenomic-reads
skills.search_text: influenza-segment-reconstruction-from-metagenomic-reads Use when paired-end metagenomic FASTQ from influenza-positive respiratory samples must be assembled into contiguous genome segments and per-sample segment counts compared against the VirMAP reference results. The input is not raw paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g., already-assembled contigs or a taxonomic abundance table) — VirMAP's hybrid assembly pipeline expects FASTQ input. The host organism/pathogen is not viral or lacks reference representation in the Genbank viral (gbvrl) and phage (gbphg) divisions used to build the database. Available RAM is below 64 GB per instance, since the prebuilt Genbank-derived VirMAP database cannot be loaded and minimum requirements expand as Genbank grows. http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reconstruct influenza genome segments from clinical respiratory metagenomes using VirMAP's hybrid mapping/de-novo assembly, reproducing the reported 9.05 average segments per influenza-positive sample (BioProject PRJEB7888) with one contig per reconstructed segment. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Reconstruct influenza genome segments from clinical respiratory metagenomes using VirMAP's hybrid mapping/de-novo assembly, reproducing the reported 9.05 average segments per influenza-positive sample (BioProject PRJEB7888) with one contig per reconstructed segment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not raw paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g., already-assembled contigs or a taxonomic abundance table) — VirMAP's hybrid assembly pipeline expects FASTQ input. The host organism/pathogen is not viral or lacks reference representation in the Genbank viral (gbvrl) and phage (gbphg) divisions used to build the database. Available RAM is below 64 GB per instance, since the prebuilt Genbank-derived VirMAP database cannot be loaded and minimum requirements expand as Genbank grows.

skills.description: Use when you must quantify, with an empirical P-value, how well a tree built from your own distance data (e.g., UPGMA trees from APSS-based synteny distances at a given subsampling depth n) agrees with an independently published reference tree over the same taxa.
skills.name: information-based-robinson-foulds-tree-comparison
skills.search_text: information-based-robinson-foulds-tree-comparison Use when you must quantify, with an empirical P-value, how well a tree built from your own distance data (e.g., UPGMA trees from APSS-based synteny distances at a given subsampling depth n) agrees with an independently published reference tree over the same taxa. The candidate and reference trees do not share a common set of taxa and cannot be pruned to identical external nodes — the Information-based generalized RFD comparison requires matching leaf sets. The goal is to compare continuous genetic distances (e.g., Mash distances or APSS values) rather than tree topologies — the article itself recommends considering continuous genomic difference measures instead of same/different classifications. Pairs have fewer than n regions available (pairs with fewer than n regions are excluded from downstream analysis, so no synteny-based tree can be built at that depth). http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Statistically tests whether a tree reconstructed from pairwise synteny distances (|APSS − 1|, UPGMA via phangorn) recapitulates a reference phylogeny (e.g., a pruned Mash-based phylogroup tree) by computing Information-based generalized Robinson-Foulds distances with the TreeDist R package and assigning empirical P-values by label shuffling (100,000 iterations). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Statistically tests whether a tree reconstructed from pairwise synteny distances (|APSS − 1|, UPGMA via phangorn) recapitulates a reference phylogeny (e.g., a pruned Mash-based phylogroup tree) by computing Information-based generalized Robinson-Foulds distances with the TreeDist R package and assigning empirical P-values by label shuffling (100,000 iterations).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate and reference trees do not share a common set of taxa and cannot be pruned to identical external nodes — the Information-based generalized RFD comparison requires matching leaf sets. The goal is to compare continuous genetic distances (e.g., Mash distances or APSS values) rather than tree topologies — the article itself recommends considering continuous genomic difference measures instead of same/different classifications. Pairs have fewer than n regions available (pairs with fewer than n regions are excluded from downstream analysis, so no synteny-based tree can be built at that depth).

skills.summary: Evaluates a text-mining information extraction system (e.g., MicroPIE) against a hand-generated gold standard taxon-by-character matrix using Relaxed precision, recall, and F1, and benchmarks it against human (undergraduate student) extraction with Student's t-Tests.

skills.description: Use when you have an rRNA insertion catalog keyed to 16S rRNA genes and need to quantify what fraction of genes carry large (≥10 bp) insertions and the max/mean/s.d. of insertion lengths.
skills.name: insertion-length-summary-statistics
skills.search_text: insertion-length-summary-statistics Use when you have an rRNA insertion catalog keyed to 16S rRNA genes and need to quantify what fraction of genes carry large (≥10 bp) insertions and the max/mean/s.d. of insertion lengths.
