skills.name: insertion-sequence-catalogue-search
skills.search_text: insertion-sequence-catalogue-search Use when you have FASTA sequences of insertion sequences (e.g. from ISC) and need to find which isolate genomes contain them and infer their taxonomic origins via compact index search. Your query sequences are raw reads or assemblies rather than IS catalogue entries — Palidis itself (not COBS querying) is the discovery tool for novel ISs from metagenomic reads The ISs of interest lack inverted terminal repeats, since ISC v1.0.0 only contains common DDE-type ISs with ITRs You need to annotate ISs in human metagenomes from sources outside the healthy oral cavity and stool, where ISC v1.0.0 is not recommended as a reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0798 Traces the origins of insertion sequences (ISs) from the Insertion Sequence Catalogue (ISC) by querying the 879-IS FASTA against a COBS compact bit-sliced index of 661,405 ENA microbial isolate genomes, then attaching BioSample taxonomy to attribute ISs to known genera and species. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Traces the origins of insertion sequences (ISs) from the Insertion Sequence Catalogue (ISC) by querying the 879-IS FASTA against a COBS compact bit-sliced index of 661,405 ENA microbial isolate genomes, then attaching BioSample taxonomy to attribute ISs to known genera and species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your query sequences are raw reads or assemblies rather than IS catalogue entries — Palidis itself (not COBS querying) is the discovery tool for novel ISs from metagenomic reads The ISs of interest lack inverted terminal repeats, since ISC v1.0.0 only contains common DDE-type ISs with ITRs You need to annotate ISs in human metagenomes from sources outside the healthy oral cavity and stool, where ISC v1.0.0 is not recommended as a reference

skills.description: Reference for quantifying the fraction of a newly built IS catalogue with known homologs, e.g. after running Palidis on metagenomes and producing a non-redundant FASTA of insertion sequences to be annotated against ISfinder.
skills.name: insertion-sequence-database-benchmarking
skills.search_text: insertion-sequence-database-benchmarking Reference for quantifying the fraction of a newly built IS catalogue with known homologs, e.g. after running Palidis on metagenomes and producing a non-redundant FASTA of insertion sequences to be annotated against ISfinder. The catalogue contains ISs lacking inverted terminal repeats, since the source ISC was generated by Palidis which only discovers ISs with ITRs and the benchmark design assumes comparable catalogue content. A local, reproducible BLAST workflow is required — the paper used ISfinder's online BLAST service, so results depend on database version and web-service parameters at the query date. The goal is de novo IS discovery from metagenomic reads rather than annotating an existing IS catalogue against a reference database. http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks a de novo insertion sequence (IS) catalogue against a reference IS database (ISfinder) by BLASTing every catalogue sequence and stratifying hits into strict/loose homology and novel bins, quantifying how much of the catalogue is previously characterized. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Benchmarks a de novo insertion sequence (IS) catalogue against a reference IS database (ISfinder) by BLASTing every catalogue sequence and stratifying hits into strict/loose homology and novel bins, quantifying how much of the catalogue is previously characterized.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The catalogue contains ISs lacking inverted terminal repeats, since the source ISC was generated by Palidis which only discovers ISs with ITRs and the benchmark design assumes comparable catalogue content. A local, reproducible BLAST workflow is required — the paper used ISfinder's online BLAST service, so results depend on database version and web-service parameters at the query date. The goal is de novo IS discovery from metagenomic reads rather than annotating an existing IS catalogue against a reference database.

skills.description: Use when the input is paired-end short-read metagenomic FASTQ.GZ data from mixed microbial communities (e.g. HMP oral/stool samples) and the goal is to detect ISs and build a non-redundant IS catalogue with novel transposase annotation.
skills.name: insertion-sequence-discovery-from-metagenomes
skills.search_text: insertion-sequence-discovery-from-metagenomes Use when the input is paired-end short-read metagenomic FASTQ.GZ data from mixed microbial communities (e.g. HMP oral/stool samples) and the goal is to detect ISs and build a non-redundant IS catalogue with novel transposase annotation. The microbial genomes/ISs of interest lack inverted terminal repeats — Palidis is 'currently only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs' and the ISC only contains common DDE types of ISs with ITRs ISs have ITRs shorter than 25 nt — the default minimum ITR length misses ITRs as short as ten nucleotides Input is isolate genomes only where a prebuilt catalogue suffices for annotation — use ISC v1.0.0 directly (it is recommended as reference for isolates from healthy human oral cavity and stool, the sources it was built from) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Discover novel insertion sequences (ISs) in short-read metagenomic data using Palidis, which detects palindromic inverted terminal repeats (ITRs) via maximal exact matching, then pools and clusters detections into a non-redundant catalogue (e.g. ISC v1.0.0 with 879 unique ISs). metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Discover novel insertion sequences (ISs) in short-read metagenomic data using Palidis, which detects palindromic inverted terminal repeats (ITRs) via maximal exact matching, then pools and clusters detections into a non-redundant catalogue (e.g. ISC v1.0.0 with 879 unique ISs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The microbial genomes/ISs of interest lack inverted terminal repeats — Palidis is 'currently only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs' and the ISC only contains common DDE types of ISs with ITRs ISs have ITRs shorter than 25 nt — the default minimum ITR length misses ITRs as short as ten nucleotides Input is isolate genomes only where a prebuilt catalogue suffices for annotation — use ISC v1.0.0 directly (it is recommended as reference for isolates from healthy human oral cavity and stool, the sources it was built from)

skills.description: Use when validating an amplicon profile correction method (e.g., GCN correction) and you need simulated communities with known ground truth, plus matched amplicon and metagenomic read datasets from the same underlying composition.
skills.name: insilico-mock-community-design
skills.search_text: insilico-mock-community-design Use when validating an amplicon profile correction method (e.g., GCN correction) and you need simulated communities with known ground truth, plus matched amplicon and metagenomic read datasets from the same underlying composition. Your profiles come from real environmental or host-associated samples with no known expected composition — no ground truth exists to score agreement against Your question concerns non-16S marker genes or fungal ITS variation, for which CopyRighter has no pre-computed trait estimates (only hypothetical pending appropriate estimates) http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Design and simulate in silico mock communities spanning defined richness tiers (10 to 1,000 species), generating 16S rRNA gene amplicon and shotgun metagenomic reads with Grinder so that gene copy number (GCN) correction methods like CopyRighter can be validated against known expected community compositions. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Design and simulate in silico mock communities spanning defined richness tiers (10 to 1,000 species), generating 16S rRNA gene amplicon and shotgun metagenomic reads with Grinder so that gene copy number (GCN) correction methods like CopyRighter can be validated against known expected community compositions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your profiles come from real environmental or host-associated samples with no known expected composition — no ground truth exists to score agreement against Your question concerns non-16S marker genes or fungal ITS variation, for which CopyRighter has no pre-computed trait estimates (only hypothetical pending appropriate estimates)

skills.description: Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. quality- and adapter-trimmed with bbduk, duplicates removed with clumpify.sh) and need a reference-free metric of Hi-C ligation quality before binning.
skills.name: inter-contig-3d-ratio-estimation
skills.search_text: inter-contig-3d-ratio-estimation Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. quality- and adapter-trimmed with bbduk, duplicates removed with clumpify.sh) and need a reference-free metric of Hi-C ligation quality before binning. Input is raw, untrimmed Hi-C FASTQ — the 3D ratio must be computed on reads preprocessed with bbduk (trimq=10 qtrim=r ftm=5 minlen=50, ftl=10) and clumpify.sh deduplication, otherwise the metric is not comparable to reported values You already have a reference assembly/BAM and want alignment-based Hi-C QC rather than the reference-free k-mer mode of qc3C The goal is downstream viral genome binning itself (ViralCC pipeline) rather than assessing Hi-C library quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Estimates the inter-contig (3D) ratio of metagenomic Hi-C libraries with qc3C in k-mer (reference-free) mode, as a quantitative measure of Hi-C ligation/library quality. In the ViralCC paper this was applied to human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater Hi-C datasets after bbduk/clumpify preprocessing. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Estimates the inter-contig (3D) ratio of metagenomic Hi-C libraries with qc3C in k-mer (reference-free) mode, as a quantitative measure of Hi-C ligation/library quality. In the ViralCC paper this was applied to human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater Hi-C datasets after bbduk/clumpify preprocessing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, untrimmed Hi-C FASTQ — the 3D ratio must be computed on reads preprocessed with bbduk (trimq=10 qtrim=r ftm=5 minlen=50, ftl=10) and clumpify.sh deduplication, otherwise the metric is not comparable to reported values You already have a reference assembly/BAM and want alignment-based Hi-C QC rather than the reference-free k-mer mode of qc3C The goal is downstream viral genome binning itself (ViralCC pipeline) rather than assessing Hi-C library quality

skills.description: Use when a genome/metagenome assembly evaluation pipeline (QUAST, WebQUAST, MetaQUAST) has computed quality metrics and plots and they must be merged into one interactive HTML file with an Icarus viewer menu for the user.
skills.name: interactive-html-report-rendering
skills.search_text: interactive-html-report-rendering Use when a genome/metagenome assembly evaluation pipeline (QUAST, WebQUAST, MetaQUAST) has computed quality metrics and plots and they must be merged into one interactive HTML file with an Icarus viewer menu for the user. The user only needs machine-readable metrics for downstream parsing — report.tsv alone suffices; the interactive HTML/Icarus rendering adds nothing for spreadsheet or programmatic consumption. The input is not a genome/metagenome assembly evaluation but another report type (e.g. annotation or read QC) — QUAST's report.html/icarus.html bundle is specific to assembly quality assessment. Matplotlib (v1.1 or higher) is unavailable and PDF plots are required — QUAST still renders HTML plots, but report.pdf cannot be produced in that environment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Bundle genome assembly evaluation results (metrics tables, plots, and Icarus contig viewers) into standalone interactive HTML reports — report.html plus an icarus.html main menu — so that a multi-module QUAST/WebQUAST run is delivered as a single downloadable, browser-readable artifact. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad406
skills.summary: Bundle genome assembly evaluation results (metrics tables, plots, and Icarus contig viewers) into standalone interactive HTML reports — report.html plus an icarus.html main menu — so that a multi-module QUAST/WebQUAST run is delivered as a single downloadable, browser-readable artifact.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The user only needs machine-readable metrics for downstream parsing — report.tsv alone suffices; the interactive HTML/Icarus rendering adds nothing for spreadsheet or programmatic consumption. The input is not a genome/metagenome assembly evaluation but another report type (e.g. annotation or read QC) — QUAST's report.html/icarus.html bundle is specific to assembly quality assessment. Matplotlib (v1.1 or higher) is unavailable and PDF plots are required — QUAST still renders HTML plots, but report.pdf cannot be produced in that environment.

skills.description: Use when a MetaPhage Nextflow run has completed and you must confirm the interactive HTML report was generated with all expected sections (miner comparison, taxonomy, diversity) before comparing against the deposited reference.
skills.name: interactive-html-report-structure-validation
skills.search_text: interactive-html-report-structure-validation Use when a MetaPhage Nextflow run has completed and you must confirm the interactive HTML report was generated with all expected sections (miner comparison, taxonomy, diversity) before comparing against the deposited reference. The report step was skipped (--skip_report true) or only intermediate step outputs (e.g., mining or taxonomy alone) exist, so no assembled HTML report is available to validate The goal is to assess biological results such as vOTU counts or richness patterns rather than the report's structure and panel completeness Input is not a MetaPhage run output (e.g., a generic MultiQC report from another pipeline), since the expected panels and deposited reference are MetaPhage-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Validate that a MetaPhage run produces its final interactive MultiQC-assembled HTML report (report/index.html) with the expected panels — Miner Comparison, Kraken2 charts, metaQUAST assembly statistics, and diversity plots — and that its structure matches the authors' deposited figshare reference report. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Validate that a MetaPhage run produces its final interactive MultiQC-assembled HTML report (report/index.html) with the expected panels — Miner Comparison, Kraken2 charts, metaQUAST assembly statistics, and diversity plots — and that its structure matches the authors' deposited figshare reference report.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The report step was skipped (--skip_report true) or only intermediate step outputs (e.g., mining or taxonomy alone) exist, so no assembled HTML report is available to validate The goal is to assess biological results such as vOTU counts or richness patterns rather than the report's structure and panel completeness Input is not a MetaPhage run output (e.g., a generic MultiQC report from another pipeline), since the expected panels and deposited reference are MetaPhage-specific

skills.description: Use when signatures-of-selection scan results (iHS, XP-EHH, SweepFinder2 CLR values) from scalepopgen need to be visualized as interactive per-population Manhattan plots to inspect candidate regions under selection.
skills.name: interactive-manhattan-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: interactive-manhattan-plot-visualization Use when signatures-of-selection scan results (iHS, XP-EHH, SweepFinder2 CLR values) from scalepopgen need to be visualized as interactive per-population Manhattan plots to inspect candidate regions under selection. The underlying selection scan has not yet been run — the plots require iHS/XP-EHH and SweepFinder2 result files as input, not raw VCFs. The analysis goal is publication-quality static figures rather than interactive exploration of flagged selection regions. The task concerns the other scalepopgen sub-workflows (filtering/basic statistics, genetic structure, TreeMix phylogeny) rather than signatures-of-selection results. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3056 Generate interactive Manhattan plots with the scalepopgen workflow's Python (Plotly) scripts to visualize results of the signatures-of-selection scans (iHS, XP-EHH, SweepFinder2), flagging genomic regions above a user-defined selection threshold with Ensembl location links when species annotation is available. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Generate interactive Manhattan plots with the scalepopgen workflow's Python (Plotly) scripts to visualize results of the signatures-of-selection scans (iHS, XP-EHH, SweepFinder2), flagging genomic regions above a user-defined selection threshold with Ensembl location links when species annotation is available.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The underlying selection scan has not yet been run — the plots require iHS/XP-EHH and SweepFinder2 result files as input, not raw VCFs. The analysis goal is publication-quality static figures rather than interactive exploration of flagged selection regions. The task concerns the other scalepopgen sub-workflows (filtering/basic statistics, genetic structure, TreeMix phylogeny) rather than signatures-of-selection results.

skills.description: Use when a Nextflow population-genomics pipeline has produced analysis outputs (PCA variance/coordinates, ADMIXTURE logs and Q-matrices, IBS and FST distance matrices, TreeMix tree files) and the user needs combined, interactive plots to interpret population structure immediately.
skills.name: interactive-population-structure-visualization
skills.search_text: interactive-population-structure-visualization Use when a Nextflow population-genomics pipeline has produced analysis outputs (PCA variance/coordinates, ADMIXTURE logs and Q-matrices, IBS and FST distance matrices, TreeMix tree files) and the user needs combined, interactive plots to interpret population structure immediately. The input data are raw VCF or PLINK binary files that have not yet been processed by the structure/phylogeny sub-workflows — run filtering, PCA, ADMIXTURE, IBS/FST, or TreeMix analyses first Only static publication figures are needed and no hover tooltips, hide/expose controls, or cross-plot color consistency are required http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Collects the outputs of scalepopgen's structure/phylogeny sub-workflows (PCA coordinates, ADMIXTURE Q-matrices, IBS/FST matrices, TreeMix trees) and renders them as interactive HTML visualizations with consistent population coloring so users can quickly interpret genomic patterns after pipeline execution. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Collects the outputs of scalepopgen's structure/phylogeny sub-workflows (PCA coordinates, ADMIXTURE Q-matrices, IBS/FST matrices, TreeMix trees) and renders them as interactive HTML visualizations with consistent population coloring so users can quickly interpret genomic patterns after pipeline execution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are raw VCF or PLINK binary files that have not yet been processed by the structure/phylogeny sub-workflows — run filtering, PCA, ADMIXTURE, IBS/FST, or TreeMix analyses first Only static publication figures are needed and no hover tooltips, hide/expose controls, or cross-plot color consistency are required

skills.description: Use when you need to visually justify or audit taxonomic assignments of vOTUs within a vConTACT2 network, e.g. inspecting which INPHARED reference genomes neighbor each vOTU in its cluster.
skills.name: interactive-subnetwork-visualization
skills.search_text: interactive-subnetwork-visualization Use when you need to visually justify or audit taxonomic assignments of vOTUs within a vConTACT2 network, e.g. inspecting which INPHARED reference genomes neighbor each vOTU in its cluster. When no vConTACT2 network has been built (e.g. classification was done by marker-based tools like Demovir or VirHostMatcher) — there is no graph neighborhood to visualize. When you only need batch taxonomic assignments without visual audit — the taxonomy table alone suffices and subgraph rendering adds runtime. When input genomes were not named with the --prefix distinguishing vOTUs from reference genomes, the script cannot separate user scaffolds from references. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Generate per-vOTU interactive (2D or 3D) subgraph views of the vConTACT2 network neighborhood so each taxonomic assignment made by graphanalyzer can be visually inspected against neighboring reference genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Generate per-vOTU interactive (2D or 3D) subgraph views of the vConTACT2 network neighborhood so each taxonomic assignment made by graphanalyzer can be visually inspected against neighboring reference genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no vConTACT2 network has been built (e.g. classification was done by marker-based tools like Demovir or VirHostMatcher) — there is no graph neighborhood to visualize. When you only need batch taxonomic assignments without visual audit — the taxonomy table alone suffices and subgraph rendering adds runtime. When input genomes were not named with the --prefix distinguishing vOTUs from reference genomes, the script cannot separate user scaffolds from references.

skills.description: Use when paired fungal and bacterial taxonomic abundance tables plus sample metadata are available and the goal is to count or rank significant inter-kingdom correlations within defined healthy cohorts (e.g., Danish vs Spanish gut).
skills.name: interkingdom-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: interkingdom-correlation-analysis Use when paired fungal and bacterial taxonomic abundance tables plus sample metadata are available and the goal is to count or rank significant inter-kingdom correlations within defined healthy cohorts (e.g., Danish vs Spanish gut). Input is still raw sequencing reads rather than per-sample fungal/bacterial abundance profiles — profile with FunOMIC (bowtie2 to FunOMIC-T) and MetaPhlAn first The analysis goal is differential abundance or single-taxon association testing rather than compositional co-occurrence network structure between kingdoms Samples cannot be cleanly subset into defined cohorts (e.g., healthy Danish and Spanish gut) via the metadata fields, since SparCC is run separately per cohort http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Estimates SparCC correlation networks between fungal taxonomic/functional profiles (from FunOMIC-T mapping of human metagenomes) and MetaPhlAn v3.0.9 bacterial profiles, retaining significant inter-kingdom links (p < 0.001, |rho| > 0.05) per cohort to quantify fungus–bacterium co-occurrence structure. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Estimates SparCC correlation networks between fungal taxonomic/functional profiles (from FunOMIC-T mapping of human metagenomes) and MetaPhlAn v3.0.9 bacterial profiles, retaining significant inter-kingdom links (p < 0.001, |rho| > 0.05) per cohort to quantify fungus–bacterium co-occurrence structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw sequencing reads rather than per-sample fungal/bacterial abundance profiles — profile with FunOMIC (bowtie2 to FunOMIC-T) and MetaPhlAn first The analysis goal is differential abundance or single-taxon association testing rather than compositional co-occurrence network structure between kingdoms Samples cannot be cleanly subset into defined cohorts (e.g., healthy Danish and Spanish gut) via the metadata fields, since SparCC is run separately per cohort

skills.description: Use when the input is paired-end metagenome sequencing data that must be converted to interleaved FASTQ and assembled de novo at strain resolution with StrainXpress, or when reproducing StrainXpress benchmark workflows.
skills.name: interleaved-fastq-read-processing
skills.search_text: interleaved-fastq-read-processing Use when the input is paired-end metagenome sequencing data that must be converted to interleaved FASTQ and assembled de novo at strain resolution with StrainXpress, or when reproducing StrainXpress benchmark workflows. Input reads are long-read (PacBio/Nanopore) — the article notes the high Error Rate of third-generation sequencing reads 'introduce a range of issues that still need to be resolved' The task requires species-level binning of an existing assembly rather than de novo strain-aware assembly from raw reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Format and run StrainXpress on interleaved paired-end FASTQ metagenome read sets (e.g. CAMISIM simulations, Bmock12, NWCs, Gut Metagenome, Salmonella spike-ins) using a conda-installed StrainXpress environment, producing strain-resolved contigs in stageb/final_contigs.fasta. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac543
skills.summary: Format and run StrainXpress on interleaved paired-end FASTQ metagenome read sets (e.g. CAMISIM simulations, Bmock12, NWCs, Gut Metagenome, Salmonella spike-ins) using a conda-installed StrainXpress environment, producing strain-resolved contigs in stageb/final_contigs.fasta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are long-read (PacBio/Nanopore) — the article notes the high Error Rate of third-generation sequencing reads 'introduce a range of issues that still need to be resolved' The task requires species-level binning of an existing assembly rather than de novo strain-aware assembly from raw reads

skills.description: Use when comparing metagenome assemblers (e.g. MetaPlatanus, metaSPAdes, OPERA-MS, metaFlye) on a mock community whose bacterial reference genomes are known, and misassembly/NGA50 counts must be extracted with metaQUAST.
skills.name: interspecies-misasassembly-quantification
skills.search_text: interspecies-misasassembly-quantification Use when comparing metagenome assemblers (e.g. MetaPlatanus, metaSPAdes, OPERA-MS, metaFlye) on a mock community whose bacterial reference genomes are known, and misassembly/NGA50 counts must be extracted with metaQUAST. Input is real (unknown-composition) metagenome data with no reference genomes for the constituent species — reference-based QUAST evaluation of interspecies misassemblies is impossible; use binning-based or read-mapping QC instead The goal is reference-informed or contig binning evaluation — the article notes 'this study focuses on de novo methods, and reference information has not been well examined' http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Quantifies misassemblies and, specifically, interspecies misassemblies of metagenome assemblies on mock communities with known reference genomes using QUAST/metaQUAST, as done in the MetaPlatanus GIS20 mock benchmark alongside NGA50 and mean sequence identity metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Quantifies misassemblies and, specifically, interspecies misassemblies of metagenome assemblies on mock communities with known reference genomes using QUAST/metaQUAST, as done in the MetaPlatanus GIS20 mock benchmark alongside NGA50 and mean sequence identity metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (unknown-composition) metagenome data with no reference genomes for the constituent species — reference-based QUAST evaluation of interspecies misassemblies is impossible; use binning-based or read-mapping QC instead The goal is reference-informed or contig binning evaluation — the article notes 'this study focuses on de novo methods, and reference information has not been well examined'

skills.description: Use when mapping-based SNV calls from inStrain profiles across multiple samples must be partitioned into within-host vs between-host variants and analyzed for selection (dN/dS) at the gene level.
skills.name: intra-vs-inter-sample-variant-classification
skills.search_text: intra-vs-inter-sample-variant-classification Use when mapping-based SNV calls from inStrain profiles across multiple samples must be partitioned into within-host vs between-host variants and analyzed for selection (dN/dS) at the gene level. Genome-level strain sharing rather than SNV-level diversity: use 'inStrain compare' for ConANI/popANI strain comparisons instead Reference-free variant discovery without a mapped reference .fasta and gene annotations — this skill requires bams mapped to a specific genome plus Prodigal ORF calls Read filtering or coverage breadth estimation as the primary goal (e.g. use CoverM for coverage calculation instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Classifies metagenomic SNVs as intra-sample (biallelic within a single sample, e.g. an infant) versus inter-sample (substitutions between samples), annotates them as synonymous/nonsynonymous from Prodigal gene calls, and computes per-gene dN/dS to test whether diversity is evolved in situ or shared between hosts. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Classifies metagenomic SNVs as intra-sample (biallelic within a single sample, e.g. an infant) versus inter-sample (substitutions between samples), annotates them as synonymous/nonsynonymous from Prodigal gene calls, and computes per-gene dN/dS to test whether diversity is evolved in situ or shared between hosts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genome-level strain sharing rather than SNV-level diversity: use 'inStrain compare' for ConANI/popANI strain comparisons instead Reference-free variant discovery without a mapped reference .fasta and gene annotations — this skill requires bams mapped to a specific genome plus Prodigal ORF calls Read filtering or coverage breadth estimation as the primary goal (e.g. use CoverM for coverage calculation instead)

skills.description: Use when predicting the obligate intracellular lifestyle of bacterial genomes from comparative-genomics COG presence/absence profiles, or reproducing the 0.997 ± 0.010 accuracy benchmark on complete genomes.
skills.name: intracellular-lifestyle-classification
skills.search_text: intracellular-lifestyle-classification Use when predicting the obligate intracellular lifestyle of bacterial genomes from comparative-genomics COG presence/absence profiles, or reproducing the 0.997 ± 0.010 accuracy benchmark on complete genomes. Input genomes are far below the reliability threshold: most traits can be reliably predicted only in 60-70% complete genomes, so highly fragmentary bins may not support this model The target trait is a presence-based phenotype not driven by genome reduction, for which a different phenotrex/PICA trait model should be trained instead Sufficient labeled training data are unavailable for further ecologically important traits, where performance is still pending http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and cross-validate an SVM classifier (PICA plug-in backed by libSVM) on a COG presence/absence feature matrix to distinguish obligate intracellular bacteria from free-living/facultative species, exploiting the fact that this trait is determined by gene absence in reduced genomes rather than gene presence. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-16-s14-s1
skills.summary: Train and cross-validate an SVM classifier (PICA plug-in backed by libSVM) on a COG presence/absence feature matrix to distinguish obligate intracellular bacteria from free-living/facultative species, exploiting the fact that this trait is determined by gene absence in reduced genomes rather than gene presence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input genomes are far below the reliability threshold: most traits can be reliably predicted only in 60-70% complete genomes, so highly fragmentary bins may not support this model The target trait is a presence-based phenotype not driven by genome reduction, for which a different phenotrex/PICA trait model should be trained instead Sufficient labeled training data are unavailable for further ecologically important traits, where performance is still pending

skills.description: Use when VIRGO mapping outputs (summary.Count.txt, summary.Abundance.txt) are available for vaginal metagenomes and the goal is to confirm that ward-linkage clustering of Jaccard distances over species-assigned gene content recovers the reported number of MG-subspecies.
skills.name: intraspecies-diversity-cluster-validation
skills.search_text: intraspecies-diversity-cluster-validation Use when VIRGO mapping outputs (summary.Count.txt, summary.Abundance.txt) are available for vaginal metagenomes and the goal is to confirm that ward-linkage clustering of Jaccard distances over species-assigned gene content recovers the reported number of MG-subspecies. The goal is taxonomic profiling of community composition rather than resolving strain-level gene-content structure — VIRGO's summary.Percentage.txt species abundances already serve that Input samples were not mapped to the VIRGO gene catalog (e.g. 16S amplicon data, which the article states cannot capture accessory-gene-content diversity) The target species has too few mapped samples or genes to support stable Jaccard/ward clustering, so cluster counts would not be comparable to the reported MG-subspecies structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Validates that hierarchical clustering of species-specific gene presence/absence profiles from VIRGO-mapped vaginal metagenomes resolves metagenomic subspecies (MG-subspecies) at the expected diversity: >=3 MG-subspecies for Lactobacillus gasseri and >4 for Gardnerella vaginalis across the 1,507 vaginal metagenomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Validates that hierarchical clustering of species-specific gene presence/absence profiles from VIRGO-mapped vaginal metagenomes resolves metagenomic subspecies (MG-subspecies) at the expected diversity: >=3 MG-subspecies for Lactobacillus gasseri and >4 for Gardnerella vaginalis across the 1,507 vaginal metagenomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is taxonomic profiling of community composition rather than resolving strain-level gene-content structure — VIRGO's summary.Percentage.txt species abundances already serve that Input samples were not mapped to the VIRGO gene catalog (e.g. 16S amplicon data, which the article states cannot capture accessory-gene-content diversity) The target species has too few mapped samples or genes to support stable Jaccard/ward clustering, so cluster counts would not be comparable to the reported MG-subspecies structure

skills.description: Use when metagenomic reads (single-end merged FASTQ) can be mapped to a reference gene catalog and you want to test whether within-community intraspecies strain co-occurrence inflates per-sample gene counts beyond isolate pangenomes.
skills.name: intraspecies-gene-content-comparison
skills.search_text: intraspecies-gene-content-comparison Use when metagenomic reads (single-end merged FASTQ) can be mapped to a reference gene catalog and you want to test whether within-community intraspecies strain co-occurrence inflates per-sample gene counts beyond isolate pangenomes. The goal is strain-level variant or SNP calling — VIRGO does not yet identify nucleotide variants within genes, so gene-count excess is only an indirect strain co-occurrence signal The species of interest is poorly represented in VIRGO's isolate-backed reference, since gaps may reflect limited isolate genomes or systematic bias in growth and recovery of vaginal species rather than true co-occurring strains Input data are 16S rRNA amplicon profiles, which cannot resolve accessory-gene content differences between strains http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantify whether a species' gene content recovered from vaginal metagenomes exceeds that of its isolate genomes, using VIRGO mapping to detect co-occurring strains (e.g., L. crispatus metagenomes show 3262 ± 586 genes vs 2064 ± 225 in isolates, a 1.6-fold excess, p < 0.001). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Quantify whether a species' gene content recovered from vaginal metagenomes exceeds that of its isolate genomes, using VIRGO mapping to detect co-occurring strains (e.g., L. crispatus metagenomes show 3262 ± 586 genes vs 2064 ± 225 in isolates, a 1.6-fold excess, p < 0.001).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is strain-level variant or SNP calling — VIRGO does not yet identify nucleotide variants within genes, so gene-count excess is only an indirect strain co-occurrence signal The species of interest is poorly represented in VIRGO's isolate-backed reference, since gaps may reflect limited isolate genomes or systematic bias in growth and recovery of vaginal species rather than true co-occurring strains Input data are 16S rRNA amplicon profiles, which cannot resolve accessory-gene content differences between strains

skills.description: Use when input is paired-end, short-read metagenomic FASTQ.GZ data (or mixed microbial genomes) and the goal is to discover novel insertion sequences via their inverted terminal repeats, e.g. to build or query an IS catalogue.
skills.name: inverted-terminal-repeat-palindrome-detection
skills.search_text: inverted-terminal-repeat-palindrome-detection Use when input is paired-end, short-read metagenomic FASTQ.GZ data (or mixed microbial genomes) and the goal is to discover novel insertion sequences via their inverted terminal repeats, e.g. to build or query an IS catalogue. The target ISs lack inverted terminal repeats or have ITRs shorter than 10 nt (Palidis is only equipped to discover ISs with ITRs, and the catalogue uses a 25 nt minimum) The ISs of interest are longer than 3000 bp or lengthened by nested insertion events, pushing ITRs outside the 500–3000 bp proximity range Input is isolate genome data intended for annotation against ISC built from healthy human oral cavity and stool metagenomes only — the catalogue's scope is limited to those sources http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Discovers novel insertion sequences (ISs) in short-read metagenomic data by detecting palindromic inverted terminal repeats (ITRs) via efficient maximal exact matching, then filtering candidates by ITR length (>=25 nt) and IS size (500–3000 bp) before clustering into a non-redundant catalogue. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Discovers novel insertion sequences (ISs) in short-read metagenomic data by detecting palindromic inverted terminal repeats (ITRs) via efficient maximal exact matching, then filtering candidates by ITR length (>=25 nt) and IS size (500–3000 bp) before clustering into a non-redundant catalogue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target ISs lack inverted terminal repeats or have ITRs shorter than 10 nt (Palidis is only equipped to discover ISs with ITRs, and the catalogue uses a 25 nt minimum) The ISs of interest are longer than 3000 bp or lengthened by nested insertion events, pushing ITRs outside the 500–3000 bp proximity range Input is isolate genome data intended for annotation against ISC built from healthy human oral cavity and stool metagenomes only — the catalogue's scope is limited to those sources

skills.description: Use when a COBS sample-hits table of ISC insertion sequences queried against 661,405 isolate genomes must be joined to genus/species metadata to identify the most widely shared IS and ISfinder coverage gaps.
skills.name: is-sharing-across-taxa-aggregation
skills.search_text: is-sharing-across-taxa-aggregation Use when a COBS sample-hits table of ISC insertion sequences queried against 661,405 isolate genomes must be joined to genus/species metadata to identify the most widely shared IS and ISfinder coverage gaps. When the ISs themselves still need to be discovered from reads — run Palidis (pal-MEM ITR detection, CD-HIT-EST clustering) first; this skill only aggregates existing COBS hit tables When genomes lack genus/species assignments in the metadata table, since the aggregation depends on mapping every COBS hit genome to species and genus When the query index is not the 661,405-genome COBS isolate index, since validation values (21 genera / 46 species for IS1249) are specific to that dataset Aggregates COBS sample-hits from the Insertion Sequence Catalogue (ISC) against 661,405 indexed microbial genomes to count, per IS, the number of distinct bacterial genera and species it occurs in, ranking insertion sequences by taxonomic breadth and flagging ISfinder annotation gaps. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Aggregates COBS sample-hits from the Insertion Sequence Catalogue (ISC) against 661,405 indexed microbial genomes to count, per IS, the number of distinct bacterial genera and species it occurs in, ranking insertion sequences by taxonomic breadth and flagging ISfinder annotation gaps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the ISs themselves still need to be discovered from reads — run Palidis (pal-MEM ITR detection, CD-HIT-EST clustering) first; this skill only aggregates existing COBS hit tables When genomes lack genus/species assignments in the metadata table, since the aggregation depends on mapping every COBS hit genome to species and genus When the query index is not the 661,405-genome COBS isolate index, since validation values (21 genera / 46 species for IS1249) are specific to that dataset

skills.description: Use when a set of predicted insertion sequence IDs (e.g. ISC entries like IS_length_1391-IPR001207_495_804) needs known/novel status resolved against ISfinder before ranking or reporting.
skills.name: isfinder-novelty-cross-referencing
skills.search_text: isfinder-novelty-cross-referencing Use when a set of predicted insertion sequence IDs (e.g. ISC entries like IS_length_1391-IPR001207_495_804) needs known/novel status resolved against ISfinder before ranking or reporting. The goal is de novo IS discovery from reads — use Palidis instead; this skill only annotates existing IS sequences against ISfinder The IS set comes from sources outside the healthy human oral cavity and stool samples that ISC v1.0.0 was built from, limiting the annotation reference's applicability Sequences are not insertion sequences with inverted terminal repeats — ISC only contains common DDE-type ISs with ITRs of 25 or more nucleotides http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Cross-references catalogue insertion sequences (e.g. the 879 ISs in ISC) against the ISfinder reference database to label each IS as known (with an ISfinder name such as IS1249) or novel, and to propagate that annotation into downstream sharing/coverage analyses. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Cross-references catalogue insertion sequences (e.g. the 879 ISs in ISC) against the ISfinder reference database to label each IS as known (with an ISfinder name such as IS1249) or novel, and to propagate that annotation into downstream sharing/coverage analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo IS discovery from reads — use Palidis instead; this skill only annotates existing IS sequences against ISfinder The IS set comes from sources outside the healthy human oral cavity and stool samples that ISC v1.0.0 was built from, limiting the annotation reference's applicability Sequences are not insertion sequences with inverted terminal repeats — ISC only contains common DDE-type ISs with ITRs of 25 or more nucleotides

skills.description: Use when you have simulated read sets mapped to a known allele database and need to validate fractional allele composition calls against an established isoform/abundance quantification baseline such as Kallisto.
skills.name: isoform-abundance-quantification-comparison
skills.search_text: isoform-abundance-quantification-comparison Use when you have simulated read sets mapped to a known allele database and need to validate fractional allele composition calls against an established isoform/abundance quantification baseline such as Kallisto. Input is real metagenomic tick sample data rather than simulated reads with known ground-truth allele composition — the precision/recall/TVD comparison requires true allele calls The organism or typing scheme is not a multi-locus sequence typing framework with a curated reference allele database (e.g. the B. burgdorferi MLST scheme) The goal is strain-type level comparison including novel strains (EvoMod1–EvoMod3 mechanisms), which requires the strainEST comparison with soft-precision/soft-recall/EMD rather than Kallisto alone http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark an MLST deconvolution pipeline's per-locus allele abundance estimates against Kallisto, a likelihood-based isoform abundance estimator, using ART-simulated reads mapped with Bowtie v0.12.7 to the B. burgdorferi MLST allele database. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Benchmark an MLST deconvolution pipeline's per-locus allele abundance estimates against Kallisto, a likelihood-based isoform abundance estimator, using ART-simulated reads mapped with Bowtie v0.12.7 to the B. burgdorferi MLST allele database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real metagenomic tick sample data rather than simulated reads with known ground-truth allele composition — the precision/recall/TVD comparison requires true allele calls The organism or typing scheme is not a multi-locus sequence typing framework with a curated reference allele database (e.g. the B. burgdorferi MLST scheme) The goal is strain-type level comparison including novel strains (EvoMod1–EvoMod3 mechanisms), which requires the strainEST comparison with soft-precision/soft-recall/EMD rather than Kallisto alone

skills.description: Use when building a non-redundant gene catalog from pooled sources and you need gene predictions from complete/draft isolate genomes (e.g., 308 urogenital isolates) to complement CDSs predicted from per-sample metagenomic assemblies.
skills.name: isolate-genome-gene-prediction
skills.search_text: isolate-genome-gene-prediction Use when building a non-redundant gene catalog from pooled sources and you need gene predictions from complete/draft isolate genomes (e.g., 308 urogenital isolates) to complement CDSs predicted from per-sample metagenomic assemblies. Input is raw vaginal metagenomic reads to be profiled against the finished catalog — map reads to VIRGO with runMapping.step1.sh instead of re-predicting genes Input is already a non-redundant gene catalog or gene abundance table — de-redundification/prediction would duplicate existing catalog structure Target is primarily viral or fungal sequence — VIRGO's database is 'primarily focused on bacteria with limited inclusion of viral and fungal gene sequences' (fungal/phage genes are handled separately in 2_fungal_phage) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Predicts coding sequences (CDSs) from cultured isolate genome sequences — in VIRGO's case 308 urogenital isolate genomes — so their genes can be pooled with metagenomic-assembly CDSs and de-redundified into a non-redundant body-site gene catalog. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Predicts coding sequences (CDSs) from cultured isolate genome sequences — in VIRGO's case 308 urogenital isolate genomes — so their genes can be pooled with metagenomic-assembly CDSs and de-redundified into a non-redundant body-site gene catalog.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw vaginal metagenomic reads to be profiled against the finished catalog — map reads to VIRGO with runMapping.step1.sh instead of re-predicting genes Input is already a non-redundant gene catalog or gene abundance table — de-redundification/prediction would duplicate existing catalog structure Target is primarily viral or fungal sequence — VIRGO's database is 'primarily focused on bacteria with limited inclusion of viral and fungal gene sequences' (fungal/phage genes are handled separately in 2_fungal_phage)

skills.description: Use when you have COBS query results against the 661k ENA compact index and need to resolve genome hits to BioSamples and taxonomic identities for IS origin tracing.
skills.name: isolate-genome-hit-parsing
skills.search_text: isolate-genome-hit-parsing Use when you have COBS query results against the 661k ENA compact index and need to resolve genome hits to BioSamples and taxonomic identities for IS origin tracing. The ISs under study lack inverted terminal repeats — the ISC only contains DDE-type ISs with ITRs of 25+ nucleotides, so hits cannot be expected You need IS origin prediction against curated reference IS databases rather than isolate genomes — query ISfinder instead of the COBS 661k index The genomes are metagenomic assemblies rather than isolates with ENA BioSample accessions and taxonomy metadata http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0798 Parses COBS query output to map positive isolate-genome hits to ENA BioSample accessions, attaches taxonomic metadata, and tallies distinct ISs, BioSamples, genera, and species — the step that traces ISC insertion sequences back to their isolate origins. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Parses COBS query output to map positive isolate-genome hits to ENA BioSample accessions, attaches taxonomic metadata, and tallies distinct ISs, BioSamples, genera, and species — the step that traces ISC insertion sequences back to their isolate origins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ISs under study lack inverted terminal repeats — the ISC only contains DDE-type ISs with ITRs of 25+ nucleotides, so hits cannot be expected You need IS origin prediction against curated reference IS databases rather than isolate genomes — query ISfinder instead of the COBS 661k index The genomes are metagenomic assemblies rather than isolates with ENA BioSample accessions and taxonomy metadata

skills.description: Use when isolate or assembly genome pairs have been compared with SynTracker and inStrain and you need per-pair APSS and popANI values to build same/different-strain classification tables.
skills.name: isolate-genome-pairwise-scores-extraction
skills.search_text: isolate-genome-pairwise-scores-extraction Use when isolate or assembly genome pairs have been compared with SynTracker and inStrain and you need per-pair APSS and popANI values to build same/different-strain classification tables. When samples are sequencing reads rather than assemblies/genomes — SynTracker compares metagenomic assemblies or genomes, and inStrain popANI requires read-mapping comparisons, not extracted APSS tables When no SNP-based comparator is available and only structural-difference information is needed — the combined APSS/popANI classification requires both score types When you expect the universal APSS 0.95 human-gut cutoff to apply to your species without validation — the paper explicitly states thresholds are species-dependent http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Extract per-pair Average Pairwise Synteny Scores (APSS) from SynTracker output tables and combine them with SNP-based popANI values from inStrain to classify isolate genome pairs as same or different strain, e.g. using APSS > 0.955 and popANI > 0.99999. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Extract per-pair Average Pairwise Synteny Scores (APSS) from SynTracker output tables and combine them with SNP-based popANI values from inStrain to classify isolate genome pairs as same or different strain, e.g. using APSS > 0.955 and popANI > 0.99999.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When samples are sequencing reads rather than assemblies/genomes — SynTracker compares metagenomic assemblies or genomes, and inStrain popANI requires read-mapping comparisons, not extracted APSS tables When no SNP-based comparator is available and only structural-difference information is needed — the combined APSS/popANI classification requires both score types When you expect the universal APSS 0.95 human-gut cutoff to apply to your species without validation — the paper explicitly states thresholds are species-dependent

skills.description: Use when predicting protein-coding genes in assembled prokaryotic genomes or metagenomic contigs/read sets with Glimmer/Glimmer-MG and you need to boot-strap and retrain IMM models on initial predictions before final calls.
skills.name: iterated-genome-model-training
skills.search_text: iterated-genome-model-training Use when predicting protein-coding genes in assembled prokaryotic genomes or metagenomic contigs/read sets with Glimmer/Glimmer-MG and you need to boot-strap and retrain IMM models on initial predictions before final calls. Sequences are very short error-prone reads with many indels where even Glimmer-MG precision is limited (54.7% precision at 2.0% 454 error rate) and assembly/base-calling improvements are needed first The organism is so highly diverged that optimal model parameters are unclear and no close phylogenetic relatives exist for Phymm-based parameterization You need a fast, cheap annotation pass — Glimmer-MG is explicitly more computationally expensive than existing software http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Iterative self-training of interpolated Markov model (IMM) gene predictors: build an initial model from long ORFs (or Phymm-based phylogenetic classification plus Scimm clustering for metagenomes), retrain on initial gene predictions, then produce final gene calls, optionally with length/adjacency filtering as in the Glimmer3.1 whole-genome pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: Iterative self-training of interpolated Markov model (IMM) gene predictors: build an initial model from long ORFs (or Phymm-based phylogenetic classification plus Scimm clustering for metagenomes), retrain on initial gene predictions, then produce final gene calls, optionally with length/adjacency filtering as in the Glimmer3.1 whole-genome pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are very short error-prone reads with many indels where even Glimmer-MG precision is limited (54.7% precision at 2.0% 454 error rate) and assembly/base-calling improvements are needed first The organism is so highly diverged that optimal model parameters are unclear and no close phylogenetic relatives exist for Phymm-based parameterization You need a fast, cheap annotation pass — Glimmer-MG is explicitly more computationally expensive than existing software

skills.description: Decision support for refining assembled metagenomic contigs down to a purely viral set: use when contigs from a mapping-assembly stage must be merged, filtered against Genbank, and rebuilt until convergence.
skills.name: iterative-contig-merging-reassembly
skills.search_text: iterative-contig-merging-reassembly Decision support for refining assembled metagenomic contigs down to a purely viral set: use when contigs from a mapping-assembly stage must be merged, filtered against Genbank, and rebuilt until convergence. Input is raw reads with no upstream mapping assembly — VirMAP requires contigs/super-scaffolds from its first-stage mapping assembly before improvement Goal is de-novo assembly alone without taxonomic filtering — this skill's filter step discards anything not resolving to the viral superkingdom Analysis targets non-viral sequences (e.g. bacterial or eukaryotic genomes) — the >50% viral-base filter will remove them by design http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 VirMAP's improvement algorithm that iteratively merges overlapping contigs and rebuilds them via pileup (and optional de-novo) assembly, filtering out non-viral contigs at each cycle so the final dual assembly consists solely of viral sequences. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: VirMAP's improvement algorithm that iteratively merges overlapping contigs and rebuilds them via pileup (and optional de-novo) assembly, filtering out non-viral contigs at each cycle so the final dual assembly consists solely of viral sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads with no upstream mapping assembly — VirMAP requires contigs/super-scaffolds from its first-stage mapping assembly before improvement Goal is de-novo assembly alone without taxonomic filtering — this skill's filter step discards anything not resolving to the viral superkingdom Analysis targets non-viral sequences (e.g. bacterial or eukaryotic genomes) — the >50% viral-base filter will remove them by design

skills.description: Use when de novo assembly of genomic flanking regions around target genes (e.g. ARGs) is needed from short-read metagenomic FASTQ data but full metagenomic de novo assembly is too computationally expensive.
skills.name: iterative-scaffold-extension-loop-implementation
skills.search_text: iterative-scaffold-extension-loop-implementation Use when de novo assembly of genomic flanking regions around target genes (e.g. ARGs) is needed from short-read metagenomic FASTQ data but full metagenomic de novo assembly is too computationally expensive. Input is long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler/ARGextender is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data and does not exploit long-read technologies The goal is full metagenomic de novo assembly of all contigs rather than extension of genomic flanks around pre-specified target genes The goal is taxonomic profiling (microbial abundance) rather than ARG detection and flanking-region reconstruction — use the mOTUs-based profiling path instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Implements ARGextender's recursive KMA-SPAdes targeted-assembly loop, which recruits reads mapping to ARG targets, assembles them de novo with SPAdes, and iteratively promotes recovered scaffolds to new targets to extend genomic flanking regions while avoiding costly full metagenomic de novo assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Implements ARGextender's recursive KMA-SPAdes targeted-assembly loop, which recruits reads mapping to ARG targets, assembles them de novo with SPAdes, and iteratively promotes recovered scaffolds to new targets to extend genomic flanking regions while avoiding costly full metagenomic de novo assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler/ARGextender is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data and does not exploit long-read technologies The goal is full metagenomic de novo assembly of all contigs rather than extension of genomic flanks around pre-specified target genes The goal is taxonomic profiling (microbial abundance) rather than ARG detection and flanking-region reconstruction — use the mOTUs-based profiling path instead

skills.description: Use when raw Illumina FASTQ reads contain a small seed set (HMM- or repeat-derived) and neighboring reads must be recruited for targeted assembly without assembling the whole dataset.
skills.name: iterative-seed-expansion-implementation
skills.search_text: iterative-seed-expansion-implementation Use when raw Illumina FASTQ reads contain a small seed set (HMM- or repeat-derived) and neighboring reads must be recruited for targeted assembly without assembling the whole dataset. The dataset has already been fully assembled and annotated — conventional assembly/annotation pipelines are the alternative CasCollect was benchmarked against, and full assembly forecloses the runtime benefit (almost two orders of magnitude) Sequencing data are not short-read DNA sequencing reads (e.g. long-read or amino-acid inputs), since VSEARCH does not support amino acid sequences or local alignments The target is a whole-genome assembly rather than a targeted specialty gene region around seed matches http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Iteratively expands a small set of seed reads (e.g. cas-gene or CRISPR-repeat matches) into a larger read subset by repeated VSEARCH identity matching, so that only the CRISPR/Cas-relevant fraction of a raw FASTQ dataset feeds targeted assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Iteratively expands a small set of seed reads (e.g. cas-gene or CRISPR-repeat matches) into a larger read subset by repeated VSEARCH identity matching, so that only the CRISPR/Cas-relevant fraction of a raw FASTQ dataset feeds targeted assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has already been fully assembled and annotated — conventional assembly/annotation pipelines are the alternative CasCollect was benchmarked against, and full assembly forecloses the runtime benefit (almost two orders of magnitude) Sequencing data are not short-read DNA sequencing reads (e.g. long-read or amino-acid inputs), since VSEARCH does not support amino acid sequences or local alignments The target is a whole-genome assembly rather than a targeted specialty gene region around seed matches

skills.description: Use when running Strainberry on a strain-oblivious long-read assembly plus indexed BAM alignment and you must decide how many separation iterations to run, when to stop, and how to organize per-iteration outputs (strainberry_n2/, strainberry_n3/, ...).
skills.name: iterative-strain-separation-control-loop
skills.search_text: iterative-strain-separation-control-loop Use when running Strainberry on a strain-oblivious long-read assembly plus indexed BAM alignment and you must decide how many separation iterations to run, when to stop, and how to organize per-iteration outputs (strainberry_n2/, strainberry_n3/, ...). Highly complex metagenomes — Strainberry is designed for single-sample low-complexity metagenomes and relies on well-represented strains Contigs that would need a variable number of strains separated within the same sequence — the paper notes this case is not handled Plasmid genome resolution — Strainberry's ability to resolve plasmids was not evaluated and was left for future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Controls Strainberry's iterative strain separation: repeated rounds of read re-phasing and per-haplotype re-assembly at increasing strain multiplicity, stopped by an average Hamming rate improvement threshold or the maximum multiplicity (--max-strains, default 5). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Controls Strainberry's iterative strain separation: repeated rounds of read re-phasing and per-haplotype re-assembly at increasing strain multiplicity, stopped by an average Hamming rate improvement threshold or the maximum multiplicity (--max-strains, default 5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Highly complex metagenomes — Strainberry is designed for single-sample low-complexity metagenomes and relies on well-represented strains Contigs that would need a variable number of strains separated within the same sequence — the paper notes this case is not handled Plasmid genome resolution — Strainberry's ability to resolve plasmids was not evaluated and was left for future work

skills.description: Use when you have read-level inverted terminal repeat (ITR) calls with LCoord/RCoord positions and paired assemblies, and need to keep only reads where repeat positions imply an IS within a plausible size range.
skills.name: itr-position-based-read-filtering
skills.search_text: itr-position-based-read-filtering Use when you have read-level inverted terminal repeat (ITR) calls with LCoord/RCoord positions and paired assemblies, and need to keep only reads where repeat positions imply an IS within a plausible size range. The input contains no read-level ITR calls (e.g. raw FASTQ.GZ that has not been through the pal-MEM maximal exact matching step) — map-and-filter would have no repeat positions to test. The target ISs lack inverted terminal repeats, since Palidis is only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs. You expect ISs whose ITRs are separated by more than the maximum IS length (e.g. regions lengthened by nested insertion events beyond 3000 bp), which this filter will discard by design. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A filtering step in the Palidis pipeline that maps repeat-containing reads (output of pal-MEM) back to their associated assemblies with Bowtie2, then retains only mapped reads whose ITR repeat coordinates fall within a user-defined minimum-to-maximum insertion sequence (IS) length interval (500–3000 bp for Palidis candidates). metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: A filtering step in the Palidis pipeline that maps repeat-containing reads (output of pal-MEM) back to their associated assemblies with Bowtie2, then retains only mapped reads whose ITR repeat coordinates fall within a user-defined minimum-to-maximum insertion sequence (IS) length interval (500–3000 bp for Palidis candidates).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input contains no read-level ITR calls (e.g. raw FASTQ.GZ that has not been through the pal-MEM maximal exact matching step) — map-and-filter would have no repeat positions to test. The target ISs lack inverted terminal repeats, since Palidis is only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs. You expect ISs whose ITRs are separated by more than the maximum IS length (e.g. regions lengthened by nested insertion events beyond 3000 bp), which this filter will discard by design.

skills.description: Use when you have FASTA files of candidate ITR and IS-region sequences from an upstream Palidis maximal-exact-match step and need to filter them into high-confidence IS predictions via cluster concordance and reverse-complement checks.
skills.name: itr-sequence-clustering
skills.search_text: itr-sequence-clustering Use when you have FASTA files of candidate ITR and IS-region sequences from an upstream Palidis maximal-exact-match step and need to filter them into high-confidence IS predictions via cluster concordance and reverse-complement checks. Input ISs lack ITRs entirely — Palidis is 'only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs', so cluster-concordance filtering cannot apply Candidate ITRs are shorter than the minimum ITR length threshold (default 25 nt; ITRs as short as 10 nt are missed at default settings) Candidate IS regions exceed the 500–3000 bp proximity range (e.g. lengthened by nested insertion events) and will be filtered out regardless of clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Cluster candidate inverted terminal repeat (ITR) sequences from the Palidis pipeline using CD-HIT-EST, then convert candidates into predicted insertion sequences by retaining candidates whose paired ITRs fall in the same cluster and are reverse complements of each other (verified with blastn). metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917

skills.description: Use when computing read-to-genome similarity with LiME's eBWT-based symbol-matching strategy and reference genomes or reads contain IUPAC ambiguity codes that must contribute matches rather than being discarded.

skills.search_text: iupac-ambiguity-code-matching Use when computing read-to-genome similarity with LiME's eBWT-based symbol-matching strategy and reference genomes or reads contain IUPAC ambiguity codes that must contribute matches rather than being discarded. If you only have the document array and prefer the color-presence variant of Step 2, compile with EBWT=0 instead — that approach reads only da(S) and does not perform eBWT symbol matching If the goal is alignment-based read mapping with identity thresholds (e.g. BLAST at 98% sequence identity), LiME's alignment-free similarity measure is the wrong tool If reads need no ambiguity-code handling and a lightweight scan of only da(S) suffices, the document-array variant avoids requiring fileFasta.ebwt http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 LiME's first similarity-measure variant (ClusterBWT_DA compiled with EBWT=1) counts symbol matches between each metagenomic read and each reference genome within alpha-clusters, treating IUPAC ambiguity codes as matching themselves or any concrete nucleotide letter associated with the code, instead of considering them placeholders. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03628-w
skills.summary: LiME's first similarity-measure variant (ClusterBWT_DA compiled with EBWT=1) counts symbol matches between each metagenomic read and each reference genome within alpha-clusters, treating IUPAC ambiguity codes as matching themselves or any concrete nucleotide letter associated with the code, instead of considering them placeholders.

skills.description: Use when reads have been assigned to viral genomes from nucleotide and translated alignments against Genbank gbvrl/gbphage and a genome's read set shows high non-unique read membership relative to larger sets, causing cross-genome ambiguity that would corrupt per-genome pileup assembly.
skills.name: jaccard-distance-genomic-read-set-filtering
skills.search_text: jaccard-distance-genomic-read-set-filtering Use when reads have been assigned to viral genomes from nucleotide and translated alignments against Genbank gbvrl/gbphage and a genome's read set shows high non-unique read membership relative to larger sets, causing cross-genome ambiguity that would corrupt per-genome pileup assembly. The goal is classification of individual reads or contigs by taxonomic scoring rather than removing cross-genome read-set ambiguity before per-genome assembly. Input has not yet been assigned to viral genomes via both nucleotide and translated alignments — the Jaccard filter operates on per-genome read sets, not raw FASTQ files. Viruses are absent from or under-represented in Genbank gbvrl/gbphage, since the mapping assembly (and hence this filter) depends on clustered alignments to that reference database. http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 VirMAP's intermediate filtering stage that drops genomically ambiguous read sets: after reads are assigned to viral genomes via nucleotide (BBMap) and translated (DIAMOND) alignments, read sets showing high numbers of non-unique read membership relative to larger sets are filtered by Jaccard distance before naive pileup assembly and super-scaffold construction. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: VirMAP's intermediate filtering stage that drops genomically ambiguous read sets: after reads are assigned to viral genomes via nucleotide (BBMap) and translated (DIAMOND) alignments, read sets showing high numbers of non-unique read membership relative to larger sets are filtered by Jaccard distance before naive pileup assembly and super-scaffold construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is classification of individual reads or contigs by taxonomic scoring rather than removing cross-genome read-set ambiguity before per-genome assembly. Input has not yet been assigned to viral genomes via both nucleotide and translated alignments — the Jaccard filter operates on per-genome read sets, not raw FASTQ files. Viruses are absent from or under-represented in Genbank gbvrl/gbphage, since the mapping assembly (and hence this filter) depends on clustered alignments to that reference database.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify concordance between two or more read-level metagenomic classifiers by comparing their classified-read sets with Jaccard similarity and per-tool missed-read tallies.

skills.summary: Computes Jaccard-based agreement rates between the sets of classified reads produced by different metagenomic classifiers (LiME vs Magic-BLAST, CLARK-S, Centrifuge, Kraken 2, TaxMaps) on the BLAST-filtered HMP real metagenome SRR1804065, reproducing Table S5-style concordance values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating classification accuracy against known ground truth on simulated metagenomes (e.g. setA2/setB2 from the Lindgreen et al. benchmark), where sensitivity/precision/F1/specificity metrics are the appropriate evaluation The input is raw unfiltered reads or taxon-abundance profiles rather than per-read classification outputs with read identifiers Comparing tools run on different reference databases or differently filtered inputs — set overlap is then confounded by preprocessing differences
