skills.summary: Maps length- and CSS-normalized gene frequencies to the KEGG database within the CAMAMED pipeline to extract functional annotations at KEGG ortholog (KO) group, EC number and reaction levels, then aggregates normalized gene values per functional category for downstream differential analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a functional abundance table (KO/EC/reaction profiles) — re-normalizing aggregated values would double-correct compositional bias; normalization must be done at the gene level first No appropriate gene catalog or KEGG annotation is available — the article notes mapping-based methods are preferred only when appropriate gene catalogs exist; otherwise assembly-based approaches are needed The goal is purely taxonomic profiling with no functional interpretation — use the taxon-level (e.g. MetaPhlAn2) branch of CAMAMED instead

skills.description: Use when PICRUSt-predicted KO metagenome tables from 16S data must be aggregated to KEGG module abundances and statistically compared between sample groups (e.g., supragingival vs subgingival plaque, menses vs rest of cycle).
skills.name: kegg-module-abundance-quantification
skills.search_text: kegg-module-abundance-quantification Use when PICRUSt-predicted KO metagenome tables from 16S data must be aggregated to KEGG module abundances and statistically compared between sample groups (e.g., supragingival vs subgingival plaque, menses vs rest of cycle). Input is raw 16S reads or an unnormalized OTU table that has not yet been processed by PICRUSt (no 16S copy-number normalization, no KO prediction, no NSTI values). The goal is strain-level or viral/eukaryotic functional inference — PICRUSt only covers bacterial and archaeal marker genes and cannot distinguish strains with identical marker sequences. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Collapses PICRUSt-predicted KEGG Ortholog (KO) abundances to KEGG module level (e.g., M00009 citrate cycle, M00240 iron complex transport) and compares module abundances across body sites or time points using Welch's t-test with Bonferroni correction in STAMP v2.0. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Collapses PICRUSt-predicted KEGG Ortholog (KO) abundances to KEGG module level (e.g., M00009 citrate cycle, M00240 iron complex transport) and compares module abundances across body sites or time points using Welch's t-test with Bonferroni correction in STAMP v2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw 16S reads or an unnormalized OTU table that has not yet been processed by PICRUSt (no 16S copy-number normalization, no KO prediction, no NSTI values). The goal is strain-level or viral/eukaryotic functional inference — PICRUSt only covers bacterial and archaeal marker genes and cannot distinguish strains with identical marker sequences.

skills.description: Use when evaluating microbial genome or MAG functional potential via KEGG Modules and needing to compare block-level Module completeness across KEMET, KEGG Mapper, and METABOLIC v4.0.
skills.name: kegg-module-block-partitioning-comparison
skills.search_text: kegg-module-block-partitioning-comparison Use when evaluating microbial genome or MAG functional potential via KEGG Modules and needing to compare block-level Module completeness across KEMET, KEGG Mapper, and METABOLIC v4.0. Input is raw sequence without prior KO annotation and only Module completeness is needed — gene calling with Prodigal v2.6.3 and annotation with eggNOG-mapper v2 must be done first The goal is HMM-based recovery of missing KOs or GSMM gapfilling rather than Module completeness comparison — use KEMET's --hmm_mode or --gsmm_mode workflows instead of --skip_hmm A single-tool completeness report suffices with no cross-tool benchmarking required http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Benchmark how KEMET partitions KEGG Modules into blocks and computes Module completeness against KEGG Mapper and METABOLIC v4.0 across genomes, verifying that KEMET captures more Modules and its block structure more closely resembles the original KEGG Module structure. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Benchmark how KEMET partitions KEGG Modules into blocks and computes Module completeness against KEGG Mapper and METABOLIC v4.0 across genomes, verifying that KEMET captures more Modules and its block structure more closely resembles the original KEGG Module structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequence without prior KO annotation and only Module completeness is needed — gene calling with Prodigal v2.6.3 and annotation with eggNOG-mapper v2 must be done first The goal is HMM-based recovery of missing KOs or GSMM gapfilling rather than Module completeness comparison — use KEMET's --hmm_mode or --gsmm_mode workflows instead of --skip_hmm A single-tool completeness report suffices with no cross-tool benchmarking required

skills.description: Use when predicted or observed gene family annotations (KOs, COGs) must be aggregated into higher-level functional categories via KEGG Modules or BRITE, or when per-category accuracy of gene-content predictions is required.
skills.name: kegg-module-brite-functional-category-mapping
skills.search_text: kegg-module-brite-functional-category-mapping Use when predicted or observed gene family annotations (KOs, COGs) must be aggregated into higher-level functional categories via KEGG Modules or BRITE, or when per-category accuracy of gene-content predictions is required. Input is raw 16S OTU abundance data that has not yet been converted to predicted gene family content via PICRUSt (normalize by 16S copy number and predict KOs first) The analysis targets viral or eukaryotic metagenome components, since PICRUSt only includes bacterial and archaeal genomes Strain-level functional variation is the question of interest, since predictions cannot distinguish strains with identical marker gene sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Maps predicted and observed KO/COG gene content through KEGG Modules and the KEGG BRITE functional hierarchy to higher-level functional categories, enabling per-category comparison of predicted versus actual gene content (e.g., genome holdout accuracy by functional category). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Maps predicted and observed KO/COG gene content through KEGG Modules and the KEGG BRITE functional hierarchy to higher-level functional categories, enabling per-category comparison of predicted versus actual gene content (e.g., genome holdout accuracy by functional category).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw 16S OTU abundance data that has not yet been converted to predicted gene family content via PICRUSt (normalize by 16S copy number and predict KOs first) The analysis targets viral or eukaryotic metagenome components, since PICRUSt only includes bacterial and archaeal genomes Strain-level functional variation is the question of interest, since predictions cannot distinguish strains with identical marker gene sequences

skills.description: Use when you have a FASTA genome/MAG plus a KEGG KO annotation file (eggNOG/kaas/kofamkoala format) and need Module-level completeness tables or a comparison of Module block partitioning across KEMET, KEGG Mapper, and METABOLIC.
skills.name: kegg-module-completeness-evaluation
skills.search_text: kegg-module-completeness-evaluation Use when you have a FASTA genome/MAG plus a KEGG KO annotation file (eggNOG/kaas/kofamkoala format) and need Module-level completeness tables or a comparison of Module block partitioning across KEMET, KEGG Mapper, and METABOLIC. You need HMM-based recovery of missing KOs or GSMM gapfilling — skip this completeness-only mode and instead run kemet.py without --skip_hmm (or with --hmm_mode onebm/module/kos). Input is raw sequence without KEGG KO annotations and you do not want to run an annotator (eggNOG-mapper/kaas/kofamkoala) first — kemet.py requires an existing KO annotation format. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Evaluate KEGG Module completeness for a microbial genome or MAG by running KEMET's kemet.py, which parses KEGG orthology annotations (e.g. eggNOG .emapper.annotations) into Module block structures and produces organized recap tables of metabolic potential. Also supports benchmarking Module partitioning against KEGG Mapper and METABOLIC v4.0. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Evaluate KEGG Module completeness for a microbial genome or MAG by running KEMET's kemet.py, which parses KEGG orthology annotations (e.g. eggNOG .emapper.annotations) into Module block structures and produces organized recap tables of metabolic potential. Also supports benchmarking Module partitioning against KEGG Mapper and METABOLIC v4.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need HMM-based recovery of missing KOs or GSMM gapfilling — skip this completeness-only mode and instead run kemet.py without --skip_hmm (or with --hmm_mode onebm/module/kos). Input is raw sequence without KEGG KO annotations and you do not want to run an annotator (eggNOG-mapper/kaas/kofamkoala) first — kemet.py requires an existing KO annotation format.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate an annotation-expansion tool (e.g., KEMET) by removing known KOs from eggNOG-mapper .emapper.annotations files and measuring recovery rates from FASTA sequences.
skills.name: kegg-ortholog-annotation-removal
skills.search_text: kegg-ortholog-annotation-removal Use when you need to quantitatively validate an annotation-expansion tool (e.g., KEMET) by removing known KOs from eggNOG-mapper .emapper.annotations files and measuring recovery rates from FASTA sequences. Your goal is KEGG Module completeness evaluation only — use KEMET with --skip_hmm rather than running mock-removal HMM searches The annotation files were produced by tools other than the supported KEGG KO annotation formats (eggnog / kaas / kofamkoala) with their default file extensions You need to test recovery from truncated sequences but your input FASTA contains full-length genes only — the 30%/70% truncation variant requires explicit sequence deletion simulation http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 A benchmarking skill that mock-removes KEGG ortholog (KO) annotations from eggNOG-mapper results and tests whether KEMET's HMM search (--hmm_mode onebm) correctly recovers the removed genes and annotations, yielding true positive rates for annotation expansion. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that mock-removes KEGG ortholog (KO) annotations from eggNOG-mapper results and tests whether KEMET's HMM search (--hmm_mode onebm) correctly recovers the removed genes and annotations, yielding true positive rates for annotation expansion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is KEGG Module completeness evaluation only — use KEMET with --skip_hmm rather than running mock-removal HMM searches The annotation files were produced by tools other than the supported KEGG KO annotation formats (eggnog / kaas / kofamkoala) with their default file extensions You need to test recovery from truncated sequences but your input FASTA contains full-length genes only — the 30%/70% truncation variant requires explicit sequence deletion simulation

skills.description: Use when mapping-based metagenomic count data (case-control design) has genes mapped to KEGG KO groups, EC numbers, and reactions, and you need to decide whether functional-level differential analysis outperforms gene-level testing at a fixed significance threshold.
skills.name: kegg-ortholog-ec-reaction-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: kegg-ortholog-ec-reaction-enrichment-analysis Use when mapping-based metagenomic count data (case-control design) has genes mapped to KEGG KO groups, EC numbers, and reactions, and you need to decide whether functional-level differential analysis outperforms gene-level testing at a fixed significance threshold. The goal is taxonomic profiling only — this skill addresses functional (KO/EC/reaction) differential analysis, not the taxon-level output of CAMAMED. No appropriate gene catalog is available for mapping-based analysis (the paper prefers mapping-based methods only 'when appropriate gene catalogs are available'). Counts are raw/unnormalized and you intend to use conventional statistics — CSS normalization plus a compositional-data-aware model is required, otherwise results are compositional-biased. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Differential analysis of metagenomic data at KEGG functional levels (KO groups, EC numbers, reactions) rather than the individual gene level, quantifying the ratio of significant features at a fixed threshold (P ≤ 0.01) to show that functional annotation surfaces more signal above chance. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Differential analysis of metagenomic data at KEGG functional levels (KO groups, EC numbers, reactions) rather than the individual gene level, quantifying the ratio of significant features at a fixed threshold (P ≤ 0.01) to show that functional annotation surfaces more signal above chance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is taxonomic profiling only — this skill addresses functional (KO/EC/reaction) differential analysis, not the taxon-level output of CAMAMED. No appropriate gene catalog is available for mapping-based analysis (the paper prefers mapping-based methods only 'when appropriate gene catalogs are available'). Counts are raw/unnormalized and you intend to use conventional statistics — CSS normalization plus a compositional-data-aware model is required, otherwise results are compositional-biased.

skills.description: Use when a MAG or genome FASTA has incomplete KEGG Module blocks and unannotated genes that may be genuine KOs recoverable by profile HMM searches, especially for partial/truncated gene sequences.
skills.name: kegg-ortholog-hmm-search
skills.search_text: kegg-ortholog-hmm-search Use when a MAG or genome FASTA has incomplete KEGG Module blocks and unannotated genes that may be genuine KOs recoverable by profile HMM searches, especially for partial/truncated gene sequences. You only need KEGG Module completeness tables from existing annotation — use --skip_hmm instead of running HMM searches The genome already has complete, manually curated KO annotation and no missing orthologs are expected Working with poor-quality MAGs below the >=90% completeness / <=5% contamination screening used in the paper's validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Searches for missing KEGG orthologs (KOs) in MAGs/genomes using nhmmer profile HMM searches in KEMET's --hmm_mode onebm, filtering candidate hits with a score-per-length threshold (default 0.43) to expand KEGG Module completeness evaluation beyond initial eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKoala annotation. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Searches for missing KEGG orthologs (KOs) in MAGs/genomes using nhmmer profile HMM searches in KEMET's --hmm_mode onebm, filtering candidate hits with a score-per-length threshold (default 0.43) to expand KEGG Module completeness evaluation beyond initial eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKoala annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need KEGG Module completeness tables from existing annotation — use --skip_hmm instead of running HMM searches The genome already has complete, manually curated KO annotation and no missing orthologs are expected Working with poor-quality MAGs below the >=90% completeness / <=5% contamination screening used in the paper's validation

skills.description: Use when you have a corrected KO abundance table from shotgun metagenomes and need higher-level KEGG pathway/module functional profiles rather than ortholog-level abundances.
skills.name: kegg-ortholog-pathway-aggregation
skills.search_text: kegg-ortholog-pathway-aggregation Use when you have a corrected KO abundance table from shotgun metagenomes and need higher-level KEGG pathway/module functional profiles rather than ortholog-level abundances. Input is raw gene or read counts that have not yet been mapped to KOs and corrected with MUSiCC — run the ortholog counting and correction steps first. You need taxonomic profiles or species-level functional stratification — EMPANADA aggregation is purely KO-to-KEGG-category summarization. Your target categories are not KEGG modules/pathways (e.g. UniRef90-based or eggNOG functional classes) — the mapping files used here are KEGG BRITE-derived. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Aggregates MUSiCC-corrected KEGG ortholog (KO) abundances into KEGG module- and pathway-level functional profiles using EMPANADA, weighted by the supporting evidence for each higher-level category. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: Aggregates MUSiCC-corrected KEGG ortholog (KO) abundances into KEGG module- and pathway-level functional profiles using EMPANADA, weighted by the supporting evidence for each higher-level category.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw gene or read counts that have not yet been mapped to KOs and corrected with MUSiCC — run the ortholog counting and correction steps first. You need taxonomic profiles or species-level functional stratification — EMPANADA aggregation is purely KO-to-KEGG-category summarization. Your target categories are not KEGG modules/pathways (e.g. UniRef90-based or eggNOG functional classes) — the mapping files used here are KEGG BRITE-derived.

skills.description: Use when a MAG or isolate genome has KEGG KO annotations (eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKOALA format) and you need to convert them into metabolic reactions for GSMM reconstruction or evidence-based gapfilling, especially after HMM-based KO recovery.
skills.name: kegg-ortholog-to-reaction-mapping
skills.search_text: kegg-ortholog-to-reaction-mapping Use when a MAG or isolate genome has KEGG KO annotations (eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKOALA format) and you need to convert them into metabolic reactions for GSMM reconstruction or evidence-based gapfilling, especially after HMM-based KO recovery. Input is already a reconstructed GSMM that needs no additional KO evidence — network gap-filling without genomic support risks erroneous predictions The goal is only KEGG Module completeness summarization without model reconstruction — use --skip_gsmm or a Module evaluation tool alone Annotations come from a format other than eggnog/kaas/kofamkoala, which KEMET's -a flag does not parse http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Maps KEGG ortholog (KO) annotations — including KOs recovered via HMM profile searches with KEMET — onto BiGG/ModelSEED reactions to gapfill or reconstruct genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs/GEMs) from MAGs or genomes, improving metabolic phenotype prediction. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Maps KEGG ortholog (KO) annotations — including KOs recovered via HMM profile searches with KEMET — onto BiGG/ModelSEED reactions to gapfill or reconstruct genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs/GEMs) from MAGs or genomes, improving metabolic phenotype prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a reconstructed GSMM that needs no additional KO evidence — network gap-filling without genomic support risks erroneous predictions The goal is only KEGG Module completeness summarization without model reconstruction — use --skip_gsmm or a Module evaluation tool alone Annotations come from a format other than eggnog/kaas/kofamkoala, which KEMET's -a flag does not parse

skills.description: Use when you have a per-sample gene abundance table and a many-to-many gene-to-KEGG-KO (or other ortholog) mapping file, and need a KO-level functional profile without double-counting multiply-annotated genes.
skills.name: kegg-orthology-annotation
skills.search_text: kegg-orthology-annotation Use when you have a per-sample gene abundance table and a many-to-many gene-to-KEGG-KO (or other ortholog) mapping file, and need a KO-level functional profile without double-counting multiply-annotated genes. Input is already an ortholog-level abundance table — the correction would re-split already aggregated counts. You need reads-to-ortholog annotation from scratch — this step operates downstream of read mapping (DIAMOND to UniRef90) and gene counting; run those first. Your mapping is one-to-one gene-to-ortholog only and you want unadjusted summed counts rather than fractional correction. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstructs MetaLAFFA's ortholog counting step, which converts per-sample gene abundance tables (gene-length normalized *.norm) into KEGG orthology group (KO) abundances by fractionally splitting each gene's abundance across all KOs it maps to, avoiding double-counting in many-to-many gene-to-ortholog mappings. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: Reconstructs MetaLAFFA's ortholog counting step, which converts per-sample gene abundance tables (gene-length normalized *.norm) into KEGG orthology group (KO) abundances by fractionally splitting each gene's abundance across all KOs it maps to, avoiding double-counting in many-to-many gene-to-ortholog mappings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an ortholog-level abundance table — the correction would re-split already aggregated counts. You need reads-to-ortholog annotation from scratch — this step operates downstream of read mapping (DIAMOND to UniRef90) and gene counting; run those first. Your mapping is one-to-one gene-to-ortholog only and you want unadjusted summed counts rather than fractional correction.

skills.description: Use when a non-redundant gene catalog has already been read-mapped to produce per-sample gene frequencies, and the analysis goal is functional profiling beyond the gene level at KO, EC number and reaction levels.
skills.name: kegg-orthology-annotation-of-mapped-genes
skills.search_text: kegg-orthology-annotation-of-mapped-genes Use when a non-redundant gene catalog has already been read-mapped to produce per-sample gene frequencies, and the analysis goal is functional profiling beyond the gene level at KO, EC number and reaction levels. The analysis goal is only taxonomic profiling (handled by the MetaPhlAn2-based taxon level of CAMAMED, not KEGG annotation). No pre-built gene catalog or upstream gene frequency table exists — assembly-based functional profiling (assemble reads to contigs, then predict gene content) would be needed instead. The data is already annotated at KO, EC and reaction levels; re-running KAAS/GhostKOALA against KEGG would be redundant. http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 Annotates genes from a mapping-based metagenomic gene catalog to the KEGG universe: assigns KO groups via KAAS/GhostKOALA, resolves KO → EC number → reaction chains, and aggregates per-sample gene frequencies upward so every sample receives frequencies at gene, KO, EC and reaction levels. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Annotates genes from a mapping-based metagenomic gene catalog to the KEGG universe: assigns KO groups via KAAS/GhostKOALA, resolves KO → EC number → reaction chains, and aggregates per-sample gene frequencies upward so every sample receives frequencies at gene, KO, EC and reaction levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is only taxonomic profiling (handled by the MetaPhlAn2-based taxon level of CAMAMED, not KEGG annotation). No pre-built gene catalog or upstream gene frequency table exists — assembly-based functional profiling (assemble reads to contigs, then predict gene content) would be needed instead. The data is already annotated at KO, EC and reaction levels; re-running KAAS/GhostKOALA against KEGG would be redundant.

skills.description: Use when you already have KO-annotated genes for a genome or MAG in eggnog/kaas/kofamkoala format and need KEGG Module completeness summaries, or need the KEGG-Mapper INCOMPLETE convention (Modules with <3 blocks) for cross-tool comparison.
skills.name: kegg-orthology-annotation-processing
skills.search_text: kegg-orthology-annotation-processing Use when you already have KO-annotated genes for a genome or MAG in eggnog/kaas/kofamkoala format and need KEGG Module completeness summaries, or need the KEGG-Mapper INCOMPLETE convention (Modules with <3 blocks) for cross-tool comparison. When the goal is de novo gene calling or functional annotation from raw sequences — gene calling with Prodigal v2.6.3 and annotation with eggNOG-mapper v2 happen upstream of this skill. When you need to recover missing KOs via HMM profile searches or gapfill a GSMM — those require the --hmm_mode or --gsmm_mode stages rather than the completeness-evaluation-only path. When the input has no KEGG orthology annotations at all (KEMET requires a KO annotation file or its own HMM pipeline to assign KOs). http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Ingest pre-computed KEGG orthology (KO) annotations — from eggNOG-Mapper (.emapper.annotations), KAAS, or KofamKOALA (.ko) formats — and process them with KEMET to produce organized KEGG Module completeness recap tables (modules_completeness_recap.tsv) summarizing metabolic potential. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Ingest pre-computed KEGG orthology (KO) annotations — from eggNOG-Mapper (.emapper.annotations), KAAS, or KofamKOALA (.ko) formats — and process them with KEMET to produce organized KEGG Module completeness recap tables (modules_completeness_recap.tsv) summarizing metabolic potential.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo gene calling or functional annotation from raw sequences — gene calling with Prodigal v2.6.3 and annotation with eggNOG-mapper v2 happen upstream of this skill. When you need to recover missing KOs via HMM profile searches or gapfill a GSMM — those require the --hmm_mode or --gsmm_mode stages rather than the completeness-evaluation-only path. When the input has no KEGG orthology annotations at all (KEMET requires a KO annotation file or its own HMM pipeline to assign KOs).

skills.description: Use when a ggpicrust2 differential abundance (DA) results table carries KO-level or raw KEGG pathway identifiers and needs pathway_name, pathway_description, pathway_class, and pathway_map joined from the KEGG database.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-annotation
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-annotation Use when a ggpicrust2 differential abundance (DA) results table carries KO-level or raw KEGG pathway identifiers and needs pathway_name, pathway_description, pathway_class, and pathway_map joined from the KEGG database. The input is a raw KO abundance table or 16S rRNA feature table with no DA statistics — annotation operates on DA results, not abundance matrices (use pathway_daa() first). The table already carries pathway_name/description/class fields — re-annotating adds redundant KEGG REST queries without changing the DA statistics. The analysis goal is differential abundance testing itself (e.g. choosing between camera, ALDEx2, DESeq2, Maaslin2 methods) rather than interpreting or labeling existing DA output. http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 ggpicrust2::pathway_annotation() enriches PICRUSt2 differential abundance (DA) results with KEGG reference annotation — pathway_name, pathway_description, pathway_class, and pathway_map — optionally converting KO-level feature identifiers to KEGG pathway-level identifiers via ko_to_kegg = TRUE. It turns a bare statistics table into a readable, pathway-level table ready for visualization. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad470
skills.summary: ggpicrust2::pathway_annotation() enriches PICRUSt2 differential abundance (DA) results with KEGG reference annotation — pathway_name, pathway_description, pathway_class, and pathway_map — optionally converting KO-level feature identifiers to KEGG pathway-level identifiers via ko_to_kegg = TRUE. It turns a bare statistics table into a readable, pathway-level table ready for visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw KO abundance table or 16S rRNA feature table with no DA statistics — annotation operates on DA results, not abundance matrices (use pathway_daa() first). The table already carries pathway_name/description/class fields — re-annotating adds redundant KEGG REST queries without changing the DA statistics. The analysis goal is differential abundance testing itself (e.g. choosing between camera, ALDEx2, DESeq2, Maaslin2 methods) rather than interpreting or labeling existing DA output.

skills.description: Use when you have PICRUSt2 KO abundance features and need pathway-level gene sets (e.g. for ggpicrust2 pathway_gsea()) rather than single-feature differential abundance testing.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-set-construction
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-set-construction Use when you have PICRUSt2 KO abundance features and need pathway-level gene sets (e.g. for ggpicrust2 pathway_gsea()) rather than single-feature differential abundance testing. Input is already a pathway-level abundance table rather than KO-level features, and single-feature differential abundance analysis is the goal Only one comparison group or a design with no contrasts is available, so no enrichment contrast can be defined Pathway sets cannot reach the minimum size threshold (fewer than 5 features), leaving no valid gene sets to test http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Constructs KEGG pathway gene sets from PICRUSt2-predicted KO abundance features so that gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) can test whole pathways instead of individual features, using ggpicrust2's pathway-to-gene-set mapping with size filtering. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad470
skills.summary: Constructs KEGG pathway gene sets from PICRUSt2-predicted KO abundance features so that gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) can test whole pathways instead of individual features, using ggpicrust2's pathway-to-gene-set mapping with size filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pathway-level abundance table rather than KO-level features, and single-feature differential abundance analysis is the goal Only one comparison group or a design with no contrasts is available, so no enrichment contrast can be defined Pathway sets cannot reach the minimum size threshold (fewer than 5 features), leaving no valid gene sets to test

skills.description: Use when a DESeq2 differential expression table or ranked gene list has produced significant KEGG pathways via ClusterProfShinyORA or ClusterProfShinyGSEA and the next step is to visualize those enriched pathways as KEGG pathway plots.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-visualization
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-visualization Use when a DESeq2 differential expression table or ranked gene list has produced significant KEGG pathways via ClusterProfShinyORA or ClusterProfShinyGSEA and the next step is to visualize those enriched pathways as KEGG pathway plots. Input is raw gene count files rather than a DE results table with Gene name/id, Log2 Fold Change, and p-adjusted columns — preprocess first (e.g. GeneCountMerger, then DESeq2Shiny) before enrichment visualization. Enrichment targets only Gene Ontology terms with no KEGG pathway analysis — Pathview KEGG plots apply to KEGG pathways, while GO visuals (goplot, cnetplot, induced graphs) are the appropriate outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Render enriched KEGG pathway plots for significant KEGG pathways identified by NASQAR's ClusterProfilerShiny ORA/GSEA apps, which wrap the clusterProfiler R package, using the Pathview package to overlay DESeq2-derived genes and log2 fold changes onto KEGG pathway maps. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03577-4
skills.summary: Render enriched KEGG pathway plots for significant KEGG pathways identified by NASQAR's ClusterProfilerShiny ORA/GSEA apps, which wrap the clusterProfiler R package, using the Pathview package to overlay DESeq2-derived genes and log2 fold changes onto KEGG pathway maps.

skills.description: Use when you need all-vs-all pairwise distance matrices between many metagenomic (or viromic) FASTA/FASTQ samples based on k-mer composition and abundance, especially when datasets are too large for sketch-based or normalization-dependent tools.
skills.name: kmer-abundance-distance-computation
skills.search_text: kmer-abundance-distance-computation Use when you need all-vs-all pairwise distance matrices between many metagenomic (or viromic) FASTA/FASTQ samples based on k-mer composition and abundance, especially when datasets are too large for sketch-based or normalization-dependent tools. Inputs are assembled contigs rather than reads — the paper's HMP WGS assembled-contig comparison (Fig. S3) shows Libra in REDUCE mode with reduced resolution and Simka collapsing to maximum distances when abundance cannot be measured from reads You need an exact reference-based taxonomic assignment rather than an unsupervised sample-to-sample distance matrix Datasets are small enough that a non-distributed tool suffices — Libra's Hadoop preprocessing/scoring stack adds setup overhead not justified for a handful of samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Compute all-vs-all metagenomic pairwise distances from k-mer abundance counts using Libra, a Hadoop-based tool that applies Cosine Similarity over full-read k-mer profiles with selectable weighting (LOGARITHM, NATURAL, BOOLEAN) and scoring (COSINESIMILARITY, BRAYCURTIS, JENSENSHANNON) algorithms. This skill covers the two-stage Libra pipeline (preprocess indexing followed by core scoring) that avoids the resolution loss caused by sketching, read-count normalization, or presence/absence metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Compute all-vs-all metagenomic pairwise distances from k-mer abundance counts using Libra, a Hadoop-based tool that applies Cosine Similarity over full-read k-mer profiles with selectable weighting (LOGARITHM, NATURAL, BOOLEAN) and scoring (COSINESIMILARITY, BRAYCURTIS, JENSENSHANNON) algorithms. You deliberately want simple relative abundances instead of copy-number-per-genome normalization (set the method parameter to 'relative'). Data are not shotgun metagenomic samples with a bacterial gene-content signal (e.g., 16S amplicon or single-isolate RNA-seq), where single-copy-gene normalization is not applicable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 In MetaLAFFA's functional annotation phase, gene-level counts mapped to KEGG orthology groups (KOs) are corrected with MUSiCC, which by default converts ortholog read counts into average copy number per genome per sample rather than leaving raw or relative abundances. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: In MetaLAFFA's functional annotation phase, gene-level counts mapped to KEGG orthology groups (KOs) are corrected with MUSiCC, which by default converts ortholog read counts into average copy number per genome per sample rather than leaving raw or relative abundances.

skills.description: Use when building a Kraken/MiniKraken k-mer database from reference genomes for taxonomic classification of metagenomic reads, or when comparing full versus shrunk databases in accuracy benchmarks.
skills.name: kraken-database-construction-lca-kmers
skills.search_text: kraken-database-construction-lca-kmers Use when building a Kraken/MiniKraken k-mer database from reference genomes for taxonomic classification of metagenomic reads, or when comparing full versus shrunk databases in accuracy benchmarks. Input is raw sequencing reads needing classification — use the built database with the Kraken classifier, not this construction workflow Abundance estimation is the goal and only a small percentage of reads need labels — abundance programs like MetaPhlAn are faster and more appropriate Reference genomes are unavailable or the study targets taxa absent from RefSeq/GenBank, since accuracy depends on the sequenced genomes in the database http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Constructs a Kraken taxonomic classification database by counting k-mers from complete RefSeq microbial genomes with Jellyfish and overwriting the 4-byte count spaces with LCA taxonomic IDs derived from the NCBI taxonomy. This LCA-labeled k-mer store is the foundation for Kraken's exact-match, minimizer-indexed classification and its reduced-memory MiniKraken variant. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Constructs a Kraken taxonomic classification database by counting k-mers from complete RefSeq microbial genomes with Jellyfish and overwriting the 4-byte count spaces with LCA taxonomic IDs derived from the NCBI taxonomy. This LCA-labeled k-mer store is the foundation for Kraken's exact-match, minimizer-indexed classification and its reduced-memory MiniKraken variant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads needing classification — use the built database with the Kraken classifier, not this construction workflow Abundance estimation is the goal and only a small percentage of reads need labels — abundance programs like MetaPhlAn are faster and more appropriate Reference genomes are unavailable or the study targets taxa absent from RefSeq/GenBank, since accuracy depends on the sequenced genomes in the database

skills.description: Use when you need an empirical P-value for similarity between two phylogenetic trees (or labeled structures) where no analytic null exists — e.g., testing if a de novo tree derived from synteny distances matches a reference classification tree.
skills.name: label-shuffle-significance-testing
skills.search_text: label-shuffle-significance-testing Use when you need an empirical P-value for similarity between two phylogenetic trees (or labeled structures) where no analytic null exists — e.g., testing if a de novo tree derived from synteny distances matches a reference classification tree. When an analytic null distribution or standard parametric test is available and appropriate for the statistic being compared. skills.name: linclust-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: linclust-parameter-configuration Use when a task requires clustering very large protein or nucleotide FASTA sets (billions of sequences) at a defined sequence identity and coverage threshold, or reproducing/re-verifying a reported Linclust/MMseqs2 clustering result. When exact clustering of every pair is required — Linclust's k-mer prefilter and hashing-based key selection are approximate; falsely clustered pairs are not verified beyond the exact-distance edge verification, which alone would be quadratic When the dataset is small enough that traditional tools like CD-HIT (run with -n 5 -c 0.9, -n 4 -c 0.7, -n 3 -c 0.5) suffice and quality differences matter When items cannot be assigned a set of m keys per item satisfying the shared-key condition, since Linclust's generalization requires such keys http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 Configure MMseqs2's Linclust to cluster huge protein sequence sets in linear time using its k-mer prefilter pipeline; this skill encodes the paper's concrete parameters (e.g. --min-seq-id 0.5 --cov-mode 1 -c 0.9) and validation workflow for reproducing clustering results such as the 424-million-cluster Metaclust run. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-04964-5
skills.summary: Configure MMseqs2's Linclust to cluster huge protein sequence sets in linear time using its k-mer prefilter pipeline; this skill encodes the paper's concrete parameters (e.g. --min-seq-id 0.5 --cov-mode 1 -c 0.9) and validation workflow for reproducing clustering results such as the 424-million-cluster Metaclust run.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When exact clustering of every pair is required — Linclust's k-mer prefilter and hashing-based key selection are approximate; falsely clustered pairs are not verified beyond the exact-distance edge verification, which alone would be quadratic When the dataset is small enough that traditional tools like CD-HIT (run with -n 5 -c 0.9, -n 4 -c 0.7, -n 3 -c 0.5) suffice and quality differences matter When items cannot be assigned a set of m keys per item satisfying the shared-key condition, since Linclust's generalization requires such keys

skills.description: Use when a two-group comparison of PICRUSt2-predicted KO/KEGG pathway abundances (e.g., prosurvival vs proinflammatory fecal-transplant groups) must be tested for significant differential pathways with a compositional DA method like LinDA.
skills.name: linda-compositional-differential-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: linda-compositional-differential-abundance-analysis Use when a two-group comparison of PICRUSt2-predicted KO/KEGG pathway abundances (e.g., prosurvival vs proinflammatory fecal-transplant groups) must be tested for significant differential pathways with a compositional DA method like LinDA. Input is raw 16S rRNA reads or OTU/ASV tables — PICRUSt2 functional prediction and KO-to-pathway conversion must precede LinDA testing. The goal is taxa-level (not pathway-level) differential abundance of the sequencing data itself rather than predicted functional profiles. Only single-group or paired longitudinal designs are present — LinDA here is applied to between-group comparisons defined in the metadata. http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Differential abundance analysis of PICRUSt2-predicted KEGG pathway profiles using the LinDA method implemented in the ggpicrust2 R package, as demonstrated on C9orf72 mouse 16S rRNA data where LinDA identified ko05016 and ko05012 as significantly different between transplantation groups. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad470
skills.summary: Differential abundance analysis of PICRUSt2-predicted KEGG pathway profiles using the LinDA method implemented in the ggpicrust2 R package, as demonstrated on C9orf72 mouse 16S rRNA data where LinDA identified ko05016 and ko05012 as significantly different between transplantation groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw 16S rRNA reads or OTU/ASV tables — PICRUSt2 functional prediction and KO-to-pathway conversion must precede LinDA testing. The goal is taxa-level (not pathway-level) differential abundance of the sequencing data itself rather than predicted functional profiles. Only single-group or paired longitudinal designs are present — LinDA here is applied to between-group comparisons defined in the metadata.

skills.description: Use when you have a PICRUSt2 predicted pathway abundance table plus sample metadata with a grouping variable and need log-linear-model-based differential abundance testing of pathways between comparison groups.
skills.name: linda-log-linear-da-testing
skills.search_text: linda-log-linear-da-testing Use when you have a PICRUSt2 predicted pathway abundance table plus sample metadata with a grouping variable and need log-linear-model-based differential abundance testing of pathways between comparison groups. The goal is gene-set-level enrichment rather than single-pathway testing — use pathway_gsea() (camera/fry) instead You need ANCOM or ANCOMBC — ggpicrust2's pathway_daa() explicitly excludes these methods Input is raw KO-level abundance without prior conversion to pathway-level abundance http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Apply LinDA (log-linear model-based differential abundance) to PICRUSt2-predicted KEGG pathway abundance tables via ggpicrust2's pathway_daa(), producing per-pathway p-values and adjusted p-values for group comparisons. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad470
skills.summary: Apply LinDA (log-linear model-based differential abundance) to PICRUSt2-predicted KEGG pathway abundance tables via ggpicrust2's pathway_daa(), producing per-pathway p-values and adjusted p-values for group comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene-set-level enrichment rather than single-pathway testing — use pathway_gsea() (camera/fry) instead You need ANCOM or ANCOMBC — ggpicrust2's pathway_daa() explicitly excludes these methods Input is raw KO-level abundance without prior conversion to pathway-level abundance

skills.description: Use when NGS variant calls from wastewater or clinical samples must be assigned to SARS-CoV-2 lineages and converted into per-sample lineage-abundance estimates to track variant dynamics over time (e.g., the rise of B.1.1.7).
skills.name: lineage-mutation-profile-matching
skills.search_text: lineage-mutation-profile-matching Use when NGS variant calls from wastewater or clinical samples must be assigned to SARS-CoV-2 lineages and converted into per-sample lineage-abundance estimates to track variant dynamics over time (e.g., the rise of B.1.1.7). Input is raw FASTQ without prior variant calling — lineagespot requires variant(s) file(s) (VCF), not raw reads Goal is consensus whole-genome lineage assignment of a single high-coverage isolate — use Pangolin directly instead of wastewater read-profile matching Samples lack sufficient depth for low-frequency (< 0.01) variant detection, e.g., heavily decayed wastewater RNA http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 A lineagespot-based R workflow that scores sample variant calls (VCF-derived amino acid substitutions) against lineage-characteristic mutation profiles (Pangolin rules / outbreak.info definitions) to infer SARS-CoV-2 lineage abundances in wastewater. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: A lineagespot-based R workflow that scores sample variant calls (VCF-derived amino acid substitutions) against lineage-characteristic mutation profiles (Pangolin rules / outbreak.info definitions) to infer SARS-CoV-2 lineage abundances in wastewater.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ without prior variant calling — lineagespot requires variant(s) file(s) (VCF), not raw reads Goal is consensus whole-genome lineage assignment of a single high-coverage isolate — use Pangolin directly instead of wastewater read-profile matching Samples lack sufficient depth for low-frequency (< 0.01) variant detection, e.g., heavily decayed wastewater RNA

skills.description: Use when a FASTQ wastewater (or similar) SARS-CoV-2 sample has been mapped and multiple variant-caller VCFs exist, and you must quantify Nt mutations per lineage to compare caller sensitivity or infer lineage composition.
skills.name: lineage-nucleotide-mutation-counting
skills.search_text: lineage-nucleotide-mutation-counting Use when a FASTQ wastewater (or similar) SARS-CoV-2 sample has been mapped and multiple variant-caller VCFs exist, and you must quantify Nt mutations per lineage to compare caller sensitivity or infer lineage composition. The input is already a per-lineage mutation count table or collapsed amino-acid substitution table — this skill operates on raw caller VCFs. You need amino-acid-level collapsed results (gene + amino acid substitution) for clustering rather than per-caller nucleotide mutation counting. The sequencing data are clinical isolates rather than low-frequency mixed wastewater populations, where a single standard caller suffices and caller comparison is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Counts unique lineage-characteristic nucleotide mutations (Nt) per SARS-CoV-2 lineage (e.g., B.1.177, B.1.1.7, B.1.351) by running the lineagespot R pipeline on VCFs from competing variant callers, enabling a side-by-side comparison that identified freebayes (low mutation frequency 0.01) as the most productive and informative tool. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: Counts unique lineage-characteristic nucleotide mutations (Nt) per SARS-CoV-2 lineage (e.g., B.1.177, B.1.1.7, B.1.351) by running the lineagespot R pipeline on VCFs from competing variant callers, enabling a side-by-side comparison that identified freebayes (low mutation frequency 0.01) as the most productive and informative tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a per-lineage mutation count table or collapsed amino-acid substitution table — this skill operates on raw caller VCFs. You need amino-acid-level collapsed results (gene + amino acid substitution) for clustering rather than per-caller nucleotide mutation counting. The sequencing data are clinical isolates rather than low-frequency mixed wastewater populations, where a single standard caller suffices and caller comparison is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when you need to convert a SARS-CoV-2 lineage definition (Pangolin rule or outbreak.info profile) into an evaluable rule vector against the NC_045512 reference, so VCF-derived variants can be scored for rule satisfaction per lineage.
skills.name: lineage-rule-vector-construction
skills.search_text: lineage-rule-vector-construction Use when you need to convert a SARS-CoV-2 lineage definition (Pangolin rule or outbreak.info profile) into an evaluable rule vector against the NC_045512 reference, so VCF-derived variants can be scored for rule satisfaction per lineage. Input is not variant call data (e.g., raw FASTQ reads) — reads must first be mapped to NC_045512 with Minimap2 and variant-called (e.g., freebayes) before rule evaluation The goal is whole-genome phylogenetic placement of a single high-coverage consensus genome, where standard Pangolin on a consensus FASTA is the established route rather than rule-satisfaction scoring of low-frequency wastewater variants http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Constructs the per-lineage rule vectors used by lineagespot to quantify how well sample mutations satisfy SARS-CoV-2 lineage definitions (e.g., Pangolin rules against reference genome NC_045512): one reference-base position entry per lineage-defining site plus inequality rules requiring observed bases to differ from the reference, with multi-allelic ALT fields split into separate rules. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: Constructs the per-lineage rule vectors used by lineagespot to quantify how well sample mutations satisfy SARS-CoV-2 lineage definitions (e.g., Pangolin rules against reference genome NC_045512): one reference-base position entry per lineage-defining site plus inequality rules requiring observed bases to differ from the reference, with multi-allelic ALT fields split into separate rules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not variant call data (e.g., raw FASTQ reads) — reads must first be mapped to NC_045512 with Minimap2 and variant-called (e.g., freebayes) before rule evaluation The goal is whole-genome phylogenetic placement of a single high-coverage consensus genome, where standard Pangolin on a consensus FASTA is the established route rather than rule-satisfaction scoring of low-frequency wastewater variants

skills.description: Use when NGS-derived variant calls (VCF) from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater samples must be converted into lineage-level inference, or when wastewater-inferred lineages need to be checked against patient-derived Pangolin lineages for the same area and time periods.
skills.name: lineagespot-output-interpretation
skills.search_text: lineagespot-output-interpretation Use when NGS-derived variant calls (VCF) from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater samples must be converted into lineage-level inference, or when wastewater-inferred lineages need to be checked against patient-derived Pangolin lineages for the same area and time periods. Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than variant call files — lineagespot expects VCF input, and the raw-data preprocessing (iVar trimming, Minimap2 mapping to NC_045512) must be run first The goal is precise within-sample variant frequency quantification rather than community-level lineage inference — the Pangolin-rule-based assignment can mislabel lineages when reads satisfy different rules of the same lineage Clinical comparison lineages are unavailable or unmatched in time/space — the concordance assessment is a qualitative alignment with predominant lineages and cannot be judged without matched Pangolin-assigned clinical samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Interpret lineagespot outputs — merged VCF-derived mutation tables collapsed at gene and amino acid substitution level — to infer SARS-CoV-2 lineage distributions in wastewater and qualitatively compare them with predominant clinical (Pangolin-assigned) lineages across matched time periods, as demonstrated on 14 Thessaloniki wastewater samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: Interpret lineagespot outputs — merged VCF-derived mutation tables collapsed at gene and amino acid substitution level — to infer SARS-CoV-2 lineage distributions in wastewater and qualitatively compare them with predominant clinical (Pangolin-assigned) lineages across matched time periods, as demonstrated on 14 Thessaloniki wastewater samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than variant call files — lineagespot expects VCF input, and the raw-data preprocessing (iVar trimming, Minimap2 mapping to NC_045512) must be run first The goal is precise within-sample variant frequency quantification rather than community-level lineage inference — the Pangolin-rule-based assignment can mislabel lineages when reads satisfy different rules of the same lineage Clinical comparison lineages are unavailable or unmatched in time/space — the concordance assessment is a qualitative alignment with predominant lineages and cannot be judged without matched Pangolin-assigned clinical samples

skills.description: Use when extracting quantitative phenotypic characters (cell diameter, width, length) from natural-language taxonomic descriptions and a deterministic, term-list-driven rule pattern is preferred over supervised classification.
skills.name: linguistic-rule-pattern-authoring
skills.search_text: linguistic-rule-pattern-authoring Use when extracting quantitative phenotypic characters (cell diameter, width, length) from natural-language taxonomic descriptions and a deterministic, term-list-driven rule pattern is preferred over supervised classification. The descriptions contain little morphological data and focus on physiological/ecological traits, where keyword-window rules for dimension characters will rarely fire A domain-independent open extraction is desired without domain knowledge — the article found OIE inadequate because the task requires substantial domain knowledge The character must be predicted where no explicit keyword co-occurs; use MicroPIE's SVM character prediction component instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 http://edamontology.org/topic_3071 Authoring linguistic-rule-based extraction patterns that pair character Term Lists with regex, POS-tag, and dependency patterns to pull numeric character states (e.g., cell diameter/width/length) from prokaryotic taxonomic descriptions, as implemented in MicroPIE's shared Character Extractor. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1396-8
skills.summary: Authoring linguistic-rule-based extraction patterns that pair character Term Lists with regex, POS-tag, and dependency patterns to pull numeric character states (e.g., cell diameter/width/length) from prokaryotic taxonomic descriptions, as implemented in MicroPIE's shared Character Extractor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The descriptions contain little morphological data and focus on physiological/ecological traits, where keyword-window rules for dimension characters will rarely fire A domain-independent open extraction is desired without domain knowledge — the article found OIE inadequate because the task requires substantial domain knowledge The character must be predicted where no explicit keyword co-occurs; use MicroPIE's SVM character prediction component instead

skills.description: Use when a genome-wide biallelic SNP dataset (VCF or PLINK binary) is being prepared for analyses that assume quasi-independent markers (e.g., ADMIXTURE, PCA) and SNPs must be pruned by linkage disequilibrium before analysis.
skills.name: linkage-disequilibrium-pruning
skills.search_text: linkage-disequilibrium-pruning Use when a genome-wide biallelic SNP dataset (VCF or PLINK binary) is being prepared for analyses that assume quasi-independent markers (e.g., ADMIXTURE, PCA) and SNPs must be pruned by linkage disequilibrium before analysis. The downstream analysis does not require LD-pruned markers (LD pruning is optional/recommended, not mandatory, in scalepopgen). Input data is raw variant calls that have not yet passed the mandated sample filtering before site filtering order of the filtering sub-workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3056 Prune biallelic SNP datasets for linked sites using user-defined LD parameters of Plink2 within the scalepopgen Nextflow workflow, so that downstream population-genomic analyses (e.g., structure inference) are not biased by linkage. In the paper's cattle case study, LD-based filtering reduced the filtered data set to 129,357 SNPs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Prune biallelic SNP datasets for linked sites using user-defined LD parameters of Plink2 within the scalepopgen Nextflow workflow, so that downstream population-genomic analyses (e.g., structure inference) are not biased by linkage. In the paper's cattle case study, LD-based filtering reduced the filtered data set to 129,357 SNPs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream analysis does not require LD-pruned markers (LD pruning is optional/recommended, not mandatory, in scalepopgen). Input data is raw variant calls that have not yet passed the mandated sample filtering before site filtering order of the filtering sub-workflow.

skills.description: Use when you have mbQTL taxa-SNP rho correlation results and need to visualize SNVs in linkage disequilibrium (e.g., a chr15 LD block) as correlated clusters in a heatmap.
skills.name: linkage-disequilibrium-snp-block-visualization
skills.search_text: linkage-disequilibrium-snp-block-visualization Use when you have mbQTL taxa-SNP rho correlation results and need to visualize SNVs in linkage disequilibrium (e.g., a chr15 LD block) as correlated clusters in a heatmap. Taxa are presence/absence (categorical) and require logistic regression via mbQTL's logistic regression analysis rather than rho correlation The goal is significant taxa-SNP relationship testing via linear regression (MatrixEQTL-based mbQTL Part A), not LD visualization Input is a raw phyloseq or metagenomeSeq object that has not yet been converted/normalized via phyloseq_to_metagenomeSeq() or metagenomeSeqToMbqtl http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Estimate rho correlations between all SNPs and all taxa with mbQTL's taxaSnpCor() applied to allToAllProduct() output and taxa-taxa correlation matrices, then render the rho table as a taxa-by-SNP heatmap with mbQtlCorHeatmap() to expose SNVs in linkage disequilibrium as visibly correlated blocks. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad565
skills.summary: Estimate rho correlations between all SNPs and all taxa with mbQTL's taxaSnpCor() applied to allToAllProduct() output and taxa-taxa correlation matrices, then render the rho table as a taxa-by-SNP heatmap with mbQtlCorHeatmap() to expose SNVs in linkage disequilibrium as visibly correlated blocks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Taxa are presence/absence (categorical) and require logistic regression via mbQTL's logistic regression analysis rather than rho correlation The goal is significant taxa-SNP relationship testing via linear regression (MatrixEQTL-based mbQTL Part A), not LD visualization Input is a raw phyloseq or metagenomeSeq object that has not yet been converted/normalized via phyloseq_to_metagenomeSeq() or metagenomeSeqToMbqtl

skills.description: Use when you need to identify taxa associated with SNPs while jointly controlling correlation (rho) and goodness-of-fit (R-squared) measures, e.g. flagging LD SNPs/regions from 16S taxa abundance and genotype matrices.
skills.name: linkage-disequilibrium-snp-identification
skills.search_text: linkage-disequilibrium-snp-identification Use when you need to identify taxa associated with SNPs while jointly controlling correlation (rho) and goodness-of-fit (R-squared) measures, e.g. flagging LD SNPs/regions from 16S taxa abundance and genotype matrices. Your taxa are presence/absence (categorical) — use mbQTL's logistic regression analysis for one SNP vs one taxa instead. You want linear-regression mbQTL testing per the core MatrixEQTL model (Approach A), not correlation-based rho estimation adjusted for taxa-taxa R. You lack taxa abundance data or a taxa x sample matrix from which coringTaxa R values can be estimated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies host-genetics-associated taxa and flags linkage-disequilibrium (LD) SNPs/regions using mbQTL's Approach B: rho values for taxa-SNP correlation are estimated after taxa-taxa R values are estimated, then adjusted for taxa-SNP association via coringTaxa, allToAllProduct, and taxaSnpCor. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad565
skills.summary: Identifies host-genetics-associated taxa and flags linkage-disequilibrium (LD) SNPs/regions using mbQTL's Approach B: rho values for taxa-SNP correlation are estimated after taxa-taxa R values are estimated, then adjusted for taxa-SNP association via coringTaxa, allToAllProduct, and taxaSnpCor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your taxa are presence/absence (categorical) — use mbQTL's logistic regression analysis for one SNP vs one taxa instead. You want linear-regression mbQTL testing per the core MatrixEQTL model (Approach A), not correlation-based rho estimation adjusted for taxa-taxa R. You lack taxa abundance data or a taxa x sample matrix from which coringTaxa R values can be estimated.

skills.description: Use when multiple high-depth 10x Chromium libraries must be compared at a controlled read coverage per fragment (CR), requiring fragment inference and per-fragment subsampling to equalize parameters.
skills.name: linked-read-fragment-parameter-tabulation
skills.search_text: linked-read-fragment-parameter-tabulation Use when multiple high-depth 10x Chromium libraries must be compared at a controlled read coverage per fragment (CR), requiring fragment inference and per-fragment subsampling to equalize parameters. Input is already low-coverage Linked-Read data whose realized per-fragment coverage matches the target CR, so subsampling would discard information without changing the comparison The goal is de novo assembly output evaluation rather than preparing matched Linked-Read input sets (see Evaluate_diploid_assembly for that task) Data are not barcode-linked short reads (e.g. PacBio or ONT long reads), since fragment inference depends on barcode-proximal read pairs http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs original input DNA fragments from high-coverage 10x Linked-Read data and subsamples reads per fragment to a target read coverage per fragment (CR), producing matched Linked-Read sets (Rid) across libraries for fair assembly-parameters comparison. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Reconstructs original input DNA fragments from high-coverage 10x Linked-Read data and subsamples reads per fragment to a target read coverage per fragment (CR), producing matched Linked-Read sets (Rid) across libraries for fair assembly-parameters comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already low-coverage Linked-Read data whose realized per-fragment coverage matches the target CR, so subsampling would discard information without changing the comparison The goal is de novo assembly output evaluation rather than preparing matched Linked-Read input sets (see Evaluate_diploid_assembly for that task) Data are not barcode-linked short reads (e.g. PacBio or ONT long reads), since fragment inference depends on barcode-proximal read pairs

skills.description: Use when high-coverage 10x Linked-Read FASTQs with different library parameters (CF, CR, fragment length) must be normalized to matched CR before assembly comparison, or when simulating realistic Linked-Reads.
skills.name: linked-read-fragment-reconstruction-from-barcode-read-pairs
skills.search_text: linked-read-fragment-reconstruction-from-barcode-read-pairs Use when high-coverage 10x Linked-Read FASTQs with different library parameters (CF, CR, fragment length) must be normalized to matched CR before assembly comparison, or when simulating realistic Linked-Reads. Input reads lack 10x barcodes / GemCode partitioning information (standard Illumina WGS) — barcode-proximal grouping cannot be performed Libraries already share the same CR and fragment-length parameters, so subsampling for comparability is unnecessary The goal is variant calling from the full-depth data rather than generating matched-depth Linked-Read sets for assembly comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs original input DNA fragments from 10x Linked-Read data by grouping barcode-proximal read pairs, then subsamples reads per fragment to a target per-fragment short-read coverage (CR) so Linked-Read libraries with different parameters become comparable (Rid sets). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Reconstructs original input DNA fragments from 10x Linked-Read data by grouping barcode-proximal read pairs, then subsamples reads per fragment to a target per-fragment short-read coverage (CR) so Linked-Read libraries with different parameters become comparable (Rid sets).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads lack 10x barcodes / GemCode partitioning information (standard Illumina WGS) — barcode-proximal grouping cannot be performed Libraries already share the same CR and fragment-length parameters, so subsampling for comparability is unnecessary The goal is variant calling from the full-depth data rather than generating matched-depth Linked-Read sets for assembly comparison

skills.description: Use when planning or simulating 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries and you need to set physical fragment coverage (CF), per-fragment read coverage (CR), fragment length (Mu_F), and droplet fragment counts (N_FP) for Supernova2 assembly testing.
skills.name: linked-read-library-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: linked-read-library-parameter-configuration Use when planning or simulating 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries and you need to set physical fragment coverage (CF), per-fragment read coverage (CR), fragment length (Mu_F), and droplet fragment counts (N_FP) for Supernova2 assembly testing. Input reference contains structural variants or indels — gen_fasta.py supports only SNVs in this version You need real sequencing data rather than simulation — the article supplements simulations with real high-depth data from NA12878 and NA24385 (PRJNA527321) Haploid simulation is desired but Hap is left at 2 — you must remove Path_Fastahap2 and set Hap=1 (line 33) http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Configure and simulate 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries by setting CF, CR, Mu_F, N_FP, insert-size, and read parameters in LRTK-SIM config files, generating realistic synthetic diploid data. Used to constrain the 10x library-parameter space (e.g., optimal CF 332x–823x, WμFL ∼50–150 kb) before costly wet-lab library preparation. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Configure and simulate 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries by setting CF, CR, Mu_F, N_FP, insert-size, and read parameters in LRTK-SIM config files, generating realistic synthetic diploid data. Used to constrain the 10x library-parameter space (e.g., optimal CF 332x–823x, WμFL ∼50–150 kb) before costly wet-lab library preparation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reference contains structural variants or indels — gen_fasta.py supports only SNVs in this version You need real sequencing data rather than simulation — the article supplements simulations with real high-depth data from NA12878 and NA24385 (PRJNA527321) Haploid simulation is desired but Hap is left at 2 — you must remove Path_Fastahap2 and set Hap=1 (line 33)

skills.description: Use when you need synthetic 10x Linked-Read FASTQs with controlled CF, CR, Mu_F, insert size, and error rate to benchmark diploid assemblers (e.g., Supernova2) or test assembly-parameter hypotheses against a gold standard.
skills.name: linked-read-library-simulation
skills.search_text: linked-read-library-simulation Use when you need synthetic 10x Linked-Read FASTQs with controlled CF, CR, Mu_F, insert size, and error rate to benchmark diploid assemblers (e.g., Supernova2) or test assembly-parameter hypotheses against a gold standard. Haploid simulation with structural variants: gen_fasta.py in this version inserts SNVs only, so SV-heavy diploid references require a different generation route Metagenomics simulation requiring species abundances: use LRTK-SIM's dedicated meta_config route with an abundance flat file rather than the diploid config workflow Evaluation of real (non-simulated) Linked-Read data where no gold standard or controlled parameter sweep is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Simulate realistic 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries with LRTK-SIM by parameterizing long-fragment coverage (CF), per-fragment read coverage (CR), fragment length (Mu_F), and diploid haplotype inputs, to explore how library parameters affect de novo diploid assembly quality with Supernova2. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Simulate realistic 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries with LRTK-SIM by parameterizing long-fragment coverage (CF), per-fragment read coverage (CR), fragment length (Mu_F), and diploid haplotype inputs, to explore how library parameters affect de novo diploid assembly quality with Supernova2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Haploid simulation with structural variants: gen_fasta.py in this version inserts SNVs only, so SV-heavy diploid references require a different generation route Metagenomics simulation requiring species abundances: use LRTK-SIM's dedicated meta_config route with an abundance flat file rather than the diploid config workflow Evaluation of real (non-simulated) Linked-Read data where no gold standard or controlled parameter sweep is needed

skills.description: Use when you have Supernova2 assemblies from 10x Linked-Read data and need to quantify the diploid fraction (windows covered by both homologous contigs) against a reference genome.
skills.name: linked-read-megabubble-haplotype-extraction
skills.search_text: linked-read-megabubble-haplotype-extraction Use when you have Supernova2 assemblies from 10x Linked-Read data and need to quantify the diploid fraction (windows covered by both homologous contigs) against a reference genome. Input data are simulated Linked-Reads evaluated only by contiguity/accuracy metrics against a simulated gold standard (LRTK-SIM workflow), not real assemblies to be assessed for diploid coverage Assemblies were produced by assemblers other than Supernova2, whose phase-block/megabubble output structure mkoutput depends on The goal is long-read (PacBio/ONT) assembly evaluation, where haplotype-resolved contigs are not organized into 10x megabubble phase blocks http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Extracts megabubble haplotype scaffold pairs from Supernova2 phase blocks (via Supernova2 mkoutput) and aligns them to hg38 to quantify what fraction of the human genome is recovered in a diploid state. skills.description: Use when deep-sequencing reads (sorted BAM/CRAM or a read MSA) from a genetically heterogeneous mixed sample need sequencing-error correction and local (window-level) haplotype reconstruction before global assembly or frequency estimation.
skills.name: local-haplotype-reconstruction
skills.search_text: local-haplotype-reconstruction Use when deep-sequencing reads (sorted BAM/CRAM or a read MSA) from a genetically heterogeneous mixed sample need sequencing-error correction and local (window-level) haplotype reconstruction before global assembly or frequency estimation. You need full-length (global) haplotype reconstruction with ShoRAH2 — global mode is disabled there; use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or the V-pipe global haplotype options instead. You only want single nucleotide variant detection with strand bias — invoke 'shorah snv' directly rather than the full windowed reconstruction. Input is a low-coverage sample where clustering cannot resolve rare variants — sensitivity of 0.1% frequency detection was demonstrated at coverage 5000. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 ShoRAH's error-correction/local-haplotype stage: overlapping windows cut from the read MSA are clustered by a Dirichlet-process Gibbs sampler (diri_sampler) so that each cluster consensus recovers a local haplotype and its prevalence from reads drawn from a genetically heterogeneous (e.g., HIV-1) mixed sample. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: ShoRAH's error-correction/local-haplotype stage: overlapping windows cut from the read MSA are clustered by a Dirichlet-process Gibbs sampler (diri_sampler) so that each cluster consensus recovers a local haplotype and its prevalence from reads drawn from a genetically heterogeneous (e.g., HIV-1) mixed sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need full-length (global) haplotype reconstruction with ShoRAH2 — global mode is disabled there; use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or the V-pipe global haplotype options instead. You only want single nucleotide variant detection with strand bias — invoke 'shorah snv' directly rather than the full windowed reconstruction. Input is a low-coverage sample where clustering cannot resolve rare variants — sensitivity of 0.1% frequency detection was demonstrated at coverage 5000.

skills.description: Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads must be mapped to a microbiome reference to detect HGT breakpoints, identify transferred genome segments, and reconstruct the local strain harboring the HGT events.

skills.search_text: local-strain-reconstruction Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads must be mapped to a microbiome reference to detect HGT breakpoints, identify transferred genome segments, and reconstruct the local strain harboring the HGT events. Input is long-read sequencing data or transcriptomic data rather than paired-end shotgun NGS reads, since LEMON's breakpoint detection relies on unique and split shotgun read alignment via BWA The goal is ancient/lineage HGT inference from genomic sequences rather than reconstructing recent HGT events from metagenomic samples No metagenomic reference sequences are available against which reads can be aligned for donor/receptor identification http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstructs the inserted local strain at horizontal gene transfer (HGT) sites from gut metagenomics shotgun data using the graph-based LEMON method, which detects raw and accurate HGT breakpoints and assembles linked transferred segments into an Eulerian circuit. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3301-8
skills.summary: Reconstructs the inserted local strain at horizontal gene transfer (HGT) sites from gut metagenomics shotgun data using the graph-based LEMON method, which detects raw and accurate HGT breakpoints and assembles linked transferred segments into an Eulerian circuit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read sequencing data or transcriptomic data rather than paired-end shotgun NGS reads, since LEMON's breakpoint detection relies on unique and split shotgun read alignment via BWA The goal is ancient/lineage HGT inference from genomic sequences rather than reconstructing recent HGT events from metagenomic samples No metagenomic reference sequences are available against which reads can be aligned for donor/receptor identification

skills.name: loess-fit-diagnostic-visualization
skills.search_text: loess-fit-diagnostic-visualization Use when running HashSeq's inferTrueSequences on 16S rRNA gene FASTQ data and you need to verify the LOESS regression is a good fit above the abundance threshold before trusting variant calls. Input is a raw FASTQ directory that has not yet been processed by inferTrueSequences, so childrenProperties.txt does not exist. The goal is low-abundance variant detection; HashSeq (and this diagnostic) is not sensitive for true low-abundance sequences and DADA2 is recommended instead. Data are long-read (e.g. PacBio) or contain frequent indels/multiple mismatches, which violate HashSeq's one-mismatch, indel-as-separate-parent assumptions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualize the relationship between the mean and standard deviation of one-mismatch children and parent abundances from HashSeq output to confirm the LOESS regression used in the normal-distribution error model fits above the filtering threshold. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Visualize the relationship between the mean and standard deviation of one-mismatch children and parent abundances from HashSeq output to confirm the LOESS regression used in the normal-distribution error model fits above the filtering threshold.
