skills.description: Use when you need to model the mean and standard deviation of one-mismatch child abundances as a smooth function of parent abundance, or to empirically choose the abundance threshold above which a LOESS background error model is a good fit.
skills.name: loess-regression-fitting
skills.search_text: loess-regression-fitting Use when you need to model the mean and standard deviation of one-mismatch child abundances as a smooth function of parent abundance, or to empirically choose the abundance threshold above which a LOESS background error model is a good fit. The input is not HashSeq cluster output (e.g., you already have a count/SvTable or feature table), since childrenProperties.txt is the required input. You need to detect true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq's LOESS-based background model is conservative and insensitive below the 1,000-read threshold; use more sensitive callers such as DADA2. Variants differ by two or more mismatches, contain indels, or come from long-read technologies like PacBio where the one-mismatch assumption of the background model fails. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0611 Fit and visualize a LOESS (locally estimated scatterplot smoothing) regression of one-mismatch child variant mean and standard deviation against parent sequencing depth, as used in HashSeq to justify the depth-dependent normal-plus-LOESS background error model for 16S rRNA gene variant calling. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Fit and visualize a LOESS (locally estimated scatterplot smoothing) regression of one-mismatch child variant mean and standard deviation against parent sequencing depth, as used in HashSeq to justify the depth-dependent normal-plus-LOESS background error model for 16S rRNA gene variant calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not HashSeq cluster output (e.g., you already have a count/SvTable or feature table), since childrenProperties.txt is the required input. You need to detect true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq's LOESS-based background model is conservative and insensitive below the 1,000-read threshold; use more sensitive callers such as DADA2. Variants differ by two or more mismatches, contain indels, or come from long-read technologies like PacBio where the one-mismatch assumption of the background model fails.

skills.description: Use when reading or reporting taxa.compare()/taxcomtab.show() output from metamicrobiomeR GAMLSS-BEZI fits, to translate beta estimates and FDR p-values into directional, group-comparable effect statements about relative abundances.
skills.name: log-odds-ratio-effect-interpretation
skills.search_text: log-odds-ratio-effect-interpretation Use when reading or reporting taxa.compare()/taxcomtab.show() output from metamicrobiomeR GAMLSS-BEZI fits, to translate beta estimates and FDR p-values into directional, group-comparable effect statements about relative abundances. Estimates come from non-GAMLSS methods (e.g. MaAsLin arcsin square-root transformed linear models) whose coefficients are not log(odds ratio) of relative abundances Only a single taxon's raw abundance difference is needed without group-level odds-ratio framing or cross-study comparability Relative abundance data have not been filtered/normalized for compositional effects, so BEZI assumptions on the zero-inflated beta distribution do not hold http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Interprets GAMLSS-BEZI differential relative abundance coefficients as log(odds ratio) of relative abundances between comparison groups (e.g. diarrhea vs no diarrhea, EBF <= 2 months vs > 2 months), which makes estimates analogous across microbiome studies and suitable for meta-analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2744-2
skills.summary: Interprets GAMLSS-BEZI differential relative abundance coefficients as log(odds ratio) of relative abundances between comparison groups (e.g. diarrhea vs no diarrhea, EBF <= 2 months vs > 2 months), which makes estimates analogous across microbiome studies and suitable for meta-analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Estimates come from non-GAMLSS methods (e.g. MaAsLin arcsin square-root transformed linear models) whose coefficients are not log(odds ratio) of relative abundances Only a single taxon's raw abundance difference is needed without group-level odds-ratio framing or cross-study comparability Relative abundance data have not been filtered/normalized for compositional effects, so BEZI assumptions on the zero-inflated beta distribution do not hold

skills.description: Use when evaluating how much of a HiFi read set a metagenome assembly (e.g. metaMDBG, metaflye, hifiasm-meta, or a user-submitted assembly.fasta) actually captures, via read-to-contig alignment ratios.
skills.name: long-read-contig-alignment
skills.search_text: long-read-contig-alignment Use when evaluating how much of a HiFi read set a metagenome assembly (e.g. metaMDBG, metaflye, hifiasm-meta, or a user-submitted assembly.fasta) actually captures, via read-to-contig alignment ratios. You only need assembly contiguity statistics (N50, length) rather than how much of the sequenced sample the assembly represents — MetaQUAST is the appropriate Mapler module. Reads are short reads, not HiFi long reads — the pipeline and metrics are built around HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies. The assembly is not available and only reads are provided without enabling an assembler — Mapler needs either a built-in assembler run or a user-submitted assembly.fasta to align against. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns HiFi long reads to metagenome assembly contigs with minimap2 (producing reads_on_contigs.bam + .bai) and computes aligned read and aligned base ratios, optionally split by bin quality category, as core assembly-representativeness metrics of the Mapler pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Aligns HiFi long reads to metagenome assembly contigs with minimap2 (producing reads_on_contigs.bam + .bai) and computes aligned read and aligned base ratios, optionally split by bin quality category, as core assembly-representativeness metrics of the Mapler pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need assembly contiguity statistics (N50, length) rather than how much of the sequenced sample the assembly represents — MetaQUAST is the appropriate Mapler module. skills.description: Use when long reads must join strain-separated contigs into scaffolds: you have a strain-oblivious/strain-separated contig FASTA, a long-read FASTQ, and need dovetail read-to-contig links to scaffold within a strain-resolved pipeline.
skills.name: long-read-dovetail-alignment-filtering
skills.search_text: long-read-dovetail-alignment-filtering Use when long reads must join strain-separated contigs into scaffolds: you have a strain-oblivious/strain-separated contig FASTA, a long-read FASTQ, and need dovetail read-to-contig links to scaffold within a strain-resolved pipeline. The input is a raw long-read metagenome that still needs de novo strain separation (strain separation via variant calling and haplotyping must precede scaffolding). High strain variability requires splitting a strain-oblivious contig into a variable number of strains within the same contig — a case Strainberry does not handle. Only short-read data are available; the skill relies on error-prone long-read dovetail alignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Filters high-confidence long-read-to-contig dovetail alignments (e.g. MAPQ > 40) and uses them to build and trim a bi-directed weighted string graph that joins strain-separated contigs into longer scaffolds, as done by Strainberry's scaffolding component. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Filters high-confidence long-read-to-contig dovetail alignments (e.g. MAPQ > 40) and uses them to build and trim a bi-directed weighted string graph that joins strain-separated contigs into longer scaffolds, as done by Strainberry's scaffolding component.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw long-read metagenome that still needs de novo strain separation (strain separation via variant calling and haplotyping must precede scaffolding). High strain variability requires splitting a strain-oblivious contig into a variable number of strains within the same contig — a case Strainberry does not handle. Only short-read data are available; the skill relies on error-prone long-read dovetail alignments.

skills.description: Use when evaluating k-mer-based metagenome comparison tools on simulated long-read (PacBio) datasets — e.g. the CAMI 'toy' HMP samples — where you must judge whether clustering-by-origin errors stem from the error model rather than the algorithm.
skills.name: long-read-error-tolerance-interpretation
skills.search_text: long-read-error-tolerance-interpretation Use when evaluating k-mer-based metagenome comparison tools on simulated long-read (PacBio) datasets — e.g. the CAMI 'toy' HMP samples — where you must judge whether clustering-by-origin errors stem from the error model rather than the algorithm. Input samples are real short-read data with low error rates, where any misclassification cannot be attributed to a PacBio-style error model and this tolerance-interpretation logic does not apply The goal is a single pairwise comparison rather than an all-vs-all distance matrix suitable for body-site clustering Data-reduction approaches (sketching-only or presence/absence metrics) are the accepted standard, since the article reports such methods 'greatly diminish the resolution' of comparative analyses — but if resolution loss is tolerable, a lighter-weight workflow is preferable http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Validates whether all-vs-all metagenome distance tools (Mash, Libra, Simka) cluster simulated PacBio long-read samples correctly despite elevated sequencing error, by clustering each tool's distance matrix and attributing any residual body-site misclassifications to the long-read error rate rather than to tool failure. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Validates whether all-vs-all metagenome distance tools (Mash, Libra, Simka) cluster simulated PacBio long-read samples correctly despite elevated sequencing error, by clustering each tool's distance matrix and attributing any residual body-site misclassifications to the long-read error rate rather than to tool failure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples are real short-read data with low error rates, where any misclassification cannot be attributed to a PacBio-style error model and this tolerance-interpretation logic does not apply The goal is a single pairwise comparison rather than an all-vs-all distance matrix suitable for body-site clustering Data-reduction approaches (sketching-only or presence/absence metrics) are the accepted standard, since the article reports such methods 'greatly diminish the resolution' of comparative analyses — but if resolution loss is tolerable, a lighter-weight workflow is preferable

skills.name: long-read-haplotype-phasing
skills.search_text: long-read-haplotype-phasing Use when you have a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly (FASTA) plus a coordinate-sorted indexed BAM of long reads and need to separate reads/scaffolds by strain using haplotype phasing rather than short reads or references. skills.name: longitudinal-menses-abundance-change-detection
skills.search_text: longitudinal-menses-abundance-change-detection Use when you have a longitudinal 16S OTU table (e.g. a vaginal time course) with per-sample metadata marking menses, and want to test whether PICRUSt-predicted KEGG module abundances change significantly during menses versus other cycle phases. Data are WGS shotgun metagenomes already annotated to KOs — direct functional profiling (e.g. HUMAnN) is appropriate rather than PICRUSt prediction Samples are from static body-site comparisons (e.g. supragingival vs subgingival plaque) rather than a longitudinal series with menses annotations — use a between-group module enrichment test instead The 16S data are not closed-reference OTU picked against a PICRUSt-compatible reference (Greengenes+IMG), since predicted genome contents assume matching tips on the marker reference tree http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Detects mean-abundance changes of predicted KEGG functional modules across a longitudinal 16S time course by contrasting menses time points against the rest of the cycle, as applied to 993 vaginal samples with PICRUSt-predicted metagenomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Detects mean-abundance changes of predicted KEGG functional modules across a longitudinal 16S time course by contrasting menses time points against the rest of the cycle, as applied to 993 vaginal samples with PICRUSt-predicted metagenomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are WGS shotgun metagenomes already annotated to KOs — direct functional profiling (e.g. HUMAnN) is appropriate rather than PICRUSt prediction Samples are from static body-site comparisons (e.g. supragingival vs subgingival plaque) rather than a longitudinal series with menses annotations — use a between-group module enrichment test instead The 16S data are not closed-reference OTU picked against a PICRUSt-compatible reference (Greengenes+IMG), since predicted genome contents assume matching tips on the marker reference tree

skills.description: Use when evaluating longitudinal differential-abundance methods on data with known true positives — simulate count datasets across sample sizes, effect sizes and covariate counts to compute accuracy, TPR and FDR.
skills.name: longitudinal-microbiome-data-simulation
skills.search_text: longitudinal-microbiome-data-simulation Use when evaluating longitudinal differential-abundance methods on data with known true positives — simulate count datasets across sample sizes, effect sizes and covariate counts to compute accuracy, TPR and FDR. You need to analyze a real longitudinal dataset for biological discovery rather than benchmark tools on data with known ground truth Your data are non-longitudinal (cross-sectional) — microbiomeDASim-simulated temporal structures and within-individual time shuffling do not apply Only a single method needs a quick sanity check without FDR/TPR ground truth, where simulation overhead outweighs benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generate simulated longitudinal microbiome count datasets (e.g. with microbiomeDASim, plus SparseDOSSA2 for covariate-correlated settings) with known ground-truth features, to benchmark longitudinal differential-abundance tools such as LongDat and MaAsLin2 on accuracy, TPR, FDR, runtime and memory. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad063
skills.summary: Generate simulated longitudinal microbiome count datasets (e.g. with microbiomeDASim, plus SparseDOSSA2 for covariate-correlated settings) with known ground-truth features, to benchmark longitudinal differential-abundance tools such as LongDat and MaAsLin2 on accuracy, TPR, FDR, runtime and memory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to analyze a real longitudinal dataset for biological discovery rather than benchmark tools on data with known ground truth Your data are non-longitudinal (cross-sectional) — microbiomeDASim-simulated temporal structures and within-individual time shuffling do not apply Only a single method needs a quick sanity check without FDR/TPR ground truth, where simulation overhead outweighs benefit

skills.description: Use when analyzing longitudinal (repeated-measures) microbiome or other high-dimensional count/continuous/binary/ordinal feature data where abundance change over time (treatment proxy) must be disentangled from multiple covariates such as medications.
skills.name: longitudinal-microbiome-differential-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: longitudinal-microbiome-differential-abundance-analysis Use when analyzing longitudinal (repeated-measures) microbiome or other high-dimensional count/continuous/binary/ordinal feature data where abundance change over time (treatment proxy) must be disentangled from multiple covariates such as medications. When the data are cross-sectional (no repeated time points or before/after structure), since LongDat tests change over time (proxy for treatments) When only one or zero covariates exist and a simple paired model suffices — LongDat's key advantage appears 'especially when there were multiple covariates' When the input is raw sequencing reads rather than a feature/abundance table with sample metadata (use a profiler like MetaPhlAn/HUMAnN first) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A covariate-sensitive longitudinal differential abundance workflow built on the LongDat R package (longdat_cont()/longdat_disc()), which tests whether high-dimensional features (e.g. species-level gut microbiome abundances) change significantly over time while detecting and controlling for covariates, and benchmarks results against MaAsLin2, ANCOM, lgpr and ZIBR. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad063
skills.summary: A covariate-sensitive longitudinal differential abundance workflow built on the LongDat R package (longdat_cont()/longdat_disc()), which tests whether high-dimensional features (e.g. species-level gut microbiome abundances) change significantly over time while detecting and controlling for covariates, and benchmarks results against MaAsLin2, ANCOM, lgpr and ZIBR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the data are cross-sectional (no repeated time points or before/after structure), since LongDat tests change over time (proxy for treatments) When only one or zero covariates exist and a simple paired model suffices — LongDat's key advantage appears 'especially when there were multiple covariates' When the input is raw sequencing reads rather than a feature/abundance table with sample metadata (use a profiler like MetaPhlAn/HUMAnN first)

skills.description: Use when you have longitudinal multivariable data (count, proportion, binary, ordinal or continuous) with a time/treatment variable and potentially many covariates, and need covariate-sensitive biomarker detection.
skills.name: longitudinal-microbiome-signal-interpretation
skills.search_text: longitudinal-microbiome-signal-interpretation Use when you have longitudinal multivariable data (count, proportion, binary, ordinal or continuous) with a time/treatment variable and potentially many covariates, and need covariate-sensitive biomarker detection. When the input is separate metadata and feature tables rather than a combined master table — use make_master_table() first When the goal is cross-sectional differential abundance with no longitudinal/time structure — tools like ANCOM or MaAsLin2 address that setting instead When the analysis must reproduce a static result and data_type = 'count' without setting a seed, since the randomized control test is stochastic http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Run the LongDat three-stage longitudinal pipeline (longdat_cont() or longdat_disc()) to test whether features change significantly over time while classifying each feature's time signal as reducible, entangled with, or independent of covariates, and interpret the Signal and EffectSize columns. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad063
skills.summary: Run the LongDat three-stage longitudinal pipeline (longdat_cont() or longdat_disc()) to test whether features change significantly over time while classifying each feature's time signal as reducible, entangled with, or independent of covariates, and interpret the Signal and EffectSize columns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is separate metadata and feature tables rather than a combined master table — use make_master_table() first When the goal is cross-sectional differential abundance with no longitudinal/time structure — tools like ANCOM or MaAsLin2 address that setting instead When the analysis must reproduce a static result and data_type = 'count' without setting a seed, since the randomized control test is stochastic

skills.description: Use when testing differential taxa relative abundances (phylum to genus, taxtab levels l2–l6) between two groups in longitudinal/repeated-measures microbiome relative abundance data with many zeros.
skills.name: longitudinal-microbiome-taxa-comparison
skills.search_text: longitudinal-microbiome-taxa-comparison Use when testing differential taxa relative abundances (phylum to genus, taxtab levels l2–l6) between two groups in longitudinal/repeated-measures microbiome relative abundance data with many zeros. Data are count-based feature tables rather than relative abundances — the zero-inflated beta model assumes relative abundance inputs The comparison variable varies within subjects but you cannot supply a person ID, since longitudinal='yes' requires repeated-measures structure The goal is pooling estimates across multiple studies — use meta.taxa random-effects meta-analysis on taxa.compare outputs instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fits zero-inflated beta GAMLSS-BEZI models (via metamicrobiomeR::taxa.compare) to test differential bacterial taxa relative abundances between groups in repeated-measures infant microbiome data, adjusting for age and handling the zero-inflated beta distribution that linear models like MaAsLin miss. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2744-2
skills.summary: Fits zero-inflated beta GAMLSS-BEZI models (via metamicrobiomeR::taxa.compare) to test differential bacterial taxa relative abundances between groups in repeated-measures infant microbiome data, adjusting for age and handling the zero-inflated beta distribution that linear models like MaAsLin miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are count-based feature tables rather than relative abundances — the zero-inflated beta model assumes relative abundance inputs The comparison variable varies within subjects but you cannot supply a person ID, since longitudinal='yes' requires repeated-measures structure The goal is pooling estimates across multiple studies — use meta.taxa random-effects meta-analysis on taxa.compare outputs instead

skills.description: Use when relative abundance taxa tables (phylum-to-genus, e.g. l2/l5/l6 levels) come from longitudinal stool sampling with repeated measures per subject and you need between-group differential abundance testing with proper type I error control.
skills.name: longitudinal-mixed-model-microbiome-testing
skills.search_text: longitudinal-mixed-model-microbiome-testing Use when relative abundance taxa tables (phylum-to-genus, e.g. l2/l5/l6 levels) come from longitudinal stool sampling with repeated measures per subject and you need between-group differential abundance testing with proper type I error control. Data are counts (not compositional relative abundances) and a count-based model such as negative binomial is intended — GAMLSS-BEZI in metamicrobiomeR targets zero-inflated beta relative abundance data Samples are independent (no repeated measures per subject), where the longitudinal='yes' random-intercept structure and per-subject random effects are unnecessary The goal is cross-study pooling rather than within-study differential abundance testing — use the package's random-effects meta-analysis (meta.taxa) workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A skill for testing differential relative abundance of bacterial taxa in repeated-measures (longitudinal) microbiome designs, using GAMLSS with a zero-inflated beta (BEZI) family via metamicrobiomeR::taxa.compare and, in parallel, linear/linear mixed models with random intercepts (LMAS/MaAsLin-style), and for validating type I error control on real data such as the Bangladesh infant cohort. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2744-2
skills.summary: A skill for testing differential relative abundance of bacterial taxa in repeated-measures (longitudinal) microbiome designs, using GAMLSS with a zero-inflated beta (BEZI) family via metamicrobiomeR::taxa.compare and, in parallel, linear/linear mixed models with random intercepts (LMAS/MaAsLin-style), and for validating type I error control on real data such as the Bangladesh infant cohort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are counts (not compositional relative abundances) and a count-based model such as negative binomial is intended — GAMLSS-BEZI in metamicrobiomeR targets zero-inflated beta relative abundance data Samples are independent (no repeated measures per subject), where the longitudinal='yes' random-intercept structure and per-subject random effects are unnecessary The goal is cross-study pooling rather than within-study differential abundance testing — use the package's random-effects meta-analysis (meta.taxa) workflow instead

skills.description: Use when validating a longitudinal microbiome pipeline's false positive rate on negative-control data where sequencing depth varies systematically across time points but all features are truly null (zero effect size).
skills.name: longitudinal-negative-binomial-type-i-error-evaluation
skills.search_text: longitudinal-negative-binomial-type-i-error-evaluation Use when validating a longitudinal microbiome pipeline's false positive rate on negative-control data where sequencing depth varies systematically across time points but all features are truly null (zero effect size). Data contain genuine non-zero time effects — this skill calibrates Type I error on all-null (zero effect size) negative controls only. Input is already compositional (proportion/TSS-normalized) rather than raw counts — the negative-binomial count mode and rarefaction step assume absolute count tables. The analysis is cross-sectional or otherwise lacks time points/replicates needed for longitudinal modeling in longdat_cont()/longdat_disc(). http://edamontology.org/topic_3050 A negative-control calibration skill that quantifies false positive rate (Type I error) of longitudinal microbiome pipelines under systematic sequencing-depth differences, contrasting LongDat's negative-binomial mode on rarefied counts against linear models on TSS-normalized non-rarefied data. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad063
skills.summary: A negative-control calibration skill that quantifies false positive rate (Type I error) of longitudinal microbiome pipelines under systematic sequencing-depth differences, contrasting LongDat's negative-binomial mode on rarefied counts against linear models on TSS-normalized non-rarefied data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contain genuine non-zero time effects — this skill calibrates Type I error on all-null (zero effect size) negative controls only. Input is already compositional (proportion/TSS-normalized) rather than raw counts — the negative-binomial count mode and rarefaction step assume absolute count tables. The analysis is cross-sectional or otherwise lacks time points/replicates needed for longitudinal modeling in longdat_cont()/longdat_disc().

skills.description: Use when evaluating tools that detect short-term within-strain evolutionary mutations in longitudinal metagenomic data, or when ground-truth mutated reads with a known mutation VCF are needed for simulated time-series communities.
skills.name: longitudinal-sample-mutation-modeling
skills.search_text: longitudinal-sample-mutation-modeling Use when evaluating tools that detect short-term within-strain evolutionary mutations in longitudinal metagenomic data, or when ground-truth mutated reads with a known mutation VCF are needed for simulated time-series communities. Input is real metagenomic data from species with low sequencing depth or poorly characterized genomes — the README warns STEMSim 'only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes' Goal is to simulate the microbial community abundance and reads themselves — use CAMISIM (or ART for single-genome reads) upstream; STEMSim only injects mutations on already-simulated reads Data are not longitudinal/concurrent time-point samples — the README states STEMSim 'is designed to work on longitudinal or concurrent simulated raw sequencing reads' http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Simulate within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations (SNVs and small InDels) on longitudinal metagenomic sequencing data using STEMSim, producing modified raw reads and a VCF of true injected mutations for benchmarking mutation-detection tools. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad302
skills.summary: Simulate within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations (SNVs and small InDels) on longitudinal metagenomic sequencing data using STEMSim, producing modified raw reads and a VCF of true injected mutations for benchmarking mutation-detection tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real metagenomic data from species with low sequencing depth or poorly characterized genomes — the README warns STEMSim 'only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes' Goal is to simulate the microbial community abundance and reads themselves — use CAMISIM (or ART for single-genome reads) upstream; STEMSim only injects mutations on already-simulated reads Data are not longitudinal/concurrent time-point samples — the README states STEMSim 'is designed to work on longitudinal or concurrent simulated raw sequencing reads'

skills.description: Use when a merged MetaPhlAn (or QIIME/BIOM) taxonomic profile table must be preprocessed for ML classification and sparse low-abundance taxa need removal prior to RF/SVM/GLM model building.
skills.name: low-abundance-feature-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: low-abundance-feature-threshold-filtering Use when a merged MetaPhlAn (or QIIME/BIOM) taxonomic profile table must be preprocessed for ML classification and sparse low-abundance taxa need removal prior to RF/SVM/GLM model building. The input is already a preprocessed feature table with sparse taxa removed (MegaR expects the raw merged MetaPhlAn/QIIME/BIOM table). The goal is differential abundance testing or temporal trend detection (tools like MetaDprof or MetaLonDa), not classification-oriented feature filtering. The analysis requires retaining rare taxa as features, e.g. when low-abundance biomarkers are biologically relevant rather than noise. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Removes sparse, low-abundance taxonomic features from MetaPhlAn/QIIME profile tables in MegaR before machine learning, using a floating abundance threshold (default 0.003) plus a percentage-of-sample filter (default 5%), which the authors report increases model accuracy. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03933-4
skills.summary: Removes sparse, low-abundance taxonomic features from MetaPhlAn/QIIME profile tables in MegaR before machine learning, using a floating abundance threshold (default 0.003) plus a percentage-of-sample filter (default 5%), which the authors report increases model accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a preprocessed feature table with sparse taxa removed (MegaR expects the raw merged MetaPhlAn/QIIME/BIOM table). The goal is differential abundance testing or temporal trend detection (tools like MetaDprof or MetaLonDa), not classification-oriented feature filtering. The analysis requires retaining rare taxa as features, e.g. when low-abundance biomarkers are biologically relevant rather than noise.

skills.description: Use when quantifying genetic diversity of a mixed NGS sample (e.g. 454 Titanium reads from an HIV-1 pol amplicon mixture) and you need to recover individual haplotypes/clone frequencies as low as 0.1% despite error-prone reads.
skills.name: low-frequency-clone-detection-in-mixed-samples
skills.search_text: low-frequency-clone-detection-in-mixed-samples Use when quantifying genetic diversity of a mixed NGS sample (e.g. 454 Titanium reads from an HIV-1 pol amplicon mixture) and you need to recover individual haplotypes/clone frequencies as low as 0.1% despite error-prone reads. Input reads have already been error-corrected or come from a low-error platform where residual error rate is below the rare-variant frequency of interest — correction by majority vote could erase true minor variants Coverage is far below ~5000x, since the article reports 0.1% haplotypes detected at coverage of 5000; lower coverage will not support rare-clone inference The goal is global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction with current ShoRAH2 — global mode is disabled and only ShoRAH1 v1.1.3 or V-pipe options support it http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Detect and quantify rare clones in a genetically heterogeneous deep-sequencing sample by using ShoRAH's model-based error correction (Dirichlet process mixture clustering of overlapping read windows), which removes the sequencing noise that otherwise masks variants present at ~0.1% frequency. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: Detect and quantify rare clones in a genetically heterogeneous deep-sequencing sample by using ShoRAH's model-based error correction (Dirichlet process mixture clustering of overlapping read windows), which removes the sequencing noise that otherwise masks variants present at ~0.1% frequency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have already been error-corrected or come from a low-error platform where residual error rate is below the rare-variant frequency of interest — correction by majority vote could erase true minor variants Coverage is far below ~5000x, since the article reports 0.1% haplotypes detected at coverage of 5000; lower coverage will not support rare-clone inference The goal is global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction with current ShoRAH2 — global mode is disabled and only ShoRAH1 v1.1.3 or V-pipe options support it

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end metatranscriptome FASTQ files show adaptor contamination or low-quality bases and must be cleaned before read joining (FLASH) and submission to an annotation server such as MG-RAST.
skills.name: low-quality-base-trimming
skills.search_text: low-quality-base-trimming Use when raw paired-end metatranscriptome FASTQ files show adaptor contamination or low-quality bases and must be cleaned before read joining (FLASH) and submission to an annotation server such as MG-RAST. Input reads are already cleaned adapter-free single-end/long reads longer than 100 bp — SAMSA notes sequences need to be either long reads (>100 bp) or joined paired-end reads, so merging/trimming may be unnecessary. The goal is ribosomal read removal — that is a separate filtering step (ribodepletion checks / discarding remaining rRNA reads), not quality trimming. Running SAMSA2 with local DIAMOND annotation where preprocessing is orchestrated by master_script.bash (which uses PEAR instead of FLASH) and Trimmomatic is invoked internally rather than as a standalone trimming pass. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Cleaning of raw metatranscriptomic FASTQ reads by removing adaptor contamination and low-quality bases with Trimmomatic as the first step of the SAMSA preprocessing phase, prior to paired-end joining and MG-RAST annotation. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1270-8
skills.summary: Cleaning of raw metatranscriptomic FASTQ reads by removing adaptor contamination and low-quality bases with Trimmomatic as the first step of the SAMSA preprocessing phase, prior to paired-end joining and MG-RAST annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already cleaned adapter-free single-end/long reads longer than 100 bp — SAMSA notes sequences need to be either long reads (>100 bp) or joined paired-end reads, so merging/trimming may be unnecessary. The goal is ribosomal read removal — that is a separate filtering step (ribodepletion checks / discarding remaining rRNA reads), not quality trimming. Running SAMSA2 with local DIAMOND annotation where preprocessing is orchestrated by master_script.bash (which uses PEAR instead of FLASH) and Trimmomatic is invoked internally rather than as a standalone trimming pass.

skills.description: Use when building or interpreting an exact k-mer-to-taxon database for metagenomic classification, e.g. deciding which taxonomic ID a shared 31-mer should carry when it appears in multiple genomes.
skills.name: lowest-common-ancestor-assignment
skills.search_text: lowest-common-ancestor-assignment Use when building or interpreting an exact k-mer-to-taxon database for metagenomic classification, e.g. deciding which taxonomic ID a shared 31-mer should carry when it appears in multiple genomes. When reads require inexact/alignment-based sensitivity because they have only weak similarity to known genomes — Kraken uses exact k-mer matches only When k-mers span ambiguous nucleotides ('N'): Kraken ignores these k-mers, so classification of such reads relies only on the remaining k-mers When the target genome is absent from the reference library and its k-mers are shared only with distant relatives — labels will resolve only to a high-level ancestor (e.g. Pelosinus fermentans not correctly identified at genus level) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Assigns each k-mer in a reference database the lowest common ancestor (LCA) taxon of all organisms whose genomes contain that k-mer, forming the core of Kraken's k-mer-to-taxonomy lookup used for metagenomic sequence classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Assigns each k-mer in a reference database the lowest common ancestor (LCA) taxon of all organisms whose genomes contain that k-mer, forming the core of Kraken's k-mer-to-taxonomy lookup used for metagenomic sequence classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads require inexact/alignment-based sensitivity because they have only weak similarity to known genomes — Kraken uses exact k-mer matches only When k-mers span ambiguous nucleotides ('N'): Kraken ignores these k-mers, so classification of such reads relies only on the remaining k-mers When the target genome is absent from the reference library and its k-mers are shared only with distant relatives — labels will resolve only to a high-level ancestor (e.g. Pelosinus fermentans not correctly identified at genus level)

skills.description: Decision support for assigning taxonomy to filtered viral contigs (>10 kbp) from ViroProfiler when combining clustering-based (vConTACT2) and homology-based (MMseqs2) evidence.
skills.name: lowest-common-ancestor-taxonomy-resolution
skills.search_text: lowest-common-ancestor-taxonomy-resolution Decision support for assigning taxonomy to filtered viral contigs (>10 kbp) from ViroProfiler when combining clustering-based (vConTACT2) and homology-based (MMseqs2) evidence. The task is classifying viruses in samples without prior viral isolation — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses Input contigs are shorter than 10 kbp, which are filtered out before taxonomy assignment The goal is viral identification/discovery (VirSorter2, VIBRANT, DeepVirFinder) rather than taxonomic placement of already-identified viral contigs http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Assigns taxonomy to viral contigs from shotgun viral metagenomic data by reconciling vConTACT2 clustering-based genus-level viral clusters with MMseqs2 homology-based calls against NCBI viral RefSeq, using lowest-common-ancestor voting to resolve conflicts, then normalising lineages with TaxonKit. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Assigns taxonomy to viral contigs from shotgun viral metagenomic data by reconciling vConTACT2 clustering-based genus-level viral clusters with MMseqs2 homology-based calls against NCBI viral RefSeq, using lowest-common-ancestor voting to resolve conflicts, then normalising lineages with TaxonKit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is classifying viruses in samples without prior viral isolation — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses Input contigs are shorter than 10 kbp, which are filtered out before taxonomy assignment The goal is viral identification/discovery (VirSorter2, VIBRANT, DeepVirFinder) rather than taxonomic placement of already-identified viral contigs

skills.description: Use when a set of candidate ortholog sequences for target KOs must be aligned into a non-redundant MSA so a profile HMM can be built and searched against protein sequences of a MAG/genome to recover missing KEGG orthologs.
skills.name: mafft-multiple-sequence-alignment
skills.search_text: mafft-multiple-sequence-alignment Use when a set of candidate ortholog sequences for target KOs must be aligned into a non-redundant MSA so a profile HMM can be built and searched against protein sequences of a MAG/genome to recover missing KEGG orthologs. When only KEGG Module completeness evaluation is needed and no missing-KO recovery is desired — run KEMET with --skip_hmm to stop after the completeness evaluation instead When the input is a KEGG annotation file without a genome (use --no_genome), since no HMM search against genome sequences can be performed When a KO assignment tool such as kofamkoala, eggNOG-mapper, or KAAS has already annotated all KOs of interest and no annotation expansion is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Within KEMET's missing-KO search workflow, MAFFT builds a non-redundant multiple sequence alignment of taxonomically relevant KEGG GENES ortholog sequences, which is then converted into a profile HMM with hmmbuild (HMMER v3.1b2) for nhmmer-based recovery of missing KOs from MAGs/genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Within KEMET's missing-KO search workflow, MAFFT builds a non-redundant multiple sequence alignment of taxonomically relevant KEGG GENES ortholog sequences, which is then converted into a profile HMM with hmmbuild (HMMER v3.1b2) for nhmmer-based recovery of missing KOs from MAGs/genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only KEGG Module completeness evaluation is needed and no missing-KO recovery is desired — run KEMET with --skip_hmm to stop after the completeness evaluation instead When the input is a KEGG annotation file without a genome (use --no_genome), since no HMM search against genome sequences can be performed When a KO assignment tool such as kofamkoala, eggNOG-mapper, or KAAS has already annotated all KOs of interest and no annotation expansion is required

skills.description: Use when you have VAMB bins (clusters.tsv), their contigs FASTA, and the original paired-end FASTQ reads, and need accurate per-MAG-cluster abundance estimates plus subspecies-level phylogenetic stratification rather than a marker-gene-only profile.
skills.name: mag-abundance-profiling-from-shotgun-reads
skills.search_text: mag-abundance-profiling-from-shotgun-reads Use when you have VAMB bins (clusters.tsv), their contigs FASTA, and the original paired-end FASTQ reads, and need accurate per-MAG-cluster abundance estimates plus subspecies-level phylogenetic stratification rather than a marker-gene-only profile. You only need a fast compositional profile from marker gene databases — mapping-based profilers like MetaPhlAn, MetaPhyler or mOTUs suffice and MAGinator's de novo MAG workflow is unnecessary. You have no MAG bins yet and no plan to assemble/bin — MAGinator requires VAMB clusters.tsv and contigs as input; run the reads_to_bins.Snakefile workflow (or your own assembly/binning) first. Your downstream question is single-sample taxonomic profiling with few samples — signature gene refinement requires multiple samples (--min_samples) and mixed-allele/noise behaviour at strain level may degrade beta diversity estimates (highest mixed-allele proportion observed was 86% in the honey-bee gut). http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Profile the absolute and relative abundances of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from shotgun metagenomics reads using MAGinator's de novo signature-gene approach, combining gene- and contig-based methods to reach subspecies-level resolution. Validated on the CAMI II strain-madness dataset with OPAL purity/completeness metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8
skills.summary: Profile the absolute and relative abundances of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from shotgun metagenomics reads using MAGinator's de novo signature-gene approach, combining gene- and contig-based methods to reach subspecies-level resolution. Validated on the CAMI II strain-madness dataset with OPAL purity/completeness metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a fast compositional profile from marker gene databases — mapping-based profilers like MetaPhlAn, MetaPhyler or mOTUs suffice and MAGinator's de novo MAG workflow is unnecessary. You have no MAG bins yet and no plan to assemble/bin — MAGinator requires VAMB clusters.tsv and contigs as input; run the reads_to_bins.Snakefile workflow (or your own assembly/binning) first. Your downstream question is single-sample taxonomic profiling with few samples — signature gene refinement requires multiple samples (--min_samples) and mixed-allele/noise behaviour at strain level may degrade beta diversity estimates (highest mixed-allele proportion observed was 86% in the honey-bee gut).

skills.description: Use when you have assembled metagenomic contigs from multiple samples in a group and need MetaBAT2 binning plus a per-sample MAG abundance table, e.g. on CAMISIM simulated reads from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.5155395.
skills.name: mag-abundance-quantification
skills.search_text: mag-abundance-quantification Use when you have assembled metagenomic contigs from multiple samples in a group and need MetaBAT2 binning plus a per-sample MAG abundance table, e.g. on CAMISIM simulated reads from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.5155395. Reads are long reads: alignment should be done with minimap2, not Bowtie2, because nf-core/mag gates alignment by read type You only need assembly or taxonomic classification without binning and abundance estimation The dataset has a single sample with no group information, so no cross-sample co-abundance patterns can be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quantifies per-sample abundances of metagenome assembled genomes (MAGs) produced by nf-core/mag, using per-sample read recruitment against assembled contigs (Bowtie2 for short reads, minimap2 for long reads) and MetaBAT2 co-abundance patterns within a sample group. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Quantifies per-sample abundances of metagenome assembled genomes (MAGs) produced by nf-core/mag, using per-sample read recruitment against assembled contigs (Bowtie2 for short reads, minimap2 for long reads) and MetaBAT2 co-abundance patterns within a sample group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are long reads: alignment should be done with minimap2, not Bowtie2, because nf-core/mag gates alignment by read type You only need assembly or taxonomic classification without binning and abundance estimation The dataset has a single sample with no group information, so no cross-sample co-abundance patterns can be computed

skills.description: Use when you have a MAG FASTA with an existing KEGG KO annotation (eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKOALA format) and need to recover missing KOs and improve MAG-derived GSMM metabolic capability predictions.
skills.name: mag-annotation-expansion-gsmm-gapfilling
skills.search_text: mag-annotation-expansion-gsmm-gapfilling Use when you have a MAG FASTA with an existing KEGG KO annotation (eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKOALA format) and need to recover missing KOs and improve MAG-derived GSMM metabolic capability predictions. Input is a complete isolate genome with exhaustive annotation rather than a gapped MAG, where annotation recovery adds little value You only need KEGG Module completeness tables without HMM search or model gap-filling — use --skip_hmm or --no_genome mode instead A draft GSMM does not exist and you do not intend to reconstruct one (stop after HMM analysis with --skip_gsmm) http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Expand KEGG functional annotations of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) with KEMET's HMM-based ortholog recovery (onebm mode) and use the recovered KOs to gapfill/reconstruct genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs), improving phenotype prediction toward complete-genome model accuracy. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Expand KEGG functional annotations of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) with KEMET's HMM-based ortholog recovery (onebm mode) and use the recovered KOs to gapfill/reconstruct genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs), improving phenotype prediction toward complete-genome model accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a complete isolate genome with exhaustive annotation rather than a gapped MAG, where annotation recovery adds little value You only need KEGG Module completeness tables without HMM search or model gap-filling — use --skip_hmm or --no_genome mode instead A draft GSMM does not exist and you do not intend to reconstruct one (stop after HMM analysis with --skip_gsmm)

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomic paired-end reads need to be assembled, binned into MAGs, and taxonomically classified, or when testing whether MAG classification accuracy (sensitivity, precision, FDR, balanced accuracy, F1) is robust to assembler choice.
skills.name: mag-binning-and-classification
skills.search_text: mag-binning-and-classification Use when shotgun metagenomic paired-end reads need to be assembled, binned into MAGs, and taxonomically classified, or when testing whether MAG classification accuracy (sensitivity, precision, FDR, balanced accuracy, F1) is robust to assembler choice. Input is raw unassembled short reads that are not quality-controlled or trimmed — the workflow assumes FastQC/Sickle (-q 32 -l 50) preprocessed reads for assembly The taxonomic classifier's reference must be prokaryotic (RefSeq bacteria/archaea); eukaryotic or viral MAGs are out of scope Machine has less than the ~22Gb storage for the kMetaShot HDF5 reference or insufficient RAM for reference loading (kMetaShot requires at least 32Gb memory to load the reference) http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A workflow that reconstructs MAGs from metagenomic reads (FastQC/Sickle QC, metaSPAdes/MegaHIT assembly, MetaBAT2 binning) and classifies them taxonomically up to strain level with the alignment-free kMetaShot k-mer/minimizer classifier, assessing whether classification reliability depends on the choice of meta-assembler. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: A workflow that reconstructs MAGs from metagenomic reads (FastQC/Sickle QC, metaSPAdes/MegaHIT assembly, MetaBAT2 binning) and classifies them taxonomically up to strain level with the alignment-free kMetaShot k-mer/minimizer classifier, assessing whether classification reliability depends on the choice of meta-assembler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unassembled short reads that are not quality-controlled or trimmed — the workflow assumes FastQC/Sickle (-q 32 -l 50) preprocessed reads for assembly The taxonomic classifier's reference must be prokaryotic (RefSeq bacteria/archaea); eukaryotic or viral MAGs are out of scope Machine has less than the ~22Gb storage for the kMetaShot HDF5 reference or insufficient RAM for reference loading (kMetaShot requires at least 32Gb memory to load the reference)

skills.description: Use when you have VAMB clusters.tsv plus assembled contigs and need taxonomic labels and MGS grouping of MAG clusters before abundance estimation, signature gene identification, or strain-level analysis with MAGinator.
skills.name: mag-cluster-taxonomic-annotation
skills.search_text: mag-cluster-taxonomic-annotation Use when you have VAMB clusters.tsv plus assembled contigs and need taxonomic labels and MGS grouping of MAG clusters before abundance estimation, signature gene identification, or strain-level analysis with MAGinator. Your MAGs are already taxonomically labelled via a database-derived binner (e.g. TaxVamb/Taxometer) rather than de novo VAMB clusters You only need to re-cluster species representatives without per-bin ORF calling and taxonomic scope assignment Input contigs and clusters.tsv still contain '@' characters that have not been replaced, which the README's preparatory sed steps exist to fix http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Taxonomically annotate de novo MAGs with GTDB-tk (release 220) and group VAMB clusters into metagenomic species (MGS) using MAGinator's taxonomic consensus and scope rules, which underpins downstream abundance estimation and mixed-allele profiling. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8
skills.summary: Taxonomically annotate de novo MAGs with GTDB-tk (release 220) and group VAMB clusters into metagenomic species (MGS) using MAGinator's taxonomic consensus and scope rules, which underpins downstream abundance estimation and mixed-allele profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your MAGs are already taxonomically labelled via a database-derived binner (e.g. TaxVamb/Taxometer) rather than de novo VAMB clusters You only need to re-cluster species representatives without per-bin ORF calling and taxonomic scope assignment Input contigs and clusters.tsv still contain '@' characters that have not been replaced, which the README's preparatory sed steps exist to fix

skills.description: Use when you have MAG or complete-genome FASTA files and need KEGG KO-level functional annotation plus Module completeness recap tables, especially for fragmented MAG assemblies where standard annotation tools miss orthologs.
skills.name: mag-functional-annotation
skills.search_text: mag-functional-annotation Use when you have MAG or complete-genome FASTA files and need KEGG KO-level functional annotation plus Module completeness recap tables, especially for fragmented MAG assemblies where standard annotation tools miss orthologs. When the goal is only Module completeness evaluation with no HMM-based ortholog expansion — use `--skip_hmm` workflows instead, since HMM search changes the hit set. When sequences are already provided as KEGG-annotated KO lists without a genome (use `--no_genome`, which stops after KEGG MODULES Completeness Evaluation). When annotating very short contigs or heavily truncated genes, where recovery rates drop (most clearly at 70% truncation in the MAG dataset) and results are unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Annotate MAGs and complete microbial genomes by calling genes with Prodigal, assigning KEGG KOs with eggNOG-mapper v2, and expanding the annotation with KEMET's profile HMM searches (default score-per-length threshold 0.43) to recover missing orthologs and summarize KEGG Module completeness. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Annotate MAGs and complete microbial genomes by calling genes with Prodigal, assigning KEGG KOs with eggNOG-mapper v2, and expanding the annotation with KEMET's profile HMM searches (default score-per-length threshold 0.43) to recover missing orthologs and summarize KEGG Module completeness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only Module completeness evaluation with no HMM-based ortholog expansion — use `--skip_hmm` workflows instead, since HMM search changes the hit set. When sequences are already provided as KEGG-annotated KO lists without a genome (use `--no_genome`, which stops after KEGG MODULES Completeness Evaluation). When annotating very short contigs or heavily truncated genes, where recovery rates drop (most clearly at 70% truncation in the MAG dataset) and results are unreliable.

skills.description: Use when building a de novo SourceApp source-associated genome database from mixed FASTA inputs (reference genomes plus MAGs) and low-quality or fragmented genome drafts must be excluded before ANI dereplication.
skills.name: mag-quality-filtering-checkm2
skills.search_text: mag-quality-filtering-checkm2 Use when building a de novo SourceApp source-associated genome database from mixed FASTA inputs (reference genomes plus MAGs) and low-quality or fragmented genome drafts must be excluded before ANI dereplication. Input is already a curated, pre-filtered database such as the SourceApp default database from Zenodo — no de novo quality filtering is needed The analysis goal is read-mapping source attribution with sourceapp.py on existing metagenomes, not building a new genome database Genomes must be assessed for taxonomic classification only (e.g., GTDB release 220 assignment) rather than completeness/redundancy quality http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Quality-filtering step in SourceApp database construction where CheckM2 scores input reference genomes and MAGs and genomes with aggregate quality (completeness − 5 × redundancy) below 50 are discarded before dereplication. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: Quality-filtering step in SourceApp database construction where CheckM2 scores input reference genomes and MAGs and genomes with aggregate quality (completeness − 5 × redundancy) below 50 are discarded before dereplication.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated, pre-filtered database such as the SourceApp default database from Zenodo — no de novo quality filtering is needed The analysis goal is read-mapping source attribution with sourceapp.py on existing metagenomes, not building a new genome database Genomes must be assessed for taxonomic classification only (e.g., GTDB release 220 assignment) rather than completeness/redundancy quality

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metagenome assembly pipelines on simulated (e.g. CAMISIM) short and long reads and you need to quantify how hybrid assembly and co-assembly change N50, assembly size, and the number of recovered MAGs.
skills.name: mag-reconstruction-counting-from-binning
skills.search_text: mag-reconstruction-counting-from-binning Use when benchmarking metagenome assembly pipelines on simulated (e.g. CAMISIM) short and long reads and you need to quantify how hybrid assembly and co-assembly change N50, assembly size, and the number of recovered MAGs. Input data is not metagenomic read data (e.g. isolate genomes or already-assembled contigs) — the skill requires raw short and/or long reads to assemble and bin. The analysis goal is taxonomic classification or functional annotation of known MAGs rather than comparing assembly/binning completeness across pipeline configurations. Read-type gating is unknown or mixed (e.g. PacBio reads that would be wrongly subjected to Porechop adapter trimming) — correct gating must be established before the comparison is valid. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Run nf-core/mag (v2.1.0) across short-read/hybrid × sample-wise/co-assembly settings on CAMISIM-simulated reads, then extract assembly size, N50, and reconstructed MAG counts from the assembly statistics and binning outputs to benchmark assembly continuity and completeness. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Run nf-core/mag (v2.1.0) across short-read/hybrid × sample-wise/co-assembly settings on CAMISIM-simulated reads, then extract assembly size, N50, and reconstructed MAG counts from the assembly statistics and binning outputs to benchmark assembly continuity and completeness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not metagenomic read data (e.g. isolate genomes or already-assembled contigs) — the skill requires raw short and/or long reads to assemble and bin. The analysis goal is taxonomic classification or functional annotation of known MAGs rather than comparing assembly/binning completeness across pipeline configurations. Read-type gating is unknown or mixed (e.g. PacBio reads that would be wrongly subjected to Porechop adapter trimming) — correct gating must be established before the comparison is valid.

skills.description: Use when you have paired MAG and matching complete isolate genomes (e.g. from NCBI/PATRIC) with KEGG KO annotations and need to benchmark HMM-recovered missing KOs against a complete-genome reference.
skills.name: mag-reference-genome-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: mag-reference-genome-concordance-analysis Use when you have paired MAG and matching complete isolate genomes (e.g. from NCBI/PATRIC) with KEGG KO annotations and need to benchmark HMM-recovered missing KOs against a complete-genome reference. You only have MAGs without matching complete reference isolate genomes — there is no reference against which to compute concordance. Your goal is KEGG Module completeness evaluation alone; run KEMET with --skip_hmm instead of the HMM concordance workflow. Your annotations are not in a supported KEGG KO format (eggnog / kaas / kofamkoala) — KEMET expects one of these annotation formats. http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quantifies agreement between KEGG ortholog (KO) hits recovered by KEMET profile HMM searches on MAGs versus the identical searches run on their corresponding complete reference isolate genomes, yielding precision/sensitivity-style concordance metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement between KEGG ortholog (KO) hits recovered by KEMET profile HMM searches on MAGs versus the identical searches run on their corresponding complete reference isolate genomes, yielding precision/sensitivity-style concordance metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have MAGs without matching complete reference isolate genomes — there is no reference against which to compute concordance. Your goal is KEGG Module completeness evaluation alone; run KEMET with --skip_hmm instead of the HMM concordance workflow. Your annotations are not in a supported KEGG KO format (eggnog / kaas / kofamkoala) — KEMET expects one of these annotation formats.

skills.description: Use when you have binned MAG FASTA files (from MetaBAT2 or similar) and need NCBI-taxonomy assignments up to strain level, comparing tools or benchmarking classification accuracy.
skills.name: mag-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: mag-taxonomic-classification Use when you have binned MAG FASTA files (from MetaBAT2 or similar) and need NCBI-taxonomy assignments up to strain level, comparing tools or benchmarking classification accuracy. Input is raw shotgun reads rather than binned MAG sequences — kMetaShot classifies assemblies/bins, not reads Available RAM cannot hold the ~22 Gb HDF5 reference (kMetaShot requires at least 32 Gb to load); use a marker-gene tool instead Target taxa are outside the prokaryotic reference (bacteria/archaea RefSeq genomes); eukaryotic or viral MAGs are out of scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Taxonomically classify metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) using kMetaShot, an alignment-free k-mer/minimizer classifier benchmarked against GTDBtk and CAMITAX, with an ass2ref reliability filter to drop unreliable calls. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: Taxonomically classify metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) using kMetaShot, an alignment-free k-mer/minimizer classifier benchmarked against GTDBtk and CAMITAX, with an ass2ref reliability filter to drop unreliable calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw shotgun reads rather than binned MAG sequences — kMetaShot classifies assemblies/bins, not reads Available RAM cannot hold the ~22 Gb HDF5 reference (kMetaShot requires at least 32 Gb to load); use a marker-gene tool instead Target taxa are outside the prokaryotic reference (bacteria/archaea RefSeq genomes); eukaryotic or viral MAGs are out of scope

skills.description: Use when assigning taxonomy to metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) produced by nf-core/mag or similar binning workflows, especially when bins have heterogeneous quality and a BUSCO-gated GTDB-Tk plus CAT/BAT fallback is appropriate.
skills.name: mag-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: mag-taxonomic-classification Use when assigning taxonomy to metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) produced by nf-core/mag or similar binning workflows, especially when bins have heterogeneous quality and a BUSCO-gated GTDB-Tk plus CAT/BAT fallback is appropriate. Input is raw reads or unassembled contigs rather than reconstructed MAG bins — this skill covers the final taxonomic annotation stage only All bins already have reference genome assignments and do not require marker-gene-based or ORF-based taxonomic classification Bins lack BUSCO completeness/contamination summaries, making the quality gating that determines GTDB-Tk eligibility impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstructs the final taxonomic classification stage of the nf-core/mag pipeline, in which MAGs passing BUSCO-based quality thresholds are classified with GTDB-Tk while remaining bins fall back to CAT/BAT, merging both results into a single per-bin taxonomy table. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Reconstructs the final taxonomic classification stage of the nf-core/mag pipeline, in which MAGs passing BUSCO-based quality thresholds are classified with GTDB-Tk while remaining bins fall back to CAT/BAT, merging both results into a single per-bin taxonomy table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or unassembled contigs rather than reconstructed MAG bins — this skill covers the final taxonomic annotation stage only All bins already have reference genome assignments and do not require marker-gene-based or ORF-based taxonomic classification Bins lack BUSCO completeness/contamination summaries, making the quality gating that determines GTDB-Tk eligibility impossible

skills.description: Use when draft metagenome-assembled genomes (e.g. estimated 91% and 60% complete) need automated phenotype predictions that are validated against an existing expert metabolic reconstruction.
skills.name: manual-metabolic-reconstruction-comparison
skills.search_text: manual-metabolic-reconstruction-comparison Use when draft metagenome-assembled genomes (e.g. estimated 91% and 60% complete) need automated phenotype predictions that are validated against an existing expert metabolic reconstruction. The input genomes are complete isolates already covered by GIDEON/Bergey's phenotype labels, so cross-validated Traitar accuracy suffices without a bespoke reconstruction comparison No prior manual metabolic reconstruction or phenotype table exists for the genomes, leaving no ground truth to compare against The goal is to integrate transcriptomic or other omics evidence — Traitar inference uses only protein family presence/absence http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduces the phenotyping of the biogas reactor population genomes unClos_1 and unFirm_1 with Traitar and benchmarks the predicted present/absent calls for 67 phenotypes against the manual metabolic reconstruction of Frank et al. (Table 4), quantifying recall and agreement on absent phenotypes. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00101-16
skills.summary: Reproduces the phenotyping of the biogas reactor population genomes unClos_1 and unFirm_1 with Traitar and benchmarks the predicted present/absent calls for 67 phenotypes against the manual metabolic reconstruction of Frank et al. (Table 4), quantifying recall and agreement on absent phenotypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input genomes are complete isolates already covered by GIDEON/Bergey's phenotype labels, so cross-validated Traitar accuracy suffices without a bespoke reconstruction comparison No prior manual metabolic reconstruction or phenotype table exists for the genomes, leaving no ground truth to compare against The goal is to integrate transcriptomic or other omics evidence — Traitar inference uses only protein family presence/absence

skills.description: Use when you have a gene-length-normalized gene abundance TSV plus a tab-separated gene-to-ortholog map (ortholog ID in column 1, gene ID in column 2) and need KO-level functional profiles.
skills.name: many-to-many-mapping-table-parsing
skills.search_text: many-to-many-mapping-table-parsing Use when you have a gene-length-normalized gene abundance TSV plus a tab-separated gene-to-ortholog map (ortholog ID in column 1, gene ID in column 2) and need KO-level functional profiles. Input is already an ortholog-level (e.g. KO-level) abundance table — no mapping-table parsing is needed, only downstream normalization or aggregation steps. You need reads mapped directly to functions without gene-level intermediates (read-based annotation) rather than gene-abundance-based annotation. The gene-to-ortholog map is strictly one-to-one, in which case simple summation (not fractional splitting across multiple KOs) is appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Parses a many-to-many gene-to-ortholog mapping table (e.g. UniRef90 genes to KEGG KOs) and converts a per-sample gene abundance table into an ortholog-level abundance table by splitting each gene's abundance fractionally across all orthologs it maps to, avoiding double-counting. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: Parses a many-to-many gene-to-ortholog mapping table (e.g. UniRef90 genes to KEGG KOs) and converts a per-sample gene abundance table into an ortholog-level abundance table by splitting each gene's abundance fractionally across all orthologs it maps to, avoiding double-counting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an ortholog-level (e.g. KO-level) abundance table — no mapping-table parsing is needed, only downstream normalization or aggregation steps. You need reads mapped directly to functions without gene-level intermediates (read-based annotation) rather than gene-abundance-based annotation. The gene-to-ortholog map is strictly one-to-one, in which case simple summation (not fractional splitting across multiple KOs) is appropriate.

skills.description: Use when building a distributed metagenomics reference database on Spark from minhash sketches stored in per-executor hash tables and the counts must be merged globally before writing to HDFS.
skills.name: map-reduce-key-count-merging
skills.search_text: map-reduce-key-count-merging Use when building a distributed metagenomics reference database on Spark from minhash sketches stored in per-executor hash tables and the counts must be merged globally before writing to HDFS. Running on a single workstation — use the AFS-MetaCache C++ version instead, which does not need a map-reduce merge across executors The database is already built and stored in HDFS — proceed directly to query mode (-m query) rather than re-merging Input is raw sequencing reads from a metagenomic sample (FASTA/FASTQ) rather than reference genome sequences — this merge step belongs to database construction, not classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 The MetaCacheSpark build phase in which executor-local minhash hash tables are globally merged via a map-reduce key-count operation across the Spark cluster, removing overpopulated k-mer features so the partitioned reference database remains loadable for classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: The MetaCacheSpark build phase in which executor-local minhash hash tables are globally merged via a map-reduce key-count operation across the Spark cluster, removing overpopulated k-mer features so the partitioned reference database remains loadable for classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Running on a single workstation — use the AFS-MetaCache C++ version instead, which does not need a map-reduce merge across executors The database is already built and stored in HDFS — proceed directly to query mode (-m query) rather than re-merging Input is raw sequencing reads from a metagenomic sample (FASTA/FASTQ) rather than reference genome sequences — this merge step belongs to database construction, not classification

skills.description: Use when a significant proportion of long (HiFi) metagenomic reads remain unmapped to an assembly and you need to determine whether low abundance (e.g. median k-mer abundance of 1), read length, or read quality explains the unassembled fraction.
skills.name: mapped-unmapped-read-fraction-comparison
skills.search_text: mapped-unmapped-read-fraction-comparison Use when a significant proportion of long (HiFi) metagenomic reads remain unmapped to an assembly and you need to determine whether low abundance (e.g. median k-mer abundance of 1), read length, or read quality explains the unassembled fraction. The dataset is short-read or hybrid rather than HiFi long reads — Mapler's evaluation and fractions workflow targets HiFi metagenome assemblies You only need bin-level quality (completeness/contamination via CheckM2/GTDB-Tk) rather than explaining reads left out of the assembly No assembly is available and the goal is de novo assembly benchmarking rather than read-fraction characterization http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Characterizes the mapped vs unmapped read fractions from aligning HiFi reads on a metagenome assembly (via the Mapler pipeline) to explain why reads failed to assemble — comparing read length, per-base quality, k-mer abundance (KAT), and taxonomic assignment (Kraken 2/Krona) between fractions. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Characterizes the mapped vs unmapped read fractions from aligning HiFi reads on a metagenome assembly (via the Mapler pipeline) to explain why reads failed to assemble — comparing read length, per-base quality, k-mer abundance (KAT), and taxonomic assignment (Kraken 2/Krona) between fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is short-read or hybrid rather than HiFi long reads — Mapler's evaluation and fractions workflow targets HiFi metagenome assemblies You only need bin-level quality (completeness/contamination via CheckM2/GTDB-Tk) rather than explaining reads left out of the assembly No assembly is available and the goal is de novo assembly benchmarking rather than read-fraction characterization

skills.description: Use when a raw nanopore signal mapper (e.g., RawHash) has produced mapping.paf and its mapping positions must be validated against sequence-level ground truth before downstream analysis.
skills.name: mapping-accuracy-evaluation-against-minimap2
skills.search_text: mapping-accuracy-evaluation-against-minimap2 Use when a raw nanopore signal mapper (e.g., RawHash) has produced mapping.paf and its mapping positions must be validated against sequence-level ground truth before downstream analysis. Output is not raw-signal mapping (e.g., Rawsamble all-vs-all overlaps for de novo assembly via miniasm) — there is no sequence-mapper ground truth to compare against. The mapper being validated does not report positions in the UNCALLED/Sigmap PAF template, making positional comparison ill-defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Validates raw-signal mapping output by checking that chain-derived mapping positions from RawHash's Sigmap-style chaining agree with minimap2-derived ground-truth positions, and that the output parses as the modified PAF template used by UNCALLED and Sigmap. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad272
skills.summary: Validates raw-signal mapping output by checking that chain-derived mapping positions from RawHash's Sigmap-style chaining agree with minimap2-derived ground-truth positions, and that the output parses as the modified PAF template used by UNCALLED and Sigmap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Output is not raw-signal mapping (e.g., Rawsamble all-vs-all overlaps for de novo assembly via miniasm) — there is no sequence-mapper ground truth to compare against. The mapper being validated does not report positions in the UNCALLED/Sigmap PAF template, making positional comparison ill-defined.

skills.description: Use when reconstructing full-length viral genome segments (e.g. influenza's 8 segments) from low-coverage metagenomic FASTQ data where de-novo assembly alone yields fragmented contigs.
skills.name: mapping-assembly-super-scaffold-construction
skills.search_text: mapping-assembly-super-scaffold-construction Use when reconstructing full-length viral genome segments (e.g. influenza's 8 segments) from low-coverage metagenomic FASTQ data where de-novo assembly alone yields fragmented contigs. Input is already assembled contigs or a feature/taxonomy table rather than raw FASTQ metagenomic reads The target organism is non-viral: contigs mapping outside the viral superkingdom are filtered by design Available memory is below the ~64 GB RAM required per simultaneous Virmap.pl instance when processing large datasets (e.g. 1.75 billion reads) http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Constructs virus-like super-scaffolds by hybridizing a mapping assembly (read recruitment against Genbank viral/phage references) with a de-novo assembly, using VirMAP's tiered nucleotide and amino-acid alignment merging to reconstruct contiguous viral genomes from metagenomic reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Constructs virus-like super-scaffolds by hybridizing a mapping assembly (read recruitment against Genbank viral/phage references) with a de-novo assembly, using VirMAP's tiered nucleotide and amino-acid alignment merging to reconstruct contiguous viral genomes from metagenomic reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled contigs or a feature/taxonomy table rather than raw FASTQ metagenomic reads The target organism is non-viral: contigs mapping outside the viral superkingdom are filtered by design Available memory is below the ~64 GB RAM required per simultaneous Virmap.pl instance when processing large datasets (e.g. 1.75 billion reads)

skills.description: Use when processing a mapped metagenomic .bam file for microdiversity or strain-level analysis and you need to remove un-paired reads and apply pair-level filters (orientation, insert size, mapQ, nucleotide identity) before downstream profiling.
skills.name: mapping-quality-based-read-pair-filtering
skills.search_text: mapping-quality-based-read-pair-filtering Use when processing a mapped metagenomic .bam file for microdiversity or strain-level analysis and you need to remove un-paired reads and apply pair-level filters (orientation, insert size, mapQ, nucleotide identity) before downstream profiling. Input reads are single-end/un-paired and you intend to retain them — inStrain removes all un-paired reads by default You only need raw coverage/breadth estimates without filtering — a faster tool like CoverM may be more appropriate than pair-level filtering You need per-read filtering statistics rather than pair-level decisions — inStrain applies filters to pairs of reads in combination, not individual reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstructs inStrain's four-stage read filtering of a sorted .bam file: un-paired reads are removed by default and the orientation/insert-size, mapQ, and nucleotide-identity filters are applied to read pairs in combination rather than to individual reads, reducing erroneous mappings before coverage, SNV, and linkage analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
