skills.summary: Assesses the quality of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) by running CheckM2 v1.0.1 'predict' to estimate per-genome Completeness and Contamination, then classifying each genome into near-complete / high-quality / medium-quality tiers under criteria revised from the MIMAG standard, retaining only genomes with ≥50% completeness and <5% contamination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is viral genome sequences — use CheckV instead (viral genomes were assessed at ≥50% completeness via CheckV, not CheckM2) Input is fungal/eukaryotic bins — the VMGC pipeline used BUSCO with thresholds C:>50% and D:<5% for fungi, not CheckM2 Input genomes are already annotated with quality values in VMGC_prokaryote_MAG.info and the task is only to read the tiers, not recompute them

skills.description: Use when contigs from a strain-aware metagenome assembler must be scored against known reference genomes to quantify reconstruction accuracy (genome fraction, misassemblies) across varying coverage levels or conditions.
skills.name: metagenome-assembly-accuracy-evaluation-with-metaquast
skills.search_text: metagenome-assembly-accuracy-evaluation-with-metaquast Use when contigs from a strain-aware metagenome assembler must be scored against known reference genomes to quantify reconstruction accuracy (genome fraction, misassemblies) across varying coverage levels or conditions. The assembly quality must be assessed without any reference genomes available — metaQuast accuracy evaluation requires known references (de novo-only scenarios cannot yield genome fraction) The goal is only to measure contig length statistics (e.g. N50) via plain Quast rather than reference-based accuracy against spiked-in strain genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Evaluates strain-aware metagenome assemblies against known reference genomes using metaQuast, extracting genome fraction and misassembly-related metrics — as done for StrainXpress contigs assembled from the Salmonella spike-in datasets (5x–40x coverage in real gut metagenomes). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac543
skills.summary: Evaluates strain-aware metagenome assemblies against known reference genomes using metaQuast, extracting genome fraction and misassembly-related metrics — as done for StrainXpress contigs assembled from the Salmonella spike-in datasets (5x–40x coverage in real gut metagenomes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly quality must be assessed without any reference genomes available — metaQuast accuracy evaluation requires known references (de novo-only scenarios cannot yield genome fraction) The goal is only to measure contig length statistics (e.g. N50) via plain Quast rather than reference-based accuracy against spiked-in strain genomes

skills.description: Use when starting from raw paired-end FASTQ reads of a multi-sample shotgun metagenomics study (e.g. reads.csv sample index) and you need de novo MAGs plus VAMB clusters as upstream input for MAGinator profiling.
skills.name: metagenome-assembly-and-binning
skills.search_text: metagenome-assembly-and-binning Use when starting from raw paired-end FASTQ reads of a multi-sample shotgun metagenomics study (e.g. reads.csv sample index) and you need de novo MAGs plus VAMB clusters as upstream input for MAGinator profiling. Input is already a feature/abundance table (e.g. MetaPhlAn2 profiles) rather than raw reads — assembly and binning would be unnecessary. You have only single-sample data with low depth where multi-sample VAMB binning performs poorly (VAMB performs excellently with multiple samples, 'pretty good on single-sample data'). You only need reference-based taxonomic profiling (MetaPhlAn/mOTUs marker-gene mapping) rather than de novo MAG reconstruction. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Preprocess shotgun metagenomics reads, assemble them per-sample, co-assemble contigs, and bin contigs into metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) with VAMB, producing the clusters.tsv, all_assemblies.fasta and dRep species-level cluster files that MAGinator requires as input. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8
skills.summary: Preprocess shotgun metagenomics reads, assemble them per-sample, co-assemble contigs, and bin contigs into metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) with VAMB, producing the clusters.tsv, all_assemblies.fasta and dRep species-level cluster files that MAGinator requires as input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/abundance table (e.g. MetaPhlAn2 profiles) rather than raw reads — assembly and binning would be unnecessary. You have only single-sample data with low depth where multi-sample VAMB binning performs poorly (VAMB performs excellently with multiple samples, 'pretty good on single-sample data'). You only need reference-based taxonomic profiling (MetaPhlAn/mOTUs marker-gene mapping) rather than de novo MAG reconstruction.

skills.description: Use when comparing metagenome assemblers on mock-community datasets (MP mock, GIS20) where reference genomes are known and NGA50, misassembly, and interspecies-misassembly metrics must be reproduced.
skills.name: metagenome-assembly-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metagenome-assembly-benchmarking Use when comparing metagenome assemblers on mock-community datasets (MP mock, GIS20) where reference genomes are known and NGA50, misassembly, and interspecies-misassembly metrics must be reproduced. Real environmental/human microbiome data with no reference genomes — metaQUAST-based NGA50 and interspecies misassembly counts cannot be computed without mock references Reference-based (mapping) assembly workflows — the article notes 'this study focuses on de novo methods, and reference information has not been well examined' Datasets lacking a short-read paired-end library — MetaPlatanus requires at least one short-read paired-end library http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmark de novo metagenome assemblers (MetaPlatanus vs IDBA-UD, SPAdes, metaSPAdes, MEGAHIT, metaFlye, OPERA-MS) on mock communities with known references, using NGA50 and misassembly metrics from QUAST/metaQUAST. Rationale: contiguity alone is insufficient — interspecies misassemblies must be quantified to detect false joins. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Benchmark de novo metagenome assemblers (MetaPlatanus vs IDBA-UD, SPAdes, metaSPAdes, MEGAHIT, metaFlye, OPERA-MS) on mock communities with known references, using NGA50 and misassembly metrics from QUAST/metaQUAST. Rationale: contiguity alone is insufficient — interspecies misassemblies must be quantified to detect false joins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real environmental/human microbiome data with no reference genomes — metaQUAST-based NGA50 and interspecies misassembly counts cannot be computed without mock references Reference-based (mapping) assembly workflows — the article notes 'this study focuses on de novo methods, and reference information has not been well examined' Datasets lacking a short-read paired-end library — MetaPlatanus requires at least one short-read paired-end library

skills.description: Use when comparing hybrid vs. short-read-only assembly, or group-wise co-assembly vs. sample-wise assembly, using metrics like N50, assembly size, and MAG counts on simulated or real metagenomic time-series data.
skills.name: metagenome-assembly-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metagenome-assembly-benchmarking Use when comparing hybrid vs. short-read-only assembly, or group-wise co-assembly vs. sample-wise assembly, using metrics like N50, assembly size, and MAG counts on simulated or real metagenomic time-series data. The analysis goal is taxonomic classification or binning quality alone rather than comparing assembly strategies — nf-core/mag supports those steps but this skill targets assembly metrics. Input data is a single-isolate genome assembly rather than metagenomic reads; hybrid-assembly and co-assembly comparisons are not meaningful there. Reads are already assembled contigs — re-running the four assembly settings requires raw FASTQ input. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark metagenome assembly strategies by running nf-core/mag v2.1.0 on CAMISIM-simulated reads under four settings (short/hybrid × sample-wise/co-assembly) and comparing assembly size, N50, and number of reconstructed MAGs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Benchmark metagenome assembly strategies by running nf-core/mag v2.1.0 on CAMISIM-simulated reads under four settings (short/hybrid × sample-wise/co-assembly) and comparing assembly size, N50, and number of reconstructed MAGs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is taxonomic classification or binning quality alone rather than comparing assembly strategies — nf-core/mag supports those steps but this skill targets assembly metrics. Input data is a single-isolate genome assembly rather than metagenomic reads; hybrid-assembly and co-assembly comparisons are not meaningful there. Reads are already assembled contigs — re-running the four assembly settings requires raw FASTQ input.

skills.description: Use when HiFi long-read FASTQ reads and a metagenome assembly (FASTA, built-in or user-provided under outputs/<sample>/<assembler>/assembly.fasta) are available and you need to quantify how representative the assembly is of the sequenced sample.
skills.name: metagenome-assembly-evaluation
skills.search_text: metagenome-assembly-evaluation Use when HiFi long-read FASTQ reads and a metagenome assembly (FASTA, built-in or user-provided under outputs/<sample>/<assembler>/assembly.fasta) are available and you need to quantify how representative the assembly is of the sequenced sample. Only short-read (Illumina) data is available — Mapler is designed for HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies (hybrid data would need OPERA-MS instead, not the primary evaluation route) You need de novo genome reconstruction benchmarks rather than assembly quality assessment — Mapler evaluates assemblies; it does not replace comparing binning-only workflows Input is raw reads with no assembly and no assembler enabled in the configfile — the evaluation rules require an assembly (built-in or user-submitted) to evaluate http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Assess the quality of HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies — either produced by Mapler's assemblers (metaMDBG, metaflye, hifiasm-meta) or user-submitted — using aligned read/base ratios, bin quality classification (CheckM2, GTDB-Tk), and k-mer/taxonomic analysis of mapped vs unmapped reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Assess the quality of HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies — either produced by Mapler's assemblers (metaMDBG, metaflye, hifiasm-meta) or user-submitted — using aligned read/base ratios, bin quality classification (CheckM2, GTDB-Tk), and k-mer/taxonomic analysis of mapped vs unmapped reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only short-read (Illumina) data is available — Mapler is designed for HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies (hybrid data would need OPERA-MS instead, not the primary evaluation route) You need de novo genome reconstruction benchmarks rather than assembly quality assessment — Mapler evaluates assemblies; it does not replace comparing binning-only workflows Input is raw reads with no assembly and no assembler enabled in the configfile — the evaluation rules require an assembly (built-in or user-submitted) to evaluate

skills.description: Use when running Strainberry on a strain-oblivious long-read assembly (FASTA plus sorted, indexed BAM) and you need to control iteration count via the Hamming rate improvement stopping rule and --max-strains multiplicity cap.
skills.name: metagenome-assembly-iteration-management
skills.search_text: metagenome-assembly-iteration-management Use when running Strainberry on a strain-oblivious long-read assembly (FASTA plus sorted, indexed BAM) and you need to control iteration count via the Hamming rate improvement stopping rule and --max-strains multiplicity cap. When the metagenome is high-complexity rather than single-sample low-complexity — Strainberry relies uniquely on long-read data and is designed for low-complexity metagenomes When strain-oblivious contigs would need separation into a variable number of strains within the same contig (high strain variability) — not handled by the method When input reads are short reads — existing strain-level assembly approaches based on short reads cannot be reused for long reads, and Strainberry requires long-read alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Manages Strainberry's iterative strain-separation loop, deciding when to trigger an additional phasing/assembly/scaffolding round based on average Hamming rate improvement and when to stop (criterion failure or maximum strain multiplicity). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Manages Strainberry's iterative strain-separation loop, deciding when to trigger an additional phasing/assembly/scaffolding round based on average Hamming rate improvement and when to stop (criterion failure or maximum strain multiplicity).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the metagenome is high-complexity rather than single-sample low-complexity — Strainberry relies uniquely on long-read data and is designed for low-complexity metagenomes When strain-oblivious contigs would need separation into a variable number of strains within the same contig (high strain variability) — not handled by the method When input reads are short reads — existing strain-level assembly approaches based on short reads cannot be reused for long reads, and Strainberry requires long-read alignments

skills.description: Use when evaluating a HiFi long-read metagenome assembly by quantifying the proportion of raw reads and read bases that align to contigs, optionally stratified by bin quality (e.g. medium quality or higher).
skills.name: metagenome-assembly-mapping-ratio-computation
skills.search_text: metagenome-assembly-mapping-ratio-computation Use when evaluating a HiFi long-read metagenome assembly by quantifying the proportion of raw reads and read bases that align to contigs, optionally stratified by bin quality (e.g. medium quality or higher). The goal is assembly reconstruction itself rather than evaluation — Mapler's evaluation ratio is an assessment metric, not an assembly step Only short-read data is available — the pipeline and its benchmarks target HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies A bin-quality-stratified mapping report is needed but binning/checkm cannot be enabled (bins absent), in which case only the unstratified report.txt can be produced http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes aligned read and aligned base ratios of HiFi reads on metagenome assembly contigs, optionally split by bin quality class, to quantify how representative an assembly is of the sequenced sample. Part of the Mapler (MAEPLR) Snakemake pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Computes aligned read and aligned base ratios of HiFi reads on metagenome assembly contigs, optionally split by bin quality class, to quantify how representative an assembly is of the sequenced sample. Part of the Mapler (MAEPLR) Snakemake pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is assembly reconstruction itself rather than evaluation — Mapler's evaluation ratio is an assessment metric, not an assembly step Only short-read data is available — the pipeline and its benchmarks target HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies A bin-quality-stratified mapping report is needed but binning/checkm cannot be enabled (bins absent), in which case only the unstratified report.txt can be produced

skills.description: Use when a set of binned metagenome contigs (e.g. MetaBAT2 bins from a HiFi co-assembly) needs to be assigned quality labels from CheckM2 completeness/contamination values for assembly comparison or reporting.
skills.name: metagenome-bin-quality-classification
skills.search_text: metagenome-bin-quality-classification Use when a set of binned metagenome contigs (e.g. MetaBAT2 bins from a HiFi co-assembly) needs to be assigned quality labels from CheckM2 completeness/contamination values for assembly comparison or reporting. Input is raw reads or an unbinned assembly with no MAG bins — quality categories are undefined without bins No completeness/contamination estimates are available (e.g. CheckM2 has not been run or the quality_report.tsv is missing) The goal is taxonomic placement of bins rather than quality tiering — use GTDB-Tk classification instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Classifies metagenome assembly bins into the GSC/MIMAG-style quality categories used by Mapler — near complete, high, medium and low quality — by combining CheckM2 completeness and contamination estimates with single-contig criteria, and reporting per-bin and per-category summaries. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Classifies metagenome assembly bins into the GSC/MIMAG-style quality categories used by Mapler — near complete, high, medium and low quality — by combining CheckM2 completeness and contamination estimates with single-contig criteria, and reporting per-bin and per-category summaries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or an unbinned assembly with no MAG bins — quality categories are undefined without bins No completeness/contamination estimates are available (e.g. CheckM2 has not been run or the quality_report.tsv is missing) The goal is taxonomic placement of bins rather than quality tiering — use GTDB-Tk classification instead

skills.description: Use when binning has produced MAG FASTA bins and you need BUSCO- or CheckM2-estimated completeness/contamination scores to gate which bins go to GTDB-Tk versus CAT/BAT, or to report MAG quality.
skills.name: metagenome-binning-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: metagenome-binning-quality-assessment Use when binning has produced MAG FASTA bins and you need BUSCO- or CheckM2-estimated completeness/contamination scores to gate which bins go to GTDB-Tk versus CAT/BAT, or to report MAG quality. Input is raw metagenomic reads or assemblies that have not yet been binned into MAG FASTA bins — quality assessment needs discrete genome bins The goal is taxonomic classification independent of quality gating — CAT/BAT can classify any MAG without BUSCO thresholds, so no quality step is needed first Analyzing metatranscriptomic or functional-annotation workflows — the paper notes functional annotation is a step 'not yet included' in nf-core/mag 2.1.0 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assesses the quality (completeness and contamination) of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) produced by the binning step of nf-core/mag using marker-gene-based estimators (BUSCO, CheckM2), and uses these estimates to gate downstream taxonomic classification with GTDB-Tk versus CAT/BAT. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Assesses the quality (completeness and contamination) of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) produced by the binning step of nf-core/mag using marker-gene-based estimators (BUSCO, CheckM2), and uses these estimates to gate downstream taxonomic classification with GTDB-Tk versus CAT/BAT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metagenomic reads or assemblies that have not yet been binned into MAG FASTA bins — quality assessment needs discrete genome bins The goal is taxonomic classification independent of quality gating — CAT/BAT can classify any MAG without BUSCO thresholds, so no quality step is needed first Analyzing metatranscriptomic or functional-annotation workflows — the paper notes functional annotation is a step 'not yet included' in nf-core/mag 2.1.0

skills.description: Use when you need simulated long-read metagenome communities of known strain composition (e.g. 2-5 conspecific E. coli strains, Mock3 downsampling at 5x-50x) to benchmark strain-separation tools like Strainberry.
skills.name: metagenome-community-composition-design
skills.search_text: metagenome-community-composition-design Use when you need simulated long-read metagenome communities of known strain composition (e.g. 2-5 conspecific E. coli strains, Mock3 downsampling at 5x-50x) to benchmark strain-separation tools like Strainberry. The input is real (non-simulated) sequencing data with unknown strain composition — this skill designs reference-truth communities, it does not characterize real samples Short-read data or Illumina simulation is required — the workflow uses Badread PacBio 2016 error modelling and PacBio-mode minimap2 alignment High-complexity metagenomes with many strains are the target — Strainberry benchmarks target low-complexity communities (2-5 conspecific strains) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Design and simulate conspecific-strain metagenome communities (PacBio long reads) with Badread to benchmark strain-resolved assembly: build strain-oblivious references with metaFlye and read alignments with minimap2/samtools, catalogued in a manifest TSV. This recreates the Strainberry benchmark datasets for coverage (5x-50x Mock3), divergence, and strain-number (2-5 E. coli strains) tests. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Design and simulate conspecific-strain metagenome communities (PacBio long reads) with Badread to benchmark strain-resolved assembly: build strain-oblivious references with metaFlye and read alignments with minimap2/samtools, catalogued in a manifest TSV. This recreates the Strainberry benchmark datasets for coverage (5x-50x Mock3), divergence, and strain-number (2-5 E. coli strains) tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real (non-simulated) sequencing data with unknown strain composition — this skill designs reference-truth communities, it does not characterize real samples Short-read data or Illumina simulation is required — the workflow uses Badread PacBio 2016 error modelling and PacBio-mode minimap2 alignment High-complexity metagenomes with many strains are the target — Strainberry benchmarks target low-complexity communities (2-5 conspecific strains)

skills.description: Use when a reproduction task requires the HiSeq, MiSeq or simBA-5 metagenomes referenced by NCBI SRA accessions (SRS019120, SRS014468, SRS015055) as classification-benchmark input.
skills.name: metagenome-dataset-retrieval-sra
skills.search_text: metagenome-dataset-retrieval-sra Use when a reproduction task requires the HiSeq, MiSeq or simBA-5 metagenomes referenced by NCBI SRA accessions (SRS019120, SRS014468, SRS015055) as classification-benchmark input. The benchmark read sets are already available locally as trimmed FASTA/FASTQ files — re-download or re-simulate would waste effort and risk version drift. The analysis target is classifying reads with Kraken/Megablast/MetaPhlAn rather than obtaining the input metagenomes (use the classification/benchmarking skills instead). A different metagenome (e.g. the simMC low/medium complexity set or a real environmental sample) is required — this skill only covers the HiSeq, MiSeq and simBA-5 benchmark sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Retrieves the three simulated benchmark metagenomes used by the Kraken paper — the HiSeq and MiSeq metagenomes by accession from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive, and the simBA-5 metagenome generated with the Mason read simulator — so that downstream classification speed and accuracy benchmarks start from the paper's exact read sets. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Retrieves the three simulated benchmark metagenomes used by the Kraken paper — the HiSeq and MiSeq metagenomes by accession from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive, and the simBA-5 metagenome generated with the Mason read simulator — so that downstream classification speed and accuracy benchmarks start from the paper's exact read sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The benchmark read sets are already available locally as trimmed FASTA/FASTQ files — re-download or re-simulate would waste effort and risk version drift. The analysis target is classifying reads with Kraken/Megablast/MetaPhlAn rather than obtaining the input metagenomes (use the classification/benchmarking skills instead). A different metagenome (e.g. the simMC low/medium complexity set or a real environmental sample) is required — this skill only covers the HiSeq, MiSeq and simBA-5 benchmark sets.

skills.description: Use when preprocessed metagenomic FASTQ reads (short-only, long-only, or hybrid short+long) per sample must be assembled de novo into contigs and per-assembler quality summaries are needed.
skills.name: metagenome-de-novo-assembly
skills.search_text: metagenome-de-novo-assembly Use when preprocessed metagenomic FASTQ reads (short-only, long-only, or hybrid short+long) per sample must be assembled de novo into contigs and per-assembler quality summaries are needed. Input reads are still raw/unpreprocessed — the assembler expects preprocessed FASTQ files, not raw sequencing output A complete reference genome exists and a reference-guided (mapping-based) approach would be more appropriate than reference-independent de novo assembly The goal is binning or taxonomic classification of existing contigs rather than producing the assemblies themselves http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reconstructs metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) contigs by de novo assembly of preprocessed short reads with MEGAHIT or SPAdes inside the nf-core/mag Nextflow pipeline, dispatching to hybridSPAdes when long reads are available, and assessing assembly quality with QUAST. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Reconstructs metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) contigs by de novo assembly of preprocessed short reads with MEGAHIT or SPAdes inside the nf-core/mag Nextflow pipeline, dispatching to hybridSPAdes when long reads are available, and assessing assembly quality with QUAST.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are still raw/unpreprocessed — the assembler expects preprocessed FASTQ files, not raw sequencing output A complete reference genome exists and a reference-guided (mapping-based) approach would be more appropriate than reference-independent de novo assembly The goal is binning or taxonomic classification of existing contigs rather than producing the assemblies themselves

skills.description: Use when you need to assemble individual strain-level genomes de novo from Illumina metagenomic short reads (interleaved FASTQ) and compare reconstruction quality against assemblers.
skills.name: metagenome-de-novo-assembly-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: metagenome-de-novo-assembly-pipeline-execution Use when you need to assemble individual strain-level genomes de novo from Illumina metagenomic short reads (interleaved FASTQ) and compare reconstruction quality against assemblers. skills.summary: Executes a de novo, strain-aware metagenome assembly benchmark by running StrainXpress (and competitor assemblers IDBA-UD, SPAdes, MetaSPAdes, GATB-Minia, MEGAHIT) on interleaved Illumina FASTQ inputs and scoring contig sets with Quast metrics such as Genome Fraction, NGA50, and Error Rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are third-generation (PacBio/ONT) long reads — the article states the high Error Rate of third-generation reads introduces unresolved issues The goal is reference-assisted assembly rather than de novo, reference-bias-free reconstruction The input is already assembled contigs rather than raw short reads

skills.description: Use when you have paired MAG and complete reference genome FASTAs with KEGG KO annotations and need to quantify how faithfully HMM-recovered annotations on MAGs reproduce isolate-genome annotations.
skills.name: metagenome-functional-annotation-comparison
skills.search_text: metagenome-functional-annotation-comparison Use when you have paired MAG and complete reference genome FASTAs with KEGG KO annotations and need to quantify how faithfully HMM-recovered annotations on MAGs reproduce isolate-genome annotations. The goal is KEGG Module completeness evaluation only (no HMM hit benchmarking) — use --skip_hmm outputs instead of running paired --hmm_mode onebm searches No matching reference isolate genome exists for the MAG, since per-pair set comparison and concordance fractions cannot be computed Evaluating de novo GSMM gapfilling quality — that requires --gsmm_mode and flux variability analysis, not HMM hit concordance http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 A benchmarking skill that compares KEGG ortholog hits recovered by KEMET HMM profile searches on MAGs against the hits found in matching reference isolate genomes, quantifying annotation-recovery concordance as precision, sensitivity, and shared/unique hit fractions. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that compares KEGG ortholog hits recovered by KEMET HMM profile searches on MAGs against the hits found in matching reference isolate genomes, quantifying annotation-recovery concordance as precision, sensitivity, and shared/unique hit fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is KEGG Module completeness evaluation only (no HMM hit benchmarking) — use --skip_hmm outputs instead of running paired --hmm_mode onebm searches No matching reference isolate genome exists for the MAG, since per-pair set comparison and concordance fractions cannot be computed Evaluating de novo GSMM gapfilling quality — that requires --gsmm_mode and flux variability analysis, not HMM hit concordance

skills.description: Use when the input is a closed-reference-picked 16S OTU table (e.g., Greengenes+IMG, QIIME 1.5.0-dev/uclust) and the goal is to infer KO/gene family abundances or pathway-level functional profiles without shotgun metagenome data.
skills.name: metagenome-functional-prediction-from-16s
skills.search_text: metagenome-functional-prediction-from-16s Use when the input is a closed-reference-picked 16S OTU table (e.g., Greengenes+IMG, QIIME 1.5.0-dev/uclust) and the goal is to infer KO/gene family abundances or pathway-level functional profiles without shotgun metagenome data. When viral or eukaryotic metagenome components are of interest — the 16S-based system only covers bacterial and archaeal genomes. When strain-level variation is the target — the software cannot distinguish variation among strains with identical marker gene sequences. When the expected NSTI is high (broad phylogenetic gaps in the reference database), prediction of laterally transferred or rapidly evolving gene families will be unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Predict metagenome gene family (KO) abundance from 16S rRNA data using PICRUSt, which normalizes OTU tables by predicted 16S copy number, applies extended ancestral-state reconstruction on a marker gene tree, and combines predicted gene contents into a composite metagenome per sample. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
