skills.search_text: metagenomic-annotation-statistics-aggregation Use when you have GeneMark-HM output on human microbiome metagenome assemblies and need to quantify how many contigs were assigned to species-level pan-genomes versus handled by the GeneMarkS-2 or MetaGeneMark fallback branches. Input sequences are complete prokaryotic genomes or non-human-microbiome metagenomes; the pan-genome database and model selection were built specifically for human microbiome contigs You need absolute gene-prediction accuracy evaluation against truth labels; this skill only quantifies model-branch routing, not prediction accuracy (which requires the paper's simulated metagenome benchmarks) The pan-genome blastn database has not been built and the branch identity per contig cannot be recovered from the run http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Aggregates per-contig gene-prediction branch assignments from a GeneMark-HM run (pan-genome-matched GeneMark.hmm-2, GeneMarkS-2 for longer unmatched contigs, MetaGeneMark for shorter unmatched contigs) into fractions comparable to the paper's Table 6, which reports 99.4% (gut), 89.0% (oral) and 79.4% (skin) pan-genome assignment rates. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047
skills.summary: Aggregates per-contig gene-prediction branch assignments from a GeneMark-HM run (pan-genome-matched GeneMark.hmm-2, GeneMarkS-2 for longer unmatched contigs, MetaGeneMark for shorter unmatched contigs) into fractions comparable to the paper's Table 6, which reports 99.4% (gut), 89.0% (oral) and 79.4% (skin) pan-genome assignment rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are complete prokaryotic genomes or non-human-microbiome metagenomes; the pan-genome database and model selection were built specifically for human microbiome contigs You need absolute gene-prediction accuracy evaluation against truth labels; this skill only quantifies model-branch routing, not prediction accuracy (which requires the paper's simulated metagenome benchmarks) The pan-genome blastn database has not been built and the branch identity per contig cannot be recovered from the run

skills.description: Use when comparing how many protein sequences different de novo assemblers recover from the same metagenomic reads, or when reproducing the Plass 2–10x recovery claim on complex metagenomes.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembler-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembler-benchmarking Use when comparing how many protein sequences different de novo assemblers recover from the same metagenomic reads, or when reproducing the Plass 2–10x recovery claim on complex metagenomes. The goal is strain-resolved nucleotide assembly of viral genomes or 16S rRNAs — use PenguiN instead, which assembles 3–40x more complete viral genomes and 6x more 16S rRNA sequences than Megahit/SPAdes Input is already assembled contigs or a protein catalogue — benchmarking requires raw short reads run through each assembler The sample is a simple isolate genome rather than a complex metagenomic/metatranscriptomic dataset, where Plass's recovery advantage was demonstrated http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmarks protein-level assembly (Plass) against nucleotide-level assemblers (Megahit, SPAdes variants) by comparing non-redundant protein sequence recovery from the same metagenomic reads, to quantify the reported 2–10x recovery improvement. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41592-019-0437-4
skills.summary: Benchmarks protein-level assembly (Plass) against nucleotide-level assemblers (Megahit, SPAdes variants) by comparing non-redundant protein sequence recovery from the same metagenomic reads, to quantify the reported 2–10x recovery improvement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is strain-resolved nucleotide assembly of viral genomes or 16S rRNAs — use PenguiN instead, which assembles 3–40x more complete viral genomes and 6x more 16S rRNA sequences than Megahit/SPAdes Input is already assembled contigs or a protein catalogue — benchmarking requires raw short reads run through each assembler The sample is a simple isolate genome rather than a complex metagenomic/metatranscriptomic dataset, where Plass's recovery advantage was demonstrated

skills.description: Use when short-read metagenomic data must be assembled and no single assembler is obviously appropriate; comparing SPAdes, metaSPAdes, and MEGAHIT by N50 lets contiguity decide the assembly carried forward.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembler-comparison
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembler-comparison Use when short-read metagenomic data must be assembled and no single assembler is obviously appropriate; comparing SPAdes, metaSPAdes, and MEGAHIT by N50 lets contiguity decide the assembly carried forward. Input is already assembled contigs or long reads — use virMine's '-A' option instead of short-read assembly Only a single-end read set is available and comparison across all three assemblers is not required Prior knowledge pins the correct assembler for the sample type, making a three-way N50 comparison unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Run multiple metagenomic assemblers (SPAdes, metaSPAdes, and MEGAHIT) on the same short-read input and select the assembly with the greatest N50 value for downstream analysis, as implemented in virMine 2.0's all3 option. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/mra.00107-22
skills.summary: Run multiple metagenomic assemblers (SPAdes, metaSPAdes, and MEGAHIT) on the same short-read input and select the assembly with the greatest N50 value for downstream analysis, as implemented in virMine 2.0's all3 option.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled contigs or long reads — use virMine's '-A' option instead of short-read assembly Only a single-end read set is available and comparison across all three assemblers is not required Prior knowledge pins the correct assembler for the sample type, making a three-way N50 comparison unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when building gene-level functional abundance profiles from shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads via de novo assembly and UniRef90 gene annotation, e.g. as input to gene-level MWAS case-control tests.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-based-gene-profiling
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-based-gene-profiling Use when building gene-level functional abundance profiles from shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads via de novo assembly and UniRef90 gene annotation, e.g. as input to gene-level MWAS case-control tests. Input reads have not passed read QC (Step 1, OMARU_read_QC.sm) — the workflow expects QCed FASTQ in result/QC/QCed_fastq The goal is phylogenetic (taxon-level) profiling from a clade reference such as UHGG/CHOCO rather than gene-level functional profiling Only amplicon (16S) data are available — the pipeline is designed for shotgun sequencing reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs OMARU's assembly-based functional (gene-level) profiling, in which shotgun reads are de novo assembled per sample with MEGAHIT, ORFs are predicted with Prokka, assigned gene identities via DIAMOND alignment against UniRef90, and gene abundances are quantified, length-normalized, and rank-based inverse normal transformed. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: Reconstructs OMARU's assembly-based functional (gene-level) profiling, in which shotgun reads are de novo assembled per sample with MEGAHIT, ORFs are predicted with Prokka, assigned gene identities via DIAMOND alignment against UniRef90, and gene abundances are quantified, length-normalized, and rank-based inverse normal transformed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not passed read QC (Step 1, OMARU_read_QC.sm) — the workflow expects QCed FASTQ in result/QC/QCed_fastq The goal is phylogenetic (taxon-level) profiling from a clade reference such as UHGG/CHOCO rather than gene-level functional profiling Only amplicon (16S) data are available — the pipeline is designed for shotgun sequencing reads

skills.description: Use when benchmarking multiple de novo assemblers on a known mock-community metagenomic sample with reference replicons available, to compare global metrics (Nx, contigs, mapped reads) and per-reference metrics (contiguity, multiplicity, validity, Lx, NAx, NGx).
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-benchmarking Use when benchmarking multiple de novo assemblers on a known mock-community metagenomic sample with reference replicons available, to compare global metrics (Nx, contigs, mapped reads) and per-reference metrics (contiguity, multiplicity, validity, Lx, NAx, NGx). Assembling a eukaryotic genome or a single bacterial isolate (e.g., Unicycler is designed exclusively for bacterial isolates, and LMAS targets metagenomic mock communities) You lack known reference replicons for the community and only reference-free contig statistics (e.g., QUAST-style) are needed You need strain-level SNP resolution from assemblies — the study found 'Meaningful strain resolution at the single-nucleotide polymorphism level was not achieved, even by the best assemblers tested.' http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks traditional and metagenomic short-read de novo assemblers on defined mock communities (e.g., BMock12 SRX4901583, ZymoBIOMICS) using the LMAS Nextflow workflow, which parallelizes assembly across containerized assemblers and computes global and per-reference quality metrics in an interactive HTML report. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Benchmarks traditional and metagenomic short-read de novo assemblers on defined mock communities (e.g., BMock12 SRX4901583, ZymoBIOMICS) using the LMAS Nextflow workflow, which parallelizes assembly across containerized assemblers and computes global and per-reference quality metrics in an interactive HTML report.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Assembling a eukaryotic genome or a single bacterial isolate (e.g., Unicycler is designed exclusively for bacterial isolates, and LMAS targets metagenomic mock communities) You lack known reference replicons for the community and only reference-free contig statistics (e.g., QUAST-style) are needed You need strain-level SNP resolution from assemblies — the study found 'Meaningful strain resolution at the single-nucleotide polymorphism level was not achieved, even by the best assemblers tested.'

skills.description: Use when multiple de novo assemblers have been run on the same recruited viral read set and you must rank their contigs against known haplotypes with MetaQUAST metrics such as N50 and genome coverage.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-evaluation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-evaluation Use when multiple de novo assemblers have been run on the same recruited viral read set and you must rank their contigs against known haplotypes with MetaQUAST metrics such as N50 and genome coverage. No ground-truth haplotypes or reference genome exist for the target virus, so MetaQUAST completeness and coverage cannot be computed The input is raw metagenomic reads that have not yet been classified/recruited; use the read-recruiting stage first rather than evaluating assemblies Only a single assembler was run and no comparison against baselines is intended http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark strain-level viral haplotype assemblies (e.g. TAR-VIR/PEHaplo contigs versus SGA, SPAdes, SAVAGE) with MetaQUAST against known reference-derived haplotypes, using N50, genome coverage and mismatch rate as the comparative metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2
skills.summary: Benchmark strain-level viral haplotype assemblies (e.g. TAR-VIR/PEHaplo contigs versus SGA, SPAdes, SAVAGE) with MetaQUAST against known reference-derived haplotypes, using N50, genome coverage and mismatch rate as the comparative metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth haplotypes or reference genome exist for the target virus, so MetaQUAST completeness and coverage cannot be computed The input is raw metagenomic reads that have not yet been classified/recruited; use the read-recruiting stage first rather than evaluating assemblies Only a single assembler was run and no comparison against baselines is intended

skills.description: Use when building a body-site non-redundant gene catalog from vaginal metagenomic FASTQ read sets and isolate genomes, requiring per-sample assembly, CDS prediction, and all-vs-all BLASTP de-redundification.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-gene-calling
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-gene-calling Use when building a body-site non-redundant gene catalog from vaginal metagenomic FASTQ read sets and isolate genomes, requiring per-sample assembly, CDS prediction, and all-vs-all BLASTP de-redundification. The analysis goal is taxonomic/functional profiling of new samples against an existing catalog — use VIRGO's read-mapping module (runMapping.step1.sh) instead of rebuilding the catalog The input community is primarily viral or fungal — VIRGO is 'primarily focused on bacteria with limited inclusion of viral and fungal gene sequences' and separate annotation files (2_fungal_phage) cover only 10,908 fungal and 15,965 bacteriophage genes The goal is identifying nucleotide variants within genes — this capability is not yet included in VIRGO http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 De novo assembles quality-filtered vaginal metagenomic reads per sample and predicts coding sequences, which are pooled with CDSs from urogenital isolate genomes and de-redundified into the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog. This is the core gene-content construction step that yielded 948,158 non-redundant CDSs from ~5.5 million original predictions. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: De novo assembles quality-filtered vaginal metagenomic reads per sample and predicts coding sequences, which are pooled with CDSs from urogenital isolate genomes and de-redundified into the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog. This is the core gene-content construction step that yielded 948,158 non-redundant CDSs from ~5.5 million original predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is taxonomic/functional profiling of new samples against an existing catalog — use VIRGO's read-mapping module (runMapping.step1.sh) instead of rebuilding the catalog The input community is primarily viral or fungal — VIRGO is 'primarily focused on bacteria with limited inclusion of viral and fungal gene sequences' and separate annotation files (2_fungal_phage) cover only 10,908 fungal and 15,965 bacteriophage genes The goal is identifying nucleotide variants within genes — this capability is not yet included in VIRGO

skills.description: Use when you have a single reference genome (or per-species references) and per-sample metagenomic assemblies/genomes, and need to extract conserved homologous regions with flanking context before downstream strain-comparison analyses.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-homology-search
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-homology-search Use when you have a single reference genome (or per-species references) and per-sample metagenomic assemblies/genomes, and need to extract conserved homologous regions with flanking context before downstream strain-comparison analyses. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than assemblies/genomes — SynTracker requires per-sample assembled contigs in FASTA form, not FASTQ The analysis goal is SNP-level strain differentiation only — the article notes most strain-comparison methods quantify SNP differences; SynTracker targets structural variation via genome synteny, and hits below 97% identity/70% coverage will be lost A single sample/assembly is provided — homologous-region binning and downstream APSS comparisons require pairs of samples or genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Identifies homologous genomic regions in per-sample metagenomic assemblies by BLASTn-searching fragmented reference-genome central regions (97% identity, 70% query coverage) and binning each hit plus 2-kbp flanks per region and sample, as the first stage of the SynTracker strain-tracking pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Identifies homologous genomic regions in per-sample metagenomic assemblies by BLASTn-searching fragmented reference-genome central regions (97% identity, 70% query coverage) and binning each hit plus 2-kbp flanks per region and sample, as the first stage of the SynTracker strain-tracking pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than assemblies/genomes — SynTracker requires per-sample assembled contigs in FASTA form, not FASTQ The analysis goal is SNP-level strain differentiation only — the article notes most strain-comparison methods quantify SNP differences; SynTracker targets structural variation via genome synteny, and hits below 97% identity/70% coverage will be lost A single sample/assembly is provided — homologous-region binning and downstream APSS comparisons require pairs of samples or genomes

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic or isolate assembly (e.g., SPAdes 3.9.1 scaffolds) contains many short contigs that are about to be classified by a kmer-based method (PlasFlow) and results for short sequences would otherwise be unreliable.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-length-filtering
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-length-filtering Use when a metagenomic or isolate assembly (e.g., SPAdes 3.9.1 scaffolds) contains many short contigs that are about to be classified by a kmer-based method (PlasFlow) and results for short sequences would otherwise be unreliable. All input contigs already exceed the 1000 bp threshold, so filtering would be a no-op Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than an assembly — read-level quality/length trimming (e.g., with sickle) is a different operation Running graph-based plasmid tools (Recycler, PlasmidSpades) that require the full assembly graph and paired reads rather than filtered FASTA contigs http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Pre-filter metagenomic assembly contigs by length (keeping only sequences longer than 1000 bp) before running kmer-signature-based classifiers such as PlasFlow, because kmer-based plasmid prediction is unreliable on short contigs and unfiltered assemblies waste RAM and runtime. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Pre-filter metagenomic assembly contigs by length (keeping only sequences longer than 1000 bp) before running kmer-signature-based classifiers such as PlasFlow, because kmer-based plasmid prediction is unreliable on short contigs and unfiltered assemblies waste RAM and runtime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All input contigs already exceed the 1000 bp threshold, so filtering would be a no-op Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than an assembly — read-level quality/length trimming (e.g., with sickle) is a different operation Running graph-based plasmid tools (Recycler, PlasmidSpades) that require the full assembly graph and paired reads rather than filtered FASTA contigs

skills.description: Use when comparing metagenomic assemblers on the same Illumina read set (mock or simulated viral/bacterial communities) and you need genome fraction, misassembly, and per-100 kb error metrics against reference genomes.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-quality-assessment Use when comparing metagenomic assemblers on the same Illumina read set (mock or simulated viral/bacterial communities) and you need genome fraction, misassembly, and per-100 kb error metrics against reference genomes. No reference genomes are available for the community members, so MetaQUAST cannot compute genome fraction, misassemblies, or per-100 kb error rates. The goal is de novo assembly quality without comparison — this skill is a benchmarking workflow requiring identical read sets assembled by multiple baseline assemblers. The data are single-strain isolates without strain-level diversity, the setting MetaCortex's local-variation graph search was designed for. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmark metagenomic assemblers (MetaCortex vs MEGAHIT, metaSPAdes, MetaVelvet, Ray Meta) on identical read sets and evaluate assemblies with MetaQUAST against reference genomes using genome fraction, misassembly counts, and mismatch/indel rates per 100 kb. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad020
skills.summary: Benchmark metagenomic assemblers (MetaCortex vs MEGAHIT, metaSPAdes, MetaVelvet, Ray Meta) on identical read sets and evaluate assemblies with MetaQUAST against reference genomes using genome fraction, misassembly counts, and mismatch/indel rates per 100 kb.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genomes are available for the community members, so MetaQUAST cannot compute genome fraction, misassemblies, or per-100 kb error rates. The goal is de novo assembly quality without comparison — this skill is a benchmarking workflow requiring identical read sets assembled by multiple baseline assemblers. The data are single-strain isolates without strain-level diversity, the setting MetaCortex's local-variation graph search was designed for.

skills.description: Use when reproducing plasmidome classification benchmarks that require downloading the four reference plasmidome assemblies and filtering contigs to >1000 bp before running kmer-based plasmid/chromosome classifiers.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-retrieval
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-retrieval Use when reproducing plasmidome classification benchmarks that require downloading the four reference plasmidome assemblies and filtering contigs to >1000 bp before running kmer-based plasmid/chromosome classifiers. When input contigs are already length-filtered or all exceed 1000 bp, re-filtering adds no value When the analysis targets plasmid recovery from assembly graphs with paired reads (e.g. Recycler or PlasmidSpades), which require an assembly graph rather than retrieved reference assemblies When analyzing isolate genome assemblies rather than reference plasmidome datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Retrieves and prepares reference plasmidome metagenomic assemblies (Brown Kav, Sentchilo, Zhang, Szczepanowski) so that kmer-based plasmid classifiers such as PlasFlow and cBar can be applied to comparable inputs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Retrieves and prepares reference plasmidome metagenomic assemblies (Brown Kav, Sentchilo, Zhang, Szczepanowski) so that kmer-based plasmid classifiers such as PlasFlow and cBar can be applied to comparable inputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When input contigs are already length-filtered or all exceed 1000 bp, re-filtering adds no value When the analysis targets plasmid recovery from assembly graphs with paired reads (e.g. Recycler or PlasmidSpades), which require an assembly graph rather than retrieved reference assemblies When analyzing isolate genome assemblies rather than reference plasmidome datasets

skills.description: Use when raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) must be turned into a filtered scaffold/contig FASTA before kmer-signature-based classification (e.g. PlasFlow plasmid prediction) on metagenomic or small-genome assemblies.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-scaffolding
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-scaffolding Use when raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) must be turned into a filtered scaffold/contig FASTA before kmer-signature-based classification (e.g. PlasFlow plasmid prediction) on metagenomic or small-genome assemblies. Input sequences are already filtered contigs longer than 1000 bp — re-assembling would be redundant The goal requires plasmid recovery from the de Bruijn assembly graph with paired reads (PlasmidSpades/Recycler approach), not kmer-signature classification of assembled scaffolds Short contigs (<1 kb) must be classified: kmer-signature methods are explicitly unreliable for short sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assembles metagenomic or isolate sequencing reads into contigs/scaffolds with SPAdes and filters the assembly by sequence length (retaining only sequences longer than 1000 bp) to prepare a kmer-appropriate input for downstream plasmid prediction with PlasFlow. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Assembles metagenomic or isolate sequencing reads into contigs/scaffolds with SPAdes and filters the assembly by sequence length (retaining only sequences longer than 1000 bp) to prepare a kmer-appropriate input for downstream plasmid prediction with PlasFlow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are already filtered contigs longer than 1000 bp — re-assembling would be redundant The goal requires plasmid recovery from the de Bruijn assembly graph with paired reads (PlasmidSpades/Recycler approach), not kmer-signature classification of assembled scaffolds Short contigs (<1 kb) must be classified: kmer-signature methods are explicitly unreliable for short sequences

skills.description: Use when tracking shared or closely related strains between pairs of metagenomic assemblies (or genomes) of the same species, especially when structural variation, low-data contexts (phages/plasmids), or SNP-insensitivity is required rather than popANI/SNP counting.
skills.name: metagenomic-assembly-strain-comparison
skills.search_text: metagenomic-assembly-strain-comparison Use when tracking shared or closely related strains between pairs of metagenomic assemblies (or genomes) of the same species, especially when structural variation, low-data contexts (phages/plasmids), or SNP-insensitivity is required rather than popANI/SNP counting. The target sequences are not conspecific with any available reference genome — SynTracker requires per-species reference genomes and only compares strains of the same species The question demands SNP-level resolution of point-mutation differences only — popANI/SNP tools (inStrain, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn) are better suited; SynTracker is deliberately low-sensitivity to SNPs Inputs are raw reads rather than assembled contigs — samples must be provided as per-sample metagenomic assemblies, not FASTQ http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Compare conspecific microbial strains across metagenomic assemblies or genomes using SynTracker's genome-synteny pipeline: BLAST-based homologous-region retrieval followed by DECIPHER synteny alignment and Average Pairwise Synteny Score (APSS) computation. It enables strain tracking where SNP-based tools fail, including phages and plasmids. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Compare conspecific microbial strains across metagenomic assemblies or genomes using SynTracker's genome-synteny pipeline: BLAST-based homologous-region retrieval followed by DECIPHER synteny alignment and Average Pairwise Synteny Score (APSS) computation. It enables strain tracking where SNP-based tools fail, including phages and plasmids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target sequences are not conspecific with any available reference genome — SynTracker requires per-species reference genomes and only compares strains of the same species The question demands SNP-level resolution of point-mutation differences only — popANI/SNP tools (inStrain, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn) are better suited; SynTracker is deliberately low-sensitivity to SNPs Inputs are raw reads rather than assembled contigs — samples must be provided as per-sample metagenomic assemblies, not FASTQ

skills.description: Use when you have a sorted .bam mapped to a reference .fasta and need per-scaffold coverage, breadth, expected breadth, and nucleotide-diversity metrics for genome populations in a metagenome.
skills.name: metagenomic-bam-position-depth-profiling
skills.search_text: metagenomic-bam-position-depth-profiling Use when you have a sorted .bam mapped to a reference .fasta and need per-scaffold coverage, breadth, expected breadth, and nucleotide-diversity metrics for genome populations in a metagenome. You only need fast whole-genome coverage/relative abundance without microdiversity — CoverM is a faster dedicated coverage calculator The task is strain-level comparison between profiles rather than single-sample profiling — use inStrain compare on existing profile objects The .bam is not sorted or contains unpaired/mis-mapped reads you cannot filter, since un-paired reads are removed by default and pairs must meet mapQ and nucleotide-identity minimums http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstruct inStrain's per-position profiling of a sorted metagenomic .bam against a reference .fasta: tally per-position read depth and A/C/G/T base counts from filtered paired reads, then compute coverage, breadth (including unmasked breadth), expected breadth, and nucleotide diversity per scaffold. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Reconstruct inStrain's per-position profiling of a sorted metagenomic .bam against a reference .fasta: tally per-position read depth and A/C/G/T base counts from filtered paired reads, then compute coverage, breadth (including unmasked breadth), expected breadth, and nucleotide diversity per scaffold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need fast whole-genome coverage/relative abundance without microdiversity — CoverM is a faster dedicated coverage calculator The task is strain-level comparison between profiles rather than single-sample profiling — use inStrain compare on existing profile objects The .bam is not sorted or contains unpaired/mis-mapped reads you cannot filter, since un-paired reads are removed by default and pairs must meet mapQ and nucleotide-identity minimums

skills.description: Reference for evaluating whether a new k-mer/minhash-based read classifier beats established metagenomics tools (CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken) on FP rate and abundance estimation accuracy over the same reference genome database.
skills.name: metagenomic-benchmark-result-comparison
skills.search_text: metagenomic-benchmark-result-comparison Reference for evaluating whether a new k-mer/minhash-based read classifier beats established metagenomics tools (CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken) on FP rate and abundance estimation accuracy over the same reference genome database. Input reads have no ground truth (unknown composition) — FP rate and quantification accuracy cannot be scored; only runtime benchmarking applies The task is long-read or contig classification benchmarking where the compared tools (CLARK, Kraken2 short-read defaults) are out of scope for the comparison protocol The reference database differs between tools — comparisons of FP rate/accuracy would be confounded by database content rather than algorithm http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Method for benchmarking alignment-free metagenomic classifiers (AFS-MetaCache, MetaCacheSpark) against established tools (CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken, MegaBLAST) by comparing classification outputs on shared reference databases, focusing on false-positive rate and quantification accuracy. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Method for benchmarking alignment-free metagenomic classifiers (AFS-MetaCache, MetaCacheSpark) against established tools (CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken, MegaBLAST) by comparing classification outputs on shared reference databases, focusing on false-positive rate and quantification accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have no ground truth (unknown composition) — FP rate and quantification accuracy cannot be scored; only runtime benchmarking applies The task is long-read or contig classification benchmarking where the compared tools (CLARK, Kraken2 short-read defaults) are out of scope for the comparison protocol The reference database differs between tools — comparisons of FP rate/accuracy would be confounded by database content rather than algorithm

skills.description: Use when a hybrid metagenome assembly (Illumina paired-end plus ONT/PacBio long reads or mate pairs) must be partitioned into species-specific scaffold clusters, or when near-complete genomes and biologically important elements must be detected per bin.
skills.name: metagenomic-binning-and-scaffold-clustering
skills.search_text: metagenomic-binning-and-scaffold-clustering Use when a hybrid metagenome assembly (Illumina paired-end plus ONT/PacBio long reads or mate pairs) must be partitioned into species-specific scaffold clusters, or when near-complete genomes and biologically important elements must be detected per bin. Input is short-read-only data without any long-range links (no long reads, mate pairs or linked reads) — the article's binning/scaffolding relies on long-range sequence links and another assembler such as MEGAHIT alone may be more appropriate Reference-based or strain-resolved analysis is required — the study focuses on de novo assembly and reference information has not been well examined Single-isolate genome assembly with no mixed species — the binning step targets separating species in microbiome samples and adds no value for pure cultures http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Species-level binning of metagenome assembly output using MetaPlatanus, which clusters scaffolds by coverage depth, k-mer/species-specific sequence composition and read-mapping of paired-end and long reads, yielding scaffold-to-bin assignments (out_finalClusters, out_finalClusters.tsv) that also feed back into contiguity improvement. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Species-level binning of metagenome assembly output using MetaPlatanus, which clusters scaffolds by coverage depth, k-mer/species-specific sequence composition and read-mapping of paired-end and long reads, yielding scaffold-to-bin assignments (out_finalClusters, out_finalClusters.tsv) that also feed back into contiguity improvement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read-only data without any long-range links (no long reads, mate pairs or linked reads) — the article's binning/scaffolding relies on long-range sequence links and another assembler such as MEGAHIT alone may be more appropriate Reference-based or strain-resolved analysis is required — the study focuses on de novo assembly and reference information has not been well examined Single-isolate genome assembly with no mixed species — the binning step targets separating species in microbiome samples and adds no value for pure cultures

skills.description: Use when short-read metagenomic (FASTQ.GZ) data from mixed microbial communities must be mined for novel insertion sequences and consolidated into a non-redundant FASTA catalogue for downstream annotation or genome querying.
skills.name: metagenomic-catalogue-construction
skills.search_text: metagenomic-catalogue-construction Use when short-read metagenomic (FASTQ.GZ) data from mixed microbial communities must be mined for novel insertion sequences and consolidated into a non-redundant FASTA catalogue for downstream annotation or genome querying. The target ISs lack inverted terminal repeats or have ITRs shorter than the 25 nt default (ITRs as short as 10 nt are missed at default settings) — Palidis only detects ISs with ITRs ISs are flanked outside the 500–3000 bp proximity range (e.g. regions lengthened by nested insertion events) — these are missed by Palidis The input is isolate genomes to annotate rather than mixed-community metagenomic reads — use the released ISC as a reference database instead of rebuilding it http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Build a non-redundant catalogue of insertion sequences (ISs) from mixed microbial community metagenomes by detecting palindromic inverted terminal repeats (ITRs ≥25 nt) with Palidis, then pooling and clustering detections across samples with CD-HIT-EST to emit a reference catalogue like ISC v1.0.0. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Build a non-redundant catalogue of insertion sequences (ISs) from mixed microbial community metagenomes by detecting palindromic inverted terminal repeats (ITRs ≥25 nt) with Palidis, then pooling and clustering detections across samples with CD-HIT-EST to emit a reference catalogue like ISC v1.0.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target ISs lack inverted terminal repeats or have ITRs shorter than the 25 nt default (ITRs as short as 10 nt are missed at default settings) — Palidis only detects ISs with ITRs ISs are flanked outside the 500–3000 bp proximity range (e.g. regions lengthened by nested insertion events) — these are missed by Palidis The input is isolate genomes to annotate rather than mixed-community metagenomic reads — use the released ISC as a reference database instead of rebuilding it

skills.description: Use when building a body-site non-redundant gene catalog from a large set of predicted CDSs (nucleotide FASTA) and redundant near-identical sequences across metagenomes must be collapsed into cluster representatives for downstream annotation and read mapping.
skills.name: metagenomic-cds-dereplication
skills.search_text: metagenomic-cds-dereplication Use when building a body-site non-redundant gene catalog from a large set of predicted CDSs (nucleotide FASTA) and redundant near-identical sequences across metagenomes must be collapsed into cluster representatives for downstream annotation and read mapping. Input sequences are already de-replicated or you need orthologous protein families rather than nucleotide-level non-redundancy — use the VIRGO VOG Jaccard clustering pipeline instead Pairs of sequences share >=95% identity but over <90% of the shorter gene and should be retained as distinct (e.g. partial vs. extended gene models) — the -aS 0.90 coverage rule would wrongly collapse/cluster them differently http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Greedy nucleotide-level de-redundancy of predicted coding sequences with CD-HIT-EST to build a non-redundant gene catalog (VIRGO), collapsing ~5.5 million predicted CDSs from assembled vaginal metagenomes into 948,158 non-redundant representatives. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Greedy nucleotide-level de-redundancy of predicted coding sequences with CD-HIT-EST to build a non-redundant gene catalog (VIRGO), collapsing ~5.5 million predicted CDSs from assembled vaginal metagenomes into 948,158 non-redundant representatives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are already de-replicated or you need orthologous protein families rather than nucleotide-level non-redundancy — use the VIRGO VOG Jaccard clustering pipeline instead Pairs of sequences share >=95% identity but over <90% of the shorter gene and should be retained as distinct (e.g. partial vs. extended gene models) — the -aS 0.90 coverage rule would wrongly collapse/cluster them differently

skills.description: Use when QCed shotgun metagenomic FASTQ data from case and control cohorts are available and per-clade disease association statistics (p-values/FDR) are needed via phylogenetic profiling.
skills.name: metagenomic-clade-association-testing
skills.search_text: metagenomic-clade-association-testing Use when QCed shotgun metagenomic FASTQ data from case and control cohorts are available and per-clade disease association statistics (p-values/FDR) are needed via phylogenetic profiling. Input is already a clade abundance/feature table rather than raw shotgun FASTQ reads — OMARU expects FASTQ in data/original_fastq and performs its own read QC and mapping The goal is gene-level or pathway-level (KEGG/GO, UniRef90) functional association testing rather than clade-level phylogenetic association Cohort samples have not passed the required QC chain — running OMARU_Phyl_AS.sm before producing QCed3_sample_list.txt is invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Performs phylogenetic case-control MWAS clade association testing with OMARU, mapping shotgun reads to UHGG-based clade references and fitting case-control models that adjust for covariates and hidden confounders (PCs) with multiple-testing correction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: Performs phylogenetic case-control MWAS clade association testing with OMARU, mapping shotgun reads to UHGG-based clade references and fitting case-control models that adjust for covariates and hidden confounders (PCs) with multiple-testing correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a clade abundance/feature table rather than raw shotgun FASTQ reads — OMARU expects FASTQ in data/original_fastq and performs its own read QC and mapping The goal is gene-level or pathway-level (KEGG/GO, UniRef90) functional association testing rather than clade-level phylogenetic association Cohort samples have not passed the required QC chain — running OMARU_Phyl_AS.sm before producing QCed3_sample_list.txt is invalid

skills.description: Use when evaluating how a taxonomic classifier behaves on reads from species missing from its database, i.e. when quantifying false positives caused by similarity to the closest available relative rather than true species presence.
skills.name: metagenomic-classifier-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metagenomic-classifier-benchmarking Use when evaluating how a taxonomic classifier behaves on reads from species missing from its database, i.e. when quantifying false positives caused by similarity to the closest available relative rather than true species presence. The true source species IS present in the classifiers' databases — this skill measures false positives on absent species, not precision/recall on known species (use the 3,269 MAG benchmark instead). The goal is abundance-estimation accuracy rather than read-level species misclassification, which the paper benchmarks separately on mock communities. Genomes cannot be verified as absent from the databases (AQ and ANI to closest relatives unknown), so a fair absence benchmark cannot be constructed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark taxonomic classifiers by simulating reads from genomes absent from all reference databases and comparing false positives (misclassified reads and misidentified species) produced by DeepMicrobes versus Kraken, Kraken 2, CLARK and CLARK-S. This isolates each tool's propensity to hallucinate species assignments for truly novel DNA. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Benchmark taxonomic classifiers by simulating reads from genomes absent from all reference databases and comparing false positives (misclassified reads and misidentified species) produced by DeepMicrobes versus Kraken, Kraken 2, CLARK and CLARK-S. This isolates each tool's propensity to hallucinate species assignments for truly novel DNA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The true source species IS present in the classifiers' databases — this skill measures false positives on absent species, not precision/recall on known species (use the 3,269 MAG benchmark instead). The goal is abundance-estimation accuracy rather than read-level species misclassification, which the paper benchmarks separately on mock communities. Genomes cannot be verified as absent from the databases (AQ and ANI to closest relatives unknown), so a fair absence benchmark cannot be constructed.

skills.description: Use when comparing taxonomic classification accuracy (sensitivity/precision) of metagenomic classifiers on simulated read sets with known origins, e.g. Kraken vs BLAST-based or k-mer-based classifiers.
skills.name: metagenomic-classifier-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metagenomic-classifier-benchmarking Use when comparing taxonomic classification accuracy (sensitivity/precision) of metagenomic classifiers on simulated read sets with known origins, e.g. Kraken vs BLAST-based or k-mer-based classifiers. Reads lack ground-truth taxonomic origins (e.g. real environmental samples), so sensitivity and precision cannot be computed The task is abundance estimation rather than per-read classification; abundance programs like MetaPhlAn classify only a small percentage of sequences and are not comparable under this protocol Reads come from taxa with no genus-level entry in the database or with fewer than two other taxa sharing the clade, since the exclusion rules void the measurement http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark genus-level sensitivity and precision of metagenomic sequence classifiers (Kraken, Megablast, PhymmBL, PhymmBL65, NBC) on simulated metagenomes such as HiSeq, MiSeq and simBA-5, using a standardized read preprocessing and clade-aware scoring protocol. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Benchmark genus-level sensitivity and precision of metagenomic sequence classifiers (Kraken, Megablast, PhymmBL, PhymmBL65, NBC) on simulated metagenomes such as HiSeq, MiSeq and simBA-5, using a standardized read preprocessing and clade-aware scoring protocol.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads lack ground-truth taxonomic origins (e.g. real environmental samples), so sensitivity and precision cannot be computed The task is abundance estimation rather than per-read classification; abundance programs like MetaPhlAn classify only a small percentage of sequences and are not comparable under this protocol Reads come from taxa with no genus-level entry in the database or with fewer than two other taxa sharing the clade, since the exclusion rules void the measurement

skills.description: Use when building a custom Kraken taxonomy database from a set of reference genomes (e.g. NCBI RefSeq complete microbial genomes) so every k-mer maps to an LCA taxonomic label.
skills.name: metagenomic-classifier-database-building
skills.search_text: metagenomic-classifier-database-building Use when building a custom Kraken taxonomy database from a set of reference genomes (e.g. NCBI RefSeq complete microbial genomes) so every k-mer maps to an LCA taxonomic label. When the goal is abundance estimation rather than per-read classification — abundance programs like MetaPhlAn only classify a small percentage of sequences and serve a different purpose When a prebuilt Kraken database already covers the taxa of interest and rebuilding from a custom genome library is unnecessary When classification requires inexact alignment of divergent sequences — Kraken relies on exact k-mer matches, so highly novel taxa absent from the library may be misclassified (e.g. Pelosinus fermentans not identified at genus level) http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Constructs a k-mer-to-LCA taxonomy database for the Kraken metagenomic classifier by counting 31-mers with Jellyfish over a user-specified genome library (e.g. NCBI RefSeq complete microbial genomes) and storing each k-mer's lowest common ancestor taxon ID in place of its count. This exact-match database enables Kraken's ultrafast k-mer-based sequence classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Constructs a k-mer-to-LCA taxonomy database for the Kraken metagenomic classifier by counting 31-mers with Jellyfish over a user-specified genome library (e.g. NCBI RefSeq complete microbial genomes) and storing each k-mer's lowest common ancestor taxon ID in place of its count. This exact-match database enables Kraken's ultrafast k-mer-based sequence classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is abundance estimation rather than per-read classification — abundance programs like MetaPhlAn only classify a small percentage of sequences and serve a different purpose When a prebuilt Kraken database already covers the taxa of interest and rebuilding from a custom genome library is unnecessary When classification requires inexact alignment of divergent sequences — Kraken relies on exact k-mer matches, so highly novel taxa absent from the library may be misclassified (e.g. Pelosinus fermentans not identified at genus level)

skills.description: Use when validating that a custom marker-gene or reference database is specific to its target kingdom by measuring how many of its sequences align against a large out-group reference catalog (e.g., fungal markers vs. a bacterial gut genome catalog).
skills.name: metagenomic-contamination-assessment
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contamination-assessment Use when validating that a custom marker-gene or reference database is specific to its target kingdom by measuring how many of its sequences align against a large out-group reference catalog (e.g., fungal markers vs. a bacterial gut genome catalog). Input is already mapped data or a feature table — this skill assesses database contamination at the sequence level, not sample-level contamination The reference catalog is from the same kingdom as the marker genes (e.g., fungal vs. fungal), where cross-mapping is expected and the <0.01% specificity bound does not apply Evaluating functional annotation contamination, which requires different thresholds (Diamond blastx: read coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Quantifies cross-mapping contamination between a taxonomic marker database and an unrelated reference catalog (here, 1.69 million FunOMIC-T fungal single-copy marker genes vs. the UHGG catalog of 204,938 gut prokaryote genomes) by simulating reads and aligning them with bowtie2 under a strict Samtools filter, accepting <0.01% cross-mapping as database specificity. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Quantifies cross-mapping contamination between a taxonomic marker database and an unrelated reference catalog (here, 1.69 million FunOMIC-T fungal single-copy marker genes vs. the UHGG catalog of 204,938 gut prokaryote genomes) by simulating reads and aligning them with bowtie2 under a strict Samtools filter, accepting <0.01% cross-mapping as database specificity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already mapped data or a feature table — this skill assesses database contamination at the sequence level, not sample-level contamination The reference catalog is from the same kingdom as the marker genes (e.g., fungal vs. fungal), where cross-mapping is expected and the <0.01% specificity bound does not apply Evaluating functional annotation contamination, which requires different thresholds (Diamond blastx: read coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10)

skills.description: Use when starting from a metagenomic de Bruijn-graph assembly (FASTA contigs >=500 bp) plus the trimmed reads, and the goal is a bin-quality table of completeness and strain heterogeneity per bin.
skills.name: metagenomic-contig-binning
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contig-binning Use when starting from a metagenomic de Bruijn-graph assembly (FASTA contigs >=500 bp) plus the trimmed reads, and the goal is a bin-quality table of completeness and strain heterogeneity per bin. Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than an assembled, length-filtered contig set — assemble first with MetaCortex SW before binning. The sample is an isolate or low-diversity assembly where strain-level binning metrics (completeness, strain heterogeneity) are not meaningful. No read-mapping coverage is available — MetaBAT2 requires per-contig coverage depth from mapping reads back to the contigs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Clusters metagenomic assembly contigs (e.g. MetaCortex SW contigs filtered to >=500 bp) into metagenomic bins by mapping trimmed reads back with Bowtie2 to derive coverage depth, binning with MetaBAT2, and assessing bin quality (completeness, strain heterogeneity) with CheckM. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad020
skills.summary: Clusters metagenomic assembly contigs (e.g. MetaCortex SW contigs filtered to >=500 bp) into metagenomic bins by mapping trimmed reads back with Bowtie2 to derive coverage depth, binning with MetaBAT2, and assessing bin quality (completeness, strain heterogeneity) with CheckM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than an assembled, length-filtered contig set — assemble first with MetaCortex SW before binning. The sample is an isolate or low-diversity assembly where strain-level binning metrics (completeness, strain heterogeneity) are not meaningful. No read-mapping coverage is available — MetaBAT2 requires per-contig coverage depth from mapping reads back to the contigs.

skills.description: Use when starting from paired-end metagenomic shotgun reads (e.g. FASTQ) and non-redundant MAG sets are needed as input for downstream MAG taxonomy classification, especially for benchmarking classifiers.
skills.name: metagenomic-contig-binning
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contig-binning Use when starting from paired-end metagenomic shotgun reads (e.g. FASTQ) and non-redundant MAG sets are needed as input for downstream MAG taxonomy classification, especially for benchmarking classifiers. Input is already binned MAG FASTA files — skip assembly/binning and go straight to taxonomy classification (e.g. kMetaShot classifier) Reads are from an isolate genome or single-organism culture rather than a mixed community where metagenomic binning applies http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Bin metagenomic contigs into MAGs with MetaBAT2 after quality-checking and meta-assembling reads, to provide the bin-level inputs required by MAG taxonomy classifiers such as kMetaShot, GTDBtk, and CAMITAX. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: Bin metagenomic contigs into MAGs with MetaBAT2 after quality-checking and meta-assembling reads, to provide the bin-level inputs required by MAG taxonomy classifiers such as kMetaShot, GTDBtk, and CAMITAX.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already binned MAG FASTA files — skip assembly/binning and go straight to taxonomy classification (e.g. kMetaShot classifier) Reads are from an isolate genome or single-organism culture rather than a mixed community where metagenomic binning applies

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic or plasmidome assembly (FASTA contigs/scaffolds) needs plasmid-vs-chromosome assignment with initial phylum-level taxonomy, and kmer-signature classification without prior knowledge of sample composition is appropriate.
skills.name: metagenomic-contig-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contig-classification Use when a metagenomic or plasmidome assembly (FASTA contigs/scaffolds) needs plasmid-vs-chromosome assignment with initial phylum-level taxonomy, and kmer-signature classification without prior knowledge of sample composition is appropriate. Input is raw reads rather than assembled contigs — PlasFlow operates on assembly FASTA, and results for short sequences (<1000 bp) are unreliable Sequences shorter than 1000 bp are the analysis target, since kmer-based signature methods do not perform well on short contigs The goal is recovering circular plasmids from a de Bruijn assembly graph with paired reads (use PlasmidSpades or Recycler instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Classifies assembled metagenomic contigs as plasmid- or chromosome-derived using kmer-frequency genome signatures and an ensemble of TensorFlow neural network models in PlasFlow, with probability thresholding to exclude uncertain calls. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Classifies assembled metagenomic contigs as plasmid- or chromosome-derived using kmer-frequency genome signatures and an ensemble of TensorFlow neural network models in PlasFlow, with probability thresholding to exclude uncertain calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than assembled contigs — PlasFlow operates on assembly FASTA, and results for short sequences (<1000 bp) are unreliable Sequences shorter than 1000 bp are the analysis target, since kmer-based signature methods do not perform well on short contigs The goal is recovering circular plasmids from a de Bruijn assembly graph with paired reads (use PlasmidSpades or Recycler instead)

skills.description: Use when metagenomic shotgun reads/contigs must be grouped by organism of origin before downstream per-group model fitting, e.g. to gate retraining of gene prediction IMMs within each cluster.
skills.name: metagenomic-contig-clustering-by-organism
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contig-clustering-by-organism Use when metagenomic shotgun reads/contigs must be grouped by organism of origin before downstream per-group model fitting, e.g. to gate retraining of gene prediction IMMs within each cluster. When sequences already have reliable per-genome provenance (e.g. assembled complete genomes) — clustering and retraining target the metagenomic case where training genomes are unknown When GC-content-based model parameterization is sufficient for the analysis goal — the article shows Phymm-based classification works much better than GC-content, so a GC-only grouping is the wrong substitute When the input is a single-organism sample where Scimm clustering adds cost without benefit; note Glimmer-MG is also more computationally expensive than existing software http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Clusters metagenomic sequences by likely organism of origin using Scimm with phylogenetic augmentation from Phymm classifications (PhyScimm), enabling per-cluster retraining of Glimmer-MG gene prediction models on initial gene predictions. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: Clusters metagenomic sequences by likely organism of origin using Scimm with phylogenetic augmentation from Phymm classifications (PhyScimm), enabling per-cluster retraining of Glimmer-MG gene prediction models on initial gene predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When sequences already have reliable per-genome provenance (e.g. assembled complete genomes) — clustering and retraining target the metagenomic case where training genomes are unknown When GC-content-based model parameterization is sufficient for the analysis goal — the article shows Phymm-based classification works much better than GC-content, so a GC-only grouping is the wrong substitute When the input is a single-organism sample where Scimm clustering adds cost without benefit; note Glimmer-MG is also more computationally expensive than existing software

skills.description: Use when you have assembled metagenomic contigs plus per-sample short-read FASTQs and need per-contig mean sequencing depths across samples to feed co-abundance-based binning (e.g., MetaBAT2) or to estimate MAG abundances.
skills.name: metagenomic-contig-depth-estimation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contig-depth-estimation Use when you have assembled metagenomic contigs plus per-sample short-read FASTQs and need per-contig mean sequencing depths across samples to feed co-abundance-based binning (e.g., MetaBAT2) or to estimate MAG abundances. Input is long reads only — nf-core/mag routes long-read alignment to minimap2, not Bowtie2, so the Bowtie2 short-read depth workflow does not apply No multi-sample or group information exists and co-abundance-based binning is not the goal — single-sample depth may not support co-abundance clustering Contigs have not yet been produced (raw reads only) — assembly must precede depth estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reconstructs the per-contig sequencing-depth estimation step of the nf-core/mag pipeline: short reads of each sample are mapped to assembled contigs with Bowtie2 and mean per-contig depths are aggregated across samples in the same user-specified group so MetaBAT2 can use co-abundance patterns for MAG binning. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Reconstructs the per-contig sequencing-depth estimation step of the nf-core/mag pipeline: short reads of each sample are mapped to assembled contigs with Bowtie2 and mean per-contig depths are aggregated across samples in the same user-specified group so MetaBAT2 can use co-abundance patterns for MAG binning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long reads only — nf-core/mag routes long-read alignment to minimap2, not Bowtie2, so the Bowtie2 short-read depth workflow does not apply No multi-sample or group information exists and co-abundance-based binning is not the goal — single-sample depth may not support co-abundance clustering Contigs have not yet been produced (raw reads only) — assembly must precede depth estimation

skills.description: Use when metaSPAdes or another de novo assembler has produced viral metagenomic seed contigs of only a few kb and the goal is to lengthen them with paired or unpaired FASTQ reads while checking accuracy against NCBI viral reference sequences.
skills.name: metagenomic-contig-extension
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contig-extension Use when metaSPAdes or another de novo assembler has produced viral metagenomic seed contigs of only a few kb and the goal is to lengthen them with paired or unpaired FASTQ reads while checking accuracy against NCBI viral reference sequences. The reads are reference-based and a de novo extension strategy is unnecessary because viral references already exist for direct assembly The seed contigs are already near-complete (e.g. ~11.9 kb full viral genomes); extension offers no gain and only adds false-extension risk Runtime is critical and read complexity screening cannot be afforded — note this still requires disabling DUST via --complex-threshold -1, accepting the loss of complexity filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Automated recursive Overlap Layout Candidates (r-OLC) extension of fragmented de novo metagenomic assembly contigs using ContigExtender, which iteratively incorporates overlapping reads to gain several kb of length while maintaining contig accuracy validated by nucleotide BLAST. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04038-2
skills.summary: Automated recursive Overlap Layout Candidates (r-OLC) extension of fragmented de novo metagenomic assembly contigs using ContigExtender, which iteratively incorporates overlapping reads to gain several kb of length while maintaining contig accuracy validated by nucleotide BLAST.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are reference-based and a de novo extension strategy is unnecessary because viral references already exist for direct assembly The seed contigs are already near-complete (e.g. ~11.9 kb full viral genomes); extension offers no gain and only adds false-extension risk Runtime is critical and read complexity screening cannot be afforded — note this still requires disabling DUST via --complex-threshold -1, accepting the loss of complexity filtering

skills.description: Use when you need to classify assembled metagenomic contigs as putative viral sequences and need a reproducible confidence label based on agreement across multiple detection tools rather than a single-tool call.
skills.name: metagenomic-contig-taxonomy-annotation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-contig-taxonomy-annotation Use when you need to classify assembled metagenomic contigs as putative viral sequences and need a reproducible confidence label based on agreement across multiple detection tools rather than a single-tool call. Input is raw reads rather than an assembled contig library — the scoring rule operates on assembled contigs, not FASTQ Samples contain excessive environmental contamination — the paper warns this can increase runtime and lower precision, and recommends isolating viral fractions before sequencing You only need single-tool viral prediction without cross-tool confidence labels — running one detector alone is simpler and this skill's value is the multi-tool consensus rule http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs ViroProfiler's viral contig identification stage, in which the assembled contig library is screened by multiple viral-detection tools and a multi-tool confidence scoring rule (>=2 criteria = high confident, exactly 1 = low confident) assigns a confidence class per contig. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Reconstructs ViroProfiler's viral contig identification stage, in which the assembled contig library is screened by multiple viral-detection tools and a multi-tool confidence scoring rule (>=2 criteria = high confident, exactly 1 = low confident) assigns a confidence class per contig.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than an assembled contig library — the scoring rule operates on assembled contigs, not FASTQ Samples contain excessive environmental contamination — the paper warns this can increase runtime and lower precision, and recommends isolating viral fractions before sequencing You only need single-tool viral prediction without cross-tool confidence labels — running one detector alone is simpler and this skill's value is the multi-tool consensus rule

skills.description: Use when a mapped gene frequency count table from a mapping-based metagenomic pipeline is sparse and compositional and must be filtered, length-corrected and CSS-normalized before taxonomic or functional (KO/EC/reaction) profiling.
skills.name: metagenomic-count-filtering
skills.search_text: metagenomic-count-filtering Use when a mapped gene frequency count table from a mapping-based metagenomic pipeline is sparse and compositional and must be filtered, length-corrected and CSS-normalized before taxonomic or functional (KO/EC/reaction) profiling. Input is already a normalized or relative-frequency table (e.g. outputs of RAIDA-style relative-frequency conversion) — reapplying CSS would double-correct compositional bias The analysis follows an assembly-based strategy (contig assembly and gene prediction) rather than mapping-based quantification against a gene catalog Only raw read-level QC is needed — this skill operates on mapped count tables, not raw sequencing data http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Preprocess CAMAMED mapped gene frequency count tables by removing genes with fewer than five mapped reads summed across all samples, dividing frequencies by gene length, and applying cumulative sum-scaling (CSS) normalization via metagenomeSeq at gene and species levels before aggregating to KO, EC number and reaction tables. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Preprocess CAMAMED mapped gene frequency count tables by removing genes with fewer than five mapped reads summed across all samples, dividing frequencies by gene length, and applying cumulative sum-scaling (CSS) normalization via metagenomeSeq at gene and species levels before aggregating to KO, EC number and reaction tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized or relative-frequency table (e.g. outputs of RAIDA-style relative-frequency conversion) — reapplying CSS would double-correct compositional bias The analysis follows an assembly-based strategy (contig assembly and gene prediction) rather than mapping-based quantification against a gene catalog Only raw read-level QC is needed — this skill operates on mapped count tables, not raw sequencing data

skills.description: Use when the input is a sparse, high-throughput marker-gene (OTU/species/taxon) count matrix with two or more sample groups, and per-feature differential abundance statistics must account for both normalization and under-sampling of microbial communities.
skills.name: metagenomic-count-normalization
skills.search_text: metagenomic-count-normalization Use when the input is a sparse, high-throughput marker-gene (OTU/species/taxon) count matrix with two or more sample groups, and per-feature differential abundance statistics must account for both normalization and under-sampling of microbial communities. The data are not sparse high-throughput sequencing counts (e.g. continuous abundance measurements or already-tested per-feature statistics) — metagenomeSeq is designed for statistical analysis of sparse high-throughput sequencing The goal is not to determine features (OTUs or other taxa) differentially abundant between two or more groups of multiple samples Input is only a diversity or composition summary with no feature-level count matrix, so no per-feature differential abundance testing is possible http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Applies metagenomeSeq's novel normalization technique together with a statistical model that accounts for under-sampling, so that differential abundance of OTUs/taxa can be assessed in sparse high-throughput marker gene count data. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nmeth.2658
skills.summary: Applies metagenomeSeq's novel normalization technique together with a statistical model that accounts for under-sampling, so that differential abundance of OTUs/taxa can be assessed in sparse high-throughput marker gene count data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not sparse high-throughput sequencing counts (e.g. continuous abundance measurements or already-tested per-feature statistics) — metagenomeSeq is designed for statistical analysis of sparse high-throughput sequencing The goal is not to determine features (OTUs or other taxa) differentially abundant between two or more groups of multiple samples Input is only a diversity or composition summary with no feature-level count matrix, so no per-feature differential abundance testing is possible

skills.description: Use when constructing a k-mer/minhash classification database from large multi-kingdom reference genome collections where full-database build exceeds workstation memory, or when benchmarking build time and peak RAM across partition/executor counts.
