skills.summary: Build minhashing-based metagenomic classification databases (MetaCache/AFS-MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark) from large reference genome collections, using database partitioning and remove-overpopulated-features filtering to keep build time and peak memory tractable for all-food-sequencing style reference sets (e.g. the 135 GB-class AFS31RS90 database).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a built MetaCache database — use query mode (-m query) instead of rebuilding The reference collection is small enough to fit in workstation RAM without partitioning and no build-time/memory benchmark is needed Reads must be aligned for downstream variant or assembly analysis — use an alignment tool (BWA, Bowtie2) rather than a k-mer classification database

skills.description: Use when raw or preprocessed paired-end metagenome FASTQ reads must be assembled into contigs de novo as the first step toward building or reproducing a gene catalog such as VIRGO, and assembly statistics are the deliverable.
skills.name: metagenomic-de-novo-assembly
skills.search_text: metagenomic-de-novo-assembly Use when raw or preprocessed paired-end metagenome FASTQ reads must be assembled into contigs de novo as the first step toward building or reproducing a gene catalog such as VIRGO, and assembly statistics are the deliverable. The goal is taxonomic/functional profiling of an existing sample: VIRGO supports reference-based mapping of reads directly against its non-redundant gene database, and de novo assembly of metagenomic datasets 'requires substantial computational resources and complicates integration of metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data'. Input is already an assembled contig set or a feature/annotation table rather than sequencing reads. The target community is not vaginal microbiome material and a site-specific catalog like VIRGO is not the downstream goal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 De novo assembly of preprocessed paired-end vaginal metagenome reads with IDBA-UD (k-mer 20–100) to produce contigs that underpin the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog, evaluated by contig count, total assembled bp, and N50. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: De novo assembly of preprocessed paired-end vaginal metagenome reads with IDBA-UD (k-mer 20–100) to produce contigs that underpin the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog, evaluated by contig count, total assembled bp, and N50.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is taxonomic/functional profiling of an existing sample: VIRGO supports reference-based mapping of reads directly against its non-redundant gene database, and de novo assembly of metagenomic datasets 'requires substantial computational resources and complicates integration of metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data'. Input is already an assembled contig set or a feature/annotation table rather than sequencing reads. The target community is not vaginal microbiome material and a site-specific catalog like VIRGO is not the downstream goal.

skills.description: Use when comparing metagenomic abundance profiles (taxon/gene/KO/EC/reaction tables) across phenotype groups (e.g. healthy vs adenoma vs carcinoma) to find significantly changed biomarker features while correcting compositional bias.
skills.name: metagenomic-differential-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: metagenomic-differential-abundance-analysis Use when comparing metagenomic abundance profiles (taxon/gene/KO/EC/reaction tables) across phenotype groups (e.g. healthy vs adenoma vs carcinoma) to find significantly changed biomarker features while correcting compositional bias. Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than normalized abundance/feature tables — run the upstream CAMAMED mapping and CSS normalization first The data are not compositional count/frequency data (e.g. RNA-seq with DESeq2/edgeR is a different context; the paper notes these were originally developed for RNA-seq) Sample size is small and false-positive control is critical — the paper reports metagenomeSeq has a high false-positive rate for differential abundance when sample size is small http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Composition-aware identification of taxa, genes, KOs, EC numbers, and reactions that differ significantly between case-control metagenomic sample groups, using CAMAMED's CSS-normalized metagenomeSeq modeling plus Kruskal-Wallis H testing with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Composition-aware identification of taxa, genes, KOs, EC numbers, and reactions that differ significantly between case-control metagenomic sample groups, using CAMAMED's CSS-normalized metagenomeSeq modeling plus Kruskal-Wallis H testing with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than normalized abundance/feature tables — run the upstream CAMAMED mapping and CSS normalization first The data are not compositional count/frequency data (e.g. RNA-seq with DESeq2/edgeR is a different context; the paper notes these were originally developed for RNA-seq) Sample size is small and false-positive control is critical — the paper reports metagenomeSeq has a high false-positive rate for differential abundance when sample size is small

skills.description: Use when you need to reproduce, reimplement, or validate scalable all-vs-all metagenome distance computation from k-mer frequency vectors, or sanity-check that a distance implementation yields near-zero self-distance.
skills.name: metagenomic-distance-behavior-validation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-distance-behavior-validation Use when you need to reproduce, reimplement, or validate scalable all-vs-all metagenome distance computation from k-mer frequency vectors, or sanity-check that a distance implementation yields near-zero self-distance. When the goal is pairwise comparison of only a few sample pairs — the sweep-line design is built for massive all-vs-all comparison and per-pair tools may be simpler When k-mer frequencies are already aggregated into a feature table and the distance matrix can be computed directly in memory (e.g. small samples with scipy/sklearn cosine distance) When presence/absence or sketch-based comparison (e.g. Mash/Sourmash MinHash) is acceptable — the paper notes such data reduction methods 'greatly diminish the resolution' but they are far cheaper http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstruct and validate Libra's all-vs-all pairwise distance computation, in which a Hadoop MapReduce sweep line over a k-mer inverted index accumulates dot-product (D) and per-sample magnitude (M) terms for every sample pair in a single pass, yielding a cosine similarity distance matrix. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Reconstruct and validate Libra's all-vs-all pairwise distance computation, in which a Hadoop MapReduce sweep line over a k-mer inverted index accumulates dot-product (D) and per-sample magnitude (M) terms for every sample pair in a single pass, yielding a cosine similarity distance matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is pairwise comparison of only a few sample pairs — the sweep-line design is built for massive all-vs-all comparison and per-pair tools may be simpler When k-mer frequencies are already aggregated into a feature table and the distance matrix can be computed directly in memory (e.g. small samples with scipy/sklearn cosine distance) When presence/absence or sketch-based comparison (e.g. Mash/Sourmash MinHash) is acceptable — the paper notes such data reduction methods 'greatly diminish the resolution' but they are far cheaper

skills.description: Use when reproducing a k-mer abundance indexing/AMQ benchmark that requires concrete public metagenomic FASTQ runs — one dataset to build the index and an independent query dataset for FPR measurement.
skills.name: metagenomic-fastq-accession-handling
skills.search_text: metagenomic-fastq-accession-handling Use when reproducing a k-mer abundance indexing/AMQ benchmark that requires concrete public metagenomic FASTQ runs — one dataset to build the index and an independent query dataset for FPR measurement. The analysis targets a single sample only — without a separate query FASTQ there is no independent FPR estimate to compute. The index/query data are non-genomic or non-sequence files (e.g. plain tabular data); fimpera indexes k-mers from biological sequences (fastq or fasta, gzipped or not). The task requires exact k-mer abundance lookup with no false positives and memory constraints make a cAMQ inappropriate (no existing method scales to petabyte-scaled datasets with abundance, but exact structures are a different tradeoff). http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Retrieves and stages specific metagenomic FASTQ accessions (e.g. TARA Oceans ERR1726642 for indexing and ERR4691696 for querying) so that counting-Bloom-filter indices and downstream fimpera false-positive-rate evaluations run on reproducible, published data. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad305
skills.summary: Retrieves and stages specific metagenomic FASTQ accessions (e.g. TARA Oceans ERR1726642 for indexing and ERR4691696 for querying) so that counting-Bloom-filter indices and downstream fimpera false-positive-rate evaluations run on reproducible, published data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets a single sample only — without a separate query FASTQ there is no independent FPR estimate to compute. The index/query data are non-genomic or non-sequence files (e.g. plain tabular data); fimpera indexes k-mers from biological sequences (fastq or fasta, gzipped or not). The task requires exact k-mer abundance lookup with no false positives and memory constraints make a cAMQ inappropriate (no existing method scales to petabyte-scaled datasets with abundance, but exact structures are a different tradeoff).

skills.description: Use when gzipped FASTQ shotgun metagenomes from water samples must be attributed to specific fecal source categories and apportioned by cell fraction, without sequencing the potential sources themselves.
skills.name: metagenomic-fecal-source-tracking
skills.search_text: metagenomic-fecal-source-tracking Use when gzipped FASTQ shotgun metagenomes from water samples must be attributed to specific fecal source categories and apportioned by cell fraction, without sequencing the potential sources themselves. The input is amplicon (16S) data or long-read metagenomes rather than short-read shotgun data — SourceApp is a short-read (bwa mem) mapping workflow Potential fecal sources are available for direct sequencing and a de novo site-specific database is preferred — build one with sourceapp_build.py instead of relying solely on the default database The goal is a mass balance of contamination or dating contamination events — SourceApp portions do not represent a mass balance and the tool cannot infer contamination age http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A metagenomic fecal source tracking (FST) skill that attributes and apportions fecal contamination amongst competing source categories (cat, chicken, cow, dog, goat, pig, sewage, septage) by mapping shotgun metagenomic reads to source-associated genome databases and normalizing to genome-equivalent cell fractions using SourceApp. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: A metagenomic fecal source tracking (FST) skill that attributes and apportions fecal contamination amongst competing source categories (cat, chicken, cow, dog, goat, pig, sewage, septage) by mapping shotgun metagenomic reads to source-associated genome databases and normalizing to genome-equivalent cell fractions using SourceApp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is amplicon (16S) data or long-read metagenomes rather than short-read shotgun data — SourceApp is a short-read (bwa mem) mapping workflow Potential fecal sources are available for direct sequencing and a de novo site-specific database is preferred — build one with sourceapp_build.py instead of relying solely on the default database The goal is a mass balance of contamination or dating contamination events — SourceApp portions do not represent a mass balance and the tool cannot infer contamination age

skills.description: Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ data must yield the genomic context (flanking regions) around ARGs or other target genes, and full de novo assembly would be computationally prohibitive.
skills.name: metagenomic-flanking-region-extraction
skills.search_text: metagenomic-flanking-region-extraction Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ data must yield the genomic context (flanking regions) around ARGs or other target genes, and full de novo assembly would be computationally prohibitive. Input data are long reads (Nanopore/PacBio) — ARGprofiler is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data You need whole-genome/metagenome-wide assemblies rather than context around specific target genes — run full SPAdes de novo assembly instead No reference database exists for the target genes — ARGextender requires KMA identification of target genes before recruiting reads and skipping assembly otherwise http://edamontology.org/topic_3837 http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 Targeted de novo assembly of genomic flanking regions around antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in metagenomic short-read data, as implemented by ARGextender within the ARGprofiler Snakemake pipeline. It combines KMA read recruitment with SPAdes assembly to reconstruct sequence context around ARGs without running full metagenomic assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Targeted de novo assembly of genomic flanking regions around antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in metagenomic short-read data, as implemented by ARGextender within the ARGprofiler Snakemake pipeline. It combines KMA read recruitment with SPAdes assembly to reconstruct sequence context around ARGs without running full metagenomic assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are long reads (Nanopore/PacBio) — ARGprofiler is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data You need whole-genome/metagenome-wide assemblies rather than context around specific target genes — run full SPAdes de novo assembly instead No reference database exists for the target genes — ARGextender requires KMA identification of target genes before recruiting reads and skipping assembly otherwise

skills.description: Decision support for choosing between gene-level and functional-level (KO/EC/reaction) differential analysis of mapped metagenomic count data, when you have per-level significance ratios from a case-control dataset such as CAMAMED's colorectal adenoma/carcinoma (CAMAMED) run.
skills.name: metagenomic-functional-annotation-level-comparison
skills.search_text: metagenomic-functional-annotation-level-comparison Decision support for choosing between gene-level and functional-level (KO/EC/reaction) differential analysis of mapped metagenomic count data, when you have per-level significance ratios from a case-control dataset such as CAMAMED's colorectal adenoma/carcinoma (CAMAMED) run. In the CAMAMED colorectal adenoma/carcinoma test case, KO/EC/reaction levels exceeded the gene-level significance rate at the same P ≤ 0.01 threshold. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107

skills.description: Use when input is unassembled metagenomic DNA reads (e.g. Sanger, 454, or Illumina shotgun reads) and the goal is nucleotide-level gene prediction with sensitivity/precision scoring against known gene coordinates.
skills.name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
skills.search_text: metagenomic-gene-prediction Use when input is unassembled metagenomic DNA reads (e.g. Sanger, 454, or Illumina shotgun reads) and the goal is nucleotide-level gene prediction with sensitivity/precision scoring against known gene coordinates. Input is a single complete prokaryotic genome — vanilla Glimmer routinely identifies >99% of genes there and Glimmer-MG's extra classification/clustering machinery is unnecessary and more computationally expensive Reads are already assembled into long contigs or a finished genome where metagenomic fragmentation handling (gene-length model, truncated-gene modeling) adds no benefit The task requires exact performance parity with prior methods under tight compute budgets — the paper notes Glimmer-MG is more computationally expensive than existing software http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Predict protein-coding genes in environmental shotgun (metagenomic) sequences using Glimmer-MG, which augments the Glimmer interpolated Markov model (IMM) framework with Phymm phylogenetic classification, Scimm clustering, per-cluster retraining, a gene-length model for truncated genes, and explicit modeling of indel and substitution sequencing errors. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: Predict protein-coding genes in environmental shotgun (metagenomic) sequences using Glimmer-MG, which augments the Glimmer interpolated Markov model (IMM) framework with Phymm phylogenetic classification, Scimm clustering, per-cluster retraining, a gene-length model for truncated genes, and explicit modeling of indel and substitution sequencing errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single complete prokaryotic genome — vanilla Glimmer routinely identifies >99% of genes there and Glimmer-MG's extra classification/clustering machinery is unnecessary and more computationally expensive Reads are already assembled into long contigs or a finished genome where metagenomic fragmentation handling (gene-length model, truncated-gene modeling) adds no benefit The task requires exact performance parity with prior methods under tight compute budgets — the paper notes Glimmer-MG is more computationally expensive than existing software

skills.description: Use when input is a metagenome assembly FASTA (human microbiome contigs) needing gene prediction in GTF format, and near-complete-genome accuracy is required for short contigs without genomic context.
skills.name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
skills.search_text: metagenomic-gene-prediction Use when input is a metagenome assembly FASTA (human microbiome contigs) needing gene prediction in GTF format, and near-complete-genome accuracy is required for short contigs without genomic context. Input is a single complete prokaryotic genome that can be annotated directly with the self-training GeneMarkS-2 algorithm — the pan-genome assignment step of GeneMark-HM adds no value Metagenomes from environments other than the human microbiome (e.g. environmental or non-human-host samples), where the human-microbiome pan-genome database has no matching taxa and most contigs will fall back to generic models Rigorous benchmarking requiring native self-trained per-genome models rather than representative pan-genome-derived models, since accuracy depends on correct pan-genome assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Predict protein-coding genes in assembled human microbiome metagenomes with the GeneMark-HM pipeline, which selects species-pan-genome-specific GeneMark.hmm-2 models via blastn against a ~20 Gb pan-genome database and falls back to GeneMarkS-2 (long contigs) or MetaGeneMark (short contigs). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047
skills.summary: Predict protein-coding genes in assembled human microbiome metagenomes with the GeneMark-HM pipeline, which selects species-pan-genome-specific GeneMark.hmm-2 models via blastn against a ~20 Gb pan-genome database and falls back to GeneMarkS-2 (long contigs) or MetaGeneMark (short contigs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single complete prokaryotic genome that can be annotated directly with the self-training GeneMarkS-2 algorithm — the pan-genome assignment step of GeneMark-HM adds no value Metagenomes from environments other than the human microbiome (e.g. environmental or non-human-host samples), where the human-microbiome pan-genome database has no matching taxa and most contigs will fall back to generic models Rigorous benchmarking requiring native self-trained per-genome models rather than representative pan-genome-derived models, since accuracy depends on correct pan-genome assignment

skills.description: Use when you have assembled genome FASTA files (MAGs, fungal genomes, viral genomes/vOTUs) and need translated protein-coding gene sequences as input for downstream gene clustering, annotation or gene catalogue construction.
skills.name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
skills.search_text: metagenomic-gene-prediction Use when you have assembled genome FASTA files (MAGs, fungal genomes, viral genomes/vOTUs) and need translated protein-coding gene sequences as input for downstream gene clustering, annotation or gene catalogue construction. Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than assembled contigs/genomes — gene prediction should follow assembly and binning (e.g. the MetaBAT2 single-/multi-coverage binning workflow). Sequences are already predicted genes or a prebuilt gene catalogue (e.g. the existing VIRGO catalogue of 0.95 million genes) rather than genome FASTA files. Genomes come from a single well-annotated isolate set where RefSeq/NCBI annotations are already available and consistent. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Predicts protein-coding genes on assembled microbial genomes using Prodigal 2.6.3 in anonymous metagenomic mode (-p meta), producing translated protein FASTA, nucleotide gene FASTA and GFF coordinates. In the VMGC paper this step converts 33,804 prokaryotic, fungal and viral genomes into the ~26 million protein-coding genes that feed the VMGC-50/90/95 non-redundant gene catalogues. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Predicts protein-coding genes on assembled microbial genomes using Prodigal 2.6.3 in anonymous metagenomic mode (-p meta), producing translated protein FASTA, nucleotide gene FASTA and GFF coordinates. In the VMGC paper this step converts 33,804 prokaryotic, fungal and viral genomes into the ~26 million protein-coding genes that feed the VMGC-50/90/95 non-redundant gene catalogues.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than assembled contigs/genomes — gene prediction should follow assembly and binning (e.g. the MetaBAT2 single-/multi-coverage binning workflow). Sequences are already predicted genes or a prebuilt gene catalogue (e.g. the existing VIRGO catalogue of 0.95 million genes) rather than genome FASTA files. Genomes come from a single well-annotated isolate set where RefSeq/NCBI annotations are already available and consistent.

skills.description: Use when you have a gene-level (e.g. UniRef90-based, length-normalized) abundance table and a gene-to-KO mapping file, and need a KO-level functional profile per sample.
skills.name: metagenomic-gene-to-ortholog-mapping
skills.search_text: metagenomic-gene-to-ortholog-mapping Use when you have a gene-level (e.g. UniRef90-based, length-normalized) abundance table and a gene-to-KO mapping file, and need a KO-level functional profile per sample. Input is already an ortholog-level abundance table — aggregating again would distort abundances. The gene catalog has no functional annotation / gene-to-ortholog mapping available (MetaLAFFA's best-hit filtering keeps genes without annotations, which cannot be counted at KO level). You need pathway-level profiles directly; this step produces KO abundances, and pathway aggregation (e.g. via KEGG ko-to-pathway mappings) is a separate downstream step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Reconstructs KEGG orthology group (KO) abundances from per-sample gene abundance tables using a many-to-many gene-to-ortholog map, splitting each gene's abundance fractionally across all KOs it maps to so total abundance is conserved without double-counting. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: Reconstructs KEGG orthology group (KO) abundances from per-sample gene abundance tables using a many-to-many gene-to-ortholog map, splitting each gene's abundance fractionally across all KOs it maps to so total abundance is conserved without double-counting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an ortholog-level abundance table — aggregating again would distort abundances. The gene catalog has no functional annotation / gene-to-ortholog mapping available (MetaLAFFA's best-hit filtering keeps genes without annotations, which cannot be counted at KO level). You need pathway-level profiles directly; this step produces KO abundances, and pathway aggregation (e.g. via KEGG ko-to-pathway mappings) is a separate downstream step.

skills.description: Use when processing shotgun viral metagenomic FASTQ reads in ViroProfiler and you need per-sample assembled contigs plus a single species-level non-redundant contig library (nrclib.fasta) for downstream annotation, taxonomy assignment, and analysis.
skills.name: metagenomic-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: metagenomic-genome-assembly Use when processing shotgun viral metagenomic FASTQ reads in ViroProfiler and you need per-sample assembled contigs plus a single species-level non-redundant contig library (nrclib.fasta) for downstream annotation, taxonomy assignment, and analysis. Input reads are from isolated viral fractions/samples with isolated viruses where per-genome assembly rather than metagenomic de novo assembly is appropriate Metagenome sequences contain excessive environmental contamination, which the article notes increases pipeline running time and lowers precision — clean or isolate viral fractions first You already have dereplicated contigs or a reference contig library and only need annotation or binning (use ViroProfiler's downstream steps, vRhyme, or phamb instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Assemble quality-filtered reads from each sample in a viral metagenomic dataset with metaSPAdes in metagenomic mode, merge contigs across samples, filter by minimum length, and dereplicate at the species level (>=95% ANI, >=85% AF per MIUViG) to build the non-redundant contig library (nrclib) used for downstream annotation in ViroProfiler. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Assemble quality-filtered reads from each sample in a viral metagenomic dataset with metaSPAdes in metagenomic mode, merge contigs across samples, filter by minimum length, and dereplicate at the species level (>=95% ANI, >=85% AF per MIUViG) to build the non-redundant contig library (nrclib) used for downstream annotation in ViroProfiler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are from isolated viral fractions/samples with isolated viruses where per-genome assembly rather than metagenomic de novo assembly is appropriate Metagenome sequences contain excessive environmental contamination, which the article notes increases pipeline running time and lowers precision — clean or isolate viral fractions first You already have dereplicated contigs or a reference contig library and only need annotation or binning (use ViroProfiler's downstream steps, vRhyme, or phamb instead)

skills.description: Use when a genome set assembled/binned from metagenomes will be used as a concatenated mapping reference or for cross-tool strain-sharing benchmarks, and redundant near-identical genomes (e.g. >98% ANI) must be collapsed first.
skills.name: metagenomic-genome-dereplication
skills.search_text: metagenomic-genome-dereplication Use when a genome set assembled/binned from metagenomes will be used as a concatenated mapping reference or for cross-tool strain-sharing benchmarks, and redundant near-identical genomes (e.g. >98% ANI) must be collapsed first. The analysis goal is strain/sub-species resolution within a single species population (strain clustering at 99.999% ANI), not collapsing redundant genomes — dereplication at 98% ANI would merge diversity you need to keep separate The genome set is already non-redundant or contains genomes from distinct taxa well below 98% ANI to each other, so no dereplication is needed Input is raw reads or a single reference genome rather than a collection of multiple genome .fasta files http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 De-replicate a set of metagenomic genome bins into a non-redundant representative set using dRep at an ANI threshold of 98% or lower before read mapping and population-comparison analyses (e.g. inStrain profile/compare), so that highly similar genomes do not split read mappings or inflate strain-sharing counts. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: De-replicate a set of metagenomic genome bins into a non-redundant representative set using dRep at an ANI threshold of 98% or lower before read mapping and population-comparison analyses (e.g. inStrain profile/compare), so that highly similar genomes do not split read mappings or inflate strain-sharing counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is strain/sub-species resolution within a single species population (strain clustering at 99.999% ANI), not collapsing redundant genomes — dereplication at 98% ANI would merge diversity you need to keep separate The genome set is already non-redundant or contains genomes from distinct taxa well below 98% ANI to each other, so no dereplication is needed Input is raw reads or a single reference genome rather than a collection of multiple genome .fasta files

skills.description: Use when metagenomic read-mapping results (per-genome sequence depth X from CoverM against source-associated genome databases) must be normalized to genome equivalents to express source signal as approximate cell fractions.
skills.name: metagenomic-genome-size-estimation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-genome-size-estimation Use when metagenomic read-mapping results (per-genome sequence depth X from CoverM against source-associated genome databases) must be normalized to genome equivalents to express source signal as approximate cell fractions. The goal is a mass balance of mass inputs — SourceApp portions are cell-fraction estimates based on genome equivalents, not mass-balance results Input is raw unassembled reads and no genome mapping has been done — normalization requires per-genome mapped sequence depths first Sources lack adequate genome representation in the database (e.g., cow fecal microbiomes were under-sampled, causing underestimation/false negatives) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Estimates average genome size and total genome equivalents (GEQ) for each metagenome with MicrobeCensus (MicrobeCensus-SourceApp 1.1.2), so that per-genome mapped read counts from CoverM can be converted into SourceApp's genomic-basis abundance unit approximating prokaryotic cell fraction for fecal source apportionment. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: Estimates average genome size and total genome equivalents (GEQ) for each metagenome with MicrobeCensus (MicrobeCensus-SourceApp 1.1.2), so that per-genome mapped read counts from CoverM can be converted into SourceApp's genomic-basis abundance unit approximating prokaryotic cell fraction for fecal source apportionment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a mass balance of mass inputs — SourceApp portions are cell-fraction estimates based on genome equivalents, not mass-balance results Input is raw unassembled reads and no genome mapping has been done — normalization requires per-genome mapped sequence depths first Sources lack adequate genome representation in the database (e.g., cow fecal microbiomes were under-sampled, causing underestimation/false negatives)

skills.description: Use when comparing viral binning tools on metagenomic Hi-C datasets (shotgun + Hi-C FASTQ pairs from SRA/ENA) and evaluating recovered vMAGs by completeness categories.
skills.name: metagenomic-hic-binning-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metagenomic-hic-binning-benchmarking Use when comparing viral binning tools on metagenomic Hi-C datasets (shotgun + Hi-C FASTQ pairs from SRA/ENA) and evaluating recovered vMAGs by completeness categories. The goal is completeness assessment for prokaryotic MAGs — CheckM with universal single-copy marker genes is the appropriate tool, since viruses lack universal single-copy marker genes Estimating contamination of vMAGs — CheckV cannot estimate contamination because no marker gene set is available for viruses Few putative viral genomes are available in the sample — the article notes benchmarking effectiveness is less convincing in this regime, and the strategy underestimates true viral community diversity because only single-contig-recoverable genomes were chosen http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A benchmarking workflow for comparing metagenomic Hi-C-based viral binning methods (ViralCC, MetaTOR, bin3C, HiCBin, CoCoNet, vRhyme) on real human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater datasets, using CheckV-estimated high/medium-completion draft viral genome counts as the evaluation metric. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: A benchmarking workflow for comparing metagenomic Hi-C-based viral binning methods (ViralCC, MetaTOR, bin3C, HiCBin, CoCoNet, vRhyme) on real human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater datasets, using CheckV-estimated high/medium-completion draft viral genome counts as the evaluation metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is completeness assessment for prokaryotic MAGs — CheckM with universal single-copy marker genes is the appropriate tool, since viruses lack universal single-copy marker genes Estimating contamination of vMAGs — CheckV cannot estimate contamination because no marker gene set is available for viruses Few putative viral genomes are available in the sample — the article notes benchmarking effectiveness is less convincing in this regime, and the strategy underestimates true viral community diversity because only single-contig-recoverable genomes were chosen

skills.description: Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads from several metagenomic Hi-C datasets and need a reference-free, quantitative measure of ligation/library quality comparable across datasets.
skills.name: metagenomic-hic-multi-dataset-quality-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metagenomic-hic-multi-dataset-quality-benchmarking Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads from several metagenomic Hi-C datasets and need a reference-free, quantitative measure of ligation/library quality comparable across datasets. You only need Hi-C library quality for a single dataset and no cross-dataset comparison — a single qc3C run suffices without the multi-dataset compilation table. You need contig-level binning results rather than library-quality metrics — use ViralCC (or another Hi-C binning tool) on assembled contigs and aligned BAM files instead. Only raw, untrimmed FASTQ is available and no access to BBTools is possible — qc3C on unprocessed reads will not reproduce the published 3D ratios. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark Hi-C library quality across multiple metagenomic Hi-C datasets by preprocessing paired-end reads (bbduk trimming, clumpify duplicate removal) and running qc3C in k-mer mode to extract inter-contig (3D) ratios and confidence-interval midpoints, as done for the human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater datasets in the ViralCC paper. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Benchmark Hi-C library quality across multiple metagenomic Hi-C datasets by preprocessing paired-end reads (bbduk trimming, clumpify duplicate removal) and running qc3C in k-mer mode to extract inter-contig (3D) ratios and confidence-interval midpoints, as done for the human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater datasets in the ViralCC paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need Hi-C library quality for a single dataset and no cross-dataset comparison — a single qc3C run suffices without the multi-dataset compilation table. You need contig-level binning results rather than library-quality metrics — use ViralCC (or another Hi-C binning tool) on assembled contigs and aligned BAM files instead. Only raw, untrimmed FASTQ is available and no access to BBTools is possible — qc3C on unprocessed reads will not reproduce the published 3D ratios.

skills.description: Use when you have filtered read-to-gene DIAMOND alignment hits ( e-value per read) from shotgun metagenomic data and need to compute per-gene abundance counts, including fractional assignment of multi-mapping reads.
skills.name: metagenomic-hit-summarization
skills.search_text: metagenomic-hit-summarization Use when you have filtered read-to-gene DIAMOND alignment hits ( e-value per read) from shotgun metagenomic data and need to compute per-gene abundance counts, including fractional assignment of multi-mapping reads. Input is already a gene abundance table rather than raw read-to-gene alignment hits Read-to-gene alignments have not yet been filtered to best e-value hits per read The goal is read-based taxonomic profiling rather than gene-centric functional abundance counting http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 MetaLAFFA-style per-gene abundance counting: retained best-hit read-to-gene alignments are converted into gene abundance counts, with reads matching multiple genes equally well contributing fractional counts split evenly, then normalized by gene length. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: MetaLAFFA-style per-gene abundance counting: retained best-hit read-to-gene alignments are converted into gene abundance counts, with reads matching multiple genes equally well contributing fractional counts split evenly, then normalized by gene length.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene abundance table rather than raw read-to-gene alignment hits Read-to-gene alignments have not yet been filtered to best e-value hits per read The goal is read-based taxonomic profiling rather than gene-centric functional abundance counting

skills.description: Use when paired-end short-read metagenomic reads have already been screened for inverted repeats by pal-MEM (LCoord/RCoord annotated FASTA) and sample assemblies exist, and you need proximity-filtered candidate ITR reads.
skills.name: metagenomic-is-candidate-screening
skills.search_text: metagenomic-is-candidate-screening Use when paired-end short-read metagenomic reads have already been screened for inverted repeats by pal-MEM (LCoord/RCoord annotated FASTA) and sample assemblies exist, and you need proximity-filtered candidate ITR reads. You are looking for insertion sequences lacking inverted terminal repeats — Palidis is only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs The repeat-containing reads have not yet been identified (no pal-MEM _IR output) — run the maximal exact matching step first Expected ISs may be longer than the proximity range, e.g. regions lengthened by nested insertion events outside 500–3000 bp http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A Palidis pipeline step that maps pal-MEM repeat-containing reads back to sample assemblies with Bowtie2 and retains reads whose inverted terminal repeat (ITR) coordinates fall within a user-defined minimum-to-maximum IS length interval (e.g. 500–3000 bp), yielding candidate insertion sequence (IS) reads for downstream clustering. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: A Palidis pipeline step that maps pal-MEM repeat-containing reads back to sample assemblies with Bowtie2 and retains reads whose inverted terminal repeat (ITR) coordinates fall within a user-defined minimum-to-maximum IS length interval (e.g. 500–3000 bp), yielding candidate insertion sequence (IS) reads for downstream clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are looking for insertion sequences lacking inverted terminal repeats — Palidis is only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs The repeat-containing reads have not yet been identified (no pal-MEM _IR output) — run the maximal exact matching step first Expected ISs may be longer than the proximity range, e.g. regions lengthened by nested insertion events outside 500–3000 bp

skills.description: Use when you have a microbial feature abundance table (taxonomic or functional profiles) plus sample metadata (e.g. geography, health status, extraction method) and need significant feature–variable associations from multivariable linear models.
skills.name: metagenomic-metadata-regression-modeling
skills.search_text: metagenomic-metadata-regression-modeling Use when you have a microbial feature abundance table (taxonomic or functional profiles) plus sample metadata (e.g. geography, health status, extraction method) and need significant feature–variable associations from multivariable linear models. Input is already a differential-abundance or association result table (no regression needed — proceed directly to filtering/ranking). Goal is ordination or between-sample community-level testing (e.g. adonis2 from the vegan R package on beta diversity) rather than per-taxon metadata regression. Feature matrix is amplicon-derived ITS data rather than shotgun metagenomic abundances produced by FunOMIC-T mapping. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Reproduces the FunOMIC study's MaAsLin2 multivariable regression linking fungal taxonomic/functional abundances from 2,679 human metagenome samples to clinical and demographic metadata, filtering associations at FDR < 0.05. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Reproduces the FunOMIC study's MaAsLin2 multivariable regression linking fungal taxonomic/functional abundances from 2,679 human metagenome samples to clinical and demographic metadata, filtering associations at FDR < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a differential-abundance or association result table (no regression needed — proceed directly to filtering/ranking). Goal is ordination or between-sample community-level testing (e.g. adonis2 from the vegan R package on beta diversity) rather than per-taxon metadata regression. Feature matrix is amplicon-derived ITS data rather than shotgun metagenomic abundances produced by FunOMIC-T mapping.

skills.description: Use when a reproducible mock compositional abundance table (with matched control/disease phenotype data) is needed to test or benchmark metagenomic feature-enrichment or causality-inference methods such as VTwins.
skills.name: metagenomic-mock-data-simulation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-mock-data-simulation Use when a reproducible mock compositional abundance table (with matched control/disease phenotype data) is needed to test or benchmark metagenomic feature-enrichment or causality-inference methods such as VTwins. You already have a real relative-abundance table (e.g. from curatedMetagenomicData, like ZellerG_2014.metaphlan_bugs_list.stool) — use the real-data workflow instead of simulating mock data. The downstream tool requires raw counts rather than compositional relative abundances — uniform random draws plus decostand 'total' normalization produce relative abundances only. You need biologically realistic covariance/phylogenetic structure in the mock data; this simulation draws features independently from a uniform distribution. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Generates a reproducible mock compositional metagenomic abundance dataset (120 samples × 10 features from runif with set.seed(12345), normalized to relative abundances with vegan::decostand 'total') plus a grp1/grp2 phenotype table, as used by the VTwins paper to test sensitivity of causative-feature inference on limited samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.scib.2023.10.024
skills.summary: Generates a reproducible mock compositional metagenomic abundance dataset (120 samples × 10 features from runif with set.seed(12345), normalized to relative abundances with vegan::decostand 'total') plus a grp1/grp2 phenotype table, as used by the VTwins paper to test sensitivity of causative-feature inference on limited samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a real relative-abundance table (e.g. from curatedMetagenomicData, like ZellerG_2014.metaphlan_bugs_list.stool) — use the real-data workflow instead of simulating mock data. The downstream tool requires raw counts rather than compositional relative abundances — uniform random draws plus decostand 'total' normalization produce relative abundances only. You need biologically realistic covariance/phylogenetic structure in the mock data; this simulation draws features independently from a uniform distribution.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify wall-clock time, peak memory footprint, and CPU-hour usage of a Snakemake-based metagenomic pipeline (e.g. ARGprofiler with fastp, KMA, ARGextender, SPAdes, Mash rules) under its final parameter settings.
skills.name: metagenomic-pipeline-benchmarking
skills.search_text: metagenomic-pipeline-benchmarking Use when you need to quantify wall-clock time, peak memory footprint, and CPU-hour usage of a Snakemake-based metagenomic pipeline (e.g. ARGprofiler with fastp, KMA, ARGextender, SPAdes, Mash rules) under its final parameter settings. Input is long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data You need a taxonomy-accuracy comparison rather than resource/throughput benchmarking — the separate argprofiler-tax-benchmark repo benchmarks microbial profilers on CAMI data instead The goal is biological result validation (e.g. flanking-region assembly quality) rather than computational cost measurement http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmark a large-scale metagenomic workflow (here ARGprofiler, a Snakemake pipeline for ARG analysis) by parsing Snakemake rule-level logs into throughput (Gbp/h), peak memory, and CPU-hour consumption so workflow cost/efficiency can be quantified per rule. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Benchmark a large-scale metagenomic workflow (here ARGprofiler, a Snakemake pipeline for ARG analysis) by parsing Snakemake rule-level logs into throughput (Gbp/h), peak memory, and CPU-hour consumption so workflow cost/efficiency can be quantified per rule.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data You need a taxonomy-accuracy comparison rather than resource/throughput benchmarking — the separate argprofiler-tax-benchmark repo benchmarks microbial profilers on CAMI data instead The goal is biological result validation (e.g. flanking-region assembly quality) rather than computational cost measurement

skills.description: Use when raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQs must be cleaned before functional annotation — removing human/host reads, PCR or optical duplicates, and low-quality or too-short reads prior to gene mapping.
skills.name: metagenomic-preprocessing
skills.search_text: metagenomic-preprocessing Use when raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQs must be cleaned before functional annotation — removing human/host reads, PCR or optical duplicates, and low-quality or too-short reads prior to gene mapping. Input data are already post-quality-control (e.g. HMP data files are post-HMP quality control, so minimal reads are discarded) — applying heavy filtering adds little value Reads still contain sequencing adapters — MetaLAFFA expects adapter-removed FASTQs as input The goal is host genome analysis rather than microbial functional annotation — discarding host reads is destructive here http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quality-control pre-processing of raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQs as implemented in MetaLAFFA: host read filtering against the hs37d5 human reference with 1000 Genomes decoy sequences using Bowtie 2, duplicate read removal with PICARD MarkDuplicates, and quality trimming/filtering with Trimmomatic's MAXINFO criterion, with per-step summary statistics. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: Quality-control pre-processing of raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQs as implemented in MetaLAFFA: host read filtering against the hs37d5 human reference with 1000 Genomes decoy sequences using Bowtie 2, duplicate read removal with PICARD MarkDuplicates, and quality trimming/filtering with Trimmomatic's MAXINFO criterion, with per-step summary statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already post-quality-control (e.g. HMP data files are post-HMP quality control, so minimal reads are discarded) — applying heavy filtering adds little value Reads still contain sequencing adapters — MetaLAFFA expects adapter-removed FASTQs as input The goal is host genome analysis rather than microbial functional annotation — discarding host reads is destructive here

skills.description: Use when raw metagenomic samples arrive as SRA archives and must be converted to FASTQ/FASTA, quality-checked, and characterized with per-sample sequence statistics before taxonomic/functional mapping.
skills.name: metagenomic-preprocessing-pipeline
skills.search_text: metagenomic-preprocessing-pipeline Use when raw metagenomic samples arrive as SRA archives and must be converted to FASTQ/FASTA, quality-checked, and characterized with per-sample sequence statistics before taxonomic/functional mapping. Input reads are already in FASTQ/FASTA and only need mapping — skip SRA conversion and go straight to the mapping stage of CAMAMED The goal is differential abundance analysis or compositional normalization (CSS/metagenomeSeq) — that is a later CAMAMED stage operating on abundance tables, not on raw reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Pre-processes raw metagenomic sequencing archives (SRA) into FASTQ/FASTA with fastq-dump (SRA Toolkit v2.8.2), then assesses read quality with FastQC v0.11.5 and extracts per-sample sequence statistics with SeqKit v0.10.1, as done in the CAMAMED pipeline before mapping. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Pre-processes raw metagenomic sequencing archives (SRA) into FASTQ/FASTA with fastq-dump (SRA Toolkit v2.8.2), then assesses read quality with FastQC v0.11.5 and extracts per-sample sequence statistics with SeqKit v0.10.1, as done in the CAMAMED pipeline before mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already in FASTQ/FASTA and only need mapping — skip SRA conversion and go straight to the mapping stage of CAMAMED The goal is differential abundance analysis or compositional normalization (CSS/metagenomeSeq) — that is a later CAMAMED stage operating on abundance tables, not on raw reads

skills.description: Use when the goal is to maximize protein sequence recovery from complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic short-read data (paired-end FASTQ or single-end FASTA/FASTQ) by assembling directly at the protein level.
skills.name: metagenomic-protein-assembly
skills.search_text: metagenomic-protein-assembly Use when the goal is to maximize protein sequence recovery from complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic short-read data (paired-end FASTQ or single-end FASTA/FASTQ) by assembling directly at the protein level. The analysis target is strain-resolved nucleotide-level reconstruction of non-coding regions such as 16S rRNA or complete viral genomes and protein-level assembly alone would miss them — use PenguiN guided_nuclassemble instead Reads are shorter than ~120 nt, since the default --min-length of 40 codons requires reads longer than 120 nt A nucleotide reference-guided or mapping-based approach is required because de novo assembly of very complex metagenomes is not the goal http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 De novo assembly of short metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads at the protein level using Plass, which six-frame-translates sequencing reads and assembles the translated sequences into protein sequences, recovering 2–10 times more protein sequences from complex metagenomes than nucleotide-level assemblers. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41592-019-0437-4
skills.summary: De novo assembly of short metagenomic/metatranscriptomic reads at the protein level using Plass, which six-frame-translates sequencing reads and assembles the translated sequences into protein sequences, recovering 2–10 times more protein sequences from complex metagenomes than nucleotide-level assemblers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is strain-resolved nucleotide-level reconstruction of non-coding regions such as 16S rRNA or complete viral genomes and protein-level assembly alone would miss them — use PenguiN guided_nuclassemble instead Reads are shorter than ~120 nt, since the default --min-length of 40 codons requires reads longer than 120 nt A nucleotide reference-guided or mapping-based approach is required because de novo assembly of very complex metagenomes is not the goal

skills.description: Use when you need to identify and type-classify proteins (e.g. DsrA/DsrB and paralogous families) in thousands of (meta)genomic protein sequences in FASTA format, at scale, without phylogenetic reconstruction.
skills.name: metagenomic-protein-sequence-screening
skills.search_text: metagenomic-protein-sequence-screening Use when you need to identify and type-classify proteins (e.g. DsrA/DsrB and paralogous families) in thousands of (meta)genomic protein sequences in FASTA format, at scale, without phylogenetic reconstruction. Input is nucleotide sequence or raw reads rather than protein sequences in FASTA format — DiSCo consumes protein FASTA only You require precise phylogenetic placement of DsrAB sequences rather than fast type-level classification — the paper notes phylogenetic approaches, though slower, are an alternative when tree topology matters Only a handful of complete genomes are available and a one-off check against known annotations suffices — blastp-based verification may be simpler http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Screen large (meta)genomic protein datasets with DiSCo, a Perl 5 tool that runs hmmsearch against a curated HMM library to detect Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism proteins and predict their enzyme type, expanding coverage from 103 complete genomes to 1738 micro-organisms across 1798 lineages. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000603
skills.summary: Screen large (meta)genomic protein datasets with DiSCo, a Perl 5 tool that runs hmmsearch against a curated HMM library to detect Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism proteins and predict their enzyme type, expanding coverage from 103 complete genomes to 1738 micro-organisms across 1798 lineages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is nucleotide sequence or raw reads rather than protein sequences in FASTA format — DiSCo consumes protein FASTA only You require precise phylogenetic placement of DsrAB sequences rather than fast type-level classification — the paper notes phylogenetic approaches, though slower, are an alternative when tree topology matters Only a handful of complete genomes are available and a one-off check against known annotations suffices — blastp-based verification may be simpler

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g., the 30-sample BIO-ML set from PRJNA544527 or a 121-sample H. pylori eradication cohort) must be mapped to a reference database to generate per-sample BAMs for downstream variant detection.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-alignment
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-alignment Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g., the 30-sample BIO-ML set from PRJNA544527 or a 121-sample H. pylori eradication cohort) must be mapped to a reference database to generate per-sample BAMs for downstream variant detection. Per-sample .filtered.sorted.bam files already exist — skip directly to cellsnp-lite pileup (minMAF = 0.02, minCOUNT = 100) and MetaQuad clustering. The analysis goal is clustering already-piled variants into shared informative variants — that is MetaQuad's role ('metaquad -i cellSNP -o Metaquad --minSample=3'), not alignment. Input is single-cell mtDNA or scRNA-seq data rather than shotgun metagenomic data — the MQuad/cellSNP single-cell lineage, not this metagenomic alignment pipeline, applies. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns shotgun metagenomic sequencing reads against a reference database (e.g., a genome set or antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) catalog) with bwa or bowtie2, producing per-sample .filtered.sorted.bam files that serve as the substrate for cellsnp-lite variant pileup and MetaQuad shared informative variant discovery. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Aligns shotgun metagenomic sequencing reads against a reference database (e.g., a genome set or antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) catalog) with bwa or bowtie2, producing per-sample .filtered.sorted.bam files that serve as the substrate for cellsnp-lite variant pileup and MetaQuad shared informative variant discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Per-sample .filtered.sorted.bam files already exist — skip directly to cellsnp-lite pileup (minMAF = 0.02, minCOUNT = 100) and MetaQuad clustering. The analysis goal is clustering already-piled variants into shared informative variants — that is MetaQuad's role ('metaquad -i cellSNP -o Metaquad --minSample=3'), not alignment. Input is single-cell mtDNA or scRNA-seq data rather than shotgun metagenomic data — the MQuad/cellSNP single-cell lineage, not this metagenomic alignment pipeline, applies.

skills.description: Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads must be mapped to a combined microbiome reference FASTA while preserving junction pairs mapping across different references, as the first stage of LEMON's HGT detection pipeline.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-alignment
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-alignment Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads must be mapped to a combined microbiome reference FASTA while preserving junction pairs mapping across different references, as the first stage of LEMON's HGT detection pipeline. Input is long-read data or single-end reads incompatible with the paired-end 'bwa mem -M' workflow the article specifies The analysis goal does not require cross-reference junction reads (e.g. simple per-genome variant calling), where retaining supplementary/split alignments via -M adds no value A valid sorted BAM with mapped read pairs already exists from a prior LEMON preprocessing run http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Align paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads against a multi-species reference FASTA using BWA mem with the -M flag, then convert/sort to BAM with samtools, so that junction read pairs whose sides map to two different references are retained for LEMON's downstream HGT breakpoint detection. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3301-8
skills.summary: Align paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads against a multi-species reference FASTA using BWA mem with the -M flag, then convert/sort to BAM with samtools, so that junction read pairs whose sides map to two different references are retained for LEMON's downstream HGT breakpoint detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read data or single-end reads incompatible with the paired-end 'bwa mem -M' workflow the article specifies The analysis goal does not require cross-reference junction reads (e.g. simple per-genome variant calling), where retaining supplementary/split alignments via -M adds no value A valid sorted BAM with mapped read pairs already exists from a prior LEMON preprocessing run

skills.description: Use when you have QC'd shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads and a non-redundant gene catalog (e.g., the IGC catalog), and you need per-sample gene frequencies as input to compositional differential-abundance analysis.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-gene-catalog
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-gene-catalog Use when you have QC'd shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads and a non-redundant gene catalog (e.g., the IGC catalog), and you need per-sample gene frequencies as input to compositional differential-abundance analysis. Your aim is taxonomic profiling of phylogenetic diversity — that is done separately with MetaPhlAn v2.0, not by catalog mapping. No appropriate non-redundant gene catalog is available for the environment under study; the article prefers mapping-based analysis only 'when appropriate gene catalogs are available'. You need contig-level reconstruction or novel gene discovery — this mapping approach does not assemble reads or predict new gene content. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Map quality-controlled shotgun metagenomic reads to a non-redundant (CD-HIT deduplicated) gene catalog with a hash-based aligner to compute per-sample gene frequencies, the foundation for CAMAMED's functional (gene, KO, EC, reaction) analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Map quality-controlled shotgun metagenomic reads to a non-redundant (CD-HIT deduplicated) gene catalog with a hash-based aligner to compute per-sample gene frequencies, the foundation for CAMAMED's functional (gene, KO, EC, reaction) analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your aim is taxonomic profiling of phylogenetic diversity — that is done separately with MetaPhlAn v2.0, not by catalog mapping. No appropriate non-redundant gene catalog is available for the environment under study; the article prefers mapping-based analysis only 'when appropriate gene catalogs are available'. You need contig-level reconstruction or novel gene discovery — this mapping approach does not assemble reads or predict new gene content.

skills.description: Use when assigning shotgun metagenomic reads from water or mesocosm samples (e.g. FASTQ reads from PRJNA1161616) to individual genomes in a source-associated database to quantify per-genome and per-source-category signal.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-genome-databases
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-genome-databases Use when assigning shotgun metagenomic reads from water or mesocosm samples (e.g. FASTQ reads from PRJNA1161616) to individual genomes in a source-associated database to quantify per-genome and per-source-category signal. The analysis goal is taxonomic profiling against a general reference catalog rather than attribution to source-associated genomes with known source labels Input data are long Nanopore reads rather than short paired-end reads; bwa mem short-read mapping with the 93% identity / 70% overlap thresholds was tuned for 2 × 150-bp short-read metagenomes You need a mass balance of contaminant mass rather than cell-fraction estimates; SourceApp portions are based on genome equivalents and do not represent a mass balance http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Maps quality-trimmed shotgun metagenomic reads to a curated source-associated reference genome database with bwa mem and summarizes per-genome mapped read counts and sequence depth with CoverM, enabling read-mapping-based fecal source tracking as implemented in SourceApp. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: Maps quality-trimmed shotgun metagenomic reads to a curated source-associated reference genome database with bwa mem and summarizes per-genome mapped read counts and sequence depth with CoverM, enabling read-mapping-based fecal source tracking as implemented in SourceApp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is taxonomic profiling against a general reference catalog rather than attribution to source-associated genomes with known source labels Input data are long Nanopore reads rather than short paired-end reads; bwa mem short-read mapping with the 93% identity / 70% overlap thresholds was tuned for 2 × 150-bp short-read metagenomes You need a mass balance of contaminant mass rather than cell-fraction estimates; SourceApp portions are based on genome equivalents and do not represent a mass balance

skills.description: Use when predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) must be binned from metagenomes and per-sample coverage tables are needed as input to vRhyme's coverage variance / effect-size binning network.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-viral-scaffolds
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-viral-scaffolds Use when predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) must be binned from metagenomes and per-sample coverage tables are needed as input to vRhyme's coverage variance / effect-size binning network. The goal is binning bacterial, archaeal, or eukaryotic genomes — vRhyme is built for viral sequences/scaffolds and 'is not meant to bin microbes' A combined coverage table already exists (use vRhyme -c input; note coverage outlier removal is disabled for -c input) Only a single input sample is available and robust coverage variance comparisons are required — vRhyme 'performs optimally with multiple input samples' http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Align metagenomic reads (paired, unpaired, or interleaved FASTQ) to predicted viral scaffold FASTAs with Bowtie2 or BWA-mem and convert the alignments into a per-scaffold, per-sample coverage table of averages and standard deviations, masking terminal scaffold coverage. This table is the input for vRhyme's Cohen's d coverage effect-size comparisons between scaffold pairs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Align metagenomic reads (paired, unpaired, or interleaved FASTQ) to predicted viral scaffold FASTAs with Bowtie2 or BWA-mem and convert the alignments into a per-scaffold, per-sample coverage table of averages and standard deviations, masking terminal scaffold coverage. This table is the input for vRhyme's Cohen's d coverage effect-size comparisons between scaffold pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is binning bacterial, archaeal, or eukaryotic genomes — vRhyme is built for viral sequences/scaffolds and 'is not meant to bin microbes' A combined coverage table already exists (use vRhyme -c input; note coverage outlier removal is disabled for -c input) Only a single input sample is available and robust coverage variance comparisons are required — vRhyme 'performs optimally with multiple input samples'

skills.description: Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (Illumina FASTQ, single- or paired-end) from metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to NCBI taxa, especially when reference genomes are incomplete or distant strains must still be classified.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-classification Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (Illumina FASTQ, single- or paired-end) from metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to NCBI taxa, especially when reference genomes are incomplete or distant strains must still be classified. Reads of interest originate from non-protein-coding genomic regions — protein-level classification cannot classify them (Kaiju's stated disadvantage) The exact sequenced strains are present in the reference database — nucleotide-level k-mer classifiers will be more sensitive, as seen in the HiSeq and MiSeq mock-community data (Kraken 78.0% genus sensitivity vs Kaiju Greedy-5 73.3%) Input is already protein sequence without the -p option being considered, or a genus-level assignment is required for genera with no reference genomes — classification is impossible for such genera http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Taxonomic classification of metagenomic sequencing reads by translating them into six reading frames and finding maximum (in-)exact protein-level matches via a Burrows-Wheeler transform FM-index (Kaiju), benchmarked against k-mer nucleotide classifiers like Kraken and Clark. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Taxonomic classification of metagenomic sequencing reads by translating them into six reading frames and finding maximum (in-)exact protein-level matches via a Burrows-Wheeler transform FM-index (Kaiju), benchmarked against k-mer nucleotide classifiers like Kraken and Clark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads of interest originate from non-protein-coding genomic regions — protein-level classification cannot classify them (Kaiju's stated disadvantage) The exact sequenced strains are present in the reference database — nucleotide-level k-mer classifiers will be more sensitive, as seen in the HiSeq and MiSeq mock-community data (Kraken 78.0% genus sensitivity vs Kaiju Greedy-5 73.3%) Input is already protein sequence without the -p option being considered, or a genus-level assignment is required for genera with no reference genomes — classification is impossible for such genera

skills.description: Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g. simulated setA2/setB2 or HMP metagenome SRR1804065) against a reference genome FASTA in alignment-free fashion, computing sensitivity/precision/F1/specificity.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-classification Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g. simulated setA2/setB2 or HMP metagenome SRR1804065) against a reference genome FASTA in alignment-free fashion, computing sensitivity/precision/F1/specificity. When an alignment- or mapping-based classifier is required (e.g. variant-aware or spliced alignment reporting) — LiME is explicitly alignment-free, mapping-free and assembly-free When reads lack a suitable curated reference database; LiME's precision/specificity claims rest on the Lindgreen et al. simulated benchmarks and a BLAST-filtered HMP sample with a customized reference database When only raw, unfiltered real metagenomes are available without the BLAST 98%-identity filtering step used in the paper's real-data protocol http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Lightweight, alignment-free metagenomic read classification with LiME, which compares reads against reference genomes via the extended Burrows-Wheeler transform (ebwt), document array (da) and LCP array, assigning each paired-end read to a taxon at species level (TaxRank=1) with high precision (99.9% positive-control assignment, <0.01% negative-control classification). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03628-w
skills.summary: Lightweight, alignment-free metagenomic read classification with LiME, which compares reads against reference genomes via the extended Burrows-Wheeler transform (ebwt), document array (da) and LCP array, assigning each paired-end read to a taxon at species level (TaxRank=1) with high precision (99.9% positive-control assignment, <0.01% negative-control classification).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When an alignment- or mapping-based classifier is required (e.g. variant-aware or spliced alignment reporting) — LiME is explicitly alignment-free, mapping-free and assembly-free When reads lack a suitable curated reference database; LiME's precision/specificity claims rest on the Lindgreen et al. simulated benchmarks and a BLAST-filtered HMP sample with a customized reference database When only raw, unfiltered real metagenomes are available without the BLAST 98%-identity filtering step used in the paper's real-data protocol

skills.description: Use when assigning taxonomic labels to large sets of metagenomic reads (FASTQ/FASTA from SRA accessions such as SRS019120, SRS014468, SRS015055, or Mason-simulated reads), or when benchmarking classifier speed and accuracy against Megablast or MetaPhlAn.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-classification Use when assigning taxonomic labels to large sets of metagenomic reads (FASTQ/FASTA from SRA accessions such as SRS019120, SRS014468, SRS015055, or Mason-simulated reads), or when benchmarking classifier speed and accuracy against Megablast or MetaPhlAn. When the goal is gene content estimation requiring classification of nearly every read with abundance estimation — abundance programs like MetaPhlAn classify only a small percentage of sequences and serve a different purpose When reads come from organisms whose clade of origin is absent from the reference database — clade exclusion experiments show sensitivity can drop to roughly 33% when the species was never seen When the input is already a taxonomy/abundance profile rather than raw sequencing reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assign taxonomic labels to metagenomic DNA sequences with Kraken by querying a Jellyfish-derived k-mer LCA database with exact k-mer matches, achieving Megablast-comparable accuracy at millions of reads per minute. It covers database construction (RefSeq genomes, NCBI taxonomy), paired-read concatenation, and genus-level sensitivity/precision evaluation. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Assign taxonomic labels to metagenomic DNA sequences with Kraken by querying a Jellyfish-derived k-mer LCA database with exact k-mer matches, achieving Megablast-comparable accuracy at millions of reads per minute. It covers database construction (RefSeq genomes, NCBI taxonomy), paired-read concatenation, and genus-level sensitivity/precision evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is gene content estimation requiring classification of nearly every read with abundance estimation — abundance programs like MetaPhlAn classify only a small percentage of sequences and serve a different purpose When reads come from organisms whose clade of origin is absent from the reference database — clade exclusion experiments show sensitivity can drop to roughly 33% when the species was never seen When the input is already a taxonomy/abundance profile rather than raw sequencing reads

skills.description: Use when classifying shotgun FASTQ/FASTA reads from complex biological samples (e.g., calibrator sausage mixtures) against large reference genome collections to detect ingredient/species composition and estimate abundances with low false-positive rates.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-classification Use when classifying shotgun FASTQ/FASTA reads from complex biological samples (e.g., calibrator sausage mixtures) against large reference genome collections to detect ingredient/species composition and estimate abundances with low false-positive rates. When a full alignment-based pipeline is required (e.g., SNP-level variant calling) — the minhashing approach is a classification/quantification substitute for alignment tools like BWA/Bowtie2, not a read aligner When the reference database must be shared between MetaCache variants — a database can only be queried with the same compiled variant (data type sizes, endianness) that built it When the target organisms lack reference genomes in the database, since classification depends entirely on indexed reference sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Alignment-free, minhashing-based taxonomic classification and abundance estimation of metagenomic sequencing reads against large multi-kingdom reference databases, as implemented in AFS-MetaCache (C++/workstation) and MetaCacheSpark (Apache Spark cluster) for all-food-sequencing (AFS) analyses. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Alignment-free, minhashing-based taxonomic classification and abundance estimation of metagenomic sequencing reads against large multi-kingdom reference databases, as implemented in AFS-MetaCache (C++/workstation) and MetaCacheSpark (Apache Spark cluster) for all-food-sequencing (AFS) analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a full alignment-based pipeline is required (e.g., SNP-level variant calling) — the minhashing approach is a classification/quantification substitute for alignment tools like BWA/Bowtie2, not a read aligner When the reference database must be shared between MetaCache variants — a database can only be queried with the same compiled variant (data type sizes, endianness) that built it When the target organisms lack reference genomes in the database, since classification depends entirely on indexed reference sequences

skills.description: Use when classifying fastq/fasta metagenomic reads at species or genus rank, especially gut microbiome reads from uncultured MAGs where k-mer/LCA tools miss species absent from reference databases.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-classification Use when classifying fastq/fasta metagenomic reads at species or genus rank, especially gut microbiome reads from uncultured MAGs where k-mer/LCA tools miss species absent from reference databases. The input is long-read or single-cell data whose read lengths and error profiles differ strongly from the training data — the paper notes retraining would be required to adapt New genomes must be incorporated into an existing model without retraining — the framework requires retraining the entire deep neural network to add species The reads come from organisms outside the gut repertoire domain used for training, where k-mer length (12-mers, optimized for thousands of genomes; try 6-12 bp otherwise) may not generalize http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Taxonomic classification of short shotgun metagenomic sequencing reads using DeepMicrobes, a deep learning framework trained on the complete bacterial repertoire of the human gut, and benchmarking it against k-mer/LCA-based (Kraken, Kraken 2, Centrifuge, CLARK) and protein-alignment-based (Kaiju, DIAMOND-MEGAN, BLAST-MEGAN) classifiers. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Taxonomic classification of short shotgun metagenomic sequencing reads using DeepMicrobes, a deep learning framework trained on the complete bacterial repertoire of the human gut, and benchmarking it against k-mer/LCA-based (Kraken, Kraken 2, Centrifuge, CLARK) and protein-alignment-based (Kaiju, DIAMOND-MEGAN, BLAST-MEGAN) classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is long-read or single-cell data whose read lengths and error profiles differ strongly from the training data — the paper notes retraining would be required to adapt New genomes must be incorporated into an existing model without retraining — the framework requires retraining the entire deep neural network to add species The reads come from organisms outside the gut repertoire domain used for training, where k-mer length (12-mers, optimized for thousands of genomes; try 6-12 bp otherwise) may not generalize

skills.description: Use when metagenomic Illumina short reads must be split into strain/species-coherent read groups before per-cluster assembly, e.g. as the preprocessing step of an overlap-layout-consensus strain-aware assembly pipeline.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-clustering
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-clustering Use when metagenomic Illumina short reads must be split into strain/species-coherent read groups before per-cluster assembly, e.g. as the preprocessing step of an overlap-layout-consensus strain-aware assembly pipeline.
