Input is long noisy third-generation reads, whose high error rate StrainXpress's short-read workflow does not resolve Reads are already partitioned into strain/species groups or a reference-guided binning already exists, making de novo overlap-based clustering redundant The goal is long contigs spanning whole strain genomes from Illumina data, which the article notes is constrained by short read length regardless of clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Clusters metagenomic short reads into small, species-coherent groups via single-linkage merging of Minimap2 overlap scores, serving as the 'Clustering Reads' preprocessing stage of StrainXpress's OLC divide-and-conquer assembly workflow. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac543
skills.summary: Clusters metagenomic short reads into small, species-coherent groups via single-linkage merging of Minimap2 overlap scores, serving as the 'Clustering Reads' preprocessing stage of StrainXpress's OLC divide-and-conquer assembly workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long noisy third-generation reads, whose high error rate StrainXpress's short-read workflow does not resolve Reads are already partitioned into strain/species groups or a reference-guided binning already exists, making de novo overlap-based clustering redundant The goal is long contigs spanning whole strain genomes from Illumina data, which the article notes is constrained by short read length regardless of clustering

skills.description: Use when scanning metagenomic FASTA reads with pal-MEM for inverted terminal repeats and you need to encode read coordinates in two-bit space, apply edge-boundary conditions, or exclude MEMs near read ends that arise from amplification artifacts.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-coordinate-processing
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-coordinate-processing Use when scanning metagenomic FASTA reads with pal-MEM for inverted terminal repeats and you need to encode read coordinates in two-bit space, apply edge-boundary conditions, or exclude MEMs near read ends that arise from amplification artifacts. Reads are in raw FASTQ.GZ format — Palidis pre-processes these to FASTA first via convertToF before coordinate processing The target insertion sequences lack inverted terminal repeats (ITRs) — Palidis is only equipped to discover ISs with ITRs, so MEM-coordinate filtering will not help The goal is de novo assembly or mapping against assemblies (Palidis uses Bowtie2 steps for that, not coordinate-based MEM filtering) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Handles read-coordinate manipulation in the pal-MEM step of the Palidis pipeline: k-mers are encoded with two bits per nucleotide, hash-table lookups respect boundary conditions, and MEMs falling inside a 20-nucleotide (40-bit) end buffer are discarded to suppress technical repeats from amplified read libraries. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Handles read-coordinate manipulation in the pal-MEM step of the Palidis pipeline: k-mers are encoded with two bits per nucleotide, hash-table lookups respect boundary conditions, and MEMs falling inside a 20-nucleotide (40-bit) end buffer are discarded to suppress technical repeats from amplified read libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are in raw FASTQ.GZ format — Palidis pre-processes these to FASTA first via convertToF before coordinate processing The target insertion sequences lack inverted terminal repeats (ITRs) — Palidis is only equipped to discover ISs with ITRs, so MEM-coordinate filtering will not help The goal is de novo assembly or mapping against assemblies (Palidis uses Bowtie2 steps for that, not coordinate-based MEM filtering)

skills.description: Use when you already have per-read taxonomic assignments from a MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark query run and need organism-level read counts and abundance percentages at a chosen rank such as species.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-counting-per-taxon
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-counting-per-taxon Use when you already have per-read taxonomic assignments from a MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark query run and need organism-level read counts and abundance percentages at a chosen rank such as species. You only need per-read taxonomic labels from classification and not aggregated abundance per organism No taxonomic tree is available to support pruning at the requested rank and proportional sub-tree redistribution http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Estimates the abundance of organisms at a selectable taxonomic level (e.g. species) by aggregating per-read classifications produced by AFS-MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark: counts are pooled up from pruned ranks and redistributed down from higher-level taxa using sub-tree weights. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Estimates the abundance of organisms at a selectable taxonomic level (e.g. species) by aggregating per-read classifications produced by AFS-MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark: counts are pooled up from pruned ranks and redistributed down from higher-level taxa using sub-tree weights.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need per-read taxonomic labels from classification and not aggregated abundance per organism No taxonomic tree is available to support pruning at the requested rank and proportional sub-tree redistribution

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end virome FASTQ reads (e.g. SRA runs like SRR3458562 or SRR9875293) feed into VirMAP's mapping assembly, pileup rebuilding, or DIAMOND/BBMap alignment and read depth is uneven or redundant.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-digital-normalization
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-digital-normalization Use when raw paired-end virome FASTQ reads (e.g. SRA runs like SRR3458562 or SRR9875293) feed into VirMAP's mapping assembly, pileup rebuilding, or DIAMOND/BBMap alignment and read depth is uneven or redundant. Input is not raw sequencing reads but already-assembled contigs, super-scaffolds, or a read-assignment table (normalization applies to the read stage before alignment). The VirMAP run is invoked without --useBbnorm, in which case reads are not normalized and this skill should not be assumed in the downstream analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Dereplicate and digitally normalize metagenomic/virome FASTQ reads before VirMAP alignment and assembly, using BBTools bbnorm (or khmer's normalize-by-median.py) with default parameters to flatten coverage and reduce redundant read depth. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Dereplicate and digitally normalize metagenomic/virome FASTQ reads before VirMAP alignment and assembly, using BBTools bbnorm (or khmer's normalize-by-median.py) with default parameters to flatten coverage and reduce redundant read depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw sequencing reads but already-assembled contigs, super-scaffolds, or a read-assignment table (normalization applies to the read stage before alignment). The VirMAP run is invoked without --useBbnorm, in which case reads are not normalized and this skill should not be assumed in the downstream analysis.

skills.description: Use when per-sample DIAMOND tabular hits against a gene catalog (e.g. UniRef90) need -e-value refinement and fractional gene counting to produce gene/orthology abundances from shotgun metagenomic FASTQs.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-gene-annotation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-gene-annotation Use when per-sample DIAMOND tabular hits against a gene catalog (e.g. UniRef90) need -e-value refinement and fractional gene counting to produce gene/orthology abundances from shotgun metagenomic FASTQs. Input is already a filtered hit table or a gene count/abundance table — resume MetaLAFFA from a later step instead of re-filtering You need all alignment hits (sensitivity-first profiling, e.g. strain-level or variant analysis) rather than the specificity-oriented best-e-value-only strategy The data are assembled contigs or metatranscriptomes rather than quality-controlled shotgun metagenomic reads destined for DIAMOND-vs-UniRef90 mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 MetaLAFFA's read mapping phase aligns quality-controlled shotgun reads to a microbial gene database (UniRef90 by default) with DIAMOND, then refines the raw hits by keeping only the best-e-value match(es) per read and computes gene abundances with fractional counts for ties. This default best-match filtering strategy prioritizes specificity in functional profiling. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: MetaLAFFA's read mapping phase aligns quality-controlled shotgun reads to a microbial gene database (UniRef90 by default) with DIAMOND, then refines the raw hits by keeping only the best-e-value match(es) per read and computes gene abundances with fractional counts for ties. This default best-match filtering strategy prioritizes specificity in functional profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered hit table or a gene count/abundance table — resume MetaLAFFA from a later step instead of re-filtering You need all alignment hits (sensitivity-first profiling, e.g. strain-level or variant analysis) rather than the specificity-oriented best-e-value-only strategy The data are assembled contigs or metatranscriptomes rather than quality-controlled shotgun metagenomic reads destined for DIAMOND-vs-UniRef90 mapping

skills.description: Use when raw or primer-trimmed amplicon FASTQ reads (454 or Illumina) show deteriorating 3'-end quality or embedded Ns and must be trimmed and length-filtered before dereplication and OTU clustering.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-length-and-n-trimming
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-length-and-n-trimming Use when raw or primer-trimmed amplicon FASTQ reads (454 or Illumina) show deteriorating 3'-end quality or embedded Ns and must be trimmed and length-filtered before dereplication and OTU clustering. Input is not raw read data — e.g. reads already dereplicated, an OTU table, or a taxonomic classification, which need no per-read trimming The analysis requires UPARSE-style stringent truncation at the first base below a quality threshold and can tolerate discarding a large fraction of sequence data Reads are untrimmed at the primer level: run primer removal (MICCA ``trim``/Cutadapt with IUPAC degenerate motifs) first, since filter does not remove primer sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Applies sliding-window adaptive quality trimming, N-truncation, and minimum/maximum length filtering to amplicon FASTQ reads, as implemented by MICCA's ``filter`` command wrapping VSEARCH and sickle, so that low-quality tails and N-containing reads do not contaminate OTU inference. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/srep09743
skills.summary: Applies sliding-window adaptive quality trimming, N-truncation, and minimum/maximum length filtering to amplicon FASTQ reads, as implemented by MICCA's ``filter`` command wrapping VSEARCH and sickle, so that low-quality tails and N-containing reads do not contaminate OTU inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw read data — e.g. reads already dereplicated, an OTU table, or a taxonomic classification, which need no per-read trimming The analysis requires UPARSE-style stringent truncation at the first base below a quality threshold and can tolerate discarding a large fraction of sequence data Reads are untrimmed at the primer level: run primer removal (MICCA ``trim``/Cutadapt with IUPAC degenerate motifs) first, since filter does not remove primer sequences

skills.description: Use when metagenomic paired-end FASTQ reads need to be mapped to a multi-genome reference .fasta to quantify genome detection, coverage, microdiversity, or strain sharing (e.g., ZymoBIOMICS mock-community benchmarking).
skills.name: metagenomic-read-mapping
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-mapping Use when metagenomic paired-end FASTQ reads need to be mapped to a multi-genome reference .fasta to quantify genome detection, coverage, microdiversity, or strain sharing (e.g., ZymoBIOMICS mock-community benchmarking). Input is already a .bam/.sam alignment or a coverage table — proceed directly to `inStrain profile` instead of re-mapping Only genome-level relative abundance/coverage is needed without microdiversity or SNV data — a fast tool like CoverM may be more appropriate than full inStrain profiling Reads are single-end or the reference genomes are not dereplicated, since un-paired reads are removed by default and highly similar genomes cause erroneous multi-mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Maps metagenomic paired-end reads to a concatenated reference genome set with Bowtie2 and profiles the resulting .bam files with inStrain's default read filters, producing coverage, breadth, SNV, and population-comparison data suitable for strain-level benchmarking against known community composition. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Maps metagenomic paired-end reads to a concatenated reference genome set with Bowtie2 and profiles the resulting .bam files with inStrain's default read filters, producing coverage, breadth, SNV, and population-comparison data suitable for strain-level benchmarking against known community composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a .bam/.sam alignment or a coverage table — proceed directly to `inStrain profile` instead of re-mapping Only genome-level relative abundance/coverage is needed without microdiversity or SNV data — a fast tool like CoverM may be more appropriate than full inStrain profiling Reads are single-end or the reference genomes are not dereplicated, since un-paired reads are removed by default and highly similar genomes cause erroneous multi-mapping

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads (FASTQ) must be quantified against de novo MAG clusters or signature gene sets to estimate organism/subspecies abundances per sample, e.g. tracking B. infantis and B. longum across the COPSAC2010 and CHILD infant cohorts.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-mapping-and-counting
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-mapping-and-counting Use when shotgun metagenomic reads (FASTQ) must be quantified against de novo MAG clusters or signature gene sets to estimate organism/subspecies abundances per sample, e.g. tracking B. infantis and B. longum across the COPSAC2010 and CHILD infant cohorts. You only need standard species-level taxonomic profiles from marker genes — a marker-gene profiler alone (MetaPhlAn, MetaPhyler, mOTUs) suffices and MAGinator's MAG-based mapping is unnecessary overhead You have no MAG bins / VAMB clusters.tsv — MAGinator requires de novo MAG clusters, contigs, and reads as input The task is functional annotation rather than abundance profiling — use EggNOG mapper output instead of read mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Map shotgun metagenomic reads against a non-redundant gene catalogue / MAG-derived signature genes and count mapped reads to estimate per-sample abundances, as implemented in MAGinator's read-mapping and counting step. Ambiguous reads are redistributed using a signature-reads profile derived from uniquely mapping reads, enabling de novo subspecies-level abundance profiling. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8
skills.summary: Map shotgun metagenomic reads against a non-redundant gene catalogue / MAG-derived signature genes and count mapped reads to estimate per-sample abundances, as implemented in MAGinator's read-mapping and counting step. Ambiguous reads are redistributed using a signature-reads profile derived from uniquely mapping reads, enabling de novo subspecies-level abundance profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need standard species-level taxonomic profiles from marker genes — a marker-gene profiler alone (MetaPhlAn, MetaPhyler, mOTUs) suffices and MAGinator's MAG-based mapping is unnecessary overhead You have no MAG bins / VAMB clusters.tsv — MAGinator requires de novo MAG clusters, contigs, and reads as input The task is functional annotation rather than abundance profiling — use EggNOG mapper output instead of read mapping

skills.description: Use when short-read shotgun metagenomes (FASTQ) must be converted from mapped-read counts into genome-equivalent relative abundances (cell fractions) against a source-associated genome database for source tracking.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-mapping-quantification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-mapping-quantification Use when short-read shotgun metagenomes (FASTQ) must be converted from mapped-read counts into genome-equivalent relative abundances (cell fractions) against a source-associated genome database for source tracking. Input data are amplicon (e.g., 16S rRNA) reads rather than short-read shotgun metagenomes, since the framework relies on genome-wide read mapping metrics A mass-based (e.g., mass-balance of mass inputs) apportionment is required, because SourceApp portions estimate proportions of cells based on genome equivalents, not mass No source-associated genome database exists for the sources of interest and none can be curated, since quantification depends on genome-to-source associations http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies short-read shotgun metagenomes by mapping them to source-associated genome databases with CoverM (v0.7.0) and normalizing mapped sequence depth by genome equivalents (GEQ, estimated with MicrobeCensus) to obtain cell-fraction-style relative abundances used by SourceApp for fecal source attribution and apportionment. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: Quantifies short-read shotgun metagenomes by mapping them to source-associated genome databases with CoverM (v0.7.0) and normalizing mapped sequence depth by genome equivalents (GEQ, estimated with MicrobeCensus) to obtain cell-fraction-style relative abundances used by SourceApp for fecal source attribution and apportionment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are amplicon (e.g., 16S rRNA) reads rather than short-read shotgun metagenomes, since the framework relies on genome-wide read mapping metrics A mass-based (e.g., mass-balance of mass inputs) apportionment is required, because SourceApp portions estimate proportions of cells based on genome equivalents, not mass No source-associated genome database exists for the sources of interest and none can be curated, since quantification depends on genome-to-source associations

skills.description: Use when you need to profile the taxonomic and/or functional composition of vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic FASTQ samples against the VIRGO gene catalog instead of assembling reads de novo.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-mapping-to-gene-catalog
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-mapping-to-gene-catalog Use when you need to profile the taxonomic and/or functional composition of vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic FASTQ samples against the VIRGO gene catalog instead of assembling reads de novo. The input is already a feature/abundance table or species profile rather than raw FASTQ reads — this skill maps reads, it does not post-process existing profiles. The sample is a fungal, viral/phage, or non-vaginal community dataset: VIRGO is primarily focused on bacteria, with limited inclusion of viral and fungal gene sequences (only 10,908 fungal and 15,965 bacteriophage genes). You need nucleotide variant calling within genes or paired-end mapping fidelity — VIRGO explicitly does not support paired-end mapping and lacks variant identification capability. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Map metagenomic or metatranscriptomic reads to a body-site-specific non-redundant gene catalog (VIRGO, 0.95 million vaginal non-redundant genes) using bowtie to quantify per-gene read counts, per-species gene counts, and taxonomic abundances. This reference-based approach avoids de novo assembly and enables integration of metagenomic and metatranscriptomic profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Map metagenomic or metatranscriptomic reads to a body-site-specific non-redundant gene catalog (VIRGO, 0.95 million vaginal non-redundant genes) using bowtie to quantify per-gene read counts, per-species gene counts, and taxonomic abundances. This reference-based approach avoids de novo assembly and enables integration of metagenomic and metatranscriptomic profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature/abundance table or species profile rather than raw FASTQ reads — this skill maps reads, it does not post-process existing profiles. The sample is a fungal, viral/phage, or non-vaginal community dataset: VIRGO is primarily focused on bacteria, with limited inclusion of viral and fungal gene sequences (only 10,908 fungal and 15,965 bacteriophage genes). You need nucleotide variant calling within genes or paired-end mapping fidelity — VIRGO explicitly does not support paired-end mapping and lacks variant identification capability.

skills.description: Use when metagenomic reads have been mapped to representative sub-species genomes (e.g. concatenated .fasta) and per-scaffold or per-genome coverage, clonality, nucleotide diversity, or SNV calls must be computed without contamination from falsely mapped read pairs.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-pair-filtering
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-pair-filtering Use when metagenomic reads have been mapped to representative sub-species genomes (e.g. concatenated .fasta) and per-scaffold or per-genome coverage, clonality, nucleotide diversity, or SNV calls must be computed without contamination from falsely mapped read pairs. Input is single-end or fragmented reads where proper-pair orientation and insert-size checks cannot be applied — inStrain removes un-paired reads by default, so most data would be discarded You only need rough coverage/abundance estimates and speed matters more than mapping accuracy — a fast tool like CoverM computes coverage without inStrain's pair-level filtering You are comparing assembled genomes directly (e.g. ANI dereplication with dRep) rather than profiling read mappings http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 inStrain's careful .bam read-pair filtering reduces erroneous mappings before coverage, clonality, and SNV-based nucleotide diversity are computed, which is essential for reliable population microdiversity estimates from metagenomic read mappings. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: inStrain's careful .bam read-pair filtering reduces erroneous mappings before coverage, clonality, and SNV-based nucleotide diversity are computed, which is essential for reliable population microdiversity estimates from metagenomic read mappings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end or fragmented reads where proper-pair orientation and insert-size checks cannot be applied — inStrain removes un-paired reads by default, so most data would be discarded You only need rough coverage/abundance estimates and speed matters more than mapping accuracy — a fast tool like CoverM computes coverage without inStrain's pair-level filtering You are comparing assembled genomes directly (e.g. ANI dereplication with dRep) rather than profiling read mappings

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a targeted assembly or annotation pipeline (e.g. CasCollect) against a complete metagenome assembly, and a simulated community with known CRISPR/Cas content and background host contamination is needed from raw FASTQ reads.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-pooling-and-spike-in-simulation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-pooling-and-spike-in-simulation Use when benchmarking a targeted assembly or annotation pipeline (e.g. CasCollect) against a complete metagenome assembly, and a simulated community with known CRISPR/Cas content and background host contamination is needed from raw FASTQ reads. The input is an already assembled metagenome or contigs rather than raw paired-end FASTQ reads — CasCollect and this pooling workflow operate on unassembled reads. The goal is profiling a real environmental metagenome (e.g. the article's ground water, lake, permafrost, wetland datasets) rather than a controlled benchmark with known ground truth. The target gene set is not amenable to HMM-based seed identification and no user-supplied HMMs or repeat references are available to reconfigure CasCollect. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Constructs a controlled in-silico metagenome by pooling paired-end Illumina isolate read sets (E. coli KLY, P. aeruginosa VA-134, S. pyogenes M39) with spiked-in mouse reads using Seqtk, so that targeted assemblers like CasCollect can be benchmarked against complete assembly baselines with a known ground-truth cas gene content. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Constructs a controlled in-silico metagenome by pooling paired-end Illumina isolate read sets (E. coli KLY, P. aeruginosa VA-134, S. pyogenes M39) with spiked-in mouse reads using Seqtk, so that targeted assemblers like CasCollect can be benchmarked against complete assembly baselines with a known ground-truth cas gene content.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an already assembled metagenome or contigs rather than raw paired-end FASTQ reads — CasCollect and this pooling workflow operate on unassembled reads. The goal is profiling a real environmental metagenome (e.g. the article's ground water, lake, permafrost, wetland datasets) rather than a controlled benchmark with known ground truth. The target gene set is not amenable to HMM-based seed identification and no user-supplied HMMs or repeat references are available to reconfigure CasCollect.

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end or single-end Illumina metagenomic FASTQ/fastq.gz reads must be adapter-trimmed and quality-trimmed before SSU rRNA read extraction or any 16S/18S-based taxonomic classification.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-quality-control Use when raw paired-end or single-end Illumina metagenomic FASTQ/fastq.gz reads must be adapter-trimmed and quality-trimmed before SSU rRNA read extraction or any 16S/18S-based taxonomic classification. Input reads have already been adapter- and quality-trimmed (re-trimming with minlength=60/trimq=20 would needlessly discard data) Data are amplicon-only reads destined for direct QIIME2 classification rather than RiboTaxa shotgun-based SSU extraction Input is a database or reference sequence (e.g. SILVA SSU 138.1 FASTA) rather than raw sequencing reads — use database indexing instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quality-control stage of the RiboTaxa pipeline: removes Illumina adapters and low-quality bases from raw Illumina (meta)genomic FASTQ reads using bbduk.sh (BBTools), then verifies results with FastQC and MultiQC reports before SSU rRNA extraction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Quality-control stage of the RiboTaxa pipeline: removes Illumina adapters and low-quality bases from raw Illumina (meta)genomic FASTQ reads using bbduk.sh (BBTools), then verifies results with FastQC and MultiQC reports before SSU rRNA extraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have already been adapter- and quality-trimmed (re-trimming with minlength=60/trimq=20 would needlessly discard data) Data are amplicon-only reads destined for direct QIIME2 classification rather than RiboTaxa shotgun-based SSU extraction Input is a database or reference sequence (e.g. SILVA SSU 138.1 FASTA) rather than raw sequencing reads — use database indexing instead

skills.description: Use when raw vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic fastq reads must be cleaned (human/rRNA removal) and mapped to a reference gene catalog such as VIRGO before taxonomic or functional profiling.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-quality-control Use when raw vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic fastq reads must be cleaned (human/rRNA removal) and mapped to a reference gene catalog such as VIRGO before taxonomic or functional profiling. Input is already a gene-count or abundance table from a prior VIRGO mapping run — proceed directly to downstream summarization instead of re-QC The goal is de novo assembly-based CDS prediction (as in building the catalog itself) rather than reference-based read mapping to an existing gene catalog VIRGO's bacterial-focused catalog is inappropriate, e.g. the target community is dominated by viral or fungal genes, which are only sparsely included (see 2_fungal_phage annotations) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quality-control and filter metagenomic/metatranscriptomic fastq reads before gene-catalog analysis, including removing host-derived reads and rRNA, then mapping filtered reads to the VIRGO non-redundant gene database with explicit read-count and seed-length cutoffs. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Quality-control and filter metagenomic/metatranscriptomic fastq reads before gene-catalog analysis, including removing host-derived reads and rRNA, then mapping filtered reads to the VIRGO non-redundant gene database with explicit read-count and seed-length cutoffs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-count or abundance table from a prior VIRGO mapping run — proceed directly to downstream summarization instead of re-QC The goal is de novo assembly-based CDS prediction (as in building the catalog itself) rather than reference-based read mapping to an existing gene catalog VIRGO's bacterial-focused catalog is inappropriate, e.g. the target community is dominated by viral or fungal genes, which are only sparsely included (see 2_fungal_phage annotations)

skills.description: Use when quality-controlling shotgun metagenomic FASTQs as part of an end-to-end functional annotation pipeline, after host and duplicate read filtering and before mapping reads to a gene database.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-quality-filtering Use when quality-controlling shotgun metagenomic FASTQs as part of an end-to-end functional annotation pipeline, after host and duplicate read filtering and before mapping reads to a gene database. Input reads have not yet had host reads and duplicate reads removed — MetaLAFFA orders host filtering and duplicate filtering before quality trimming Input is already a functional profile or gene abundance table — this skill operates on raw/host-filtered FASTQ read data only Input data have already undergone stringent external quality control (e.g. post-HMP quality control), where minimal reads would be discarded during this step http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 MetaLAFFA's third pre-processing step trims low-quality bases from read ends and discards short reads using Trimmomatic's MAXINFO criterion, producing quality-filtered FASTQs plus per-sample summary statistics before read mapping. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: MetaLAFFA's third pre-processing step trims low-quality bases from read ends and discards short reads using Trimmomatic's MAXINFO criterion, producing quality-filtered FASTQs plus per-sample summary statistics before read mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not yet had host reads and duplicate reads removed — MetaLAFFA orders host filtering and duplicate filtering before quality trimming Input is already a functional profile or gene abundance table — this skill operates on raw/host-filtered FASTQ read data only Input data have already undergone stringent external quality control (e.g. post-HMP quality control), where minimal reads would be discarded during this step

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. SRA accession SRR606249, 2 x 100 bp) must be cleaned prior to meta-assembly with metaSPAdes or MegaHIT.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-quality-trimming
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-quality-trimming Use when raw paired-end Illumina shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. SRA accession SRR606249, 2 x 100 bp) must be cleaned prior to meta-assembly with metaSPAdes or MegaHIT. Input is already assembled contigs or binned MAGs (FASTA) — kMetaShot classification works directly on binning output and requires no read trimming Reads are long single-end (2nd/3rd generation) reads rather than paired-end Illumina, where Sickle paired-end mode and the -l 50 length cutoff from this benchmark would not map to the data The analysis goal is MAG classification only and a pre-trimmed or QC'd dataset is already available http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quality-control and trim paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads with FastQC followed by Sickle (quality cutoff -q 32, minimum length -l 50) before meta-assembly, as used in the kMetaShot benchmark on the real mock community dataset (SRR606249). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: Quality-control and trim paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads with FastQC followed by Sickle (quality cutoff -q 32, minimum length -l 50) before meta-assembly, as used in the kMetaShot benchmark on the real mock community dataset (SRR606249).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled contigs or binned MAGs (FASTA) — kMetaShot classification works directly on binning output and requires no read trimming Reads are long single-end (2nd/3rd generation) reads rather than paired-end Illumina, where Sickle paired-end mode and the -l 50 length cutoff from this benchmark would not map to the data The analysis goal is MAG classification only and a pre-trimmed or QC'd dataset is already available

skills.description: Use when benchmarking fimpera-style amplified s-mer querying of a counting Bloom filter on metagenomic FASTQ reads, specifically to verify that query time stays flat or slightly decreases as z increases.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-query-execution
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-query-execution Use when benchmarking fimpera-style amplified s-mer querying of a counting Bloom filter on metagenomic FASTQ reads, specifically to verify that query time stays flat or slightly decreases as z increases. When the goal is assessing false positive rate or abundance precision rather than query execution time — use the FPR/precision benchmark instead. When the index is not a counting AMQ (e.g. no abundance support); fimpera's strategy requires an AMQ that supports abundance queries. When memory overhead of the amplified index is the quantity of interest — fimpera introduces no memory overhead, so timing benchmarks are uninformative there. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduce the fimpera query-time benchmark showing that wrapping a counting Bloom filter with fimpera does not increase query execution time as the z parameter grows; runtimes are tabulated against z alongside a raw-cBF baseline, mirroring Table 2 of the paper. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad305
skills.summary: Reproduce the fimpera query-time benchmark showing that wrapping a counting Bloom filter with fimpera does not increase query execution time as the z parameter grows; runtimes are tabulated against z alongside a raw-cBF baseline, mirroring Table 2 of the paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is assessing false positive rate or abundance precision rather than query execution time — use the FPR/precision benchmark instead. When the index is not a counting AMQ (e.g. no abundance support); fimpera's strategy requires an AMQ that supports abundance queries. When memory overhead of the amplified index is the quantity of interest — fimpera introduces no memory overhead, so timing benchmarks are uninformative there.

skills.description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking a reference gene catalogue's sequence-capture efficiency on shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples, or comparing a new catalogue (e.g. VMGC-90) against an incumbent (e.g. VIRGO) via per-sample mapping rates.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-recruitment-analysis
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-recruitment-analysis Use when evaluating or benchmarking a reference gene catalogue's sequence-capture efficiency on shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples, or comparing a new catalogue (e.g. VMGC-90) against an incumbent (e.g. VIRGO) via per-sample mapping rates. Input is 16S/ITS amplicon data — catalogue read recruitment assumes shotgun reads and will not yield comparable mapping rates Samples are from non-vaginal body sites — the VMGC/VIRGO comparison is calibrated on vaginal metagenomes from 32 studies and may not transfer to gut or oral microbiome data The goal is taxonomic abundance profiling rather than capture-efficiency benchmarking — the VMGC project uses customized Kraken2/Bracken databases from the 786 SGBs for that purpose instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Recruits metagenomic reads against a reference gene/genome catalogue to quantify how much microbial sequence the catalogue captures. Used here to benchmark the VMGC-90 vaginal gene catalogue (74.5% average mapping rate) against the VIRGO catalogue (71.7%) across 4,472 vaginal metagenomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Recruits metagenomic reads against a reference gene/genome catalogue to quantify how much microbial sequence the catalogue captures. Used here to benchmark the VMGC-90 vaginal gene catalogue (74.5% average mapping rate) against the VIRGO catalogue (71.7%) across 4,472 vaginal metagenomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is 16S/ITS amplicon data — catalogue read recruitment assumes shotgun reads and will not yield comparable mapping rates Samples are from non-vaginal body sites — the VMGC/VIRGO comparison is calibrated on vaginal metagenomes from 32 studies and may not transfer to gut or oral microbiome data The goal is taxonomic abundance profiling rather than capture-efficiency benchmarking — the VMGC project uses customized Kraken2/Bracken databases from the 786 SGBs for that purpose instead

skills.description: Use when you need genomic flanking regions around antimicrobial resistance genes (or other target genes) from short-read metagenomic FASTQ data, and full metagenomic de novo assembly is too computationally expensive.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-recruitment-targeted-assembly
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-recruitment-targeted-assembly Use when you need genomic flanking regions around antimicrobial resistance genes (or other target genes) from short-read metagenomic FASTQ data, and full metagenomic de novo assembly is too computationally expensive. Input is long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler/ARGextender is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data You already have a full metagenomic de novo assembly or finished genomes to mine for flanks — direct sequence extraction is cheaper than read recruitment No target genes are identified in the pre-screen — running the assembly step is wasted compute since the KMA filter step exists precisely to avoid this http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 ARGextender-style targeted de novo assembly: iteratively recruit reads to ARG targets with KMA, assemble the recruited reads with SPAdes, and re-target scaffolds until read recruitment saturates — recovering ARG flanking regions without full metagenomic de novo assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: ARGextender-style targeted de novo assembly: iteratively recruit reads to ARG targets with KMA, assemble the recruited reads with SPAdes, and re-target scaffolds until read recruitment saturates — recovering ARG flanking regions without full metagenomic de novo assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read sequencing data — ARGprofiler/ARGextender is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data You already have a full metagenomic de novo assembly or finished genomes to mine for flanks — direct sequence extraction is cheaper than read recruitment No target genes are identified in the pre-screen — running the assembly step is wasted compute since the KMA filter step exists precisely to avoid this

skills.description: Use when you need synthetic longitudinal metagenomic reads carrying within-strain SNVs and small InDels with configurable allele-frequency trajectories, to benchmark mutation-detection tools.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-simulation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-simulation Use when you need synthetic longitudinal metagenomic reads carrying within-strain SNVs and small InDels with configurable allele-frequency trajectories, to benchmark mutation-detection tools. Data are real metagenomic samples from low-depth or poorly characterized species — STEMSim only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes Goal is community-level abundance simulation rather than within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations — use CAMISIM alone to generate the input community Non-longitudinal data with no within-strain evolutionary signal to model across timepoints http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Simulate within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations on longitudinal metagenomic raw reads using STEMSIM, in either camisim mode (CAMISIM output directory as input) or reads mode (externally simulated FASTQs with a supplied reference genome), producing modified reads plus a VCF of true injected mutations. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad302
skills.summary: Simulate within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations on longitudinal metagenomic raw reads using STEMSIM, in either camisim mode (CAMISIM output directory as input) or reads mode (externally simulated FASTQs with a supplied reference genome), producing modified reads plus a VCF of true injected mutations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are real metagenomic samples from low-depth or poorly characterized species — STEMSim only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes Goal is community-level abundance simulation rather than within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations — use CAMISIM alone to generate the input community Non-longitudinal data with no within-strain evolutionary signal to model across timepoints

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a taxonomic classifier needs simulated reads with known origin, e.g., ART-generated Illumina/Roche-454 FASTQ sets from genomes whose proteins are excluded from the reference database.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-simulation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-simulation Use when benchmarking a taxonomic classifier needs simulated reads with known origin, e.g., ART-generated Illumina/Roche-454 FASTQ sets from genomes whose proteins are excluded from the reference database. Input is real metagenomic FASTQ data that simply needs taxonomic classification — simulation is only for controlled benchmarking with known ground truth The sequenced strain is already present in the reference database — the genome-exclusion design (database must not contain the source genome) is what makes sensitivity to underrepresented genera measurable; nucleotide-level classifiers will dominate when the strain is in the database The goal is to assess classification of non-protein-coding regions — protein-level classifiers like Kaiju cannot classify reads from non-coding genomic regions, so a nucleotide-level simulation/benchmark is needed instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Simulates ground-truth high-throughput sequencing reads (Illumina single-end 100 nt, single-end 250 nt, paired-end 250 nt, and Roche/454) from complete annotated genomes with ART so that taxonomic classifiers such as Kaiju, Kraken, and Clark can be benchmarked in a genome-exclusion design. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Simulates ground-truth high-throughput sequencing reads (Illumina single-end 100 nt, single-end 250 nt, paired-end 250 nt, and Roche/454) from complete annotated genomes with ART so that taxonomic classifiers such as Kaiju, Kraken, and Clark can be benchmarked in a genome-exclusion design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real metagenomic FASTQ data that simply needs taxonomic classification — simulation is only for controlled benchmarking with known ground truth The sequenced strain is already present in the reference database — the genome-exclusion design (database must not contain the source genome) is what makes sensitivity to underrepresented genera measurable; nucleotide-level classifiers will dominate when the strain is in the database The goal is to assess classification of non-protein-coding regions — protein-level classifiers like Kaiju cannot classify reads from non-coding genomic regions, so a nucleotide-level simulation/benchmark is needed instead

skills.description: Use when benchmarking HGT breakpoint detection or local strain reconstruction pipelines against known ground truth, so sensitivity and FDR can be computed from simulated reads at defined coverages.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-simulation
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-simulation Use when benchmarking HGT breakpoint detection or local strain reconstruction pipelines against known ground truth, so sensitivity and FDR can be computed from simulated reads at defined coverages. Analyzing real shotgun metagenomics samples where no ground-truth breakpoints exist — sensitivity/FDR against true positions cannot be computed Evaluating tools whose input requirements differ from paired-end shotgun reads (e.g., long-read or assembly-based HGT callers) Simulations requiring realistic community abundance profiles or sequencing error models beyond WGSIM's defaults when the benchmark design does not specify them http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Simulate paired-end shotgun reads from constructed true local strains (with HGT-inserted segments) using WGSIM across multiple coverage levels to create controlled benchmark data for evaluating HGT breakpoint detection and strain reconstruction tools like LEMON and LUMPY. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3301-8
skills.summary: Simulate paired-end shotgun reads from constructed true local strains (with HGT-inserted segments) using WGSIM across multiple coverage levels to create controlled benchmark data for evaluating HGT breakpoint detection and strain reconstruction tools like LEMON and LUMPY.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analyzing real shotgun metagenomics samples where no ground-truth breakpoints exist — sensitivity/FDR against true positions cannot be computed Evaluating tools whose input requirements differ from paired-end shotgun reads (e.g., long-read or assembly-based HGT callers) Simulations requiring realistic community abundance profiles or sequencing error models beyond WGSIM's defaults when the benchmark design does not specify them

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metagenome binners against curated ground-truth genomes: simulated/sampled per-sample reads must be converted into sorted BAM coverage files and ORF predictions before binning and F1/precision/specificity scoring.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-simulation-and-alignment
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-simulation-and-alignment Use when benchmarking metagenome binners against curated ground-truth genomes: simulated/sampled per-sample reads must be converted into sorted BAM coverage files and ORF predictions before binning and F1/precision/specificity scoring. Input is an already-binned set of vMAGs or a non-simulated natural metagenome where ground-truth genome membership is unknown (e.g., GOV2 or agricultural soil viromes), since no per-bin accuracy scoring is possible The target is binning non-viral (microbial) genomes — the article notes MetaBat2 performed better than vRhyme on a synthetic dataset of predominately non-viral sequences and that this was an anticipated limitation Only a single coverage sample is available and robust coverage variance comparisons cannot be made, as vRhyme performs optimally with multiple input samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Generates per-sample metagenomic read sets from curated reference genomes (e.g., the paper's nine benchmark datasets of 999 fragmented complete viral genomes as 4,324 scaffolds), aligns them to scaffolds with Bowtie2 or BWA, and supplies coverage BAMs plus Prodigal gene/protein predictions to binners such as vRhyme for supervised benchmarking of viral genome binning. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Generates per-sample metagenomic read sets from curated reference genomes (e.g., the paper's nine benchmark datasets of 999 fragmented complete viral genomes as 4,324 scaffolds), aligns them to scaffolds with Bowtie2 or BWA, and supplies coverage BAMs plus Prodigal gene/protein predictions to binners such as vRhyme for supervised benchmarking of viral genome binning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an already-binned set of vMAGs or a non-simulated natural metagenome where ground-truth genome membership is unknown (e.g., GOV2 or agricultural soil viromes), since no per-bin accuracy scoring is possible The target is binning non-viral (microbial) genomes — the article notes MetaBat2 performed better than vRhyme on a synthetic dataset of predominately non-viral sequences and that this was an anticipated limitation Only a single coverage sample is available and robust coverage variance comparisons cannot be made, as vRhyme performs optimally with multiple input samples

skills.description: Use when a genome in a simulated community is assembled at extreme coverage (e.g. >1000x) and you need to confirm that coverage — not biology — drives the observed misassembled blocks.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-subsampling
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-subsampling Use when a genome in a simulated community is assembled at extreme coverage (e.g. >1000x) and you need to confirm that coverage — not biology — drives the observed misassembled blocks. The goal is strain-variation capture or sequence-graph output rather than diagnosing coverage-driven misassembly — use the standard MetaCortex two-stage workflow at full coverage instead Reads are experimental/environmental data (e.g. the SRR961514 tutorial reads) with unknown per-genome coverage, where a controlled full-vs-subsampled comparison is not meaningful Misassemblies are already attributable to causes other than coverage (e.g. strain divergence), so downsampling would not test the hypothesis http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Test whether ultra-high sequencing coverage causes assembly errors by subsampling a simulated metagenomic read set (e.g. to 10% of original coverage) and reassembling with MetaCortex, then comparing misassembled-block counts per genome against the reference. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad020
skills.summary: Test whether ultra-high sequencing coverage causes assembly errors by subsampling a simulated metagenomic read set (e.g. to 10% of original coverage) and reassembling with MetaCortex, then comparing misassembled-block counts per genome against the reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is strain-variation capture or sequence-graph output rather than diagnosing coverage-driven misassembly — use the standard MetaCortex two-stage workflow at full coverage instead Reads are experimental/environmental data (e.g. the SRR961514 tutorial reads) with unknown per-genome coverage, where a controlled full-vs-subsampled comparison is not meaningful Misassemblies are already attributable to causes other than coverage (e.g. strain divergence), so downsampling would not test the hypothesis

skills.description: Use when a user wants to quantify how classification sensitivity and reconstruction completeness degrade with sequencing depth, e.g. testing a pipeline on SRA mock-community reads (FASTQ) at 10/1/0.1% subsampling across replicate trials.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-subsampling-replication
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-subsampling-replication Use when a user wants to quantify how classification sensitivity and reconstruction completeness degrade with sequencing depth, e.g. testing a pipeline on SRA mock-community reads (FASTQ) at 10/1/0.1% subsampling across replicate trials. The dataset has no ground-truth mock community composition, so detection rates of known constituents cannot be scored. Only a single sequencing depth is available and the goal is one-shot classification rather than depth-robustness benchmarking. Input is already a taxonomic abundance table rather than raw FASTQ reads, so subsampling of original reads is impossible. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark a viral metagenomic classifier's robustness by randomly subsampling paired FASTQ reads to fixed depth fractions (10%, 1%, 0.1%) across ten independent trials per depth, then scoring taxonomic detection and viral-base retention against full-depth results. It reproduces the VirMAP paper's viral mock community degradation analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Benchmark a viral metagenomic classifier's robustness by randomly subsampling paired FASTQ reads to fixed depth fractions (10%, 1%, 0.1%) across ten independent trials per depth, then scoring taxonomic detection and viral-base retention against full-depth results. It reproduces the VirMAP paper's viral mock community degradation analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no ground-truth mock community composition, so detection rates of known constituents cannot be scored. Only a single sequencing depth is available and the goal is one-shot classification rather than depth-robustness benchmarking. Input is already a taxonomic abundance table rather than raw FASTQ reads, so subsampling of original reads is impossible.

skills.description: Use when disease-associated genes from MWAS must be assigned to taxa in a shotgun metagenome, e.g., tracing which organisms reads of a specific gene derive from.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-attribution
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-attribution Use when disease-associated genes from MWAS must be assigned to taxa in a shotgun metagenome, e.g., tracing which organisms reads of a specific gene derive from. When the goal is de novo taxonomic profiling of the whole metagenome rather than attributing specific known target genes — use the phylogenetic profiling steps (OMARU_Phyl_AS.sm) instead When reads have not passed OMARU read/sample QC stages; raw FASTQ should not be fed directly to the traceback module When no suitable phylogenetic reference database (e.g., UHGG-based) covers the candidate organisms, since attribution depends on reference databases http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Applies OMARU's phylogenetic-functional link module to trace sequencing reads of target genes (e.g., disease-associated genes such as the SCZ-associated Vpar_1847) back to their organisms of origin, producing a gene-to-taxon attribution table for the metagenomic sample. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: Applies OMARU's phylogenetic-functional link module to trace sequencing reads of target genes (e.g., disease-associated genes such as the SCZ-associated Vpar_1847) back to their organisms of origin, producing a gene-to-taxon attribution table for the metagenomic sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo taxonomic profiling of the whole metagenome rather than attributing specific known target genes — use the phylogenetic profiling steps (OMARU_Phyl_AS.sm) instead When reads have not passed OMARU read/sample QC stages; raw FASTQ should not be fed directly to the traceback module When no suitable phylogenetic reference database (e.g., UHGG-based) covers the candidate organisms, since attribution depends on reference databases

skills.description: Use when you have FASTQ read fractions (mapped/unmapped from read-contig alignment) from a HiFi metagenome assembly and need to know whether low-representation taxa are missing from the assembly.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-classification Use when you have FASTQ read fractions (mapped/unmapped from read-contig alignment) from a HiFi metagenome assembly and need to know whether low-representation taxa are missing from the assembly. The input is genomic bins needing taxonomic assignment — Mapler handles that separately with GTDB-Tk, not Kraken 2. Reads are short reads or non-HiFi data outside Mapler's HiFi long-read assembly-evaluation scope. You only need a single taxonomic label per sample with no mapped/unmapped comparison — standalone Kraken 2 suffices without the Mapler fraction split. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Classifies HiFi metagenomic reads taxonomically with Kraken 2, applied separately to mapped and unmapped read fractions produced by the Mapler assembly-quality pipeline, and renders interactive Krona plots to quantify which taxa the assembly fails to capture. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Classifies HiFi metagenomic reads taxonomically with Kraken 2, applied separately to mapped and unmapped read fractions produced by the Mapler assembly-quality pipeline, and renders interactive Krona plots to quantify which taxa the assembly fails to capture.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is genomic bins needing taxonomic assignment — Mapler handles that separately with GTDB-Tk, not Kraken 2. Reads are short reads or non-HiFi data outside Mapler's HiFi long-read assembly-evaluation scope. You only need a single taxonomic label per sample with no mapped/unmapped comparison — standalone Kraken 2 suffices without the Mapler fraction split.

skills.description: Use when quality-assuring preprocessed short-read FASTQ metagenomic samples prior to assembly: to classify reads against a reference database, detect contamination, and visualize microbial community composition per sample with Krona charts and a MultiQC report.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-classification Use when quality-assuring preprocessed short-read FASTQ metagenomic samples prior to assembly: to classify reads against a reference database, detect contamination, and visualize microbial community composition per sample with Krona charts and a MultiQC report. The input reads are long reads (e.g., Nanopore/PacBio) at this stage — nf-core/mag explicitly gates tools by read type and this classification/QC step is scoped to preprocessed short reads only The goal is taxonomic classification of assembled contigs or MAG bins rather than individual preprocessed reads Samples have already been classified and the task is downstream genome binning or MAG annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Classifies preprocessed metagenomic short reads taxonomically with Kraken2 or Centrifuge inside the nf-core/mag pipeline, rendering per-sample Krona charts and an aggregated MultiQC report to assess contamination and community composition before assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Classifies preprocessed metagenomic short reads taxonomically with Kraken2 or Centrifuge inside the nf-core/mag pipeline, rendering per-sample Krona charts and an aggregated MultiQC report to assess contamination and community composition before assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input reads are long reads (e.g., Nanopore/PacBio) at this stage — nf-core/mag explicitly gates tools by read type and this classification/QC step is scoped to preprocessed short reads only The goal is taxonomic classification of assembled contigs or MAG bins rather than individual preprocessed reads Samples have already been classified and the task is downstream genome binning or MAG annotation

skills.description: Use when quality-filtered (host-filtered, duplicate-filtered, quality-trimmed) shotgun metagenomic FASTQs must be mapped to a microbial protein gene database like UniRef90 to obtain read-to-gene matches for functional profiling.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-to-protein-alignment
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-to-protein-alignment Use when quality-filtered (host-filtered, duplicate-filtered, quality-trimmed) shotgun metagenomic FASTQs must be mapped to a microbial protein gene database like UniRef90 to obtain read-to-gene matches for functional profiling. Input reads have not undergone host read filtering, duplicate removal, or quality trimming — MetaLAFFA requires these quality control steps before the read mapping phase The analysis requires nucleotide-to-nucleotide or contig/gene-family-level alignment rather than 6-frame translated read-to-protein alignment The goal is assembling microbial genomes; the article notes assembly is prohibitively time and memory intensive and read-based annotation is the alternative pursued here http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Align quality-controlled shotgun metagenomic reads to a protein-sequence gene database (UniRef90) in translated-alignment mode using DIAMOND, as done in MetaLAFFA's read mapping phase, to produce a read-to-gene hit table that feeds best-hit filtering and gene abundance counting. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: Align quality-controlled shotgun metagenomic reads to a protein-sequence gene database (UniRef90) in translated-alignment mode using DIAMOND, as done in MetaLAFFA's read mapping phase, to produce a read-to-gene hit table that feeds best-hit filtering and gene abundance counting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not undergone host read filtering, duplicate removal, or quality trimming — MetaLAFFA requires these quality control steps before the read mapping phase The analysis requires nucleotide-to-nucleotide or contig/gene-family-level alignment rather than 6-frame translated read-to-protein alignment The goal is assembling microbial genomes; the article notes assembly is prohibitively time and memory intensive and read-based annotation is the alternative pursued here

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic run mixes short-read-only, long-read-only, and paired short+long-read samples, and each sample must be routed to the correct assembly path (MEGAHIT vs SPAdes vs hybridSPAdes) before QUAST-based quality comparison.
skills.name: metagenomic-read-type-gating
skills.search_text: metagenomic-read-type-gating Use when a metagenomic run mixes short-read-only, long-read-only, and paired short+long-read samples, and each sample must be routed to the correct assembly path (MEGAHIT vs SPAdes vs hybridSPAdes) before QUAST-based quality comparison. The dataset contains only short reads — gating adds no value; just run MEGAHIT or SPAdes directly. The dataset contains only long reads for a sample — hybridSPAdes is not applicable; a long-read assembler path is the wrong route for hybrid gating. Reads are raw and unpreprocessed — gating operates on preprocessed reads; run adapter/quality trimming (e.g. fastp, Porechop, Filtlong) first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Classifies each metagenomic sample by its read content (short-read only, long-read only, or hybrid short+long) inside a Nextflow pipeline, and uses that classification to dispatch the sample to the correct de novo assembler (MEGAHIT, SPAdes, or hybridSPAdes) in the nf-core/mag workflow. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Classifies each metagenomic sample by its read content (short-read only, long-read only, or hybrid short+long) inside a Nextflow pipeline, and uses that classification to dispatch the sample to the correct de novo assembler (MEGAHIT, SPAdes, or hybridSPAdes) in the nf-core/mag workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains only short reads — gating adds no value; just run MEGAHIT or SPAdes directly. The dataset contains only long reads for a sample — hybridSPAdes is not applicable; a long-read assembler path is the wrong route for hybrid gating. Reads are raw and unpreprocessed — gating operates on preprocessed reads; run adapter/quality trimming (e.g. fastp, Porechop, Filtlong) first.

skills.description: Use when a study needs large, publicly available, redundancy-filtered reference protein catalogs (e.g. as search database input for HH-suite3/BFD or for catalog size/provenance audits) and the input is metagenomic or metatranscriptomic protein sequence space.
skills.name: metagenomic-reference-catalog-retrieval
skills.search_text: metagenomic-reference-catalog-retrieval Use when a study needs large, publicly available, redundancy-filtered reference protein catalogs (e.g. as search database input for HH-suite3/BFD or for catalog size/provenance audits) and the input is metagenomic or metatranscriptomic protein sequence space. The analysis requires nucleotide contigs or whole-genome assemblies rather than protein sequences — use PenguiN nucleotide assembly instead. A curated, annotated protein database (e.g. UniProt) suffices; these catalogs are redundancy-filtered at 90% but not functionally annotated. The metagenomic dataset is small or low-complexity where downloading a 2-billion-sequence reference catalog is unnecessary overhead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Retrieves and verifies the Plass-built reference protein catalogs — the Soil Reference Catalog (SRC, 2 billion sequences from 640 soil metagenome samples) and the Marine Eukaryotic Reference Catalog (MERC, 292 million sequences from 775 TARA ocean metatranscriptomes) — as single FASTA files, confirming their 90%/90% redundancy-reduction provenance. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41592-019-0437-4
skills.summary: Retrieves and verifies the Plass-built reference protein catalogs — the Soil Reference Catalog (SRC, 2 billion sequences from 640 soil metagenome samples) and the Marine Eukaryotic Reference Catalog (MERC, 292 million sequences from 775 TARA ocean metatranscriptomes) — as single FASTA files, confirming their 90%/90% redundancy-reduction provenance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires nucleotide contigs or whole-genome assemblies rather than protein sequences — use PenguiN nucleotide assembly instead. A curated, annotated protein database (e.g. UniProt) suffices; these catalogs are redundancy-filtered at 90% but not functionally annotated. The metagenomic dataset is small or low-complexity where downloading a 2-billion-sequence reference catalog is unnecessary overhead.

skills.description: Use when candidate transferred segments reconstructed from shotgun metagenomics data must be scored against donor/receptor reference segment sequences to measure local alignment similarity and reconstruction accuracy.
skills.name: metagenomic-reference-sequence-comparison
skills.search_text: metagenomic-reference-sequence-comparison Use when candidate transferred segments reconstructed from shotgun metagenomics data must be scored against donor/receptor reference segment sequences to measure local alignment similarity and reconstruction accuracy. When no reference donor/receptor sequences are available, since the scoring is defined only against corresponding reference segment sequences (hi) When a global (end-to-end) alignment is required rather than local alignment, since Smith-Waterman scores only the best local match and may understate divergence outside the aligned region When the goal is HGT breakpoint detection itself rather than scoring already-reconstructed segments — use LEMON's raw/accurate breakpoint detection steps instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 Quantifies how well reconstructed transferred segments (Hi) match their reference counterparts (hi) by performing Smith-Waterman local sequence alignment, as used in LEMON's transferred-segment identification stage to compute per-strain reconstruction accuracy (RAi). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3301-8
skills.summary: Quantifies how well reconstructed transferred segments (Hi) match their reference counterparts (hi) by performing Smith-Waterman local sequence alignment, as used in LEMON's transferred-segment identification stage to compute per-strain reconstruction accuracy (RAi).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no reference donor/receptor sequences are available, since the scoring is defined only against corresponding reference segment sequences (hi) When a global (end-to-end) alignment is required rather than local alignment, since Smith-Waterman scores only the best local match and may understate divergence outside the aligned region When the goal is HGT breakpoint detection itself rather than scoring already-reconstructed segments — use LEMON's raw/accurate breakpoint detection steps instead

skills.description: Use when you have a metagenomic taxonomic profile table (MetaPhlAn merged table or QIIME OTU/BIOM) plus sample metadata with class labels, and the goal is to train a classifier or predict the phenotype of unknown samples.
skills.name: metagenomic-sample-phenotype-classification
skills.search_text: metagenomic-sample-phenotype-classification Use when you have a metagenomic taxonomic profile table (MetaPhlAn merged table or QIIME OTU/BIOM) plus sample metadata with class labels, and the goal is to train a classifier or predict the phenotype of unknown samples. The input is raw sequencing reads rather than an already-profiled taxonomic abundance table (MetaPhlAn/QIIME output) — MegaR does not profile reads. The goal is differential abundance testing or time-interval analysis rather than phenotype classification (tools like MetaDprof or MetaLonDa are cited for those tasks). You need >2-class models with automatic class handling — use the 'Select level to classify' tab only to remove control/less important classes; deep learning classifiers are not yet supported. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Train and apply machine learning classifiers (Random Forest, SVM, GLM) in MegaR on 16S rRNA OTU/BIOM or WGS MetaPhlAn taxonomic profiles to classify samples into phenotype categories (e.g., T1D diagnosed t/f) and predict unknown samples from a saved RDS model. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03933-4
skills.summary: Train and apply machine learning classifiers (Random Forest, SVM, GLM) in MegaR on 16S rRNA OTU/BIOM or WGS MetaPhlAn taxonomic profiles to classify samples into phenotype categories (e.g., T1D diagnosed t/f) and predict unknown samples from a saved RDS model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw sequencing reads rather than an already-profiled taxonomic abundance table (MetaPhlAn/QIIME output) — MegaR does not profile reads. The goal is differential abundance testing or time-interval analysis rather than phenotype classification (tools like MetaDprof or MetaLonDa are cited for those tasks). skills.description: Use when scaffolding metagenomic contigs with paired long-range links and you must decide which contig-pair links are probable interspecies misjoins based on coverage depth and oligonucleotide composition.

skills.search_text: metagenomic-scaffolding-misjoin-detection Use when scaffolding metagenomic contigs with paired long-range links and you must decide which contig-pair links are probable interspecies misjoins based on coverage depth and oligonucleotide composition. Input is a finished or reference-based assembly where binning/coverage-based link filtering is unnecessary Only single-end short reads are available — MetaPlatanus requires at least one short-read paired-end library Contigs are all shorter than 1000 bp, so the F_4-mer component is forced to 1 and the filter degenerates to coverage ratio alone http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstructs MetaPlatanus's interspecies link-exclusion filter used during scaffolding: links between contigs are tested against empirical complementary cumulative distributions of coverage-depth ratios (F_coverage) and 4-mer frequency distances (F_4-mer), and a link is excluded when F_coverage(r) × F_4-mer(d) < 0.05. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Reconstructs MetaPlatanus's interspecies link-exclusion filter used during scaffolding: links between contigs are tested against empirical complementary cumulative distributions of coverage-depth ratios (F_coverage) and 4-mer frequency distances (F_4-mer), and a link is excluded when F_coverage(r) × F_4-mer(d) < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a finished or reference-based assembly where binning/coverage-based link filtering is unnecessary Only single-end short reads are available — MetaPlatanus requires at least one short-read paired-end library Contigs are all shorter than 1000 bp, so the F_4-mer component is forced to 1 and the filter degenerates to coverage ratio alone
