skills.description: Use when metagenomic/virome contigs must be mined with multiple phage predictors and the goal is a vOTU set plus a per-miner overlap visualization to assess cross-miner concordance.
skills.name: miner-agreement-visualization
skills.search_text: miner-agreement-visualization Use when metagenomic/virome contigs must be mined with multiple phage predictors and the goal is a vOTU set plus a per-miner overlap visualization to assess cross-miner concordance. Input is raw reads rather than assembled contigs — the mining step expects MEGAHIT-assembled consensus scaffolds, not FASTQ A single-miner viral prediction is sufficient and no cross-miner concordance assessment is needed — the multi-miner merge and upSet visualization add runtime (e.g., all-versus-all comparisons are time-consuming) without benefit Short contigs below the --minlen cutoff are the target — the dereplication step discards consensus scaffolds under the threshold (default 1000 bp, 3000 bp for Liang et al. reproduction) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduce the vOTU identification stage of the MetaPhage pipeline and quantify agreement across phage miners by merging VirFinder, VirSorter, Phigaro, and VIBRANT predictions, dereplicating with CD-HIT-EST, and rendering per-miner overlaps as an upSet plot. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Reproduce the vOTU identification stage of the MetaPhage pipeline and quantify agreement across phage miners by merging VirFinder, VirSorter, Phigaro, and VIBRANT predictions, dereplicating with CD-HIT-EST, and rendering per-miner overlaps as an upSet plot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than assembled contigs — the mining step expects MEGAHIT-assembled consensus scaffolds, not FASTQ A single-miner viral prediction is sufficient and no cross-miner concordance assessment is needed — the multi-miner merge and upSet visualization add runtime (e.g., all-versus-all comparisons are time-consuming) without benefit Short contigs below the --minlen cutoff are the target — the dereplication step discards consensus scaffolds under the threshold (default 1000 bp, 3000 bp for Liang et al. reproduction)

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic (or virome) dataset has been mined by multiple phage-mining tools and you need to quantify per-miner prediction counts and overlap/difference in vOTU assignments across miners.
skills.name: miner-prediction-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: miner-prediction-overlap-analysis Use when a metagenomic (or virome) dataset has been mined by multiple phage-mining tools and you need to quantify per-miner prediction counts and overlap/difference in vOTU assignments across miners. You only have predictions from a single miner, so no cross-miner overlap can be computed Contigs have not yet been dereplicated into vOTUs (95% identity / 85% coverage), so miner outputs cannot be assigned to a shared unit The goal is viral quality assessment rather than miner agreement — CheckV is used in the paper to attribute vOTU count differences to partial/low-quality genome predictions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compares which vOTUs each phage miner (DeepVirFinder, VirSorter2, VIBRANT, Phigaro) predicted in a MetaPhage run, building an upSet plot and per-miner count table that reveals consensus versus miner-specific calls on metagenomic assemblies. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Compares which vOTUs each phage miner (DeepVirFinder, VirSorter2, VIBRANT, Phigaro) predicted in a MetaPhage run, building an upSet plot and per-miner count table that reveals consensus versus miner-specific calls on metagenomic assemblies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have predictions from a single miner, so no cross-miner overlap can be computed Contigs have not yet been dereplicated into vOTUs (95% identity / 85% coverage), so miner outputs cannot be assigned to a shared unit The goal is viral quality assessment rather than miner agreement — CheckV is used in the paper to attribute vOTU count differences to partial/low-quality genome predictions

skills.description: Use when assembled plasmid contigs (e.g. Unicycler output FASTA from Plassembler) need to be matched against a known plasmid database to annotate similarity to PLSDB entries.
skills.name: minhash-database-matching
skills.search_text: minhash-database-matching Use when assembled plasmid contigs (e.g. Unicycler output FASTA from Plassembler) need to be matched against a known plasmid database to annotate similarity to PLSDB entries. Input is raw long/short reads rather than assembled plasmid contigs (read removal and assembly are handled by earlier Plassembler steps, not this Mash-based matching) Goal is functional/gene-level plasmid annotation rather than database-level similarity to known plasmids (Mash gives MinHash distance, not gene content) No Plassembler/PLSDB sketch database has been installed (install_database.py has not been run), so no reference sketches are available http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Sketch assembled plasmid contigs with Mash and screen them against the PLSDB sketch database shipped with the Plassembler database (install_database.py) to identify which contigs match known plasmids, keeping the lowest-distance top hit per contig under a 0.1 mash distance threshold. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Sketch assembled plasmid contigs with Mash and screen them against the PLSDB sketch database shipped with the Plassembler database (install_database.py) to identify which contigs match known plasmids, keeping the lowest-distance top hit per contig under a 0.1 mash distance threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw long/short reads rather than assembled plasmid contigs (read removal and assembly are handled by earlier Plassembler steps, not this Mash-based matching) Goal is functional/gene-level plasmid annotation rather than database-level similarity to known plasmids (Mash gives MinHash distance, not gene content) No Plassembler/PLSDB sketch database has been installed (install_database.py has not been run), so no reference sketches are available

skills.description: Use when you have paired WGS/FASTQ read files for many metagenomic samples and need a fast MinHash-based all-vs-all distance matrix to test whether samples cluster by a known metadata attribute such as body site.
skills.name: minhash-genome-sketching
skills.search_text: minhash-genome-sketching Use when you have paired WGS/FASTQ read files for many metagenomic samples and need a fast MinHash-based all-vs-all distance matrix to test whether samples cluster by a known metadata attribute such as body site. When abundance resolution matters — the article reports Mash's data-reduction/unique-k-mer approach gives decreased clustering resolution versus Libra's all-read k-mer abundance calculation When inputs are already assembled genomes or sketch files rather than raw WGS reads for all-vs-all metagenome comparison When the target distance requires abundance-aware normalization (e.g., Cosine Similarity on composition and abundance normalized for sequencing depth) rather than MinHash presence/absence-style distance http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Sketches metagenomic samples with Mash MinHash and computes an all-vs-all distance matrix to cluster samples (e.g., 48 HMP whole-genome shotgun read samples by body site), benchmarking Mash's resolution against abundance-aware tools like Libra and Simka. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giy165
skills.summary: Sketches metagenomic samples with Mash MinHash and computes an all-vs-all distance matrix to cluster samples (e.g., 48 HMP whole-genome shotgun read samples by body site), benchmarking Mash's resolution against abundance-aware tools like Libra and Simka.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When abundance resolution matters — the article reports Mash's data-reduction/unique-k-mer approach gives decreased clustering resolution versus Libra's all-read k-mer abundance calculation When inputs are already assembled genomes or sketch files rather than raw WGS reads for all-vs-all metagenome comparison When the target distance requires abundance-aware normalization (e.g., Cosine Similarity on composition and abundance normalized for sequencing depth) rather than MinHash presence/absence-style distance

skills.description: Use when you have many genome assemblies (e.g. 3269 MAG FASTA files) and need to find each one's closest relative in a reference genome set (e.g. 2505 HGR genomes) to assign species labels.
skills.name: minhash-genome-sketching
skills.search_text: minhash-genome-sketching Use when you have many genome assemblies (e.g. 3269 MAG FASTA files) and need to find each one's closest relative in a reference genome set (e.g. 2505 HGR genomes) to assign species labels. You need direct read-level taxonomic classification of metagenomic reads rather than genome-to-genome comparison — use DeepMicrobes or Kraken instead Genomes are highly fragmented so the 60% aligned-query-fraction criterion would mislabel novel species as matches; fragmentation degrades alignment-based classifier performance as noted in the paper You only need coarse similarity clustering of genomes without ANI confirmation (a single Mash-distance clustering may suffice) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Rapidly computes pairwise genome distances by sketching genome FASTA files with Mash (MinHash k-mer sketches), identifying each query genome's closest relative among a reference database, then confirming the match with MUMmer whole-genome alignment. Used to assign species labels to benchmark MAGs relative to the 2505 HGR training genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Rapidly computes pairwise genome distances by sketching genome FASTA files with Mash (MinHash k-mer sketches), identifying each query genome's closest relative among a reference database, then confirming the match with MUMmer whole-genome alignment. Used to assign species labels to benchmark MAGs relative to the 2505 HGR training genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need direct read-level taxonomic classification of metagenomic reads rather than genome-to-genome comparison — use DeepMicrobes or Kraken instead Genomes are highly fragmented so the 60% aligned-query-fraction criterion would mislabel novel species as matches; fragmentation degrades alignment-based classifier performance as noted in the paper You only need coarse similarity clustering of genomes without ANI confirmation (a single Mash-distance clustering may suffice)

skills.description: Use when shotgun reads (FASTA/FASTQ, short or long) from metagenomic or all-food-sequencing (AFS) samples must be taxonomically classified and quantified against massive multi-kingdom reference genome collections faster than alignment-based tools like BWA or MegaBLAST.
skills.name: minhash-kmer-read-classification
skills.search_text: minhash-kmer-read-classification Use when shotgun reads (FASTA/FASTQ, short or long) from metagenomic or all-food-sequencing (AFS) samples must be taxonomically classified and quantified against massive multi-kingdom reference genome collections faster than alignment-based tools like BWA or MegaBLAST. The task requires base-level alignment of reads to reference sequences (use BWA, Bowtie2, or CUSHAW instead) — MetaCache only assigns reads to taxa via k-mer/minhash similarity The reference database and the classification executable were compiled with different data type settings (e.g. MC_TARGET_ID_TYPE or MC_KMER_TYPE) — the README warns a database can only be queried with the same variant that built it Highly accurate alignment-based quantification is required for novel or highly divergent organisms absent from reference genomes, where k-mer matching false positives matter http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Classify metagenomic/food-sample sequencing reads against large reference genome databases using MetaCache's alignment-free, minhashing-subsampled k-mer matching, implemented either as the C++ workstation tool (AFS-MetaCache) or as the Apache Spark cluster tool (MetaCacheSpark). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Classify metagenomic/food-sample sequencing reads against large reference genome databases using MetaCache's alignment-free, minhashing-subsampled k-mer matching, implemented either as the C++ workstation tool (AFS-MetaCache) or as the Apache Spark cluster tool (MetaCacheSpark).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires base-level alignment of reads to reference sequences (use BWA, Bowtie2, or CUSHAW instead) — MetaCache only assigns reads to taxa via k-mer/minhash similarity The reference database and the classification executable were compiled with different data type settings (e.g. MC_TARGET_ID_TYPE or MC_KMER_TYPE) — the README warns a database can only be queried with the same variant that built it Highly accurate alignment-based quantification is required for novel or highly divergent organisms absent from reference genomes, where k-mer matching false positives matter

skills.description: Use when building a large reference genome classification database (e.g. multi-kingdom food or RefSeq-scale collections) where storing all k-mers would exhaust memory and a minhash sketch must be computed into partitioned hash tables.
skills.name: minhash-kmer-sketching
skills.search_text: minhash-kmer-sketching Use when building a large reference genome classification database (e.g. multi-kingdom food or RefSeq-scale collections) where storing all k-mers would exhaust memory and a minhash sketch must be computed into partitioned hash tables. Input is already a built classification database or a query read set (use query mode, not sketch construction) The reference collection is small enough to fit all k-mers in memory on one machine with the plain C++ metacache, where a distributed Spark sketch adds unnecessary complexity http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Subsample k-mers from reference genomes using locality-sensitive minhashing so that only an order-of-magnitude fewer k-mers are stored while read classification accuracy is retained. This is the core indexing technique behind MetaCache, AFS-MetaCache, and MetaCacheSpark. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Subsample k-mers from reference genomes using locality-sensitive minhashing so that only an order-of-magnitude fewer k-mers are stored while read classification accuracy is retained. This is the core indexing technique behind MetaCache, AFS-MetaCache, and MetaCacheSpark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a built classification database or a query read set (use query mode, not sketch construction) The reference collection is small enough to fit all k-mers in memory on one machine with the plain C++ metacache, where a distributed Spark sketch adds unnecessary complexity

skills.description: Use when you need sample-level similarity/distance estimates from raw short-read FASTQ files — e.g. clustering metagenomes, identifying re-sequencings, or selecting Mash sketch/k-mer defaults.
skills.name: minhash-sketch-distance-estimation
skills.search_text: minhash-sketch-distance-estimation Use when you need sample-level similarity/distance estimates from raw short-read FASTQ files — e.g. clustering metagenomes, identifying re-sequencings, or selecting Mash sketch/k-mer defaults. Input data are long reads — ARGprofiler (and this Mash-based comparison) is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data You need genome-level reference comparison or alignment-based distances rather than fast sample-level similarity of sequencing runs Sketch memory/space constraints force sketch sizes below ~10^4 — results will not reliably distinguish near-identical samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmark and apply MinHash sketching (Mash 2.3) to estimate sequence distances between metagenomic sequencing runs, tuning sketch size and k-mer size so that distances reliably separate technical replicates from distinct samples. In ARGprofiler this established k=31 and sketch size 10^4 as defaults for k-mer-based comparison of sequencing runs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Benchmark and apply MinHash sketching (Mash 2.3) to estimate sequence distances between metagenomic sequencing runs, tuning sketch size and k-mer size so that distances reliably separate technical replicates from distinct samples. In ARGprofiler this established k=31 and sketch size 10^4 as defaults for k-mer-based comparison of sequencing runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are long reads — ARGprofiler (and this Mash-based comparison) is designed to only work with short-read sequencing data You need genome-level reference comparison or alignment-based distances rather than fast sample-level similarity of sequencing runs Sketch memory/space constraints force sketch sizes below ~10^4 — results will not reliably distinguish near-identical samples

skills.description: Use when a large pool of candidate qPCR primer pairs (e.g., nondegenerate forms expanded from degenerate EcoFunPrimer outputs) must be reduced to the smallest set still amplifying the maximum number of environmentally ranked reference genes.
skills.name: minimal-primer-set-optimization
skills.search_text: minimal-primer-set-optimization Use when a large pool of candidate qPCR primer pairs (e.g., nondegenerate forms expanded from degenerate EcoFunPrimer outputs) must be reduced to the smallest set still amplifying the maximum number of environmentally ranked reference genes. When the gene of interest is not phylogenetically diverse or the input is a single aligned sequence — degenerate or simple Primer3 design suffices When only a handful of primer pairs are already available and no candidate-pool reduction is needed When genes are too low-abundance to rank (the article notes HT-qPCR or conventional qPCR combined with MetaFunPrimer may be needed for very low relative abundance genes) http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Final selection step of the MetaFunPrimer pipeline that reduces an expanded pool of candidate primer pairs (e.g., 181 nondegenerate amoA-AOB candidates) down to the minimal set (78 pairs) that captures the maximum number of reference gene products via 100% forward-and-reverse in silico PCR matches. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00201-21
skills.summary: Final selection step of the MetaFunPrimer pipeline that reduces an expanded pool of candidate primer pairs (e.g., 181 nondegenerate amoA-AOB candidates) down to the minimal set (78 pairs) that captures the maximum number of reference gene products via 100% forward-and-reverse in silico PCR matches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the gene of interest is not phylogenetically diverse or the input is a single aligned sequence — degenerate or simple Primer3 design suffices When only a handful of primer pairs are already available and no candidate-pool reduction is needed When genes are too low-abundance to rank (the article notes HT-qPCR or conventional qPCR combined with MetaFunPrimer may be needed for very low relative abundance genes)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a nanopore read classifier (e.g. SPUMONI) and you need a per-read truth label set: align the same read set with minimap2 against the same references and take confident alignments (MAPQ >= 30) as ground truth.
skills.name: minimap2-alignment-gold-standard-calling
skills.search_text: minimap2-alignment-gold-standard-calling Use when benchmarking a nanopore read classifier (e.g. SPUMONI) and you need a per-read truth label set: align the same read set with minimap2 against the same references and take confident alignments (MAPQ >= 30) as ground truth. The task is de novo alignment or variant calling rather than generating truth labels for a read-classification benchmark The reference contains substantial sequence similarity between target and non-target sequences (e.g. conserved genes between species), making MAPQ-based confidence unreliable Reads are too short or low-quality for minimap2 to produce confident MAPQ >= 30 alignments, leaving most reads without gold-standard labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Derives a trusted per-read classification gold standard by aligning base-called nanopore reads with minimap2 against both single-reference and pan-genome indexes, using a MAPQ >= 30 threshold on trimmed read suffixes, so that faster classifiers such as SPUMONI can be scored by F1 against it. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Derives a trusted per-read classification gold standard by aligning base-called nanopore reads with minimap2 against both single-reference and pan-genome indexes, using a MAPQ >= 30 threshold on trimmed read suffixes, so that faster classifiers such as SPUMONI can be scored by F1 against it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is de novo alignment or variant calling rather than generating truth labels for a read-classification benchmark The reference contains substantial sequence similarity between target and non-target sequences (e.g. conserved genes between species), making MAPQ-based confidence unreliable Reads are too short or low-quality for minimap2 to produce confident MAPQ >= 30 alignments, leaving most reads without gold-standard labels

skills.description: Use when evaluating raw nanopore signal mapping tools against a trusted reference: minimap2 alignments of basecalled reads serve as ground truth to compute per-dataset precision/recall/F1 for raw-signal mappers.
skills.name: minimap2-ground-truth-generation
skills.search_text: minimap2-ground-truth-generation Use when evaluating raw nanopore signal mapping tools against a trusted reference: minimap2 alignments of basecalled reads serve as ground truth to compute per-dataset precision/recall/F1 for raw-signal mappers. When the goal is the raw-signal mapping itself rather than benchmarking — minimap2 operates on basecalled sequences, not raw signals, and cannot replace the signal mappers being evaluated When no high-quality basecalled reads are available for the dataset, since the truth set cannot be generated from raw signals alone with this method When evaluating on r10.4.1 chemistry data — UNCALLED (whose PAF template and pafstats are reused) only supports legacy r9.4.1 data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates ground-truth basecalled-read alignments with minimap2 to score raw-signal mappers (RawHash/RawHash2, UNCALLED, Sigmap) on precision, recall, and error rate using UNCALLED's pafstats utility. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad272
skills.summary: Generates ground-truth basecalled-read alignments with minimap2 to score raw-signal mappers (RawHash/RawHash2, UNCALLED, Sigmap) on precision, recall, and error rate using UNCALLED's pafstats utility.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is the raw-signal mapping itself rather than benchmarking — minimap2 operates on basecalled sequences, not raw signals, and cannot replace the signal mappers being evaluated When no high-quality basecalled reads are available for the dataset, since the truth set cannot be generated from raw signals alone with this method When evaluating on r10.4.1 chemistry data — UNCALLED (whose PAF template and pafstats are reused) only supports legacy r9.4.1 data

skills.description: Use when decontaminating Oxford Nanopore (ONT) long reads from (meta)genomic FASTQ input against a human reference index such as human-t2t-hla, or when benchmarking long-read host depletion against tools like NCBI's HRRT.
skills.name: minimap2-long-read-alignment
skills.search_text: minimap2-long-read-alignment Use when decontaminating Oxford Nanopore (ONT) long reads from (meta)genomic FASTQ input against a human reference index such as human-t2t-hla, or when benchmarking long-read host depletion against tools like NCBI's HRRT. Input is paired Illumina short-read data — Hostile auto-selects Bowtie2 (--sensitive, -k 1) instead of Minimap2 in that case Goal is exhaustive host read removal rather than precise microbial retention — HRRT masks more aggressively but removes 21-43 times more bacterial reads Reference is mouse (mouse-mm39) or a custom non-human genome requiring different index construction http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Applies Minimap2 with the map-ont preset (secondary alignments disabled) as the long-read aligner inside Hostile's streaming host-read decontamination pipeline, aligning single-end ONT FASTQ reads against a human reference index so aligned reads can be counted with Samtools and discarded. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad728
skills.summary: Applies Minimap2 with the map-ont preset (secondary alignments disabled) as the long-read aligner inside Hostile's streaming host-read decontamination pipeline, aligning single-end ONT FASTQ reads against a human reference index so aligned reads can be counted with Samtools and discarded.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is paired Illumina short-read data — Hostile auto-selects Bowtie2 (--sensitive, -k 1) instead of Minimap2 in that case Goal is exhaustive host read removal rather than precise microbial retention — HRRT masks more aggressively but removes 21-43 times more bacterial reads Reference is mouse (mouse-mm39) or a custom non-human genome requiring different index construction

skills.description: Use when assembler-generated contigs must be mapped to known reference replicons (multi-FASTA passed via --reference) to compute reference-based assembly quality metrics like LSA.
skills.name: minimap2-reference-alignment
skills.search_text: minimap2-reference-alignment Use when assembler-generated contigs must be mapped to known reference replicons (multi-FASTA passed via --reference) to compute reference-based assembly quality metrics like LSA. No reference replicon sequences are available — reference-free/global contig metrics should be used instead Input is raw reads rather than assembler-generated contigs — this skill aligns FS contigs only Contigs shorter than the --minLength threshold (default 1000 bp) — they are excluded before alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Align BBTools-filtered (FS) assembler contigs against reference replicons with minimap2 (v2.22) to produce per-sample PAF alignments that underpin LMAS reference-dependent metrics such as the LSA (longest single alignment) fraction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Align BBTools-filtered (FS) assembler contigs against reference replicons with minimap2 (v2.22) to produce per-sample PAF alignments that underpin LMAS reference-dependent metrics such as the LSA (longest single alignment) fraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference replicon sequences are available — reference-free/global contig metrics should be used instead Input is raw reads rather than assembler-generated contigs — this skill aligns FS contigs only Contigs shorter than the --minLength threshold (default 1000 bp) — they are excluded before alignment

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic classifier must query each query-sequence k-mer against a large exact-match k-mer database (Jellyfish count spaces storing LCA taxon IDs) and per-k-mer alignment is too slow.
skills.name: minimizer-index-database-query
skills.search_text: minimizer-index-database-query Use when a metagenomic classifier must query each query-sequence k-mer against a large exact-match k-mer database (Jellyfish count spaces storing LCA taxon IDs) and per-k-mer alignment is too slow. When inexact/alignments-based similarity is required — Kraken's speed derives from exact-match database queries of k-mers rather than inexact alignment When query k-mers contain ambiguous nucleotides — Kraken ignores these k-mers, so they cannot be resolved by this query path When a sequence has no k-mers present in the database — it will simply be left unclassified rather than classified by homology http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A method for rapidly resolving exact k-mer lookups in a Kraken-style database by grouping k-mers under their minimizer, storing them consecutively sorted by canonical representation, and answering each query with an index lookup followed by a binary search to recover the k-mer's LCA taxon ID. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: A method for rapidly resolving exact k-mer lookups in a Kraken-style database by grouping k-mers under their minimizer, storing them consecutively sorted by canonical representation, and answering each query with an index lookup followed by a binary search to recover the k-mer's LCA taxon ID.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When inexact/alignments-based similarity is required — Kraken's speed derives from exact-match database queries of k-mers rather than inexact alignment When query k-mers contain ambiguous nucleotides — Kraken ignores these k-mers, so they cannot be resolved by this query path When a sequence has no k-mers present in the database — it will simply be left unclassified rather than classified by homology

skills.description: Use when implementing or reconstructing an exact k-mer lookup database (e.g., k-mer→LCA taxon maps) that must support fast per-k-mer queries without alignment, via minimizer grouping and indexed binary search.
skills.name: minimizer-partitioned-database-indexing
skills.search_text: minimizer-partitioned-database-indexing Use when implementing or reconstructing an exact k-mer lookup database (e.g., k-mer→LCA taxon maps) that must support fast per-k-mer queries without alignment, via minimizer grouping and indexed binary search. The task requires inexact alignment or sensitivity to mutations/indels rather than exact k-mer matches (Kraken's speed derives from exact-match database queries, not alignment). Query k-mers contain ambiguous nucleotides — Kraken ignores k-mers with ambiguous nucleotides, so they yield no lookup. A ranked/quantitative abundance estimate is needed from only a small fraction of reads; this scheme classifies every read via k-mer LCA voting rather than estimating abundance. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A database layout and lookup scheme (used by Kraken) that partitions k-mer/LCA records by their minimizer, stores each minimizer group consecutively sorted by canonical representation, and answers exact k-mer queries via a fixed-size minimizer index plus binary search within the group range. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: A database layout and lookup scheme (used by Kraken) that partitions k-mer/LCA records by their minimizer, stores each minimizer group consecutively sorted by canonical representation, and answers exact k-mer queries via a fixed-size minimizer index plus binary search within the group range.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires inexact alignment or sensitivity to mutations/indels rather than exact k-mer matches (Kraken's speed derives from exact-match database queries, not alignment). Query k-mers contain ambiguous nucleotides — Kraken ignores k-mers with ambiguous nucleotides, so they yield no lookup. A ranked/quantitative abundance estimate is needed from only a small fraction of reads; this scheme classifies every read via k-mer LCA voting rather than estimating abundance.

skills.description: Use when you have freebayes VCFs from wastewater NGS samples mapped to SARS-CoV-2 NC_045512 and need to reproduce or recompute lineage-specific AF statistics such as the non-zero minimum AF of B.1.1.7-unique mutations.
skills.name: minimum-allele-frequency-computation
skills.search_text: minimum-allele-frequency-computation Use when you have freebayes VCFs from wastewater NGS samples mapped to SARS-CoV-2 NC_045512 and need to reproduce or recompute lineage-specific AF statistics such as the non-zero minimum AF of B.1.1.7-unique mutations. Samples lacking freebayes VCF calls (e.g., if another caller such as mpileup or GATK Mutect2 was used, AF values may not reproduce the reported Table 5 statistics) Samples for which primer trimming and remapping were skipped (e.g., the four samples between 19 March and 15 April 2021), making AF comparability questionable http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Recomputes the reported per-period allele frequency statistics for B.1.1.7 (Alpha)-unique mutations in Thessaloniki wastewater samples by extracting allele frequencies from freebayes VCFs and taking the non-zero minimum (e.g., 16.67% for 5–11 Feb 2021; 76.71% for 5–11 Mar 2021). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: Recomputes the reported per-period allele frequency statistics for B.1.1.7 (Alpha)-unique mutations in Thessaloniki wastewater samples by extracting allele frequencies from freebayes VCFs and taking the non-zero minimum (e.g., 16.67% for 5–11 Feb 2021; 76.71% for 5–11 Mar 2021).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lacking freebayes VCF calls (e.g., if another caller such as mpileup or GATK Mutect2 was used, AF values may not reproduce the reported Table 5 statistics) Samples for which primer trimming and remapping were skipped (e.g., the four samples between 19 March and 15 April 2021), making AF comparability questionable

skills.description: Use when combining multiple studies across multiple related markers (e.g., 6 α-diversity indices) from summary statistics only (effect estimates and standard errors) and an omnibus hypothesis test is needed without a priori marker-by-marker correlations.
skills.name: minimum-p-value-statistic-testing
skills.search_text: minimum-p-value-statistic-testing Use when combining multiple studies across multiple related markers (e.g., 6 α-diversity indices) from summary statistics only (effect estimates and standard errors) and an omnibus hypothesis test is needed without a priori marker-by-marker correlations. When pooled effect estimates (not just hypothesis testing) across markers are needed — aMeta is limited to hypothesis testing; use mMeta instead When fewer than 10 studies per marker are available — the mMeta.aMeta function requires the number of studies to be ≥ 10 When marker-by-marker correlations are already known and a multivariate method exploiting them directly is preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Implements the adaptive multi-marker meta-analysis (aMeta) test statistic, formed as the minimum p-value across Q marker-specific random effects meta-analyses, with its null distribution generated by the Follmann–Proschan group permutation method without prior marker-by-marker correlations. metagenomics/v1 10.1002/sim.8940
skills.summary: Implements the adaptive multi-marker meta-analysis (aMeta) test statistic, formed as the minimum p-value across Q marker-specific random effects meta-analyses, with its null distribution generated by the Follmann–Proschan group permutation method without prior marker-by-marker correlations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When pooled effect estimates (not just hypothesis testing) across markers are needed — aMeta is limited to hypothesis testing; use mMeta instead When fewer than 10 studies per marker are available — the mMeta.aMeta function requires the number of studies to be ≥ 10 When marker-by-marker correlations are already known and a multivariate method exploiting them directly is preferred

skills.description: Use when combining multiple studies (≥10) across multiple related markers (e.g., six α-diversity indices) from summary statistics alone, with no prior marker-by-marker correlations, and the goal is a single omnibus hypothesis test rather than a pooled effect estimate.
skills.name: minimum-pvalue-adaptive-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: minimum-pvalue-adaptive-hypothesis-testing Use when combining multiple studies (≥10) across multiple related markers (e.g., six α-diversity indices) from summary statistics alone, with no prior marker-by-marker correlations, and the goal is a single omnibus hypothesis test rather than a pooled effect estimate. You need a pooled effect estimate with 95% CI across all markers — use mMeta's weighted pooling instead, since aMeta is limited to hypothesis testing Fewer than 10 studies: the package requires ≥10 studies for mMeta.aMeta, and with <15 studies all possible permutations run and n.perm/seed are ignored Only raw sequence data are available and effect estimates/standard errors have not been derived (the article notes these summary statistics are hard to obtain in practice) http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 aMeta (adaptive multi-marker meta-analysis) tests the overall null hypothesis across multiple related markers using only study-specific effect estimates and standard errors, via the minimum p-value among marker-specific random-effects meta-analyses calibrated by sign-flipping group permutation; it delivers near-maximal power for hypothesis testing but yields no pooled effect estimate. metagenomics/v1 10.1002/sim.8940
skills.summary: aMeta (adaptive multi-marker meta-analysis) tests the overall null hypothesis across multiple related markers using only study-specific effect estimates and standard errors, via the minimum p-value among marker-specific random-effects meta-analyses calibrated by sign-flipping group permutation; it delivers near-maximal power for hypothesis testing but yields no pooled effect estimate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a pooled effect estimate with 95% CI across all markers — use mMeta's weighted pooling instead, since aMeta is limited to hypothesis testing Fewer than 10 studies: the package requires ≥10 studies for mMeta.aMeta, and with <15 studies all possible permutations run and n.perm/seed are ignored Only raw sequence data are available and effect estimates/standard errors have not been derived (the article notes these summary statistics are hard to obtain in practice)

skills.description: Use when input is Illumina FASTQ from samples suspected of containing low-frequency resistant alleles (mixed infections, heteroresistance, XDR-TB second-line drug testing) and Mykrobe predictor's major-clone calls alone miss resistance.
skills.name: minor-allele-variant-detection
skills.search_text: minor-allele-variant-detection Use when input is Illumina FASTQ from samples suspected of containing low-frequency resistant alleles (mixed infections, heteroresistance, XDR-TB second-line drug testing) and Mykrobe predictor's major-clone calls alone miss resistance. The sample is a clean single-clone isolate with no suspected minority resistant population — minor-allele mode is unnecessary and the extra threshold may reduce specificity Mycobacterial samples direct from sputum needing a general mixture model — the current implementation models only major/minor clones Drugs whose known resistance mutations are poorly predictive (e.g. pyrazinamide), which Mykrobe completely excludes from prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_0798 Enables Mykrobe predictor to call resistance-determining variants present only as low-frequency (minor) alleles in mixed populations, using a single 10% allele-frequency threshold to boost sensitivity for second-line drug resistance (e.g. capreomycin, amikacin, ofloxacin) in M. tuberculosis and to detect minority resistant populations in simulated S. aureus/CoNS mixtures. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Enables Mykrobe predictor to call resistance-determining variants present only as low-frequency (minor) alleles in mixed populations, using a single 10% allele-frequency threshold to boost sensitivity for second-line drug resistance (e.g. capreomycin, amikacin, ofloxacin) in M. tuberculosis and to detect minority resistant populations in simulated S. aureus/CoNS mixtures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is a clean single-clone isolate with no suspected minority resistant population — minor-allele mode is unnecessary and the extra threshold may reduce specificity Mycobacterial samples direct from sputum needing a general mixture model — the current implementation models only major/minor clones Drugs whose known resistance mutations are poorly predictive (e.g. pyrazinamide), which Mykrobe completely excludes from prediction

skills.description: Use when you have a KO (KEGG Orthology) abundance table from 16S-based functional prediction and need MetaCyc pathway presence/abundance inferred by minimum-parsimony reconstruction.
skills.name: minpath-pathway-reconstruction
skills.search_text: minpath-pathway-reconstruction Use when you have a KO (KEGG Orthology) abundance table from 16S-based functional prediction and need MetaCyc pathway presence/abundance inferred by minimum-parsimony reconstruction. Input is already a pathway abundance table or another functional profile (e.g. pre-computed from Piphillin, PanFP, Tax4Fun, or Tax4Fun2) rather than KO-level abundances requiring parsimony-based pathway reconstruction. Input sequences have not been processed through the upstream PICRUSt2 functional-prediction steps (e.g. DADA2-corrected 16S rDNA sequences and KO prediction), so no KO abundance table exists yet. You need habitat-specific or pangenome-based functional profiles rather than pathway-level reconstruction over KEGG/MetaCyc databases. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Run MinPath minimum-parsimony pathway inference, as bundled within the PICRUSt2 repository (GPL-licensed source), to map KO abundance tables onto MetaCyc/KEGG pathway abundances and write the reconstructed pathway table. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-0548-6
skills.summary: Run MinPath minimum-parsimony pathway inference, as bundled within the PICRUSt2 repository (GPL-licensed source), to map KO abundance tables onto MetaCyc/KEGG pathway abundances and write the reconstructed pathway table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pathway abundance table or another functional profile (e.g. pre-computed from Piphillin, PanFP, Tax4Fun, or Tax4Fun2) rather than KO-level abundances requiring parsimony-based pathway reconstruction. Input sequences have not been processed through the upstream PICRUSt2 functional-prediction steps (e.g. DADA2-corrected 16S rDNA sequences and KO prediction), so no KO abundance table exists yet. You need habitat-specific or pangenome-based functional profiles rather than pathway-level reconstruction over KEGG/MetaCyc databases.

skills.description: Use when you have multiple FASTA assemblies of a model organism plus a reference genome (e.g. NC_000913.3) and read pairs, and you need to count extensive misassemblies, genome fraction, duplication ratio, NGA50, and mismatches/indels per 100 kb.
skills.name: misassembly-detection-from-alignment-breakpoints
skills.search_text: misassembly-detection-from-alignment-breakpoints Use when you have multiple FASTA assemblies of a model organism plus a reference genome (e.g. NC_000913.3) and read pairs, and you need to count extensive misassemblies, genome fraction, duplication ratio, NGA50, and mismatches/indels per 100 kb. No reference genome (true or close substrain) is available for the organism — use QUAST's reference-free metrics (30 contiguity/completeness metrics) instead of misassembly detection Assemblies are of a metagenomic dataset — use MetaQUAST rather than single-reference misassembly evaluation The genome is very large (e.g. mammalian) — QUAST-LG is the intended extension rather than standard QUAST reference-based evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Detects large structural misassemblies (relocations, translocations, inversions) and per-base errors in genome assemblies by aligning contigs against a true or close reference genome with QUAST, optionally using read-pair SV detection for more precise breakpoints. Grounded in the WebQUAST/QUAST Use Case 2 evaluation of four E. coli K-12 MG1655 assemblies. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad406
skills.summary: Detects large structural misassemblies (relocations, translocations, inversions) and per-base errors in genome assemblies by aligning contigs against a true or close reference genome with QUAST, optionally using read-pair SV detection for more precise breakpoints. Grounded in the WebQUAST/QUAST Use Case 2 evaluation of four E. coli K-12 MG1655 assemblies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome (true or close substrain) is available for the organism — use QUAST's reference-free metrics (30 contiguity/completeness metrics) instead of misassembly detection Assemblies are of a metagenomic dataset — use MetaQUAST rather than single-reference misassembly evaluation The genome is very large (e.g. mammalian) — QUAST-LG is the intended extension rather than standard QUAST reference-based evaluation

skills.description: Use when validating that a metagenomic assembler's scaffold corresponds to a specific reference genome (e.g. B. longum 51A scaffold2094 in gut sample V06-T-0501-S07) and you need to quantify edge misassembly and fragmentation per assembler.
skills.name: misassembly-edge-error-quantification
skills.search_text: misassembly-edge-error-quantification Use when validating that a metagenomic assembler's scaffold corresponds to a specific reference genome (e.g. B. longum 51A scaffold2094 in gut sample V06-T-0501-S07) and you need to quantify edge misassembly and fragmentation per assembler. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than assembled scaffolds — use a read-mapping preset (map-ont) not the asm-to-asm workflow Reference-based evaluation is out of scope and only de novo assembly quality assessment is needed (the article notes reference information 'has not been well examined' in its own benchmarks) Aligning sequences between divergent species (>~15% divergence), where asm5 intra-species assumptions no longer hold per the Minimap2 README http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quantifies residual assembly error at scaffold termini by aligning extracted scaffolds to a complete reference genome with Minimap2 (asm5 preset) and computing the minor 1k-mer rate within 1 kb of each scaffold edge, complemented by CheckM completeness/contamination estimates, to confirm whether an assembler produced a single near-complete, structurally correct genome scaffold versus fragmented, misjoined assemblies. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Quantifies residual assembly error at scaffold termini by aligning extracted scaffolds to a complete reference genome with Minimap2 (asm5 preset) and computing the minor 1k-mer rate within 1 kb of each scaffold edge, complemented by CheckM completeness/contamination estimates, to confirm whether an assembler produced a single near-complete, structurally correct genome scaffold versus fragmented, misjoined assemblies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than assembled scaffolds — use a read-mapping preset (map-ont) not the asm-to-asm workflow Reference-based evaluation is out of scope and only de novo assembly quality assessment is needed (the article notes reference information 'has not been well examined' in its own benchmarks) Aligning sequences between divergent species (>~15% divergence), where asm5 intra-species assumptions no longer hold per the Minimap2 README

skills.description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic classifiers for false-positive behavior on reads whose true source species is missing from every tool's reference database (e.g. AQ<60%, ANI<95% novelty cutoffs).
skills.name: misclassification-count-quantification
skills.search_text: misclassification-count-quantification Use when benchmarking taxonomic classifiers for false-positive behavior on reads whose true source species is missing from every tool's reference database (e.g. AQ<60%, ANI<95% novelty cutoffs). The true source species IS present in the tools' reference databases — use a precision/recall benchmark on training-excluded genomes (e.g. the 3,269 MAGs) instead The goal is genus-level or abundance-estimation comparison rather than species-level false-positive counting Input data are real metagenomes (e.g. the IBD/iHMP dataset) where ground-truth species labels per read are unavailable http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies false positives of taxonomic classifiers on reads simulated from species absent from all reference databases, tallying misclassified reads and misidentified species per tool. It isolates database-independence of error rates, as in the DeepMicrobes Figure 4 benchmark. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Quantifies false positives of taxonomic classifiers on reads simulated from species absent from all reference databases, tallying misclassified reads and misidentified species per tool. It isolates database-independence of error rates, as in the DeepMicrobes Figure 4 benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The true source species IS present in the tools' reference databases — use a precision/recall benchmark on training-excluded genomes (e.g. the 3,269 MAGs) instead The goal is genus-level or abundance-estimation comparison rather than species-level false-positive counting Input data are real metagenomes (e.g. the IBD/iHMP dataset) where ground-truth species labels per read are unavailable

skills.description: Use when the summary-statistics table has missing study-by-marker entries so the number of studies (Kj) varies by marker, and you need pooled estimates plus mMeta/aMeta p-values using all available data.
skills.name: missing-summary-data-handling
skills.search_text: missing-summary-data-handling Use when the summary-statistics table has missing study-by-marker entries so the number of studies (Kj) varies by marker, and you need pooled estimates plus mMeta/aMeta p-values using all available data. The input is raw sequencing data (e.g., paired-end Illumina reads or OTU tables) rather than per-study, per-marker summary statistics (effect estimates and standard errors) Fewer than 10 studies are available, since mMeta.aMeta requires the number of rows (studies) to be >= 10 NA positions differ between 'est' and 'std.err' (locations of NAs must be matched), or a single-marker conventional meta-analysis is the actual goal rather than combining multiple related markers http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Implements the mMeta and aMeta multi-marker meta-analysis functions on unbalanced summary-statistic tables (study-by-marker regression coefficient estimates 'est' and standard errors 'std.err') in which selected entries are set to NA, exploiting the methods' design to robustly handle missing summary data across studies and markers. metagenomics/v1 10.1002/sim.8940
skills.summary: Implements the mMeta and aMeta multi-marker meta-analysis functions on unbalanced summary-statistic tables (study-by-marker regression coefficient estimates 'est' and standard errors 'std.err') in which selected entries are set to NA, exploiting the methods' design to robustly handle missing summary data across studies and markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw sequencing data (e.g., paired-end Illumina reads or OTU tables) rather than per-study, per-marker summary statistics (effect estimates and standard errors) Fewer than 10 studies are available, since mMeta.aMeta requires the number of rows (studies) to be >= 10 NA positions differ between 'est' and 'std.err' (locations of NAs must be matched), or a single-marker conventional meta-analysis is the actual goal rather than combining multiple related markers

skills.description: Use when you need to transfer an existing linear-reference annotation (e.g., a GTF of mitochondrial gene coordinates) onto a graph pangenome and confirm each gene region resolves uniquely in graph coordinates.
skills.name: mitochondrial-genome-annotation-verification
skills.search_text: mitochondrial-genome-annotation-verification Use when you need to transfer an existing linear-reference annotation (e.g., a GTF of mitochondrial gene coordinates) onto a graph pangenome and confirm each gene region resolves uniquely in graph coordinates. Gene elements shorter than k (= 22), which may map to multiple nodes on the graph, making the analysis complicated and ambiguous Graphs where sequence similarity is insufficient (source number far less than variant number), where the variant/coordinate model is not applicable Highly repetitive sequences (especially tandem repeats), where the cutting method fragments the sequence too much, increasing computational difficulty and error http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Project linear-reference mitochondrial gene annotations (GTF) onto a colored de Bruijn graph pangenome via the paper's tri-tuple coordinate system (position, bubid, basecolor), verifying that existing reference coordinates remain accommodated on the graph. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04149-w
skills.summary: Project linear-reference mitochondrial gene annotations (GTF) onto a colored de Bruijn graph pangenome via the paper's tri-tuple coordinate system (position, bubid, basecolor), verifying that existing reference coordinates remain accommodated on the graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene elements shorter than k (= 22), which may map to multiple nodes on the graph, making the analysis complicated and ambiguous Graphs where sequence similarity is insufficient (source number far less than variant number), where the variant/coordinate model is not applicable Highly repetitive sequences (especially tandem repeats), where the cutting method fragments the sequence too much, increasing computational difficulty and error

skills.search_text: mitogenome-panel-simulation Use when you need simulated human mitogenome FASTA panels with known SNP/indel ground truth to benchmark graph-based variant detection (precision/recall) or to measure wall-clock time and memory scaling of VARI-merge + cSupB pipelines. skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences with insufficient similarity (source number far less than variant number) — the variant detection model the simulations benchmark is not applicable in that regime Studies targeting large indels, inversions, or reverse tandem duplications — cSupB variant detection only addresses small indels (< 50 bp) Highly repetitive sequences, especially tandem repeats — the cutting method fragments them, increasing computational difficulty and error

skills.description: Use when you have run (or plan to run) MAGinator on shotgun metagenomics data with VAMB MAG clusters and need to quantify within-cluster strain mixtures — i.e. which samples/MAG clusters carry more than one variant of a MAG.
skills.name: mixed-allele-frequency-statistics
skills.search_text: mixed-allele-frequency-statistics Use when you have run (or plan to run) MAGinator on shotgun metagenomics data with VAMB MAG clusters and need to quantify within-cluster strain mixtures — i.e. which samples/MAG clusters carry more than one variant of a MAG. The goal is species-level taxonomic profiling or abundance estimation only, not strain-level within-cluster variant diversity Samples fail the --min_mapped_signature_genes detection threshold, so their SNV statistics cannot be included in the phylogenetic/mixed-allele analysis No MAG clusters exist (e.g. input is only a marker-gene profile from MetaPhlAn/mOTUs) — there are no signature genes to collect SNV information from http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Identify MAG clusters harbouring multiple intra-cluster variants ('mixed alleles') by parsing MAGinator's per-sample SNV statistics (phylo/stats.tab, phylo/pileup) and classifying clusters whose signature or marker genes show multiple alleles above the allele frequency cutoff in at least one sample. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8
skills.summary: Identify MAG clusters harbouring multiple intra-cluster variants ('mixed alleles') by parsing MAGinator's per-sample SNV statistics (phylo/stats.tab, phylo/pileup) and classifying clusters whose signature or marker genes show multiple alleles above the allele frequency cutoff in at least one sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is species-level taxonomic profiling or abundance estimation only, not strain-level within-cluster variant diversity Samples fail the --min_mapped_signature_genes detection threshold, so their SNV statistics cannot be included in the phylogenetic/mixed-allele analysis No MAG clusters exist (e.g. input is only a marker-gene profile from MetaPhlAn/mOTUs) — there are no signature genes to collect SNV information from

skills.description: Use when you have a feature-abundance matrix (e.g. fungal species from shotgun metagenomes) plus sample metadata and need significant taxon–metadata associations while controlling for repeated or nuisance covariates like age.
skills.name: mixed-effects-microbiome-statistics
skills.search_text: mixed-effects-microbiome-statistics Use when you have a feature-abundance matrix (e.g. fungal species from shotgun metagenomes) plus sample metadata and need significant taxon–metadata associations while controlling for repeated or nuisance covariates like age. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than a per-sample abundance/feature table — profile reads with FunOMIC first The question is co-occurrence/inter-kingdom correlation structure, which this paper addressed with correlation network analysis (p < 0.001, |r| > 0.05) instead of fixed-effect association testing Sample size or metadata design cannot support a multivariable mixed-effects model with age as a random effect http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Run multivariable linear association testing (MaAsLin2 in R 4.1.2) between fungal taxonomic/functional abundance features (from FunOMIC-T/FunOMIC-P profiling) and clinical/demographic metadata, with age as a random effect and FDR < 0.05 significance filtering. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Run multivariable linear association testing (MaAsLin2 in R 4.1.2) between fungal taxonomic/functional abundance features (from FunOMIC-T/FunOMIC-P profiling) and clinical/demographic metadata, with age as a random effect and FDR < 0.05 significance filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than a per-sample abundance/feature table — profile reads with FunOMIC first The question is co-occurrence/inter-kingdom correlation structure, which this paper addressed with correlation network analysis (p < 0.001, |r| > 0.05) instead of fixed-effect association testing Sample size or metadata design cannot support a multivariable mixed-effects model with age as a random effect

skills.description: Use when assigning strain types to samples from per-locus allele sets and proportions (geneX_proportions.csv) against a known MLST strain database, and novel-strain detection under proportion constraints is required.
skills.name: mixed-integer-linear-program-formulation
skills.search_text: mixed-integer-linear-program-formulation Use when assigning strain types to samples from per-locus allele sets and proportions (geneX_proportions.csv) against a known MLST strain database, and novel-strain detection under proportion constraints is required. The first-stage ADP has not been run and no per-locus allele sets/proportions exist for the samples The organism has no curated MLST strain-type database, so no known strains Ω or edit-distance weighting can be defined Only fractional allele composition per locus is needed — solving the Allele Diversity Problem ILP (first stage) is the appropriate formulation instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Formulates and solves the Strain Diversity Problem (and Allele Diversity Problem) as a mixed integer linear program that associates each Borrelia burgdorferi MLST sample with a minimal set of strain types, penalizing novel strains by edit distance to known strains while bounding deviations from the observed allele proportions. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
