skills.description: Use when WGS reads from heterogeneous samples must be decomposed into known MLST strain types plus novel strains, given a reference allele database (e.g. 8 housekeeping genes, 1726 alleles, 753 strain types) and mixed samples where strain proportions vary.
skills.name: mixed-integer-linear-programming-strain-deconvolution
skills.search_text: mixed-integer-linear-programming-strain-deconvolution Use when WGS reads from heterogeneous samples must be decomposed into known MLST strain types plus novel strains, given a reference allele database (e.g. 8 housekeeping genes, 1726 alleles, 753 strain types) and mixed samples where strain proportions vary. When reference genomes or strain types are unknown — de novo methods such as DESMAN are the appropriate choice since this pipeline relies on a known MLST allele/strain database When samples are single-strain (no within-host heterogeneity), where the two-stage deconvolution adds unnecessary complexity When exact strain-level precision is the sole requirement even from imperfect allele calls: the paper's Table 2 shows full-pipeline SDP exact precision/recall drops to ~0.3-0.5 versus ~0.8 with perfect allele input http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A two-stage MILP pipeline that deconvolves within-host pathogen strain mixtures from WGS reads in the B. burgdorferi MLST framework: an Allele Diversity Problem (ADP) ILP infers per-locus allele sets and proportions, and a Strain Diversity Problem (SDP) MILP jointly infers strain types across samples, including novel strains. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: A two-stage MILP pipeline that deconvolves within-host pathogen strain mixtures from WGS reads in the B. burgdorferi MLST framework: an Allele Diversity Problem (ADP) ILP infers per-locus allele sets and proportions, and a Strain Diversity Problem (SDP) MILP jointly infers strain types across samples, including novel strains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reference genomes or strain types are unknown — de novo methods such as DESMAN are the appropriate choice since this pipeline relies on a known MLST allele/strain database When samples are single-strain (no within-host heterogeneity), where the two-stage deconvolution adds unnecessary complexity When exact strain-level precision is the sole requirement even from imperfect allele calls: the paper's Table 2 shows full-pipeline SDP exact precision/recall drops to ~0.3-0.5 versus ~0.8 with perfect allele input

skills.description: Use when an ILP/MILP (e.g. the Allele Diversity Problem solved with CPLEX) returns multiple optimal solutions and you must (a) pick one biologically plausible solution and (b) derive fractional allele abundances from the selected solution.
skills.name: mixed-integer-program-solution-post-processing
skills.search_text: mixed-integer-program-solution-post-processing Use when an ILP/MILP (e.g. the Allele Diversity Problem solved with CPLEX) returns multiple optimal solutions and you must (a) pick one biologically plausible solution and (b) derive fractional allele abundances from the selected solution. The ILP has a unique optimal solution — GAML-based tie-breaking is unnecessary and proportions can be computed directly from that solution The downstream goal is the Stage-2 Strain Diversity Problem rather than per-locus allele calling; that stage is solved by a separate MILP (globalStrainDiversity.py) Input data are de novo assemblies without a reference allele database — this post-processing relies on known MLST alleles and read-allele mapping scores Resolves the degeneracy of a 0-1 ILP solution by selecting a single optimal solution with the likelihood-based assembler GAML, then converts the selected allele set into per-locus allele proportions by weighting reads across the h alleles attaining the chosen optimal mapping score. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Resolves the degeneracy of a 0-1 ILP solution by selecting a single optimal solution with the likelihood-based assembler GAML, then converts the selected allele set into per-locus allele proportions by weighting reads across the h alleles attaining the chosen optimal mapping score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ILP has a unique optimal solution — GAML-based tie-breaking is unnecessary and proportions can be computed directly from that solution The downstream goal is the Stage-2 Strain Diversity Problem rather than per-locus allele calling; that stage is solved by a separate MILP (globalStrainDiversity.py) Input data are de novo assemblies without a reference allele database — this post-processing relies on known MLST alleles and read-allele mapping scores

skills.description: Use when calling resistance in M. tuberculosis samples with minor resistant allele populations, especially for capreomycin, amikacin or ofloxacin where major-clone-only calls miss phenotypic resistance.
skills.name: mixed-sample-heteroresistance-interpretation
skills.search_text: mixed-sample-heteroresistance-interpretation Use when calling resistance in M. tuberculosis samples with minor resistant allele populations, especially for capreomycin, amikacin or ofloxacin where major-clone-only calls miss phenotypic resistance. The sample is a first-line drug call (e.g. pyrazinamide), which is excluded because known mutations are poorly predictive The data set is large enough to estimate per-drug allele-frequency thresholds — a uniform 10% threshold is a compromise forced by limited M. tuberculosis training data The goal is direct-from-sputum analysis requiring a general mixture model; the current implementation models only major/minor clones http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Interprets Mykrobe predictor resistance calls in Mycobacterium tuberculosis samples where minor (low-frequency) resistant alleles indicate mixed populations or heteroresistance, which improves detection of extremely drug-resistant (XDR) strains for second-line drugs. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Interprets Mykrobe predictor resistance calls in Mycobacterium tuberculosis samples where minor (low-frequency) resistant alleles indicate mixed populations or heteroresistance, which improves detection of extremely drug-resistant (XDR) strains for second-line drugs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is a first-line drug call (e.g. pyrazinamide), which is excluded because known mutations are poorly predictive The data set is large enough to estimate per-drug allele-frequency thresholds — a uniform 10% threshold is a compromise forced by limited M. tuberculosis training data The goal is direct-from-sputum analysis requiring a general mixture model; the current implementation models only major/minor clones

skills.description: Use when simulated sinks with known ground-truth source mixing proportions and unknown-source contributions (0–90%) are available and you must compare source tracking methods on estimation accuracy.
skills.name: mixing-proportion-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: mixing-proportion-accuracy-evaluation Use when simulated sinks with known ground-truth source mixing proportions and unknown-source contributions (0–90%) are available and you must compare source tracking methods on estimation accuracy. When sinks have no known ground-truth composition (real-world sinks), since MSE/FPR/unknown-error metrics require simulated truth When the goal is only to estimate contributions for a small pre-defined source set without nuisance candidates — the skill's value comes from many candidate sources (M=50) with K=10 true contributors http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A benchmarking skill that quantifies how accurately microbial source tracking methods (STENSL, FEAST, SourceTracker2, RAD) estimate source mixing proportions, using MSE of estimated proportions, false positive rate of identified contributing sources, and absolute error of the estimated unknown contribution on simulated sinks built from EMP samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00995-21
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that quantifies how accurately microbial source tracking methods (STENSL, FEAST, SourceTracker2, RAD) estimate source mixing proportions, using MSE of estimated proportions, false positive rate of identified contributing sources, and absolute error of the estimated unknown contribution on simulated sinks built from EMP samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When sinks have no known ground-truth composition (real-world sinks), since MSE/FPR/unknown-error metrics require simulated truth When the goal is only to estimate contributions for a small pre-defined source set without nuisance candidates — the skill's value comes from many candidate sources (M=50) with K=10 true contributors

skills.description: Use when you have a microbiome feature table with a binary grouping outcome and need to quantify overall association strength and discovery robustness by tracking significant-feature counts across progressive permutation mixing proportions (U-curve).
skills.name: mixing-proportion-scaling-analysis
skills.search_text: mixing-proportion-scaling-analysis Use when you have a microbiome feature table with a binary grouping outcome and need to quantify overall association strength and discovery robustness by tracking significant-feature counts across progressive permutation mixing proportions (U-curve). You need FDR-controlled or adjusted p-values / formal inferential guarantees — the paper states the method does not control the false discovery rate and that AOI/AUMC measures are descriptive only The grouping outcome is not binary (the bin_* workflow, e.g., bin_permute_all with a 'variable' binary outcome, is built for two-group comparisons) top_pm would be greater than or equal to the number of microbial features — the README requires top_pm to be less than the feature count http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Progressive-permutation analysis that plots the number (and, scaled by sample size, the proportion) of significant differential features against the proportion of mixing of grouping labels, producing a U-curve whose depth conveys the strength of the microbiome–grouping-factor association. P-values default to the Wilcoxon rank sum test but can be swapped for DESeq2. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04061-3
skills.summary: Progressive-permutation analysis that plots the number (and, scaled by sample size, the proportion) of significant differential features against the proportion of mixing of grouping labels, producing a U-curve whose depth conveys the strength of the microbiome–grouping-factor association. P-values default to the Wilcoxon rank sum test but can be swapped for DESeq2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need FDR-controlled or adjusted p-values / formal inferential guarantees — the paper states the method does not control the false discovery rate and that AOI/AUMC measures are descriptive only The grouping outcome is not binary (the bin_* workflow, e.g., bin_permute_all with a 'variable' binary outcome, is built for two-group comparisons) top_pm would be greater than or equal to the number of microbial features — the README requires top_pm to be less than the feature count

skills.description: Use when you have unfolded site frequency spectrum (DAF) data plus divergence counts for neutral (4-fold/0) and selected (0-fold/i) classes per gene and need to estimate α, or to compare α of a user-selected gene set (e.g. high-recombination bins) against the genome-wide distribution.
skills.name: mkt-based-adaptive-evolution-estimation
skills.search_text: mkt-based-adaptive-evolution-estimation Use when you have unfolded site frequency spectrum (DAF) data plus divergence counts for neutral (4-fold/0) and selected (0-fold/i) classes per gene and need to estimate α, or to compare α of a user-selected gene set (e.g. high-recombination bins) against the genome-wide distribution. Input data are raw VCF/FASTA rather than the iMKTData-derived DAF and divergence count tables — first run the iMKTData python/bash pipelines to unfold the site frequency spectrum Your question requires inferring selection on non-coding or non-protein-coding sequence, whereas iMKT targets protein-coding DNA (0-fold/4-fold functional classes) You need per-variant selective inference rather than gene/gene-set level α estimates; the MKT framework outputs aggregate selection regime fractions (α, b, d, f) per unit http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Estimates adaptive evolution (α) and other selection regimes using the McDonald and Kreitman test family (standard MKT, FWWMKT, eMKT, aMKT) on polymorphism and divergence data, e.g. via the iMKT R package or web service on PopFly/PopHuman-derived DAF and divergence tables. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkz372
skills.summary: Estimates adaptive evolution (α) and other selection regimes using the McDonald and Kreitman test family (standard MKT, FWWMKT, eMKT, aMKT) on polymorphism and divergence data, e.g. via the iMKT R package or web service on PopFly/PopHuman-derived DAF and divergence tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are raw VCF/FASTA rather than the iMKTData-derived DAF and divergence count tables — first run the iMKTData python/bash pipelines to unfold the site frequency spectrum Your question requires inferring selection on non-coding or non-protein-coding sequence, whereas iMKT targets protein-coding DNA (0-fold/4-fold functional classes) You need per-variant selective inference rather than gene/gene-set level α estimates; the MKT framework outputs aggregate selection regime fractions (α, b, d, f) per unit

skills.description: Use when a user-selected set of protein-coding genes (e.g. selected by recombination rate bins or chromosome localization) must be analyzed jointly for a single selective regime rather than gene-by-gene, and per-gene MKT count tables are available.
skills.name: mkt-count-table-concatenation
skills.search_text: mkt-count-table-concatenation Use when a user-selected set of protein-coding genes (e.g. selected by recombination rate bins or chromosome localization) must be analyzed jointly for a single selective regime rather than gene-by-gene, and per-gene MKT count tables are available. The goal is gene-by-gene selective regime estimates rather than a regime for the whole gene set — concatenate mode analyzes the set jointly, not individual genes The per-gene MKT count tables (Dn, Ds, Pn, Ps) have not yet been extracted; run the iMKTData pipeline (e.g. dmelProteins.ipynb) first The data are human (1000GP/PopHuman VCF) and the CMH/bootstrap concatenated workflow has only been documented for the D. melanogaster DGN/PopFly protein-coding example http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Concatenates per-gene MKT divergence/polymorphism count tables (Dn, Ds, Pn, Ps) into a single multi-gene contingency table and statistically assesses heterogeneity of selection among genes using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test plus a bootstrap 95% CI for alpha, as implemented in iMKT's 'Concatenate genes' mode. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkz372
skills.summary: Concatenates per-gene MKT divergence/polymorphism count tables (Dn, Ds, Pn, Ps) into a single multi-gene contingency table and statistically assesses heterogeneity of selection among genes using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test plus a bootstrap 95% CI for alpha, as implemented in iMKT's 'Concatenate genes' mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene-by-gene selective regime estimates rather than a regime for the whole gene set — concatenate mode analyzes the set jointly, not individual genes The per-gene MKT count tables (Dn, Ds, Pn, Ps) have not yet been extracted; run the iMKTData pipeline (e.g. dmelProteins.ipynb) first The data are human (1000GP/PopHuman VCF) and the CMH/bootstrap concatenated workflow has only been documented for the D. melanogaster DGN/PopFly protein-coding example

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether a metagenomic allele/strain deconvolution pipeline recovers fractional allele composition per MLST locus from simulated WGS reads with known ground truth.
skills.name: mlst-allele-panel-simulation
skills.search_text: mlst-allele-panel-simulation Use when benchmarking whether a metagenomic allele/strain deconvolution pipeline recovers fractional allele composition per MLST locus from simulated WGS reads with known ground truth. Evaluating the Strain Diversity Problem stage — use the separate SDP simulation with random strain-type distributions under perfect allele calls instead Data are real WGS samples with unknown ground truth — precision/recall/TVD against truth cannot be computed Target organism/pathogen uses an MLST scheme other than the B. burgdorferi 8-locus scheme (the simulation draws from that specific allele database) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Simulates mixed B. burgdorferi MLST allele panels per locus to benchmark allele-diversity inference: draws random allele sets and proportions, simulates reads with ART, maps with Bowtie, and scores precision/recall/TVD against truth. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Simulates mixed B. burgdorferi MLST allele panels per locus to benchmark allele-diversity inference: draws random allele sets and proportions, simulates reads with ART, maps with Bowtie, and scores precision/recall/TVD against truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating the Strain Diversity Problem stage — use the separate SDP simulation with random strain-type distributions under perfect allele calls instead Data are real WGS samples with unknown ground truth — precision/recall/TVD against truth cannot be computed Target organism/pathogen uses an MLST scheme other than the B. burgdorferi 8-locus scheme (the simulation draws from that specific allele database)

skills.description: Use when the ADP ILP has already identified the allele set for an MLST locus and you need fractional allele abundances per gene from the per-sample, per-gene read mapping files.
skills.name: mlst-allele-proportion-normalization
skills.search_text: mlst-allele-proportion-normalization Use when the ADP ILP has already identified the allele set for an MLST locus and you need fractional allele abundances per gene from the per-sample, per-gene read mapping files. Allele selection (the ILP itself) has not yet been run — proportions cannot be computed before the allele set is fixed Input is not short-read WGS mapped to a known MLST allele database (e.g. de novo assemblies without read-to-allele mapping scores) The goal is strain-level deconvolution rather than per-locus allele proportions — that requires the separate globalStrainDiversity.py MILP stage http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Converts the 0-1 ILP allele-selection output of the Allele Diversity Problem (ADP) into per-locus allele proportions by weighting each retained read across the alleles attaining its optimal mapping score and normalizing to a distribution. This supplies the fractional allele abundances per MLST housekeeping gene that feed the downstream Strain Diversity Problem. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Converts the 0-1 ILP allele-selection output of the Allele Diversity Problem (ADP) into per-locus allele proportions by weighting each retained read across the alleles attaining its optimal mapping score and normalizing to a distribution. This supplies the fractional allele abundances per MLST housekeeping gene that feed the downstream Strain Diversity Problem.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Allele selection (the ILP itself) has not yet been run — proportions cannot be computed before the allele set is fixed Input is not short-read WGS mapped to a known MLST allele database (e.g. de novo assemblies without read-to-allele mapping scores) The goal is strain-level deconvolution rather than per-locus allele proportions — that requires the separate globalStrainDiversity.py MILP stage

skills.description: Use when you already possess a chewBBACA-created or adapted cgMLST/wgMLST schema (schema_seed folder) plus draft genome FASTA files, and must stage and validate these inputs before running chewBBACA.py AlleleCall.
skills.name: mlst-schema-input-preparation
skills.search_text: mlst-schema-input-preparation Use when you already possess a chewBBACA-created or adapted cgMLST/wgMLST schema (schema_seed folder) plus draft genome FASTA files, and must stage and validate these inputs before running chewBBACA.py AlleleCall. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than draft/complete genome FASTA assemblies — chewBBACA's allele-calling engine takes FASTA assemblies, while read-based callers like MentaLiST handle reads No schema exists yet and loci must first be defined de novo — this skill stages an existing schema_seed, it does not perform CreateSchema The schema was produced by another platform and has not been adapted — first run PrepExternalSchema (backing up the source FASTA, since it is modified) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Prepares the schema and assembly inputs required for chewBBACA's BLAST-based allele calling: a schema seed directory of representative loci (optionally restricted by a gene list), a species Prodigal training file, and FASTA draft/complete genome assemblies that are fed to the AlleleCall engine. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000166
skills.summary: Prepares the schema and assembly inputs required for chewBBACA's BLAST-based allele calling: a schema seed directory of representative loci (optionally restricted by a gene list), a species Prodigal training file, and FASTA draft/complete genome assemblies that are fed to the AlleleCall engine.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than draft/complete genome FASTA assemblies — chewBBACA's allele-calling engine takes FASTA assemblies, while read-based callers like MentaLiST handle reads No schema exists yet and loci must first be defined de novo — this skill stages an existing schema_seed, it does not perform CreateSchema The schema was produced by another platform and has not been adapted — first run PrepExternalSchema (backing up the source FASTA, since it is modified)

skills.description: Use when per-locus allele sets and allele proportions are available for MLST samples and you must infer which known/novel strain types explain the observed within-host diversity.
skills.name: mlst-strain-diversity-deconvolution
skills.search_text: mlst-strain-diversity-deconvolution Use when per-locus allele sets and allele proportions are available for MLST samples and you must infer which known/novel strain types explain the observed within-host diversity. You only have raw reads and have not yet run Stage 1 (allele calling and allele proportion computation per locus); the SDP requires per-locus allele proportions as input. The pathogen has no MLST database of known strain types/alleles to compare against; the method relies on reference strain types and edit-distance weighting. You need per-locus allele identification rather than whole-sample strain composition — the Allele Diversity Problem (alleleDiversity.py) addresses that stage instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Solves the Strain Diversity Problem (SDP) — associating each MLST sample with a set of strain types and proportions from per-locus allele calls via mixed integer linear programming — minimizing novel strains while respecting observed allele proportions. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Solves the Strain Diversity Problem (SDP) — associating each MLST sample with a set of strain types and proportions from per-locus allele calls via mixed integer linear programming — minimizing novel strains while respecting observed allele proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw reads and have not yet run Stage 1 (allele calling and allele proportion computation per locus); the SDP requires per-locus allele proportions as input. The pathogen has no MLST database of known strain types/alleles to compare against; the method relies on reference strain types and edit-distance weighting. You need per-locus allele identification rather than whole-sample strain composition — the Allele Diversity Problem (alleleDiversity.py) addresses that stage instead.

skills.description: Use when per-sample MLST allele sets and allele proportions (geneX_proportions.csv) are available and you need to jointly infer which known and novel strain types, with proportions, explain the samples.
skills.name: mlst-strain-type-inference
skills.search_text: mlst-strain-type-inference Use when per-sample MLST allele sets and allele proportions (geneX_proportions.csv) are available and you need to jointly infer which known and novel strain types, with proportions, explain the samples. Input is raw reads or unmapped sequencing data — the first-stage ADP solver (alleleDiversity.py) must have already produced geneX_proportions.csv allele sets and proportions No reference strain-type/allele database exists for the organism (the MILP is reference-based, like known-strain approaches rather than de novo methods such as DESMAN) A quick single-locus allele composition estimate is all that is needed — use the ADP ILP stage instead of the global strain-type MILP http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Solves the Strain Diversity Problem (SDP) by formulating and solving a mixed integer linear program (MILP) that assigns each sample a set of strain types from per-sample allele sets and allele proportions, minimizing previously unobserved strains while respecting allele proportions. Implemented in Python 2.7 with the CPLEX 12.6.3.0 Python API and editdistance for weighting novel strains. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Solves the Strain Diversity Problem (SDP) by formulating and solving a mixed integer linear program (MILP) that assigns each sample a set of strain types from per-sample allele sets and allele proportions, minimizing previously unobserved strains while respecting allele proportions. Implemented in Python 2.7 with the CPLEX 12.6.3.0 Python API and editdistance for weighting novel strains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or unmapped sequencing data — the first-stage ADP solver (alleleDiversity.py) must have already produced geneX_proportions.csv allele sets and proportions No reference strain-type/allele database exists for the organism (the MILP is reference-based, like known-strain approaches rather than de novo methods such as DESMAN) A quick single-locus allele composition estimate is all that is needed — use the ADP ILP stage instead of the global strain-type MILP

skills.search_text: mock-community-benchmark-analysis Use when a community of known composition (mock or synthetic gut) with sequenced shotgun reads is available and you must quantify which SSU extraction, reconstruction, or classification tool recovers the expected variants, taxa and runtimes. The input is real environmental metagenomic data with no known community composition — there is no ground truth against which to compute precision/recall/F-measure The goal is novel taxonomic discovery or novelty detection rather than head-to-head tool benchmarking Input is already an assembled or amplicon OTU/ASV feature table rather than raw shotgun FASTQ reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark SSU rRNA read-extraction tools (BBMap vs SortMeRNA), reference-targeted assemblers (Emirge.py, Emirge_amplicon.py, MATAM, MetaRib) and taxonomic classifiers (RiboTaxa, Kraken2, Centrifuge, METAXA2, phyloFlash, SPINGO, BLCA, MEGAN6) on a microbial mock community (SRA SRR5381736) and a synthetic human gut community, using known 16S rRNA variants as ground truth for precision/recall/F-measure evaluation. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Benchmark SSU rRNA read-extraction tools (BBMap vs SortMeRNA), reference-targeted assemblers (Emirge.py, Emirge_amplicon.py, MATAM, MetaRib) and taxonomic classifiers (RiboTaxa, Kraken2, Centrifuge, METAXA2, phyloFlash, SPINGO, BLCA, MEGAN6) on a microbial mock community (SRA SRR5381736) and a synthetic human gut community, using known 16S rRNA variants as ground truth for precision/recall/F-measure evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real environmental metagenomic data with no known community composition — there is no ground truth against which to compute precision/recall/F-measure The goal is novel taxonomic discovery or novelty detection rather than head-to-head tool benchmarking Input is already an assembled or amplicon OTU/ASV feature table rather than raw shotgun FASTQ reads

skills.description: Use when deposited LMAS metric tables (global and per-reference) from mock metagenomic communities are available and the goal is to test whether assembler branding (genomic vs metagenomic) predicts performance on complex samples.
skills.name: mock-community-benchmark-data-analysis
skills.search_text: mock-community-benchmark-data-analysis Use when deposited LMAS metric tables (global and per-reference) from mock metagenomic communities are available and the goal is to test whether assembler branding (genomic vs metagenomic) predicts performance on complex samples. Input is raw sequencing reads or assembled contigs rather than already-computed LMAS metric tables — run the LMAS workflow first The question is about strain-level (SNP-level) resolution: the paper found meaningful strain resolution was not achieved even by the best assemblers, so metric aggregation cannot answer it Assemblies include contigs < 1 kbp in scope: the paper's genomic vs metagenomic conclusion specifically concerns comparisons after the 1 kbp filter http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Analysis of LMAS benchmark output tables on defined mock communities (e.g. ZymoBIOMICS evenly/logarithmically distributed, in silico and real samples) to compare genomic versus metagenomic de novo assembler performance using global and per-reference normalized metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Analysis of LMAS benchmark output tables on defined mock communities (e.g. ZymoBIOMICS evenly/logarithmically distributed, in silico and real samples) to compare genomic versus metagenomic de novo assembler performance using global and per-reference normalized metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or assembled contigs rather than already-computed LMAS metric tables — run the LMAS workflow first The question is about strain-level (SNP-level) resolution: the paper found meaningful strain resolution was not achieved even by the best assemblers, so metric aggregation cannot answer it Assemblies include contigs < 1 kbp in scope: the paper's genomic vs metagenomic conclusion specifically concerns comparisons after the 1 kbp filter

skills.description: Reference for validating or benchmarking a 16S rRNA gene sequence variant caller on data with known composition, or for reproducing runtime, memory, and variant-count comparisons between HashSeq and DADA2.
skills.name: mock-community-benchmark-datasets
skills.search_text: mock-community-benchmark-datasets Reference for validating or benchmarking a 16S rRNA gene sequence variant caller on data with known composition, or for reproducing runtime, memory, and variant-count comparisons between HashSeq and DADA2. The goal is detecting true low-abundance sequence variants — the article recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 for low-abundance variants, so mock-community confirmation of low-abundance taxa is the wrong scope Input reads are raw and unprocessed — this skill's benchmark data sets were already primer-trimmed, paired, and trimmed to 250 bases, so applying it to untrimmed data breaks comparability Working with long-read technologies such as PacBio — HashSeq assumes multiple-mismatch sequences are rare, which may not hold for long reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Use pre-processed 16S rRNA gene mock community FASTQ data sets (e.g., the three zymo communities from NCBI PRJEB24409) as controlled benchmarks for validating variant callers like HashSeq against DADA2, including accuracy of taxon recovery and runtime/memory performance. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Use pre-processed 16S rRNA gene mock community FASTQ data sets (e.g., the three zymo communities from NCBI PRJEB24409) as controlled benchmarks for validating variant callers like HashSeq against DADA2, including accuracy of taxon recovery and runtime/memory performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detecting true low-abundance sequence variants — the article recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 for low-abundance variants, so mock-community confirmation of low-abundance taxa is the wrong scope Input reads are raw and unprocessed — this skill's benchmark data sets were already primer-trimmed, paired, and trimmed to 250 bases, so applying it to untrimmed data breaks comparability Working with long-read technologies such as PacBio — HashSeq assumes multiple-mismatch sequences are rare, which may not hold for long reads

skills.description: Use when comparing taxonomic classification tools on simulated mock communities with known ground-truth abundance profiles, to quantify genus/species identification, abundance estimation accuracy, and read classification rate.
skills.name: mock-community-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: mock-community-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing taxonomic classification tools on simulated mock communities with known ground-truth abundance profiles, to quantify genus/species identification, abundance estimation accuracy, and read classification rate. Input is real-world metagenome data without ground-truth abundance profiles (e.g. the IBD/iHMP dataset), where precision/recall versus truth and L2 abundance distance cannot be computed Goal is classifying novel or long-read data whose error profiles and lengths differ from the training data — DeepMicrobes requires retraining for such reads The reference database must incorporate newly sequenced species without retraining — the current DNN framework requires retraining the entire network when new species are added http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Benchmark a taxonomic classifier against state-of-the-art tools (Kraken, Kraken 2, Centrifuge, CLARK, CLARK-S, Kaiju, DIAMOND-MEGAN, BLAST-MEGAN) on ten mock communities built from HBC gut isolate genomes, using ground-truth genus profiles to compute precision/recall, L2 abundance distance, and read classification rate. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Benchmark a taxonomic classifier against state-of-the-art tools (Kraken, Kraken 2, Centrifuge, CLARK, CLARK-S, Kaiju, DIAMOND-MEGAN, BLAST-MEGAN) on ten mock communities built from HBC gut isolate genomes, using ground-truth genus profiles to compute precision/recall, L2 abundance distance, and read classification rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real-world metagenome data without ground-truth abundance profiles (e.g. the IBD/iHMP dataset), where precision/recall versus truth and L2 abundance distance cannot be computed Goal is classifying novel or long-read data whose error profiles and lengths differ from the training data — DeepMicrobes requires retraining for such reads The reference database must incorporate newly sequenced species without retraining — the current DNN framework requires retraining the entire network when new species are added

skills.description: Use when you have simulated/metagenomic mock community samples with known taxonomic composition and need to quantify a profiler's precision, sensitivity or F1 per taxonomic rank and abundance threshold.
skills.name: mock-community-benchmark-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: mock-community-benchmark-metrics-computation Use when you have simulated/metagenomic mock community samples with known taxonomic composition and need to quantify a profiler's precision, sensitivity or F1 per taxonomic rank and abundance threshold. Input samples have no known ground-truth composition — precision/sensitivity cannot be computed without a reference Samples contain excessive environmental contamination rather than isolated viral fractions, which the article notes lowers precision and inflates running time The goal is functional annotation (DRAM-v, EggNOG, VOGDB) rather than taxonomic detection performance http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark viral taxonomic profilers (ViroProfiler vs Kraken2/Bracken) against the known ground truth of simulated mock virome samples by computing precision, sensitivity and F1 across taxonomic ranks and abundance thresholds. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Benchmark viral taxonomic profilers (ViroProfiler vs Kraken2/Bracken) against the known ground truth of simulated mock virome samples by computing precision, sensitivity and F1 across taxonomic ranks and abundance thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples have no known ground-truth composition — precision/sensitivity cannot be computed without a reference Samples contain excessive environmental contamination rather than isolated viral fractions, which the article notes lowers precision and inflates running time The goal is functional annotation (DRAM-v, EggNOG, VOGDB) rather than taxonomic detection performance

skills.description: Use when a newly generated strain-separated metagenome assembly must be quantitatively benchmarked per recovered strain against known reference genomes from a mock community (Mock3, Mock9).
skills.name: mock-community-benchmark-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: mock-community-benchmark-metrics-computation Use when a newly generated strain-separated metagenome assembly must be quantitatively benchmarked per recovered strain against known reference genomes from a mock community (Mock3, Mock9). The sample is a complex/high-diversity microbiome with no closed reference genomes available, so ANI and coverage against references cannot be computed The input is a raw long-read FASTQ that has not yet been assembled and strain-separated (assemble and run Strainberry first) Evaluating plasmid or other extrachromosomal elements, which the authors explicitly did not assess http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compute per-strain evaluation metrics (average nucleotide identity, reference coverage, duplication ratio) on strain-separated assemblies of mock communities, mirroring the Strainberry Fig. 2 / Supplementary Data 1 tables comparing ssFlye/ssCanu against strain-oblivious Flye/Canu. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Compute per-strain evaluation metrics (average nucleotide identity, reference coverage, duplication ratio) on strain-separated assemblies of mock communities, mirroring the Strainberry Fig. 2 / Supplementary Data 1 tables comparing ssFlye/ssCanu against strain-oblivious Flye/Canu.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is a complex/high-diversity microbiome with no closed reference genomes available, so ANI and coverage against references cannot be computed The input is a raw long-read FASTQ that has not yet been assembled and strain-separated (assemble and run Strainberry first) Evaluating plasmid or other extrachromosomal elements, which the authors explicitly did not assess

skills.description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic classifiers on mock community Illumina reads and you need to reproduce genus/phylum sensitivity and precision comparisons between protein-level (Kaiju) and k-mer-based (Kraken) classifiers.
skills.name: mock-community-benchmark-reproduction
skills.search_text: mock-community-benchmark-reproduction Use when benchmarking taxonomic classifiers on mock community Illumina reads and you need to reproduce genus/phylum sensitivity and precision comparisons between protein-level (Kaiju) and k-mer-based (Kraken) classifiers. Reads derive from simulated data where the sequenced strain genomes are present in the reference database — nucleotide-level classifiers like Kraken will dominate and the protein-level comparison is not informative The goal is strain- or species-level resolution for genera with no reference genomes — genus-level classification is impossible in that case for any classifier Input is already a genus/phylum abundance table; this skill operates on raw FASTQ reads and classifier outputs http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduces the genus- and phylum-level sensitivity/precision benchmark of Kaiju (Greedy-5 mode) versus Kraken (k=31) on the HiSeq and MiSeq mock community FASTQ datasets, yielding the eight sensitivity/precision values of Supplementary Table 2. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Reproduces the genus- and phylum-level sensitivity/precision benchmark of Kaiju (Greedy-5 mode) versus Kraken (k=31) on the HiSeq and MiSeq mock community FASTQ datasets, yielding the eight sensitivity/precision values of Supplementary Table 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads derive from simulated data where the sequenced strain genomes are present in the reference database — nucleotide-level classifiers like Kraken will dominate and the protein-level comparison is not informative The goal is strain- or species-level resolution for genera with no reference genomes — genus-level classification is impossible in that case for any classifier Input is already a genus/phylum abundance table; this skill operates on raw FASTQ reads and classifier outputs

skills.description: Use when a 16S rRNA amplicon profile has been CopyRighter-corrected and a known expected mock community composition (equal 16S rRNA gene copies per species) is available to quantify accuracy by Hellinger/euclidean distance.
skills.name: mock-community-composition-comparison
skills.search_text: mock-community-composition-comparison Use when a 16S rRNA amplicon profile has been CopyRighter-corrected and a known expected mock community composition (equal 16S rRNA gene copies per species) is available to quantify accuracy by Hellinger/euclidean distance. No mock community with a known expected composition is available — distances to an expected profile cannot be computed and validation is meaningless The input table contains relative abundances/percentages instead of raw read counts, which the copyrighter -i input explicitly requires Taxonomic assignments have been altered from the Greengenes taxonomic string format (e.g., k__Bacteria; p__Proteobacteria; ...), preventing GCN trait lookup at the description level http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates GCN-corrected 16S rRNA amplicon profiles by computing Hellinger and euclidean distances between uncorrected/corrected profiles and the expected composition of an in vitro mock community (e.g., HMP SRR074387, 22 species). Correction is accepted when it reduces the distance to the known expected profile. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Validates GCN-corrected 16S rRNA amplicon profiles by computing Hellinger and euclidean distances between uncorrected/corrected profiles and the expected composition of an in vitro mock community (e.g., HMP SRR074387, 22 species). Correction is accepted when it reduces the distance to the known expected profile.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No mock community with a known expected composition is available — distances to an expected profile cannot be computed and validation is meaningless The input table contains relative abundances/percentages instead of raw read counts, which the copyrighter -i input explicitly requires Taxonomic assignments have been altered from the Greengenes taxonomic string format (e.g., k__Bacteria; p__Proteobacteria; ...), preventing GCN trait lookup at the description level

skills.description: Use when classifying reads or reconstructed SSU sequences from a mock/synthetic community with a known expected taxonomy, and you need per-rank precision/recall/F-measure to compare classifiers.
skills.name: mock-community-ground-truth-comparison
skills.search_text: mock-community-ground-truth-comparison Use when classifying reads or reconstructed SSU sequences from a mock/synthetic community with a known expected taxonomy, and you need per-rank precision/recall/F-measure to compare classifiers. The community composition is unknown (no ground truth), so TP/FP/FN binning against an expected taxonomy is impossible The input is raw short Illumina reads rather than reconstructed full-length SSU sequences — the article shows inferring taxa directly to short-length reads results in a high rate of false positives The goal is de novo novelty discovery rather than controlled benchmarking of classifier accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3050 Benchmarks taxonomic classifiers (Centrifuge, Kraken2, mothur, RDP, SPINGO, BLCA, QIIME 2's Sklearn) on reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences from a mock/synthetic community whose true taxonomy is known, by binning assignments as true/false positives and false negatives at each rank and computing precision, recall and F-measure. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Benchmarks taxonomic classifiers (Centrifuge, Kraken2, mothur, RDP, SPINGO, BLCA, QIIME 2's Sklearn) on reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences from a mock/synthetic community whose true taxonomy is known, by binning assignments as true/false positives and false negatives at each rank and computing precision, recall and F-measure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The community composition is unknown (no ground truth), so TP/FP/FN binning against an expected taxonomy is impossible The input is raw short Illumina reads rather than reconstructed full-length SSU sequences — the article shows inferring taxa directly to short-length reads results in a high rate of false positives The goal is de novo novelty discovery rather than controlled benchmarking of classifier accuracy

skills.description: Use when Illumina paired-end plus 4 kbp/8 kbp mate-pair reads from a known-composition mock metagenome (e.g. DDBJ PRJDB4377) must be assembled with several assemblers and compared by NGA50 contiguity.
skills.name: mock-community-metagenome-analysis
skills.search_text: mock-community-metagenome-analysis Use when Illumina paired-end plus 4 kbp/8 kbp mate-pair reads from a known-composition mock metagenome (e.g. DDBJ PRJDB4377) must be assembled with several assemblers and compared by NGA50 contiguity. The dataset is real (unknown-composition) metagenomic data with no ground-truth reference genomes, so NGA50 cannot be computed and the mock-benchmark validation is impossible Only short-read paired-end data are available without mate-pair or long-read libraries, since the benchmark targets MetaPlatanus's long-range mate-pair scaffolding advantage Reference-based or hybrid long-read (PacBio/ONT) assembly is the goal — this study notes reference information has not been well examined and its MP benchmark is mate-pair based http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmarks de novo metagenome assemblers (MetaPlatanus vs IDBA-UD, SPAdes, metaSPAdes, MEGAHIT) on mock human gut bacterial communities sequenced with Illumina paired-end and mate-pair libraries, using NGA50 as the primary contiguity metric to show MetaPlatanus attains the largest NGA50s. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Benchmarks de novo metagenome assemblers (MetaPlatanus vs IDBA-UD, SPAdes, metaSPAdes, MEGAHIT) on mock human gut bacterial communities sequenced with Illumina paired-end and mate-pair libraries, using NGA50 as the primary contiguity metric to show MetaPlatanus attains the largest NGA50s.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is real (unknown-composition) metagenomic data with no ground-truth reference genomes, so NGA50 cannot be computed and the mock-benchmark validation is impossible Only short-read paired-end data are available without mate-pair or long-read libraries, since the benchmark targets MetaPlatanus's long-range mate-pair scaffolding advantage Reference-based or hybrid long-read (PacBio/ONT) assembly is the goal — this study notes reference information has not been well examined and its MP benchmark is mate-pair based

skills.description: Use when comparing de novo short-read assembler performance on a known mock community standard with reference genomes available, to judge which assemblers produce accurate, contiguous assemblies.
skills.name: mock-community-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: mock-community-quality-assessment Use when comparing de novo short-read assembler performance on a known mock community standard with reference genomes available, to judge which assemblers produce accurate, contiguous assemblies. The input is a single isolate genome without a mock community reference set — LMAS's benchmarking logic assumes defined communities with known replicons Strain-level (SNP-level) discrimination is the goal — the article reports meaningful strain resolution was not achieved, even by the best assemblers tested Long-read or hybrid assembly is required — LMAS evaluates short-read metagenomic prokaryotic de novo assembly only http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark de novo metagenomic assemblers on a defined mock community (e.g. the 12-strain BMock12 standard, SRX4901583) using LMAS, a containerized Nextflow workflow that runs assemblers in parallel and scores global (Contigs, Nx, Mapped reads, Misassembled contigs) and per-reference metrics (Contiguity, Multiplicity, Validity, Parsimony, Identity, Breadth of coverage, Lx, NAx, NGx) against a multi-fasta of reference replicons. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Benchmark de novo metagenomic assemblers on a defined mock community (e.g. the 12-strain BMock12 standard, SRX4901583) using LMAS, a containerized Nextflow workflow that runs assemblers in parallel and scores global (Contigs, Nx, Mapped reads, Misassembled contigs) and per-reference metrics (Contiguity, Multiplicity, Validity, Parsimony, Identity, Breadth of coverage, Lx, NAx, NGx) against a multi-fasta of reference replicons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single isolate genome without a mock community reference set — LMAS's benchmarking logic assumes defined communities with known replicons Strain-level (SNP-level) discrimination is the goal — the article reports meaningful strain resolution was not achieved, even by the best assemblers tested Long-read or hybrid assembly is required — LMAS evaluates short-read metagenomic prokaryotic de novo assembly only

skills.description: Use when validating a taxonomic or functional profiling database against cross-kingdom false-positive mapping, by simulating mock-community FASTQ reads with ART and measuring mapping rates or specificity.
skills.name: mock-community-read-simulation
skills.search_text: mock-community-read-simulation Use when validating a taxonomic or functional profiling database against cross-kingdom false-positive mapping, by simulating mock-community FASTQ reads with ART and measuring mapping rates or specificity. Input is real shotgun metagenome FASTQ rather than simulated reads with known ground truth — specificity cannot be computed without truth labels The target database is bacterial (e.g. UHGG) and the question is fungal-to-bacterial contamination measured by marker-gene alignment, not read-level mock simulation Profiling a real sample through the FunOMIC.sh pipeline (this skill is the validation/benchmarking step, not the profiling step) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Simulate synthetic Illumina reads with ART from defined bacterial and mixed bacterial:fungal mock communities to benchmark the specificity of the FunOMIC-T taxonomic database and the Diamond blastx thresholds of the FunOMIC-P functional database. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Simulate synthetic Illumina reads with ART from defined bacterial and mixed bacterial:fungal mock communities to benchmark the specificity of the FunOMIC-T taxonomic database and the Diamond blastx thresholds of the FunOMIC-P functional database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real shotgun metagenome FASTQ rather than simulated reads with known ground truth — specificity cannot be computed without truth labels The target database is bacterial (e.g. UHGG) and the question is fungal-to-bacterial contamination measured by marker-gene alignment, not read-level mock simulation Profiling a real sample through the FunOMIC.sh pipeline (this skill is the validation/benchmarking step, not the profiling step)

skills.description: Use when a known-composition mock metagenome (e.g. GIS20 bacteria with Illumina paired-end plus ONT or PacBio long reads) is being assembled and contiguity/accuracy must be compared across assemblers against reference genomes.
skills.name: mock-community-reference-based-evaluation
skills.search_text: mock-community-reference-based-evaluation Use when a known-composition mock metagenome (e.g. GIS20 bacteria with Illumina paired-end plus ONT or PacBio long reads) is being assembled and contiguity/accuracy must be compared across assemblers against reference genomes. Real environmental metagenomes or clinical samples without known reference genomes — the article notes 'this study focuses on de novo methods, and reference information has not been well examined', and the reference-based NGA50/interspecies-misassembly evaluation requires known mock composition Evaluating a single assembly rather than comparing multiple assemblers on identical read sets — the benchmark design depends on the same Illumina PE plus ONT/PacBio inputs being run through each assembler Assembly questions that depend on local graph structures or polishing quality alone, where metaQUAST NGA50/misassembly statistics are not the deciding metric http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark metagenome assemblers (MetaPlatanus v1.3.0 vs metaSPAdes hybrid, OPERA-MS de novo, metaFlye) on a mock community with known reference genomes, using QUAST/metaQUAST to extract NGA50, misassemblies, sequence identity, and interspecies misassemblies. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Benchmark metagenome assemblers (MetaPlatanus v1.3.0 vs metaSPAdes hybrid, OPERA-MS de novo, metaFlye) on a mock community with known reference genomes, using QUAST/metaQUAST to extract NGA50, misassemblies, sequence identity, and interspecies misassemblies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real environmental metagenomes or clinical samples without known reference genomes — the article notes 'this study focuses on de novo methods, and reference information has not been well examined', and the reference-based NGA50/interspecies-misassembly evaluation requires known mock composition Evaluating a single assembly rather than comparing multiple assemblers on identical read sets — the benchmark design depends on the same Illumina PE plus ONT/PacBio inputs being run through each assembler Assembly questions that depend on local graph structures or polishing quality alone, where metaQUAST NGA50/misassembly statistics are not the deciding metric

skills.description: Use when a strain-separated long-read metagenome assembly (e.g., assembly.scaffolds.fa from Strainberry on a mock community) must be evaluated for completeness and base-level accuracy against known reference strain genomes.
skills.name: mock-community-scaffold-completeness-evaluation
skills.search_text: mock-community-scaffold-completeness-evaluation Use when a strain-separated long-read metagenome assembly (e.g., assembly.scaffolds.fa from Strainberry on a mock community) must be evaluated for completeness and base-level accuracy against known reference strain genomes. The sample is a complex real microbiome without known reference strain genomes (e.g., the Human Stool Microbiome dataset), where reference-coverage-based completeness benchmarks cannot be computed The input is a strain-oblivious assembly (e.g., metaFlye assembly.fasta) rather than a strain-resolved Strainberry output to be benchmarked The goal is strain separation itself (running Strainberry) rather than post-hoc evaluation of already-generated scaffolds Benchmarks strain-resolved long-read metagenome assemblies (e.g., Strainberry scaffolds from the Mock3/Mock9/NWC2 mock communities) against reference strain genomes, judging success by near-complete reference coverage and ~99.9% base accuracy. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Benchmarks strain-resolved long-read metagenome assemblies (e.g., Strainberry scaffolds from the Mock3/Mock9/NWC2 mock communities) against reference strain genomes, judging success by near-complete reference coverage and ~99.9% base accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is a complex real microbiome without known reference strain genomes (e.g., the Human Stool Microbiome dataset), where reference-coverage-based completeness benchmarks cannot be computed The input is a strain-oblivious assembly (e.g., metaFlye assembly.fasta) rather than a strain-resolved Strainberry output to be benchmarked The goal is strain separation itself (running Strainberry) rather than post-hoc evaluation of already-generated scaffolds

skills.description: Use when a target-detection tool must be quantitatively validated on a defined mock community, e.g. per-species read classification accuracy/F1 for 16S MinION reads under stratified 5-fold cross-validation.
skills.name: mock-community-species-benchmarking
skills.search_text: mock-community-species-benchmarking Use when a target-detection tool must be quantitatively validated on a defined mock community, e.g. per-species read classification accuracy/F1 for 16S MinION reads under stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Your goal is abundance estimation of a target genome in a pure sample rather than per-read species classification — baseLess abundance mode, not read-detection benchmarking, is appropriate Your input is already basecalled FASTQ/FASTA sequence data — this skill evaluates detection directly on raw MinION electrical signal (fast5), which is the point of baseLess You need genome-level taxonomy profiling of a complex metagenome rather than targeted detection of a defined set of mock-community species http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark per-species read-detection accuracy of a sequence detector (baseLess read_detection mode) on a defined mock community (16S rRNA HM-278D, 21 species) using stratified 5-fold cross-validation, reporting per-species accuracy and F1 scores. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017
skills.summary: Benchmark per-species read-detection accuracy of a sequence detector (baseLess read_detection mode) on a defined mock community (16S rRNA HM-278D, 21 species) using stratified 5-fold cross-validation, reporting per-species accuracy and F1 scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is abundance estimation of a target genome in a pure sample rather than per-read species classification — baseLess abundance mode, not read-detection benchmarking, is appropriate Your input is already basecalled FASTQ/FASTA sequence data — this skill evaluates detection directly on raw MinION electrical signal (fast5), which is the point of baseLess You need genome-level taxonomy profiling of a complex metagenome rather than targeted detection of a defined set of mock-community species

skills.description: Use when benchmarking OTU-count fidelity of 16S pipelines on mock communities with known strain composition, to judge which pipeline's OTU count deviates least from truth.
skills.name: mock-community-strain-count-comparison
skills.search_text: mock-community-strain-count-comparison Use when benchmarking OTU-count fidelity of 16S pipelines on mock communities with known strain composition, to judge which pipeline's OTU count deviates least from truth. skills.search_text: modification-enzyme-hmm-detection Use when assembled contigs or RefSeq genomes paired with tandem mass spectra must be mined for RiPPs: after 6-frame translation, modification-enzyme HMM hits define which 10 kbp windows feed motif-ORF/all-ORF precursor prediction in MetaMiner. skills.summary: Scans 6-frame translated genomic or metagenomic contigs with HMMer profile HMMs to detect RiPP modification enzymes, delimiting each hit as a 10 kbp putative biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) window from which candidate precursor peptides are enumerated.

skills.description: Use when you need to select a taxonomic classifier by benchmarking several (e.g. Centrifuge, Kraken2, SPINGO, BLCA, QIIME 2 Sklearn) on sequences with a known ground-truth taxonomy, such as a mock community.
skills.name: multi-classifier-performance-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-classifier-performance-comparison Use when you need to select a taxonomic classifier by benchmarking several (e.g. Centrifuge, Kraken2, SPINGO, BLCA, QIIME 2 Sklearn) on sequences with a known ground-truth taxonomy, such as a mock community. Input is raw short Illumina reads classified directly without prior SSU reconstruction — the article shows this yields a high rate of false positives, so benchmarking classifiers on unassembled reads answers a different question There is no ground-truth community composition (no mock/synthetic community), so true positives/false positives cannot be defined The goal is runtime/throughput comparison rather than assignment accuracy — RiboTaxa is admittedly slower than Kraken2/Centrifuge and this skill measures precision/recall/F-measure, not speed http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark multiple taxonomic classifiers (Centrifuge, Kraken2, mothur, RDP Classifier, SPINGO, BLCA, QIIME 2's classify-sklearn) against a known mock/synthetic community by classifying reconstructed SSU rRNA sequences and computing precision, recall and F-measure per taxonomic level, to identify which classifier gives the most accurate species-level assignment. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple taxonomic classifiers (Centrifuge, Kraken2, mothur, RDP Classifier, SPINGO, BLCA, QIIME 2's classify-sklearn) against a known mock/synthetic community by classifying reconstructed SSU rRNA sequences and computing precision, recall and F-measure per taxonomic level, to identify which classifier gives the most accurate species-level assignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw short Illumina reads classified directly without prior SSU reconstruction — the article shows this yields a high rate of false positives, so benchmarking classifiers on unassembled reads answers a different question There is no ground-truth community composition (no mock/synthetic community), so true positives/false positives cannot be defined The goal is runtime/throughput comparison rather than assignment accuracy — RiboTaxa is admittedly slower than Kraken2/Centrifuge and this skill measures precision/recall/F-measure, not speed

skills.description: Use when you have a mixed FASTA collection of genomes (e.g. prokaryotic MAGs, fungal genomes, vOTUs) and need a non-redundant pan-genome gene catalogue at a defined amino acid identity threshold.

skills.search_text: multi-kingdom-genome-collection-processing Use when you have a mixed FASTA collection of genomes (e.g. prokaryotic MAGs, fungal genomes, vOTUs) and need a non-redundant pan-genome gene catalogue at a defined amino acid identity threshold. skills.summary: Constructs a non-redundant multi-kingdom gene catalogue (e.g. VMGC-90) by predicting protein-coding genes across prokaryotic MAGs, fungal and viral genomes with Prodigal, then clustering the ~26 million concatenated proteins with MMseqs2 at 90% amino acid identity.

skills.description: Use when adaptor-preprocessed metagenomic FASTQ reads must be assembled de novo to produce fragmented seed contigs that feed a contig-extension step such as ContigExtender.
skills.name: multi-kmer-de-bruijn-graph-assembly
skills.search_text: multi-kmer-de-bruijn-graph-assembly Use when adaptor-preprocessed metagenomic FASTQ reads must be assembled de novo to produce fragmented seed contigs that feed a contig-extension step such as ContigExtender. skills.summary: Generates seed contigs for downstream contig extension by running de novo metagenomic assembly with metaSPAdes (SPAdes 3.13.0, -meta mode) using a multi-k de Bruijn graph (k=21,33,55,77), all other parameters at default.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a set of assembled contigs — this skill only produces the initial seed contigs before extension. skills.description: Use when QCed2/QCed3 OMARU profiling tables (clade levels L2–L7 and gene abundance) are available for case-control metagenome cohorts and the goal is to test whether diversity differs between cases and controls.
skills.name: multi-level-taxonomic-diversity-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-level-taxonomic-diversity-analysis Use when QCed2/QCed3 OMARU profiling tables (clade levels L2–L7 and gene abundance) are available for case-control metagenome cohorts and the goal is to test whether diversity differs between cases and controls. Input is raw FASTQ reads or read-QC outputs — profiling (OMARU_QCed1.sm / OMARU_QCed2.sm) must produce abundance tables first The goal is a case-control clade or gene association test (OMARU_Phyl_AS.sm / OMARU_Func_AS.sm), not a diversity comparison Covariates must be integrated directly into the case-control diversity model — covariate integration is not implemented in OMARU, so only post-hoc or confounding-factor correction paths apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Case-control assessment of metagenome diversity using OMARU outputs: Shannon alpha-diversity computed on clade relative abundances at taxonomic levels L2–L7 and on gene abundance, plus Bray-Curtis beta-diversity with PERMANOVA and MDS visualization. It detects disrupted diversity, as demonstrated for T2D (n=171) versus the null result in SCZ (n=344). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: Case-control assessment of metagenome diversity using OMARU outputs: Shannon alpha-diversity computed on clade relative abundances at taxonomic levels L2–L7 and on gene abundance, plus Bray-Curtis beta-diversity with PERMANOVA and MDS visualization. It detects disrupted diversity, as demonstrated for T2D (n=171) versus the null result in SCZ (n=344).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads or read-QC outputs — profiling (OMARU_QCed1.sm / OMARU_QCed2.sm) must produce abundance tables first The goal is a case-control clade or gene association test (OMARU_Phyl_AS.sm / OMARU_Func_AS.sm), not a diversity comparison Covariates must be integrated directly into the case-control diversity model — covariate integration is not implemented in OMARU, so only post-hoc or confounding-factor correction paths apply

skills.description: Use when evaluating a HiFi metagenome assembly with reads that map to contigs belonging to multiple bins of different CheckM2 quality levels, and you need non-double-counted aligned read/base ratios split by bin quality.
skills.name: multi-mapping-read-quality-resolution
skills.search_text: multi-mapping-read-quality-resolution Use when evaluating a HiFi metagenome assembly with reads that map to contigs belonging to multiple bins of different CheckM2 quality levels, and you need non-double-counted aligned read/base ratios split by bin quality. Input is only an unfiltered global aligned/unaligned ratio (report.txt of reads_on_contigs_mapping_evaluation) with no binning information — the simple, non-binning-aware metric suffices and no multi-mapping resolution is needed. No bin quality classification (e.g., no CheckM2 quality_report.tsv) is available, so contigs cannot be assigned to quality categories. Assembly is of an isolate or low-diversity sample where per-bin-quality breakdown of mapping ratios adds no information over global ratios. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Binning-aware metric computation from Mapler that resolves reads mapping to multiple contigs into a single bin-quality category (near complete > high > medium > low > unbinned), then reports aligned read and aligned base ratios per category so assembly representativeness can be judged per genome quality tier. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Binning-aware metric computation from Mapler that resolves reads mapping to multiple contigs into a single bin-quality category (near complete > high > medium > low > unbinned), then reports aligned read and aligned base ratios per category so assembly representativeness can be judged per genome quality tier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only an unfiltered global aligned/unaligned ratio (report.txt of reads_on_contigs_mapping_evaluation) with no binning information — the simple, non-binning-aware metric suffices and no multi-mapping resolution is needed. No bin quality classification (e.g., no CheckM2 quality_report.tsv) is available, so contigs cannot be assigned to quality categories. Assembly is of an isolate or low-diversity sample where per-bin-quality breakdown of mapping ratios adds no information over global ratios.

skills.description: Use when combining ≥10 studies across multiple related markers (e.g., six α-diversity indices: Richness, Shannon, Simpson, PD, PE, PQE) from summary statistics alone, with no priori marker-by-marker correlation estimates and possible missing data.
skills.name: multi-marker-covariance-weighted-pooling
skills.search_text: multi-marker-covariance-weighted-pooling Use when combining ≥10 studies across multiple related markers (e.g., six α-diversity indices: Richness, Shannon, Simpson, PD, PE, PQE) from summary statistics alone, with no priori marker-by-marker correlation estimates and possible missing data. You have raw sequence data (e.g., FASTQ/16S reads) rather than summary statistics — mMeta/aMeta require only effect estimates and standard errors, not raw OTU tables You have < 10 studies or fewer rows in est/std.err than the minimum required by the package You need flexible handling of many different types of summary data (e.g., only graphs, stratified means/medians/IQRs per group) — the authors note no fully flexible method was achieved in this paper http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Applies the mMeta and aMeta methods (R package mMeta) to combine multiple studies across multiple related markers using only summary statistics (effect estimates and standard errors), without prior marker-by-marker correlations. mMeta yields a covariance-weighted pooled estimate with its SE across all studies and markers, while aMeta delivers a more powerful across-marker hypothesis test via a minimum-p-value approach. metagenomics/v1 10.1002/sim.8940
skills.summary: Applies the mMeta and aMeta methods (R package mMeta) to combine multiple studies across multiple related markers using only summary statistics (effect estimates and standard errors), without prior marker-by-marker correlations. mMeta yields a covariance-weighted pooled estimate with its SE across all studies and markers, while aMeta delivers a more powerful across-marker hypothesis test via a minimum-p-value approach.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have raw sequence data (e.g., FASTQ/16S reads) rather than summary statistics — mMeta/aMeta require only effect estimates and standard errors, not raw OTU tables You have < 10 studies or fewer rows in est/std.err than the minimum required by the package You need flexible handling of many different types of summary data (e.g., only graphs, stratified means/medians/IQRs per group) — the authors note no fully flexible method was achieved in this paper

skills.description: Use when combining ≥10 studies across multiple related markers with only summary statistics (effect estimates and their standard errors, possibly with matched NAs), and no prior marker-by-marker correlations, e.g., α-diversity indices across microbiome studies.
skills.name: multi-marker-summary-statistics-meta-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-marker-summary-statistics-meta-analysis Use when combining ≥10 studies across multiple related markers with only summary statistics (effect estimates and their standard errors, possibly with matched NAs), and no prior marker-by-marker correlations, e.g., α-diversity indices across microbiome studies. Input is raw sequencing data (e.g., FASTQ, OTU tables) rather than per-study effect estimates and standard errors — sequence processing (FLASH, Trimmomatic, PyNAST, Acacia, UCLUST, Bowtie2) and regression fitting must precede this skill Fewer than 10 studies are available, since mMeta.aMeta requires the number of studies (rows) to be greater than or equal to 10 Only one marker needs meta-analysis — mMeta/aMeta are designed for combining multiple related markers, and aMeta is limited to hypothesis testing (no pooled estimate/CI) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 This skill implements mMeta and aMeta, two random effects meta-analysis methods that combine multiple studies across multiple related markers (e.g., six α-diversity indices) using only effect estimates (regression coefficients) and standard errors, with no a priori marker-by-marker correlations. mMeta estimates marker-by-marker correlations non-parametrically via group permutations for pooled estimates and tests, while aMeta adaptively weights single-marker tests and approaches the highest power metagenomics/v1 10.1002/sim.8940
skills.summary: This skill implements mMeta and aMeta, two random effects meta-analysis methods that combine multiple studies across multiple related markers (e.g., six α-diversity indices) using only effect estimates (regression coefficients) and standard errors, with no a priori marker-by-marker correlations. mMeta estimates marker-by-marker correlations non-parametrically via group permutations for pooled estimates and tests, while aMeta adaptively weights single-marker tests and approaches the highest power
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data (e.g., FASTQ, OTU tables) rather than per-study effect estimates and standard errors — sequence processing (FLASH, Trimmomatic, PyNAST, Acacia, UCLUST, Bowtie2) and regression fitting must precede this skill Fewer than 10 studies are available, since mMeta.aMeta requires the number of studies (rows) to be greater than or equal to 10 Only one marker needs meta-analysis — mMeta/aMeta are designed for combining multiple related markers, and aMeta is limited to hypothesis testing (no pooled estimate/CI)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a viral binning method against baselines on assembled metagenomic Hi-C data and you need per-method counts of high/medium-completion bins (CheckV) to quantify improvement percentages.
skills.name: multi-method-bin-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: multi-method-bin-count-aggregation Use when benchmarking a viral binning method against baselines on assembled metagenomic Hi-C data and you need per-method counts of high/medium-completion bins (CheckV) to quantify improvement percentages. The task is to bin prokaryotic MAGs rather than viral genomes — CheckM marker-gene assessment, not CheckV, applies and HiCBin/TAXAassign are appropriate The dataset has too few putative viral genomes for the benchmarking to be convincing, or the goal is to estimate contamination of vMAGs (CheckV cannot estimate contamination since no marker gene set exists for viruses) Only a single binning method is being run without baselines — no improvement percentages can be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Runs multiple metagenomic binning tools (ViralCC, MetaTOR, bin3C, HiCBin, CoCoNet, vRhyme, VAMB) on the same shotgun+Hi-C dataset and aggregates per-method counts of high/medium-completion viral bins as scored by CheckV, then computes ViralCC's percentage improvements over each baseline. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Runs multiple metagenomic binning tools (ViralCC, MetaTOR, bin3C, HiCBin, CoCoNet, vRhyme, VAMB) on the same shotgun+Hi-C dataset and aggregates per-method counts of high/medium-completion viral bins as scored by CheckV, then computes ViralCC's percentage improvements over each baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is to bin prokaryotic MAGs rather than viral genomes — CheckM marker-gene assessment, not CheckV, applies and HiCBin/TAXAassign are appropriate The dataset has too few putative viral genomes for the benchmarking to be convincing, or the goal is to estimate contamination of vMAGs (CheckV cannot estimate contamination since no marker gene set exists for viruses) Only a single binning method is being run without baselines — no improvement percentages can be computed
