skills.description: Use when metagenomic samples (e.g., NICU infant stool) have been profiled with inStrain and compared pairwise, and you need to test and visualize whether shared strains are enriched between siblings, whether MZ twins share more than DZ twins, and whether similarity tracks physiological properties.
skills.name: multi-panel-figure-visualization
skills.search_text: multi-panel-figure-visualization Use when metagenomic samples (e.g., NICU infant stool) have been profiled with inStrain and compared pairwise, and you need to test and visualize whether shared strains are enriched between siblings, whether MZ twins share more than DZ twins, and whether similarity tracks physiological properties. You only have single-sample inStrain profiles (nucleotide diversity, SNVs, linkage) and no pairwise comparisons between infants — run 'inStrain compare' first; this skill operates on cross-sample sharing statistics Samples lack paired metadata (sibling/twin status, birth day, birth weight, gestational age), so the sibling-enrichment, MZ-vs-DZ, and physiology panels cannot be populated The goal is a generic single-panel plot of one metric rather than the reproducible multi-panel strain-sharing analysis with its associated statistical tests http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Reproduces the Figure 3-style multi-panel analysis of strain-sharing among NICU infants: sibling enrichment of two-infant strains, MZ-vs-DZ twin comparison, and association of strain-composition Jaccard similarity with birth-day distance, birth weight, and gestational age, drawn with Matplotlib/Seaborn on top of inStrain compare outputs. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Reproduces the Figure 3-style multi-panel analysis of strain-sharing among NICU infants: sibling enrichment of two-infant strains, MZ-vs-DZ twin comparison, and association of strain-composition Jaccard similarity with birth-day distance, birth weight, and gestational age, drawn with Matplotlib/Seaborn on top of inStrain compare outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have single-sample inStrain profiles (nucleotide diversity, SNVs, linkage) and no pairwise comparisons between infants — run 'inStrain compare' first; this skill operates on cross-sample sharing statistics Samples lack paired metadata (sibling/twin status, birth day, birth weight, gestational age), so the sibling-enrichment, MZ-vs-DZ, and physiology panels cannot be populated The goal is a generic single-panel plot of one metric rather than the reproducible multi-panel strain-sharing analysis with its associated statistical tests

skills.description: Use when classifying microbiome samples (OTU/species abundance table + sample metadata) into disease or control status categories and you want a phylogeny-aware deep learning classifier benchmarked against ML baselines.
skills.name: multi-path-convolutional-ensemble-classification
skills.search_text: multi-path-convolutional-ensemble-classification Use when classifying microbiome samples (OTU/species abundance table + sample metadata) into disease or control status categories and you want a phylogeny-aware deep learning classifier benchmarked against ML baselines. When no phylogenetic tree or OTU representative sequences are available and features cannot be ordered by phylogeny, undermining the multi-path convolution design When the goal is only a simple taxonomic summary or differential abundance test rather than supervised status/disease classification When the input is not a microbial feature table (OTU/species abundance), which is a stated prerequisite for PM-CNN http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and evaluate PM-CNN, a phylogeny-based four-path convolutional neural network whose per-path features are flattened and fused by a fully connected ensemble to classify microbiome disease status, scoring predictions with Kappa, Recall, Accuracy, Precision, and F1. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae013
skills.summary: Train and evaluate PM-CNN, a phylogeny-based four-path convolutional neural network whose per-path features are flattened and fused by a fully connected ensemble to classify microbiome disease status, scoring predictions with Kappa, Recall, Accuracy, Precision, and F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no phylogenetic tree or OTU representative sequences are available and features cannot be ordered by phylogeny, undermining the multi-path convolution design When the goal is only a simple taxonomic summary or differential abundance test rather than supervised status/disease classification When the input is not a microbial feature table (OTU/species abundance), which is a stated prerequisite for PM-CNN

skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks a known ground truth number of OTUs, so accuracy fractions cannot be computed — use consistency/robustness comparisons instead The goal is a biological community analysis (e.g. genus profiling of HMP or environmental samples) rather than pipeline benchmarking Input is already an OTU table or feature table; this skill operates on raw reads through each pipeline end-to-end

skills.description: Use when Sentinel-1 gamma_0 temporal stacks (e.g. VH/VV GeoTIFFs such as ALB_gamma0_VH.tif and ALB_gamma0_VV.tif) must be summarized into neighborhood texture variables representing habitat structural heterogeneity.
skills.name: multi-polarization-backscatter-characterization
skills.search_text: multi-polarization-backscatter-characterization Use when Sentinel-1 gamma_0 temporal stacks (e.g. VH/VV GeoTIFFs such as ALB_gamma0_VH.tif and ALB_gamma0_VV.tif) must be summarized into neighborhood texture variables representing habitat structural heterogeneity. Input is still raw GRDH digital numbers in slant-range coordinates — apply the SNAP gamma_0 processing chain (precise orbit, border/thermal noise removal, radiometric calibration, terrain flattening, range-doppler terrain correction) first The goal is pixel-based mean backscatter statistics per plot (e.g. the S1_mean.csv temporal medians) rather than neighborhood texture heterogeneity layers The target variable depends on understorey structure that C-band backscatter cannot characterize due to weak permeability through overstorey layers Transforms temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 VH and VV gamma_0 backscatter into GLCM texture layers (contrast-group and orderliness-group indices) that quantify horizontal structural heterogeneity of forest habitats, using R's glcm and raster packages. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Transforms temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 VH and VV gamma_0 backscatter into GLCM texture layers (contrast-group and orderliness-group indices) that quantify horizontal structural heterogeneity of forest habitats, using R's glcm and raster packages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw GRDH digital numbers in slant-range coordinates — apply the SNAP gamma_0 processing chain (precise orbit, border/thermal noise removal, radiometric calibration, terrain flattening, range-doppler terrain correction) first The goal is pixel-based mean backscatter statistics per plot (e.g. the S1_mean.csv temporal medians) rather than neighborhood texture heterogeneity layers The target variable depends on understorey structure that C-band backscatter cannot characterize due to weak permeability through overstorey layers

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify what fraction of reads from independent, population-diverse metagenomes map to a reference gene catalog versus a smaller subset reference, to assess catalog comprehensiveness.
skills.name: multi-population-metagenome-coverage-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-population-metagenome-coverage-benchmarking Use when you need to quantify what fraction of reads from independent, population-diverse metagenomes map to a reference gene catalog versus a smaller subset reference, to assess catalog comprehensiveness. The goal is taxonomic/functional profiling of samples rather than benchmarking the reference catalog itself — mapping to VIRGO for abundance estimation is a different skill Your mapper or workflow requires paired-end mapping; VIRGO's runMapping.step1.sh does not support paired-end input, so reads must be merged first The held-out samples come from a body site or population far outside the catalog's scope (VIRGO is vagina-focused and primarily bacterial, with limited viral/fungal sequences), making coverage benchmarks uninterpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark the geographic comprehensiveness of a reference gene catalog by mapping held-out metagenomes from multiple populations (North American, African, Chinese vaginal samples) against the full catalog and a subset reference, then comparing read-mapping rates. Used to validate that VIRGO provides >95% coverage of the human vaginal microbiome across continents. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Benchmark the geographic comprehensiveness of a reference gene catalog by mapping held-out metagenomes from multiple populations (North American, African, Chinese vaginal samples) against the full catalog and a subset reference, then comparing read-mapping rates. Used to validate that VIRGO provides >95% coverage of the human vaginal microbiome across continents.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is taxonomic/functional profiling of samples rather than benchmarking the reference catalog itself — mapping to VIRGO for abundance estimation is a different skill Your mapper or workflow requires paired-end mapping; VIRGO's runMapping.step1.sh does not support paired-end input, so reads must be merged first The held-out samples come from a body site or population far outside the catalog's scope (VIRGO is vagina-focused and primarily bacterial, with limited viral/fungal sequences), making coverage benchmarks uninterpretable

skills.description: Use when building a species-level non-redundant viral contig catalog from multiple shotgun viral metagenomic samples, requiring per-sample assembly followed by cross-sample dereplication.
skills.name: multi-sample-contig-pooling
skills.search_text: multi-sample-contig-pooling Use when building a species-level non-redundant viral contig catalog from multiple shotgun viral metagenomic samples, requiring per-sample assembly followed by cross-sample dereplication. Input is already a dereplicated contig catalog or feature table — re-clustering would not add species-level resolution Samples contain isolated viruses rather than metagenomic communities — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses, and assembly/dereplication of mixed communities is the wrong framing Excessive environmental contamination is present in the metagenome sequences — contamination increases pipeline running time and lowers precision; isolate viral fractions before sequencing instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assembles quality-filtered reads per sample with metaSPAdes in metagenomic mode, pools contigs from all samples, and dereplicates them by ANI clustering into a non-redundant contig library (nrclib) used for downstream annotation and analysis in ViroProfiler. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Assembles quality-filtered reads per sample with metaSPAdes in metagenomic mode, pools contigs from all samples, and dereplicates them by ANI clustering into a non-redundant contig library (nrclib) used for downstream annotation and analysis in ViroProfiler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a dereplicated contig catalog or feature table — re-clustering would not add species-level resolution Samples contain isolated viruses rather than metagenomic communities — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses, and assembly/dereplication of mixed communities is the wrong framing Excessive environmental contamination is present in the metagenome sequences — contamination increases pipeline running time and lowers precision; isolate viral fractions before sequencing instead

skills.description: Use when input is archived (raw) FASTA files from time-series multi-omics data (e.g., metaproteomics) and the goal is to convert sequences into a numeric feature table suitable for downstream clustering or visualization.
skills.name: multi-sequence-vector-averaging
skills.search_text: multi-sequence-vector-averaging Use when input is archived (raw) FASTA files from time-series multi-omics data (e.g., metaproteomics) and the goal is to convert sequences into a numeric feature table suitable for downstream clustering or visualization. The data are already tabular (CSV/TSV feature tables) — MOVIS's filtering step is present only for tabular data sets and FASTA embedding is unnecessary. The input is raw microarray-based data, which MOVIS cannot use directly as input and requires preprocessing first. Only per-sequence vectors (not per-file representative vectors) are needed, since this skill specifically averages vectors within each FASTA file. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Embeds FASTA sequences into 100-dimensional Word2Vec vectors and averages the per-sequence vectors within each FASTA file to yield one representative vector per file, enabling tabular clustering (e.g., K-Means with the Elbow rule) in MOVIS's data analysis core. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.02.012
skills.summary: Embeds FASTA sequences into 100-dimensional Word2Vec vectors and averages the per-sequence vectors within each FASTA file to yield one representative vector per file, enabling tabular clustering (e.g., K-Means with the Elbow rule) in MOVIS's data analysis core.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already tabular (CSV/TSV feature tables) — MOVIS's filtering step is present only for tabular data sets and FASTA embedding is unnecessary. The input is raw microarray-based data, which MOVIS cannot use directly as input and requires preprocessing first. Only per-sequence vectors (not per-file representative vectors) are needed, since this skill specifically averages vectors within each FASTA file.

skills.description: Use when predicting secondary structure, solvent accessibility, or residue-residue contacts from a protein sequence via its MSA, or when benchmarking 1D/2D structure prediction against RaptorX-Property and SCRATCH-1D on CASP targets.
skills.name: multi-task-protein-structure-prediction
skills.search_text: multi-task-protein-structure-prediction Use when predicting secondary structure, solvent accessibility, or residue-residue contacts from a protein sequence via its MSA, or when benchmarking 1D/2D structure prediction against RaptorX-Property and SCRATCH-1D on CASP targets. The goal is tertiary structure construction only — build models from contacts separately using CONFOLD with the top 2L contacts instead No HHblits setup or MSA can be generated (e.g., no UniProt20_2016 database available), since the multitask model consumes MSA-derived 2D feature maps The evaluation requires RaptorX-Contact local execution — RaptorX-Contact has no local execution file and runs only on its web server with different MSAs http://edamontology.org/topic_0082 http://edamontology.org/topic_2275 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and run DeepECA's multitask network, which jointly predicts protein contacts, secondary structure, and solvent-accessible surface area (ASA) from a single MSA using a shared 20-residual-block trunk with task-specific 10-block heads, so that the auxiliary 1D tasks improve overall representation and prediction accuracy. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3190-x
skills.summary: Train and run DeepECA's multitask network, which jointly predicts protein contacts, secondary structure, and solvent-accessible surface area (ASA) from a single MSA using a shared 20-residual-block trunk with task-specific 10-block heads, so that the auxiliary 1D tasks improve overall representation and prediction accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is tertiary structure construction only — build models from contacts separately using CONFOLD with the top 2L contacts instead No HHblits setup or MSA can be generated (e.g., no UniProt20_2016 database available), since the multitask model consumes MSA-derived 2D feature maps The evaluation requires RaptorX-Contact local execution — RaptorX-Contact has no local execution file and runs only on its web server with different MSAs

skills.description: Use when you need to compare computational efficiency (wall-clock time and max memory) of Plassembler versus Unicycler across multiple thread counts on simulated or real hybrid (short+long read) bacterial read sets.
skills.name: multi-threaded-performance-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-threaded-performance-comparison Use when you need to compare computational efficiency (wall-clock time and max memory) of Plassembler versus Unicycler across multiple thread counts on simulated or real hybrid (short+long read) bacterial read sets. skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of Plassembler (Flye or Raven long-read assembler modes) against Unicycler at 1, 8, and 16 threads across 20 simulated and 6 real read sets, quantifying the reported 3- to 10-fold speedup.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need assembly accuracy comparison (plasmid recovery, misassemblies) rather than runtime/memory benchmarking Your input is not a bacterial isolate hybrid read set — Unicycler is designed exclusively for bacterial isolates, so timing comparisons on eukaryotic or metagenomic data are out of scope You are comparing Plassembler v1.2.0 results against v1.3.0 results directly, since the old benchmarking used different simulated read sets (R9 vs R10), making the comparison unfair

skills.search_text: multi-tool-binning-benchmark-comparison Use when a binning tool's relative performance on large, complex high-dimensional datasets must be quantified against baselines using standard AMBER metrics (purity, completeness, F1) on shared inputs. skills.name: multi-tool-result-harmonization
skills.search_text: multi-tool-result-harmonization Use when multiple viral-detection tools (VirSorter2, VIBRANT, DeepVirFinder, CheckV, MMseqs2 taxonomy) have been run on the same assembled contig library and per-contig viral calls must be reconciled into a single confidence-scored table. Input is raw reads or FASTQ rather than an assembled contig library — detection must run on contigs first Only one detection tool's output is available — the ≥2-criteria confidence rule cannot be applied The goal is read-level virus detection or assembly itself rather than reconciling existing per-contig tool predictions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Harmonizes contig identifiers across the outputs of multiple viral-detection tools used in ViroProfiler (VirSorter2, VIBRANT, DeepVirFinder, CheckV, plus MMseqs2 taxonomy annotation) and applies a confidence-scoring rule to classify viral contigs as 'high confident' (≥2 tools) or 'low confident' (exactly 1 tool). metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Harmonizes contig identifiers across the outputs of multiple viral-detection tools used in ViroProfiler (VirSorter2, VIBRANT, DeepVirFinder, CheckV, plus MMseqs2 taxonomy annotation) and applies a confidence-scoring rule to classify viral contigs as 'high confident' (≥2 tools) or 'low confident' (exactly 1 tool).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or FASTQ rather than an assembled contig library — detection must run on contigs first Only one detection tool's output is available — the ≥2-criteria confidence rule cannot be applied The goal is read-level virus detection or assembly itself rather than reconciling existing per-contig tool predictions

skills.description: Use when a trained multiclass classifier (e.g., PM-CNN predicting Control/Periodontitis/Gingivitis or gut disease labels) must be scored on held-out samples with the five paper-standard metrics and reported to a metrics CSV.
skills.name: multiclass-classification-metric-computation
skills.search_text: multiclass-classification-metric-computation Use when a trained multiclass classifier (e.g., PM-CNN predicting Control/Periodontitis/Gingivitis or gut disease labels) must be scored on held-out samples with the five paper-standard metrics and reported to a metrics CSV. The task is regression or ranking rather than labeled multiclass classification with discrete status labels. The input abundance table has not yet been reordered by the phylogeny-based multi-layer hierarchical clustering order, so the model itself cannot be validly trained or tested. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computes Kappa, Recall, Accuracy, Precision, and F1 scores to quantify PM-CNN classification performance on held-out human microbiome samples, following the paper's Results 3.2 evaluation protocol. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae013
skills.summary: Computes Kappa, Recall, Accuracy, Precision, and F1 scores to quantify PM-CNN classification performance on held-out human microbiome samples, following the paper's Results 3.2 evaluation protocol.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is regression or ranking rather than labeled multiclass classification with discrete status labels. The input abundance table has not yet been reordered by the phylogeny-based multi-layer hierarchical clustering order, so the model itself cannot be validly trained or tested.

skills.description: Use when multiple network inference association matrices (interaction + pvalue matrices) have been filtered and consensus edges must be assembled with per-method weights for export to the MIND database.
skills.name: multigraph-edge-weight-annotation
skills.search_text: multigraph-edge-weight-annotation Use when multiple network inference association matrices (interaction + pvalue matrices) have been filtered and consensus edges must be assembled with per-method weights for export to the MIND database. Input is raw 16S sequencing reads or unfiltered interaction matrices — the consensus assembly presupposes eight already-filtered NI association matrices Only a single inference network is available — SV/SS consensus thresholds across w=8 networks cannot be computed The goal is the 16S processing steps upstream of network inference (demultiplexing, trimming, OTU assignment) rather than consensus network assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assembles edges surviving the MiCoNE simple voting (SV) and scaled-sum (SS) consensus thresholds into a multigraph whose edges carry the per-network-inference-method interaction weights, exported as a MIND-compatible JSON file. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: Assembles edges surviving the MiCoNE simple voting (SV) and scaled-sum (SS) consensus thresholds into a multigraph whose edges carry the per-network-inference-method interaction weights, exported as a MIND-compatible JSON file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw 16S sequencing reads or unfiltered interaction matrices — the consensus assembly presupposes eight already-filtered NI association matrices Only a single inference network is available — SV/SS consensus thresholds across w=8 networks cannot be computed The goal is the 16S processing steps upstream of network inference (demultiplexing, trimming, OTU assignment) rather than consensus network assembly

skills.description: Use when you have a sparse high-throughput OTU/taxon count matrix with sample group labels and need to identify features differentially abundant between two or more groups.
skills.name: multiple-sample-group-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: multiple-sample-group-statistical-testing Use when you have a sparse high-throughput OTU/taxon count matrix with sample group labels and need to identify features differentially abundant between two or more groups. Input is not sparse marker-gene count data (e.g. already normalized composition data or non-sequencing feature tables) The goal is feature correlation testing rather than differential abundance between two or more groups Differential abundance testing of sparse microbial marker-gene (OTU/taxon) count features across two or more sample groups using metagenomeSeq, whose normalization and statistical model explicitly address undersampling of microbial communities. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nmeth.2658
skills.summary: Differential abundance testing of sparse microbial marker-gene (OTU/taxon) count features across two or more sample groups using metagenomeSeq, whose normalization and statistical model explicitly address undersampling of microbial communities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not sparse marker-gene count data (e.g. already normalized composition data or non-sequencing feature tables) The goal is feature correlation testing rather than differential abundance between two or more groups

skills.description: Use when deep-sequencing reads from a mixed sample (shotgun or amplicon, e.g. 454 Titanium pyrosequencing or Illumina viral data) must be placed in a common reference coordinate frame before windowed error correction or haplotype reconstruction.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-construction-from-ngs-reads
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-construction-from-ngs-reads Use when deep-sequencing reads from a mixed sample (shotgun or amplicon, e.g. 454 Titanium pyrosequencing or Illumina viral data) must be placed in a common reference coordinate frame before windowed error correction or haplotype reconstruction. The reads are already assembled in a gap-padded MSA against the reference, so re-aligning would only duplicate ShoRAH's first step. The goal is global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction with current ShoRAH2, where global mode is disabled — instead use ShoRAH1 v1.1.3 or the V-pipe global haplotype options. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Builds a multiple sequence alignment (MSA) of error-prone NGS reads from a genetically heterogeneous mixed sample (e.g., 454 Titanium pyrosequencing reads of HIV-1 subtype B pol) against a reference sequence, putting all reads in a common coordinate frame as the first step of ShoRAH's local haplotype reconstruction pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: Builds a multiple sequence alignment (MSA) of error-prone NGS reads from a genetically heterogeneous mixed sample (e.g., 454 Titanium pyrosequencing reads of HIV-1 subtype B pol) against a reference sequence, putting all reads in a common coordinate frame as the first step of ShoRAH's local haplotype reconstruction pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are already assembled in a gap-padded MSA against the reference, so re-aligning would only duplicate ShoRAH's first step. The goal is global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction with current ShoRAH2, where global mode is disabled — instead use ShoRAH1 v1.1.3 or the V-pipe global haplotype options.

skills.description: Use when rRNA gene sequences contain large insertion sequences (≥10 bp) that must be stripped prior to multiple sequence alignment, or when building a phylogeny from divergent 16S sequences (e.g. CPR) where naive alignment would be unreliable.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-curation
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-curation Use when rRNA gene sequences contain large insertion sequences (≥10 bp) that must be stripped prior to multiple sequence alignment, or when building a phylogeny from divergent 16S sequences (e.g. CPR) where naive alignment would be unreliable. Sequences lack rRNA introns/insertions — insertion stripping is unnecessary and the standard alignment suffices The alignment is for protein-coding genes rather than structurally modeled rRNA genes — SSUAlign per-domain structural models do not apply Sequences are shorter than the ≥800 bp aligned-residue threshold and are intended for phylogenetic placement rather than being excluded http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Curates 16S rRNA gene sequences before phylogenetic inference by removing self-splicing intron insertions (≥10 bp), structurally aligning with SSUAlign, and applying length/redundancy filters so CPR monophyly is not an artifact of insertion sequences. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: Curates 16S rRNA gene sequences before phylogenetic inference by removing self-splicing intron insertions (≥10 bp), structurally aligning with SSUAlign, and applying length/redundancy filters so CPR monophyly is not an artifact of insertion sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences lack rRNA introns/insertions — insertion stripping is unnecessary and the standard alignment suffices The alignment is for protein-coding genes rather than structurally modeled rRNA genes — SSUAlign per-domain structural models do not apply Sequences are shorter than the ≥800 bp aligned-residue threshold and are intended for phylogenetic placement rather than being excluded

skills.description: Use when evaluating individual loci in a cg/wgMLST schema — i.e. when you have per-locus FASTA files of allelic diversity and want to inspect alignment/phylogenetic structure of alleles per locus.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-mlst-alleles
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-mlst-alleles Use when evaluating individual loci in a cg/wgMLST schema — i.e. when you have per-locus FASTA files of allelic diversity and want to inspect alignment/phylogenetic structure of alleles per locus. You only need an allelic profile matrix or allele calls, not per-locus alignment/phylogeny inspection — run chewBBACA AlleleCall instead You are adapting an external schema (PrepExternalSchema), which removes non-translating alleles rather than aligning allelic diversity Input is whole-cgMLST concatenated data rather than per-locus allele FASTA files http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Generates per-locus nucleotide multiple sequence alignments (MAFFT) and neighbour-joining trees (ClustalW2) for every locus in a chewBBACA cg/wgMLST schema, enabling assessment of the allelic variability at each locus during schema evaluation. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000166
skills.summary: Generates per-locus nucleotide multiple sequence alignments (MAFFT) and neighbour-joining trees (ClustalW2) for every locus in a chewBBACA cg/wgMLST schema, enabling assessment of the allelic variability at each locus during schema evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need an allelic profile matrix or allele calls, not per-locus alignment/phylogeny inspection — run chewBBACA AlleleCall instead You are adapting an external schema (PrepExternalSchema), which removes non-translating alleles rather than aligning allelic diversity Input is whole-cgMLST concatenated data rather than per-locus allele FASTA files

skills.description: Use when you have recovered homologous single-copy marker sequences (e.g. USCOs/near-USCOs) for multiple specimens and need per-locus multiple sequence alignments as input for trimming, concatenation, and tree inference.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-ortholog-loci
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-ortholog-loci Use when you have recovered homologous single-copy marker sequences (e.g. USCOs/near-USCOs) for multiple specimens and need per-locus multiple sequence alignments as input for trimming, concatenation, and tree inference. The sequences are not homologous single-copy markers (e.g. variable-copy or chimeric sequences) — the article recommends limiting reference use to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences Only a single sequence is available per locus, so no multiple sequence alignment can be computed The goal is marker retrieval from raw WGS reads itself — that is Patchwork's upstream role (DIAMOND search, hit stitching, sliding-window trimming), not the downstream MSA step http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Aligns Patchwork-recovered ortholog marker sequences (e.g. 957 near-USCOs from H. robusta) per-locus with MAFFT using --globalpair --ep 0.123, so that the resulting alignments can be trimmed, concatenated, and used for maximum-likelihood phylogenomic tree inference. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Aligns Patchwork-recovered ortholog marker sequences (e.g. 957 near-USCOs from H. robusta) per-locus with MAFFT using --globalpair --ep 0.123, so that the resulting alignments can be trimmed, concatenated, and used for maximum-likelihood phylogenomic tree inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequences are not homologous single-copy markers (e.g. variable-copy or chimeric sequences) — the article recommends limiting reference use to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences Only a single sequence is available per locus, so no multiple sequence alignment can be computed The goal is marker retrieval from raw WGS reads itself — that is Patchwork's upstream role (DIAMOND search, hit stitching, sliding-window trimming), not the downstream MSA step

skills.description: Use when starting from PROKKA-annotated genome GFF files (e.g. 56 RefSeq coronavirus genomes) and homologous gene families must be aligned, tree-ordered, and collapsed into representative sequences for downstream LCA assignment.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-viral-genes
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-viral-genes Use when starting from PROKKA-annotated genome GFF files (e.g. 56 RefSeq coronavirus genomes) and homologous gene families must be aligned, tree-ordered, and collapsed into representative sequences for downstream LCA assignment. Genomes are unknown or unannotatable — 'HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to efficiently cluster sequences. Probes cannot be designed for targets with unknown, or unannotatable genomes.' Input is raw, unannotated assemblies or reads rather than annotated GFF files; annotation (PROKKA is suggested) must precede clustering. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Clusters homologous gene sequences from annotated viral genomes using supported multiple sequence aligners (MAFFT 7.0+, MUSCLE 3.8.425+, CLUSTAL OMEGA 1.2.1+) with BioPerl-built neighbour-joining gene trees, collapsing sequences at nodes with root-to-tip divergence of at most 15% into representative consensus sequences (RepSeq.fna). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: Clusters homologous gene sequences from annotated viral genomes using supported multiple sequence aligners (MAFFT 7.0+, MUSCLE 3.8.425+, CLUSTAL OMEGA 1.2.1+) with BioPerl-built neighbour-joining gene trees, collapsing sequences at nodes with root-to-tip divergence of at most 15% into representative consensus sequences (RepSeq.fna).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genomes are unknown or unannotatable — 'HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to efficiently cluster sequences. Probes cannot be designed for targets with unknown, or unannotatable genomes.' Input is raw, unannotated assemblies or reads rather than annotated GFF files; annotation (PROKKA is suggested) must precede clustering.

skills.description: Use when you need to type or classify viral genomes/OTUs from a conserved marker gene (e.g., L1) and place them on a phylogeny against reference sequences from RefSeq.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-viral-genes
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-viral-genes Use when you need to type or classify viral genomes/OTUs from a conserved marker gene (e.g., L1) and place them on a phylogeny against reference sequences from RefSeq. The viral genomes lack the target marker gene (e.g., non-papillomaviruses without an L1 gene) — use whole-genome or different marker approaches instead The goal is abundance/taxonomic profiling of metagenomic reads rather than phylogenetic placement of assembled genomes — use Kraken2/Bracken with a customized database instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Align a homologous viral gene set (e.g., the L1 major capsid protein gene extracted from Papillomaviridae genomes) with MAFFT and infer a maximum-likelihood phylogeny with IQ-TREE to resolve taxonomy and phylogenetic clade structure across vOTUs. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Align a homologous viral gene set (e.g., the L1 major capsid protein gene extracted from Papillomaviridae genomes) with MAFFT and infer a maximum-likelihood phylogeny with IQ-TREE to resolve taxonomy and phylogenetic clade structure across vOTUs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The viral genomes lack the target marker gene (e.g., non-papillomaviruses without an L1 gene) — use whole-genome or different marker approaches instead The goal is abundance/taxonomic profiling of metagenomic reads rather than phylogenetic placement of assembled genomes — use Kraken2/Bracken with a customized database instead

skills.description: Use when many raw permutational ANOVA P-values are produced from pairwise treatment-group contrasts (e.g. LEVO vs OTHERS, CLA vs OTHERS across time points) and adjusted P-values must be reported to avoid false-positive group differences.
skills.name: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction Use when many raw permutational ANOVA P-values are produced from pairwise treatment-group contrasts (e.g. LEVO vs OTHERS, CLA vs OTHERS across time points) and adjusted P-values must be reported to avoid false-positive group differences. The P-values are already multiple-testing adjusted (e.g. previously Bonferroni- or FDR-corrected), so a second correction would over-conservatively inflate them There is a single pre-planned comparison rather than a family of pairwise contrasts (LEVO/CLA vs OTHERS across time points), making correction unnecessary The input is upstream raw variant detection (FASTQ/BAM pileups from cellSNP-lite) — variant flagging is MetaQuad's job, not the correction step http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies Bonferroni correction to raw P-values from multilevel pairwise.adonis (permutational multivariate ANOVA) tests so that group-differentiation claims across antibiotic treatment arms and time points (e.g. LEVO vs OTHERS, CLA vs OTHERS at T+6W) retain family-wise error control. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Applies Bonferroni correction to raw P-values from multilevel pairwise.adonis (permutational multivariate ANOVA) tests so that group-differentiation claims across antibiotic treatment arms and time points (e.g. LEVO vs OTHERS, CLA vs OTHERS at T+6W) retain family-wise error control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The P-values are already multiple-testing adjusted (e.g. previously Bonferroni- or FDR-corrected), so a second correction would over-conservatively inflate them There is a single pre-planned comparison rather than a family of pairwise contrasts (LEVO/CLA vs OTHERS across time points), making correction unnecessary The input is upstream raw variant detection (FASTQ/BAM pileups from cellSNP-lite) — variant flagging is MetaQuad's job, not the correction step

skills.description: Use when a multivariable association analysis (e.g. MaAsLin2 on the FunOMIC-derived 2,679-sample abundance tables) tests many fungal taxa against many metadata variables and raw p-values must be corrected before calling significance.
skills.name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-fdr-correction Use when a multivariable association analysis (e.g. MaAsLin2 on the FunOMIC-derived 2,679-sample abundance tables) tests many fungal taxa against many metadata variables and raw p-values must be corrected before calling significance. When only a single hypothesis or a small pre-specified set of taxa–metadata tests is performed — correction would only reduce power without meaningfully changing the error rate When the abundance table has not yet been generated by FunOMIC-T/FunOMIC-P mapping; this skill corrects association results, it does not produce the feature matrix For descriptive network visualization, which in this paper was filtered on raw p-values (<0.001) and absolute correlation coefficient >0.05 rather than FDR http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies multiple-testing correction (false discovery rate control) when ranking thousands of fungal taxa–metadata associations, so only associations surviving FDR < 0.05 are reported as significant. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Applies multiple-testing correction (false discovery rate control) when ranking thousands of fungal taxa–metadata associations, so only associations surviving FDR < 0.05 are reported as significant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single hypothesis or a small pre-specified set of taxa–metadata tests is performed — correction would only reduce power without meaningfully changing the error rate When the abundance table has not yet been generated by FunOMIC-T/FunOMIC-P mapping; this skill corrects association results, it does not produce the feature matrix For descriptive network visualization, which in this paper was filtered on raw p-values (<0.001) and absolute correlation coefficient >0.05 rather than FDR

skills.description: Use when a taxa–SNP regression sweep (e.g., mbQTL linearTaxaSnp over microbeAbund × SnpFile) yields thousands of P values that must be corrected for multiple comparisons and diagnostic-checked before calling mbQTL associations.
skills.name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-fdr-correction Use when a taxa–SNP regression sweep (e.g., mbQTL linearTaxaSnp over microbeAbund × SnpFile) yields thousands of P values that must be corrected for multiple comparisons and diagnostic-checked before calling mbQTL associations. Taxa are being analyzed as presence/absence (categorical) variables — mbQTL uses logistic regression for that case, not the linear-regression/FDR workflow The goal is correlation-based estimation of rho values for taxa–SNP association and linkage disequilibrium (Approach B-type analysis), rather than linear regression testing Only one taxon–SNP hypothesis is tested, so no multiple-testing correction is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies FDR (and Bonferroni) multiple-testing correction to taxa–SNP association results from mbQTL's linearTaxaSnp(), and evaluates the resulting P value distributions with histPvalueLm() and qqPlotLm() so that significant microbe–SNV calls are statistically valid across the large number of tested taxon–SNP pairs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad565
skills.summary: Applies FDR (and Bonferroni) multiple-testing correction to taxa–SNP association results from mbQTL's linearTaxaSnp(), and evaluates the resulting P value distributions with histPvalueLm() and qqPlotLm() so that significant microbe–SNV calls are statistically valid across the large number of tested taxon–SNP pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Taxa are being analyzed as presence/absence (categorical) variables — mbQTL uses logistic regression for that case, not the linear-regression/FDR workflow The goal is correlation-based estimation of rho values for taxa–SNP association and linkage disequilibrium (Approach B-type analysis), rather than linear regression testing Only one taxon–SNP hypothesis is tested, so no multiple-testing correction is needed

skills.description: Use when DAA results on pathway-level KEGG abundance tables contain raw p_val columns and significance must be judged on p_adjust, because hundreds of pathways are tested at once.
skills.name: multiple-testing-pvalue-adjustment
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-pvalue-adjustment Use when DAA results on pathway-level KEGG abundance tables contain raw p_val columns and significance must be judged on p_adjust, because hundreds of pathways are tested at once. Input is a raw KO abundance table that has not yet been converted to KEGG pathway-level abundance — ko2kegg_abundance() must run first The analysis goal is gene-set-level enrichment (use pathway_gsea() instead of per-pathway DAA testing) Fewer than a handful of features are tested, so multiple-testing correction would be unnecessary or uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Adjusts per-pathway p-values from differential abundance analysis (DAA) of PICRUSt2-predicted functional profiles for multiple hypothesis testing, so that the p_adjust column of ggpicrust2's pathway_daa() results reflects corrected significance across the many KEGG pathway features tested simultaneously. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad470
skills.summary: Adjusts per-pathway p-values from differential abundance analysis (DAA) of PICRUSt2-predicted functional profiles for multiple hypothesis testing, so that the p_adjust column of ggpicrust2's pathway_daa() results reflects corrected significance across the many KEGG pathway features tested simultaneously.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw KO abundance table that has not yet been converted to KEGG pathway-level abundance — ko2kegg_abundance() must run first The analysis goal is gene-set-level enrichment (use pathway_gsea() instead of per-pathway DAA testing) Fewer than a handful of features are tested, so multiple-testing correction would be unnecessary or uninformative

skills.description: Use when a gene-level differential expression results table contains raw p-values from a negative-binomial or similar GLM fit and per-gene FDR-adjusted values (padj) are needed for downstream filtering or enrichment input.
skills.name: multiple-testing-pvalue-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-pvalue-correction Use when a gene-level differential expression results table contains raw p-values from a negative-binomial or similar GLM fit and per-gene FDR-adjusted values (padj) are needed for downstream filtering or enrichment input. Input is already a table of adjusted p-values (padj) exported from DESeq2Shiny — no second correction should be applied Analysis goal is single-cell RNA-seq (use the Seurat-based SeuratV3Wizard path in NASQAR instead of DESeq2Shiny) Input is pre-processed metagenomic count data, where SHAMAN performs its own differential analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment to per-gene p-values produced by bulk RNA-seq differential expression analysis (e.g., the DESeq2 negative-binomial model wrapped by NASQAR's Deseq2Shiny/DEApp), yielding per-gene adjusted p-values that control for thousands of simultaneous gene-level tests. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03577-4
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment to per-gene p-values produced by bulk RNA-seq differential expression analysis (e.g., the DESeq2 negative-binomial model wrapped by NASQAR's Deseq2Shiny/DEApp), yielding per-gene adjusted p-values that control for thousands of simultaneous gene-level tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a table of adjusted p-values (padj) exported from DESeq2Shiny — no second correction should be applied Analysis goal is single-cell RNA-seq (use the Seurat-based SeuratV3Wizard path in NASQAR instead of DESeq2Shiny) Input is pre-processed metagenomic count data, where SHAMAN performs its own differential analysis

skills.description: Use when a pipeline stage produces many scattered per-sample QC/classification outputs (Kraken2/Centrifuge reports, Krona charts, preprocessing QC) and a single aggregated HTML report is needed to assess contamination before assembly.

skills.search_text: multiqc-aggregation-of-qc-outputs Use when a pipeline stage produces many scattered per-sample QC/classification outputs (Kraken2/Centrifuge reports, Krona charts, preprocessing QC) and a single aggregated HTML report is needed to assess contamination before assembly. The input reads are long reads or hybrid data at this stage — classification/QC of this kind is applied to preprocessed short reads only, since not every tool is valid for every read type You need quantitative taxonomic abundance estimation rather than a QC-style contamination screen before assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Aggregates per-sample, per-tool QC outputs (e.g., Kraken2/Centrifuge read-classification reports, Krona charts, read-preprocessing QC) into a single interactive MultiQC HTML report within the nf-core/mag pipeline, enabling contamination assessment and QC review before metagenome assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Aggregates per-sample, per-tool QC outputs (e.g., Kraken2/Centrifuge read-classification reports, Krona charts, read-preprocessing QC) into a single interactive MultiQC HTML report within the nf-core/mag pipeline, enabling contamination assessment and QC review before metagenome assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input reads are long reads or hybrid data at this stage — classification/QC of this kind is applied to preprocessed short reads only, since not every tool is valid for every read type You need quantitative taxonomic abundance estimation rather than a QC-style contamination screen before assembly

skills.description: Use when a metagenomics QC stage has produced per-sample FastQC HTML/zip reports for raw and trimmed FASTQ pairs and you need one aggregated overview to verify adapter removal and Q20 trimming.
skills.name: multiqc-report-aggregation
skills.search_text: multiqc-report-aggregation Use when a metagenomics QC stage has produced per-sample FastQC HTML/zip reports for raw and trimmed FASTQ pairs and you need one aggregated overview to verify adapter removal and Q20 trimming. No per-sample QC reports exist yet — run FastQC on the raw and trimmed FASTQ files before aggregating Input is not FASTQ-based Illumina (meta)genomic data processed by the RiboTaxa QC stage, so before/after FastQC comparison is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregate per-file FastQC quality reports (before and after bbduk.sh adapter/quality trimming) from the RiboTaxa quality-control stage into a single MultiQC HTML report, so read-quality improvements across all (meta)genomic FASTQ files can be reviewed at a glance. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Aggregate per-file FastQC quality reports (before and after bbduk.sh adapter/quality trimming) from the RiboTaxa quality-control stage into a single MultiQC HTML report, so read-quality improvements across all (meta)genomic FASTQ files can be reviewed at a glance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No per-sample QC reports exist yet — run FastQC on the raw and trimmed FASTQ files before aggregating Input is not FASTQ-based Illumina (meta)genomic data processed by the RiboTaxa QC stage, so before/after FastQC comparison is meaningless

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing a 16S rRNA taxonomic classifier that needs local motif features (e.g., k=3/5/7 convolution windows over BPE-tokenized DNA) fused with long-range transformer context.
skills.name: multiscale-cnn-sequence-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: multiscale-cnn-sequence-feature-extraction Use when building or reproducing a 16S rRNA taxonomic classifier that needs local motif features (e.g., k=3/5/7 convolution windows over BPE-tokenized DNA) fused with long-range transformer context. Input is already a feature table or k-mer count matrix rather than raw sequence data The task requires long-range dependencies only and you intend a BERT-only model — the article notes a from-scratch transformer alone underperforms substantially at the species rank, but the CNN pathway specifically targets local motif capture Input sequences carry base-level quality scores or require quality-aware modeling — DeepTaxa operates on FASTA-formatted sequences only http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Extract local sequence features from 16S rRNA sequences using DeepTaxa's multiscale CNN pathway: 896-dimensional token embeddings over the DNABERT-2 BPE vocabulary convolved with parallel kernels of size 3, 5, and 7 at 256 filters each, then projected back to 896 dimensions for downstream rank-specific classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Extract local sequence features from 16S rRNA sequences using DeepTaxa's multiscale CNN pathway: 896-dimensional token embeddings over the DNABERT-2 BPE vocabulary convolved with parallel kernels of size 3, 5, and 7 at 256 filters each, then projected back to 896 dimensions for downstream rank-specific classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or k-mer count matrix rather than raw sequence data The task requires long-range dependencies only and you intend a BERT-only model — the article notes a from-scratch transformer alone underperforms substantially at the species rank, but the CNN pathway specifically targets local motif capture Input sequences carry base-level quality scores or require quality-aware modeling — DeepTaxa operates on FASTA-formatted sequences only

skills.description: Use when two multivariate feature tables measured on the same plot/observation units (e.g. Sentinel-1 gamma_0 temporal-stack metrics vs ALS structural metrics) must be compared for shared variance and axis-level association.
skills.name: multivariate-canonical-axis-interpretation
skills.search_text: multivariate-canonical-axis-interpretation Use when two multivariate feature tables measured on the same plot/observation units (e.g. Sentinel-1 gamma_0 temporal-stack metrics vs ALS structural metrics) must be compared for shared variance and axis-level association. Input rows are species/biodiversity observations rather than aligned per-plot structural metric tables — biodiversity modelling in this study used NMDS and R² comparisons, not CCoA Sentinel-1 data are raw GRDH digital numbers rather than processed gamma_0 temporal stacks — apply the SNAP/GPT pre-processing workflow first (orbit, border/thermal noise, calibration, terrain flattening, terrain correction) The two variable sets are not measured on the same spatial units (e.g. mismatched plot extents or resolutions), so canonical pairs would be confounded by location rather than structure http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Perform and interpret canonical correlation analysis (CCoA) between two multivariate remote-sensing variable sets — in this study the 13 radar-derived (Sentinel-1 VH/VV gamma_0) plot-mean habitat metrics and the corresponding ALS-derived structural metrics — to quantify shared structural information and identify statistically significant canonical axis pairs. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Perform and interpret canonical correlation analysis (CCoA) between two multivariate remote-sensing variable sets — in this study the 13 radar-derived (Sentinel-1 VH/VV gamma_0) plot-mean habitat metrics and the corresponding ALS-derived structural metrics — to quantify shared structural information and identify statistically significant canonical axis pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input rows are species/biodiversity observations rather than aligned per-plot structural metric tables — biodiversity modelling in this study used NMDS and R² comparisons, not CCoA Sentinel-1 data are raw GRDH digital numbers rather than processed gamma_0 temporal stacks — apply the SNAP/GPT pre-processing workflow first (orbit, border/thermal noise, calibration, terrain flattening, terrain correction) The two variable sets are not measured on the same spatial units (e.g. mismatched plot extents or resolutions), so canonical pairs would be confounded by location rather than structure

skills.description: Use when ground-truth presence-absence community data (e.g. 463 monitoring plots across 12 taxa/functional groups) must be reduced to per-plot ordination axes (NMDS1/NMDS2) to model assemblage composition against remote-sensing predictors.
skills.name: multivariate-site-score-extraction
skills.search_text: multivariate-site-score-extraction Use when ground-truth presence-absence community data (e.g. 463 monitoring plots across 12 taxa/functional groups) must be reduced to per-plot ordination axes (NMDS1/NMDS2) to model assemblage composition against remote-sensing predictors. The goal is modelling α-diversity (species richness) or phylogenetic diversity rather than assemblage composition (β-diversity) — those use different response variables in the paper. Only spectral or radar predictor stacks are available with no ground-truth species composition data — this skill derives responses from ground-truth biodiversity data, not Sentinel-1 gamma_0 statistics. Community data are abundance/continuous counts where Bray-Curtis on presence-absence would discard meaningful information; verify the presence-absence transformation is appropriate first. Quantifies species assemblage composition (β-diversity) per functional group as NMDS ordination site scores derived from presence-absence data, so the scores can serve as response variables in biodiversity models built from ALS and Sentinel-1 radar metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Quantifies species assemblage composition (β-diversity) per functional group as NMDS ordination site scores derived from presence-absence data, so the scores can serve as response variables in biodiversity models built from ALS and Sentinel-1 radar metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is modelling α-diversity (species richness) or phylogenetic diversity rather than assemblage composition (β-diversity) — those use different response variables in the paper. Only spectral or radar predictor stacks are available with no ground-truth species composition data — this skill derives responses from ground-truth biodiversity data, not Sentinel-1 gamma_0 statistics. Community data are abundance/continuous counts where Bray-Curtis on presence-absence would discard meaningful information; verify the presence-absence transformation is appropriate first.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a hotspot mutation caller on nanopore data and you need simulated FASTQ mixtures with known truth sets across mutant frequencies, replicates, and negative controls.
skills.name: mutation-frequency-mixture-design
skills.search_text: mutation-frequency-mixture-design Use when benchmarking a hotspot mutation caller on nanopore data and you need simulated FASTQ mixtures with known truth sets across mutant frequencies, replicates, and negative controls. Input is real experimental nanopore data without a known truth set — this skill designs simulation mixtures with engineered mutant reads, not analysis of real samples You need whole-genome or non-hotspot variant calling on long reads — the mixtures are restricted to a small BED-defined hotspot panel, not genome-wide discovery Training data for deep-learning callers (e.g. iGDA, PEPPER-Margin-DeepVariant) is required — the article notes simulated ONT data were 'not generated on the same experimental and sequencing platforms' and their own experimental data were insufficient as a training dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Design in silico nanopore read mixtures carrying hotspot mutations at graded mutant frequencies (10%, 5%, 1%, 0.5%, 0.1%) with wild-type/mutant read counts of 9000:1000 per hotspot, to benchmark hotspot mutation detection methods such as Nano2NGS-Muta. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac033
skills.summary: Design in silico nanopore read mixtures carrying hotspot mutations at graded mutant frequencies (10%, 5%, 1%, 0.5%, 0.1%) with wild-type/mutant read counts of 9000:1000 per hotspot, to benchmark hotspot mutation detection methods such as Nano2NGS-Muta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental nanopore data without a known truth set — this skill designs simulation mixtures with engineered mutant reads, not analysis of real samples You need whole-genome or non-hotspot variant calling on long reads — the mixtures are restricted to a small BED-defined hotspot panel, not genome-wide discovery Training data for deep-learning callers (e.g. iGDA, PEPPER-Margin-DeepVariant) is required — the article notes simulated ONT data were 'not generated on the same experimental and sequencing platforms' and their own experimental data were insufficient as a training dataset

skills.description: Use when both MWAS pathway enrichment results (e.g. sumstats_*_annot.txt from OMARU) and host GWAS pathway enrichment results (e.g. PASCAL output as <Phenotype>_GWAS_<Pathway_reference>.txt) are available and you need to assess their overlap significance.
skills.name: mwas-gwas-pathway-overlap-testing
skills.search_text: mwas-gwas-pathway-overlap-testing Use when both MWAS pathway enrichment results (e.g. sumstats_*_annot.txt from OMARU) and host GWAS pathway enrichment results (e.g. PASCAL output as <Phenotype>_GWAS_<Pathway_reference>.txt) are available and you need to assess their overlap significance. When only one side of the comparison is available (no PASCAL-processed GWAS pathway enrichment file, or no OMARU sumstats_*_annot.txt MWAS results) — the contingency table cannot be built. When the goal is testing overlap of individual taxa or genes rather than biological pathways — use OMARU's taxa-gene linking analysis instead of the MWAS-GWAS pathway interaction module. When a significance threshold other than the enrichment-level P<0.05 definition is required for pathway significance, since the contingency table construction here is defined at that threshold. http://edamontology.org/topic_3837 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Tests whether biological pathways enriched in a disease metagenome (MWAS) significantly overlap with those enriched in the host germline GWAS, using OMARU's 2x2 contingency-table Fisher's exact test at P<0.05. It quantifies disease-specific pathway-level links between the human genome and metagenome (e.g. PFisher = 0.011 SCZ, 0.008 T2D). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: Tests whether biological pathways enriched in a disease metagenome (MWAS) significantly overlap with those enriched in the host germline GWAS, using OMARU's 2x2 contingency-table Fisher's exact test at P<0.05. It quantifies disease-specific pathway-level links between the human genome and metagenome (e.g. PFisher = 0.011 SCZ, 0.008 T2D).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one side of the comparison is available (no PASCAL-processed GWAS pathway enrichment file, or no OMARU sumstats_*_annot.txt MWAS results) — the contingency table cannot be built. When the goal is testing overlap of individual taxa or genes rather than biological pathways — use OMARU's taxa-gene linking analysis instead of the MWAS-GWAS pathway interaction module. When a significance threshold other than the enrichment-level P<0.05 definition is required for pathway significance, since the contingency table construction here is defined at that threshold.

skills.description: Use when raw FASTQ reads from MTBC isolates need rapid per-drug resistance calls (e.g. rifampicin, isoniazid, ethambutol) without assembling genomes or variant calling, or when benchmarking against phenotypic DST or KvarQ.
skills.name: mycobacterial-drug-resistance-prediction
skills.search_text: mycobacterial-drug-resistance-prediction Use when raw FASTQ reads from MTBC isolates need rapid per-drug resistance calls (e.g. rifampicin, isoniazid, ethambutol) without assembling genomes or variant calling, or when benchmarking against phenotypic DST or KvarQ. The sample may contain non-tuberculous mycobacteria or mixed strains — such samples are removed for QC or flagged by the >40 heterozygous SNP contamination threshold, so predictions on them are invalid You need pyrazinamide predictions — known pyrazinamide mutations are poorly predictive and the drug is completely excluded from the panel The organism is not one of the supported species (M. tuberculosis, S. aureus, S. sonnei, S. typhi, S. enterica Paratyphi B); the tb panel will not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Predict M. tuberculosis antibiotic resistance directly from raw sequencing reads using Mykrobe predictor's de Bruijn graph approach, then parse the JSON output into per-drug resistant/susceptible calls with the PHAC Mykrobe Parser. On the n=1,609 MTBC_B validation set this yields overall sensitivity/specificity of 82.6%/98.5%. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Predict M. tuberculosis antibiotic resistance directly from raw sequencing reads using Mykrobe predictor's de Bruijn graph approach, then parse the JSON output into per-drug resistant/susceptible calls with the PHAC Mykrobe Parser. On the n=1,609 MTBC_B validation set this yields overall sensitivity/specificity of 82.6%/98.5%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample may contain non-tuberculous mycobacteria or mixed strains — such samples are removed for QC or flagged by the >40 heterozygous SNP contamination threshold, so predictions on them are invalid You need pyrazinamide predictions — known pyrazinamide mutations are poorly predictive and the drug is completely excluded from the panel The organism is not one of the supported species (M. tuberculosis, S. aureus, S. sonnei, S. typhi, S. enterica Paratyphi B); the tb panel will not apply

skills.description: Use when benchmarking host read-removal tools on known-composition microbial data: you need simulated bacterial reads with a ground truth so that false-removal (retention) percentages of Hostile versus HRRT can be measured exactly.
skills.name: mycobacterial-genome-read-simulation
skills.search_text: mycobacterial-genome-read-simulation Use when benchmarking host read-removal tools on known-composition microbial data: you need simulated bacterial reads with a ground truth so that false-removal (retention) percentages of Hostile versus HRRT can be measured exactly. You want to measure human read removal sensitivity on real human data — use 1000 Genomes Project samples instead of simulated bacterial reads Your goal is microbial taxonomic profiling or assembly, not decontamination benchmarking You lack the ground-truth assemblies, so retention percentages cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Simulate paired Illumina short reads and Oxford Nanopore long reads from complete mycobacterial assemblies (DWGSIM and PBSIM2) to benchmark how much host-decontamination tools such as Hostile and HRRT remove non-host microbial reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad728
skills.summary: Simulate paired Illumina short reads and Oxford Nanopore long reads from complete mycobacterial assemblies (DWGSIM and PBSIM2) to benchmark how much host-decontamination tools such as Hostile and HRRT remove non-host microbial reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to measure human read removal sensitivity on real human data — use 1000 Genomes Project samples instead of simulated bacterial reads Your goal is microbial taxonomic profiling or assembly, not decontamination benchmarking You lack the ground-truth assemblies, so retention percentages cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when raw FASTQ reads from suspected mycobacterial isolates (MTBC or NTM, e.g. MGIT culture positives or SRA downloads) need phylo_group/species/lineage calls, or when Mykrobe species calls must be compared against KvarQ lineage labels.
skills.name: mycobacterial-species-identification
skills.search_text: mycobacterial-species-identification Use when raw FASTQ reads from suspected mycobacterial isolates (MTBC or NTM, e.g. MGIT culture positives or SRA downloads) need phylo_group/species/lineage calls, or when Mykrobe species calls must be compared against KvarQ lineage labels. Input samples are already known non-mycobacterial species — the panel targets Mycobacterium (and the parser explicitly drops NTM-positive samples from its output) The goal is antimicrobial resistance prediction rather than species/lineage identification — use the resistance-prediction skill with the tb probe set and mykrobe-parser report output instead Reads are nanopore or other long-read data where this validated depth/conf-thresholded Illumina-style workflow has not been demonstrated http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Identify mycobacterial phylo_group, species, and lineage directly from raw sequencing reads using Mykrobe predictor's species/lineage probe panel (e.g. 202010) with default QC thresholds, discriminating MTBC from non-tuberculous mycobacteria and assigning MTBC lineages concordant with KvarQ. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Identify mycobacterial phylo_group, species, and lineage directly from raw sequencing reads using Mykrobe predictor's species/lineage probe panel (e.g. 202010) with default QC thresholds, discriminating MTBC from non-tuberculous mycobacteria and assigning MTBC lineages concordant with KvarQ.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples are already known non-mycobacterial species — the panel targets Mycobacterium (and the parser explicitly drops NTM-positive samples from its output) The goal is antimicrobial resistance prediction rather than species/lineage identification — use the resistance-prediction skill with the tb probe set and mykrobe-parser report output instead Reads are nanopore or other long-read data where this validated depth/conf-thresholded Illumina-style workflow has not been demonstrated

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples must be profiled for fungal species composition, e.g. building per-sample abundance/prevalence tables for gut, infant, or disease-cohort mycobiome analysis.
skills.name: mycobiome-abundance-table-generation
skills.search_text: mycobiome-abundance-table-generation Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples must be profiled for fungal species composition, e.g. building per-sample abundance/prevalence tables for gut, infant, or disease-cohort mycobiome analysis. Input is amplicon (ITS) data — FunOMIC-T is designed for shotgun metagenomic reads mapped to single-copy marker genes The goal is fungal functional profiling of proteins — use the FunOMIC-P database with Diamond blastx instead Data are non-fungal-targeted RNA-seq or metatranscriptomic reads where the marker-gene mapping model was not validated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Generates per-sample fungal species abundance tables from human shotgun metagenomes by mapping quality-controlled reads to the FunOMIC-T database of 1.69 million fungal single-copy marker genes, enabling downstream taxonomic profiling and prevalence statistics of the human mycobiome. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Generates per-sample fungal species abundance tables from human shotgun metagenomes by mapping quality-controlled reads to the FunOMIC-T database of 1.69 million fungal single-copy marker genes, enabling downstream taxonomic profiling and prevalence statistics of the human mycobiome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is amplicon (ITS) data — FunOMIC-T is designed for shotgun metagenomic reads mapped to single-copy marker genes The goal is fungal functional profiling of proteins — use the FunOMIC-P database with Diamond blastx instead Data are non-fungal-targeted RNA-seq or metatranscriptomic reads where the marker-gene mapping model was not validated

skills.description: Use when fungal taxonomic or functional abundance tables (e.g. from FunOMIC-T/FunOMIC-P profiling) must be tested for significant associations with metadata variables such as health status, country, body site, or DNA extraction method.
skills.name: mycobiome-clinical-variable-mapping
skills.search_text: mycobiome-clinical-variable-mapping Use when fungal taxonomic or functional abundance tables (e.g. from FunOMIC-T/FunOMIC-P profiling) must be tested for significant associations with metadata variables such as health status, country, body site, or DNA extraction method. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than a FunOMIC-derived abundance table — profile reads with FunOMIC first (FunOMIC.sh) before association testing. The study design lacks repeated measures or covariates suited to MaAsLin2's fixed/random-effect formulation; a simple univariate test would suffice. Sample metadata is not available or cannot be joined to the abundance table by sample identifier. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduce multivariable association testing (MaAsLin2, R 4.1.2) linking FunOMIC-derived fungal taxonomic/functional abundance profiles of 2,679 human metagenome samples to clinical and demographic metadata, identifying significant species–metadata associations at FDR < 0.05. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Reproduce multivariable association testing (MaAsLin2, R 4.1.2) linking FunOMIC-derived fungal taxonomic/functional abundance profiles of 2,679 human metagenome samples to clinical and demographic metadata, identifying significant species–metadata associations at FDR < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than a FunOMIC-derived abundance table — profile reads with FunOMIC first (FunOMIC.sh) before association testing. The study design lacks repeated measures or covariates suited to MaAsLin2's fixed/random-effect formulation; a simple univariate test would suffice. Sample metadata is not available or cannot be joined to the abundance table by sample identifier.

skills.name: mykrobe-output-parsing
skills.search_text: mykrobe-output-parsing Use when you have raw Mykrobe predictor . outputs (e.g. from MTBC_A1 or St_B1 isolates run with --format ) and need per-mutation, per-genetic-region tabular data for per-drug error or concordance tables. Mykrobe output is in text/CSV format rather than JSON — Mykrobe Parser only works with JSON files produced via --format  You need a unified parser for species beyond M. tuberculosis / S. aureus — the parser targets the Mycobacterium tuberculosis-specific results of Mykrobe You need non-tuberculous mycobacteria results retained — the parser removes such samples for quality control purposes http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Parses Mykrobe predictor JSON resistance-call outputs into a tidy per-sample CSV (output-report.csv) with mutations separated into individual genetic regions, using the phac-nml mykrobe-parser R script so downstream error-rate and genotype-concordance analyses can be computed. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Parses Mykrobe predictor JSON resistance-call outputs into a tidy per-sample CSV (output-report.csv) with mutations separated into individual genetic regions, using the phac-nml mykrobe-parser R script so downstream error-rate and genotype-concordance analyses can be computed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Mykrobe output is in text/CSV format rather than JSON — Mykrobe Parser only works with JSON files produced via --format  You need a unified parser for species beyond M. tuberculosis / S. aureus — the parser targets the Mycobacterium tuberculosis-specific results of Mykrobe You need non-tuberculous mycobacteria results retained — the parser removes such samples for quality control purposes
