skills.search_text: mysql-sample-record-querying Use when sample metadata held in the MetaLIMS MySQL database must be queried through PHP's mysqli interface and mapped — including lab-specific custom fields — to build a Clarity LIMS-compatible sequencing submission form. The lab does not need to interface with the proprietary Clarity LIMS system used by some sequencing facilities — the mapping is Clarity-specific The sample metadata is not stored in MetaLIMS's MySQL schema (e.g. raw spreadsheets or another LIMS's database) and cannot be queried via mysqli The requirement is to record or manage NGS or analysis data, which MetaLIMS explicitly does not handle Retrieves stored sample metadata (generic sample collection fields, DNA/RNA processing fields, and lab-specific custom fields) from MetaLIMS's MySQL 5.5.43 database via the PHP mysqli module, as the data-extraction step that feeds Clarity LIMS-compatible sequencing submission form generation. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/gix025
skills.summary: Retrieves stored sample metadata (generic sample collection fields, DNA/RNA processing fields, and lab-specific custom fields) from MetaLIMS's MySQL 5.5.43 database via the PHP mysqli module, as the data-extraction step that feeds Clarity LIMS-compatible sequencing submission form generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The lab does not need to interface with the proprietary Clarity LIMS system used by some sequencing facilities — the mapping is Clarity-specific The sample metadata is not stored in MetaLIMS's MySQL schema (e.g. raw spreadsheets or another LIMS's database) and cannot be queried via mysqli The requirement is to record or manage NGS or analysis data, which MetaLIMS explicitly does not handle

skills.description: Use when benchmarking sequence recovery of paired-end Illumina assembly against a naive perfect-overlap baseline on a control library (e.g. SRA024100), to reproduce reported 4-50% yield gains from relaxing quality thresholds 0.9 to 0.6.
skills.name: naive-overlap-baseline-comparison
skills.search_text: naive-overlap-baseline-comparison Use when benchmarking sequence recovery of paired-end Illumina assembly against a naive perfect-overlap baseline on a control library (e.g. SRA024100), to reproduce reported 4-50% yield gains from relaxing quality thresholds 0.9 to 0.6. Input is already an assembled or clustered sequence table — no paired-end overlap assembly or baseline comparison is needed Reads have no expected overlap between pairs (e.g. short inserts / long reads), so a perfect-overlap baseline is meaningless The goal is accuracy/error-rate evaluation rather than yield recovery comparison (use simulated data with known errors instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantifies how much a probabilistic paired-end assembler (PANDAseq) recovers over a naive perfect-overlap baseline by assembling the same control-library read pairs (SRA024100) at multiple quality-score thresholds and computing relative yield increases. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Quantifies how much a probabilistic paired-end assembler (PANDAseq) recovers over a naive perfect-overlap baseline by assembling the same control-library read pairs (SRA024100) at multiple quality-score thresholds and computing relative yield increases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an assembled or clustered sequence table — no paired-end overlap assembly or baseline comparison is needed Reads have no expected overlap between pairs (e.g. short inserts / long reads), so a perfect-overlap baseline is meaningless The goal is accuracy/error-rate evaluation rather than yield recovery comparison (use simulated data with known errors instead)

skills.description: Use when metagenomic paired-end reads must be reconstructed into virus-like super-scaffolds by mapping to Genbank viral/phage references (gbvrl, gbphage) with low-coverage or divergent viruses where de-novo assembly alone is insufficient.
skills.name: naive-pileup-mapping-assembly-of-viral-genomes
skills.search_text: naive-pileup-mapping-assembly-of-viral-genomes Use when metagenomic paired-end reads must be reconstructed into virus-like super-scaffolds by mapping to Genbank viral/phage references (gbvrl, gbphage) with low-coverage or divergent viruses where de-novo assembly alone is insufficient. When sufficient coverage exists for a high-quality de-novo assembly with MEGAHIT or Tadpole and reference-based reconstruction is unnecessary When the goal is taxonomic classification only and no genome-scale reconstruction is required (VirMAP's bits-per-base classification path) When reads do not plausibly derive from viruses or phages represented in the Genbank gbvrl/gbphage reference divisions http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 VirMAP's mapping assembly stage builds virus-like super-scaffolds by combining nucleotide (BBMap) and translated/protein (DIAMOND) alignments in a tiered manner, then reconstructing each genome entry via naive pileup assembly and merging protein and nucleotide information into one super-scaffold per genome with nucleotide precedence. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: VirMAP's mapping assembly stage builds virus-like super-scaffolds by combining nucleotide (BBMap) and translated/protein (DIAMOND) alignments in a tiered manner, then reconstructing each genome entry via naive pileup assembly and merging protein and nucleotide information into one super-scaffold per genome with nucleotide precedence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When sufficient coverage exists for a high-quality de-novo assembly with MEGAHIT or Tadpole and reference-based reconstruction is unnecessary When the goal is taxonomic classification only and no genome-scale reconstruction is required (VirMAP's bits-per-base classification path) When reads do not plausibly derive from viruses or phages represented in the Genbank gbvrl/gbphage reference divisions

skills.description: Use when refining VirMAP super-scaffolds/contigs so the final dual assembly consists solely of viral sequences, after viral filtering and contig merging, by rebuilding each genome's contigs from its assigned read set.
skills.name: naive-pileup-viral-contig-reconstruction
skills.search_text: naive-pileup-viral-contig-reconstruction Use when refining VirMAP super-scaffolds/contigs so the final dual assembly consists solely of viral sequences, after viral filtering and contig merging, by rebuilding each genome's contigs from its assigned read set. Input contigs are already classified as non-viral (top scoring pass one taxon not in superkingdom Virus) — these are filtered out rather than rebuilt. Goal is de-novo assembly of a whole metagenome without viral targeting — use MEGAHIT/standalone assembly instead of VirMAP's iterative rebuild loop. Genomic read sets show high non-unique read membership requiring Jaccard-distance filtering — resolve assignment ambiguity before pileup reconstruction. http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Rebuild viral contigs within VirMAP's improvement loop by naive pileup assembly of dereplicated, digitally normalized reads assigned to each viral genome, optionally supported by MEGAHIT or Tadpole multi-kmer de-novo assembly, and iterate the merge-and-rebuild cycle until convergence. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Rebuild viral contigs within VirMAP's improvement loop by naive pileup assembly of dereplicated, digitally normalized reads assigned to each viral genome, optionally supported by MEGAHIT or Tadpole multi-kmer de-novo assembly, and iterate the merge-and-rebuild cycle until convergence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contigs are already classified as non-viral (top scoring pass one taxon not in superkingdom Virus) — these are filtered out rather than rebuilt. Goal is de-novo assembly of a whole metagenome without viral targeting — use MEGAHIT/standalone assembly instead of VirMAP's iterative rebuild loop. Genomic read sets show high non-unique read membership requiring Jaccard-distance filtering — resolve assignment ambiguity before pileup reconstruction.

skills.description: Use when raw Nanopore FASTQ reads enter a metagenome assembly workflow and adapters must be removed before control-read decontamination (NanoLyse), quality filtering (Filtlong) and long-read assembly.
skills.name: nanopore-adapter-trimming
skills.search_text: nanopore-adapter-trimming Use when raw Nanopore FASTQ reads enter a metagenome assembly workflow and adapters must be removed before control-read decontamination (NanoLyse), quality filtering (Filtlong) and long-read assembly. Input reads are PacBio — Porechop adapter trimming is skipped for PacBio reads in nf-core/mag conventions Reads are Illumina short reads — use short-read trimming tools (e.g. fastp) instead of the Nanopore-specific Porechop step Reads are already adapter-trimmed and only require control decontamination or length/quality filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 Adapter trimming of raw Oxford Nanopore long reads with Porechop, as implemented in the nf-core/mag long-read pre-processing module, so that chimeric and adapter-containing reads are cleaned before decontamination, quality filtering and metagenome assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Adapter trimming of raw Oxford Nanopore long reads with Porechop, as implemented in the nf-core/mag long-read pre-processing module, so that chimeric and adapter-containing reads are cleaned before decontamination, quality filtering and metagenome assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are PacBio — Porechop adapter trimming is skipped for PacBio reads in nf-core/mag conventions Reads are Illumina short reads — use short-read trimming tools (e.g. fastp) instead of the Nanopore-specific Porechop step Reads are already adapter-trimmed and only require control decontamination or length/quality filtering

skills.description: Use when a nanopore FASTQ (e.g., .fq.gz from ONT) must be converted into NGS-liked short-read sets to run conventional NGS pipelines for hotspot mutation detection in a hotspot panel.

skills.search_text: nanopore-long-read-to-short-read-conversion Use when a nanopore FASTQ (e.g., .fq.gz from ONT) must be converted into NGS-liked short-read sets to run conventional NGS pipelines for hotspot mutation detection in a hotspot panel. Input is already short-read NGS FASTQ data — no long-to-short conversion is needed and the extraction would discard information The goal is metagenomic taxonomical classification — the authors route that use case to the separate Nano2NGS-Meta module (nano2ngs-meta.pl) Reads/bases require explicit error correction before analysis — the current Nano2NGS version only converts long reads into short reads with no error correction for reads and/or bases Target variant types are copy number variation, structural variation, gene fusion, or gene expression — these are only planned future algorithm development for Nano2NGS http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Converts Oxford Nanopore long reads into NGS-liked short-read sets using Nano2NGS-Muta's paired-seed extraction, so standard NGS pipelines (e.g., GATK Best Practice) can detect hotspot mutations while statistical weighting controls nanopore-specific non-random errors and indels. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac033
skills.summary: Converts Oxford Nanopore long reads into NGS-liked short-read sets using Nano2NGS-Muta's paired-seed extraction, so standard NGS pipelines (e.g., GATK Best Practice) can detect hotspot mutations while statistical weighting controls nanopore-specific non-random errors and indels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already short-read NGS FASTQ data — no long-to-short conversion is needed and the extraction would discard information The goal is metagenomic taxonomical classification — the authors route that use case to the separate Nano2NGS-Meta module (nano2ngs-meta.pl) Reads/bases require explicit error correction before analysis — the current Nano2NGS version only converts long reads into short reads with no error correction for reads and/or bases Target variant types are copy number variation, structural variation, gene fusion, or gene expression — these are only planned future algorithm development for Nano2NGS

skills.description: Use when the input is raw nanopore signal data (FAST5, POD5, SLOW5, or BLOW5) from legacy r9.4 chemistry that must be mapped to a reference genome in real time, especially for large genomes such as human NA12878.
skills.name: nanopore-raw-signal-mapping
skills.search_text: nanopore-raw-signal-mapping Use when the input is raw nanopore signal data (FAST5, POD5, SLOW5, or BLOW5) from legacy r9.4 chemistry that must be mapped to a reference genome in real time, especially for large genomes such as human NA12878. The input is already basecalled sequence data (FASTQ/BAM) — use a base-level mapper such as minimap2 instead of raw-signal mapping The reads are from r10.4.1 chemistry — UNCALLED can only be applied to legacy r9.4.1 data, and the legacy 6-mer pore model used here is r9.4-specific (use ReadFish or ONT builtin adaptive sampling instead) No reference genome is available and all-vs-all overlaps are needed for de novo assembly — use Rawsamble rather than reference-based raw signal mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Maps raw nanopore electrical signals (not basecalled reads) directly to a reference genome using hash-based signal-to-hash search with RawHash/RawHash2, benchmarked against signal mappers UNCALLED and Sigmap, with accuracy scored against minimap2 basecalled-read ground truth. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad272
skills.summary: Maps raw nanopore electrical signals (not basecalled reads) directly to a reference genome using hash-based signal-to-hash search with RawHash/RawHash2, benchmarked against signal mappers UNCALLED and Sigmap, with accuracy scored against minimap2 basecalled-read ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already basecalled sequence data (FASTQ/BAM) — use a base-level mapper such as minimap2 instead of raw-signal mapping The reads are from r10.4.1 chemistry — UNCALLED can only be applied to legacy r9.4.1 data, and the legacy 6-mer pore model used here is r9.4-specific (use ReadFish or ONT builtin adaptive sampling instead) No reference genome is available and all-vs-all overlaps are needed for de novo assembly — use Rawsamble rather than reference-based raw signal mapping

skills.description: Use when mapping raw nanopore signal reads to a reference genome via hash-based seed matching, or when reproducing how RawHash converts matching seed hash values into a mapped genomic region through colinear chaining.
skills.name: nanopore-raw-signal-seed-hash-matching
skills.search_text: nanopore-raw-signal-seed-hash-matching Use when mapping raw nanopore signal reads to a reference genome via hash-based seed matching, or when reproducing how RawHash converts matching seed hash values into a mapped genomic region through colinear chaining. You need base-level or signal-level alignment of the mapped region (RawHash reports approximate mapping via chaining, not aligned bases); use a downstream aligner such as DTW-based signal alignment instead There is no reference genome and the goal is all-vs-all overlap finding between raw signals — use Rawsamble instead Reads are r10.4.1 data with tools like UNCALLED that only support legacy r9.4.1 — verify tool compatibility with the pore chemistry http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs RawHash's mapping step: seed hashes generated from raw nanopore signals (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5/BLOW5) are looked up in a hash-table index of the reference genome, and the best colinear chain of seed matches — found with Sigmap's chaining algorithm with the distance coefficient disabled — defines the mapped region. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad272
skills.summary: Reconstructs RawHash's mapping step: seed hashes generated from raw nanopore signals (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5/BLOW5) are looked up in a hash-table index of the reference genome, and the best colinear chain of seed matches — found with Sigmap's chaining algorithm with the distance coefficient disabled — defines the mapped region.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need base-level or signal-level alignment of the mapped region (RawHash reports approximate mapping via chaining, not aligned bases); use a downstream aligner such as DTW-based signal alignment instead There is no reference genome and the goal is all-vs-all overlap finding between raw signals — use Rawsamble instead Reads are r10.4.1 data with tools like UNCALLED that only support legacy r9.4.1 — verify tool compatibility with the pore chemistry

skills.description: Use when base-called nanopore reads must be classified as target vs non-target (e.g., adaptive-sampling host/strain depletion) against one-genome or multi-strain pan-genome references where minimap2 alignment is too slow or memory-hungry.
skills.name: nanopore-read-classification
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-classification Use when base-called nanopore reads must be classified as target vs non-target (e.g., adaptive-sampling host/strain depletion) against one-genome or multi-strain pan-genome references where minimap2 alignment is too slow or memory-hungry. Direct real-time control through the nanopore Read Until API is required: SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences, not the raw signal batches, so a separate base caller must run upstream (as with Readfish) Depletion-target and non-target reads share substantial sequence similarity (e.g., conserved genes between species) — the reversed null index may fail to discriminate Read accuracy or reference differs markedly from the real nanopore data used to tune the single shared KS-statistic threshold; no per-experiment thresholding method is provided http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Rapid target/non-target classification of base-called nanopore reads using SPUMONI's matching statistics (MS) or pseudomatching lengths (PML) computed against a compressed one-genome or multi-strain pan-genome index, with a reversed 'null index' and KS-statistic hypothesis testing to make principled ejection decisions. Achieves minimap2-comparable F1 (~97-99%) at ~12x the throughput with a much smaller index. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Rapid target/non-target classification of base-called nanopore reads using SPUMONI's matching statistics (MS) or pseudomatching lengths (PML) computed against a compressed one-genome or multi-strain pan-genome index, with a reversed 'null index' and KS-statistic hypothesis testing to make principled ejection decisions. Achieves minimap2-comparable F1 (~97-99%) at ~12x the throughput with a much smaller index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Direct real-time control through the nanopore Read Until API is required: SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences, not the raw signal batches, so a separate base caller must run upstream (as with Readfish) Depletion-target and non-target reads share substantial sequence similarity (e.g., conserved genes between species) — the reversed null index may fail to discriminate Read accuracy or reference differs markedly from the real nanopore data used to tune the single shared KS-statistic threshold; no per-experiment thresholding method is provided

skills.description: Use when you have raw single-molecule nanopore (MinION) reads of a bacterial isolate and need antibiotic resistance predictions without prior error correction, ideally benchmarked against a second sequencing platform.
skills.name: nanopore-read-resistance-genotyping
skills.search_text: nanopore-read-resistance-genotyping Use when you have raw single-molecule nanopore (MinION) reads of a bacterial isolate and need antibiotic resistance predictions without prior error correction, ideally benchmarked against a second sequencing platform. The aim is M. tuberculosis resistance prediction from direct sputum mixtures: the article notes the current implementation models only major/minor clones and a more general mixture model would be needed You need validated per-drug sensitivity for nanopore data: the MinION test is only an N=1 proof-of-principle with a single isolate Input is not raw sequence data but already-called variant lists or phenotype tables; Mykrobe predictor requires raw reads as input http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Runs Mykrobe predictor's de Bruijn graph genotyper directly on high-error-rate Oxford Nanopore MinION reads (e.g. a 39x-depth MDR S. aureus isolate, 10% error model, base qualities ignored) to call a resistance profile that can be validated against Illumina MiSeq calls from the same isolate. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Runs Mykrobe predictor's de Bruijn graph genotyper directly on high-error-rate Oxford Nanopore MinION reads (e.g. a 39x-depth MDR S. aureus isolate, 10% error model, base qualities ignored) to call a resistance profile that can be validated against Illumina MiSeq calls from the same isolate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The aim is M. tuberculosis resistance prediction from direct sputum mixtures: the article notes the current implementation models only major/minor clones and a more general mixture model would be needed You need validated per-drug sensitivity for nanopore data: the MinION test is only an N=1 proof-of-principle with a single isolate Input is not raw sequence data but already-called variant lists or phenotype tables; Mykrobe predictor requires raw reads as input

skills.search_text: nanopore-read-simulation Use when you need ground-truth nanopore read sets of known origin and adjustable accuracy to benchmark read classification or alignment accuracy (F1, precision, recall) and throughput. You already have real sequencer reads with verified labels (e.g. a SRA set like SRX6602475 spiked with simulated host reads); simulation is only needed for the ground-truth component You need to model raw nanopore electrical signal or Read Until API signal batches — PBSIM2 operates at the base-sequence level and SPUMONI-class workflows require a separate upstream base caller You need exact reproduction of a specific real sequencing run's error profile rather than controlled accuracy sweeps Simulate Oxford-Nanopore-like long reads with PBSIM2 at controlled mean base-call accuracies (e.g. 85%, 90%, 95%, 98%) from reference FASTAs, to generate benchmark read sets for evaluating read classifiers such as SPUMONI against alignment baselines like minimap2. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Simulate Oxford-Nanopore-like long reads with PBSIM2 at controlled mean base-call accuracies (e.g. 85%, 90%, 95%, 98%) from reference FASTAs, to generate benchmark read sets for evaluating read classifiers such as SPUMONI against alignment baselines like minimap2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have real sequencer reads with verified labels (e.g. a SRA set like SRX6602475 spiked with simulated host reads); simulation is only needed for the ground-truth component You need to model raw nanopore electrical signal or Read Until API signal batches — PBSIM2 operates at the base-sequence level and SPUMONI-class workflows require a separate upstream base caller You need exact reproduction of a specific real sequencing run's error profile rather than controlled accuracy sweeps

The goal is accuracy of species detection or classification (use the baseLess validation/accuracy evaluation instead of speed benchmarking) Input data are already basecalled FASTQ/FASTA rather than raw fast5 signal files, since baseLess and UNCALLED/SquiggleNet comparisons operate on raw electrical signal Hardware differs from the benchmarked configurations (2GB Jetson Nano or the paper's desktop) without re-running the protocol, since kbp/s values are hardware-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Benchmarks the wall-clock inference speed (kb processed per second) of raw-signal nanopore tools such as baseLess against basecalling+alignment pipelines (Guppy+minimap2, SquiggleNet, DeepNano+minimap2, UNCALLED) on low-power (Jetson Nano) and desktop hardware, following the baseLess evaluation protocol. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017

skills.description: Use when input is raw ONT fast5 signal data (amplified or metagenomic 16S) and you need per-read target-species detection on inexpensive hardware without basecalling, e.g. MinION as a species detector.
skills.name: nanopore-signal-read-classification
skills.search_text: nanopore-signal-read-classification Use when input is raw ONT fast5 signal data (amplified or metagenomic 16S) and you need per-read target-species detection on inexpensive hardware without basecalling, e.g. MinION as a species detector. You need full basecalled sequences rather than target-detection-only output — baseLess reduces the MinION to a species detector and does not produce base calls. Samples are pure and you want genome-wide detection with larger genomes — abundance mode ('--model-type abundance') is the tested route, not read_detection. Your target is not tuned for 16S-style sequence context — read detection mode 'has been tested for and attuned to 16S sequence at the moment'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Classify individual MinION reads as originating from a target species by detecting k-mers directly in the raw electrical signal with baseLess read_detection mode, avoiding basecalling entirely. Benchmarked on a 21-species 16S rRNA mock community (HM-278D) under stratified 5-fold cross-validation. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017
skills.summary: Classify individual MinION reads as originating from a target species by detecting k-mers directly in the raw electrical signal with baseLess read_detection mode, avoiding basecalling entirely. Benchmarked on a 21-species 16S rRNA mock community (HM-278D) under stratified 5-fold cross-validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need full basecalled sequences rather than target-detection-only output — baseLess reduces the MinION to a species detector and does not produce base calls. Samples are pure and you want genome-wide detection with larger genomes — abundance mode ('--model-type abundance') is the tested route, not read_detection. Your target is not tuned for 16S-style sequence context — read detection mode 'has been tested for and attuned to 16S sequence at the moment'.

Input is long-read (PacBio/ONT) data — StrainXpress as published targets Illumina-type short reads, and the paper notes third-generation read error rates remain unresolved A reference-based or strain-typing analysis is the goal; this skill only supplies raw de novo assembly inputs, not reference genomes The target study has no deposited SRA accessions in the source card (only Bmock12, NWCs and Gut Metagenome accessions are grounded here) http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Retrieve the raw interleaved FASTQ read sets underlying the StrainXpress real-data benchmark (Bmock12 mock community, natural whey starter cultures, and 5 Gut Metagenome patient samples) from NCBI SRA/ENA using the accessions reported in the paper, so the benchmark can be reproduced end-to-end. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac543

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read (PacBio/ONT) data — StrainXpress as published targets Illumina-type short reads, and the paper notes third-generation read error rates remain unresolved A reference-based or strain-typing analysis is the goal; this skill only supplies raw de novo assembly inputs, not reference genomes The target study has no deposited SRA accessions in the source card (only Bmock12, NWCs and Gut Metagenome accessions are grounded here)

skills.description: Use when you need to explain a classifier's per-sequence errors by distance to training data: bucket held-out 16S sequences by nearest-neighbor percent identity (>97%, 90–97%, <90%) to stratify F1 degradation.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-sequence-identity-search
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-sequence-identity-search Use when you need to explain a classifier's per-sequence errors by distance to training data: bucket held-out 16S sequences by nearest-neighbor percent identity (>97%, 90–97%, <90%) to stratify F1 degradation. You need classifier accuracy on the full held-out test set rather than identity-stratified breakdowns — the pooled `deeptaxa predict --evaluate` metrics already cover this The sequences are not 16S rRNA gene sequences drawn from the same reference universe as the training pool (e.g. 18S or shotgun metagenomic data), since identity to the Greengenes2 training set would be uninformative You want database-wide similarity search for annotation (e.g. MEGAN-style assignment) rather than a single nearest-neighbor identity value per query for evaluation stratification http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Aligns each test sequence against the training pool with BLAST or VSEARCH to find its nearest training neighbor and record percent nucleotide identity, enabling similarity-stratified evaluation of taxonomic classifier performance (e.g. DeepTaxa species F1 from 0.95 at >97% identity down to 0.45 at <90%). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Aligns each test sequence against the training pool with BLAST or VSEARCH to find its nearest training neighbor and record percent nucleotide identity, enabling similarity-stratified evaluation of taxonomic classifier performance (e.g. DeepTaxa species F1 from 0.95 at >97% identity down to 0.45 at <90%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need classifier accuracy on the full held-out test set rather than identity-stratified breakdowns — the pooled `deeptaxa predict --evaluate` metrics already cover this The sequences are not 16S rRNA gene sequences drawn from the same reference universe as the training pool (e.g. 18S or shotgun metagenomic data), since identity to the Greengenes2 training set would be uninformative You want database-wide similarity search for annotation (e.g. MEGAN-style assignment) rather than a single nearest-neighbor identity value per query for evaluation stratification

skills.search_text: negative-binomial-abundance-model-fitting Use when estimating per-sample abundances of MAG clusters from shotgun metagenomics and you need to pick an optimal, statistically validated set of de novo signature genes from a gene count matrix. When MAGs already have database-derived strain marker genes — the article notes a similar cross-cohort transfer phenomenon would be expected, and de novo signature genes from one cohort can be missing in another, causing abundance underestimation When the input is raw reads/contigs rather than an upstream read-mapping gene count matrix — signature gene identification requires the read-mapping and gene-counting step to have been completed first http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fit a rank-based negative binomial model of expected detected signature genes versus mapped read counts to select and refine de novo signature genes for MAGinator MAG-cluster abundance estimation. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8

skills.description: Use when the input is a longitudinal microbiome count dataset (master table with samples x features over time) and the goal is to detect features changing significantly over time while comparing error control (TPR/FDR) across negative-binomial methods.
skills.name: negative-binomial-association-testing
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-association-testing Use when the input is a longitudinal microbiome count dataset (master table with samples x features over time) and the goal is to detect features changing significantly over time while comparing error control (TPR/FDR) across negative-binomial methods. The data are not longitudinal or the test variable is not time/treatment over repeated measurements — LongDat is designed for longitudinal analysis of feature change over time. The data are already a preprocessed proportion/binary/continuous feature table where data_type='count' (and thus the randomized control test) does not apply. A single method's absolute sensitivity matters more than calibrated error control — MaAsLin2 NEGBIN can attain higher TPR at small sample sizes but with higher FDR, whereas this skill's benchmark target is LongDat's zero-FDR behavior. Benchmark and apply negative-binomial-based longitudinal feature association testing by running LongDat's longdat_cont() (count data type) against MaAsLin2 in NEGBIN mode, on simulated or real longitudinal microbiome count data, scoring accuracy, true positive rate and false discovery rate. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad063
skills.summary: Benchmark and apply negative-binomial-based longitudinal feature association testing by running LongDat's longdat_cont() (count data type) against MaAsLin2 in NEGBIN mode, on simulated or real longitudinal microbiome count data, scoring accuracy, true positive rate and false discovery rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not longitudinal or the test variable is not time/treatment over repeated measurements — LongDat is designed for longitudinal analysis of feature change over time. The data are already a preprocessed proportion/binary/continuous feature table where data_type='count' (and thus the randomized control test) does not apply. A single method's absolute sensitivity matters more than calibrated error control — MaAsLin2 NEGBIN can attain higher TPR at small sample sizes but with higher FDR, whereas this skill's benchmark target is LongDat's zero-FDR behavior.

skills.description: Use when raw gene-level RNA-seq count matrices plus sample metadata are available and per-gene log2 fold changes and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values are needed for differential expression between conditions.

skills.search_text: negative-binomial-glm-fitting Use when raw gene-level RNA-seq count matrices plus sample metadata are available and per-gene log2 fold changes and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values are needed for differential expression between conditions. Input is single-cell RNA-seq data — NASQAR wraps scRNA analysis through SeuratV3Wizard/SeuratWizard rather than the DESeq2 workflow. Input is already a normalized/transformed expression table rather than raw counts, since the negative binomial model requires raw count data. Gene count columns do not match across files that need merging first — use GeneCountMerger preprocessing instead (first column must contain the genes). http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Fits a negative binomial generalized linear model to bulk RNA-seq gene count data to estimate per-gene differential expression, as wrapped by NASQAR's DESeq2Shiny/DEApp applications around the DESeq2 R package ('Differential gene expression analysis based on the negative binomial distribution'). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03577-4
skills.summary: Fits a negative binomial generalized linear model to bulk RNA-seq gene count data to estimate per-gene differential expression, as wrapped by NASQAR's DESeq2Shiny/DEApp applications around the DESeq2 R package ('Differential gene expression analysis based on the negative binomial distribution').
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq data — NASQAR wraps scRNA analysis through SeuratV3Wizard/SeuratWizard rather than the DESeq2 workflow. Input is already a normalized/transformed expression table rather than raw counts, since the negative binomial model requires raw count data. Gene count columns do not match across files that need merging first — use GeneCountMerger preprocessing instead (first column must contain the genes).

skills.description: Use when validating a longitudinal microbiome method's type-I error control: you need simulated null (zero-effect) count data whose library sizes differ systematically across time points to expose normalization-induced false positives.

skills.search_text: negative-control-microbiome-count-simulation Use when validating a longitudinal microbiome method's type-I error control: you need simulated null (zero-effect) count data whose library sizes differ systematically across time points to expose normalization-induced false positives. Data contain a real treatment/time effect — this is a negative-control benchmark with effect size zero across time points Feature values are already relative-abundance or continuous measurements rather than raw counts — LongDat's randomized control test and the rarefaction step apply to data_type='count' The goal is differential-abundance power benchmarking rather than type-I error (false positive rate) assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Generate simulated negative-control longitudinal microbiome count tables (zero effect size) with systematic sequencing-depth variation via SparseDOSSA2, then compare false positive rates of LongDat's rarefied negative-binomial pipeline against a non-rarefied TSS-normalized linear-model comparator, as in the LongDat Supplementary Fig. S9 benchmark. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad063
skills.summary: Generate simulated negative-control longitudinal microbiome count tables (zero effect size) with systematic sequencing-depth variation via SparseDOSSA2, then compare false positive rates of LongDat's rarefied negative-binomial pipeline against a non-rarefied TSS-normalized linear-model comparator, as in the LongDat Supplementary Fig. S9 benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contain a real treatment/time effect — this is a negative-control benchmark with effect size zero across time points Feature values are already relative-abundance or continuous measurements rather than raw counts — LongDat's randomized control test and the rarefaction step apply to data_type='count' The goal is differential-abundance power benchmarking rather than type-I error (false positive rate) assessment

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single multi-locus allelic profile matrix rather than per-locus allele FASTA files — the skill requires one FASTA per locus with full allelic diversity The goal is strain-level phylogeny or core-genome phylogenetic reconstruction across genomes rather than per-locus assessment of allelic variability within a schema The schema has not been allele called yet and per-locus allele FASTA files do not exist

skills.description: Use when annotated (e.g., PROKKA GFF) gene sequences from multiple taxa must be grouped into homologous clusters with phylogenetic support before assigning representatives to taxonomic nodes for probe or pseudo-genome design.
skills.name: neighbour-joining-tree-construction
skills.search_text: neighbour-joining-tree-construction Use when annotated (e.g., PROKKA GFF) gene sequences from multiple taxa must be grouped into homologous clusters with phylogenetic support before assigning representatives to taxonomic nodes for probe or pseudo-genome design. Target genomes are unknown or unannotatable — HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to efficiently cluster sequences, so probes cannot be designed for such targets Sequences within a candidate cluster exceed the r2t-divergence threshold and should not be collapsed (over-collapsing would produce representatives too divergent for effective capture) Only a single genome or a handful of closely related genomes is involved — cluster/LCA-based pseudo-genome construction adds complexity without benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Within the HUBDesign clustering stage, homologous gene sequences from PROKKA-annotated genomes are aligned with a supported multiple sequence aligner (MAFFT 7.0+, MUSCLE 3.8.425+, or CLUSTAL OMEGA 1.2.1+) via BioPerl, neighbour-joining gene trees are built, and sequences whose root-to-tip divergence is at most 15% are collapsed into representative consensus sequences (RepSeq.fna) that later feed LCA-based pseudo-genome construction. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: Within the HUBDesign clustering stage, homologous gene sequences from PROKKA-annotated genomes are aligned with a supported multiple sequence aligner (MAFFT 7.0+, MUSCLE 3.8.425+, or CLUSTAL OMEGA 1.2.1+) via BioPerl, neighbour-joining gene trees are built, and sequences whose root-to-tip divergence is at most 15% are collapsed into representative consensus sequences (RepSeq.fna) that later feed LCA-based pseudo-genome construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target genomes are unknown or unannotatable — HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to efficiently cluster sequences, so probes cannot be designed for such targets Sequences within a candidate cluster exceed the r2t-divergence threshold and should not be collapsed (over-collapsing would produce representatives too divergent for effective capture) Only a single genome or a handful of closely related genomes is involved — cluster/LCA-based pseudo-genome construction adds complexity without benefit

skills.summary: Reproduces Traitar's 10-fold nested cross-validation benchmark of the phypat (phyletic-pattern) and phypat+PGL (phyletic pattern plus maximum-likelihood ancestral protein family gains/losses) classifiers for 67 phenotypes across 234 GIDEON I bacterial species, reporting overall accuracy and macroaccuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is phenotyping new/independent genomes rather than estimating classifier performance on a labeled benchmark (use the standard `traitar phenotype` workflow instead). skills.description: Use when a new network-based association predictor must be benchmarked against published baselines on a known association matrix with precomputed similarity networks, and reported AUC/AUPR values must be reproduced to validate the comparison.
skills.name: network-based-baseline-method-reproduction
skills.search_text: network-based-baseline-method-reproduction Use when a new network-based association predictor must be benchmarked against published baselines on a known association matrix with precomputed similarity networks, and reported AUC/AUPR values must be reproduced to validate the comparison. The goal is de novo host prediction for new viruses rather than benchmarking against published baselines on a labeled association matrix. The association data are drug-target pairs (PyDTI's native nr, gpcr, ic, e datasets) rather than virus-host associations, unless the same CV protocol is being deliberately ported. No precomputed similarity networks are available and the task does not include constructing virus dissimilarity (Jie Ren's d2* tools) or host SNF networks first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Reproduces benchmark AUC/AUPR results for five recent network-based virus-host prediction baselines (LMFH-VH, KBMF2K, BLM-NII, NetLapRLS, CMF) under five-fold cross validation using the PyDTI framework, so a new method such as ILMF-VH can be fairly compared against Table 2 reference values. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Reproduces benchmark AUC/AUPR results for five recent network-based virus-host prediction baselines (LMFH-VH, KBMF2K, BLM-NII, NetLapRLS, CMF) under five-fold cross validation using the PyDTI framework, so a new method such as ILMF-VH can be fairly compared against Table 2 reference values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo host prediction for new viruses rather than benchmarking against published baselines on a labeled association matrix. The association data are drug-target pairs (PyDTI's native nr, gpcr, ic, e datasets) rather than virus-host associations, unless the same CV protocol is being deliberately ported. No precomputed similarity networks are available and the task does not include constructing virus dissimilarity (Jie Ren's d2* tools) or host SNF networks first.

skills.search_text: neural-network-architecture-coding Use when coding or reproducing a DNN that maps variable-length short metagenomic sequencing reads to species/genus labels via k-mer embedding -> BiLSTM -> multi-head self-attention -> 3-layer MLP, per the DeepMicrobes Model Architectures specification. skills.description: Use when stitched (hit-stitched) query-to-reference protein alignments contain putative noncoding stretches — many indels with occasional matches — that must be trimmed before concatenating phylogenetic markers.
skills.name: noncoding-region-detection-in-protein-alignments
skills.search_text: noncoding-region-detection-in-protein-alignments Use when stitched (hit-stitched) query-to-reference protein alignments contain putative noncoding stretches — many indels with occasional matches — that must be trimmed before concatenating phylogenetic markers. The input is raw reads or unassembled contigs before the DIAMOND similarity search and hit-stitching phase — this skill operates on stitched alignments only. Reference sequences are so divergent (not near-USCOs) that most of the alignment is low-identity; Patchwork's authors recommend limiting references to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences. A post-hoc check for artifactual noncoding stretches in already-built alignments is needed — PREQUAL is recommended instead for detecting and removing such regions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Patchwork's final processing stage: a sliding window algorithm scans stitched DIAMOND query-to-reference alignments and cuts regions whose average gap-excluded query-reference distance exceeds a threshold, removing noncoding stretches from the stitched marker sequences. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Patchwork's final processing stage: a sliding window algorithm scans stitched DIAMOND query-to-reference alignments and cuts regions whose average gap-excluded query-reference distance exceeds a threshold, removing noncoding stretches from the stitched marker sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw reads or unassembled contigs before the DIAMOND similarity search and hit-stitching phase — this skill operates on stitched alignments only. Reference sequences are so divergent (not near-USCOs) that most of the alignment is low-identity; Patchwork's authors recommend limiting references to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences. A post-hoc check for artifactual noncoding stretches in already-built alignments is needed — PREQUAL is recommended instead for detecting and removing such regions.

skills.description: Use when comparing the number of sequence variants called from 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data by HashSeq's normal/LOESS error model at 5% FDR versus DADA2 defaults, especially on mock communities of known taxa.
skills.name: normal-loess-error-model-inference
skills.search_text: normal-loess-error-model-inference Use when comparing the number of sequence variants called from 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data by HashSeq's normal/LOESS error model at 5% FDR versus DADA2 defaults, especially on mock communities of known taxa. The goal is to detect true low-abundance sequence variants — HashSeq is not sensitive there; the paper recommends more sensitive algorithms such as DADA2 for low-abundance variants. Input reads require modeling of indels or two-or-more-mismatch differences — HashSeq only considers one-mismatch variants and treats indel events as separate parent sequences. skills.summary: Reproduces HashSeq's variant calling, in which one-mismatch children of parent 16S rRNA sequences are tested against a normally distributed background error estimated with LOESS regression as a function of parent abundance, and compares the resulting variant counts to DADA2 defaults on mock-community (zymo) FASTQ data.
