skills.description: Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., FASTQ from a QIITA study) must be converted into an OTU-level feature table, RDP taxonomy table, and FastTree phylogeny that are structurally consistent with a deposited phyloseq/biom dataset.
skills.name: open-reference-otu-picking-greengenes
skills.search_text: open-reference-otu-picking-greengenes Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., FASTQ from a QIITA study) must be converted into an OTU-level feature table, RDP taxonomy table, and FastTree phylogeny that are structurally consistent with a deposited phyloseq/biom dataset. The processed data already exist (otu.tab.txt, tax.tab.txt, tree.tre, or biom.Rdata are available in the MiSurvGit Data folder), so only validation against those deposits is needed rather than re-clustering. Input is shotgun metagenomics data rather than 16S rRNA amplicon reads (the MiSurv article lists MetaPhlAn/MEGAN for shotgun metagenomics, not QIIME 2.0 OTU picking). The downstream goal is a denoised amplicon sequence variant (ASV) table instead of 97% OTU clusters, since this skill reproduces the paper's specific open-reference OTU protocol. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs a 16S rRNA amplicon feature table by open-reference OTU picking at 97% sequence similarity against the Greengenes database in QIIME 2.0, as used to build the processed example data (otu.tab.txt, tax.tab.txt, tree.tre, biom.Rdata) for the MiSurv platform from QIITA study 10508 raw reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/spectrum.05059-22
skills.summary: Reconstructs a 16S rRNA amplicon feature table by open-reference OTU picking at 97% sequence similarity against the Greengenes database in QIIME 2.0, as used to build the processed example data (otu.tab.txt, tax.tab.txt, tree.tre, biom.Rdata) for the MiSurv platform from QIITA study 10508 raw reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The processed data already exist (otu.tab.txt, tax.tab.txt, tree.tre, or biom.Rdata are available in the MiSurvGit Data folder), so only validation against those deposits is needed rather than re-clustering. Input is shotgun metagenomics data rather than 16S rRNA amplicon reads (the MiSurv article lists MetaPhlAn/MEGAN for shotgun metagenomics, not QIIME 2.0 OTU picking). The downstream goal is a denoised amplicon sequence variant (ASV) table instead of 97% OTU clusters, since this skill reproduces the paper's specific open-reference OTU protocol.

skills.description: Use when you have simulated or real metagenomic shotgun reads (454, Sanger, or Illumina) and need to run an open-source gene prediction pipeline end-to-end, from installation through prediction output for benchmarking.
skills.name: open-source-bioinformatics-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: open-source-bioinformatics-pipeline-execution Use when you have simulated or real metagenomic shotgun reads (454, Sanger, or Illumina) and need to run an open-source gene prediction pipeline end-to-end, from installation through prediction output for benchmarking. Input is complete prokaryotic genomes rather than metagenomic fragments — plain Glimmer routinely identifies >99% of genes there and Glimmer-MG's training machinery is unnecessary Reads are error-free and pre-assembled with no need for indel/frame-error modeling — the added computational cost of classification, clustering, and error modeling is not justified The task is taxonomic classification or assembly rather than gene finding — Glimmer-MG outputs gene coordinates, not an assembled metagenome or abundance table http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Install and execute the Glimmer-MG metagenomic gene-prediction pipeline (classification via Phymm, clustering via Scimm, then IMM-based gene prediction) on shotgun sequencing reads, reproducing the Nucleic Acids Research gkr1067 benchmark workflow. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: Install and execute the Glimmer-MG metagenomic gene-prediction pipeline (classification via Phymm, clustering via Scimm, then IMM-based gene prediction) on shotgun sequencing reads, reproducing the Nucleic Acids Research gkr1067 benchmark workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is complete prokaryotic genomes rather than metagenomic fragments — plain Glimmer routinely identifies >99% of genes there and Glimmer-MG's training machinery is unnecessary Reads are error-free and pre-assembled with no need for indel/frame-error modeling — the added computational cost of classification, clustering, and error modeling is not justified The task is taxonomic classification or assembly rather than gene finding — Glimmer-MG outputs gene coordinates, not an assembled metagenome or abundance table

skills.description: Use when per-sample AD/DP allele counts (cellsnp-lite output) are available for a shotgun metagenomic population and variants must be classified as shared/informative versus background noise by clustering sample allele frequencies.
skills.name: optics-cluster-extraction
skills.search_text: optics-cluster-extraction Use when per-sample AD/DP allele counts (cellsnp-lite output) are available for a shotgun metagenomic population and variants must be classified as shared/informative versus background noise by clustering sample allele frequencies. Input is not per-sample allele-count data (no AD/DP from cellsnp-lite or an equivalent pileup) — the AF-per-sample vectors required by 1-D OPTICS cannot be formed Goal is mitochondrial/mtDNA variant detection in single-cell omics — use MQuad's binomial mixture model instead, which is the predecessor tool MetaQuad extends Sample count is below the minSample threshold (e.g. fewer than 5 samples at minSample=5), since no cluster can meet the minimum size constraint MetaQuad's core method: run one-dimensional OPTICS density-based clustering (scikit-learn) over per-sample allele frequencies for each cellsnp-lite variant, to separate shared informative variants from background noise (sequencing errors, non-polymorphic sites) in shotgun metagenomic data. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: MetaQuad's core method: run one-dimensional OPTICS density-based clustering (scikit-learn) over per-sample allele frequencies for each cellsnp-lite variant, to separate shared informative variants from background noise (sequencing errors, non-polymorphic sites) in shotgun metagenomic data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not per-sample allele-count data (no AD/DP from cellsnp-lite or an equivalent pileup) — the AF-per-sample vectors required by 1-D OPTICS cannot be formed Goal is mitochondrial/mtDNA variant detection in single-cell omics — use MQuad's binomial mixture model instead, which is the predecessor tool MetaQuad extends Sample count is below the minSample threshold (e.g. fewer than 5 samples at minSample=5), since no cluster can meet the minimum size constraint

skills.description: Use when comparing predicted functional (KO/KEGG module) abundances between body sites or physiological states from 16S-only data, e.g. supragingival vs subgingival plaque or menses vs rest-of-cycle vaginal samples.
skills.name: oral-niche-differential-abundance-testing
skills.search_text: oral-niche-differential-abundance-testing Use when comparing predicted functional (KO/KEGG module) abundances between body sites or physiological states from 16S-only data, e.g. supragingival vs subgingival plaque or menses vs rest-of-cycle vaginal samples. Data are already shotgun metagenomes annotated to KOs (e.g. via HUMaN); direct KO comparison, not PICRUSt prediction, is appropriate Communities contain substantial viral or eukaryotic components, or strains share an identical marker gene sequence — PICRUSt cannot infer these or resolve strain-level variation Samples have high NSTI values with wide confidence intervals, indicating too few related reference genomes for reliable prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Differential testing of PICRUSt-predicted KEGG module abundances between oral/vaginal niches: 16S OTU tables are converted to predicted metagenomes, collapsed to KEGG modules (e.g. M00009 citrate cycle, M00240 iron complex transport), and compared with Welch's t-test plus Bonferroni correction in STAMP. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Differential testing of PICRUSt-predicted KEGG module abundances between oral/vaginal niches: 16S OTU tables are converted to predicted metagenomes, collapsed to KEGG modules (e.g. M00009 citrate cycle, M00240 iron complex transport), and compared with Welch's t-test plus Bonferroni correction in STAMP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already shotgun metagenomes annotated to KOs (e.g. via HUMaN); direct KO comparison, not PICRUSt prediction, is appropriate Communities contain substantial viral or eukaryotic components, or strains share an identical marker gene sequence — PICRUSt cannot infer these or resolve strain-level variation Samples have high NSTI values with wide confidence intervals, indicating too few related reference genomes for reliable prediction

skills.description: Use when working with six-frame-translated short-read assemblies (e.g. 'plass assemble' output FASTA) where short ORFs below 60 aa may be spurious and a coding-potential decision is needed per candidate protein.
skills.name: orf-coding-potential-classification
skills.search_text: orf-coding-potential-classification Use when working with six-frame-translated short-read assemblies (e.g. 'plass assemble' output FASTA) where short ORFs below 60 aa may be spurious and a coding-potential decision is needed per candidate protein. Input is already a curated, redundancy-reduced protein catalog (e.g. SRC/MERC released at 90% identity, 90% coverage) rather than raw assembly candidates containing all start/end-codon ORFs The goal is nucleotide-level contig assembly (use PenguiN's nuclassemble/guided_nuclassemble instead of Plass's protein filter) ORFs are already length-filtered above 100 amino acids, where the paper states assemblies are mostly genuine and the filter contributes little discrimination http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Classifies candidate open reading frames produced during Plass protein-level assembly as coding or spurious using Plass's neural network protein filter, toggled by the --filter-proteins option, so that only genuine protein sequences are retained in the assembled catalog. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41592-019-0437-4
skills.summary: Classifies candidate open reading frames produced during Plass protein-level assembly as coding or spurious using Plass's neural network protein filter, toggled by the --filter-proteins option, so that only genuine protein sequences are retained in the assembled catalog.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated, redundancy-reduced protein catalog (e.g. SRC/MERC released at 90% identity, 90% coverage) rather than raw assembly candidates containing all start/end-codon ORFs The goal is nucleotide-level contig assembly (use PenguiN's nuclassemble/guided_nuclassemble instead of Plass's protein filter) ORFs are already length-filtered above 100 amino acids, where the paper states assemblies are mostly genuine and the filter contributes little discrimination

skills.when_to_use_negative: You need true operon-level structure — MAGinator's synteny clustering lacks operon awareness, so operon inference is out of scope Input lacks per-contig gene ordering (e.g. gene clusters without ORF sequences on contigs) — adjacency cannot be derived You only need taxonomic/abundance profiling without functional annotation improvement via syntenic grouping

skills.search_text: orf-frame-branching-error-correction Use when predicting genes in raw metagenomic reads (454, Sanger, or Illumina) that carry indel or substitution sequencing errors, so that coding-frame tracking must tolerate insertions, deletions, and stop-codon-introducing substitutions. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw short-read FASTQ and no assembly has been run — this skill operates on assembled contigs or supplied long-read/contig FASTA No viral or nonviral protein databases are available — -v and -nv are required parameters and the gene-origin scoring cannot proceed without them The goal is coverage statistics or read QC rather than contig classification — those are handled by earlier virMine stages (BBMap 38.94 coverage computation, read quality control)

skills.search_text: orf-prediction-on-insertion-sequence-contigs Use when candidate IS nucleotide sequences (e.g. FASTA of ISs from ITR-based discovery) must be annotated to decide which encode transposase-family proteins. The ISs of interest lack inverted terminal repeats — Palidis is 'currently only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs', so no candidate IS FASTA exists to run Prodigal on Candidate regions fall outside the 500-3000 bp IS length range (e.g. lengthened by nested insertion events) and would be missed by the default --min_is_len/--max_is_len settings http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Predicts protein-coding ORFs on candidate insertion-sequence (IS) nucleotide sequences using Prodigal and annotates the predicted proteins with InterProScan to obtain InterPro and PANTHER family signatures, so that only ISs encoding transposase-family proteins are retained in the Palidis output. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917

skills.description: Use when you need to enumerate all possible short peptide precursors from nucleotide FASTA genomes/contigs — e.g. estimating candidate short ORFs for RiPP precursor databases or benchmarking motif-ORF vs all-ORF search-space sizes.
skills.name: orf-six-frame-translation
skills.search_text: orf-six-frame-translation Use when you need to enumerate all possible short peptide precursors from nucleotide FASTA genomes/contigs — e.g. estimating candidate short ORFs for RiPP precursor databases or benchmarking motif-ORF vs all-ORF search-space sizes. When the goal is a small, high-precision candidate set and known RiPP modification enzymes are detectable — the motif-ORF strategy (HMMer + 10 kbp BGC windows) already reduces candidates by ~4 orders of magnitude (67 vs 565,138 on the ACTI genomes) When peptides have sequence similarity to known RiPPs — the all-ORF mode is unnecessary search-space inflation; motif-ORF suffices On raw unassembled short reads — assemble reads into contigs first; MetaMiner itself does this before translation http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Enumerates candidate short ORFs by translating microbial genome (or metagenome contig) sequences in all six frames and collecting open reading frames shorter than a pre-defined length threshold (default 200 amino acids), feeding the all-ORF candidate precursor database for MetaMiner RiPP peptidogenomics. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.09.004
skills.summary: Enumerates candidate short ORFs by translating microbial genome (or metagenome contig) sequences in all six frames and collecting open reading frames shorter than a pre-defined length threshold (default 200 amino acids), feeding the all-ORF candidate precursor database for MetaMiner RiPP peptidogenomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a small, high-precision candidate set and known RiPP modification enzymes are detectable — the motif-ORF strategy (HMMer + 10 kbp BGC windows) already reduces candidates by ~4 orders of magnitude (67 vs 565,138 on the ACTI genomes) When peptides have sequence similarity to known RiPPs — the all-ORF mode is unnecessary search-space inflation; motif-ORF suffices On raw unassembled short reads — assemble reads into contigs first; MetaMiner itself does this before translation

skills.description: Use when preprocessed metatranscriptome reads (post-PEAR/Trimmomatic/SortMeRNA) need organism and functional annotations, and a local protein reference FASTA with informative headers is available or can be built.
skills.name: organism-function-assignment-from-alignment
skills.search_text: organism-function-assignment-from-alignment Use when preprocessed metatranscriptome reads (post-PEAR/Trimmomatic/SortMeRNA) need organism and functional annotations, and a local protein reference FASTA with informative headers is available or can be built. Input is raw unpreprocessed FASTQ still containing adapters, low-quality reads, or rRNA — SAMSA2 preprocessing must run first The annotation target is 16S rRNA-based taxonomic profiling without activity information; the paper notes 16S approaches 'provide no information about potential activities' Only a web-based service is acceptable or the user cannot host a local DIAMOND-indexed database locally http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Assigns organism and function labels to preprocessed metatranscriptome reads by aligning them with DIAMOND blastx against a local DIAMOND-indexed protein database whose FASTA headers encode sequence ID, function, and organism, then parsing the tabular output into a per-read annotation table. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-018-2189-z
skills.summary: Assigns organism and function labels to preprocessed metatranscriptome reads by aligning them with DIAMOND blastx against a local DIAMOND-indexed protein database whose FASTA headers encode sequence ID, function, and organism, then parsing the tabular output into a per-read annotation table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unpreprocessed FASTQ still containing adapters, low-quality reads, or rRNA — SAMSA2 preprocessing must run first The annotation target is 16S rRNA-based taxonomic profiling without activity information; the paper notes 16S approaches 'provide no information about potential activities' Only a web-based service is acceptable or the user cannot host a local DIAMOND-indexed database locally

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how accurately a metatranscriptome annotation pipeline recovers known organism identities (species/genus) and functions from reads with simulated ground-truth labels, e.g. to compare pipeline versions like SAMSA2 vs SAMSA 1.0.
skills.name: organism-taxonomic-accuracy-assessment
skills.search_text: organism-taxonomic-accuracy-assessment Use when you need to quantify how accurately a metatranscriptome annotation pipeline recovers known organism identities (species/genus) and functions from reads with simulated ground-truth labels, e.g. to compare pipeline versions like SAMSA2 vs SAMSA 1.0. Input reads are real experimental data with no simulated ground-truth labels — annotation-to-truth matching cannot be performed You need quantitative differential abundance analysis between control and experimental samples rather than annotation-accuracy benchmarking The pipeline of interest depends on a web service (e.g. MG-RAST) whose databases are not under user control, preventing a reproducible local-database comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark organism-level annotation accuracy of a metatranscriptome pipeline by annotating MetaSim-simulated gut microbiome reads against local RefSeq/SEED databases with DIAMOND (SAMSA2) and matching each read's annotation back to its simulated ground-truth label at species, genus, and SEED Subsystems hierarchy levels. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-018-2189-z
skills.summary: Benchmark organism-level annotation accuracy of a metatranscriptome pipeline by annotating MetaSim-simulated gut microbiome reads against local RefSeq/SEED databases with DIAMOND (SAMSA2) and matching each read's annotation back to its simulated ground-truth label at species, genus, and SEED Subsystems hierarchy levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are real experimental data with no simulated ground-truth labels — annotation-to-truth matching cannot be performed You need quantitative differential abundance analysis between control and experimental samples rather than annotation-accuracy benchmarking The pipeline of interest depends on a web service (e.g. MG-RAST) whose databases are not under user control, preventing a reproducible local-database comparison

skills.description: Use when a KO-level abundance table from shotgun metagenomic read mapping needs normalization before pathway aggregation, and per-genome copy-number values (not raw relative abundances) are required.
skills.name: ortholog-abundance-correction
skills.search_text: ortholog-abundance-correction Use when a KO-level abundance table from shotgun metagenomic read mapping needs normalization before pathway aggregation, and per-genome copy-number values (not raw relative abundances) are required. The user explicitly wants simple relative abundances of KOs — in that case switch the 'method' parameter to 'relative' instead of using the MUSiCC default. Input is not a KO-level ortholog abundance table from shotgun metagenomic read mapping (e.g. it is a pathway-level table already aggregated from corrected KOs). Working on Windows — MetaLAFFA, which hosts this step, is only supported on Mac and Linux. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 MetaLAFFA's default orthology-group abundance correction step: KO-level counts (already fractionally counted and gene-length-normalized) are converted by MUSiCC into average copy number per genome per sample, instead of being left as raw read-count relative abundances. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: MetaLAFFA's default orthology-group abundance correction step: KO-level counts (already fractionally counted and gene-length-normalized) are converted by MUSiCC into average copy number per genome per sample, instead of being left as raw read-count relative abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The user explicitly wants simple relative abundances of KOs — in that case switch the 'method' parameter to 'relative' instead of using the MUSiCC default. Input is not a KO-level ortholog abundance table from shotgun metagenomic read mapping (e.g. it is a pathway-level table already aggregated from corrected KOs). Working on Windows — MetaLAFFA, which hosts this step, is only supported on Mac and Linux.

skills.description: Use when you have assembled fungal genomes (high-quality or draft) and need to extract single-copy marker gene sequences to build a taxonomic marker catalog or assess genome completeness across a strain collection.
skills.name: ortholog-hmm-gene-prediction
skills.search_text: ortholog-hmm-gene-prediction Use when you have assembled fungal genomes (high-quality or draft) and need to extract single-copy marker gene sequences to build a taxonomic marker catalog or assess genome completeness across a strain collection. Input data is raw sequencing reads rather than assembled genomes — marker prediction requires assemblies for gene prediction with AUGUSTUS The target is bacterial or archaeal marker extraction — the 758 HMMs here are the Fungi OrthoDB v10.1 set, specific to fungal universal orthologs You only need functional (protein) profiling rather than taxonomic marker genes — use a protein database workflow (e.g., FunOMIC-P with Diamond blastx) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Identify single-copy marker genes in fungal genomes by running BUSCO with a curated set of universal single-copy ortholog HMMs (Fungi OrthoDB v10.1, 758 orthologs) using the AUGUSTUS gene predictor, then extract marker-gene sequences for database construction. This is the core step FunOMIC used to build its 1.6-million-gene FunOMIC-T taxonomic database. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Identify single-copy marker genes in fungal genomes by running BUSCO with a curated set of universal single-copy ortholog HMMs (Fungi OrthoDB v10.1, 758 orthologs) using the AUGUSTUS gene predictor, then extract marker-gene sequences for database construction. This is the core step FunOMIC used to build its 1.6-million-gene FunOMIC-T taxonomic database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is raw sequencing reads rather than assembled genomes — marker prediction requires assemblies for gene prediction with AUGUSTUS The target is bacterial or archaeal marker extraction — the 758 HMMs here are the Fungi OrthoDB v10.1 set, specific to fungal universal orthologs You only need functional (protein) profiling rather than taxonomic marker genes — use a protein database workflow (e.g., FunOMIC-P with Diamond blastx) instead

skills.description: Use when recovered marker FASTA sequences from genome-skimming retrieval runs (e.g. Patchwork, ALiBaSeq, aTRAM 2 outputs) must be quantitatively scored against a curated USCO reference set to compare accuracy across programs or coverages.
skills.name: ortholog-marker-accuracy-scoring
skills.search_text: ortholog-marker-accuracy-scoring Use when recovered marker FASTA sequences from genome-skimming retrieval runs (e.g. Patchwork, ALiBaSeq, aTRAM 2 outputs) must be quantitatively scored against a curated USCO reference set to compare accuracy across programs or coverages. Reference sequences are not near-universal single-copy orthologs — the authors recommend limiting references to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric retrieved sequences, so scoring against multi-copy or paralogous loci is out of scope The goal is de novo assembly quality assessment rather than marker-retrieval accuracy (that belongs to QUAST-based assembly evaluation) Retrieved markers are destined for direct tree inference without accuracy benchmarking — PREQUAL/MACSE-style cleaning and phylogenetic reconstruction are separate downstream steps http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scores recovered phylogenetic marker sequences (e.g. USCO/near-USCO retrievals from Patchwork, ALiBaSeq, or aTRAM 2) by searching them against a validated same-species reference ortholog set with DIAMOND and computing the joint metric pidentical,cov (percent identical aligned positions × reference coverage). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Scores recovered phylogenetic marker sequences (e.g. USCO/near-USCO retrievals from Patchwork, ALiBaSeq, or aTRAM 2) by searching them against a validated same-species reference ortholog set with DIAMOND and computing the joint metric pidentical,cov (percent identical aligned positions × reference coverage).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference sequences are not near-universal single-copy orthologs — the authors recommend limiting references to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric retrieved sequences, so scoring against multi-copy or paralogous loci is out of scope The goal is de novo assembly quality assessment rather than marker-retrieval accuracy (that belongs to QUAST-based assembly evaluation) Retrieved markers are destined for direct tree inference without accuracy benchmarking — PREQUAL/MACSE-style cleaning and phylogenetic reconstruction are separate downstream steps

skills.description: Use when you need to mine (near-)universal single-copy ortholog markers from a de novo short-read assembly (e.g. SPAdes contigs) or raw WGS reads for phylogenomics, with DNA-to-protein similarity search against a curated OrthoDB-based USCO reference set.
skills.name: ortholog-marker-retrieval-from-genomic-assemblies
skills.search_text: ortholog-marker-retrieval-from-genomic-assemblies Use when you need to mine (near-)universal single-copy ortholog markers from a de novo short-read assembly (e.g. SPAdes contigs) or raw WGS reads for phylogenomics, with DNA-to-protein similarity search against a curated OrthoDB-based USCO reference set. Reference sequences are not near-USCOs — the article recommends limiting references to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences You need gene annotation or full gene-model prediction rather than alignment-based marker mining (gene-prediction tools like GeMoMa target a different task) The query is already a fully annotated genome from which BUSCO could directly extract reference sequences for downstream use http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Retrieve universal single-copy orthologs (USCOs) from fragmented or high-quality genome assemblies by searching translated nucleotide contigs against amino acid reference markers with Patchwork (DIAMOND BLASTX), then stitching, trimming, and evaluating retrieval accuracy against same-species or divergent references. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Retrieve universal single-copy orthologs (USCOs) from fragmented or high-quality genome assemblies by searching translated nucleotide contigs against amino acid reference markers with Patchwork (DIAMOND BLASTX), then stitching, trimming, and evaluating retrieval accuracy against same-species or divergent references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference sequences are not near-USCOs — the article recommends limiting references to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences You need gene annotation or full gene-model prediction rather than alignment-based marker mining (gene-prediction tools like GeMoMa target a different task) The query is already a fully annotated genome from which BUSCO could directly extract reference sequences for downstream use

skills.description: Use when you have run (or are about to trust) all-vs-all BLASTP + modified Jaccard clustering on the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog and must verify the resulting VOG cluster tables are complete and correctly merged.
skills.name: orthologous-cluster-count-validation
skills.search_text: orthologous-cluster-count-validation Use when you have run (or are about to trust) all-vs-all BLASTP + modified Jaccard clustering on the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog and must verify the resulting VOG cluster tables are complete and correctly merged. The task is mapping sample reads against VIRGO for taxonomic/functional profiling (use VIRGO Module 1 runMapping.step1.sh/step2.sh instead of Jaccard clustering). You only need to BLAST a single sequence or gene list against VIRGO (Module 6 blastn/blastp), not to build or validate orthologous protein families. Your input is not the VIRGO non-redundant polypeptide set — this skill's expected cluster counts are specific to that catalog and cannot be used as invariants for other gene catalogs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validates the output of Jaccard-index clustering of the VIRGO non-redundant polypeptide set into Vaginal Orthologous Groups (VOGs), checking that the produced JAC/JOC cluster counts, multi-gene clusters, and singleton fractions match expected invariants. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Validates the output of Jaccard-index clustering of the VIRGO non-redundant polypeptide set into Vaginal Orthologous Groups (VOGs), checking that the produced JAC/JOC cluster counts, multi-gene clusters, and singleton fractions match expected invariants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is mapping sample reads against VIRGO for taxonomic/functional profiling (use VIRGO Module 1 runMapping.step1.sh/step2.sh instead of Jaccard clustering). You only need to BLAST a single sequence or gene list against VIRGO (Module 6 blastn/blastp), not to build or validate orthologous protein families. Your input is not the VIRGO non-redundant polypeptide set — this skill's expected cluster counts are specific to that catalog and cannot be used as invariants for other gene catalogs.

skills.description: Use when an OTU abundance table (e.g. .tsv, .csv or BIOM, such as HMP_SRA_gut_tiny.tsv) must be normalized automatically before FlashWeave-style statistical co-occurrence network inference.
skills.name: otu-abundance-table-normalization
skills.search_text: otu-abundance-table-normalization Use when an OTU abundance table (e.g. .tsv, .csv or BIOM, such as HMP_SRA_gut_tiny.tsv) must be normalized automatically before FlashWeave-style statistical co-occurrence network inference. The input table still contains missing entries — FlashWeave requires all samples with missing entries (in OTU and meta data tables) to be removed prior to running The data are not compositional OTU counts from sequencing data (FlashWeave's statistical co-occurrence framework is designed for large-scale compositional abundance data) Network inference or downstream graph analysis (save_network, LightGraphs.jl, Cytoscape) is the actual goal rather than reproducing the normalization step http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstructs FlashWeave's automatic pre-inference normalization of compositional OTU abundance tables, in which the normalization scheme is chosen automatically from the sensitive and heterogeneous flags (mirroring normalize=true in learn_network) before statistical co-occurrence/co-abundance network inference. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.08.002
skills.summary: Reconstructs FlashWeave's automatic pre-inference normalization of compositional OTU abundance tables, in which the normalization scheme is chosen automatically from the sensitive and heterogeneous flags (mirroring normalize=true in learn_network) before statistical co-occurrence/co-abundance network inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input table still contains missing entries — FlashWeave requires all samples with missing entries (in OTU and meta data tables) to be removed prior to running The data are not compositional OTU counts from sequencing data (FlashWeave's statistical co-occurrence framework is designed for large-scale compositional abundance data) Network inference or downstream graph analysis (save_network, LightGraphs.jl, Cytoscape) is the actual goal rather than reproducing the normalization step

skills.description: Use when you have chimera-filtered paired-end 16S reads (never merged) plus an annotated 16S FASTA database and need annotated OTUs at species-level resolution without merging reads.
skills.name: otu-clustering-against-annotated-database
skills.search_text: otu-clustering-against-annotated-database Use when you have chimera-filtered paired-end 16S reads (never merged) plus an annotated 16S FASTA database and need annotated OTUs at species-level resolution without merging reads. Input is already an OTU/feature table rather than raw paired-end FASTQ reads plus a FASTA reference database The workflow requires merged (assembled) reads or denoised amplicon sequence variants (e.g. DADA2/deblur) rather than cluster-based OTUs from unmerged pairs Reads are so short that 97% clustering cannot resolve species-level groups without database fragments matching the read length http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Annotate OTUs by clustering quality-filtered paired-end 16S reads together with fragments of an annotated 16S reference database (Greengenes or SILVA) at 97% similarity, so each OTU inherits a taxonomic annotation from the database sequence it groups with. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03591-6
skills.summary: Annotate OTUs by clustering quality-filtered paired-end 16S reads together with fragments of an annotated 16S reference database (Greengenes or SILVA) at 97% similarity, so each OTU inherits a taxonomic annotation from the database sequence it groups with.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an OTU/feature table rather than raw paired-end FASTQ reads plus a FASTA reference database The workflow requires merged (assembled) reads or denoised amplicon sequence variants (e.g. DADA2/deblur) rather than cluster-based OTUs from unmerged pairs Reads are so short that 97% clustering cannot resolve species-level groups without database fragments matching the read length

skills.description: Use when a 16S rRNA OTU table must be converted to per-organism abundances (correcting 16S copy-number variation) before predicting gene family (KO) abundances with PICRUSt.
skills.name: otu-copy-number-normalization
skills.search_text: otu-copy-number-normalization Use when a 16S rRNA OTU table must be converted to per-organism abundances (correcting 16S copy-number variation) before predicting gene family (KO) abundances with PICRUSt. Input is shotgun metagenome data annotated directly to KOs (e.g. HUMAnN-annotated WGS reads) — no 16S copy-number correction applies. The OTU table is not PICRUSt-compatible (not closed-reference picked against Greengenes+IMG), since copy-number predictions are keyed to that reference tree's tips. Only taxonomic (not functional) profiling of the community is needed — normalization is a preparatory step for metagenome prediction, not an end in itself. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Normalize a PICRUSt-compatible OTU table (BIOM format, closed-reference picked against Greengenes+IMG) by predicted 16S rRNA copy number so OTU abundances represent estimated organism counts rather than marker gene counts, as the first step of PICRUSt metagenome prediction (Langille et al. 2013, Nature Biotechnology). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Normalize a PICRUSt-compatible OTU table (BIOM format, closed-reference picked against Greengenes+IMG) by predicted 16S rRNA copy number so OTU abundances represent estimated organism counts rather than marker gene counts, as the first step of PICRUSt metagenome prediction (Langille et al. 2013, Nature Biotechnology).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is shotgun metagenome data annotated directly to KOs (e.g. HUMAnN-annotated WGS reads) — no 16S copy-number correction applies. The OTU table is not PICRUSt-compatible (not closed-reference picked against Greengenes+IMG), since copy-number predictions are keyed to that reference tree's tips. Only taxonomic (not functional) profiling of the community is needed — normalization is a preparatory step for metagenome prediction, not an end in itself.

skills.description: Use when comparing how different quality-filtering strategies (MICCA's expected-error-based filtering vs UPARSE's truncation-based filtering) change retained-read and retained-chimera fractions on simulated 16S or ITS amplicon datasets.

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) data with unknown chimeric fraction — chimera-retention percentages cannot be validated without ground truth The goal is OTU-count accuracy or ecological-index estimation (e.g. RSS of top-20 OTU abundances) rather than filtering/read-retention behavior Data are Illumina paired-end rather than the 454 single-end reads this benchmark's error model targets

skills.description: Use when comparing OTU-picking pipelines on data with a known composition (e.g. the 16S-R synthetic dataset of 500 OTUs and 100000 reads), and you need a quantitative abundance-accuracy metric rather than OTU-count or rarefaction curves.
skills.name: otu-relative-abundance-computation
skills.search_text: otu-relative-abundance-computation Use when comparing OTU-picking pipelines on data with a known composition (e.g. the 16S-R synthetic dataset of 500 OTUs and 100000 reads), and you need a quantitative abundance-accuracy metric rather than OTU-count or rarefaction curves. The dataset has no known/synthetic truth composition (e.g. real HMP, Delaware Bay, or Dethlefsen data), so RSS against truth cannot be computed The question is OTU-count estimation accuracy or chimeric-read retention rather than relative-abundance accuracy of the most abundant OTUs http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Converts per-pipeline OTU count tables to relative abundances and scores the top-20 most abundant OTUs against known/synthetic truth compositions using Residual Sum of Squares (RSS), to quantify which OTU-picking pipeline (MICCA, QIIME, UPARSE, mothur) best estimates true abundances. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/srep09743
skills.summary: Converts per-pipeline OTU count tables to relative abundances and scores the top-20 most abundant OTUs against known/synthetic truth compositions using Residual Sum of Squares (RSS), to quantify which OTU-picking pipeline (MICCA, QIIME, UPARSE, mothur) best estimates true abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no known/synthetic truth composition (e.g. real HMP, Delaware Bay, or Dethlefsen data), so RSS against truth cannot be computed The question is OTU-count estimation accuracy or chimeric-read retention rather than relative-abundance accuracy of the most abundant OTUs

skills.description: Use when an OTU/amplicon abundance table with unaltered Greengenes taxonomic assignments (read counts, not percentages) must be corrected for 16S rRNA gene copy number bias, or when 16S qPCR totals need GCN correction.
skills.name: otu-table-abundance-processing
skills.search_text: otu-table-abundance-processing Use when an OTU/amplicon abundance table with unaltered Greengenes taxonomic assignments (read counts, not percentages) must be corrected for 16S rRNA gene copy number bias, or when 16S qPCR totals need GCN correction. The input table contains percentages rather than read counts, or taxa assignments have been altered from the Greengenes format CopyRighter expects The taxonomy is not Greengenes — CopyRighter does not yet cover other taxonomies such as Silva, which is only anticipated for future extension The bias of interest is GC percent, genome length, or fungal ITS variation without appropriate pre-computed trait estimates — CopyRighter is currently limited to 16S rRNA GCN correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Correct 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) bias in OTU abundance tables using CopyRighter, which weights each OTU's read counts by the inverse of its lineage-specific GCN estimated within the Greengenes taxonomy, and optionally corrects qPCR total abundance by the community-average GCN. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Correct 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) bias in OTU abundance tables using CopyRighter, which weights each OTU's read counts by the inverse of its lineage-specific GCN estimated within the Greengenes taxonomy, and optionally corrects qPCR total abundance by the community-average GCN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input table contains percentages rather than read counts, or taxa assignments have been altered from the Greengenes format CopyRighter expects The taxonomy is not Greengenes — CopyRighter does not yet cover other taxonomies such as Silva, which is only anticipated for future extension The bias of interest is GC percent, genome length, or fungal ITS variation without appropriate pre-computed trait estimates — CopyRighter is currently limited to 16S rRNA GCN correction

skills.description: Use when raw 16S amplicon data (e.g., mockrobiota mock4, mock12, mock16) must be converted into per-method feature tables that are QC-checked, formatted for qiime2, and compared to true community compositions via weighted UniFrac.
skills.name: otu-table-qc-and-formatting
skills.search_text: otu-table-qc-and-formatting Use when raw 16S amplicon data (e.g., mockrobiota mock4, mock12, mock16) must be converted into per-method feature tables that are QC-checked, formatted for qiime2, and compared to true community compositions via weighted UniFrac. skills.name: overlap-score-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: overlap-score-threshold-filtering Use when quality-controlled NGS reads must be linked by suffix-prefix overlaps for OLC assembly, and each Minimap2-derived overlap needs a weighted identity/length score plus a length and identity cutoff. When reads are long, high-error-rate third-generation reads (e.g. PacBio CLR or noisy ONT) — the paper notes the high error rate of third-generation reads still introduces unresolved issues When the goal is generic read mapping to a reference rather than constructing read-overlap edges for strain-aware de novo assembly When overlaps are already scored by a downstream tool with its own scoring scheme (e.g. SAVAGE's statistically calibrated overlap grouping in HaploConduct) Computes StrainXpress overlap scores D = 0.9*i + 0.1*o/((r1+r2)/2) from Minimap2 CIGAR strings for suffix-prefix read overlaps, then filters overlaps by length (>= 30 bp) and identity (>= 0.9). skills.name: paired-end-fastq-mate-synchronization
skills.search_text: paired-end-fastq-mate-synchronization Use when raw paired-end shotgun viral metagenomic FASTQ files (R1/R2) need adapter removal, low-quality base trimming, and host/contaminant read removal before viral identification, and mates must stay in register. Input reads are already cleaned — ViroProfiler skips this step in that case Data are single-end reads, since the paired-end adapter detection (--detect_adapter_for_pe) and R1/R2 synchronization logic do not apply Samples with excessive environmental contaminations, which per the article increase pipeline running time and reduce precision — isolate viral fractions before sequencing instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 A read-cleaning skill from the ViroProfiler pipeline that trims and filters shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads with FASTP and the BBMap DECONTAM filter while keeping R1/R2 mates synchronized, producing cleaned paired-end FASTQ files per sample. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: A read-cleaning skill from the ViroProfiler pipeline that trims and filters shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads with FASTP and the BBMap DECONTAM filter while keeping R1/R2 mates synchronized, producing cleaned paired-end FASTQ files per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already cleaned — ViroProfiler skips this step in that case Data are single-end reads, since the paired-end adapter detection (--detect_adapter_for_pe) and R1/R2 synchronization logic do not apply Samples with excessive environmental contaminations, which per the article increase pipeline running time and reduce precision — isolate viral fractions before sequencing instead

skills.description: Use when building synthetic FASTQ benchmarks from known viral reference genomes (e.g. BASV, BKV, HIV-1) to evaluate contig extension or assembly accuracy under varied read length, error rate, and depth conditions.
skills.name: paired-end-illumina-read-simulation
skills.search_text: paired-end-illumina-read-simulation Use when building synthetic FASTQ benchmarks from known viral reference genomes (e.g. BASV, BKV, HIV-1) to evaluate contig extension or assembly accuracy under varied read length, error rate, and depth conditions. Your goal is evaluating on real metagenomics data — the article separately benchmarks ContigExtender on real animal and human metagenomics datasets, so synthetic reads are only needed for controlled parameter sweeps You need realistic background-community complexity — these simulations come from single reference genomes and cannot model mixed viral populations or host contamination http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Generates in silico synthetic Illumina FASTQ read sets with pIRS to benchmark ContigExtender under controlled read lengths (100 bp and 250 bp), error rates (1% and 5%), coverage depths (10x/20x/50x), and uneven-coverage spike-in peaks (50x 250 bp reads every 1 kb). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04038-2
skills.summary: Generates in silico synthetic Illumina FASTQ read sets with pIRS to benchmark ContigExtender under controlled read lengths (100 bp and 250 bp), error rates (1% and 5%), coverage depths (10x/20x/50x), and uneven-coverage spike-in peaks (50x 250 bp reads every 1 kb).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is evaluating on real metagenomics data — the article separately benchmarks ContigExtender on real animal and human metagenomics datasets, so synthetic reads are only needed for controlled parameter sweeps You need realistic background-community complexity — these simulations come from single reference genomes and cannot model mixed viral populations or host contamination

skills.description: Use when profiling metagenomic read mappings against reference genomes and needing to discard improperly paired or aberrant-insert-size reads before computing coverage, ANI, or SNVs.
skills.name: paired-end-insert-size-distribution-filtering
skills.search_text: paired-end-insert-size-distribution-filtering Use when profiling metagenomic read mappings against reference genomes and needing to discard improperly paired or aberrant-insert-size reads before computing coverage, ANI, or SNVs. Input alignments are single-end reads with no mate information, since all un-paired reads are removed by default and filters operate on read pairs The goal is only raw read counting or abundance estimation (e.g. with CoverM), not accurate microdiversity/SNV profiling where erroneous mappings must be reduced http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Filters metagenomic read pairs in a sorted .bam file during 'inStrain profile' by removing un-paired reads and keeping only pairs mapped in proper orientation with insert size within an expected distribution (>50 bp and <3x the median), reducing erroneous mappings. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Filters metagenomic read pairs in a sorted .bam file during 'inStrain profile' by removing un-paired reads and keeping only pairs mapped in proper orientation with insert size within an expected distribution (>50 bp and <3x the median), reducing erroneous mappings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input alignments are single-end reads with no mate information, since all un-paired reads are removed by default and filters operate on read pairs The goal is only raw read counting or abundance estimation (e.g. with CoverM), not accurate microdiversity/SNV profiling where erroneous mappings must be reduced

skills.description: Use when reconstructing full-length SSU rRNA genes (16S/18S) from paired-end Illumina metagenomic FASTQ to enable species-level taxonomic profiling via RiboTaxa's dual-assembler strategy.
skills.name: paired-end-metagenomic-read-preprocessing
skills.search_text: paired-end-metagenomic-read-preprocessing Use when reconstructing full-length SSU rRNA genes (16S/18S) from paired-end Illumina metagenomic FASTQ to enable species-level taxonomic profiling via RiboTaxa's dual-assembler strategy. When the goal is rapid taxonomic profiling of short reads without reconstruction — the article notes RiboTaxa 'is not as fast as short-read classifiers (i.e. Kraken2, Centrifuge)' When the input is already a set of full-length rRNA sequences or an ASV/OTU feature table rather than raw metagenomic reads When copy-number-corrected abundances are required — RiboTaxa explicitly does not apply 16S rRNA gene copy number normalization http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 RiboTaxa's SSU rRNA gene reconstruction layer, which reconstructs full-length 16S/18S rRNA gene sequences from Illumina shotgun (meta)genomic FASTQ by running two reference-targeted assemblers in parallel — EMIRGE (Emirge_amplicon.py) on SortMeRNA-extracted SSU reads and MetaRib on the unfiltered high-quality reads — and merging both reconstructions into metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: RiboTaxa's SSU rRNA gene reconstruction layer, which reconstructs full-length 16S/18S rRNA gene sequences from Illumina shotgun (meta)genomic FASTQ by running two reference-targeted assemblers in parallel — EMIRGE (Emirge_amplicon.py) on SortMeRNA-extracted SSU reads and MetaRib on the unfiltered high-quality reads — and merging both reconstructions into metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is rapid taxonomic profiling of short reads without reconstruction — the article notes RiboTaxa 'is not as fast as short-read classifiers (i.e. Kraken2, Centrifuge)' When the input is already a set of full-length rRNA sequences or an ASV/OTU feature table rather than raw metagenomic reads When copy-number-corrected abundances are required — RiboTaxa explicitly does not apply 16S rRNA gene copy number normalization

skills.description: Use when you have a FASTA of mixed single- and paired-end viral reads (e.g. TAR-VIR recruited_reads.fa) and need to reconstruct strain-level haplotypes de novo, without a complete reference genome.
skills.name: paired-end-overlap-graph-assembly
skills.search_text: paired-end-overlap-graph-assembly Use when you have a FASTA of mixed single- and paired-end viral reads (e.g. TAR-VIR recruited_reads.fa) and need to reconstruct strain-level haplotypes de novo, without a complete reference genome. You only need generic de novo assembly of non-strain-resolved contigs (e.g. SPAdes-style whole-genome assembly) rather than haplotype reconstruction from recruited reads No paired-end information is available, since PEHaplo relies on paired-end read connections to resolve haplotypes The target virus shares no conservation with any reference, so the upstream read-recruiting stage that generates PEHaplo's input cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 De novo strain-level assembly of viral haplotypes from recruited reads using PEHaplo, which builds a paired-end overlap graph and merges linked cliques to reconstruct haplotypes without any reference genome. In TAR-VIR this is the second stage applied after overlap-extension read recruitment. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2
skills.summary: De novo strain-level assembly of viral haplotypes from recruited reads using PEHaplo, which builds a paired-end overlap graph and merges linked cliques to reconstruct haplotypes without any reference genome. In TAR-VIR this is the second stage applied after overlap-extension read recruitment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need generic de novo assembly of non-strain-resolved contigs (e.g. SPAdes-style whole-genome assembly) rather than haplotype reconstruction from recruited reads No paired-end information is available, since PEHaplo relies on paired-end read connections to resolve haplotypes The target virus shares no conservation with any reference, so the upstream read-recruiting stage that generates PEHaplo's input cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when scoring overlapping paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. 108-base Illumina reads) to decide which assembled sequences pass a quality threshold such as p = 0.9 or p = 0.6.
skills.name: paired-end-overlap-match-probability-computation
skills.search_text: paired-end-overlap-match-probability-computation Use when scoring overlapping paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. 108-base Illumina reads) to decide which assembled sequences pass a quality threshold such as p = 0.9 or p = 0.6. Read pairs have no suitable overlap at all — the pair should simply be discarded rather than scored ('If no suitable overlap is found, then the read pair is discarded.') Input is SAM/BAM formatted and the goal is assembly with alignment output rather than overlap probability scoring — pandaseq-sam extends PANDAseq for that purpose Sequences are already assembled and a feature/OTU table exists — scoring overlap match probabilities is only relevant before or during paired-end assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes, for each position in an Illumina paired-end read overlap, the probability that the two observed nucleotides are derived from the same true base, using per-base CASAVA PHRED error probabilities and quality-mask handling; these probabilities are geometrically averaged into the overall assembly quality score used for threshold acceptance/discard decisions. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Computes, for each position in an Illumina paired-end read overlap, the probability that the two observed nucleotides are derived from the same true base, using per-base CASAVA PHRED error probabilities and quality-mask handling; these probabilities are geometrically averaged into the overall assembly quality score used for threshold acceptance/discard decisions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Read pairs have no suitable overlap at all — the pair should simply be discarded rather than scored ('If no suitable overlap is found, then the read pair is discarded.') Input is SAM/BAM formatted and the goal is assembly with alignment output rather than overlap probability scoring — pandaseq-sam extends PANDAseq for that purpose Sequences are already assembled and a feature/OTU table exists — scoring overlap match probabilities is only relevant before or during paired-end assembly

skills.description: Use when merging overlapping paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads (e.g. 16S rRNA amplicons) where naive perfect-match overlap fails due to uncalled (N) or miscalled bases, and error-correcting probabilistic assembly is needed.
skills.name: paired-end-overlap-scoring
skills.search_text: paired-end-overlap-scoring Use when merging overlapping paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads (e.g. 16S rRNA amplicons) where naive perfect-match overlap fails due to uncalled (N) or miscalled bases, and error-correcting probabilistic assembly is needed. Reads are not expected to overlap (e.g. long-insert libraries without adapter/overlap) — SeqPrep's README notes the overlapping procedure should be saved for libraries where a significant portion of reads overlap Sequencing platform with non-negligible gap probability — PANDAseq relies on Illumina-specific properties including the low probability of gap-inclusion Input is already assembled contigs or a feature/OTU table rather than raw paired-end reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Probabilistically scores every candidate overlap between forward and reverse Illumina paired-end reads to select the overlap amount that maximizes Pr[F,R|c], then reconstructs the joined sequence while correcting uncalled and miscalled bases in the overlap region, as implemented in PANDAseq. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Probabilistically scores every candidate overlap between forward and reverse Illumina paired-end reads to select the overlap amount that maximizes Pr[F,R|c], then reconstructs the joined sequence while correcting uncalled and miscalled bases in the overlap region, as implemented in PANDAseq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are not expected to overlap (e.g. long-insert libraries without adapter/overlap) — SeqPrep's README notes the overlapping procedure should be saved for libraries where a significant portion of reads overlap Sequencing platform with non-negligible gap probability — PANDAseq relies on Illumina-specific properties including the low probability of gap-inclusion Input is already assembled contigs or a feature/OTU table rather than raw paired-end reads

skills.description: Use when metagenomic FASTQ (paired-end WGSIM-simulated or real shotgun) reads must be mapped to a bacterial reference set to produce unique/split read BAMs for HGT breakpoint detection.
skills.name: paired-end-read-alignment
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-alignment Use when metagenomic FASTQ (paired-end WGSIM-simulated or real shotgun) reads must be mapped to a bacterial reference set to produce unique/split read BAMs for HGT breakpoint detection. When the goal is de novo assembly or strain typing without a reference — BWA mapping against a fixed reference set will miss reads from genomes absent from the 16,093-species reference When analyzing transcript-level fusions or isoforms (STAR-Fusion's role in the paper), not genomic HGT breakpoints from shotgun DNA reads When only ancient/lineage HGT inference from single genomes is needed rather than breakpoint-level detection from population shotgun data http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Aligns paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads against a reference set of microbiome genomes using BWA, then partitions the mapped BAM into unique-read and split-read files that feed LEMON's HGT breakpoint detection and LUMPY benchmarking. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3301-8
skills.summary: Aligns paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads against a reference set of microbiome genomes using BWA, then partitions the mapped BAM into unique-read and split-read files that feed LEMON's HGT breakpoint detection and LUMPY benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo assembly or strain typing without a reference — BWA mapping against a fixed reference set will miss reads from genomes absent from the 16,093-species reference When analyzing transcript-level fusions or isoforms (STAR-Fusion's role in the paper), not genomic HGT breakpoints from shotgun DNA reads When only ancient/lineage HGT inference from single genomes is needed rather than breakpoint-level detection from population shotgun data

skills.description: Use when Illumina paired-end FASTQ (or SAM/BAM) amplicon reads overlap and must be merged into full-length sequences with mismatch/uncalled-base correction, e.g., 16S rRNA libraries where naive assembly discards ~40% of reads.
skills.name: paired-end-read-assembly
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-assembly Use when Illumina paired-end FASTQ (or SAM/BAM) amplicon reads overlap and must be merged into full-length sequences with mismatch/uncalled-base correction, e.g., 16S rRNA libraries where naive assembly discards ~40% of reads. Input reads do not overlap (fragment length exceeds forward+reverse read span) — no suitable overlap exists and all pairs will be discarded Input is already an assembled contig or a feature/OTU table rather than raw paired-end reads Quality information is absent or unusable (e.g., FASTA-only input), since PANDAseq's probabilistic error correction relies on per-base quality scores http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assemble overlapping Illumina paired-end amplicon reads (e.g., 16S rRNA V3) into a single error-corrected sequence using PANDAseq, which determines primer locations, identifies the optimal overlap, and reconstructs the sequence probabilistically from quality scores. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Assemble overlapping Illumina paired-end amplicon reads (e.g., 16S rRNA V3) into a single error-corrected sequence using PANDAseq, which determines primer locations, identifies the optimal overlap, and reconstructs the sequence probabilistically from quality scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads do not overlap (fragment length exceeds forward+reverse read span) — no suitable overlap exists and all pairs will be discarded Input is already an assembled contig or a feature/OTU table rather than raw paired-end reads Quality information is absent or unusable (e.g., FASTA-only input), since PANDAseq's probabilistic error correction relies on per-base quality scores

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina reads (e.g. SRA FASTQ like ERR008613) must be converted into genome assembly contig FASTAs for comparison with QUAST/WebQUAST.
skills.name: paired-end-read-assembly
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-assembly Use when raw paired-end Illumina reads (e.g. SRA FASTQ like ERR008613) must be converted into genome assembly contig FASTAs for comparison with QUAST/WebQUAST. Input is long reads or a hybrid dataset — the shortlisted tools here are short-read assemblers (ABySS, MEGAHIT, SPAdes, Velvet). The goal is only to evaluate existing assemblies — use QUAST/WebQUAST directly instead of re-running assembly. A finished reference-quality assembly is required — assembled contigs (90–176 contigs, ~4.6–4.8 Mb) are drafts suitable for comparison, not finished genomes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Generates draft genome assemblies from paired-end short reads by quality-trimming with Trimmomatic and assembling with multiple short-read assemblers (ABySS, MEGAHIT, SPAdes, Velvet), producing contig FASTAs later assessed with WebQUAST/QUAST metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad406
skills.summary: Generates draft genome assemblies from paired-end short reads by quality-trimming with Trimmomatic and assembling with multiple short-read assemblers (ABySS, MEGAHIT, SPAdes, Velvet), producing contig FASTAs later assessed with WebQUAST/QUAST metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long reads or a hybrid dataset — the shortlisted tools here are short-read assemblers (ABySS, MEGAHIT, SPAdes, Velvet). The goal is only to evaluate existing assemblies — use QUAST/WebQUAST directly instead of re-running assembly. A finished reference-quality assembly is required — assembled contigs (90–176 contigs, ~4.6–4.8 Mb) are drafts suitable for comparison, not finished genomes.

skills.description: Use when a draft scaffold FASTA contains N-wildcard gap regions between contigs and a paired-end short-read dataset (e.g. Illumina GAGE PE reads) is available to fill those gaps by local reassembly.
skills.name: paired-end-read-local-reassembly
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-local-reassembly Use when a draft scaffold FASTA contains N-wildcard gap regions between contigs and a paired-end short-read dataset (e.g. Illumina GAGE PE reads) is available to fill those gaps by local reassembly. The draft assembly has no N-wildcard gap regions (contigs only, no scaffolds), so there is nothing for GapCloser to fill No paired-end or mate-pair read information is available, since gap replacement relies on 'the context and PE reads information' Gaps must be resolved using only reads from the current alignment cycle rather than the cumulative read set, i.e. when reproducing the original SOAPdenovo GapCloser behavior is the goal rather than the SOAPdenovo2 improvement http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Locally reassembles N-wildcard gap regions in draft scaffolds using paired-end (PE) short reads and read context, as implemented in the GapCloser module of SOAPdenovo2. SOAPdenovo2's GapCloser considers all reads aligned in previous iterative cycles — not only the current cycle — to better resolve conflicting bases in repetitive regions during gap closure. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: Locally reassembles N-wildcard gap regions in draft scaffolds using paired-end (PE) short reads and read context, as implemented in the GapCloser module of SOAPdenovo2. SOAPdenovo2's GapCloser considers all reads aligned in previous iterative cycles — not only the current cycle — to better resolve conflicting bases in repetitive regions during gap closure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The draft assembly has no N-wildcard gap regions (contigs only, no scaffolds), so there is nothing for GapCloser to fill No paired-end or mate-pair read information is available, since gap replacement relies on 'the context and PE reads information' Gaps must be resolved using only reads from the current alignment cycle rather than the cumulative read set, i.e. when reproducing the original SOAPdenovo GapCloser behavior is the goal rather than the SOAPdenovo2 improvement

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic analysis needs paired-end shotgun reads mapped against many reference genomes simultaneously so junction read pairs spanning two different references can seed donor/receptor detection.
skills.name: paired-end-read-mapping-to-multi-genome-reference
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-mapping-to-multi-genome-reference Use when a metagenomic analysis needs paired-end shotgun reads mapped against many reference genomes simultaneously so junction read pairs spanning two different references can seed donor/receptor detection. Input is metatranscriptomic or long-read data rather than paired-end short-read shotgun NGS datasets The goal is variant calling or quantification on a single reference genome rather than identifying cross-reference junction reads for HGT breakpoint detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Aligns paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads against a multi-genome reference (all bacterial references indexed together) using BWA mem, retaining split/junction alignments, to identify candidate donor and receptor genomes for downstream HGT breakpoint detection in LEMON. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3301-8
skills.summary: Aligns paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads against a multi-genome reference (all bacterial references indexed together) using BWA mem, retaining split/junction alignments, to identify candidate donor and receptor genomes for downstream HGT breakpoint detection in LEMON.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is metatranscriptomic or long-read data rather than paired-end short-read shotgun NGS datasets The goal is variant calling or quantification on a single reference genome rather than identifying cross-reference junction reads for HGT breakpoint detection

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads from stool metatranscriptomes must be joined into longer single fragments (longer than 100 bp) before annotation, as the SAMSA pipeline aligns paired-end files after Trimmomatic cleaning.
skills.name: paired-end-read-merging
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-merging Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads from stool metatranscriptomes must be joined into longer single fragments (longer than 100 bp) before annotation, as the SAMSA pipeline aligns paired-end files after Trimmomatic cleaning. Input is already single-end or long reads longer than 100 bp — SAMSA states sequences need to be either long reads (longer than 100 bp) or joined paired-end reads, so merging is unnecessary Input FASTQ files have not yet been cleaned — SAMSA performs cleaning and removal of adaptor contamination before aligning paired-end files, so merging raw untrimmed reads deviates from the pipeline order The goal is shotgun metagenomic population-size measurement rather than metatranscriptome annotation — merging alone cannot address the pipeline's noted limitations on measuring microbial population shifts http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Merging (joining) overlapping paired-end FASTQ reads into single, longer fragments as done in the SAMSA preprocessing phase with FLASH (or PEAR in SAMSA2), after Trimmomatic cleaning, so that merged reads exceed the ~100 bp minimum required for MG-RAST/DIAMOND annotation. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1270-8
skills.summary: Merging (joining) overlapping paired-end FASTQ reads into single, longer fragments as done in the SAMSA preprocessing phase with FLASH (or PEAR in SAMSA2), after Trimmomatic cleaning, so that merged reads exceed the ~100 bp minimum required for MG-RAST/DIAMOND annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already single-end or long reads longer than 100 bp — SAMSA states sequences need to be either long reads (longer than 100 bp) or joined paired-end reads, so merging is unnecessary Input FASTQ files have not yet been cleaned — SAMSA performs cleaning and removal of adaptor contamination before aligning paired-end files, so merging raw untrimmed reads deviates from the pipeline order The goal is shotgun metagenomic population-size measurement rather than metatranscriptome annotation — merging alone cannot address the pipeline's noted limitations on measuring microbial population shifts

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end metatranscriptome RNA-seq data in FASTQ form must be converted into a single merged, trimmed, rRNA-filtered FASTQ before DIAMOND annotation, as in the SAMSA2 preprocessing step.
skills.name: paired-end-read-merging
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-merging Use when raw paired-end metatranscriptome RNA-seq data in FASTQ form must be converted into a single merged, trimmed, rRNA-filtered FASTQ before DIAMOND annotation, as in the SAMSA2 preprocessing step. Input is single-end sequencing — PEAR merging is only used when the sequencing was paired-end Input is already merged, trimmed or rRNA-filtered FASTQ, or a downstream abundance summary — re-running preprocessing would waste CPU-intensive compute The goal is 16S rRNA amplicon analysis — SortMeRNA would discard the rRNA signal these steps are designed to remove http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Merges paired-end metatranscriptomic FASTQ mate pairs with PEAR, then quality/adaptor-trims with Trimmomatic and filters rRNA with SortMeRNA so only non-ribosomal reads feed DIAMOND annotation in the SAMSA2 pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-018-2189-z
skills.summary: Merges paired-end metatranscriptomic FASTQ mate pairs with PEAR, then quality/adaptor-trims with Trimmomatic and filters rRNA with SortMeRNA so only non-ribosomal reads feed DIAMOND annotation in the SAMSA2 pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end sequencing — PEAR merging is only used when the sequencing was paired-end Input is already merged, trimmed or rRNA-filtered FASTQ, or a downstream abundance summary — re-running preprocessing would waste CPU-intensive compute The goal is 16S rRNA amplicon analysis — SortMeRNA would discard the rRNA signal these steps are designed to remove

skills.description: Use when a paired-end QC/trimming step (e.g. fastp) has produced cleaned_1.fastq.gz and cleaned_2.fastq.gz and you must confirm the pair is synchronized, non-empty, and valid gzip FASTQ before hybrid assembly.
skills.name: paired-end-read-pair-integrity-checking
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-pair-integrity-checking Use when a paired-end QC/trimming step (e.g. fastp) has produced cleaned_1.fastq.gz and cleaned_2.fastq.gz and you must confirm the pair is synchronized, non-empty, and valid gzip FASTQ before hybrid assembly. Input is single-end FASTQ or long-read (Nanopore/PacBio) data — pairing integrity is undefined; long reads are filtered with chopper in Plassembler instead Reads have already been mapped and split (e.g. chromosomal reads removed by the Plassembler minimap2 mapping approach), where mate synchronization is re-established by the mapping step itself You only need QC statistics (Q20/Q30, adapter content) rather than pair integrity — fastp's JSON/HTML report already provides those http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Validate that quality-controlled paired-end short-read FASTQs remain synchronized: both cleaned R1/R2 gzip FASTQ outputs exist, parse as valid gzip FASTQ, and contain matching numbers of reads. This guards the Plassembler short-read QC stage (fastp) so downstream hybrid assembly receives intact read pairs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Validate that quality-controlled paired-end short-read FASTQs remain synchronized: both cleaned R1/R2 gzip FASTQ outputs exist, parse as valid gzip FASTQ, and contain matching numbers of reads. This guards the Plassembler short-read QC stage (fastp) so downstream hybrid assembly receives intact read pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end FASTQ or long-read (Nanopore/PacBio) data — pairing integrity is undefined; long reads are filtered with chopper in Plassembler instead Reads have already been mapped and split (e.g. chromosomal reads removed by the Plassembler minimap2 mapping approach), where mate synchronization is re-established by the mapping step itself You only need QC statistics (Q20/Q30, adapter content) rather than pair integrity — fastp's JSON/HTML report already provides those

skills.description: Use when classifying paired-end FASTQ read pairs (e.g. simulated 2x250 nt Illumina reads) with Kaiju, or when benchmarking throughput where read-pair ordering and naming conventions must be preserved.
skills.name: paired-end-read-pairing-handling
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-pairing-handling Use when classifying paired-end FASTQ read pairs (e.g. simulated 2x250 nt Illumina reads) with Kaiju, or when benchmarking throughput where read-pair ordering and naming conventions must be preserved. Input is single-end reads or already-translated protein sequences — then only -i (or additionally -p for protein input) is needed and pairing logic is irrelevant Read pairs are unordered or names mismatched (e.g. after subsetting only one mate) — Kaiju will error because mate names are compared after stripping suffixes after '/' or spaces http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Correctly supplies and validates paired-end FASTQ read pairs to Kaiju's taxonomic classifier, using the -i/-j input arguments and ensuring read-name consistency so both mates of a pair are classified jointly. Paired-end length strongly affects runtime, so pairing handling is integral to the runtime/memory benchmark. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Correctly supplies and validates paired-end FASTQ read pairs to Kaiju's taxonomic classifier, using the -i/-j input arguments and ensuring read-name consistency so both mates of a pair are classified jointly. Paired-end length strongly affects runtime, so pairing handling is integral to the runtime/memory benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end reads or already-translated protein sequences — then only -i (or additionally -p for protein input) is needed and pairing logic is irrelevant Read pairs are unordered or names mismatched (e.g. after subsetting only one mate) — Kaiju will error because mate names are compared after stripping suffixes after '/' or spaces

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. from SRA accessions like ERR008613) must be quality-checked and low-quality ends removed before assembly, with surviving mate pairs kept as FASTQ.GZ.
skills.name: paired-end-read-quality-trimming
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-quality-trimming Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. from SRA accessions like ERR008613) must be quality-checked and low-quality ends removed before assembly, with surviving mate pairs kept as FASTQ.GZ. Input reads are single-end, so Trimmomatic paired-end (PE) mode with surviving mate pairs does not apply Reads have already been quality-trimmed and a valid FastQC report exists for them The goal is assembly quality evaluation rather than read preprocessing — use WebQUAST/QUAST on the assemblies instead Quality-controls raw paired-end short reads with FastQC and trims low-quality read ends with Trimmomatic before genome assembly, as done for the E. coli K-12 MG1655 SRA dataset ERR008613 used to prepare sample data for WebQUAST. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad406
skills.summary: Quality-controls raw paired-end short reads with FastQC and trims low-quality read ends with Trimmomatic before genome assembly, as done for the E. coli K-12 MG1655 SRA dataset ERR008613 used to prepare sample data for WebQUAST.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are single-end, so Trimmomatic paired-end (PE) mode with surviving mate pairs does not apply Reads have already been quality-trimmed and a valid FastQC report exists for them The goal is assembly quality evaluation rather than read preprocessing — use WebQUAST/QUAST on the assemblies instead

skills.description: Use when processing paired-end 16S FASTQ reads with highly overlapping mates where quality drops in the overlap region make read merging lossy, and you want annotated OTUs without a merging step.
skills.name: paired-end-read-separate-clustering
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-separate-clustering Use when processing paired-end 16S FASTQ reads with highly overlapping mates where quality drops in the overlap region make read merging lossy, and you want annotated OTUs without a merging step. Your analysis requires merged/consensus full-length amplicon sequences or ASV inference (e.g. QIIME2-DADA2 or deblur workflows) — this approach entirely avoids read merging rather than performing it. Input is already a merged-read or single-end dataset, or a precomputed feature/OTU table — the separate-clustering scheme depends on intact R1/R2 mate pairs.
