Reads are not cropped/filtered appropriately (e.g. quality collapses before 100 nt remain) — Trimmomatic's MINLEN 100 cutoff would discard the reads entirely. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Cluster R1 and R2 reads of paired-end 16S amplicon data separately (never merging or concatenating mates), following the CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq scheme, so chimeric read pairs can be detected by discordant cluster voting and OTUs retrieved with less read discarding than merging-based pipelines. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03591-6
skills.summary: Cluster R1 and R2 reads of paired-end 16S amplicon data separately (never merging or concatenating mates), following the CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq scheme, so chimeric read pairs can be detected by discordant cluster voting and OTUs retrieved with less read discarding than merging-based pipelines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your analysis requires merged/consensus full-length amplicon sequences or ASV inference (e.g. QIIME2-DADA2 or deblur workflows) — this approach entirely avoids read merging rather than performing it. Input is already a merged-read or single-end dataset, or a precomputed feature/OTU table — the separate-clustering scheme depends on intact R1/R2 mate pairs. Reads are not cropped/filtered appropriately (e.g. quality collapses before 100 nt remain) — Trimmomatic's MINLEN 100 cutoff would discard the reads entirely.

skills.description: Use when deciding whether paired-end sequencing is necessary for metatranscriptome annotation, or when quantifying how much annotation information is lost by processing paired-end reads as single-end.
skills.name: paired-end-read-simulation-to-single-end
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-simulation-to-single-end Use when deciding whether paired-end sequencing is necessary for metatranscriptome annotation, or when quantifying how much annotation information is lost by processing paired-end reads as single-end. Input reads are already single-end — no simulation is possible or meaningful. Annotation is done locally with SAMSA2/DIAMOND against a custom database rather than via MG-RAST, since the comparison workflow is tied to MG-RAST v3.6 submission and its queue. The goal is organism abundance estimation from already-annotated summary tables rather than a raw-read preprocessing comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Simulates single-end metatranscriptome data from paired-end FASTQ files by truncating each read to 100 bp with Trimmomatic, enabling a controlled comparison of annotation loss between paired-end and single-end processing in the SAMSA/MG-RAST pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1270-8
skills.summary: Simulates single-end metatranscriptome data from paired-end FASTQ files by truncating each read to 100 bp with Trimmomatic, enabling a controlled comparison of annotation loss between paired-end and single-end processing in the SAMSA/MG-RAST pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already single-end — no simulation is possible or meaningful. Annotation is done locally with SAMSA2/DIAMOND against a custom database rather than via MG-RAST, since the comparison workflow is tied to MG-RAST v3.6 submission and its queue. The goal is organism abundance estimation from already-annotated summary tables rather than a raw-read preprocessing comparison.

skills.description: Use when classifying paired-end reads (e.g., setB2_1/setB2_2 FASTA files) whose strand orientation is unknown, and classification quality depends on considering forward and reverse-complement strands.
skills.name: paired-end-reverse-complement-handling
skills.search_text: paired-end-reverse-complement-handling Use when classifying paired-end reads (e.g., setB2_1/setB2_2 FASTA files) whose strand orientation is unknown, and classification quality depends on considering forward and reverse-complement strands. Reads are single-end with no reverse-complement variant required for orientation handling A classifier already handles strand direction internally and paired-end data structures would be redundant Only raw reads without a reference genome database to merge against http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Handles unknown strand direction in paired-end metagenomic classification (LiME workflow) by building and analyzing data structures for both the original reads and their reverse complements, so each read pair is classified with reads properly oriented. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03628-w
skills.summary: Handles unknown strand direction in paired-end metagenomic classification (LiME workflow) by building and analyzing data structures for both the original reads and their reverse complements, so each read pair is classified with reads properly oriented.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are single-end with no reverse-complement variant required for orientation handling A classifier already handles strand direction internally and paired-end data structures would be redundant Only raw reads without a reference genome database to merge against

skills.description: Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads with LiME and you must build similarity matrices for all four collections (Reads1F, Reads1RC, Reads2F, Reads2RC) merged against the reference genomes.
skills.name: paired-end-similarity-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: paired-end-similarity-matrix-computation Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads with LiME and you must build similarity matrices for all four collections (Reads1F, Reads1RC, Reads2F, Reads2RC) merged against the reference genomes. The input requires a taxonomy classification decision (species/genus/phylum assignment) — that is handled by the separate Classify step, not the similarity computation The reads are single-end only and no paired-end strand re-examination is needed — only forward and reverse-complement structures of one mate are required The goal is alignment-based classification against a full nucleotide database (e.g., BLAST-based filtering at 98% identity) — LiME's similarity matrix is alignment-free http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Computes a many-to-many read-vs-genome similarity matrix using LiME's alpha-cluster analysis over the eBWT, lcp, and da data structures of a merged read+genome collection, repeating the computation for forward and reverse-complement strands of both mates of paired-end reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03628-w
skills.summary: Computes a many-to-many read-vs-genome similarity matrix using LiME's alpha-cluster analysis over the eBWT, lcp, and da data structures of a merged read+genome collection, repeating the computation for forward and reverse-complement strands of both mates of paired-end reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input requires a taxonomy classification decision (species/genus/phylum assignment) — that is handled by the separate Classify step, not the similarity computation The reads are single-end only and no paired-end strand re-examination is needed — only forward and reverse-complement structures of one mate are required The goal is alignment-based classification against a full nucleotide database (e.g., BLAST-based filtering at 98% identity) — LiME's similarity matrix is alignment-free

skills.description: Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g. 100 bp Illumina mates from SRR1804065 or setB2) with LiME, when strand direction is unknown and ambiguous reads must be resolved with mate information.
skills.name: paired-end-strand-and-mate-handling
skills.search_text: paired-end-strand-and-mate-handling Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g. 100 bp Illumina mates from SRR1804065 or setB2) with LiME, when strand direction is unknown and ambiguous reads must be resolved with mate information. Input is single-end reads — the paired-end procedure (four collections and mate-based re-examination) does not apply; use the single-read-collection strategy Reads are already strand-oriented and mate-aware classification is unnecessary — running both strands duplicates the alpha-cluster and similarity steps for no gain Reference structures have not been merged (no ebwt/lcp/da for S) — classification requires merged collection data structures, not raw FASTA alone http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Handles paired-end read collections in the LiME eBWT-based metagenomic classifier: because read strand direction is unknown, classification is run over four collections (forward and reverse-complement of both mates), and ambiguous reads are re-examined using mate-pair information. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03628-w
skills.summary: Handles paired-end read collections in the LiME eBWT-based metagenomic classifier: because read strand direction is unknown, classification is run over four collections (forward and reverse-complement of both mates), and ambiguous reads are re-examined using mate-pair information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end reads — the paired-end procedure (four collections and mate-based re-examination) does not apply; use the single-read-collection strategy Reads are already strand-oriented and mate-aware classification is unnecessary — running both strands duplicates the alpha-cluster and similarity steps for no gain Reference structures have not been merged (no ebwt/lcp/da for S) — classification requires merged collection data structures, not raw FASTA alone

skills.description: Use when classifying paired-end reads from simulated or real metagenomes (e.g., HiSeq, MiSeq or simBA-5 read sets) with a k-mer LCA classifier that accepts single sequences, and you want both mates of a pair to vote together for one taxon.
skills.name: paired-read-concatenation-for-classification
skills.search_text: paired-read-concatenation-for-classification Use when classifying paired-end reads from simulated or real metagenomes (e.g., HiSeq, MiSeq or simBA-5 read sets) with a k-mer LCA classifier that accepts single sequences, and you want both mates of a pair to vote together for one taxon. When the classifier accepts paired-end input natively or when read mates must be scored independently (e.g., per-mate sensitivity analyses) When k-mer content spanning the mate junction matters — the 'NNNNN' spacer creates ambiguous k-mers that Kraken ignores, so any signal across the insert is lost For long single reads or contigs that are not paired-end data http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Concatenates paired-end metagenomic read mates with an 'NNNNN' spacer so that a taxonomic classifier such as Kraken processes each mate pair as a single sequence unit rather than two independent reads, preserving paired evidence during LCA-based k-mer classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Concatenates paired-end metagenomic read mates with an 'NNNNN' spacer so that a taxonomic classifier such as Kraken processes each mate pair as a single sequence unit rather than two independent reads, preserving paired evidence during LCA-based k-mer classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the classifier accepts paired-end input natively or when read mates must be scored independently (e.g., per-mate sensitivity analyses) When k-mer content spanning the mate junction matters — the 'NNNNN' spacer creates ambiguous k-mers that Kraken ignores, so any signal across the insert is lost For long single reads or contigs that are not paired-end data

skills.description: Use when preparing .bam files for inStrain profile/compare so that genome coverage, SNV calls, and strain-level comparisons (ConANI/popANI) rest on correctly mapped read pairs rather than spurious single-end or mis-oriented alignments.
skills.name: paired-read-filtering-quality-control
skills.search_text: paired-read-filtering-quality-control Use when preparing .bam files for inStrain profile/compare so that genome coverage, SNV calls, and strain-level comparisons (ConANI/popANI) rest on correctly mapped read pairs rather than spurious single-end or mis-oriented alignments. Input .bam contains only single-end reads — un-paired reads are removed by default, so no usable data would remain for profiling The goal is raw read-count quantification (e.g. with CoverM) where aggressive pair filtering would discard signal; inStrain's filters target genome-comparison accuracy, not general coverage estimation Sequencing technology or library layout differs such that proper-orientation and expected-insert-size assumptions do not hold for the read pairs http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A read-filtering QC step used by inStrain before profiling metagenomic .bam files: un-paired reads are removed and read pairs must pass mapping-orientation, insert-size, mapQ, and nucleotide-identity criteria so that downstream coverage, SNV, and popANI calculations are not skewed by erroneously mapped reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: A read-filtering QC step used by inStrain before profiling metagenomic .bam files: un-paired reads are removed and read pairs must pass mapping-orientation, insert-size, mapQ, and nucleotide-identity criteria so that downstream coverage, SNV, and popANI calculations are not skewed by erroneously mapped reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input .bam contains only single-end reads — un-paired reads are removed by default, so no usable data would remain for profiling The goal is raw read-count quantification (e.g. with CoverM) where aggressive pair filtering would discard signal; inStrain's filters target genome-comparison accuracy, not general coverage estimation Sequencing technology or library layout differs such that proper-orientation and expected-insert-size assumptions do not hold for the read pairs

skills.description: Use when paired-end read pairs (e.g. KAL_D, 26,114K read pairs) must be taxonomically assigned against multi-kingdom reference genome databases, especially when benchmarking MetaCache/AFS-MetaCache, CLARK, or Kraken2+Bracken classification quality or runtime.
skills.name: paired-read-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: paired-read-taxonomic-classification Use when paired-end read pairs (e.g. KAL_D, 26,114K read pairs) must be taxonomically assigned against multi-kingdom reference genome databases, especially when benchmarking MetaCache/AFS-MetaCache, CLARK, or Kraken2+Bracken classification quality or runtime. Input is single-end reads only and paired-read mode (-r) cannot be exploited The task requires alignment-based read placement (e.g. BWA/Bowtie2 in the original AFS pipeline) rather than alignment-free k-mer classification The database was built with different MetaCache data-type compilation settings than the querying binary (databases only work with the same variant) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Classifies paired-end sequencing reads against large AFS reference databases (AFS20, AFS31, AFS20RS90, AFS31RS90) using minhashing-based metagenomic classifiers in paired-read mode with threshold query logic, for detection and quantification of food sample composition. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Classifies paired-end sequencing reads against large AFS reference databases (AFS20, AFS31, AFS20RS90, AFS31RS90) using minhashing-based metagenomic classifiers in paired-read mode with threshold query logic, for detection and quantification of food sample composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end reads only and paired-read mode (-r) cannot be exploited The task requires alignment-based read placement (e.g. BWA/Bowtie2 in the original AFS pipeline) rather than alignment-free k-mer classification The database was built with different MetaCache data-type compilation settings than the querying binary (databases only work with the same variant)

skills.description: Use when you need sensitive strain-level comparison of microbial populations across metagenomic samples, e.g. testing whether related individuals share more strains than unrelated ones.
skills.name: pairwise-genome-ani-comparison
skills.search_text: pairwise-genome-ani-comparison Use when you need sensitive strain-level comparison of microbial populations across metagenomic samples, e.g. testing whether related individuals share more strains than unrelated ones. You only need coarse coverage and breadth of genomes per sample — CoverM or standard mapping-based quantification suffices without popANI comparison. You need species-level community profiling from reference databases (e.g. MetaPhlAn-style) rather than strain-level resolution on a custom genome set. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Use inStrain compare to obtain all pairwise ConANI and popANI values between metagenomic samples, then cluster sub-species into strains with 'average' hierarchical clustering at a 99.999% ANI threshold to quantify strain sharing across samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Use inStrain compare to obtain all pairwise ConANI and popANI values between metagenomic samples, then cluster sub-species into strains with 'average' hierarchical clustering at a 99.999% ANI threshold to quantify strain sharing across samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need coarse coverage and breadth of genomes per sample — CoverM or standard mapping-based quantification suffices without popANI comparison. You need species-level community profiling from reference databases (e.g. MetaPhlAn-style) rather than strain-level resolution on a custom genome set.

skills.description: Use when pairwise genomic comparison of the same genome set across metagenomic samples must distinguish true shared strains from co-occurring but divergent populations, e.g. twin strain-sharing benchmarks.
skills.name: pairwise-instrain-profile-comparison
skills.search_text: pairwise-instrain-profile-comparison Use when pairwise genomic comparison of the same genome set across metagenomic samples must distinguish true shared strains from co-occurring but divergent populations, e.g. twin strain-sharing benchmarks. When only genome-level dereplication of a single genome set is needed (no per-sample profiles) — use 'dRep dereplicate' instead When reads have not been mapped to a shared reference .fasta, since inStrain compare requires profile objects created from mappings to the same genome set When quick coverage/breadth calculation alone is sufficient — a tool like CoverM can compute coverage without microdiversity-aware comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Compare inStrain profile objects built from different samples' read mappings to compute microdiversity-aware popANI and coverage overlap between all sample pairs, enabling accurate strain-sharing detection that outperforms ANI-only tools like dRep and MIDAS. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Compare inStrain profile objects built from different samples' read mappings to compute microdiversity-aware popANI and coverage overlap between all sample pairs, enabling accurate strain-sharing detection that outperforms ANI-only tools like dRep and MIDAS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only genome-level dereplication of a single genome set is needed (no per-sample profiles) — use 'dRep dereplicate' instead When reads have not been mapped to a shared reference .fasta, since inStrain compare requires profile objects created from mappings to the same genome set When quick coverage/breadth calculation alone is sufficient — a tool like CoverM can compute coverage without microdiversity-aware comparison

skills.description: Use when detecting recent selective sweeps by contrasting haplotype lengths between two populations from chromosome-split, tabix-indexed biallelic VCFs plus a sample-to-population .map file.
skills.name: pairwise-population-xpehh-comparison
skills.search_text: pairwise-population-xpehh-comparison Use when detecting recent selective sweeps by contrasting haplotype lengths between two populations from chromosome-split, tabix-indexed biallelic VCFs plus a sample-to-population .map file. Input VCFs are not phased or not split/indexed per chromosome — phase with Beagle or SHAPEIT5 first, as selscan requires phased haplotypes Only a single population is present — XP-EHH is a between-population comparison; use a within-population scan such as iHS or SweepFinder2 instead Data are multi-allelic or non-SNP variants — scalepopgen's selection sub-workflow targets biallelic SNP data only http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Computes XP-EHH (cross-population extended haplotype homozygosity) between each possible pair of populations on biallelic SNP data, as implemented in the scalepopgen Nextflow signatures-of-selection sub-workflow using selscan on Beagle/SHAPEIT5-phased haplotypes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Computes XP-EHH (cross-population extended haplotype homozygosity) between each possible pair of populations on biallelic SNP data, as implemented in the scalepopgen Nextflow signatures-of-selection sub-workflow using selscan on Beagle/SHAPEIT5-phased haplotypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input VCFs are not phased or not split/indexed per chromosome — phase with Beagle or SHAPEIT5 first, as selscan requires phased haplotypes Only a single population is present — XP-EHH is a between-population comparison; use a within-population scan such as iHS or SweepFinder2 instead Data are multi-allelic or non-SNP variants — scalepopgen's selection sub-workflow targets biallelic SNP data only

skills.description: Use when you have a FASTA of predicted viral scaffolds and need a scaffold-by-scaffold nucleotide feature distance table (7 features per pair) to feed ML-based viral binning like vRhyme's.
skills.name: pairwise-scaffold-distance-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: pairwise-scaffold-distance-matrix-construction Use when you have a FASTA of predicted viral scaffolds and need a scaffold-by-scaffold nucleotide feature distance table (7 features per pair) to feed ML-based viral binning like vRhyme's. Input is an entire unfiltered metagenome rather than predicted viral scaffolds — vRhyme's performance on whole metagenomes has not been fully evaluated and it is not meant to bin microbes Scaffolds shorter than 2000bp or circular (complete viral genome) scaffolds removed pre-binning — these are filtered before distance construction Binning should rely on coverage information rather than sequence composition — this skill produces only nucleotide-feature distances, not coverage effect-size comparisons Reconstructs vRhyme's nucleotide feature distance module: compute per-scaffold composition features (tetranucleotide frequencies, GC, CpG, GC skew, codon usage) and convert them into length-7 pairwise distance vectors M_i,j for every scaffold pair, written to vRhyme_machine_distances.tsv as input to vRhyme's supervised ML binning models. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Reconstructs vRhyme's nucleotide feature distance module: compute per-scaffold composition features (tetranucleotide frequencies, GC, CpG, GC skew, codon usage) and convert them into length-7 pairwise distance vectors M_i,j for every scaffold pair, written to vRhyme_machine_distances.tsv as input to vRhyme's supervised ML binning models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an entire unfiltered metagenome rather than predicted viral scaffolds — vRhyme's performance on whole metagenomes has not been fully evaluated and it is not meant to bin microbes Scaffolds shorter than 2000bp or circular (complete viral genome) scaffolds removed pre-binning — these are filtered before distance construction Binning should rely on coverage information rather than sequence composition — this skill produces only nucleotide-feature distances, not coverage effect-size comparisons

skills.description: Use when two raw FASTA/FASTQ read collections from related samples must be compared for SNP/INDEL discovery without aligning to a reference genome, and sensitivity against a de Bruijn graph baseline (DISCOSNP++) must be quantified.
skills.name: pairwise-snp-indel-discovery-between-samples
skills.search_text: pairwise-snp-indel-discovery-between-samples Use when two raw FASTA/FASTQ read collections from related samples must be compared for SNP/INDEL discovery without aligning to a reference genome, and sensitivity against a de Bruijn graph baseline (DISCOSNP++) must be quantified. A high-quality reference genome and mature reference-based calling are required or preferred — ebwt2InDel is deliberately reference-free/alignment-free Only a single sample (one read collection) is available and no pairwise comparison is needed INDEL calls from a parallelized pipeline are required: the parallel pipeline works for SNPs only, so sequential ebwt2InDel must be used for INDELs http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reference-free, alignment-free discovery of SNPs and INDELs between two read sets (e.g. mother NA12892 and son NA12878 whole-genome data at ~10x each) by running ebwt2InDel on the extended Burrows-Wheeler Transforms of the two collections, then benchmarking sensitivity against DISCOSNP++ with hap.py. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Reference-free, alignment-free discovery of SNPs and INDELs between two read sets (e.g. mother NA12892 and son NA12878 whole-genome data at ~10x each) by running ebwt2InDel on the extended Burrows-Wheeler Transforms of the two collections, then benchmarking sensitivity against DISCOSNP++ with hap.py.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A high-quality reference genome and mature reference-based calling are required or preferred — ebwt2InDel is deliberately reference-free/alignment-free Only a single sample (one read collection) is available and no pairwise comparison is needed INDEL calls from a parallelized pipeline are required: the parallel pipeline works for SNPs only, so sequential ebwt2InDel must be used for INDELs

skills.description: Use when you already have raw per-region synteny scores (e.g. synteny_scores_per_region.csv) and need a robust pairwise relatedness matrix over sample pairs, controlling for unequal region counts per pair.
skills.name: pairwise-synteny-score-averaging
skills.search_text: pairwise-synteny-score-averaging Use when you already have raw per-region synteny scores (e.g. synteny_scores_per_region.csv) and need a robust pairwise relatedness matrix over sample pairs, controlling for unequal region counts per pair. You only need SNP-based strain differences: SynTracker's synteny score has low sensitivity to SNPs, so use an SNP-based tool instead (combining both detects strains enriched in either point mutations or structural changes) Pairs of samples have fewer than n available homologous regions — such pairs are excluded from downstream analysis and cannot receive an n-region APSS You need a universal same-strain cutoff: the APSS 0.95 cutoff was averaged across per-species cutoffs and may not be optimal for all settings; thresholds are subjective and species-dependent http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Compute the Average Pairwise Synteny Score (APSS) by randomly subsampling n per-region pairwise synteny scores per pair of metagenomic samples or genomes and averaging them, with reproducible seeding and an all-regions variant. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Compute the Average Pairwise Synteny Score (APSS) by randomly subsampling n per-region pairwise synteny scores per pair of metagenomic samples or genomes and averaging them, with reproducible seeding and an all-regions variant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need SNP-based strain differences: SynTracker's synteny score has low sensitivity to SNPs, so use an SNP-based tool instead (combining both detects strains enriched in either point mutations or structural changes) Pairs of samples have fewer than n available homologous regions — such pairs are excluded from downstream analysis and cannot receive an n-region APSS You need a universal same-strain cutoff: the APSS 0.95 cutoff was averaged across per-species cutoffs and may not be optimal for all settings; thresholds are subjective and species-dependent

skills.description: Use when you need to classify nanopore reads against one or many related reference genomes (e.g. one-genome vs multi-strain pan-genome FASTA) for targeted depletion, and must build MS and PML indexes plus a null index before running SPUMONI classification.
skills.name: pan-genome-index-construction
skills.search_text: pan-genome-index-construction Use when you need to classify nanopore reads against one or many related reference genomes (e.g. one-genome vs multi-strain pan-genome FASTA) for targeted depletion, and must build MS and PML indexes plus a null index before running SPUMONI classification. Input is raw nanopore electrical signal — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences, so a separate base caller must run upstream The task requires base-level alignments rather than classify/eject decisions — use minimap2 alignment instead There is substantial sequence similarity between depletion-target reads and non-target reads (e.g. conserved genes between species) — the reverse-sequence null index may be insufficient http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Constructs SPUMONI pan-genome indexes containing both matching-statistics (MS) and pseudo-matching-length (PML) structures, plus a reverse-sequence null index, to support streaming nanopore read classification against large repetitive references. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Constructs SPUMONI pan-genome indexes containing both matching-statistics (MS) and pseudo-matching-length (PML) structures, plus a reverse-sequence null index, to support streaming nanopore read classification against large repetitive references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nanopore electrical signal — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences, so a separate base caller must run upstream The task requires base-level alignments rather than classify/eject decisions — use minimap2 alignment instead There is substantial sequence similarity between depletion-target reads and non-target reads (e.g. conserved genes between species) — the reverse-sequence null index may be insufficient

skills.description: Use when a reduced nucleotide reference of species-level gene space is needed to assign metagenomic contigs to close relatives or to select species-specific gene prediction models, as in the GeneMark-HM pipeline.
skills.name: pan-genome-sequence-construction
skills.search_text: pan-genome-sequence-construction Use when a reduced nucleotide reference of species-level gene space is needed to assign metagenomic contigs to close relatives or to select species-specific gene prediction models, as in the GeneMark-HM pipeline. When the goal is annotating metagenomic contigs themselves rather than building the reference database (the downstream GeneMark-HM assignment step consumes this database, it does not produce it) When you need per-taxon gene finding models directly — those live in the separate 'refmod' database of model files, not in the pan-genome sequence database When studying taxa outside the set of species known to be present in human microbiomes, since the database was built from genomes of species present in human gut/oral/skin metagenomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Builds a species-level pan-genome sequence database for the human microbiome from reference genomes, seeding each pan-genome with its representative genome's predicted genes and admitting additional genes only when no MegaBLAST target shows ANI >95% with >90% query coverage, yielding 5082 pan-genomes compiled into a ~20 Gb BLAST-searchable nucleotide FASTA. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047
skills.summary: Builds a species-level pan-genome sequence database for the human microbiome from reference genomes, seeding each pan-genome with its representative genome's predicted genes and admitting additional genes only when no MegaBLAST target shows ANI >95% with >90% query coverage, yielding 5082 pan-genomes compiled into a ~20 Gb BLAST-searchable nucleotide FASTA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is annotating metagenomic contigs themselves rather than building the reference database (the downstream GeneMark-HM assignment step consumes this database, it does not produce it) When you need per-taxon gene finding models directly — those live in the separate 'refmod' database of model files, not in the pan-genome sequence database When studying taxa outside the set of species known to be present in human microbiomes, since the database was built from genomes of species present in human gut/oral/skin metagenomes

skills.description: Use when annotating short human-microbiome metagenomic contigs that cannot support de novo self-training, and species-specific parameters must be imported via pan-genome model selection.
skills.name: pan-genome-similarity-search-execution
skills.search_text: pan-genome-similarity-search-execution Use when annotating short human-microbiome metagenomic contigs that cannot support de novo self-training, and species-specific parameters must be imported via pan-genome model selection. Input is a complete prokaryotic genome long enough for direct GeneMarkS-2 self-training rather than short anonymous contigs The metagenome is outside the human microbiome scope and its taxa are absent from the >5000-taxon gut-derived pan-genome database A contig cannot be reliably assigned to any reference pan-genome, in which case the fallback MetaGeneMark-2/GeneMarkS-2 path applies instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assigns metagenomic contigs to species-level pan-genomes by a fast blastn similarity search that uses initially predicted genes as queries against a ~20 Gb pan-genome database; the best matches select taxa-specific GeneMark.hmm-2 model files for downstream gene prediction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047
skills.summary: Assigns metagenomic contigs to species-level pan-genomes by a fast blastn similarity search that uses initially predicted genes as queries against a ~20 Gb pan-genome database; the best matches select taxa-specific GeneMark.hmm-2 model files for downstream gene prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a complete prokaryotic genome long enough for direct GeneMarkS-2 self-training rather than short anonymous contigs The metagenome is outside the human microbiome scope and its taxa are absent from the >5000-taxon gut-derived pan-genome database A contig cannot be reliably assigned to any reference pan-genome, in which case the fallback MetaGeneMark-2/GeneMarkS-2 path applies instead

skills.description: Use when predicting protein-coding genes in assembled human microbiome metagenome contigs and you need species-level parameter selection via pan-genome assignment rather than generic metagenomic models.
skills.name: pangenome-contig-assignment
skills.search_text: pangenome-contig-assignment Use when predicting protein-coding genes in assembled human microbiome metagenome contigs and you need species-level parameter selection via pan-genome assignment rather than generic metagenomic models. The metagenome is not from the human microbiome — the pan-genome database was built from human gut/oral/skin taxa, so contigs from environmental or non-human sources will largely miss assignment and fall back to crude GC-based models The contigs are complete or nearly complete genomes — GeneMarkS-2 alone can self-train directly and does not need the pan-genome assignment step A species-specific model for the organism of interest already exists and can be supplied externally http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assigns metagenomic contigs from the human microbiome to species-level pan-genomes by BLASTing initially predicted genes against a pan-gene database, then selects the corresponding pre-computed GeneMark.hmm-2 model (fallback: GeneMarkS-2 for long contigs, MetaGeneMark for short ones). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047
skills.summary: Assigns metagenomic contigs from the human microbiome to species-level pan-genomes by BLASTing initially predicted genes against a pan-gene database, then selects the corresponding pre-computed GeneMark.hmm-2 model (fallback: GeneMarkS-2 for long contigs, MetaGeneMark for short ones).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metagenome is not from the human microbiome — the pan-genome database was built from human gut/oral/skin taxa, so contigs from environmental or non-human sources will largely miss assignment and fall back to crude GC-based models The contigs are complete or nearly complete genomes — GeneMarkS-2 alone can self-train directly and does not need the pan-genome assignment step A species-specific model for the organism of interest already exists and can be supplied externally

skills.description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking GeneMark-HM's efficiency claims, specifically the factor-15 database reduction and single-CPU run-time comparisons on metagenomic contigs.
skills.name: pangenome-database-volume-reduction-analysis
skills.search_text: pangenome-database-volume-reduction-analysis Use when reproducing or benchmarking GeneMark-HM's efficiency claims, specifically the factor-15 database reduction and single-CPU run-time comparisons on metagenomic contigs. The goal is gene prediction accuracy evaluation (gene start error rates, TGA codon assignment) rather than computational efficiency of the pan-genome database The input metagenome is not from the human microbiome — the pipeline is parameterized for human microbiome data and pan-genome assignment rates drop for oral (89.0%) and skin (79.4%) metagenomes Multi-CPU benchmarking is required; the published targets (≈12 min, ~80% in BLASTn) are single-CPU conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmarks the GeneMark-HM pipeline's computational efficiency: quantifies the volume/memory reduction achieved by species-level pan-genome databases versus non-redundant SGB/tCluster gene sets, and measures wall-clock run-times of GeneMark-HM versus MetaGeneMark and MetaProdigal on a fixed 45 Mb metagenome sequence. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047
skills.summary: Benchmarks the GeneMark-HM pipeline's computational efficiency: quantifies the volume/memory reduction achieved by species-level pan-genome databases versus non-redundant SGB/tCluster gene sets, and measures wall-clock run-times of GeneMark-HM versus MetaGeneMark and MetaProdigal on a fixed 45 Mb metagenome sequence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene prediction accuracy evaluation (gene start error rates, TGA codon assignment) rather than computational efficiency of the pan-genome database The input metagenome is not from the human microbiome — the pipeline is parameterized for human microbiome data and pan-genome assignment rates drop for oral (89.0%) and skin (79.4%) metagenomes Multi-CPU benchmarking is required; the published targets (≈12 min, ~80% in BLASTn) are single-CPU conditions

skills.description: Use when computing core-genome partitioning from presence/absence patterns of gene clusters or traits in genome sets of highly diverse completeness (e.g. MAGs/SAGs with CheckM completeness/contamination estimates), and when the quality of that partitioning must be quantified via bootstrapping.
skills.name: pangenome-partitioning-quality-bootstrapping
skills.search_text: pangenome-partitioning-quality-bootstrapping Use when computing core-genome partitioning from presence/absence patterns of gene clusters or traits in genome sets of highly diverse completeness (e.g. MAGs/SAGs with CheckM completeness/contamination estimates), and when the quality of that partitioning must be quantified via bootstrapping. You are looking for mOTUs, the read-based OTU-table tool (motu-tool.org) — mOTUlizer is a different tool for MAG/bin pangenomics Your goal is only gene clustering, not core/accessory classification — use --genome2cog_only (mmseqs easy_cluster) or Roary/PPanGGOLiN on high-quality complete genomes instead The genomes are complete/high-quality isolates where standard pangenome tools like Roary or PPanGGOLiN already perform comparably http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 An iterative Bayesian core/accessory genome partitioning procedure (mOTUpan in the mOTUlizer package) that classifies genome-encoded traits by core-vs-accessory likelihood ratios, re-estimates genome completeness from the partitioning until convergence, and bootstraps artificial genomes to estimate false-positive rate, recall, and 'lowest false'. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac060
skills.summary: An iterative Bayesian core/accessory genome partitioning procedure (mOTUpan in the mOTUlizer package) that classifies genome-encoded traits by core-vs-accessory likelihood ratios, re-estimates genome completeness from the partitioning until convergence, and bootstraps artificial genomes to estimate false-positive rate, recall, and 'lowest false'.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are looking for mOTUs, the read-based OTU-table tool (motu-tool.org) — mOTUlizer is a different tool for MAG/bin pangenomics Your goal is only gene clustering, not core/accessory classification — use --genome2cog_only (mmseqs easy_cluster) or Roary/PPanGGOLiN on high-quality complete genomes instead The genomes are complete/high-quality isolates where standard pangenome tools like Roary or PPanGGOLiN already perform comparably

skills.description: Use when comparing read-classification tool performance (bases/second throughput, index size, peak RSS) across references of differing repetitiveness, e.g. single-genome vs many-strain pan-genome indexes on mock-community reads.
skills.name: pangenome-reference-repetitiveness-analysis
skills.search_text: pangenome-reference-repetitiveness-analysis Use when comparing read-classification tool performance (bases/second throughput, index size, peak RSS) across references of differing repetitiveness, e.g. single-genome vs many-strain pan-genome indexes on mock-community reads. The task is raw read classification or alignment itself rather than quantifying resource/performance scaling between existing benchmark runs Only a single reference of fixed repetitiveness is available, so the throughput-vs-repetitiveness trend cannot be computed The goal is accuracy evaluation (F1 score, KS-stat thresholding) rather than throughput, index-size, or memory-footprint ratios http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies how SPUMONI's throughput, index-size, and peak-RSS advantages over minimap2 scale with reference repetitiveness, using benchmark metrics from simulated ZymoMC, real ZymoMC mock-community, and human 3-genome nanopore experiments. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Quantifies how SPUMONI's throughput, index-size, and peak-RSS advantages over minimap2 scale with reference repetitiveness, using benchmark metrics from simulated ZymoMC, real ZymoMC mock-community, and human 3-genome nanopore experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is raw read classification or alignment itself rather than quantifying resource/performance scaling between existing benchmark runs Only a single reference of fixed repetitiveness is available, so the throughput-vs-repetitiveness trend cannot be computed The goal is accuracy evaluation (F1 score, KS-stat thresholding) rather than throughput, index-size, or memory-footprint ratios

skills.description: Use when variants detected on a colored de Bruijn graph pangenome need graph coordinates (position, bubid, basecolor) transformed into locus-level annotations in VCF format for highly similar haplotype sequences.
skills.name: pangenome-triplet-coordinate-annotation
skills.search_text: pangenome-triplet-coordinate-annotation Use when variants detected on a colored de Bruijn graph pangenome need graph coordinates (position, bubid, basecolor) transformed into locus-level annotations in VCF format for highly similar haplotype sequences. Sample sequence similarity is insufficient (number of source nodes far less than the number of variants) — the variant detection model is not applicable Variants of interest include large indels (≥ 50 bp), inversions, or reverse tandem duplications — the node-based detection only addresses small indels Highly repetitive sequences, especially tandem repeats — sequence cutting fragments them, increasing computational difficulty and error http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assigns each variant detected on a colored de Bruijn graph-based pangenome a tri-tuple coordinate (offset value/position, bubble id, sample color) and writes calls in VCF format, enabling precise graph-to-locus variant annotation as demonstrated on 12 human mitochondrial genomes with VARI-merge and cSupB. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04149-w
skills.summary: Assigns each variant detected on a colored de Bruijn graph-based pangenome a tri-tuple coordinate (offset value/position, bubble id, sample color) and writes calls in VCF format, enabling precise graph-to-locus variant annotation as demonstrated on 12 human mitochondrial genomes with VARI-merge and cSupB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample sequence similarity is insufficient (number of source nodes far less than the number of variants) — the variant detection model is not applicable Variants of interest include large indels (≥ 50 bp), inversions, or reverse tandem duplications — the node-based detection only addresses small indels Highly repetitive sequences, especially tandem repeats — sequence cutting fragments them, increasing computational difficulty and error

skills.description: Use when sample mutations in a VCF must be matched against SARS-CoV-2 lineage-defining rules (Pangolin or outbreak.info) to explain or validate a lineage assignment from wastewater NGS data.
skills.name: pangolin-lineage-assignment-interpretation
skills.search_text: pangolin-lineage-assignment-interpretation Use when sample mutations in a VCF must be matched against SARS-CoV-2 lineage-defining rules (Pangolin or outbreak.info) to explain or validate a lineage assignment from wastewater NGS data. Input is raw FASTQ rather than variant calls — variant calling (freebayes against NC_045512) must precede rule matching A single high-confidence lineage assignment is needed for pure clinical isolates without concern for mixed populations — the rule-counting assumption can misassign when different reads satisfy different rules of the same lineage Lineage definitions are needed for viruses other than SARS-CoV-2 mapped to NC_045512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs how lineagespot interprets Pangolin lineage rules by building a per-lineage rule vector (position rules plus four inequality rules per position) over the NC_045512 reference and tallying satisfied rules against sample variants, so lineage assignments can be reproduced and critiqued. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: Reconstructs how lineagespot interprets Pangolin lineage rules by building a per-lineage rule vector (position rules plus four inequality rules per position) over the NC_045512 reference and tallying satisfied rules against sample variants, so lineage assignments can be reproduced and critiqued.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ rather than variant calls — variant calling (freebayes against NC_045512) must precede rule matching A single high-confidence lineage assignment is needed for pure clinical isolates without concern for mixed populations — the rule-counting assumption can misassign when different reads satisfy different rules of the same lineage Lineage definitions are needed for viruses other than SARS-CoV-2 mapped to NC_045512

skills.description: Use when a pipeline step must be repeated independently over many input files (e.g. 4,472 vaginal metagenomic assemblies or ~26 million predicted genes) and each invocation is a standalone CLI tool that can be embarrassingly parallelized.
skills.name: parallel-command-line-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: parallel-command-line-pipeline-execution Use when a pipeline step must be repeated independently over many input files (e.g. 4,472 vaginal metagenomic assemblies or ~26 million predicted genes) and each invocation is a standalone CLI tool that can be embarrassingly parallelized. Steps with inter-item dependencies or shared-state reduction (e.g. dereplication or clustering of all ~26 million proteins into VMGC-90) that need a dedicated tool like MMseqs2 rather than naive per-item parallelism A single large sample where per-item overhead dominates and a multi-threaded single invocation (e.g. one bwa-mem2 mem -t $thread run) is simpler http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Use GNU parallel to fan out per-sample command-line steps (Mash distance, bwa-mem2 mapping, MetaBAT2 binning, Kraken2 profiling, Prodigal gene calling) across thousands of genomes/samples with controlled job concurrency (-j), as done throughout the VMGC pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Use GNU parallel to fan out per-sample command-line steps (Mash distance, bwa-mem2 mapping, MetaBAT2 binning, Kraken2 profiling, Prodigal gene calling) across thousands of genomes/samples with controlled job concurrency (-j), as done throughout the VMGC pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Steps with inter-item dependencies or shared-state reduction (e.g. dereplication or clustering of all ~26 million proteins into VMGC-90) that need a dedicated tool like MMseqs2 rather than naive per-item parallelism A single large sample where per-item overhead dominates and a multi-threaded single invocation (e.g. one bwa-mem2 mem -t $thread run) is simpler

skills.description: Use when a reference-free SNP-discovery job on a large read set (e.g. 30x Human chromosome 1) is too slow sequentially and a multi-core machine (24 cores) is available.
skills.name: parallel-pipeline-execution-24-core
skills.search_text: parallel-pipeline-execution-24-core Use when a reference-free SNP-discovery job on a large read set (e.g. 30x Human chromosome 1) is too slow sequentially and a multi-core machine (24 cores) is available. INDEL discovery is required — the parallel pipeline works for SNPs only, and the external pre-processing tool does not account for INDELs in the read set The input reads have not been pre-filtered to contain only 'A','C','G','T' (reads containing 'N' must be removed or replaced before running) Only a single-core machine is available, so no parallel speedup over the sequential pipeline can be realized http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Runs the reference-free SNP-discovery pipeline in parallel by pre-sorting the fasta with HARC, splitting it into 24 pieces, building per-piece BWTs with BCR_LCP_GSA, and running ebwt2InDel concurrently via pebwt2InDel, achieving roughly 10x speedup over the sequential pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Runs the reference-free SNP-discovery pipeline in parallel by pre-sorting the fasta with HARC, splitting it into 24 pieces, building per-piece BWTs with BCR_LCP_GSA, and running ebwt2InDel concurrently via pebwt2InDel, achieving roughly 10x speedup over the sequential pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: INDEL discovery is required — the parallel pipeline works for SNPs only, and the external pre-processing tool does not account for INDELs in the read set The input reads have not been pre-filtered to contain only 'A','C','G','T' (reads containing 'N' must be removed or replaced before running) Only a single-core machine is available, so no parallel speedup over the sequential pipeline can be realized

skills.description: Use when you need to reproduce or compare reported compute times for ShoRAH's error-correction or frequency-estimation steps on deep-sequencing (e.g. 40,000-read pyrosequencing) samples, or to document hardware requirements of a viral diversity workflow.
skills.name: parallel-runtime-profiling-multi-cpu
skills.search_text: parallel-runtime-profiling-multi-cpu Use when you need to reproduce or compare reported compute times for ShoRAH's error-correction or frequency-estimation steps on deep-sequencing (e.g. 40,000-read pyrosequencing) samples, or to document hardware requirements of a viral diversity workflow. Your goal is accuracy of haplotype reconstruction or SNV calling rather than computational-efficiency measurement of the timed steps Your sample is far outside the benchmark regime (e.g. Illumina tumour-dissection data or a few hundred reads), so the <12 h / two-days targets are not comparable You intend to run ShoRAH2's global haplotype reconstruction, which is disabled in current versions and would alter the timed pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmarks the wall-clock runtime of ShoRAH's compute-heavy stages — diri_sampler error correction and freqEst EM frequency estimation — on large pyrosequencing samples, recording the CPU count, clock speed, and read volume under which published timings (<12 h error correction; ~2 days frequency estimation) were obtained. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: Benchmarks the wall-clock runtime of ShoRAH's compute-heavy stages — diri_sampler error correction and freqEst EM frequency estimation — on large pyrosequencing samples, recording the CPU count, clock speed, and read volume under which published timings (<12 h error correction; ~2 days frequency estimation) were obtained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is accuracy of haplotype reconstruction or SNV calling rather than computational-efficiency measurement of the timed steps Your sample is far outside the benchmark regime (e.g. Illumina tumour-dissection data or a few hundred reads), so the <12 h / two-days targets are not comparable You intend to run ShoRAH2's global haplotype reconstruction, which is disabled in current versions and would alter the timed pipeline

skills.description: Use when training per-k-mer neural detectors from raw MinION squiggle reads and the resulting .h5 models must stay small enough to run in limited memory (e.g. baseLess with --mem 256 on a Jetson Nano).
skills.name: parameter-count-model-size-control
skills.search_text: parameter-count-model-size-control Use when training per-k-mer neural detectors from raw MinION squiggle reads and the resulting .h5 models must stay small enough to run in limited memory (e.g. baseLess with --mem 256 on a Jetson Nano). You only need to run detection/inference — pre-generated 16S k-mer networks are available via 'baseLess update_16s_db' (<1MB), so retraining is unnecessary. Your reads are not signal-level fast5 corrected with tombo (e.g. FASTQ-only input) — the training pipeline requires tombo-resquiggle corrected reads. You need full basecalling or whole-genome analysis; baseLess is explicitly a target-detection-only tool. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains baseLess k-mer detection 1D CNNs with an explicit model-size penalty so that each per-k-mer network is small enough for single-board computers like the 2GB Jetson Nano. Hyperopt's tree-structured Parzen estimator minimizes L=(1-F1)+lambda*p_c/p_max (lambda=0.01) over 100 rounds, jointly maximizing F1 and shrinking parameter count. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017
skills.summary: Trains baseLess k-mer detection 1D CNNs with an explicit model-size penalty so that each per-k-mer network is small enough for single-board computers like the 2GB Jetson Nano. Hyperopt's tree-structured Parzen estimator minimizes L=(1-F1)+lambda*p_c/p_max (lambda=0.01) over 100 rounds, jointly maximizing F1 and shrinking parameter count.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to run detection/inference — pre-generated 16S k-mer networks are available via 'baseLess update_16s_db' (<1MB), so retraining is unnecessary. Your reads are not signal-level fast5 corrected with tombo (e.g. FASTQ-only input) — the training pipeline requires tombo-resquiggle corrected reads. You need full basecalling or whole-genome analysis; baseLess is explicitly a target-detection-only tool.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking LiME (or an eBWT-based classifier) across parameter grids: you need to measure how alpha-clusters of minimum length alpha and threshold beta jointly affect classification sensitivity, precision and F1 against known read provenances.
skills.name: parameter-sensitivity-sweep-analysis
skills.search_text: parameter-sensitivity-sweep-analysis Use when benchmarking LiME (or an eBWT-based classifier) across parameter grids: you need to measure how alpha-clusters of minimum length alpha and threshold beta jointly affect classification sensitivity, precision and F1 against known read provenances. The goal is classifying a real metagenome (e.g. SRR1804065) with a single fixed parameter setting rather than characterizing parameter sensitivity on simulated data with known provenances The classifier is not LiME and does not expose an alpha (minimum context length) or beta (similarity threshold) parameter, so the grid is not meaningful Only summary performance is needed and the full sweep table would not be checked against the monotone trade-off or Table S2 near-optimality of alpha=16, beta=0.25 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduces LiME's parameter sweep over minimum context length alpha (16-22) and similarity threshold beta (0.15-0.40) on simulated metagenomes, quantifying the sensitivity-vs-precision trade-off and identifying the best F1 configuration reported in Additional file 1 Table S2. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03628-w
skills.summary: Reproduces LiME's parameter sweep over minimum context length alpha (16-22) and similarity threshold beta (0.15-0.40) on simulated metagenomes, quantifying the sensitivity-vs-precision trade-off and identifying the best F1 configuration reported in Additional file 1 Table S2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is classifying a real metagenome (e.g. SRR1804065) with a single fixed parameter setting rather than characterizing parameter sensitivity on simulated data with known provenances The classifier is not LiME and does not expose an alpha (minimum context length) or beta (similarity threshold) parameter, so the grid is not meaningful Only summary performance is needed and the full sweep table would not be checked against the monotone trade-off or Table S2 near-optimality of alpha=16, beta=0.25

skills.description: Use when selecting the k-mer length k for baseLess salient-k-mer models: sweep candidate k values against non-target lengths (30/50 kb) and target lengths (0.6/1.5/30 kb) and pick the k minimizing FPR.
skills.name: parameter-sweep-evaluation
skills.search_text: parameter-sweep-evaluation Use when selecting the k-mer length k for baseLess salient-k-mer models: sweep candidate k values against non-target lengths (30/50 kb) and target lengths (0.6/1.5/30 kb) and pick the k minimizing FPR. The k-mer lengths are already fixed (e.g. using the pre-generated 16S k-mer detection networks shipped with baseLess) and no new k selection is required Empirical FPR on real read data is needed rather than the analytical Poisson estimate; this skill evaluates the analytical model only, not baseLess run_inference output Reproduce the analytical Poisson k-mer false-positive-rate sweep from Section 4.2 of the baseLess paper, which identified k=8 and k=9 as the k-mer sizes minimizing false positives for detecting salient subsequences of target sequences in raw MinION signal. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017

skills.description: Use when you have HashSeq OneMismatchCluster.txt output from 16S rRNA amplicon data and need to show how one-mismatch child discovery scales with parent read abundance and fit a Poisson error model.
skills.name: parent-abundance-fit-curve-visualization
skills.search_text: parent-abundance-fit-curve-visualization Use when you have HashSeq OneMismatchCluster.txt output from 16S rRNA amplicon data and need to show how one-mismatch child discovery scales with parent read abundance and fit a Poisson error model. skills.description: Use when you have a sample-by-variant allele-frequency matrix (e.g., from cellSNP.cells_ARG.vcf.gz with MetaQuad num_of_clusters >= 2 variants) and need to test whether predefined sample groups (e.g., antibiotic treatments) differ in variant composition at a given time point.
skills.name: pcoa-ordination-of-variant-frequencies
skills.search_text: pcoa-ordination-of-variant-frequencies Use when you have a sample-by-variant allele-frequency matrix (e.g., from cellSNP.cells_ARG.vcf.gz with MetaQuad num_of_clusters >= 2 variants) and need to test whether predefined sample groups (e.g., antibiotic treatments) differ in variant composition at a given time point. The variants have not been filtered for informativeness — raw cellSNP pileups containing non-polymorphic/background noise sites will inflate dissimilarities spuriously; use MetaQuad's num_of_clusters >= 2 flag first. The goal is detecting which variants are informative in the first place — that is MetaQuad's density-clustering step, not the downstream ordination and group-comparison step. Sample groups lack replication (single sample per group), making PERMANOVA / pairwise.adonis testing undefined or underpowered. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Ordinates samples by Bray-Curtis dissimilarity computed from shared informative ARG allele-frequency profiles (MetaQuad-filtered cellSNP VCF) using PCoA, and tests treatment-group separation with PERMANOVA and multilevel pairwise.adonis with Bonferroni adjustment. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Ordinates samples by Bray-Curtis dissimilarity computed from shared informative ARG allele-frequency profiles (MetaQuad-filtered cellSNP VCF) using PCoA, and tests treatment-group separation with PERMANOVA and multilevel pairwise.adonis with Bonferroni adjustment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variants have not been filtered for informativeness — raw cellSNP pileups containing non-polymorphic/background noise sites will inflate dissimilarities spuriously; use MetaQuad's num_of_clusters >= 2 flag first. skills.summary: Fits the Wang and Zhao penalized Dirichlet-tree multinomial (DTM) regression with a sparse grouped-lasso penalty to genus-level microbiome compositional data, selecting covariate-branch associations without a Bayesian MCMC sampler. It serves as the frequentist comparator to the MicroBVS Bayesian variable-selection DTM on the same dietary gut-microbiome case study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis requires posterior inclusion probabilities (MPPI) or calibrated Bayesian FDR control per covariate-branch — use the MicroBVS Bayesian variable-selection DTM instead When the compositional data have no known tree-like structure, so branch-level grouped penalties are not meaningful When covariates are highly correlated and the model is dense, since sampler/fit convergence is highly dependent on the correlation structure between covariates and count data as well as model sparsity

skills.description: Use when assigning tandem mass spectra (mzML/GNPS spectral datasets) to computationally predicted RiPP structures and you need an empirical FDR to set an acceptance threshold on peptide-spectrum matches.
skills.name: peptide-sequence-shuffling-decoy-generation
skills.search_text: peptide-sequence-shuffling-decoy-generation Use when assigning tandem mass spectra (mzML/GNPS spectral datasets) to computationally predicted RiPP structures and you need an empirical FDR to set an acceptance threshold on peptide-spectrum matches. Spectra lack paired genomics/metagenomics data — the paper notes the other 99% of GNPS spectra cannot be searched, so no target/decoy peptidogenomic FDR is meaningful. Candidate compounds are non-ribosomal peptides or other non-RiPP classes — Dereplicator+ family dereplication, not RiPP target-decoy peptidogenomics, is the appropriate route. Cyclic RiPPs requiring blind modification searches — the paper states blind modification searches are not currently performed for cyclic peptides due to computational complexity, so decoy-based scoring for such candidates is unsupported. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A target-decoy FDR estimation strategy for RiPP peptidogenomics: decoy RiPP precursor sequences are created by randomly shuffling each target precursor peptide BEFORE applying the same post-translational modifications, so decoys preserve the target modification/mass profile while randomizing the sequence. Comparing target vs decoy peptide-spectrum matches at a given threshold yields the FDR used to accept RiPP identifications. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.09.004
skills.summary: A target-decoy FDR estimation strategy for RiPP peptidogenomics: decoy RiPP precursor sequences are created by randomly shuffling each target precursor peptide BEFORE applying the same post-translational modifications, so decoys preserve the target modification/mass profile while randomizing the sequence. Comparing target vs decoy peptide-spectrum matches at a given threshold yields the FDR used to accept RiPP identifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra lack paired genomics/metagenomics data — the paper notes the other 99% of GNPS spectra cannot be searched, so no target/decoy peptidogenomic FDR is meaningful. Candidate compounds are non-ribosomal peptides or other non-RiPP classes — Dereplicator+ family dereplication, not RiPP target-decoy peptidogenomics, is the appropriate route. Cyclic RiPPs requiring blind modification searches — the paper states blind modification searches are not currently performed for cyclic peptides due to computational complexity, so decoy-based scoring for such candidates is unsupported.

skills.description: Use when scoring peptide-spectrum matches between GNPS tandem MS spectra and a precursor peptide database derived from genomes/metagenomes, and when controlling identifications by target-decoy FDR.
skills.name: peptide-spectrum-matching-scoring
skills.search_text: peptide-spectrum-matching-scoring Use when scoring peptide-spectrum matches between GNPS tandem MS spectra and a precursor peptide database derived from genomes/metagenomes, and when controlling identifications by target-decoy FDR. The spectra lack paired genomics/metagenomics data — as noted in the paper, the other 99% of spectra in GNPS cannot be searched against genomes The peptides of interest are cyclic and require blind modification searches — MetaMiner does not perform blind modification searches for cyclic peptides due to computational complexity The task is generic non-RiPP spectral annotation (e.g. dereplication against known structures with Dereplicator+ or molecular networking alone) rather than peptidogenomics search against a precursor peptide database http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 MetaMiner's peptidogenomics scoring pipeline: tandem MS spectra are searched against target/decoy databases of putative RiPP precursor peptides using a modified Dereplicator scoring function (with blind modification search), peptide-spectrum match p-values are computed with MS-DPR, and identifications are filtered with a target-decoy FDR estimate (1% threshold, down to 0% for conservative comparisons). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.09.004
skills.summary: MetaMiner's peptidogenomics scoring pipeline: tandem MS spectra are searched against target/decoy databases of putative RiPP precursor peptides using a modified Dereplicator scoring function (with blind modification search), peptide-spectrum match p-values are computed with MS-DPR, and identifications are filtered with a target-decoy FDR estimate (1% threshold, down to 0% for conservative comparisons).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra lack paired genomics/metagenomics data — as noted in the paper, the other 99% of spectra in GNPS cannot be searched against genomes The peptides of interest are cyclic and require blind modification searches — MetaMiner does not perform blind modification searches for cyclic peptides due to computational complexity The task is generic non-RiPP spectral annotation (e.g. dereplication against known structures with Dereplicator+ or molecular networking alone) rather than peptidogenomics search against a precursor peptide database

skills.description: Use when tandem mass spectra are paired with genomic/metagenomic data and you need to identify RiPPs—including those with unknown or blind modifications—by peptidogenomic database search at controlled FDR.
skills.name: peptide-spectrum-matching-with-blind-modifications
skills.search_text: peptide-spectrum-matching-with-blind-modifications Use when tandem mass spectra are paired with genomic/metagenomic data and you need to identify RiPPs—including those with unknown or blind modifications—by peptidogenomic database search at controlled FDR. The spectra are not accompanied by paired genomic/metagenomic data (about 99% of GNPS spectra cannot be searched this way) The RiPP of interest is a cyclic peptide — blind modification searches are not performed for cyclic peptides due to inherent computational complexity The producer genome is unavailable and no previously described biosynthetic gene cluster exists — the lacticin case required searching against a described BGC instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A peptidogenomics scoring skill in which tandem MS spectra from GNPS datasets are searched against target and decoy databases of putative RiPP precursor peptides using a modified Dereplicator scoring function that permits blind (unspecified) post-translational modifications while penalizing matches with more than one modification, with FDR controlled by the target-decoy approach at 1%. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.09.004
skills.summary: A peptidogenomics scoring skill in which tandem MS spectra from GNPS datasets are searched against target and decoy databases of putative RiPP precursor peptides using a modified Dereplicator scoring function that permits blind (unspecified) post-translational modifications while penalizing matches with more than one modification, with FDR controlled by the target-decoy approach at 1%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are not accompanied by paired genomic/metagenomic data (about 99% of GNPS spectra cannot be searched this way) The RiPP of interest is a cyclic peptide — blind modification searches are not performed for cyclic peptides due to inherent computational complexity The producer genome is unavailable and no previously described biosynthetic gene cluster exists — the lacticin case required searching against a described BGC instead

skills.description: Use when you have tandem MS spectra (e.g. GNPS datasets) paired with producer genomes, RefSeq assemblies, or metagenomic/metatranscriptomic short reads, and want to identify RiPPs (lanthipeptides, lassopeptides, LAPs, linaridins, glycocins, cyanobactins, proteusins) at 1% FDR.
skills.name: peptidogenomics-spectrum-genome-searching
skills.search_text: peptidogenomics-spectrum-genome-searching Use when you have tandem MS spectra (e.g. GNPS datasets) paired with producer genomes, RefSeq assemblies, or metagenomic/metatranscriptomic short reads, and want to identify RiPPs (lanthipeptides, lassopeptides, LAPs, linaridins, glycocins, cyanobactins, proteusins) at 1% FDR. Spectra are not accompanied by paired genomics/metagenomics data (about 99% of GNPS spectra), making spectrum-to-genome searching impossible. The goal is blind modification search for cyclic peptides — MetaMiner does not perform blind modification searches for cyclic peptides due to inherent computational complexity. The spectral families are non-ribosomal peptides — Dereplicator+ analysis shows many GNPS spectral families belong to non-ribosomal peptides, outside the RiPP scope of this skill. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A peptidogenomics skill for searching tandem MS spectra (e.g. from GNPS molecular networking) against putative RiPP precursor peptides derived from genomic or metagenomic sequence, enabling discovery of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides with blind modifications. It integrates computational mass spectrometry with genome mining to link spectra to biosynthetic gene clusters. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.09.004
skills.summary: A peptidogenomics skill for searching tandem MS spectra (e.g. from GNPS molecular networking) against putative RiPP precursor peptides derived from genomic or metagenomic sequence, enabling discovery of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides with blind modifications. It integrates computational mass spectrometry with genome mining to link spectra to biosynthetic gene clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra are not accompanied by paired genomics/metagenomics data (about 99% of GNPS spectra), making spectrum-to-genome searching impossible. The goal is blind modification search for cyclic peptides — MetaMiner does not perform blind modification searches for cyclic peptides due to inherent computational complexity. The spectral families are non-ribosomal peptides — Dereplicator+ analysis shows many GNPS spectral families belong to non-ribosomal peptides, outside the RiPP scope of this skill.

skills.description: Use when you have a BAM from mapping read subsets onto a specific reference FASTA and need the per-base covered fraction, gap identification, or coverage progression across iterative read-subset expansion cycles.
skills.name: per-base-coverage-extraction-with-samtools-depth
skills.search_text: per-base-coverage-extraction-with-samtools-depth Use when you have a BAM from mapping read subsets onto a specific reference FASTA and need the per-base covered fraction, gap identification, or coverage progression across iterative read-subset expansion cycles. You need assembly-level completeness metrics (N50, contig count) rather than read-level per-base coverage of a single reference sequence The reference is an entire multi-contig genome where aggregate depth statistics are desired instead of a single-target gap-infilling assessment The input is not an alignment (no BAM/SAM from mapping the reads to the target contig) — depth extraction requires a coordinate-sorted alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies sequencing read coverage of a target reference (e.g. the largest ground water cas operon contig) at single-base resolution using 'samtools depth -a', enabling computation of the fraction of reference bases covered by a read subset. This is used to evaluate how CasCollect read-subset expansion infills coverage gaps versus the full raw dataset. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Quantifies sequencing read coverage of a target reference (e.g. the largest ground water cas operon contig) at single-base resolution using 'samtools depth -a', enabling computation of the fraction of reference bases covered by a read subset. This is used to evaluate how CasCollect read-subset expansion infills coverage gaps versus the full raw dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need assembly-level completeness metrics (N50, contig count) rather than read-level per-base coverage of a single reference sequence The reference is an entire multi-contig genome where aggregate depth statistics are desired instead of a single-target gap-infilling assessment The input is not an alignment (no BAM/SAM from mapping the reads to the target contig) — depth extraction requires a coordinate-sorted alignment

skills.description: Use when you have binned contig FASTA files from a metagenome assembly and need per-MAG quality metrics (contig count, N50, completeness, contamination) consolidated for bin selection.
skills.name: per-bin-summary-table-generation
skills.search_text: per-bin-summary-table-generation Use when you have binned contig FASTA files from a metagenome assembly and need per-MAG quality metrics (contig count, N50, completeness, contamination) consolidated for bin selection. Input is raw reads or an unbinned assembly — no per-bin QC table can be produced before genome binning has generated MAG contig sets. The goal is assembly QC of unbinned contigs only — QUAST alone on the primary assembly suffices without per-bin aggregation. Bin refinement or dereplication across multiple binners is the goal — DAS Tool-style integration, not QC summarization, is the appropriate skill. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregates QUAST assembly statistics and BUSCO completeness/contamination estimates into a single per-bin quality-control table (mag_qc_summary.tsv) for reconstructed MAGs, as implemented in the nf-core/mag pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Aggregates QUAST assembly statistics and BUSCO completeness/contamination estimates into a single per-bin quality-control table (mag_qc_summary.tsv) for reconstructed MAGs, as implemented in the nf-core/mag pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or an unbinned assembly — no per-bin QC table can be produced before genome binning has generated MAG contig sets. The goal is assembly QC of unbinned contigs only — QUAST alone on the primary assembly suffices without per-bin aggregation. Bin refinement or dereplication across multiple binners is the goal — DAS Tool-style integration, not QC summarization, is the appropriate skill.
