skills.description: Use when a read-filtering pipeline must account for exactly how each .bam read (pair) was removed — e.g. un-paired, insert size, mapQ, or nucleotide identity — and per-filter counts must be reported per sequence and validated.
skills.name: per-filter-count-report-generation
skills.search_text: per-filter-count-report-generation Use when a read-filtering pipeline must account for exactly how each .bam read (pair) was removed — e.g. un-paired, insert size, mapQ, or nucleotide identity — and per-filter counts must be reported per sequence and validated. The analysis works with single-end reads only — inStrain removes all un-paired reads by default, so nearly everything would be discarded You need coverage/breadth or SNV calls rather than an account of which filter removed each read pair (use inStrain profile's downstream outputs instead) Input is raw reads rather than an already-mapped, sorted .bam file — mapping must be done first (e.g. with Bowtie2) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Generates a per-sequence, per-stage read-filtering report (read_report.tsv) that aggregates pass/fail counts for each filter applied to .bam read pairs, following inStrain profile's four-stage read-filtering scheme. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Generates a per-sequence, per-stage read-filtering report (read_report.tsv) that aggregates pass/fail counts for each filter applied to .bam read pairs, following inStrain profile's four-stage read-filtering scheme.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis works with single-end reads only — inStrain removes all un-paired reads by default, so nearly everything would be discarded You need coverage/breadth or SNV calls rather than an account of which filter removed each read pair (use inStrain profile's downstream outputs instead) Input is raw reads rather than an already-mapped, sorted .bam file — mapping must be done first (e.g. with Bowtie2)

skills.description: Use when multiple high-coverage 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries must be compared at matched parameters, or when an experiment needs to fix read coverage per DNA fragment (CR) while varying fragment-level parameters such as physical coverage (CF) or fragment length (Mu_F).
skills.name: per-fragment-read-subsampling-coverage-control
skills.search_text: per-fragment-read-subsampling-coverage-control Use when multiple high-coverage 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries must be compared at matched parameters, or when an experiment needs to fix read coverage per DNA fragment (CR) while varying fragment-level parameters such as physical coverage (CF) or fragment length (Mu_F). Data are not barcode-based 10x Chromium Linked-Reads — fragment reconstruction relies on barcode-proximal read pairs and would be meaningless for PacBio/ONT long reads Libraries are already low-coverage at or below the target CR — subsampling cannot increase per-fragment coverage The goal is to simulate Linked-Reads from scratch rather than downsample existing sequenced libraries — use LRTK-SIM generation directly instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A method for making heterogeneous high-coverage 10x Linked-Read libraries comparable by reconstructing the original input DNA fragments from barcode-proximal read pairs and randomly subsampling reads within each fragment to a fixed per-fragment short-read coverage (CR). It was used in the Zhang et al. 2019 GigaScience study of human diploid assembly with 10x Linked-Reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: A method for making heterogeneous high-coverage 10x Linked-Read libraries comparable by reconstructing the original input DNA fragments from barcode-proximal read pairs and randomly subsampling reads within each fragment to a fixed per-fragment short-read coverage (CR). It was used in the Zhang et al. 2019 GigaScience study of human diploid assembly with 10x Linked-Reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not barcode-based 10x Chromium Linked-Reads — fragment reconstruction relies on barcode-proximal read pairs and would be meaningless for PacBio/ONT long reads Libraries are already low-coverage at or below the target CR — subsampling cannot increase per-fragment coverage The goal is to simulate Linked-Reads from scratch rather than downsample existing sequenced libraries — use LRTK-SIM generation directly instead

skills.name: per-genome-sequence-depth-quantification
skills.search_text: per-genome-sequence-depth-quantification Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ data must be quantified against a set of reference genomes to obtain per-genome mapped read counts and sequence depth, e.g. for read-mapping-based source attribution. Input is already a per-genome abundance or coverage table — re-running the mapping adds no information Long-read metagenomic data requiring different filtering/alignment (the SourceApp framework and these thresholds were tuned for short Illumina reads; long reads were only used to recover MAGs via filtlong-filtered minION data) The goal is de novo source database construction rather than quantifying reads against an existing curated database (use sourceapp_build.py instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Summarizes how many metagenomic reads map to each genome in a source-associated reference database, and at what sequence depth, using CoverM v0.7.0 after bwa mem mapping — the read quantification backbone of SourceApp's fecal source tracking. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: Summarizes how many metagenomic reads map to each genome in a source-associated reference database, and at what sequence depth, using CoverM v0.7.0 after bwa mem mapping — the read quantification backbone of SourceApp's fecal source tracking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-genome abundance or coverage table — re-running the mapping adds no information Long-read metagenomic data requiring different filtering/alignment (the SourceApp framework and these thresholds were tuned for short Illumina reads; long reads were only used to recover MAGs via filtlong-filtered minION data) The goal is de novo source database construction rather than quantifying reads against an existing curated database (use sourceapp_build.py instead)

skills.description: Use when comparing read-recruitment strategies for viral metagenomic data and you need recruited-read counts plus per-haplotype genome coverage/fraction to judge which mapper parameters enrich the target virus .
skills.name: per-haplotype-read-coverage-quantification
skills.search_text: per-haplotype-read-coverage-quantification Use when comparing read-recruitment strategies for viral metagenomic data and you need recruited-read counts plus per-haplotype genome coverage/fraction to judge which mapper parameters enrich the target virus . The target virus shares no conservation with any available reference genome — TAR-VIR's recruitment cannot detect it You only have raw mapper alignment counts and need no coverage-based comparison — alignment counts alone (52,688 vs 52,377) can mislead since recruited reads may cover 20%-30% more genome Reads have not been error-corrected — exact overlap detection will fail on error-containing reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Quantifies how many reads TAR-VIR's overlap-recruitment stage pulls in and how deeply and completely each viral haplotype genome is covered, enabling comparison of read-mapper seed parameter sweeps (e.g. Bowtie2 score-min 'L,0,-x' vs BWA -B) for targeted viral read enrichment. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2
skills.summary: Quantifies how many reads TAR-VIR's overlap-recruitment stage pulls in and how deeply and completely each viral haplotype genome is covered, enabling comparison of read-mapper seed parameter sweeps (e.g. Bowtie2 score-min 'L,0,-x' vs BWA -B) for targeted viral read enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target virus shares no conservation with any available reference genome — TAR-VIR's recruitment cannot detect it You only have raw mapper alignment counts and need no coverage-based comparison — alignment counts alone (52,688 vs 52,377) can mislead since recruited reads may cover 20%-30% more genome Reads have not been error-corrected — exact overlap detection will fail on error-containing reads

skills.description: Use when a viral taxonomic classification run (e.g., VirMAP on a mock community such as the NetoVir control SRR3458562) must be converted into per-lineage read fractions and benchmarked against published relative abundance proportions.
skills.name: per-lineage-viral-read-fraction-quantification
skills.search_text: per-lineage-viral-read-fraction-quantification Use when a viral taxonomic classification run (e.g., VirMAP on a mock community such as the NetoVir control SRR3458562) must be converted into per-lineage read fractions and benchmarked against published relative abundance proportions. The goal is absolute viral load quantification rather than relative per-lineage fractions of total reads. The sample is a real environmental/clinical virome with no published reference proportions, leaving no external benchmark for the R² comparison step. Input is raw unassembled reads with no VirMAP (or equivalent lineage-level) classification yet produced. http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Aggregates VirMAP-classified reads by viral lineage to compute the fraction of total reads assigned to each lineage in a mock virome sample, then correlates those proportions against independently published per-lineage values (e.g., Conceição-Neto proportions) to quantify concordance. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Aggregates VirMAP-classified reads by viral lineage to compute the fraction of total reads assigned to each lineage in a mock virome sample, then correlates those proportions against independently published per-lineage values (e.g., Conceição-Neto proportions) to quantify concordance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is absolute viral load quantification rather than relative per-lineage fractions of total reads. The sample is a real environmental/clinical virome with no published reference proportions, leaving no external benchmark for the R² comparison step. Input is raw unassembled reads with no VirMAP (or equivalent lineage-level) classification yet produced.

skills.description: Use when you have a sorted .bam of reads mapped to a reference .fasta and need per-position nucleotide diversity plus scaffold-level coverage, breadth, and expected-breadth metrics for microdiversity profiling.
skills.name: per-position-nucleotide-diversity-calculation
skills.search_text: per-position-nucleotide-diversity-calculation Use when you have a sorted .bam of reads mapped to a reference .fasta and need per-position nucleotide diversity plus scaffold-level coverage, breadth, and expected-breadth metrics for microdiversity profiling. Input is raw reads or an unsorted .sam/.bam rather than a sorted .bam aligned to a fixed reference .fasta — coverage/diversity profiling needs position-resolved alignments The goal is genome dereplication or ANI comparison between assemblies (e.g. dRep/skani territory), not within-genome microdiversity profiling Coverage is too low for positions to pass the min_cov threshold of 5 reads — diversity estimates will be undefined or unreliable at low coverage http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Compute per-position nucleotide diversity (1 − clonality, the sum of squared A/C/G/T base frequencies) across a reference genome from properly paired, filtered .bam alignments, then aggregate per-scaffold coverage, breadth, and diversity statistics as inStrain does for profiling co-occurring genome populations from metagenomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Compute per-position nucleotide diversity (1 − clonality, the sum of squared A/C/G/T base frequencies) across a reference genome from properly paired, filtered .bam alignments, then aggregate per-scaffold coverage, breadth, and diversity statistics as inStrain does for profiling co-occurring genome populations from metagenomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or an unsorted .sam/.bam rather than a sorted .bam aligned to a fixed reference .fasta — coverage/diversity profiling needs position-resolved alignments The goal is genome dereplication or ANI comparison between assemblies (e.g. dRep/skani territory), not within-genome microdiversity profiling Coverage is too low for positions to pass the min_cov threshold of 5 reads — diversity estimates will be undefined or unreliable at low coverage

skills.description: Use when DeepTaxa (or comparable hierarchical 16S rRNA classifier) predictions on labeled test sequences must be scored per taxonomic rank, e.g. reproducing the Greengenes2 2024.09 species-level accuracy/F1/ECE benchmarks.
skills.name: per-rank-classification-metrics-evaluation
skills.search_text: per-rank-classification-metrics-evaluation Use when DeepTaxa (or comparable hierarchical 16S rRNA classifier) predictions on labeled test sequences must be scored per taxonomic rank, e.g. reproducing the Greengenes2 2024.09 species-level accuracy/F1/ECE benchmarks. Input is an unlabeled FASTA with no ground-truth taxonomy file — `deeptaxa predict` will classify but cannot emit accuracy/F1/ECE The goal is similarity-stratified degradation analysis: per-rank metrics must be joined with BLAST/VSEARCH nearest-neighbor identity buckets first, so this skill alone is insufficient Input comes from an alternative reference database (SILVA, RDP) or a different marker gene — the article notes DeepTaxa was trained and evaluated primarily on Greengenes2 and cross-database performance remains untested http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Computes classification metrics (accuracy, weighted F1, expected calibration error) separately at each of the seven taxonomic ranks (domain through species) for DeepTaxa predictions on the Greengenes2 2024.09 held-out test set. Because DeepTaxa emits all ranks in one forward pass, evaluation must decompose performance per rank rather than report a single aggregate score. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Computes classification metrics (accuracy, weighted F1, expected calibration error) separately at each of the seven taxonomic ranks (domain through species) for DeepTaxa predictions on the Greengenes2 2024.09 held-out test set. skills.description: Use when comparing de novo assembler performance on mock metagenomic communities with known reference replicons, and per-reference metrics from LMAS global/per-reference tables must be placed on a comparable scale across assemblers.
skills.name: per-reference-assembly-metric-normalization
skills.search_text: per-reference-assembly-metric-normalization Use when comparing de novo assembler performance on mock metagenomic communities with known reference replicons, and per-reference metrics from LMAS global/per-reference tables must be placed on a comparable scale across assemblers. When no reference ground truth is available for the sample — per-reference normalization requires known reference replicons, so metagenomic samples without defined mock composition cannot be normalized this way When the analysis targets global (whole-assembly) metrics rather than replicon-specific performance; the paper's global tables do not need per-reference normalization When comparing assemblies that include contigs below the 1 kbp --minLength filter, since the reported genomic-vs-metagenomic pattern holds after filtering contigs <1 kbp http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Normalize LMAS per-reference assembly metrics (Contiguity, Multiplicity, Validity, Parsimony, Identity, Breadth of coverage, Lx, NAx, NGx) across assemblers for each reference replicon of defined mock communities, using the paper's targets l_target=0.9 and n_target=0.5, to enable fair cross-assembler comparisons in metagenomic samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Normalize LMAS per-reference assembly metrics (Contiguity, Multiplicity, Validity, Parsimony, Identity, Breadth of coverage, Lx, NAx, NGx) across assemblers for each reference replicon of defined mock communities, using the paper's targets l_target=0.9 and n_target=0.5, to enable fair cross-assembler comparisons in metagenomic samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no reference ground truth is available for the sample — per-reference normalization requires known reference replicons, so metagenomic samples without defined mock composition cannot be normalized this way When the analysis targets global (whole-assembly) metrics rather than replicon-specific performance; the paper's global tables do not need per-reference normalization When comparing assemblies that include contigs below the 1 kbp --minLength filter, since the reported genomic-vs-metagenomic pattern holds after filtering contigs <1 kbp

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic de novo assemblers against a defined mock community and you need a per-reference-replicon completeness fraction (LSA) from contig-to-reference alignments.
skills.name: per-replicon-metric-normalization
skills.search_text: per-replicon-metric-normalization Use when benchmarking metagenomic de novo assemblers against a defined mock community and you need a per-reference-replicon completeness fraction (LSA) from contig-to-reference alignments. The goal is a global assembly metric (e.g. N50, total length) rather than a per-replicon completeness fraction Input assemblies have not been filtered by the minimum contig size (--minLength, default 1000 bp), so contig lengths are not comparable across assemblers There is no reference replicon set available for the mock community (LSA is reference-dependent) http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Computes the LMAS LSA (longest single alignment) metric per reference replicon: the length of the longest single contiguous contig-to-reference alignment (from minimap2 PAF records of filtered-size contigs) normalized by the reference replicon length. This yields a per-assembler, per-replicon completeness fraction bounded in (0, 1] rather than a global assembly statistic. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Computes the LMAS LSA (longest single alignment) metric per reference replicon: the length of the longest single contiguous contig-to-reference alignment (from minimap2 PAF records of filtered-size contigs) normalized by the reference replicon length. This yields a per-assembler, per-replicon completeness fraction bounded in (0, 1] rather than a global assembly statistic.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a global assembly metric (e.g. N50, total length) rather than a per-replicon completeness fraction Input assemblies have not been filtered by the minimum contig size (--minLength, default 1000 bp), so contig lengths are not comparable across assemblers There is no reference replicon set available for the mock community (LSA is reference-dependent)

skills.description: Use when constructing simulated shotgun metagenomic benchmark datasets where each sample must hit a target mean depth, and per-sample read counts must be computed from depth, reference size, and read length.
skills.name: per-sample-depth-calibration
skills.search_text: per-sample-depth-calibration Use when constructing simulated shotgun metagenomic benchmark datasets where each sample must hit a target mean depth, and per-sample read counts must be computed from depth, reference size, and read length. The input is real sequencing data with fixed observed depths — depth calibration here applies only to in silico read generation. The downstream analysis needs single-cell or amplicon data where the depth x reference size / (2 x read length) paired-end shotgun read-count formula does not apply. No target depth schedule has been defined — the skill presumes prescribed per-sample/group depth values to calibrate against. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 A benchmark-simulation skill for setting per-sample read counts in shotgun metagenomic simulations so that each sample realizes a prescribed mean sequencing depth (here 3x–35.5x), enabling depth-controlled evaluation of strain-variant callers such as MetaQuad. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: A benchmark-simulation skill for setting per-sample read counts in shotgun metagenomic simulations so that each sample realizes a prescribed mean sequencing depth (here 3x–35.5x), enabling depth-controlled evaluation of strain-variant callers such as MetaQuad.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real sequencing data with fixed observed depths — depth calibration here applies only to in silico read generation. The downstream analysis needs single-cell or amplicon data where the depth x reference size / (2 x read length) paired-end shotgun read-count formula does not apply. No target depth schedule has been defined — the skill presumes prescribed per-sample/group depth values to calibrate against.

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads must be converted into a sample-by-gene count/frequency matrix via alignment against a non-redundant gene catalog, prior to CSS normalization or KEGG-based functional annotation.
skills.name: per-sample-gene-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-sample-gene-count-aggregation Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads must be converted into a sample-by-gene count/frequency matrix via alignment against a non-redundant gene catalog, prior to CSS normalization or KEGG-based functional annotation. The goal is taxonomic profiling of phylogenetic diversity — CAMAMED performs that with MetaPhlAn v2.0 rather than gene-catalog mapping. No appropriate non-redundant gene catalog exists for the habitat — assembly to contigs followed by gene content prediction may be required instead. Input is already a gene count/frequency table — proceed directly to CSS normalization rather than re-mapping reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 CAMAMED's mapping module aligns quality-controlled metagenomic reads to a CD-HIT deduplicated non-redundant gene catalog with MOSAIK v2.2.3 and aggregates read-to-gene alignments into per-sample gene frequencies, written to gene_frequency_counts.csv. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: CAMAMED's mapping module aligns quality-controlled metagenomic reads to a CD-HIT deduplicated non-redundant gene catalog with MOSAIK v2.2.3 and aggregates read-to-gene alignments into per-sample gene frequencies, written to gene_frequency_counts.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is taxonomic profiling of phylogenetic diversity — CAMAMED performs that with MetaPhlAn v2.0 rather than gene-catalog mapping. No appropriate non-redundant gene catalog exists for the habitat — assembly to contigs followed by gene content prediction may be required instead. Input is already a gene count/frequency table — proceed directly to CSS normalization rather than re-mapping reads.

skills.description: Use when you need per-sample, per-species gene counts from vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic FASTQ data to assess intraspecies gene-content diversity, such as testing whether multiple strains of a species co-occur in a community.
skills.name: per-sample-gene-richness-quantification
skills.search_text: per-sample-gene-richness-quantification Use when you need per-sample, per-species gene counts from vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic FASTQ data to assess intraspecies gene-content diversity, such as testing whether multiple strains of a species co-occur in a community. Input is paired-end data that cannot or should not be merged into single-end reads — VIRGO's mapping module only accepts one FASTQ per sample The analysis goal is variant detection or nucleotide-level diversity within genes — VIRGO does not yet identify nucleotide variants The target community is dominated by non-bacterial microbes (viral/fungal) — VIRGO has only limited inclusion of viral and fungal gene sequences (10,908 fungal and 15,965 phage genes) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies the number of microbial genes per species and per sample in vaginal metagenomes by mapping reads to the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog with bowtie, then summarizing per-sample gene counts to reveal within-community intraspecies diversity (e.g., L. crispatus metagenomes carrying 3262 ± 586 genes vs 2064 ± 225 in isolate genomes). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-020-14677-3
skills.summary: Quantifies the number of microbial genes per species and per sample in vaginal metagenomes by mapping reads to the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog with bowtie, then summarizing per-sample gene counts to reveal within-community intraspecies diversity (e.g., L. crispatus metagenomes carrying 3262 ± 586 genes vs 2064 ± 225 in isolate genomes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is paired-end data that cannot or should not be merged into single-end reads — VIRGO's mapping module only accepts one FASTQ per sample The analysis goal is variant detection or nucleotide-level diversity within genes — VIRGO does not yet identify nucleotide variants The target community is dominated by non-bacterial microbes (viral/fungal) — VIRGO has only limited inclusion of viral and fungal gene sequences (10,908 fungal and 15,965 phage genes)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a metagenomic fecal source tracking tool against mesocosms of known composition and you need per-source accuracy, e.g. to detect under-performing sources like cow.
skills.name: per-source-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: per-source-sensitivity-analysis Use when benchmarking a metagenomic fecal source tracking tool against mesocosms of known composition and you need per-source accuracy, e.g. to detect under-performing sources like cow. Input is a single environmental metagenome without known ground-truth source composition — sensitivity cannot be computed without spiked-in reference truth You need overall (pooled) tool performance rather than source-resolved breakdown — the aggregate sensitivity/specificity near 0.90 is a separate metric The attribution tool does not report per-source estimated cell fractions, since the 0.01% LOD call cannot be applied http://edamontology.org/topic_3837 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A benchmarking skill that computes per-source sensitivity and specificity for fecal source attribution (cat, chicken, cow, dog, goat, pig, sewage, septage) by comparing SourceApp attribution calls against ground-truth spike-in cell fractions from mesocosm metagenomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that computes per-source sensitivity and specificity for fecal source attribution (cat, chicken, cow, dog, goat, pig, sewage, septage) by comparing SourceApp attribution calls against ground-truth spike-in cell fractions from mesocosm metagenomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single environmental metagenome without known ground-truth source composition — sensitivity cannot be computed without spiked-in reference truth You need overall (pooled) tool performance rather than source-resolved breakdown — the aggregate sensitivity/specificity near 0.90 is a separate metric The attribution tool does not report per-source estimated cell fractions, since the 0.01% LOD call cannot be applied

skills.description: Use when comparing microbiome classification models on multi-class datasets (e.g. 3-class oral or 5-class gut status labels) and the question is whether per-class performance is balanced, not just whether overall Kappa or accuracy is higher.
skills.name: per-status-f1-variance-analysis
skills.search_text: per-status-f1-variance-analysis Use when comparing microbiome classification models on multi-class datasets (e.g. 3-class oral or 5-class gut status labels) and the question is whether per-class performance is balanced, not just whether overall Kappa or accuracy is higher. The analysis goal is overall performance (e.g. Kappa or accuracy) comparison rather than per-class balance — use a standard metric comparison instead. Only a single-class or binary task is available with no per-status F1 breakdown, so variance across statuses is undefined or trivial. Per-class F1 scores for the baseline models are not reported and cannot be recomputed, making cross-model variance ranking impossible. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies classification balance by computing mean, standard deviation, and variance of per-status (per-class) F1 scores for PM-CNN versus RF and other baselines, then ranking models by ascending F1 variance. Used to verify the claim that PM-CNN achieves more balanced per-status performance even when overall Kappa only slightly improves over RF. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae013
skills.summary: Quantifies classification balance by computing mean, standard deviation, and variance of per-status (per-class) F1 scores for PM-CNN versus RF and other baselines, then ranking models by ascending F1 variance. Used to verify the claim that PM-CNN achieves more balanced per-status performance even when overall Kappa only slightly improves over RF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is overall performance (e.g. Kappa or accuracy) comparison rather than per-class balance — use a standard metric comparison instead. Only a single-class or binary task is available with no per-status F1 breakdown, so variance across statuses is undefined or trivial. Per-class F1 scores for the baseline models are not reported and cannot be recomputed, making cross-model variance ranking impossible.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking trajectory-reconstruction accuracy of denoised relative abundances per taxon across samples, e.g. comparing LUMINATE against TGP-CODA/MALLARD on simulated longitudinal count data.
skills.name: per-taxon-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: per-taxon-accuracy-benchmarking Use when benchmarking trajectory-reconstruction accuracy of denoised relative abundances per taxon across samples, e.g. comparing LUMINATE against TGP-CODA/MALLARD on simulated longitudinal count data. You need to compare methods on biological zero detection or cLV parameter fitting rather than relative abundance trajectory accuracy — this skill only scores per-taxon reconstruction accuracy and runtime No ground-truth trajectories exist (e.g. purely real observational data) — the squared-correlation-per-taxon metric requires known true relative abundances Datasets contain ultra-sparse taxa (>90% missing entries), which the paper recommends filtering out as a pre-processing step before benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Evaluates and compares methods that reconstruct latent relative abundances from longitudinal 16S count data by computing a mean per-taxon r-squared between ground-truth and estimated trajectories, alongside wall-clock runtime comparisons (e.g., LUMINATE vs TGP-CODA vs MALLARD). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2020.05.006
skills.summary: Evaluates and compares methods that reconstruct latent relative abundances from longitudinal 16S count data by computing a mean per-taxon r-squared between ground-truth and estimated trajectories, alongside wall-clock runtime comparisons (e.g., LUMINATE vs TGP-CODA vs MALLARD).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to compare methods on biological zero detection or cLV parameter fitting rather than relative abundance trajectory accuracy — this skill only scores per-taxon reconstruction accuracy and runtime No ground-truth trajectories exist (e.g. purely real observational data) — the squared-correlation-per-taxon metric requires known true relative abundances Datasets contain ultra-sparse taxa (>90% missing entries), which the paper recommends filtering out as a pre-processing step before benchmarking

skills.description: Use when building a hybridization-capture probe set from HUBDesign CandidateBaitRegions.tab and you need the final probe count capped and distributed fairly across all input taxa, e.g. tiling to 5x density with at most 13,500 baits.

skills.search_text: per-taxon-probe-count-balancing Use when building a hybridization-capture probe set from HUBDesign CandidateBaitRegions.tab and you need the final probe count capped and distributed fairly across all input taxa, e.g. tiling to 5x density with at most 13,500 baits. Input is unannotated or unannotatable genomes — HUBDesign cannot design probes and only close relatives can be targeted You only need to quantify specificity of an existing probe set (map probes back via BLASTn rather than re-run selection) You need intermediate-stage reprocessing only up to candidate identification (CandidateBaitRegions.tab) without final tiling http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Balanced probe selection in the HUBDesign pipeline: after filtering off-target candidates against blacklist BLAST databases, the Selection stage tiles remaining candidate bait regions while balancing the number of probes per input genome under a minimum tiling-density target. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: Balanced probe selection in the HUBDesign pipeline: after filtering off-target candidates against blacklist BLAST databases, the Selection stage tiles remaining candidate bait regions while balancing the number of probes per input genome under a minimum tiling-density target.

skills.description: Use when inferred sequence variants (FASTA from a variant caller) need validation against a reference database such as SILVA132 to confirm they match previously observed sequences with high identity (>99%).
skills.name: percent-identity-variant-mapping
skills.search_text: percent-identity-variant-mapping Use when inferred sequence variants (FASTA from a variant caller) need validation against a reference database such as SILVA132 to confirm they match previously observed sequences with high identity (>99%). Input is a raw fastq file that has not yet been processed by a variant caller (primers removed, reads paired, trimmed to 250 bases) — this skill validates inferred variants, not raw reads. The goal is detecting novel or low-abundance variants; HashSeq is conservative and not sensitive for true low-abundance sequences, so low-identity or novel-variant discovery is out of scope. Sequences with two or more mismatches to a parent or indel variation are not modeled by HashSeq, so identity mapping cannot support claims about indel-containing variants. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Validates de novo inferred 16S rRNA sequence variants (from HashSeq or DADA2) by aligning each variant against the SILVA132 reference database (e.g., BLASTN), keeping the top bit-score hit, and computing percent identity (identical positions over aligned length) to judge whether variants are real biological sequences rather than sequencing errors. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Validates de novo inferred 16S rRNA sequence variants (from HashSeq or DADA2) by aligning each variant against the SILVA132 reference database (e.g., BLASTN), keeping the top bit-score hit, and computing percent identity (identical positions over aligned length) to judge whether variants are real biological sequences rather than sequencing errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw fastq file that has not yet been processed by a variant caller (primers removed, reads paired, trimmed to 250 bases) — this skill validates inferred variants, not raw reads. The goal is detecting novel or low-abundance variants; HashSeq is conservative and not sensitive for true low-abundance sequences, so low-identity or novel-variant discovery is out of scope. Sequences with two or more mismatches to a parent or indel variation are not modeled by HashSeq, so identity mapping cannot support claims about indel-containing variants.

skills.description: Use when deploying CopyRighter from source in a Perl environment: setting up Makefile.PL-driven installation, resolving CPAN dependencies (Bio::Community, Getopt::Euclid >= 0.4.3, Method::Signatures, Scalar::Util), or handling non-administrator installation via local::lib.
skills.name: perl-bioinformatics-tool-configuration
skills.search_text: perl-bioinformatics-tool-configuration Use when deploying CopyRighter from source in a Perl environment: setting up Makefile.PL-driven installation, resolving CPAN dependencies (Bio::Community, Getopt::Euclid >= 0.4.3, Method::Signatures, Scalar::Util), or handling non-administrator installation via local::lib. CopyRighter is already installed and COPYRIGHTER_DB is set — proceed directly to running the GCN correction rather than reinstalling The task is the downstream GCN correction itself (converting an OTU table, running correction, computing Hellinger/euclidean distances) — this skill only covers installation and configuration Your pipeline does not involve CopyRighter or other Makefile.PL-based Perl bioinformatics tools — a generic dependency manager is more appropriate Installs and configures the Perl-based CopyRighter (fangly/AmpliCopyrighter, version 0.46) from source using perl Makefile.PL, make, and make install, pulling in CPAN dependencies so that 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) correction can be run on microbial community profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Installs and configures the Perl-based CopyRighter (fangly/AmpliCopyrighter, version 0.46) from source using perl Makefile.PL, make, and make install, pulling in CPAN dependencies so that 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) correction can be run on microbial community profiles.

skills.description: Use when you need to reproduce or verify the resource requirements (seconds and MB RAM per genome) of a Perl-based CLI genome-mining tool like DiSCo on FASTA protein inputs, or to demonstrate a tool runs on a personal computer without HPC.
skills.name: perl-command-line-tool-execution
skills.search_text: perl-command-line-tool-execution Use when you need to reproduce or verify the resource requirements (seconds and MB RAM per genome) of a Perl-based CLI genome-mining tool like DiSCo on FASTA protein inputs, or to demonstrate a tool runs on a personal computer without HPC. Input is raw nucleotide contigs or reads rather than FASTA-formatted protein sequences — DiSCo.pl takes user-supplied protein sequences only The goal is classification accuracy evaluation against curated labels rather than measuring runtime/memory cost Only a handful of genomes are at stake and no performance claim needs verification — a single ad-hoc run suffices without benchmarking overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark the computational footprint of DiSCo.pl, a Perl 5 command-line tool, by running it single-threaded against 5100 complete genome protein FASTA files and recording wall-clock runtime and peak resident memory per genome with process-level monitors such as /usr/bin/time or psutil. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000603
skills.summary: Benchmark the computational footprint of DiSCo.pl, a Perl 5 command-line tool, by running it single-threaded against 5100 complete genome protein FASTA files and recording wall-clock runtime and peak resident memory per genome with process-level monitors such as /usr/bin/time or psutil.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nucleotide contigs or reads rather than FASTA-formatted protein sequences — DiSCo.pl takes user-supplied protein sequences only The goal is classification accuracy evaluation against curated labels rather than measuring runtime/memory cost Only a handful of genomes are at stake and no performance claim needs verification — a single ad-hoc run suffices without benchmarking overhead

skills.description: Use when predicting protein-coding genes in assembled metagenome contigs from shotgun sequencing of the human microbiome, especially short contigs where contig-specific parameter estimation is impossible and taxa-specific models are needed.
skills.name: perl-pipeline-configuration-and-execution
skills.search_text: perl-pipeline-configuration-and-execution Use when predicting protein-coding genes in assembled metagenome contigs from shotgun sequencing of the human microbiome, especially short contigs where contig-specific parameter estimation is impossible and taxa-specific models are needed. Input is a single complete prokaryotic genome where GeneMarkS-2 self-training is appropriate rather than metagenomic model assignment Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than assembled contigs Metagenome is not from the human microbiome and taxon coverage of the human-microbiome pan-genome database (>5,000 taxa) is likely too low for reliable pan-genome assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Configure and run the GeneMark-HM Perl pipeline (gm_hm.pl) for protein-coding gene prediction in assembled human-microbiome metagenomes, which assigns contigs to species-level pan-genomes and applies taxa-specific GeneMark models instead of generic metagenomic parameters. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single complete prokaryotic genome where GeneMarkS-2 self-training is appropriate rather than metagenomic model assignment Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than assembled contigs Metagenome is not from the human microbiome and taxon coverage of the human-microbiome pan-genome database (>5,000 taxa) is likely too low for reliable pan-genome assignment

skills.description: Use when you have a relative-abundance or compositional feature table (e.g. MetaPhlAn2 or MAGinator taxon-by-sample matrices) plus two-level metadata (IBD vs control) and need a statistical test of between-group beta-diversity separation.
skills.name: permanova-group-separation-testing
skills.search_text: permanova-group-separation-testing Use when you have a relative-abundance or compositional feature table (e.g. MetaPhlAn2 or MAGinator taxon-by-sample matrices) plus two-level metadata (IBD vs control) and need a statistical test of between-group beta-diversity separation. When the input is raw reads or MAG clusters rather than a completed sample-by-taxon abundance table — the test requires a distance matrix computed from abundances. When group separation in species-level composition has already been established and the goal is taxon-level effect direction — use the Wilcoxon two-cohort discovery/replication differential abundance workflow instead. When samples lack two-level grouping metadata (e.g. IBD vs control); PERMANOVA requires a pre-defined grouping factor. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Tests whether pre-defined sample groups (e.g. IBD patients vs controls) separate in beta-diversity space by running PERMANOVA on a distance matrix and reporting F statistics and R², as done in the MAGinator reanalysis of the Franzosa et al. IBD study using Jensen-Shannon distances on MetaPhlAn2 and MAGinator abundance matrices with PCoA ordination. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8
skills.summary: Tests whether pre-defined sample groups (e.g. IBD patients vs controls) separate in beta-diversity space by running PERMANOVA on a distance matrix and reporting F statistics and R², as done in the MAGinator reanalysis of the Franzosa et al. IBD study using Jensen-Shannon distances on MetaPhlAn2 and MAGinator abundance matrices with PCoA ordination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw reads or MAG clusters rather than a completed sample-by-taxon abundance table — the test requires a distance matrix computed from abundances. When group separation in species-level composition has already been established and the goal is taxon-level effect direction — use the Wilcoxon two-cohort discovery/replication differential abundance workflow instead. When samples lack two-level grouping metadata (e.g. IBD vs control); PERMANOVA requires a pre-defined grouping factor.

skills.description: Use when a microbiome abundance table with a binary grouping variable is available and you must decide which top differential features are true discoveries rather than noise from label mixing, via full-permutation confidence intervals.
skills.name: permutation-based-discovery-selection
skills.search_text: permutation-based-discovery-selection Use when a microbiome abundance table with a binary grouping variable is available and you must decide which top differential features are true discoveries rather than noise from label mixing, via full-permutation confidence intervals. You need confirmatory inference with false discovery rate control or adjusted p-values — the authors state the method does not control FDR and provides no formal inference. The grouping factor is not binary — the bin_* functions and coverage/interval logic are built for a binary outcome ('variable' denotes the name of binary outcome). You intend to set top_pm greater than or equal to the number of microbial features — the README requires top_pm to be less than the feature count. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Selects robust microbiome feature discoveries by comparing p-values of the observed (unpermuted) data against p-values from the fully mixed (fully permuted) data, using the ProgPermute package, and assembles the final discoveries list with signed effect sizes and individual abundance plots. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04061-3
skills.summary: Selects robust microbiome feature discoveries by comparing p-values of the observed (unpermuted) data against p-values from the fully mixed (fully permuted) data, using the ProgPermute package, and assembles the final discoveries list with signed effect sizes and individual abundance plots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need confirmatory inference with false discovery rate control or adjusted p-values — the authors state the method does not control FDR and provides no formal inference. The grouping factor is not binary — the bin_* functions and coverage/interval logic are built for a binary outcome ('variable' denotes the name of binary outcome). You intend to set top_pm greater than or equal to the number of microbial features — the README requires top_pm to be less than the feature count.

skills.description: Use when combining ≥10 studies across multiple related markers (e.g., 6 α-diversity indices) using only effect estimates and standard errors, with no a priori marker-by-marker correlations, and p-values must be obtained via permutations.
skills.name: permutation-based-meta-analysis-pvalue-estimation
skills.search_text: permutation-based-meta-analysis-pvalue-estimation Use when combining ≥10 studies across multiple related markers (e.g., 6 α-diversity indices) using only effect estimates and standard errors, with no a priori marker-by-marker correlations, and p-values must be obtained via permutations. Fewer than 10 studies are available — the mMeta.aMeta function requires the number of studies (rows) to be greater than or equal to 10 Only raw sequencing count data (e.g., OTU tables) are available and study-specific effect estimates and standard errors have not yet been computed via regression — mMeta and aMeta require only the effect estimates and their standard errors A priori marker-by-marker correlations are already known, in which case conventional multivariate meta-analysis methods that use the correlation matrix directly are more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 Estimate marker-specific and multi-marker meta-analysis p-values by non-parametrically permuting study labels via the group permutation method, as implemented in the mMeta R package's mMeta.aMeta function for combining multiple studies across multiple related markers using only summary statistics (effect estimates and standard errors). metagenomics/v1 10.1002/sim.8940
skills.summary: Estimate marker-specific and multi-marker meta-analysis p-values by non-parametrically permuting study labels via the group permutation method, as implemented in the mMeta R package's mMeta.aMeta function for combining multiple studies across multiple related markers using only summary statistics (effect estimates and standard errors).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Fewer than 10 studies are available — the mMeta.aMeta function requires the number of studies (rows) to be greater than or equal to 10 Only raw sequencing count data (e.g., OTU tables) are available and study-specific effect estimates and standard errors have not yet been computed via regression — mMeta and aMeta require only the effect estimates and their standard errors A priori marker-by-marker correlations are already known, in which case conventional multivariate meta-analysis methods that use the correlation matrix directly are more appropriate

skills.description: Use when running mMeta.aMeta on study-by-marker summary statistics (regression coefficient estimates and standard errors) and hypothesis-testing p-values are needed across multiple related markers, particularly when marker-by-marker correlations are unknown.
skills.name: permutation-based-pvalue-computation
skills.search_text: permutation-based-pvalue-computation Use when running mMeta.aMeta on study-by-marker summary statistics (regression coefficient estimates and standard errors) and hypothesis-testing p-values are needed across multiple related markers, particularly when marker-by-marker correlations are unknown. You need a pooled effect estimate rather than hypothesis testing — aMeta's permutation-based across-marker p-value is limited to hypothesis testing, while mMeta's power is only moderate You have fewer than 10 studies per the mMeta.aMeta argument specification (the number of studies, i.e., the number of rows, should be greater than or equal to 10) Marker-by-marker correlations are known a priori, which would make a conventional covariance-aware meta-analysis preferable to the permutation-based correlation estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes p-values for mMeta and aMeta multi-marker meta-analysis using sign-flipping group permutation with n.perm=5000 instead of asymptotic normality, because the group permutation method is more powerful for testing whether multiple related markers (e.g., six α-diversity indices across 15 HIV microbiome studies) are jointly associated with the trait. metagenomics/v1 10.1002/sim.8940
skills.summary: Computes p-values for mMeta and aMeta multi-marker meta-analysis using sign-flipping group permutation with n.perm=5000 instead of asymptotic normality, because the group permutation method is more powerful for testing whether multiple related markers (e.g., six α-diversity indices across 15 HIV microbiome studies) are jointly associated with the trait.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a pooled effect estimate rather than hypothesis testing — aMeta's permutation-based across-marker p-value is limited to hypothesis testing, while mMeta's power is only moderate You have fewer than 10 studies per the mMeta.aMeta argument specification (the number of studies, i.e., the number of rows, should be greater than or equal to 10) Marker-by-marker correlations are known a priori, which would make a conventional covariance-aware meta-analysis preferable to the permutation-based correlation estimation

skills.description: Use when a microbiome association test statistic (e.g. SPU/aSPU/AMAT T_AMAT) has no tractable analytic null distribution and an empirical P-value must be calibrated by permuting the phenotype vector.
skills.name: permutation-based-pvalue-estimation
skills.search_text: permutation-based-pvalue-estimation Use when a microbiome association test statistic (e.g. SPU/aSPU/AMAT T_AMAT) has no tractable analytic null distribution and an empirical P-value must be calibrated by permuting the phenotype vector. A valid asymptotic or kernel-based analytic null distribution exists for the test statistic (e.g. kernel-matrix-based tests with closed-form nulls), making permutation an unnecessary computational burden. The analysis is not testing an association statistic at all (e.g. pure OTU table QC or taxonomic classification), where permutation calibration is out of scope. Extremely low B is required for runtime reasons; a truncated null distribution cannot support P-values at the 0.05 threshold. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Estimate empirical P-values for microbiome multivariate association tests by permuting the outcome vector and comparing the observed statistic against the null distribution; in AMAT the same null statistics are reused to build both the PSPU(γ) combined statistic and the final P-value. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab120
skills.summary: Estimate empirical P-values for microbiome multivariate association tests by permuting the outcome vector and comparing the observed statistic against the null distribution; in AMAT the same null statistics are reused to build both the PSPU(γ) combined statistic and the final P-value.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A valid asymptotic or kernel-based analytic null distribution exists for the test statistic (e.g. kernel-matrix-based tests with closed-form nulls), making permutation an unnecessary computational burden. The analysis is not testing an association statistic at all (e.g. pure OTU table QC or taxonomic classification), where permutation calibration is out of scope. Extremely low B is required for runtime reasons; a truncated null distribution cannot support P-values at the 0.05 threshold.

skills.description: Use when screening high-dimensional OTU/count features for outcome association by permuting an adjusted response (B = 500) to build per-feature distance-correlation nulls and select a data-driven testing subset S.
skills.name: permutation-based-threshold-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-based-threshold-testing Use when screening high-dimensional OTU/count features for outcome association by permuting an adjusted response (B = 500) to build per-feature distance-correlation nulls and select a data-driven testing subset S. Input is already a small prespecified taxa-set (e.g. taxa-sets restricted to at least five taxa) where per-feature screening adds unnecessary permutation cost The response is unadjusted and confounders have not yet been regressed out — the procedure requires an adjusted response vector Only a single omnibus p-value per clade is needed (e.g. FWER-controlled testing at 0.05 via Bonferroni across 115 genera, 57 families, 27 orders, 16 classes, 11 phyla) without feature-level screening Builds per-feature null distributions by repeatedly permuting the adjusted response and recomputing a statistic (e.g. distance correlation between each OTU abundance vector and the response), then screens features whose observed statistic exceeds the permuted mean. It is the thresholding engine behind AMAT's data-driven testing subset S selection. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab120
skills.summary: Builds per-feature null distributions by repeatedly permuting the adjusted response and recomputing a statistic (e.g. distance correlation between each OTU abundance vector and the response), then screens features whose observed statistic exceeds the permuted mean. It is the thresholding engine behind AMAT's data-driven testing subset S selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a small prespecified taxa-set (e.g. taxa-sets restricted to at least five taxa) where per-feature screening adds unnecessary permutation cost The response is unadjusted and confounders have not yet been regressed out — the procedure requires an adjusted response vector Only a single omnibus p-value per clade is needed (e.g. FWER-controlled testing at 0.05 via Bonferroni across 115 genera, 57 families, 27 orders, 16 classes, 11 phyla) without feature-level screening

skills.description: Use when validating a longitudinal tool's false-positive control on semi-synthetic or real count/proportion data by shuffling the continuous time variable within each individual, as done for the fasting stool microbiome benchmark.
skills.name: permutation-null-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-null-significance-testing Use when validating a longitudinal tool's false-positive control on semi-synthetic or real count/proportion data by shuffling the continuous time variable within each individual, as done for the fasting stool microbiome benchmark. The data are not longitudinal or lack a within-individual time variable that can be permuted to create a valid null The goal is to detect real time/treatment effects rather than to benchmark false-positive control under a null hypothesis The analysis is on data types where LongDat's randomized control table is not produced (e.g. measurement/others data return a Normalize_method table instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 A null-control evaluation strategy for longitudinal high-dimensional analyses in which the time variable is permuted within each individual (LongDat's randomized control test) so all true time-feature associations are erased, allowing false-positive rates of LongDat versus MaAsLin2, lgpr and ZIBR to be measured on count-type microbiome data. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad063
skills.summary: A null-control evaluation strategy for longitudinal high-dimensional analyses in which the time variable is permuted within each individual (LongDat's randomized control test) so all true time-feature associations are erased, allowing false-positive rates of LongDat versus MaAsLin2, lgpr and ZIBR to be measured on count-type microbiome data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not longitudinal or lack a within-individual time variable that can be permuted to create a valid null The goal is to detect real time/treatment effects rather than to benchmark false-positive control under a null hypothesis The analysis is on data types where LongDat's randomized control table is not produced (e.g. measurement/others data return a Normalize_method table instead)

skills.description: Use when sample groupings must be tested for significant differences in multivariate dispersion (e.g. allele-frequency or community profiles) and only per-sample distance matrices — not raw feature tables — are available for group-wise hypothesis testing.
skills.name: permutational-multivariate-anova-on-distance-matrices
skills.search_text: permutational-multivariate-anova-on-distance-matrices Use when sample groupings must be tested for significant differences in multivariate dispersion (e.g. allele-frequency or community profiles) and only per-sample distance matrices — not raw feature tables — are available for group-wise hypothesis testing. The question concerns alpha-level diversity within single samples (e.g. nucleotide diversity per gene) rather than between-group differences in multivariate profiles Variants are not shared informative variants — using noisy, non-polymorphic sites inflates false positives and masks group signal Sample groups have fewer replicates than feasible for permutation testing (permutation-based P-values will be unstable) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies permutational multivariate ANOVA (PERMANOVA) with multilevel pairwise.adonis and Bonferroni adjustment to a Bray-Curtis dissimilarity matrix of shared ARG allele frequencies, testing whether antibiotic treatment groups (LEVO, CLA, OTHERS) differ in beta diversity at 6 weeks post-treatment. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Applies permutational multivariate ANOVA (PERMANOVA) with multilevel pairwise.adonis and Bonferroni adjustment to a Bray-Curtis dissimilarity matrix of shared ARG allele frequencies, testing whether antibiotic treatment groups (LEVO, CLA, OTHERS) differ in beta diversity at 6 weeks post-treatment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns alpha-level diversity within single samples (e.g. nucleotide diversity per gene) rather than between-group differences in multivariate profiles Variants are not shared informative variants — using noisy, non-polymorphic sites inflates false positives and masks group signal Sample groups have fewer replicates than feasible for permutation testing (permutation-based P-values will be unstable)

No Pfam (or equivalent domain-family) annotations exist for the input proteins — the V score requires an external functional ground truth Evaluating a supervised classification/model step (e.g. Snekmer apply predictions scored by cosine similarity) rather than de novo cluster assignments Input is nucleotide sequence or the clusters come from a non-protein workflow; V-score benchmarking here is defined for protein clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Evaluates protein clustering results (e.g. MMseqs2 easy-cluster output) against Pfam domain annotations using the V-score, providing an external ground-truth-based measure of cluster quality that can be tracked across parameter sweeps. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad005
skills.summary: Evaluates protein clustering results (e.g. MMseqs2 easy-cluster output) against Pfam domain annotations using the V-score, providing an external ground-truth-based measure of cluster quality that can be tracked across parameter sweeps.

skills.description: Use when evaluating the quality of protein sequence clusterings (e.g. from Linclust, UCLUST, CD-HIT at 90/70/50% identity) by measuring how often cluster members share identical Pfam domain annotations with their cluster representative.
skills.name: pfam-domain-annotation-comparison
skills.search_text: pfam-domain-annotation-comparison Use when evaluating the quality of protein sequence clusterings (e.g. from Linclust, UCLUST, CD-HIT at 90/70/50% identity) by measuring how often cluster members share identical Pfam domain annotations with their cluster representative. When the goal is global functional coherence based on GO terms rather than local domain architecture — use the GO-based 'mean'/'worst' pairwise annotation similarity scores instead. When sequences carry no UniProt Pfam annotations (e.g. novel metagenomic contigs without Pfam hits) — the match/mismatch scoring requires existing domain annotations. When clustering quality must be judged on structural or phylogenetic criteria rather than shared Pfam domain composition. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Assesses local functional consistency of protein sequence clusters by comparing the Pfam domain annotations of each cluster representative against all cluster members, scoring exact domain-annotation matches as 1 and mismatches as 0. Used in the Linclust paper to show that Linclust/MMseqs2 clusterings of UniProt 2016_03 are more locally consistent than UCLUST and CD-HIT. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-04964-5
skills.summary: Assesses local functional consistency of protein sequence clusters by comparing the Pfam domain annotations of each cluster representative against all cluster members, scoring exact domain-annotation matches as 1 and mismatches as 0. Used in the Linclust paper to show that Linclust/MMseqs2 clusterings of UniProt 2016_03 are more locally consistent than UCLUST and CD-HIT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is global functional coherence based on GO terms rather than local domain architecture — use the GO-based 'mean'/'worst' pairwise annotation similarity scores instead. When sequences carry no UniProt Pfam annotations (e.g. novel metagenomic contigs without Pfam hits) — the match/mismatch scoring requires existing domain annotations. When clustering quality must be judged on structural or phylogenetic criteria rather than shared Pfam domain composition.

When no Hi-C proximity-ligation data exist — CRISPR spacers alone cannot confirm pairs present in a given sample since some CRISPR associations are historical When viral contigs lack identifiable CRISPR arrays (PILER-CR finds none), as no spacer-based validation signal will be produced For discriminating viral from non-viral contigs — upstream viral contig identification (e.g. VirSorter) is a prerequisite, not part of this skill http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Validates Hi-C-inferred virus-host MAG pairs by independently predicting CRISPR spacers in vMAGs (PILER-CR) and aligning them against host MAG contigs (BLAST), then measuring the overlap between CRISPR-supported pairs and Hi-C linkages. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y

skills.description: Use when you have quality-assessed viral contigs (e.g., identified by VirSorter2/DeepVirFinder/VIBRANT and checked with CheckV) and need to know which bacteria they infect, or when reproducing host-based findings such as phage–host links in UC vs healthy viromes.
skills.name: phage-host-prediction-interpretation
skills.search_text: phage-host-prediction-interpretation Use when you have quality-assessed viral contigs (e.g., identified by VirSorter2/DeepVirFinder/VIBRANT and checked with CheckV) and need to know which bacteria they infect, or when reproducing host-based findings such as phage–host links in UC vs healthy viromes. Input is isolated viral fractions/single-virus samples rather than metagenomic contigs — the article notes ViroProfiler is 'specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses', and host prediction requires assembled community contigs. Sequences carry excessive environmental contamination — this 'could increase the running time of the pipeline and result in lower precision', degrading host-prediction reliability. Only genome taxonomy or AMG annotation is needed with no host attribution goal — host prediction is a costly step (300 GB memory in the validation run) that is unnecessary for taxonomy-only questions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Predict bacterial hosts for viral contigs assembled from shotgun virome data using ViroProfiler's host-prediction module (iPHoP), then interpret predicted host assignments biologically — e.g., counting phages infecting Bacteroidia in ulcerative-colitis versus healthy fecal samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Predict bacterial hosts for viral contigs assembled from shotgun virome data using ViroProfiler's host-prediction module (iPHoP), then interpret predicted host assignments biologically — e.g., counting phages infecting Bacteroidia in ulcerative-colitis versus healthy fecal samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is isolated viral fractions/single-virus samples rather than metagenomic contigs — the article notes ViroProfiler is 'specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses', and host prediction requires assembled community contigs. Sequences carry excessive environmental contamination — this 'could increase the running time of the pipeline and result in lower precision', degrading host-prediction reliability. Only genome taxonomy or AMG annotation is needed with no host attribution goal — host prediction is a costly step (300 GB memory in the validation run) that is unnecessary for taxonomy-only questions.

skills.description: Use when raw Nanopore metagenomic FASTQ reads contain phage-lambda sequencing control contamination and must be decontaminated after adapter trimming and before quality filtering and assembly.
skills.name: phage-lambda-control-read-removal
skills.search_text: phage-lambda-control-read-removal Use when raw Nanopore metagenomic FASTQ reads contain phage-lambda sequencing control contamination and must be decontaminated after adapter trimming and before quality filtering and assembly. Input reads are PacBio, not Nanopore — Porechop adapter trimming is explicitly skipped for PacBio reads in nf-core/mag, and the Nanopore control-removal gating does not apply. Input is already adapter-trimmed and control-free (e.g. an already quality-filtered FASTQ) — re-running removal would not change the read set. The goal is short-read (Illumina) preprocessing — nf-core/mag handles short reads with a separate short-read QC path rather than the Porechop/NanoLyse/Filtlong long-read chain. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Removal of phage-lambda sequencing-control contamination from raw Oxford Nanopore metagenomic reads within the nf-core/mag long-read pre-processing subworkflow, so that downstream Filtlong quality filtering, NanoPlot QC, and assembly operate only on true sample reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac007
skills.summary: Removal of phage-lambda sequencing-control contamination from raw Oxford Nanopore metagenomic reads within the nf-core/mag long-read pre-processing subworkflow, so that downstream Filtlong quality filtering, NanoPlot QC, and assembly operate only on true sample reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are PacBio, not Nanopore — Porechop adapter trimming is explicitly skipped for PacBio reads in nf-core/mag, and the Nanopore control-removal gating does not apply. Input is already adapter-trimmed and control-free (e.g. an already quality-filtered FASTQ) — re-running removal would not change the read set. The goal is short-read (Illumina) preprocessing — nf-core/mag handles short reads with a separate short-read QC path rather than the Porechop/NanoLyse/Filtlong long-read chain.

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a SNP table or feature table with no read-level mappings — inStrain profiling requires .bam read-pair data Question is about strain sharing/comparison between profiles (use 'inStrain compare' ConANI/popANI instead of gene-level dN/dS visualization) Only rapid coverage/breadth estimates are needed, e.g. subspecies detection at >= 0.5 unmaskedBreadth — use CoverM or inStrain genome-level output rather than the full dN/dS workflow

skills.search_text: phage-mining-multi-tool-prediction Use when FASTQ metagenomic or virome reads need viral contig identification and vOTU counting, and a single-miner prediction would miss phages detectable only by complementary k-mer, homology, or HMM-based approaches. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than a curated set of predicted viral contigs — the classifier expects contigs already identified as viral Samples contain excessive environmental contamination: ViroProfiler notes this 'could increase the running time of the pipeline and result in lower precision', so pre-isolate the viral fraction before sequencing You only need lytic/lysogenic calls and cannot run both tools — the skill's core value is reconciling BACPHLIP and Replidec per contig

skills.name: phage-taxonomy-assignment-from-reference-clusters
skills.search_text: phage-taxonomy-assignment-from-reference-clusters Use when a dereplicated vOTU multifasta needs phylum-to-genus (and species-level) taxonomic labels by shared-protein-content similarity to curated INPHARED/GenBank phage reference genomes. When sequences have no vOTU-style naming prefix and cannot be distinguished from reference genomes in the network files, since graphanalyzer relies on --prefix matching When reference-based cluster sharing is expected to fail, e.g. deeply novel phages with no INPHARED relatives — assignments will remain unclassified at genus level For direct read-level taxonomy (use Kraken2/MiniKraken2_V1 read classification instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assigns taxonomy to dereplicated vOTUs by clustering them with curated bacteriophage references in a protein-sharing network (vConTACT2 on INPHARED) and automatically transferring labels from the network with graphanalyzer, because vConTACT2 alone leaves classification to manual inspection. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Assigns taxonomy to dereplicated vOTUs by clustering them with curated bacteriophage references in a protein-sharing network (vConTACT2 on INPHARED) and automatically transferring labels from the network with graphanalyzer, because vConTACT2 alone leaves classification to manual inspection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When sequences have no vOTU-style naming prefix and cannot be distinguished from reference genomes in the network files, since graphanalyzer relies on --prefix matching When reference-based cluster sharing is expected to fail, e.g. deeply novel phages with no INPHARED relatives — assignments will remain unclassified at genus level For direct read-level taxonomy (use Kraken2/MiniKraken2_V1 read classification instead)

skills.description: Use when shotgun viral metagenomic reads (FASTQ) must be turned into viral contigs with assigned taxonomy and family-level composition, e.g., comparing phage community structure between conditions such as UC vs healthy fecal viromes.
skills.name: phage-taxonomy-composition-analysis
skills.search_text: phage-taxonomy-composition-analysis Use when shotgun viral metagenomic reads (FASTQ) must be turned into viral contigs with assigned taxonomy and family-level composition, e.g., comparing phage community structure between conditions such as UC vs healthy fecal viromes. Samples are whole-cell metagenomes without viral fraction isolation — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses, and excessive contamination lowers precision. Input is already a curated viral contig set with CheckV scores and taxonomic labels — only the composition/aggregation step is needed, not the full identification pipeline. Viruses are RNA viruses or eukaryotic viruses outside the phage-focused annotation scope of ViroProfiler's toolchain (VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder + vConTACT2). http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assign taxonomy to viral contigs assembled from shotgun virome data with ViroProfiler's vConTACT2 + MMseqs2 workflow, then compute family-level viral composition (e.g., Podoviridae proportion) across sample groups. This is the core composition-profiling purpose of the containerized ViroProfiler pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Assign taxonomy to viral contigs assembled from shotgun virome data with ViroProfiler's vConTACT2 + MMseqs2 workflow, then compute family-level viral composition (e.g., Podoviridae proportion) across sample groups. This is the core composition-profiling purpose of the containerized ViroProfiler pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are whole-cell metagenomes without viral fraction isolation — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses, and excessive contamination lowers precision. Input is already a curated viral contig set with CheckV scores and taxonomic labels — only the composition/aggregation step is needed, not the full identification pipeline. Viruses are RNA viruses or eukaryotic viruses outside the phage-focused annotation scope of ViroProfiler's toolchain (VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder + vConTACT2).

skills.description: Use when vConTACT2 has produced genome_by_genome_overview.csv and c1.ntw for vOTUs (e.g., from MetaPhage) and a direct taxonomic label per vOTU is needed instead of manual network inspection.
skills.name: phage-taxonomy-conservatism-rules
skills.search_text: phage-taxonomy-conservatism-rules Use when vConTACT2 has produced genome_by_genome_overview.csv and c1.ntw for vOTUs (e.g., from MetaPhage) and a direct taxonomic label per vOTU is needed instead of manual network inspection. vConTACT2 outputs were not generated with the INPHARED excluding-refseq database, so reference taxonomy metadata in the expected format is unavailable A genus-level ICTV classification requiring exhaustive evidence is needed — this rule-based inheritance only propagates taxonomy of the closest reference neighbor Input is raw reads or unassembled contigs rather than already-clustered vOTUs with a vConTACT2 network http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Automates vOTU taxonomic assignment from vConTACT2 network outputs by inheriting taxonomy from same-cluster reference genomes ordered by edge weight, applying conservatism rules that truncate assignments at subfamily/family level depending on the neighbor's status and origin. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Automates vOTU taxonomic assignment from vConTACT2 network outputs by inheriting taxonomy from same-cluster reference genomes ordered by edge weight, applying conservatism rules that truncate assignments at subfamily/family level depending on the neighbor's status and origin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: vConTACT2 outputs were not generated with the INPHARED excluding-refseq database, so reference taxonomy metadata in the expected format is unavailable A genus-level ICTV classification requiring exhaustive evidence is needed — this rule-based inheritance only propagates taxonomy of the closest reference neighbor Input is raw reads or unassembled contigs rather than already-clustered vOTUs with a vConTACT2 network

skills.description: Use when Traitar (Pfam 27.0-based, phypat or phypat+PGL models) has been applied to genomes and you need the ranked Pfam families underlying a specific phenotype prediction, e.g. to interpret a trait assignment mechanistically.
skills.name: phenotype-associated-protein-family-ranking
skills.search_text: phenotype-associated-protein-family-ranking Use when Traitar (Pfam 27.0-based, phypat or phypat+PGL models) has been applied to genomes and you need the ranked Pfam families underlying a specific phenotype prediction, e.g. to interpret a trait assignment mechanistically. The genome of interest is highly incomplete: absence of a phenotype prediction may simply reflect missing protein families in the input genome, so family rankings would be misleading You need trait prediction from data other than presence/absence of protein families - Traitar currently uses only Pfam presence/absence and does not integrate other omics data You want to predict plant biomass phenotypes: the plant biomass predictor is not included in the released Traitar software http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extracts and verifies the Pfam protein families that Traitar's phypat/phypat+PGL classifiers rank as most important for specific phenotypes, such as motility (flagellar export chaperone FliS, PF02561), nitrate-to-nitrite conversion (Nar PF02665/PF02613, NapB PF03892, NapD PF03927), and l-arabinose fermentation (l-arabinose isomerase PF11762, arabinofuranosidase PF06964). metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00101-16
skills.summary: Extracts and verifies the Pfam protein families that Traitar's phypat/phypat+PGL classifiers rank as most important for specific phenotypes, such as motility (flagellar export chaperone FliS, PF02561), nitrate-to-nitrite conversion (Nar PF02665/PF02613, NapB PF03892, NapD PF03927), and l-arabinose fermentation (l-arabinose isomerase PF11762, arabinofuranosidase PF06964).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The genome of interest is highly incomplete: absence of a phenotype prediction may simply reflect missing protein families in the input genome, so family rankings would be misleading You need trait prediction from data other than presence/absence of protein families - Traitar currently uses only Pfam presence/absence and does not integrate other omics data You want to predict plant biomass phenotypes: the plant biomass predictor is not included in the released Traitar software
