skills.description: Use when evaluating genotype-to-phenotype classifiers: you have genome FASTAs plus externally curated phenotype labels (e.g., Bergey's Manual, GIDEON) and need to align predicted trait labels with the reference labels to compute accuracy.
skills.name: phenotype-label-mapping
skills.search_text: phenotype-label-mapping Use when evaluating genotype-to-phenotype classifiers: you have genome FASTAs plus externally curated phenotype labels (e.g., Bergey's Manual, GIDEON) and need to align predicted trait labels with the reference labels to compute accuracy. Input genomes are already gene-predicted and you only need Pfam annotation onward — use 'traitar phenotype ... from_genes' instead of the full from_nucleotides workflow Genomes are highly incomplete (e.g., SAGs) and you need high-specificity labels — a missing prediction may just reflect absent Pfam families, not a true phenotype absence You need phenotypes beyond Traitar's 67 traits (e.g., the plant biomass predictor, which is not included in the Traitar release) Map Traitar's 67 phenotype predictions (from phypat and phypat+PGL classifiers) onto curated phenotype labels extracted from literature sources such as Bergey's Manual of Systematic Bacteriology or GIDEON, so classifier accuracy can be scored against an independent gold standard. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00101-16
skills.summary: Map Traitar's 67 phenotype predictions (from phypat and phypat+PGL classifiers) onto curated phenotype labels extracted from literature sources such as Bergey's Manual of Systematic Bacteriology or GIDEON, so classifier accuracy can be scored against an independent gold standard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input genomes are already gene-predicted and you only need Pfam annotation onward — use 'traitar phenotype ... from_genes' instead of the full from_nucleotides workflow Genomes are highly incomplete (e.g., SAGs) and you need high-specificity labels — a missing prediction may just reflect absent Pfam families, not a true phenotype absence You need phenotypes beyond Traitar's 67 traits (e.g., the plant biomass predictor, which is not included in the Traitar release)

skills.description: Use when validating a published accuracy claim stated as a count of phenotypes above macroaccuracy thresholds (e.g. >80%, >=90%) and you have a per-phenotype, per-classifier cross-validation accuracy table.
skills.name: phenotype-macroaccuracy-threshold-counting
skills.search_text: phenotype-macroaccuracy-threshold-counting Use when validating a published accuracy claim stated as a count of phenotypes above macroaccuracy thresholds (e.g. >80%, >=90%) and you have a per-phenotype, per-classifier cross-validation accuracy table. Input is raw phenotype prediction output (e.g. predictions_majority-vote_combined.txt) rather than a per-phenotype macroaccuracy summary table — you would first need cross-validation accuracies, not predictions The claim concerns a single fixed classifier's overall accuracy (82.6% or 85.5%) rather than a best-of-two-classifier phenotype count The phenotype set is not the 67 GIDEON phenotypes (e.g. Bergey's Manual phenotypes), since the 53/26 counts are tied to the GIDEON cross-validation table http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Verifies reported phenotype-level performance claims by recomputing, per phenotype, the best macroaccuracy across Traitar's two classifiers (phypat and phypat+PGL) from the Table S2 GIDEON cross-validation table and counting how many of the 67 phenotypes exceed the >80% and >=90% thresholds (expected: 53 and 26). metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00101-16
skills.summary: Verifies reported phenotype-level performance claims by recomputing, per phenotype, the best macroaccuracy across Traitar's two classifiers (phypat and phypat+PGL) from the Table S2 GIDEON cross-validation table and counting how many of the 67 phenotypes exceed the >80% and >=90% thresholds (expected: 53 and 26).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw phenotype prediction output (e.g. predictions_majority-vote_combined.txt) rather than a per-phenotype macroaccuracy summary table — you would first need cross-validation accuracies, not predictions The claim concerns a single fixed classifier's overall accuracy (82.6% or 85.5%) rather than a best-of-two-classifier phenotype count The phenotype set is not the 67 GIDEON phenotypes (e.g. Bergey's Manual phenotypes), since the 53/26 counts are tied to the GIDEON cross-validation table

skills.description: Use when a trained linear-kernel phenotype model (e.g. PICA SVM on COG features) must be interpreted feature-wise, to test whether a trait is predicted by gene absence rather than gene presence.
skills.name: phenotype-model-interpretation
skills.search_text: phenotype-model-interpretation Use when a trained linear-kernel phenotype model (e.g. PICA SVM on COG features) must be interpreted feature-wise, to test whether a trait is predicted by gene absence rather than gene presence. Input is a raw genome or metagenomic bin requiring a trait prediction — use the PICA/phenotrex prediction workflow instead of model interpretation No trained linear-kernel model exists for the trait of interest (e.g. insufficient training data), so there is no weight vector to rank Input is already a ranked feature table and only re-analysis or re-formatting is needed Extracts and ranks the signed SVM weight vector of a trained PICA/libSVM phenotype model (e.g. the obligate intracellular model trained on 97 labelled species) to identify which COG features — by presence or absence — drive the trait prediction, and validates the ranking against the published table (Additional File 1: Table S2). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-16-s14-s1
skills.summary: Extracts and ranks the signed SVM weight vector of a trained PICA/libSVM phenotype model (e.g. the obligate intracellular model trained on 97 labelled species) to identify which COG features — by presence or absence — drive the trait prediction, and validates the ranking against the published table (Additional File 1: Table S2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw genome or metagenomic bin requiring a trait prediction — use the PICA/phenotrex prediction workflow instead of model interpretation No trained linear-kernel model exists for the trait of interest (e.g. insufficient training data), so there is no weight vector to rank Input is already a ranked feature table and only re-analysis or re-formatting is needed

Input is a continuous or non-binary phenotype rather than the case-control labels (1 = case, 0 = control) that the sample list's Phenotype column must contain Only raw QCed FASTQ or abundance tables are available and the Step 4-1 phylogenetic association summary statistics (sumstats_*.txt) have not yet been generated The goal is direct adjustment of hidden confounding factors by integrating covariates into the case-control model — the article notes this is not currently implemented in OMARU http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Estimate an empirical Bonferroni significance threshold (Psig) for OMARU clade-level case-control association tests by permuting binary phenotype labels 10,000 times and building the null distribution of the minimum P-value, with a Harrell-Davis bootstrap 95% CI reported for Pmin. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019

skills.description: Use when a trained phenotypic trait model exists and you need to score every genome/species in a large database (e.g. eggNOG 4.0 core and periphery) and assemble the positives into a validated prediction table.
skills.name: phenotype-prediction-table-compilation
skills.search_text: phenotype-prediction-table-compilation Use when a trained phenotypic trait model exists and you need to score every genome/species in a large database (e.g. eggNOG 4.0 core and periphery) and assemble the positives into a validated prediction table. The input is a raw genome FASTA rather than precomputed COG presence/absence trait profiles — train/sample extraction must happen first. You need predictions on incomplete metagenomic genome bins with no trait model trained on marker COGs; the paper cautions that reliable prediction requires roughly 60-70% genome completeness. The target trait has no pre-trained model; the paper notes performance for further ecologically important traits awaits sufficient training data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Apply a trained intracellular phenotype model (PICA SVM with libSVM backend) across all prokaryotic species in eggNOG 4.0 and compile the positive predictions into a species-level table. This reproduces the paper's screening that identified 169 obligate intracellular species (160 bacteria, 9 archaea). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-16-s14-s1
skills.summary: Apply a trained intracellular phenotype model (PICA SVM with libSVM backend) across all prokaryotic species in eggNOG 4.0 and compile the positive predictions into a species-level table. This reproduces the paper's screening that identified 169 obligate intracellular species (160 bacteria, 9 archaea).

skills.description: Use when the goal is to semi-automatically extract phenotypic characters (e.g., cell shape, Gram stain, NaCl/pH/temperature ranges, antibiotic sensitivity) from taxonomic description text into a taxon-by-character matrix for phylogenetic or phenomic analysis.
skills.name: phenotypic-character-information-extraction
skills.search_text: phenotypic-character-information-extraction Use when the goal is to semi-automatically extract phenotypic characters (e.g., cell shape, Gram stain, NaCl/pH/temperature ranges, antibiotic sensitivity) from taxonomic description text into a taxon-by-character matrix for phylogenetic or phenomic analysis. Descriptions are morphological/semi-structured botanical texts better handled by CharaParser — MicroPIE targets prokaryotic descriptions rich in physiological and ecological traits The task requires domain-general open extraction without curated term lists — OIE/DeepDive-style systems are a different (inadequate per the paper) approach You need characters outside the 42 supported phenotypic character types of MicroPIE 0.1.0 http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extract microbial phenotypic characters and character states from natural-language prokaryotic taxonomic descriptions using MicroPIE, which combines an SVM-based Character Predictor with rule-based, term-list-driven extraction to produce a structured taxon-by-character matrix. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1396-8
skills.summary: Extract microbial phenotypic characters and character states from natural-language prokaryotic taxonomic descriptions using MicroPIE, which combines an SVM-based Character Predictor with rule-based, term-list-driven extraction to produce a structured taxon-by-character matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Descriptions are morphological/semi-structured botanical texts better handled by CharaParser — MicroPIE targets prokaryotic descriptions rich in physiological and ecological traits The task requires domain-general open extraction without curated term lists — OIE/DeepDive-style systems are a different (inadequate per the paper) approach You need characters outside the 42 supported phenotypic character types of MicroPIE 0.1.0

skills.description: Use when per-taxon extraction records from MicroPIE's character extractors must be pivoted into a structured taxon-by-character matrix, especially when a taxon has multiple extracted values for the same character that must be merged.
skills.name: phenotypic-character-value-concatenation
skills.search_text: phenotypic-character-value-concatenation Use when per-taxon extraction records from MicroPIE's character extractors must be pivoted into a structured taxon-by-character matrix, especially when a taxon has multiple extracted values for the same character that must be merged. The input is already a structured taxon-by-character matrix rather than raw natural language taxonomic descriptions or per-taxon extraction records The task requires character prediction or state extraction itself rather than matrix assembly — those are handled by upstream MicroPIE components (SVM Character Predictor, value extractors) Taxonomic descriptions contain little phenotypic content (e.g., morphology-only focus unsuited to MicroPIE's prokaryotic physiological/ecological character set) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Assembles character and character-state values extracted by MicroPIE into a final taxon-by-character matrix, concatenating multiple values per character into a single cell separated by number signs (#) so the output can be used by phylogenetic comparative analysis software. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1396-8
skills.summary: Assembles character and character-state values extracted by MicroPIE into a final taxon-by-character matrix, concatenating multiple values per character into a single cell separated by number signs (#) so the output can be used by phylogenetic comparative analysis software.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a structured taxon-by-character matrix rather than raw natural language taxonomic descriptions or per-taxon extraction records The task requires character prediction or state extraction itself rather than matrix assembly — those are handled by upstream MicroPIE components (SVM Character Predictor, value extractors) Taxonomic descriptions contain little phenotypic content (e.g., morphology-only focus unsuited to MicroPIE's prokaryotic physiological/ecological character set)

The lab needs a LIMS that records NGS or analysis data itself — MetaLIMS intentionally omits recording NGS or analysis data The task requires active maintenance guarantees — MetaLIMS is no longer being actively maintained and has not been updated for recent Ubuntu, MySQL, PHP, or Apache versions The goal is a full-featured commercial LIMS with instrument integration and complex workflows rather than simple sample metadata storage http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Implement and deploy a PHP/MySQL web module inside MetaLIMS, a free open-source LIMS built on XAMPP/Apache/HTML5, so that stored sample metadata can be queried, rendered (e.g., with Php Excel and DataTables), and exported for downstream tasks such as Clarity LIMS submission. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/gix025

skills.description: Use when you have per-alignment contig-to-reference-replicon identities (contigs above the --minLength threshold) from an assembly benchmark like LMAS and need a per-contig, Phred-like quality score comparable across assemblers.
skills.name: phred-like-quality-score-computation
skills.search_text: phred-like-quality-score-computation Use when you have per-alignment contig-to-reference-replicon identities (contigs above the --minLength threshold) from an assembly benchmark like LMAS and need a per-contig, Phred-like quality score comparable across assemblers. Contigs shorter than the --minLength threshold (1000 bp) — they are excluded from the alignment input and therefore from Pls computation Assemblies with no reference replicons available — the score requires contig-to-reference alignment identity and cannot be computed from contig features alone (unlike QUAST-style reference-free metrics) http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Computes the LMAS Pls (Phred-like) assembly quality score per contig by converting contig-to-reference identity into a Phred-style value, following Equation 1 with E = 1 - Identity as the error function and a cap of 60 when E = 0. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giac122
skills.summary: Computes the LMAS Pls (Phred-like) assembly quality score per contig by converting contig-to-reference identity into a Phred-style value, following Equation 1 with E = 1 - Identity as the error function and a cap of 60 when E = 0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Contigs shorter than the --minLength threshold (1000 bp) — they are excluded from the alignment input and therefore from Pls computation Assemblies with no reference replicons available — the score requires contig-to-reference alignment identity and cannot be computed from contig features alone (unlike QUAST-style reference-free metrics)

skills.description: Use when FASTQ or SAM input from Illumina CASAVA pipelines contains ASCII quality values that must be turned into per-base error probabilities for probabilistic scoring, overlap alignment, or assembly quality filtering.
skills.name: phred-quality-probability-conversion
skills.search_text: phred-quality-probability-conversion Use when FASTQ or SAM input from Illumina CASAVA pipelines contains ASCII quality values that must be turned into per-base error probabilities for probabilistic scoring, overlap alignment, or assembly quality filtering. Input is a feature table, amplicon sequence variant table, or already-assembled contigs with no per-base PHRED quality strings Reads carry non-CASAVA quality encoding without verification — SeqPrep README notes ASCII < 33 characters appear when phred+64 data is misread, so check the encoding offset before applying the conversion http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Convert CASAVA-encoded ASCII PHRED quality characters in Illumina FASTQ reads into per-base error probabilities using ε = 10^(-A/10), which is the basis for PANDAseq's probabilistic overlap scoring, error correction, and assembly quality thresholds. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-13-31
skills.summary: Convert CASAVA-encoded ASCII PHRED quality characters in Illumina FASTQ reads into per-base error probabilities using ε = 10^(-A/10), which is the basis for PANDAseq's probabilistic overlap scoring, error correction, and assembly quality thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a feature table, amplicon sequence variant table, or already-assembled contigs with no per-base PHRED quality strings Reads carry non-CASAVA quality encoding without verification — SeqPrep README notes ASCII < 33 characters appear when phred+64 data is misread, so check the encoding offset before applying the conversion

skills.description: Use when short reads have been mapped to known MLST alleles and you need to encode read-allele mapping quality as a cost matrix (Phred-scaled mismatch scores) before solving the allele diversity ILP.
skills.name: phred-score-mapping-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: phred-score-mapping-matrix-construction Use when short reads have been mapped to known MLST alleles and you need to encode read-allele mapping quality as a cost matrix (Phred-scaled mismatch scores) before solving the allele diversity ILP. No Phred quality scores are available for the reads (e.g. pseudo-aligned or quantified reads), since the matrix entries depend on per-base quality values Reads have not yet been mapped to the allele database with Bowtie — the matrix is built from .sam-derived mapping information, not raw reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Constructs the weighted bipartite read-allele incidence matrix M used by the Allele Diversity Problem ILP, where entry m_ij is the sum of Phred scores of mismatched bases (normalized over the ASCII 33-126 range) between read r_i and allele a_j, with non-mapping reads set to infinity. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Constructs the weighted bipartite read-allele incidence matrix M used by the Allele Diversity Problem ILP, where entry m_ij is the sum of Phred scores of mismatched bases (normalized over the ASCII 33-126 range) between read r_i and allele a_j, with non-mapping reads set to infinity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No Phred quality scores are available for the reads (e.g. pseudo-aligned or quantified reads), since the matrix entries depend on per-base quality values Reads have not yet been mapped to the allele database with Bowtie — the matrix is built from .sam-derived mapping information, not raw reads

skills.description: Use when starting from shotgun metagenomic FASTQ files and you need clade-resolved (UHGG-based) phylogenetic abundance profiles with rigorous read, sample, and clade QC ahead of case-control MWAS testing.

skills.search_text: phylogenetic-abundance-profiling Use when starting from shotgun metagenomic FASTQ files and you need clade-resolved (UHGG-based) phylogenetic abundance profiles with rigorous read, sample, and clade QC ahead of case-control MWAS testing. Input is already a phylogenetic/clade abundance table rather than raw shotgun FASTQ reads — use the association-test Snakefiles (Step 4) directly instead The goal is functional (gene/pathway) profiling based on UniRef90 and GO rather than clade-level phylogenetic profiling Only short-read 16S amplicon data are available — OMARU's workflow is built for shotgun sequencing reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Construct clade-level phylogenetic abundance profiles of shotgun metagenomic samples by mapping reads to a UHGG-based reference with OMARU's Snakemake workflow, then quality-control clades and samples before case-control association testing. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: Construct clade-level phylogenetic abundance profiles of shotgun metagenomic samples by mapping reads to a UHGG-based reference with OMARU's Snakemake workflow, then quality-control clades and samples before case-control association testing.

skills.description: Use when training gene-prediction models on short metagenomic shotgun reads (e.g. 454 human gut microbiome reads) where GC-content-based genome selection is unreliable and organism-of-origin must be inferred per read.
skills.name: phylogenetic-classification-based-model-parameterization
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-classification-based-model-parameterization Use when training gene-prediction models on short metagenomic shotgun reads (e.g. 454 human gut microbiome reads) where GC-content-based genome selection is unreliable and organism-of-origin must be inferred per read. Input is a complete prokaryotic genome where standard Glimmer can train directly on the full sequence without phylogenetic classification Sequences are long enough that GC-content reliably identifies evolutionarily related training genomes (the limitation motivating classification applies to short reads) Analysis goal is quantification or assembly of already-predicted genes rather than gene prediction model training http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Parameterize metagenomic gene-prediction models (Glimmer-MG interpolated Markov models) using Phymm phylogenetic classifications of individual reads rather than GC-content binning, because read-level phylogenetic assignments identify appropriate training genomes for short fragmented metagenomic sequences. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: Parameterize metagenomic gene-prediction models (Glimmer-MG interpolated Markov models) using Phymm phylogenetic classifications of individual reads rather than GC-content binning, because read-level phylogenetic assignments identify appropriate training genomes for short fragmented metagenomic sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a complete prokaryotic genome where standard Glimmer can train directly on the full sequence without phylogenetic classification Sequences are long enough that GC-content reliably identifies evolutionarily related training genomes (the limitation motivating classification applies to short reads) Analysis goal is quantification or assembly of already-predicted genes rather than gene prediction model training

skills.description: Use when 16S marker gene OTUs must be mapped to predicted gene families (KO/COG) for organisms without reference genomes, and a phylogenetic reference tree with annotated tips (e.g. Greengenes + IMG) is available.
skills.name: phylogenetic-distance-weighting
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-distance-weighting Use when 16S marker gene OTUs must be mapped to predicted gene families (KO/COG) for organisms without reference genomes, and a phylogenetic reference tree with annotated tips (e.g. Greengenes + IMG) is available. The target organism's genome is already present in the IMG reference table, so observed gene content should be used directly instead of inferred Inference concerns viral or eukaryotic community components, since only bacterial and archaeal 16S marker sequences are included The marker gene sequences of the strains in question are identical, so strain-level variation cannot be distinguished http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Predicts gene family content for organisms lacking sequenced reference genomes by averaging extant and ancestral (ancestral-state-reconstructed) genome contents on a marker gene tree, weighting each contributor exponentially by the reciprocal of its phylogenetic distance to the target tip — the core PICRUSt gene content inference mechanism. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Predicts gene family content for organisms lacking sequenced reference genomes by averaging extant and ancestral (ancestral-state-reconstructed) genome contents on a marker gene tree, weighting each contributor exponentially by the reciprocal of its phylogenetic distance to the target tip — the core PICRUSt gene content inference mechanism.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target organism's genome is already present in the IMG reference table, so observed gene content should be used directly instead of inferred Inference concerns viral or eukaryotic community components, since only bacterial and archaeal 16S marker sequences are included The marker gene sequences of the strains in question are identical, so strain-level variation cannot be distinguished

skills.description: Use when you have an OTU/species count table per sample plus a phylogenetic tree and need per-sample phylogenetic α-diversity indices (PD, PE, PQE, or richness/Shannon/Simpson) as regression outcomes for downstream meta-analysis.
skills.name: phylogenetic-diversity-calculation
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-diversity-calculation Use when you have an OTU/species count table per sample plus a phylogenetic tree and need per-sample phylogenetic α-diversity indices (PD, PE, PQE, or richness/Shannon/Simpson) as regression outcomes for downstream meta-analysis. Input is raw, un-rarefied sequence data — the article rarefies the OTU table to an even level of total reads per sample before computing diversity, so diversity computed on uneven depths is not comparable You only need taxonomic (non-phylogenetic) indices and have no phylogenetic tree — PD/PE/PQE require branch lengths and the tree http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Compute phylogenetically weighted α-diversity indices (PD, PE, PQE) for each sample from a rarefied OTU count table and its phylogenetic tree, in R using the vegan package, so that study-specific effect estimates for phylogenetic diversity can feed downstream meta-analysis (mMeta/aMeta). metagenomics/v1 10.1002/sim.8940
skills.summary: Compute phylogenetically weighted α-diversity indices (PD, PE, PQE) for each sample from a rarefied OTU count table and its phylogenetic tree, in R using the vegan package, so that study-specific effect estimates for phylogenetic diversity can feed downstream meta-analysis (mMeta/aMeta).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, un-rarefied sequence data — the article rarefies the OTU table to an even level of total reads per sample before computing diversity, so diversity computed on uneven depths is not comparable You only need taxonomic (non-phylogenetic) indices and have no phylogenetic tree — PD/PE/PQE require branch lengths and the tree

skills.description: Use when 16S rRNA amplicon count tables (biom, QIIME, generic) need GCN-bias correction, or when qPCR-derived total abundance must be adjusted by average community GCN before downstream diversity or enterotype analyses.
skills.name: phylogenetic-gcn-correction
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-gcn-correction Use when 16S rRNA amplicon count tables (biom, QIIME, generic) need GCN-bias correction, or when qPCR-derived total abundance must be adjusted by average community GCN before downstream diversity or enterotype analyses. The input table already contains percentages or altered taxonomic strings — CopyRighter requires raw read counts and unaltered assignments The community was profiled with a taxonomy other than Greengenes (e.g. Silva) — GCN estimates are currently only distributed for the Greengenes database The bias of interest is GC percent, genome length beyond metagenomic trait data, or fungal ITS variation — these corrections are only hypothetical pending appropriate pre-computed estimates http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Corrects 16S rRNA amplicon microbial profiles and associated qPCR total abundance for 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) bias using CopyRighter, which reweights OTU abundances by the inverse of phylogenetically-inferred, lineage-specific GCN estimates from the Greengenes database. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Corrects 16S rRNA amplicon microbial profiles and associated qPCR total abundance for 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) bias using CopyRighter, which reweights OTU abundances by the inverse of phylogenetically-inferred, lineage-specific GCN estimates from the Greengenes database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input table already contains percentages or altered taxonomic strings — CopyRighter requires raw read counts and unaltered assignments The community was profiled with a taxonomy other than Greengenes (e.g. Silva) — GCN estimates are currently only distributed for the Greengenes database The bias of interest is GC percent, genome length beyond metagenomic trait data, or fungal ITS variation — these corrections are only hypothetical pending appropriate pre-computed estimates

skills.description: Use when Greengenes OTUs or taxa lack sequenced genomes (hence no measured 16S rRNA copy number) and a phylogenetically-based GCN estimate is needed for CopyRighter correction.
skills.name: phylogenetic-independent-contrasts-ancestral-state-estimation
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-independent-contrasts-ancestral-state-estimation Use when Greengenes OTUs or taxa lack sequenced genomes (hence no measured 16S rRNA copy number) and a phylogenetically-based GCN estimate is needed for CopyRighter correction. The taxon of interest already has a fully sequenced genome with a measured 16S rRNA copy number — use the measured value directly rather than the PIC estimate Your amplicon profiles use a non-Greengenes taxonomy (e.g. Silva), since CopyRighter's pre-computed estimates cover only the Oct 2012 Greengenes taxonomy You need corrections other than 16S rRNA copy number (e.g. GC percent or genome length bias) without appropriate pre-computed trait estimates http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3302 A CopyRighter preprocessing method that infers 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) for unsequenced Greengenes taxa by mapping measured GCN of curated genomes onto a 99%-identity OTU tree and propagating estimates to internal nodes and unsequenced leaves via phylogenetically independent contrasts (PIC) with rerooting. This fills the GCN gap that otherwise blocks lineage-specific correction of amplicon and qPCR profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: A CopyRighter preprocessing method that infers 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) for unsequenced Greengenes taxa by mapping measured GCN of curated genomes onto a 99%-identity OTU tree and propagating estimates to internal nodes and unsequenced leaves via phylogenetically independent contrasts (PIC) with rerooting. This fills the GCN gap that otherwise blocks lineage-specific correction of amplicon and qPCR profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The taxon of interest already has a fully sequenced genome with a measured 16S rRNA copy number — use the measured value directly rather than the PIC estimate Your amplicon profiles use a non-Greengenes taxonomy (e.g. Silva), since CopyRighter's pre-computed estimates cover only the Oct 2012 Greengenes taxonomy You need corrections other than 16S rRNA copy number (e.g. GC percent or genome length bias) without appropriate pre-computed trait estimates

skills.description: Use when assessing whether DIAMOND's tantan masking suppresses alignments during Patchwork marker retrieval — especially for read-based query data — by A/B comparing --masking 0 against the default masking configuration.
skills.name: phylogenetic-marker-benchmarking
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-marker-benchmarking Use when assessing whether DIAMOND's tantan masking suppresses alignments during Patchwork marker retrieval — especially for read-based query data — by A/B comparing --masking 0 against the default masking configuration. The goal is marker retrieval itself rather than comparing DIAMOND masking settings — a single default Patchwork run suffices Query and reference are highly divergent (e.g., cross-species near-USCOs like the H. robusta references), where percent-identity drops may confound the masking comparison Input is already a concatenated alignment or feature table rather than WGS contigs/reads to be searched http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Benchmark a DIAMOND-based marker retrieval pipeline (Patchwork) by running paired configurations that differ only in the DIAMOND tantan masking setting (--masking 0 vs. default), then compare percent identity and query coverage of recovered markers against same-species USCO references. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Benchmark a DIAMOND-based marker retrieval pipeline (Patchwork) by running paired configurations that differ only in the DIAMOND tantan masking setting (--masking 0 vs. default), then compare percent identity and query coverage of recovered markers against same-species USCO references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is marker retrieval itself rather than comparing DIAMOND masking settings — a single default Patchwork run suffices Query and reference are highly divergent (e.g., cross-species near-USCOs like the H. robusta references), where percent-identity drops may confound the masking comparison Input is already a concatenated alignment or feature table rather than WGS contigs/reads to be searched

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether a quantitative trait estimated for OTUs or taxa (e.g., 16S rRNA GCN from CopyRighter's Greengenes data files) shows significant phylogenetic autocorrelation on a tree.
skills.name: phylogenetic-signal-estimation
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-signal-estimation Use when you need to test whether a quantitative trait estimated for OTUs or taxa (e.g., 16S rRNA GCN from CopyRighter's Greengenes data files) shows significant phylogenetic autocorrelation on a tree. The input is an amplicon profile to be corrected for GCN bias — use CopyRighter's copyrighter correction workflow instead; this skill only validates the phylogenetic signal underlying the GCN estimates The trait data are not anchored to Greengenes OTU IDs or Greengenes taxstrings, since CopyRighter only distributes GCN data files based on the Oct 2012 Greengenes taxonomy and other taxonomies (e.g. Silva) are not yet covered http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Quantifies the strength of phylogenetic signal (Pagel's lambda) in empirically determined 16S rRNA gene copy numbers (GCN) mapped onto the Greengenes phylogenetic tree and taxonomic tree, establishing that GCN can be reliably inferred from phylogeny. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Quantifies the strength of phylogenetic signal (Pagel's lambda) in empirically determined 16S rRNA gene copy numbers (GCN) mapped onto the Greengenes phylogenetic tree and taxonomic tree, establishing that GCN can be reliably inferred from phylogeny.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an amplicon profile to be corrected for GCN bias — use CopyRighter's copyrighter correction workflow instead; this skill only validates the phylogenetic signal underlying the GCN estimates The trait data are not anchored to Greengenes OTU IDs or Greengenes taxstrings, since CopyRighter only distributes GCN data files based on the Oct 2012 Greengenes taxonomy and other taxonomies (e.g. Silva) are not yet covered

skills.description: Use when starting a PM-CNN analysis from an OTU/species feature table whose representative nucleotide sequences are available (e.g. from GreenGenes) and no phylogenetic tree in NEWICK format has yet been supplied.
skills.name: phylogenetic-tree-inference
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-tree-inference Use when starting a PM-CNN analysis from an OTU/species feature table whose representative nucleotide sequences are available (e.g. from GreenGenes) and no phylogenetic tree in NEWICK format has yet been supplied. A phylogenetic tree in NEWICK format is already available (the README marks this step as optional and supports user-supplied NEWICK trees, e.g. for shotgun data) Only a species/OTU abundance table exists and the representative sequences cannot be retrieved from a reference database such as GreenGenes The input sequences are not nucleotide sequences (the -nt option configures FastTree for nucleotides) http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Constructs a phylogenetic tree from representative OTU marker-gene sequences by multiple sequence alignment with Mafft (--auto) followed by tree inference with FastTree (-nt -gtr), producing the NEWICK-format tree consumed by PM-CNN's cophenetic-distance step. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae013
skills.summary: Constructs a phylogenetic tree from representative OTU marker-gene sequences by multiple sequence alignment with Mafft (--auto) followed by tree inference with FastTree (-nt -gtr), producing the NEWICK-format tree consumed by PM-CNN's cophenetic-distance step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A phylogenetic tree in NEWICK format is already available (the README marks this step as optional and supports user-supplied NEWICK trees, e.g. for shotgun data) Only a species/OTU abundance table exists and the representative sequences cannot be retrieved from a reference database such as GreenGenes The input sequences are not nucleotide sequences (the -nt option configures FastTree for nucleotides)

skills.description: Use when you have a FASTA of de-novo clustered OTU representative sequences (e.g. from micca otu) and need a Newick phylogenetic tree with one leaf per OTU for downstream diversity or ecology analyses.

skills.description: Use when a phylogenetic tree exists in NEWICK format (from FastTree/Mafft or user-provided) and a pairwise tip-to-tip distance matrix is needed to encode phylogenetic relationships between OTUs/species.

skills.description: Use when a population-genomics pipeline has produced IBS or FST distance matrices and TreeMix tree files, and you need interactive visual trees plus detection of populations that split across clades (polyphyly).

skills.search_text: phylogenetic-tree-rendering-and-polyphyletic-cluster-detection Use when a population-genomics pipeline has produced IBS or FST distance matrices and TreeMix tree files, and you need interactive visual trees plus detection of populations that split across clades (polyphyly). Input is raw VCF or PLINK binary data rather than processed distance-matrix/tree outputs of the scalepopgen pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Builds neighbor-joining trees from scalepopgen's '1-ibs' and pairwise-FST distance matrices plus TreeMix tree files, renders them as interactive HTML trees with Toytree/ete3, and flags polyphyletic population clusters so users can immediately assess genomic patterns after pipeline execution. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Builds neighbor-joining trees from scalepopgen's '1-ibs' and pairwise-FST distance matrices plus TreeMix tree files, renders them as interactive HTML trees with Toytree/ete3, and flags polyphyletic population clusters so users can immediately assess genomic patterns after pipeline execution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No distance matrices or TreeMix tree files exist yet — run the filtering/structure or phylogeny sub-workflows first to generate them. skills.description: Use when the input is compositional taxa/count abundance data (e.g., microbiome or diet-taxa tables) with a known phylogenetic tree, and the goal is to identify covariate-branch associations while respecting tree-like structure.
skills.name: phylogenetic-tree-structured-compositional-modeling
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-tree-structured-compositional-modeling Use when the input is compositional taxa/count abundance data (e.g., microbiome or diet-taxa tables) with a known phylogenetic tree, and the goal is to identify covariate-branch associations while respecting tree-like structure. skills.summary: Fit Dirichlet-tree multinomial (DTM) regression models with Bayesian variable selection to relate clinical covariates to phylogenetically structured compositional (e.g., microbiome) abundance data using the MicroBVS R package, selecting branch-by-covariate associations via MPPI thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is a fixed, non-compositional response (e.g., a binary phenotype or continuous outcome) rather than covariate-branch selection over compositional taxa data The user expects a deterministic penalized-regression selection rather than Bayesian posterior inclusion — the paper contrasts a penalized approach that identified 271 associations overall with the BVS method's 232 dietary factor-branch associations No MCMC budget or C++/Rcpp toolchain is available, since the core samplers operate in C++ via Rcpp wrappers and require burn-in and convergence checking

skills.description: Use when designing or simulating 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries and you must choose CF, CR, or fragment length (Mu_F) at a fixed total coverage C to maximize contig N50 of a Supernova2 diploid assembly.
skills.name: physical-coverage-parameter-optimization
skills.search_text: physical-coverage-parameter-optimization Use when designing or simulating 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries and you must choose CF, CR, or fragment length (Mu_F) at a fixed total coverage C to maximize contig N50 of a Supernova2 diploid assembly. You are using an assembler other than Supernova2 — the fragment-length and CF effects are implementation-specific ('until there is another assembler that can be compared to Supernova2 it will not be possible to reason about this effect'). Total coverage C is not held constant across the libraries being compared — varying CF and C simultaneously confounds the physical-coverage effect the skill isolates. The technology is not barcode-based linked reads (e.g. PacBio/ONT long reads); the CF/CR decomposition is specific to 10x Chromium-style partitioned libraries. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Optimizes 10x Linked-Read library parameters — especially physical coverage of long DNA fragments (CF) versus short-read coverage per fragment (CR) at constant total coverage C = CR × CF — to maximize de novo diploid assembly contiguity. The article found contig contiguity decreases as CF rises, with an optimal CF window of 332×–823× and degradation above 1,000× at the recommended C = 56×. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Optimizes 10x Linked-Read library parameters — especially physical coverage of long DNA fragments (CF) versus short-read coverage per fragment (CR) at constant total coverage C = CR × CF — to maximize de novo diploid assembly contiguity. The article found contig contiguity decreases as CF rises, with an optimal CF window of 332×–823× and degradation above 1,000× at the recommended C = 56×.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are using an assembler other than Supernova2 — the fragment-length and CF effects are implementation-specific ('until there is another assembler that can be compared to Supernova2 it will not be possible to reason about this effect'). The technology is not barcode-based linked reads (e.g. PacBio/ONT long reads); the CF/CR decomposition is specific to 10x Chromium-style partitioned libraries.

skills.summary: Benchmark plasmid assemblers (Plassembler-Flye, Plassembler-Raven, Unicycler) against a Trycycler-derived manually curated ground truth on Nanopore/Illumina read sets, scoring assemblies with QUAST (genome fraction, indels/mismatches per 100 kbp) plus counts of missed, additional, fragmented, and misassembled plasmids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no independently curated ground truth (e.g. Trycycler-derived plasmid sequences) is available, so QUAST accuracy and missed-plasmid counts cannot be computed When the sample is heterogeneous or too difficult for ground-truth assembly — e.g. barcode08 Serratia marcescens was excluded from this benchmarking because Trycycler assembly was unreliable When the goal is whole-chromosome (not plasmid) assembly quality assessment, since this pipeline scores only plasmid recovery against plasmid ground truth

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify and compare plasmid content across metagenomic/plasmidome assemblies by computing plasmid:chromosome contig ratios from kmer-signature-based classifiers such as PlasFlow and cBar.
skills.name: plasmid-chromosome-ratio-calculation
skills.search_text: plasmid-chromosome-ratio-calculation Use when you need to quantify and compare plasmid content across metagenomic/plasmidome assemblies by computing plasmid:chromosome contig ratios from kmer-signature-based classifiers such as PlasFlow and cBar. Input contains large numbers of contigs shorter than 1000 bp and you cannot filter — kmer-based classification results on short sequences are unreliable You require recovery of circular plasmids from assembly graphs with paired reads — use PlasmidSpades or Recycler instead, which use the assembly graph rather than genomic signatures You need replicate/plasmid replicon typing of known plasmid families — PlasmidFinder is a replicon-identification web tool, not a contig-level plasmid/chromosome classifier Quantifies plasmid enrichment in metagenomic assemblies by classifying filtered contigs with PlasFlow (and optionally cBar) into plasmid, chromosome, and unclassified bins, then computing plasmid-to-chromosome contig ratios as a comparative metric across plasmidome datasets. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Quantifies plasmid enrichment in metagenomic assemblies by classifying filtered contigs with PlasFlow (and optionally cBar) into plasmid, chromosome, and unclassified bins, then computing plasmid-to-chromosome contig ratios as a comparative metric across plasmidome datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contains large numbers of contigs shorter than 1000 bp and you cannot filter — kmer-based classification results on short sequences are unreliable You require recovery of circular plasmids from assembly graphs with paired reads — use PlasmidSpades or Recycler instead, which use the assembly graph rather than genomic signatures You need replicate/plasmid replicon typing of known plasmid families — PlasmidFinder is a replicon-identification web tool, not a contig-level plasmid/chromosome classifier

skills.description: Use when you have metagenomic or bacterial genome assembly contigs (ideally >1000 bp) and need to label them as plasmid-derived versus chromosomal without prior knowledge of sample taxonomic composition.
skills.name: plasmid-contig-classification
skills.search_text: plasmid-contig-classification Use when you have metagenomic or bacterial genome assembly contigs (ideally >1000 bp) and need to label them as plasmid-derived versus chromosomal without prior knowledge of sample taxonomic composition. Input contains many contigs shorter than 1000 bp — results for short sequences are unreliable because k-mer coverage is insufficient; filter by length first The plasmids of interest require an assembly graph and paired reads (e.g., Recycler/PlasmidSpades-style recovery of circular contigs) rather than signature-based contig labeling You need replicon typing of known Enterobacteriaceae plasmids (PlasmidFinder use case) rather than sequence-origin classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Classify assembled metagenomic/isolate contigs as plasmid, chromosome, or unclassified using PlasFlow, a neural-network classifier trained on k-mer genome signatures of 9,565 RefSeq bacterial chromosomes and plasmids, with probability thresholding to exclude uncertain predictions. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Classify assembled metagenomic/isolate contigs as plasmid, chromosome, or unclassified using PlasFlow, a neural-network classifier trained on k-mer genome signatures of 9,565 RefSeq bacterial chromosomes and plasmids, with probability thresholding to exclude uncertain predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contains many contigs shorter than 1000 bp — results for short sequences are unreliable because k-mer coverage is insufficient; filter by length first The plasmids of interest require an assembly graph and paired reads (e.g., Recycler/PlasmidSpades-style recovery of circular contigs) rather than signature-based contig labeling You need replicon typing of known Enterobacteriaceae plasmids (PlasmidFinder use case) rather than sequence-origin classification

skills.description: Use when assembled plasmid contigs (e.g. Unicycler output FASTA) need to be matched against a known-plasmid reference database such as PLSDB to annotate novelty or similarity.
skills.name: plasmid-database-similarity-search
skills.search_text: plasmid-database-similarity-search Use when assembled plasmid contigs (e.g. Unicycler output FASTA) need to be matched against a known-plasmid reference database such as PLSDB to annotate novelty or similarity. When contigs need full gene-level functional annotation rather than database-level similarity (Mash gives MinHash distance, not gene content) When plasmid contigs have not yet been assembled/extracted (this skill operates on assembled FASTA contigs, not raw reads) When a chromosome-contig classification is needed — mash PLSDB matching is for plasmid similarity, not chromosomal read removal http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Screens assembled plasmid contigs against the PLSDB database using Mash MinHash distances, keeping the lowest-distance PLSDB hit per contig as the top match. Plassembler uses this to annotate whether each assembled plasmid resembles known plasmids. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Screens assembled plasmid contigs against the PLSDB database using Mash MinHash distances, keeping the lowest-distance PLSDB hit per contig as the top match. Plassembler uses this to annotate whether each assembled plasmid resembles known plasmids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When contigs need full gene-level functional annotation rather than database-level similarity (Mash gives MinHash distance, not gene content) When plasmid contigs have not yet been assembled/extracted (this skill operates on assembled FASTA contigs, not raw reads) When a chromosome-contig classification is needed — mash PLSDB matching is for plasmid similarity, not chromosomal read removal

skills.description: Use when evaluating or reproducing plasmid prediction performance on assembled bacterial contigs, e.g. recovering plasmid recall/precision on the 42 plasmid-rich genomes of Arredondo-Alonso et al. and comparing against cBar and Recycler baselines.
skills.name: plasmid-prediction-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: plasmid-prediction-benchmark-evaluation Use when evaluating or reproducing plasmid prediction performance on assembled bacterial contigs, e.g. recovering plasmid recall/precision on the 42 plasmid-rich genomes of Arredondo-Alonso et al. and comparing against cBar and Recycler baselines. Input is raw paired-end reads rather than assembled contigs — Recycler- or PlasmidSpades-style approaches requiring an assembly graph fit that case instead Contigs are shorter than 1000 bp: 'PlasFlow, similarly to other kmer-based methods, does not perform well on short sequences' The goal is identifying plasmid replicons by database similarity (PlasmidFinder) rather than signature-based whole-sequence classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark protocol for comparing plasmid-sequence prediction tools (PlasFlow, cBar, Recycler) on SPAdes-assembled bacterial genomes, computing plasmid recall and precision against GenBank reference plasmids using k-mer-signature neural-network classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for comparing plasmid-sequence prediction tools (PlasFlow, cBar, Recycler) on SPAdes-assembled bacterial genomes, computing plasmid recall and precision against GenBank reference plasmids using k-mer-signature neural-network classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw paired-end reads rather than assembled contigs — Recycler- or PlasmidSpades-style approaches requiring an assembly graph fit that case instead Contigs are shorter than 1000 bp: 'PlasFlow, similarly to other kmer-based methods, does not perform well on short sequences' The goal is identifying plasmid replicons by database similarity (PlasmidFinder) rather than signature-based whole-sequence classification

skills.description: Use when a bacterial hybrid-assembly workflow needs to remove chromosomal reads from FASTQ inputs to speed up plasmid assembly, retaining unmapped reads and reads on putative plasmid contigs.
skills.name: plasmid-read-extraction
skills.search_text: plasmid-read-extraction Use when a bacterial hybrid-assembly workflow needs to remove chromosomal reads from FASTQ inputs to speed up plasmid assembly, retaining unmapped reads and reads on putative plasmid contigs. Input is a long-read-only (kmer_mode) Plassembler run with no short-read set — the hybrid read-extraction design described here presumes both long- and short-read inputs The sample has no expected plasmids or the assembly consists of a single chromosomal contig — extraction would reduce to retaining unmapped reads only Reads are from eukaryotic or metagenomic samples, outside Plassembler's bacterial-isolate hybrid assembly scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs the Plassembler chromosomal-read-removal step: map long- and short-read sets to a Flye (or Raven) long-read-only assembly with minimap2, then use SAMtools to extract and combine reads mapping to non-chromosome (putative plasmid) contigs plus unmapped reads, so only chromosomal reads are removed before hybrid assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Reconstructs the Plassembler chromosomal-read-removal step: map long- and short-read sets to a Flye (or Raven) long-read-only assembly with minimap2, then use SAMtools to extract and combine reads mapping to non-chromosome (putative plasmid) contigs plus unmapped reads, so only chromosomal reads are removed before hybrid assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a long-read-only (kmer_mode) Plassembler run with no short-read set — the hybrid read-extraction design described here presumes both long- and short-read inputs The sample has no expected plasmids or the assembly consists of a single chromosomal contig — extraction would reduce to retaining unmapped reads only Reads are from eukaryotic or metagenomic samples, outside Plassembler's bacterial-isolate hybrid assembly scope

skills.description: Use when input genotype data are VCF or PLINK binary files that must be converted to PLINK BED format, chromosome IDs recoded to integers, and LD-pruned before PCA, ADMIXTURE, TreeMix, or selection-scan analyses.
skills.name: plink-binary-genotype-processing
skills.search_text: plink-binary-genotype-processing Use when input genotype data are VCF or PLINK binary files that must be converted to PLINK BED format, chromosome IDs recoded to integers, and LD-pruned before PCA, ADMIXTURE, TreeMix, or selection-scan analyses. Data are not biallelic SNPs — scalepopgen is built for biallelic SNP data in VCF or PLINK binary format, so multi-allelic variants or haplotypes fall outside its scope The analysis at hand requires unpruned SNP density (e.g. signature-of-selection statistics that need full SNP sets rather than the LD-pruned subset recommended before structure analyses) The input needs extensive sample/site filtering first — those belong to the separate 'filtering and basic statistics' sub-workflow, not this genotype-processing step http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Prepare biallelic SNP genotype data in PLINK binary (BED/BIM/FAM) format for downstream scalepopgen analyses, including VCF-to-BED conversion with plink, chromosome-ID recoding to integers, and LD pruning with user-defined PLINK2 parameters before structure analyses such as smartpca and ADMIXTURE. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Prepare biallelic SNP genotype data in PLINK binary (BED/BIM/FAM) format for downstream scalepopgen analyses, including VCF-to-BED conversion with plink, chromosome-ID recoding to integers, and LD pruning with user-defined PLINK2 parameters before structure analyses such as smartpca and ADMIXTURE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not biallelic SNPs — scalepopgen is built for biallelic SNP data in VCF or PLINK binary format, so multi-allelic variants or haplotypes fall outside its scope The analysis at hand requires unpruned SNP density (e.g. signature-of-selection statistics that need full SNP sets rather than the LD-pruned subset recommended before structure analyses) The input needs extensive sample/site filtering first — those belong to the separate 'filtering and basic statistics' sub-workflow, not this genotype-processing step

skills.description: Use when assembling strain-resolved haplotigs from pre-clustered metagenomic short reads (interleaved FASTQ per cluster), where co-occurring mutation patterns must be preserved per strain rather than collapsed into a consensus.
skills.name: ploidy-aware-haplotig-consensus-generation
skills.search_text: ploidy-aware-haplotig-consensus-generation Use when assembling strain-resolved haplotigs from pre-clustered metagenomic short reads (interleaved FASTQ per cluster), where co-occurring mutation patterns must be preserved per strain rather than collapsed into a consensus. Input reads have not been pre-partitioned into strain-aware clusters by the StrainXpress 'Clustering Reads' stage — overlap-graph assembly on unclustered high-complexity metagenome input is computationally infeasible The goal is maximum contig length (N50) rather than strain resolution — the paper notes MEGAHIT outperforms all methods in contig length, and short Illumina reads constrain haplotig length Input is third-generation long-read data with high error rates — the paper states these 'introduce a range of issues that still need to be resolved' http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Per-read-cluster local assembly stage of StrainXpress that reconstructs strain-aware contigs (haplotigs) using an overlap-graph-based (OLC) ploidy-aware strategy from HaploConduct, with read-to-read overlaps computed by minimap2 instead of FM-index seeding. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac543
skills.summary: Per-read-cluster local assembly stage of StrainXpress that reconstructs strain-aware contigs (haplotigs) using an overlap-graph-based (OLC) ploidy-aware strategy from HaploConduct, with read-to-read overlaps computed by minimap2 instead of FM-index seeding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not been pre-partitioned into strain-aware clusters by the StrainXpress 'Clustering Reads' stage — overlap-graph assembly on unclustered high-complexity metagenome input is computationally infeasible The goal is maximum contig length (N50) rather than strain resolution — the paper notes MEGAHIT outperforms all methods in contig length, and short Illumina reads constrain haplotig length Input is third-generation long-read data with high error rates — the paper states these 'introduce a range of issues that still need to be resolved'

skills.description: Use when you have per-mutation-site reference/alternate k-mer depths from a Mykrobe predictor JSON output (MTBC sample) and need to recompute or audit susceptible/minor/major genotype calls and drug resistance predictions.
skills.name: poisson-competing-model-genotyping
skills.search_text: poisson-competing-model-genotyping Use when you have per-mutation-site reference/alternate k-mer depths from a Mykrobe predictor JSON output (MTBC sample) and need to recompute or audit susceptible/minor/major genotype calls and drug resistance predictions. Input is a S. aureus sample where per-drug frequency thresholds exist and should be estimated from training data instead of using the single 10% M. tuberculosis threshold The sample is direct-from-sputum M. tuberculosis requiring a general mixture model beyond the major/minor clone formulation Mykrobe has already flagged the sample as non-tuberculous mycobacteria (removed for quality control) or a gene prediction failed, in which case predictions are 'failed' and calls cannot be recomputed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Classifies each resistance mutation site as susceptible, minor resistant, or major resistant by comparing Poisson k-mer depth likelihoods under three competing models and selecting the maximum a posteriori (MAP) genotype, then converting minor/major calls into resistance phenotypes at a 10% threshold. This reproduces the core genotyping logic of Mykrobe predictor (Bradley et al. 2015) for M. tuberculosis. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Classifies each resistance mutation site as susceptible, minor resistant, or major resistant by comparing Poisson k-mer depth likelihoods under three competing models and selecting the maximum a posteriori (MAP) genotype, then converting minor/major calls into resistance phenotypes at a 10% threshold. This reproduces the core genotyping logic of Mykrobe predictor (Bradley et al. 2015) for M. tuberculosis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a S. aureus sample where per-drug frequency thresholds exist and should be estimated from training data instead of using the single 10% M. tuberculosis threshold The sample is direct-from-sputum M. tuberculosis requiring a general mixture model beyond the major/minor clone formulation Mykrobe has already flagged the sample as non-tuberculous mycobacteria (removed for quality control) or a gene prediction failed, in which case predictions are 'failed' and calls cannot be recomputed

skills.description: Use when you have HashSeq's OneMismatchCluster.txt output (parents plus one-mismatch children from 16S rRNA amplicon data) and want to quantify the sequencing error rate or check whether child accumulation follows a Poisson process.
skills.name: poisson-error-model-fitting
skills.search_text: poisson-error-model-fitting Use when you have HashSeq's OneMismatchCluster.txt output (parents plus one-mismatch children from 16S rRNA amplicon data) and want to quantify the sequencing error rate or check whether child accumulation follows a Poisson process. The goal is de novo variant inference rather than error-rate characterization — HashSeq's own pipeline uses a normal distribution + LOESS (makeLoessPlot) for background error, and the paper notes a Poisson model failed to control one-mismatch child distributions due to overdispersion. Data come from long-read platforms such as PacBio, where the rarity of multiple-mismatch sequences underlying the one-mismatch child model may not hold. You need to model indel errors — HashSeq treats indel events as separate parent sequences and the Poisson substitution model covers only nucleotide differences. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fit a single-parameter Poisson model of the fraction of all possible one-mismatch children observed per parent sequence as a function of parent abundance, estimating the per-nucleotide error rate P (found to be ~10^-4 for Illumina MiSeq 16S data). This reproduces the HashSeq paper's Fig. 2 error-model characterization. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: Fit a single-parameter Poisson model of the fraction of all possible one-mismatch children observed per parent sequence as a function of parent abundance, estimating the per-nucleotide error rate P (found to be ~10^-4 for Illumina MiSeq 16S data). This reproduces the HashSeq paper's Fig. 2 error-model characterization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo variant inference rather than error-rate characterization — HashSeq's own pipeline uses a normal distribution + LOESS (makeLoessPlot) for background error, and the paper notes a Poisson model failed to control one-mismatch child distributions due to overdispersion. Data come from long-read platforms such as PacBio, where the rarity of multiple-mismatch sequences underlying the one-mismatch child model may not hold. You need to model indel errors — HashSeq treats indel events as separate parent sequences and the Poisson substitution model covers only nucleotide differences.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a Poisson error model with equal mean-variance assumption adequately controls one-mismatch child distributions in amplicon variant calling, or when reproducing the Fig. S1 anticonservativeness benchmark.
skills.name: poisson-one-sided-significance-testing
skills.search_text: poisson-one-sided-significance-testing Use when evaluating whether a Poisson error model with equal mean-variance assumption adequately controls one-mismatch child distributions in amplicon variant calling, or when reproducing the Fig. S1 anticonservativeness benchmark. When the goal is to call true variants in a production pipeline — the Poisson test is anticonservative (calls nearly all one-mismatch variants as true) and HashSeq instead uses a normal-distribution-plus-LOESS error model When the child count data show variance less than the mean (underdispersion), where alternate models like the negative binomial are undefined and a normal distribution is preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A diagnostic procedure from the HashSeq paper that runs one-sided poisson.test calls on one-mismatch children, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at 5%, to demonstrate that the Poisson model is anticonservative (rejecting the null for >83% of children) because of overdispersion. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00697-21
skills.summary: A diagnostic procedure from the HashSeq paper that runs one-sided poisson.test calls on one-mismatch children, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at 5%, to demonstrate that the Poisson model is anticonservative (rejecting the null for >83% of children) because of overdispersion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to call true variants in a production pipeline — the Poisson test is anticonservative (calls nearly all one-mismatch variants as true) and HashSeq instead uses a normal-distribution-plus-LOESS error model When the child count data show variance less than the mean (underdispersion), where alternate models like the negative binomial are undefined and a normal distribution is preferred

skills.description: Decision support for choosing the k-mer length k for a k-mer-detection model (e.g. baseLess composite networks) by computing expected false positive rates of salient k-mers occurring by chance in non-target sequences.
skills.name: poisson-probability-modeling
skills.search_text: poisson-probability-modeling Decision support for choosing the k-mer length k for a k-mer-detection model (e.g. baseLess composite networks) by computing expected false positive rates of salient k-mers occurring by chance in non-target sequences. Target sequences are so long that k-mers occur by chance with negligible Poisson probability — the simulation would not change the k choice. The salient k-mer set is already fixed (e.g. pre-generated 16S k-mer networks from `baseLess update_16s_db`) and no re-selection of k is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Analytical Poisson k-mer occurrence modeling used in the baseLess paper (Section 4.2) to predict the probability that non-target sequences spuriously contain salient k-mers of a target sequence, and to select the k-mer sizes (k=8, k=9) that minimize the false positive rate for library design. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017
skills.summary: Analytical Poisson k-mer occurrence modeling used in the baseLess paper (Section 4.2) to predict the probability that non-target sequences spuriously contain salient k-mers of a target sequence, and to select the k-mer sizes (k=8, k=9) that minimize the false positive rate for library design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target sequences are so long that k-mers occur by chance with negligible Poisson probability — the simulation would not change the k choice. The salient k-mer set is already fixed (e.g. pre-generated 16S k-mer networks from `baseLess update_16s_db`) and no re-selection of k is needed.

skills.description: Use when pairwise isolate genomes or metagenomic assemblies of the same species must be classified as same vs. different strain, especially when structural variation may be missed by SNP-only comparisons.
skills.name: popani-strain-delineation
skills.search_text: popani-strain-delineation Use when pairwise isolate genomes or metagenomic assemblies of the same species must be classified as same vs. different strain, especially when structural variation may be missed by SNP-only comparisons. When only a continuous measure of genomic difference is needed — the authors recommend avoiding same/different strain classifications in favor of continuous measures because thresholds are subjective and species-dependent When the target sequences are phages, plasmids, or other low-data contexts where SNP-based tools like inStrain underperform relative to SynTracker alone (SynTracker achieved a significantly higher AUC on phages and plasmids) When pairs have fewer than n available homologous regions — SynTracker excludes such pairs from downstream analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Delineate whether two conspecific genomes/metagenome assemblies represent the same strain by combining an SNP-based popANI metric (inStrain) with synteny-based APSS scores (SynTracker), so that strains enriched in point mutations versus structural changes are distinguishable. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Delineate whether two conspecific genomes/metagenome assemblies represent the same strain by combining an SNP-based popANI metric (inStrain) with synteny-based APSS scores (SynTracker), so that strains enriched in point mutations versus structural changes are distinguishable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a continuous measure of genomic difference is needed — the authors recommend avoiding same/different strain classifications in favor of continuous measures because thresholds are subjective and species-dependent When the target sequences are phages, plasmids, or other low-data contexts where SNP-based tools like inStrain underperform relative to SynTracker alone (SynTracker achieved a significantly higher AUC on phages and plasmids) When pairs have fewer than n available homologous regions — SynTracker excludes such pairs from downstream analysis

skills.description: Use when you have chromosome-split, tabix-indexed biallelic VCF files (or PLINK BED/BIM/FAM) plus a sample-to-population map and need QC filtering plus per-sample and per-window population statistics (MAF, Ho, He) before downstream population-genomic analyses.
skills.name: population-allele-frequency-summary-statistics
skills.search_text: population-allele-frequency-summary-statistics Use when you have chromosome-split, tabix-indexed biallelic VCF files (or PLINK BED/BIM/FAM) plus a sample-to-population map and need QC filtering plus per-sample and per-window population statistics (MAF, Ho, He) before downstream population-genomic analyses. The input is already a filtered PLINK binary dataset with per-population statistics computed — re-running sample filtering first would only remove additional samples The data are multiallelic variants, indels, or whole-genome haplotypes rather than biallelic SNP VCF/PLINK files, which the scalepopgen sub-workflows do not accept The goal is structural analyses (PCA, ADMIXTURE, TreeMix phylogeny, selection scans) rather than filtering and basic summary statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3056 Implements the 'filtering and basic statistics' sub-workflow of scalepopgen: sample- then site-filtering of biallelic SNP genotype data (VCF or PLINK BED) with PLINK v1.9, PLINK2, and Vcftools v0.1.16, followed by computation of individual- and population-level allele-frequency summary statistics such as MAF, observed and expected heterozygosity, and transition/transversion counts. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Implements the 'filtering and basic statistics' sub-workflow of scalepopgen: sample- then site-filtering of biallelic SNP genotype data (VCF or PLINK BED) with PLINK v1.9, PLINK2, and Vcftools v0.1.16, followed by computation of individual- and population-level allele-frequency summary statistics such as MAF, observed and expected heterozygosity, and transition/transversion counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a filtered PLINK binary dataset with per-population statistics computed — re-running sample filtering first would only remove additional samples The data are multiallelic variants, indels, or whole-genome haplotypes rather than biallelic SNP VCF/PLINK files, which the scalepopgen sub-workflows do not accept The goal is structural analyses (PCA, ADMIXTURE, TreeMix phylogeny, selection scans) rather than filtering and basic summary statistics

skills.description: Use when building the polymorphism/divergence inputs for McDonald–Kreitman analyses, i.e. when DAF spectra and divergence counts must be pre-calculated from PopFly FASTA alignments or PopHuman 1000GP Phase III VCFs.
skills.name: population-genomic-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: population-genomic-data-retrieval Use when building the polymorphism/divergence inputs for McDonald–Kreitman analyses, i.e. when DAF spectra and divergence counts must be pre-calculated from PopFly FASTA alignments or PopHuman 1000GP Phase III VCFs. The user already possesses pre-calculated SFS/divergence tables or plans to run iMKT on their own population genomic data rather than pre-loaded D. melanogaster/human genes The target organism is not D. melanogaster or human — the pipelines are specific to PopFly/DGN and PopHuman/1000GP Phase III data Only a standard MKT on user-supplied daf and divergence data frames is needed — the iMKT R package consumes those directly without any data retrieval http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3796 Retrieves the population variation, divergence, recombination, and mask data required to pre-calculate unfolded 0-fold/4-fold SFS and divergence tables for iMKT analyses of D. melanogaster (DGN/PopFly) and human (1000GP Phase III/PopHuman) protein-coding genes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkz372
skills.summary: Retrieves the population variation, divergence, recombination, and mask data required to pre-calculate unfolded 0-fold/4-fold SFS and divergence tables for iMKT analyses of D. melanogaster (DGN/PopFly) and human (1000GP Phase III/PopHuman) protein-coding genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The user already possesses pre-calculated SFS/divergence tables or plans to run iMKT on their own population genomic data rather than pre-loaded D. melanogaster/human genes The target organism is not D. melanogaster or human — the pipelines are specific to PopFly/DGN and PopHuman/1000GP Phase III data Only a standard MKT on user-supplied daf and divergence data frames is needed — the iMKT R package consumes those directly without any data retrieval

skills.description: Use when the goal is to produce per-gene polymorphism (DAF spectrum: Pi, P0) and divergence (mi, Di, m0, D0) count tables from FASTA alignments or VCF population data as input to MKT-based estimation of adaptive evolution (alpha).
skills.name: population-genomics-divergence-counting
skills.search_text: population-genomics-divergence-counting Use when the goal is to produce per-gene polymorphism (DAF spectrum: Pi, P0) and divergence (mi, Di, m0, D0) count tables from FASTA alignments or VCF population data as input to MKT-based estimation of adaptive evolution (alpha). skills.summary: Runs scalepopgen's 'phylogeny using treemix' sub-workflow: it converts filtered biallelic SNP VCF data to TreeMix input, infers population trees with TreeMix (v1.13) with optional bootstrapping and migration edges, selects the optimal number of migration edges with OptM (v0.1.6) via Δm (second-order rate of change in likelihood), collapses bootstrap replicates into consensus trees with PHYLIP CONSENSE (v3.697), and plots trees with TreeMix R scripts and ete3 (v3.1.3).

skills.summary: This skill constructs the searchable RiPP structure database by applying the post-translational modifications of each HMMer-detected modification enzyme to its precursor peptide(s), and analogously to shuffled decoy precursors for FDR estimation.
