skills.search_text: presence-absence-matrix-construction Use when you need to establish which ribosomal proteins (or other universal single-copy proteins) are present or absent across bacterial lineages from genome bins of mixed completeness, especially where sequence divergence defeats keyword-based gene calling. Genome bins that fail the quality cutoffs (≥75% single-copy genes with ≤1.125 copies and an assembled 16S rRNA gene) — apparent absences may reflect incomplete sampling Input is 16S amplicon data or assemblies without predicted ORFs — no protein inventory can be built Organisms outside the survey scope where the target protein is known to be variably present (e.g. ribosomal protein L30, often absent in symbionts) — absence is not lineage-diagnostic without the phylogenetic assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Builds a lineage-by-protein binary presence/absence matrix (e.g. rpL30, rpL9, rpL1, Der across CPR and TM6 lineages) by inventorying ribosomal proteins with HMMER hmmscan against Pfam HMM profiles and ggKbase keyword gene lists, so that divergent homologs missed by keyword annotation are still detected. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: Builds a lineage-by-protein binary presence/absence matrix (e.g. rpL30, rpL9, rpL1, Der across CPR and TM6 lineages) by inventorying ribosomal proteins with HMMER hmmscan against Pfam HMM profiles and ggKbase keyword gene lists, so that divergent homologs missed by keyword annotation are still detected.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genome bins that fail the quality cutoffs (≥75% single-copy genes with ≤1.125 copies and an assembled 16S rRNA gene) — apparent absences may reflect incomplete sampling Input is 16S amplicon data or assemblies without predicted ORFs — no protein inventory can be built Organisms outside the survey scope where the target protein is known to be variably present (e.g. ribosomal protein L30, often absent in symbionts) — absence is not lineage-diagnostic without the phylogenetic assignment

skills.description: Use when assigning taxonomy to metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) FASTA bins at strain-level resolution with k-mer/minimizer counting against the kMetaShot HDF5 reference, and when a reliability ratio (ass2ref) is needed to filter questionable strain/species calls.
skills.name: prevalence-based-taxon-assignment
skills.search_text: prevalence-based-taxon-assignment Use when assigning taxonomy to metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) FASTA bins at strain-level resolution with k-mer/minimizer counting against the kMetaShot HDF5 reference, and when a reliability ratio (ass2ref) is needed to filter questionable strain/species calls. The task requires marker-gene identification or sequence-alignment-based classification (e.g. GTDBtk or CAMITAX workflows) rather than alignment-free k-mer/minimizer counting. The target taxa are not represented in the prokaryotic (bacteria and archaea) RefSeq kMetaShot reference, e.g. eukaryotic or viral MAGs. Only raw reads need classification — kMetaShot works directly on MAG bins/binned contigs, not FASTQ reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 kMetaShot's mechanism for assigning a MAG taxonomy up to the strain level: after shredding the MAG into q-minimizers and querying the HDF5 storage matrix, taxonomy is resolved with a prevalence-based approach (most abundant genus, then species, then the strain maximizing the ass2ref ratio), with an optional ass2ref filter (range 0–1) to drop unreliable classifications. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: kMetaShot's mechanism for assigning a MAG taxonomy up to the strain level: after shredding the MAG into q-minimizers and querying the HDF5 storage matrix, taxonomy is resolved with a prevalence-based approach (most abundant genus, then species, then the strain maximizing the ass2ref ratio), with an optional ass2ref filter (range 0–1) to drop unreliable classifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires marker-gene identification or sequence-alignment-based classification (e.g. GTDBtk or CAMITAX workflows) rather than alignment-free k-mer/minimizer counting. The target taxa are not represented in the prokaryotic (bacteria and archaea) RefSeq kMetaShot reference, e.g. eukaryotic or viral MAGs. Only raw reads need classification — kMetaShot works directly on MAG bins/binned contigs, not FASTQ reads.

skills.description: Use when you have degenerate primer sequences (IUPAC ambiguity codes) from a primer-design tool like MetaFunPrimer or EcoFunPrimer and need nondegenerate variants to test 100% both-primer match coverage against reference gene sequences.
skills.name: primer-degeneracy-expansion
skills.search_text: primer-degeneracy-expansion Use when you have degenerate primer sequences (IUPAC ambiguity codes) from a primer-design tool like MetaFunPrimer or EcoFunPrimer and need nondegenerate variants to test 100% both-primer match coverage against reference gene sequences. Reference sequences contain ambiguous bases or sequencing errors, so a strict 100% both-primer match criterion would undercount real amplification The goal is thermodynamic primer quality assessment (Tm, hairpin, homodimer) rather than enumerating degenerate variants — use EcoFunPrimer's design parameters instead Primer pairs are already nondegenerate; expansion is a no-op and direct matching suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 Expand degenerate primer outputs (e.g., the 78 amoA-AOB primer pairs designed by MetaFunPrimer/EcoFunPrimer) into all constituent nondegenerate forward/reverse forms so that per-sequence primer matching can be scored exactly during in silico PCR coverage evaluation. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00201-21
skills.summary: Expand degenerate primer outputs (e.g., the 78 amoA-AOB primer pairs designed by MetaFunPrimer/EcoFunPrimer) into all constituent nondegenerate forward/reverse forms so that per-sequence primer matching can be scored exactly during in silico PCR coverage evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference sequences contain ambiguous bases or sequencing errors, so a strict 100% both-primer match criterion would undercount real amplification The goal is thermodynamic primer quality assessment (Tm, hairpin, homodimer) rather than enumerating degenerate variants — use EcoFunPrimer's design parameters instead Primer pairs are already nondegenerate; expansion is a no-op and direct matching suffices

skills.description: Use when you have curated 16S rRNA gene sequences (or a new primer pair) and need to estimate what fraction of a community or lineage amplicon surveys would fail to detect due to primer-binding-site mismatches.
skills.name: primer-mismatch-evasion-quantification
skills.search_text: primer-mismatch-evasion-quantification Use when you have curated 16S rRNA gene sequences (or a new primer pair) and need to estimate what fraction of a community or lineage amplicon surveys would fail to detect due to primer-binding-site mismatches. Input is a metagenomic read set or genome bins rather than curated full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences spanning the primer regions 16S sequences still contain self-splicing introns/insertions ≥10 bp, which would falsely inflate apparent primer mismatch The goal is mapping metatranscriptomic reads to 16S genes rather than predicting amplicon-survey detectability http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies the fraction of 16S rRNA gene sequences that would evade detection by the widely used 515F/806R amplicon-survey primers, by testing primer binding against curated, de-redundantized 16S sequences with Primer Prospector. Applied in Brown et al. (Nature, 2015) to show 50-100% of specific CPR phyla and ~20% of all bacteria in the study would be missed. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: Quantifies the fraction of 16S rRNA gene sequences that would evade detection by the widely used 515F/806R amplicon-survey primers, by testing primer binding against curated, de-redundantized 16S sequences with Primer Prospector. Applied in Brown et al. (Nature, 2015) to show 50-100% of specific CPR phyla and ~20% of all bacteria in the study would be missed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a metagenomic read set or genome bins rather than curated full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences spanning the primer regions 16S sequences still contain self-splicing introns/insertions ≥10 bp, which would falsely inflate apparent primer mismatch The goal is mapping metatranscriptomic reads to 16S genes rather than predicting amplicon-survey detectability

skills.description: Use when a designed primer set (e.g., 78 nondegenerate amoA-AOB pairs) must be pared down or evaluated: you need the minimal subset of primer pairs that captures maximum reference gene diversity, quantified as in silico PCR coverage.
skills.name: primer-set-coverage-curve-analysis
skills.search_text: primer-set-coverage-curve-analysis Use when a designed primer set (e.g., 78 nondegenerate amoA-AOB pairs) must be pared down or evaluated: you need the minimal subset of primer pairs that captures maximum reference gene diversity, quantified as in silico PCR coverage. When the goal is to design new primers from raw gene/metagenome input rather than evaluate coverage of an existing designed set — use MetaFunPrimer's design pipeline instead When primer–template matching tolerates mismatches (e.g., in silico PCR with relaxed 3'-end rules); this skill's coverage numbers are defined only by the 100% forward-and-reverse match criterion When genes are too diverse for a practical qPCR panel — the article notes MetaFunPrimer 'will likely design numerous primer pairs, which may require numerous runs, even on HT-qPCR platforms', so coverage curves for such targets may not identify a practical subset http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes the tradeoff between the number of designed primer pairs (k) and cumulative in silico gene coverage, following MetaFunPrimer's approach for the amoA-AOB case study where 78 nondegenerate primer pairs achieved 94% coverage (676/720 reference genes) versus 49% for previously published primers. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00201-21
skills.summary: Computes the tradeoff between the number of designed primer pairs (k) and cumulative in silico gene coverage, following MetaFunPrimer's approach for the amoA-AOB case study where 78 nondegenerate primer pairs achieved 94% coverage (676/720 reference genes) versus 49% for previously published primers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to design new primers from raw gene/metagenome input rather than evaluate coverage of an existing designed set — use MetaFunPrimer's design pipeline instead When primer–template matching tolerates mismatches (e.g., in silico PCR with relaxed 3'-end rules); this skill's coverage numbers are defined only by the 100% forward-and-reverse match criterion When genes are too diverse for a practical qPCR panel — the article notes MetaFunPrimer 'will likely design numerous primer pairs, which may require numerous runs, even on HT-qPCR platforms', so coverage curves for such targets may not identify a practical subset

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how many genes from a curated reference set a primer pair (new or published) would detect, or to compare coverage of designed vs published primers before committing to qPCR.
skills.name: primer-set-sensitivity-benchmarking
skills.search_text: primer-set-sensitivity-benchmarking Use when you need to quantify how many genes from a curated reference set a primer pair (new or published) would detect, or to compare coverage of designed vs published primers before committing to qPCR. When the goal is experimental wet-lab validation of primer sensitivity or qPCR quantification — the article notes that 'further experimental validation is required' beyond computational/in silico checks When input is a raw metagenome rather than a curated reference gene set — gene targets must first be identified and ranked via the MetaFunPrimer pipeline When primers have known mismatches and you need permissive amplification criteria — this benchmark requires a 100% match for both primers http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Benchmark the sensitivity of primer sets (e.g., newly designed vs previously published) by running in silico PCR against a curated reference gene set and comparing the fraction of target genes amplified. In the MetaFunPrimer case study, 78 designed amoA-AOB primer pairs were compared to published primers against 720 Fungene-derived amoA-AOB reference genes. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00201-21
skills.summary: Benchmark the sensitivity of primer sets (e.g., newly designed vs previously published) by running in silico PCR against a curated reference gene set and comparing the fraction of target genes amplified. In the MetaFunPrimer case study, 78 designed amoA-AOB primer pairs were compared to published primers against 720 Fungene-derived amoA-AOB reference genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is experimental wet-lab validation of primer sensitivity or qPCR quantification — the article notes that 'further experimental validation is required' beyond computational/in silico checks When input is a raw metagenome rather than a curated reference gene set — gene targets must first be identified and ranked via the MetaFunPrimer pipeline When primers have known mismatches and you need permissive amplification criteria — this benchmark requires a 100% match for both primers

skills.description: Use when running an OMARU phylogenetic or gene case-control association test and you must decide how many PCs to add as covariates on top of metadata (e.g. sex, age, BMI) to control hidden confounders.
skills.name: principal-component-confounder-adjustment
skills.search_text: principal-component-confounder-adjustment Use when running an OMARU phylogenetic or gene case-control association test and you must decide how many PCs to add as covariates on top of metadata (e.g. sex, age, BMI) to control hidden confounders. The sample list has not passed read QC, profiling QC, and abundance QC — association tests must use QCed3_sample_list.txt, not original_sample_list.txt You expect hidden confounders to be adjusted inside the case-control model itself — the article states this integration 'is not currently implemented in OMARU' and must instead be handled via explicit covariates Input is a single pre-specified model with no need to compare PC counts — then just run the fixed-covariate association test without the N_PCs sweep Selects the number of principal components (plus fixed covariates such as sex, age, and BMI) to include as covariates in OMARU case-control association tests, to suppress inflation of P-values from hidden confounding factors before multiple-testing correction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: Selects the number of principal components (plus fixed covariates such as sex, age, and BMI) to include as covariates in OMARU case-control association tests, to suppress inflation of P-values from hidden confounding factors before multiple-testing correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample list has not passed read QC, profiling QC, and abundance QC — association tests must use QCed3_sample_list.txt, not original_sample_list.txt You expect hidden confounders to be adjusted inside the case-control model itself — the article states this integration 'is not currently implemented in OMARU' and must instead be handled via explicit covariates Input is a single pre-specified model with no need to compare PC counts — then just run the fixed-covariate association test without the N_PCs sweep

skills.description: Use when implementing or reproducing supervised kmer-based family scoring/confidence scores that must penalize kmers shared between families and bound scores to (-1, 1), as in Snekmer's model/search scoring.
skills.name: probabilistic-confidence-score-implementation
skills.search_text: probabilistic-confidence-score-implementation Use when implementing or reproducing supervised kmer-based family scoring/confidence scores that must penalize kmers shared between families and bound scores to (-1, 1), as in Snekmer's model/search scoring. Inputs are raw protein sequences not yet recoded into AAR kmer vectors — the scoring module requires kmer count vectors, not FASTA input. The goal is unsupervised clustering (Snekmer's cluster mode) — this scoring is defined for supervised family classification only. A different scoring scheme is required, e.g., cosine-similarity-to-training-profile scores used in Snekmer's apply-mode snekmer_results.csv (Sequence, Prediction, Score, delta, Confidence). http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements Snekmer's supervised kmer scoring formulas: the family probability F_kmer = n_kmer/N, the modified family probability F'_kmer that penalizes kmers shared across families, and the overall score S_kmer combining F'_kmer with background kmer prevalence to produce confidence values in the open interval (-1, 1). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad005
skills.summary: Implements Snekmer's supervised kmer scoring formulas: the family probability F_kmer = n_kmer/N, the modified family probability F'_kmer that penalizes kmers shared across families, and the overall score S_kmer combining F'_kmer with background kmer prevalence to produce confidence values in the open interval (-1, 1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inputs are raw protein sequences not yet recoded into AAR kmer vectors — the scoring module requires kmer count vectors, not FASTA input. The goal is unsupervised clustering (Snekmer's cluster mode) — this scoring is defined for supervised family classification only. A different scoring scheme is required, e.g., cosine-similarity-to-training-profile scores used in Snekmer's apply-mode snekmer_results.csv (Sequence, Prediction, Score, delta, Confidence).

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic or genome assembly in fasta form must be partitioned into plasmid-derived vs chromosomal scaffolds based on kmer genome signatures, with unreliable low-confidence calls filtered out.
skills.name: probability-threshold-classification-of-scaffolds
skills.search_text: probability-threshold-classification-of-scaffolds Use when a metagenomic or genome assembly in fasta form must be partitioned into plasmid-derived vs chromosomal scaffolds based on kmer genome signatures, with unreliable low-confidence calls filtered out. Input consists of raw short reads rather than assembled contigs — PlasFlow requires an assembly because kmer signatures of short sequences are unreliable Sequences shorter than 1000 bp are the target — results for short sequences are explicitly unreliable in kmer-based methods like PlasFlow The goal is replicon reconstruction from paired reads and an assembly graph — tools like PlasmidSpades or Recycler are required for that, not signature-based classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Classify metagenomic assembly contigs/scaffolds as plasmid, chromosomal, or unclassified using PlasFlow's kmer-signature neural network, applying a 0.7 probability threshold to exclude uncertain predictions before binning sequences into fasta files. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Classify metagenomic assembly contigs/scaffolds as plasmid, chromosomal, or unclassified using PlasFlow's kmer-signature neural network, applying a 0.7 probability threshold to exclude uncertain predictions before binning sequences into fasta files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of raw short reads rather than assembled contigs — PlasFlow requires an assembly because kmer signatures of short sequences are unreliable Sequences shorter than 1000 bp are the target — results for short sequences are explicitly unreliable in kmer-based methods like PlasFlow The goal is replicon reconstruction from paired reads and an assembly graph — tools like PlasmidSpades or Recycler are required for that, not signature-based classification

skills.description: Use when classifying metagenomic contigs with PlasFlow and you need to control the accuracy/unclassified-fraction trade-off, or when reproducing the paper's reported accuracy at thresholds 0.7 (94.79%) and 0.8 (96.41%).
skills.name: probability-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: probability-threshold-filtering Use when classifying metagenomic contigs with PlasFlow and you need to control the accuracy/unclassified-fraction trade-off, or when reproducing the paper's reported accuracy at thresholds 0.7 (94.79%) and 0.8 (96.41%). Input contigs are shorter than 1000 bp, where k-mer-based probabilities are unreliable anyway (pre-filter them out instead) Complete recovery of every input sequence into a plasmid/chromosome bin is required and no unclassified output can be tolerated The task requires identifying plasmid replicons or using assembly graph/paired-read information (use PlasmidFinder, PlasmidSpades, or Recycler instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Applies a class-probability cutoff (default 0.7, tunable to 0.8) to PlasFlow's ensemble neural network predictions so that contigs whose maximum averaged probability falls below the threshold are labelled 'unclassified.unclassified', trading coverage for accuracy. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkx1321
skills.summary: Applies a class-probability cutoff (default 0.7, tunable to 0.8) to PlasFlow's ensemble neural network predictions so that contigs whose maximum averaged probability falls below the threshold are labelled 'unclassified.unclassified', trading coverage for accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contigs are shorter than 1000 bp, where k-mer-based probabilities are unreliable anyway (pre-filter them out instead) Complete recovery of every input sequence into a plasmid/chromosome bin is required and no unclassified output can be tolerated The task requires identifying plasmid replicons or using assembly graph/paired-read information (use PlasmidFinder, PlasmidSpades, or Recycler instead)

skills.description: Use when comparing hybrid-capture probe design methods on the same target genome set and you need a quantitative cross-reactivity/coverage metric, i.e., the mean number of distinct target genomes hit per probe.
skills.name: probe-cross-reactivity-efficiency-calculation
skills.search_text: probe-cross-reactivity-efficiency-calculation Use when comparing hybrid-capture probe design methods on the same target genome set and you need a quantitative cross-reactivity/coverage metric, i.e., the mean number of distinct target genomes hit per probe. The genome targets are unknown or unannotatable — HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to cluster sequences, so probes cannot be designed for such targets (only close relatives) You need empirical wet-lab enrichment performance rather than in silico cross-reactivity — the paper notes enrichment level is target-sequence dependent and will vary for each probe set produced The target set is a single organism with no diversity to capture — the efficiency metric (distinct genomes hit per probe) is uninformative Benchmark metric that captures probe-set cross-reactivity: map each designed probe set (HUBDesign, CATCH strict/permissive, naive tiling) back to the target genomes with BLASTn and compute the average number of distinct genomes each probe hits ('efficiency'). It quantifies how compactly and broadly a probe set covers diverse targets on a shared genome set. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: Benchmark metric that captures probe-set cross-reactivity: map each designed probe set (HUBDesign, CATCH strict/permissive, naive tiling) back to the target genomes with BLASTn and compute the average number of distinct genomes each probe hits ('efficiency'). It quantifies how compactly and broadly a probe set covers diverse targets on a shared genome set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The genome targets are unknown or unannotatable — HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to cluster sequences, so probes cannot be designed for such targets (only close relatives) You need empirical wet-lab enrichment performance rather than in silico cross-reactivity — the paper notes enrichment level is target-sequence dependent and will vary for each probe set produced The target set is a single organism with no diversity to capture — the efficiency metric (distinct genomes hit per probe) is uninformative

skills.description: Reference for reanalyzing a published HUBDesign probe set: when you have probe sequences plus the annotated source genomes (e.g. GenomeInfo.tab listing 56 RefSeq coronavirus genomes) and need per-genome probe counts, specificity fractions, or comparison to reported extremes.
skills.name: probe-genome-alignment-mapping
skills.search_text: probe-genome-alignment-mapping Reference for reanalyzing a published HUBDesign probe set: when you have probe sequences plus the annotated source genomes (e.g. GenomeInfo.tab listing 56 RefSeq coronavirus genomes) and need per-genome probe counts, specificity fractions, or comparison to reported extremes. You need to design a new probe set from genomes rather than audit an existing one — use the full HUBDesign pipeline (Clustering through Selection) instead The probe set lacks accompanying genome-to-taxon metadata, so BLASTn hits cannot be assigned to species/genus Goal is experimental capture enrichment analysis (read deduplication, qPCR-amplicon removal) rather than in silico probe-to-genome mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns a deposited HUBDesign probe FASTA back to its source annotated genomes with BLASTn (2.9.1+ defaults) to quantify per-genome (or per-species/per-genus) probe density and each probe's taxonomic specificity (single-virus vs multi-virus hits). It validates that the published probe set behaves as described before it is reused for new capture experiments. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: Aligns a deposited HUBDesign probe FASTA back to its source annotated genomes with BLASTn (2.9.1+ defaults) to quantify per-genome (or per-species/per-genus) probe density and each probe's taxonomic specificity (single-virus vs multi-virus hits). It validates that the published probe set behaves as described before it is reused for new capture experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to design a new probe set from genomes rather than audit an existing one — use the full HUBDesign pipeline (Clustering through Selection) instead The probe set lacks accompanying genome-to-taxon metadata, so BLASTn hits cannot be assigned to species/genus Goal is experimental capture enrichment analysis (read deduplication, qPCR-amplicon removal) rather than in silico probe-to-genome mapping

skills.description: Use when comparing probe-design pipelines or hybridization parameter sets on a fixed multi-genome target set and you need a quantitative metric (probes per set, average distinct genomes hit per probe) to judge compactness vs coverage trade-offs.
skills.name: probe-hybridization-parameter-benchmarking
skills.search_text: probe-hybridization-parameter-benchmarking Use when comparing probe-design pipelines or hybridization parameter sets on a fixed multi-genome target set and you need a quantitative metric (probes per set, average distinct genomes hit per probe) to judge compactness vs coverage trade-offs. You only have a single genome or a set of nearly identical strains — hybridization-parameter benchmarking across diverse genomes is not informative there. Targets have unknown or unannotatable genomes — HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to cluster sequences, so annotated-genome-dependent designs (including its efficiency comparison) cannot be produced. You need experimentally validated capture performance (fold enrichment) rather than in silico probe-set comparison — this skill only benchmarks computational probe sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark hybridization-based probe design (CATCH strict/permissive, HUBDesign) against naive tiling on the same 56 RefSeq coronavirus genomes, using probe-set size and 'efficiency' (average number of distinct genomes each probe maps to) as comparison metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: Benchmark hybridization-based probe design (CATCH strict/permissive, HUBDesign) against naive tiling on the same 56 RefSeq coronavirus genomes, using probe-set size and 'efficiency' (average number of distinct genomes each probe maps to) as comparison metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single genome or a set of nearly identical strains — hybridization-parameter benchmarking across diverse genomes is not informative there. Targets have unknown or unannotatable genomes — HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to cluster sequences, so annotated-genome-dependent designs (including its efficiency comparison) cannot be produced. You need experimentally validated capture performance (fold enrichment) rather than in silico probe-set comparison — this skill only benchmarks computational probe sets.

skills.description: Use when raw unassembled Illumina FASTQ reads must be screened for cas genes (or any specialty protein family) so matched reads can seed targeted assembly instead of whole-genome assembly.
skills.name: profile-hmm-protein-search-for-seed-generation
skills.search_text: profile-hmm-protein-search-for-seed-generation Use when raw unassembled Illumina FASTQ reads must be screened for cas genes (or any specialty protein family) so matched reads can seed targeted assembly instead of whole-genome assembly. Input is already assembled contigs or a genome rather than raw short reads — the HMM seed search on reads is designed to bypass complete assembly The target gene family has no profile HMM or reference sequence available and none can be constructed — seed generation relies on HMM profiles or CRISPR repeat references Long-read or non-Illumina data, since CasCollect targets short DNA sequencing reads from Illumina sequencing http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Identifies short DNA sequencing reads matching cas protein HMM profiles with HMMER to generate 'seed' reads that prime CasCollect's targeted assembly of CRISPR/Cas loci, avoiding complete genome/metagenome assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Identifies short DNA sequencing reads matching cas protein HMM profiles with HMMER to generate 'seed' reads that prime CasCollect's targeted assembly of CRISPR/Cas loci, avoiding complete genome/metagenome assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled contigs or a genome rather than raw short reads — the HMM seed search on reads is designed to bypass complete assembly The target gene family has no profile HMM or reference sequence available and none can be constructed — seed generation relies on HMM profiles or CRISPR repeat references Long-read or non-Illumina data, since CasCollect targets short DNA sequencing reads from Illumina sequencing

skills.description: Use when a microbiome feature table has a binary grouping factor and you need to assess the robustness/overall association of differential abundance discoveries by progressively permuting group labels and tracking significant-feature counts across mixing levels.
skills.name: progressive-permutation-label-exchange
skills.search_text: progressive-permutation-label-exchange Use when a microbiome feature table has a binary grouping factor and you need to assess the robustness/overall association of differential abundance discoveries by progressively permuting group labels and tracking significant-feature counts across mixing levels. The task requires formal inference, FDR-controlled or adjusted p-values — the article states the method 'does not come with a formal inference method' and does not control the false discovery rate The goal is comparing grouping factors via ordination/PERMANOVA rather than robustness of individual differential features (e.g., PCoA/NMDS or PERMANOVA analysis) The grouping factor is not a binary outcome that bin_permute_all can progressively permute http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Applies the ProgPermute progressive permutation method: it progressively exchanges grouping-factor labels between groups and repeats differential abundance testing (default Wilcoxon rank sum test, alpha=0.05) at each mixing level, producing a characteristic U-curve of significant-feature counts versus proportion of mixing whose shape conveys the strength of the overall microbiome-group association. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04061-3
skills.summary: Applies the ProgPermute progressive permutation method: it progressively exchanges grouping-factor labels between groups and repeats differential abundance testing (default Wilcoxon rank sum test, alpha=0.05) at each mixing level, producing a characteristic U-curve of significant-feature counts versus proportion of mixing whose shape conveys the strength of the overall microbiome-group association.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires formal inference, FDR-controlled or adjusted p-values — the article states the method 'does not come with a formal inference method' and does not control the false discovery rate The goal is comparing grouping factors via ordination/PERMANOVA rather than robustness of individual differential features (e.g., PCoA/NMDS or PERMANOVA analysis) The grouping factor is not a binary outcome that bin_permute_all can progressively permute

skills.description: Use when you have a feature-by-sample microbiome count table with a binary grouping factor and need to assess whether top differential features are robust to label permutation, or to rank them by fragility index.
skills.name: progressive-permutation-signal-analysis
skills.search_text: progressive-permutation-signal-analysis Use when you have a feature-by-sample microbiome count table with a binary grouping factor and need to assess whether top differential features are robust to label permutation, or to rank them by fragility index. You want to train new models rather than run inference — use the training path (multitask.py, 2–3 days on an NVIDIA TITAN GTX GPU) instead Your goal is precision-matrix-based ECA comparison (e.g. CCMpred/PSICOV timings or baselines) rather than DNN-based end-to-end prediction Proteins exceed 700 residues or are shorter than 25 residues, which the paper's data preparation explicitly excludes http://edamontology.org/topic_0082 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Run the DeepECA pre-trained multitask DNN to predict residue-residue contacts and secondary structures directly from a protein's MSA, producing contact probability maps in ./contact_pred and ./ss_pred without retraining. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3190-x
skills.summary: Run the DeepECA pre-trained multitask DNN to predict residue-residue contacts and secondary structures directly from a protein's MSA, producing contact probability maps in ./contact_pred and ./ss_pred without retraining.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to train new models rather than run inference — use the training path (multitask.py, 2–3 days on an NVIDIA TITAN GTX GPU) instead Your goal is precision-matrix-based ECA comparison (e.g. CCMpred/PSICOV timings or baselines) rather than DNN-based end-to-end prediction Proteins exceed 700 residues or are shorter than 25 residues, which the paper's data preparation explicitly excludes

skills.description: Use when multiple DNN contact-prediction models trained on cross-validation splits of the same data (e.g. DeepECA multitask models) are available and the goal is to boost per-target contact accuracy by combining their probability outputs.
skills.name: protein-contact-probability-ensemble-averaging
skills.search_text: protein-contact-probability-ensemble-averaging Use when multiple DNN contact-prediction models trained on cross-validation splits of the same data (e.g. DeepECA multitask models) are available and the goal is to boost per-target contact accuracy by combining their probability outputs. Only a single trained model is available and no cross-validation splits exist to average over The goal is comparing predictor architectures rather than squeezing accuracy out of one model family — meta-predictor comparisons (e.g. vs RaptorX-Contact) need different tooling Predictions are hard classifications or ranked lists rather than raw probabilities — simple averaging requires probability outputs http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Averages per-residue-pair contact probabilities from multiple DeepECA models trained on different cross-validation splits (up to 10-fold) to raise contact prediction accuracy over any single model. The number of folds has only a small effect, with the 10-fold ensemble being highest in almost all prediction categories. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3190-x
skills.summary: Averages per-residue-pair contact probabilities from multiple DeepECA models trained on different cross-validation splits (up to 10-fold) to raise contact prediction accuracy over any single model. The number of folds has only a small effect, with the 10-fold ensemble being highest in almost all prediction categories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single trained model is available and no cross-validation splits exist to average over The goal is comparing predictor architectures rather than squeezing accuracy out of one model family — meta-predictor comparisons (e.g. vs RaptorX-Contact) need different tooling Predictions are hard classifications or ranked lists rather than raw probabilities — simple averaging requires probability outputs

skills.description: Use when calibrating a minimum match length or score cutoff for a protein-level metagenomic classifier: simulate/spurious match length distributions on a composition-preserving shuffled database to pick a threshold excluding random matches.
skills.name: protein-database-shuffling-null-model
skills.search_text: protein-database-shuffling-null-model Use when calibrating a minimum match length or score cutoff for a protein-level metagenomic classifier: simulate/spurious match length distributions on a composition-preserving shuffled database to pick a threshold excluding random matches. When calibrating nucleotide-level k-mer classifiers such as Kraken (k=31) or Clark — this null model addresses protein-level MEM match lengths, not nucleotide k-mer thresholds When the reads originate from non-protein-coding genomic regions, since protein-level classification cannot classify them regardless of cutoff When a pre-built or custom database is already the target and no cutoff calibration is needed — use kaiju-makedb directly instead of a shuffled null model http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Builds a null model of spurious protein matches by shuffling the microbial subset of the NCBI nr protein database with uShuffle (window length 100 aa to preserve local amino acid composition), then comparing Kaiju MEM-mode match-length distributions against the shuffled vs. original index to justify a minimum match length cutoff (m=11). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Builds a null model of spurious protein matches by shuffling the microbial subset of the NCBI nr protein database with uShuffle (window length 100 aa to preserve local amino acid composition), then comparing Kaiju MEM-mode match-length distributions against the shuffled vs. original index to justify a minimum match length cutoff (m=11).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When calibrating nucleotide-level k-mer classifiers such as Kraken (k=31) or Clark — this null model addresses protein-level MEM match lengths, not nucleotide k-mer thresholds When the reads originate from non-protein-coding genomic regions, since protein-level classification cannot classify them regardless of cutoff When a pre-built or custom database is already the target and no cutoff calibration is needed — use kaiju-makedb directly instead of a shuffled null model

skills.search_text: protein-family-profile-generation Use when nucleotide (or protein) FASTA genomes must be converted into Pfam protein-family profiles as input for phenotype classification, e.g. Traitar phypat/phypat+PGL workflows. Genes are already predicted externally and only Pfam annotation is needed — use the 'from_genes' workflow instead of re-running Prodigal Pfam 27.0 models are unavailable and no download/network access exists — profiles cannot be built without the models The goal is direct trait prediction from assembled genes with consistent external GFFs rather than profile generation itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0176 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Generates binary presence/absence protein-family (Pfam) profile vectors for bacterial genomes by predicting ORFs with Prodigal and scanning proteins against Pfam 27.0 HMMs with HMMER hmmsearch, the feature representation Traitar uses for all 67-phenotype prediction. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00101-16

skills.description: Use when you need Pfam protein family presence/absence profiles for nucleotide or protein FASTAs (draft genomes, metagenome bins, SAGs) to feed phenotype prediction or comparative genotype-phenotype inference.
skills.name: protein-family-profiling-with-pfam-hmms
skills.search_text: protein-family-profiling-with-pfam-hmms Use when you need Pfam protein family presence/absence profiles for nucleotide or protein FASTAs (draft genomes, metagenome bins, SAGs) to feed phenotype prediction or comparative genotype-phenotype inference. The input is already a Pfam domain table or other feature matrix — proceed directly to phenotype classification rather than re-scanning. You need trait predictions integrating transcriptomic or other omics evidence: Traitar currently uses only presence/absence of protein families. The claim rests on complete absence of a trait in a highly incomplete draft genome (e.g. 60%-complete unFirm_1): absent predictions may simply reflect missing protein families in the input genome. http://edamontology.org/topic_0176 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Annotate bacterial genomes with Pfam 27.0 protein family profiles by running Prodigal gene calling followed by HMMER hmmsearch, as implemented inside the Traitar phenotype workflow. This profile is the input representation from which Traitar's phypat and phypat+PGL classifiers assign 67 phenotypes. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00101-16
skills.summary: Annotate bacterial genomes with Pfam 27.0 protein family profiles by running Prodigal gene calling followed by HMMER hmmsearch, as implemented inside the Traitar phenotype workflow. This profile is the input representation from which Traitar's phypat and phypat+PGL classifiers assign 67 phenotypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a Pfam domain table or other feature matrix — proceed directly to phenotype classification rather than re-scanning. skills.description: Use when candidate IS nucleotide sequences (FASTA) need protein family annotation — e.g. to decide whether an IS encodes a transposase via InterPro (IPR) / PANTHER (PTHR) accessions before reporting it.
skills.name: protein-family-signature-annotation
skills.search_text: protein-family-signature-annotation Use when candidate IS nucleotide sequences (FASTA) need protein family annotation — e.g. to decide whether an IS encodes a transposase via InterPro (IPR) / PANTHER (PTHR) accessions before reporting it. The insertion sequences lack inverted terminal repeats — Palidis is currently only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs, so no candidates will reach this annotation step Candidate ISs have ITRs shorter than the default minimum of 25 nt (ITRs can be as short as ten nucleotides but are missed at default settings) The goal is annotation of non-transposase protein families — the filter retains only Transposase, Integrase-like and/or Ribonuclease H family descriptions http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Annotate predicted protein-coding ORFs from candidate insertion sequences with InterProScan to obtain InterPro and PANTHER protein family signatures, then filter candidates so only those encoding transposase-family proteins are retained as final Palidis IS records. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Annotate predicted protein-coding ORFs from candidate insertion sequences with InterProScan to obtain InterPro and PANTHER protein family signatures, then filter candidates so only those encoding transposase-family proteins are retained as final Palidis IS records.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The insertion sequences lack inverted terminal repeats — Palidis is currently only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs, so no candidates will reach this annotation step Candidate ISs have ITRs shorter than the default minimum of 25 nt (ITRs can be as short as ten nucleotides but are missed at default settings) The goal is annotation of non-transposase protein families — the filter retains only Transposase, Integrase-like and/or Ribonuclease H family descriptions

skills.description: Use when preparing the -v (viral) and -nv (nonviral) protein FASTA databases required as input to virMine.py, or when rebuilding virMine 2.0 reference databases after a COG or RefSeq release update.
skills.name: protein-fasta-file-formatting
skills.search_text: protein-fasta-file-formatting Use when preparing the -v (viral) and -nv (nonviral) protein FASTA databases required as input to virMine.py, or when rebuilding virMine 2.0 reference databases after a COG or RefSeq release update. The input is nucleotide (e.g. genomic FASTQ or contig) data rather than protein sequences — these databases must be amino-acid FASTA for BLAST-based contig scoring. The user only intends to run virMine on supplied long-read/contig assemblies with pre-existing viral and nonviral databases; rebuilding the databases is unnecessary. A de novo viral discovery context that deliberately avoids any reference database; this skill builds virMine-specific reference inputs, not a general reference preparation tool. http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Format virMine 2.0's reference protein databases: derive a nonviral bacterial database from the 2020 COG release (dropping category X viral/phage sequences) and a viral database from RefSeq viral/phage proteins, writing both as valid protein FASTA files consumed by virMine.py. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/mra.00107-22
skills.summary: Format virMine 2.0's reference protein databases: derive a nonviral bacterial database from the 2020 COG release (dropping category X viral/phage sequences) and a viral database from RefSeq viral/phage proteins, writing both as valid protein FASTA files consumed by virMine.py.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is nucleotide (e.g. genomic FASTQ or contig) data rather than protein sequences — these databases must be amino-acid FASTA for BLAST-based contig scoring. The user only intends to run virMine on supplied long-read/contig assemblies with pre-existing viral and nonviral databases; rebuilding the databases is unnecessary. A de novo viral discovery context that deliberately avoids any reference database; this skill builds virMine-specific reference inputs, not a general reference preparation tool.

skills.description: Use when nucleotide query sequences (SPAdes contigs or raw short reads) must be searched against protein reference sequences (e.g., 957 H. robusta near-USCOs) to recover homologous phylogenetic markers from fragmented genome-skimming data.
skills.name: protein-guided-nucleotide-alignment-execution
skills.search_text: protein-guided-nucleotide-alignment-execution Use when nucleotide query sequences (SPAdes contigs or raw short reads) must be searched against protein reference sequences (e.g., 957 H. robusta near-USCOs) to recover homologous phylogenetic markers from fragmented genome-skimming data. The references are not near-USCOs — the article recommends limiting reference sequences to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences The query is already a high-quality annotated protein set rather than fragmented nucleotide WGS data, so translated alignment adds no value Coding-region artifacts are expected in output — use PREQUAL to detect and remove artifactual noncoding stretches before trusting alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Executes translated nucleotide-to-protein similarity searches (DIAMOND BLASTX) so that DNA query contigs or reads from fragmented assemblies can be aligned against amino acid reference markers, as implemented in Patchwork for retrieving phylogenetic markers from WGS data. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Executes translated nucleotide-to-protein similarity searches (DIAMOND BLASTX) so that DNA query contigs or reads from fragmented assemblies can be aligned against amino acid reference markers, as implemented in Patchwork for retrieving phylogenetic markers from WGS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The references are not near-USCOs — the article recommends limiting reference sequences to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences The query is already a high-quality annotated protein set rather than fragmented nucleotide WGS data, so translated alignment adds no value Coding-region artifacts are expected in output — use PREQUAL to detect and remove artifactual noncoding stretches before trusting alignments

skills.description: Use when implementing or reproducing supervised kmer-based protein family scoring from reduced-alphabet (AAR) kmer count matrices, needing family-specific kmer weights that penalize kmers present in out-group families.
skills.name: protein-kmer-family-scoring
skills.search_text: protein-kmer-family-scoring Use when implementing or reproducing supervised kmer-based protein family scoring from reduced-alphabet (AAR) kmer count matrices, needing family-specific kmer weights that penalize kmers present in out-group families. Unsupervised clustering of sequences (Snekmer's 'cluster' mode) is the goal — no family labels exist to compute F_kmer against Input is already a trained supervised model or a scored results table (e.g. results/apply/snekmer_results.csv) — scoring has already been performed Sequences have not yet been recoded into AAR kmer vectors — run Snekmer's encoding/kmerization step first http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstructs Snekmer's supervised kmer scoring scheme: family probability F_kmer = n_kmer/N, a modified family probability F'_kmer that penalizes kmers shared with other families, and the overall score S_kmer combining F'_kmer with background kmer prevalence P_kmer to yield values strictly within (-1, 1). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad005
skills.summary: Reconstructs Snekmer's supervised kmer scoring scheme: family probability F_kmer = n_kmer/N, a modified family probability F'_kmer that penalizes kmers shared with other families, and the overall score S_kmer combining F'_kmer with background kmer prevalence P_kmer to yield values strictly within (-1, 1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Unsupervised clustering of sequences (Snekmer's 'cluster' mode) is the goal — no family labels exist to compute F_kmer against Input is already a trained supervised model or a scored results table (e.g. results/apply/snekmer_results.csv) — scoring has already been performed Sequences have not yet been recoded into AAR kmer vectors — run Snekmer's encoding/kmerization step first

skills.description: Use when clustering huge protein sequence sets (e.g. UniProt-sized FASTA) and you need a per-sequence subset of k-mers that still guarantees that homologous sequences share at least one exact k-mer match, without enumerating all k-mers.
skills.name: protein-kmer-hash-selection
skills.search_text: protein-kmer-hash-selection Use when clustering huge protein sequence sets (e.g. UniProt-sized FASTA) and you need a per-sequence subset of k-mers that still guarantees that homologous sequences share at least one exact k-mer match, without enumerating all k-mers. Input sequences are very short, so that m=20 lowest-hash k-mers cannot be extracted or k between 10 and 14 is not meaningful The clustering criterion requires gapped-alignable homology at low identity where sharing an exact reduced-alphabet k-mer match is too insensitive and full all-against-all search (e.g. MMseqs2 search) is needed The data are non-sequence items for which no shared-key function can be defined, since Linclust requires m keys per item satisfying shared-key conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 Selects a fixed number m of representative k-mers per protein sequence by keeping those with the lowest 16-bit rolling hash values, the core k-mer generation step (Step 1) of Linclust's linear-time clustering algorithm, implemented in MMseqs2. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-04964-5
skills.summary: Selects a fixed number m of representative k-mers per protein sequence by keeping those with the lowest 16-bit rolling hash values, the core k-mer generation step (Step 1) of Linclust's linear-time clustering algorithm, implemented in MMseqs2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are very short, so that m=20 lowest-hash k-mers cannot be extracted or k between 10 and 14 is not meaningful The clustering criterion requires gapped-alignable homology at low identity where sharing an exact reduced-alphabet k-mer match is too insensitive and full all-against-all search (e.g. MMseqs2 search) is needed The data are non-sequence items for which no shared-key function can be defined, since Linclust requires m keys per item satisfying shared-key conditions

skills.description: Use when starting from protein FASTA sequences that lack a supplied MSA and an MSA is required as input for DeepECA-style contact prediction, feature computation, or controlled noisy-MSA robustness tests.
skills.name: protein-msa-generation
skills.search_text: protein-msa-generation Use when starting from protein FASTA sequences that lack a supplied MSA and an MSA is required as input for DeepECA-style contact prediction, feature computation, or controlled noisy-MSA robustness tests. The DeepECA training/test datasets already ship with MSAs — download them from the Google Drive folder rather than regenerating them You need alignments with canonical DeepECA parameters for reproducibility but plan to use non-canonical E-value/coverage settings (those belong only to the explicit noisy-MSA robustness experiment) The downstream task does not consume an MSA at all (e.g. single-sequence structure prediction methods) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Generates multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) for protein domains with HHblits using DeepECA's canonical settings (three iterations, E-value 0.001, 60% coverage against UniProt20_2016), providing the core MSA input from which one-hot, PSSM, weighted-MSA entropy, and mutual-information features are computed for DNN-based contact prediction. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3190-x
skills.summary: Generates multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) for protein domains with HHblits using DeepECA's canonical settings (three iterations, E-value 0.001, 60% coverage against UniProt20_2016), providing the core MSA input from which one-hot, PSSM, weighted-MSA entropy, and mutual-information features are computed for DNN-based contact prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The DeepECA training/test datasets already ship with MSAs — download them from the Google Drive folder rather than regenerating them You need alignments with canonical DeepECA parameters for reproducibility but plan to use non-canonical E-value/coverage settings (those belong only to the explicit noisy-MSA robustness experiment) The downstream task does not consume an MSA at all (e.g. single-sequence structure prediction methods)

skills.description: Use when the goal is protein contact prediction from an MSA and MSA noise (e.g., metagenomic or noisy HHblits hits) may be degrading accuracy, and you want supervised, learned sequence weighting instead of fixed PSICOV-style weights.
skills.name: protein-msa-sequence-weighting
skills.search_text: protein-msa-sequence-weighting Use when the goal is protein contact prediction from an MSA and MSA noise (e.g., metagenomic or noisy HHblits hits) may be degrading accuracy, and you want supervised, learned sequence weighting instead of fixed PSICOV-style weights. When a high-quality, noise-free MSA is already available and a simpler unweighted baseline suffices — weighting helps most when MSA noise or shallow MSAs are a concern When a local execution of the comparison method is required and only a web server exists (e.g., RaptorX-Contact had no local execution file available) When the input is not an MSA (e.g., a covariance or precision matrix from another tool such as DeepCov or ResPRE is already the input feature) http://edamontology.org/topic_2814 Learn per-sequence weights of a deep multiple sequence alignment end-to-end inside a DNN (DeepECA's Weighted MSA Model) so noisy sequences are automatically down-weighted, boosting protein contact prediction accuracy over an unweighted baseline. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3190-x
skills.summary: Learn per-sequence weights of a deep multiple sequence alignment end-to-end inside a DNN (DeepECA's Weighted MSA Model) so noisy sequences are automatically down-weighted, boosting protein contact prediction accuracy over an unweighted baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a high-quality, noise-free MSA is already available and a simpler unweighted baseline suffices — weighting helps most when MSA noise or shallow MSAs are a concern When a local execution of the comparison method is required and only a web server exists (e.g., RaptorX-Contact had no local execution file available) When the input is not an MSA (e.g., a covariance or precision matrix from another tool such as DeepCov or ResPRE is already the input feature)

skills.description: Use when comparing protein sequence recovery of a protein-level assembler against nucleotide-level baselines on metagenomic reads, or when validating a manyfold recovery-improvement claim.
skills.name: protein-recovery-fold-change-analysis
skills.search_text: protein-recovery-fold-change-analysis Use when comparing protein sequence recovery of a protein-level assembler against nucleotide-level baselines on metagenomic reads, or when validating a manyfold recovery-improvement claim. The goal is nucleotide-level metrics such as complete viral genomes or 16S rRNA recovery — PenguiN, not Plass, is the tool that assembles 3-40 times more complete viral genomes and six times as many 16S rRNA sequences than Megahit and SPAdes variants. Input is a single-end read set where paired-end overlap information is unavailable and the paired-end assembly comparison design cannot be reproduced. The reads are not from a complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic sample; the 2-10x recovery claim was established on complex metagenomes and may not transfer. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmarks protein-level assembly (Plass) against nucleotide-level assemblers (Megahit, SPAdes) to quantify how many times more non-redundant protein sequences Plass recovers from complex metagenomes, the paper's central 2-10x recovery claim. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41592-019-0437-4
skills.summary: Benchmarks protein-level assembly (Plass) against nucleotide-level assemblers (Megahit, SPAdes) to quantify how many times more non-redundant protein sequences Plass recovers from complex metagenomes, the paper's central 2-10x recovery claim.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is nucleotide-level metrics such as complete viral genomes or 16S rRNA recovery — PenguiN, not Plass, is the tool that assembles 3-40 times more complete viral genomes and six times as many 16S rRNA sequences than Megahit and SPAdes variants. Input is a single-end read set where paired-end overlap information is unavailable and the paired-end assembly comparison design cannot be reproduced. The reads are not from a complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic sample; the 2-10x recovery claim was established on complex metagenomes and may not transfer.

Binning microbial (non-viral) genomes: vRhyme is not meant to bin microbes, and viruses lack universal single-copy marker genes so redundancy logic differs Datasets expected to contain many redundant genes (e.g., non-viral genomes), where the protein-redundancy assumption behind the scoring breaks down http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 vRhyme's mechanism for selecting the best genome bins by scoring candidate binning iterations on protein redundancy (via Mmseqs2 homology clustering), number of scaffolds binned, and bins generated, exploiting the observation that viruses seldom encode redundant genes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: vRhyme's mechanism for selecting the best genome bins by scoring candidate binning iterations on protein redundancy (via Mmseqs2 homology clustering), number of scaffolds binned, and bins generated, exploiting the observation that viruses seldom encode redundant genes.

skills.name: protein-redundancy-clustering
skills.search_text: protein-redundancy-clustering Use when constructing a reference protein database for functional annotation (e.g. DIAMOND/BLAST searches) from large multi-source FASTA sets where redundant near-identical sequences would inflate search space and ambiguity. Input is already a non-redundant or curated reference (e.g. UniProt/Swiss-Prot reviewed subset alone) where clustering would destroy deliberate redundancy-free curation Building a taxonomic marker-gene database, where the article instead uses a stricter 99% identity CD-HIT threshold on single-copy marker genes Sequences lack functional annotations and the goal is an annotated functional database — unannotated proteins must be discarded first (~1.5 million were in FunOMIC), leaving little to cluster http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Builds a non-redundant protein reference database by first discarding proteins lacking explicit functional annotation, then clustering the annotated set with CD-HIT at 95% identity. skills.description: Use when comparing the runtime scalability, speed, or sensitivity of protein sequence clustering tools on large FASTA sets, or when reproducing power-law runtime exponents and false-negative rates at fixed sequence-identity thresholds (e.g. 50% or 90%).
skills.name: protein-sequence-clustering-benchmarking
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-clustering-benchmarking Use when comparing the runtime scalability, speed, or sensitivity of protein sequence clustering tools on large FASTA sets, or when reproducing power-law runtime exponents and false-negative rates at fixed sequence-identity thresholds (e.g. 50% or 90%). The input is a small sequence set where any tool finishes in minutes — the linear-vs-quadratic scaling differences being benchmarked will not be measurable The goal is pairwise search or alignment speed comparison (e.g. BLAST vs MMseqs2 search) rather than full-set redundancy clustering Exact, verified clustering is mandatory and false positives are unacceptable without quadratic-time verification, since approximate k-mer prefiltering trades exactness for speed http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 A benchmarking method for protein sequence clustering tools (Linclust/MMseqs2, MMseqs, CD-HIT, UCLUST) that measures runtime scaling, speedup factors, and clustering quality (false-negative rates, cluster counts) on huge FASTA sequence sets such as UniProt 2016_03 (~123M sequences with reversed sequences) and Metaclust (1.59B metagenomic fragments). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-04964-5
skills.summary: A benchmarking method for protein sequence clustering tools (Linclust/MMseqs2, MMseqs, CD-HIT, UCLUST) that measures runtime scaling, speedup factors, and clustering quality (false-negative rates, cluster counts) on huge FASTA sequence sets such as UniProt 2016_03 (~123M sequences with reversed sequences) and Metaclust (1.59B metagenomic fragments).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a small sequence set where any tool finishes in minutes — the linear-vs-quadratic scaling differences being benchmarked will not be measurable The goal is pairwise search or alignment speed comparison (e.g. BLAST vs MMseqs2 search) rather than full-set redundancy clustering Exact, verified clustering is mandatory and false positives are unacceptable without quadratic-time verification, since approximate k-mer prefiltering trades exactness for speed

skills.description: Use when you already have a per-domain list of predicted residue-pair contacts and predicted secondary structures and need to fold them into 3D models whose quality is measured by TMscore.
skills.name: protein-tertiary-structure-reconstruction-from-contacts
skills.search_text: protein-tertiary-structure-reconstruction-from-contacts Use when you already have a per-domain list of predicted residue-pair contacts and predicted secondary structures and need to fold them into 3D models whose quality is measured by TMscore. The goal is contact or secondary-structure prediction itself — this skill starts from those predictions and folds structures, it does not produce the ./contact_pred and ./ss_pred inputs. Contact-map analysis or top-L accuracy benchmarking is the end goal — high contact accuracy does not guarantee model quality (e.g., T0845-D1 reached 86.6% contact accuracy but TMscore 0.276). No predicted secondary structures are available and CONFOLD must be run with contacts alone, deviating from the article's input protocol. Reconstructs protein tertiary structures from predicted residue contacts and secondary structures using the CONFOLD script, then quantifies model quality with TMscore against native CASP domain structures. It bridges contact-prediction output (e.g., from DeepECA's multitask model) to an assessable 3D model. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3190-x
skills.summary: Reconstructs protein tertiary structures from predicted residue contacts and secondary structures using the CONFOLD script, then quantifies model quality with TMscore against native CASP domain structures. It bridges contact-prediction output (e.g., from DeepECA's multitask model) to an assessable 3D model.

skills.description: Use when a clade of MAGs/SGBs (e.g. Saccharofermentanales SGB009, SGB034, SGB080) may lack a conserved set of universal single-copy orthologs and you need to identify which missing USCO genes map to a specific pathway such as de novo purine biosynthesis.
skills.name: purine-biosynthesis-gene-functional-annotation
skills.search_text: purine-biosynthesis-gene-functional-annotation Use when a clade of MAGs/SGBs (e.g. Saccharofermentanales SGB009, SGB034, SGB080) may lack a conserved set of universal single-copy orthologs and you need to identify which missing USCO genes map to a specific pathway such as de novo purine biosynthesis. Input genomes are already provided as a BUSCO full_table.tsv from a non-bacteria_odb10 lineage — the 124-USCO prokaryote set is lineage-specific and re-running with a different database will not reproduce the matrix The goal is de novo pathway reconstruction of a single genome rather than detecting clade-wide absence of universal single-copy orthologs across multiple genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Screens Saccharofermentanales (and other VMGC SGB) genomes for missing universal single-copy orthologs (USCOs) using BUSCO bacteria_odb10 (124 USCOs), then functionally annotates the universally absent USCOs via KEGG to flag those involved in de novo purine biosynthesis. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Screens Saccharofermentanales (and other VMGC SGB) genomes for missing universal single-copy orthologs (USCOs) using BUSCO bacteria_odb10 (124 USCOs), then functionally annotates the universally absent USCOs via KEGG to flag those involved in de novo purine biosynthesis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input genomes are already provided as a BUSCO full_table.tsv from a non-bacteria_odb10 lineage — the 124-USCO prokaryote set is lineage-specific and re-running with a different database will not reproduce the matrix The goal is de novo pathway reconstruction of a single genome rather than detecting clade-wide absence of universal single-copy orthologs across multiple genomes

skills.description: Use when case-control metagenomic association summary statistics (sumstats_*.txt) must be checked for P-value inflation and the correct number of PC covariates (e.g. N_PC_PHYL = 2) must be chosen before final reporting.
skills.name: pvalue-inflation-qq-plot-assessment
skills.search_text: pvalue-inflation-qq-plot-assessment Use when case-control metagenomic association summary statistics (sumstats_*.txt) must be checked for P-value inflation and the correct number of PC covariates (e.g. N_PC_PHYL = 2) must be chosen before final reporting. Input is raw FASTQ or pre-QC abundance data rather than association test summary statistics from Step 4-1 — QC and profiling steps (OMARU_read_QC.sm, OMARU_QCed1/2.sm) must run first. The goal is functional/gene-level (UniRef90/KEGG) association assessment rather than the phylogenetic (UHGG-based clade) association test — use the corresponding gene/permutation workflow instead. Hidden confounders need direct adjustment in the case-control model — the article notes covariate integration for hidden confounding factors is not currently implemented in OMARU; PCs only partially address this. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assess P-value inflation in OMARU phylogenetic association tests by comparing QQ and P-value distribution figures between covariate-adjusted (PC) and no-PC runs, and validate significance via the empirical Bonferroni threshold derived from 10,000 phenotype permutations. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: Assess P-value inflation in OMARU phylogenetic association tests by comparing QQ and P-value distribution figures between covariate-adjusted (PC) and no-PC runs, and validate significance via the empirical Bonferroni threshold derived from 10,000 phenotype permutations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or pre-QC abundance data rather than association test summary statistics from Step 4-1 — QC and profiling steps (OMARU_read_QC.sm, OMARU_QCed1/2.sm) must run first. The goal is functional/gene-level (UniRef90/KEGG) association assessment rather than the phylogenetic (UHGG-based clade) association test — use the corresponding gene/permutation workflow instead. Hidden confounders need direct adjustment in the case-control model — the article notes covariate integration for hidden confounding factors is not currently implemented in OMARU; PCs only partially address this.

skills.description: Use when you have FASTA/FASTQ reads already flagged as containing inverted terminal repeats (with LCoord/RCoord ITR positions from pal-MEM) and need to keep only those whose flanking genomic context maps to assemblies within the expected IS length range (e.g. 500-3000 bp).
skills.name: python-script-based-alignment-filtering
skills.search_text: python-script-based-alignment-filtering Use when you have FASTA/FASTQ reads already flagged as containing inverted terminal repeats (with LCoord/RCoord ITR positions from pal-MEM) and need to keep only those whose flanking genomic context maps to assemblies within the expected IS length range (e.g. 500-3000 bp). Input reads have not yet been screened for inverted repeats by pal-MEM (no LCoord/RCoord ITR coordinates available in read names) Target insertion sequences lack ITRs or have ITRs shorter than the tool's minimum (e.g. ITRs as short as ten nucleotides are missed at default settings) Regions whose ITRs are separated beyond the 500-3000 bp proximity range, e.g. lengthened by nested insertion events — these will be incorrectly filtered out http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Palidis Step 2-style proximity filter: map repeat-containing reads (output of pal-MEM) to their associated assemblies with Bowtie2, then apply a Python filter script that retains only mapped reads whose ITR repeat positions fall within the user-defined minimum-to-maximum insertion sequence (IS) length interval (default 500-3000 bp), producing candidate ITR reads for downstream clustering. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Palidis Step 2-style proximity filter: map repeat-containing reads (output of pal-MEM) to their associated assemblies with Bowtie2, then apply a Python filter script that retains only mapped reads whose ITR repeat positions fall within the user-defined minimum-to-maximum insertion sequence (IS) length interval (default 500-3000 bp), producing candidate ITR reads for downstream clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not yet been screened for inverted repeats by pal-MEM (no LCoord/RCoord ITR coordinates available in read names) Target insertion sequences lack ITRs or have ITRs shorter than the tool's minimum (e.g. ITRs as short as ten nucleotides are missed at default settings) Regions whose ITRs are separated beyond the 500-3000 bp proximity range, e.g. lengthened by nested insertion events — these will be incorrectly filtered out

skills.description: Use when a labeled microbial feature table (OTU/species abundance table plus sample metadata) must be classified with a phylogeny-aware deep learning model whose features are ordered by hierarchical clustering of phylogenetic distances.
skills.name: pytorch-model-training-and-testing
skills.search_text: pytorch-model-training-and-testing Use when a labeled microbial feature table (OTU/species abundance table plus sample metadata) must be classified with a phylogeny-aware deep learning model whose features are ordered by hierarchical clustering of phylogenetic distances. When the goal is unsupervised ordination or differential abundance testing rather than supervised status/disease classification from labeled samples When no phylogenetic tree or feature clustering order is available and phylogeny-informed feature adjacency cannot be constructed (the convolutional paths assume phylogenetically ordered features) When the input is raw sequence data rather than a microbial feature table (README requires an OTU/species abundance table as input) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and test PM-CNN, a phylogeny-ordered multi-path convolutional neural network with ensemble (fully-connected) feature fusion, on microbiome abundance tables to classify disease/status labels, evaluated with Kappa, Recall, Accuracy, Precision, and F1. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae013
skills.summary: Train and test PM-CNN, a phylogeny-ordered multi-path convolutional neural network with ensemble (fully-connected) feature fusion, on microbiome abundance tables to classify disease/status labels, evaluated with Kappa, Recall, Accuracy, Precision, and F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is unsupervised ordination or differential abundance testing rather than supervised status/disease classification from labeled samples When no phylogenetic tree or feature clustering order is available and phylogeny-informed feature adjacency cannot be constructed (the convolutional paths assume phylogenetically ordered features) When the input is raw sequence data rather than a microbial feature table (README requires an OTU/species abundance table as input)

skills.description: Use when a hybrid sequence classifier needs a from-scratch transformer pathway over BPE-tokenized DNA (512-token inputs) whose output is fused with CNN features, rather than fine-tuning a pre-trained language model.
skills.name: pytorch-transformer-encoder-implementation
skills.search_text: pytorch-transformer-encoder-implementation Use when a hybrid sequence classifier needs a from-scratch transformer pathway over BPE-tokenized DNA (512-token inputs) whose output is fused with CNN features, rather than fine-tuning a pre-trained language model. A pre-trained genome language model (e.g. full DNABERT-2 weights) is to be fine-tuned rather than used only for its BPE vocabulary Only local motif features are needed and the CNNClassifier variant suffices (faster training, slightly lower species accuracy) Input is short-read data without quality handling needs beyond FASTA — note the model does not incorporate base-level quality scores http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Constructs a transformer encoder from scratch in PyTorch/Hugging Face Transformers (4 layers, 7 heads, hidden size 896, FFN 3584, GELU) over the DNABERT-2 BPE vocabulary, as used in DeepTaxa's HybridCNNBERTClassifier for 16S rRNA taxonomic classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Constructs a transformer encoder from scratch in PyTorch/Hugging Face Transformers (4 layers, 7 heads, hidden size 896, FFN 3584, GELU) over the DNABERT-2 BPE vocabulary, as used in DeepTaxa's HybridCNNBERTClassifier for 16S rRNA taxonomic classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A pre-trained genome language model (e.g. full DNABERT-2 weights) is to be fine-tuned rather than used only for its BPE vocabulary Only local motif features are needed and the CNNClassifier variant suffices (faster training, slightly lower species accuracy) Input is short-read data without quality handling needs beyond FASTA — note the model does not incorporate base-level quality scores

skills.description: Use when ADMIXTURE runs over a range of K values have produced per-run Q-matrix and log files, and you need to select the K with the lowest cross-validation error and interactively visualize ancestry proportions per sample.
