skills.search_text: q-matrix-interactive-visualization Use when ADMIXTURE runs over a range of K values have produced per-run Q-matrix and log files, and you need to select the K with the lowest cross-validation error and interactively visualize ancestry proportions per sample. The goal is PCA rather than admixture proportions — use the smartpca (Eigensoft) branch of the sub-workflow instead of Q-matrix plotting. Input is raw VCF rather than a filtered, LD-pruned PLINK BED file — run the filtering and LD-pruning sub-workflow first. Data are not biallelic SNP genotypes in VCF or PLINK binary format, which is the only input scalepopgen accepts. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2885 Prepare ADMIXTURE Q-matrix output files and render them as interactive population-structure plots using PONG (with Poppins/pophelper-style plotting and Bokeh/Plotly scripts) within the scalepopgen explore-genetic-structure sub-workflow, so users can inspect ancestry proportions per individual at the optimal K. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Prepare ADMIXTURE Q-matrix output files and render them as interactive population-structure plots using PONG (with Poppins/pophelper-style plotting and Bokeh/Plotly scripts) within the scalepopgen explore-genetic-structure sub-workflow, so users can inspect ancestry proportions per individual at the optimal K.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is PCA rather than admixture proportions — use the smartpca (Eigensoft) branch of the sub-workflow instead of Q-matrix plotting. Input is raw VCF rather than a filtered, LD-pruned PLINK BED file — run the filtering and LD-pruning sub-workflow first. Data are not biallelic SNP genotypes in VCF or PLINK binary format, which is the only input scalepopgen accepts.

skills.description: Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads (no reference assembly yet) and need a reference-free metric of Hi-C ligation/library quality, such as the inter-contig 3D ratio.
skills.name: qc3c-kmer-mode-ligation-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: qc3c-kmer-mode-ligation-quality-assessment Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads (no reference assembly yet) and need a reference-free metric of Hi-C ligation/library quality, such as the inter-contig 3D ratio. You want Hi-C binning output (viral genomes or host pairs) rather than a library-quality metric — use the ViralCC pipeline instead. You already have aligned Hi-C BAM files mapped to assembled contigs; qc3C k-mer mode is reference-free and operates on cleaned FASTQ reads. Reads are raw and unprocessed — the 3D ratio should be computed on reads cleaned with the bbduk (trimq=10 qtrim=r ftm=5 minlen=50, ftl=10) and clumpify.sh steps first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Runs qc3C in reference-free k-mer mode on quality-cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads to compute the inter-contig (3D) ratio and its confidence-interval midpoint as a measure of Hi-C library ligation quality. In the ViralCC paper this quantifies library quality for the human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater metagenomic Hi-C datasets. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Runs qc3C in reference-free k-mer mode on quality-cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads to compute the inter-contig (3D) ratio and its confidence-interval midpoint as a measure of Hi-C library ligation quality. In the ViralCC paper this quantifies library quality for the human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater metagenomic Hi-C datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want Hi-C binning output (viral genomes or host pairs) rather than a library-quality metric — use the ViralCC pipeline instead. You already have aligned Hi-C BAM files mapped to assembled contigs; qc3C k-mer mode is reference-free and operates on cleaned FASTQ reads. Reads are raw and unprocessed — the 3D ratio should be computed on reads cleaned with the bbduk (trimq=10 qtrim=r ftm=5 minlen=50, ftl=10) and clumpify.sh steps first.

skills.description: Use when a reconstructed SSU sequences FASTA (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta from RiboTaxa's EMIRGE/MetaRib assembly) must be converted into a QIIME 2 .qza artifact before classify-sklearn classification.
skills.name: qiime2-artifact-format-conversion
skills.search_text: qiime2-artifact-format-conversion Use when a reconstructed SSU sequences FASTA (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta from RiboTaxa's EMIRGE/MetaRib assembly) must be converted into a QIIME 2 .qza artifact before classify-sklearn classification. The input sequences are already a QIIME 2 artifact (.qza) — re-importing a FASTA conversion step is unnecessary The input is unassembled short Illumina reads: the article found that 'inferring taxa directly to short-length Illumina reads resulted in a high rate of false positives while reconstructed sequences were correctly assigned', so reads should first be filtered and reconstructed before this conversion/classification step http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Converts RiboTaxa-reconstructed full-length/nearly full-length SSU rRNA sequences from plain FASTA into a QIIME 2 feature-data artifact (.qza) so they can be taxonomically classified with QIIME 2's sklearn feature-classifier using the SILVA 138 trained classifier. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Converts RiboTaxa-reconstructed full-length/nearly full-length SSU rRNA sequences from plain FASTA into a QIIME 2 feature-data artifact (.qza) so they can be taxonomically classified with QIIME 2's sklearn feature-classifier using the SILVA 138 trained classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input sequences are already a QIIME 2 artifact (.qza) — re-importing a FASTA conversion step is unnecessary The input is unassembled short Illumina reads: the article found that 'inferring taxa directly to short-length Illumina reads resulted in a high rate of false positives while reconstructed sequences were correctly assigned', so reads should first be filtered and reconstructed before this conversion/classification step

skills.search_text: qiime2-classify-sklearn-configuration Use when reconstructed or clustered SSU rRNA FASTA sequences (e.g. EMIRGE/MetaRib output from metagenomics reads) must be assigned taxonomy down to genus/species level via a naive-Bayes trained classifier. skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is training or applying DeepTaxa itself rather than establishing a classical naive-Bayes baseline Input sequences are V3–V4/V4 amplicons from a different reference database (e.g. SILVA or RDP) that the Greengenes2 2024.09-trained classifier does not cover You need alignment-based or k-mer classification (Kraken 2, SINTAX, BLAST) rather than QIIME 2's sklearn naive Bayesian plugin

Input is already transformed or normally distributed abundance data where the rank transform would destroy meaningful quantitative differences between samples Target is phylogenetic (clade-level) abundance rather than gene-level functional abundance — use OMARU's phylogenetic QC path instead Raw gene counts are needed, e.g. for absolute-abundance or length-normalized reporting rather than association testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 A normalization transform applied to OMARU's gene abundance matrix, in which quantified gene abundances are converted to ranks and mapped onto a normal distribution via inverse normal transformation, stabilizing non-normal abundance distributions before gene-level case-control association testing. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: A normalization transform applied to OMARU's gene abundance matrix, in which quantified gene abundances are converted to ranks and mapped onto a normal distribution via inverse normal transformation, stabilizing non-normal abundance distributions before gene-level case-control association testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already transformed or normally distributed abundance data where the rank transform would destroy meaningful quantitative differences between samples Target is phylogenetic (clade-level) abundance rather than gene-level functional abundance — use OMARU's phylogenetic QC path instead Raw gene counts are needed, e.g. for absolute-abundance or length-normalized reporting rather than association testing

skills.description: Use when improved viral contigs must be taxonomically classified with per-contig scores and LCA ranks, especially for low-coverage or divergent viruses where single -hit assignment is unreliable.
skills.name: rank-wise-lowest-common-ancestor-assignment
skills.search_text: rank-wise-lowest-common-ancestor-assignment Use when improved viral contigs must be taxonomically classified with per-contig scores and LCA ranks, especially for low-coverage or divergent viruses where single -hit assignment is unreliable. Input is raw reads or pre-assembly contigs that have not passed through VirMAP's dereplication, normalization, assembly, and improvement stages The goal is host or non-viral sequence classification — the algorithm filters contigs to the superkingdom Virus and discards everything else Only a single best-hit taxonomic label is needed without ambiguity handling — a simple top-hit BLAST/DIAMOND report suffices and avoids the two-pass scoring overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assigns taxonomy to viral contigs by running Virmap.pl's two-pass bits-per-base scoring followed by a rank-wise lowest common ancestor (LCA) over all pass-one taxa falling within a dynamically calculated radius, with majority thresholds computed from the reference database volume. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Assigns taxonomy to viral contigs by running Virmap.pl's two-pass bits-per-base scoring followed by a rank-wise lowest common ancestor (LCA) over all pass-one taxa falling within a dynamically calculated radius, with majority thresholds computed from the reference database volume.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or pre-assembly contigs that have not passed through VirMAP's dereplication, normalization, assembly, and improvement stages The goal is host or non-viral sequence classification — the algorithm filters contigs to the superkingdom Virus and discards everything else Only a single best-hit taxonomic label is needed without ambiguity handling — a simple top-hit BLAST/DIAMOND report suffices and avoids the two-pass scoring overhead

skills.summary: Aggregates per-read DIAMOND annotation output from SAMSA2 metatranscriptome runs into ranked abundance summary tables of organism and functional features, using SAMSA2's Python aggregation scripts (e.g., DIAMOND_analysis_counter.py). skills.description: Use when a trained linear SVM phenotype model must be inspected or its feature ranking reproduced and checked against a published table, e.g. verifying that trait absence rather than gene presence drives prediction.

skills.description: Use when per-sample shotgun sequencing is shallow and you need to verify that genome cover plateaus (saturates) for rare or low-prevalence taxa once coverage is composited across like samples from the same environment.

skills.search_text: rare-species-prevalence-stratification Use when per-sample shotgun sequencing is shallow and you need to verify that genome cover plateaus (saturates) for rare or low-prevalence taxa once coverage is composited across like samples from the same environment. Alignments were not generated against the Web of Life database (calculate_coverages.py currently only works with WoL) You already have a feature/abundance table and only want to filter it — the README warns this approach decreases apparent read counts rather than redistributing them as Woltka would Per-sample coverage is already deep enough that saturation is evident without compositing across like samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregates unique genome coverage across like samples (e.g., human fecal metagenomes aligned to the Web of Life reference genomes) and stratifies genomes by prevalence/rarity to confirm that composited genome cover saturates even for rare or low-prevalence species. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00758-22
skills.summary: Aggregates unique genome coverage across like samples (e.g., human fecal metagenomes aligned to the Web of Life reference genomes) and stratifies genomes by prevalence/rarity to confirm that composited genome cover saturates even for rare or low-prevalence species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Alignments were not generated against the Web of Life database (calculate_coverages.py currently only works with WoL) You already have a feature/abundance table and only want to filter it — the README warns this approach decreases apparent read counts rather than redistributing them as Woltka would Per-sample coverage is already deep enough that saturation is evident without compositing across like samples

skills.description: Use when you have temporal stacks of geocoded Sentinel-1 gamma_0 rasters (VH and VV) plus acquisition dates, and need per-pixel seasonal/temporal summary statistics for downstream ecological modelling.
skills.name: raster-stack-temporal-analysis-in-r
skills.search_text: raster-stack-temporal-analysis-in-r Use when you have temporal stacks of geocoded Sentinel-1 gamma_0 rasters (VH and VV) plus acquisition dates, and need per-pixel seasonal/temporal summary statistics for downstream ecological modelling. The input imagery is raw Sentinel-1 GRDH digital numbers not yet processed to gamma_0 — first run the SNAP/GPT pre-processing chain (precise orbit, noise removal, calibration, terrain flattening, range-doppler correction). Spatial speckle filtering is explicitly required (e.g. for single-acquisition scenes) — this skill deliberately smooths speckle in time via multi-acquisition medians instead of in space. http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Computes pixel-based summary statistics (medians, VV-VH differences, VV/VH ratios, seasonal differences) from temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 gamma_0 VH/VV backscatter rasters in R, using multi-acquisition medians to smooth speckle implicitly in time rather than by spatial filtering. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Computes pixel-based summary statistics (medians, VV-VH differences, VV/VH ratios, seasonal differences) from temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 gamma_0 VH/VV backscatter rasters in R, using multi-acquisition medians to smooth speckle implicitly in time rather than by spatial filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input imagery is raw Sentinel-1 GRDH digital numbers not yet processed to gamma_0 — first run the SNAP/GPT pre-processing chain (precise orbit, noise removal, calibration, terrain flattening, range-doppler correction). Spatial speckle filtering is explicitly required (e.g. for single-acquisition scenes) — this skill deliberately smooths speckle in time via multi-acquisition medians instead of in space.

skills.description: Use when Sentinel-1 gamma_0 summary rasters must be sampled at field-plot center locations (e.g. ALB_example_plots.* shapefile) to derive plot-level means or validate them against reference values such as S1_mean.csv.
skills.name: raster-vector-plot-extraction
skills.search_text: raster-vector-plot-extraction Use when Sentinel-1 gamma_0 summary rasters must be sampled at field-plot center locations (e.g. ALB_example_plots.* shapefile) to derive plot-level means or validate them against reference values such as S1_mean.csv. Samples Sentinel-1 gamma_0 pixel-based summary statistic rasters (medians, VV-VH differences, VV/VH ratios) at forest plot-center vector locations in R, aggregating 10 m pixels to 1-ha plot means and validating them against reference values. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Samples Sentinel-1 gamma_0 pixel-based summary statistic rasters (medians, VV-VH differences, VV/VH ratios) at forest plot-center vector locations in R, aggregating 10 m pixels to 1-ha plot means and validating them against reference values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inputs are raw Sentinel-1 GRDH digital numbers in slant-range coordinates; these must first be processed to gamma_0 via the SNAP/GPT chain (precise orbit, border/thermal noise removal, calibration, terrain flattening, range-doppler correction). The goal is biodiversity modeling itself (e.g. R² or NMDS of assemblage composition) rather than extracting plot-level raster values from the summary statistics. Input is already a table of plot-level means (e.g. S1_mean.csv); no raster sampling is needed.

skills.description: Use when you need to convert raw Oxford Nanopore electrical signals (FAST5, POD5, SLOW5, BLOW5) into deterministic hash values for real-time hash-based mapping or overlap search, and signal-to-signal variability must not change the hash for the same DNA content.
skills.name: raw-signal-adaptive-quantization
skills.search_text: raw-signal-adaptive-quantization Use when you need to convert raw Oxford Nanopore electrical signals (FAST5, POD5, SLOW5, BLOW5) into deterministic hash values for real-time hash-based mapping or overlap search, and signal-to-signal variability must not change the hash for the same DNA content. The task is basecalling or full base-level alignment rather than hash-based raw signal mapping (use a basecaller or RawHash's downstream chaining step instead) You need base-level CIGAR/PAF alignment output directly from raw signal alignment — this skill only produces the upstream 32-bit hashes; chaining over seed matches happens afterwards in RawHash Data is not nanopore raw electrical current signal (e.g., Illumina FASTQ input) Implements RawHash's raw-signal-to-hash pipeline for nanopore data: raw FAST5/BLOW5 signals are segmented into events (Scrappie-style Welch's t-test segmentation), z-score normalized, adaptively quantized (Q-bit trimming with p-bit pruning encoding E[1,2]E[3+p,Q]) so that signals from the same DNA content yield identical quantized values, and packed n consecutive events into a single 32-bit hash value. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad272
skills.summary: Implements RawHash's raw-signal-to-hash pipeline for nanopore data: raw FAST5/BLOW5 signals are segmented into events (Scrappie-style Welch's t-test segmentation), z-score normalized, adaptively quantized (Q-bit trimming with p-bit pruning encoding E[1,2]E[3+p,Q]) so that signals from the same DNA content yield identical quantized values, and packed n consecutive events into a single 32-bit hash value.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is basecalling or full base-level alignment rather than hash-based raw signal mapping (use a basecaller or RawHash's downstream chaining step instead) You need base-level CIGAR/PAF alignment output directly from raw signal alignment — this skill only produces the upstream 32-bit hashes; chaining over seed matches happens afterwards in RawHash Data is not nanopore raw electrical current signal (e.g., Illumina FASTQ input)

skills.description: Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon reads need taxonomic annotation via RDP classification with ChimeraSlayer chimera removal, to yield a taxonomy table compatible with an OTU count table and Newick tree.
skills.name: rdp-taxonomic-annotation-16s
skills.search_text: rdp-taxonomic-annotation-16s Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon reads need taxonomic annotation via RDP classification with ChimeraSlayer chimera removal, to yield a taxonomy table compatible with an OTU count table and Newick tree. Input is already a processed phyloseq object or feature table (e.g. biom.Rdata or otu.tab.txt) rather than raw reads Data are shotgun metagenomic reads, where taxonomic profiling tools like MetaPhlAn or MEGAN apply instead of 16S RDP annotation An ASV/DADA2-style amplicon workflow is required, since this skill is tied to 97% open-reference OTU picking against Greengenes http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assigns taxonomy to 16S rRNA OTUs using the RDP classifier while removing chimeric sequences with ChimeraSlayer, as done in MiSurv for QIITA study 10508 to produce the deposited tax.tab.txt that feeds the phyloseq object (biom.Rdata). metagenomics/v1 10.1128/spectrum.05059-22
skills.summary: Assigns taxonomy to 16S rRNA OTUs using the RDP classifier while removing chimeric sequences with ChimeraSlayer, as done in MiSurv for QIITA study 10508 to produce the deposited tax.tab.txt that feeds the phyloseq object (biom.Rdata).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed phyloseq object or feature table (e.g. biom.Rdata or otu.tab.txt) rather than raw reads Data are shotgun metagenomic reads, where taxonomic profiling tools like MetaPhlAn or MEGAN apply instead of 16S RDP annotation An ASV/DADA2-style amplicon workflow is required, since this skill is tied to 97% open-reference OTU picking against Greengenes

skills.name: read-alignment-against-multiple-reference-genomes
skills.search_text: read-alignment-against-multiple-reference-genomes Use when reproducing or benchmarking the original alignment-based AFS pipeline on food metagenomics samples (e.g. KAL_D, Kal/KLyo on the AFS10 reference set), or when establishing the runtime/accuracy baseline that AFS-MetaCache is compared to. You only need classification/quantification speed at modern throughput — AFS-MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark queries at 17.1 MR/m versus 0.04 MR/m here, so alignment is the wrong choice for large collections Reference genome collection is large or growing — the per-genome alignment strategy scales linearly with the number of genomes and was the motivation for the alignment-free substitute Input is already a classified/quantified abundance table rather than raw reads needing alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reproduces the legacy alignment-based AFS pipeline, in which sequencing reads are aligned with BWA against each considered reference genome separately, to quantify ingredient composition and benchmark it against the k-mer based AFS-MetaCache approach (Tables 9-10). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Reproduces the legacy alignment-based AFS pipeline, in which sequencing reads are aligned with BWA against each considered reference genome separately, to quantify ingredient composition and benchmark it against the k-mer based AFS-MetaCache approach (Tables 9-10).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need classification/quantification speed at modern throughput — AFS-MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark queries at 17.1 MR/m versus 0.04 MR/m here, so alignment is the wrong choice for large collections Reference genome collection is large or growing — the per-genome alignment strategy scales linearly with the number of genomes and was the motivation for the alignment-free substitute Input is already a classified/quantified abundance table rather than raw reads needing alignment

skills.description: Use when simulating within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations in longitudinal (multi-time-point) simulated raw sequencing reads and a ground-truth mutation record (VCF) is needed for benchmarking.

skills.search_text: read-alignment-based-variant-writing Use when simulating within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations in longitudinal (multi-time-point) simulated raw sequencing reads and a ground-truth mutation record (VCF) is needed for benchmarking. Input is real metagenomic data rather than simulated reads — the README warns STEMSim only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes in that case The goal is community-level abundance simulation rather than within-strain mutation injection — use CAMISIM to generate the input community reads instead Longitudinal/within-strain evolutionary signal is not needed; a standard metagenome simulator alone suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Rewrites simulated longitudinal metagenomic raw reads so that reads overlapping injected SNV/InDel sites carry the new alleles, using Bowtie2 alignments of reads to reference genomes as the coordinate system, and exports the injected mutations as a VCF. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real metagenomic data rather than simulated reads — the README warns STEMSim only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes in that case The goal is community-level abundance simulation rather than within-strain mutation injection — use CAMISIM to generate the input community reads instead Longitudinal/within-strain evolutionary signal is not needed; a standard metagenome simulator alone suffices

skills.description: Use when comparing read-classification accuracy (F1, precision, recall) of a fast classifier like SPUMONI against an aligner like minimap2 across reference index compositions (target strain present vs excluded) on simulated or real nanopore reads.
skills.name: read-alignment-benchmarking
skills.search_text: read-alignment-benchmarking Use when comparing read-classification accuracy (F1, precision, recall) of a fast classifier like SPUMONI against an aligner like minimap2 across reference index compositions (target strain present vs excluded) on simulated or real nanopore reads. Reads are raw nanopore electrical signal rather than base-called sequences — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences and cannot interface with the Read Until API directly Substantial sequence similarity exists between depletion-target and non-target reads (e.g. conserved genes between species), where the null-index hypothesis test may be insufficient The task requires per-experiment threshold optimization rather than a single KS-stat threshold tuned on real nanopore data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark read-classification accuracy of SPUMONI (PML and MS modes) against minimap2 across reference index strategies, computing precision, recall, and F1 scores on simulated ZymoMC nanopore reads to reproduce the paper's Table 1 comparison of one-genome versus pan-genome indexes. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Benchmark read-classification accuracy of SPUMONI (PML and MS modes) against minimap2 across reference index strategies, computing precision, recall, and F1 scores on simulated ZymoMC nanopore reads to reproduce the paper's Table 1 comparison of one-genome versus pan-genome indexes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are raw nanopore electrical signal rather than base-called sequences — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences and cannot interface with the Read Until API directly Substantial sequence similarity exists between depletion-target and non-target reads (e.g. conserved genes between species), where the null-index hypothesis test may be insufficient The task requires per-experiment threshold optimization rather than a single KS-stat threshold tuned on real nanopore data

skills.description: Use when a simulated metagenomic dataset with known reference genomes (e.g. Sim50, Sim100, CAMI2 UG) has been assembled into contigs and you need per-contig truth labels to evaluate binning tools with AMBER.
skills.name: read-alignment-ground-truth-generation
skills.search_text: read-alignment-ground-truth-generation Use when a simulated metagenomic dataset with known reference genomes (e.g. Sim50, Sim100, CAMI2 UG) has been assembled into contigs and you need per-contig truth labels to evaluate binning tools with AMBER. The dataset is a real-world metagenome with no reference genomes available, so contigs cannot be assigned a genome of origin (e.g. a fully de novo environmental sample without simulated truth). You need to evaluate the binner on all contigs regardless of mapping confidence and cannot afford discarding multi-mapping contigs from the benchmark. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates a binning ground-truth label set for AMBER evaluation by aligning assembled contigs to known reference genomes with Minimap2 and SAMTools, retaining only contigs whose best mapping has the highest mapping quality. This converts reference genome assignments into the per-contig bin labels AMBER needs to score purity, completeness, and F1. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.compbiolchem.2022.107734
skills.summary: Generates a binning ground-truth label set for AMBER evaluation by aligning assembled contigs to known reference genomes with Minimap2 and SAMTools, retaining only contigs whose best mapping has the highest mapping quality. This converts reference genome assignments into the per-contig bin labels AMBER needs to score purity, completeness, and F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a real-world metagenome with no reference genomes available, so contigs cannot be assigned a genome of origin (e.g. a fully de novo environmental sample without simulated truth). You need to evaluate the binner on all contigs regardless of mapping confidence and cannot afford discarding multi-mapping contigs from the benchmark.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing paired-end FASTQ metatranscriptome reads with Trimmomatic + FLASh and you need to quantify the merged-read fraction and average merged read length before annotation submission.
skills.name: read-alignment-statistics-computation
skills.search_text: read-alignment-statistics-computation Use when preprocessing paired-end FASTQ metatranscriptome reads with Trimmomatic + FLASh and you need to quantify the merged-read fraction and average merged read length before annotation submission. Input reads are already single-end long reads longer than 100 bp, so no paired-end joining step is needed and merge-fraction statistics do not apply. Reads have already been merged and quality-trimmed upstream; recomputing trimming/joining statistics on preprocessed files would double-count losses. The goal is annotation or statistical comparison (MG-RAST annotation, DESeq2 analysis), which are downstream SAMSA stages, not preprocessing alignment statistics. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Computes the fraction of raw paired-end reads successfully aligned (joined) after Trimmomatic trimming and FLASh merging in the SAMSA preprocessing phase, plus the average aligned read length (~178 bp for 100 bp paired-end input). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1270-8
skills.summary: Computes the fraction of raw paired-end reads successfully aligned (joined) after Trimmomatic trimming and FLASh merging in the SAMSA preprocessing phase, plus the average aligned read length (~178 bp for 100 bp paired-end input).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already single-end long reads longer than 100 bp, so no paired-end joining step is needed and merge-fraction statistics do not apply. Reads have already been merged and quality-trimmed upstream; recomputing trimming/joining statistics on preprocessed files would double-count losses. The goal is annotation or statistical comparison (MG-RAST annotation, DESeq2 analysis), which are downstream SAMSA stages, not preprocessing alignment statistics.

skills.description: Use when you must decide, from a streaming read prefix (FASTQ/base-called nanopore reads), whether a read belongs to a target set versus random chance, and a compressed pan-genome index is preferable to full alignment.
skills.name: read-classification-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: read-classification-hypothesis-testing Use when you must decide, from a streaming read prefix (FASTQ/base-called nanopore reads), whether a read belongs to a target set versus random chance, and a compressed pan-genome index is preferable to full alignment. When there is substantial sequence similarity between depletion-target reads and non-target reads (e.g. conserved genes between species) — the null index built from reversed sequences may then be insufficient to distinguish target from chance matches When operating directly on raw nanopore electrical signal via the Read Until API — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences, so a separate base caller must run upstream When per-base alignment coordinates (as minimap2 provides) are required rather than a target/nontarget classification decision http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Classify sequencing reads against a target set by comparing matching statistics (MSs) or pseudomatching lengths (PMLs) computed against a positive pan-genome index against a null index built from the reverse of the positive-index sequences, using a Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistic threshold and majority-of-regions voting, as implemented in SPUMONI. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Classify sequencing reads against a target set by comparing matching statistics (MSs) or pseudomatching lengths (PMLs) computed against a positive pan-genome index against a null index built from the reverse of the positive-index sequences, using a Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistic threshold and majority-of-regions voting, as implemented in SPUMONI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When there is substantial sequence similarity between depletion-target reads and non-target reads (e.g. conserved genes between species) — the null index built from reversed sequences may then be insufficient to distinguish target from chance matches When operating directly on raw nanopore electrical signal via the Read Until API — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences, so a separate base caller must run upstream When per-base alignment coordinates (as minimap2 provides) are required rather than a target/nontarget classification decision

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ metatranscriptome reads must be reduced to per-sample counts of reads matching a reference genome (e.g., host/human) to test whether host transcriptomes are recoverable.
skills.name: read-count-quantification-per-sample
skills.search_text: read-count-quantification-per-sample Use when raw paired-end FASTQ metatranscriptome reads must be reduced to per-sample counts of reads matching a reference genome (e.g., host/human) to test whether host transcriptomes are recoverable. skills.summary: Quantify per-sample read counts against a reference genome by cleaning paired-end FASTQ metatranscriptome reads with Trimmomatic, joining mates with FLASH, aligning to the reference (e.g., human genome), and tabulating matched read counts and percentages per replicate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-sample annotation or abundance summary table produced by analysis_counter.py or DIAMOND_analysis_counter.py — counting has already been done. skills.search_text: read-depth-normalization Use when comparing case-control metagenomic diversity (alpha or beta) across samples whose read depths differ, e.g. T2D (n=171) or SCZ (n=344) fecal metagenomes, prior to Shannon/Bray-Curtis computation. skills.summary: Down-samples shotgun metagenomic reads from each sample to a common sequencing depth using the OMARU normalization step, so that sequencing-depth-driven bias is removed before Shannon alpha-diversity and Bray-Curtis beta-diversity estimation on taxonomic (L2-L7) and gene abundance data.

skills.search_text: read-mapping-based-contaminant-screening Use when retained reads after host decontamination show unexpectedly high human retention (e.g. NA12878 0.641% vs 0.406%) and a recurring contaminant such as EBV is suspected across a genome set. The input FASTQs have not yet passed host decontamination (raw reads rather than Hostile-retained *.clean_*.fastq.gz) The goal is removal of human host reads with the default human-t2t-hla index rather than screening for a specific non-human contaminant Long-read or single-end data where paired clean_1/clean_2 retained FASTQs are not available http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Detects and subtracts contaminant sequences (e.g. Epstein-Barr Virus) from Hostile-cleaned retained FASTQs by de novo assembly with MEGAHIT, alignment to contaminant references (NC_007605.1/NC_009334.1) using Minimap2/Bowtie2, and a custom Hostile clean pass with a contaminant-only index, so host read retention metrics are corrected. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad728
skills.summary: Detects and subtracts contaminant sequences (e.g. Epstein-Barr Virus) from Hostile-cleaned retained FASTQs by de novo assembly with MEGAHIT, alignment to contaminant references (NC_007605.1/NC_009334.1) using Minimap2/Bowtie2, and a custom Hostile clean pass with a contaminant-only index, so host read retention metrics are corrected.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input FASTQs have not yet passed host decontamination (raw reads rather than Hostile-retained *.clean_*.fastq.gz) The goal is removal of human host reads with the default human-t2t-hla index rather than screening for a specific non-human contaminant Long-read or single-end data where paired clean_1/clean_2 retained FASTQs are not available

skills.search_text: read-mapping-based-genome-comparison Use when you need accurate strain-level genome similarity (ANI) between genomes across metagenomic samples — e.g. benchmarking genome comparison accuracy or detecting shared strains — from read mappings rather than raw assemblies. When genomes are only available as assemblies and no read mappings exist — assembly-based tools like dRep's built-in ANI operate directly on FASTA files When you only need coverage/breadth quantification of genomes rather than strain-level similarity — CoverM or 'inStrain profile' alone suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 Compare microbial genomes by mapping reads to reference genomes, profiling each mapping with inStrain, and then running 'inStrain compare' to obtain microdiversity-aware population-level ANI (popANI) and consensus ANI (ConANI) values that are more accurate than strain-comparison methods operating on assemblies alone. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Compare microbial genomes by mapping reads to reference genomes, profiling each mapping with inStrain, and then running 'inStrain compare' to obtain microdiversity-aware population-level ANI (popANI) and consensus ANI (ConANI) values that are more accurate than strain-comparison methods operating on assemblies alone.

skills.search_text: read-mapping-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing mapping accuracy or throughput of raw-signal nanopore mappers against a reference genome, or when validating that a new mapper's precision/recall matches published orderings on datasets spanning small to large genomes. skills.description: Use when evaluating a metagenome assembly by measuring what fraction of HiFi reads and read bases align to contigs, especially when the breakdown should be stratified by bin quality (near complete/high/medium/low/unbinned).
skills.name: read-mapping-ratio-computation
skills.search_text: read-mapping-ratio-computation Use when evaluating a metagenome assembly by measuring what fraction of HiFi reads and read bases align to contigs, especially when the breakdown should be stratified by bin quality (near complete/high/medium/low/unbinned). The goal is assembler-level contiguity or completeness statistics (e.g. N50, MetaQUAST metrics) rather than how much of the read set the assembly represents. No assembly contigs are available yet — this skill evaluates an existing assembly and cannot be run pre-assembly. Reads are short reads rather than HiFi long reads, since Mapler's evaluation logic and tooling are designed for HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Compute aligned read and aligned base ratios by aligning HiFi long reads to assembly contigs, optionally broken down by bin quality category, to quantify how much of the sequenced sample's diversity the assembly captures. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Compute aligned read and aligned base ratios by aligning HiFi long reads to assembly contigs, optionally broken down by bin quality category, to quantify how much of the sequenced sample's diversity the assembly captures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is assembler-level contiguity or completeness statistics (e.g. N50, MetaQUAST metrics) rather than how much of the read set the assembly represents. No assembly contigs are available yet — this skill evaluates an existing assembly and cannot be run pre-assembly. Reads are short reads rather than HiFi long reads, since Mapler's evaluation logic and tooling are designed for HiFi long-read metagenomic assemblies.

skills.description: Use when shotgun reads have been mapped back to de novo MAG clusters (e.g. VAMB bins via MAGinator) and you must QC mapping depth/allele-frequency statistics to flag MAG clusters with mixed strains per sample or environment.
skills.name: read-mapping-statistics-qc
skills.search_text: read-mapping-statistics-qc Use when shotgun reads have been mapped back to de novo MAG clusters (e.g. VAMB bins via MAGinator) and you must QC mapping depth/allele-frequency statistics to flag MAG clusters with mixed strains per sample or environment. Input is already a computed abundance or mixed-allele summary table — no re-mapping or SNV pileup is needed. Data are not shotgun metagenomic reads mappable back to assembled MAGs (e.g. 16S amplicon data), since SNV-based mixed-allele classification requires read-level alleles on signature/marker genes. Read depth is so low that most bases fall below the allele frequency cutoff, making mixed-allele calls unreliable from stats.tab/pileup alone. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 QC and interpretation of MAGinator read-mapping statistics — the phylo/stats.tab (non-N fraction, signature/marker gene counts, read depth, bases not reaching the allele frequency cutoff) and phylo/pileup SNV information — to classify which MAG clusters harbour mixed alleles (multiple strain variants) in a sample. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8
skills.summary: QC and interpretation of MAGinator read-mapping statistics — the phylo/stats.tab (non-N fraction, signature/marker gene counts, read depth, bases not reaching the allele frequency cutoff) and phylo/pileup SNV information — to classify which MAG clusters harbour mixed alleles (multiple strain variants) in a sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a computed abundance or mixed-allele summary table — no re-mapping or SNV pileup is needed. skills.description: Use when a short-read metagenome assembly or clustering pipeline needs pairwise read overlaps with identity and overlap-length scores, e.g. to build overlap graphs for strain-aware (haplotype-aware) OLC assembly.
skills.name: read-overlap-computation
skills.search_text: read-overlap-computation Use when a short-read metagenome assembly or clustering pipeline needs pairwise read overlaps with identity and overlap-length scores, e.g. to build overlap graphs for strain-aware (haplotype-aware) OLC assembly. Input reads are long third-generation reads with high error rate — the paper notes third-generation error rates introduce unresolved issues and the method targets NGS short reads You need full-length strain-specific contigs spanning whole genomes — the paper states short Illumina read length constrains contig length A de Bruijn graph assembler (SPAdes, MEGAHIT, IDBA-UD, Minia3) is already required, since this skill implements the OLC overlap step of a strain-aware assembler rather than generic metagenome assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Compute suffix-prefix read-to-read overlaps and weighted overlap scores as in StrainXpress, using Minimap2 all-vs-all alignment of interleaved NGS FASTQ reads and scoring each overlap from its CIGAR string as D = 0.9*i + 0.1*o/((r1+r2)/2). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac543
skills.summary: Compute suffix-prefix read-to-read overlaps and weighted overlap scores as in StrainXpress, using Minimap2 all-vs-all alignment of interleaved NGS FASTQ reads and scoring each overlap from its CIGAR string as D = 0.9*i + 0.1*o/((r1+r2)/2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are long third-generation reads with high error rate — the paper notes third-generation error rates introduce unresolved issues and the method targets NGS short reads You need full-length strain-specific contigs spanning whole genomes — the paper states short Illumina read length constrains contig length A de Bruijn graph assembler (SPAdes, MEGAHIT, IDBA-UD, Minia3) is already required, since this skill implements the OLC overlap step of a strain-aware assembler rather than generic metagenome assembly

skills.description: Use when filtering mapped metagenomic reads before SNV calling or coverage profiling, and you must discard read pairs whose alignment to the reference .fasta falls below a user-defined minimum nucleotide identity.
skills.name: read-pair-nucleotide-identity-calculation
skills.search_text: read-pair-nucleotide-identity-calculation Use when filtering mapped metagenomic reads before SNV calling or coverage profiling, and you must discard read pairs whose alignment to the reference .fasta falls below a user-defined minimum nucleotide identity. Input .bam contains single-end (un-paired) reads — all un-paired reads are removed by default, so this skill will discard everything. You need per-individual-read filtering rather than pair-level filtering — inStrain's filters are explicitly applied to pairs of reads in combination. You are at the SNV-calling stage (minimum 5 reads per position, >5% variant reads, null-model FDR) rather than the read-pair mapping-fidelity stage — those are separate criteria applied to filtered reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compute per-pair nucleotide identity (ANI vs. the reference .fasta) for read pairs within inStrain's read-filtering pipeline, applying the identity cutoff at the read-pair level to reduce erroneous mappings in metagenomic .bam files. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Compute per-pair nucleotide identity (ANI vs. the reference .fasta) for read pairs within inStrain's read-filtering pipeline, applying the identity cutoff at the read-pair level to reduce erroneous mappings in metagenomic .bam files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input .bam contains single-end (un-paired) reads — all un-paired reads are removed by default, so this skill will discard everything. You need per-individual-read filtering rather than pair-level filtering — inStrain's filters are explicitly applied to pairs of reads in combination. You are at the SNV-calling stage (minimum 5 reads per position, >5% variant reads, null-model FDR) rather than the read-pair mapping-fidelity stage — those are separate criteria applied to filtered reads.

skills.search_text: read-pair-overlap-scoring Use when a metagenomic assembly needs its initial divide step: you have interleaved Illumina FASTQ reads from a complex community and must partition them into small clusters that each correspond roughly to one species before local/global assembly. skills.search_text: read-prefix-length-quantification Use when comparing adaptive/real-time nanopore signal mappers (RawHash, UNCALLED, Sigmap) on how early each stops sequencing a mapped read, i.e., estimating time and cost via read-prefix lengths and chunk counts from PAF records. skills.description: Use when comparing host read removal tools on the same human sequencing data (Illumina paired-end or ONT FASTQ) and you need a quantitative per-tool retained/removed read proportion table to benchmark decontamination stringency.
skills.name: read-retention-benchmarking-across-tools
skills.search_text: read-retention-benchmarking-across-tools Use when comparing host read removal tools on the same human sequencing data (Illumina paired-end or ONT FASTQ) and you need a quantitative per-tool retained/removed read proportion table to benchmark decontamination stringency. skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure that compares how many human reads two host-decontamination tools retain on identical real human FASTQ datasets, e.g. Hostile versus the NCBI Human Read Removal Tool (HRRT), to quantify relative removal performance.

skills.search_text: read-simulation-with-hiseq-error-profile Use when benchmarking a SNP/INDEL caller on synthetic data with a known ground truth: you need reads simulated from a bi-allelic genome (e.g. Human chromosome 1 at 30x, HiSeq error profile) instead of real reads with an approximated truth set.
