The chosen cutoff has no relation to read recruitment string matching (e.g. classifying classifier-level alignment scores or mapping quality) — the ROC here is specifically over LCS sizes between genome pairs You need a general binary-classifier evaluation rather than a sequence-similarity threshold justification between reference genomes The target virus shares no conservation with any reference genome, since LCS-based cutoffs cannot be calibrated for it http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Reproduce the longest-common-substring (LCS) ROC analysis that justifies TAR-VIR's read-recruitment overlap cutoff (e.g. 100 bp or more, with 150 bp used in simulations), by computing LCS sizes between viral genomes and between viruses and other microbes, then evaluating true/false positive rates for candidate cutoffs. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2

skills.when_to_use_negative: The chosen cutoff has no relation to read recruitment string matching (e.g. classifying classifier-level alignment scores or mapping quality) — the ROC here is specifically over LCS sizes between genome pairs You need a general binary-classifier evaluation rather than a sequence-similarity threshold justification between reference genomes The target virus shares no conservation with any reference genome, since LCS-based cutoffs cannot be calibrated for it

skills.description: Use when comparing binary classifiers of sample pairs (same-strain vs different-strain) that output continuous scores on a labeled benchmark, and you need threshold-free performance (ROC/AUC, sensitivity, specificity) across tools.
skills.name: roc-curve-performance-evaluation
skills.search_text: roc-curve-performance-evaluation Use when comparing binary classifiers of sample pairs (same-strain vs different-strain) that output continuous scores on a labeled benchmark, and you need threshold-free performance (ROC/AUC, sensitivity, specificity) across tools. The article's authors caution that classifying strains as same or different is inherently subjective and thresholds (e.g., inStrain popANI 99.999%, APSS 0.95) are species-dependent, so this benchmarking approach is wrong when a continuous genomic-difference measure is more appropriate than a binary classification The score table has fewer than n usable regions per sample pair — SynTracker excludes pairs with fewer than n regions from downstream analysis, so those pairs cannot contribute valid ROC points No ground-truth labels exist for sample-pair relatedness; ROC/AUC cannot be computed without a labeled benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 Benchmark a pairwise strain-classification score (e.g., SynTracker's APSS) by sweeping classification thresholds to build ROC curves and compute AUC, enabling head-to-head comparison of strain-tracking tools (SynTracker vs MIDAS, StrainPhlAn, inStrain) on a labeled ground-truth dataset. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Benchmark a pairwise strain-classification score (e.g., SynTracker's APSS) by sweeping classification thresholds to build ROC curves and compute AUC, enabling head-to-head comparison of strain-tracking tools (SynTracker vs MIDAS, StrainPhlAn, inStrain) on a labeled ground-truth dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The article's authors caution that classifying strains as same or different is inherently subjective and thresholds (e.g., inStrain popANI 99.999%, APSS 0.95) are species-dependent, so this benchmarking approach is wrong when a continuous genomic-difference measure is more appropriate than a binary classification The score table has fewer than n usable regions per sample pair — SynTracker excludes pairs with fewer than n regions from downstream analysis, so those pairs cannot contribute valid ROC points No ground-truth labels exist for sample-pair relatedness; ROC/AUC cannot be computed without a labeled benchmark

skills.name: rrna-alignment-gap-curation
skills.search_text: rrna-alignment-gap-curation Use when you have full-length bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequences (≥800 bp aligned) aligned to an rRNA covariance model and need to flag intron-like insertion sequences and quantify their length statistics before phylogenetic analysis. Sequences are short amplicon reads rather than near-full-length (≥800 bp aligned) 16S rRNA genes — gap-based insertion calls are unreliable below this length You need insertions in eukaryotic or archaeal rRNAs — the paper's analysis and statistics target bacterial 16S rRNA genes, where insertions are rare outside the CPR Your goal is primer-binding or amplicon-detection assessment (e.g. 515F/806R coverage) rather than insertion detection and length statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Detect large insertions in curated 16S rRNA gene sequences by identifying big gaps in HMM/covariance-model alignments (e.g. cmscan against Rfam or a Comparative RNA Web-derived model), then compute the fraction of genes carrying ≥10 bp insertions and the max/mean/s.d. of insertion lengths. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486

skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are short amplicon reads rather than near-full-length (≥800 bp aligned) 16S rRNA genes — gap-based insertion calls are unreliable below this length You need insertions in eukaryotic or archaeal rRNAs — the paper's analysis and statistics target bacterial 16S rRNA genes, where insertions are rare outside the CPR Your goal is primer-binding or amplicon-detection assessment (e.g. 515F/806R coverage) rather than insertion detection and length statistics

skills.description: Use when surveying bacterial 16S rRNA gene collections (e.g., SILVA 115) for large interhelical insertions, or when testing whether such insertions are CPR-restricted versus broadly distributed in bacteria.
skills.name: rrna-insertion-prevalence-comparison
skills.search_text: rrna-insertion-prevalence-comparison Use when surveying bacterial 16S rRNA gene collections (e.g., SILVA 115) for large interhelical insertions, or when testing whether such insertions are CPR-restricted versus broadly distributed in bacteria. When the goal is phylogenetic placement of 16S sequences — introns/insertions ≥10 bp should first be removed rather than quantified before alignment and phylogeny When testing whether insertions are retained in transcripts — that requires mapping metatranscriptomic (not genomic) reads to the assembled 16S rRNA genes When 16S records cannot be confidently identified by the SSUAlign/infernal structural model (score below the T 1 threshold) — gap-based insertion calls are unreliable on non-16S sequence http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Quantifies the prevalence and length distribution of large (≥10 bp) insertions in 16S rRNA genes by aligning sequences (e.g., non-redundant SILVA version 115) to a curated 16S rRNA covariance model with Infernal cmsearch, and compares the rate outside the candidate phyla radiation (CPR) against the 31% large-insertion rate observed within CPR organisms. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: Quantifies the prevalence and length distribution of large (≥10 bp) insertions in 16S rRNA genes by aligning sequences (e.g., non-redundant SILVA version 115) to a curated 16S rRNA covariance model with Infernal cmsearch, and compares the rate outside the candidate phyla radiation (CPR) against the 31% large-insertion rate observed within CPR organisms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is phylogenetic placement of 16S sequences — introns/insertions ≥10 bp should first be removed rather than quantified before alignment and phylogeny When testing whether insertions are retained in transcripts — that requires mapping metatranscriptomic (not genomic) reads to the assembled 16S rRNA genes When 16S records cannot be confidently identified by the SSUAlign/infernal structural model (score below the T 1 threshold) — gap-based insertion calls are unreliable on non-16S sequence

skills.description: Use when curating 16S rRNA genes that contain large insertion sequences (≥10 bp, up to 2,004 bp in this dataset) before multiple sequence alignment or phylogenetic tree building.
skills.name: rrna-insertion-sequence-removal
skills.search_text: rrna-insertion-sequence-removal Use when curating 16S rRNA genes that contain large insertion sequences (≥10 bp, up to 2,004 bp in this dataset) before multiple sequence alignment or phylogenetic tree building. When the goal is to characterize the insertion-encoded proteins or introns themselves — those ORFs are analyzed separately (e.g. Pfam searches with ≥90% ORF-overlap-with-insertion criterion), not removed When sequences are non-rRNA or already insertion-free and pre-aligned; stripping ≥10 bp insertions is specific to intron-laden rRNA gene curation When working with bacterial rRNA genes outside CPR, where such insertions are rare ('their rarity in bacteria outside the CPR') Removes intervening insertion sequences (≥10 bp, putative self-splicing introns) from 16S rRNA gene sequences prior to structural alignment and phylogenetic inference. In CPR bacteria these insertions are common (31% of 16S genes) and, if left in place, disrupt rRNA alignment so a reliable phylogeny cannot be established. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: Removes intervening insertion sequences (≥10 bp, putative self-splicing introns) from 16S rRNA gene sequences prior to structural alignment and phylogenetic inference. In CPR bacteria these insertions are common (31% of 16S genes) and, if left in place, disrupt rRNA alignment so a reliable phylogeny cannot be established.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to characterize the insertion-encoded proteins or introns themselves — those ORFs are analyzed separately (e.g. Pfam searches with ≥90% ORF-overlap-with-insertion criterion), not removed When sequences are non-rRNA or already insertion-free and pre-aligned; stripping ≥10 bp insertions is specific to intron-laden rRNA gene curation When working with bacterial rRNA genes outside CPR, where such insertions are rare ('their rarity in bacteria outside the CPR')

skills.description: Use when you must compare CPU time, memory peaks, and job runtimes of multiple MAG taxonomic classifiers on the same benchmark MAG sets and need a reproducible resource comparison table.

skills.search_text: runtime-and-memory-measurement Use when you must compare CPU time, memory peaks, and job runtimes of multiple MAG taxonomic classifiers on the same benchmark MAG sets and need a reproducible resource comparison table. The goal is to compare classification accuracy/sensitivity rather than computational cost — the accuracy benchmarking uses different inputs and metrics (sensitivity, balanced accuracy, FPR). skills.search_text: runtime-measurement-with-linux-time Use when comparing the computational scalability or speed of clustering/search tools on large sequence sets, or when reproducing reported runtime scaling exponents and speedup factors. When comparing clustering quality (e.g. functional consistency via GO annotations or Pfam) rather than runtime — quality metrics, not timing, are the relevant outputs. When the tools cannot be run on identical hardware with identical thread counts (e.g. CD-HIT -T 16 vs single-threaded baselines), since runtime ratios are then confounded. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 A benchmarking method for measuring wall-clock runtimes of sequence-clustering tools (Linclust, MMseqs2, CD-HIT, UCLUST) with the Linux 'time' command and fitting power laws T = a*N^b to quantify how runtime scales with input set size N. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-04964-5

skills.when_to_use_negative: When comparing clustering quality (e.g. functional consistency via GO annotations or Pfam) rather than runtime — quality metrics, not timing, are the relevant outputs. skills.description: Use when comparing the computational performance of two tools or implementations on identical inputs and settings, e.g. to verify a reported speedup or memory reduction for alignment-free dissimilarity calculation.

skills.search_text: runtime-memory-profiling Use when comparing the computational performance of two tools or implementations on identical inputs and settings, e.g. to verify a reported speedup or memory reduction for alignment-free dissimilarity calculation. skills.description: Use when you need to determine the minimum CPU/RAM allocation at which an aligner or pipeline step reaches peak efficiency, e.g. before sizing cluster jobs for SAMSA2 DIAMOND annotation runs.
skills.name: runtime-speedup-curve-visualization
skills.search_text: runtime-speedup-curve-visualization Use when you need to determine the minimum CPU/RAM allocation at which an aligner or pipeline step reaches peak efficiency, e.g. before sizing cluster jobs for SAMSA2 DIAMOND annotation runs. The goal is annotating a full production sample rather than characterizing resource scaling — run the standard SAMSA2 master_script pipeline instead of a benchmark sweep. The reference database is small enough to trivially fit in the target node's memory, making a saturation benchmark unnecessary. The tool is not I/O- or memory-bound (e.g. single-threaded personal-computer aggregation scripts like DIAMOND_analysis_counter.py), where RAM-scaling curves would be uninformative. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark wall-clock runtime of a tool (here, DIAMOND v0.8.3 annotation within SAMSA2) as a compute resource is swept stepwise, then compute and plot relative speedup to identify the resource saturation point. This reveals when adding resources (e.g. RAM to hold the ~6 GB NCBI nr Bacteria database in memory) stops yielding further gains. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-018-2189-z
skills.summary: Benchmark wall-clock runtime of a tool (here, DIAMOND v0.8.3 annotation within SAMSA2) as a compute resource is swept stepwise, then compute and plot relative speedup to identify the resource saturation point. skills.description: Use when a variant caller outputs reference-free calls (e.g. ebwt2InDel's .snp fasta) and a reference genome (e.g. hg38) is available, so calls must be expressed as coordinate-anchored .vcf entries for validation or downstream use.
skills.name: sam-to-vcf-variant-annotation
skills.search_text: sam-to-vcf-variant-annotation Use when a variant caller outputs reference-free calls (e.g. ebwt2InDel's .snp fasta) and a reference genome (e.g. hg38) is available, so calls must be expressed as coordinate-anchored .vcf entries for validation or downstream use. No reference genome is available for the organism — the whole point of ebwt2InDel is reference-free discovery, and this skill requires aligning variant fragments to hg38 (or an equivalent reference). The input is already a valid VCF or alignment-coordinate callset rather than a KisSNP2-format .snp/fasta of variant contexts. The .snp calls have not been low-coverage filtered when coverage is marginal — the paper suggests filter_snp with m=5 only for datasets covered at >=25x. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Converts reference-free SNP/INDEL calls (e.g. the KisSNP2-format .snp output of ebwt2InDel) into standard .vcf records by realigning variant fragments to a reference assembly. The paper's snp2vcf pipeline — seqtk → bwa-mem → sam2vcf — translates mismatches and INDELs in a SAM alignment into reference-coordinate VCF entries. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Converts reference-free SNP/INDEL calls (e.g. the KisSNP2-format .snp output of ebwt2InDel) into standard .vcf records by realigning variant fragments to a reference assembly. The paper's snp2vcf pipeline — seqtk → bwa-mem → sam2vcf — translates mismatches and INDELs in a SAM alignment into reference-coordinate VCF entries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome is available for the organism — the whole point of ebwt2InDel is reference-free discovery, and this skill requires aligning variant fragments to hg38 (or an equivalent reference). The input is already a valid VCF or alignment-coordinate callset rather than a KisSNP2-format .snp/fasta of variant contexts. The .snp calls have not been low-coverage filtered when coverage is marginal — the paper suggests filter_snp with m=5 only for datasets covered at >=25x.

skills.description: Use when a phyloseq OTU/feature table with uneven per-sample read depths must be QC-filtered before composition or survival analysis, and shallow samples (e.g., <3,000 reads) should be removed.
skills.name: sample-library-size-filtering
skills.search_text: sample-library-size-filtering Use when a phyloseq OTU/feature table with uneven per-sample read depths must be QC-filtered before composition or survival analysis, and shallow samples (e.g., <3,000 reads) should be removed. The input is already a post-QC phyloseq object (e.g., biom.Rdata from the MiSurv Data folder) — re-filtering would drop additional samples and break reproducibility against the deposited data. The plan is rarefaction to even depth rather than whole-sample removal — rarefaction via rarefy_even_depth normalizes depth but does not exclude shallow samples the way the library-size QC does. Analysis target is raw sequence reads, not a feature/OTU table — read-level filtering (e.g., Phred <20 runs) is a separate earlier step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Drops microbiome samples whose total sequencing library size falls below a minimum read threshold (MiSurv default: 3,000 reads) during quality control, so downstream survival and composition analyses are not driven by under-sequenced samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/spectrum.05059-22
skills.summary: Drops microbiome samples whose total sequencing library size falls below a minimum read threshold (MiSurv default: 3,000 reads) during quality control, so downstream survival and composition analyses are not driven by under-sequenced samples.

skills.search_text: sar-gamma0-plot-summary-statistics Use when you have Sentinel-1 gamma_0 temporal stacks (VH/VV GeoTIFFs), acquisition dates, and plot-center shapefiles and need per-plot radar structural metrics as predictors for ecological models (CCoA, NMDS composition models). Input is raw GRDH digital-number imagery — it must first be converted to gamma_0 via the SNAP batch chain (orbit file, border/thermal noise removal, calibration, terrain flattening, range-doppler terrain correction) before summary statistics are meaningful. Analysis requires understorey-sensitive metrics: C-band SAR has weak permeability through overstorey layers, so species richness and phylogenetic diversity of understorey-driven groups are poorly predicted from these radar statistics. Spatial speckle smoothing is explicitly desired — this workflow smooths speckle implicitly in time via multi-acquisition medians instead, and adding spatial filtering would cause further loss of geometric detail. http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Compute pixel- and neighborhood-based summary statistics (e.g., mean backscatter and GLCM texture) from temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 VH/VV gamma_0 data for fixed plot areas (1-ha), producing the radar predictor table (S1_mean.csv) used in biodiversity models. Median compositing across acquisitions suppresses speckle implicitly in time rather than in space. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Compute pixel- and neighborhood-based summary statistics (e.g., mean backscatter and GLCM texture) from temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 VH/VV gamma_0 data for fixed plot areas (1-ha), producing the radar predictor table (S1_mean.csv) used in biodiversity models. Median compositing across acquisitions suppresses speckle implicitly in time rather than in space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw GRDH digital-number imagery — it must first be converted to gamma_0 via the SNAP batch chain (orbit file, border/thermal noise removal, calibration, terrain flattening, range-doppler terrain correction) before summary statistics are meaningful. Analysis requires understorey-sensitive metrics: C-band SAR has weak permeability through overstorey layers, so species richness and phylogenetic diversity of understorey-driven groups are poorly predicted from these radar statistics. Spatial speckle smoothing is explicitly desired — this workflow smooths speckle implicitly in time via multi-acquisition medians instead, and adding spatial filtering would cause further loss of geometric detail.

skills.search_text: sar-radiometric-calibration-beta0 Use when Sentinel-1 GRDH IW data held as uncalibrated digital numbers (DN) must be converted to calibrated backscatter (beta_0) comparable across acquisitions and sensors, prior to terrain flattening to gamma_0. The scene is SLC data or the analysis requires phase/interferometric information — the study only used backscatter coefficients from GRDH and explicitly avoided deriving GRDH from SLC. The input is already calibrated (beta_0/gamma_0) or already orthorectified gamma_0 in geographic coordinates — recalibration would be redundant or wrong. You intend to apply spatial speckle filtering instead — this chain deliberately skips it, relying on temporal median compositing over multiple acquisitions for speckle suppression. Radiometric calibration converts uncalibrated Sentinel-1 GRDH IW digital numbers (DN) into beta_0 radar brightness coefficients using SNAP's Calibration operator. It is the required data-level precursor to radiometric terrain flattening that yields gamma_0. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x

skills.search_text: sars-cov-2-lineage-inference Use when you have VCF files of low-frequency SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., from ARTIC-amplicon wastewater sequencing) and need to detect which lineages are present and estimate their relative abundance over time. skills.summary: Infer SARS-CoV-2 lineage composition and per-lineage abundance metrics from wastewater NGS variant calls using the lineagespot R package, which matches detected mutations against lineage-characteristic mutation profiles (Pangolin rules / outbreak.info definitions).

skills.description: Use when profiling genome populations from metagenomic read mappings and you need per-scaffold coverage, breadth (fraction of reference bases covered ≥1 read), and nucleotide diversity from sorted .bam files plus a reference .fasta.
skills.name: scaffold-breadth-metric-computation
skills.search_text: scaffold-breadth-metric-computation Use when profiling genome populations from metagenomic read mappings and you need per-scaffold coverage, breadth (fraction of reference bases covered ≥1 read), and nucleotide diversity from sorted .bam files plus a reference .fasta. You only need fast read coverage/abundance estimates without microdiversity — a tool like CoverM's `coverm genome`/`coverm contig` is the article's suggested alternative for plain coverage and breadth Your .bam contains unpaired reads or pairs lacking proper orientation/insert size, minimum mapQ, or minimum nucleotide identity — these pairs are filtered out by default, so the metrics will not reflect them The task is strain-level comparison of two profiles rather than single-profile scaffold metrics — use inStrain's `compare` operation instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reconstructs inStrain's per-scaffold coverage, breadth, and nucleotide-diversity profiling module: tally per-position read depth and A/C/G/T counts from a sorted .bam against a reference .fasta, then aggregate mean/median coverage, breadth, unmasked breadth, expected breadth, and nucleotide diversity per scaffold. This is why the skill exists — breadth and microdiversity are the metrics inStrain reports for accurate genome comparisons. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Reconstructs inStrain's per-scaffold coverage, breadth, and nucleotide-diversity profiling module: tally per-position read depth and A/C/G/T counts from a sorted .bam against a reference .fasta, then aggregate mean/median coverage, breadth, unmasked breadth, expected breadth, and nucleotide diversity per scaffold. This is why the skill exists — breadth and microdiversity are the metrics inStrain reports for accurate genome comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need fast read coverage/abundance estimates without microdiversity — a tool like CoverM's `coverm genome`/`coverm contig` is the article's suggested alternative for plain coverage and breadth Your .bam contains unpaired reads or pairs lacking proper orientation/insert size, minimum mapQ, or minimum nucleotide identity — these pairs are filtered out by default, so the metrics will not reflect them The task is strain-level comparison of two profiles rather than single-profile scaffold metrics — use inStrain's `compare` operation instead

skills.name: scaffold-dereplication
skills.search_text: scaffold-dereplication Use when a viral scaffold FASTA contains redundant/duplicate sequences (e.g., multiple assemblies or fragmented genomes) and you need to collapse them pre-binning or investigate how vRhyme's composite merging joins scaffold pairs. Input is a whole (unfiltered) metagenome — vRhyme's performance on entire metagenomes has not been fully evaluated and it is built for viral scaffolds The goal is microbial binning — vRhyme is explicitly 'not meant to bin microbes' Composite mode output must be non-chimeric for downstream taxonomy — composite merging can produce artificially chimeric representative scaffolds http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Standalone scaffold dereplication in vRhyme using Mash sketching for rough duplicate grouping followed by Nucmer alignment and either 'longest' (keep one representative) or 'composite' (merge overlapping pairs) modes, optionally with --derep_only to skip binning entirely. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341

skills.description: Use when multiple network inference methods (e.g., 8 NI association matrices from correlation or direct-model tools) must be merged into one consensus co-occurrence network and edge weighting (not just vote counting) should drive edge selection.
skills.name: scaled-weight-normalization-and-summing
skills.search_text: scaled-weight-normalization-and-summing Use when multiple network inference methods (e.g., 8 NI association matrices from correlation or direct-model tools) must be merged into one consensus co-occurrence network and edge weighting (not just vote counting) should drive edge selection. You have only a single network inference result — consensus aggregation requires multiple (e.g., w=8) NI networks to normalize and sum. You want purely presence/absence edge selection by vote count; the simple voting (SV) algorithm, not scaled-sum, is the matching choice. Input is raw 16S sequence data upstream of network inference — the sequence processing (SP), OTU assignment, and correlation/direct inference steps must run first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 The scaled-sum (SS) consensus algorithm from the MiCoNE pipeline: max-normalize each network inference method's interaction scores, sum the scaled edge weights across the w networks, and retain an edge only when |s_j| exceeds (w-1) x theta. It produces a more robust consensus co-occurrence network than any single inference method. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: The scaled-sum (SS) consensus algorithm from the MiCoNE pipeline: max-normalize each network inference method's interaction scores, sum the scaled edge weights across the w networks, and retain an edge only when |s_j| exceeds (w-1) x theta. It produces a more robust consensus co-occurrence network than any single inference method.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether a sequence-clustering tool's wall-clock runtime grows linearly or quadratically with input set size N, or when reproducing published power-law runtime exponents at a fixed sequence-identity threshold.
skills.name: scaling-exponent-analysis-of-clustering-tools
skills.search_text: scaling-exponent-analysis-of-clustering-tools Use when benchmarking whether a sequence-clustering tool's wall-clock runtime grows linearly or quadratically with input set size N, or when reproducing published power-law runtime exponents at a fixed sequence-identity threshold. The goal is cluster quality (functional or annotation consistency) rather than runtime scaling — the article evaluates quality separately via GO annotations and Pfam. The input is not a sequence set amenable to nested random subsampling, so the N-dependence of runtime cannot be isolated. skills.summary: Attribution of disease-associated metagenomic genes (e.g., SCZ-associated gene Vpar_1847) to their organisms of origin via OMARU's read-level traceback phylogenetic-functional link module, which links taxa and genes in the metagenome.

skills.description: Use when temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 gamma_0 (VH and VV) plus an acquisition-dates table are available and you need pixel-based seasonal backscatter summaries (medians, differences, ratios) as forest-structure predictors.
skills.name: seasonal-backscatter-statistics-derivation
skills.search_text: seasonal-backscatter-statistics-derivation Use when temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 gamma_0 (VH and VV) plus an acquisition-dates table are available and you need pixel-based seasonal backscatter summaries (medians, differences, ratios) as forest-structure predictors. Input is raw Sentinel-1 GRDH digital numbers rather than pre-processed, terrain-flattened gamma_0 stacks (run the SNAP/GPT preprocessing chain first) You need to characterize the understorey layer — C-band SAR has weak permeability through overstorey layers and performs poorly for groups driven by understorey development A spatially explicit single-date backscatter product is required — this skill produces temporally aggregated summary statistics, not instantaneous scenes Derives per-pixel seasonal (yearly, summer, winter) summary statistics — median VV/VH gamma_0, VV−VH difference, VV/VH ratio, and winter-minus-summer differences — from temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 gamma_0 in R, using temporal medians to smooth speckle instead of spatial filtering. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Derives per-pixel seasonal (yearly, summer, winter) summary statistics — median VV/VH gamma_0, VV−VH difference, VV/VH ratio, and winter-minus-summer differences — from temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 gamma_0 in R, using temporal medians to smooth speckle instead of spatial filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Sentinel-1 GRDH digital numbers rather than pre-processed, terrain-flattened gamma_0 stacks (run the SNAP/GPT preprocessing chain first) You need to characterize the understorey layer — C-band SAR has weak permeability through overstorey layers and performs poorly for groups driven by understorey development A spatially explicit single-date backscatter product is required — this skill produces temporally aggregated summary statistics, not instantaneous scenes

skills.description: Use when a tabular time-series omics dataset with an embedded temporal feature (e.g., Herold et al. BWWTP metagenomics depth-of-coverage) should be screened for periodic or seasonal dynamics such as quartile envelopes tracing a sine-like curve.
skills.name: seasonal-pattern-identification-in-omics-time-series
skills.search_text: seasonal-pattern-identification-in-omics-time-series Use when a tabular time-series omics dataset with an embedded temporal feature (e.g., Herold et al. BWWTP metagenomics depth-of-coverage) should be screened for periodic or seasonal dynamics such as quartile envelopes tracing a sine-like curve. The input data has no embedded temporal feature — MOVIS's sanitizing step presupposes time-series data that passes its data quality checks Raw microarray-based data is the input, since such data cannot be used directly as input to MOVIS and must be preprocessed (quality controlled and filtered) The goal is linking taxa in metagenomics data — MOVIS is not explicitly designed to work with meta-omics data and no taxa linking is enabled http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Identify recurring (e.g., ~monthly sine-curve) temporal patterns in time-series multi-omics data by importing the tabular depth-of-coverage series into MOVIS, passing it through the importing/sanitizing/filtering core, and inspecting quartile envelopes (Q3 and upper limits) in a Whisker plot visualization. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.02.012

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data has no embedded temporal feature — MOVIS's sanitizing step presupposes time-series data that passes its data quality checks Raw microarray-based data is the input, since such data cannot be used directly as input to MOVIS and must be preprocessed (quality controlled and filtered) The goal is linking taxa in metagenomics data — MOVIS is not explicitly designed to work with meta-omics data and no taxa linking is enabled

skills.description: Use when raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads (isolate genomes or metagenomes) must be assembled around cas genes/CRISPR arrays without complete genome or metagenome assembly, e.g. when runtime or compute limits full metaSPAdes assembly.
skills.name: seed-based-read-subset-expansion
skills.search_text: seed-based-read-subset-expansion Use when raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads (isolate genomes or metagenomes) must be assembled around cas genes/CRISPR arrays without complete genome or metagenome assembly, e.g. when runtime or compute limits full metaSPAdes assembly. Input is already assembled contigs rather than raw unassembled sequencing reads — CasCollect is designed for raw FASTQ input A complete, unbiased metagenome assembly is required for purposes beyond CRISPR/Cas detection (e.g. strain-resolved binning of non-Cas loci) Data is not short paired-end Illumina reads (CasCollect targets short DNA sequencing reads; read lengths tested were 90–226 bp) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 CasCollect's targeted assembly strategy: seed reads matching cas genes (via HMMER against 120 Cas protein HMMs) or CRISPR array repeats (via VSEARCH in DNA mode) prime iterative VSEARCH expansion cycles (default five cycles at 95% identity) that pull in overlapping reads, so only CRISPR/Cas loci are assembled instead of the full metagenome. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: CasCollect's targeted assembly strategy: seed reads matching cas genes (via HMMER against 120 Cas protein HMMs) or CRISPR array repeats (via VSEARCH in DNA mode) prime iterative VSEARCH expansion cycles (default five cycles at 95% identity) that pull in overlapping reads, so only CRISPR/Cas loci are assembled instead of the full metagenome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled contigs rather than raw unassembled sequencing reads — CasCollect is designed for raw FASTQ input A complete, unbiased metagenome assembly is required for purposes beyond CRISPR/Cas detection (e.g. strain-resolved binning of non-Cas loci) Data is not short paired-end Illumina reads (CasCollect targets short DNA sequencing reads; read lengths tested were 90–226 bp)

skills.description: Use when metagenomic reads need de novo-assembled seed contigs before a contig-extension step: input is adaptor-trimmed FASTQ and the downstream tool expects a FASTA seed contig set.
skills.name: seed-contig-generation-for-extension
skills.search_text: seed-contig-generation-for-extension Use when metagenomic reads need de novo-assembled seed contigs before a contig-extension step: input is adaptor-trimmed FASTQ and the downstream tool expects a FASTA seed contig set. A seed contig set already exists (e.g. the examples folder's BKV_seed_1000_867.fa) — skip assembly and feed that FASTA directly to the extender Reads still contain adaptors — preprocess fastq by removing adaptors first, since extension quality depends on it The goal is reference-based mapping rather than de novo assembly of viral metagenomic reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generate the initial seed contigs that ContigExtender consumes by running SPAdes 3.13.0 in metaSPAdes mode (-meta) with multi-k sizes 21, 33, 55, 77 on adaptor-preprocessed metagenomic FASTQ reads, then passing the resulting contigs.fasta downstream for recursive extension. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04038-2
skills.summary: Generate the initial seed contigs that ContigExtender consumes by running SPAdes 3.13.0 in metaSPAdes mode (-meta) with multi-k sizes 21, 33, 55, 77 on adaptor-preprocessed metagenomic FASTQ reads, then passing the resulting contigs.fasta downstream for recursive extension.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A seed contig set already exists (e.g. the examples folder's BKV_seed_1000_867.fa) — skip assembly and feed that FASTA directly to the extender Reads still contain adaptors — preprocess fastq by removing adaptors first, since extension quality depends on it The goal is reference-based mapping rather than de novo assembly of viral metagenomic reads

skills.description: Use when raw, unassembled Illumina sequencing reads must be reduced to a small seed-read subset matching cas proteins or CRISPR repeats before targeted assembly, especially for large or metagenomic datasets where full assembly is too slow.
skills.name: seed-read-subset-selection
skills.search_text: seed-read-subset-selection Use when raw, unassembled Illumina sequencing reads must be reduced to a small seed-read subset matching cas proteins or CRISPR repeats before targeted assembly, especially for large or metagenomic datasets where full assembly is too slow. The input is already an assembled genome or contig set — seed generation targets raw, unassembled reads and adds no value there. You need a complete de novo assembly of the whole metagenome rather than only CRISPR/Cas (or other targeted specialty gene) regions. The genes of interest lack any profile HMM or reference nucleotide sequence to search against, and no user-defined seed FASTA can be supplied. Generates a compact 'seed' read set from raw Illumina FASTQ reads that match cas genes or CRISPR repeats, using CasCollect's three optional seed-generation modes: protein-mode HMM search of translated reads, DNA-mode VSEARCH identity matching to repeat sequences, and user-defined FASTA seeds. This avoids assembling entire genomes and primes only the CRISPR/Cas-encoding regions for assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Generates a compact 'seed' read set from raw Illumina FASTQ reads that match cas genes or CRISPR repeats, using CasCollect's three optional seed-generation modes: protein-mode HMM search of translated reads, DNA-mode VSEARCH identity matching to repeat sequences, and user-defined FASTA seeds. This avoids assembling entire genomes and primes only the CRISPR/Cas-encoding regions for assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an assembled genome or contig set — seed generation targets raw, unassembled reads and adds no value there. You need a complete de novo assembly of the whole metagenome rather than only CRISPR/Cas (or other targeted specialty gene) regions. The genes of interest lack any profile HMM or reference nucleotide sequence to search against, and no user-defined seed FASTA can be supplied.

skills.description: Use when raw DIAMOND annotation output is line-by-line per-read text and you need condensed, descending-sorted organism or SEED Subsystems functional abundance tables for downstream statistics.
skills.name: seed-subsystems-hierarchy-parsing
skills.search_text: seed-subsystems-hierarchy-parsing Use when raw DIAMOND annotation output is line-by-line per-read text and you need condensed, descending-sorted organism or SEED Subsystems functional abundance tables for downstream statistics. Input is already a condensed feature/abundance table ready for DESeq import — aggregation would double-count or re-sort an already summarized file. Only per-read alignment statistics (e.g. identity, bit scores) are needed — this skill reduces lines to counts and discards alignment detail. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Aggregation-stage parsing of per-read DIAMOND annotation output into ranked abundance summary tables, preserving the SEED Subsystems hierarchical ontology levels (1/2/3) for functional annotations alongside organism-level counts. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-018-2189-z
skills.summary: Aggregation-stage parsing of per-read DIAMOND annotation output into ranked abundance summary tables, preserving the SEED Subsystems hierarchical ontology levels (1/2/3) for functional annotations alongside organism-level counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a condensed feature/abundance table ready for DESeq import — aggregation would double-count or re-sort an already summarized file. Annotations come from a web service such as MG-RAST rather than local DIAMOND output; this skill operates on SAMSA2's per-read DIAMOND outfiles. Only per-read alignment statistics (e.g. identity, bit scores) are needed — this skill reduces lines to counts and discards alignment detail.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a taxonomic classifier's generalization to species not represented in its training label vocabulary, e.g. on Greengenes2 test sequences held out from training.
skills.name: seen-unseen-sequence-stratification
skills.search_text: seen-unseen-sequence-stratification Use when evaluating a taxonomic classifier's generalization to species not represented in its training label vocabulary, e.g. on Greengenes2 test sequences held out from training. You only need overall test-set metrics (species accuracy/F1/ECE) — use full-test-set evaluation instead You need to evaluate calibration (ECE) or benchmark against DADA2/QIIME 2 — stratification by Seen/Unseen is orthogonal to those analyses Your test species labels are all present in the training vocabulary, leaving an empty Unseen subset http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3301 Stratifies held-out test sequences by whether their species label is present ('Seen') or absent ('Unseen') from the training vocabulary, then computes per-rank top-1 accuracy on the Unseen subset to quantify generalization to novel taxa. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Stratifies held-out test sequences by whether their species label is present ('Seen') or absent ('Unseen') from the training vocabulary, then computes per-rank top-1 accuracy on the Unseen subset to quantify generalization to novel taxa.

skills.description: Use when comparing two genome assembly versions for how completely they represent segmental duplications, or when quantifying SD representation via contig-to-SD coverage fractions.

The question is overall assembly accuracy (misassemblies, substitution/copy-number error) measured against a reference rather than representation of duplicated sequences The comparison target is a single genome's coverage of a reference (e.g. hg19 alignment for genome coverage), not a side-by-side contrast of two assembly versions against SD sequences Reads or scaffolds rather than contigs are the input; the reported SD-representation metric is computed from contigs http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 A comparison procedure that aligns de novo assembly contigs (YH v1 vs SOAPdenovo2 YH v2) against 134 Mb of published human segmental duplication (SD) sequences from the hg19 UCSC SD track, computing the fraction of SD sequence sufficiently covered (>=90% per SD) to quantify how well an assembly represents duplicated regions. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: A comparison procedure that aligns de novo assembly contigs (YH v1 vs SOAPdenovo2 YH v2) against 134 Mb of published human segmental duplication (SD) sequences from the hg19 UCSC SD track, computing the fraction of SD sequence sufficiently covered (>=90% per SD) to quantify how well an assembly represents duplicated regions.

skills.description: Use when simulating longitudinal metagenomic samples that require injected within-strain mutations to follow prescribed per-timepoint allele-frequency trajectories emulating positive or purifying selection with STEMSim.
skills.name: selection-trajectory-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: selection-trajectory-parameter-configuration Use when simulating longitudinal metagenomic samples that require injected within-strain mutations to follow prescribed per-timepoint allele-frequency trajectories emulating positive or purifying selection with STEMSim. Real metagenomic data on low-depth or poorly characterized species — STEMSim only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes Static single-timepoint communities without a longitudinal design, since trajectories are defined per timepoint across samples When the goal is simulating de novo community abundance rather than within-strain mutation injection — use CAMISIM alone Configure STEMSim config.txt files to specify allele-frequency trajectories of injected within-strain mutations across longitudinal timepoints (e.g., increasing 0.2/0.5/0.8/1 for positive selection; decreasing 0.8/0.5/0.3/0 for purifying selection), so that downstream metagenomic reads carry mutations at the intended frequencies. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad302
skills.summary: Configure STEMSim config.txt files to specify allele-frequency trajectories of injected within-strain mutations across longitudinal timepoints (e.g., increasing 0.2/0.5/0.8/1 for positive selection; decreasing 0.8/0.5/0.3/0 for purifying selection), so that downstream metagenomic reads carry mutations at the intended frequencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real metagenomic data on low-depth or poorly characterized species — STEMSim only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes Static single-timepoint communities without a longitudinal design, since trajectories are defined per timepoint across samples When the goal is simulating de novo community abundance rather than within-strain mutation injection — use CAMISIM alone

skills.description: Use when implementing or reconstructing DeepMicrobes' Embed + LSTM + Attention species classifier: you have k-mer-embedded DNA reads and need a length-independent, attention-pooled representation for taxonomic classification.
skills.name: self-attention-mechanism-implementation
skills.search_text: self-attention-mechanism-implementation Use when implementing or reconstructing DeepMicrobes' Embed + LSTM + Attention species classifier: you have k-mer-embedded DNA reads and need a length-independent, attention-pooled representation for taxonomic classification. Reads whose lengths and error profiles differ strongly from training data (e.g. long-read sequencing) — the paper notes retraining might be required to adapt Classifying species newly added to the database — adding new species requires retraining the entire deep neural network Abundance estimation-only tasks where a simpler k-mer or alignment classifier already suffices and the attention architecture's read-level precision/recall gains are not the goal http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements the r-row self-attention layer of DeepMicrobes (A = softmax(Ws2 tanh(H^T Ws1))) that aggregates a BiLSTM's hidden states into a fixed-size attention-weighted matrix M = H·A, which is then classified by a 3-layer ReLU MLP + softmax over taxonomic labels. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Implements the r-row self-attention layer of DeepMicrobes (A = softmax(Ws2 tanh(H^T Ws1))) that aggregates a BiLSTM's hidden states into a fixed-size attention-weighted matrix M = H·A, which is then classified by a 3-layer ReLU MLP + softmax over taxonomic labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads whose lengths and error profiles differ strongly from training data (e.g. long-read sequencing) — the paper notes retraining might be required to adapt Classifying species newly added to the database — adding new species requires retraining the entire deep neural network Abundance estimation-only tasks where a simpler k-mer or alignment classifier already suffices and the attention architecture's read-level precision/recall gains are not the goal
