skills.description: Use when Illumina FASTQ reads (real or ART-simulated) must be mapped to a fungal taxonomic database and off-target bacterial mapping must be quantified or minimized via strict alignment-length and quality thresholds.
skills.name: sequencing-read-alignment-filtering
skills.search_text: sequencing-read-alignment-filtering Use when Illumina FASTQ reads (real or ART-simulated) must be mapped to a fungal taxonomic database and off-target bacterial mapping must be quantified or minimized via strict alignment-length and quality thresholds. Input is not Illumina next-generation sequencing reads — the article's ART simulation and bowtie2 filtering were designed and benchmarked for Illumina-formatted output only The goal is bacterial or general taxonomic profiling, not human mycobiome specificity assessment — FunOMIC-T is by design restricted to fungal sequences and would under-report bacteria Functional (protein-level) annotation is the goal — use the DIAMOND blastx route against FunOMIC-P (coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value < 10e-10) rather than bowtie2 read mapping to FunOMIC-T http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Aligns simulated or real Illumina next-generation sequencing reads to the FunOMIC-T fungal marker-gene database with bowtie2 and applies a strict samtools mapping filter (>80% of read length aligned, q-score >30) to enforce fungal specificity in mycobiome profiling. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Aligns simulated or real Illumina next-generation sequencing reads to the FunOMIC-T fungal marker-gene database with bowtie2 and applies a strict samtools mapping filter (>80% of read length aligned, q-score >30) to enforce fungal specificity in mycobiome profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not Illumina next-generation sequencing reads — the article's ART simulation and bowtie2 filtering were designed and benchmarked for Illumina-formatted output only The goal is bacterial or general taxonomic profiling, not human mycobiome specificity assessment — FunOMIC-T is by design restricted to fungal sequences and would under-report bacteria Functional (protein-level) annotation is the goal — use the DIAMOND blastx route against FunOMIC-P (coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value < 10e-10) rather than bowtie2 read mapping to FunOMIC-T

skills.summary: Performs the CAMAMED pre-processing stage: converting SRA archives to FASTQ/FASTA with fastq-dump (SRA Toolkit v2.8.2), running FastQC v0.11.5 quality control on each converted read file, and extracting per-sample sequence statistics with SeqKit v0.10.1.

skills.description: Use when comparing classification speed and accuracy of a lightweight read classifier against an aligner baseline on real nanopore reads, with a gold standard derived from the baseline under a MAPQ threshold.
skills.name: sequencing-throughput-benchmarking
skills.search_text: sequencing-throughput-benchmarking Use when comparing classification speed and accuracy of a lightweight read classifier against an aligner baseline on real nanopore reads, with a gold standard derived from the baseline under a MAPQ threshold. The goal is direct interaction with the nanopore Read Until API — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences, not raw electrical signal batches The reference contains few genomes (e.g., single human genome), where the throughput advantage over minimap2 is limited and only expected to improve as the number of genomes in the reference increases Input reads are already classified by a trusted method and no speed/accuracy comparison is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark per-read classification throughput and accuracy (F1) of a fast read classifier like SPUMONI against an aligner baseline like minimap2 on the same preprocessed read set, using an independently derived gold standard. This skill captures the paper's protocol for showing that SPUMONI is ~11.9-12x faster than minimap2 with comparable or better F1 on pan-genomic indexes. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Benchmark per-read classification throughput and accuracy (F1) of a fast read classifier like SPUMONI against an aligner baseline like minimap2 on the same preprocessed read set, using an independently derived gold standard. This skill captures the paper's protocol for showing that SPUMONI is ~11.9-12x faster than minimap2 with comparable or better F1 on pan-genomic indexes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is direct interaction with the nanopore Read Until API — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences, not raw electrical signal batches The reference contains few genomes (e.g., single human genome), where the throughput advantage over minimap2 is limited and only expected to improve as the number of genomes in the reference increases Input reads are already classified by a trusted method and no speed/accuracy comparison is needed

skills.description: Use when two protein clustering or assignment methods have been run over the same protein universe and you need to measure non-shared fraction and union coverage gain from integration.
skills.name: set-union-coverage-calculation
skills.search_text: set-union-coverage-calculation Use when two protein clustering or assignment methods have been run over the same protein universe and you need to measure non-shared fraction and union coverage gain from integration. Only one clustering method's assignments are available — set operations require two partitions over the same proteins The two method outputs cover different protein universes or use non-matching protein identifiers without prior harmonization You need cluster-level (rather than protein-membership-level) agreement metrics such as pairwise Jaccard between Snekmer clusters http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 Quantifies per-protein overlap between two clustering partitions (e.g., Snekmer AAR-kmer clusters and MMseqs2 sequence-similarity clusters) via intersection, symmetric difference, and union sets, and computes the coverage gain from integrating both methods — here raising assignment from ~50-60% per method to ~85% combined on the 10-genome Uniprot benchmark. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad005
skills.summary: Quantifies per-protein overlap between two clustering partitions (e.g., Snekmer AAR-kmer clusters and MMseqs2 sequence-similarity clusters) via intersection, symmetric difference, and union sets, and computes the coverage gain from integrating both methods — here raising assignment from ~50-60% per method to ~85% combined on the 10-genome Uniprot benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one clustering method's assignments are available — set operations require two partitions over the same proteins The two method outputs cover different protein universes or use non-matching protein identifiers without prior harmonization You need cluster-level (rather than protein-membership-level) agreement metrics such as pairwise Jaccard between Snekmer clusters

skills.search_text: sex-chromosome-hemizygosity-verification Use when evaluating diploid-state recovery of a de novo human genome assembly and you must verify that single-copy (hemizygous) X regions are reconstructed as one contig rather than incorrectly diploid or uncovered. skills.description: Use when the task requires running a bulk RNA-seq differential-expression analysis on a gene count matrix with sample metadata through a GUI-driven Shiny app rather than hand-written R scripts.
skills.name: shiny-app-bulk-rnaseq-workflow-execution
skills.search_text: shiny-app-bulk-rnaseq-workflow-execution Use when the task requires running a bulk RNA-seq differential-expression analysis on a gene count matrix with sample metadata through a GUI-driven Shiny app rather than hand-written R scripts. Input is single-cell RNA-seq data — use NASQAR's SeuratV3Wizard instead, which is the single-cell Shiny interface to Seurat. The task is count preprocessing/merging rather than differential expression — GeneCountMerger handles merging individual gene count files (e.g., htseq output), and it will not work if the gene columns do not match across files. A scripted, reproducible DESeq2 pipeline with custom model fitting is required — the Shiny wrapper is aimed at researchers avoiding code, not at programmatic workflow execution. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Executes a bulk RNA-seq differential gene expression workflow through NASQAR's DESeq2Shiny Shiny app, which wraps the DESeq2 R package (negative binomial model) behind an intuitive GUI so non-programming experts can upload counts, run DE analysis, and export results without scripting. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03577-4
skills.summary: Executes a bulk RNA-seq differential gene expression workflow through NASQAR's DESeq2Shiny Shiny app, which wraps the DESeq2 R package (negative binomial model) behind an intuitive GUI so non-programming experts can upload counts, run DE analysis, and export results without scripting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq data — use NASQAR's SeuratV3Wizard instead, which is the single-cell Shiny interface to Seurat. The task is count preprocessing/merging rather than differential expression — GeneCountMerger handles merging individual gene count files (e.g., htseq output), and it will not work if the gene columns do not match across files. A scripted, reproducible DESeq2 pipeline with custom model fitting is required — the Shiny wrapper is aimed at researchers avoiding code, not at programmatic workflow execution.

skills.name: short-read-alignment-to-host-reference
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-to-host-reference Use when microbial short- or long-read (meta)genomic FASTQ (single or paired, optionally gzip-compressed) is contaminated with human host sequences that must be removed for ethical and legal reasons. Input reads are already non-host or host-depleted (e.g. the bundled tuberculosis sample yields reads_removed_proportion of 0.0) and decontamination would add no value The goal is to keep host reads and discard microbial reads — use `hostile clean --invert` instead of the default removal direction The goal is to mask human reads with 'N' in place (as NCBI's sra-human-scrubber does by default) rather than remove aligned reads from the output FASTQ http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Streaming decontamination of microbial FASTQ reads by aligning them to a human reference index (Bowtie2 for short reads, Minimap2 for long reads) and discarding aligned reads together with their mates, as implemented in Hostile. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad728
skills.summary: Streaming decontamination of microbial FASTQ reads by aligning them to a human reference index (Bowtie2 for short reads, Minimap2 for long reads) and discarding aligned reads together with their mates, as implemented in Hostile.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already non-host or host-depleted (e.g. the bundled tuberculosis sample yields reads_removed_proportion of 0.0) and decontamination would add no value The goal is to keep host reads and discard microbial reads — use `hostile clean --invert` instead of the default removal direction The goal is to mask human reads with 'N' in place (as NCBI's sra-human-scrubber does by default) rather than remove aligned reads from the output FASTQ

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify cross-mapping between a query sequence set (e.g., fungal marker genes) and a reference catalog, or validate taxonomic database specificity via simulated read mapping.
skills.name: short-read-alignment-to-reference-catalog
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-to-reference-catalog Use when you need to quantify cross-mapping between a query sequence set (e.g., fungal marker genes) and a reference catalog, or validate taxonomic database specificity via simulated read mapping. Query and reference are proteins/translated sequences — use Diamond blastx with coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10 thresholds instead Input is a functional profiling task where reads should be annotated against FunOMIC-P rather than tested for cross-mapping against a bacterial reference catalog The query sequence set is small enough to align directly without ART read simulation (simulation was only needed because of memory limits) http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns short sequencing reads (real or simulated) against a large reference catalog (e.g., the UHGG catalog of 204,938 non-redundant gut prokaryote genomes or the FunOMIC-T fungal marker-gene database) with bowtie2, then applies stringent Samtools-based mapping filters to quantify cross-mapping/contamination rates. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Aligns short sequencing reads (real or simulated) against a large reference catalog (e.g., the UHGG catalog of 204,938 non-redundant gut prokaryote genomes or the FunOMIC-T fungal marker-gene database) with bowtie2, then applies stringent Samtools-based mapping filters to quantify cross-mapping/contamination rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query and reference are proteins/translated sequences — use Diamond blastx with coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10 thresholds instead Input is a functional profiling task where reads should be annotated against FunOMIC-P rather than tested for cross-mapping against a bacterial reference catalog The query sequence set is small enough to align directly without ART read simulation (simulation was only needed because of memory limits)

skills.description: Use when you have reference-free variant calls (KisSNP2-format fasta / .snp file from ebwt2InDel) and an available reference genome, and you need reference-coordinate .vcf entries for downstream validation or comparison.
skills.name: short-read-alignment-to-reference-genome
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-to-reference-genome Use when you have reference-free variant calls (KisSNP2-format fasta / .snp file from ebwt2InDel) and an available reference genome, and you need reference-coordinate .vcf entries for downstream validation or comparison. No reference genome is available for the organism — ebwt2InDel is designed precisely for reference-free discovery, and alignment cannot place calls in reference coordinates Input reads contain characters other than A/C/G/T (e.g. 'N') — reads must be filtered or N replaced/removed before the upstream ebwt2InDel step You need genotypes/haplotypes rather than variant positions — this pipeline only maps mismatch/INDEL records to reference coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Converts reference-free SNP/INDEL calls from ebwt2InDel into VCF format by aligning variant-context fragments against the hg38 Human assembly via the snp2vcf pipeline (seqtk -> bwa-mem -> sam2vcf). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Converts reference-free SNP/INDEL calls from ebwt2InDel into VCF format by aligning variant-context fragments against the hg38 Human assembly via the snp2vcf pipeline (seqtk -> bwa-mem -> sam2vcf).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference genome is available for the organism — ebwt2InDel is designed precisely for reference-free discovery, and alignment cannot place calls in reference coordinates Input reads contain characters other than A/C/G/T (e.g. 'N') — reads must be filtered or N replaced/removed before the upstream ebwt2InDel step You need genotypes/haplotypes rather than variant positions — this pipeline only maps mismatch/INDEL records to reference coordinates

skills.description: Use when raw 10x Chromium paired-end FASTQ reads must be mapped to hg38 as a prerequisite for barcode-aware duplicate removal, fragment inference, and read coverage (CR) subsampling.
skills.name: short-read-alignment-to-reference-genome
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-to-reference-genome Use when raw 10x Chromium paired-end FASTQ reads must be mapped to hg38 as a prerequisite for barcode-aware duplicate removal, fragment inference, and read coverage (CR) subsampling. The goal is de novo assembly directly from the raw data without subsampling to matched CR across libraries — use Supernova2 on the full library instead. Input is long-read PacBio or Oxford Nanopore (ONT) data; Long Ranger and this fragment-inference logic are specific to 10x Linked-Read short reads. The aim is simulation of new Linked-Reads rather than processing real libraries — use LRTK-SIM directly with its config parameters (CF, CR, Mu_F, SR). http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Align 10x Linked-Read paired-end reads to the hg38 human reference with the Long Ranger pipeline as the first step of the LRTK-SIM subsampling workflow, preserving barcode information so PCR duplicates can be removed in a barcode-aware manner before DNA fragments are inferred. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Align 10x Linked-Read paired-end reads to the hg38 human reference with the Long Ranger pipeline as the first step of the LRTK-SIM subsampling workflow, preserving barcode information so PCR duplicates can be removed in a barcode-aware manner before DNA fragments are inferred.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo assembly directly from the raw data without subsampling to matched CR across libraries — use Supernova2 on the full library instead. Input is long-read PacBio or Oxford Nanopore (ONT) data; Long Ranger and this fragment-inference logic are specific to 10x Linked-Read short reads. The aim is simulation of new Linked-Reads rather than processing real libraries — use LRTK-SIM directly with its config parameters (CF, CR, Mu_F, SR).

skills.description: Use when a draft scaffold FASTA contains N-run wildcards between contigs and paired-end short-read data is available to locally reassemble and fill scaffold gap regions.
skills.name: short-read-alignment-to-scaffolds
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-to-scaffolds Use when a draft scaffold FASTA contains N-run wildcards between contigs and paired-end short-read data is available to locally reassemble and fill scaffold gap regions. The assembly is a fresh de novo run from reads only — use the full SOAPdenovo2 pregraph-contig-map-scaff pipeline with the -F flag instead of standalone gap closing The scaffolds contain no N-wildcard gaps to fill Only single-end or mate-pair data with inadequate physical coverage of gaps is available and no PE library with asm_flags=4 can be supplied http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Close N-wildcard gaps in draft scaffolds by locally reassembling all short reads aligned at each gap using SOAPdenovo2's GapCloser, which considers reads aligned across all previous iterative cycles rather than only the current cycle. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2047-217x-1-18
skills.summary: Close N-wildcard gaps in draft scaffolds by locally reassembling all short reads aligned at each gap using SOAPdenovo2's GapCloser, which considers reads aligned across all previous iterative cycles rather than only the current cycle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembly is a fresh de novo run from reads only — use the full SOAPdenovo2 pregraph-contig-map-scaff pipeline with the -F flag instead of standalone gap closing The scaffolds contain no N-wildcard gaps to fill Only single-end or mate-pair data with inadequate physical coverage of gaps is available and no PE library with asm_flags=4 can be supplied

skills.description: Use when raw sequencing reads were simulated by software other than CAMISIM (e.g., ART) and must be placed against a reference genome (.fas) as input to STEMSIM's reads mode.
skills.name: short-read-alignment-with-bowtie2
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-with-bowtie2 Use when raw sequencing reads were simulated by software other than CAMISIM (e.g., ART) and must be placed against a reference genome (.fas) as input to STEMSIM's reads mode. Input is already the output directory of CAMISIM — use STEMSIM's 'camisim' mode instead, which reads CAMISIM's own genome_to_id.tsv mapping and does not require re-alignment Reads originate from more than one reference genome/species — the reads mode is designed for simulated raw reads from one reference genome Real metagenomic data from species with low depth or poorly characterized genomes — the README warns STEMSIM only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Align externally produced raw metagenomic reads (fastq or unaligned BAM, e.g., from ART) to a supplied reference genome with Bowtie2, then process alignments with samtools via pysam so STEMSIM can establish read-to-genome placement before applying its within-strain mutation model. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad302
skills.summary: Align externally produced raw metagenomic reads (fastq or unaligned BAM, e.g., from ART) to a supplied reference genome with Bowtie2, then process alignments with samtools via pysam so STEMSIM can establish read-to-genome placement before applying its within-strain mutation model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already the output directory of CAMISIM — use STEMSIM's 'camisim' mode instead, which reads CAMISIM's own genome_to_id.tsv mapping and does not require re-alignment Reads originate from more than one reference genome/species — the reads mode is designed for simulated raw reads from one reference genome Real metagenomic data from species with low depth or poorly characterized genomes — the README warns STEMSIM only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes

skills.description: Use when you need to partition bacterial long- and short-read FASTQs against a draft assembly so only chromosomal reads are discarded and plasmid-derived reads (mapped to non-chromosome contigs or unmapped) are retained for downstream assembly.
skills.name: short-read-and-long-read-mapping
skills.search_text: short-read-and-long-read-mapping Use when you need to partition bacterial long- and short-read FASTQs against a draft assembly so only chromosomal reads are discarded and plasmid-derived reads (mapped to non-chromosome contigs or unmapped) are retained for downstream assembly. Input is already an assembled genome or plasmid FASTA rather than raw read sets — no mapping-based read filtering applies Only short reads are available with no long-read assembly to map against (Plassembler's chromosomal-read removal requires the Flye/Raven long-read-only assembly) Reads come from a non-bacterial or multi-isolate metagenome, where a single chromosomal contig classification against the '-c' threshold is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Maps both long-read and paired short-read sets onto a long-read-only assembly (Flye draft) with minimap2, then uses SAMtools to keep reads on non-chromosome (putative plasmid) contigs plus unmapped reads, removing only chromosomal reads before hybrid assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Maps both long-read and paired short-read sets onto a long-read-only assembly (Flye draft) with minimap2, then uses SAMtools to keep reads on non-chromosome (putative plasmid) contigs plus unmapped reads, removing only chromosomal reads before hybrid assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an assembled genome or plasmid FASTA rather than raw read sets — no mapping-based read filtering applies Only short reads are available with no long-read assembly to map against (Plassembler's chromosomal-read removal requires the Flye/Raven long-read-only assembly) Reads come from a non-bacterial or multi-isolate metagenome, where a single chromosomal contig classification against the '-c' threshold is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when evaluating clustering accuracy (ACC) of a DNA sequence clustering tool on synthetic FASTA datasets, especially regimes excluded from the iDeLUCS paper: average read length <500 bp or expected cluster counts above 200 (e.g. ~5000).
skills.name: short-read-clustering-benchmarking
skills.search_text: short-read-clustering-benchmarking Use when evaluating clustering accuracy (ACC) of a DNA sequence clustering tool on synthetic FASTA datasets, especially regimes excluded from the iDeLUCS paper: average read length <500 bp or expected cluster counts above 200 (e.g. ~5000). Input is real biological data with unknown cluster structure and no ground-truth labels — the workflow requires GT cluster_id columns for ACC computation The question is about ACC results reported in the iDeLUCS paper itself — such results do not exist for short reads (<500 bp) or >200 clusters; the paper explicitly deferred these to future work Sequences require alignment-based clustering or taxonomic identifiers — iDeLUCS is explicitly alignment-free and identifier-free http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Benchmark alignment-free clustering of DNA sequences (including short reads <500 bp and large cluster counts >200) using iDeLUCS, a deep learning tool that clusters genomic k-mer signatures without alignment, and compute clustering accuracy (ACC) against ground-truth labels held out from training. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad508
skills.summary: Benchmark alignment-free clustering of DNA sequences (including short reads <500 bp and large cluster counts >200) using iDeLUCS, a deep learning tool that clusters genomic k-mer signatures without alignment, and compute clustering accuracy (ACC) against ground-truth labels held out from training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real biological data with unknown cluster structure and no ground-truth labels — the workflow requires GT cluster_id columns for ACC computation The question is about ACC results reported in the iDeLUCS paper itself — such results do not exist for short reads (<500 bp) or >200 clusters; the paper explicitly deferred these to future work Sequences require alignment-based clustering or taxonomic identifiers — iDeLUCS is explicitly alignment-free and identifier-free

skills.description: Use when you must benchmark a retrieval/assembly pipeline across sequencing depths and only full-coverage paired-end Illumina reads (e.g. D. gyrociliatus PRJEB37657) are available — subsample to simulate lower-coverage genome-skimming arms.
skills.name: short-read-coverage-subsampling
skills.search_text: short-read-coverage-subsampling Use when you must benchmark a retrieval/assembly pipeline across sequencing depths and only full-coverage paired-end Illumina reads (e.g. D. gyrociliatus PRJEB37657) are available — subsample to simulate lower-coverage genome-skimming arms. Your analysis question does not involve sequencing-depth response (e.g. full-coverage assemblies are already available and only a single-depth retrieval run is needed). Input reads are not paired-end, or the FASTQ naming structure does not allow selecting corresponding read pairs — random independent subsampling would break read-pair correspondence and bias assemblies. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Generates a sequencing-depth gradient by randomly selecting corresponding read pairs from paired-end short-read FASTQ data (Subsample.jl), producing coverage arms (e.g. 1×, 3×, 5×, 10×, 20×, 40×) used to benchmark marker-retrieval accuracy and runtime across depths. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Generates a sequencing-depth gradient by randomly selecting corresponding read pairs from paired-end short-read FASTQ data (Subsample.jl), producing coverage arms (e.g. 1×, 3×, 5×, 10×, 20×, 40×) used to benchmark marker-retrieval accuracy and runtime across depths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your analysis question does not involve sequencing-depth response (e.g. full-coverage assemblies are already available and only a single-depth retrieval run is needed). Input reads are not paired-end, or the FASTQ naming structure does not allow selecting corresponding read pairs — random independent subsampling would break read-pair correspondence and bias assemblies.

skills.description: Use when WGS read pairs must be aligned against known MLST allele sequences so per-read allele match/mismatch evidence (e.g., Phred-weighted mismatches) can be extracted as ILP input for strain deconvolution.
skills.name: short-read-mapping-to-allele-database
skills.search_text: short-read-mapping-to-allele-database Use when WGS read pairs must be aligned against known MLST allele sequences so per-read allele match/mismatch evidence (e.g., Phred-weighted mismatches) can be extracted as ILP input for strain deconvolution. Input is de novo assembled contigs or full genomes rather than short reads — reference-based strain methods like strainEST or genome-level comparison are more appropriate No reference allele database exists for the organism (de novo methods such as DESMAN are designed for that case) Reads do not come from MLST loci or cannot align to known allele sequences (the ILP stage has no allele-candidate space to work with) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Maps WGS read pairs onto a curated MLST allele database (the 8-gene B. burgdorferi scheme with 1726 known alleles) using Bowtie v0.12.7, then extracts per-locus mapping information from the SAM files with samtools v1.3.1 to feed the downstream Allele Diversity ILP. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Maps WGS read pairs onto a curated MLST allele database (the 8-gene B. burgdorferi scheme with 1726 known alleles) using Bowtie v0.12.7, then extracts per-locus mapping information from the SAM files with samtools v1.3.1 to feed the downstream Allele Diversity ILP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is de novo assembled contigs or full genomes rather than short reads — reference-based strain methods like strainEST or genome-level comparison are more appropriate No reference allele database exists for the organism (de novo methods such as DESMAN are designed for that case) Reads do not come from MLST loci or cannot align to known allele sequences (the ILP stage has no allele-candidate space to work with)

skills.description: Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads from water samples must be attributed to competing fecal source categories (e.g., human, sewage, septage, cow, dog, goose) using a genome-to-source database without sequencing the sources themselves.
skills.name: short-read-mapping-to-genome-databases
skills.search_text: short-read-mapping-to-genome-databases Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads from water samples must be attributed to competing fecal source categories (e.g., human, sewage, septage, cow, dog, goose) using a genome-to-source database without sequencing the sources themselves. When potential fecal sources are available and cheap to sequence directly, and a de novo source database is preferred over the default genome database When reads are long-read (Oxford Nanopore) rather than short reads, since the pipeline and benchmark are built around short-read mapping with bwa mem When a mass-balance answer is required, since SourceApp portions estimate proportions of cells by genome equivalents and do not represent a mass balance http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A metagenomic fecal source tracking method (SourceApp) that maps short shotgun reads to curated source-associated genome databases and normalizes mapped sequence depth to genome-equivalent cell fractions to infer source attribution and apportionment. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: A metagenomic fecal source tracking method (SourceApp) that maps short shotgun reads to curated source-associated genome databases and normalizes mapped sequence depth to genome-equivalent cell fractions to infer source attribution and apportionment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When potential fecal sources are available and cheap to sequence directly, and a de novo source database is preferred over the default genome database When reads are long-read (Oxford Nanopore) rather than short reads, since the pipeline and benchmark are built around short-read mapping with bwa mem When a mass-balance answer is required, since SourceApp portions estimate proportions of cells by genome equivalents and do not represent a mass balance

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end short-read (Illumina) FASTQ files must be cleaned of low-quality reads, adapters and poor-quality trailing bases before hybrid assembly or downstream polishing.
skills.name: short-read-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: short-read-quality-filtering Use when raw paired-end short-read (Illumina) FASTQ files must be cleaned of low-quality reads, adapters and poor-quality trailing bases before hybrid assembly or downstream polishing. The input is long (ONT/PacBio) reads — Plassembler uses chopper with -l 500 and -q 9 for long-read filtering, not fastp The paired short reads have already been adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered and Plassembler is run with --skip_qc The data are single-end or non-Illumina short reads where paired-end adapter/quality trimming does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quality-controls Illumina paired-end FASTQs before hybrid plasmid assembly by filtering and trimming them with fastp (>=0.24.2), exactly as Plassembler does inside its QC step (skippable via --skip_qc). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Quality-controls Illumina paired-end FASTQs before hybrid plasmid assembly by filtering and trimming them with fastp (>=0.24.2), exactly as Plassembler does inside its QC step (skippable via --skip_qc).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is long (ONT/PacBio) reads — Plassembler uses chopper with -l 500 and -q 9 for long-read filtering, not fastp The paired short reads have already been adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered and Plassembler is run with --skip_qc The data are single-end or non-Illumina short reads where paired-end adapter/quality trimming does not apply

skills.search_text: short-read-quality-trimming Use when raw Illumina paired-end metagenomic FASTQ/fastq.gz reads must be stripped of Illumina adapters and low-quality bases before downstream SSU rRNA filtering, assembly, or classification. Input reads are long-read (PacBio/ONT) data — bbduk adapter trimming with kmer=21 targets short Illumina reads only Reads are already trimmed FASTQ sequences, e.g. the filtered 16S/18S output of SortMeRNA ('This folder contains filtered 16S/18S sequences from your trimmed (meta)genomics sequence files') http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Adapter removal and quality trimming of raw Illumina (meta)genomic FASTQ reads using bbduk.sh from BBTools, as performed in the RiboTaxa pipeline's quality-control stage prior to SSU rRNA read extraction and reconstruction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Adapter removal and quality trimming of raw Illumina (meta)genomic FASTQ reads using bbduk.sh from BBTools, as performed in the RiboTaxa pipeline's quality-control stage prior to SSU rRNA read extraction and reconstruction.

skills.description: Use when raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads must be quality-trimmed and adapter-stripped to remove low-quality sequence and adapters before targeted assembly or seed-read searching.

skills.search_text: short-read-quality-trimming Use when raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads must be quality-trimmed and adapter-stripped to remove low-quality sequence and adapters before targeted assembly or seed-read searching. Input is already trimmed, cleaned, or assembled contigs rather than raw short reads — re-running bbduk trimming adds runtime with little benefit Long-read or single-end-only data where bbmerge overlap merging of paired reads is not applicable A complete de novo assembly is the goal and trimming is handled by the assembler's own filtering options http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 The CasCollect read filtering step: quality trimming, adapter removal, optional contaminant-read removal and merging of overlapping paired-end reads using BBTools (bbduk/bbmerge), run with the --trim or --clean flag before seed generation. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063

skills.search_text: short-read-quality-trimming Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ (e.g. CAMISIM simulated metagenomic test data) enters nf-core/mag and must be adapter/quality trimmed and decontaminated before assembly. skills.name: short-read-reference-mapping-with-bowtie2
skills.search_text: short-read-reference-mapping-with-bowtie2 Use when you need to quantify how completely a raw or subsetted set of short paired-end reads (FASTQ) covers a specific reference contig (FASTA), e.g. tracking cas operon coverage across read-subset expansion cycles. The reads are already assembled contigs or long reads (PacBio/ONT) — bowtie2 end-to-end short-read paired-end mapping is designed for short Illumina reads, not de novo contig or long-read alignment You need annotation or assembly of the CRISPR/Cas locus rather than a coverage quantification — use CasCollect's own assembly (SPAdes/metaSPAdes) and CRISPRCasFinder annotation steps instead The reference contig is not the target of interest (e.g. no cas operon reference FASTA has been extracted yet) — mapping cannot proceed without a defined reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Maps short paired-end sequencing reads (e.g. CasCollect seed read subsets) onto a reference FASTA such as the largest ground water cas operon contig using bowtie2 in end-to-end paired-end mode, then quantifies per-base coverage with 'samtools depth -a' to compute the fraction of reference bases covered. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Maps short paired-end sequencing reads (e.g. CasCollect seed read subsets) onto a reference FASTA such as the largest ground water cas operon contig using bowtie2 in end-to-end paired-end mode, then quantifies per-base coverage with 'samtools depth -a' to compute the fraction of reference bases covered.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are already assembled contigs or long reads (PacBio/ONT) — bowtie2 end-to-end short-read paired-end mapping is designed for short Illumina reads, not de novo contig or long-read alignment You need annotation or assembly of the CRISPR/Cas locus rather than a coverage quantification — use CasCollect's own assembly (SPAdes/metaSPAdes) and CRISPRCasFinder annotation steps instead The reference contig is not the target of interest (e.g. no cas operon reference FASTA has been extracted yet) — mapping cannot proceed without a defined reference

skills.description: Use when building simulated benchmark read sets for the B. burgdorferi MLST deconvolution pipeline (ADP/SDP, EvoMod mechanisms, coverage/edit-distance sweeps) or when reads must be mapped to a known allele database to produce ILP input files.
skills.name: short-read-simulation-and-mapping
skills.search_text: short-read-simulation-and-mapping Use when building simulated benchmark read sets for the B. burgdorferi MLST deconvolution pipeline (ADP/SDP, EvoMod mechanisms, coverage/edit-distance sweeps) or when reads must be mapped to a known allele database to produce ILP input files. When the target organism or MLST scheme is not B. burgdorferi — the pipeline, allele database, and edit-distance matrices are Borrelia-specific When real sequencing data is already available and mapped; this skill is for simulation/benchmarking, not for the real-sample analysis path When a modern aligner (e.g. Bowtie2) is required for other purposes — the article's pipeline is pinned to Bowtie v0.12.7 and its SAM output format http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Simulate Illumina-style NGS reads from known B. burgdorferi MLST alleles or strain mixtures with ART, then map them to the 8-gene/1726-allele database with Bowtie v0.12.7 and extract per-read mapping evidence with samtools to feed the allele and strain diversity ILPs. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Simulate Illumina-style NGS reads from known B. burgdorferi MLST alleles or strain mixtures with ART, then map them to the 8-gene/1726-allele database with Bowtie v0.12.7 and extract per-read mapping evidence with samtools to feed the allele and strain diversity ILPs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target organism or MLST scheme is not B. burgdorferi — the pipeline, allele database, and edit-distance matrices are Borrelia-specific When real sequencing data is already available and mapped; this skill is for simulation/benchmarking, not for the real-sample analysis path When a modern aligner (e.g. Bowtie2) is required for other purposes — the article's pipeline is pinned to Bowtie v0.12.7 and its SAM output format

skills.description: Use when reads must be simulated from genomes whose true species are absent from every classifier database, in order to measure false-positive misclassification of taxonomic classifiers as a function of similarity to the closest database relative.
skills.name: short-read-simulation-from-reference-genomes
skills.search_text: short-read-simulation-from-reference-genomes Use when reads must be simulated from genomes whose true species are absent from every classifier database, in order to measure false-positive misclassification of taxonomic classifiers as a function of similarity to the closest database relative. The true source species IS present in one or more classifier databases — assignments are then not unambiguous false positives and this absent-species design is invalid The goal is read-level precision/recall on known taxa rather than false positives; use the 3,269 MAG benchmark reads excluded from training instead Reads have strongly different lengths or error profiles (e.g. long reads); the paper notes retraining might be required to adapt to such data Simulate short sequencing reads at 1x coverage from genomes whose true species are absent from all reference databases (AQ<60%, ANI<95% to closest relative), then benchmark false-positive species misclassification across DeepMicrobes, Kraken, Kraken 2, CLARK and CLARK-S. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Simulate short sequencing reads at 1x coverage from genomes whose true species are absent from all reference databases (AQ<60%, ANI<95% to closest relative), then benchmark false-positive species misclassification across DeepMicrobes, Kraken, Kraken 2, CLARK and CLARK-S.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The true source species IS present in one or more classifier databases — assignments are then not unambiguous false positives and this absent-species design is invalid The goal is read-level precision/recall on known taxa rather than false positives; use the 3,269 MAG benchmark reads excluded from training instead Reads have strongly different lengths or error profiles (e.g. long reads); the paper notes retraining might be required to adapt to such data

skills.description: Use when you have FASTA reads flagged by pal-MEM as containing inverted repeats and per-sample assemblies, and need to anchor those reads genomically and filter candidate ITRs by IS-length proximity before clustering.
skills.name: short-read-to-assembly-mapping
skills.search_text: short-read-to-assembly-mapping Use when you have FASTA reads flagged by pal-MEM as containing inverted repeats and per-sample assemblies, and need to anchor those reads genomically and filter candidate ITRs by IS-length proximity before clustering. Input reads have not been pre-processed through convertToFasta and pal-MEM, so no ITR-containing reads or LCoord/RCoord coordinates exist to filter The goal is to discover ISs lacking ITRs — Palidis is only equipped for ISs with ITRs, so mapping-and-proximity filtering cannot recover them Suspected insertions are lengthened by nested insertion events extending beyond the 500–3000 bp proximity range, which this filter will incorrectly discard http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Maps repeat-containing metagenomic short reads (output of pal-MEM) back to their associated sample assemblies with Bowtie2, then applies a distance filter so only mapped reads whose ITR LCoord/RCoord positions fall within the user-defined minimum-to-maximum IS length interval (e.g. the 500–3000 bp proximity range) are retained as candidate ITR reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Maps repeat-containing metagenomic short reads (output of pal-MEM) back to their associated sample assemblies with Bowtie2, then applies a distance filter so only mapped reads whose ITR LCoord/RCoord positions fall within the user-defined minimum-to-maximum IS length interval (e.g. the 500–3000 bp proximity range) are retained as candidate ITR reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not been pre-processed through convertToFasta and pal-MEM, so no ITR-containing reads or LCoord/RCoord coordinates exist to filter The goal is to discover ISs lacking ITRs — Palidis is only equipped for ISs with ITRs, so mapping-and-proximity filtering cannot recover them Suspected insertions are lengthened by nested insertion events extending beyond the 500–3000 bp proximity range, which this filter will incorrectly discard

skills.description: Use when you have standard Illumina FASTQ or 10x Linked-Read FASTQ from a GIAB cell line and need benchmarkable SNV/SV call sets to compare against an alternative strategy such as assembly-based variant calling.
skills.name: short-read-variant-calling
skills.search_text: short-read-variant-calling Use when you have standard Illumina FASTQ or 10x Linked-Read FASTQ from a GIAB cell line and need benchmarkable SNV/SV call sets to compare against an alternative strategy such as assembly-based variant calling. When the goal is de novo assembly quality assessment rather than reference-based variant discovery (use assembly with Supernova2 instead) When no GIAB benchmark call set exists for the sample, since vcfeval/truvari benchmarking is central to validating the call sets When input data is simulated Linked-Reads generated by LRTK-SIM solely for assembly-parameter exploration; only SNV/SV variant output is needed, not coverage/contiguity simulation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reference-based variant discovery from standard short-read data: align NA12878/NA24385 Illumina reads to hg38 with BWA-MEM, call SNVs with FreeBayes and SVs with SvABA, process 10x Linked-Reads with Long Ranger, and benchmark all calls against GIAB with RTG vcfeval and truvari. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/giz141
skills.summary: Reference-based variant discovery from standard short-read data: align NA12878/NA24385 Illumina reads to hg38 with BWA-MEM, call SNVs with FreeBayes and SVs with SvABA, process 10x Linked-Reads with Long Ranger, and benchmark all calls against GIAB with RTG vcfeval and truvari.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo assembly quality assessment rather than reference-based variant discovery (use assembly with Supernova2 instead) When no GIAB benchmark call set exists for the sample, since vcfeval/truvari benchmarking is central to validating the call sets When input data is simulated Linked-Reads generated by LRTK-SIM solely for assembly-parameter exploration; only SNV/SV variant output is needed, not coverage/contiguity simulation

skills.description: Use when two short nucleotide sequences (e.g. candidate inverted terminal repeats ≥25 nt, up to 50 nt) must be tested for reverse-complement concordance before accepting an IS candidate.
skills.name: short-sequence-nucleotide-alignment
skills.search_text: short-sequence-nucleotide-alignment Use when two short nucleotide sequences (e.g. candidate inverted terminal repeats ≥25 nt, up to 50 nt) must be tested for reverse-complement concordance before accepting an IS candidate. The insertion sequences of interest lack ITRs — Palidis is 'currently only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs', so reverse-complement ITR verification is inapplicable ITRs are shorter than the minimum ITR length threshold (e.g. 25 nt default; ITRs as short as 10 nt are missed at default settings) Sequences are long genomic contigs requiring general-purpose homology search rather than short paired-sequence concordance testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0798 Verifies that paired candidate ITRs are reverse complements of each other using blastn in short-sequence mode (-task blastn -word_size 4), a key concordance check within the Palidis Step 3 conversion of clustered candidate ITRs into predicted insertion sequences. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Verifies that paired candidate ITRs are reverse complements of each other using blastn in short-sequence mode (-task blastn -word_size 4), a key concordance check within the Palidis Step 3 conversion of clustered candidate ITRs into predicted insertion sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The insertion sequences of interest lack ITRs — Palidis is 'currently only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs', so reverse-complement ITR verification is inapplicable ITRs are shorter than the minimum ITR length threshold (e.g. 25 nt default; ITRs as short as 10 nt are missed at default settings) Sequences are long genomic contigs requiring general-purpose homology search rather than short paired-sequence concordance testing

skills.description: Use when starting from cleaned paired-end shotgun FASTQ files from a metagenomic Hi-C experiment and you need assembled contigs as the substrate for aligning Hi-C reads and binning viral genomes.
skills.name: shotgun-metagenome-assembly
skills.search_text: shotgun-metagenome-assembly Use when starting from cleaned paired-end shotgun FASTQ files from a metagenomic Hi-C experiment and you need assembled contigs as the substrate for aligning Hi-C reads and binning viral genomes. Input is already an assembly or contig FASTA — skip assembly and proceed directly to Hi-C alignment (BWA MEM -5SP) and viral contig identification Data are single-cell or long-read assemblies where MEGAHIT's short-read de Bruijn graph (k up to 141) is not the appropriate assembler Only Hi-C reads are available without matching shotgun reads — co-assembly from Hi-C alone is not the designed workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assemble cleaned shotgun metagenomic reads into long contigs with MEGAHIT (min-contig-len 1000, k=21-141 step 12) to serve as the reference for Hi-C read alignment and downstream viral binning with ViralCC. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Assemble cleaned shotgun metagenomic reads into long contigs with MEGAHIT (min-contig-len 1000, k=21-141 step 12) to serve as the reference for Hi-C read alignment and downstream viral binning with ViralCC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an assembly or contig FASTA — skip assembly and proceed directly to Hi-C alignment (BWA MEM -5SP) and viral contig identification Data are single-cell or long-read assemblies where MEGAHIT's short-read de Bruijn graph (k up to 141) is not the appropriate assembler Only Hi-C reads are available without matching shotgun reads — co-assembly from Hi-C alone is not the designed workflow

skills.description: Use when converting per-read DIAMOND alignments ( e-value hits per read) against a UniRef90-style gene catalog into a gene-by-sample abundance table, especially when reads tie across multiple equally good gene hits.
skills.name: shotgun-metagenome-gene-abundance-estimation
skills.search_text: shotgun-metagenome-gene-abundance-estimation Use when converting per-read DIAMOND alignments ( e-value hits per read) against a UniRef90-style gene catalog into a gene-by-sample abundance table, especially when reads tie across multiple equally good gene hits. Input is already a gene-by-sample abundance table (proceed directly to ortholog counting/aggregation) You need strictly integer read counts per gene with no handling of equally well-mapping multi-hits (fractional counting would be inappropriate) Input reads have not passed MetaLAFFA's quality control phase (host filtering, duplicate removal, Trimmomatic MAXINFO trimming), since unfiltered hits skew counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 MetaLAFFA's gene counting step computes per-gene abundances from filtered DIAMOND read-to-gene alignments by summing retained best-e-value hits, assigning fractional counts (1/n) to genes tied in a read's best match, and dividing each gene's count by a length normalization factor (gene length / average gene length). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03815-9
skills.summary: MetaLAFFA's gene counting step computes per-gene abundances from filtered DIAMOND read-to-gene alignments by summing retained best-e-value hits, assigning fractional counts (1/n) to genes tied in a read's best match, and dividing each gene's count by a length normalization factor (gene length / average gene length).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-by-sample abundance table (proceed directly to ortholog counting/aggregation) You need strictly integer read counts per gene with no handling of equally well-mapping multi-hits (fractional counting would be inappropriate) Input reads have not passed MetaLAFFA's quality control phase (host filtering, duplicate removal, Trimmomatic MAXINFO trimming), since unfiltered hits skew counts

skills.description: Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. an SRA run such as SRR606249) must be turned into MAGs to feed taxonomic classifiers like kMetaShot, GTDBtk, or CAMITAX, starting from raw FASTQ.
skills.name: shotgun-metagenome-meta-assembly
skills.search_text: shotgun-metagenome-meta-assembly Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. an SRA run such as SRR606249) must be turned into MAGs to feed taxonomic classifiers like kMetaShot, GTDBtk, or CAMITAX, starting from raw FASTQ. Input is already binned MAG FASTA files — go directly to the classifier (kMetaShot_classifier_NV.py -b bins/) instead of re-assembling The task is reference-based strain typing of isolated genomes rather than de novo recovery of community MAGs from mixed reads Only short contigs (< 1500 bp) are expected, since MetaBAT2 here bins with -m 1500 and would discard them http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A meta-assembly workflow that converts paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. SRA run SRR606249, Illumina HiSeq 2000, 2 x 100 bp) into MAGs by quality-trimming reads, meta-assembling them with two independent assemblers (metaSPAdes and MegaHIT), and binning contigs with MetaBAT2. It supplies the MAG inputs that downstream taxonomic classifiers such as kMetaShot, GTDBtk, and CAMITAX require. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bib/bbae680
skills.summary: A meta-assembly workflow that converts paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. SRA run SRR606249, Illumina HiSeq 2000, 2 x 100 bp) into MAGs by quality-trimming reads, meta-assembling them with two independent assemblers (metaSPAdes and MegaHIT), and binning contigs with MetaBAT2. It supplies the MAG inputs that downstream taxonomic classifiers such as kMetaShot, GTDBtk, and CAMITAX require.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already binned MAG FASTA files — go directly to the classifier (kMetaShot_classifier_NV.py -b bins/) instead of re-assembling The task is reference-based strain typing of isolated genomes rather than de novo recovery of community MAGs from mixed reads Only short contigs (< 1500 bp) are expected, since MetaBAT2 here bins with -m 1500 and would discard them

skills.description: Use when you have shotgun metagenomic reads that passed all QC stages and need to assign reads to reference taxa/genes, or attribute a disease-associated gene to its source organisms via read-level traceback.
skills.name: shotgun-metagenome-qced-read-mapping
skills.search_text: shotgun-metagenome-qced-read-mapping Use when you have shotgun metagenomic reads that passed all QC stages and need to assign reads to reference taxa/genes, or attribute a disease-associated gene to its source organisms via read-level traceback. Input reads have not passed read/sample QC — run OMARU_read_QC.sm and update the sample list first You need de novo assembly or binning of the metagenome rather than reference-based mapping against UHGG/CHOCO Your question is case-control association testing rather than gene-to-taxon attribution or profiling http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Maps QCed shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads against a phylogenetic reference (e.g., UHGG-based CHOCO in Bowtie format) with OMARU to construct taxonomic/functional profiles and perform read-level traceback linking genes (e.g., SCZ-associated Vpar_1847) to their organisms of origin. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac019
skills.summary: Maps QCed shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads against a phylogenetic reference (e.g., UHGG-based CHOCO in Bowtie format) with OMARU to construct taxonomic/functional profiles and perform read-level traceback linking genes (e.g., SCZ-associated Vpar_1847) to their organisms of origin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not passed read/sample QC — run OMARU_read_QC.sm and update the sample list first You need de novo assembly or binning of the metagenome rather than reference-based mapping against UHGG/CHOCO Your question is case-control association testing rather than gene-to-taxon attribution or profiling

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end shotgun metagenome FASTQ files (e.g. from NCBI SRA human gut, infant, or patient cohorts) must be cleaned of low-quality bases and host/contaminant reads before fungal taxonomic or functional profiling.
skills.name: shotgun-metagenome-quality-control-decontamination
skills.search_text: shotgun-metagenome-quality-control-decontamination Use when raw paired-end shotgun metagenome FASTQ files (e.g. from NCBI SRA human gut, infant, or patient cohorts) must be cleaned of low-quality bases and host/contaminant reads before fungal taxonomic or functional profiling. Input is already a QC'd feature/abundance table rather than raw FASTQ reads The goal is fungal functional profiling with FunOMIC-P, which requires DIAMOND blastx thresholds (coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10) rather than read-level QC and Bowtie2 mapping Input is amplicon (16S/ITS) data rather than shotgun metagenomic reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quality-control and decontamination of human shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g. the 2,679 public human metagenomes processed with KneadData v0.7.7-alpha) so that only cleaned reads are mapped against the FunOMIC-T fungal marker-gene database for taxonomic profiling. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Quality-control and decontamination of human shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g. the 2,679 public human metagenomes processed with KneadData v0.7.7-alpha) so that only cleaned reads are mapped against the FunOMIC-T fungal marker-gene database for taxonomic profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a QC'd feature/abundance table rather than raw FASTQ reads The goal is fungal functional profiling with FunOMIC-P, which requires DIAMOND blastx thresholds (coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10) rather than read-level QC and Bowtie2 mapping Input is amplicon (16S/ITS) data rather than shotgun metagenomic reads

skills.description: Use when raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g., gzipped Illumina NovaSeq 6000 2x150-bp mesocosm reads) must be cleaned of adapters and low-quality sequence prior to genome mapping or abundance estimation.
skills.name: shotgun-metagenome-read-qc-and-trimming
skills.search_text: shotgun-metagenome-read-qc-and-trimming Use when raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g., gzipped Illumina NovaSeq 6000 2x150-bp mesocosm reads) must be cleaned of adapters and low-quality sequence prior to genome mapping or abundance estimation. Input reads are already trimmed or supplied as BAM/sorted alignment files — fastp trimming would be redundant before CoverM, which can consume BAM directly The goal is long-read MAG recovery without short-read QC — filtlong (--min_length 1000 --min_window_q 0.8 --window_size 250) and bbnorm are the appropriate filters, not paired-end fastp trimming The user only needs source attribution from a prebuilt database and is running the full sourceapp.py pipeline, which already performs the fastp quality-check step internally http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Quality-check and trim shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads with fastp to remove leftover adapter sequences and low-quality reads before mapping reads to a source-associated genome database with bwa mem/CoverM, as performed in the SourceApp fecal source tracking pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: Quality-check and trim shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads with fastp to remove leftover adapter sequences and low-quality reads before mapping reads to a source-associated genome database with bwa mem/CoverM, as performed in the SourceApp fecal source tracking pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already trimmed or supplied as BAM/sorted alignment files — fastp trimming would be redundant before CoverM, which can consume BAM directly The goal is long-read MAG recovery without short-read QC — filtlong (--min_length 1000 --min_window_q 0.8 --window_size 250) and bbnorm are the appropriate filters, not paired-end fastp trimming The user only needs source attribution from a prebuilt database and is running the full sourceapp.py pipeline, which already performs the fastp quality-check step internally

skills.description: Use when 16S OTU tables and matched shotgun metagenome KO tables are available for the same samples and you need to quantify at what sequencing depth PICRUSt prediction rivals direct metagenomic sequencing.
skills.name: shotgun-metagenome-vs-predicted-metagenome-comparison
skills.search_text: shotgun-metagenome-vs-predicted-metagenome-comparison Use when 16S OTU tables and matched shotgun metagenome KO tables are available for the same samples and you need to quantify at what sequencing depth PICRUSt prediction rivals direct metagenomic sequencing. No matched shotgun metagenomic data exist for the samples — accuracy benchmarking against observed KO abundances is impossible The community contains substantial viral or eukaryotic components — PICRUSt only infers bacterial and archaeal contributions, so the comparison would be invalid The 16S data are not OTU-picked against Greengenes+IMG reference (e.g. ASV-based or de novo picking), so PICRUSt copy-number normalization and per-genome KO lookup cannot be applied as described http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmarks PICRUSt-predicted KO abundance profiles (built from 16S OTU tables) against rarefied shallow shotgun metagenomic KO profiles using Spearman rank correlation across sequencing depths, to determine the read depth below which 16S-based prediction outperforms direct sequencing. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nbt.2676
skills.summary: Benchmarks PICRUSt-predicted KO abundance profiles (built from 16S OTU tables) against rarefied shallow shotgun metagenomic KO profiles using Spearman rank correlation across sequencing depths, to determine the read depth below which 16S-based prediction outperforms direct sequencing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched shotgun metagenomic data exist for the samples — accuracy benchmarking against observed KO abundances is impossible The community contains substantial viral or eukaryotic components — PICRUSt only infers bacterial and archaeal contributions, so the comparison would be invalid The 16S data are not OTU-picked against Greengenes+IMG reference (e.g. ASV-based or de novo picking), so PICRUSt copy-number normalization and per-genome KO lookup cannot be applied as described

skills.description: Use when you have .filtered.sorted.bam files from shotgun metagenomic sequencing and need an allele-count (SNP x sample) pileup matrix to feed variant discovery such as MetaQuad.
skills.name: shotgun-metagenomic-pileup-processing
skills.search_text: shotgun-metagenomic-pileup-processing Use when you have .filtered.sorted.bam files from shotgun metagenomic sequencing and need an allele-count (SNP x sample) pileup matrix to feed variant discovery such as MetaQuad. Reads are not yet filtered and aligned — the pipeline requires .filtered.sorted.bam from bwa or bowtie2 as upstream input, not raw FASTQ Data are single-cell mitochondrial/mtDNA data intended for MQuad's original scope rather than shotgun metagenomic samples (MQuad/CellSNP serve that lineage; MetaQuad is the metagenomic extension) The goal is bulk per-sample variant calling rather than detecting shared informative variants across a population of metagenomic samples Pile up SNPs from aligned shotgun metagenomic samples using cellsnp-lite (minMAF = 0.02, minCOUNT = 100) to produce a cellSNP output folder that downstream tools like MetaQuad consume to discover shared informative variants. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Pile up SNPs from aligned shotgun metagenomic samples using cellsnp-lite (minMAF = 0.02, minCOUNT = 100) to produce a cellSNP output folder that downstream tools like MetaQuad consume to discover shared informative variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are not yet filtered and aligned — the pipeline requires .filtered.sorted.bam from bwa or bowtie2 as upstream input, not raw FASTQ Data are single-cell mitochondrial/mtDNA data intended for MQuad's original scope rather than shotgun metagenomic samples (MQuad/CellSNP serve that lineage; MetaQuad is the metagenomic extension) The goal is bulk per-sample variant calling rather than detecting shared informative variants across a population of metagenomic samples

skills.description: Use when input is raw paired-end or single-end Illumina shotgun metagenomics FASTQ (fastq.gz) and the goal is to isolate 16S/18S rRNA fragments prior to reference-targeted SSU assembly or taxonomic profiling.
skills.name: shotgun-metagenomics-rrna-read-extraction
skills.search_text: shotgun-metagenomics-rrna-read-extraction Use when input is raw paired-end or single-end Illumina shotgun metagenomics FASTQ (fastq.gz) and the goal is to isolate 16S/18S rRNA fragments prior to reference-targeted SSU assembly or taxonomic profiling. Input is already amplicon 16S FASTQ (e.g. from a 16S PCR workflow) where no shotgun rRNA extraction step is needed The goal is direct taxonomic classification of short reads with fast classifiers (Kraken2, Centrifuge) rather than reconstruction of full-length SSU sequences The data contain no rRNA-derived reads (e.g. mRNA-only meta-transcriptomic libraries depleted of rRNA) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Extract small-subunit (16S/18S) rRNA reads from shotgun (meta)genomic Illumina FASTQ data using an rRNA-specialized mapper (SortMeRNA) and/or a general-purpose read mapper (BBMap) against the indexed SILVA SSU 138.1 database, producing the filtered read sets needed for full-length SSU reconstruction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Extract small-subunit (16S/18S) rRNA reads from shotgun (meta)genomic Illumina FASTQ data using an rRNA-specialized mapper (SortMeRNA) and/or a general-purpose read mapper (BBMap) against the indexed SILVA SSU 138.1 database, producing the filtered read sets needed for full-length SSU reconstruction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already amplicon 16S FASTQ (e.g. from a 16S PCR workflow) where no shotgun rRNA extraction step is needed The goal is direct taxonomic classification of short reads with fast classifiers (Kraken2, Centrifuge) rather than reconstruction of full-length SSU sequences The data contain no rRNA-derived reads (e.g. mRNA-only meta-transcriptomic libraries depleted of rRNA)

skills.description: Use when starting a MAGinator/VAMB metagenomic profiling run: raw shotgun paired-end reads have been downloaded from ENA/SRA and must be indexed as a reads.csv before preprocessing, assembly and binning.
skills.name: shotgun-read-sample-index-preparation
skills.search_text: shotgun-read-sample-index-preparation Use when starting a MAGinator/VAMB metagenomic profiling run: raw shotgun paired-end reads have been downloaded from ENA/SRA and must be indexed as a reads.csv before preprocessing, assembly and binning. Input is already a feature/abundance table (e.g. a MetaPhlAn2 or MAGinator abundance matrix) rather than raw reads — no read index is needed. Data are single-end reads or non-fastq contig assemblies only — the index format requires paired forward/reverse fastq paths. skills.search_text: signal-event-z-score-normalization Use when segmenting raw nanopore FAST5/SLOW5 signals into events and you need event means normalized and quantized such that identical DNA content yields identical hash values despite signal noise, e.g. for RawHash-style hash-based mapping. Input is already basecalled sequence (FASTQ/FASTA) rather than raw signal — use a sequence-based aligner such as minimap2 instead Reads are R10.4.1 data for adaptive-sampling-style signal mapping, where legacy R9.4 6-mer-model-based approaches like UNCALLED do not apply You need per-sample absolute current-level statistics rather than hash-comparable normalized/quantized events http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Z-score normalizes nanopore event means per read and quantizes them into Q-bit values using RawHash's p-bit pruning encoding (E[1,2]E[3+p,Q]), so that signals from the same DNA content map to identical quantized values that can be packed into 32-bit hash values. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad272
skills.summary: Z-score normalizes nanopore event means per read and quantizes them into Q-bit values using RawHash's p-bit pruning encoding (E[1,2]E[3+p,Q]), so that signals from the same DNA content map to identical quantized values that can be packed into 32-bit hash values.

skills.search_text: signature-gene-abundance-estimation Use when shotgun metagenomics samples have been assembled and binned into VAMB clusters/MAGs and you need accurate abundance profiles (and subspecies-level stratification) of those de novo MAGs rather than database-based marker gene profiling. skills.search_text: signature-gene-multiple-sequence-alignment Use when MAGinator has produced signature genes for a MAG cluster and per-sample BAMs, and you need SNV-resolution phylogenetic trees to stratify samples at subspecies/strain level or associate metadata with strain differences. Input is a per-sample abundance table or StrainPhlAn marker-based profile rather than MAGinator signature genes with mapped BAMs — use marker-gene tools like MetaPhlAn/StrainPhlAn instead Only a single sample (or fewer samples than needed to meet the --min_mapped_signature_genes / --min_samples thresholds) is available — a cross-sample SNV tree cannot be constructed The goal is species- or genome-level phylogeny of bins (e.g. GTDB-tk/dRep placement), not within-MAG-cluster SNV-resolution tree — MAGinator's trees are rooted using marker genes within MAG clusters, not whole-genome trees http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Aligns per-sample SNV-bearing signature genes of each MAG cluster with MAFFT and concatenates the per-gene alignments so that maximum-likelihood phylogenies (FastTree or IQ-TREE) can be built with leaves corresponding to samples, enabling SNV-resolution subspecies/strain stratification of MAGs. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a per-sample abundance table or StrainPhlAn marker-based profile rather than MAGinator signature genes with mapped BAMs — use marker-gene tools like MetaPhlAn/StrainPhlAn instead Only a single sample (or fewer samples than needed to meet the --min_mapped_signature_genes / --min_samples thresholds) is available — a cross-sample SNV tree cannot be constructed The goal is species- or genome-level phylogeny of bins (e.g. GTDB-tk/dRep placement), not within-MAG-cluster SNV-resolution tree — MAGinator's trees are rooted using marker genes within MAG clusters, not whole-genome trees

skills.search_text: signature-gene-selection-from-gene-count-matrices Use when you have a read-mapping gene count matrix (small_gene_count_matrix.tsv) plus MAG cluster assignments (metagenomicspecies.tab) and need to identify de novo signature genes for per-sample MAG cluster abundance estimation. skills.summary: MAGinator's de novo selection and statistical refinement of MAG-cluster-specific signature genes from a read-mapping gene count matrix, using co-abundance ranking and a rank-based negative binomial model to pick an ideal gene set for abundance estimation.

skills.description: Use when you have run bin_permute_all on a binary-grouped microbiome feature table and need to aggregate per-scenario p-values into a significant-feature count curve (nsig(k)) to visualize overall association strength and validate that top hits are true positives.

skills.search_text: significant-feature-count-summarization Use when you have run bin_permute_all on a binary-grouped microbiome feature table and need to aggregate per-scenario p-values into a significant-feature count curve (nsig(k)) to visualize overall association strength and validate that top hits are true positives. You need formal inference on individual features (adjusted p-values or FDR control) — the article states the method does not control the false discovery rate or calculate adjusted p-values The grouping factor is not binary — the bin_* family (bin_permute_all, plot_bin_psig) targets binary outcomes only You have raw OTU counts but have not yet run progressive permutation — plot_bin_psig requires the alloutputs object from bin_permute_all, not a feature table directly http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Summarizes the per-scenario outputs of ProgPermute's progressive permutation (per-scenario median p-values from Wilcoxon rank sum tests at alpha=0.05) into the count of significant taxa nsig(k) at each mixing level, and renders the characteristic U-curve of significant-feature count versus proportion of mixing via plot_bin_psig. The U-curve's depth and shape convey the strength of the overall microbiome–grouping association. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04061-3

skills.search_text: silva-database-comparative-analysis Use when quantifying large (≥10 bp) insertions in bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequences — e.g. comparing a CPR/CRISPR-adjacent genome set against SILVA 115 reference sequences — or when auditing primer-amplicon bias caused by rRNA introns. skills.description: Use when preparing host-host (or drug-target analogous) similarity inputs for SNF: you have a binary interaction adjacency matrix Y and need kernel similarity beyond sequence information.
skills.name: similarity-network-fusion-input-preparation
skills.search_text: similarity-network-fusion-input-preparation Use when preparing host-host (or drug-target analogous) similarity inputs for SNF: you have a binary interaction adjacency matrix Y and need kernel similarity beyond sequence information. The input is a continuous similarity/distance matrix already (e.g. oligonucleotide frequency similarity from Jie Ren's d2* tools) — GIP kernel construction would be redundant. No known virus-host associations are available, so interaction profiles cannot be defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Compute the Gaussian interaction profile (GIP) kernel host-host similarity matrix from the binary virus-host adjacency matrix Y, producing one of the similarity inputs (alongside oligonucleotide frequency similarity) that are fused via similarity network fusion (SNF) in the ILMF-VH pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Compute the Gaussian interaction profile (GIP) kernel host-host similarity matrix from the binary virus-host adjacency matrix Y, producing one of the similarity inputs (alongside oligonucleotide frequency similarity) that are fused via similarity network fusion (SNF) in the ILMF-VH pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a continuous similarity/distance matrix already (e.g. oligonucleotide frequency similarity from Jie Ren's d2* tools) — GIP kernel construction would be redundant. No known virus-host associations are available, so interaction profiles cannot be defined.

skills.description: Use when two or more similarity matrices cover the same set of entities (e.g., hosts) and must be combined into one fused similarity network to feed a downstream matrix factorization or prediction model.
skills.name: similarity-network-integration
skills.search_text: similarity-network-integration Use when two or more similarity matrices cover the same set of entities (e.g., hosts) and must be combined into one fused similarity network to feed a downstream matrix factorization or prediction model. The entity set is a bipartite pair (viruses and hosts) rather than a single entity type with multiple similarity views — the virus network here uses only oligonucleotide frequency similarity and is not fused. Only one similarity matrix is available per entity set, leaving nothing for the diffusion process to integrate. The downstream model expects raw dissimilarity values (d2*) rather than fused similarity matrices in the [0, 1] range. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fuses multiple similarity networks describing the same entity set (here, host oligonucleotide-frequency similarity and Gaussian interaction profile kernel similarity) into a single host-host similarity matrix using similarity network fusion (SNF), as done in ILMF-VH before kernelized logistic matrix factorization. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Fuses multiple similarity networks describing the same entity set (here, host oligonucleotide-frequency similarity and Gaussian interaction profile kernel similarity) into a single host-host similarity matrix using similarity network fusion (SNF), as done in ILMF-VH before kernelized logistic matrix factorization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The entity set is a bipartite pair (viruses and hosts) rather than a single entity type with multiple similarity views — the virus network here uses only oligonucleotide frequency similarity and is not fused. Only one similarity matrix is available per entity set, leaving nothing for the diffusion process to integrate. The downstream model expects raw dissimilarity values (d2*) rather than fused similarity matrices in the [0, 1] range.
