skills.when_to_use_negative: When abundance-resolved distances are required — presence/absence k-mer metrics 'greatly diminish the resolution' and compress or saturate differences (e.g., maximum distance already between mock 3 and mock 4) When datasets are massive and a scalable Hadoop-based implementation is needed — the Libra paper's scalable alternative is Libra itself, not Simka When the input is already a k-mer count index or feature table rather than raw read files

skills.description: Use when benchmarking OTU-picking pipelines (MICCA, MICCA-FAST, QIIME, UPARSE, mothur) against a synthetic dataset whose true OTU count is known, to quantify estimation accuracy across sequencing depths.
skills.name: simulated-dataset-pipeline-validation
skills.search_text: simulated-dataset-pipeline-validation Use when benchmarking OTU-picking pipelines (MICCA, MICCA-FAST, QIIME, UPARSE, mothur) against a synthetic dataset whose true OTU count is known, to quantify estimation accuracy across sequencing depths. Input data has no ground truth (e.g. real HMP or environmental samples) — convergence to a true OTU count cannot be evaluated; use consistency or taxonomy-based checks instead The goal is downstream profiling accuracy (relative abundances, genus counts) rather than OTU-count estimation — use RSS of top-20 OTU relative abundances or RDP genus classification comparisons instead Datasets with substantially different read technology or OTU counts (e.g. 454-based 16S-10/ITS-10 with 20% chimeras) where the chimeric-read and read-retention metrics, not OTU-count convergence, are the target http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validates amplicon metagenomic pipelines by running them on synthetic datasets with known ground truth (e.g. the 16S-R dataset with 500 true OTUs and 100000 reads) and measuring how estimated OTU counts converge to the real number as sequencing depth increases via rarefaction. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/srep09743
skills.summary: Validates amplicon metagenomic pipelines by running them on synthetic datasets with known ground truth (e.g. the 16S-R dataset with 500 true OTUs and 100000 reads) and measuring how estimated OTU counts converge to the real number as sequencing depth increases via rarefaction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has no ground truth (e.g. real HMP or environmental samples) — convergence to a true OTU count cannot be evaluated; use consistency or taxonomy-based checks instead The goal is downstream profiling accuracy (relative abundances, genus counts) rather than OTU-count estimation — use RSS of top-20 OTU relative abundances or RDP genus classification comparisons instead Datasets with substantially different read technology or OTU counts (e.g. 454-based 16S-10/ITS-10 with 20% chimeras) where the chimeric-read and read-retention metrics, not OTU-count convergence, are the target

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene prediction on real (non-simulated) metagenomes, where no reference annotation exists to compute sensitivity/precision against truth Comparing clustering methods themselves (Scimm) rather than quantifying downstream gene-prediction retraining gains Reads are long contiguous genomic sequences (e.g. complete prokaryotic genomes), where Glimmer's standard iterative training regime applies instead of the metagenomic simulation benchmark

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a metagenomic classifier (Kraken, Megablast, PhymmBL, NBC) or measuring reads-per-minute throughput and you need reads with known taxonomic origins, or when a standard-error (HiSeq/MiSeq-like) and a high-error (simBA-5, 2% mismatch) read set must be contrasted.
skills.name: simulated-metagenome-read-generation
skills.search_text: simulated-metagenome-read-generation Use when benchmarking a metagenomic classifier (Kraken, Megablast, PhymmBL, NBC) or measuring reads-per-minute throughput and you need reads with known taxonomic origins, or when a standard-error (HiSeq/MiSeq-like) and a high-error (simBA-5, 2% mismatch) read set must be contrasted. You already have real metagenomic reads with known or trusted origins (e.g. SRA accessions for HiSeq/MiSeq) and simulation would only add model-artifact bias You need to characterize organisms absent from the database rather than benchmark classifier accuracy — the clade exclusion experiments require masking database hits, not new simulations Your sequencing platform is not Illumina-like, since the article grounds the error model solely in Mason's Illumina model http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Generates benchmark metagenomic read sets by simulating Illumina reads with Mason from complete bacterial and archaeal RefSeq genomes (e.g. the simBA-5 metagenome at a five-fold elevated error rate, average mismatch rate 2%), enabling controlled comparison of classifiers like Kraken against Megablast, PhymmBL and NBC where every read's true origin is known. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Generates benchmark metagenomic read sets by simulating Illumina reads with Mason from complete bacterial and archaeal RefSeq genomes (e.g. the simBA-5 metagenome at a five-fold elevated error rate, average mismatch rate 2%), enabling controlled comparison of classifiers like Kraken against Megablast, PhymmBL and NBC where every read's true origin is known.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have real metagenomic reads with known or trusted origins (e.g. SRA accessions for HiSeq/MiSeq) and simulation would only add model-artifact bias You need to characterize organisms absent from the database rather than benchmark classifier accuracy — the clade exclusion experiments require masking database hits, not new simulations Your sequencing platform is not Illumina-like, since the article grounds the error model solely in Mason's Illumina model

skills.description: Use when you must quantify a reconstruction method's sensitivity and accuracy on known ground truth, e.g., verifying that rare variants down to 0.1% frequency at ~5000x coverage are recovered from simulated reads.
skills.name: simulated-read-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: simulated-read-benchmark-evaluation Use when you must quantify a reconstruction method's sensitivity and accuracy on known ground truth, e.g., verifying that rare variants down to 0.1% frequency at ~5000x coverage are recovered from simulated reads. Only real wet-lab data are available and no ground-truth clone frequencies exist — sensitivity to a specific 0.1% variant cannot be verified without simulated or spiked-in mixtures The goal is global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction rather than local window-based evaluation Coverage is far below the ~5000x level at which 0.1%-frequency haplotype detection was validated in this setup http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark a haplotype-inference pipeline by simulating NGS reads from a known ground-truth mixture of variants (e.g., 10 HIV-1 subtype B pol variants) and testing whether low-frequency clones are detected and correctly quantified against the known mixture proportions. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: Benchmark a haplotype-inference pipeline by simulating NGS reads from a known ground-truth mixture of variants (e.g., 10 HIV-1 subtype B pol variants) and testing whether low-frequency clones are detected and correctly quantified against the known mixture proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only real wet-lab data are available and no ground-truth clone frequencies exist — sensitivity to a specific 0.1% variant cannot be verified without simulated or spiked-in mixtures The goal is global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction rather than local window-based evaluation Coverage is far below the ~5000x level at which 0.1%-frequency haplotype detection was validated in this setup

skills.description: Use when evaluating a streaming read classifier against large, repetitive pan-genome indexes and you need ground-truth labels; simulated Nanopore/PacBio reads give known target vs. nontarget origins for computing accuracy and F1.
skills.name: simulated-read-benchmarking
skills.search_text: simulated-read-benchmarking Use when evaluating a streaming read classifier against large, repetitive pan-genome indexes and you need ground-truth labels; simulated Nanopore/PacBio reads give known target vs. nontarget origins for computing accuracy and F1. The input is raw nanopore electrical signal — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences and cannot use the Read Until API directly; a separate base caller must run upstream Target and nontarget reads share substantial sequence similarity (e.g. conserved genes between species) — the null index of reversed sequences may be insufficient for principled ejection decisions Ground truth is already available from real data with confident alignments — simulation adds no labeling value and the single published KS-stat threshold may not transfer to your read accuracy/reference http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark read-classification methods by generating reads of known provenance with a long-read simulator (PBSIM2 for PacBio CLR and Nanopore) and scoring a classifier such as SPUMONI, whose positive/null matching-statistic distributions and KS-stat thresholds (0.25 for MS, 0.10 for PML) can be validated against ground truth. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102696
skills.summary: Benchmark read-classification methods by generating reads of known provenance with a long-read simulator (PBSIM2 for PacBio CLR and Nanopore) and scoring a classifier such as SPUMONI, whose positive/null matching-statistic distributions and KS-stat thresholds (0.25 for MS, 0.10 for PML) can be validated against ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw nanopore electrical signal — SPUMONI operates on base-called sequences and cannot use the Read Until API directly; a separate base caller must run upstream Target and nontarget reads share substantial sequence similarity (e.g. conserved genes between species) — the null index of reversed sequences may be insufficient for principled ejection decisions Ground truth is already available from real data with confident alignments — simulation adds no labeling value and the single published KS-stat threshold may not transfer to your read accuracy/reference

Evaluating strain-level sensitivity when the sequenced organism IS in the reference database — protein-level classifiers like Kaiju are less sensitive than nucleotide-level classifiers in that setting Classifying reads from non-protein-coding genomic regions, which protein-level classifiers cannot assign Benchmarking genus-level recovery for genera with no available reference genomes — such classification is impossible by design http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark a taxonomic classifier by simulating HTS reads with ART from reference genomes (optionally excluding the source genome from the database), classifying them, and computing sensitivity and precision of the assignments. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Benchmark a taxonomic classifier by simulating HTS reads with ART from reference genomes (optionally excluding the source genome from the database), classifying them, and computing sensitivity and precision of the assignments.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking plasmid assembler accuracy on simulated read sets: QUAST genome fraction, indels/mismatches per 100 kbp, missed-plasmid counts and fragmented-assembly counts vs a curated ground truth.
skills.name: simulated-readset-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: simulated-readset-benchmark-comparison Use when benchmarking plasmid assembler accuracy on simulated read sets: QUAST genome fraction, indels/mismatches per 100 kbp, missed-plasmid counts and fragmented-assembly counts vs a curated ground truth. The input is a real (non-simulated) read benchmark — the paper benchmarks real reads separately, and the old v1.2.0 comparison used different read sets (simulated R9 vs R10) so is 'not truly a fair comparison'. No Trycycler-derived ground truth exists for the samples — missed-plasmid and fragmentation counts cannot be computed without it. You need QUAST metrics for the changelog/v1.3.0 benchmark on badread nanopore2023 reads — the author notes 'I was too lazy to run QUAST' for those results. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reproduces the Plassembler paper's simulated-read benchmark (20 read sets) comparing Plassembler-Flye, Plassembler-Raven and Unicycler using QUAST accuracy metrics plus missed-plasmid and fragmented-assembly counts against Trycycler-derived ground truth. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Reproduces the Plassembler paper's simulated-read benchmark (20 read sets) comparing Plassembler-Flye, Plassembler-Raven and Unicycler using QUAST accuracy metrics plus missed-plasmid and fragmented-assembly counts against Trycycler-derived ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a real (non-simulated) read benchmark — the paper benchmarks real reads separately, and the old v1.2.0 comparison used different read sets (simulated R9 vs R10) so is 'not truly a fair comparison'. No Trycycler-derived ground truth exists for the samples — missed-plasmid and fragmentation counts cannot be computed without it. You need QUAST metrics for the changelog/v1.3.0 benchmark on badread nanopore2023 reads — the author notes 'I was too lazy to run QUAST' for those results.

skills.name: simulation-based-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: simulation-based-benchmark-evaluation Use when a variant-calling or clustering method must be validated against simulated data with a known ground-truth mutation list, especially to test scalability to larger sample sizes. The data is real (non-simulated) patient or environmental metagenomic data with no ground-truth mutation list — recovery-based TP/FP scoring is impossible The analysis goal is downstream strain/clonal inference rather than benchmarking detection performance http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark a variant-discovery method on simulated shotgun metagenomic data with known ground truth, scaling to large sample sizes (e.g. n=1000 at mean depth 11.8) and scoring recovered true positives against false positives. Used to demonstrate that a tool's performance holds when the benchmark is scaled 10-fold. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Benchmark a variant-discovery method on simulated shotgun metagenomic data with known ground truth, scaling to large sample sizes (e.g. n=1000 at mean depth 11.8) and scoring recovered true positives against false positives. Used to demonstrate that a tool's performance holds when the benchmark is scaled 10-fold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is real (non-simulated) patient or environmental metagenomic data with no ground-truth mutation list — recovery-based TP/FP scoring is impossible The analysis goal is downstream strain/clonal inference rather than benchmarking detection performance

skills.description: Use when comparing statistical meta-analysis or testing methods' empirical power and type I error across scenarios, using simulated summary statistics rather than real data.
skills.name: simulation-based-power-and-type-i-error-estimation
skills.search_text: simulation-based-power-and-type-i-error-estimation Use when comparing statistical meta-analysis or testing methods' empirical power and type I error across scenarios, using simulated summary statistics rather than real data. The goal is estimation of a pooled effect (mMeta provides pooled estimates and 95% CIs, but aMeta is limited to hypothesis testing with no estimation facilities) Only one study is available — mMeta.aMeta requires at least 10 studies (rows in est/std.err) Raw microbiome sequences need processing (quality control, OTU picking) rather than meta-analysis of already-computed summary statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 In-silico evaluation of meta-analysis methods (mMeta, aMeta, and single-marker meta-analyses) by simulating microbiome count data from a Dirichlet-multinomial distribution and estimating empirical power at the 5% significance level, plus type I error under the null. metagenomics/v1 10.1002/sim.8940
skills.summary: In-silico evaluation of meta-analysis methods (mMeta, aMeta, and single-marker meta-analyses) by simulating microbiome count data from a Dirichlet-multinomial distribution and estimating empirical power at the 5% significance level, plus type I error under the null.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is estimation of a pooled effect (mMeta provides pooled estimates and 95% CIs, but aMeta is limited to hypothesis testing with no estimation facilities) Only one study is available — mMeta.aMeta requires at least 10 studies (rows in est/std.err) Raw microbiome sequences need processing (quality control, OTU picking) rather than meta-analysis of already-computed summary statistics

skills.description: Use when validating a new or competing multivariate association test on simulated count data: you need empirical type I error under β = 0 and empirical power under alternatives varying signal density (10%, 20%, 30%) and effect size.
skills.name: simulation-based-type-i-error-estimation
skills.search_text: simulation-based-type-i-error-estimation Use when validating a new or competing multivariate association test on simulated count data: you need empirical type I error under β = 0 and empirical power under alternatives varying signal density (10%, 20%, 30%) and effect size. The input is real (not simulated) association data with a tested hypothesis — use permutation-based significance testing with the full 10,000 permutations rather than simulation-based error calibration. The goal is taxonomic profiling or OTU clustering (e.g. PAM clustering by cophenetic distance) rather than evaluating statistical test calibration. Only one method's raw P-value is needed per replicate with no need for empirical calibration checks across scenarios. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Empirically estimates the type I error rate of a multivariate microbiome association test (here AMAT) by generating replicate null datasets (β = 0) from Dirichlet-multinomial OTU simulations modeled on a real 856-OTU throat microbiome, then computing the proportion of rejections at the nominal 0.05 level. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab120
skills.summary: Empirically estimates the type I error rate of a multivariate microbiome association test (here AMAT) by generating replicate null datasets (β = 0) from Dirichlet-multinomial OTU simulations modeled on a real 856-OTU throat microbiome, then computing the proportion of rejections at the nominal 0.05 level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real (not simulated) association data with a tested hypothesis — use permutation-based significance testing with the full 10,000 permutations rather than simulation-based error calibration. The goal is taxonomic profiling or OTU clustering (e.g. PAM clustering by cophenetic distance) rather than evaluating statistical test calibration. Only one method's raw P-value is needed per replicate with no need for empirical calibration checks across scenarios.

skills.search_text: simulation-dataset-manifest-curation Use when benchmarking strain-resolved assembly tools on simulated low-complexity metagenomes and you need reproducible read simulations, coverage series, aligned BAM artifacts, and a manifest enumerating all datasets. The analysis targets real (non-simulated) long-read datasets such as the human stool microbiome, Mock9, or NWC2 runs handled by the strainberry-analyses Snakefiles Strain variability is high enough that strain-oblivious contigs would need separation into a variable number of strains, a case Strainberry does not handle The community is high-complexity rather than low-complexity with a limited number of well-represented strains http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Simulates a panel of conspecific-strain metagenome communities (seven two-strain E. coli divergence communities, Mock3, and 2-5 strain communities) with Badread v0.2.0 PacBio reads, downsamples Mock3 to 5x-50x, prepares strain-oblivious assemblies and BAM alignments, and compiles a manifest TSV enumerating every dataset and artifact. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Simulates a panel of conspecific-strain metagenome communities (seven two-strain E. coli divergence communities, Mock3, and 2-5 strain communities) with Badread v0.2.0 PacBio reads, downsamples Mock3 to 5x-50x, prepares strain-oblivious assemblies and BAM alignments, and compiles a manifest TSV enumerating every dataset and artifact.

skills.description: Use when a paper claims a quantitative simulation result (e.g., 'all ΔRA are positive and ΔRA decreases as coverage increases') and raw or aggregated reproduction outputs exist from which the metric can be recomputed and checked.
skills.name: simulation-result-verification
skills.search_text: simulation-result-verification Use when a paper claims a quantitative simulation result (e.g., 'all ΔRA are positive and ΔRA decreases as coverage increases') and raw or aggregated reproduction outputs exist from which the metric can be recomputed and checked. The claim to verify is qualitative or based on real (non-simulated) data — this skill is specific to recomputing ΔRA from simulated reproduction outputs. Upstream reproduction output files for LEMON and LUMPY RA at both coverage levels are unavailable, since ΔRA cannot be recomputed without paired RA values per tool per coverage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantitatively verifies a published simulation finding by recomputing derived metrics — here, delta Reconstruction Accuracy (ΔRA = RA_LEMON − RA_LUMPY) from simulated gut metagenomics reproduction outputs at 5X and 30X coverage — and checking explicit positivity and trend criteria against the paper's Fig. 5a claim. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3301-8
skills.summary: Quantitatively verifies a published simulation finding by recomputing derived metrics — here, delta Reconstruction Accuracy (ΔRA = RA_LEMON − RA_LUMPY) from simulated gut metagenomics reproduction outputs at 5X and 30X coverage — and checking explicit positivity and trend criteria against the paper's Fig. 5a claim.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The claim to verify is qualitative or based on real (non-simulated) data — this skill is specific to recomputing ΔRA from simulated reproduction outputs. Upstream reproduction output files for LEMON and LUMPY RA at both coverage levels are unavailable, since ΔRA cannot be recomputed without paired RA values per tool per coverage.

skills.description: Use when classifying full-length or amplicon 16S rRNA FASTA sequences against a reference database (e.g. Greengenes2 2024.09) with a fast k-mer classifier and needing per-rank bootstrap confidence assignments as a benchmark baseline.
skills.name: sintax-bootstrap-taxonomy-classification
skills.search_text: sintax-bootstrap-taxonomy-classification Use when classifying full-length or amplicon 16S rRNA FASTA sequences against a reference database (e.g. Greengenes2 2024.09) with a fast k-mer classifier and needing per-rank bootstrap confidence assignments as a benchmark baseline. Input is a feature table or already-classified taxonomy profiles rather than raw FASTA amplicon sequences Maximum species-level accuracy is required: SINTAX's 0.8 bootstrap cutoff returns many unclassified calls and it underperforms DADA2, QIIME 2, and DeepTaxa on the same Greengenes2 test set Evaluating short V3-V4/V4 amplicons where a model trained specifically on in-silico amplicons (e.g. DeepTaxa V3-V4 checkpoint, 87.55%) may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Species-level taxonomic classification of 16S rRNA amplicon sequences using SINTAX, the k-mer-based naive-Bayes classifier in USEARCH, with bootstrap confidence support. skills.name: six-frame-translation-of-genome-assemblies
skills.search_text: six-frame-translation-of-genome-assemblies Use when assembled nucleotide contigs (or metagenomic contigs) must be converted to protein sequences in all six frames to enumerate short ORFs (<200 aa) as candidate RiPP precursor peptides within putative biosynthetic gene clusters. When a motif-based candidate set is preferred: the all-ORF mode does not filter by RiPP sequence motifs and yields a much larger candidate set (e.g., 14,694 short ORFs across six BGCs in one genome) at the cost of a larger search space When the input is unassembled short reads — MetaMiner requires reads to be first assembled into contigs before six-frame translation When the spectra of interest lack paired genomics/metagenomics data (about 99% of GNPS spectra), since translated ORFs can only be searched against spectra with matched genomic context http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A candidate-generation step from MetaMiner's all-ORF genome-mining mode: assembled nucleotide contigs are translated into protein sequence in all six frames so that HMMer-detected RiPP modification enzymes can anchor 10 kbp putative biosynthetic gene cluster windows from which all short ORFs are exhaustively extracted. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.09.004

skills.when_to_use_negative: When a motif-based candidate set is preferred: the all-ORF mode does not filter by RiPP sequence motifs and yields a much larger candidate set (e.g., 14,694 short ORFs across six BGCs in one genome) at the cost of a larger search space When the input is unassembled short reads — MetaMiner requires reads to be first assembled into contigs before six-frame translation When the spectra of interest lack paired genomics/metagenomics data (about 99% of GNPS spectra), since translated ORFs can only be searched against spectra with matched genomic context

skills.description: Use when classifying whole-genome shotgun metagenomic reads (Illumina FASTQ/FASTA) against protein reference databases, especially when taxa are underrepresented in the database or divergence prevents exact k-mer nucleotide matches.
skills.name: six-frame-translation-protein-search
skills.search_text: six-frame-translation-protein-search Use when classifying whole-genome shotgun metagenomic reads (Illumina FASTQ/FASTA) against protein reference databases, especially when taxa are underrepresented in the database or divergence prevents exact k-mer nucleotide matches. Reads originate from non-protein-coding genomic regions — protein-level classification cannot assign them Sequenced strains are already in the reference database — nucleotide-level classifiers (e.g. Kraken) will be more sensitive since they can assess the entire genome Input is already protein sequence without enabling option -p to disable translation http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Kaiju's core classification method: translate each NGS read into six reading frames, split at stop codons into amino acid fragments, and query maximum (in-)exact protein matches via backwards search in the BWT to assign NCBI taxonomy. skills.description: Use when short-read metagenomic or metatranscriptomic FASTQ/FASTA data must be assembled de novo into protein sequences rather than nucleotide contigs.
skills.name: six-frame-translation-read-assembly
skills.search_text: six-frame-translation-read-assembly Use when short-read metagenomic or metatranscriptomic FASTQ/FASTA data must be assembled de novo into protein sequences rather than nucleotide contigs. Nucleotide contigs are the required output (e.g. strain-resolved assembly of viral genomes or microbial 16S rRNAs) — use PenguiN (`penguin nuclassemble` or `penguin guided_nuclassemble`), since Plass only outputs protein sequences. Input is already-assembled contigs or long reads rather than short-read sequencing data — Plass is a short-read assembler. The dataset is a low-complexity, non-metagenomic sample where standard nucleotide assemblers suffice; the tool is meant to work best for complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic datasets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 De novo protein-level assembly: Plass six-frame-translates short sequencing reads and assembles the translated sequences directly into protein FASTA, recovering 2–10 times more protein sequences from complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic samples than nucleotide-level assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41592-019-0437-4
skills.summary: De novo protein-level assembly: Plass six-frame-translates short sequencing reads and assembles the translated sequences directly into protein FASTA, recovering 2–10 times more protein sequences from complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic samples than nucleotide-level assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Nucleotide contigs are the required output (e.g. strain-resolved assembly of viral genomes or microbial 16S rRNAs) — use PenguiN (`penguin nuclassemble` or `penguin guided_nuclassemble`), since Plass only outputs protein sequences. Input is already-assembled contigs or long reads rather than short-read sequencing data — Plass is a short-read assembler. The dataset is a low-complexity, non-metagenomic sample where standard nucleotide assemblers suffice; the tool is meant to work best for complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic datasets.

skills.description: Use when highly similar sample sequences (e.g., human mitogenomes) have been assembled into an acyclic colored de Bruijn graph and you need to call small indels (< 50 bp) and SNPs with graph-coordinate output.
skills.name: small-indel-variant-detection
skills.search_text: small-indel-variant-detection Use when highly similar sample sequences (e.g., human mitogenomes) have been assembled into an acyclic colored de Bruijn graph and you need to call small indels (< 50 bp) and SNPs with graph-coordinate output. skills.description: Use when comparing feature (OTU/species/taxon) abundance across two or more sample groups in sparse, high-throughput marker-gene survey count data where under-sampling and normalization effects must be modeled to detect differential abundance.
skills.name: sparse-sequencing-data-statistics
skills.search_text: sparse-sequencing-data-statistics Use when comparing feature (OTU/species/taxon) abundance across two or more sample groups in sparse, high-throughput marker-gene survey count data where under-sampling and normalization effects must be modeled to detect differential abundance. The analysis does not involve two or more sample groups — metagenomeSeq is designed to determine features (be it OTU, species, etc.) differentially abundant between two or more groups of multiple samples, so single-group summaries are out of scope. Sample annotations do not define groups, so a design matrix encoding the group comparison cannot be set up for the zig EM fit. The data are not sparse high-throughput sequencing counts, since the model accounts for under-sampling, a common feature of large-scale marker gene studies. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Statistical analysis for sparse high-throughput marker-gene sequencing data: metagenomeSeq combines a novel normalization technique with a zero-inflated statistical model that accounts for under-sampling of microbial communities to identify features (OTU/species/taxa) differentially abundant between two or more groups. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nmeth.2658
skills.summary: Statistical analysis for sparse high-throughput marker-gene sequencing data: metagenomeSeq combines a novel normalization technique with a zero-inflated statistical model that accounts for under-sampling of microbial communities to identify features (OTU/species/taxa) differentially abundant between two or more groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis does not involve two or more sample groups — metagenomeSeq is designed to determine features (be it OTU, species, etc.) differentially abundant between two or more groups of multiple samples, so single-group summaries are out of scope. Sample annotations do not define groups, so a design matrix encoding the group comparison cannot be set up for the zig EM fit. The data are not sparse high-throughput sequencing counts, since the model accounts for under-sampling, a common feature of large-scale marker gene studies.

skills.description: Use when you have terrain-corrected Sentinel-1 gamma_0 raster stacks (10 m pixels) and need spatial texture variables representing habitat structural heterogeneity for biodiversity models.
skills.name: spatial-neighborhood-statistics-computation
skills.search_text: spatial-neighborhood-statistics-computation Use when you have terrain-corrected Sentinel-1 gamma_0 raster stacks (10 m pixels) and need spatial texture variables representing habitat structural heterogeneity for biodiversity models. skills.summary: Validates PICRUSt 16S-predicted metagenomes by computing Spearman correlations between predicted and shotgun-annotated KO (KEGG Ortholog) abundances across all 6,885 KO groups, using HMP paired 16S/shotgun samples and synthetic mock communities as benchmarks.

skills.description: Use when a published HUBDesign probe FASTA (e.g., probes/Sepsis) must be evaluated for taxonomic breadth — which strains of a multi-genome design dataset carry species-level versus genus-level probes.
skills.name: species-and-genus-coverage-assessment
skills.search_text: species-and-genus-coverage-assessment Use when a published HUBDesign probe FASTA (e.g., probes/Sepsis) must be evaluated for taxonomic breadth — which strains of a multi-genome design dataset carry species-level versus genus-level probes. skills.search_text: spectral-networking-clustering-of-tandem-ms Use when you have millions of tandem MS/MS spectra (e.g. GNPS molecular networking datasets such as MSV000079506–MSV000080102) and need to group spectra with related fragmentation patterns into spectral families before or after database search. The goal is de novo peptide-spectrum identification rather than clustering/diversity estimation — use MetaMiner/RiPPquest search with MS-DPR p-values and the 1% FDR target-decoy threshold instead. In MetaMiner it is used to enlarge RiPP identifications and to contextualize discovery yield (10 million spectra -> 8,071 families). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.09.004

skills.search_text: spike-in-coverage-peak-library-construction Use when benchmarking contig extension or de novo assembly tools on viral metagenomic data and you need a controlled in silico ground truth with uneven, spike-like coverage profiles mimicking abundant-virus read distributions. The goal is real metagenomic (non-simulated) analysis — this skill only produces synthetic ground-truth datasets for benchmarking. Platform is not Illumina-like short reads; pIRS simulates paired-end Illumina reads and the 100/250 bp parameterization assumes short-read chemistry. skills.search_text: spike-in-ground-truth-accuracy-evaluation Use when a prediction method (e.g., metagenomic fecal source tracking) must be validated against samples with known, predetermined input proportions, such as spike-in mesocosms or mock communities. Samples have no known composition — without ground-truth fractions, sensitivity/specificity cannot be computed Evaluating abundance accuracy for sources whose reference genomes are under-sampled (e.g., cow fecal microbiomes), where false negatives are systematic rather than method-driven Input is a single environmental sample without spike-in or mock-community controls http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks a source-tracking or abundance-inference method against spike-in mesocosms of known composition by scoring predicted attribution/apportionment (cell fractions) against the ground-truth cell fractions established during mesocosm construction, reporting sensitivity, specificity, and residual correlations. metagenomics/v1 10.1021/acs.est.5c03603
skills.summary: Benchmarks a source-tracking or abundance-inference method against spike-in mesocosms of known composition by scoring predicted attribution/apportionment (cell fractions) against the ground-truth cell fractions established during mesocosm construction, reporting sensitivity, specificity, and residual correlations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples have no known composition — without ground-truth fractions, sensitivity/specificity cannot be computed Evaluating abundance accuracy for sources whose reference genomes are under-sampled (e.g., cow fecal microbiomes), where false negatives are systematic rather than method-driven Input is a single environmental sample without spike-in or mock-community controls

skills.description: Use when a lab needs to convert sample records stored in MetaLIMS (generic collection fields, DNA/RNA processing fields, and lab-specific custom fields) into a submission form for a sequencing facility running Clarity LIMS.
skills.name: spreadsheet-report-export
skills.search_text: spreadsheet-report-export Use when a lab needs to convert sample records stored in MetaLIMS (generic collection fields, DNA/RNA processing fields, and lab-specific custom fields) into a submission form for a sequencing facility running Clarity LIMS. The target facility does not use Clarity LIMS — the export produces a form compatible specifically with Clarity LIMS, not arbitrary submission templates The lab needs to record or export NGS or analysis data — MetaLIMS does not record NGS or analysis data, which is 'common in many NGS LIMS' The user needs post-sequencing pipeline results — MetaLIMS' focus is storing sample metadata prior to sequencing and analysis pipelines http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Export stored sample metadata from MetaLIMS as a basic sequencing submission form (clarity_submission_form.csv) compatible with the proprietary Clarity LIMS system used by some sequencing facilities. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gigascience/gix025
skills.summary: Export stored sample metadata from MetaLIMS as a basic sequencing submission form (clarity_submission_form.csv) compatible with the proprietary Clarity LIMS system used by some sequencing facilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target facility does not use Clarity LIMS — the export produces a form compatible specifically with Clarity LIMS, not arbitrary submission templates The lab needs to record or export NGS or analysis data — MetaLIMS does not record NGS or analysis data, which is 'common in many NGS LIMS' The user needs post-sequencing pipeline results — MetaLIMS' focus is storing sample metadata prior to sequencing and analysis pipelines

skills.description: Use when an analysis requires raw metagenomic reads (FASTQ) identified by specific NCBI SRA accession IDs (e.g., SRS-prefixed accessions) as starting material for classification or abundance profiling.
skills.name: sra-accession-retrieval
skills.search_text: sra-accession-retrieval Use when an analysis requires raw metagenomic reads (FASTQ) identified by specific NCBI SRA accession IDs (e.g., SRS-prefixed accessions) as starting material for classification or abundance profiling. The reads are already simulated or locally available (e.g., Mason-simulated simBA-5 reads) and do not need archival retrieval. The required data are reference genomes from NCBI RefSeq or the NCBI taxonomy database, which are downloaded for database building, not SRA read accessions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Retrieves raw metagenomic sequencing data from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive by accession ID, as done for the HMP saliva samples (SRS019120, SRS014468, SRS015055) in the Kraken evaluation. This supplies the FASTQ inputs required for downstream trimming and taxonomic classification. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: Retrieves raw metagenomic sequencing data from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive by accession ID, as done for the HMP saliva samples (SRS019120, SRS014468, SRS015055) in the Kraken evaluation. This supplies the FASTQ inputs required for downstream trimming and taxonomic classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are already simulated or locally available (e.g., Mason-simulated simBA-5 reads) and do not need archival retrieval. The required data are reference genomes from NCBI RefSeq or the NCBI taxonomy database, which are downloaded for database building, not SRA read accessions.

skills.description: Use when input metagenomic samples arrive as NCBI SRA archives and must be converted to FASTQ/FASTA and quality-checked before mapping-based taxonomic or functional profiling in the CAMAMED pipeline.
skills.name: sra-archive-to-fastq-conversion
skills.search_text: sra-archive-to-fastq-conversion Use when input metagenomic samples arrive as NCBI SRA archives and must be converted to FASTQ/FASTA and quality-checked before mapping-based taxonomic or functional profiling in the CAMAMED pipeline. Input samples are already in FASTQ/FASTA format and only need QC statistics rather than SRA conversion The goal is downstream CAMAMED analysis (mapping to non-redundant gene catalogs, CSS normalization, KEGG/KEGG ortholog annotation) rather than pre-processing raw SRA archives http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Pre-processes metagenomic sample archives by converting SRA files to FASTQ/FASTA with SRA Toolkit's fastq-dump, then validating each converted file with FastQC v0.11.5 quality reports and SeqKit v0.10.1 sequence statistics before the CAMAMED mapping stage. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Pre-processes metagenomic sample archives by converting SRA files to FASTQ/FASTA with SRA Toolkit's fastq-dump, then validating each converted file with FastQC v0.11.5 quality reports and SeqKit v0.10.1 sequence statistics before the CAMAMED mapping stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples are already in FASTQ/FASTA format and only need QC statistics rather than SRA conversion The goal is downstream CAMAMED analysis (mapping to non-redundant gene catalogs, CSS normalization, KEGG/KEGG ortholog annotation) rather than pre-processing raw SRA archives

skills.description: Use when an analysis pipeline starts from a public NCBI SRA run accession (e.g. SRR6287056) and raw paired-end FASTQ files for both mates must be downloaded before preprocessing steps such as hg19 host-read depletion.
skills.name: sra-fastq-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: sra-fastq-data-retrieval Use when an analysis pipeline starts from a public NCBI SRA run accession (e.g. SRR6287056) and raw paired-end FASTQ files for both mates must be downloaded before preprocessing steps such as hg19 host-read depletion. The reads are already available locally as FASTQ files — downloading from SRA again is unnecessary. The required data are aligned reads (BAM) or assembled contigs rather than raw reads; fasterq-dump is designed for raw read extraction. The target data are not deposited in NCBI SRA/ENA (e.g. only available as in silico simulated reads bundled with the contig-extender examples folder). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Retrieves raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads for a metagenomic SRA accession (e.g. SRR6287056) from NCBI using sra-tools (prefetch/fasterq-dump), yielding the mate FASTQ files needed downstream for hg19 host depletion and de novo assembly with tools like ContigExtender/metaSPAdes. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04038-2
skills.summary: Retrieves raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads for a metagenomic SRA accession (e.g. SRR6287056) from NCBI using sra-tools (prefetch/fasterq-dump), yielding the mate FASTQ files needed downstream for hg19 host depletion and de novo assembly with tools like ContigExtender/metaSPAdes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are already available locally as FASTQ files — downloading from SRA again is unnecessary. The required data are aligned reads (BAM) or assembled contigs rather than raw reads; fasterq-dump is designed for raw read extraction. The target data are not deposited in NCBI SRA/ENA (e.g. only available as in silico simulated reads bundled with the contig-extender examples folder).

skills.description: Use when a downstream variant-discovery or strain-analysis pipeline (e.g. cellsnp-lite + MetaQuad) needs raw sequencing reads from a publicly archived metagenomic study and only the BioProject accession is known.
skills.name: sra-metagenomic-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: sra-metagenomic-data-retrieval Use when a downstream variant-discovery or strain-analysis pipeline (e.g. cellsnp-lite + MetaQuad) needs raw sequencing reads from a publicly archived metagenomic study and only the BioProject accession is known. When the raw reads are already available locally as FASTQ or BAM files — go straight to bwa/samtools alignment instead. When the input is single-cell sequencing data rather than shotgun metagenomic samples — the MetaQuad BIO-ML workflow is tailored to shotgun metagenomic data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Retrieve raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQ files from a public BioProject on SRA/NCBI (e.g. the 30-sample BIO-ML dataset from BioProject PRJNA544527) using sra-tools' fasterq-dump, as the entry step of a MetaQuad shared-informative-variant pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Retrieve raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQ files from a public BioProject on SRA/NCBI (e.g. the 30-sample BIO-ML dataset from BioProject PRJNA544527) using sra-tools' fasterq-dump, as the entry step of a MetaQuad shared-informative-variant pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the raw reads are already available locally as FASTQ or BAM files — go straight to bwa/samtools alignment instead. When the input is single-cell sequencing data rather than shotgun metagenomic samples — the MetaQuad BIO-ML workflow is tailored to shotgun metagenomic data.

skills.description: Use when a task requires reproducing the MTBC_B (n=1,609) Mykrobe resistance-prediction validation and the raw isolate FASTQ reads must first be downloaded from ENA/NCBI SRA using accession codes in Supplementary Data.
skills.name: sra-read-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: sra-read-data-retrieval Use when a task requires reproducing the MTBC_B (n=1,609) Mykrobe resistance-prediction validation and the raw isolate FASTQ reads must first be downloaded from ENA/NCBI SRA using accession codes in Supplementary Data. The sequencing reads are already available locally as FASTQ — proceed directly to running Mykrobe predictor rather than re-downloading. No accession codes or phenotyping tables are available (Supplementary Data 1–10 not accessible), so isolates cannot be traced to SRA entries. The task targets S. aureus or other species validation sets (St_A1, St_B1) whose accessions and QC thresholds differ from the MTBC workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Retrieves raw MTBC clinical-isolate sequencing reads from ENA/NCBI SRA using accession codes listed in the paper's Supplementary Data, paired with per-isolate phenotypic DST resistance labels, to enable reproduction of Mykrobe predictor validation results (82.6%/98.5% sensitivity/specificity on n=1,609 MTBC_B samples). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms10063
skills.summary: Retrieves raw MTBC clinical-isolate sequencing reads from ENA/NCBI SRA using accession codes listed in the paper's Supplementary Data, paired with per-isolate phenotypic DST resistance labels, to enable reproduction of Mykrobe predictor validation results (82.6%/98.5% sensitivity/specificity on n=1,609 MTBC_B samples).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequencing reads are already available locally as FASTQ — proceed directly to running Mykrobe predictor rather than re-downloading. No accession codes or phenotyping tables are available (Supplementary Data 1–10 not accessible), so isolates cannot be traced to SRA entries. The task targets S. aureus or other species validation sets (St_A1, St_B1) whose accessions and QC thresholds differ from the MTBC workflow.

skills.description: Use when a benchmark or reproduction task requires downloading raw short-read and long-read FASTQ data for specific samples identified by archive accessions (e.g. BioProject PRJDB4377, Supplementary Table S7).
skills.name: sra-read-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: sra-read-data-retrieval Use when a benchmark or reproduction task requires downloading raw short-read and long-read FASTQ data for specific samples identified by archive accessions (e.g. BioProject PRJDB4377, Supplementary Table S7). The analysis only needs the authors' published assemblies rather than raw reads — download the FigShare assembly bundle directly instead The input data are already local FASTQ/FASTA files and only the assembly step (MetaPlatanus) remains to be executed The target study provides no public accession or supplementary accession table for its raw reads (a noted missing signal for some mock/human gut benchmarks) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Retrieves raw sequencing reads (Illumina paired-end and ONT/PacBio long reads) from public sequence read archives such as DDBJ SRA, using BioProject accessions and supplementary accession tables, to serve as the input reads for de novo metagenome assembly benchmarks like the MetaPlatanus saliva PromethION study. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Retrieves raw sequencing reads (Illumina paired-end and ONT/PacBio long reads) from public sequence read archives such as DDBJ SRA, using BioProject accessions and supplementary accession tables, to serve as the input reads for de novo metagenome assembly benchmarks like the MetaPlatanus saliva PromethION study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis only needs the authors' published assemblies rather than raw reads — download the FigShare assembly bundle directly instead The input data are already local FASTQ/FASTA files and only the assembly step (MetaPlatanus) remains to be executed The target study provides no public accession or supplementary accession table for its raw reads (a noted missing signal for some mock/human gut benchmarks)

skills.description: Use when you have full-length/nearly full-length 16S/18S SSU sequences reconstructed by EMIRGE and MetaRib (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta) plus per-sequence abundance counts, and need clustered representatives and consolidated abundances prior to taxonomic classification.
skills.name: ssu-fasta-output-processing
skills.search_text: ssu-fasta-output-processing Use when you have full-length/nearly full-length 16S/18S SSU sequences reconstructed by EMIRGE and MetaRib (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta) plus per-sequence abundance counts, and need clustered representatives and consolidated abundances prior to taxonomic classification. Input is already a clustered representative FASTA or an abundance table at the cluster level — re-clustering would merge distinct taxa. You are classifying short Illumina reads directly rather than reconstructed full-length SSU sequences; RiboTaxa showed direct short-read classification yields a high rate of false positives. Input sequences are amplicon ASVs already denoised/merged at 100% (e.g. via EMIRGE JOIN_TRESHOLD identity merging) and no abundance consolidation across reconstructions is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Deduplicate reconstructed SSU rRNA gene sequences before taxonomic affiliation by clustering the EMIRGE/MetaRib outputs at 97% identity with VSEARCH and summing BBMap-assigned read counts per cluster so relative abundances reflect clusters rather than redundant reconstructed variants. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Deduplicate reconstructed SSU rRNA gene sequences before taxonomic affiliation by clustering the EMIRGE/MetaRib outputs at 97% identity with VSEARCH and summing BBMap-assigned read counts per cluster so relative abundances reflect clusters rather than redundant reconstructed variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a clustered representative FASTA or an abundance table at the cluster level — re-clustering would merge distinct taxa. You are classifying short Illumina reads directly rather than reconstructed full-length SSU sequences; RiboTaxa showed direct short-read classification yields a high rate of false positives. Input sequences are amplicon ASVs already denoised/merged at 100% (e.g. via EMIRGE JOIN_TRESHOLD identity merging) and no abundance consolidation across reconstructions is needed.

skills.description: Use when you have reconstructed SSU rRNA sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta) and quality-controlled metagenomic reads, and need per-sequence relative abundance estimates before clustering or classification.
skills.name: ssu-rna-sequence-abundance-quantification
skills.search_text: ssu-rna-sequence-abundance-quantification Use when you have reconstructed SSU rRNA sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta) and quality-controlled metagenomic reads, and need per-sequence relative abundance estimates before clustering or classification. Input is a feature/abundance table already derived from amplicon ASVs/OTUs rather than reconstructed SSU sequences needing read-mapping quantification You want to estimate relative abundance of raw short reads directly with a classifier (Kraken2, Centrifuge) instead of validating reconstructed SSU sequences The reference SSU sequences have not yet been reconstructed (BBMap mapping requires the metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta reference to exist) http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies the relative abundance of reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences in RiboTaxa by mapping unfiltered high-quality reads back onto them with BBMap and normalizing per-sequence read counts to percentages, prior to 97% clustering and taxonomic affiliation. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Quantifies the relative abundance of reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences in RiboTaxa by mapping unfiltered high-quality reads back onto them with BBMap and normalizing per-sequence read counts to percentages, prior to 97% clustering and taxonomic affiliation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a feature/abundance table already derived from amplicon ASVs/OTUs rather than reconstructed SSU sequences needing read-mapping quantification You want to estimate relative abundance of raw short reads directly with a classifier (Kraken2, Centrifuge) instead of validating reconstructed SSU sequences The reference SSU sequences have not yet been reconstructed (BBMap mapping requires the metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta reference to exist)

skills.description: Use when you have full-length/nearly full-length 16S/18S SSU rRNA sequences reconstructed from metagenomic reads (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.

skills.search_text: ssu-rna-sequence-clustering-vsearch Use when you have full-length/nearly full-length 16S/18S SSU rRNA sequences reconstructed from metagenomic reads (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences. Input is already a non-redundant cluster representative set or a feature/abundance table rather than reconstructed SSU FASTA sequences You need to cluster raw short reads or amplicon ASVs rather than full-length reconstructed SSU rRNA sequences You are applying 16S rRNA gene copy number normalization — RiboTaxa explicitly chooses not to correct for copy number, so abundance adjustment at this stage would conflict with the pipeline's design http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Deduplicate reconstructed SSU rRNA gene sequences (from EMIRGE and MetaRib within RiboTaxa) by clustering at 97% identity with VSEARCH, summing the BBMap-derived 'Assigned reads' abundances of all cluster members before taxonomic affiliation so that relative abundances reflect consolidated clusters rather than redundant reconstructions. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Deduplicate reconstructed SSU rRNA gene sequences (from EMIRGE and MetaRib within RiboTaxa) by clustering at 97% identity with VSEARCH, summing the BBMap-derived 'Assigned reads' abundances of all cluster members before taxonomic affiliation so that relative abundances reflect consolidated clusters rather than redundant reconstructions.

skills.description: Use when metagenomic Illumina (meta)genomic FASTQ reads need enrichment for SSU rRNA fragments before targeted full-length 16S/18S reconstruction, e.g. RiboTaxa-style extraction against SILVA SSU 138.1.

The reads are long assembled contigs or genomes rather than short Illumina reads — use rRNA feature annotation (e.g. barrnap) instead The goal is taxonomic classification directly on reads; the article warns that 'inferring taxa directly to short-length Illumina reads resulted in a high rate of false positives while reconstructed sequences were correctly assigned' http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Filters 16S/18S SSU rRNA reads out of adapter-trimmed metagenomic FASTQ reads using SortMeRNA against a pre-indexed SILVA SSU 138.1 database, producing rRNA-enriched FASTQ files that feed EMIRGE-based SSU gene reconstruction in the RiboTaxa pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Filters 16S/18S SSU rRNA reads out of adapter-trimmed metagenomic FASTQ reads using SortMeRNA against a pre-indexed SILVA SSU 138.1 database, producing rRNA-enriched FASTQ files that feed EMIRGE-based SSU gene reconstruction in the RiboTaxa pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are long assembled contigs or genomes rather than short Illumina reads — use rRNA feature annotation (e.g. barrnap) instead The goal is taxonomic classification directly on reads; the article warns that 'inferring taxa directly to short-length Illumina reads resulted in a high rate of false positives while reconstructed sequences were correctly assigned'

skills.description: Use when input is Illumina paired-end or single-end (meta)genomic FASTQ and the goal is near-full-length SSU rRNA gene sequences (not short-read taxonomic classification), e.g. to enable species-level 16S/18S assignment or to recover novel rRNA variants.
skills.name: ssu-rrna-sequence-reconstruction
skills.search_text: ssu-rrna-sequence-reconstruction Use when input is Illumina paired-end or single-end (meta)genomic FASTQ and the goal is near-full-length SSU rRNA gene sequences (not short-read taxonomic classification), e.g. to enable species-level 16S/18S assignment or to recover novel rRNA variants. When the goal is rapid taxonomic profiling of short reads rather than full-length SSU reconstruction — RiboTaxa is not as fast as short-read classifiers (Kraken2, Centrifuge) When the analysis target is not ribosomal RNA (e.g. whole-genome assembly or mRNA expression) When read data are amplicon-only 16S PCR products that are already full-length and need no reference-targeted assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reconstruct full-length/near-full-length SSU (16S/18S) rRNA gene sequences from shotgun Illumina metagenomic reads by combining EMIRGE (Emirge_amplicon.py) on SortMeRNA-filtered SSU reads with MetaRib on unfiltered high-quality reads, merging outputs into metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta. This combined strategy gave greater population characterisation than any single extractor/assembler combination in the RiboTaxa benchmarking. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Reconstruct full-length/near-full-length SSU (16S/18S) rRNA gene sequences from shotgun Illumina metagenomic reads by combining EMIRGE (Emirge_amplicon.py) on SortMeRNA-filtered SSU reads with MetaRib on unfiltered high-quality reads, merging outputs into metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta. This combined strategy gave greater population characterisation than any single extractor/assembler combination in the RiboTaxa benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is rapid taxonomic profiling of short reads rather than full-length SSU reconstruction — RiboTaxa is not as fast as short-read classifiers (Kraken2, Centrifuge) When the analysis target is not ribosomal RNA (e.g. whole-genome assembly or mRNA expression) When read data are amplicon-only 16S PCR products that are already full-length and need no reference-targeted assembly

skills.description: Use when reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta from RiboTaxa's EMIRGE/MetaRib reconstruction) must be taxonomically assigned down to species level with per-sequence confidence and relative abundance.
skills.name: ssu-rrna-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: ssu-rrna-taxonomic-classification Use when reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta from RiboTaxa's EMIRGE/MetaRib reconstruction) must be taxonomically assigned down to species level with per-sequence confidence and relative abundance. Input is raw short Illumina reads to be classified directly without prior SSU reconstruction — the article shows inferring taxa directly to short reads results in a high rate of false positives Only rapid approximate profiling is needed and runtime dominates — the article notes RiboTaxa is not as fast as short-read classifiers (Kraken2, Centrifuge) Chimera detection or 16S rRNA gene copy-number normalization are mandatory requirements — neither was included in this workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Taxonomic classification of reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA gene sequences from metagenomics data, using QIIME 2's sklearn classifier against a SILVA 138 reference classifier at a confidence threshold of 0.7, optionally benchmarked against seven classifiers to compute precision/recall/F-measure at each rank. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac070
skills.summary: Taxonomic classification of reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA gene sequences from metagenomics data, using QIIME 2's sklearn classifier against a SILVA 138 reference classifier at a confidence threshold of 0.7, optionally benchmarked against seven classifiers to compute precision/recall/F-measure at each rank.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw short Illumina reads to be classified directly without prior SSU reconstruction — the article shows inferring taxa directly to short reads results in a high rate of false positives Only rapid approximate profiling is needed and runtime dominates — the article notes RiboTaxa is not as fast as short-read classifiers (Kraken2, Centrifuge) Chimera detection or 16S rRNA gene copy-number normalization are mandatory requirements — neither was included in this workflow

skills.summary: Generates per-sequence stacked bar plots of relative-abundance trajectories over time from an OTU table (taxa by samples with sequence IDs and sampling times), optionally overlaying external perturbation events, to visually inspect raw or LUMINATE-denoised longitudinal microbiome data.
