skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how accurately a gene caller predicts start codons (not just gene presence) by scoring exact and near-correct start-site calls against a curated annotation truth set.
skills.name: start-codon-position-comparison
skills.search_text: start-codon-position-comparison Use when you need to quantify how accurately a gene caller predicts start codons (not just gene presence) by scoring exact and near-correct start-site calls against a curated annotation truth set. Input is metagenomic sequence fragments without a curated whole-genome truth set — use Glimmer-MG's simulated/real metagenome evaluation instead The goal is only gene-region detection (whole-gene accuracy), not start-codon-position accuracy — a simpler whole-gene sensitivity/precision score suffices Sequences are highly error-prone reads with indels where the paper notes accuracy evaluation of start sites is dominated by frame-tracking errors http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A benchmarking procedure that evaluates gene-prediction pipelines (Glimmer3.0, Glimmer3.1, Glimmer-MG) by comparing predicted gene start positions against curated reference annotations, computing 3' (start-site) and 5' sensitivity and precision per genome. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure that evaluates gene-prediction pipelines (Glimmer3.0, Glimmer3.1, Glimmer-MG) by comparing predicted gene start positions against curated reference annotations, computing 3' (start-site) and 5' sensitivity and precision per genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is metagenomic sequence fragments without a curated whole-genome truth set — use Glimmer-MG's simulated/real metagenome evaluation instead The goal is only gene-region detection (whole-gene accuracy), not start-codon-position accuracy — a simpler whole-gene sensitivity/precision score suffices Sequences are highly error-prone reads with indels where the paper notes accuracy evaluation of start sites is dominated by frame-tracking errors

skills.description: Use when you have a longitudinal OTU table (taxa by samples with sequence IDs and sampling times) of noisy sequencing counts and need denoised relative abundances plus posterior probabilities that observed zeros are sampling zeros rather than absences.
skills.name: state-space-model-variational-inference
skills.search_text: state-space-model-variational-inference Use when you have a longitudinal OTU table (taxa by samples with sequence IDs and sampling times) of noisy sequencing counts and need denoised relative abundances plus posterior probabilities that observed zeros are sampling zeros rather than absences. Ultra-sparse taxa (>90% missing entries) dominate the table without pre-filtering — the README recommends removing them first because little information exists in their trajectory The goal is cross-sectional (single time point) compositional inference — LUMINATE is designed for longitudinal count data with temporal dependence between states A comparison baseline requires MALLARD's model in the Silverman et al. (2019) framework — the article notes no public implementation of MALLARD's in that framework exists Run LUMINATE's state-space variational inference to reconstruct latent relative-abundance trajectories from longitudinal sequencing counts and to distinguish biological zeros (taxon absent) from technical zeros (taxon below detection threshold). The approach reformulates posterior inference in a state-space model as a structured optimization problem, making it orders of magnitude faster than TGP-CODA or MALLARD with similar or better accuracy. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2020.05.006
skills.summary: Run LUMINATE's state-space variational inference to reconstruct latent relative-abundance trajectories from longitudinal sequencing counts and to distinguish biological zeros (taxon absent) from technical zeros (taxon below detection threshold). The approach reformulates posterior inference in a state-space model as a structured optimization problem, making it orders of magnitude faster than TGP-CODA or MALLARD with similar or better accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ultra-sparse taxa (>90% missing entries) dominate the table without pre-filtering — the README recommends removing them first because little information exists in their trajectory The goal is cross-sectional (single time point) compositional inference — LUMINATE is designed for longitudinal count data with temporal dependence between states A comparison baseline requires MALLARD's model in the Silverman et al. (2019) framework — the article notes no public implementation of MALLARD's in that framework exists

skills.description: Use when meta-analyzing summary statistics (effect estimates and standard errors) across multiple related markers and you need to decide between or verify that the group permutation p-value method outperforms asymptotic normality.
skills.name: statistical-power-comparison-across-meta-analysis-methods
skills.search_text: statistical-power-comparison-across-meta-analysis-methods Use when meta-analyzing summary statistics (effect estimates and standard errors) across multiple related markers and you need to decide between or verify that the group permutation p-value method outperforms asymptotic normality. Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ/OTU tables) rather than summary statistics — mMeta/aMeta require only effect estimates and their standard errors, which are hard to obtain from studies reporting only graphs or stratified summary values Fewer than 10 studies are available — the mMeta.aMeta function requires the number of studies (rows) to be >= 10 Marker-by-marker correlation estimates (not just p-value/power comparison) are the goal — use mMeta's non-parametric permutation correlation estimation instead, since aMeta is limited to hypothesis testing http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks the p-value calculation methods underlying mMeta/aMeta — the semi-parametric group permutation method (Follmann-Proschan) versus the parametric method based on asymptotic normality (mu_hat/sigma_mu ~ N(0,1)) — by comparing p-values and power at the 5% significance level across markers. metagenomics/v1 10.1002/sim.8940
skills.summary: Benchmarks the p-value calculation methods underlying mMeta/aMeta — the semi-parametric group permutation method (Follmann-Proschan) versus the parametric method based on asymptotic normality (mu_hat/sigma_mu ~ N(0,1)) — by comparing p-values and power at the 5% significance level across markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ/OTU tables) rather than summary statistics — mMeta/aMeta require only effect estimates and their standard errors, which are hard to obtain from studies reporting only graphs or stratified summary values Fewer than 10 studies are available — the mMeta.aMeta function requires the number of studies (rows) to be >= 10 Marker-by-marker correlation estimates (not just p-value/power comparison) are the goal — use mMeta's non-parametric permutation correlation estimation instead, since aMeta is limited to hypothesis testing

skills.description: Use when you must show whether a new statistical test is more than existing multivariate microbiome association tests across controlled simulation scenarios at a fixed significance level.
skills.name: statistical-power-comparison-across-methods
skills.search_text: statistical-power-comparison-across-methods Use when you must show whether a new statistical test is more than existing multivariate microbiome association tests across controlled simulation scenarios at a fixed significance level. The goal is testing association on one real dataset rather than benchmarking relative power of competing methods across scenarios The outcome is neither continuous nor binary in the simulated generalized linear model framework, or no null scenarios are available to check type I error Only one method is of interest, so no cross-method power comparison can be assembled http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark empirical power and type I error of competing association tests (here AMAT vs aMiSPU, OMiRKAT, OMiAT, LDM, MiHC) on identical simulated OTU count datasets, estimating power at the 0.05 level from 10,000 permutations per test per scenario. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab120
skills.summary: Benchmark empirical power and type I error of competing association tests (here AMAT vs aMiSPU, OMiRKAT, OMiAT, LDM, MiHC) on identical simulated OTU count datasets, estimating power at the 0.05 level from 10,000 permutations per test per scenario.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is testing association on one real dataset rather than benchmarking relative power of competing methods across scenarios The outcome is neither continuous nor binary in the simulated generalized linear model framework, or no null scenarios are available to check type I error Only one method is of interest, so no cross-method power comparison can be assembled

skills.description: Use when you must empirically compare detection power of two differential-abundance methods for zero-inflated relative abundance data across graded effect sizes, e.g. replicating the paper's Fig 1b simulation (mu1=0.5 vs mu2=0.4/0.3/0.2).
skills.name: statistical-power-estimation-by-monte-carlo
skills.search_text: statistical-power-estimation-by-monte-carlo Use when you must empirically compare detection power of two differential-abundance methods for zero-inflated relative abundance data across graded effect sizes, e.g. replicating the paper's Fig 1b simulation (mu1=0.5 vs mu2=0.4/0.3/0.2). Input is real observed relative abundance data to be tested for differential abundance rather than synthetic data for power estimation — use taxa.compare directly instead The competing methods model counts/absolute abundances (e.g. negative-binomial frameworks) rather than zero-inflated beta relative abundances with arcsin square-root transformation Analytical power formulas are available for the chosen model — Monte Carlo simulation is unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Empirical power estimation for microbiome differential-abundance tests by simulating zero-inflated beta (BEZI) relative-abundance data across effect sizes and comparing GAMLSS-BEZI (metamicrobiomeR) against the MaAsLin-style arcsin square-root transformed linear model (LMAS) over many replicates. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2744-2
skills.summary: Empirical power estimation for microbiome differential-abundance tests by simulating zero-inflated beta (BEZI) relative-abundance data across effect sizes and comparing GAMLSS-BEZI (metamicrobiomeR) against the MaAsLin-style arcsin square-root transformed linear model (LMAS) over many replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real observed relative abundance data to be tested for differential abundance rather than synthetic data for power estimation — use taxa.compare directly instead The competing methods model counts/absolute abundances (e.g. negative-binomial frameworks) rather than zero-inflated beta relative abundances with arcsin square-root transformation Analytical power formulas are available for the chosen model — Monte Carlo simulation is unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when comparing competing source-tracking methods on identical simulated or benchmark inputs and you need significance levels for accuracy differences, e.g., testing MSE gaps against P < 1e-6 thresholds across varying unknown-source fractions.
skills.name: statistical-significance-testing-of-method-comparisons
skills.search_text: statistical-significance-testing-of-method-comparisons Use when comparing competing source-tracking methods on identical simulated or benchmark inputs and you need significance levels for accuracy differences, e.g., testing MSE gaps against P < 1e-6 thresholds across varying unknown-source fractions. Your data are real (not simulated) sinks without known ground-truth mixing proportions, so MSE and false positive rate cannot be computed You are evaluating a single method in isolation rather than a head-to-head comparison on identical inputs — significance testing of differences is meaningless without a paired competitor run Only one candidate source environment is being considered, so sparsity/source-selection error (the driver of MSE differences in this benchmark) does not arise http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_3301 Benchmark multiple microbial source tracking methods (STENSL, FEAST, SourceTracker2, RAD) on identical simulated sinks and attach statistical significance to their performance differences, so claims of superior accuracy (e.g., lower MSE) are quantitatively supported rather than anecdotal. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00995-21
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple microbial source tracking methods (STENSL, FEAST, SourceTracker2, RAD) on identical simulated sinks and attach statistical significance to their performance differences, so claims of superior accuracy (e.g., lower MSE) are quantitatively supported rather than anecdotal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data are real (not simulated) sinks without known ground-truth mixing proportions, so MSE and false positive rate cannot be computed You are evaluating a single method in isolation rather than a head-to-head comparison on identical inputs — significance testing of differences is meaningless without a paired competitor run Only one candidate source environment is being considered, so sparsity/source-selection error (the driver of MSE differences in this benchmark) does not arise

skills.description: Use when comparing per-character extraction performance (Relaxed precision/recall/F1) of two systems—e.g., an NLP tool vs. a human-curated matrix—scored against one shared gold standard and a significance verdict is needed.
skills.name: statistical-significance-testing-students-ttest
skills.search_text: statistical-significance-testing-students-ttest Use when comparing per-character extraction performance (Relaxed precision/recall/F1) of two systems—e.g., an NLP tool vs. a human-curated matrix—scored against one shared gold standard and a significance verdict is needed. The two systems were not evaluated against the same gold standard matrix, so the paired per-character scores are not comparable. Fewer than the 12 compared characters have complete Relaxed scores for both systems, undermining the paired t-Test. The comparison target is micro-level per-character accuracy rather than detecting a statistically significant aggregate performance difference between two extractors. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Student's t-Tests to determine whether an automated text-mining extractor (MicroPIE 0.1.0) and a human baseline (undergraduate microbiology students) differ significantly in per-character Relaxed scores when both are evaluated against the same hand-generated gold standard matrix on 46 prokaryotic taxonomic descriptions. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1396-8
skills.summary: Applies Student's t-Tests to determine whether an automated text-mining extractor (MicroPIE 0.1.0) and a human baseline (undergraduate microbiology students) differ significantly in per-character Relaxed scores when both are evaluated against the same hand-generated gold standard matrix on 46 prokaryotic taxonomic descriptions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two systems were not evaluated against the same gold standard matrix, so the paired per-character scores are not comparable. Fewer than the 12 compared characters have complete Relaxed scores for both systems, undermining the paired t-Test. The comparison target is micro-level per-character accuracy rather than detecting a statistically significant aggregate performance difference between two extractors.

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end stool metatranscriptome FASTQ files (ribodepleted or poly(A)-enriched) need screening for human/host read contamination, or when deciding if host transcriptomes are recoverable from a gut microbiome sequencing run.
skills.name: stool-host-transcriptome-contamination-assessment
skills.search_text: stool-host-transcriptome-contamination-assessment Use when raw paired-end stool metatranscriptome FASTQ files (ribodepleted or poly(A)-enriched) need screening for human/host read contamination, or when deciding if host transcriptomes are recoverable from a gut microbiome sequencing run. Input is already a feature/abundance table or MG-RAST annotation output rather than raw FASTQ reads Sequencing reads are short single-end reads under 100 bp, since SAMSA requires long reads or joined paired-end reads The goal is within-sample microbiome functional annotation rather than host contamination assessment — MG-RAST is not tailored to work with eukaryotic organisms http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantifies how many sequenced stool metatranscriptome reads align to the human genome, using SAMSA preprocessing (Trimmomatic cleaning, FLASH paired-end joining) followed by human reference alignment, to judge whether host transcriptomes can be recovered from ribodepleted or poly(A)-enriched stool libraries. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1270-8
skills.summary: Quantifies how many sequenced stool metatranscriptome reads align to the human genome, using SAMSA preprocessing (Trimmomatic cleaning, FLASH paired-end joining) followed by human reference alignment, to judge whether host transcriptomes can be recovered from ribodepleted or poly(A)-enriched stool libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/abundance table or MG-RAST annotation output rather than raw FASTQ reads Sequencing reads are short single-end reads under 100 bp, since SAMSA requires long reads or joined paired-end reads The goal is within-sample microbiome functional annotation rather than host contamination assessment — MG-RAST is not tailored to work with eukaryotic organisms

skills.description: Use when comparing de novo strain-aware metagenome assemblers on real short-read community datasets and need reproducible Quast genome-fraction, N50 and identity comparisons across assemblers.
skills.name: strain-aware-assembly-benchmarking
skills.search_text: strain-aware-assembly-benchmarking Use when comparing de novo strain-aware metagenome assemblers on real short-read community datasets and need reproducible Quast genome-fraction, N50 and identity comparisons across assemblers. Reads are long third-generation sequencing data — the paper notes the high error rate of third-generation reads 'introduce a range of issues that still need to be resolved' and StrainXpress targets Illumina-type short reads The goal is a single-genome (isolate) assembly rather than separating multiple strains within a metagenome Input is already-assembled contigs and only evaluation is needed — use Quast/metaQuast directly instead of re-running the assembly benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark StrainXpress against state-of-the-art metagenome assemblers (SPAdes, IDBA-UD, Minia3, MEGAHIT) on real datasets (Bmock12, NWCs, Gut Metagenome) using Quast metrics such as genome fraction and N50. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac543
skills.summary: Benchmark StrainXpress against state-of-the-art metagenome assemblers (SPAdes, IDBA-UD, Minia3, MEGAHIT) on real datasets (Bmock12, NWCs, Gut Metagenome) using Quast metrics such as genome fraction and N50.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are long third-generation sequencing data — the paper notes the high error rate of third-generation reads 'introduce a range of issues that still need to be resolved' and StrainXpress targets Illumina-type short reads The goal is a single-genome (isolate) assembly rather than separating multiple strains within a metagenome Input is already-assembled contigs and only evaluation is needed — use Quast/metaQuast directly instead of re-running the assembly benchmark

skills.description: Use when assembling strain-aware metagenome contigs from cluster-specific haplotigs produced by a local assembly stage (StrainXpress stage-a output), needing global assembly into final master contigs.
skills.name: strain-aware-haplotype-contig-merging
skills.search_text: strain-aware-haplotype-contig-merging Use when assembling strain-aware metagenome contigs from cluster-specific haplotigs produced by a local assembly stage (StrainXpress stage-a output), needing global assembly into final master contigs. Input is raw metagenomic short reads that have not been clustered and locally assembled — the Clustering Reads and Local Assembly stages must run first Input is long third-generation sequencing reads — the paper notes the high error rate of third-generation reads remains an unresolved issue for this overlap-graph pipeline A reference-based (reference-assisted) assembly is desired — StrainXpress is a de novo method and this stage operates on de novo haplotigs http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reconstruct master strain-level contigs by building a master overlap graph over cluster-specific haplotigs (from StrainXpress local assembly), computing overlaps with minimap2, and simplifying/extending along unique paths. This is StrainXpress's Global Assembly stage that merges haplotigs into final contigs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac543
skills.summary: Reconstruct master strain-level contigs by building a master overlap graph over cluster-specific haplotigs (from StrainXpress local assembly), computing overlaps with minimap2, and simplifying/extending along unique paths. This is StrainXpress's Global Assembly stage that merges haplotigs into final contigs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metagenomic short reads that have not been clustered and locally assembled — the Clustering Reads and Local Assembly stages must run first Input is long third-generation sequencing reads — the paper notes the high error rate of third-generation reads remains an unresolved issue for this overlap-graph pipeline A reference-based (reference-assisted) assembly is desired — StrainXpress is a de novo method and this stage operates on de novo haplotigs

skills.description: Use when a deconvolution pipeline that infers allele distributions and strain types must be validated against ground truth from simulated samples, requiring both set-membership and proportion-based accuracy measures.
skills.name: strain-calling-accuracy-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: strain-calling-accuracy-metrics-computation Use when a deconvolution pipeline that infers allele distributions and strain types must be validated against ground truth from simulated samples, requiring both set-membership and proportion-based accuracy measures. When no ground-truth strain or allele composition exists (real samples such as the 24 tick samples) — metrics require known truth from simulation When evaluating abundance estimators against a single reference strain rather than mixed within-host populations; tools like Kallisto or strainEST baselines have different target quantities When comparing strains at the whole-genome level rather than MLST allele/strain-type level, where 5-SNP soft matching on housekeeping genes is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 A set of evaluation metrics — precision, recall, total variation distance (TVD), earth mover's distance (EMD), and soft-precision/soft-recall with a 5-SNP tolerance — used to quantify how accurately an ADP (allele diversity) and SDP (strain diversity) pipeline recovers known allele compositions and strain types from simulated B. burgdorferi MLST samples. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: A set of evaluation metrics — precision, recall, total variation distance (TVD), earth mover's distance (EMD), and soft-precision/soft-recall with a 5-SNP tolerance — used to quantify how accurately an ADP (allele diversity) and SDP (strain diversity) pipeline recovers known allele compositions and strain types from simulated B. burgdorferi MLST samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no ground-truth strain or allele composition exists (real samples such as the 24 tick samples) — metrics require known truth from simulation When evaluating abundance estimators against a single reference strain rather than mixed within-host populations; tools like Kallisto or strainEST baselines have different target quantities When comparing strains at the whole-genome level rather than MLST allele/strain-type level, where 5-SNP soft matching on housekeeping genes is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when pairwise genome or metagenome comparisons must be split into same-strain vs. different-strain calls, especially when SNP-based tools alone miss structurally divergent strains (e.g., clonal popANI but wide APSS range).
skills.name: strain-classification-threshold-application
skills.search_text: strain-classification-threshold-application Use when pairwise genome or metagenome comparisons must be split into same-strain vs. different-strain calls, especially when SNP-based tools alone miss structurally divergent strains (e.g., clonal popANI but wide APSS range). When the species under study lacks a training dataset or known strain pairs to calibrate thresholds — cutoffs are subjective and species-dependent, so a generic cutoff may misclassify When only SNP-level differences matter and structural variation is irrelevant — inStrain popANI alone suffices and SynTracker's SNP insensitivity adds little When comparing phages, plasmids, or very low-data contexts where strain delineation thresholds calibrated on cellular genomes do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Applies combined APSS (SynTracker synteny) and popANI (inStrain SNP-based) thresholds to classify isolate or metagenome pairs as same vs. different strains, enabling detection of strains enriched in either structural changes or point mutations. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2

skills.description: Use when you have inStrain profile objects for multiple samples (e.g., NICU infant metagenomes mapped to a dereplicated genome set) and need strain-level identities to test whether specific strains are shared between related individuals.
skills.name: strain-clustering-average-linkage-popani
skills.search_text: strain-clustering-average-linkage-popani Use when you have inStrain profile objects for multiple samples (e.g., NICU infant metagenomes mapped to a dereplicated genome set) and need strain-level identities to test whether specific strains are shared between related individuals. The analysis goal is species- or genome-level comparisons rather than strain-level sharing (genome de-replication at 98% ANI with dRep is the appropriate step instead) The input is raw reads or .bam files without inStrain profile objects having been built first — 'inStrain profile' must be run per sample before 'inStrain compare' Samples share no sub-species with sufficient coverage-overlap, so popANI comparisons cannot resolve shared strains http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Clusters inStrain sub-species into individual microbial strains by running 'inStrain compare' on profile objects and applying 'average' hierarchical clustering with a 99.999% popANI threshold, then builds a strain-by-infant presence/absence matrix for strain-sharing statistics. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Clusters inStrain sub-species into individual microbial strains by running 'inStrain compare' on profile objects and applying 'average' hierarchical clustering with a 99.999% popANI threshold, then builds a strain-by-infant presence/absence matrix for strain-sharing statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is species- or genome-level comparisons rather than strain-level sharing (genome de-replication at 98% ANI with dRep is the appropriate step instead) The input is raw reads or .bam files without inStrain profile objects having been built first — 'inStrain profile' must be run per sample before 'inStrain compare' Samples share no sub-species with sufficient coverage-overlap, so popANI comparisons cannot resolve shared strains

skills.description: Use when WGS reads from a bacterial sample (e.g. B. burgdorferi ticks) must be decomposed into constituent MLST strain types and allele/strain proportions despite within-host heterogeneity.
skills.name: strain-composition-estimation
skills.search_text: strain-composition-estimation Use when WGS reads from a bacterial sample (e.g. B. burgdorferi ticks) must be decomposed into constituent MLST strain types and allele/strain proportions despite within-host heterogeneity. The reference strain/allele database for the organism is unavailable — de novo approaches such as DESMAN are the alternative the paper cites The goal is SNP-level variant calling on a single clonal isolate rather than deconvolution of a multi-strain mixture The sample's loci do not map to a characterized MLST scheme, since the pipeline requires known alleles and strain types http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Infers the set of MLST strain types and their relative abundances present in a within-host heterogeneous sample by first solving the Allele Diversity Problem (allele composition per housekeeping locus) and then the Strain Diversity Problem, both formulated and solved as mixed integer linear programs with CPLEX. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Infers the set of MLST strain types and their relative abundances present in a within-host heterogeneous sample by first solving the Allele Diversity Problem (allele composition per housekeeping locus) and then the Strain Diversity Problem, both formulated and solved as mixed integer linear programs with CPLEX.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference strain/allele database for the organism is unavailable — de novo approaches such as DESMAN are the alternative the paper cites The goal is SNP-level variant calling on a single clonal isolate rather than deconvolution of a multi-strain mixture The sample's loci do not map to a characterized MLST scheme, since the pipeline requires known alleles and strain types

skills.description: Use when the goal is to compare how many microbial strains are shared between samples (e.g., twin siblings) under different strain-comparison criteria, or to validate inStrain's popANI approach against dRep/MIDAS/StrainPhlAn on the same mappings.
skills.name: strain-detection-benchmarking-across-tools
skills.search_text: strain-detection-benchmarking-across-tools Use when the goal is to compare how many microbial strains are shared between samples (e.g., twin siblings) under different strain-comparison criteria, or to validate inStrain's popANI approach against dRep/MIDAS/StrainPhlAn on the same mappings. Input is a single sample or a species-level abundance question — this skill addresses sub-species strain sharing, not presence/absence at species rank. Read mappings are to heterogeneous genome sets dereplicated above 98% ANI; multi-mapped reads will confound the comparison (the paper notes de-replication at 98% ANI reduces multi-mapped reads). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark strain-sharing detection by comparing inStrain's microdiversity-aware popANI-based comparisons against dRep, MIDAS, and StrainPhlAn on the same infant twin metagenomic read sets, tabulating genomes shared at each ANI threshold per tool. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Benchmark strain-sharing detection by comparing inStrain's microdiversity-aware popANI-based comparisons against dRep, MIDAS, and StrainPhlAn on the same infant twin metagenomic read sets, tabulating genomes shared at each ANI threshold per tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single sample or a species-level abundance question — this skill addresses sub-species strain sharing, not presence/absence at species rank. Read mappings are to heterogeneous genome sets dereplicated above 98% ANI; multi-mapped reads will confound the comparison (the paper notes de-replication at 98% ANI reduces multi-mapped reads).

skills.description: Use when a strain-separated metagenome assembly (e.g., Strainberry assembly.scaffolds.fa) must be quantitatively assessed per reference strain using ANI, NG50, and duplication-ratio metrics.
skills.name: strain-duplication-ratio-assessment
skills.search_text: strain-duplication-ratio-assessment Use when a strain-separated metagenome assembly (e.g., Strainberry assembly.scaffolds.fa) must be quantitatively assessed per reference strain using ANI, NG50, and duplication-ratio metrics. Input is a conventional strain-oblivious metagenome assembly (e.g., metaFlye output) rather than a strain-separated assembly, since per-strain duplication ratio is meaningless for mixed consensus contigs The sample is a high-complexity microbiome rather than a low-complexity mock community with reference genomes, since ANI/NG50/duplication ratio require strain-level references to compare against http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Evaluate strain-resolved metagenome assemblies (e.g., Strainberry output on Mock9) by computing per-strain average nucleotide identity (ANI), NG50, and duplication ratio against reference genomes, then comparing to the paper's reported values (e.g., S. aureus ANI 99.97%, NG50 ~2.2/~2.7 Mbp, duplication ratios 1.08/1.18/1.25). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Evaluate strain-resolved metagenome assemblies (e.g., Strainberry output on Mock9) by computing per-strain average nucleotide identity (ANI), NG50, and duplication ratio against reference genomes, then comparing to the paper's reported values (e.g., S. aureus ANI 99.97%, NG50 ~2.2/~2.7 Mbp, duplication ratios 1.08/1.18/1.25).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a conventional strain-oblivious metagenome assembly (e.g., metaFlye output) rather than a strain-separated assembly, since per-strain duplication ratio is meaningless for mixed consensus contigs The sample is a high-complexity microbiome rather than a low-complexity mock community with reference genomes, since ANI/NG50/duplication ratio require strain-level references to compare against

skills.description: Use when you have a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly, a strain-resolved assembly (e.g., Strainberry scaffolds), and closed strain reference genomes, and you need per-strain coverage fractions or recovered additional genomic material.
skills.name: strain-genome-coverage-quantification
skills.search_text: strain-genome-coverage-quantification Use when you have a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly, a strain-resolved assembly (e.g., Strainberry scaffolds), and closed strain reference genomes, and you need per-strain coverage fractions or recovered additional genomic material. No closed strain reference genomes are available to compute per-strain coverage fractions against The metagenome is high-complexity rather than low-complexity: Strainberry separation is demonstrated for a limited number of well-represented strains and haplotype phasing assumes strains can be separated by SNV density The goal is de novo assembly itself rather than benchmarking coverage recovery of an existing strain-resolved assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies how much of each strain reference genome is covered by strain-oblivious versus strain-resolved long-read assemblies (e.g., Flye vs. Strainberry scaffolds) by mapping long reads back to the assemblies and computing per-strain reference coverage fractions, mirroring Fig. 5 / Supplementary Data 2 of the Strainberry paper. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Quantifies how much of each strain reference genome is covered by strain-oblivious versus strain-resolved long-read assemblies (e.g., Flye vs. Strainberry scaffolds) by mapping long reads back to the assemblies and computing per-strain reference coverage fractions, mirroring Fig. 5 / Supplementary Data 2 of the Strainberry paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No closed strain reference genomes are available to compute per-strain coverage fractions against The metagenome is high-complexity rather than low-complexity: Strainberry separation is demonstrated for a limited number of well-represented strains and haplotype phasing assumes strains can be separated by SNV density The goal is de novo assembly itself rather than benchmarking coverage recovery of an existing strain-resolved assembly

skills.description: Use when a benchmark with known ground-truth strain composition and controlled mean sequencing depth is needed to evaluate strain-level variant detection (e.g. MetaQuad) on simulated shotgun metagenomic data.
skills.name: strain-genome-reference-construction
skills.search_text: strain-genome-reference-construction Use when a benchmark with known ground-truth strain composition and controlled mean sequencing depth is needed to evaluate strain-level variant detection (e.g. MetaQuad) on simulated shotgun metagenomic data. Input is real clinical or environmental metagenomic FASTQ with unknown strain composition — this skill only constructs synthetic benchmarks, not real-data references The goal is variant discovery itself (e.g. running MetaQuad/cellsnp-lite on already-aligned data) rather than building the simulation template A single reference genome with no strain variants is sufficient for the downstream analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Constructs multi-strain reference genomes and simulated shotgun metagenomic benchmark datasets by combining public reference genomes (e.g. Fusobacterium genomes from NCBI), BBMap mutate.sh-derived strain variants, and InSilicoSeq (iss generate) read simulation with the Novaseq error model, so that strain composition and sequencing depth (3x-35.5x) are known ground truth for evaluating shared-variant detection tools such as MetaQuad. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Constructs multi-strain reference genomes and simulated shotgun metagenomic benchmark datasets by combining public reference genomes (e.g. Fusobacterium genomes from NCBI), BBMap mutate.sh-derived strain variants, and InSilicoSeq (iss generate) read simulation with the Novaseq error model, so that strain composition and sequencing depth (3x-35.5x) are known ground truth for evaluating shared-variant detection tools such as MetaQuad.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real clinical or environmental metagenomic FASTQ with unknown strain composition — this skill only constructs synthetic benchmarks, not real-data references The goal is variant discovery itself (e.g. running MetaQuad/cellsnp-lite on already-aligned data) rather than building the simulation template A single reference genome with no strain variants is sufficient for the downstream analysis

skills.description: Use when long PacBio or Nanopore reads from a single low-complexity metagenomic sample must be separated into conspecific strain-level assemblies, rather than left collapsed in a strain-oblivious metagenome assembly.
skills.name: strain-haplotype-separation
skills.search_text: strain-haplotype-separation Use when long PacBio or Nanopore reads from a single low-complexity metagenomic sample must be separated into conspecific strain-level assemblies, rather than left collapsed in a strain-oblivious metagenome assembly. The metagenome is high-complexity — Strainberry is designed for single-sample low-complexity metagenomes Only short reads are available — the pipeline relies uniquely on long-read data and cannot reuse short-read strain methods The input is a species-level profile or marker-gene abundance table (e.g., StrainPhlAn/StrainEst output) rather than raw long reads plus an assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Automated strain separation of low-complexity metagenomes from error-prone long reads: Strainberry takes a strain-oblivious metaFlye assembly plus a sorted, indexed long-read BAM and reconstructs individual strain haplotypes via variant calling, haplotype phasing, and strain-aware scaffolding. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Automated strain separation of low-complexity metagenomes from error-prone long reads: Strainberry takes a strain-oblivious metaFlye assembly plus a sorted, indexed long-read BAM and reconstructs individual strain haplotypes via variant calling, haplotype phasing, and strain-aware scaffolding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metagenome is high-complexity — Strainberry is designed for single-sample low-complexity metagenomes Only short reads are available — the pipeline relies uniquely on long-read data and cannot reuse short-read strain methods The input is a species-level profile or marker-gene abundance table (e.g., StrainPhlAn/StrainEst output) rather than raw long reads plus an assembly

skills.description: Use when comparing metagenomic assemblers on short-read viral/metagenomic data containing closely related strains, where assemblies must be scored against reference genomes for genome fraction, misassemblies and per-100 kb error rates.
skills.name: strain-level-diversity-benchmarking
skills.search_text: strain-level-diversity-benchmarking Use when comparing metagenomic assemblers on short-read viral/metagenomic data containing closely related strains, where assemblies must be scored against reference genomes for genome fraction, misassemblies and per-100 kb error rates. The input is long-read data or non-viral isolate genomes rather than short-read metagenomic communities with strain-level diversity — the benchmark is grounded in Illumina mock viral communities The goal is variant calling or sequence graph exploration only, not end-to-end assembly benchmarking against reference genomes No reference genomes are available for MetaQUAST-based evaluation, so genome fraction and misassembly metrics cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark the MetaCortex metagenome assembler (k=95) against MEGAHIT, metaSPAdes and Ray Meta on the Mock A 12-virus Illumina community, scoring genome fraction, misassemblies, and mismatch/indel rates per 100 kb with MetaQUAST to quantify performance on high strain-level diversity. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad020
skills.summary: Benchmark the MetaCortex metagenome assembler (k=95) against MEGAHIT, metaSPAdes and Ray Meta on the Mock A 12-virus Illumina community, scoring genome fraction, misassemblies, and mismatch/indel rates per 100 kb with MetaQUAST to quantify performance on high strain-level diversity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is long-read data or non-viral isolate genomes rather than short-read metagenomic communities with strain-level diversity — the benchmark is grounded in Illumina mock viral communities The goal is variant calling or sequence graph exploration only, not end-to-end assembly benchmarking against reference genomes No reference genomes are available for MetaQUAST-based evaluation, so genome fraction and misassembly metrics cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when comparing microbial populations across metagenomic samples to quantify shared strains, needing pairwise popANI/ConANI and breadth-based detection against a concatenated reference genome set.
skills.name: strain-level-popani-comparison
skills.search_text: strain-level-popani-comparison Use when comparing microbial populations across metagenomic samples to quantify shared strains, needing pairwise popANI/ConANI and breadth-based detection against a concatenated reference genome set. The goal is rapid de-replication of a large genome set by average nucleotide identity rather than read-mapped, microdiversity-aware strain comparison (use dRep dereplicate instead) Reads are single-end or not properly paired, since inStrain removes all un-paired reads by default and filters read pairs in combination Genomes in the reference set are highly similar (e.g. not de-replicated around 98% ANI), which increases multi-mapped reads and distorts comparison accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes microdiversity-aware, strain-level genomic comparisons between metagenomic samples using inStrain's profile-then-compare workflow: map reads with Bowtie2, profile each .bam, then run inStrain compare to obtain pairwise popANI and coverage overlap that are more accurate than dRep/MIDAS/StrainPhlAn ANI estimates. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Computes microdiversity-aware, strain-level genomic comparisons between metagenomic samples using inStrain's profile-then-compare workflow: map reads with Bowtie2, profile each .bam, then run inStrain compare to obtain pairwise popANI and coverage overlap that are more accurate than dRep/MIDAS/StrainPhlAn ANI estimates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is rapid de-replication of a large genome set by average nucleotide identity rather than read-mapped, microdiversity-aware strain comparison (use dRep dereplicate instead) Reads are single-end or not properly paired, since inStrain removes all un-paired reads by default and filters read pairs in combination Genomes in the reference set are highly similar (e.g. not de-replicated around 98% ANI), which increases multi-mapped reads and distorts comparison accuracy

skills.description: Use when assembling metagenomic or mock viral community FASTQ reads with high strain-level diversity (e.g. mixed HIV-1 strains at ~2.8% abundance in a host background) and you need intra-species diversity preserved instead of a single consensus per species.
skills.name: strain-level-variation-assembly
skills.search_text: strain-level-variation-assembly Use when assembling metagenomic or mock viral community FASTQ reads with high strain-level diversity (e.g. mixed HIV-1 strains at ~2.8% abundance in a host background) and you need intra-species diversity preserved instead of a single consensus per species. Input is already assembled contigs or a pre-built graph rather than raw/trimmed FASTQ reads — MetaCortex imports reads files into the de Bruijn graph itself. Goal is a single-isolate reference assembly with no intra-species strain variation to capture — a consensus assembler suffices. Building on macOS with only LLVM available — LLVM will not compile MetaCortex, so the build must use GCC. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assemble metagenomic (environmental) reads with MetaCortex, a de Bruijn graph assembler based on cortex_con, so that signatures of local (strain-level) variation are captured along assembled sequences and output as contigs and sequence graphs rather than collapsed into a consensus. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad020
skills.summary: Assemble metagenomic (environmental) reads with MetaCortex, a de Bruijn graph assembler based on cortex_con, so that signatures of local (strain-level) variation are captured along assembled sequences and output as contigs and sequence graphs rather than collapsed into a consensus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled contigs or a pre-built graph rather than raw/trimmed FASTQ reads — MetaCortex imports reads files into the de Bruijn graph itself. Goal is a single-isolate reference assembly with no intra-species strain variation to capture — a consensus assembler suffices. Building on macOS with only LLVM available — LLVM will not compile MetaCortex, so the build must use GCC.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic assemblers on communities with high strain-level diversity, where a simulated ground-truth community with known reference genomes is needed to compute per-genome fraction and misassembly counts.
skills.name: strain-level-viral-community-simulation
skills.search_text: strain-level-viral-community-simulation Use when benchmarking metagenomic assemblers on communities with high strain-level diversity, where a simulated ground-truth community with known reference genomes is needed to compute per-genome fraction and misassembly counts. Input is real environmental metagenomic data without reference genomes — genome fraction and misassembly validation against ground truth is not possible The research question concerns isolate (single-strain) assembly rather than intra-species strain-level variation within a mixed community http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Generates a CAMISIM-simulated viral community containing real virus species plus simulated Influenza B strains to benchmark metagenomic assemblers on strain-level variation, evaluated by genome fraction and misassemblies (e.g. MetaCortex achieving 98.78% genome fraction with no misassemblies). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad020
skills.summary: Generates a CAMISIM-simulated viral community containing real virus species plus simulated Influenza B strains to benchmark metagenomic assemblers on strain-level variation, evaluated by genome fraction and misassemblies (e.g. MetaCortex achieving 98.78% genome fraction with no misassemblies).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real environmental metagenomic data without reference genomes — genome fraction and misassembly validation against ground truth is not possible The research question concerns isolate (single-strain) assembly rather than intra-species strain-level variation within a mixed community

skills.description: Use when a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly has been strain-separated with Strainberry and you must quantify per-bin additional genomic material, scaffold-count gains, and halved coverage into a summary table.
skills.name: strain-resolution-benchmark-tabulation
skills.search_text: strain-resolution-benchmark-tabulation Use when a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly has been strain-separated with Strainberry and you must quantify per-bin additional genomic material, scaffold-count gains, and halved coverage into a summary table. The sample is a high-complexity metagenome rather than the low-complexity single-sample setting Strainberry was designed and benchmarked for You need to resolve plasmid genomes — Strainberry's ability to resolve plasmids was not evaluated and was explicitly left for future work Strains within a single contig need separation into a variable number of strains (high strain variability within one contig is not handled) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Tabulates Strainberry strain-separation results (per-bin additional genomic material, scaffold counts, and depth-of-coverage changes) against the input strain-oblivious assembly to verify strain-level resolution, e.g. ~86% extra genomic material for the V. atypica bin on the HSM dataset. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Tabulates Strainberry strain-separation results (per-bin additional genomic material, scaffold counts, and depth-of-coverage changes) against the input strain-oblivious assembly to verify strain-level resolution, e.g. ~86% extra genomic material for the V. atypica bin on the HSM dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is a high-complexity metagenome rather than the low-complexity single-sample setting Strainberry was designed and benchmarked for You need to resolve plasmid genomes — Strainberry's ability to resolve plasmids was not evaluated and was explicitly left for future work Strains within a single contig need separation into a variable number of strains (high strain variability within one contig is not handled)

skills.description: Reference for judging whether Strainberry correctly separated two or more conspecific strains from a long-read metagenome assembly, using ANI, reference coverage, and duplication-ratio metrics per recovered strain.
skills.name: strain-separated-assembly-evaluation
skills.search_text: strain-separated-assembly-evaluation Reference for judging whether Strainberry correctly separated two or more conspecific strains from a long-read metagenome assembly, using ANI, reference coverage, and duplication-ratio metrics per recovered strain. The sample is a high-complexity microbiome rather than a low-complexity metagenome — Strainberry and this evaluation target low-complexity communities with well-represented strains Only short-read data are available — the workflow relies uniquely on error-prone long reads and strain-oblivious long-read assemblers You only need a raw strain-oblivious assembly without strain separation or per-strain quality assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Evaluate Strainberry strain-separated metagenome assemblies against reference genomes by computing per-strain average nucleotide identity (ANI), reference coverage, and duplication ratio, mirroring the Fig. 2 / Supplementary Data 1 tables of the Mock3 and Mock9 benchmarks. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Evaluate Strainberry strain-separated metagenome assemblies against reference genomes by computing per-strain average nucleotide identity (ANI), reference coverage, and duplication ratio, mirroring the Fig. 2 / Supplementary Data 1 tables of the Mock3 and Mock9 benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is a high-complexity microbiome rather than a low-complexity metagenome — Strainberry and this evaluation target low-complexity communities with well-represented strains Only short-read data are available — the workflow relies uniquely on error-prone long reads and strain-oblivious long-read assemblers You only need a raw strain-oblivious assembly without strain separation or per-strain quality assessment

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic assembly graph (GFA sequence graph from MetaCortex MC mode) encodes intra-species/strain-level variation and you need to extract per-strain paths and quantify their accuracy against strain references.
skills.name: strain-specific-contig-reconstruction
skills.search_text: strain-specific-contig-reconstruction Use when a metagenomic assembly graph (GFA sequence graph from MetaCortex MC mode) encodes intra-species/strain-level variation and you need to extract per-strain paths and quantify their accuracy against strain references. The input is a finished consensus contig or standard FASTA assembly with no accompanying GFA sequence graph — the per-strain walk requires graph elements (branching paths) that only MetaCortex MC mode emits The community has low or no strain-level diversity, so there are no local-variation signatures in the graph to walk The goal is generic metagenomic contig assembly without strain resolution — other popular metagenomic assemblers may be simpler http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reconstruct strain-specific contigs by walking the MetaCortex MC sequence graph (GFA) with per-strain BLAST-scored branch selection, then validate each reconstructed contig against its cognate reference with dnadiff to show per-strain accuracy exceeds the consensus contig. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad020
skills.summary: Reconstruct strain-specific contigs by walking the MetaCortex MC sequence graph (GFA) with per-strain BLAST-scored branch selection, then validate each reconstructed contig against its cognate reference with dnadiff to show per-strain accuracy exceeds the consensus contig.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a finished consensus contig or standard FASTA assembly with no accompanying GFA sequence graph — the per-strain walk requires graph elements (branching paths) that only MetaCortex MC mode emits The community has low or no strain-level diversity, so there are no local-variation signatures in the graph to walk The goal is generic metagenomic contig assembly without strain resolution — other popular metagenomic assemblers may be simpler

skills.description: Use when comparing conspecific microbial strains from metagenomic assemblies or assembled genomes where SNP-based tools are insufficient (e.g., structural variation, phages, plasmids) and a per-region synteny-based relatedness score is needed.
skills.name: strain-tracking-synteny-analysis
skills.search_text: strain-tracking-synteny-analysis Use when comparing conspecific microbial strains from metagenomic assemblies or assembled genomes where SNP-based tools are insufficient (e.g., structural variation, phages, plasmids) and a per-region synteny-based relatedness score is needed. When the research question is only about point mutations / SNP differences and no structural variation is of interest — the paper notes most SNP-quantifying methods are insensitive to structural changes, but SynTracker's strength is synteny, not SNP calling When strains are too divergent for BLAST hits to pass the 97% identity / 70% coverage thresholds on 5-kbp regions (default -length 5000), since homologous regions will not be recovered When fewer than n homologous regions per sample pair exist (e.g., small phages/plasmids relative to the subsampling depth) — such pairs are excluded from downstream analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Track closely related microbial strains by comparing genome synteny (the order of sequence blocks in homologous genomic regions) between pairs of metagenomic assemblies or genomes using SynTracker, which converts region-level synteny scores into an average pairwise synteny score (APSS) for phylogenetic and strain-delineation analyses. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Track closely related microbial strains by comparing genome synteny (the order of sequence blocks in homologous genomic regions) between pairs of metagenomic assemblies or genomes using SynTracker, which converts region-level synteny scores into an average pairwise synteny score (APSS) for phylogenetic and strain-delineation analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the research question is only about point mutations / SNP differences and no structural variation is of interest — the paper notes most SNP-quantifying methods are insensitive to structural changes, but SynTracker's strength is synteny, not SNP calling When strains are too divergent for BLAST hits to pass the 97% identity / 70% coverage thresholds on 5-kbp regions (default -length 5000), since homologous regions will not be recovered When fewer than n homologous regions per sample pair exist (e.g., small phages/plasmids relative to the subsampling depth) — such pairs are excluded from downstream analysis

skills.description: Use when per-locus allele proportions have already been inferred for multiple samples and you need a global, multi-sample strain-type decomposition that can include strains not present in the MLST database.
skills.name: strain-type-distribution-milp-deconvolution
skills.search_text: strain-type-distribution-milp-deconvolution Use when per-locus allele proportions have already been inferred for multiple samples and you need a global, multi-sample strain-type decomposition that can include strains not present in the MLST database. Input is raw reads rather than already-computed allele proportions — run the Bowtie mapping and allele diversity ILP stages first No reference MLST strain/allele database is available for the organism, since novel-strain weights depend on edit distance to the 753 known strain types De novo strain discovery without any known reference strains is required — the paper notes de novo methods such as DESMAN serve that setting instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Solves the Strain Diversity Problem as a mixed integer linear program that maps per-sample allele distributions from the 8-gene B. burgdorferi MLST scheme (1726 alleles, 753 known strain types) onto a minimal set of strain types, allowing novel strains weighted by edit distance to known types, with error bounds ε=0.1 per allele proportion and smallest-proportion tolerance δ=0.001. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Solves the Strain Diversity Problem as a mixed integer linear program that maps per-sample allele distributions from the 8-gene B. burgdorferi MLST scheme (1726 alleles, 753 known strain types) onto a minimal set of strain types, allowing novel strains weighted by edit distance to known types, with error bounds ε=0.1 per allele proportion and smallest-proportion tolerance δ=0.001.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than already-computed allele proportions — run the Bowtie mapping and allele diversity ILP stages first No reference MLST strain/allele database is available for the organism, since novel-strain weights depend on edit distance to the 753 known strain types De novo strain discovery without any known reference strains is required — the paper notes de novo methods such as DESMAN serve that setting instead

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a strain-deconvolution or MLST strain-typing solver against known ground truth: you need simulated multi-strain samples with controlled novel-strain and recombination events, plus precision/recall/TVD/EMD evaluation of inferred strain type proportions.
skills.name: strain-type-distribution-simulation
skills.search_text: strain-type-distribution-simulation Use when benchmarking a strain-deconvolution or MLST strain-typing solver against known ground truth: you need simulated multi-strain samples with controlled novel-strain and recombination events, plus precision/recall/TVD/EMD evaluation of inferred strain type proportions. When the goal is typing real samples without ground truth — this skill is a simulation/benchmark harness, not a production typing pipeline When evaluating only the ADP (per-locus allele) stage — allele-level simulation without strain type distributions is a separate, simpler task When reference strain types are unavailable for the organism, since novel-strain weighting depends on edit distance to the 753 known MLST strain types http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Simulates ground-truth strain type distributions under five evolutionary mechanisms (EvoMod1/2/2e/2n/3) for the B. burgdorferi MLST scheme, then scores SDP strain-typing recovery with precision, recall, TVD, soft metrics (5-SNP threshold), and Earth-Mover's distance. Used both with perfect allele input and chained behind ADP-inferred alleles to quantify error propagation. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Simulates ground-truth strain type distributions under five evolutionary mechanisms (EvoMod1/2/2e/2n/3) for the B. burgdorferi MLST scheme, then scores SDP strain-typing recovery with precision, recall, TVD, soft metrics (5-SNP threshold), and Earth-Mover's distance. Used both with perfect allele input and chained behind ADP-inferred alleles to quantify error propagation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is typing real samples without ground truth — this skill is a simulation/benchmark harness, not a production typing pipeline When evaluating only the ADP (per-locus allele) stage — allele-level simulation without strain type distributions is a separate, simpler task When reference strain types are unavailable for the organism, since novel-strain weighting depends on edit distance to the 753 known MLST strain types

skills.description: Use when a Strainberry run on a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly (e.g., Lathe/metaFlye FASTA plus coordinate-sorted Nanopore BAM) has finished and you must quantify per-bin additional genomic material, coverage halving, and strain-level classifications of the separated scaffolds.
skills.name: strain-variant-haplotyping-interpretation
skills.search_text: strain-variant-haplotyping-interpretation Use when a Strainberry run on a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly (e.g., Lathe/metaFlye FASTA plus coordinate-sorted Nanopore BAM) has finished and you must quantify per-bin additional genomic material, coverage halving, and strain-level classifications of the separated scaffolds. The metagenome is high-complexity rather than low-complexity; Strainberry is designed for single-sample low-complexity metagenomes and even-coverage separation was shown only for a limited number of well-represented strains You only need species-level binning or abundance profiling with no strain-resolution question — variant calling/haplotyping interpretation of separated scaffolds is unnecessary overhead Coverage of target strains is far below the ~60–80x depth the paper reports as sufficient to assemble individual strains with almost complete coverage and >99.9% sequence identity http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Interpret Strainberry's strain-separated assembly outputs (assembly.scaffolds.fa and assembly.scaffolds.bam) by computing per-scaffold length and depth of coverage and comparing them against the strain-oblivious input assembly, quantifying additional genomic material and confirming halved coverage of separated strains, as demonstrated on the Human Stool Microbiome (HSM) V. atypica and E. eligens bins. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-021-24515-9
skills.summary: Interpret Strainberry's strain-separated assembly outputs (assembly.scaffolds.fa and assembly.scaffolds.bam) by computing per-scaffold length and depth of coverage and comparing them against the strain-oblivious input assembly, quantifying additional genomic material and confirming halved coverage of separated strains, as demonstrated on the Human Stool Microbiome (HSM) V. atypica and E. eligens bins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metagenome is high-complexity rather than low-complexity; Strainberry is designed for single-sample low-complexity metagenomes and even-coverage separation was shown only for a limited number of well-represented strains You only need species-level binning or abundance profiling with no strain-resolution question — variant calling/haplotyping interpretation of separated scaffolds is unnecessary overhead Coverage of target strains is far below the ~60–80x depth the paper reports as sufficient to assemble individual strains with almost complete coverage and >99.9% sequence identity

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomic MAG clusters must be resolved below species level — e.g. to separate B. infantis from B. longum — via SNV phylogenies from signature genes and abundance-based cluster validation.
skills.name: strainphylan-phylogenetic-stratification
skills.search_text: strainphylan-phylogenetic-stratification Use when shotgun metagenomic MAG clusters must be resolved below species level — e.g. to separate B. infantis from B. longum — via SNV phylogenies from signature genes and abundance-based cluster validation. You only need species-level taxonomic composition — marker-gene profilers like MetaPhlAn, MetaPhyler, or mOTUs suffice without SNV phylogenies The signature gene set defined in one cohort does not transfer: a subset of COPSAC2010 signature genes was missing in the CHILD cohort, which presumably resulted in an underestimation of abundance for a subset of samples MAG clusters cannot be phylogenetically separated above the noise level; altering synteny/clustering parameters to remove noise comes at the expense of sensitivity http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Uses StrainPhlAn SNV-resolution phylogenetic trees built from de novo signature genes to split a MAG cluster into mutually exclusive subspecies clusters, then cross-validates the stratification against MAGinator-estimated subspecies abundances (e.g. B. infantis vs. B. longum in the COPSAC2010 and CHILD infant cohorts). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8
skills.summary: Uses StrainPhlAn SNV-resolution phylogenetic trees built from de novo signature genes to split a MAG cluster into mutually exclusive subspecies clusters, then cross-validates the stratification against MAGinator-estimated subspecies abundances (e.g. B. infantis vs. B. longum in the COPSAC2010 and CHILD infant cohorts).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need species-level taxonomic composition — marker-gene profilers like MetaPhlAn, MetaPhyler, or mOTUs suffice without SNV phylogenies The signature gene set defined in one cohort does not transfer: a subset of COPSAC2010 signature genes was missing in the CHILD cohort, which presumably resulted in an underestimation of abundance for a subset of samples MAG clusters cannot be phylogenetically separated above the noise level; altering synteny/clustering parameters to remove noise comes at the expense of sensitivity

skills.description: Use when testing a binary exposure (e.g., diarrhea status) against microbiome relative abundances within an exclusive-breastfeeding-duration stratum in a longitudinal infant cohort, expecting log(odds ratio) estimates with FDR-adjusted p-values.
skills.name: stratified-cohort-analysis-by-breastfeeding-duration
skills.search_text: stratified-cohort-analysis-by-breastfeeding-duration Use when testing a binary exposure (e.g., diarrhea status) against microbiome relative abundances within an exclusive-breastfeeding-duration stratum in a longitudinal infant cohort, expecting log(odds ratio) estimates with FDR-adjusted p-values. The goal is cross-study pooling of estimates rather than within-cohort stratified testing — use meta.taxa random effects meta-analysis instead The exposure of interest is continuous or multi-level (e.g., alpha diversity indexes over breastfeeding statuses) and the zero-inflated beta model for binary group comparison is not appropriate Data are counts or absolute abundances rather than relative abundances resembling a zero-inflated beta distribution http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Stratify a longitudinal infant microbiome cohort (e.g., Bangladesh) by duration of exclusive breastfeeding (<=2 months vs >2 months) and, within each stratum, test differential phylum-level relative abundances (e.g., diarrhea vs no diarrhea) using GAMLSS zero-inflated beta models via metamicrobiomeR, with FDR correction. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2744-2
skills.summary: Stratify a longitudinal infant microbiome cohort (e.g., Bangladesh) by duration of exclusive breastfeeding (<=2 months vs >2 months) and, within each stratum, test differential phylum-level relative abundances (e.g., diarrhea vs no diarrhea) using GAMLSS zero-inflated beta models via metamicrobiomeR, with FDR correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cross-study pooling of estimates rather than within-cohort stratified testing — use meta.taxa random effects meta-analysis instead The exposure of interest is continuous or multi-level (e.g., alpha diversity indexes over breastfeeding statuses) and the zero-inflated beta model for binary group comparison is not appropriate Data are counts or absolute abundances rather than relative abundances resembling a zero-inflated beta distribution

skills.description: Use when quantifying β-diversity (assemblage composition) from a presence-absence species matrix per functional group and you must decide how many NMDS dimensions to retain before extracting site scores as response variables.
skills.name: stress-based-dimensionality-selection
skills.search_text: stress-based-dimensionality-selection Use when quantifying β-diversity (assemblage composition) from a presence-absence species matrix per functional group and you must decide how many NMDS dimensions to retain before extracting site scores as response variables. The response variables needed are α-diversity (species richness) or phylogenetic diversity measures rather than assemblage composition (β-diversity) ordination scores The composition data are already summarized (e.g. a dissimilarity matrix is provided) so dimensionality selection must be made on a different basis than recomputing Bray-Curtis from presence-absence data A stress value ≥ 0.2 persists at all candidate dimensionalities, in which case NMDS scores should not be accepted as response variables without revisiting the composition data Selects the dimensionality of non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) ordinations of assemblage composition by choosing the solution with the lowest stress that meets the stress < 0.2 criterion, so that NMDS1/NMDS2 site scores are valid β-diversity response variables for biodiversity modelling. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-019-12737-x
skills.summary: Selects the dimensionality of non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) ordinations of assemblage composition by choosing the solution with the lowest stress that meets the stress < 0.2 criterion, so that NMDS1/NMDS2 site scores are valid β-diversity response variables for biodiversity modelling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response variables needed are α-diversity (species richness) or phylogenetic diversity measures rather than assemblage composition (β-diversity) ordination scores The composition data are already summarized (e.g. a dissimilarity matrix is provided) so dimensionality selection must be made on a different basis than recomputing Bray-Curtis from presence-absence data A stress value ≥ 0.2 persists at all candidate dimensionalities, in which case NMDS scores should not be accepted as response variables without revisiting the composition data

skills.description: Use when comparing multiple assemblies of one genome against a close-reference genome (e.g. a substrain rather than the true reference) and you need to determine whether reported misassemblies are shared true structural variants or assembler-specific errors.
skills.name: structural-variant-coordinate-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: structural-variant-coordinate-overlap-analysis Use when comparing multiple assemblies of one genome against a close-reference genome (e.g. a substrain rather than the true reference) and you need to determine whether reported misassemblies are shared true structural variants or assembler-specific errors. When only a single assembly is evaluated — breakpoint overlap across assemblers cannot be computed When the provided reference is the true reference genome rather than a close variant — reported misassemblies then reflect genuine assembly errors, not shared structural variants When no reference genome is available — QUAST falls back to reference-free metrics (30 metrics, no misassembly reporting) http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Quantifies and cross-compares reference-based misassemblies (inversions, relocations, translocations, local) reported by QUAST/WebQUAST for multiple assemblies evaluated against a close reference genome, distinguishing true structural variants from assembly errors by checking breakpoint coordinate overlap across assemblers. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkad406
skills.summary: Quantifies and cross-compares reference-based misassemblies (inversions, relocations, translocations, local) reported by QUAST/WebQUAST for multiple assemblies evaluated against a close reference genome, distinguishing true structural variants from assembly errors by checking breakpoint coordinate overlap across assemblers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single assembly is evaluated — breakpoint overlap across assemblers cannot be computed When the provided reference is the true reference genome rather than a close variant — reported misassemblies then reflect genuine assembly errors, not shared structural variants When no reference genome is available — QUAST falls back to reference-free metrics (30 metrics, no misassembly reporting)

skills.description: Use when evaluating or reproducing comparisons of HGT breakpoint detection or local strain reconstruction methods on simulated shotgun metagenomic reads, where ground-truth breakpoints and transferred segments are known.
skills.name: structural-variant-tool-benchmarking
skills.search_text: structural-variant-tool-benchmarking Use when evaluating or reproducing comparisons of HGT breakpoint detection or local strain reconstruction methods on simulated shotgun metagenomic reads, where ground-truth breakpoints and transferred segments are known. Input data are real metagenomic samples without known ground-truth breakpoints — sensitivity/FDR against true positions cannot be computed The goal is de novo HGT discovery rather than head-to-head tool comparison against reported benchmark figures Data are long-read assemblies or non-shotgun data; the LEMON/LUMPY pipeline assumes short paired-end shotgun reads aligned with BWA http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A benchmarking skill for comparing structural-variant / HGT-breakpoint detection tools (LEMON vs LUMPY) on simulated gut metagenomics data, measuring breakpoint sensitivity/FDR with a 20 bp tolerance and local-strain reconstruction accuracy (RA) via Smith-Waterman alignment across coverage levels. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3301-8
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for comparing structural-variant / HGT-breakpoint detection tools (LEMON vs LUMPY) on simulated gut metagenomics data, measuring breakpoint sensitivity/FDR with a 20 bp tolerance and local-strain reconstruction accuracy (RA) via Smith-Waterman alignment across coverage levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are real metagenomic samples without known ground-truth breakpoints — sensitivity/FDR against true positions cannot be computed The goal is de novo HGT discovery rather than head-to-head tool comparison against reported benchmark figures Data are long-read assemblies or non-shotgun data; the LEMON/LUMPY pipeline assumes short paired-end shotgun reads aligned with BWA

skills.name: subgroup-survival-response-analysis
