skills.description: Reference for reproducing or extending depth-benchmarking of viral genome reconstruction: subsample a large FASTQ cohort to lower read depths, rerun assembly-based reconstruction at each depth, and compare segment contiguity/length against a baseline method.
skills.name: subsampled-assembly-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: subsampled-assembly-benchmark-comparison Reference for reproducing or extending depth-benchmarking of viral genome reconstruction: subsample a large FASTQ cohort to lower read depths, rerun assembly-based reconstruction at each depth, and compare segment contiguity/length against a baseline method. The dataset is small or low-depth already — subsampling provides no informative gradient and comparison power is lost. The question is taxonomic abundance profiling rather than reconstruction contiguity/length benchmarking — depth-vs-length comparison is not the right evaluation. No baseline/standard-approach reconstruction is run at matched depths — comparing VirMAP against itself across depths does not test the method. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Benchmark a reconstruction pipeline against a baseline by downsampling sequence data to graded depths, rerunning reconstruction at each depth, and comparing output contiguity/length. In the VirMAP influenza UMERS dataset (PRJEB7888, 1.75 billion reads), this reproduces the Fig. 4 VirMAP-vs-standard-approach comparison. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Benchmark a reconstruction pipeline against a baseline by downsampling sequence data to graded depths, rerunning reconstruction at each depth, and comparing output contiguity/length. In the VirMAP influenza UMERS dataset (PRJEB7888, 1.75 billion reads), this reproduces the Fig. 4 VirMAP-vs-standard-approach comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small or low-depth already — subsampling provides no informative gradient and comparison power is lost. The question is taxonomic abundance profiling rather than reconstruction contiguity/length benchmarking — depth-vs-length comparison is not the right evaluation. No baseline/standard-approach reconstruction is run at matched depths — comparing VirMAP against itself across depths does not test the method.

skills.description: Use when metagenomic reads have been mapped to concatenated representative sub-species FASTAs and you must decide which sub-species count as detected per sample before comparing metrics (e.g. nucleotide diversity) across groups such as birth mode.
skills.name: subspecies-detection-thresholding
skills.search_text: subspecies-detection-thresholding Use when metagenomic reads have been mapped to concatenated representative sub-species FASTAs and you must decide which sub-species count as detected per sample before comparing metrics (e.g. nucleotide diversity) across groups such as birth mode. Reads have not yet been mapped to representative sub-species genomes (no .bam available) — profile with inStrain first The reference genome set has not been de-replicated near 98% ANI — multi-mapped reads will distort coverage and diversity estimates The question is strain sharing or ANI comparison between samples rather than per-sample presence/abundance of sub-species http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Applies breadth-based detection thresholds and contaminant flags to inStrain sub-species profiles, so that only genomes genuinely present (>= 0.5 unmaskedBreadth) in an infant fecal metagenome contribute to microdiversity statistics such as Klebsiella nucleotide diversity. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0

skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads have not yet been mapped to representative sub-species genomes (no .bam available) — profile with inStrain first The reference genome set has not been de-replicated near 98% ANI — multi-mapped reads will distort coverage and diversity estimates The question is strain sharing or ANI comparison between samples rather than per-sample presence/abundance of sub-species

skills.description: Use when predicting genes in metagenomic reads with substitution errors (e.g. Illumina data), where a single base error can introduce a spurious stop codon that fragments an otherwise correct ORF prediction.
skills.name: substitution-error-orf-merging
skills.search_text: substitution-error-orf-merging Use when predicting genes in metagenomic reads with substitution errors (e.g. Illumina data), where a single base error can introduce a spurious stop codon that fragments an otherwise correct ORF prediction. When reads are high-quality assembled contigs or complete genomes — use standard Glimmer, which routinely identifies >99% of genes in complete prokaryotic genomes When the dominant error mode is indels in homopolymer runs (454) and you specifically want frame-branching indel prediction rather than stop-codon substitution merging When computational cost is a hard constraint — the article notes Glimmer-MG is more computationally expensive than existing software http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Glimmer-MG's approach to Illumina-style substitution errors: adjacent predicted ORFs whose apparent stop codons are attributable to sequencing substitutions are merged so gene predictions track the true coding frame in error-prone short reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkr1067
skills.summary: Glimmer-MG's approach to Illumina-style substitution errors: adjacent predicted ORFs whose apparent stop codons are attributable to sequencing substitutions are merged so gene predictions track the true coding frame in error-prone short reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads are high-quality assembled contigs or complete genomes — use standard Glimmer, which routinely identifies >99% of genes in complete prokaryotic genomes When the dominant error mode is indels in homopolymer runs (454) and you specifically want frame-branching indel prediction rather than stop-codon substitution merging When computational cost is a hard constraint — the article notes Glimmer-MG is more computationally expensive than existing software

skills.description: Use when implementing or verifying protein-level read classifiers in the Kaiju style, where MEM hits found via BWT backwards search must be mapped to NCBI taxon IDs and ambiguous hits collapsed to an LCA.
skills.name: suffix-array-taxon-lookup
skills.search_text: suffix-array-taxon-lookup Use when implementing or verifying protein-level read classifiers in the Kaiju style, where MEM hits found via BWT backwards search must be mapped to NCBI taxon IDs and ambiguous hits collapsed to an LCA. Reads originate from non-protein-coding genomic regions — protein-level classification cannot assign them (an acknowledged Kaiju limitation) Input sequences are already proteins and you only need match positions, not taxon resolution via the suffix array and taxonomy tree http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Recover the NCBI taxon identifier of a matched database sequence from Kaiju's suffix array after a BWT backwards search, and resolve equally long matches across multiple taxa to their least common ancestor (LCA) in the NCBI taxonomic tree (nodes.dmp). This step converts raw FM-index matches into a taxonomic assignment per read. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/ncomms11257
skills.summary: Recover the NCBI taxon identifier of a matched database sequence from Kaiju's suffix array after a BWT backwards search, and resolve equally long matches across multiple taxa to their least common ancestor (LCA) in the NCBI taxonomic tree (nodes.dmp). This step converts raw FM-index matches into a taxonomic assignment per read.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads originate from non-protein-coding genomic regions — protein-level classification cannot assign them (an acknowledged Kaiju limitation) Input sequences are already proteins and you only need match positions, not taxon resolution via the suffix array and taxonomy tree

skills.description: Use when pooling per-contig results (seed length, final length, extension gain) from several ContigExtender runs into a single combined statistics table such as summary_statistics.csv.

skills.summary: Aggregates per-contig length and quality measurements from multiple ContigExtender runs (e.g., NIBSC, Animal, Human metagenomic datasets) into combined summary statistics, reporting means, medians, and chimera-free counts to quantify aggregate extension improvement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-run result with no cross-run pooling needed — compute per-run statistics directly instead Contigs lack parsable pairing between extended output and seed contigs (e.g., headers were renamed), making per-contig gain computation impossible The goal is accuracy assessment against references (e.g., BLAST to NCBI viral reference nucleotide sequences) rather than length/quality aggregation

skills.description: Use when you already hold recovered marker sequences (e.g., FASTA per specimen per locus) for multiple specimens and need to align, trim, concatenate them into a supermatrix, and infer a maximum-likelihood phylogeny.
skills.name: supermatrix-concatenation-phylogenomics
skills.search_text: supermatrix-concatenation-phylogenomics Use when you already hold recovered marker sequences (e.g., FASTA per specimen per locus) for multiple specimens and need to align, trim, concatenate them into a supermatrix, and infer a maximum-likelihood phylogeny. Markers are not (putatively) single-copy orthologs shared across specimens (e.g., multi-copy or non-homologous sequences), as concatenation assumes locus equivalence across taxa You have only one or very few loci, where a supermatrix/partitioned approach adds no benefit over single-locus phylogenetics Sequences still contain unaligned residues, stop codons, or artifactual noncoding stretches that have not been cleaned (e.g., via Patchwork's alignment masking or PREQUAL), which would corrupt the MAFFT/trimAl step http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Carries marker sequences (e.g., Patchwork-recovered USCOs) through a downstream phylogenomic pipeline: per-locus MAFFT alignment, trimAl trimming, FASconCAT-G concatenation with a gene partition file, and IQ-TREE 2 maximum-likelihood tree inference with ultrafast bootstraps. It tests whether retrieved markers can support a well-resolved, well-supported phylogeny. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Carries marker sequences (e.g., Patchwork-recovered USCOs) through a downstream phylogenomic pipeline: per-locus MAFFT alignment, trimAl trimming, FASconCAT-G concatenation with a gene partition file, and IQ-TREE 2 maximum-likelihood tree inference with ultrafast bootstraps. It tests whether retrieved markers can support a well-resolved, well-supported phylogeny.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Markers are not (putatively) single-copy orthologs shared across specimens (e.g., multi-copy or non-homologous sequences), as concatenation assumes locus equivalence across taxa You have only one or very few loci, where a supermatrix/partitioned approach adds no benefit over single-locus phylogenetics Sequences still contain unaligned residues, stop codons, or artifactual noncoding stretches that have not been cleaned (e.g., via Patchwork's alignment masking or PREQUAL), which would corrupt the MAFFT/trimAl step

skills.description: Use when comparing variant callers by association performance: variant count tables plus sample metadata are available and the goal is to test whether different callers yield comparable supervised classification performance.
skills.name: supervised-classifier-training-16s-variants
skills.search_text: supervised-classifier-training-16s-variants Use when comparing variant callers by association performance: variant count tables plus sample metadata are available and the goal is to test whether different callers yield comparable supervised classification performance. skills.search_text: svm-classifier-training-on-cog-profiles Use when training phenotype prediction models from comparative-genomics feature tables (e.g. eggNOG COG presence/absence profiles) and you need fast, accurate SVM-only classification without an explicit feature-selection step. Training labels for the trait of interest are insufficient; the article notes further ecologically important traits await sufficient training data. skills.summary: Train purely SVM-based phenotypic trait classifiers (PICA libSVM plug-in) on eggNOG COG presence/absence profiles, benchmarked against CPAR2SVM (association-rule feature selection + SVM) to show SVM-only achieves comparable prediction quality at roughly one-third the runtime.

skills.description: Use when a trained linear SVM phenotype model (e.g. PICA intracellular model on 97 labelled species) must be inspected to determine whether a trait is predicted by gene presence or absence, and to compare the ranking against a published table.

skills.search_text: svm-feature-weight-ranking Use when a trained linear SVM phenotype model (e.g. PICA intracellular model on 97 labelled species) must be inspected to determine whether a trait is predicted by gene presence or absence, and to compare the ranking against a published table. The model is nonlinear (non-linear kernel), so per-feature weights do not exist or are not interpretable as signed presence/absence predictors. Input is raw genome data rather than a trained classifier — this skill interprets an already-trained PICA/libSVM model, it does not train one or make phenotype predictions for new genomes. Genome completeness is far below the ~60-70% threshold at which traits are reliably predicted, since features derived from fragmentary genomes may not support stable rankings. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduce and interpret a signed COG feature ranking from a trained PICA/libSVM linear SVM phenotype model by extracting the raw SVM weight vector and ranking features by absolute weight, with the sign encoding whether gene presence or absence predicts the trait (here, the obligate intracellular phenotype). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-16-s14-s1
skills.summary: Reproduce and interpret a signed COG feature ranking from a trained PICA/libSVM linear SVM phenotype model by extracting the raw SVM weight vector and ranking features by absolute weight, with the sign encoding whether gene presence or absence predicts the trait (here, the obligate intracellular phenotype).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is nonlinear (non-linear kernel), so per-feature weights do not exist or are not interpretable as signed presence/absence predictors. Genome completeness is far below the ~60-70% threshold at which traits are reliably predicted, since features derived from fragmentary genomes may not support stable rankings.

skills.summary: Benchmark and compare SVM kernel choices (linear vs. RBF, sigmoid, polynomial) for phenotypic trait prediction from COG presence/absence profiles using PICA's libSVM-backed plug-in, as in the Feldbauer et al. 2015 evaluation of PICA.

skills.description: Use when predicting a binary microbial phenotypic trait (e.g. obligate intracellular lifestyle) from comparative-genomics feature matrices such as COG presence/absence vectors, or when screening whole genome databases like eggNOG for species carrying a trained trait.

skills.summary: Train and apply support vector machine phenotype models on COG presence/absence profiles using the PICA framework (libSVM backend), e.g. the obligate intracellular lifestyle model that reached 0.997 ± 0.010 cross-validated balanced accuracy on 97 complete bacterial genomes.

skills.description: Use when comparing strains of the same microbial species from metagenomic assemblies or isolate genomes — especially when SNP-based tools (inStrain popANI, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn) call pairs clonal but structural differences may exist.
skills.name: synteny-based-strain-comparison
skills.search_text: synteny-based-strain-comparison Use when comparing strains of the same microbial species from metagenomic assemblies or isolate genomes — especially when SNP-based tools (inStrain popANI, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn) call pairs clonal but structural differences may exist. When the goal is purely SNP-level differentiation of hypermutator strains — SynTracker has low sensitivity to SNPs, so an SNP-based tool like inStrain popANI or read-mapping analysis is the appropriate primary method When pairs of samples/genomes share fewer than n homologous regions — SynTracker excludes such pairs from downstream analysis When a universal same-strain cutoff is expected — the authors warn that thresholds (e.g., popANI 99.999%, APSS 0.95) are subjective, species-dependent, and tailored cutoffs require a training dataset relevant to the research question http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Compare conspecific microbial strains using genome synteny via SynTracker: BLAST-derived homologous regions per reference genome are scored for synteny block conservation and averaged into APSS values, detecting structural variation that SNP-based tools miss. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Compare conspecific microbial strains using genome synteny via SynTracker: BLAST-derived homologous regions per reference genome are scored for synteny block conservation and averaged into APSS values, detecting structural variation that SNP-based tools miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is purely SNP-level differentiation of hypermutator strains — SynTracker has low sensitivity to SNPs, so an SNP-based tool like inStrain popANI or read-mapping analysis is the appropriate primary method When pairs of samples/genomes share fewer than n homologous regions — SynTracker excludes such pairs from downstream analysis When a universal same-strain cutoff is expected — the authors warn that thresholds (e.g., popANI 99.999%, APSS 0.95) are subjective, species-dependent, and tailored cutoffs require a training dataset relevant to the research question

skills.description: Use when you already have region-specific bins of homologous sequences (e.g., central 1-kbp regions plus 2-kbp flanks per BLAST hit) and need per-pair synteny scores based on synteny-block structure rather than SNPs.
skills.name: synteny-block-alignment-with-decipher
skills.search_text: synteny-block-alignment-with-decipher Use when you already have region-specific bins of homologous sequences (e.g., central 1-kbp regions plus 2-kbp flanks per BLAST hit) and need per-pair synteny scores based on synteny-block structure rather than SNPs. skills.search_text: tabular-result-export Use when per-dataset, per-method benchmark scores (e.g., Quast/metaQuast genome fraction percentages) have been computed and must be aggregated and persisted as a CSV with per-dataset rows plus summary statistics for verification. Input is not a per-method score table (e.g., raw sequencing FASTQ reads or assembled contig FASTA) — assembly and Quast/metaQuast evaluation must happen first. skills.summary: Export per-dataset benchmark results (e.g., genome-fraction gains of StrainXpress over IDBA-UD, SPAdes, Minia3, MEGAHIT) and their aggregate summary statistics (mean, Q1, median, Q3) to a structured CSV such as gain_summary.csv, enabling verification against reported values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a per-method score table (e.g., raw sequencing FASTQ reads or assembled contig FASTA) — assembly and Quast/metaQuast evaluation must happen first. The comparison target is a metric other than per-dataset relative gain over a best-competitor baseline (e.g., N50 contig length rankings, where MEGAHIT leads).

skills.description: Use when a Patchwork/DIAMOND marker-retrieval run shows low query coverage and you need to decide whether disabling DIAMOND's tantan masking (--masking 0) recovers longer alignments, particularly with raw-read (FASTQ-derived) rather than assembly queries.
skills.name: tantan-masking-ablation-comparison
skills.search_text: tantan-masking-ablation-comparison Use when a Patchwork/DIAMOND marker-retrieval run shows low query coverage and you need to decide whether disabling DIAMOND's tantan masking (--masking 0) recovers longer alignments, particularly with raw-read (FASTQ-derived) rather than assembly queries. Query material is already high-coverage, well-assembled contigs where default masking already yields near-complete coverage (e.g. the 95.9% identity / 92.2% coverage same-species benchmark) Percent identity is the binding constraint on downstream phylogenetic use, since disabling tantan slightly decreases identity even as coverage improves The alignment tool in use is not DIAMOND, since tantan masking is a DIAMOND-specific low-complexity filter toggled by --masking 0 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 An ablation protocol comparing Patchwork runs with DIAMOND's tantan low-complexity masking enabled versus disabled (--masking 0), to quantify the effect on percent identity and query coverage of recovered phylogenetic markers. Disabling tantan yields higher query coverages, especially for read-based (non-assembled) queries, at only a slight identity cost. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: An ablation protocol comparing Patchwork runs with DIAMOND's tantan low-complexity masking enabled versus disabled (--masking 0), to quantify the effect on percent identity and query coverage of recovered phylogenetic markers. Disabling tantan yields higher query coverages, especially for read-based (non-assembled) queries, at only a slight identity cost.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query material is already high-coverage, well-assembled contigs where default masking already yields near-complete coverage (e.g. the 95.9% identity / 92.2% coverage same-species benchmark) Percent identity is the binding constraint on downstream phylogenetic use, since disabling tantan slightly decreases identity even as coverage improves The alignment tool in use is not DIAMOND, since tantan masking is a DIAMOND-specific low-complexity filter toggled by --masking 0

skills.description: Use when validating RiPP peptide-spectrum matches produced by searching spectra against a putative precursor-peptide database (e.g., MetaMiner/Dereplicator output) and an acceptance threshold (e.g., 1% FDR per dataset) is needed before reporting identifications.
skills.name: target-decoy-fdr-estimation
skills.search_text: target-decoy-fdr-estimation Use when validating RiPP peptide-spectrum matches produced by searching spectra against a putative precursor-peptide database (e.g., MetaMiner/Dereplicator output) and an acceptance threshold (e.g., 1% FDR per dataset) is needed before reporting identifications. Spectra lacking paired genomic/metagenomic data — the paper notes 99% of GNPS spectra cannot be searched, so there is no target-decoy RiPP search to validate Non-RiPP compound classes (e.g., non-ribosomal peptides) — Dereplicator+ structure-based search, not RiPP target-decoy peptidogenomics, is the appropriate route Blind modification searches on cyclic peptides — MetaMiner does not currently perform them due to computational complexity, so FDR results in that regime are out of scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Statistical validation strategy for RiPP identifications in MetaMiner: a decoy database is built by randomly shuffling each target precursor peptide, MS-DPR computes peptide-spectrum match p-values, and FDR estimated via the target-decoy approach gates identifications at a 1% threshold per dataset. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.cels.2019.09.004
skills.summary: Statistical validation strategy for RiPP identifications in MetaMiner: a decoy database is built by randomly shuffling each target precursor peptide, MS-DPR computes peptide-spectrum match p-values, and FDR estimated via the target-decoy approach gates identifications at a 1% threshold per dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spectra lacking paired genomic/metagenomic data — the paper notes 99% of GNPS spectra cannot be searched, so there is no target-decoy RiPP search to validate Non-RiPP compound classes (e.g., non-ribosomal peptides) — Dereplicator+ structure-based search, not RiPP target-decoy peptidogenomics, is the appropriate route Blind modification searches on cyclic peptides — MetaMiner does not currently perform them due to computational complexity, so FDR results in that regime are out of scope

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a targeted-assembly approach (e.g. CasCollect in protein mode with --trim --meta) outperforms full metaSPAdes assembly or PRICE for cas gene/operon recovery from pooled metagenomic FASTQ reads, with runtime and contig-count comparisons.
skills.name: targeted-cas-gene-assembly-benchmarking
skills.search_text: targeted-cas-gene-assembly-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a targeted-assembly approach (e.g. CasCollect in protein mode with --trim --meta) outperforms full metaSPAdes assembly or PRICE for cas gene/operon recovery from pooled metagenomic FASTQ reads, with runtime and contig-count comparisons. Input is a single isolate genome rather than a pooled metagenome — the isolate benchmarks in the paper showed CasCollect was sometimes slower than complete assembly (e.g. 23.3 vs 17.4 min for E. coli KLY) No CRISPR/Cas content is expected in the reads — targeted seed generation from Cas HMMs will find no seeds and the runtime advantage vanishes You need a whole-genome assembly or genome-wide variant calls — CasCollect only assembles the read subset around CRISPR/Cas loci http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark a targeted CRISPR/Cas assembly pipeline (CasCollect) against complete metagenome assembly (metaSPAdes) and the PRICE assembler on a simulated metagenome, comparing wall-clock runtime, contig output counts, and recovery of all known cas genes and correctly assembled cas operons. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Benchmark a targeted CRISPR/Cas assembly pipeline (CasCollect) against complete metagenome assembly (metaSPAdes) and the PRICE assembler on a simulated metagenome, comparing wall-clock runtime, contig output counts, and recovery of all known cas genes and correctly assembled cas operons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single isolate genome rather than a pooled metagenome — the isolate benchmarks in the paper showed CasCollect was sometimes slower than complete assembly (e.g. 23.3 vs 17.4 min for E. coli KLY) No CRISPR/Cas content is expected in the reads — targeted seed generation from Cas HMMs will find no seeds and the runtime advantage vanishes You need a whole-genome assembly or genome-wide variant calls — CasCollect only assembles the read subset around CRISPR/Cas loci

skills.when_to_use_negative: Before the full-permutation step has been run — dotplot_bin_sig requires best$goodpvname; use bin_permute_all/plot_bin_psig first to assess the overall U-curve association. skills.description: Use when estimating rho correlations between SNPs and microbial taxa across a sample cohort while simultaneously controlling for taxa–taxa correlation (R) and goodness-of-fit (R²) to flag LD SNPs/regions, per mbQTL Approach B.
skills.name: taxa-snp-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: taxa-snp-correlation-analysis Use when estimating rho correlations between SNPs and microbial taxa across a sample cohort while simultaneously controlling for taxa–taxa correlation (R) and goodness-of-fit (R²) to flag LD SNPs/regions, per mbQTL Approach B. The goal is linear regression testing of taxa–SNP relationships, which mbQTL handles separately via its core MatrixEQTL model (Approach A), not the rho-estimation correlation workflow. The taxa are presence/absence (categorical), where the article prescribes logistic regression to estimate the relationship of one SNP and one taxa instead. Input is a phyloseq S4 object or metagenomeSeq MRexperiment object not yet converted — normalize/aggregate and convert via phyloseq_to_metagenomeSeq() and metagenomeSeqToMbqtl first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Reproduces mbQTL's Approach B correlation workflow: estimate taxa–taxa R values with coringTaxa, retain extreme taxa–taxa correlations with allToAllProduct(probs=c(0.0001,0.9999)), then call taxaSnpCor to estimate rho for all SNP–taxa pairs adjusted for those R values. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad565
skills.summary: Reproduces mbQTL's Approach B correlation workflow: estimate taxa–taxa R values with coringTaxa, retain extreme taxa–taxa correlations with allToAllProduct(probs=c(0.0001,0.9999)), then call taxaSnpCor to estimate rho for all SNP–taxa pairs adjusted for those R values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is linear regression testing of taxa–SNP relationships, which mbQTL handles separately via its core MatrixEQTL model (Approach A), not the rho-estimation correlation workflow. The taxa are presence/absence (categorical), where the article prescribes logistic regression to estimate the relationship of one SNP and one taxa instead. Input is a phyloseq S4 object or metagenomeSeq MRexperiment object not yet converted — normalize/aggregate and convert via phyloseq_to_metagenomeSeq() and metagenomeSeqToMbqtl first.

skills.search_text: taxa-snp-linear-regression-qtl-mapping Use when you have a microbial abundance matrix (taxa x samples), a genotype/SNP matrix (SNPs x samples), optional covariates, and you need to detect significant taxa–SNP host-genetic associations via linear regression. skills.summary: mbQTL's Approach A identifies microbial QTLs by covariate-adjusted linear regression of each taxon's abundance against each host SNP using the core MatrixEQTL model, with P value diagnostics (histPvalueLm, qqPlotLm) and FDR/Bonferroni multiple-testing reporting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Taxa are presence/absence (categorical) rather than continuous abundances — mbQTL provides logistic regression for that case instead The goal is correlation-based rho estimation or identification of linkage disequilibrium (LD) SNPs via taxa-taxa R values (Approach B), rather than per-pair linear regression Input is not in the required sample-matched taxa/SNP data-frame format and has not been converted via metagenomeSeqToMbqtl or phyloseq_to_metagenomeSeq()

skills.search_text: taxon-count-vector-validation Use when a reconstructed source or sink taxon profile has been derived by arithmetic on count vectors (e.g., residual subtraction after L1 sparse source selection) and must be verified before downstream use. Input is already a validated source profile from FEAST's EM output (matrix P rows summing to 1) rather than a residual-derived count vector The mixing proportions are still unnormalized EM estimates and the L1 sparse selection step has not been run, so argmax(αhat) is not defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Validates reconstructed taxon count vectors — specifically STENSL's unknown-source profile computed as the clamped residual Yhat_{M+1} = max(0, x − αhat*Y_{argmax αhat}) — by checking non-negativity, dimensional consistency with the sink vector, and correctness of the clamped subtraction. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00995-21
skills.summary: Validates reconstructed taxon count vectors — specifically STENSL's unknown-source profile computed as the clamped residual Yhat_{M+1} = max(0, x − αhat*Y_{argmax αhat}) — by checking non-negativity, dimensional consistency with the sink vector, and correctness of the clamped subtraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a validated source profile from FEAST's EM output (matrix P rows summing to 1) rather than a residual-derived count vector The mixing proportions are still unnormalized EM estimates and the L1 sparse selection step has not been run, so argmax(αhat) is not defined

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic taxonomic classifiers via genome exclusion — i.e., simulating reads (ART, Illumina/Roche-454 read models), classifying them against databases that omit the source genome, and computing genus/phylum sensitivity and precision.

skills.search_text: taxonomic-classifier-sensitivity-precision-computation Use when benchmarking metagenomic taxonomic classifiers via genome exclusion — i.e., simulating reads (ART, Illumina/Roche-454 read models), classifying them against databases that omit the source genome, and computing genus/phylum sensitivity and precision. Input is already a filtered feature table or non-taxonomic data (e.g. raw sequencing reads or gene-count matrices not produced by MetaPhlAn/QIIME) The goal is visualization or differential-abundance analysis (e.g. MetaDprof/MetaLonDa tasks) rather than building classification models You need to keep all taxa including very sparse features, e.g. when low-abundance taxa are themselves the biological signal of interest — threshold filtering may remove them http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Preprocesses merged MetaPhlAn or QIIME OTU/BIOM taxonomic profiles in MegaR by selecting a taxonomic level, removing low-abundance features below a floating threshold (default 0.003), applying a percentage-of-sample filter (default 5%), and optionally normalizing, to boost downstream machine learning accuracy. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03933-4
skills.summary: Preprocesses merged MetaPhlAn or QIIME OTU/BIOM taxonomic profiles in MegaR by selecting a taxonomic level, removing low-abundance features below a floating threshold (default 0.003), applying a percentage-of-sample filter (default 5%), and optionally normalizing, to boost downstream machine learning accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered feature table or non-taxonomic data (e.g. raw sequencing reads or gene-count matrices not produced by MetaPhlAn/QIIME) The goal is visualization or differential-abundance analysis (e.g. MetaDprof/MetaLonDa tasks) rather than building classification models You need to keep all taxa including very sparse features, e.g. when low-abundance taxa are themselves the biological signal of interest — threshold filtering may remove them

skills.description: Use when choosing among candidate taxonomic profilers or reference databases for metagenomic profiling, and benchmark results (e.g. CAMI profiler outputs, KMA .mapstat files) need to be scored and compared.
skills.name: taxonomic-profiler-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-profiler-benchmark-evaluation Use when choosing among candidate taxonomic profilers or reference databases for metagenomic profiling, and benchmark results (e.g. CAMI profiler outputs, KMA .mapstat files) need to be scored and compared. The goal is to profile a new real (non-simulated) metagenome rather than to compare profiler performance — use the chosen profiler directly instead of re-benchmarking Profiler outputs are already in OPAL/CAMI-evaluated form with metrics computed — re-running the scoring would duplicate work The data are long-read or single-cell metagenomes; the ARGprofiler benchmark validated mOTUs choice only on in silico short-read CAMI datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark microbial profiling tool/database combinations (KMA with mOTUs, Silva, and genomic databases; MetaPhlAn 4; mOTUs 3; Bracken 2.8 on Kraken2) on CAMI in silico datasets using OPAL-style binary classification metrics to select the profiler for a downstream pipeline such as ARGprofiler. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Benchmark microbial profiling tool/database combinations (KMA with mOTUs, Silva, and genomic databases; MetaPhlAn 4; mOTUs 3; Bracken 2.8 on Kraken2) on CAMI in silico datasets using OPAL-style binary classification metrics to select the profiler for a downstream pipeline such as ARGprofiler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to profile a new real (non-simulated) metagenome rather than to compare profiler performance — use the chosen profiler directly instead of re-benchmarking Profiler outputs are already in OPAL/CAMI-evaluated form with metrics computed — re-running the scoring would duplicate work The data are long-read or single-cell metagenomes; the ARGprofiler benchmark validated mOTUs choice only on in silico short-read CAMI datasets

skills.description: Use when metagenomic sequencing reads (post quality-control) need organism-level phylogenetic characterization prior to or alongside gene-catalog mapping, as in the CAMAMED case-control colorectal cancer gut metagenome workflow.
skills.name: taxonomic-profiling-with-marker-genes
skills.search_text: taxonomic-profiling-with-marker-genes Use when metagenomic sequencing reads (post quality-control) need organism-level phylogenetic characterization prior to or alongside gene-catalog mapping, as in the CAMAMED case-control colorectal cancer gut metagenome workflow. Input is already a taxonomic or gene abundance feature table — the profiling step expects raw/quality-controlled reads. No appropriate gene catalog or marker-gene database is available; the article states mapping-based methods are preferred only when appropriate gene catalogs exist. The goal is functional annotation at KO/EC/reaction level without any taxonomic component — that uses the KEGG mapping stage instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Performs taxonomic profiling of quality-controlled metagenomic reads with MetaPhlAn v2.0 inside the CAMAMED pipeline, describing the phylogenetic diversity of microorganisms in each sample as the first analytical stage before mapping-based functional analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa107
skills.summary: Performs taxonomic profiling of quality-controlled metagenomic reads with MetaPhlAn v2.0 inside the CAMAMED pipeline, describing the phylogenetic diversity of microorganisms in each sample as the first analytical stage before mapping-based functional analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a taxonomic or gene abundance feature table — the profiling step expects raw/quality-controlled reads. No appropriate gene catalog or marker-gene database is available; the article states mapping-based methods are preferred only when appropriate gene catalogs exist. The goal is functional annotation at KO/EC/reaction level without any taxonomic component — that uses the KEGG mapping stage instead.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a taxonomic classifier's precision and sensitivity at species/genus/family/phylum ranks on simulated reads from organisms whose clades were excluded from the reference database.
skills.name: taxonomic-rank-precision-evaluation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-rank-precision-evaluation Use when benchmarking a taxonomic classifier's precision and sensitivity at species/genus/family/phylum ranks on simulated reads from organisms whose clades were excluded from the reference database. Input reads are from organisms fully represented in the database — this skill is designed for clade-exclusion (novel organism) scenarios, not standard classification benchmarks The goal is abundance estimation from a real community rather than rank-level classification accuracy on simulated metagenomes A read's origin lacks a taxonomic entry at the measured or excluded rank, or fewer than two other taxa at the excluded rank share the origin's measured-rank clade — such reads are excluded from the experiment by design http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A clade-exclusion evaluation protocol that measures Kraken's rank-level precision and sensitivity on the simBA-5 metagenome by masking database hits from each read's clade of origin (species through phylum) and scoring whether classified reads land at the correct measured-rank taxon. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: A clade-exclusion evaluation protocol that measures Kraken's rank-level precision and sensitivity on the simBA-5 metagenome by masking database hits from each read's clade of origin (species through phylum) and scoring whether classified reads land at the correct measured-rank taxon.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are from organisms fully represented in the database — this skill is designed for clade-exclusion (novel organism) scenarios, not standard classification benchmarks The goal is abundance estimation from a real community rather than rank-level classification accuracy on simulated metagenomes A read's origin lacks a taxonomic entry at the measured or excluded rank, or fewer than two other taxa at the excluded rank share the origin's measured-rank clade — such reads are excluded from the experiment by design

skills.description: Use when you have per-read taxonomic assignments from a MetaCacheSpark/AFS-MetaCache query run and need read counts and abundance percentages per organism at a chosen rank via the -a/--abundance_per parameter.
skills.name: taxonomic-rank-pruning-and-count-propagation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-rank-pruning-and-count-propagation Use when you have per-read taxonomic assignments from a MetaCacheSpark/AFS-MetaCache query run and need read counts and abundance percentages per organism at a chosen rank via the -a/--abundance_per parameter. Input is raw FASTA/FASTQ reads that have not yet been classified by a MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark query — this skill operates on per-read classifications, not on sequences You only need a ranked list of candidate taxa per read (classification), not sample-level abundance quantification The analysis does not require a selectable taxonomic level and raw per-taxon read counts from the classifier suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Estimates organism abundances at a selectable taxonomic rank (e.g. species) from per-read classifications by pruning the taxonomy below the requested rank, propagating read counts upward to parent taxa, and redistributing reads from higher-level taxa to children proportionally to sub-tree weights. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-3429-6
skills.summary: Estimates organism abundances at a selectable taxonomic rank (e.g. species) from per-read classifications by pruning the taxonomy below the requested rank, propagating read counts upward to parent taxa, and redistributing reads from higher-level taxa to children proportionally to sub-tree weights.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTA/FASTQ reads that have not yet been classified by a MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark query — this skill operates on per-read classifications, not on sequences You only need a ranked list of candidate taxa per read (classification), not sample-level abundance quantification The analysis does not require a selectable taxonomic level and raw per-taxon read counts from the classifier suffice

skills.description: Use when reproducing or validating taxonomic classification counts of vOTUs from virome or shotgun metagenome assemblies, where expected per-rank tallies (phylum through genus/species) must be matched against published values.
skills.name: taxonomic-rank-tally-validation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-rank-tally-validation Use when reproducing or validating taxonomic classification counts of vOTUs from virome or shotgun metagenome assemblies, where expected per-rank tallies (phylum through genus/species) must be matched against published values. The goal is de novo viral taxonomy discovery rather than reproducing the MetaPhage benchmark tallies against INPHARED-based reference assignment Input contigs have not been dereplicated into vOTUs (95% ANI / 85% aligned fraction clustering), so counts would not be comparable to the published per-rank tallies http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduce the MetaPhage taxonomy-assignment benchmark: run Prodigal -> vConTACT2 (custom INPHARED Jan2022 reference) -> graphanalyzer on dereplicated vOTUs, aggregate per-rank assignments into a taxonomy_table.csv, and validate per-rank tallies against published counts (DNA virome: 3 phyla/3 classes/4 orders/9 families/32 genera). metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Reproduce the MetaPhage taxonomy-assignment benchmark: run Prodigal -> vConTACT2 (custom INPHARED Jan2022 reference) -> graphanalyzer on dereplicated vOTUs, aggregate per-rank assignments into a taxonomy_table.csv, and validate per-rank tallies against published counts (DNA virome: 3 phyla/3 classes/4 orders/9 families/32 genera).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo viral taxonomy discovery rather than reproducing the MetaPhage benchmark tallies against INPHARED-based reference assignment Input contigs have not been dereplicated into vOTUs (95% ANI / 85% aligned fraction clustering), so counts would not be comparable to the published per-rank tallies

skills.description: Use when a newly built taxonomic database (e.g. fungal marker genes) must be shown to reject reads from off-target organisms such as bacteria before deployment on real metagenomes.
skills.name: taxonomic-read-mapping-validation
skills.search_text: taxonomic-read-mapping-validation Use when a newly built taxonomic database (e.g. fungal marker genes) must be shown to reject reads from off-target organisms such as bacteria before deployment on real metagenomes. Validating the functional database FunOMIC-P, which uses DIAMOND blastx thresholds (coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10) rather than the Bowtie2 read-mapping workflow Assessing the taxonomic database's coverage or recall of true fungal targets — this skill measures off-target (bacterial) rejection only Input data are real metagenome reads rather than simulated mock communities with known ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Validates the specificity of a taxonomic marker-gene database (e.g. FunOMIC-T) by simulating bacterial Illumina reads with ART and confirming they fail to map, quantifying cross-kingdom false-positive mapping. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.010
skills.summary: Validates the specificity of a taxonomic marker-gene database (e.g. FunOMIC-T) by simulating bacterial Illumina reads with ART and confirming they fail to map, quantifying cross-kingdom false-positive mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Validating the functional database FunOMIC-P, which uses DIAMOND blastx thresholds (coverage >95%, identity >99%, e-value <10e-10) rather than the Bowtie2 read-mapping workflow Assessing the taxonomic database's coverage or recall of true fungal targets — this skill measures off-target (bacterial) rejection only Input data are real metagenome reads rather than simulated mock communities with known ground truth

skills.description: Use when you have a deposited probe set (e.g. from the HUBDesign probes/Coronavirus directory) plus the annotated source genomes, and need to determine what fraction of probes are genome-specific versus cross-reactive across multiple viruses.
skills.name: taxonomic-specificity-classification
skills.search_text: taxonomic-specificity-classification Use when you have a deposited probe set (e.g. from the HUBDesign probes/Coronavirus directory) plus the annotated source genomes, and need to determine what fraction of probes are genome-specific versus cross-reactive across multiple viruses. Probes cannot be meaningfully classified for genomes that are unknown or unannotatable, since HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to cluster sequences and probes only exist for targets with known genomes If the goal is capture enrichment validation (wet-lab hybridization performance), this BLASTn-based in silico specificity mapping does not measure enrichment efficiency, which varies per probe set depending on target sequence properties http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Classify each probe in a HUBDesign-designed probe set by the number of distinct genomes it hits after BLASTn mapping back to the source genomes, yielding a per-genome probe-count table and a single-virus vs multi-virus specificity distribution. This quantifies how specific the deposited probe set is at the taxonomic level of individual genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: Classify each probe in a HUBDesign-designed probe set by the number of distinct genomes it hits after BLASTn mapping back to the source genomes, yielding a per-genome probe-count table and a single-virus vs multi-virus specificity distribution. This quantifies how specific the deposited probe set is at the taxonomic level of individual genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Probes cannot be meaningfully classified for genomes that are unknown or unannotatable, since HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to cluster sequences and probes only exist for targets with known genomes If the goal is capture enrichment validation (wet-lab hybridization performance), this BLASTn-based in silico specificity mapping does not measure enrichment efficiency, which varies per probe set depending on target sequence properties

skills.description: Use when implementing or auditing k-mer-based taxonomic label assignment where root-to-leaf path scores can tie, and a deterministic, conservative label (the LCA of tied leaves) must be emitted.
skills.name: taxonomic-tie-resolution-via-lca
skills.search_text: taxonomic-tie-resolution-via-lca Use when implementing or auditing k-mer-based taxonomic label assignment where root-to-leaf path scores can tie, and a deterministic, conservative label (the LCA of tied leaves) must be emitted. The query has no k-mers present in the database — Kraken leaves such sequences unclassified, and no tie resolution applies The classification method is alignment-based (e.g., BLAST/Megablast or MEGAN LCA over BLAST hits) rather than Kraken's RTL path scoring over a k-mer LCA database, since tie-breaking semantics differ http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 A decision rule from Kraken's classification algorithm: when multiple root-to-leaf (RTL) paths in the k-mer-weighted classification tree tie for the maximum score, the query sequence is labeled with the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of the tied leaves rather than an arbitrary winner. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46
skills.summary: A decision rule from Kraken's classification algorithm: when multiple root-to-leaf (RTL) paths in the k-mer-weighted classification tree tie for the maximum score, the query sequence is labeled with the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of the tied leaves rather than an arbitrary winner.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query has no k-mers present in the database — Kraken leaves such sequences unclassified, and no tie resolution applies The classification method is alignment-based (e.g., BLAST/Megablast or MEGAN LCA over BLAST hits) rather than Kraken's RTL path scoring over a k-mer LCA database, since tie-breaking semantics differ

skills.description: Use when MEMs computed from amplified metagenomic short reads (pal-MEM/E-MEM style output) must be filtered to remove edge-proximal technical repeats before ITR candidate selection.
skills.name: technical-repeat-end-buffer-filtering
skills.search_text: technical-repeat-end-buffer-filtering Use when MEMs computed from amplified metagenomic short reads (pal-MEM/E-MEM style output) must be filtered to remove edge-proximal technical repeats before ITR candidate selection. Input is already-filtered MEM output or reads without amplification bias where edge-buffer exclusion would discard genuine terminal signal Discovering insertion sequences that lack inverted terminal repeats — Palidis/pal-MEM is 'only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs' Long-read or isolate assembly data where the 20-nt edge-buffer assumption for short amplified reads does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A post-MEM filtering step from the Palidis pipeline that suppresses technical repeats introduced by amplified read libraries by discarding maximal exact matches (MEMs) whose start or end falls within a 20-nucleotide (40-bit) buffer of either read edge. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: A post-MEM filtering step from the Palidis pipeline that suppresses technical repeats introduced by amplified read libraries by discarding maximal exact matches (MEMs) whose start or end falls within a 20-nucleotide (40-bit) buffer of either read edge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already-filtered MEM output or reads without amplification bias where edge-buffer exclusion would discard genuine terminal signal Discovering insertion sequences that lack inverted terminal repeats — Palidis/pal-MEM is 'only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs' Long-read or isolate assembly data where the 20-nt edge-buffer assumption for short amplified reads does not apply

Input is raw microarray-based data, which cannot be used directly as input per the MOVIS discussion section Input has not been preprocessed at all — the core presupposes quality controlled and filtered data, so run external preprocessing first Goal is taxa linking for metagenomics data — MOVIS is not explicitly designed for this and no taxa linking is currently enabled http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3077 Validates that a tabular time-series multi-omics dataset (e.g., MOVIS Example 1 metagenomics depth-of-coverage data from Data/cached/example_1/) passes the MOVIS sanitizing data quality checks and that its embedded temporal feature is correctly recognized before any visualization or clustering step. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.02.012
skills.summary: Validates that a tabular time-series multi-omics dataset (e.g., MOVIS Example 1 metagenomics depth-of-coverage data from Data/cached/example_1/) passes the MOVIS sanitizing data quality checks and that its embedded temporal feature is correctly recognized before any visualization or clustering step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw microarray-based data, which cannot be used directly as input per the MOVIS discussion section Input has not been preprocessed at all — the core presupposes quality controlled and filtered data, so run external preprocessing first Goal is taxa linking for metagenomics data — MOVIS is not explicitly designed for this and no taxa linking is currently enabled

Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than variant-called VCF/lineage tables — run freebayes variant calling and the lineagespot merge/collapse steps first Samples are single clinical isolates without a time-series design, so no temporal trajectory can be assembled Only a single sample/time point is available, leaving no successive periods to verify a rising fraction http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Assemble a per-sample lineage-abundance table from lineagespot output across 14 Thessaloniki wastewater time periods and extract/visualize the B.1.1.7 (Alpha) abundance time series to capture the variant's rise over the 6-month window. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: Assemble a per-sample lineage-abundance table from lineagespot output across 14 Thessaloniki wastewater time periods and extract/visualize the B.1.1.7 (Alpha) abundance time series to capture the variant's rise over the 6-month window.

skills.search_text: tenfold-cross-validation Use when a machine learning model (e.g. Random Forest) has been trained in MegaR on taxonomic profiles (16S or WGS) and you need a variance-minimized, unbiased estimate of predictive accuracy before reporting or deployment. You still have raw reads or an unpreprocessed abundance table — preprocess via MegaR's getGoodfeature (threshold 0.003, 5% sample percentage) first, since CV on unfiltered sparse features yields poor models The model is intended only for quick exploratory training-error inspection, not for reporting defensible accuracy — the confusion-matrix test error on the held-out split alone may suffice There are more than two classes and you have not used the 'Select level to classify' tab to remove control/irrelevant classes, which the article notes increases model accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Validate a MegaR-trained Random Forest (or other) classification model on metagenomic profiles using N independent runs of 10-fold cross validation, as prescribed by the MegaR pipeline for DIABIMMUNE T1D data, to estimate robust cross-validated accuracy and guard against overfitting and bias. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03933-4
skills.summary: Validate a MegaR-trained Random Forest (or other) classification model on metagenomic profiles using N independent runs of 10-fold cross validation, as prescribed by the MegaR pipeline for DIABIMMUNE T1D data, to estimate robust cross-validated accuracy and guard against overfitting and bias.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You still have raw reads or an unpreprocessed abundance table — preprocess via MegaR's getGoodfeature (threshold 0.003, 5% sample percentage) first, since CV on unfiltered sparse features yields poor models The model is intended only for quick exploratory training-error inspection, not for reporting defensible accuracy — the confusion-matrix test error on the held-out split alone may suffice There are more than two classes and you have not used the 'Select level to classify' tab to remove control/irrelevant classes, which the article notes increases model accuracy

skills.description: Use when generating custom k-mer detection networks for baseLess from corrected raw signal reads — i.e., you have training/test fast5 reads for a known species and a k-mer list, and no pre-generated network exists.
skills.name: tensorflow-1d-cnn-model-training
skills.search_text: tensorflow-1d-cnn-model-training Use when generating custom k-mer detection networks for baseLess from corrected raw signal reads — i.e., you have training/test fast5 reads for a known species and a k-mer list, and no pre-generated network exists. A pre-generated k-mer detection network for your target 16S k-mers already exists (use 'baseLess update_16s_db' instead of retraining) You need full basecalling/sequence reconstruction rather than target-detection-only analysis on raw signal You lack a good reference genome for tombo resquiggle or a large read set of a known species to train on http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Train per-k-mer 1D CNN detectors in TensorFlow whose hyperparameters are optimized with hyperopt's tree-structured Parzen estimator, minimizing loss L=(1-F1)+lambda*p_c/p_max (lambda=0.01) to jointly maximize F1 and shrink network size. Each network outputs the posterior probability that its target k-mer is present in a squiggle segment of raw MinION signal. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbad017
skills.summary: Train per-k-mer 1D CNN detectors in TensorFlow whose hyperparameters are optimized with hyperopt's tree-structured Parzen estimator, minimizing loss L=(1-F1)+lambda*p_c/p_max (lambda=0.01) to jointly maximize F1 and shrink network size. Each network outputs the posterior probability that its target k-mer is present in a squiggle segment of raw MinION signal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A pre-generated k-mer detection network for your target 16S k-mers already exists (use 'baseLess update_16s_db' instead of retraining) You need full basecalling/sequence reconstruction rather than target-detection-only analysis on raw signal You lack a good reference genome for tombo resquiggle or a large read set of a known species to train on

skills.description: Use when natural-language taxonomic description sentences must be converted into taxon-by-character values using curated term lists, especially when term-list coverage is insufficient for coordinated noun phrases.
skills.name: term-list-based-value-extraction
skills.search_text: term-list-based-value-extraction Use when natural-language taxonomic description sentences must be converted into taxon-by-character values using curated term lists, especially when term-list coverage is insufficient for coordinated noun phrases. Descriptions are morphological/semi-structured plant-style descriptions better served by CharaParser — prokaryotic descriptions focus on physiological and ecological traits, which is MicroPIE's scope. Extraction requires open-domain context without domain knowledge — OIE-style systems were found inadequate here, but term matching alone will miss characters outside the 42 covered types. The target character types (e.g. antibiotic production, pressure preference in 0.2.0) are absent from the 0.1.0 Term Lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Extracts phenotypic character values from prokaryotic taxonomic description sentences by segmenting them into noun phrases and matching each noun phrase against curated per-character Term Lists (models\CharacterValueExtractors0.1.0) in MicroPIE, expanding coordinated noun phrases so all conjuncts become values once one matches. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1396-8
skills.summary: Extracts phenotypic character values from prokaryotic taxonomic description sentences by segmenting them into noun phrases and matching each noun phrase against curated per-character Term Lists (models\CharacterValueExtractors0.1.0) in MicroPIE, expanding coordinated noun phrases so all conjuncts become values once one matches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Descriptions are morphological/semi-structured plant-style descriptions better served by CharaParser — prokaryotic descriptions focus on physiological and ecological traits, which is MicroPIE's scope. Extraction requires open-domain context without domain knowledge — OIE-style systems were found inadequate here, but term matching alone will miss characters outside the 42 covered types. The target character types (e.g. antibiotic production, pressure preference in 0.2.0) are absent from the 0.1.0 Term Lists.

skills.name: terminal-coverage-masking-of-scaffold-ends
skills.search_text: terminal-coverage-masking-of-scaffold-ends Use when computing per-scaffold read coverage tables for viral scaffold binning from BAM/CRAM alignments, where terminal coverage on scaffold ends should be excluded before pairwise coverage effect-size comparisons. Input is already a pre-computed coverage table via the -c flag: outlier removal (and by extension vRhyme's internal coverage recalculation) is turned off for -c coverage-table input The goal is binning microbial (non-viral) genomes: vRhyme is explicitly not meant to bin microbes and performance on whole metagenomes is not fully evaluated Scaffolds are shorter than twice the --mask window (e.g. 2 x 150 bases), where masking would remove most of the scaffold's usable coverage signal http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A coverage-processing step in vRhyme that zeroes out coverage accumulated in the terminal --mask bases (default 150) at each end of every input viral scaffold, so that coverage effect-size comparisons between scaffold pairs are not biased by edge-mapping artifacts before the Cohen's d / d' distances reach the machine learning layer. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341

Input genomes are already near-complete annotated genome sequences for which the PICA framework can annotate phenotypes directly without simulated thinning The analysis target is not SVM-based trait prediction from COG profiles but e.g. a different feature type (e.g. k-mer or gene-content models outside the PICA profile format) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Simulates genome incompleteness by randomly removing 10–90% of COG entries from eggNOG 4.0 COG presence/absence profiles (3 replicates per level), producing PICA-compatible incomplete test sets to evaluate how well SVM-based phenotypic trait prediction tolerates metagenomic bins of reduced completeness. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-16-s14-s1

skills.description: Use when annotating human microbiome metagenomic contigs of unknown provenance where the genetic code is unknown, and correct interpretation of TGA (stop vs. sense/tryptophan) is needed before or during gene prediction.
skills.name: tga-codon-role-classification
skills.search_text: tga-codon-role-classification Use when annotating human microbiome metagenomic contigs of unknown provenance where the genetic code is unknown, and correct interpretation of TGA (stop vs. sense/tryptophan) is needed before or during gene prediction. The input sequences come from organisms with a known standard genetic code already recorded (e.g. complete GenBank genomes) — use GeneMarkS-2 with the known code instead of classifying TGA de novo. The goal is protein-level functional annotation or taxonomic binning rather than gene prediction in contigs with ambiguous genetic code. Prerequisites (gmhmmp2 key, blastn in PATH, refmod model library, pan-genome BLAST database) cannot be installed, since the TGA-role determination depends on the full GeneMark-HM model-selection machinery. http://edamontology.org/topic_3941 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classify whether TGA acts as a stop codon or a sense codon in anonymous metagenomic contigs using GeneMark-HM's dual MetaGeneMark classifier, which runs each contig with models for the two possible TGA roles and selects the more likely one. This matters because in some bacterial genomes TGA codes for tryptophan, and misassigning its role corrupts downstream gene prediction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047
skills.summary: Classify whether TGA acts as a stop codon or a sense codon in anonymous metagenomic contigs using GeneMark-HM's dual MetaGeneMark classifier, which runs each contig with models for the two possible TGA roles and selects the more likely one. This matters because in some bacterial genomes TGA codes for tryptophan, and misassigning its role corrupts downstream gene prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input sequences come from organisms with a known standard genetic code already recorded (e.g. complete GenBank genomes) — use GeneMarkS-2 with the known code instead of classifying TGA de novo. skills.search_text: three-phase-taxonomic-read-classification Use when similarity matrices from ClusterBWT_DA (one per strand of both mates) must be converted into per-read-pair taxonomic assignments at species rank or higher, output as C/U/A/H,IdSeqRead,TaxID,maxSim lines. No similarity value for a read reaches the threshold beta, so the read must simply be reported as unclassified rather than pushed through taxonomic-rank fallback The reference database lacks a taxonomic lineage file, making higher-rank reassignment via lineage impossible Single-end data where the paired-end re-examination phase cannot add resolving information http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 LiME's Step 3 assigns each metagenomic read pair to a taxon by thresholding the r x g similarity matrices (threshold beta=0.25), selecting genomes within tolerance 0.02 of the maximum similarity, re-examining ambiguous pairs using paired-end information, and falling back to higher taxonomic ranks via the lineage file (Reference_database.csv). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03628-w

skills.description: Use when annotated genomes (e.g., PROKKA GFFs) and a guide tree are available and you need a compact, balanced hybridization-capture probe set that captures known and related (up to ~20% divergent) sequences across multiple taxa.
skills.name: tiling-probe-selection
skills.search_text: tiling-probe-selection Use when annotated genomes (e.g., PROKKA GFFs) and a guide tree are available and you need a compact, balanced hybridization-capture probe set that captures known and related (up to ~20% divergent) sequences across multiple taxa. Targets have unknown or unannotatable genomes: HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to cluster sequences, so probes cannot be designed for unknown targets (only close relatives can be targeted). Setting --tiling-density higher than the data can support: an unrealistically high target can make it impossible to balance baits across organisms, causing unexpectedly small probe sets. Single-organism, known-sequence detection tasks better served by PCR/multiplexed primer design rather than a taxonomically hierarchical capture probe set. http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 HUBDesign's post-identification pipeline for hybridization-capture probe design: candidate bait regions identified by SA_BOND on pseudo-genomes are filtered against blacklist BLAST databases and low-complexity sequence, then a balanced probe set is selected by iterative tiling-density balancing across input genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: HUBDesign's post-identification pipeline for hybridization-capture probe design: candidate bait regions identified by SA_BOND on pseudo-genomes are filtered against blacklist BLAST databases and low-complexity sequence, then a balanced probe set is selected by iterative tiling-density balancing across input genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Targets have unknown or unannotatable genomes: HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to cluster sequences, so probes cannot be designed for unknown targets (only close relatives can be targeted). Setting --tiling-density higher than the data can support: an unrealistically high target can make it impossible to balance baits across organisms, causing unexpectedly small probe sets. Single-organism, known-sequence detection tasks better served by PCR/multiplexed primer design rather than a taxonomically hierarchical capture probe set.

skills.description: Use when a scoring model (e.g., kernelized logistic matrix factorization on a virus-host heterogeneous network) outputs ranked host predictions per virus and you want a more robust species-level host call than the single top-ranked prediction provides.
skills.name: top-k-consensus-host-prediction
skills.search_text: top-k-consensus-host-prediction Use when a scoring model (e.g., kernelized logistic matrix factorization on a virus-host heterogeneous network) outputs ranked host predictions per virus and you want a more robust species-level host call than the single top-ranked prediction provides. The question requires a single definitive host per virus (e.g., strain-level attribution), since consensus blurs ranks into a top-k call The prediction model already reports calibrated probabilities or a validated single-host decision rule rather than a score ranking Evaluation is restricted to a metric other than species-level accuracy of the assigned host (e.g., AUROC over all pairs), where top-k aggregation is not the target http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Boosts ILMF-VH virus host prediction accuracy by aggregating the top-ranked predicted hosts into a top-5 consensus call instead of reporting only the single highest-scoring host. On the Edwards et al. benchmark (820 viruses, 2699 hosts), consensus lifted species-level accuracy from 58.90% (top-1) to 63.66%. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Boosts ILMF-VH virus host prediction accuracy by aggregating the top-ranked predicted hosts into a top-5 consensus call instead of reporting only the single highest-scoring host. On the Edwards et al. benchmark (820 viruses, 2699 hosts), consensus lifted species-level accuracy from 58.90% (top-1) to 63.66%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question requires a single definitive host per virus (e.g., strain-level attribution), since consensus blurs ranks into a top-k call The prediction model already reports calibrated probabilities or a validated single-host decision rule rather than a score ranking Evaluation is restricted to a metric other than species-level accuracy of the assigned host (e.g., AUROC over all pairs), where top-k aggregation is not the target
