skills.name: translated-read-gene-screening
skills.search_text: translated-read-gene-screening Use when you have raw short DNA sequencing reads (FASTQ) and need to find reads encoding a known protein family without assembling the dataset first. The target genes are nucleotide features such as CRISPR repeat arrays rather than proteins — use CasCollect DNA mode (--nucl with -query) which VSEARCH-matches reads against repeat FASTA files instead You already have a user-defined seed FASTA to assemble around — use --seed -define file.fasta, which bypasses protein and DNA searches entirely Input is assembled contigs or genomes rather than raw reads — standard HMMER annotation of ORF-called assemblies is more appropriate than read-level translation http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Screen raw unassembled Illumina reads for protein-coding genes of interest by predicting open reading frames directly on reads (FragGeneScan/FragGeneScan-Plus) and searching the translations with HMMER against profile HMMs — here the default 120 Cas protein family profile HMMs used by CasCollect's protein mode to collect cas gene seed reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Screen raw unassembled Illumina reads for protein-coding genes of interest by predicting open reading frames directly on reads (FragGeneScan/FragGeneScan-Plus) and searching the translations with HMMER against profile HMMs — here the default 120 Cas protein family profile HMMs used by CasCollect's protein mode to collect cas gene seed reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target genes are nucleotide features such as CRISPR repeat arrays rather than proteins — use CasCollect DNA mode (--nucl with -query) which VSEARCH-matches reads against repeat FASTA files instead You already have a user-defined seed FASTA to assemble around — use --seed -define file.fasta, which bypasses protein and DNA searches entirely Input is assembled contigs or genomes rather than raw reads — standard HMMER annotation of ORF-called assemblies is more appropriate than read-level translation

skills.description: Use when benchmarking gene start prediction tools (e.g., GeneMark-HM vs MetaProdigal) on complete genomes and you need to stratify results by translation initiation signal type — canonical RBS, non-canonical RBS, or leaderless.
skills.name: translation-initiation-signal-classification
skills.search_text: translation-initiation-signal-classification Use when benchmarking gene start prediction tools (e.g., GeneMark-HM vs MetaProdigal) on complete genomes and you need to stratify results by translation initiation signal type — canonical RBS, non-canonical RBS, or leaderless. Input is metagenomic contigs rather than complete genomes — the classes are defined by GeneMarkS-2 self-training, which requires sufficiently long sequences (complete genomes) You only need overall (unstratified) gene start accuracy — the class partition adds value only when initiation-signal-specific behavior matters No reference annotation with GeneMarkS-2-identified initiation signals is available, since class assignment depends on signals upstream of each annotated start http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Partition complete prokaryotic genomes into classes defined by the translation initiation signal upstream of each annotated start codon — canonical RBS, non-canonical RBS, or leaderless transcription — to enable stratified benchmarking of gene start prediction accuracy (as done in the GeneMark-HM paper's Table 4 analysis of 625 test genomes grouped by GeneMarkS-2). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqab047
skills.summary: Partition complete prokaryotic genomes into classes defined by the translation initiation signal upstream of each annotated start codon — canonical RBS, non-canonical RBS, or leaderless transcription — to enable stratified benchmarking of gene start prediction accuracy (as done in the GeneMark-HM paper's Table 4 analysis of 625 test genomes grouped by GeneMarkS-2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is metagenomic contigs rather than complete genomes — the classes are defined by GeneMarkS-2 self-training, which requires sufficiently long sequences (complete genomes) You only need overall (unstratified) gene start accuracy — the class partition adds value only when initiation-signal-specific behavior matters No reference annotation with GeneMarkS-2-identified initiation signals is available, since class assignment depends on signals upstream of each annotated start

skills.description: Use when you have a FASTA catalogue of candidate insertion sequences (e.g. from Palidis/ISC) and need to determine which have known homologs in ISfinder and at what stringency.
skills.name: transposable-element-annotation
skills.search_text: transposable-element-annotation Use when you have a FASTA catalogue of candidate insertion sequences (e.g. from Palidis/ISC) and need to determine which have known homologs in ISfinder and at what stringency. Input sequences are not insertion sequences or lack inverted terminal repeats — the ISC is restricted to DDE-type ISs with ITRs of 25 or more nucleotides, so results will not generalize to ITR-less elements You need de novo IS discovery from reads rather than annotation of an existing catalogue — use Palidis first to generate the IS sequences The catalogue derives from sources outside healthy human oral cavity and stool metagenomes — ISC v1.0.0 is recommended as a reference only for isolates from those sources http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates a catalogue of discovered insertion sequences (ISs) by BLASTing each sequence against ISfinder and classifying hits into strict homology (e-value <1e-50), loose homology (0.01 > e-value >= 1e-50), or novel (no hit at the 0.01 threshold), enabling quantification of how much of a novel IS catalogue is already characterized. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Annotates a catalogue of discovered insertion sequences (ISs) by BLASTing each sequence against ISfinder and classifying hits into strict homology (e-value <1e-50), loose homology (0.01 > e-value >= 1e-50), or novel (no hit at the 0.01 threshold), enabling quantification of how much of a novel IS catalogue is already characterized.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are not insertion sequences or lack inverted terminal repeats — the ISC is restricted to DDE-type ISs with ITRs of 25 or more nucleotides, so results will not generalize to ITR-less elements You need de novo IS discovery from reads rather than annotation of an existing catalogue — use Palidis first to generate the IS sequences The catalogue derives from sources outside healthy human oral cavity and stool metagenomes — ISC v1.0.0 is recommended as a reference only for isolates from those sources

skills.description: Use when candidate insertion sequences (putative IS nucleotide contigs with ITRs, 500-3000 bp) must be validated as bona fide transposase-family elements before inclusion in an IS catalogue or output table.
skills.name: transposase-integrase-annotation-filtering
skills.search_text: transposase-integrase-annotation-filtering Use when candidate insertion sequences (putative IS nucleotide contigs with ITRs, 500-3000 bp) must be validated as bona fide transposase-family elements before inclusion in an IS catalogue or output table. Candidates lack inverted terminal repeats — Palidis is 'currently only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs', so ITR-lacking (non-DDE) elements will not reach this annotation step Input is already-annotated genomes where IS family membership is known from a reference database such as ISfinder — query the catalogue/reference instead of re-annotating ORFs Sequences fall outside the 500-3000 bp IS length window (e.g. nested insertions lengthened beyond max_is_len), which are missed before annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Annotates predicted ORFs on candidate insertion sequences with InterPro/PANTHER protein-family signatures (via Prodigal + InterProScan) and retains only ISs whose family descriptions include Transposase, Integrase-like and/or Ribonuclease H, so that the final IS catalogue contains proteins consistent with transposase-family function. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Annotates predicted ORFs on candidate insertion sequences with InterPro/PANTHER protein-family signatures (via Prodigal + InterProScan) and retains only ISs whose family descriptions include Transposase, Integrase-like and/or Ribonuclease H, so that the final IS catalogue contains proteins consistent with transposase-family function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidates lack inverted terminal repeats — Palidis is 'currently only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs', so ITR-lacking (non-DDE) elements will not reach this annotation step Input is already-annotated genomes where IS family membership is known from a reference database such as ISfinder — query the catalogue/reference instead of re-annotating ORFs Sequences fall outside the 500-3000 bp IS length window (e.g. nested insertions lengthened beyond max_is_len), which are missed before annotation

skills.description: Use when comparing a survival outcome (time-to-event with censoring) between pre-defined treatment groups and the comparison must be adjusted for covariates such as Sex via Cox regression.
skills.name: treatment-group-comparison-statistics
skills.search_text: treatment-group-comparison-statistics Use when comparing a survival outcome (time-to-event with censoring) between pre-defined treatment groups and the comparison must be adjusted for covariates such as Sex via Cox regression. The analysis goal involves microbiome composition rather than a pure treatment-group survival comparison — MiSurv Modules 2–4 handle composition, association testing, and prediction modeling instead; Module 1 explicitly does not involve microbiome data. The response is continuous or binary rather than a survival (time-to-event) response — the authors note MiSurv is designed for survival responses while MiCloud handles continuous or binary responses. No censoring structure or survival time is available in the metadata, so a Cox model on Surv(time, event) cannot be constructed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits a covariate-adjusted Cox proportional hazards model in R's 'survival' package to compare survival rates between treatment groups (e.g., control vs tylosin) in a microbiome survival-data workflow, as performed by Module 1 of the MiSurv platform. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/spectrum.05059-22
skills.summary: Fits a covariate-adjusted Cox proportional hazards model in R's 'survival' package to compare survival rates between treatment groups (e.g., control vs tylosin) in a microbiome survival-data workflow, as performed by Module 1 of the MiSurv platform.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal involves microbiome composition rather than a pure treatment-group survival comparison — MiSurv Modules 2–4 handle composition, association testing, and prediction modeling instead; Module 1 explicitly does not involve microbiome data. The response is continuous or binary rather than a survival (time-to-event) response — the authors note MiSurv is designed for survival responses while MiCloud handles continuous or binary responses. No censoring structure or survival time is available in the metadata, so a Cox model on Surv(time, event) cannot be constructed.

skills.description: Use when validating an annotation-expansion method by removing known KO annotations from eggNOG (.emapper.annotations) results and scoring whether an HMM search correctly recovers the removed gene and annotation.
skills.name: true-positive-rate-computation
skills.search_text: true-positive-rate-computation Use when validating an annotation-expansion method by removing known KO annotations from eggNOG (.emapper.annotations) results and scoring whether an HMM search correctly recovers the removed gene and annotation. Gene sequences have been truncated (e.g. 30% or 70% of original length deleted) — those are separate truncation benchmarks, not the untruncated TPR test You need Module completeness evaluation or GSMM gapfilling rather than benchmarking HMM-based KO recovery (use --skip_hmm / --skip_gsmm workflows instead) Input annotations are not in a supported KEGG KO format (eggnog / kaas / kofamkoala) with maintained file extensions such as .emapper.annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Benchmark skill that quantifies how reliably a functional annotation-recovery tool (KEMET's --hmm_mode onebm HMM search) restores deliberately mock-removed KO annotations, expressed as true positive rates (e.g. 55% for MAGs, 67% for complete genomes). metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.015
skills.summary: Benchmark skill that quantifies how reliably a functional annotation-recovery tool (KEMET's --hmm_mode onebm HMM search) restores deliberately mock-removed KO annotations, expressed as true positive rates (e.g. 55% for MAGs, 67% for complete genomes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene sequences have been truncated (e.g. 30% or 70% of original length deleted) — those are separate truncation benchmarks, not the untruncated TPR test You need Module completeness evaluation or GSMM gapfilling rather than benchmarking HMM-based KO recovery (use --skip_hmm / --skip_gsmm workflows instead) Input annotations are not in a supported KEGG KO format (eggnog / kaas / kofamkoala) with maintained file extensions such as .emapper.annotations

skills.description: Use when a simulated metagenomic benchmark has a known ground-truth mutation list and you must quantify how many true shared variants a caller (e.g. MetaQuad) recovers and whether it introduces false positives.
skills.name: true-positive-recovery-assessment
skills.search_text: true-positive-recovery-assessment Use when a simulated metagenomic benchmark has a known ground-truth mutation list and you must quantify how many true shared variants a caller (e.g. MetaQuad) recovers and whether it introduces false positives. Input is real (non-simulated) metagenomic data with no ground-truth mutation list, so true-positive recovery cannot be counted Data are single-cell mitochondrial variants intended for clonal substructure inference — use MQuad rather than this metagenomic benchmark Sample size is very small so the recommended minSample = 5% of total sample size threshold becomes degenerate http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark skill for verifying that MetaQuad recovers simulated ground-truth shared informative variants at scale, as demonstrated by scaling the simulated benchmark 10-fold to n = 1000 samples at mean depth 11.8 and counting recovered true positives versus false positives. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Benchmark skill for verifying that MetaQuad recovers simulated ground-truth shared informative variants at scale, as demonstrated by scaling the simulated benchmark 10-fold to n = 1000 samples at mean depth 11.8 and counting recovered true positives versus false positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) metagenomic data with no ground-truth mutation list, so true-positive recovery cannot be counted Data are single-cell mitochondrial variants intended for clonal substructure inference — use MQuad rather than this metagenomic benchmark Sample size is very small so the recommended minSample = 5% of total sample size threshold becomes degenerate

skills.description: Use when you have per-sequence embeddings from a trained classifier checkpoint and need to test whether the representation space is taxonomically structured at a given rank (e.g., species or phylum).
skills.name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-of-sequence-embeddings
skills.search_text: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-of-sequence-embeddings Use when you have per-sequence embeddings from a trained classifier checkpoint and need to test whether the representation space is taxonomically structured at a given rank (e.g., species or phylum). You need classification predictions or accuracy/F1/ECE metrics rather than an embedding-space qualitative/structural check — use deeptaxa predict instead Input is raw FASTQ/FASTA sequence data and no trained checkpoint is available to produce embeddings You need to compare performance across alternative reference databases (SILVA, RDP) or independent datasets, which the paper does not evaluate http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Projects high-dimensional neural embeddings (e.g., DeepTaxa's 896-dim fused CNN-BERT representations of 16S rRNA sequences) to 2D with t-SNE to visually and quantitatively assess whether embeddings cluster by taxonomic label. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbag166
skills.summary: Projects high-dimensional neural embeddings (e.g., DeepTaxa's 896-dim fused CNN-BERT representations of 16S rRNA sequences) to 2D with t-SNE to visually and quantitatively assess whether embeddings cluster by taxonomic label.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need classification predictions or accuracy/F1/ECE metrics rather than an embedding-space qualitative/structural check — use deeptaxa predict instead Input is raw FASTQ/FASTA sequence data and no trained checkpoint is available to produce embeddings You need to compare performance across alternative reference databases (SILVA, RDP) or independent datasets, which the paper does not evaluate

skills.description: Use when running Plassembler hybrid plasmid assembly and you need a machine-readable per-contig table capturing circularity and PLSDB mash-screening matches for downstream validation or reporting.
skills.name: tsv-summary-reporting
skills.search_text: tsv-summary-reporting Use when running Plassembler hybrid plasmid assembly and you need a machine-readable per-contig table capturing circularity and PLSDB mash-screening matches for downstream validation or reporting. The Plassembler PLSDB database (install_database.py) has not been installed, so no mash sketch database exists to screen contigs against The contigs come from an assembly method that does not supply Unicycler-style circularity information, making the circularity columns unreliable The goal is read filtering or assembly rather than summarizing already-assembled plasmid contigs Aggregate Plassembler's per-contig plasmid results into a single tab-separated summary table (plasmid_summary.tsv) that pairs each assembled plasmid contig's Unicycler-derived circularity status with its top PLSDB mash hit below the 0.1 distance threshold. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Aggregate Plassembler's per-contig plasmid results into a single tab-separated summary table (plasmid_summary.tsv) that pairs each assembled plasmid contig's Unicycler-derived circularity status with its top PLSDB mash hit below the 0.1 distance threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The Plassembler PLSDB database (install_database.py) has not been installed, so no mash sketch database exists to screen contigs against The contigs come from an assembly method that does not supply Unicycler-style circularity information, making the circularity columns unreliable The goal is read filtering or assembly rather than summarizing already-assembled plasmid contigs

skills.description: Use when quantifying microbial strains shared between related individuals (e.g., twin pairs) from metagenomic read mappings, or when benchmarking a strain-comparison method's accuracy against existing ANI-based tools.
skills.name: twin-cohort-metagenome-strain-sharing-quantification
skills.search_text: twin-cohort-metagenome-strain-sharing-quantification Use when quantifying microbial strains shared between related individuals (e.g., twin pairs) from metagenomic read mappings, or when benchmarking a strain-comparison method's accuracy against existing ANI-based tools. Input is raw reads without a curated set of sub-species reference genomes to concatenate and map against — inStrain profile requires a .fasta of representative genomes The question is species-level abundance profiling rather than sub-species strain sharing — tools like CoverM for genome coverage would be more appropriate Genomes were dereplicated at >98% ANI, which risks multi-mapped reads and inflated comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmarks strain-sharing detection across infant twin metagenomes by quantifying genomes shared between siblings using inStrain's microdiversity-aware popANI comparisons against dRep, MIDAS, and StrainPhlAn native criteria. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Benchmarks strain-sharing detection across infant twin metagenomes by quantifying genomes shared between siblings using inStrain's microdiversity-aware popANI comparisons against dRep, MIDAS, and StrainPhlAn native criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads without a curated set of sub-species reference genomes to concatenate and map against — inStrain profile requires a .fasta of representative genomes The question is species-level abundance profiling rather than sub-species strain sharing — tools like CoverM for genome coverage would be more appropriate Genomes were dereplicated at >98% ANI, which risks multi-mapped reads and inflated comparisons

skills.description: Use when re-analyzing the 280-sample twin/mother gut V1-V2 amplicon cohort (samples with >=1,000 reads) to test whether GCN correction changes enterotype classification or phylum-level profiles.
skills.name: twin-cohort-microbiome-reanalysis
skills.search_text: twin-cohort-microbiome-reanalysis Use when re-analyzing the 280-sample twin/mother gut V1-V2 amplicon cohort (samples with >=1,000 reads) to test whether GCN correction changes enterotype classification or phylum-level profiles. Input profiles are already GCN-corrected or expressed as percentages rather than raw read counts (CopyRighter requires counts and unaltered taxonomic assignments) The OTU table uses a taxonomy other than Greengenes (e.g., Silva), since CopyRighter's shipped GCN estimates cover only the Oct 2012 Greengenes taxonomy Metagenomic (not amplicon) profiles, unless correcting genome length bias rather than 16S rRNA GCN http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Re-analysis protocol for the human gut twin-cohort 16S rRNA amplicon dataset in which CopyRighter's phylogenetic-level 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) correction shifts phylum-level abundances, changes the Berger-Parker dominance index, and reclassifies enterotypes from two into three community types. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/2049-2618-2-11
skills.summary: Re-analysis protocol for the human gut twin-cohort 16S rRNA amplicon dataset in which CopyRighter's phylogenetic-level 16S rRNA gene copy number (GCN) correction shifts phylum-level abundances, changes the Berger-Parker dominance index, and reclassifies enterotypes from two into three community types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input profiles are already GCN-corrected or expressed as percentages rather than raw read counts (CopyRighter requires counts and unaltered taxonomic assignments) The OTU table uses a taxonomy other than Greengenes (e.g., Silva), since CopyRighter's shipped GCN estimates cover only the Oct 2012 Greengenes taxonomy Metagenomic (not amplicon) profiles, unless correcting genome length bias rather than 16S rRNA GCN

skills.description: Use when metagenomic samples from related and unrelated individuals (e.g. NICU infant stool) have inStrain compare popANI profiles and you need to test sibling enrichment and MZ-vs-DZ strain-sharing patterns.
skills.name: twin-strain-sharing-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: twin-strain-sharing-enrichment-testing Use when metagenomic samples from related and unrelated individuals (e.g. NICU infant stool) have inStrain compare popANI profiles and you need to test sibling enrichment and MZ-vs-DZ strain-sharing patterns. Strains cannot be resolved because samples were compared with species-level abundance tools (e.g. MetaPhlAn) rather than inStrain popANI comparisons The question is within-sample microdiversity or nucleotide diversity (e.g. Klebsiella diversity by birth mode), not between-sample strain sharing Samples lack relationship metadata (sibling/MZ/DZ status, birth day, birth weight, gestational age), making the enrichment and correlation tests underpowered http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Tests whether microbial strains (clustered from inStrain popANI profiles at 99.999% ANI) are shared between sibling premature infants more than expected by chance, and whether MZ twins share more strains than DZ twins, reproducing the Figure 3 strain-sharing analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-020-00797-0
skills.summary: Tests whether microbial strains (clustered from inStrain popANI profiles at 99.999% ANI) are shared between sibling premature infants more than expected by chance, and whether MZ twins share more strains than DZ twins, reproducing the Figure 3 strain-sharing analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Strains cannot be resolved because samples were compared with species-level abundance tools (e.g. MetaPhlAn) rather than inStrain popANI comparisons The question is within-sample microdiversity or nucleotide diversity (e.g. Klebsiella diversity by birth mode), not between-sample strain sharing Samples lack relationship metadata (sibling/MZ/DZ status, birth day, birth weight, gestational age), making the enrichment and correlation tests underpowered

skills.description: Use when implementing k-mer hashing or maximal exact match (MEM) detection over FASTA reads/genomes where memory-efficient nucleotide representation and bit-space coordinate thresholds are needed, as in the pal-MEM repeat-detection step of Palidis.
skills.name: two-bit-nucleotide-sequence-encoding
skills.search_text: two-bit-nucleotide-sequence-encoding Use when implementing k-mer hashing or maximal exact match (MEM) detection over FASTA reads/genomes where memory-efficient nucleotide representation and bit-space coordinate thresholds are needed, as in the pal-MEM repeat-detection step of Palidis. Input reads lack ITR-containing insertion sequences — Palidis is 'only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs', so the encoding pipeline cannot find ITR-lacking ISs The task needs ITRs shorter than the k-mer-supported thresholds: the ISC catalogue contains ITRs of 25 or more nucleotides although ITRs can be as short as ten nucleotides Input is protein or quality-trimmed variable-length sequences where a 2-bit per nucleotide alphabet (ACGT only) is insufficient Compact two-bit encoding (2 bits per nucleotide) of reference k-mers as used by Palidis/pal-MEM, enabling hash-table MEM lookup over metagenomic reads and letting coordinate filters operate in bit space (e.g. a 20-nucleotide edge buffer = 40 bits). metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000917
skills.summary: Compact two-bit encoding (2 bits per nucleotide) of reference k-mers as used by Palidis/pal-MEM, enabling hash-table MEM lookup over metagenomic reads and letting coordinate filters operate in bit space (e.g. a 20-nucleotide edge buffer = 40 bits).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads lack ITR-containing insertion sequences — Palidis is 'only equipped with discovering ISs with ITRs', so the encoding pipeline cannot find ITR-lacking ISs The task needs ITRs shorter than the k-mer-supported thresholds: the ISC catalogue contains ITRs of 25 or more nucleotides although ITRs can be as short as ten nucleotides Input is protein or quality-trimmed variable-length sequences where a 2-bit per nucleotide alphabet (ACGT only) is insufficient

skills.description: Use when paired-end shotgun reads mapped with BWA yield junction pairs whose two sides map to different references, and the discordant pairs must be converted into 2D points for density-based clustering of HGT breakpoint candidates.
skills.name: two-dimensional-coordinate-transform-of-mapped-read-pairs
skills.search_text: two-dimensional-coordinate-transform-of-mapped-read-pairs Use when paired-end shotgun reads mapped with BWA yield junction pairs whose two sides map to different references, and the discordant pairs must be converted into 2D points for density-based clustering of HGT breakpoint candidates. Read pairs map concordantly to a single reference (no junction pairs across different references) — there are no discordant coordinates to transform Downstream analysis needs exact breakpoint positions from split reads — this transform only generates raw candidates and precedes LEMON's accurate breakpoint-detection step http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Transforms each discordant junction pair's two mapped positions (one on each of two different references) into a single point on a two-dimensional plane, so that HGT breakpoint-pair candidates can be clustered geometrically with DBSCAN in LEMON's raw breakpoint-detection stage. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3301-8
skills.summary: Transforms each discordant junction pair's two mapped positions (one on each of two different references) into a single point on a two-dimensional plane, so that HGT breakpoint-pair candidates can be clustered geometrically with DBSCAN in LEMON's raw breakpoint-detection stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Read pairs map concordantly to a single reference (no junction pairs across different references) — there are no discordant coordinates to transform Downstream analysis needs exact breakpoint positions from split reads — this transform only generates raw candidates and precedes LEMON's accurate breakpoint-detection step

skills.description: Use when you need to demonstrate that a differential abundance testing method controls false positives at nominal alpha (e.g. 0.01, 0.05, 0.1) on real 16S relative abundance data with known null group labels.
skills.name: type-i-error-simulation-analysis
skills.search_text: type-i-error-simulation-analysis Use when you need to demonstrate that a differential abundance testing method controls false positives at nominal alpha (e.g. 0.01, 0.05, 0.1) on real 16S relative abundance data with known null group labels. The goal is testing real, biologically defined group differences (e.g. gender or breastfeeding status) rather than validating false-positive control under artificial null splits The input is raw sequencing reads or an unprocessed OTU/ASV table rather than taxa relative abundance tables prepared via the package's taxa.filter/taxtab workflow Comparing methods on simulated count data with a known generative model instead of real microbiome data with randomized group labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Empirically assesses whether differential abundance tests (GAMLSS-BEZI via metamicrobiomeR and LMAS linear/mixed models) hold their nominal type I error rate on real microbiome data by repeatedly splitting the Bangladesh infant cohort into artificial case/control groups and tabulating the fraction of taxa called significant. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2744-2
skills.summary: Empirically assesses whether differential abundance tests (GAMLSS-BEZI via metamicrobiomeR and LMAS linear/mixed models) hold their nominal type I error rate on real microbiome data by repeatedly splitting the Bangladesh infant cohort into artificial case/control groups and tabulating the fraction of taxa called significant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is testing real, biologically defined group differences (e.g. gender or breastfeeding status) rather than validating false-positive control under artificial null splits The input is raw sequencing reads or an unprocessed OTU/ASV table rather than taxa relative abundance tables prepared via the package's taxa.filter/taxtab workflow Comparing methods on simulated count data with a known generative model instead of real microbiome data with randomized group labels

skills.description: Use when multiple binary grouping factors (e.g. location vs gender) are available and you need a single quantitative value per factor to rank which factor better explains microbiome community differences.
skills.name: u-curve-area-under-mixing-curve-calculation
skills.search_text: u-curve-area-under-mixing-curve-calculation Use when multiple binary grouping factors (e.g. location vs gender) are available and you need a single quantitative value per factor to rank which factor better explains microbiome community differences. You need inferential statistics or FDR-controlled p-values — the paper explicitly states AUMC/AOI are descriptive measures and the method does not control the false discovery rate The grouping factor is not binary — ProgPermute's bin_* functions operate on a binary outcome ('variable' denotes the name of binary outcome) You only need to identify individual robust features rather than compare overall association strength across factors http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computes the AUMC (area under the mixing curve) from the U-curve of significant features versus proportion of label mixing produced by ProgPermute's progressive permutation, giving a descriptive 0–1 metric for ranking grouping factors by their overall association with the microbiome. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04061-3
skills.summary: Computes the AUMC (area under the mixing curve) from the U-curve of significant features versus proportion of label mixing produced by ProgPermute's progressive permutation, giving a descriptive 0–1 metric for ranking grouping factors by their overall association with the microbiome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need inferential statistics or FDR-controlled p-values — the paper explicitly states AUMC/AOI are descriptive measures and the method does not control the false discovery rate The grouping factor is not binary — ProgPermute's bin_* functions operate on a binary outcome ('variable' denotes the name of binary outcome) You only need to identify individual robust features rather than compare overall association strength across factors

skills.description: Use when progressive permutation results (bin_permute_all output) are available and you need to visualize significant-feature counts across mixing proportions to assess overall microbiome–group association.
skills.name: u-curve-visualization
skills.search_text: u-curve-visualization Use when progressive permutation results (bin_permute_all output) are available and you need to visualize significant-feature counts across mixing proportions to assess overall microbiome–group association. When no progressive permutation results exist yet — plot_bin_psig requires the alloutputs from bin_permute_all, not raw count data When the goal is per-feature robustness ranking (fragility index, progressive coverage) rather than overall association — use bin_fragility or bin_progresscoverage instead When a formal inferential measure is required — the U-curve is descriptive and the method does not control FDR or compute adjusted p-values http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Renders the ProgPerm U-curve: the number of significant microbial features versus the proportion of label mixing under progressive permutation, where the U-shape conveys the strength of the overall association between the microbiome and the grouping factor. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04061-3
skills.summary: Renders the ProgPerm U-curve: the number of significant microbial features versus the proportion of label mixing under progressive permutation, where the U-shape conveys the strength of the overall association between the microbiome and the grouping factor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no progressive permutation results exist yet — plot_bin_psig requires the alloutputs from bin_permute_all, not raw count data When the goal is per-feature robustness ranking (fragility index, progressive coverage) rather than overall association — use bin_fragility or bin_progresscoverage instead When a formal inferential measure is required — the U-curve is descriptive and the method does not control FDR or compute adjusted p-values

skills.name: ultrafast-bootstrap-support-assessment
skills.search_text: ultrafast-bootstrap-support-assessment Use when a trimmed concatenated alignment and gene partition file (e.g., FASconCAT-G output from 957 Patchwork-recovered USCO loci) are ready and node-support statistics are needed for a maximum-likelihood tree. Input is a set of raw Patchwork hit fragments or untrimmed MAFFT alignments rather than the concatenated supermatrix and partition file — alignment, trimming, and concatenation (MAFFT, trimAl, FASconCAT-G) must precede tree inference The goal is marker retrieval quality assessment (identity/coverage benchmarking against ALiBaSeq or aTRAM 2) rather than phylogenetic inference http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Infers a maximum-likelihood phylogeny from the trimmed, concatenated Patchwork-recovered USCO supermatrix using IQ-TREE 2 with extended model selection (-m MFP) and 1,000 ultrafast bootstrap replicates (-B 1000), producing a well-supported tree whose support values can be assessed against a reference phylogeny. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Infers a maximum-likelihood phylogeny from the trimmed, concatenated Patchwork-recovered USCO supermatrix using IQ-TREE 2 with extended model selection (-m MFP) and 1,000 ultrafast bootstrap replicates (-B 1000), producing a well-supported tree whose support values can be assessed against a reference phylogeny.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a set of raw Patchwork hit fragments or untrimmed MAFFT alignments rather than the concatenated supermatrix and partition file — alignment, trimming, and concatenation (MAFFT, trimAl, FASconCAT-G) must precede tree inference The goal is marker retrieval quality assessment (identity/coverage benchmarking against ALiBaSeq or aTRAM 2) rather than phylogenetic inference

skills.description: Use when implementing a linear-time sequence clustering pipeline and needing to prune center-vs-member candidate pairs after Hamming pre-clustering but before expensive gapped alignment, to cut gapped-alignment workload while keeping ~1% false negatives.
skills.name: ungapped-local-alignment-filtering
skills.search_text: ungapped-local-alignment-filtering Use when implementing a linear-time sequence clustering pipeline and needing to prune center-vs-member candidate pairs after Hamming pre-clustering but before expensive gapped alignment, to cut gapped-alignment workload while keeping ~1% false negatives. Pairs already removed by the Hamming distance pre-clustering step (3a) because they meet the identity and coverage thresholds on the entire diagonal — the ungapped filter would be redundant Analyses that require full gapped sensitivity on every k-mer-sharing pair, since this filter is approximate and tuned for a ~1% false negative rate, not exact Datasets without an assigned center sequence and stored diagonal (i.e. no prior k-mer grouping from step 2), as the filter aligns along the precomputed diagonal only http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 A fast intermediate filter in Linclust's clustering pipeline (step 3b) that computes optimal ungapped local alignment scores between each k-mer group's center sequence and its members along the stored diagonal, discarding matches whose score-per-diagonal-length falls below empirically tuned thresholds, so that only surviving pairs enter the costly gapped alignment step. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-04964-5
skills.summary: A fast intermediate filter in Linclust's clustering pipeline (step 3b) that computes optimal ungapped local alignment scores between each k-mer group's center sequence and its members along the stored diagonal, discarding matches whose score-per-diagonal-length falls below empirically tuned thresholds, so that only surviving pairs enter the costly gapped alignment step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pairs already removed by the Hamming distance pre-clustering step (3a) because they meet the identity and coverage thresholds on the entire diagonal — the ungapped filter would be redundant Analyses that require full gapped sensitivity on every k-mer-sharing pair, since this filter is approximate and tuned for a ~1% false negative rate, not exact Datasets without an assigned center sequence and stored diagonal (i.e. no prior k-mer grouping from step 2), as the filter aligns along the precomputed diagonal only

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomic alignments (.sam from bowtie2 or SHOGUN) show taxonomic hits against Web of Life reference genomes but per-sample sequencing is too shallow for coverage-based presence calls.
skills.name: unique-coverage-aggregation-across-samples
skills.search_text: unique-coverage-aggregation-across-samples Use when shotgun metagenomic alignments (.sam from bowtie2 or SHOGUN) show taxonomic hits against Web of Life reference genomes but per-sample sequencing is too shallow for coverage-based presence calls. Input is already a feature/abundance table rather than .sam alignments — Woltka can filter feature tables directly, but the aggregated coverage must be computed from alignments Alignments were not generated against the Web of Life database — the script currently only works with the WoL database and its metadata.tsv You plan to drop genomes directly from an abundance table using calculate_coverages.py output alone — the README states this is not recommended because it decreases apparent read counts rather than redistributing reads via Woltka http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Aggregate unique genome coverage from .sam alignments across all samples in a dataset to create 'artificially deep' shotgun sequencing, so that true microbial positives (high genome cover) can be distinguished from false positives caused by reads mis-mapping to short motifs and transposable elements. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00758-22
skills.summary: Aggregate unique genome coverage from .sam alignments across all samples in a dataset to create 'artificially deep' shotgun sequencing, so that true microbial positives (high genome cover) can be distinguished from false positives caused by reads mis-mapping to short motifs and transposable elements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/abundance table rather than .sam alignments — Woltka can filter feature tables directly, but the aggregated coverage must be computed from alignments Alignments were not generated against the Web of Life database — the script currently only works with the WoL database and its metadata.tsv You plan to drop genomes directly from an abundance table using calculate_coverages.py output alone — the README states this is not recommended because it decreases apparent read counts rather than redistributing reads via Woltka

skills.description: Use when assembling strain-resolved master contigs from cluster-specific haplotigs produced by local assembly, e.g. merging per-cluster contigs into final_contigs.fasta in a de novo strain-aware metagenome assembly pipeline.
skills.name: unique-path-contig-extension
skills.search_text: unique-path-contig-extension Use when assembling strain-resolved master contigs from cluster-specific haplotigs produced by local assembly, e.g. merging per-cluster contigs into final_contigs.fasta in a de novo strain-aware metagenome assembly pipeline. Input is raw short reads rather than cluster-specific haplotigs — the clustering and local assembly stages must run first Overlaps between contigs fall below the >100 bp / >=0.99 identity thresholds, leaving ambiguous or absent edges — no unique-path extension is possible A strain-aware assembler is not needed, e.g. isolates or a single reference genome, where standard assemblers suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 The Global Assembly stage of StrainXpress, which combines cluster-specific haplotigs (stage-a output) into master contigs via a master overlap graph and iteratively extends contigs only along unique (unambiguous) paths. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac543
skills.summary: The Global Assembly stage of StrainXpress, which combines cluster-specific haplotigs (stage-a output) into master contigs via a master overlap graph and iteratively extends contigs only along unique (unambiguous) paths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw short reads rather than cluster-specific haplotigs — the clustering and local assembly stages must run first Overlaps between contigs fall below the >100 bp / >=0.99 identity thresholds, leaving ambiguous or absent edges — no unique-path extension is possible A strain-aware assembler is not needed, e.g. isolates or a single reference genome, where standard assemblers suffice

skills.search_text: unit-normalization-of-measurements Use when free-text taxonomic description sentences yield numeric measurements for characters like Cell Diameter, Cell Width, or Cell Length whose units vary in surface form and must be standardized before building a matrix. The measurements are already in a normalized numeric table or feature matrix — re-running extraction would re-introduce errors The target characters have no unit-bearing numeric states (e.g. categorical characters like Gram stain type), for which the keyword-window unit normalization does not apply Descriptions are morphology-poor prokaryotic texts without dimension keywords such as diameter, width, or length, leaving the extractor with no trigger terms http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Post-processing step in MicroPIE's linguistic-rule-based character extractor that converts extracted numeric measurement values with heterogeneous spelled-out or symbol units (e.g. 'microns') into canonical unit forms (e.g. 'um') while preserving range notation, so cell dimension states can be written consistently into the taxon-by-character matrix. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1396-8

skills.description: Use when scoring every prokaryotic species in a COG-annotated genome database with a trained phenotype model whose feature space is limited to universal marker COGs, or when building prediction inputs for incomplete genomes where a full COG profile would be inconsistent.
skills.name: universal-marker-cog-selection
skills.search_text: universal-marker-cog-selection Use when scoring every prokaryotic species in a COG-annotated genome database with a trained phenotype model whose feature space is limited to universal marker COGs, or when building prediction inputs for incomplete genomes where a full COG profile would be inconsistent. The target model was trained on the full COG presence/absence profile rather than a marker-COG subset — restricting features would discard signal the model expects. The goal is de novo identification of trait-associated functions rather than applying a pre-trained model; then the full feature space is needed for model analysis/explanation. Genomes lack COG annotation entirely, so no marker-COG vector can be constructed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Restrict the COG presence/absence trait profiles from a large genome database (e.g. eggNOG 4.0 core and periphery genomes) to the small set of ~39/40 universal marker COGs used by the PICA phenotype model, so that all species — including incomplete ones — can be scored on a comparable feature space. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-16-s14-s1
skills.summary: Restrict the COG presence/absence trait profiles from a large genome database (e.g. eggNOG 4.0 core and periphery genomes) to the small set of ~39/40 universal marker COGs used by the PICA phenotype model, so that all species — including incomplete ones — can be scored on a comparable feature space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target model was trained on the full COG presence/absence profile rather than a marker-COG subset — restricting features would discard signal the model expects. No trained model exists yet — this skill requires a previously trained model; train one first via MegaR's Model building tab The unknown-sample table format does not match the model's training data format (e.g. a BIOM file for a MetaPhlAn-derived model) The goal is benchmarking model accuracy or cross-validation rather than labeling new samples — use MegaR's Validation / confusion matrix workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Classify unknown metagenomic samples against a previously trained MegaR model by reloading the serialized RDS file (via Download Model / saveRDS) and running the prediction module, avoiding any re-training. This enables fast phenotype prediction (e.g. T1D t/f status) from taxonomic profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03933-4

skills.search_text: unknown-source-initialization-inference Use when a sink community cannot be fully explained by candidate sources — i.e., residual taxa remain after sparse Lasso-based source selection, and the fraction of an unobserved source environment must be estimated. When all sink mass is fully explained by candidate sources and no unknown/unobserved environment is suspected — the unknown column is unnecessary. When the analysis goal is ordinary FEAST-style proportion estimation over a small, fixed source set without source exploration or unknown-source estimation. When input is raw sequencing reads rather than a taxa-by-sample count table with matching Env/SourceSink/id metadata. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Initializes the unobserved (unknown) source in STENSL microbial source tracking by subtracting the scaled counts of the top contributing source, ranked by L1 regularization, so that unexplained sink taxa can be attributed to an unsequenced environment. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00995-21

skills.description: Use when a STENSL L1-regularized sparse selection output (sink vector x, source matrix Y, sparse alphahat) is available and an explicit profile for the unknown/unobserved source must be derived, not just its mixing proportion.
skills.name: unknown-source-profile-residual-reconstruction
skills.search_text: unknown-source-profile-residual-reconstruction Use when a STENSL L1-regularized sparse selection output (sink vector x, source matrix Y, sparse alphahat) is available and an explicit profile for the unknown/unobserved source must be derived, not just its mixing proportion. You only need the unknown source's mixing proportion, which STENSL's EM/FEAST-style output P already reports as an 'unknown' column — not its taxon-level profile No sparse source selection has been run yet (x, Y, alphahat are unavailable), since the residual heuristic is defined on the L1 solution Candidate source set contains no plausible contributing source, making argmax(alphahat) uninformative for subtraction http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reconstructs the unknown (unobserved) source profile in STENSL by taking the clamped residual of the sink counts minus the top contributing source's counts scaled by its L1-regularized mixing proportion: Yhat_{M+1} = max(0, x − alphahat * Y_{argmax alphahat}). This leverages STENSL's sparse selection step so taxa unexplained by contributing sources become the estimated unknown-source profile. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00995-21
skills.summary: Reconstructs the unknown (unobserved) source profile in STENSL by taking the clamped residual of the sink counts minus the top contributing source's counts scaled by its L1-regularized mixing proportion: Yhat_{M+1} = max(0, x − alphahat * Y_{argmax alphahat}). This leverages STENSL's sparse selection step so taxa unexplained by contributing sources become the estimated unknown-source profile.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the unknown source's mixing proportion, which STENSL's EM/FEAST-style output P already reports as an 'unknown' column — not its taxon-level profile No sparse source selection has been run yet (x, Y, alphahat are unavailable), since the residual heuristic is defined on the L1 solution Candidate source set contains no plausible contributing source, making argmax(alphahat) uninformative for subtraction

skills.description: Use when you have predicted cluster assignments for DNA sequences and a ground-truth TSV with sequence_id and cluster_id columns, and need to quantify clustering quality without training on labels.
skills.name: unsupervised-clustering-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: unsupervised-clustering-accuracy-evaluation Use when you have predicted cluster assignments for DNA sequences and a ground-truth TSV with sequence_id and cluster_id columns, and need to quantify clustering quality without training on labels. No ground-truth labels exist for the dataset — the GT_file requires cluster_id assignments; without them ACC cannot be computed. You need labels during training — iDeLUCS is unsupervised; the GT labels 'won't be used during training, just for posthoc analysis', so this skill must never influence clustering itself. Input is not DNA sequence clustering output (e.g., already a feature table or metadata matrix) — the skill evaluates cluster identifier assignments against biological truth labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates DNA-sequence clustering results (e.g., from iDeLUCS, DeLUCS, or k-means++) by computing unsupervised clustering accuracy (ACC) against ground-truth cluster_id labels via posthoc optimal label alignment, never using labels during training. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad508
skills.summary: Evaluates DNA-sequence clustering results (e.g., from iDeLUCS, DeLUCS, or k-means++) by computing unsupervised clustering accuracy (ACC) against ground-truth cluster_id labels via posthoc optimal label alignment, never using labels during training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth labels exist for the dataset — the GT_file requires cluster_id assignments; without them ACC cannot be computed. You need labels during training — iDeLUCS is unsupervised; the GT labels 'won't be used during training, just for posthoc analysis', so this skill must never influence clustering itself. Input is not DNA sequence clustering output (e.g., already a feature table or metadata matrix) — the skill evaluates cluster identifier assignments against biological truth labels.

skills.description: Use when clustering unlabeled DNA sequences from a single FASTA file into known or estimated clusters without alignment or taxonomic identifiers, e.g. mitochondrial genomes, bacterial, or viral datasets with 2-199 expected clusters.
skills.name: unsupervised-dna-sequence-clustering
skills.search_text: unsupervised-dna-sequence-clustering Use when clustering unlabeled DNA sequences from a single FASTA file into known or estimated clusters without alignment or taxonomic identifiers, e.g. mitochondrial genomes, bacterial, or viral datasets with 2-199 expected clusters. Datasets with average sequence length below 500 bp or more than 200 expected clusters — these regimes were explicitly excluded from the evaluation and flagged as future work Datasets where the number of true clusters is unknown and fine-grained automatic cluster discovery is required, unless willing to use n_clusters=0 (iDeLUCS+HDBSCAN mode) Tasks requiring aligned phylogenetic placement or taxonomic classification with reference databases rather than unsupervised clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Cluster DNA sequences in an alignment-free, unsupervised manner using iDeLUCS, a PyTorch-based deep learning tool that detects genomic signatures (k-mer frequencies) and clusters sequences without alignment or taxonomic identifiers, benchmarked against k-means++, GMM, DeLUCS, and MeShClust v3.0. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad508
skills.summary: Cluster DNA sequences in an alignment-free, unsupervised manner using iDeLUCS, a PyTorch-based deep learning tool that detects genomic signatures (k-mer frequencies) and clusters sequences without alignment or taxonomic identifiers, benchmarked against k-means++, GMM, DeLUCS, and MeShClust v3.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with average sequence length below 500 bp or more than 200 expected clusters — these regimes were explicitly excluded from the evaluation and flagged as future work Datasets where the number of true clusters is unknown and fine-grained automatic cluster discovery is required, unless willing to use n_clusters=0 (iDeLUCS+HDBSCAN mode) Tasks requiring aligned phylogenetic placement or taxonomic classification with reference databases rather than unsupervised clustering

skills.description: Use when predicting genes in fragmented metagenomic reads where no reference genomes for training are available, and sequences should first be grouped by likely organism of origin so models can be retrained unsupervised per cluster.
skills.name: unsupervised-gene-model-retraining-per-cluster
skills.search_text: unsupervised-gene-model-retraining-per-cluster Use when predicting genes in fragmented metagenomic reads where no reference genomes for training are available, and sequences should first be grouped by likely organism of origin so models can be retrained unsupervised per cluster. skills.summary: Builds a UPGMA hierarchical clustering tree from a CAFE-computed alignment-free d2S distance matrix (exported in PHYLIP format) so that sequence relationships among genomes — e.g. the 27 E. coli/Shigella genomes and their ECOR groups — can be assessed via clade monophyly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a phylogeny or an alignment — use alignment-based tree building rather than clustering an alignment-free distance matrix Only k-mer count vectors are available and no pairwise distance matrix has been computed — CAFE must first produce the PHYLIP distances The downstream visualization expected by the user is CAFE's built-in dendrogram, which uses neighbour-joining rather than UPGMA

skills.name: upgma-phylogeny-construction
skills.search_text: upgma-phylogeny-construction Use when you have a pairwise APSS (average pairwise synteny score) matrix from SynTracker and need a hierarchical strain phylogeny, or when validating a synteny-based tree against a reference tree (e.g., a Mash-based phylogroup tree). skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is SNP-level strain differentiation only — SynTracker's synteny-based approach is designed to capture structural changes and is deliberately insensitive to SNPs When comparing strains of different species — the pipeline is designated for conspecific (same-species) strains When a reference genome cannot yield enough homologous regions for a pair (fewer than n regions), as those pairs are excluded from downstream analysis

skills.description: Use when several co-occurrence networks have been inferred from the same counts table by different methods (e.g., SparCC, propr, SpiecEasi, FlashWeave, COZINE, HARMONIES, SPRING, mLDM) and you need to quantify which nodes/edges they share.
skills.name: upset-set-intersection-analysis
skills.search_text: upset-set-intersection-analysis Use when several co-occurrence networks have been inferred from the same counts table by different methods (e.g., SparCC, propr, SpiecEasi, FlashWeave, COZINE, HARMONIES, SPRING, mLDM) and you need to quantify which nodes/edges they share. You have only one inferred network — intersection analysis needs multiple networks from the same underlying abundance table Networks are built from different datasets or different taxonomy groupings; intersection counts would not be comparable The goal is abundance/OTU comparison rather than comparing network topology (edge and node overlap) http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies shared and unique nodes and edges across networks inferred by multiple network inference (NI) methods using UpSet-style set intersection analysis, as done in MiCoNE to reveal substantial rewiring despite taxonomic overlap. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: Quantifies shared and unique nodes and edges across networks inferred by multiple network inference (NI) methods using UpSet-style set intersection analysis, as done in MiCoNE to reveal substantial rewiring despite taxonomic overlap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only one inferred network — intersection analysis needs multiple networks from the same underlying abundance table Networks are built from different datasets or different taxonomy groupings; intersection counts would not be comparable The goal is abundance/OTU comparison rather than comparing network topology (edge and node overlap)
