skills.search_text: usco-presence-absence-matrix-construction Use when a set of related MAGs/species-level genome bins (e.g. SGB009, SGB034, SGB080) must be screened for shared absence of universal single-copy orthologs to infer lineage-specific metabolic gene loss. Input genomes have not passed quality screening (article required ≥50% completeness and <5% contamination) — missing USCOs in low-quality MAGs may reflect incompleteness, not gene loss The goal is general gene-family clustering or pan-genome construction across all genes, not assessment of universal single-copy ortholog presence/absence Assessing genome quality itself (BUSCO-based completeness/contamination scoring) rather than mining a shared-loss pattern across a lineage http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Constructs a genome-by-gene presence/absence matrix of the 124 universal single-copy orthologs (USCOs) from BUSCO bacteria_odb10 full_table.tsv outputs, to detect gene losses shared across a lineage (e.g. Saccharofermentanales in the VMGC) and flag missing genes in de novo purine biosynthesis. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Constructs a genome-by-gene presence/absence matrix of the 124 universal single-copy orthologs (USCOs) from BUSCO bacteria_odb10 full_table.tsv outputs, to detect gene losses shared across a lineage (e.g. Saccharofermentanales in the VMGC) and flag missing genes in de novo purine biosynthesis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input genomes have not passed quality screening (article required ≥50% completeness and <5% contamination) — missing USCOs in low-quality MAGs may reflect incompleteness, not gene loss The goal is general gene-family clustering or pan-genome construction across all genes, not assessment of universal single-copy ortholog presence/absence Assessing genome quality itself (BUSCO-based completeness/contamination scoring) rather than mining a shared-loss pattern across a lineage

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how accurately a fragmented or assembled genome-skimming query recovers a known set of universal single-copy ortholog (USCO) references, producing reproducible accuracy statistics.
skills.name: usco-retrieval-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: usco-retrieval-benchmark-evaluation Use when you need to quantify how accurately a fragmented or assembled genome-skimming query recovers a known set of universal single-copy ortholog (USCO) references, producing reproducible accuracy statistics. The query data are already an annotated feature table or gene set rather than unassembled contigs or WGS reads — Patchwork's DIAMOND BLASTX and stitching steps are not needed You need whole-genome structural comparison rather than retrieval of near-universal single-copy ortholog markers Reference sequences are not near-USCOs; the article recommends limiting reference sequences to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark the accuracy and completeness of Patchwork marker retrieval by searching a high-quality query assembly against same-species USCO reference sequences (e.g. 815 D. gyrociliatus USCOs from GCA_904063045.1) and computing percent identical aligned positions, query coverage, and combined (pidentical, cov) measures. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/gbe/evad227
skills.summary: Benchmark the accuracy and completeness of Patchwork marker retrieval by searching a high-quality query assembly against same-species USCO reference sequences (e.g. 815 D. gyrociliatus USCOs from GCA_904063045.1) and computing percent identical aligned positions, query coverage, and combined (pidentical, cov) measures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query data are already an annotated feature table or gene set rather than unassembled contigs or WGS reads — Patchwork's DIAMOND BLASTX and stitching steps are not needed You need whole-genome structural comparison rather than retrieval of near-universal single-copy ortholog markers Reference sequences are not near-USCOs; the article recommends limiting reference sequences to near-USCOs to avoid chimeric sequences

skills.description: Use when a curated set of near-full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences (or similar amplicon/marker sequences) contains redundant variants and downstream per-sequence analyses (e.g. 515F/806R primer binding) should be counted once per ~species-level cluster rather than once per assembled copy.
skills.name: usearch-sequence-clustering-de-redundancy
skills.search_text: usearch-sequence-clustering-de-redundancy Use when a curated set of near-full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences (or similar amplicon/marker sequences) contains redundant variants and downstream per-sequence analyses (e.g. 515F/806R primer binding) should be counted once per ~species-level cluster rather than once per assembled copy. The input is already a non-redundant representative set or a pre-clustered OTU/ASV table — re-clustering would discard legitimate within-cluster diversity needed for primer-binding counts. Sequences contain large ≥10 bp intron insertions that have not yet been removed, since insertions (present in 31% of CPR 16S rRNA genes here, up to 2,004 bp) would corrupt identity-based clustering. The goal is phyla-level counting, for which the paper used a 75% sequence identity clustering, not the 97% de-redundancy step. http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 De-redundantize curated sequence sets (here, 1,543 assembled and error-corrected bacterial 16S rRNA genes ≥800 bp) by clustering at 97% sequence identity with USEARCH cluster_smallmem, so that downstream primer-binding and diversity analyses operate on non-redundant cluster representatives. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/nature14486
skills.summary: De-redundantize curated sequence sets (here, 1,543 assembled and error-corrected bacterial 16S rRNA genes ≥800 bp) by clustering at 97% sequence identity with USEARCH cluster_smallmem, so that downstream primer-binding and diversity analyses operate on non-redundant cluster representatives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a non-redundant representative set or a pre-clustered OTU/ASV table — re-clustering would discard legitimate within-cluster diversity needed for primer-binding counts. Sequences contain large ≥10 bp intron insertions that have not yet been removed, since insertions (present in 31% of CPR 16S rRNA genes here, up to 2,004 bp) would corrupt identity-based clustering. The goal is phyla-level counting, for which the paper used a 75% sequence identity clustering, not the 97% de-redundancy step.

skills.description: Use when merging multiple gene reference collections (e.g. ResFinder, CARD, MegaRes, AMRFinderPlus, ARGANNOT) into one catalog and you need unique sequences plus homology-reduced centroids.
skills.name: usearch-sequence-deduplication-and-clustering
skills.search_text: usearch-sequence-deduplication-and-clustering Use when merging multiple gene reference collections (e.g. ResFinder, CARD, MegaRes, AMRFinderPlus, ARGANNOT) into one catalog and you need unique sequences plus homology-reduced centroids. You need read-level profiling of metagenomic samples against existing references — use ARGprofiler/KMA mapping instead of rebuilding the catalog. Your sequences require exact full-length identity handling or long-read assembly context — ARGprofiler only supports short-read data and PanRes is a static combined collection. You need strain-level resolution below 90% identity, since 90/90 clustering collapses sequences into centroids. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Deduplicate and cluster combined gene collections with Usearch 11.0.667 (fastx_uniques for deduplication, cluster_fast at 90% identity / 90% coverage for centroid extraction) as used to build the PanRes ARG database from ~30,400 genes down to 14,078 unique sequences and 5,280 centroids. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae086
skills.summary: Deduplicate and cluster combined gene collections with Usearch 11.0.667 (fastx_uniques for deduplication, cluster_fast at 90% identity / 90% coverage for centroid extraction) as used to build the PanRes ARG database from ~30,400 genes down to 14,078 unique sequences and 5,280 centroids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need read-level profiling of metagenomic samples against existing references — use ARGprofiler/KMA mapping instead of rebuilding the catalog. Your sequences require exact full-length identity handling or long-read assembly context — ARGprofiler only supports short-read data and PanRes is a static combined collection. You need strain-level resolution below 90% identity, since 90/90 clustering collapses sequences into centroids.

skills.description: Use when raw natural-language taxonomic or scientific prose contains XML entities, non-UTF-8 symbols, or punctuation that would break sentence splitting or downstream NLP parsing before character extraction.
skills.name: utf8-text-cleaning
skills.search_text: utf8-text-cleaning Use when raw natural-language taxonomic or scientific prose contains XML entities, non-UTF-8 symbols, or punctuation that would break sentence splitting or downstream NLP parsing before character extraction. Input is already clean, normalized plain text with no XML entities or non-UTF-8 characters Input is structured or semi-structured markup where punctuation and symbols carry extraction meaning (stripping non-alphanumerics would destroy it) The task targets morphological characters in semi-structured descriptions better suited to a tool like CharaParser rather than prokaryotic physiological/ecological prose http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 A preprocessing step from the MicroPIE pipeline that segments taxonomic description paragraphs into sentences and normalizes them by decoding XML entities and stripping non-UTF-8 and non-alphanumeric characters, so downstream SVM character prediction and extraction receive clean text with fewer syntactic parsing errors. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-016-1396-8
skills.summary: A preprocessing step from the MicroPIE pipeline that segments taxonomic description paragraphs into sentences and normalizes them by decoding XML entities and stripping non-UTF-8 and non-alphanumeric characters, so downstream SVM character prediction and extraction receive clean text with fewer syntactic parsing errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already clean, normalized plain text with no XML entities or non-UTF-8 characters Input is structured or semi-structured markup where punctuation and symbols carry extraction meaning (stripping non-alphanumerics would destroy it) The task targets morphological characters in semi-structured descriptions better suited to a tool like CharaParser rather than prokaryotic physiological/ecological prose

skills.description: Use when you have a .snp file of KisSNP2-format variant calls produced by ebwt2InDel (or ebwt2snp) and need to retain only SNP/INDEL events supported by a minimum number of reads before VCF conversion.
skills.name: variant-call-coverage-filtering
skills.search_text: variant-call-coverage-filtering Use when you have a .snp file of KisSNP2-format variant calls produced by ebwt2InDel (or ebwt2snp) and need to retain only SNP/INDEL events supported by a minimum number of reads before VCF conversion. The input is not a .snp call file from ebwt2InDel/ebwt2snp (e.g. it is already a VCF, BAM, or SAM from a mapping-based caller) — filter_snp only understands the KisSNP2 .snp format The read dataset has very low coverage (< ~10-25x), where a fixed m=5 threshold would remove true variants rather than only noise The goal is depth filtering of reference-mapped alignments rather than coverage filtering of reference-free variant calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Post-processing filter that discards low-coverage SNP/INDEL calls from ebwt2InDel's .snp output using the tool filter_snp, keeping only events supported by at least m reads (m=5 in the paper, recommended for datasets at >= 25x coverage). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Post-processing filter that discards low-coverage SNP/INDEL calls from ebwt2InDel's .snp output using the tool filter_snp, keeping only events supported by at least m reads (m=5 in the paper, recommended for datasets at >= 25x coverage).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a .snp call file from ebwt2InDel/ebwt2snp (e.g. it is already a VCF, BAM, or SAM from a mapping-based caller) — filter_snp only understands the KisSNP2 .snp format The read dataset has very low coverage (< ~10-25x), where a fixed m=5 threshold would remove true variants rather than only noise The goal is depth filtering of reference-mapped alignments rather than coverage filtering of reference-free variant calls

skills.description: Use when simulated longitudinal metagenomic reads must carry ground-truth variants: STEMSIM writes mutated reads plus a VCF detailing the exact mutations it introduced.
skills.name: variant-call-file-generation
skills.search_text: variant-call-file-generation Use when simulated longitudinal metagenomic reads must carry ground-truth variants: STEMSIM writes mutated reads plus a VCF detailing the exact mutations it introduced. You need to call variants from real, experimentally derived metagenomic reads for discovery rather than simulation ground truth — STEMSIM only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes Input data are already CAMISIM output with an existing simulated community; the 'camisim' mode with --input_from_camisim and --genome_to_id.tsv is the appropriate path instead The goal is de novo variant discovery without a supplied reference genome; the reads mode requires --reference_genome and --genome_id to place reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Generation of a VCF of true mutations produced when simulating within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations on longitudinal metagenomic reads with STEMSIM, optionally annotated with SnpEff. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad302
skills.summary: Generation of a VCF of true mutations produced when simulating within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations on longitudinal metagenomic reads with STEMSIM, optionally annotated with SnpEff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to call variants from real, experimentally derived metagenomic reads for discovery rather than simulation ground truth — STEMSIM only works well on species with high depth and well-characterized genomes Input data are already CAMISIM output with an existing simulated community; the 'camisim' mode with --input_from_camisim and --genome_to_id.tsv is the appropriate path instead The goal is de novo variant discovery without a supplied reference genome; the reads mode requires --reference_genome and --genome_id to place reads

skills.description: Use when a variant caller emits fasta/KisSNP2-format variant contexts that must be converted to VCF and benchmarked for SNP/INDEL sensitivity and precision against a known truth set (e.g., NCBI GIAB NA12878_HG001).
skills.name: variant-call-validation-against-ground-truth-vcf
skills.search_text: variant-call-validation-against-ground-truth-vcf Use when a variant caller emits fasta/KisSNP2-format variant contexts that must be converted to VCF and benchmarked for SNP/INDEL sensitivity and precision against a known truth set (e.g., NCBI GIAB NA12878_HG001). Calls are already in normalized VCF coordinates against the same reference build as the truth set and need no fasta-to-VCF conversion or strand-duplicate removal No reliable ground-truth VCF exists for the sample (the article notes real-data evaluation relies on an approximated ground truth, lowering precision estimates) http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark reference-free variant calls (SNPs and INDELs) against a gold-standard truth VCF using hap.py, converting caller outputs to VCF first via the snp2vcf pipeline (seqtk -> bwa-mem -> sam2vcf) aligned against hg38, to obtain per-variant-type sensitivity/precision for tools like EBWT2INDEL and DISCOSNP++. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Benchmark reference-free variant calls (SNPs and INDELs) against a gold-standard truth VCF using hap.py, converting caller outputs to VCF first via the snp2vcf pipeline (seqtk -> bwa-mem -> sam2vcf) aligned against hg38, to obtain per-variant-type sensitivity/precision for tools like EBWT2INDEL and DISCOSNP++.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calls are already in normalized VCF coordinates against the same reference build as the truth set and need no fasta-to-VCF conversion or strand-duplicate removal No reliable ground-truth VCF exists for the sample (the article notes real-data evaluation relies on an approximated ground truth, lowering precision estimates)

skills.description: Use when two or more variant-calling outputs (VCF) must be compared against a trusted truth VCF to quantify SNP/INDEL sensitivity and precision, e.g. benchmarking a new caller against a baseline.
skills.name: variant-call-validation-with-happy
skills.search_text: variant-call-validation-with-happy Use when two or more variant-calling outputs (VCF) must be compared against a trusted truth VCF to quantify SNP/INDEL sensitivity and precision, e.g. benchmarking a new caller against a baseline. Caller output is still in raw fragment/context format (e.g. KisSNP2 fasta from ebwt2InDel) and has not yet been converted to VCF via seqtk/bwa-mem/sam2vcf The evaluation goal is positional/allele-identity matching of somatic callsets without haplotype resolution — use som.py-style comparison instead Real-data ground truth is only approximate: the paper notes lower precision for both tools due to an approximated ground truth, so precision estimates on such data are not comparable to synthetic-data results Benchmark variant call sets (from ebwt2InDel/DISCOSNP++ style reference-free callers or any caller emitting VCF) against a ground-truth VCF using Illumina's hap.py, yielding SNP and INDEL sensitivity/precision figures. In the paper this step validated both call sets after conversion to VCF via the snp2vcf pipeline (seqtk -> bwa-mem -> sam2vcf). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-020-03586-3
skills.summary: Benchmark variant call sets (from ebwt2InDel/DISCOSNP++ style reference-free callers or any caller emitting VCF) against a ground-truth VCF using Illumina's hap.py, yielding SNP and INDEL sensitivity/precision figures. In the paper this step validated both call sets after conversion to VCF via the snp2vcf pipeline (seqtk -> bwa-mem -> sam2vcf).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Caller output is still in raw fragment/context format (e.g. KisSNP2 fasta from ebwt2InDel) and has not yet been converted to VCF via seqtk/bwa-mem/sam2vcf The evaluation goal is positional/allele-identity matching of somatic callsets without haplotype resolution — use som.py-style comparison instead Real-data ground truth is only approximate: the paper notes lower precision for both tools due to an approximated ground truth, so precision estimates on such data are not comparable to synthetic-data results

skills.description: Use when you need to empirically compare shared-variant callers on shotgun metagenomic data with known ground truth, especially to quantify false positive reduction and F1 trends across mean sequencing depths.
skills.name: variant-caller-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: variant-caller-benchmark-comparison Use when you need to empirically compare shared-variant callers on shotgun metagenomic data with known ground truth, especially to quantify false positive reduction and F1 trends across mean sequencing depths. Input is real (non-simulated) metagenomic data without a ground-truth variant set — F1/TPR/FP cannot be computed and the benchmark design does not apply. The goal is single-sample variant calling rather than detecting shared informative variants across a population of shotgun metagenomic samples. Data are single-cell mitochondrial (mtDNA) datasets, where MQuad rather than MetaQuad is the appropriate tool. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A benchmarking skill for comparing MetaQuad against state-of-the-art variant callers (BCFtools, GATK HaplotypeCaller, VarScan2, MetaSNV, inStrain) on simulated shotgun metagenomic datasets across varying mean depths, scoring F1, true positive rate, and false positive counts against a simulated ground-truth variant set. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for comparing MetaQuad against state-of-the-art variant callers (BCFtools, GATK HaplotypeCaller, VarScan2, MetaSNV, inStrain) on simulated shotgun metagenomic datasets across varying mean depths, scoring F1, true positive rate, and false positive counts against a simulated ground-truth variant set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) metagenomic data without a ground-truth variant set — F1/TPR/FP cannot be computed and the benchmark design does not apply. The goal is single-sample variant calling rather than detecting shared informative variants across a population of shotgun metagenomic samples. Data are single-cell mitochondrial (mtDNA) datasets, where MQuad rather than MetaQuad is the appropriate tool.

skills.description: Decision support for choosing a variant caller for low-frequency (<0.01) SARS-CoV-2 mutation detection in wastewater FASTQ data when lineages must be inferred per variant caller before committing to one VCF source.
skills.name: variant-caller-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: variant-caller-benchmark-comparison Decision support for choosing a variant caller for low-frequency (<0.01) SARS-CoV-2 mutation detection in wastewater FASTQ data when lineages must be inferred per variant caller before committing to one VCF source. The input is clinical isolate data with high-frequency variants only — freebayes at 0.01 mutation frequency is motivated by detecting variants below 1% frequency in mixed wastewater samples. A single caller's output has already been fixed for the project and no benchmarking decision is needed — this skill would duplicate existing variant calling. The sample fails preprocessing quality checks (e.g., insufficient paired-end read depth after trimming to a 200 nt minimum with sliding-window quality 15), making per-caller Nt counts incomparable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark three SARS-CoV-2 variant callers (freebayes at low mutation frequency 0.01, GATK Mutect2 in cancer-only mode, and mpileup reporting every position) on the same wastewater alignment to compare lineage-characteristic mutation counts (Nt) and select the most productive caller for downstream lineagespot analysis. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: Benchmark three SARS-CoV-2 variant callers (freebayes at low mutation frequency 0.01, GATK Mutect2 in cancer-only mode, and mpileup reporting every position) on the same wastewater alignment to compare lineage-characteristic mutation counts (Nt) and select the most productive caller for downstream lineagespot analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is clinical isolate data with high-frequency variants only — freebayes at 0.01 mutation frequency is motivated by detecting variants below 1% frequency in mixed wastewater samples. A single caller's output has already been fixed for the project and no benchmarking decision is needed — this skill would duplicate existing variant calling. The sample fails preprocessing quality checks (e.g., insufficient paired-end read depth after trimming to a 200 nt minimum with sliding-window quality 15), making per-caller Nt counts incomparable.

skills.description: Use when calling variants from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater or other mixed viral populations where mutations occur at very low allele frequencies (<0.01) and a caller comparison or freebayes-based VCF is needed.

skills.search_text: variant-calling-low-frequency-variants Use when calling variants from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater or other mixed viral populations where mutations occur at very low allele frequencies (<0.01) and a caller comparison or freebayes-based VCF is needed. skills.description: Use when the input is one or more VCF files from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater NGS data (e.g., freebayes calls against NC_045512) and the goal is to list detected mutations and identify which lineages (e.g., B.1.177, B.1.1.7, B.1.351) are present.
skills.name: vcf-lineage-mutation-annotation
skills.search_text: vcf-lineage-mutation-annotation Use when the input is one or more VCF files from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater NGS data (e.g., freebayes calls against NC_045512) and the goal is to list detected mutations and identify which lineages (e.g., B.1.177, B.1.1.7, B.1.351) are present. Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than called variants — variant calling (mapping with Minimap2, freebayes at 0.01 mutation frequency) must happen first The organism/reference is not SARS-CoV-2 (NC_045512): the Pangolin-rule and outbreak.info mutation matching is SARS-CoV-2 specific The goal is absolute lineage abundance quantification rather than detection/monitoring of lineages — the method identifies lineages present but the article notes assignment assumptions can mis-assign lineages http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotate and merge SARS-CoV-2 VCF files from wastewater sequencing into a combined table of nucleotide mutations, amino acid substitutions, allele frequencies and overlapping genes, then infer lineage-characteristic mutations per lineage using Pangolin rules / outbreak.info definitions via the lineagespot R framework. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: Annotate and merge SARS-CoV-2 VCF files from wastewater sequencing into a combined table of nucleotide mutations, amino acid substitutions, allele frequencies and overlapping genes, then infer lineage-characteristic mutations per lineage using Pangolin rules / outbreak.info definitions via the lineagespot R framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than called variants — variant calling (mapping with Minimap2, freebayes at 0.01 mutation frequency) must happen first The organism/reference is not SARS-CoV-2 (NC_045512): the Pangolin-rule and outbreak.info mutation matching is SARS-CoV-2 specific The goal is absolute lineage abundance quantification rather than detection/monitoring of lineages — the method identifies lineages present but the article notes assignment assumptions can mis-assign lineages

skills.description: Use when downstream population-genomic tools require PLINK binary (BED) input but the available genotype data are VCF files split by chromosome and indexed with tabix, e.g. before running ADMIXTURE in scalepopgen.
skills.name: vcf-to-plink-bed-conversion
skills.search_text: vcf-to-plink-bed-conversion Use when downstream population-genomic tools require PLINK binary (BED) input but the available genotype data are VCF files split by chromosome and indexed with tabix, e.g. before running ADMIXTURE in scalepopgen. Input is already a PLINK binary (BED/BIM/FAM) dataset — specify the files in a plink_input.csv sheet with header 'prefix,bed,bim,fam' instead of converting from VCF. Data are multi-allelic or non-SNP variants — scalepopgen is designed for biallelic SNP data stored in VCF or PLINK binary files. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2885 Convert chromosome-split, tabix-indexed biallelic SNP VCF files into PLINK binary (BED/BIM/FAM) format within the scalepopgen Nextflow pipeline, producing the binary genotype input required by downstream tools such as ADMIXTURE and PCA. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Convert chromosome-split, tabix-indexed biallelic SNP VCF files into PLINK binary (BED/BIM/FAM) format within the scalepopgen Nextflow pipeline, producing the binary genotype input required by downstream tools such as ADMIXTURE and PCA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a PLINK binary (BED/BIM/FAM) dataset — specify the files in a plink_input.csv sheet with header 'prefix,bed,bim,fam' instead of converting from VCF. Data are multi-allelic or non-SNP variants — scalepopgen is designed for biallelic SNP data stored in VCF or PLINK binary files.

skills.description: Use when inferring population trees and migration events from filtered biallelic SNP genotype data (VCF or PLINK binary) that must be transformed into TreeMix-compatible input, especially when bootstrapping and optimal migration-edge selection are needed.
skills.name: vcf-to-treemix-input-conversion
skills.search_text: vcf-to-treemix-input-conversion Use when inferring population trees and migration events from filtered biallelic SNP genotype data (VCF or PLINK binary) that must be transformed into TreeMix-compatible input, especially when bootstrapping and optimal migration-edge selection are needed. The analysis goal is admixture proportions or PCA rather than a population tree with migration edges (use the explore-genetic-structure sub-workflow with ADMIXTURE/PCA instead) The genotype data are multi-allelic or not filtered (sample/site filtering, and recommended LD pruning, should precede TreeMix input conversion) Only pairwise population differentiation statistics are needed and no phylogenetic tree is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 http://edamontology.org/topic_3056 Converts filtered biallelic SNP VCF genotype data into TreeMix-compatible input and runs the TreeMix phylogeny sub-workflow of scalepopgen, including bootstrapping, migration-edge estimation, and consensus tree construction. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/molbev/msae057
skills.summary: Converts filtered biallelic SNP VCF genotype data into TreeMix-compatible input and runs the TreeMix phylogeny sub-workflow of scalepopgen, including bootstrapping, migration-edge estimation, and consensus tree construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is admixture proportions or PCA rather than a population tree with migration edges (use the explore-genetic-structure sub-workflow with ADMIXTURE/PCA instead) The genotype data are multi-allelic or not filtered (sample/site filtering, and recommended LD pruning, should precede TreeMix input conversion) Only pairwise population differentiation statistics are needed and no phylogenetic tree is required

skills.description: Use when input consists of single or multiple SARS-CoV-2 VCF files (e.g., from freebayes variant calling of wastewater or ARTIC NGS samples) and the goal is to detect lineage-characteristic mutations and quantify per-lineage abundance.
skills.name: vcf-variant-table-processing
skills.search_text: vcf-variant-table-processing Use when input consists of single or multiple SARS-CoV-2 VCF files (e.g., from freebayes variant calling of wastewater or ARTIC NGS samples) and the goal is to detect lineage-characteristic mutations and quantify per-lineage abundance. Input is raw FASTQ sequencing data — variant calling (e.g., freebayes after Minimap2 mapping and primer trimming) must happen first Samples are from non-SARS-CoV-2 organisms or VCFs not aligned to the NC_045512 Wuhan reference genome A consensus-genome Pangolin-style single-lineage assignment is needed for a pure clinical isolate rather than mixed lineage detection in wastewater http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 An R-based skill that ingests one or more SARS-CoV-2 VCF files and produces a merged variant table (nucleotide mutations, amino acid substitutions, allele frequencies) plus lineage hits and a per-lineage abundance report using the lineagespot package. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: An R-based skill that ingests one or more SARS-CoV-2 VCF files and produces a merged variant table (nucleotide mutations, amino acid substitutions, allele frequencies) plus lineage hits and a per-lineage abundance report using the lineagespot package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ sequencing data — variant calling (e.g., freebayes after Minimap2 mapping and primer trimming) must happen first Samples are from non-SARS-CoV-2 organisms or VCFs not aligned to the NC_045512 Wuhan reference genome A consensus-genome Pangolin-style single-lineage assignment is needed for a pure clinical isolate rather than mixed lineage detection in wastewater

skills.description: Use when classified viral contigs (vOTUs) from a metagenomic/virome assembly need phage taxonomy assignments (phylum–genus), and a curated protein-sharing clustering against INPHARED reference genomes is required instead of a generic vConTACT2 reference.
skills.name: vcontact2-custom-reference-database-configuration
skills.search_text: vcontact2-custom-reference-database-configuration Use when classified viral contigs (vOTUs) from a metagenomic/virome assembly need phage taxonomy assignments (phylum–genus), and a curated protein-sharing clustering against INPHARED reference genomes is required instead of a generic vConTACT2 reference. vConTACT2's all-versus-all protein comparison against large reference databases is time-consuming and the network is rebuilt every time new data are added — impractical for rapid, incremental updates When only read-level taxonomic profiling is needed (e.g. Kraken2/MiniKraken2_V1 read classification) rather than genome-level vOTU clustering When a single viral genome already matches a reference directly and no network-based classification is necessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 Run vConTACT2 in custom-reference modality using the INPHARED Jan2022 split (vConTACT2_proteins.faa, vConTACT2_gene_to_genome.csv, data_excluding_refseq.tsv) to cluster predicted vOTU proteins together with curated bacteriophage reference genomes by shared protein content, then transfer taxonomy from the clustered references (e.g. via graphanalyzer). metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Run vConTACT2 in custom-reference modality using the INPHARED Jan2022 split (vConTACT2_proteins.faa, vConTACT2_gene_to_genome.csv, data_excluding_refseq.tsv) to cluster predicted vOTU proteins together with curated bacteriophage reference genomes by shared protein content, then transfer taxonomy from the clustered references (e.g. via graphanalyzer).
skills.when_to_use_negative: vConTACT2's all-versus-all protein comparison against large reference databases is time-consuming and the network is rebuilt every time new data are added — impractical for rapid, incremental updates When only read-level taxonomic profiling is needed (e.g. Kraken2/MiniKraken2_V1 read classification) rather than genome-level vOTU clustering When a single viral genome already matches a reference directly and no network-based classification is necessary

skills.description: Use when vOTU contigs have been clustered against INPHARED references with vConTACT2 (producing genome_by_genome_overview.csv and c1.ntw) and you need automated per-vOTU taxonomy plus supporting network views.
skills.name: vcontact2-network-taxonomy-inference
skills.search_text: vcontact2-network-taxonomy-inference Use when vOTU contigs have been clustered against INPHARED references with vConTACT2 (producing genome_by_genome_overview.csv and c1.ntw) and you need automated per-vOTU taxonomy plus supporting network views. You have not run vConTACT2 against INPHARED references — graphanalyzer specifically interprets vConTACT2 outputs (c1.ntw, genome_by_genome_overview.csv) built with INPHARED input files Your vOTU names do not match the --prefix convention (e.g. vOTU_1, vOTU_2), since the prefix distinguishes the vOTUs to classify from the other genomes in the network You need direct taxonomic calls from vConTACT2 itself — the tool provides no taxonomic association for user sequences, so this skill is about network-based inheritance, not direct vConTACT2 classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Automates taxonomic classification of vOTUs from the vConTACT2 network using the graphanalyzer tool, which orders same-cluster neighbors by edge weight and inherits taxonomy from the first reference genome, replacing the manual inspection that vConTACT2 otherwise requires. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Automates taxonomic classification of vOTUs from the vConTACT2 network using the graphanalyzer tool, which orders same-cluster neighbors by edge weight and inherits taxonomy from the first reference genome, replacing the manual inspection that vConTACT2 otherwise requires.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have not run vConTACT2 against INPHARED references — graphanalyzer specifically interprets vConTACT2 outputs (c1.ntw, genome_by_genome_overview.csv) built with INPHARED input files Your vOTU names do not match the --prefix convention (e.g. vOTU_1, vOTU_2), since the prefix distinguishes the vOTUs to classify from the other genomes in the network You need direct taxonomic calls from vConTACT2 itself — the tool provides no taxonomic association for user sequences, so this skill is about network-based inheritance, not direct vConTACT2 classification

skills.description: Use when a tabular time-series omic data set (CSV/TSV or pickled Pandas DataFrame with a temporal feature column) needs a reproducible, publication-ready chart exported as SVG, e.g. from Data/cached/example_1.
skills.name: vega-lite-visualization-authoring
skills.search_text: vega-lite-visualization-authoring Use when a tabular time-series omic data set (CSV/TSV or pickled Pandas DataFrame with a temporal feature column) needs a reproducible, publication-ready chart exported as SVG, e.g. from Data/cached/example_1. Input is raw microarray-based data, which cannot be used directly as input without preprocessing (quality control and filtering) The analysis goal is direct integrative linking across omic-types (e.g. taxa linking for metagenomics), which MOVIS does not currently support The data lack an embedded temporal dimension and cannot be cast as time-series tabular data http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Authoring task-specific, publication-ready time-series visualizations with Altair 4.1.0 (Vega-Lite grammar) and altair_saver 0.5.0, as practiced in MOVIS for multi-omics data sets, with accessibility-aware color encoding and reproducible SVG export. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.02.012
skills.summary: Authoring task-specific, publication-ready time-series visualizations with Altair 4.1.0 (Vega-Lite grammar) and altair_saver 0.5.0, as practiced in MOVIS for multi-omics data sets, with accessibility-aware color encoding and reproducible SVG export.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw microarray-based data, which cannot be used directly as input without preprocessing (quality control and filtering) The analysis goal is direct integrative linking across omic-types (e.g. taxa linking for metagenomics), which MOVIS does not currently support The data lack an embedded temporal dimension and cannot be cast as time-series tabular data

skills.description: Use when measuring how much viral sequence information a reconstruction pipeline retains as sequencing depth decreases — e.g., subsampled paired-end FASTQ from a viral mock community at 10%, 1%, and 0.1% depth with replicate trials per depth.
skills.name: viral-base-retention-quantification
skills.search_text: viral-base-retention-quantification Use when measuring how much viral sequence information a reconstruction pipeline retains as sequencing depth decreases — e.g., subsampled paired-end FASTQ from a viral mock community at 10%, 1%, and 0.1% depth with replicate trials per depth. Input is an already-assembled viral genome or contigs rather than subsampled read data — retention must be measured from reconstructions of the same sample at varying depth The goal is general taxonomic classification of a virome without a full-depth reference run to define the 100% retention baseline The dataset lacks a defined mock community composition (e.g., seven known constituents), making detection-rate scoring against known members impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Quantifies the percentage of viral bases recovered by VirMAP reconstructions relative to a full-depth analysis of the Viral Mock Community (BioProject PRJNA431646), benchmarking retention across 10%, 1%, and 0.1% subsampling depths (ten trials each) against a standard read-classification approach. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Quantifies the percentage of viral bases recovered by VirMAP reconstructions relative to a full-depth analysis of the Viral Mock Community (BioProject PRJNA431646), benchmarking retention across 10%, 1%, and 0.1% subsampling depths (ten trials each) against a standard read-classification approach.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an already-assembled viral genome or contigs rather than subsampled read data — retention must be measured from reconstructions of the same sample at varying depth The goal is general taxonomic classification of a virome without a full-depth reference run to define the 100% retention baseline The dataset lacks a defined mock community composition (e.g., seven known constituents), making detection-rate scoring against known members impossible

skills.description: Use when multiple Hi-C or composition-based binners have been run on a mock metagenomic dataset with known ground-truth genome labels and you must quantify binning accuracy via clustering metrics and vMAG completeness counts.
skills.name: viral-bin-clustering-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: viral-bin-clustering-metric-evaluation Use when multiple Hi-C or composition-based binners have been run on a mock metagenomic dataset with known ground-truth genome labels and you must quantify binning accuracy via clustering metrics and vMAG completeness counts. Real datasets with no ground-truth genome labels — the clustering metrics require known labels, which the paper notes cannot be obtained from real samples Datasets with very few putative viral genomes, where the paper states benchmarking effectiveness is less convincing Evaluating shotgun-only binners lacking Hi-C co-occurrence profiles from multiple samples, which the paper notes impairs CoCoNet and vRhyme http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks metagenomic viral binning tools (ViralCC vs VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, MetaTOR) on the mock human gut Hi-C dataset by matching predicted clusters against ground-truth genome labels of the 1010 mock viral contigs and computing F-score, ARI, NMI, and homogeneity, plus CheckV-based near-complete/high-quality vMAG counts. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Benchmarks metagenomic viral binning tools (ViralCC vs VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, MetaTOR) on the mock human gut Hi-C dataset by matching predicted clusters against ground-truth genome labels of the 1010 mock viral contigs and computing F-score, ARI, NMI, and homogeneity, plus CheckV-based near-complete/high-quality vMAG counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real datasets with no ground-truth genome labels — the clustering metrics require known labels, which the paper notes cannot be obtained from real samples Datasets with very few putative viral genomes, where the paper states benchmarking effectiveness is less convincing Evaluating shotgun-only binners lacking Hi-C co-occurrence profiles from multiple samples, which the paper notes impairs CoCoNet and vRhyme

skills.description: Use when a metagenomic Hi-C dataset has assembled contigs, a name-sorted filtered BAM, and an identified viral contig list, and you need to bin viral contigs and quantify whether graph integration improves vMAG recovery.
skills.name: viral-contig-binning-evaluation
skills.search_text: viral-contig-binning-evaluation Use when a metagenomic Hi-C dataset has assembled contigs, a name-sorted filtered BAM, and an identified viral contig list, and you need to bin viral contigs and quantify whether graph integration improves vMAG recovery. The input is shotgun-only data with no Hi-C proximity-ligation BAM, since the Hi-C interaction graph is the core input to ViralCC You need contamination estimates for vMAGs — CheckV cannot estimate contamination of vMAGs because no viral marker gene set exists Comparing methods using CheckV completeness alone without a random binning control, which the paper says is necessary because random binning does not reduce CheckV completeness http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reproduce and evaluate ViralCC-style viral binning by integrating the Hi-C interaction graph with a host proximity graph (k=30) and running Leiden clustering (leidenalg, seed 42) on a mock human gut dataset, then assessing vMAG completeness with CheckV against graph-only ablation baselines. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Reproduce and evaluate ViralCC-style viral binning by integrating the Hi-C interaction graph with a host proximity graph (k=30) and running Leiden clustering (leidenalg, seed 42) on a mock human gut dataset, then assessing vMAG completeness with CheckV against graph-only ablation baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is shotgun-only data with no Hi-C proximity-ligation BAM, since the Hi-C interaction graph is the core input to ViralCC You need contamination estimates for vMAGs — CheckV cannot estimate contamination of vMAGs because no viral marker gene set exists Comparing methods using CheckV completeness alone without a random binning control, which the paper says is necessary because random binning does not reduce CheckV completeness

skills.description: Use when metagenomic Hi-C data (assembled contig FASTA, read-pair-sorted BAM, viral contig list) must be binned into viral genomes and compared against other binning tools using clustering metrics and completeness-based vMAG counts.
skills.name: viral-contig-binning-hic-data
skills.search_text: viral-contig-binning-hic-data Use when metagenomic Hi-C data (assembled contig FASTA, read-pair-sorted BAM, viral contig list) must be binned into viral genomes and compared against other binning tools using clustering metrics and completeness-based vMAG counts. Input contigs have not been filtered to putative viral contigs — shotgun/Hi-C-based general binners like HiCBin cannot bin viral contigs because TAXAassign can hardly annotate viral contigs Only a handful of putative viral genomes are present — the paper notes benchmarking effectiveness is less convincing when there are few putative viral genomes The goal is contamination estimation of vMAGs via marker genes — CheckV cannot estimate contamination of vMAGs since no marker gene set is available for viruses http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark viral contig binning from metagenomic Hi-C data by running ViralCC against comparator binners (VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, MetaTOR) on the same contigs and read-pair-sorted Hi-C BAM, then scoring clusters against ground-truth genome labels with F-score, ARI, NMI, homogeneity and CheckV-based vMAG counts. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Benchmark viral contig binning from metagenomic Hi-C data by running ViralCC against comparator binners (VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, MetaTOR) on the same contigs and read-pair-sorted Hi-C BAM, then scoring clusters against ground-truth genome labels with F-score, ARI, NMI, homogeneity and CheckV-based vMAG counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contigs have not been filtered to putative viral contigs — shotgun/Hi-C-based general binners like HiCBin cannot bin viral contigs because TAXAassign can hardly annotate viral contigs Only a handful of putative viral genomes are present — the paper notes benchmarking effectiveness is less convincing when there are few putative viral genomes The goal is contamination estimation of vMAGs via marker genes — CheckV cannot estimate contamination of vMAGs since no marker gene set is available for viruses

skills.description: Use when assembled metagenomic contigs (SPAdes/metaSPAdes/MEGAHIT assemblies or supplied long-read/contig FASTA via -A) must be classified as viral without relying solely on direct homology to known viral sequences.
skills.name: viral-contig-classification-by-gene-content
skills.search_text: viral-contig-classification-by-gene-content Use when assembled metagenomic contigs (SPAdes/metaSPAdes/MEGAHIT assemblies or supplied long-read/contig FASTA via -A) must be classified as viral without relying solely on direct homology to known viral sequences. Input is raw short reads and the goal is assembly itself — this skill is the downstream scoring step; run QC/assembly (SPAdes, metaSPAdes, or MEGAHIT via -a) first or use -A with preassembled contigs The analysis targets taxonomy/annotation of known viral genomes by homology alone — this skill's exclusion-based scoring is designed to avoid sole dependency on homology identification, not to replicate it A strict BLAST-based taxonomy assignment to a reference viral genome is required — contigs here are scored as cellular/viral/unknown by gene-content origin, not assigned to a specific virus http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Scores assembled contigs for viral origin by predicting ORFs, BLAST-searching predicted proteins against user-supplied viral (-v) and nonviral (-nv) databases, and classifying each contig by the origin of its gene content as cellular, viral, or unknown using an exclusion technique that avoids sole dependency on homology to known viruses. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/mra.00107-22
skills.summary: Scores assembled contigs for viral origin by predicting ORFs, BLAST-searching predicted proteins against user-supplied viral (-v) and nonviral (-nv) databases, and classifying each contig by the origin of its gene content as cellular, viral, or unknown using an exclusion technique that avoids sole dependency on homology to known viruses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw short reads and the goal is assembly itself — this skill is the downstream scoring step; run QC/assembly (SPAdes, metaSPAdes, or MEGAHIT via -a) first or use -A with preassembled contigs The analysis targets taxonomy/annotation of known viral genomes by homology alone — this skill's exclusion-based scoring is designed to avoid sole dependency on homology identification, not to replicate it A strict BLAST-based taxonomy assignment to a reference viral genome is required — contigs here are scored as cellular/viral/unknown by gene-content origin, not assigned to a specific virus

skills.description: Use when you have assembled contigs (FASTA), a name-sorted Hi-C alignment BAM, and a viral contig list, and need to bin viral contigs into draft genomes using Hi-C linkages plus virus-host proximity.
skills.name: viral-contig-graph-clustering
skills.search_text: viral-contig-graph-clustering Use when you have assembled contigs (FASTA), a name-sorted Hi-C alignment BAM, and a viral contig list, and need to bin viral contigs into draft genomes using Hi-C linkages plus virus-host proximity. No Hi-C (proximity-ligation) data are available — the Hi-C interaction graph is a core input, so co-abundance-only tools like CoCoNet or vRhyme may be more appropriate Viral contigs have not yet been identified — the pipeline requires a pre-computed viral contig list (VIRAL_file), not raw assemblies The BAM is not sorted by name — ViralCC requires name-sorted alignments before graph construction http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Integrates ViralCC's Hi-C interaction graph and host proximity graph into a unified graph G_int and applies Leiden clustering to reconstruct draft viral genomes (vMAGs) from metagenomic Hi-C data. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Integrates ViralCC's Hi-C interaction graph and host proximity graph into a unified graph G_int and applies Leiden clustering to reconstruct draft viral genomes (vMAGs) from metagenomic Hi-C data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No Hi-C (proximity-ligation) data are available — the Hi-C interaction graph is a core input, so co-abundance-only tools like CoCoNet or vRhyme may be more appropriate Viral contigs have not yet been identified — the pipeline requires a pre-computed viral contig list (VIRAL_file), not raw assemblies The BAM is not sorted by name — ViralCC requires name-sorted alignments before graph construction

skills.description: Use when you have a non-redundant contig library (e.g. metaSPAdes --meta output) from viral metagenomic data and need to decide which contigs are viral and how confident those calls are.
skills.name: viral-contig-identification
skills.search_text: viral-contig-identification Use when you have a non-redundant contig library (e.g. metaSPAdes --meta output) from viral metagenomic data and need to decide which contigs are viral and how confident those calls are. Input is raw reads or isolated viral fractions requiring no contig-level viral/non-viral discrimination — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in metagenomic assemblies, not samples with isolated viruses Sequences carry excessive environmental contamination, which the paper warns increases running time and lowers precision Only a single viral detector's output is available and no multi-tool evidence can be gathered to support the confidence scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Identify putative viral contigs in shotgun virome assemblies by combining multiple detection tools (VirSorter2, VIBRANT, DeepVirFinder, CheckV, MMseqs2 taxonomy) and classifying contigs by the number of tools that detect them, as implemented in the ViroProfiler pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Identify putative viral contigs in shotgun virome assemblies by combining multiple detection tools (VirSorter2, VIBRANT, DeepVirFinder, CheckV, MMseqs2 taxonomy) and classifying contigs by the number of tools that detect them, as implemented in the ViroProfiler pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or isolated viral fractions requiring no contig-level viral/non-viral discrimination — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in metagenomic assemblies, not samples with isolated viruses Sequences carry excessive environmental contamination, which the paper warns increases running time and lowers precision Only a single viral detector's output is available and no multi-tool evidence can be gathered to support the confidence scoring

skills.description: Use when comparing viral recovery across tools or pipelines on metagenomic (virome) FASTQ samples, e.g. to express recovered viral sequence as contig megabases and taxa-per-sample counts under matched filtering.

skills.search_text: viral-contig-megabase-quantification Use when comparing viral recovery across tools or pipelines on metagenomic (virome) FASTQ samples, e.g. to express recovered viral sequence as contig megabases and taxa-per-sample counts under matched filtering. skills.summary: Quantifies viral sequence content of virome samples as viral contig megabases and related per-sample metrics (filtered taxa IDs, contigs-per-taxon ratios, taxa-per-sample counts) from VirMAP or standard assembly-and-mapping outputs, aggregating them across subsampling levels into a comparison CSV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered taxa ID table or feature table — this skill quantifies from raw contig/alignment outputs and would double-filter Dataset is not viral metagenomic sequence data (e.g. 16S amplicon or host-only data) — contigs mapping outside the viral superkingdom are filtered and metrics would be near zero No matched filtering thresholds can be applied across pipelines — megabase and taxa counts are only comparable at equivalent bits-per-contig/bits-per-taxon cutoffs

skills.description: Use when draft vMAGs (e.g., from ViralCC's VIRAL_BIN output directories) need family-level taxonomic labels to compute bin purity, or when reproducing the Caudovirales-family purity fractions reported for the human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater Hi-C datasets.
skills.name: viral-family-taxonomic-annotation
skills.search_text: viral-family-taxonomic-annotation Use when draft vMAGs (e.g., from ViralCC's VIRAL_BIN output directories) need family-level taxonomic labels to compute bin purity, or when reproducing the Caudovirales-family purity fractions reported for the human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater Hi-C datasets. Input is raw shotgun/Hi-C reads rather than assembled, binned vMAG FASTA contigs — viral identification (VirSorter) and binning (ViralCC pipeline) must happen first Goal is discriminating viral from bacterial/archaeal contigs — family-level classifiers are for classifying already-identified viral contigs, not detecting them (per Demovir's own scope note) TAXAassign is expected to fail because contigs are heavily novel: the article notes 'TAXAassign can hardly annotate viral contigs', so low-coverage dark-matter vMAGs may yield no family assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates draft vMAGs at the family level using a TAXAassign-style alignment-based assignment against a curated viral reference genome database, then tabulates per-dataset family-consistency (purity) fractions with pandas — reproducing ViralCC's family-level purity analysis (90.6% human gut, 82.8% cow fecal, 85.4% wastewater; Fig. 5). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Annotates draft vMAGs at the family level using a TAXAassign-style alignment-based assignment against a curated viral reference genome database, then tabulates per-dataset family-consistency (purity) fractions with pandas — reproducing ViralCC's family-level purity analysis (90.6% human gut, 82.8% cow fecal, 85.4% wastewater; Fig. 5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw shotgun/Hi-C reads rather than assembled, binned vMAG FASTA contigs — viral identification (VirSorter) and binning (ViralCC pipeline) must happen first Goal is discriminating viral from bacterial/archaeal contigs — family-level classifiers are for classifying already-identified viral contigs, not detecting them (per Demovir's own scope note) TAXAassign is expected to fail because contigs are heavily novel: the article notes 'TAXAassign can hardly annotate viral contigs', so low-coverage dark-matter vMAGs may yield no family assignment

skills.description: Use when input is a set of predicted viral contigs (from VirSorter2/VIBRANT etc.) and the goal is gene prediction, functional annotation (KEGG/PFAM/COG/VOG hits), and AMG identification.
skills.name: viral-gene-function-annotation
skills.search_text: viral-gene-function-annotation Use when input is a set of predicted viral contigs (from VirSorter2/VIBRANT etc.) and the goal is gene prediction, functional annotation (KEGG/PFAM/COG/VOG hits), and AMG identification. Input is raw reads or an unassembled metagenome rather than a curated set of predicted viral contigs — run viral discovery/assembly (e.g. metaSPAdes + VirSorter2/VIBRANT) first The metagenome has excessive environmental contamination: the article notes this can increase pipeline running time and lower precision, so viral fractions should be isolated before sequencing The goal is taxonomy/host/replication-cycle assignment only, with no need for gene-level functional annotation or AMG calls http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Annotates protein-coding genes on viral contigs by clustering predicted proteins with MMseqs2 and running eggNOG-mapper, VOGDB, and DRAM-v to produce a merged gene-by-annotation table with an auxiliary metabolic gene (AMG) flag, as implemented in the ViroProfiler pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Annotates protein-coding genes on viral contigs by clustering predicted proteins with MMseqs2 and running eggNOG-mapper, VOGDB, and DRAM-v to produce a merged gene-by-annotation table with an auxiliary metabolic gene (AMG) flag, as implemented in the ViroProfiler pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or an unassembled metagenome rather than a curated set of predicted viral contigs — run viral discovery/assembly (e.g. metaSPAdes + VirSorter2/VIBRANT) first The metagenome has excessive environmental contamination: the article notes this can increase pipeline running time and lower precision, so viral fractions should be isolated before sequencing The goal is taxonomy/host/replication-cycle assignment only, with no need for gene-level functional annotation or AMG calls

skills.description: Use when you have a set of identified viral contigs (e.g., from VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder/CheckV in ViroProfiler) and need gene predictions, KEGG/PFAM/VOGDB functional hits, or AMG identification.
skills.name: viral-gene-prediction
skills.search_text: viral-gene-prediction Use when you have a set of identified viral contigs (e.g., from VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder/CheckV in ViroProfiler) and need gene predictions, KEGG/PFAM/VOGDB functional hits, or AMG identification. Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than identified viral contigs — run viral identification (VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder) and CheckV first, as ViroProfiler is designed to work on viral contig sets. Samples contain isolated viruses only — the article notes ViroProfiler is 'specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses', so bacterial (non-viral) gene annotation workflows are out of scope. Excessive environmental contamination is present in the metagenome sequences, which the article warns can increase running time and lower precision. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Predicts protein-coding genes on viral contigs and functionally annotates them with DRAM-v, eggNOG-mapper (EggNOG5), and VOGDB within ViroProfiler, distilling auxiliary metabolic gene (AMG) calls. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Predicts protein-coding genes on viral contigs and functionally annotates them with DRAM-v, eggNOG-mapper (EggNOG5), and VOGDB within ViroProfiler, distilling auxiliary metabolic gene (AMG) calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metagenomic reads rather than identified viral contigs — run viral identification (VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder) and CheckV first, as ViroProfiler is designed to work on viral contig sets. Samples contain isolated viruses only — the article notes ViroProfiler is 'specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses', so bacterial (non-viral) gene annotation workflows are out of scope. Excessive environmental contamination is present in the metagenome sequences, which the article warns can increase running time and lower precision.

skills.summary: Annotate raw viral genome FASTA files with PROKKA (kingdom set to viruses) to produce the GFF annotations and taxon-id mapping that HUBDesign requires as input for probe design.

skills.description: Use when building simulated virome benchmarks with fragmented complete viral genomes as ground truth to evaluate viral binners such as vRhyme, MetaBat2, VAMB, CONCOCT, BinSanity, or CoCoNet.
skills.name: viral-genome-benchmark-dataset-preparation
skills.search_text: viral-genome-benchmark-dataset-preparation Use when building simulated virome benchmarks with fragmented complete viral genomes as ground truth to evaluate viral binners such as vRhyme, MetaBat2, VAMB, CONCOCT, BinSanity, or CoCoNet. The input is a natural metagenome (e.g., GOV2 or agricultural soil virome) rather than a simulated dataset with fragmented ground-truth genomes, so metrics cannot be computed against known references The goal is binning microbes or non-viral genomes; vRhyme is explicitly not meant for this and MetaBat2 outperformed vRhyme on a non-viral synthetic dataset Input scaffolds have not been predicted as viral (the typical workflow is to pre-predict viruses with VIBRANT or VirSorter before binning) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Prepare simulated virome benchmark datasets from curated reference viral genomes (999 complete genomes fragmented into 4,324 scaffolds across nine datasets) with per-sample read sets, sorted BAM alignments, and Prodigal ORF predictions so that viral binning tools can be scored against ground truth with recall, precision, accuracy, specificity, and F1. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Prepare simulated virome benchmark datasets from curated reference viral genomes (999 complete genomes fragmented into 4,324 scaffolds across nine datasets) with per-sample read sets, sorted BAM alignments, and Prodigal ORF predictions so that viral binning tools can be scored against ground truth with recall, precision, accuracy, specificity, and F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a natural metagenome (e.g., GOV2 or agricultural soil virome) rather than a simulated dataset with fragmented ground-truth genomes, so metrics cannot be computed against known references The goal is binning microbes or non-viral genomes; vRhyme is explicitly not meant for this and MetaBat2 outperformed vRhyme on a non-viral synthetic dataset Input scaffolds have not been predicted as viral (the typical workflow is to pre-predict viruses with VIBRANT or VirSorter before binning)

skills.description: Use when you have a set of quality-filtered viral genomes (e.g. CheckV >=50% completeness) and need to dereplicate them into species-level vOTUs and/or test their novelty against existing virome catalogues.
skills.name: viral-genome-clustering-dereplication
skills.search_text: viral-genome-clustering-dereplication Use when you have a set of quality-filtered viral genomes (e.g. CheckV >=50% completeness) and need to dereplicate them into species-level vOTUs and/or test their novelty against existing virome catalogues. Input viral genomes have not been quality-filtered (no CheckV completeness assessment); clustering unfiltered contigs inflates vOTU counts with fragments The goal is prokaryotic species dereplication at 95% ANI over whole genomes (SGB clustering), not viral OTU definition Only a handful of viral genomes are present; all-vs-all BLASTn clustering and database overlap statistics are not meaningful at that scale http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Dereplicate quality-filtered viral genomes into species-level viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) via all-vs-all nucleotide comparison, then quantify overlap against external virome databases. In the VMGC workflow this reduced 14,224 viral genomes to 4,263 vOTUs at 95% identity over 85% of the genome. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Dereplicate quality-filtered viral genomes into species-level viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) via all-vs-all nucleotide comparison, then quantify overlap against external virome databases. In the VMGC workflow this reduced 14,224 viral genomes to 4,263 vOTUs at 95% identity over 85% of the genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input viral genomes have not been quality-filtered (no CheckV completeness assessment); clustering unfiltered contigs inflates vOTU counts with fragments The goal is prokaryotic species dereplication at 95% ANI over whole genomes (SGB clustering), not viral OTU definition Only a handful of viral genomes are present; all-vs-all BLASTn clustering and database overlap statistics are not meaningful at that scale

skills.description: Use when you have recovered draft viral bins (FASTA) from metagenomic Hi-C or shotgun binning and need to quantify completeness (e.g., to compare ViralCC vs VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, MetaTOR) rather than using marker-gene tools like CheckM.
skills.name: viral-genome-completeness-estimation-checkv
skills.search_text: viral-genome-completeness-estimation-checkv Use when you have recovered draft viral bins (FASTA) from metagenomic Hi-C or shotgun binning and need to quantify completeness (e.g., to compare ViralCC vs VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, MetaTOR) rather than using marker-gene tools like CheckM. The goal is to estimate contamination of vMAGs — CheckV is unable to estimate contamination because no marker gene set is available for viruses Evaluating bacterial/archaeal MAGs via universal single-copy marker genes — use CheckM instead The dataset has few putative viral genomes, which makes completeness-based benchmarking less convincing per the paper's discussion http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Estimate the completeness of draft viral genomes (vMAGs) recovered by metagenomic binning by comparing them to CheckV's curated database from NCBI GenBank and environmental samples, then classify bins into high/medium completion categories to benchmark viral binning methods like ViralCC. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Estimate the completeness of draft viral genomes (vMAGs) recovered by metagenomic binning by comparing them to CheckV's curated database from NCBI GenBank and environmental samples, then classify bins into high/medium completion categories to benchmark viral binning methods like ViralCC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to estimate contamination of vMAGs — CheckV is unable to estimate contamination because no marker gene set is available for viruses Evaluating bacterial/archaeal MAGs via universal single-copy marker genes — use CheckM instead The dataset has few putative viral genomes, which makes completeness-based benchmarking less convincing per the paper's discussion

skills.description: Use when viral scaffolds have been binned into vMAGs (e.g., by vRhyme) and you need to classify bins as low- vs. high-redundancy and estimate completeness/contamination per bin.
skills.name: viral-genome-completeness-evaluation
skills.search_text: viral-genome-completeness-evaluation Use when viral scaffolds have been binned into vMAGs (e.g., by vRhyme) and you need to classify bins as low- vs. high-redundancy and estimate completeness/contamination per bin. Input is an entire unfiltered metagenome or microbial scaffolds — vRhyme is built for viral sequences/scaffolds and 'is not meant to bin microbes' Binning non-viral or multiple inactive (non-replicating) prophages from the same host genome, where vRhyme has documented difficulties The question is raw binning coverage rather than quality — completeness/redundancy evaluation presupposes bins already exist http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assess the quality of viral metagenome-assembled genomes (vMAGs) produced by vRhyme by combining vRhyme's Mmseqs2-based protein redundancy scoring with CheckV completeness/contamination estimation, exploiting the observation that viruses seldom encode redundant genes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Assess the quality of viral metagenome-assembled genomes (vMAGs) produced by vRhyme by combining vRhyme's Mmseqs2-based protein redundancy scoring with CheckV completeness/contamination estimation, exploiting the observation that viruses seldom encode redundant genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an entire unfiltered metagenome or microbial scaffolds — vRhyme is built for viral sequences/scaffolds and 'is not meant to bin microbes' Binning non-viral or multiple inactive (non-replicating) prophages from the same host genome, where vRhyme has documented difficulties The question is raw binning coverage rather than quality — completeness/redundancy evaluation presupposes bins already exist

skills.description: Use when you need labeled training data for viral scaffold binning models: complete viral genomes must be converted into metagenome-like fragments and paired as 'same' vs 'different' genome origin.
skills.name: viral-genome-fragmentation-simulation
skills.search_text: viral-genome-fragmentation-simulation Use when you need labeled training data for viral scaffold binning models: complete viral genomes must be converted into metagenome-like fragments and paired as 'same' vs 'different' genome origin. The input is an entire metagenome rather than predicted viral sequences — vRhyme is built to run on viral sequences/scaffolds and whole-metagenome performance 'has not been fully evaluated'. The goal is binning non-viral (microbial) genomes — vRhyme 'is not meant to bin microbes' and this is an anticipated limitation. Only pre-binned scaffolds are available and no labeled pairs need to be generated from complete genomes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 Simulates metagenome fragmentation by downloading complete viral genomes from NCBI RefSeq/GenBank and IMG/VR, cutting them into scaffold fragments (39,105 total), and constructing labeled same/different scaffold pairs (69,632 pairs) to train vRhyme's supervised classifiers (ExtraTrees and MLP). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Simulates metagenome fragmentation by downloading complete viral genomes from NCBI RefSeq/GenBank and IMG/VR, cutting them into scaffold fragments (39,105 total), and constructing labeled same/different scaffold pairs (69,632 pairs) to train vRhyme's supervised classifiers (ExtraTrees and MLP).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an entire metagenome rather than predicted viral sequences — vRhyme is built to run on viral sequences/scaffolds and whole-metagenome performance 'has not been fully evaluated'. The goal is binning non-viral (microbial) genomes — vRhyme 'is not meant to bin microbes' and this is an anticipated limitation. Only pre-binned scaffolds are available and no labeled pairs need to be generated from complete genomes.

skills.description: Use when a virome/metagenome pipeline (e.g. MetaPhage) yields unexpectedly many vOTUs and you must classify each contig as complete, high/medium/low-quality, partial, or provirus to validate the excess predictions.
skills.name: viral-genome-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: viral-genome-quality-assessment Use when a virome/metagenome pipeline (e.g. MetaPhage) yields unexpectedly many vOTUs and you must classify each contig as complete, high/medium/low-quality, partial, or provirus to validate the excess predictions. Input contigs have not been dereplicated and length-filtered by the upstream MetaPhage postprocessing (minlen 1000 bp default) — quality tiers would be dominated by redundant or trivially short scaffolds The goal is taxonomic classification or network analysis of vOTUs (use vConTACT2/graphanalyzer instead), not completeness estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Assesses the quality/completeness of predicted viral contigs (vOTUs) with CheckV to determine whether a phage-mining pipeline's predictions are complete, partial, or low-quality genomes. In the MetaPhage validation it explained why 5,284 predicted vOTUs far exceeded the 1,029 phage contigs reported by Liang et al. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Assesses the quality/completeness of predicted viral contigs (vOTUs) with CheckV to determine whether a phage-mining pipeline's predictions are complete, partial, or low-quality genomes. In the MetaPhage validation it explained why 5,284 predicted vOTUs far exceeded the 1,029 phage contigs reported by Liang et al.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contigs have not been dereplicated and length-filtered by the upstream MetaPhage postprocessing (minlen 1000 bp default) — quality tiers would be dominated by redundant or trivially short scaffolds The goal is taxonomic classification or network analysis of vOTUs (use vConTACT2/graphanalyzer instead), not completeness estimation

skills.summary: Quality-assessment and completeness filtering of metagenome-assembled viral genomes using CheckV, as applied to the VMGC to retain 14,224 viral sequences with at least 50% completeness and classify them into complete/high/medium-quality tiers before vOTU clustering.
