skills.description: Use when comparing oligonucleotide probe sets designed across multiple related viral genomes (e.g., 56 RefSeq coronaviruses) and you need a quantitative efficiency metric — mean distinct-genome hits per probe — to rank competing design strategies.
skills.name: viral-genome-sequence-homology-mapping
skills.search_text: viral-genome-sequence-homology-mapping Use when comparing oligonucleotide probe sets designed across multiple related viral genomes (e.g., 56 RefSeq coronaviruses) and you need a quantitative efficiency metric — mean distinct-genome hits per probe — to rank competing design strategies. Input genomes are unknown or unannotatable — HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to efficiently cluster sequences, so probes cannot be designed for such targets, only close relatives The task is wet-lab capture validation (enrichment on real or spiked samples) rather than in-silico probe-set benchmarking; this skill computes design metrics only A single near-identical genome target where homology-aware hierarchical design offers no advantage over simple tiling http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmarks hybridization-capture probe sets for coronavirus genomes by mapping each probe set back to the target genomes with BLASTn and computing probe-set efficiency (the average number of distinct genomes each probe maps to), enabling head-to-head comparison of HUBDesign, CATCH (strict and permissive), and naive tiling. metagenomics/v1 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100069
skills.summary: Benchmarks hybridization-capture probe sets for coronavirus genomes by mapping each probe set back to the target genomes with BLASTn and computing probe-set efficiency (the average number of distinct genomes each probe maps to), enabling head-to-head comparison of HUBDesign, CATCH (strict and permissive), and naive tiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input genomes are unknown or unannotatable — HUBDesign relies on annotated genomes to efficiently cluster sequences, so probes cannot be designed for such targets, only close relatives The task is wet-lab capture validation (enrichment on real or spiked samples) rather than in-silico probe-set benchmarking; this skill computes design metrics only A single near-identical genome target where homology-aware hierarchical design offers no advantage over simple tiling

skills.description: Use when error-prone NGS reads (e.g. 454 Titanium pyrosequencing) from a genetically heterogeneous viral sample are aligned to a reference (e.g. HIV-1 subtype B pol) and low-frequency variants (~0.1%) must be separated from sequencing errors.
skills.name: viral-haplotype-error-correction
skills.search_text: viral-haplotype-error-correction Use when error-prone NGS reads (e.g. 454 Titanium pyrosequencing) from a genetically heterogeneous viral sample are aligned to a reference (e.g. HIV-1 subtype B pol) and low-frequency variants (~0.1%) must be separated from sequencing errors. Global (whole-genome-length) haplotype reconstruction is required and ShoRAH2 is installed — global mode is disabled there; use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or the global options in V-pipe instead The input is not an alignment of reads to a reference (e.g. only unaligned FASTQ or a finished consensus sequence) — the MSA must be built first, or a different tool is needed Only single-nucleotide variants with strand-bias correction are wanted from a clean sample, without read error correction — call 'shorah snv' directly rather than running the full correction pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 ShoRAH-based error correction for deep sequencing of mixed viral samples: reads overlapping the same genome window (~read length) are clustered with a Dirichlet process mixture (diri_sampler) to reconstruct local haplotypes, and original reads are corrected by majority vote across windows. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: ShoRAH-based error correction for deep sequencing of mixed viral samples: reads overlapping the same genome window (~read length) are clustered with a Dirichlet process mixture (diri_sampler) to reconstruct local haplotypes, and original reads are corrected by majority vote across windows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Global (whole-genome-length) haplotype reconstruction is required and ShoRAH2 is installed — global mode is disabled there; use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or the global options in V-pipe instead The input is not an alignment of reads to a reference (e.g. only unaligned FASTQ or a finished consensus sequence) — the MSA must be built first, or a different tool is needed Only single-nucleotide variants with strand-bias correction are wanted from a clean sample, without read error correction — call 'shorah snv' directly rather than running the full correction pipeline

skills.description: Use when a viral metagenomic read set (e.g. ART-illumina MiSeq 250 bp paired-end reads) must be classified against a partial or remotely related reference and resolved into strain-level haplotype contigs without a high-quality reference genome.
skills.name: viral-haplotype-reconstruction
skills.search_text: viral-haplotype-reconstruction Use when a viral metagenomic read set (e.g. ART-illumina MiSeq 250 bp paired-end reads) must be classified against a partial or remotely related reference and resolved into strain-level haplotype contigs without a high-quality reference genome. The target virus shares no conservation with any reference genome — TAR-VIR's read recruiting will not detect a completely new virus Only generic species-level abundance profiling is needed and strain-level haplotypes are not of interest (generic assemblers suffice) A complete high-quality reference genome exists for the exact strain, making reference-based haplotype reconstruction tools more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Reconstructs viral strain haplotypes de novo from metagenomic reads by combining overlap-extension read recruiting (TAR-VIR) with paired-end overlap-graph haplotype assembly (PEHaplo), without requiring complete or high-quality reference genomes. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2
skills.summary: Reconstructs viral strain haplotypes de novo from metagenomic reads by combining overlap-extension read recruiting (TAR-VIR) with paired-end overlap-graph haplotype assembly (PEHaplo), without requiring complete or high-quality reference genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target virus shares no conservation with any reference genome — TAR-VIR's read recruiting will not detect a completely new virus Only generic species-level abundance profiling is needed and strain-level haplotypes are not of interest (generic assemblers suffice) A complete high-quality reference genome exists for the exact strain, making reference-based haplotype reconstruction tools more appropriate

skills.description: Use when input is predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) plus per-sample sorted BAM alignments, and the goal is to assemble fragmented viral genomes into near-complete vMAGs.
skills.name: viral-mag-binning-execution
skills.search_text: viral-mag-binning-execution Use when input is predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) plus per-sample sorted BAM alignments, and the goal is to assemble fragmented viral genomes into near-complete vMAGs. The goal is binning non-viral (bacterial/archaeal/eukaryotic) genomes — vRhyme is not meant to bin microbes, and MetaBat2 outperformed vRhyme on a synthetic non-viral dataset Only a single sample is available and coverage variance is unreliable — vRhyme performs optimally with multiple input samples The target is separating multiple inactive (non-replicating) prophages from the same host genome — vRhyme had difficulties with this case http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Execute vRhyme to bin viral scaffolds into viral metagenome-assembled genomes (vMAGs) using supervised machine learning (neural network + extra trees) on nucleotide sequence features combined with single- or multi-sample read coverage effect size comparisons, plus protein-redundancy-based bin refinement. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Execute vRhyme to bin viral scaffolds into viral metagenome-assembled genomes (vMAGs) using supervised machine learning (neural network + extra trees) on nucleotide sequence features combined with single- or multi-sample read coverage effect size comparisons, plus protein-redundancy-based bin refinement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is binning non-viral (bacterial/archaeal/eukaryotic) genomes — vRhyme is not meant to bin microbes, and MetaBat2 outperformed vRhyme on a synthetic non-viral dataset Only a single sample is available and coverage variance is unreliable — vRhyme performs optimally with multiple input samples The target is separating multiple inactive (non-replicating) prophages from the same host genome — vRhyme had difficulties with this case

skills.description: Use when assembling low-abundance viral genomes (e.g. mock viral communities or strain mixes spiked into host reads) from FASTQ reads and you need strain-level genome fraction, misassembly, and mismatch/indel metrics per assembler.
skills.name: viral-metagenome-assembly
skills.search_text: viral-metagenome-assembly Use when assembling low-abundance viral genomes (e.g. mock viral communities or strain mixes spiked into host reads) from FASTQ reads and you need strain-level genome fraction, misassembly, and mismatch/indel metrics per assembler. Input is already assembled contigs or a reference-mapped analysis — MetaCortex is a de novo metagenome assembler for environmental sequence reads. MacOS user relying on LLVM as the compiler — LLVM will not compile MetaCortex; GCC with CC pointing at the GCC binary is required. K-mer sizes above 127 are needed and installation is via Conda — the Conda build supports only up to kmer 127, so source compilation with make MAXK=160/192 is required instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assemble viral genomes from metagenomic Illumina reads with MetaCortex, a Cortex-derived de Bruijn graph assembler that captures intra-species diversity from the assembly graph, and benchmark the contigs against reference viral genomes with MetaQUAST. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad020
skills.summary: Assemble viral genomes from metagenomic Illumina reads with MetaCortex, a Cortex-derived de Bruijn graph assembler that captures intra-species diversity from the assembly graph, and benchmark the contigs against reference viral genomes with MetaQUAST.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled contigs or a reference-mapped analysis — MetaCortex is a de novo metagenome assembler for environmental sequence reads. MacOS user relying on LLVM as the compiler — LLVM will not compile MetaCortex; GCC with CC pointing at the GCC binary is required. K-mer sizes above 127 are needed and installation is via Conda — the Conda build supports only up to kmer 127, so source compilation with make MAXK=160/192 is required instead.

skills.description: Use when you have predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) plus multi-sample metagenomic read coverage and need to cluster scaffolds into vMAGs while controlling contamination.
skills.name: viral-metagenome-genome-binning
skills.search_text: viral-metagenome-genome-binning Use when you have predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) plus multi-sample metagenomic read coverage and need to cluster scaffolds into vMAGs while controlling contamination. Input is an entire (unfiltered) metagenome of mostly non-viral sequences — vRhyme is built to run on viral sequences/scaffolds and whole-metagenome performance has not been fully evaluated Goal is binning microbial (bacterial/archaeal) genomes — MetaBat2 performed better than vRhyme on a synthetic dataset of predominately non-viral sequences Few or single input coverage samples are available when robust coverage variance comparisons are required for accurate binning http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Bins viral scaffolds into viral metagenome-assembled genomes (vMAGs) using vRhyme, which combines supervised machine learning (neural network + Extra Trees) on sequence features with single- or multi-sample read coverage effect size comparisons, refined via a protein redundancy scoring mechanism exploiting the observation that viruses seldom encode redundant genes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Bins viral scaffolds into viral metagenome-assembled genomes (vMAGs) using vRhyme, which combines supervised machine learning (neural network + Extra Trees) on sequence features with single- or multi-sample read coverage effect size comparisons, refined via a protein redundancy scoring mechanism exploiting the observation that viruses seldom encode redundant genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an entire (unfiltered) metagenome of mostly non-viral sequences — vRhyme is built to run on viral sequences/scaffolds and whole-metagenome performance has not been fully evaluated Goal is binning microbial (bacterial/archaeal) genomes — MetaBat2 performed better than vRhyme on a synthetic dataset of predominately non-viral sequences Few or single input coverage samples are available when robust coverage variance comparisons are required for accurate binning

skills.description: Use when analyzing raw shotgun virome reads (e.g., FASTQ from SRA) to identify viral contigs, assess their quality, assign taxonomy, and predict phage hosts — as in the UC fecal virome validation with 20 samples.
skills.name: viral-metagenome-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: viral-metagenome-pipeline-execution Use when analyzing raw shotgun virome reads (e.g., FASTQ from SRA) to identify viral contigs, assess their quality, assign taxonomy, and predict phage hosts — as in the UC fecal virome validation with 20 samples. Input is already assembled contigs or a feature/abundance table rather than raw shotgun reads — the trimming/DECONTAM/metaSPAdes front end would be redundant or invalid Samples contain isolated (purified) viral fractions only — the article notes ViroProfiler is designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses, but whole shotgun metagenomes with excessive environmental contamination increase run time and lower precision The goal is bacterial (non-viral) community profiling — standardized tools like Qiime/Mothur are the article's reference point for bacteria, not this virome pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Execute the ViroProfiler containerized Nextflow pipeline (deng-lab/viroprofiler) on shotgun viral metagenomic data, chaining quality trimming (FASTP), host removal (DECONTAM), assembly (metaSPAdes --meta), viral identification (VirSorter2, DeepVirFinder, VIBRANT), quality assessment (CheckV), taxonomy assignment (vConTACT2, MMseqs2), and host prediction (iPHoP) to produce annotated viral contigs and community profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Execute the ViroProfiler containerized Nextflow pipeline (deng-lab/viroprofiler) on shotgun viral metagenomic data, chaining quality trimming (FASTP), host removal (DECONTAM), assembly (metaSPAdes --meta), viral identification (VirSorter2, DeepVirFinder, VIBRANT), quality assessment (CheckV), taxonomy assignment (vConTACT2, MMseqs2), and host prediction (iPHoP) to produce annotated viral contigs and community profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled contigs or a feature/abundance table rather than raw shotgun reads — the trimming/DECONTAM/metaSPAdes front end would be redundant or invalid Samples contain isolated (purified) viral fractions only — the article notes ViroProfiler is designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses, but whole shotgun metagenomes with excessive environmental contamination increase run time and lower precision The goal is bacterial (non-viral) community profiling — standardized tools like Qiime/Mothur are the article's reference point for bacteria, not this virome pipeline

skills.description: Use when you have FASTQ reads and VirMAP-reconstructed viral contigs/super-scaffolds and need per-genome read abundance, read sets, and taxonomic classifications from metagenomic virome data.
skills.name: viral-metagenomic-read-abundance-quantification
skills.search_text: viral-metagenomic-read-abundance-quantification Use when you have FASTQ reads and VirMAP-reconstructed viral contigs/super-scaffolds and need per-genome read abundance, read sets, and taxonomic classifications from metagenomic virome data. You only have a precomputed feature/abundance table and no raw reads to align to reconstructed viral genomes The goal is de-novo viral discovery or assembly itself rather than quantifying abundance of already-reconstructed viral genomes Sequences come from an isolate genome with no mixed-community background, so read sets will not require dereplication, normalization, or Jaccard-distance filtering Assign metagenomic reads to reconstructed viral genomes via nucleotide (BBMap) and translated (DIAMOND) alignments against VirMAP's custom viral databases, then compute per-genome read abundance from the converged read assignments of the final dual assembly. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Assign metagenomic reads to reconstructed viral genomes via nucleotide (BBMap) and translated (DIAMOND) alignments against VirMAP's custom viral databases, then compute per-genome read abundance from the converged read assignments of the final dual assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a precomputed feature/abundance table and no raw reads to align to reconstructed viral genomes The goal is de-novo viral discovery or assembly itself rather than quantifying abundance of already-reconstructed viral genomes Sequences come from an isolate genome with no mixed-community background, so read sets will not require dereplication, normalization, or Jaccard-distance filtering

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a viral read-recruitment or haplotype-assembly pipeline and a ground-truth simulated metagenome with known haplotype counts and coverage is needed.
skills.name: viral-metagenomic-read-simulation
skills.search_text: viral-metagenomic-read-simulation Use when benchmarking a viral read-recruitment or haplotype-assembly pipeline and a ground-truth simulated metagenome with known haplotype counts and coverage is needed. The analysis targets real clinical or environmental metagenomic data rather than a controlled benchmark with known ground truth The sequencer/platform differs from MiSeq paired-end 250 bp chemistry and ART-illumina error models would misrepresent it A completely new virus sharing no conservation with any reference genome must be detected, since simulation from known references cannot represent it http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Simulate error-containing MiSeq paired-end viral metagenomic read sets with ART-illumina so that downstream recruitment/assembly pipelines (e.g. TAR-VIR) can be benchmarked against a known ground-truth composition of haplotypes and off-target viruses. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-2878-2
skills.summary: Simulate error-containing MiSeq paired-end viral metagenomic read sets with ART-illumina so that downstream recruitment/assembly pipelines (e.g. TAR-VIR) can be benchmarked against a known ground-truth composition of haplotypes and off-target viruses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets real clinical or environmental metagenomic data rather than a controlled benchmark with known ground truth The sequencer/platform differs from MiSeq paired-end 250 bp chemistry and ART-illumina error models would misrepresent it A completely new virus sharing no conservation with any reference genome must be detected, since simulation from known references cannot represent it

skills.description: Use when you have shotgun Illumina paired-end virome FASTQ data and need viral contig identification, taxonomic assignment and abundance profiling, or when benchmarking a profiler against ground-truth mock community composition.

skills.search_text: viral-metagenomic-taxonomic-profiling Use when you have shotgun Illumina paired-end virome FASTQ data and need viral contig identification, taxonomic assignment and abundance profiling, or when benchmarking a profiler against ground-truth mock community composition. Samples contain excessive environmental contamination rather than isolated viral fractions — the paper notes contamination increases runtime and lowers precision, so isolate viral fractions before sequencing Input is already assembled viral contigs or a taxonomic abundance table — assembly/binning modules would be redundant The goal is profiling bacteria or mixed microbiomes without viral enrichment — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 End-to-end containerized profiling of shotgun virome samples with the ViroProfiler Nextflow pipeline (metaSPAdes assembly, vRhyme/phamb binning, VirSorter2/DeepVirFinder/VIBRANT viral-contig identification, taxonomy and functional annotation), including benchmarking against Kraken2/Bracken with precision, sensitivity and F1 metrics. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: End-to-end containerized profiling of shotgun virome samples with the ViroProfiler Nextflow pipeline (metaSPAdes assembly, vRhyme/phamb binning, VirSorter2/DeepVirFinder/VIBRANT viral-contig identification, taxonomy and functional annotation), including benchmarking against Kraken2/Bracken with precision, sensitivity and F1 metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples contain excessive environmental contamination rather than isolated viral fractions — the paper notes contamination increases runtime and lowers precision, so isolate viral fractions before sequencing Input is already assembled viral contigs or a taxonomic abundance table — assembly/binning modules would be redundant The goal is profiling bacteria or mixed microbiomes without viral enrichment — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses

skills.description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads or assembled contigs must be classified as viral, annotated for taxonomy/function, binned into vMAGs, or assigned hosts and lytic/lysogenic/chronic replication cycles.
skills.name: viral-metagenomics-annotation
skills.search_text: viral-metagenomics-annotation Use when shotgun metagenomic reads or assembled contigs must be classified as viral, annotated for taxonomy/function, binned into vMAGs, or assigned hosts and lytic/lysogenic/chronic replication cycles. Input is already a feature table or isolate virus genomes rather than shotgun metagenomic data — ViroProfiler 'is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses' and expects metagenomic input You only need bacterial community profiling (e.g., Qiime/Mothur amplicon workflows), not viral discovery and annotation Heavy environmental contamination without prior viral-fraction isolation is expected, which the authors warn increases runtime and lowers precision http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Annotate shotgun viral metagenomic data end-to-end with ViroProfiler: assemble reads, identify viral contigs (VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder), bin viral genomes (vRhyme/phamb), assign taxonomy and gene function, and predict hosts and replication cycles (iPhoP, BACPHLIP, Replidec). metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Annotate shotgun viral metagenomic data end-to-end with ViroProfiler: assemble reads, identify viral contigs (VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder), bin viral genomes (vRhyme/phamb), assign taxonomy and gene function, and predict hosts and replication cycles (iPhoP, BACPHLIP, Replidec).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or isolate virus genomes rather than shotgun metagenomic data — ViroProfiler 'is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses' and expects metagenomic input You only need bacterial community profiling (e.g., Qiime/Mothur amplicon workflows), not viral discovery and annotation Heavy environmental contamination without prior viral-fraction isolation is expected, which the authors warn increases runtime and lowers precision

skills.description: Use when a taxonomic classifier (read-, contig-, or marker-gene-based) must be validated on sequencing data with a known ground-truth viral composition, or when robustness to reduced sequencing depth must be quantified.
skills.name: viral-mock-community-benchmarking
skills.search_text: viral-mock-community-benchmarking Use when a taxonomic classifier (read-, contig-, or marker-gene-based) must be validated on sequencing data with a known ground-truth viral composition, or when robustness to reduced sequencing depth must be quantified. The goal is taxonomic classification of a real environmental or clinical virome rather than benchmarking a classifier against mock-community truth. The input is already a classified taxonomy table or feature table — rerunning the pipeline and rescoring would be redundant. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Benchmark a viral taxonomic classification pipeline against a viral mock community of known composition (e.g. PRJNA431646's seven constituents) by computing precision, recall, and F-score, and by quantifying detection robustness and viral-base retention under depth subsampling. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Benchmark a viral taxonomic classification pipeline against a viral mock community of known composition (e.g. PRJNA431646's seven constituents) by computing precision, recall, and F-score, and by quantifying detection robustness and viral-base retention under depth subsampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input dataset has no known ground-truth viral composition — precision/recall/F-score against intended constituents cannot be computed and retention cannot be referenced to a full-depth baseline. The goal is taxonomic classification of a real environmental or clinical virome rather than benchmarking a classifier against mock-community truth. The input is already a classified taxonomy table or feature table — rerunning the pipeline and rescoring would be redundant.
