skills.summary: Reconstruct full-length (global) viral haplotypes from error-corrected local window haplotypes and estimate their population frequencies by maximum likelihood, using ShoRAH's contain/mm.py/freqEst chain as the final two steps of the four-step ShoRAH pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only SNV calling is needed — run shorah snv or the local-only analysis (shorah shotgun / shorah amplicon) instead Running ShoRAH2 — global haplotype reconstruction is disabled in that version and ShoRAH1 v1.1.3 or V-pipe must be used Input reads have not yet been error-corrected — global reconstruction assumes the local haplotype reconstruction stage has already been completed

skills.description: Use when deep sequencing reads from a genetically heterogeneous viral sample must be error-corrected, clustered into local/global haplotypes, and their frequencies estimated, especially to detect rare variants.
skills.name: viral-quasispecies-diversity-estimation
skills.search_text: viral-quasispecies-diversity-estimation Use when deep sequencing reads from a genetically heterogeneous viral sample must be error-corrected, clustered into local/global haplotypes, and their frequencies estimated, especially to detect rare variants. Only the consensus sequence is needed and low-frequency variants are irrelevant — Sanger-style consensus analysis suffices Global haplotype reconstruction is required while using ShoRAH2, which has global mode disabled; use ShoRAH1 v1.1.3 or V-pipe's global options instead Data are not from deep sequencing of a mixed viral sample (e.g. single-isolate sequencing or non-viral variant tasks outside quasispecies scope) http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Estimate the genetic diversity of a mixed viral sample and quantify constituent haplotypes from deep sequencing data using ShoRAH, which corrects sequencing errors via Dirichlet-process clustering of overlapping reads. Enables detection of rare variants, e.g. haplotypes at 0.1% frequency at 5000x coverage in simulated HIV-1 pol data. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: Estimate the genetic diversity of a mixed viral sample and quantify constituent haplotypes from deep sequencing data using ShoRAH, which corrects sequencing errors via Dirichlet-process clustering of overlapping reads. Enables detection of rare variants, e.g. haplotypes at 0.1% frequency at 5000x coverage in simulated HIV-1 pol data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only the consensus sequence is needed and low-frequency variants are irrelevant — Sanger-style consensus analysis suffices Global haplotype reconstruction is required while using ShoRAH2, which has global mode disabled; use ShoRAH1 v1.1.3 or V-pipe's global options instead Data are not from deep sequencing of a mixed viral sample (e.g. single-isolate sequencing or non-viral variant tasks outside quasispecies scope)

skills.description: Use when metagenomic FASTQ reads must be assigned to known viruses by both nucleotide and translated protein alignments to build per-genome read sets for mapping assembly.
skills.name: viral-read-alignment-to-genbank-nucleotide-protein-databases
skills.search_text: viral-read-alignment-to-genbank-nucleotide-protein-databases Use when metagenomic FASTQ reads must be assigned to known viruses by both nucleotide and translated protein alignments to build per-genome read sets for mapping assembly. The goal is de-novo assembly of novel viruses with no database representatives — VirMAP's mapping assembly tier requires reference genomes; use MEGAHIT or Tadpole de-novo assembly instead. Input is already assembled contigs rather than raw reads — the read-assignment and per-genome pileup logic assumes read-level alignments. The target organisms are non-viral (e.g. bacterial or eukaryotic classification) — the databases and thresholds here are tuned to the viral superkingdom and VirMAP filters contigs mapping outside it. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Align digitally normalized metagenomic reads against comprehensive viral nucleotide (Genbank gbvrl/gbphage) and viral protein databases using BBMap and DIAMOND, forming the tiered alignment layer VirMAP uses to assign reads to putative viral genomes and protein pseudo-scaffolds. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Align digitally normalized metagenomic reads against comprehensive viral nucleotide (Genbank gbvrl/gbphage) and viral protein databases using BBMap and DIAMOND, forming the tiered alignment layer VirMAP uses to assign reads to putative viral genomes and protein pseudo-scaffolds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de-novo assembly of novel viruses with no database representatives — VirMAP's mapping assembly tier requires reference genomes; use MEGAHIT or Tadpole de-novo assembly instead. Input is already assembled contigs rather than raw reads — the read-assignment and per-genome pileup logic assumes read-level alignments. The target organisms are non-viral (e.g. bacterial or eukaryotic classification) — the databases and thresholds here are tuned to the viral superkingdom and VirMAP filters contigs mapping outside it.

skills.description: Use when retained reads from host read removal show anomalously high retention (e.g. NA12878 0.641% vs 0.406% after correction) and viral contamination such as EBV is suspected in 1000 Genomes or similar Illumina data.
skills.name: viral-read-detection-and-subtraction
skills.search_text: viral-read-detection-and-subtraction Use when retained reads from host read removal show anomalously high retention (e.g. NA12878 0.641% vs 0.406% after correction) and viral contamination such as EBV is suspected in 1000 Genomes or similar Illumina data. Input is raw host-mixed FASTQ that has not yet passed hostile clean against a human index — viral subtraction is a second-pass step on retained reads The analysis goal is host read removal itself rather than quantifying/subtracting viral contamination inflating retention figures The retained reads come from data where EBV or other viral contamination is expected biological signal (e.g. tumor virome studies) rather than a contaminant to remove http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Detects viral contamination (e.g. Epstein-Barr Virus, NC_007605.1/NC_009334.1) in host-depleted FASTQs via de novo assembly and alignment, then subtracts viral reads with a custom Hostile index so host read retention metrics are not inflated by viral contaminant reads. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad728
skills.summary: Detects viral contamination (e.g. Epstein-Barr Virus, NC_007605.1/NC_009334.1) in host-depleted FASTQs via de novo assembly and alignment, then subtracts viral reads with a custom Hostile index so host read retention metrics are not inflated by viral contaminant reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw host-mixed FASTQ that has not yet passed hostile clean against a human index — viral subtraction is a second-pass step on retained reads The analysis goal is host read removal itself rather than quantifying/subtracting viral contamination inflating retention figures The retained reads come from data where EBV or other viral contamination is expected biological signal (e.g. tumor virome studies) rather than a contaminant to remove

skills.description: Use when paired-end viral metagenomic FASTQ data (e.g., SRA clinical respiratory samples) must have reads assigned to specific viral genomes and genomes reconstructed as super-scaffolds, especially with low coverage or divergent viruses.
skills.name: viral-read-recruitment-and-genome-assignment
skills.search_text: viral-read-recruitment-and-genome-assignment Use when paired-end viral metagenomic FASTQ data (e.g., SRA clinical respiratory samples) must have reads assigned to specific viral genomes and genomes reconstructed as super-scaffolds, especially with low coverage or divergent viruses. Input is already a viral taxonomic abundance table or contig catalog rather than raw metagenomic reads — read recruitment and assembly are unnecessary and the 64 GB RAM pipeline cost is not justified. The goal is only rough abundance profiling of known viruses per read, without genome reconstruction; individual-read classifiers are far cheaper than VirMAP's assembly/improvement pipeline. Samples contain almost no viral signal and the study target is host or bacterial genomics — contamination filtering thresholds (>50% aligning bases resolving to virus) will filter nearly everything. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Assign metagenomic reads to viral genomes by tiered nucleotide and translated (protein) alignments to the Genbank viral/phage divisions (gbvrl/gbphg), then filter and pileup-assemble per-genome read sets into virus-like super-scaffolds using VirMAP. The skill reproduces VirMAP's influenza reconstruction on the UMERS respiratory dataset (PRJEB7888), where it recruited 509,039 influenza reads and averaged 9.05 contiguous segments per positive sample. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Assign metagenomic reads to viral genomes by tiered nucleotide and translated (protein) alignments to the Genbank viral/phage divisions (gbvrl/gbphg), then filter and pileup-assemble per-genome read sets into virus-like super-scaffolds using VirMAP. The skill reproduces VirMAP's influenza reconstruction on the UMERS respiratory dataset (PRJEB7888), where it recruited 509,039 influenza reads and averaged 9.05 contiguous segments per positive sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a viral taxonomic abundance table or contig catalog rather than raw metagenomic reads — read recruitment and assembly are unnecessary and the 64 GB RAM pipeline cost is not justified. The goal is only rough abundance profiling of known viruses per read, without genome reconstruction; individual-read classifiers are far cheaper than VirMAP's assembly/improvement pipeline. Samples contain almost no viral signal and the study target is host or bacterial genomics — contamination filtering thresholds (>50% aligning bases resolving to virus) will filter nearly everything.

skills.description: Use when installing or rebuilding the VirMAP pipeline's reference databases before processing metagenomic samples, or when Genbank gbvrl/gbphage content has grown and the prebuilt viral nucleotide/protein databases must be regenerated.
skills.name: viral-reference-database-preparation
skills.search_text: viral-reference-database-preparation Use when installing or rebuilding the VirMAP pipeline's reference databases before processing metagenomic samples, or when Genbank gbvrl/gbphage content has grown and the prebuilt viral nucleotide/protein databases must be regenerated. When the VirMAP prebuilt databases already exist and match the desired Genbank snapshot — rebuilding wastes significant SSD/RAM provisioning time When the analysis targets non-viral taxonomy only, since these databases span only the viral superkingdom (gbvrl/gbphg divisions) When working with a custom non-Genbank reference set not supported by the virmapInstall.pl pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Prepare the VirMAP reference databases (Taxonomy.virmap, virDmnd.dmnd, virBbmap, gbBlastn, gbBlastx.dmnd) from the Genbank viral (gbvrl) and phage (gbphg) divisions so that metagenomic reads can be taxonomically classified by both nucleotide and translated alignments. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Prepare the VirMAP reference databases (Taxonomy.virmap, virDmnd.dmnd, virBbmap, gbBlastn, gbBlastx.dmnd) from the Genbank viral (gbvrl) and phage (gbphg) divisions so that metagenomic reads can be taxonomically classified by both nucleotide and translated alignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the VirMAP prebuilt databases already exist and match the desired Genbank snapshot — rebuilding wastes significant SSD/RAM provisioning time When the analysis targets non-viral taxonomy only, since these databases span only the viral superkingdom (gbvrl/gbphg divisions) When working with a custom non-Genbank reference set not supported by the virmapInstall.pl pipeline

skills.description: Use when predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., VIBRANT/VirSorter output) plus single- or multi-sample coverage data must be binned into vMAGs, and you need weighted-network construction, KMeans/Label Propagation refinement, and redundancy-based iteration selection.
skills.name: viral-scaffold-network-binning
skills.search_text: viral-scaffold-network-binning Use when predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., VIBRANT/VirSorter output) plus single- or multi-sample coverage data must be binned into vMAGs, and you need weighted-network construction, KMeans/Label Propagation refinement, and redundancy-based iteration selection. Input is an entire metagenome expected to contain microbial genomes — vRhyme is not meant to bin microbes and MetaBat2 outperformed it on a non-viral synthetic dataset Sequences are multiple inactive (non-replicating) prophages from the same host genome — vRhyme had difficulties separating these Input scaffolds are already circular complete viral genomes — vRhyme v1.1.0 removes these pre-binning instead of binning them http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Converts machine-learning-classified viral scaffold pairs into weighted networks of unrefined bins, refines them iteratively with MiniBatchKMeans (vRhyme v1.0) or Label Propagation (v1.1.0), and selects the best iteration by protein redundancy scoring via Mmseqs2, exploiting the observation that viruses seldom encode redundant genes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkac341
skills.summary: Converts machine-learning-classified viral scaffold pairs into weighted networks of unrefined bins, refines them iteratively with MiniBatchKMeans (vRhyme v1.0) or Label Propagation (v1.1.0), and selects the best iteration by protein redundancy scoring via Mmseqs2, exploiting the observation that viruses seldom encode redundant genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an entire metagenome expected to contain microbial genomes — vRhyme is not meant to bin microbes and MetaBat2 outperformed it on a non-viral synthetic dataset Sequences are multiple inactive (non-replicating) prophages from the same host genome — vRhyme had difficulties separating these Input scaffolds are already circular complete viral genomes — vRhyme v1.1.0 removes these pre-binning instead of binning them

skills.description: Use when benchmarking metagenome assemblies — e.g. 18 human gut nanopore samples assembled with hybrid ONT + Illumina paired-end tools — for near-complete viral sequence recovery as a biological evaluation criterion.
skills.name: viral-sequence-identification-in-assemblies
skills.search_text: viral-sequence-identification-in-assemblies Use when benchmarking metagenome assemblies — e.g. 18 human gut nanopore samples assembled with hybrid ONT + Illumina paired-end tools — for near-complete viral sequence recovery as a biological evaluation criterion. Input is raw reads rather than cleaned metagenome assembly scaffolds — viral identification is an assembly evaluation step, not a read-level step The analysis goal is reference-based characterization; this study focuses on de novo methods and reference information was not well examined Assemblies have not had human contaminant scaffolds removed, since evaluation must be performed on cleaned assemblies http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Identifies near-complete viral sequences within metagenome assembly scaffolds to quantify how well different assemblers (MetaPlatanus, metaFlye, MEGAHIT, OPERA-MS) recover biologically important elements from human gut nanopore data. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nar/gkab831
skills.summary: Identifies near-complete viral sequences within metagenome assembly scaffolds to quantify how well different assemblers (MetaPlatanus, metaFlye, MEGAHIT, OPERA-MS) recover biologically important elements from human gut nanopore data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than cleaned metagenome assembly scaffolds — viral identification is an assembly evaluation step, not a read-level step The analysis goal is reference-based characterization; this study focuses on de novo methods and reference information was not well examined Assemblies have not had human contaminant scaffolds removed, since evaluation must be performed on cleaned assemblies

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end virome reads with uneven genome coverage must be dereplicated and digitally normalized to default parameters prior to de-novo and mapping assembly in a VirMAP classification run.
skills.name: viral-sequence-read-normalization
skills.search_text: viral-sequence-read-normalization Use when raw paired-end virome reads with uneven genome coverage must be dereplicated and digitally normalized to default parameters prior to de-novo and mapping assembly in a VirMAP classification run. The input reads are already dereplicated and digitally normalized — rerunning bbnorm would further reduce coverage needed for a quality assembly. The analysis goal is taxonomic classification only on pre-assembled contigs or marker genes, not on raw reads, since normalization is a pre-assembly step of the read-based VirMAP pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Dereplication and digital normalization of raw viral metagenomic reads (e.g., SRR9875293 from the Viral Mock Community PRJNA431646) using BBMap's bbnorm, as enabled by the --useBbnorm flag of Virmap.pl, to even out coverage before multi-kmer de-novo assembly with MEGAHIT. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Dereplication and digital normalization of raw viral metagenomic reads (e.g., SRR9875293 from the Viral Mock Community PRJNA431646) using BBMap's bbnorm, as enabled by the --useBbnorm flag of Virmap.pl, to even out coverage before multi-kmer de-novo assembly with MEGAHIT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input reads are already dereplicated and digitally normalized — rerunning bbnorm would further reduce coverage needed for a quality assembly. The analysis goal is taxonomic classification only on pre-assembled contigs or marker genes, not on raw reads, since normalization is a pre-assembly step of the read-based VirMAP pipeline.

skills.description: Use when assembled viral contigs or vOTUs (e.g. from MAG-derived metagenomic assemblies) need family-, genus-, species- or type-level taxonomic labels, or when viral OTU clusters must be typed against a reference set such as NCBI RefSeq.
skills.name: viral-taxonomic-annotation
skills.search_text: viral-taxonomic-annotation Use when assembled viral contigs or vOTUs (e.g. from MAG-derived metagenomic assemblies) need family-, genus-, species- or type-level taxonomic labels, or when viral OTU clusters must be typed against a reference set such as NCBI RefSeq. When input is raw reads rather than assembled viral contigs — taxonomic profiling of reads is handled separately (e.g. Kraken2/Bracken against customized databases) When the goal is host prediction rather than taxonomic annotation (use the virusHost.sh host-assignment step) When viral genomes lack the type-defining locus (e.g. no L1 gene), identity-threshold typing cannot be applied and genomes must remain 'unidentified' types http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assigns taxonomy to assembled viral genomes/vOTUs using combined feature- and homology-based identification plus family- and type-level annotation against reference databases, as applied to the 14,224 viral genomes in the VMGC (e.g. classifying 627 Papillomaviridae genomes into 61 vOTUs and 58 HPV types via L1 gene identities). metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Assigns taxonomy to assembled viral genomes/vOTUs using combined feature- and homology-based identification plus family- and type-level annotation against reference databases, as applied to the 14,224 viral genomes in the VMGC (e.g. classifying 627 Papillomaviridae genomes into 61 vOTUs and 58 HPV types via L1 gene identities).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When input is raw reads rather than assembled viral contigs — taxonomic profiling of reads is handled separately (e.g. Kraken2/Bracken against customized databases) When the goal is host prediction rather than taxonomic annotation (use the virusHost.sh host-assignment step) When viral genomes lack the type-defining locus (e.g. no L1 gene), identity-threshold typing cannot be applied and genomes must remain 'unidentified' types

skills.description: Use when improved dual-assembly viral contigs need taxonomic labels and read-level or simple BLAST--hit classification is expected to fail due to low coverage, divergent viruses, or ambiguous mapping.
skills.name: viral-taxonomic-classification
skills.search_text: viral-taxonomic-classification Use when improved dual-assembly viral contigs need taxonomic labels and read-level or simple BLAST--hit classification is expected to fail due to low coverage, divergent viruses, or ambiguous mapping. Input is a set of unassembled reads requiring taxonomic binning only (VirMAP classifies reconstructed contigs, not individual reads) The analysis target is non-viral taxa or host/microbiome classification outside the viral superkingdom Genome coverage is high and non-divergent, making a standard MEGAHIT+BLASTn/BLASTx approach sufficient (VirMAP's advantage is largest for low coverage and divergent viruses) http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Taxonomic classification of reconstructed viral contigs using VirMAP's two-pass bits-per-base scoring system, which merges nucleotide (BBMap) and translated/protein (DIAMOND) alignment information against the Genbank viral/phage database before rank-wise LCA assignment. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Taxonomic classification of reconstructed viral contigs using VirMAP's two-pass bits-per-base scoring system, which merges nucleotide (BBMap) and translated/protein (DIAMOND) alignment information against the Genbank viral/phage database before rank-wise LCA assignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a set of unassembled reads requiring taxonomic binning only (VirMAP classifies reconstructed contigs, not individual reads) The analysis target is non-viral taxa or host/microbiome classification outside the viral superkingdom Genome coverage is high and non-divergent, making a standard MEGAHIT+BLASTn/BLASTx approach sufficient (VirMAP's advantage is largest for low coverage and divergent viruses)

skills.description: Use when metagenomic paired-end FASTQ data must be classified to viral taxa and reconstructed into virus-like super-scaffolds, especially with low-coverage or highly divergent viruses that defeat read-only classifiers.
skills.name: viral-taxonomic-classification-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: viral-taxonomic-classification-pipeline-execution Use when metagenomic paired-end FASTQ data must be classified to viral taxa and reconstructed into virus-like super-scaffolds, especially with low-coverage or highly divergent viruses that defeat read-only classifiers. Input is already a classified feature table or taxonomy assignments rather than raw metagenomic FASTQ reads The question only requires individual-read or kmer-based classification without reconstruction — VirMAP's mapping assembly and improvement algorithms are designed for reconstruction-plus-classification RAM/SSD resources cannot accommodate the Genbank-based databases (minimum SSD and RAM requirements grow as Genbank expands) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Executes the VirMAP Perl pipeline (Virmap.pl) to taxonomically classify viral reconstructions from metagenomic paired-end FASTQ reads, merging nucleotide and protein alignments against Genbank viral/phage databases. It combines de-novo (MEGAHIT) and mapping assembly (BBMap), read assignment with Jaccard-distance filtering, and a bits-per-base LCA scoring system. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-018-05658-8
skills.summary: Executes the VirMAP Perl pipeline (Virmap.pl) to taxonomically classify viral reconstructions from metagenomic paired-end FASTQ reads, merging nucleotide and protein alignments against Genbank viral/phage databases. It combines de-novo (MEGAHIT) and mapping assembly (BBMap), read assignment with Jaccard-distance filtering, and a bits-per-base LCA scoring system.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a classified feature table or taxonomy assignments rather than raw metagenomic FASTQ reads The question only requires individual-read or kmer-based classification without reconstruction — VirMAP's mapping assembly and improvement algorithms are designed for reconstruction-plus-classification RAM/SSD resources cannot accommodate the Genbank-based databases (minimum SSD and RAM requirements grow as Genbank expands)

skills.description: Use when viral contigs predicted from shotgun viral metagenomes (VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder output) need genus- or family-level taxonomic labels in a ViroProfiler run.
skills.name: viral-taxonomy-annotation
skills.search_text: viral-taxonomy-annotation Use when viral contigs predicted from shotgun viral metagenomes (VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder output) need genus- or family-level taxonomic labels in a ViroProfiler run. Samples contain isolated viruses rather than metagenomic data — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses is not its target use Sequences are heavily contaminated with non-viral material — excessive environmental contaminations in metagenome sequences could increase running time and result in lower precision Input contigs are shorter than 10 kbp — they are filtered out before taxonomy assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Assign taxonomy to viral contigs/bins in ViroProfiler by combining vConTACT2 clustering (genus-level viral clusters) with MMseqs2 homology-based calls against NCBI viral RefSeq, reconciled by LCA voting and normalised with TaxonKit. metagenomics/v1 10.1080/19490976.2023.2192522
skills.summary: Assign taxonomy to viral contigs/bins in ViroProfiler by combining vConTACT2 clustering (genus-level viral clusters) with MMseqs2 homology-based calls against NCBI viral RefSeq, reconciled by LCA voting and normalised with TaxonKit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples contain isolated viruses rather than metagenomic data — ViroProfiler is specifically designed for classifying viruses in samples with isolated viruses is not its target use Sequences are heavily contaminated with non-viral material — excessive environmental contaminations in metagenome sequences could increase running time and result in lower precision Input contigs are shorter than 10 kbp — they are filtered out before taxonomy assignment

skills.description: Use when the input is quality-controlled shotgun/VLP virome FASTQ reads (e.g., infant gut metagenomes) and the goal is assembled contigs, vOTU counts, per-miner overlap comparison, or vOTU-level ORF statistics.
skills.name: virome-assembly-contig-analysis
skills.search_text: virome-assembly-contig-analysis Use when the input is quality-controlled shotgun/VLP virome FASTQ reads (e.g., infant gut metagenomes) and the goal is assembled contigs, vOTU counts, per-miner overlap comparison, or vOTU-level ORF statistics. Input is already a dereplicated vOTU multifasta or a feature/abundance table rather than raw reads or assembled contigs The dataset is not a virome (e.g., bulk metagenome with abundant host scaffolds) where the --virome sensitivity setting for removing nonviral scaffolds may be inappropriate The goal is taxonomic classification/network analysis of known vOTUs via vConTACT2 rather than vOTU discovery and miner comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assemble quality-controlled virome reads into contigs with MEGAHIT and convert them into dereplicated vOTUs using the MetaPhage pipeline's multiple phage miners (VirFinder, VirSorter, Phigaro, VIBRANT) plus CD-HIT-EST clustering, enabling per-miner comparison of viral contig discovery on virome datasets. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Assemble quality-controlled virome reads into contigs with MEGAHIT and convert them into dereplicated vOTUs using the MetaPhage pipeline's multiple phage miners (VirFinder, VirSorter, Phigaro, VIBRANT) plus CD-HIT-EST clustering, enabling per-miner comparison of viral contig discovery on virome datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a dereplicated vOTU multifasta or a feature/abundance table rather than raw reads or assembled contigs The dataset is not a virome (e.g., bulk metagenome with abundant host scaffolds) where the --virome sensitivity setting for removing nonviral scaffolds may be inappropriate The goal is taxonomic classification/network analysis of known vOTUs via vConTACT2 rather than vOTU discovery and miner comparison

skills.description: Use when you need to benchmark the computational tractability (wall-clock runtime and peak memory) of a trait-prediction pipeline at training-set sizes beyond your real labeled data, by simulating genomes with realistic feature-matrix dimensions.
skills.name: virtual-species-genome-simulation
skills.search_text: virtual-species-genome-simulation Use when you need to benchmark the computational tractability (wall-clock runtime and peak memory) of a trait-prediction pipeline at training-set sizes beyond your real labeled data, by simulating genomes with realistic feature-matrix dimensions. Your goal is to measure predictive accuracy on real genomes with real trait labels — this simulation uses random labels and yields no biological performance estimate Your feature matrix is far smaller than the eggNOG 4.0-scale dimensions (~200,000 COGs); smaller feature spaces will not exercise the scalability limits this benchmark targets You are using the successor phenotrex/scikit-learn stack rather than PICA's libSVM plug-in; the runtime envelope measured here applies to PICA's SVM backend, not the newer classifiers (e.g. XGBoost) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates synthetic 'virtual species' genotype profiles inside PICA by randomly sampling features from a pool of ~200,000 virtual COGs and assigning random trait labels, then benchmarks SVM cross-validation runtime and memory as training sets scale toward 5,000 genomes. This establishes the computational feasibility envelope of PICA's libSVM-backed phenotype prediction at large-genome-database scale (Figure 4 of the paper). metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-16-s14-s1
skills.summary: Generates synthetic 'virtual species' genotype profiles inside PICA by randomly sampling features from a pool of ~200,000 virtual COGs and assigning random trait labels, then benchmarks SVM cross-validation runtime and memory as training sets scale toward 5,000 genomes. This establishes the computational feasibility envelope of PICA's libSVM-backed phenotype prediction at large-genome-database scale (Figure 4 of the paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to measure predictive accuracy on real genomes with real trait labels — this simulation uses random labels and yields no biological performance estimate Your feature matrix is far smaller than the eggNOG 4.0-scale dimensions (~200,000 COGs); smaller feature spaces will not exercise the scalability limits this benchmark targets You are using the successor phenotrex/scikit-learn stack rather than PICA's libSVM plug-in; the runtime envelope measured here applies to PICA's SVM backend, not the newer classifiers (e.g. XGBoost)

skills.description: Use when a binary virus-host association matrix Y is available and you need interaction-profile-based host-host (or virus-virus) kernel similarity to feed into similarity network fusion or kernelized matrix factorization.
skills.name: virus-host-adjacency-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: virus-host-adjacency-matrix-processing Use when a binary virus-host association matrix Y is available and you need interaction-profile-based host-host (or virus-virus) kernel similarity to feed into similarity network fusion or kernelized matrix factorization. When only virus oligonucleotide frequency (d2*) dissimilarity data is available and no known virus-host associations exist — the GIP kernel requires the adjacency matrix's interaction profiles When the goal is virus-virus similarity, which in ILMF-VH is computed from oligonucleotide frequency (Jie Ren's d2* tools) rather than from interaction profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Processes the binary virus-host adjacency matrix Y (rows = viruses, columns = hosts) to derive host-host similarity via the Gaussian interaction profile (GIP) kernel, where each host's interaction profile is a column of Y. This supplies the interaction-profile-based similarity that similarity network fusion combines with oligonucleotide frequency similarity in the ILMF-VH pipeline. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Processes the binary virus-host adjacency matrix Y (rows = viruses, columns = hosts) to derive host-host similarity via the Gaussian interaction profile (GIP) kernel, where each host's interaction profile is a column of Y. This supplies the interaction-profile-based similarity that similarity network fusion combines with oligonucleotide frequency similarity in the ILMF-VH pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only virus oligonucleotide frequency (d2*) dissimilarity data is available and no known virus-host associations exist — the GIP kernel requires the adjacency matrix's interaction profiles When the goal is virus-virus similarity, which in ILMF-VH is computed from oligonucleotide frequency (Jie Ren's d2* tools) rather than from interaction profiles

skills.description: Use when you need to rank candidate hosts for uncultured phage/virus genomes from sequence data alone, given a known virus-host association matrix plus virus-virus and host-host similarity networks.
skills.name: virus-host-association-prediction
skills.search_text: virus-host-association-prediction Use when you need to rank candidate hosts for uncultured phage/virus genomes from sequence data alone, given a known virus-host association matrix plus virus-virus and host-host similarity networks. The query virus's host is absent from the host genome database — sequence-homology/oligonucleotide-based similarity signals are limited in this case, as noted in the article's limitations You already have direct biological evidence of virus-host interaction (e.g. cultured infection data) — a prediction method is unnecessary The task is genus-level-only prediction with an ONF-based method already sufficient; ILMF-VH targets improving species-level accuracy, which prior ONF methods achieved at less than 40% http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Culture-free prediction of bacteriophage hosts using ILMF-VH: kernelized logistic matrix factorization with neighborhood regularization applied to a virus-host heterogeneous network built from oligonucleotide-frequency (d2*) virus similarity, SNF-fused host similarity, and known associations. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Culture-free prediction of bacteriophage hosts using ILMF-VH: kernelized logistic matrix factorization with neighborhood regularization applied to a virus-host heterogeneous network built from oligonucleotide-frequency (d2*) virus similarity, SNF-fused host similarity, and known associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query virus's host is absent from the host genome database — sequence-homology/oligonucleotide-based similarity signals are limited in this case, as noted in the article's limitations You already have direct biological evidence of virus-host interaction (e.g. cultured infection data) — a prediction method is unnecessary The task is genus-level-only prediction with an ONF-based method already sufficient; ILMF-VH targets improving species-level accuracy, which prior ONF methods achieved at less than 40%

skills.description: Use when you have metagenomic Hi-C data (name-sorted BAM aligned to assembled contigs), identified viral contigs and host MAGs, and need to determine which phages infect which host MAGs and validate those pairings independently.
skills.name: virus-host-linkage-detection-from-hi-c
skills.search_text: virus-host-linkage-detection-from-hi-c Use when you have metagenomic Hi-C data (name-sorted BAM aligned to assembled contigs), identified viral contigs and host MAGs, and need to determine which phages infect which host MAGs and validate those pairings independently. No Hi-C (proximity-ligation) data are available — virus-host inference must then rely on co-abundance (CoCoNet, vRhyme) or CRISPR spacers alone Contigs are short and sparse Hi-C signal is expected without a complementary information source; ViralCC explicitly leverages the host proximity graph to compensate for the sparse Hi-C interaction map You only need viral genome binning without host assignment — virus-host linkage steps are unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Infers and validates virus-host MAG pairs from metagenomic Hi-C data by linking ViralCC viral bins to HiCBin host MAG contigs through the normalized Hi-C linkage graph, then cross-validating the pairs with CRISPR spacer-protospacer matches (PILER-CR + BLAST). This is the core application that turns Hi-C proximity-ligation signal into a phage-host network. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Infers and validates virus-host MAG pairs from metagenomic Hi-C data by linking ViralCC viral bins to HiCBin host MAG contigs through the normalized Hi-C linkage graph, then cross-validating the pairs with CRISPR spacer-protospacer matches (PILER-CR + BLAST). This is the core application that turns Hi-C proximity-ligation signal into a phage-host network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No Hi-C (proximity-ligation) data are available — virus-host inference must then rely on co-abundance (CoCoNet, vRhyme) or CRISPR spacers alone Contigs are short and sparse Hi-C signal is expected without a complementary information source; ViralCC explicitly leverages the host proximity graph to compensate for the sparse Hi-C interaction map You only need viral genome binning without host assignment — virus-host linkage steps are unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when binning viral contigs from metagenomic Hi-C data and you need to build a virus-host proximity graph from shared host contacts to complement the sparse Hi-C interaction graph.
skills.name: virus-host-proximity-graph-construction
skills.search_text: virus-host-proximity-graph-construction Use when binning viral contigs from metagenomic Hi-C data and you need to build a virus-host proximity graph from shared host contacts to complement the sparse Hi-C interaction graph. Input Hi-C BAM is not name-sorted — the pipeline requires 'samtools sort' by read name No viral contig list is available or contigs are shorter than the --min-len default of 1000 bp The analysis goal is taxonomic classification of viral contigs from sequence homology rather than Hi-C-based binning http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Constructs ViralCC's host proximity graph, in which two viral contigs are linked when they share at least k host contigs contacted via Hi-C interactions, with k chosen automatically so the proximity signal complements rather than overwhelms the Hi-C interaction signal. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Constructs ViralCC's host proximity graph, in which two viral contigs are linked when they share at least k host contigs contacted via Hi-C interactions, with k chosen automatically so the proximity signal complements rather than overwhelms the Hi-C interaction signal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input Hi-C BAM is not name-sorted — the pipeline requires 'samtools sort' by read name No viral contig list is available or contigs are shorter than the --min-len default of 1000 bp The analysis goal is taxonomic classification of viral contigs from sequence homology rather than Hi-C-based binning

skills.description: Use when a newly sequenced phage genome (e.g., an NCBI accession not in the 820-virus RefSeq benchmark) must be added as a node to an existing virus similarity network before virus-host association prediction.
skills.name: virus-similarity-network-augmentation
skills.search_text: virus-similarity-network-augmentation Use when a newly sequenced phage genome (e.g., an NCBI accession not in the 820-virus RefSeq benchmark) must be added as a node to an existing virus similarity network before virus-host association prediction. The query virus's host is absent from the host genome database — the article notes homology/similarity-based host inference depends on hosts existing in the database The task is de novo host prediction from metagenomic contigs without a genome that can be aligned to the 820-virus oligonucleotide framework Abundance-profile co-variation (not sequence-based network augmentation) is the intended signal, since co-variation may reflect time-delayed dynamics rather than real interaction http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Appends a new query virus (e.g., crAssphage, JQ995537.1) as an extra node in the 820-virus oligonucleotide-frequency similarity network by computing d2* dissimilarity via Jie Ren's tools and transforming it to similarity, so kernelized logistic matrix factorization (ILMF-VH) can score it against all 2699 candidate hosts. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3082-0
skills.summary: Appends a new query virus (e.g., crAssphage, JQ995537.1) as an extra node in the 820-virus oligonucleotide-frequency similarity network by computing d2* dissimilarity via Jie Ren's tools and transforming it to similarity, so kernelized logistic matrix factorization (ILMF-VH) can score it against all 2699 candidate hosts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query virus's host is absent from the host genome database — the article notes homology/similarity-based host inference depends on hosts existing in the database The task is de novo host prediction from metagenomic contigs without a genome that can be aligned to the 820-virus oligonucleotide framework Abundance-profile co-variation (not sequence-based network augmentation) is the intended signal, since co-variation may reflect time-delayed dynamics rather than real interaction

skills.description: Use when comparing phage predictions from paired VLP-enriched and shotgun metagenome assemblies and you need to explain differences in vOTU counts via genome-quality stratification rather than raw counts.
skills.name: vlp-vs-shotgun-dataset-comparison
skills.search_text: vlp-vs-shotgun-dataset-comparison Use when comparing phage predictions from paired VLP-enriched and shotgun metagenome assemblies and you need to explain differences in vOTU counts via genome-quality stratification rather than raw counts. Input is raw reads or unassembled contigs that have not been through MetaPhage phage detection and CD-HIT-EST dereplication — CheckV quality tiers assume candidate viral contigs The analysis goal is taxonomic classification of vOTUs (e.g., vConTACT2 network placement) rather than genome completeness/quality assessment Single-dataset analysis with no VLP-vs-shotgun contrast to compute http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Reproduces the MetaPhage paper's comparison of VLP-enriched versus shotgun infant metagenomes by classifying dereplicated vOTUs with CheckV quality tiers, showing that MetaPhage's excess vOTU counts (5,284 vs 1,029 reported phage contigs) are driven by partial and low-quality genome predictions. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Reproduces the MetaPhage paper's comparison of VLP-enriched versus shotgun infant metagenomes by classifying dereplicated vOTUs with CheckV quality tiers, showing that MetaPhage's excess vOTU counts (5,284 vs 1,029 reported phage contigs) are driven by partial and low-quality genome predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or unassembled contigs that have not been through MetaPhage phage detection and CD-HIT-EST dereplication — CheckV quality tiers assume candidate viral contigs The analysis goal is taxonomic classification of vOTUs (e.g., vConTACT2 network placement) rather than genome completeness/quality assessment Single-dataset analysis with no VLP-vs-shotgun contrast to compute

skills.description: Use when you need to evaluate the quality of draft viral bins (e.g., from ViralCC, VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, MetaTOR) against ground-truth or reference genomes, specifically counting near-complete and high-quality vMAGs.
skills.name: vmag-completeness-assessment
skills.search_text: vmag-completeness-assessment Use when you need to evaluate the quality of draft viral bins (e.g., from ViralCC, VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, MetaTOR) against ground-truth or reference genomes, specifically counting near-complete and high-quality vMAGs. When the goal is to estimate contamination of vMAGs — CheckV cannot do this because no universal marker gene set exists for viruses When assessing prokaryotic MAGs — use CheckM's single-copy marker gene approach instead When the community has few putative viral genomes — the article notes benchmarking effectiveness is less convincing in that case http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Assess the completeness of recovered viral MAGs (vMAGs) produced by Hi-C-based binning using CheckV, categorizing bins as near-complete, substantially complete, or moderately complete, and pairing the counts with a random binning control since CheckV cannot estimate vMAG contamination. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-35945-y
skills.summary: Assess the completeness of recovered viral MAGs (vMAGs) produced by Hi-C-based binning using CheckV, categorizing bins as near-complete, substantially complete, or moderately complete, and pairing the counts with a random binning control since CheckV cannot estimate vMAG contamination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to estimate contamination of vMAGs — CheckV cannot do this because no universal marker gene set exists for viruses When assessing prokaryotic MAGs — use CheckM's single-copy marker gene approach instead When the community has few putative viral genomes — the article notes benchmarking effectiveness is less convincing in that case

skills.description: Use when preparing a deep-learning taxonomic classifier (e.g. DeepMicrobes Embed+LSTM+Attention) that needs a k-mer-to-integer vocabulary file feeding an embedding layer, or when building a canonical k-mer lexicon from FASTA training genomes.
skills.name: vocabulary-index-mapping-construction
skills.search_text: vocabulary-index-mapping-construction Use when preparing a deep-learning taxonomic classifier (e.g. DeepMicrobes Embed+LSTM+Attention) that needs a k-mer-to-integer vocabulary file feeding an embedding layer, or when building a canonical k-mer lexicon from FASTA training genomes. The input is already a TFRecord or a finished vocabulary file — use DeepMicrobes' fastq/fasta-to-TFRecord conversion step instead of rebuilding the vocabulary You only need a k-mer database for an alignment/LCA classifier like Kraken or Kaiju — those tools build their own databases and do not consume an embedding-layer vocabulary file You are classifying already-trained DeepMicrobes models on new reads — prediction reuses the existing vocabulary and does not require reconstruction http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Construct the canonical k-mer vocabulary for DeepMicrobes by counting k-mers over the training genome corpus with Jellyfish in canonicalization mode (-C), then assign each distinct canonical k-mer a unique integer index that backs the embedding layer, reserving index 0 for padding and using <unk> for k-mers containing ambiguous N bases. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa009
skills.summary: Construct the canonical k-mer vocabulary for DeepMicrobes by counting k-mers over the training genome corpus with Jellyfish in canonicalization mode (-C), then assign each distinct canonical k-mer a unique integer index that backs the embedding layer, reserving index 0 for padding and using <unk> for k-mers containing ambiguous N bases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a TFRecord or a finished vocabulary file — use DeepMicrobes' fastq/fasta-to-TFRecord conversion step instead of rebuilding the vocabulary You only need a k-mer database for an alignment/LCA classifier like Kraken or Kaiju — those tools build their own databases and do not consume an embedding-layer vocabulary file You are classifying already-trained DeepMicrobes models on new reads — prediction reuses the existing vocabulary and does not require reconstruction

skills.description: Use when you have a set of quality-filtered viral contigs/genomes (e.g. CheckV-screened FASTA) and need to dereplicate them into species-level vOTUs and quantify overlap with reference virome catalogues.
skills.name: votu-definition-at-nucleotide-identity-thresholds
skills.search_text: votu-definition-at-nucleotide-identity-thresholds Use when you have a set of quality-filtered viral contigs/genomes (e.g. CheckV-screened FASTA) and need to dereplicate them into species-level vOTUs and quantify overlap with reference virome catalogues. Input is raw metagenomic contigs that have not been screened for viral origin and completeness (run virus identification and CheckV-quality filtering first) The goal is prokaryotic species dereplication — the paper clusters those separately at 95% nucleotide similarity into SGBs, not vOTUs Only amino-acid-level gene clustering is needed (VMGC-50/90/95 gene catalogues) rather than whole-genome nucleotide clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Defines species-level viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) by all-vs-all nucleotide comparison of quality-filtered viral genomes, clustering at 95% identity over 85% of the genome — in the VMGC study this reduced 14,224 viral genomes (>=50% completeness by CheckV) to 4,263 vOTUs whose novelty against external virome databases was then quantified. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41564-024-01751-5
skills.summary: Defines species-level viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) by all-vs-all nucleotide comparison of quality-filtered viral genomes, clustering at 95% identity over 85% of the genome — in the VMGC study this reduced 14,224 viral genomes (>=50% completeness by CheckV) to 4,263 vOTUs whose novelty against external virome databases was then quantified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw metagenomic contigs that have not been screened for viral origin and completeness (run virus identification and CheckV-quality filtering first) The goal is prokaryotic species dereplication — the paper clusters those separately at 95% nucleotide similarity into SGBs, not vOTUs Only amino-acid-level gene clustering is needed (VMGC-50/90/95 gene catalogues) rather than whole-genome nucleotide clustering

skills.description: Use when you have multi-FASTA viral scaffolds merged from several phage miners (e.g. VirFinder, VirSorter, Phigaro, VIBRANT) and need to reduce redundancy to species-level vOTUs before counting, overlap analysis, or classification.
skills.name: votu-dereplication-clustering
skills.search_text: votu-dereplication-clustering Use when you have multi-FASTA viral scaffolds merged from several phage miners (e.g. VirFinder, VirSorter, Phigaro, VIBRANT) and need to reduce redundancy to species-level vOTUs before counting, overlap analysis, or classification. Input is raw reads or unfiltered assembled contigs that have not yet passed phage mining — clustering should act on miner-predicted viral scaffolds only Short viral scaffolds below the minimum length cutoff are of interest — the --minlen filter (e.g. 3000 bp) will discard them A strain-level (>95% ANI) clustering granularity is required — the 0.95/0.85 parameters correspond to phage species-level vOTUs http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Dereplicates viral scaffolds predicted by multiple phage miners into viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) using CD-HIT-EST at the phage species level (0.95 sequence identity, word size 9, 0.85 alignment coverage), with a minimum consensus scaffold length filter (e.g. --minlen 3000). metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00741-22
skills.summary: Dereplicates viral scaffolds predicted by multiple phage miners into viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) using CD-HIT-EST at the phage species level (0.95 sequence identity, word size 9, 0.85 alignment coverage), with a minimum consensus scaffold length filter (e.g. --minlen 3000).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or unfiltered assembled contigs that have not yet passed phage mining — clustering should act on miner-predicted viral scaffolds only Short viral scaffolds below the minimum length cutoff are of interest — the --minlen filter (e.g. 3000 bp) will discard them A strain-level (>95% ANI) clustering granularity is required — the 0.95/0.85 parameters correspond to phage species-level vOTUs

skills.description: Use when raw FASTQ/Illumina reads contain a small set of seed reads of interest (e.g. HMM-derived cas-gene hits or CRISPR array repeats) and neighboring reads must be recruited to enable targeted assembly without assembling the full dataset.

skills.search_text: vsearch-read-identity-recruitment Use when raw FASTQ/Illumina reads contain a small set of seed reads of interest (e.g. HMM-derived cas-gene hits or CRISPR array repeats) and neighboring reads must be recruited to enable targeted assembly without assembling the full dataset. Input is already an assembled contig set or a feature/annotation table — this skill operates on raw unassembled FASTQ reads only The target gene set has no usable seed (no HMM hits, no reference FASTA repeats/genes) — the expansion stage requires an initial seed read set to prime recruitment Full de novo assembly of the complete metagenome/genome is required rather than targeted recovery of a specific operon or locus http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Iterative VSEARCH-based identity matching that expands a small set of seed reads (e.g. cas-gene or CRISPR-array hits from CasCollect) into a larger read subset from raw FASTQ data, recruiting neighboring reads at a 95% identity threshold over repeated cycles. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Iterative VSEARCH-based identity matching that expands a small set of seed reads (e.g. cas-gene or CRISPR-array hits from CasCollect) into a larger read subset from raw FASTQ data, recruiting neighboring reads at a 95% identity threshold over repeated cycles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an assembled contig set or a feature/annotation table — this skill operates on raw unassembled FASTQ reads only The target gene set has no usable seed (no HMM hits, no reference FASTA repeats/genes) — the expansion stage requires an initial seed read set to prime recruitment Full de novo assembly of the complete metagenome/genome is required rather than targeted recovery of a specific operon or locus

skills.description: Use when running CasCollect's read subset expansion step to grow seed reads (matching cas gene HMM profiles or CRISPR array repeats) into a larger read subset prior to targeted SPAdes assembly.

skills.search_text: vsearch-read-subset-expansion Use when running CasCollect's read subset expansion step to grow seed reads (matching cas gene HMM profiles or CRISPR array repeats) into a larger read subset prior to targeted SPAdes assembly. Input is not raw unassembled sequencing reads (e.g. a finished genome or existing assembly) — the expansion step is designed to avoid complete assembly of raw reads DNA repeat mode when the goal is cas gene detection in protein mode, or vice versa: VSEARCH identity matching is used for user-defined CRISPR array repeats in DNA mode, while protein mode uses HMMER profiles for seeds Data are metagenomic and metagenome-scale diversity is expected to overwhelm the 95% identity threshold with strain variants, unless metaSPAdes is substituted downstream http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Iterative read-subset expansion from seed reads using VSEARCH in CasCollect: matched reads are cycled against the read database at a 95% identity threshold to grow the targeted assembly input around CRISPR/Cas loci, then assembled with SPAdes. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqaa063
skills.summary: Iterative read-subset expansion from seed reads using VSEARCH in CasCollect: matched reads are cycled against the read database at a 95% identity threshold to grow the targeted assembly input around CRISPR/Cas loci, then assembled with SPAdes.

skills.description: Use when comparing computational cost of two contact-prediction pipelines on the same pre-computed MSAs, needing measured runtimes per hardware configuration (CPU vs GPU) rather than accuracy metrics.
skills.name: wall-clock-performance-tabulation
skills.search_text: wall-clock-performance-tabulation Use when comparing computational cost of two contact-prediction pipelines on the same pre-computed MSAs, needing measured runtimes per hardware configuration (CPU vs GPU) rather than accuracy metrics. The goal is prediction accuracy evaluation (precision, TMscore of CONFOLD-built models) rather than computational cost — use an accuracy benchmarking skill instead. The input MSAs are not shared between the compared methods (e.g. RaptorX-Contact server predictions use different MSAs), making wall-clock comparisons non-commensurable. No GPU or reproducible hardware environment is available and only a single hardware configuration can be timed, so the CPU/GPU ordering cannot be tested. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Tabulates wall-clock runtimes of DeepECA DNN inference versus CCMpred precision-matrix optimization on the 150-protein PSICOV dataset, on CPU and GPU, to benchmark end-to-end deep learning against the fastest existing ECA method. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3190-x
skills.summary: Tabulates wall-clock runtimes of DeepECA DNN inference versus CCMpred precision-matrix optimization on the 150-protein PSICOV dataset, on CPU and GPU, to benchmark end-to-end deep learning against the fastest existing ECA method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is prediction accuracy evaluation (precision, TMscore of CONFOLD-built models) rather than computational cost — use an accuracy benchmarking skill instead. The input MSAs are not shared between the compared methods (e.g. RaptorX-Contact server predictions use different MSAs), making wall-clock comparisons non-commensurable. No GPU or reproducible hardware environment is available and only a single hardware configuration can be timed, so the CPU/GPU ordering cannot be tested.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking reported execution times of a Snakemake/SBATCH pipeline per dataset, e.g. to validate Mapler's 2h4m/3h46m/5h3m figures under a 48-thread, 200G allocation.
skills.name: wall-clock-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: wall-clock-runtime-benchmarking Use when reproducing or benchmarking reported execution times of a Snakemake/SBATCH pipeline per dataset, e.g. to validate Mapler's 2h4m/3h46m/5h3m figures under a 48-thread, 200G allocation. The goal is assembly or binning quality (completeness/contamination, mapped read ratios), not runtime measurement — use Mapler's evaluation outputs instead. Only a quick installation check is needed — the README's test dataset with 16 CPUs / 15G RAM (~15 minutes) is the appropriate lightweight path, not the full three-dataset benchmark. Runs use different thread/memory allocations than the reported 48 CPU / 200G, making wall-clock times non-comparable to the reference durations. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of the Mapler Snakemake pipeline (assembly with metaMDBG, metaflye, hifiasm-meta plus evaluation) on the Mock community, Gut microbiome, and Deadwood HiFi datasets under a fixed 48 CPU / 200G SLURM allocation, and compare measured durations against reference values (2 h 4 min, 3 h 46 min, 5 h 3 min). metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf334
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of the Mapler Snakemake pipeline (assembly with metaMDBG, metaflye, hifiasm-meta plus evaluation) on the Mock community, Gut microbiome, and Deadwood HiFi datasets under a fixed 48 CPU / 200G SLURM allocation, and compare measured durations against reference values (2 h 4 min, 3 h 46 min, 5 h 3 min).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is assembly or binning quality (completeness/contamination, mapped read ratios), not runtime measurement — use Mapler's evaluation outputs instead. Only a quick installation check is needed — the README's test dataset with 16 CPUs / 15G RAM (~15 minutes) is the appropriate lightweight path, not the full three-dataset benchmark. Runs use different thread/memory allocations than the reported 48 CPU / 200G, making wall-clock times non-comparable to the reference durations.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or re-verifying runtime benchmark claims for Plassembler vs Unicycler, e.g. from run logs/timing records in Zenodo record 7996690, or when measuring assembler speedup across thread counts.
skills.name: wallclock-speedup-quantification
skills.search_text: wallclock-speedup-quantification Use when reproducing or re-verifying runtime benchmark claims for Plassembler vs Unicycler, e.g. from run logs/timing records in Zenodo record 7996690, or when measuring assembler speedup across thread counts. Evaluating assembly accuracy rather than runtime — the article's accuracy claims (e.g. missed plasmid counts, the linear plasmid misassembly in K. variicola) require assembly comparison, not timing records Comparing against assemblers other than Unicycler (e.g. Dragonflye) — no timing records for those tools are present in the deposited benchmarking outputs Input read sets differ from the benchmarked ones (e.g. simulated R9 vs R10), since the article notes such comparisons are 'not truly a fair comparison' http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies wall-clock runtime (and peak memory) speedup of Plassembler (Flye or Raven modes) versus Unicycler across 20 simulated and 6 real read sets at 1, 8, and 16 threads, verifying the paper's 3- to 10-fold improvement claim using deposited Zenodo benchmarking outputs. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad409
skills.summary: Quantifies wall-clock runtime (and peak memory) speedup of Plassembler (Flye or Raven modes) versus Unicycler across 20 simulated and 6 real read sets at 1, 8, and 16 threads, verifying the paper's 3- to 10-fold improvement claim using deposited Zenodo benchmarking outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating assembly accuracy rather than runtime — the article's accuracy claims (e.g. missed plasmid counts, the linear plasmid misassembly in K. variicola) require assembly comparison, not timing records Comparing against assemblers other than Unicycler (e.g. Dragonflye) — no timing records for those tools are present in the deposited benchmarking outputs Input read sets differ from the benchmarked ones (e.g. simulated R9 vs R10), since the article notes such comparisons are 'not truly a fair comparison'

skills.name: wastewater-lineage-time-series-analysis
skills.search_text: wastewater-lineage-time-series-analysis Use when you have variant calls (VCFs) from multiple sequenced wastewater time-point samples and need to infer per-sample lineage distributions and visualize how one lineage's abundance changes over time. skills.name: wastewater-ngs-read-alignment
skills.search_text: wastewater-ngs-read-alignment Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater sequencing (e.g., ENA study PRJEB44141) must be mapped to the SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan reference NC_045512 before low-frequency variant calling. Input is already a VCF from variant calling — this skill operates upstream on FASTQ reads Reads are single-end or contain unmatched/multiple mappings that cannot be filtered to paired-end pairs The target organism or reference is not the SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan genome NC_045512 (e.g., host or metagenomic assembly workflows) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns cleaned paired-end NGS reads from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater samples to the Wuhan reference genome NC_045512 using Minimap2 with a minimal chaining score of 40, as a variation of the Illumina ARTIC pipeline, to prepare BAM alignments for downstream variant calling with freebayes, mpileup, or GATK Mutect2. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: Aligns cleaned paired-end NGS reads from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater samples to the Wuhan reference genome NC_045512 using Minimap2 with a minimal chaining score of 40, as a variation of the Illumina ARTIC pipeline, to prepare BAM alignments for downstream variant calling with freebayes, mpileup, or GATK Mutect2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a VCF from variant calling — this skill operates upstream on FASTQ reads Reads are single-end or contain unmatched/multiple mappings that cannot be filtered to paired-end pairs The target organism or reference is not the SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan genome NC_045512 (e.g., host or metagenomic assembly workflows)

skills.description: Use when analyzing NGS wastewater sequencing reads to detect SARS-CoV-2 mutations below 0.01 frequency and infer the distribution of lineages (e.g., Alpha/B.1.1.7) across sampling periods.
skills.name: wastewater-surveillance-variant-analysis
skills.search_text: wastewater-surveillance-variant-analysis Use when analyzing NGS wastewater sequencing reads to detect SARS-CoV-2 mutations below 0.01 frequency and infer the distribution of lineages (e.g., Alpha/B.1.1.7) across sampling periods. When input is clinical isolate consensus genomes already assigned by Pangolin rather than low-frequency wastewater VCFs When the goal is de novo assembly or consensus-genome calling rather than detecting mutations below 0.01 allele frequency in mixed samples When no reference genome/annotation is available to match nucleotide mutations to genes and amino-acid substitutions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 A pipeline for detecting SARS-CoV-2 mutations and inferring lineage abundance in wastewater NGS data, built around the lineagespot R framework that matches freebayes-called low-frequency variants against lineage-characteristic mutation profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41598-022-06625-6
skills.summary: A pipeline for detecting SARS-CoV-2 mutations and inferring lineage abundance in wastewater NGS data, built around the lineagespot R framework that matches freebayes-called low-frequency variants against lineage-characteristic mutation profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When input is clinical isolate consensus genomes already assigned by Pangolin rather than low-frequency wastewater VCFs When the goal is de novo assembly or consensus-genome calling rather than detecting mutations below 0.01 allele frequency in mixed samples When no reference genome/annotation is available to match nucleotide mutations to genes and amino-acid substitutions

skills.description: Use when wastewater-inferred lineage calls (e.g., from lineagespot on VCF inputs) must be compared against clinical WGS lineage assignments from the same area and time windows to assess surveillance agreement.
skills.name: wastewater-vs-clinical-lineage-agreement-quantification
