skills.summary: A validation skill that quantifies how well SARS-CoV-2 lineages inferred by lineagespot from wastewater samples align with predominant patient-derived lineages (Pangolin-assigned) across matched time periods, reproducing the paper's qualitative assessment over 14 Thessaloniki sampling periods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is exact lineage-frequency reconstruction per sample rather than qualitative agreement with predominant clinical lineages — the paper's assessment is explicitly qualitative Clinical lineage calls for the same area and time periods are unavailable, so no matched comparison can be made Input variant calls were not produced under the lineagespot methodology (e.g., Pangolin run directly on wastewater consensus genomes), as the Pangolin-rule matching on wastewater reads can mis-assign lineages

skills.description: Use when a metatranscriptome analysis pipeline depends on an external web annotation service (e.g., MG-RAST as in SAMSA 1.0), or when a web-service runtime/accuracy baseline is needed to compare against a standalone pipeline.
skills.name: web-service-metatranscriptome-annotation
skills.search_text: web-service-metatranscriptome-annotation Use when a metatranscriptome analysis pipeline depends on an external web annotation service (e.g., MG-RAST as in SAMSA 1.0), or when a web-service runtime/accuracy baseline is needed to compare against a standalone pipeline. Input files contain millions of sequences per sample and a fast, fully controllable local pipeline is required — web services may become oversubscribed and slow Custom reference databases must be mapped against — MG-RAST and COMAN do not support custom reference databases Maximum reproducibility is required — the web service's software and database are not under user control http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Annotates metatranscriptome sequence files by submitting them to a web-based service such as MG-RAST, which performs the annotation remotely. Used here as the SAMSA 1.0 baseline against which standalone pipelines like SAMSA2 are benchmarked for runtime and accuracy. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-018-2189-z
skills.summary: Annotates metatranscriptome sequence files by submitting them to a web-based service such as MG-RAST, which performs the annotation remotely. Used here as the SAMSA 1.0 baseline against which standalone pipelines like SAMSA2 are benchmarked for runtime and accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input files contain millions of sequences per sample and a fast, fully controllable local pipeline is required — web services may become oversubscribed and slow Custom reference databases must be mapped against — MG-RAST and COMAN do not support custom reference databases Maximum reproducibility is required — the web service's software and database are not under user control

skills.description: Use when Nano2NGS-Muta has produced per-set mutation detection results from N extracted short-read sets and final target hotspot mutation calls must be integrated and checked against a complete check-hotspot.list.
skills.name: weighted-hotspot-mutation-result-integration
skills.search_text: weighted-hotspot-mutation-result-integration Use when Nano2NGS-Muta has produced per-set mutation detection results from N extracted short-read sets and final target hotspot mutation calls must be integrated and checked against a complete check-hotspot.list. Input is already conventional short-read NGS data with no nanopore long-read conversion step — no extraction sets exist to integrate. The goal is unbiased genome-wide variant discovery rather than detection of mutations in a predefined hotspot panel; Nano2NGS-Muta is designed for hotspot panel detection (e.g. clinical diagnosis). Reads need base-level error correction before calling — the framework only converts long reads into a set of short reads with no error correction for reads and/or bases. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Integrates hotspot mutation calls from N NGS-liked short-read sets extracted from nanopore reads using a weighted-sum equation with position-based weights that sum to 1, filtering results not detected across the extracted datasets to produce final hotspot mutation calls. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/nargab/lqac033
skills.summary: Integrates hotspot mutation calls from N NGS-liked short-read sets extracted from nanopore reads using a weighted-sum equation with position-based weights that sum to 1, filtering results not detected across the extracted datasets to produce final hotspot mutation calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already conventional short-read NGS data with no nanopore long-read conversion step — no extraction sets exist to integrate. The goal is unbiased genome-wide variant discovery rather than detection of mutations in a predefined hotspot panel; Nano2NGS-Muta is designed for hotspot panel detection (e.g. clinical diagnosis). Reads need base-level error correction before calling — the framework only converts long reads into a set of short reads with no error correction for reads and/or bases.

skills.description: Use when comparing feature/OTU tables generated by alternative DC methods (vsearch closed/open/de novo at 0.97, DADA2, Deblur) on 16S data, or benchmarking a method against a known mock-community composition on a reference phylogeny.
skills.name: weighted-unifrac-distance-computation
skills.search_text: weighted-unifrac-distance-computation Use when comparing feature/OTU tables generated by alternative DC methods (vsearch closed/open/de novo at 0.97, DADA2, Deblur) on 16S data, or benchmarking a method against a known mock-community composition on a reference phylogeny. Input is raw reads with no feature/OTU table and reference phylogeny yet — the DC step and tree building must precede UniFrac computation The comparison depends only on presence/absence of low-abundance taxa and abundance weighting should be ignored — unweighted UniFrac is the appropriate metric instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0637 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Compute abundance-weighted, phylogeny-aware UniFrac distances between representative-sequence (feature) distributions produced by different denoising/clustering methods or against expected mock-community compositions, to quantify how faithfully each DC method recapitulates true community sequences. metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00961-22
skills.summary: Compute abundance-weighted, phylogeny-aware UniFrac distances between representative-sequence (feature) distributions produced by different denoising/clustering methods or against expected mock-community compositions, to quantify how faithfully each DC method recapitulates true community sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads with no feature/OTU table and reference phylogeny yet — the DC step and tree building must precede UniFrac computation The comparison depends only on presence/absence of low-abundance taxa and abundance weighting should be ignored — unweighted UniFrac is the appropriate metric instead

skills.description: Use when two independent groups of per-pair scores (e.g., APSS from SNP-only vs indel-only Bacmeta simulations) must be compared statistically, and per-point variances or sample sizes may be unequal.
skills.name: welch-t-test-statistical-comparison
skills.search_text: welch-t-test-statistical-comparison Use when two independent groups of per-pair scores (e.g., APSS from SNP-only vs indel-only Bacmeta simulations) must be compared statistically, and per-point variances or sample sizes may be unequal. When the two score distributions are paired rather than independent (e.g., the same genome pair measured under both regimes) — a paired test would be required instead. When only the 40/60/80/100/200 subsampled APSS tables are used without verifying the all-regions APSS, since subsampling with seed=1 introduces run-to-run reproducibility assumptions. When the goal is effect-size or nonparametric inference on APSS distributions whose normality or variance structure has not been checked. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Apply Welch's t-test to compare Average Pairwise Synteny Score (APSS) distributions between experimental regimes — here, SNP-based vs indel-based in silico evolved populations — without assuming equal variances, to establish whether SynTracker synteny scores differ significantly by mutation mode. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41587-024-02276-2
skills.summary: Apply Welch's t-test to compare Average Pairwise Synteny Score (APSS) distributions between experimental regimes — here, SNP-based vs indel-based in silico evolved populations — without assuming equal variances, to establish whether SynTracker synteny scores differ significantly by mutation mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the two score distributions are paired rather than independent (e.g., the same genome pair measured under both regimes) — a paired test would be required instead. When only the 40/60/80/100/200 subsampled APSS tables are used without verifying the all-regions APSS, since subsampling with seed=1 introduces run-to-run reproducibility assumptions. When the goal is effect-size or nonparametric inference on APSS distributions whose normality or variance structure has not been checked.

skills.description: Use when the input is a collection of draft or complete genome FASTA assemblies and the goal is to define a new wgMLST or cgMLST schema seed from the distinct loci present in those genomes, prior to allele calling.
skills.name: wgmlst-schema-construction
skills.search_text: wgmlst-schema-construction Use when the input is a collection of draft or complete genome FASTA assemblies and the goal is to define a new wgMLST or cgMLST schema seed from the distinct loci present in those genomes, prior to allele calling. Input is raw sequencing reads rather than de novo assemblies — chewBBACA's schema creation and allele calling operate on complete or draft genome FASTA files A pre-existing or external schema already defines the loci (use AlleleCall against the existing schema, or PrepExternalSchema to adapt external schemas from platforms like EnteroBase, PubMLST, or Ridom cgMLST) The goal is allele calling only against an already-built schema seed rather than de novo locus definition Constructs a novel wg/cgMLST schema seed from a set of draft or complete bacterial genome assemblies using chewBBACA's CreateSchema, which predicts CDSs with Prodigal and clusters translated CDSs into loci via all-against-all BLASTp using a BLAST Score Ratio (BSR) threshold of 0.6. metagenomics/v1 10.1099/mgen.0.000166
skills.summary: Constructs a novel wg/cgMLST schema seed from a set of draft or complete bacterial genome assemblies using chewBBACA's CreateSchema, which predicts CDSs with Prodigal and clusters translated CDSs into loci via all-against-all BLASTp using a BLAST Score Ratio (BSR) threshold of 0.6.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than de novo assemblies — chewBBACA's schema creation and allele calling operate on complete or draft genome FASTA files A pre-existing or external schema already defines the loci (use AlleleCall against the existing schema, or PrepExternalSchema to adapt external schemas from platforms like EnteroBase, PubMLST, or Ridom cgMLST) The goal is allele calling only against an already-built schema seed rather than de novo locus definition

skills.description: Use when a sample-keyed WGS SNP distance matrix must be joined to a header-present clinical/epidemiological metadata CSV so downstream cluster visualization and analysis retain per-sample metadata.
skills.name: wgs-distance-matrix-metadata-coupling
skills.search_text: wgs-distance-matrix-metadata-coupling Use when a sample-keyed WGS SNP distance matrix must be joined to a header-present clinical/epidemiological metadata CSV so downstream cluster visualization and analysis retain per-sample metadata. Input is already a coupled genomic-plus-metadata record table produced by a prior CATHAI 'process' run Sample identifiers in the metadata CSV do not correspond to the IDs in the distance matrix (no shared sample-ID join key) The task is interactive cluster visualization only — in that case run the CATHAI webapp ('run' command) rather than re-deriving the metadata coupling http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Couple patient clinical and epidemiological metadata to a sample-keyed WGS distance matrix by joining on the shared sample-ID field, keeping metadata synchronized with selected genomic samples for clinically meaningful cluster interpretation in CATHAI. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbac040
skills.summary: Couple patient clinical and epidemiological metadata to a sample-keyed WGS distance matrix by joining on the shared sample-ID field, keeping metadata synchronized with selected genomic samples for clinically meaningful cluster interpretation in CATHAI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a coupled genomic-plus-metadata record table produced by a prior CATHAI 'process' run Sample identifiers in the metadata CSV do not correspond to the IDs in the distance matrix (no shared sample-ID join key) The task is interactive cluster visualization only — in that case run the CATHAI webapp ('run' command) rather than re-deriving the metadata coupling

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate metagenomic strain-specific contigs (e.g. walked from a MetaCortex GFA sequence graph) against per-strain references by comparing identity and variant counts against a baseline contig.
skills.name: whole-genome-alignment-variant-comparison
skills.search_text: whole-genome-alignment-variant-comparison Use when you need to quantitatively validate metagenomic strain-specific contigs (e.g. walked from a MetaCortex GFA sequence graph) against per-strain references by comparing identity and variant counts against a baseline contig. Input is a set of isolate (single-strain) assemblies with no mixed intra-species variation — a consensus contig already matches the reference and graph walking adds no value You only have a final contigs FASTA with no assembly graph (GFA), so strain-specific paths cannot be extracted for the per-strain comparison Strain references are unavailable, since dnadiff requires a cognate reference genome to compute identity and SNP/indel metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Validates reconstructed strain-specific contigs against cognate reference genomes using whole-genome pairwise alignment (dnadiff), quantifying average alignment identity and SNP/indel counts to demonstrate that graph-walked strain assemblies are more accurate per strain than the original consensus contig. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad020
skills.summary: Validates reconstructed strain-specific contigs against cognate reference genomes using whole-genome pairwise alignment (dnadiff), quantifying average alignment identity and SNP/indel counts to demonstrate that graph-walked strain assemblies are more accurate per strain than the original consensus contig.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a set of isolate (single-strain) assemblies with no mixed intra-species variation — a consensus contig already matches the reference and graph walking adds no value You only have a final contigs FASTA with no assembly graph (GFA), so strain-specific paths cannot be extracted for the per-strain comparison Strain references are unavailable, since dnadiff requires a cognate reference genome to compute identity and SNP/indel metrics

skills.description: Use when comparing taxon abundances between two cohorts (e.g. IBD patients vs controls) across a discovery and an independent replication cohort to identify validated differentially abundant taxa from MAGinator-derived abundance tables.
skills.name: wilcoxon-discovery-replication-differential-abundance
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-discovery-replication-differential-abundance Use when comparing taxon abundances between two cohorts (e.g. IBD patients vs controls) across a discovery and an independent replication cohort to identify validated differentially abundant taxa from MAGinator-derived abundance tables. The analysis question is about community-wide beta diversity separation (e.g. Jensen-Shannon PCoA and PERMANOVA testing) rather than per-taxon differential abundance The goal is functional annotation (KEGG orthologs, GO terms) or synteny clustering of genes rather than taxon-level abundance testing Abundances come directly from a marker-gene database profiler (e.g. MetaPhlAn2) when the intent is to exploit MAGinator's subspecies-level resolution instead of replicating the original baseline http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A two-cohort Wilcoxon rank-sum discovery/replication workflow for identifying and validating differentially abundant taxa between IBD patients and controls, applied to MAGinator's high-phylogenetic-resolution abundance matrices instead of the original MetaPhlAn2 profiles. metagenomics/v1 10.1038/s41467-024-49958-8
skills.summary: A two-cohort Wilcoxon rank-sum discovery/replication workflow for identifying and validating differentially abundant taxa between IBD patients and controls, applied to MAGinator's high-phylogenetic-resolution abundance matrices instead of the original MetaPhlAn2 profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis question is about community-wide beta diversity separation (e.g. Jensen-Shannon PCoA and PERMANOVA testing) rather than per-taxon differential abundance The goal is functional annotation (KEGG orthologs, GO terms) or synteny clustering of genes rather than taxon-level abundance testing Abundances come directly from a marker-gene database profiler (e.g. MetaPhlAn2) when the intent is to exploit MAGinator's subspecies-level resolution instead of replicating the original baseline

skills.description: Use when comparing a continuous per-gene metric (e.g., nucleotide diversity) between two independent patient groups — such as pre-treatment vs post-antibiotic time points — without assuming normality.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison Use when comparing a continuous per-gene metric (e.g., nucleotide diversity) between two independent patient groups — such as pre-treatment vs post-antibiotic time points — without assuming normality. The input is raw variant calls or BAM files — these must first be converted to per-gene nucleotide diversity values via cellsnp-lite, MetaQuad, and nucleotide_diversity_code.R. Comparing more than two groups or paired samples — the Wilcoxon rank-sum test as applied here is for two independent groups. Genes with insufficient coverage where diversity is undefined (e.g., zero covered bases in genome_length.csv/cov_bases.csv). http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Non-parametric Wilcoxon rank-sum testing used to identify antibiotic resistance genes whose nucleotide diversity differs significantly between LEVO-treated patient groups (pre-treatment '00' vs 6-weeks-post-treatment '01'), flagging the seven ARGs with P < .05. metagenomics/v1 10.1093/bioadv/vbae030
skills.summary: Non-parametric Wilcoxon rank-sum testing used to identify antibiotic resistance genes whose nucleotide diversity differs significantly between LEVO-treated patient groups (pre-treatment '00' vs 6-weeks-post-treatment '01'), flagging the seven ARGs with P < .05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw variant calls or BAM files — these must first be converted to per-gene nucleotide diversity values via cellsnp-lite, MetaQuad, and nucleotide_diversity_code.R. Comparing more than two groups or paired samples — the Wilcoxon rank-sum test as applied here is for two independent groups. Genes with insufficient coverage where diversity is undefined (e.g., zero covered bases in genome_length.csv/cov_bases.csv).

skills.description: Use when comparing microbial feature abundances between two binary groups from a 267-feature OTU/count table (e.g., testdata1) and you need robust nonparametric p-values per scenario of progressive permutation.
skills.name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing Use when comparing microbial feature abundances between two binary groups from a 267-feature OTU/count table (e.g., testdata1) and you need robust nonparametric p-values per scenario of progressive permutation. When you need false discovery rate control or adjusted p-values — the method explicitly does not control the FDR or calculate adjusted p-values When the grouping variable is not binary or you require a formal inferential test on the permutation results — AOI/AUMC measures are descriptive only When you specifically want a parametric negative binomial model — DESeq is supported as an alternative p-value source, but the article reports the Wilcoxon version achieves higher accuracy on simulated data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Applies the Wilcoxon rank sum test, the default differential abundance test in ProgPerm's progressive permutation, to compute per-feature p-values between two microbiome groups in each permutation scenario. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-021-04061-3
skills.summary: Applies the Wilcoxon rank sum test, the default differential abundance test in ProgPerm's progressive permutation, to compute per-feature p-values between two microbiome groups in each permutation scenario.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need false discovery rate control or adjusted p-values — the method explicitly does not control the FDR or calculate adjusted p-values When the grouping variable is not binary or you require a formal inferential test on the permutation results — AOI/AUMC measures are descriptive only When you specifically want a parametric negative binomial model — DESeq is supported as an alternative p-value source, but the article reports the Wilcoxon version achieves higher accuracy on simulated data

skills.description: Use when comparing two methods' error metrics (e.g., MSE of estimated source mixing proportions) measured on the same paired benchmark instances — such as in vitro gut-mixture sinks with known ground-truth proportions — and a nonparametric paired significance test is needed.
skills.name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
skills.search_text: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing Use when comparing two methods' error metrics (e.g., MSE of estimated source mixing proportions) measured on the same paired benchmark instances — such as in vitro gut-mixture sinks with known ground-truth proportions — and a nonparametric paired significance test is needed. The comparison samples are independent/unpaired (e.g., different sinks per method) rather than the same sinks tested by all methods — a rank-sum/unpaired formulation would then be the appropriate framing The metric distribution is known to be normal and sample sizes are large enough that a paired t-test is preferred, or the data are ordinal with many ties that violate signed-rank assumptions There is no ground truth (true mixing proportions) available to compute per-sink error, so no paired error metric exists to test http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Apply Wilcoxon signed-rank tests to nonparametrically compare mixing-proportion estimation errors (MSE) of microbial source tracking methods — STENSL vs FEAST, SourceTracker2, and RAD — across the same set of in vitro gut-mixture sinks, yielding the significance thresholds reported in the STENSL paper (Fig 3). metagenomics/v1 10.1128/msystems.00995-21
skills.summary: Apply Wilcoxon signed-rank tests to nonparametrically compare mixing-proportion estimation errors (MSE) of microbial source tracking methods — STENSL vs FEAST, SourceTracker2, and RAD — across the same set of in vitro gut-mixture sinks, yielding the significance thresholds reported in the STENSL paper (Fig 3).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison samples are independent/unpaired (e.g., different sinks per method) rather than the same sinks tested by all methods — a rank-sum/unpaired formulation would then be the appropriate framing The metric distribution is known to be normal and sample sizes are large enough that a paired t-test is preferred, or the data are ordinal with many ties that violate signed-rank assumptions There is no ground truth (true mixing proportions) available to compute per-sink error, so no paired error metric exists to test

skills.description: Use when deep-sequencing reads of a genetically heterogeneous viral sample must be aligned to a reference and split into overlapping windows to support local haplotype reconstruction and error correction.
skills.name: windowed-multiple-sequence-alignment-construction

You only need single nucleotide variant calls without local haplotype context — shorah snv can be run for SNV calling directly, taking strand bias into account You require global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction from ShoRAH2, which has global mode disabled; use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or V-pipe's global haplotype options instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Construct and window a multiple sequence alignment (MSA) of reads aligned to a reference (e.g., HIV-1 subtype B pol) so that each genome position is covered by multiple overlapping windows of approximately read length, enabling local haplotype reconstruction with ShoRAH's diri_sampler. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/1471-2105-12-119
skills.summary: Construct and window a multiple sequence alignment (MSA) of reads aligned to a reference (e.g., HIV-1 subtype B pol) so that each genome position is covered by multiple overlapping windows of approximately read length, enabling local haplotype reconstruction with ShoRAH's diri_sampler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need single nucleotide variant calls without local haplotype context — shorah snv can be run for SNV calling directly, taking strand bias into account You require global (full-length) haplotype reconstruction from ShoRAH2, which has global mode disabled; use ShoRAH v1.1.3 or V-pipe's global haplotype options instead

skills.description: Use when WGS read pairs from mixed-infected samples must be typed at MLST loci (e.g. the 8-gene B. burgdorferi scheme with 1726 alleles and 753 strain types) to infer per-sample allele proportions and strain-type mixtures, including novel strains.
skills.name: within-host-pathogen-strain-diversity-analysis
skills.search_text: within-host-pathogen-strain-diversity-analysis Use when WGS read pairs from mixed-infected samples must be typed at MLST loci (e.g. the 8-gene B. burgdorferi scheme with 1726 alleles and 753 strain types) to infer per-sample allele proportions and strain-type mixtures, including novel strains. De novo strain reconstruction is required where reference alleles or known MLST strain types are unavailable — the paper explicitly notes de novo methods like DESMAN 'cannot take advantage of known reference strains', and this pipeline depends on the MLST database Samples with a single, clonal strain and no within-host heterogeneity, where a simple allele caller suffices Species or pathogens other than B. burgdorferi without an equivalent MLST allele/strain-type database and per-gene edit-distance matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Deconvolves within-host pathogen strain composition by applying the paper's two-stage mixed integer linear programming pipeline (Allele Diversity Problem, then Strain Diversity Problem) to MLST-sequenced Borrelia burgdorferi tick samples, detecting both known and novel strains despite within-host heterogeneity. metagenomics/v1 10.1186/s12859-019-3204-8
skills.summary: Deconvolves within-host pathogen strain composition by applying the paper's two-stage mixed integer linear programming pipeline (Allele Diversity Problem, then Strain Diversity Problem) to MLST-sequenced Borrelia burgdorferi tick samples, detecting both known and novel strains despite within-host heterogeneity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: De novo strain reconstruction is required where reference alleles or known MLST strain types are unavailable — the paper explicitly notes de novo methods like DESMAN 'cannot take advantage of known reference strains', and this pipeline depends on the MLST database Samples with a single, clonal strain and no within-host heterogeneity, where a simple allele caller suffices Species or pathogens other than B. burgdorferi without an equivalent MLST allele/strain-type database and per-gene edit-distance matrices

skills.description: Use when you have simulated longitudinal metagenomic reads (e.g. CAMISIM output directory or ART-simulated FASTQ reads) and need ground-truth within-strain SNV/InDel mutations injected across time points.
skills.name: within-strain-mutation-injection
